name: 10,000 Bird Genomes
summary: Aims to produce draft genome sequences for all living bird species.

name: 10,000 Plant Genomes
summary: Aims to sequence over 10,000 genomes across the major clades of plants and eukaryotic microbes.

name: 100 Island Challenge
summary: Collaborative effort based at Scripps that combines classical field surveys with imaging and data technologies to archive coral reefs digitally.

name: 5,000 Insect Genomes
summary: Sequences and analyses the genomes of 5,000 arthropod species and sets guidelines for arthropod genome projects.

name: 51 Degrees Ltd.
summary: Kenyan company offering protected area management, ranger training and technology services. It is a partner of EarthRanger and says its developers work with the EarthRanger team.

name: Aarhus University
summary: Danish public research university that coordinates the Horizon Europe MAMBO biodiversity monitoring project.

name: ABALOBI
summary: South African-based non-profit that builds data and traceability tools with small-scale fishing communities, including toolkits for recording local ecological knowledge.

name: ABC Scientific Sound Collection
summary: Freely available library of bioacoustic recordings from southern Africa, kept by the African Bioacoustics Community under Creative Commons licences.

name: Aberystwyth University
summary: Welsh university with remote sensing researchers in its Department of Geography and Earth Sciences who work on Global Mangrove Watch.

name: abrdn Charitable Foundation
summary: Corporate charitable foundation of abrdn that committed £1 million to a research programme with The Alan Turing Institute and the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology on AI monitoring of biodiversity.

name: Accenture
summary: Professional services company that built Project CORaiL with Intel and the Sulubaaï Environmental Foundation.

name: ACCOBAMS
summary: Agreement on cetacean conservation with its secretariat in Monaco, which runs the ACCOBAMS Survey Initiative of large coordinated surveys and offers access to its data.

name: Accounting for Nature
summary: Publisher of a science-backed standard for measuring the state of nature, listed as Australia and the UK in the Biodiversity Accelerator+.

name: Acoustic_Indices
summary: Python library that extracts acoustic indices such as the Acoustic Complexity Index and Bioacoustic Index from audio as a biodiversity proxy, with research reportedly funded by a Leverhulme grant.

name: Actility
summary: Co-inventor of LoRaWAN technology. Its network server connects sensors for conservation projects with the Connected Conservation Foundation in Kenya, South Africa and Uganda.

name: Acústica Marina
summary: Chilean start-up from Valdivia making hydroacoustic hardware and an AI ocean intelligence platform, used for marine fauna detection and detecting illegal activities.

name: AdAstra Sustainability
summary: Swiss company behind Orbae, which uses satellite data to map land conversion in agricultural supply chains and is free to use. A project partner of Trase.

name: Addax Data Science
summary: Offers custom coding for ecologists and makes AddaxAI, open-source software for identifying animals in camera-trap images.

name: AddaxAI
summary: Open-source software that identifies animals in camera-trap photos and videos, using MegaDetector and regional species models.

name: Adessium Foundation
summary: Independent philanthropic fund supporting civil society organisations in the Netherlands and Europe since 2005. It is a listed funder of Global Fishing Watch.

name: Adopt-a-water-tower initiative
summary: IBM and Kenyan government initiative under the National Tree Growing and Restoration Campaign, with a digital platform that uses IBM's geospatial foundation model to track tree planting in water tower areas.

name: Advanced Telemetry Systems
summary: Minnesota company that makes fish and wildlife tracking equipment, including GPS collars and acoustic tags for researchers.

name: Adventure Scientists
summary: Non-profit in Bozeman, Montana, that trains outdoor enthusiasts and local communities to collect field data for conservation partners.

name: AECOM
summary: Consultancy working with the Lifescape Project to run the Natural Capital Laboratory in the Scottish Highlands.

name: Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences
summary: Beijing institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Its State Key Laboratory of Remote Sensing produced GLC_FCS30, a global 30 m land cover product.

name: African Association of Remote Sensing of the Environment
summary: Regional member of ISPRS for remote sensing of the environment in Africa; ISPRS lists its contact at Obafemi Awolowo University in Nigeria.

name: African BioGenome Project
summary: Pan-African initiative supporting genome sequencing of African species for conservation and food systems.

name: African Carnivore Wildbook
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that uses AI to identify African carnivores from photographs.

name: African Development Bank Group
summary: Development bank group whose African Development Fund approved a grant in 2026 to integrate natural capital into development financing in 13 countries. No AI work found in this search.

name: African Institute for Mathematical Sciences
summary: Institute whose South African centre in Muizenberg, Cape Town, hosts the Machine Learning for Ecology Research Group.

name: African Parks
summary: Non-profit that manages protected areas in partnership with governments and local communities across African countries, and uses EarthRanger across its parks.

name: African Space Agency
summary: Space agency of the African Union, with its permanent headquarters in Cairo, inaugurated in April 2025. It is a member of the Committee on Earth Observation Satellites and has a memorandum with the European Space Agency that covers Earth observation and data sharing.

name: African Tropical Rainforest Observation Network
summary: International network of researchers doing long-term, on-the-ground monitoring of African tropical forests, following RAINFOR protocols.

name: African Union Commission
summary: Secretariat of the African Union in Addis Ababa. It co-funds GMES and Africa, the Earth observation programme, with the European Union.

name: African Wildlife Foundation
summary: Conservation organisation headquartered in Nairobi. It has trained rangers to record wildlife and threats with CyberTracker and to manage patrol data in SMART.

name: African-Eurasian Waterbird Census
summary: Regional part of the International Waterbird Census, coordinated by a regional office of Wetlands International.

name: AfriGEO
summary: African group of the Group on Earth Observations, set up to take GEO's work to member states, reduce duplicated effort and increase the use of Earth observation in decisions.

name: AfrikENCA
summary: Geospatial platform for ecosystem accounts in Africa that uses satellite imagery to characterise land use and ecosystem condition in six countries.

name: Agreement on the Conservation of African-Eurasian Migratory Waterbirds
summary: Intergovernmental treaty on migratory waterbirds and their habitats, with a secretariat among the UN organisations in Bonn. It prepares a conservation status report on waterbirds and collects population status reports from its parties.

name: Agreement on the Conservation of Albatrosses and Petrels
summary: Multilateral agreement that coordinates international action on threats to albatrosses, petrels and shearwaters, and runs a data portal.

name: AGRHYMET Regional Centre
summary: Regional centre of CILSS, the Sahel intergovernmental drought committee, based in Niamey. Its site carries SERVIR West Africa, a satellite data programme, and land management work in the Sahel and West Africa.

name: AgriSound
summary: British company using continuous acoustic monitoring of pollinators on farms to report on production, biodiversity and environmental data.

name: AI and Biodiversity Change Global Center
summary: International research centre led by The Ohio State University that develops AI-enabled approaches to monitoring how environmental change affects biodiversity, with six universities in the United States and Canada and partners elsewhere.

name: AI Earth
summary: Alibaba Cloud platform from DAMO Academy for retrieving, processing and analysing remote sensing data and for training and deploying models.

name: AI for Climate
summary: The conservation AI programme lists reserve living labs and reports automated species detection at Dzilam State Reserve in 2022–2024, with 24 camera traps and 600,000-plus audio files collected.

name: AI for Climate and Nature Grand Challenge
summary: Bezos Earth Fund grant competition, launched in 2024 with a commitment of up to $100 million, for AI work on biodiversity loss, climate change and food. It paid 24 Phase I grants of $50,000 in May 2025 and 15 Phase II awards of up to $2 million each in October 2025.

name: AI for Earth
summary: Microsoft programme announced in 2017 that gave researchers and organisations grants of cloud and AI computing on water, agriculture, biodiversity and climate change. No source seen says whether it still runs.

name: AI for Earth Innovation Grant
summary: $1 million grant programme from Microsoft and National Geographic, announced in 2018, for between five and 15 projects using AI in conservation research. Grants supported open-source models and algorithms.

name: AI for European Wildlife Challenge
summary: FruitPunch AI challenge, in April 2023 with the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, Rewilding Europe and WWF Spain, to build computer vision models that identify European wildlife in camera trap images.

name: AI for Good AI for Biodiversity series
summary: Discovery series launched in February 2023 by ITU's AI for Good with the CBD, NatureServe and Colombia's Humboldt Institute on AI and biodiversity knowledge. Whether it is still running is not confirmed.

name: AI for Nature and Climate grant fund
summary: Open call for AI-enabled solutions from Brazilian nonprofits and research centres on biodiversity, bioeconomy and regenerative agriculture, paid for by $3 million from Google.org and run by Instituto Clima e Sociedade.

name: AI for the Planet Initiative
summary: NCEAS programme supporting skill building and community around environmental applications of AI.

name: AI Guardian of Endangered Species
summary: Image recognition model from Baidu's PaddlePaddle team and the International Fund for Animal Welfare that finds wildlife product images in online trade, trained on IFAW's image data.

name: Ai2 Wildlands
summary: Ai2 work that applies machine learning to wildlands management, helping land managers record and assess conditions.

name: AiDash
summary: Company that developed BNGAI, an AI nature intelligence platform used for biodiversity assessment.

name: AIM4Commodities
summary: FAO programme under which the Whisp and GeoID tools for deforestation risk in supply chains are developed.

name: AIM4Forests
summary: FAO programme with the United Kingdom that supports countries' forest monitoring data systems and digital public infrastructure, including through AI and machine learning.

name: AIR Centre
summary: Atlantic International Research Centre, which runs an Earth observation catalogue of data received at its station in the Azores. MBON lists it as a collaborator.

name: Airbus
summary: Aerospace group whose space division runs Pléiades Neo and SPOT Earth observation data and the Starling deforestation monitoring service.

name: Airbus Foundation
summary: Corporate foundation under French law, established in 2008. With the Connected Conservation Foundation it gives environmental NGOs very high-resolution satellite imagery and runs the Satellites for Biodiversity Award.

name: AirSeed
summary: Carries out technology-led restoration and land management using drones, with teams of ecologists, data scientists and engineers.

name: Alana Foundation
summary: Part of Alana, a social and environmental impact group. It sponsored the XPRIZE Rainforest competition on autonomous biodiversity monitoring.

name: Alfred Wegener Institute
summary: German polar and marine research centre in Bremerhaven, a Helmholtz member, whose researchers built the DeepLOKI zooplankton classifier and collaborate on the AqQua foundation model.

name: AlgaeBase
summary: Database of information on algae, including terrestrial, marine and freshwater organisms.

name: Alianza Aguas Amazónicas
summary: Network of more than 30 organisations from seven countries working to keep Amazon Basin aquatic ecosystems intact and connected, and a publisher of records through GBIF.

name: Alibaba Cloud
summary: Cloud arm of Alibaba whose DAMO Academy built AI Earth, a platform for remote sensing analysis used in natural resources, water and environmental work.

name: Allen Coral Atlas
summary: Global maps of coral reef habitats with a bleaching monitoring system and turbidity detection, powered by Arizona State University.

name: Allen Family Philanthropies
summary: Philanthropy founded in 1988 by Jody Allen and Paul G. Allen, with arts, youth and environment programmes. It invests in science and technology to protect wildlife and habitats, unveiled the Allen Coral Atlas under its earlier name and funds Earth Species Project.

name: Allen Institute for AI
summary: Seattle non-profit AI research institute founded by Paul Allen that builds OlmoEarth, EarthRanger, Skylight and Satlas.

name: Alliance for Zero Extinction
summary: Joint initiative of biodiversity conservation organisations that identifies and maps the sites holding the last populations of highly threatened species. Its data and website are managed by American Bird Conservancy and BirdLife International.

name: Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT
summary: Research alliance that hosted the SERVIR Amazonia hub in Cali and a SERVIR East Africa role in Nairobi.

name: ALOS Kyoto & Carbon Initiative
summary: International research project led by JAXA that develops L-band radar products on forest extent and biomass, wetland inundation and glaciers.

name: AlphaEarth Foundations
summary: AI model that integrates Earth observation data into embeddings of the planet's terrestrial land and coastal waters, released through the Satellite Embedding dataset in Google Earth Engine.

name: Alumbra Innovations Foundation
summary: Foundation in Bentonville, Arkansas. Kindora lists a $150,000 grant to Red de Observadores Ciudadanos in 2025 to strengthen marine surveillance in Baja California Sur, Mexico.

name: Amazon Conservation
summary: Non-profit working in the Amazon that runs the Monitoring of the Andes Amazon Program, which uses satellites and automated forest loss alerts to detect deforestation.

name: Amazon Conservation Team
summary: NGO working with Indigenous communities in Amazonia; it partnered with Amazon Conservation Association on near-real-time forest monitoring from remote sensing.

name: Amazon Cooperation Treaty Organization
summary: Intergovernmental organisation of Amazon countries that runs the Amazon Regional Observatory.

name: Amazon Frontlines
summary: Organisation started with Indigenous peoples in the Amazon, with a monitoring and mapping programme. It co-created the Earth Defenders Toolkit.

name: Amazon Mining Watch
summary: Platform that uses AI on satellite imagery to map gold mining across all nine Amazonian countries, developed by the Pulitzer Center's Rainforest Investigations Network, Amazon Conservation Association and Earth Genome.

name: Amazon Regional Observatory
summary: ACTO's reference centre for scientific knowledge and regional cooperation on the Amazon, publishing data bulletins.

name: Amazon Sustainability Data Initiative
summary: Amazon programme that hosts commonly used sustainability datasets for free on AWS and offers cloud credits to researchers who analyse them, including biodiversity and ecosystem modelling work.

name: Amazon Sustainable Landscapes Programme
summary: World Bank-led programme in the Amazon. APA News says it lets countries share data to improve monitoring and predictive modelling.

name: Amazon Web Services
summary: Cloud company that hosts open environmental data through the Registry of Open Data and the Amazon Sustainability Data Initiative and funds nonprofit technology work through the AWS Imagine Grant.

name: Amazon.ia – Inteligencia Ambiental
summary: Multi-partner initiative announced by Planet in September 2026 that combines satellite imagery with field data and uses AI to track biodiversity and ecosystem health across the Amazon.

name: Amazonia Forever
summary: IDB Group regional coordination programme for sustainable and inclusive development in the Amazon, which scales financing and shares evidence-based innovations.

name: AmazoniaForever360+
summary: Pan-Amazonian territorial intelligence platform launched by the IDB in 2025, with more than 140 georeferenced indicators and reports with AI-powered narratives. Built with Vizzuality.

name: American Bird Conservancy
summary: Bird conservation organisation working across the Americas. Its BirdsPlus Index uses recorders and AI to identify bird calls and track biodiversity. A co-leader of Conserva Aves.

name: Americas Biodiversity Observation Network
summary: Regional arm of GEO BON, coordinated by NatureServe, that brings organisations across the Americas together on biodiversity data.

name: AMI Dataset
summary: Dataset for identifying insects in images from camera traps, described in the paper Insect Identification in the Wild, by Aditya Jain and 27 other authors.

name: Amphibian and Reptile Wildbook
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that uses AI to identify amphibians and reptiles from photographs.

name: Amphibian Genomics Consortium
summary: International initiative bringing together people who use genomic tools to study amphibian ecology, evolution and conservation.

name: AmphibiaWeb
summary: Collaboration that synthesises and shares information about amphibians to enable research, education and conservation, led by the University of California Berkeley.

name: amt Animal Movement Tools
summary: R package for managing and analysing animal movement data, covering home ranges, track statistics, habitat selection and space-use simulation; its latest version reached CRAN on 30 January 2026.

name: Ancient Environmental Genomics Initiative for Sustainability
summary: Global consortium led by the Globe Institute at the University of Copenhagen that uses ancient environmental DNA to study natural and farmed ecosystems, including biodiversity in cropping systems.

name: Andes Amazon Fund
summary: Grant maker that funds protected areas and Indigenous land recognition in the Andes and the Amazon. It is a regranting partner in Amazon.ia and has funded analyses by the Monitoring of the Andes Amazon Program.

name: Animal Borne Ocean Sensors
summary: Network of the Global Ocean Observing System that provides free oceanographic data collected by sensors deployed on marine animals.

name: Animal Scanner
summary: Software that classifies humans, animals and empty frames in camera-trap images, using background subtraction across sequences to find moving objects and a deep convolutional network to classify regions.

name: ANIMAL-SPOT
summary: Animal-independent deep learning framework for identifying bioacoustic signals, built on a ResNet18 convolutional network and evaluated on ten species and one genus, including killer whale and Atlantic cod.

name: Animl
summary: Web application for viewing and labelling camera trap data, with machine learning resources for camera trap data processing, from The Nature Conservancy.

name: Anitra
summary: Czech company offering GSM-GPS tags and a tracking data system, working with the Czech ringing station.

name: Another Earth
summary: Vienna start-up that generates synthetic satellite imagery to train AI models, and says this helps monitor biodiversity and track deforestation.

name: Ant Group
summary: Financial technology company, an Alibaba affiliate, that launched Ant Forest on Alipay.

name: Antenna
summary: Insect data platform from Mila, a partner in the global Automated Monitoring of Insects consortium, that helps scientists study insect populations.

name: ANTENNA pollinator monitoring project
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project, 2024 to 2027, developing automated sample sorting and image recognition tools for European pollinator monitoring.

name: AnuraSet
summary: Open dataset of Neotropical frog calls for benchmarking automated identification in passive acoustic monitoring, with authors in Colombia, Brazil and the United States.

name: Aphorism Foundation
summary: Foundation recorded as giving Earth Species Project $10 million in 2024.

name: apic.ai
summary: Start-up in Karlsruhe that uses computer vision and artificial intelligence to monitor bees, for work on protecting bees and biodiversity.

name: Applied Conservation Technology Congress
summary: Conference for rangers, researchers and technologists on field conservation technology. The first edition took place in Hanoi with more than 400 participants, co-hosted by EarthRanger, the SMART Partnership, Vietnam's forestry administration and Save Vietnam's Wildlife.

name: Applied Remote Sensing Training Program
summary: NASA-run training programme in applied remote sensing, which held an online satellite series on conservation and biodiversity in January 2019 and offers GEDI lidar vegetation mapping training.

name: Appsilon
summary: Warsaw data science company whose Data for Good work on climate and biodiversity includes the Mbaza AI camera trap app.

name: AqQua
summary: Helmholtz project compiling billions of images to train a foundation AI model for pelagic imaging, covering species classification and organic carbon.

name: AquaINFRA
summary: EU project building a virtual environment of FAIR data and services for marine and freshwater scientists.

name: AquaMaps
summary: Standardised distribution maps for over 33,500 species of fishes, marine mammals and invertebrates.

name: AquaMonitor
summary: Multimodal, multi-view image sequence dataset for monitoring aquatic invertebrate biodiversity.

name: Aquatic Symbiosis Genomics Project
summary: Project applying genomics to 1,000 aquatic species in 500 symbiotic relationships, hosted by the Wellcome Sanger Institute and funded with the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation.

name: Arbimon
summary: Ecoacoustic analysis platform for uploading, storing and analysing large amounts of acoustic data with AI tools.

name: Arbonaut
summary: Finnish forest inventory and geospatial company offering forest carbon monitoring and REDD+ solutions, with work it says spans more than 30 countries.

name: Arcadia
summary: Family philanthropy founded by Lisbet Rausing and Peter Baldwin in 2002, with funding areas in nature, culture and open access. It gave Plazi and the Biodiversity Literature Repository EUR 1.1 million to open up data held in biodiversity publications.

name: Archeda
summary: Japanese company using satellite data to measure nature-based carbon credits.

name: Archipelago Marine Research
summary: Canadian fisheries monitoring company in Victoria, on the NOAA list of approved electronic monitoring providers, with an AI-assisted video review product.

name: Arctic Biodiversity Dashboard
summary: Interactive platform from the Conservation of Arctic Flora and Fauna working group that visualises Arctic biodiversity datasets for tracking and reporting.

name: Arctic Biodiversity Data Service
summary: CAFF data service for Arctic biodiversity data.

name: Arctic Council
summary: High-level intergovernmental forum of the Arctic states, whose working groups include the Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Programme and Conservation of Arctic Flora and Fauna.

name: Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Programme
summary: Arctic Council working group that monitors and assesses pollution and climate issues in the Arctic. This entry covers its documentation of their effects on ecosystems.

name: Arctos Consortium
summary: Self-governing consortium that runs Arctos, a web-based system for managing and publishing biological, geological and cultural collections data.

name: ArgusWild AI
summary: Tech4Conservation's AI platform for wildlife research data, which it says spans five continents.

name: ARIES
summary: International collaboration, presented on its site as ARtificial Intelligence for Environment and Sustainability, that has built a shared semantic web knowledge space and trains scientists and policy analysts.

name: ARIES for SEEA Explorer
summary: AI application for compiling ecosystem accounts under the SEEA standard, launched in beta in 2021 by UNSD, UNEP and the Basque Centre for Climate Change, using the ARIES platform.

name: ARISE
summary: Dutch research infrastructure for identifying all multicellular species in the Netherlands, combining DNA, images, sounds and AI models.

name: Arizona State University
summary: US university whose Center for Global Discovery and Conservation Science leads the Allen Coral Atlas.

name: Arkadiah Technology
summary: Nature technology start-up that uses AI to fuse LiDAR, satellite imagery and ground data for forest carbon and natural capital measurement. It signed a five-year agreement with Golden Agri-Resources in February 2026.

name: Arm
summary: British semiconductor and software design company headquartered in Cambridge. WILDLABS says it provides the core funding for the WILDLABS Awards.

name: Arribada Initiative
summary: UK-based not-for-profit that co-develops open source conservation technology, such as biologging tags, with conservation organisations.

name: artemis
summary: R package for designing and analysing eDNA survey studies, with Bayesian models for sampling and qPCR data fitted using Stan.

name: ascr
summary: R package that fits spatial capture-recapture models to estimate animal density from acoustic surveys; it is no longer under active development, as work has moved to the acre package.

name: ASEAN Biodiversity Dashboard
summary: Map-based tool for monitoring species distributions, richness, habitat change and zoonotic threats in the ASEAN region, with over 23 million occurrence records as of June 2026.

name: ASEAN Centre for Biodiversity
summary: ASEAN regional body that runs the ASEAN Biodiversity Dashboard and a biodiversity knowledge platform.

name: Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment
summary: Non-profit Indian research organisation on environmental conservation and sustainable development, funded by the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation to broaden access to data on natural assets.

name: Asia-Pacific Biodiversity Observation Network
summary: Regional network linked to GEO BON, covering most Asia-Pacific countries, which links biodiversity observation from remote sensing, ecological research and species and genetic research.

name: Asia-Pacific Network for Global Change Research
summary: Asia-Pacific network supporting global change research in its member countries. It has funded an environmental DNA reference database for Southeast Asian mangroves.

name: Asian Association on Remote Sensing
summary: Regional member of ISPRS for remote sensing in Asia, with its secretariat in Tokyo.

name: Asian Development Bank
summary: Development bank that announced in 2026 a biodiversity bond, an investment incubator and a joint report on tracking nature finance. No AI work found in this search.

name: Asian Disaster Preparedness Center
summary: Centre in Bangkok that SERVIR lists as the host of a regional hub with a consortium of partners.

name: Asian Waterbird Census
summary: Regional part of the International Waterbird Census, coordinated by a regional office of Wetlands International.

name: Ask Google Earth
summary: Chat panel in Google Earth, powered by Google's Geospatial Reasoning agent, that answers spatial questions in natural language using Gemini and Earth AI models and data. Experimental, in early access; the partner tests named are in health and disaster work, one of which used forest loss data.

name: ASL Environmental Sciences
summary: Canadian maker of oceanographic and underwater acoustic instruments, including the Acoustic Zooplankton Fish Profiler, which also sells DeCAF, a satellite monitoring service using AI.

name: AstraZeneca
summary: Pharmaceutical company whose AZ Forest programme funds tree planting in Kenya, reported with an AI monitoring system.

name: AtlantECO
summary: EU-funded research project on Atlantic Ocean microbiomes, microplastics and seascape connectivity, with experts from Europe, South America and Africa.

name: Atlas of Living Australia
summary: Australia's open biodiversity data infrastructure, hosted by CSIRO and the country's GBIF node.

name: AudioMoth
summary: Low-cost, open-source acoustic monitoring device used for work such as listening for bats and monitoring poaching by gunshot.

name: Australian Acoustic Observatory
summary: Continental-scale acoustic sensor network across Australian ecosystems, recording for a five-year period, with data freely available.

name: Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
summary: Australian government department named as a funding partner of Digital Earth Africa, with the Helmsley Charitable Trust.

name: Australian Institute of Marine Science
summary: Tropical marine research centre near Townsville, Queensland, that created ReefCloud with reef scientists across the Indo-Pacific.

name: Auto Arborist
summary: Google dataset of over 2 million urban trees in more than 300 genera across 23 cities in the United States and Canada, built from public tree censuses with street and aerial imagery. It was taken down on 27 May 2025.

name: Avian Knowledge Network
summary: Partnership of federal and state agencies and non-governmental organisations that shares bird data and informatics across the Western Hemisphere.

name: Avina Foundation
summary: Foundation founded in 1994 by Stephan Schmidheiny and based in Panama. MapBiomas Alerta lists it among institutional partners.

name: Avisoft Bioacoustics
summary: German bioacoustics equipment and software company, acquired by Lafayette Instrument Company in July 2026.

name: AVONET
summary: Functional trait data for all birds, with morphological measurements from 90,020 individuals of 11,009 extant species.

name: Awana Digital
summary: Non-profit building decentralised technology with Indigenous partners, including CoMapeo, Terrastories and the Earth Defenders Toolkit.

name: awesome-forests
summary: Curated list of ground-truth, validation and in situ forest datasets for machine learning, covering topics such as biodiversity, carbon and wildfire, and excluding algorithm-generated products like global maps.

name: AWS Imagine Grant
summary: Public grant from AWS for registered nonprofits using cloud technology, with a generative AI award. Its 2024-2025 winners included The Nature Conservancy, Kent Wildlife Trust and the Wildlife Conservation Society.

name: AXOLOTL
summary: Three-year Horizon Europe project coordinated by the Cyprus Marine and Maritime Institute that applies deep learning to monitoring maritime traffic and marine biodiversity in the Mediterranean.

name: B-Cubed
summary: EU project, March 2023 to August 2026, that standardised access to biodiversity data as data cubes for indicators; its outputs include the DeepMaxent species distribution model.

name: BAGEL
summary: Benchmark of animal knowledge in language models.

name: Baidu
summary: Technology company whose PaddlePaddle deep learning platform underlies the AI Guardian of Endangered Species, built with the International Fund for Animal Welfare.

name: Ballmer Group
summary: Philanthropy that is a named donor to the Audacious Project raise for Global Fishing Watch and a listed funder of MapBiomas.

name: bambird
summary: Python package offering a workflow to build a labelling function that separates bird song from noise, using DBSCAN or BirdNET, and tested on songs from 44 West-Palearctic bird species.

name: BAND Foundation
summary: Foundation that Kindora lists in Wilmington, Delaware. Its grants include species recovery funds and $150,000 to iNaturalist in 2025.

name: BANTER
summary: R package for building hierarchical acoustic event classifiers from several call type detectors, using training data that carry a species label for each event.

name: Barcode of Life Data Systems
summary: Data platform for the acquisition, validation, analysis and publication of DNA barcodes, used for DNA-based species identification.

name: Basecamp Research
summary: London company that trains AI models for therapeutic design on BaseData, a proprietary evolutionary genomic dataset it says comes from biodiversity partners on all seven continents.

name: Basque Centre for Climate Change
summary: Research centre founded by the Basque Government and the University of the Basque Country, whose ARIES platform integrates data and models to simulate environmental and socioeconomic systems, used in the UN ARIES for SEEA Explorer.

name: Bat1K
summary: Consortium that aims to sequence the genomes of all living bat species, about 1,400 in total.

name: BEAGLE
summary: Horizon Europe project on biodiversity methods for advanced monitoring at large scales, coordinated by Aarhus University, with an EU contribution of about 11 million euros.

name: BEANS
summary: Benchmark of bioacoustics classification and detection tasks built from 12 public datasets, used to measure machine learning methods on animal sounds.

name: BearID Project
summary: Project developing machine learning software to identify individual bears from face recognition, for use with camera trap imagery.

name: Becht Foundation
summary: Foundation funding marine conservation and climate communications, registered as a charity in England and Wales. Global Fishing Watch names it among the funders of its Audacious Project.

name: BeeOdiversity
summary: Belgian company that measures biodiversity for businesses and says it works in more than 25 countries, listing satellite and AI methods among its tools.

name: Beery Lab
summary: MIT research group that combines computer vision, deep learning and ecology to develop methods for global-scale environmental and biodiversity monitoring.

name: Belmont Forum
summary: Partnership of funding agencies, international scientific councils and regional consortia that funds transnational research on global environmental change through coordinated calls, and promotes open data access.

name: Benguela Current Convention
summary: Intergovernmental organisation set up by Angola, Namibia and South Africa for the Benguela Current, listed as a member of the GMES and Africa marine consortium.

name: BenthicNet
summary: Global compilation of seafloor images for deep learning, assembled by a multi-institution team.

name: Bertarelli Foundation
summary: Foundation that announced a marine science programme in the British Indian Ocean Territory in 2017, with a $12 million investment for 50 researchers from 14 institutions, coordinated by the Zoological Society of London.

name: BeWild
summary: Fugro project with partners to measure biodiversity at offshore wind farms in the North Sea by remotely collecting environmental DNA samples.

name: Bezos Earth Fund
summary: Philanthropic fund set up by Jeff Bezos with an initial $10 billion commitment, which funds work on climate and nature, including AI through its AI Grand Challenge and monitoring through satellite and data programmes.

name: BiCIKL
summary: EU project that linked European research infrastructures for biodiversity, opening access to data and literature.

name: BiCOME
summary: ESA project on global Earth observation products for biodiversity science and policy in the coastal zone.

name: BIG_PICTURE
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project, 2024 to 2027, building data management, AI image processing and statistical tools to join professional and citizen science camera trapping across Europe.

name: BigEarthNet
summary: Benchmark data set of 549,488 paired Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 patches from ten European countries with land cover labels, built at TU Berlin.

name: Bio-ORACLE
summary: Marine physical, chemical, biological and topographic data layers with global extent for modelling the distribution of marine biodiversity.

name: BioacAI
summary: Horizon Europe doctoral network coordinated by Naturalis that develops AI methods for acoustic wildlife monitoring.

name: BioBench
summary: Benchmark library for biology-related computer vision tasks that lets people evaluate models and add new tasks.

name: BioBoost+
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project, 2024 to 2027, applying AI to identify and count marine species from photographs, video and aerial images.

name: BiOceanOr
summary: French company combining biology and AI to provide water quality data services, mainly for aquaculture.

name: BioClima
summary: EU-China project that merges AI with ground and remote sensing data for biodiversity and climate monitoring of land ecosystems, coordinated by the University of West Bohemia.

name: BioCLIP
summary: Vision foundation model for the tree of life, a CLIP model trained on 10 million images of organisms with fine-grained taxonomic labels.

name: BioCLIP 2
summary: Biological image foundation model trained on TreeOfLife-200M, a dataset of biology images, for species classification and trait patterns.

name: Biodiv-Wind
summary: French company that develops and operates AI wildlife detection systems to reduce collisions of flying fauna with wind turbines, with more than 500 turbines equipped in western Europe.

name: Biodiversa+
summary: European Biodiversity Partnership launched in 2021 by BiodivERsA and the European Commission, which funds transnational biodiversity research. Its BiodivMon call supported projects to improve monitoring of biodiversity.

name: Biodiversity Accelerator+
summary: Silverstrand Capital's accelerator for early-stage biodiversity companies. Its 2023 cohort included the eco-acoustics platform Arbimon.

name: Biodiversity and Protected Areas Management Programme
summary: EU-financed programme for African, Caribbean and Pacific countries on protected area management, with regional observatories and a regional information system on protected areas and species. It closed in 2025 after 13 years.

name: Biodiversity Digital Twin
summary: Horizon Europe project coordinated by CSC in Finland that uses the LUMI supercomputer, FAIR data, predictive modelling and AI to build prototype digital twins for biodiversity protection and restoration.

name: Biodiversity Funders Group
summary: Professional association of environmental, conservation, and climate and energy grantmakers, active since 1987. Its members include the Moore, Packard, Oak, Hewlett and MacArthur foundations.

name: Biodiversity Futures Initiative
summary: UK-based non-profit launched in 2023 that gives independent academic peer review of project design and biodiversity claims in the biodiversity credit market.

name: Biodiversity Heritage Library
summary: Open access digital library for biodiversity literature and archives, run as an international consortium of libraries and hosted administratively by the Council on Library and Information Resources.

name: Biodiversity Indicators Partnership
summary: A partnership of international organisations working on biodiversity indicators, with its secretariat provided by UNEP-WCMC. Germany's International Climate Initiative funds a project from 2023 to 2030 that uses it to strengthen national monitoring.

name: Biodiversity Information Standards
summary: Open membership body for people and institutions that manage biodiversity information, and maintainer of standards including Darwin Core.

name: Biodiversity Meets Data
summary: Project building a Single Access Point that gives natural resource managers and policy makers high-throughput biodiversity monitoring tools and AI driven taxon identification services.

name: Biodiversity+ Precursors
summary: ESA activity contributing to the joint EC-ESA Earth System Science Initiative, with projects on Earth observation for terrestrial, freshwater and coastal biodiversity.

name: Biologging Solutions
summary: Japanese company founded in 2014 by biologging researchers, making geolocators, video loggers, Argos tags and tags for underwater soundscape monitoring.

name: Biological Collection Access Service
summary: Transnational network linking specimen data from natural history collections, gardens and research institutions, with provider software that publishes collection data.

name: Biome Conservation
summary: Canadian charity, formerly the International Conservation Fund of Canada, that funds conservation in tropical regions. The Monitoring of the Andes Amazon Program lists it among its funders.

name: BIOMONDO
summary: ESA Biodiversity+ Precursors project on freshwater biodiversity and Earth observation.

name: BIOSCAN
summary: International Barcode of Life project that builds DNA-based systems for species discovery and aims to lay the foundation for a global biodiversity monitoring system.

name: BIOSCAN-1M
summary: Data set of one million insect specimens with DNA barcodes, taxonomy and images, used in TreeOfLife-10M.

name: BioSCape
summary: Research project using remote sensing and field data to study biodiversity in South Africa's Greater Cape Floristic Region, funded by NASA, South Africa and UNESCO.

name: BioSonics
summary: Seattle maker of hydroacoustic equipment for monitoring aquatic ecosystems, founded in 1978.

name: BioTIME
summary: Open access global database of assemblage time series for quantifying biodiversity change, hosted at the University of St Andrews.

name: Bird Buddy
summary: Company selling smart bird feeders that identify visiting species with AI. Registered in New York, with a subsidiary in Ljubljana, Slovenia.

name: Birda
summary: Birdwatching app with an AI-powered bird identifier, which sends the sightings it collects to the Global Biodiversity Information Facility.

name: BirdLife International
summary: Partnership of 125 conservation organisations that supplies global bird data, including species extinction risk assessments and important sites, through its DataZone.

name: BirdNET
summary: Open-source deep learning model and tools that recognise over 11,000 bird and other species by sound, built by Cornell and Chemnitz University of Technology.

name: BirdsCaribbean
summary: International network of members and partners, founded in 1988, that works to conserve Caribbean birds and their habitats and coordinates the Caribbean Waterbird Census.

name: BirdSet
summary: Benchmark data set collection for bird sound classification in avian bioacoustics.

name: BirdsPlus Index
summary: American Bird Conservancy's index that measures biodiversity from bird recordings identified by AI.

name: BirdVis
summary: Source code for a bird-distribution visualisation that compares occurrence maps, seasonal curves and habitat predictors across different bird species.

name: BirdWeather
summary: Visualisation platform that uses the BirdNET neural network to monitor bird vocalisations through about 2,000 active audio stations.

name: Bloomberg Ocean Initiative
summary: Bloomberg Philanthropies programme, launched in 2014, on marine protected areas and fisheries reform. It uses data collection, satellite monitoring and AI, and supports open platforms that track commercial fishing.

name: Bloomberg Philanthropies
summary: Philanthropy that runs the Bloomberg Ocean Initiative, which funds data collection, satellite monitoring and AI for transparency at sea, and is a listed funder of Global Fishing Watch.

name: Blue Ventures
summary: Marine conservation charity that began in Madagascar in 2003 and supports coastal communities with fisheries management and participatory data systems.

name: Blue w(AI)ve Accelerator
summary: Sixteen-week accelerator in Portland, Maine for seven early-stage start-ups using AI on ocean problems, run with the Gulf of Maine Research Institute and Northeastern University.

name: Blue-Cloud
summary: EU project that built cloud services for marine data, under the Future of Seas and Oceans flagship initiative.

name: Bobolink Foundation
summary: Foundation that has supported biodiversity conservation since 1986. Global Nature Watch names it among its founding partners.

name: BON in a Box Africa
summary: Project listed by IPBES to produce a customisable online toolkit for starting or strengthening national and regional biodiversity observation systems in sub-Saharan Africa, with Ghana, Uganda and Mozambique as pilots.

name: Botanic Gardens Conservation International
summary: Membership organisation for botanic gardens in more than 100 countries, which maintains the PlantSearch and ThreatSearch databases.

name: Botanical Information and Ecology Network
summary: Open-source tools and a database of plant observation, plot and trait data, built to harmonise and validate plant biodiversity data.

name: Boulder Imaging
summary: Machine vision company in Louisville, Colorado, that makes IdentiFlight, a system for detecting sensitive bird species at wind farms.

name: Broad Institute
summary: Research institute in Cambridge, Massachusetts, that the Earth BioGenome Project names as the body behind Zoonomia, a comparison of the DNA of over 200 mammals.

name: Browning Trail Cameras
summary: Trail camera brand of Prometheus Group, Birmingham, Alabama, with a line of cameras sold for wildlife observation and research.

name: Bugg
summary: Real-time acoustic monitoring device and cloud system developed by Sarab Sethi and his research team at Imperial College London, used in Norway, Malaysia, Mexico and Taiwan.

name: Builders Vision
summary: Investment and philanthropy platform working on food and agriculture, energy and oceans. It is a partner in the sustainable fisheries initiative of Schmidt Marine Technology Partners and a listed supporter of Earth Species Project.

name: Cali Fund
summary: Financial arm of the multilateral mechanism adopted at CBD COP16 for sharing benefits from digital sequence information on genetic resources, a data source that AI systems analyse.

name: California Academy of Sciences
summary: Research institute and natural history museum in San Francisco that received a Moore Foundation grant for biodiversity and community science.

name: California Institute of Technology
summary: Research university in California, home of the Perona Lab, whose machine vision work has conservation applications, and former host of the CV4Ecology Workshop.

name: Calling in Our Corals
summary: Google Arts & Culture listening project in which people marked fish sounds in over 400 hours of reef audio, producing training data for SurfPerch.

name: Caltech Camera Traps
summary: Labelled data set of 243,100 camera trap images from 140 locations in the south-western United States, published with the paper Recognition in Terra Incognita.

name: CAMBioMed
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project on coordinated monitoring of Mediterranean rocky ecosystems, using eDNA metabarcoding, satellite remote sensing and AI among its tools.

name: Cambridge Centre for Carbon Credits
summary: University of Cambridge centre, launched in 2021, that works to scale up deforestation avoidance carbon credits and offers a digital credit calculation platform to conservation organisations.

name: Camelot Project
summary: Free, open-source camera trap software whose reports work with analysis tools such as PRESENCE and camtrapR, and which its site says the WWF recommends in its camera trapping guidelines.

name: Camera Trap Data Package
summary: Community-developed data exchange format for camera trap data, built on the Frictionless Data Package and hosted under TDWG.

name: Camera Trap Image Classifier
summary: Repository with code and documentation for training and applying convolutional neural networks to identify animal species in camera-trap photographs, based on a 2018 deep learning and citizen science study.

name: Campbell Scientific
summary: Logan, Utah maker of dataloggers and measurement systems used in environmental research worldwide.

name: camtrapR
summary: R package for managing and analysing camera-trap data.

name: Canopy Height Maps
summary: Open model and global maps of tree canopy height made by Meta and the World Resources Institute; the first version, at 1-metre resolution, was launched in April 2024, and version 2 uses DINOv3.

name: Carbontribe
summary: The company verifies environmental impact with satellite imagery and computer vision, speeds up verification with an LLM agent and says its published mangrove and forest methodologies are independently audited.

name: Caribbean Coastal Data Centre
summary: Archive of data on coastal and marine resources for more than 30 Caribbean countries, part of the Centre for Marine Sciences.

name: Caribbean Protected Areas Gateway
summary: BIOPAMA-established regional observatory for data and reporting on biodiversity and protected areas in the Caribbean.

name: Caribbean Waterbird Census
summary: Regional part of the International Waterbird Census, coordinated by BirdsCaribbean.

name: Catalogue of Life
summary: Online index of known species of animals, plants, fungi and microorganisms, compiled from peer-reviewed taxonomic databases.

name: CatchCam Technologies
summary: English maker of rugged underwater camera systems and environmental sensors for commercial fishing and marine research, founded in 2024 by former staff of SafetyNet Technologies, which closed.

name: Cecil
summary: Sells an API giving access to more than 40 commercial and open spatial datasets, including deforestation, forest and biodiversity layers, for EUDR and nature risk work.

name: Cellular Tracking Technologies
summary: United States maker of wildlife telemetry devices, including cellular, digital radio and satellite tags, established in 2007.

name: Center for Geospatial Analytics, Clark University
summary: Interdisciplinary research centre at Clark University, established in 2023 and building on Clark Labs, that works on geospatial data and AI for conservation and environmental sustainability.

name: Center for Global Discovery and Conservation Science
summary: Arizona State University centre that leads the Allen Coral Atlas, which uses satellite imagery to map and monitor coral reefs.

name: Central African Forest Commission
summary: Intergovernmental organisation for the sustainable management of Central African forests. It supports the data collection groups of the Central Africa forest observatory, OFAC.

name: Central African Forest Initiative
summary: Coalition of donors and Central African partner countries for forest protection, which is building geospatial and AI capacity to monitor payments for ecosystem services.

name: Central American Waterbird Census
summary: Regional part of the International Waterbird Census, coordinated by the Western Hemisphere Shorebird Reserve Network.

name: Centre for Biodiversity Genomics
summary: Research centre that develops DNA-based systems for species identification using DNA barcodes.

name: Ceres Tag
summary: Australian maker of satellite ear tags for livestock with a line of wildlife and conservation applications.

name: Cetacean Genomes Project
summary: Project that began in early 2020 to generate chromosome-resolved reference genomes for all cetacean species, affiliated to the Earth BioGenome Project.

name: Cetacean Research Technology
summary: United States supplier of underwater and bioacoustics instruments, including hydrophone systems for whale watching.

name: Challenge IA-Biodiv
summary: Research challenge from the French National Research Agency and AFD supporting AI research on biodiversity, open to scientific communities in France and AFD partner countries in Africa.

name: Charles University
summary: Largest university in the Czech Republic, in Prague. Three of the five authors of the GEM-Forest preprint have affiliations in its Faculty of Science.

name: ChatIPT
summary: GBIF Norway's chatbot that takes a spreadsheet from a first-time data publisher, cleans it, writes basic metadata and publishes it to GBIF as a Darwin Core Archive. A new version was released for testing in 2025.

name: Chelonia
summary: British maker of PODs, automated passive acoustic instruments that detect porpoises, dolphins and other toothed whales, since 2006.

name: CHELSA
summary: Global, kilometre-scale climate datasets including bioclimatic variables, generated with the CHELSA downscaling model, on a site run by the Swiss research institute WSL.

name: Chemnitz University of Technology
summary: German university whose Chair of Media Informatics co-develops the BirdNET sound recognition model with the Cornell Lab of Ornithology.

name: Children's Investment Fund Foundation
summary: Philanthropic organisation and registered charity in England and Wales. MapBiomas Alerta lists it as a funder in 2018 and 2019.

name: Chimp&See
summary: Citizen science project hosted by Zooniverse in which volunteers classify camera trap videos from sites across Africa, collected for the Pan African Programme.

name: Chloris Geospatial
summary: Sells satellite-based forest carbon data for carbon projects, supply chain due diligence and financial institutions.

name: CIFOR-ICRAF
summary: Forest and agroforestry research organisation formed by the merger of CIFOR and ICRAF, with CIFOR headquartered in Bogor, Indonesia.

name: CIRAD
summary: French agricultural research organisation for tropical and Mediterranean regions, one of the four research bodies in the Pl@ntNet consortium.

name: Circumpolar Biodiversity Monitoring Program
summary: International network of monitoring professionals and organisations that works to harmonise and integrate efforts to monitor Arctic biodiversity, under CAFF.

name: Cisco
summary: Networking company that works with the Connected Conservation Foundation on protecting rhinos, elephants and other wildlife.

name: Citclops
summary: Observatory for coast and ocean optical monitoring, funded under European Union Seventh Framework Programme grant agreement 308469, whose app has been replaced by the EyeOnWater app.

name: CITES Secretariat
summary: Secretariat of the convention on trade in endangered species, which works with Interpol and the World Customs Organisation on enforcement and has spoken publicly about AI at border checks.

name: CITES Trade Database
summary: Database of international trade in CITES-listed species. OCCRP reports more than 25 million transactions over 50 years, and the Cambridge Network describes a technical overhaul led by the CITES Secretariat, UNEP and UNEP-WCMC.

name: Clay Foundation Model
summary: Open foundation model of Earth that takes satellite imagery with location and time and outputs embeddings for downstream nature and climate applications.

name: Climate and Land Use Alliance
summary: Collaborative of foundations that coordinates funding for tropical forests and the people who live in them. It is a listed funder of MapBiomas since 2024.

name: Climate Change AI
summary: Volunteer organisation from academia and industry that supports work on climate change and machine learning through education, funding, tools and datasets.

name: Climate Change AI Innovation Grants
summary: Grants from Climate Change AI for teams applying AI to climate challenges and creating public datasets and tools. Past rounds have funded nature work including a plant trait database, forest logging detection and kelp reef monitoring.

name: Climate Collective
summary: Organisation that runs accelerators, training and summits on AI and digital tools for climate and nature. The McGovern Foundation funded its launch of an AI for Climate and Nature incubator.

name: Climate TRACE
summary: Non-profit coalition building an open greenhouse gas emissions inventory with AI and satellite data. It is on this map only for its monitoring of forestry and land use; its other sectors are not in scope.

name: ClimateQ&A
summary: Ekimetrics' public chatbot that answers climate and biodiversity questions from IPCC and IPBES reports, with the source passages shown beside each answer.

name: ClimateWorks Foundation
summary: San Francisco foundation, and a founding member in 2010 of the Climate and Land Use Alliance.

name: Cloud-Native Geospatial Forum
summary: Radiant Earth initiative that works on open formats and cloud-native access to geospatial data, through events, content and education.

name: Coalition to End Wildlife Trafficking Online
summary: Coalition in which WWF, TRAFFIC and IFAW work with technology and e-commerce companies to remove illegal wildlife listings, including through AI detection.

name: Coastal Carbon Network
summary: Consortium of coastal wetland carbon scientists and land managers that shares open data through a Data Clearinghouse and the Coastal Carbon Atlas.

name: CoForFunc
summary: Biodiversa+ project working towards biome-scale monitoring of the functional composition of Congo Basin forests, using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery among other sources.

name: COICA
summary: Umbrella body of Indigenous organisations of the Amazon Basin, based in Quito. LandMark lists it in its steering group.

name: Collect Earth
summary: Free, open-source desktop tool in the Open Foris suite for interpreting satellite images to monitor land use and land use change.

name: Collect Earth Online
summary: Free, open-source web platform for interpreting satellite imagery for land cover, land use and forestry surveys, first developed by SERVIR.

name: Collecte Localisation Satellites
summary: Earth observation and monitoring company headquartered in Toulouse, founded by CNES in 1986 as operator of the Argos system.

name: CollectiveCrunch
summary: Sells AI-based forest data products, including forest inventory, bark beetle detection, a biodiversity index and storm damage maps, built on country lidar and satellite data.

name: Colossal Foundation
summary: Foundation set up by Colossal Biosciences that says it funds projects in conservation technology, including drone and machine learning tracking of elephants and a biobank. Dallas Innovates describes it as North Texas-based.

name: CoMapeo
summary: Free, open-source offline toolset for territory monitoring and mapping, built by Awana Digital with Indigenous partners.

name: Comisión Permanente del Pacífico Sur
summary: South Pacific commission based in Guayaquil that holds the CPPS node of the Ocean Biodiversity Information System.

name: Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources
summary: Body established by international convention in 1982 to conserve Antarctic marine life. Its Secretariat runs an acoustic data repository for krill work and has tested the Krillscan Python package.

name: Commission Internationale du Bassin Congo-Oubangui-Sangha
summary: Central African institution seated in Kinshasa that manages river navigation and water resources in the Congo basin. It is a GMES & Africa partner for water and natural resources.

name: Committee on Earth Observation Satellites
summary: Body that coordinates civil space-based Earth observation programmes internationally and promotes data exchange, with a biodiversity topic on its site.

name: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation
summary: Australian Government science agency that hosts the Atlas of Living Australia.

name: Computer Vision Group Jena
summary: Friedrich Schiller University Jena group developing computer vision and machine learning for areas including biodiversity, with projects such as LEPMON on moths and the InsectAI COST action.

name: Connected Conservation Foundation
summary: Non-profit registered in the UK and South Africa that gives local conservation partners technology, satellite imagery, grants and training. It runs the Satellites for Biodiversity Award with the Airbus Foundation.

name: Conserva Aves
summary: Initiative creating and managing subnational protected areas for birds in Latin America. Its partners in Colombia, Bolivia and Peru work on an Audubon project analysing bird recordings with AI.

name: Conservation AI
summary: UK-based non-profit platform that used machine learning and computer vision to detect and classify animals, humans and poaching-related objects in camera trap and thermal images. A 2026 preprint says it wound down as a public service in 2025 and was rebuilt as Trap Tracker.

name: Conservation Finance Alliance
summary: Network on conservation finance, with a Secretariat hosted by the Wildlife Conservation Society, which offers an AI assistant on conservation finance topics.

name: Conservation International
summary: Conservation organisation with offices in 35 countries. It leads Wildlife Insights, publishes a position on AI for nature and people, and has run AI biodiversity monitoring pilots such as its expedition on the outskirts of Yaguas National Park in Peru.

name: Conservation Metrics
summary: Builds biodiversity monitoring systems using passive acoustic monitoring, camera traps and machine learning, for customers and through community-driven projects.

name: Conservation of Arctic Flora and Fauna
summary: Arctic Council working group that runs the Circumpolar Biodiversity Monitoring Program and the Arctic Biodiversity Data Service.

name: Conservation Technology Working Group
summary: Working group of the Society for Conservation Biology that promotes the agenda of conservation technology within the discipline.

name: Conservation X Labs
summary: Conservation innovation and technology organisation that builds its own tools, such as the Sentinel hardware, and runs open innovation prizes. Wild Me is part of it.

name: ConservationDrones
summary: Group that develops and shares drone methods for conservation, with founding directors Lian Pin Koh and Serge Wich, and the DroneMegaDetector AI model.

name: ConservationDronesAI
summary: Work by the Conservation Drones team on deep learning models that detect animals, their signs and objects such as cars and people, with models shared on GitHub.

name: Consorcio para el Desarrollo Sostenible de la Ecorregión Andina
summary: Regional non-governmental organisation working on sustainable development in the Andes, with offices in Lima and Quito, whose site hosts the Red de Bosques Andinos forest plot platform.

name: Consortium of European Taxonomic Facilities
summary: European consortium of natural history museums, botanic gardens and research centres. Its 81 institutions hold an estimated 1.5 billion specimens.

name: ConTech Africa
summary: Tanzanian start-up started in 2023 that gives conservation organisations across Africa training and support in using conservation technology, and is listed as an EarthRanger partner.

name: Convention on Migratory Species Secretariat
summary: Secretariat of the UN treaty on migratory species, located in Bonn. Movebank lists the convention as a funder and the ICARUS Initiative lists it as a partner; a global atlas of ungulate migrations was built in partnership with it.

name: COPEPOD
summary: Global plankton database project, the Coastal and Oceanic Plankton Ecology, Production, and Observation Database.

name: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem
summary: Service giving access to Earth observation data from the Copernicus Sentinel satellites and datasets from the Copernicus Services.

name: Copernicus Land Monitoring Service
summary: EU Copernicus service giving geographical information on land cover, land use, vegetation and the water cycle for Europe and the globe, implemented by the European Environment Agency and the Joint Research Centre.

name: Copernicus Marine Service
summary: Marine part of the EU Copernicus Programme, giving free information on the state of the ocean, implemented by Mercator Ocean International.

name: Copernicus Observia AI
summary: AI assistant in public beta, built on the European Environment Agency's GPT-LAB platform, that helps people find, understand and use Copernicus data products, including land monitoring data. Runs on a Mistral language model on the agency's own servers.

name: Copernicus Sentinel-2
summary: Copernicus mission based on a constellation of two identical satellites in the same orbit, whose imagery underlies many global land cover and foundation models.

name: CopernicusLAC Chile
summary: Regional Copernicus centre for Latin America and the Caribbean, hosted by the Center for Mathematical Modeling at the University of Chile, with land cover and land use maps made by deep neural networks.

name: Coral Gardeners
summary: Coral reef restoration organisation with branches in French Polynesia, Fiji and Thailand. It built ReefOS, a network of underwater cameras and sensors that uses computer vision to monitor reef health.

name: CoralNet
summary: Resource for benthic image analysis that uses deep neural networks for automated annotation, and also serves as a data repository and collaboration platform.

name: Coralscapes
summary: General-purpose dense semantic segmentation data set for coral reefs with 2,075 images and 174,000 annotations from five countries.

name: Cornell Lab of Ornithology
summary: Part of Cornell University, it builds the eBird platform, holds the Macaulay Library and co-develops BirdNET through its Center for Conservation Bioacoustics.

name: Cornell Lab of Ornithology acoustic sensors and AI for forest threats
summary: Bezos Earth Fund grant of $1.8 million to the Cornell Lab of Ornithology's K. Lisa Yang Center for Conservation Bioacoustics for acoustic sensors and AI analytics that identify threats to forests from illegal activities.

name: Cornell University
summary: Private research university in Ithaca, New York, home of the Cornell Lab of Ornithology and the Institute for Computational Sustainability.

name: Cos4Cloud
summary: EU project that built services for biodiversity citizen observatories, including deep machine learning and automatic video recognition to improve data quality.

name: crawl
summary: R package that fits continuous-time correlated random walk models to animal movement data, built by Devin Johnson; its latest version reached CRAN on 26 February 2026.

name: CREAF
summary: Catalan ecology and forestry research centre on the Bellaterra campus, whose researchers work on the Mosquito Alert citizen science project and which is a CoForFunc partner.

name: CreditNature
summary: Oxford company that measures ecosystem recovery with its Ecosystem Condition Index and issues nature credits and certificates, with projects in seven countries.

name: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund
summary: Fund started in 2000 that gives grants to civil society in biodiversity hotspots, as a joint initiative of development agencies, governments and foundations. A final report shows a $148,500 grant to NatureMetrics for DNA-based freshwater monitoring in Côte d'Ivoire.

name: Critical Site Network Tool
summary: Online resource on 294 waterbird species and the sites they depend on in Africa and Western Eurasia, drawing on several databases.

name: CSC - IT Center for Science
summary: Finnish IT centre for science that coordinates the Horizon Europe Biodiversity Digital Twin project.

name: CTrees
summary: US non-profit that has built a global system to monitor, report and verify carbon stocks and land-use activities for land ecosystems, drawing on remote sensing and AI.

name: Cultivo
summary: US land regeneration company that sources nature-based projects and carbon credits and says it uses machine learning and generative AI. Projects include Sierra del Carmen in Mexico.

name: CV4Ecology Workshop
summary: Two-week intensive programme that teaches ecologists computer vision methods for analysing large image, audio or video datasets, hosted at the Smithsonian Conservation Biology Institute and previously at Caltech.

name: CVEDIA
summary: Company selling AI video analytics that worked with RESOLVE on TrailGuard AI, deploying smart camera applications in Asia and Africa with AI built on synthetic data.

name: CyberTracker
summary: Develops free smartphone software for gathering and visualising field data, and certifies trackers. It is based in Cape Town.

name: Cyprus Marine and Maritime Institute
summary: Cypriot institute that launched and coordinates the AXOLOTL project on AI for maritime surveillance and the marine environment.

name: Daffy Charitable Fund
summary: California donor-advised fund recorded as giving Earth Species Project $1 million in 2024.

name: Dalio Philanthropies
summary: Philanthropy listed as a funder of Global Fishing Watch.

name: Danish International Development Agency
summary: Denmark's development cooperation, an area of work within its Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Copenhagen. The Global Forest Watch about page shows it among founding partners.

name: Dartmouth Ocean Technologies
summary: Canadian maker of underwater sensors and environmental DNA samplers for oceans, lakes and waterways.

name: Darwin Core
summary: Standard vocabulary and schemas for sharing information about biological diversity, used to exchange species occurrence data.

name: Darwin Initiative
summary: UK government grants scheme for biodiversity conservation and poverty reduction in eligible low and middle income countries, with a related Darwin Plus fund for the UK Overseas Territories.

name: DataONE
summary: Community-driven programme giving access to Earth and environmental data across member repositories, administered at the National Center for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis.

name: David and Lucile Packard Foundation
summary: Foundation with an Ocean Initiative and climate grantmaking. It is a founding member of the Climate and Land Use Alliance, and OpenAlex records it as a funder on published research on illegal fishing, environmental DNA and passive acoustic monitoring.

name: Deep Forestry
summary: Swedish company making autonomous under-canopy forest drones and AI analysis for tree-level forest inventory, with customers in Sweden and Spain.

name: Deep learning for camera-trap images (Snapshot Serengeti models)
summary: Code and pre-trained models for extracting information from camera-trap images, trained on Snapshot Serengeti data and accompanying a paper on identifying, counting and describing wild animals with deep learning.

name: Deep Voice
summary: Israeli organisation developing AI-based passive acoustic monitoring for the protection of marine mammals.

name: Deep-Ocean Genomes Project
summary: Project using genomics to test ecological and evolutionary hypotheses across deep-sea habitats and lineages, affiliated to the Earth BioGenome Project.

name: DeepFaune
summary: Collaborative project building an AI model and free desktop software that identify European animal species in camera-trap images.

name: DeepForest
summary: Open-source library for object detection and geospatial analysis in ecology, specifically for analysing forest canopy data.

name: DeepForestSound
summary: Multi-species automatic detector for passive acoustic monitoring in African tropical forests, with a case study in Kibale National Park, Uganda.

name: DeepForestVision
summary: Open camera trap classifier for African tropical forests, working on photos and videos offline. Version 2 was trained on a multi-country corpus.

name: DeepLabCut
summary: Software package for animal pose estimation across species and behaviours, using transfer learning with deep neural networks, with a quadruped model trained on images including elephants and gazelles.

name: DeepLOKI
summary: Deep learning software that classifies zooplankton from high-resolution images for use on board research vessels, from authors at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf and the Alfred Wegener Institute.

name: DeepMeerkat
summary: Machine learning tool for video-based biodiversity surveys that uses a scene-specific convolutional neural network, with a tutorial on finding periods when manakins are present in field video.

name: DeerSpotter
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that uses AI to identify deer from photographs.

name: DEIMS
summary: Metadatabase on which ILTER carries out yearly accreditation of the sites in its 39 member networks.

name: Dendra Systems
summary: UK company that provided analytics and drone planting for large-scale ecosystem restoration. Companies House lists Dendra Systems Ltd as in insolvency proceedings, and its site could not be reached.

name: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
summary: UK government department that hosts the Darwin Initiative Secretariat.

name: Desert Star Systems
summary: United States underwater technology maker of Argos satellite tags and underwater passive acoustic monitoring equipment.

name: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit
summary: German federal enterprise for international cooperation, with registered offices in Bonn and Eschborn. It works on the FAIR Forward AI for development initiative, and on energy and the environment.

name: Development Seed
summary: Engineering and product company that applies earth data, cloud computing and geospatial AI, including work with Land & Carbon Lab.

name: DHI
summary: Water modelling organisation in Hørsholm, Denmark. Global Wetland Watch says DHI leads algorithm and system development for that project and provides hydrological mapping and modelling services.

name: Digital and Technology Dialogues at CBD COP17
summary: COP17 session on digital tools and AI for biodiversity, co-hosted with Armenia's Ministry of Environment, the Connected Conservation Foundation and UNEP.

name: Digital Belt and Road Program
summary: Programme of the International Research Center of Big Data for Sustainable Development Goals, with a Big Earth Data Platform and agreements with research bodies in Africa and Europe.

name: Digital Deep-sea Typical Habitats Programme
summary: UN Ocean Decade programme approved in June 2023 and initiated by China, on deep-sea science and governance, including habitat mapping and an intelligent observation system.

name: Digital Earth Africa
summary: Programme of icipe that delivers an operational Earth observation data service for the whole of Africa, including a wetlands monitoring workflow using machine learning.

name: Dimension Data
summary: Technology company, part of NTT Ltd. The Connected Conservation Foundation names it as a technology collaborator; it connected live video of rhinos in Kenya.

name: DINOv3
summary: Meta's self-supervised vision model, with a backbone pre-trained on the SAT-493M satellite imagery dataset that is used in Canopy Height Maps v2.

name: Distant Imagery Solutions
summary: Company registered in the Sharjah free zone that builds drones, kites, marine robots and AI monitoring for ecosystem restoration, and won a Tech4Nature Award in 2025 for mangrove planting.

name: Distributed System of Scientific Collections
summary: European research infrastructure for natural history collections, with its coordination office in Leiden, building a digital specimen infrastructure with AI-supported workflows.

name: DITTO
summary: UN Ocean Decade programme that aims to develop a common understanding, best practices and a digital framework for digital twins of the ocean.

name: DiverSea
summary: Horizon Europe project coordinated by NTNU that develops marine observation and monitoring technology, including DNA-based identification, for coastal seas.

name: DNAqua-Net
summary: COST Action CA15219, funded from 2016 to 2021, developing genetic tools for bioassessment of aquatic ecosystems in Europe.

name: DNAquaIMG
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project developing and testing DNA-based and automated image-based monitoring of freshwater invertebrates and diatoms in rivers.

name: DOB Ecology
summary: Dutch non-profit foundation set up by an entrepreneurial family that gives grants to NGOs for nature conservation. It is named as a supporter of Global Mangrove Watch.

name: Dodotronic
summary: Italian maker of ultrasonic USB microphones and parabolic microphones, founded in 2003 and used for listening to ultrasound such as bat calls.

name: DOFA
summary: Unified multimodal foundation model for different data modalities in remote sensing and Earth observation.

name: DolphinGemma
summary: AI model from Google, trained on the Wild Dolphin Project's acoustic database, that learns the structure of dolphin vocalisations and generates dolphin-like sound sequences.

name: Donor Advised Charitable Giving
summary: San Francisco donor-advised giving body named among recent grant makers to Global Fishing Watch in 2024.

name: Draper Richards Kaplan Foundation
summary: Venture philanthropy funder for social entrepreneurs, based in Menlo Park, California. It was a founding funder of OceanMind.

name: DrivenData
summary: Denver firm helping mission-driven organisations with data science and AI, which built automated wildlife identification from trail camera videos with the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology and the Wild Chimpanzee Foundation.

name: DroneMegaDetector
summary: General-purpose AI model for detecting animals in drone imagery across species, habitats and survey conditions, from a study led by Chaim Chai Elchik.

name: Druid Technology
summary: Chinese maker of the DEBUT series of lightweight wildlife trackers, with the Ecotopia data management app.

name: Dryad Networks
summary: Makes wildfire sensors and says its system gives ultra-early detection and autonomous suppression, including for rangers in remote areas.

name: DTO-BioFlow
summary: EU project that brings biodiversity data into the Digital Twin of the Ocean, including data processed by AI.

name: Dunya Analytics
summary: United States software company offering biodiversity and nature risk analytics for disclosure, according to Silverstrand Capital.

name: Dynamic World
summary: Near real-time global land cover dataset at ten metres, made by Google with the World Resources Institute, that estimates nine land cover types in each Sentinel-2 image.

name: e-obs
summary: German maker of wildlife telemetry collars and tags combining GPS, acceleration and other sensors.

name: E.O. Wilson Biodiversity Foundation
summary: Foundation with the purpose of inspiring collective action to save the biosphere. Its president led development of the Half-Earth Project Map, a global map of species.

name: Earth BioGenome Project
summary: Coordinated effort to sequence, catalogue and characterise the genomes of all of Earth's eukaryotic biodiversity over ten years.

name: Earth Blox
summary: Sells software for nature and climate assessment and prioritisation, used among other things for reporting under the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures.

name: Earth Defenders Toolkit
summary: Collaborative space with resources and training for communities defending ecosystems, listed by Awana Digital among its tools.

name: Earth Fire Alliance
summary: Nonprofit coalition, registered in San Francisco, established to launch the FireSat satellite constellation for near real-time data on wildfires. R&D World reports $13 million from Google.org.

name: Earth Genome
summary: Non-profit that applies AI to Earth data and builds tools on water, food systems, emissions and biodiversity, including Earth Index.

name: Earth Index
summary: Tool from Earth Genome that uses Earth foundation models to let users search satellite imagery for features by labelling examples.

name: Earth Map
