summary: FAO platform built with Google that turns satellite and climate data into maps and statistics on forests, land, water and biodiversity, developed further under AIM4Forests with machine learning.

name: Earth Microbiome Project
summary: Collaborative effort to characterise microbial life using DNA sequencing and mass spectrometry of crowd-sourced samples; not currently accepting new samples.

name: Earth Observation for Wetlands Inventory
summary: Project to develop a global solution for wetland inventories with user countries, assigning ecosystem classes through a crosswalk of Ramsar, IUCN and SEEA wetland typologies.

name: Earth Species Project
summary: Non-profit that builds AI models to analyse animal communication across species, and publishes open bioacoustics benchmarks and models.

name: Earthbanc
summary: Climate and agricultural technology company in Stockholm that sells AI measurement, reporting and verification of vegetation and assets, with forestry and carbon removal among its uses.

name: EarthDaily
summary: Earth observation company in Vancouver with a satellite constellation and data products, including a forestry line covering forest health and wildfire.

name: EarthRanger
summary: Software platform from Ai2 that brings field reports, sensors and tracking data together so that protected area managers can see wildlife and teams in real time. It now sits within the SMART-EarthRanger Conservation Alliance.

name: Earthworm Foundation
summary: Non-profit working on the relationship between people and nature in commodity supply chains, and co-developer of the Starling deforestation monitoring service.

name: Eawag
summary: Swiss water research institute whose Plankifier project built deep learning classifiers for lake plankton images.

name: eBioAtlas
summary: Joint programme of IUCN and NatureMetrics to gather eDNA species data at scale and fill global biodiversity knowledge gaps, with a focus on freshwater.

name: EBVs on the Cloud
summary: Grant programme from Microsoft's AI for Earth and GEO BON, announced in 2020, for projects that produce cloud-based biodiversity data, with free software from Esri.

name: Echoview Software
summary: Australian maker of hydroacoustic data processing software, working with governments, scientists, commercial fisheries and NGOs on aquatic resources.

name: Eco-LLM benchmark
summary: Code for evaluating language models on ecological questions, in a GitHub repository by Filip Dorm.

name: EcoCode
summary: GEO BON modelling hub that aims to synthesise biodiversity modelling and build a Biodiversity Projection Platform and a model intercomparison project.

name: ecoObs
summary: German company in Nuremberg making batcorder recorders and related bat monitoring hardware.

name: Ecopath International Initiative
summary: Not-for-profit research organisation in Barcelona that maintains the Ecopath with Ecosim ecosystem modelling software.

name: Ecopath with Ecosim
summary: Ecological modelling software suite with static, time-dynamic and spatial modules. DITTO lists it as a science partner.

name: ECOPOTENTIAL
summary: EU project on using Earth observation to assess and monitor ecosystems in protected areas.

name: Ecoregions 2017
summary: Map of terrestrial ecoregions from the 2017 paper An Ecoregion-Based Approach to Protecting Half the Terrestrial Realm, by Eric Dinerstein and co-authors.

name: Ecosia
summary: Berlin-based not-for-profit search engine that funds tree planting and works with the French startup Kanop to monitor its reforestation sites with satellite data and AI.

name: ECOSTRESS
summary: NASA thermal Earth observation data, used according to its applications page for vegetation health, water stress and the monitoring of habitats and coastal wetlands.

name: Ecosystem Insights Hub
summary: Connected Conservation Foundation hub that helps local organisations integrate very high-resolution satellite imagery, AI and in-situ data for conservation.

name: Ecosystem Sensing Group
summary: Imperial College London group, led by Sarab Sethi, that develops sensors, systems and AI for environmental and biodiversity monitoring.

name: EcoTaxa
summary: Web tool for the taxonomic classification of plankton and other images, hosting over 900 million images from about 900 institutions.

name: Ecotone Telemetry
summary: Polish maker of ornithological nets and, since 2012, GPS telemetry equipment for monitoring birds, mammals and some reptiles.

name: EcoVision Lab
summary: University of Zurich research group headed by Jan Dirk Wegner within the Department of Mathematical Modeling and Machine Learning.

name: EDITO AI chatbot
summary: AI chatbot on EDITO, the European Digital Twin Ocean led by Mercator Ocean International, for users with questions about the ocean. Shown to the public in June 2026; no page read says which model it uses or how many people use it.

name: eDNA Explorer
summary: United States platform combining eDNA, geospatial data and AI to help natural resource managers judge ecosystem health and conservation.

name: eDNAtec
summary: Provides environmental genomics services for biodiversity and ecological health across offshore, onshore and terrestrial settings.

name: Ekimetrics
summary: French AI and data management company that built ClimateQ&A, a public chatbot over IPCC and IPBES reports.

name: Electronic Monitoring Group
summary: New Zealand company selling fisheries monitoring technology, vessel monitoring and AI and machine vision tools for reviewing fishing footage. Teem Fish Monitoring now operates as EMG Americas.

name: Elekon
summary: Swiss company in Lucerne that makes the BATLOGGER devices for recording bat calls.

name: ElephantVoices
summary: Elephant research and conservation organisation with field studies in Amboseli, Maasai Mara and Gorongosa. It publishes on machine learning work on elephant vocal communication.

name: ELLIS Unit Jena
summary: Unit of the European ELLIS AI network that advances understanding of Earth's dynamic systems through AI and machine learning.

name: eLTER
summary: European long-term ecosystem research infrastructure, with its head office hosted at UFZ in Germany; its data feed a digital twin prototype for biodiversity with GBIF, DiSSCo and LifeWatch.

name: EMSO ERIC
summary: Pan-European research infrastructure of seafloor and water-column observatories, with marine ecosystem functioning among its research topics.

name: ENCORE
summary: Tool and knowledge base that helps financial institutions understand their dependencies and impacts on nature, with a site copyrighted to UNEP.

name: Encosh
summary: Collaborative platform, co-created by an international interdisciplinary team, where stakeholders exchange knowledge on human-wildlife interaction and members build their own toolbox of local management initiatives.

name: Encyclopedia of Life
summary: Free online encyclopedia intended to document all known living species, compiled from existing databases.

name: EnviroDNA
summary: Australian company providing eDNA biodiversity monitoring.

name: Environmental Computational Science and Earth Observation Laboratory
summary: EPFL laboratory that extracts patterns from Earth observation data with machine learning and applies them to animal conservation and land change.

name: Environmental Justice Foundation
summary: NGO behind the DASE app, with which artisanal fishers in West Africa record geo-located evidence of illegal fishing for experts to verify and report.

name: EnvironmentGPT
summary: UNEP language model prototype trained on scientific information to give references to vetted UNEP literature on environmental issues, shown at UNEA-6 in 2024. Its current status is not confirmed by the source.

name: EO4Diversity
summary: ESA Biodiversity+ Precursor project that combines multi-sensor Earth observation with ecological models to predict and monitor terrestrial biodiversity.

name: EO4wildlife
summary: EU project that brought biologists, ecologists and ornithologists together to use Copernicus Sentinel Earth observation data with animal tracking.

name: EOMAP
summary: German company producing satellite-based information on shallow water depth, benthic habitats and inland and coastal water quality, with work on several continents.

name: EOS Data Analytics
summary: Sells satellite data and analytics, including deforestation detection and forest health products, for forestry and other sectors.

name: Epicollect5
summary: Free mobile data-gathering platform developed by the CGPS team at Oxford's Big Data Institute.

name: EQO
summary: United States company offering aquatic species detection and biodiversity assessment with eDNA and eRNA, according to Silverstrand Capital.

name: Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellows
summary: Six-year $148 million Schmidt Sciences programme funding postdoctoral researchers to use AI across science. Cornell's 2026 cohort includes work on hydropower dam impacts and global forest biomass.

name: ES-PAS
summary: Russian developer and manufacturer of Argos transmitters for tracking marine and land animals since 2007.

name: ESA Biomass Mission
summary: European Space Agency forest-monitoring satellite carrying a P-band synthetic aperture radar.

name: ESA CCI Biomass
summary: European Space Agency Climate Change Initiative project providing global annual maps of above-ground biomass.

name: ESA CCI Land Cover
summary: European Space Agency Climate Change Initiative project producing global land cover maps, with a team that includes UCLouvain and Brockmann Consult.

name: ESA WorldCover
summary: Global land cover products for 2020 and 2021 at 10 m resolution based on Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data, developed by a consortium of European providers.

name: ESA Φ-lab
summary: ESA unit for transformational Earth observation innovation and commercialisation, whose work includes the TerraMind foundation model and the EVE language model.

name: Esri
summary: Geographic information system company that gives software to conservation groups through its Conservation Program and publishes the Sentinel-2 10-metre land use and land cover time series.

name: Esri Conservation Program
summary: Esri programme, founded in the 1980s, that gives geographic information technology to conservation organisations at little or no cost.

name: ETH BiodivX
summary: ETH Zurich team that used drones to collect environmental DNA and was a finalist in XPRIZE Rainforest, co-led by Kristy Deiner and Stefano Mintchev.

name: ETH Zurich
summary: Swiss public university where the EcoVision Lab produced the Global Canopy Height 2020 map by deep learning from satellite images.

name: Eurasian-African Bird Migration Atlas
summary: Online platform mapping bird movements on the Eurasian-African flyway, combining ringing data on 300 species with tracking data for over 100, built by EURING and the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior.

name: EURING
summary: Named by EuroBirdPortal as working with it on avian influenza monitoring tools. EURING's own site was in maintenance when read, so nothing here comes from it.

name: EuroBirdPortal
summary: European Bird Census Council project that brings together bird records from online portals, developed with a partnership of 52 institutions in 41 countries.

name: EuroGOOS
summary: Non-profit, Brussels-based European organisation for sustained ocean observing, the European component of the Global Ocean Observing System, with 47 members.

name: EuropaBON
summary: Horizon 2020 project on a European biodiversity observation network, whose final stakeholder conference was announced for 2024 as the end of the project.

name: European Association of Remote Sensing Laboratories
summary: Scientific network of European remote sensing institutes from academia and industry, with its seat in Strasbourg.

name: European Bioinformatics Institute
summary: Intergovernmental organisation in the EMBL family, on the Wellcome Genome Campus at Hinxton near Cambridge, focused on bioinformatics research and services.

name: European Bird Census Council
summary: Association under Dutch law of ornithologists who work to improve bird monitoring and atlas work in Europe; it runs the EuroBirdPortal viewer and the European Breeding Bird Atlas.

name: European Breeding Bird Atlas 2
summary: Atlas of where 596 bird species breed in Europe and how their distribution has changed since the 1980s, carried out by the European Bird Census Council network in 48 countries.

name: European Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: Citizen science network that gathers butterfly and moth counts from volunteers, with a shared database and mobile application.

name: European Commission
summary: Executive of the European Union, based in Brussels. Its Directorate General for International Partnerships funds the Biodiversity Information for Development programme.

name: European Cooperation in Science and Technology
summary: Funding organisation for research and innovation networks called COST Actions, one of which is InsectAI.

name: European Environment Agency
summary: EU agency that provides environmental knowledge and data and co-implements the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service.

name: European Marine Biological Resource Centre
summary: Europe's research infrastructure for marine biology and ecology, which runs EMO BON, a genomics biodiversity observatory, and coordinated the MARCO-BOLO project.

name: European Marine Observation and Data Network
summary: Network of organisations supported by the EU's integrated maritime policy that supplies marine data, including seabed habitats.

name: European Marine Omics Biodiversity Observation Network
summary: Permanent, coordinated genomics biodiversity observatory in Europe, run through the European Marine Biological Resource Centre.

name: European Network for the Radar surveillance of Animal Movement
summary: Research network on radar surveillance of animal movement, funded through the COST Programme from October 2013 to October 2017, which aims at continental-scale remote sensing of migration and still functions.

name: European Nucleotide Archive
summary: Archive of nucleotide sequences produced and maintained by the European Bioinformatics Institute and a member of the INSDC.

name: European Reference Genome Atlas
summary: Pan-European effort to generate reference genomes representing European biodiversity.

name: European Space Agency
summary: European intergovernmental space agency that flies the Biomass forest mission, funds global land cover and biomass data products, and through its Φ-lab develops AI models for Earth observation.

name: European Tracking Network
summary: Network for tagging and tracking fish and other aquatic animals across Europe, with a data platform and telemetry database.

name: Eurostat
summary: Carries out the LUCAS land use and land cover survey every three to four years, and has done so since 2006.

name: Evaluating Large Language Models for IUCN Red List Species Information
summary: Paper by Shinya Uryu evaluating large language models on IUCN Red List species information.

name: EVE
summary: AI question-and-answer platform for Earth observation built by ESA Φ-lab with Pi School, Mistral and Imperative Space.

name: exci
summary: Australian company selling AI wildfire detection for plantations, parks and government agencies, with deployments it says in California and Australia.

name: Eye of the Species
summary: Tencent AI model that sorts camera trap images, first made for snow leopard studies in China and adapted for use in Nepal; it recognised 286 species at the time of the source.

name: Eyes on Recovery
summary: WWF and Conservation International project, supported by Google, that used 1,100 motion-activated cameras to study wildlife recovery after Australia's bushfires.

name: Faculty of Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation (ITC)
summary: University of Twente faculty working on geospatial AI, which says it aims for real-world impact primarily in the Global South.

name: FAIR Forward
summary: German development cooperation project, implemented by GIZ for the federal development ministry, on open AI for development in seven countries in Africa and Asia. Its examples include satellite data to protect Indonesian rainforests.

name: FAIRiCUBE
summary: EU project that opened gridded Earth observation data and algorithms to users beyond the EO field, applying machine learning to multi-thematic datacubes.

name: Farmscapes 2020
summary: High-resolution map of hedgerows, stone walls and copses across England from Google Research and the Leverhulme Centre for Nature Recovery, later released in a vectorised form.

name: FathomNet
summary: Open image database and tools that give access to AI and machine learning for analysing ocean visual data, started by Kakani Katija at MBARI.

name: Fauna & Flora
summary: International wildlife conservation charity working with partners in 48 countries. It uses camera traps and remote sensing, and hosts the WILDLABS programme.

name: Fin Finder
summary: AI mobile app that helps customs inspectors identify shark and ray species from fins, managed by Wild Me and piloted with Singapore's National Parks Board.

name: Finnish Environment Institute
summary: Multidisciplinary research and expert institute under Finland's Ministry of the Environment that coordinates the OBSGESSION project.

name: FireSat
summary: Satellite constellation programme for wildfire data, the flagship programme of Earth Fire Alliance.

name: Fish 10,000 Genomes
summary: Aims to sequence the genomes of about 10,000 fish species and build a genome database of fishes.

name: FishBase
summary: Global database of fish species, supervised by a consortium of international institutions and edited by Rainer Froese and Daniel Pauly.

name: FishBase Consortium
summary: Consortium of international institutions that has supervised FishBase since 2000, coordinated by the GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel.

name: FishEye Collaborative
summary: Conservation technology non-profit working on marine bioacoustics, building methods, tools and a sound library, and training AI systems to recognise fish sounds.

name: Fishial.AI
summary: Project sponsored by The Wye Foundation, building an open-source fish species image library labelled for machine learning and an open-source fish identification model.

name: FishOASIS
summary: Repository with instructions for building the camera of the Fish Optical and passive Acoustic Sensor Identification System, described in a 2021 Oceanography article on imaging in low-light aquatic habitats.

name: FishSounds
summary: Global inventory of fish sound production research, searchable by taxon, recording or reference, listing 1,344 recordings and 1,062 sound-producing species.

name: FishVue AI
summary: AI-assisted workflow from Archipelago Marine Research for reviewing fisheries electronic monitoring data.

name: Flanders Marine Institute
summary: Marine institute in Ostend that manages Marine Regions, developed the Aphia database behind the World Register of Marine Species and hosts Bio-ORACLE.

name: FLightR
summary: R package for positioning animals from solar geolocation archival tags, with worked examples for red-backed shrike, black-tailed godwit and tree swallow data.

name: Flora Family Foundation
summary: Family foundation in Menlo Park, California. Global Fishing Watch names it as a source of flexible funding, and a grant listing shows $57,000 in general support in 2025.

name: Flora Incognita
summary: Research project and free app for AI-supported plant identification with citizen science, covering more than 30,000 plant species, run by Technische Universität Ilmenau and the Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry.

name: Florida International University
summary: US university whose researchers lead Global FinPrint, a worldwide video survey of reef sharks and rays.

name: Flukebook
summary: Wild Me platform that applies AI to photographs of whales and dolphins.

name: Fondation Franklinia
summary: Private Swiss foundation, established in 2005, that gives grants to conserve threatened tree species and supports the Global Tree Assessment.

name: Fonds Français pour l'Environnement Mondial
summary: French facility that finances pilot projects in developing countries on biodiversity, climate, land, water and other environmental issues; it is acknowledged as a supporter of DeepForestVision.

name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
summary: UN agency whose Forestry Division builds open-source forest and land monitoring tools, including Open Foris, and runs the AIM4Forests programme.

name: For-Growth
summary: Initiative under AIM4Forests that aims to provide more precise data on forest carbon removals, using the MATRIX model with forest plot data.

name: Ford Foundation
summary: New York foundation, and a founding member in 2010 of the Climate and Land Use Alliance.

name: Forest 500
summary: Global Canopy's assessment of companies and financial institutions on deforestation, which draws on publicly available data points.

name: Forest Advanced Computing and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
summary: Purdue University laboratory that uses machine learning and statistical methods to study forest resource management and biodiversity conservation at global, regional and local scales; it founded the Science-i collaboration platform.

name: Forest Data Partnership
summary: Partnership that improves global monitoring of commodity-driven deforestation and supply chain tracking, combining datasets with ensemble machine learning and open community models.

name: Forest Foresight
summary: Open-source predictive model from WWF that combines satellite imagery with geospatial and socioeconomic data to predict forest loss up to six months ahead.

name: Forest Global Earth Observatory
summary: Network of scientists and long-term forest dynamics plots across the Earth's major forest types, formerly the Center for Tropical Forest Science.

name: Forest IQ
summary: Open access data platform on how companies and financial institutions address their links to deforestation, created by an alliance of not-for-profit organisations.

name: Forest Landscape Integrity Index
summary: Global map-based indicator of forest condition that estimates human modification of forest ecosystems, developed by a team led by the Wildlife Conservation Society.

name: Forest Listeners
summary: Online experiment from Google Arts & Culture and Google DeepMind, made with WildMon, in which people listen to Brazilian rainforest recordings to help tune the Perch model.

name: Forest Observation System
summary: Global reference dataset for remote sensing of forest biomass, from a team led at the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis. Its site now redirects to data.geo-trees.org.

name: Forest Peoples Programme
summary: Named by the Earth Defenders Toolkit as one of the groups that co-created it. Its own site refuses the fetcher, so nothing here comes from it.

name: Forest Stewardship Council
summary: International non-profit that sets standards for responsible forest management and forest-product supply chains, and uses satellite imagery and GIS maps to help auditors monitor certified forests.

name: Forest Trends
summary: Conservation finance organisation that publishes country dashboards on illegal deforestation and forest-risk commodities.

name: Forest Typology (ForTy) 2020
summary: Global 10-metre map that sorts land into six forest and land-use types, released in October 2026 with an early time series, as a baseline for the EU deforestation regulation.

name: Forest Watcher
summary: Set of mobile apps for on-the-ground monitors of forested areas, part of the wider Global Forest Watch technology offering and described as delivering real-time data to frontline forest guardians.

name: ForestCast
summary: Deep learning approach and benchmark dataset for forecasting deforestation risk from satellite data, released by Google DeepMind and Google Research in November 2025.

name: ForestPlots.NET
summary: Platform of partners who measure, monitor and analyse the world's tropical forests through standardised tree measurements, from the School of Geography at the University of Leeds.

name: Forgotten Parks Foundation
summary: Non-profit registered in Florida that manages national parks in Africa and Latin America through public-private partnerships and helps EarthRanger customers deploy the platform.

name: Forschungszentrum Jülich
summary: German research centre in the Helmholtz Association, named as a lead of the AqQua aquatic foundation model project.

name: Forêts d'Afrique Centrale Evaluées par Télédétection
summary: Atlases of forest cover and forest cover loss made from Landsat data, published for DR Congo, the Republic of Congo and Gabon.

name: Founders Factory Western Australia Nature Tech Accelerator
summary: Accelerator in Perth run by Founders Factory with the Government of Western Australia for start-ups in biodiversity, oceans, land and forests.

name: Founders Pledge
summary: Charity through which company founders pledge money to charitable causes, registered in England and Wales. SPUN lists it among its funders.

name: Framework for Ecosystem Restoration Monitoring
summary: Platform giving access to data, guidance and tools for tracking restoration, supporting reporting for the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration and Target 2 of the Global Biodiversity Framework.

name: Frankfurt Zoological Society
summary: Conservation organisation based in Frankfurt. It is a member of the SMART Partnership and a partner on Conservation International's AI expedition in Yaguas National Park.

name: Freshwater Ecosystems Explorer
summary: Free geospatial data platform showing how the extent of freshwater ecosystems changes over time, updated annually to align with SDG indicator 6.6.1.

name: FreshWater Watch
summary: Earthwatch's global citizen science programme measuring nitrates, phosphates and turbidity, with a data platform showing water quality data recorded worldwide. Groups include river catchments in Kenya.

name: Frontier Labs
summary: Makes long-term bioacoustic recorders for research.

name: Fugro
summary: Dutch geo-data and survey company. It contributes seabed mapping data to the Nippon Foundation-GEBCO Seabed 2030 project and co-chairs the Ocean Decade Corporate Data Group.

name: Fujitsu
summary: Technology company developing an ocean digital twin that uses LiDAR, AI and autonomous underwater vehicles to capture coral reefs and other features in 3D.

name: Fujitsu ocean digital twin
summary: Fujitsu research project that uses LiDAR and AI on autonomous underwater vehicles to map coral reefs in 3D, tested near Ishigaki Island, with seaweed beds as the planned next target.

name: Fund for Science and Technology
summary: Private foundation launched in 2025 from the estate of Paul G. Allen, planning at least $500 million over four years for bioscience, the environment and AI. Its environment focus includes biodiversity and ocean health.

name: FunDive
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project combining citizen science, AI tools and sporocarp and eDNA monitoring to map fungal diversity for nature conservation.

name: FutureWater
summary: Research and consulting organisation on water resources with offices in Wageningen and Cartagena. It offers satellite remote sensing and flying sensors and lists the HiHydroSoil dataset.

name: GainForest
summary: Swiss non-profit that works with Indigenous and local communities on biodiversity data, AI and field tools including bioacoustics, and on ways to pay people protecting nature.

name: Galileo
summary: Family of remote sensing models pretrained on a diversity of inputs, published with authors from NASA Harvest and Ai2.

name: GAPeDNA
summary: Web interface giving a global overview of genetic database completeness for a taxon across space and conservation status, for eDNA metabarcoding.

name: Gatsby Africa
summary: Private foundation established by Lord David Sainsbury that works on commercial forestry in East Africa and developed the Geospatial Forestry Platform with Swift Geospatial.

name: GBIF Integrated Publishing Toolkit
summary: GBIF's software for publishing biodiversity datasets, kept in a public repository.

name: GCOOS ERDDAP MCP Server
summary: Open-source connector from GCOOS that lets AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT search and read ocean data on ERDDAP servers from plain-language questions. Anyone can install it; no page read gives user numbers.

name: GEF EarthRanger project for African protected areas
summary: GEF-supported project deploying the EarthRanger system to protected areas in Botswana, Mozambique and the Republic of Congo, executed by AI2 and Conservation International with national agencies.

name: GEM-Forest
summary: Global satellite embedding-based dataset at 10 m resolution for 2020, classifying forests and tree crops.

name: GEMS/Water
summary: UNEP programme on global freshwater quality, whose data centre in Koblenz, Germany, hosts the GEMStat database.

name: GEMStat
summary: Global freshwater quality database giving data on the state and trend of inland water quality, hosted by the GEMS/Water Data Centre in Koblenz.

name: GenBank
summary: The NIH genetic sequence database, an annotated collection of all publicly available DNA sequences and part of the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration.

name: General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans
summary: International group of ocean mapping experts that develops and publishes bathymetric data sets, and partner with The Nippon Foundation in Seabed 2030.

name: Genome 10K
summary: Project to sequence the genome of at least one individual from each vertebrate genus, about 10,000 genomes.

name: Genomic Standards Consortium
summary: Open-membership working body, formed in 2005, that sets community standards for genomic data, including descriptors for metagenomes and the sampling environment. OBON lists it as a partner.

name: Gentian
summary: London company whose AI reads very high resolution satellite images to map biodiversity across habitats.

name: Gentian True Sight
summary: Tool that blends satellite and aerial imagery with Gentian's AI to give baseline biodiversity assessments for sites, priced per hectare.

name: Geo for Good Summit
summary: Summit held by Google Earth Outreach for nonprofit, academic, public sector, private sector, Indigenous and local community users of Earth Engine and other geospatial tools; the 2025 editions were in New York City and Singapore.

name: GEO Mountains
summary: Group on Earth Observations activity on mountains. Its site offers a Global Mountain Explorer and an in situ inventory.

name: GEO Wetlands
summary: Partnership founded by a group coordinated by the University of Bonn, Wetlands International and ESA, supporting users with Earth observation based mapping, monitoring and inventory of wetlands.

name: GEO-Bench
summary: General Earth observation benchmark for evaluating pre-trained models on geospatial data, a ServiceNow Research project with a successor, GEO-Bench-2, from the AI Alliance with IBM, ServiceNow and TUM.

name: GEO-TREES
summary: Initiative for high-accuracy ground data to support satellite-derived biomass mapping.

name: GEOARC Pilot
summary: Group on Earth Observations pilot that promotes Earth observation collaboration for environmental monitoring.

name: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel
summary: German ocean research centre in Kiel, named with Kiel University on the Digital Twins of the Ocean programme's about page.

name: GeoPlant
summary: Plant species prediction data set for species distribution modelling, from authors including the Pl@ntNet leads.

name: Georgia Institute of Technology
summary: Public research university in Atlanta whose researchers worked with Google on DolphinGemma, a model of dolphin vocalisations.

name: GeoRSPO
summary: Public interactive map from the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil showing members' concessions, land cover and active hotspots.

name: Geoscience Australia
summary: Named by Indonesia's Piksel platform as a development partner, with Auspatious.

name: German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research
summary: DFG research centre based in Halle, Jena and Leipzig, a central facility of Leipzig University, where sPlot, the global vegetation plot database, is a research platform.

name: German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
summary: German development ministry whose digital programme includes FAIR Forward, a project on open AI for development.

name: German Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety
summary: German federal ministry in which the International Climate Initiative is anchored.

name: gibbonR
summary: R package for detecting and classifying acoustic signals with machine learning, described as covering female gibbon calls in long-term recordings, with a worked example using Borneo gibbon training data.

name: Giraffe Africa Database
summary: Central repository of historical and current wild giraffe population records for all four species, kept by the Giraffe Conservation Foundation.

name: Giraffe Conservation Foundation
summary: Charity established in the UK in 2009 that works on giraffe conservation with partners in Africa. It partnered with Wild Me to create GiraffeSpotter.

name: GiraffeSpotter
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that applies AI to photographs of giraffe species.

name: GIST Impact
summary: Data company founded in 2008 that sells what it calls AI-powered data on nature, climate and social impact to companies and investors.

name: Glacier mapping and glacial lakes monitoring
summary: Microsoft AI for Good Lab project that uses machine learning to map glaciers and monitor glacial lakes for ecological monitoring.

name: GLC_FCS30
summary: Global land cover product at 30 m with a fine classification system, built from time-series Landsat imagery, from Chinese Academy of Sciences researchers.

name: Global Ant Genome Alliance
summary: Provides a dataset of the genomic diversity of the world's ants.

name: Global Biodiversity Framework Fund
summary: Fund set up after CBD COP15 to scale up financing for the Global Biodiversity Framework. Pledges reached $386 million by June 2025.

name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility
summary: International network that makes biodiversity data, mainly species occurrence records from many institutions, available through a single open portal.

name: Global Biodiversity Observing System
summary: GEO BON system named in draft CBD COP17 monitoring framework text, alongside the Global Ecosystems Atlas, as a resource for tracking headline indicators.

name: Global Biodiversity Portal
summary: Open-access database at EMBL-EBI that brings together genomic data from the projects that make up the Earth BioGenome Project.

name: Global Biotic Interactions
summary: Open access to species interaction data such as predator-prey and pollinator-plant, made by combining existing open datasets with open source software.

name: Global Canopy
summary: Data-driven not-for-profit that provides open-access data and metrics to companies, financial institutions and governments on deforestation and nature loss. It co-founded Trase.

name: Global Canopy Height 2020
summary: Global canopy top height map for 2020 at 10 m from Sentinel-2, produced with a deep learning model trained on sparse GEDI lidar data, from ETH Zurich.

name: Global Conservation
summary: Group that funds park protection systems and trains and equips rangers in national parks and UNESCO World Heritage Sites in developing countries. An EarthRanger deployment partner.

name: Global Conservation Tech and Drone Forum
summary: Non-profit initiative that held a five-day forum in Nairobi and Konza in March 2026 on conservation drones, AI and GIS, sensors, satellites and marine technology.

name: Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network
summary: Network of scientists, managers and organisations established by the International Coral Reef Initiative in 1995 that collates coral reef data and reports on reef status and trends.

name: Global Dam Watch
summary: International collaboration that provides open access data and tools on dams and reservoirs.

name: Global drivers of forest loss at 1 km resolution
summary: Global 1 km map of the dominant drivers of tree cover loss, made by the World Resources Institute and Google DeepMind with a deep learning model and updated annually with the Global Forest Change product.

name: Global Drone Forum
summary: Platform for the responsible use of drones across sectors including conservation. It keeps a database of national drone laws and of drone use in ecology and conservation. The African Drone Forum was a 2020 programme in Rwanda.

name: Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation
summary: Laser ranging instrument on the International Space Station that measures the 3D structure of Earth's forests and topography. FAO notes deep learning models trained on its measurements.

name: Global Ecosystem Research Infrastructure
summary: Network of site-based research infrastructures that studies how indicator ecosystems function and change across global biomes.

name: Global Ecosystems Atlas
summary: Standardised global map of Earth's ecosystems convened by GEO, bringing together global, regional and national ecosystem maps. A beta is out, with the full global release expected by early 2027.

name: Global Environment Facility
summary: Family of funds serving as financial mechanism for six multilateral conventions, which funds nature projects in developing countries, including the EarthRanger deployment in African protected areas.

name: Global Environmental Data Strategy
summary: UNEP strategy covering data quality, interoperability, governance and access for environmental data.

name: Global FinPrint
summary: Paul G. Allen initiative led by researchers at Florida International University that surveyed reef sharks and rays worldwide with baited remote underwater video.

name: Global Fishing Watch
summary: Organisation that creates and publicly shares knowledge about human activity at sea, founded by Oceana, SkyTruth and Google.

name: Global Forest Biodiversity Initiative
summary: International team of forest scientists that manages a tree-level forest inventory database of over 1.2 million plots, operated by InterNodes, Inc.

name: Global Forest Change
summary: Annual global forest loss data derived from Landsat time-series imagery by the GLAD laboratory at the University of Maryland.

name: Global Forest Cover 2020
summary: Global map of where forests existed in 2020, made by combining global datasets on tree cover, tree height, land cover and land use.

name: Global Forest Observations Initiative
summary: Partnership that supports tropical countries in creating forest monitoring systems, with a research component that held a 2026 session on AI in forest monitoring.

name: Global Forest Resources Assessment
summary: FAO's recurring global assessment of forest resources, with published remote sensing surveys alongside country reporting through national correspondents.

name: Global Forest Watch Pro
summary: Tool for monitoring deforestation in commodity supply chains, aimed at manufacturers, traders and banks. Trase lists it as a project partner.

name: Global Genome Biodiversity Network
summary: International network of institutions, founded in 2011, that makes DNA and tissue samples from biodiversity biobanks discoverable for research.

name: Global Green Growth Institute
summary: International body piloting AI-powered seagrass mapping for blue carbon monitoring in Indonesia with the marine affairs ministry and Spatial Informatics Group.

name: Global Intertidal Change
summary: Collaborative project producing high-resolution maps of the world's intertidal environments and their change, including tidal wetland change for 1999 to 2019 at 30 m resolution.

name: Global Invasive Species Database
summary: Database of invasive species developed and managed by the Invasive Species Specialist Group of the IUCN Species Survival Commission.

name: Global Invertebrate Genome Alliance
summary: Network of scientists working on genome and transcriptome sequencing standards for invertebrates.

name: Global Lake Ecological Observatory Network
summary: International network of researchers and instrumented lake buoys that conducts team science on lakes in a changing environment.

name: Global Lakes and Wetlands Database
summary: Global map of inland surface waters distinguished into 33 waterbody and wetland types.

name: Global Land Analysis and Discovery
summary: Laboratory at the University of Maryland that studies global land surface change from Earth observation imagery, led by Matthew Hansen.

name: Global Landscapes Forum
summary: Knowledge-led platform on sustainable and inclusive landscapes that runs an AI Hub on technology for land use, conservation and climate action.

name: Global Library of Underwater Biological Sound
summary: Platform that connects underwater sound repositories, analysis tools and reference libraries and develops machine learning to detect and classify biological sounds.

name: Global Mangrove Alliance
summary: Worldwide collaboration of NGOs, governments, scientists, industry, local communities and funders on conserving and restoring mangroves, launched in 2018. It lists Global Mangrove Watch among its initiatives.

name: Global Mangrove Trust
summary: Singapore-based non-profit that crowdfunds mangrove planting. Its co-founder says it tracks growth with satellites and AI.

name: Global Mangrove Watch
summary: Online platform with remote sensing data and tools for monitoring mangroves, including cover change, soil carbon, biomass and canopy height.

name: Global Messenger
summary: Chinese wild animal tracking technology company established in 2014, offering grants of tracking equipment to bird researchers with the International Ornithologists' Union.

name: Global Mountain Biodiversity Assessment
summary: Platform for international collaboration on mountain biodiversity, a Future Earth project, with developing tools and data infrastructures among its priorities.

name: Global Nature Watch
summary: Open monitoring platform of the World Resources Institute, formerly Global Forest Watch, renamed in September 2026 as it expands from forests to other land ecosystems.

name: Global Nature Watch Horizon
summary: AI-driven platform, in preview, that answers plain-language questions about land ecosystems using data from Land & Carbon Lab and Global Nature Watch.

name: Global Observations of Forest Cover and Land-use Dynamics
summary: International programme that coordinates space-based and in situ observations of the land surface. Its land cover team develops and evaluates methods for land cover monitoring.

name: Global Ocean Accounts Partnership
summary: Global partnership that helps countries measure progress towards ocean sustainable development through ocean accounts. Its secretariat is at the University of New South Wales in Sydney.

name: Global Program on Sustainability
summary: World Bank programme that helps countries develop and apply natural capital accounts and bring nature into economic decisions.

name: Global Record of Fishing Vessels, Refrigerated Transport Vessels and Supply Vessels
summary: FAO record of vessels intended as a tool against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.

name: Global Register of Introduced and Invasive Species
summary: Validated and verified national and subnational checklists of introduced and invasive alien species, led by the IUCN Invasive Species Specialist Group.

name: Global Restoration Initiative
summary: World Resources Institute initiative of nearly 50 experts in Africa, Asia, Latin America and Washington, DC that works on restoring land, including ways to set baselines and track restoration progress. TerraMatch is part of it.

name: Global Safety Net
summary: Open-source initiative providing a regularly updated global assessment of critical land and marine areas, from One Earth and Nature Data Lab.

name: Global Soil Biodiversity Initiative
summary: Global scientific and policy platform advancing the understanding, monitoring and protection of soil biodiversity.

name: Global Soil Partnership
summary: Voluntary multi-stakeholder initiative set up in 2012 by FAO members that shares soil information and supports soil surveys, monitoring and information systems.

name: Global Surface Water Explorer
summary: Dataset from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre mapping the location and distribution of water surfaces worldwide over four decades from Landsat imagery.

name: Global Tagging of Pelagic Predators
summary: International collaboration that plans to show animal tracking data alongside oceanographic datasets, building on the Census of Marine Life's Tagging of Pacific Predators and describing tagged animals as ocean sensors.

name: Global Tree Assessment
summary: Effort to assess the conservation status of the world's tree species, led by Botanic Gardens Conservation International.

name: Global Wetland Watch
summary: Alliance of DHI, UNEP-DHI and UNEP building a wetland information system that generates high-resolution maps and statistics, funded by Google.org through its call for projects using AI.

name: Global Wetlands Project
summary: Project at Griffith University that studies critical issues facing coastal wetlands and builds online tools, and a member of the Global Mangrove Alliance.

name: GlobalFungi
summary: Global database of fungal occurrences from high-throughput-sequencing metabarcoding studies, from a team at the Czech Academy of Sciences.

name: GlobalGeoTree
summary: Vision-language data set for global tree species classification.

name: GlobalTreeSearch
summary: Botanic Gardens Conservation International database of all known tree species and their country-level distributions.

name: GloBAM
summary: Project that aimed to quantify biomass flows of aerial migrants from weather radar data across Europe and North America, funded by two national science foundations and concluded in December 2022.

name: GLOBIS-B
summary: EU project on advancing Essential Biodiversity Variables, for predicting how the biosphere changes under global environmental change.

name: GlobWetland II
summary: European Space Agency funded project that built a pilot Global Wetlands Observing System, mapping over 200 wetland sites in the coastal catchments of the southern and eastern Mediterranean from satellite data.

name: GMES & Africa
summary: Joint programme co-funded by the African Union Commission and the European Union on Earth observation capacity in Africa. RCMRD lists it among its projects.

name: Good Energies Foundation
summary: Funder working on access to clean energy and protection of tropical forests, part of the Porticus Earth portfolio. MapBiomas lists it as a funder.

name: Google
summary: Technology company that builds Earth Engine, geospatial and nature AI models and datasets, and runs an accelerator and grant funding for nature AI through its programmes and Google.org.

name: Google DeepMind
summary: AI research laboratory within Google whose ecosystem modelling work covers deforestation risk, forest typology, species range maps, the Perch bioacoustics model and AlphaEarth Foundations.

name: Google DeepMind Accelerator: AI for the Planet (APAC)
summary: Three-month accelerator for 16 Asia-Pacific organisations using AI on environmental problems, with mentorship and access to Google AI tools.

name: Google Earth AI
summary: Google's collection of geospatial AI models and datasets, covering weather, floods, wildfire, urban planning and public health, and including AlphaEarth Foundations, SpeciesNet and Remote Sensing Foundations.

name: Google Earth Engine
summary: Cloud platform that combines a multi-petabyte catalogue of satellite imagery and geospatial datasets with analysis tools, free for academic and research use.

name: Google Earth Outreach
summary: Google programme, directed by Rebecca Moore, that supports nonprofit and environmental uses of Google Earth and Earth Engine. Current form not checked.

name: Google for Startups Accelerator: AI for Nature
summary: Ten-week accelerator for early-stage startups in the Americas that use AI and other technology to measure, monitor, protect and restore nature, with mentoring and technical support from Google.

name: Google genomics work for endangered species
summary: Google's technical support, through AI tools such as DeepPolisher and DeepVariant, for sequencing endangered animals with the Vertebrate Genomes Project, with Google.org funding to The Rockefeller University for 150 more species.

name: Google Research
summary: Research division of Google that co-develops nature models and datasets with Google DeepMind, including ForestCast, Natural Forests of the World 2020 and Farmscapes 2020, and publishes SpeciesNet.

name: Google species range maps
summary: Google research using a graph neural network on field observations, AlphaEarth Foundations embeddings and species traits to produce range maps, with a pilot on Australian mammals and 23 maps released through the UN Biodiversity Lab and Earth Engine.

name: Google.org
summary: Google's philanthropic arm, which funded AI-enabled nature solutions in Brazil through Instituto Clima e Sociedade and runs a $20 million AI for Science fund with biodiversity recipients.

name: Google.org AI for Science fund
summary: $20 million Google.org fund for academic, nonprofit and startup organisations using AI on scientific problems; its biodiversity recipients include UNEP-WCMC, mapping plant species, and The Rockefeller University, sequencing genomes.

name: Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation
summary: Foundation set up by Gordon and Betty Moore, with an Environmental Conservation Program. It has funded biodiversity data work including a $10 million grant to iNaturalist, and is a listed funder of Global Fishing Watch and MapBiomas.

name: granite-geospatial-biomass
summary: IBM geospatial foundation model fine-tuned to predict total above-ground biomass from Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery, using GEDI labels from 15 biomes.

name: Green Climate Fund
summary: International climate fund and a member of the Leads Group of the Global Forest Observations Initiative.

name: GreenGPT
summary: AI assistant in Justdiggit's Greener.Land app and website that gives farmers, residents and partners tailored advice on regreening degraded land. OutSystems, which supplied the app platform, gives a reach of 60,000 people a year and is the only source read that uses the name GreenGPT.

name: GRID-Arendal
summary: Norwegian non-profit environmental organisation that works with UNEP. Store norske leksikon says it was set up to collect environmental data and communicate it to decision-makers.

name: Griffith University
summary: Public research university in South East Queensland, Australia, behind the Global Wetlands Project, which builds online tools on coastal wetlands.

name: Ground Control
summary: British satellite communications company in Gloucester with an animal tracking section, working with tag makers such as Vectronic and ATS.

name: Group on Earth Observations
summary: Intergovernmental partnership of more than 100 governments and more than 100 participating organisations that coordinates Earth observation data, and convenes the Global Ecosystems Atlas.

name: Group on Earth Observations Biodiversity Observation Network
summary: Global network of researchers that coordinates biodiversity observation, generates Essential Biodiversity Variables and develops indicators and forecasts.

name: Grouper Spotter
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that applies AI to photographs of grouper species.

name: GS Donor Advised Philanthropy Fund for Wealth Management
summary: New York donor-advised fund recorded as giving Global Fishing Watch $2 million in 2023 and 2024.

name: GUANO
summary: Open, extensible metadata format for bat acoustic recordings, intended for adoption by any manufacturer or software, whose specification has reached version 1.0 and is described as production-ready.

name: GUARDEN
summary: EU project building decision support tools for biodiversity and ecosystem services, using deep learning, Earth observation and hybrid models.

name: Guardian Connector
summary: Open-source data integration and monitoring platform for Indigenous Peoples to collect, manage and own data about their territories, from Nia Tero.

name: Guardians of Earth
summary: Network of mapped Nature Realms that aggregates ecological observations from citizen science sources such as iNaturalist and eBird, and gives each realm a composite BioScore computed by the platform.

name: Gundi
summary: Open-source tool that takes data from wildlife trackers, camera traps and acoustic monitors, puts it into a common format and sends it on for analysis. Mongabay reported it in use at 600 sites in 2024.

name: Hack the Planet
summary: Dutch non-profit foundation that builds hardware and software for rangers and NGOs, including AI camera traps that send images by satellite.

name: Haikubox
summary: United States company selling devices that identify birds and bats by sound, including the Skylark range for wildlife professionals.

name: Half-Earth Project Map
summary: Biodiversity map used for species-focused indicators and decision support, shown alongside Map of Life at a GEO session at the 2024 UN biodiversity conference. The Half-Earth Project site is that of the E.O. Wilson Biodiversity Foundation.

name: Hampshire Foundation
summary: Foundation funding non-profit partners who help people build resilience against poverty in harmony with nature. Global Nature Watch lists it among its funders.

name: Hans Wilsdorf Foundation
summary: Foundation listed as a funder of Global Fishing Watch.

name: Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2
summary: NASA project that combines Landsat and Sentinel-2 data into consistent surface reflectance products, and the training data behind the Prithvi models.

name: Harvard University
summary: Private research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts, home of the Teamcore group, whose topics include conservation.

name: Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf
summary: Public university in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. Authors of the DeepLOKI zooplankton classification software work there.

name: Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research
summary: German environmental research centre and a participant in the MAMBO biodiversity monitoring project.

name: Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon
summary: German Helmholtz research centre for coasts and climate. It coordinates AqQua, a foundation AI model for pelagic imaging of plankton and organic particles.

name: Helsinki Commission
summary: Intergovernmental commission under the Helsinki Convention that protects the Baltic Sea, and publishes the geospatial data used in its assessments through a map and data service.

name: Hemmersbach Rhino Force
summary: Direct action rhino conservation organisation, registered in Germany and South Africa, with five squads in the Greater Kruger region using infrared and night-vision cameras, plus a CryoVault storing rhino genes.

name: Hempel Foundation
summary: Danish foundation that funds biodiversity conservation and education. It says it works to strengthen data and evidence for conservation and is a partner in the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund.

name: High Carbon Stock Approach
summary: Provides tools for plantation companies, farmers and brands to remove deforestation from their operations, with a mapping portal and an alert and monitoring platform built on Global Forest Watch Pro.

name: HiRAD
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project, 2024 to 2027, building software tools to harmonise biological data from radar systems across Europe for monitoring aerial biodiversity.

name: Holohil Systems
summary: Canadian maker of wildlife tracking transmitters, which says it has worked in the field for more than 40 years.

name: Horn of Africa Regional Environment Centre and Network
summary: Regional environment centre and network, listed as an Associate participant of GBIF, which hosts regional workshops on environmental initiatives in Eastern Africa.

name: Huawei
summary: Technology company whose TECH4ALL initiative funds and builds nature monitoring projects with AI, cloud and acoustic sensors, including Tech4Nature with IUCN and Nature Guardian with Rainforest Connection.

name: HUB Ocean
summary: Non-profit technology foundation founded in Norway that runs the Ocean Data Platform and leads the Ocean Data Action Coalition. It came out of a collaboration between the World Economic Forum and the Aker Group.

name: Hula Earth
summary: Sells biodiversity monitoring that combines solar-powered BioT sensors with on-device AI species detection and satellite imagery.

name: HydroLAKES
summary: Shoreline polygons of global lakes of at least 10 hectares, covering 1.4 million lakes and reservoirs.

name: HydroSHEDS
summary: Free digital data layers for hydro-ecological research worldwide, started in 2006 by World Wildlife Fund US, with river networks, catchments and related products.

name: I3S Interactive Individual Identification System
summary: Free software with GNU GPL v2 source code that identifies animals from natural marks, helping extract spot patterns for database comparison, with whale shark, manta and fluke variants.

name: IBM
summary: Technology company that builds open geospatial foundation models with NASA and ESA, including Prithvi and TerraMind, and is working with WWF-Germany on identifying forest elephants from camera trap photos.

name: IBM and WWF-Germany forest elephant monitoring
summary: Project announced in 2024 by IBM and WWF-Germany to identify individual African forest elephants from camera trap photos with AI-powered visual inspection.

name: iBOL Europe
summary: European node of the International Barcode of Life consortium, run by it, serving as a regional hub for DNA barcoding communities and publishing a gap list of species missing from barcode databases.

name: Icarus
summary: Animal tracking system with a receiver in orbit that reads transmitters on animals, back in space on a CubeSat launched on 28 November 2025 after its earlier ISS-based prototype.

name: ICCA Consortium
summary: Member association for territories and areas conserved by Indigenous Peoples and local communities, registered under Swiss law, which has held conversations on Indigenous knowledge and AI.

name: Iceberg Data Lab
summary: Paris company supplying climate, biodiversity and deforestation data to financial institutions, with offices in London and Frankfurt. It launched an AI called Barbatus to extract environmental data from annual reports.

name: ICES Working Group on Machine Learning in Marine Science
summary: ICES group that reviews machine learning applications in marine science, advises on data collection for machine learning and identifies future needs.

name: ICESat-2
summary: NASA satellite laser altimetry mission measuring ice sheet elevation, sea ice thickness and land characteristics, launched in 2018.

name: ICEYE
summary: Operates a radar (SAR) satellite constellation and sells a deforestation monitoring service, alongside defence and insurance products.

name: iChatBio
summary: University of Florida chatbot with specialist agents that find and retrieve biodiversity records, media and literature from iDigBio, GBIF, iNaturalist, BHL, OBIS and ALA. Pages show it presented to researchers and open to new agents; no page read gives user numbers.

name: Icoteq
summary: British designer of small low-power tracking devices whose work includes tracking animals, listed by Argos for bird, land and marine animal transmitters.

name: IdentiFlight
summary: Bird detection system that classifies birds near wind turbines so that turbines can be curtailed, sold by Boulder Imaging.

name: Ifremer
summary: French ocean research institute headquartered in Brest, with deep learning work on underwater imagery of fish and benthic life.

name: IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre
summary: Climate centre of IGAD, the East African intergovernmental body. It hosts GMES & Africa for the region and says it uses Earth observation to monitor forests, natural habitats, agriculture and rangelands.

name: ILIAD
summary: EU project that aimed to establish an interoperable, data-intensive Digital Twin of the Ocean.

name: Image and Signal Processing group
summary: Universitat de València group that develops AI methods to model and understand complex systems including Earth and climate systems.

name: Imageomics Institute
summary: US research institute that applies machine learning to images of organisms, publisher of BioCLIP, TreeOfLife-10M and biobench.

name: Impact Observatory
summary: Sells AI-based land cover maps and change detection from satellite imagery, at 3 metre and 10 metre resolution.

name: Imperative Global
summary: The organisation designs, develops, owns and operates native-species restoration projects, with a final Phase 2 investment decision reached in South Africa and mangrove projects planned in Mexico and India.

name: Imperial College London
summary: Public research university in London, home of the Ecosystem Sensing Group.

name: iNatSounds
summary: Bioacoustics data sets drawn from iNaturalist sound recordings, with a 2024 release.

name: iNaturalist
summary: Non-profit social network where people record and identify observations of species, with an automated species identification tool, and whose research-grade records feed GBIF.

name: iNaturalist Competition Datasets
summary: Species image classification competition data sets drawn from iNaturalist, released for 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021.

name: iNaturalist Research-grade Observations
summary: Openly licensed research-grade species observations from iNaturalist, published to GBIF.

name: Indian Ocean Biodiversity Information System
summary: Regional node of the Ocean Biodiversity Information System that collects and shares marine species distribution records, run by India's Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology.

name: Indian Ocean Tuna Commission
summary: Tuna commission for the Indian Ocean, whose site offers datasets and a data browser.

name: Inland Norway University of Applied Sciences
summary: Norwegian university whose Department of Forestry and Wildlife Management leads BIG_PICTURE, a European camera trapping project with AI image processing.

name: Innovasea
summary: Maker of acoustic fish tags and receivers for tracking aquatic animals, formed in this field through buying Vemco and HTI in 2019. It also sells aquaculture technology.

name: INRAE
summary: French national research institute. It publishes the One Forest Vision initiative's website, from Castanet Tolosan, and is one of the four bodies in the Pl@ntNet consortium.

name: Inria
summary: French national research institution for computer science, a member of the Pl@ntNet consortium and a participant in MAMBO.

name: Insight Robotics
summary: Hong Kong forestry risk management company selling a wildfire detection system and aerial surveys for plantation and agroforestry owners.

name: Institut de recherche pour le développement
summary: French national research institute for sustainable development. Its MARBEC research unit at Sète leads MooByF, a European project monitoring open-ocean biodiversity with fishers using AI.

name: Institute for Computational Sustainability
summary: Cornell University institute directed by Carla Gomes, linked to the Computational Sustainability Network.

name: Instituto Humboldt
summary: Colombian government research institute on the country's biodiversity. Its researchers are lead authors of the AnuraSet frog call dataset.

name: Instituto Regional de Biodiversidad
summary: Central American biodiversity institute linked to the regional environment commission CCAD, which executed the PROMEBIO monitoring programme. The newest page found dates from about 2012, so its current state is unconfirmed.

name: Instituto Tecnológico de Costa Rica
summary: Costa Rican public university whose School of Computing at the Alajuela campus is named as lead of the Redbioma network on biodiversity data science.

name: Integrated Biodiversity Assessment Tool
summary: Alliance of IUCN, BirdLife International, Conservation International and UNEP-WCMC that sells commercial access to the Red List, protected area and Key Biodiversity Area datasets and reinvests fees in them.

name: Integrated Carbon Observation System
summary: European research infrastructure that publishes standardised open data from close to 180 stations in 16 countries, covering greenhouse gases in the atmosphere and carbon fluxes with land and ocean.

name: Integrated Taxonomic Information System
summary: Taxonomic information on plants, animals, fungi and microbes of North America and the world, and a founding partner of the Catalogue of Life.

name: Intel
summary: Chip maker whose vision processors and AI work are used in TrailGuard AI, an anti-poaching camera, and Project CORaiL, a coral reef monitoring system.

name: Inter-American Development Bank Group
summary: Development bank group that runs Amazonia Forever, its regional programme for the Amazon, and the AmazoniaForever360+ territorial intelligence platform.

name: Inter-American Institute for Global Change Research
summary: Regional intergovernmental organisation for research on global environmental change in the Americas. This entry covers its research on biodiversity and ecosystem services and its open data catalogue.

name: Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission
summary: Tuna fisheries commission for the eastern Pacific with headquarters in La Jolla, publishing catch and other data for public download.

name: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
summary: Independent intergovernmental body strengthening the science-policy interface on biodiversity and ecosystem services, with a task force on knowledge and data that guides how its assessments manage data.

name: International Barcode of Life Consortium
summary: International consortium working to establish an Earth observation system that discovers species and sets biodiversity baselines through DNA barcoding, with its secretariat at the Centre for Biodiversity Genomics in Guelph.

name: International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development
summary: Intergovernmental knowledge and learning centre for the Hindu Kush Himalaya, based in Kathmandu, working for eight regional member countries. It hosts a SERVIR hub.

name: International Centre for Water Resources and Global Change
summary: UNESCO Category 2 centre in Koblenz, Germany. It operates GEMStat, the global freshwater quality database, under UNEP GEMS/Water.

name: International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology
summary: Nairobi-based research institute on insects and other arthropods. It took over long-term ownership of Digital Earth Africa, the open Earth observation programme for Africa.

name: International Climate Initiative
summary: German government funding programme for climate action and biodiversity conservation in the Global South since 2008, anchored in the federal environment ministry.

name: International Commission for the Protection of the Danube River
summary: International organisation set up under the Danube River Protection Convention. Its water quality database holds the TransNational Monitoring Network data for the Danube river basin.

name: International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature
summary: Body that provides and regulates the system of zoological nomenclature and maintains ZooBank, supported by a secretariat at the Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum in Singapore.

name: International Coral Reef Initiative
summary: Global partnership for preserving coral reefs and associated ecosystems, which established the Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network in 1995.

name: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea
summary: Marine science organisation based in Copenhagen that gives advice on conservation, management and sustainability and has a working group on machine learning in marine science.

name: International Development Research Centre
summary: Canadian funder of international development research, based in Ottawa. It co-founded the Lacuna Fund for labelled machine learning datasets.

name: International Food Policy Research Institute
summary: Research institute whose Moore Foundation grant covers modelling agricultural land use change in tropical forest and savannah areas of Brazil and Argentina. Its logo is among Land & Carbon Lab's partners.

name: International Fund for Animal Welfare
summary: Global non-profit working in more than 40 countries to rescue animals and protect their habitats. It is named as a partner in Baidu's AI Guardian of Endangered Species work.

name: International Hydrographic Organization
summary: Intergovernmental hydrographic body based in Monaco. It governs GEBCO jointly with the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission.

name: International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis
summary: Independent international research institute in Laxenburg, Austria, that worked with Google DeepMind and the World Resources Institute on the Forest Typology map.

name: International Land Coalition
summary: Coalition of 319 members in 86 countries working on land rights, based in Rome. It sits on the steering group of LandMark, the global map of Indigenous and community lands.

name: International Long Term Ecological Research Network
summary: Network of long-term ecological research sites with regional groups in East Asia Pacific, Europe and the United States.

name: International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration
summary: Global collaboration of governmental and non-profit bodies that manage nucleotide sequence databases and exchange data openly, including GenBank, the source of reference sequences for eDNA work.

name: International Ocean Carbon Coordination Project
summary: Science infrastructure with a project office that coordinates ocean carbon and biogeochemistry research, observations and standards internationally.

name: International Ocean Colour Coordinating Group
summary: International group that coordinates ocean-colour remote sensing. An affiliated programme of the Scientific Committee on Oceanic Research, with a project office at the Bedford Institute of Oceanography in Canada.

name: International Partnership Programme
summary: UK Space Agency programme, described in 2017 as five years and £152 million, supporting British satellite expertise in international projects. It paid for a £5.3 million project against illegal logging in Guatemala.

name: International Quiet Ocean Experiment
summary: International scientific programme of the Scientific Committee on Oceanic Research on ocean soundscapes and the effects of sound on marine life.

name: International Research Center of Big Data for Sustainable Development Goals
summary: Research centre launched by the Chinese Academy of Sciences to use and share Earth observation data for the Sustainable Development Goals, which runs the SDGSAT-1 satellite and the Digital Belt and Road Program.

name: International Research Centre on Artificial Intelligence
summary: Research centre on AI under the auspices of UNESCO, which is establishing the Water Observatory, a set of tools for water management and reporting.

name: International Seabed Authority
summary: Autonomous international organisation under UNCLOS that controls mineral-related activity in the international seabed area and hosts the DeepData database.

name: International Soil Carbon Network
summary: Science-based network that assembles soil carbon databases and shares data. It has a data-sharing agreement with ISRIC.

name: International Telecommunication Union
summary: UN agency for digital technologies whose standards sector has a work item on AI-driven wildlife conservation and monitoring, and which runs AI for Good.

name: International Union for Conservation of Nature
summary: Membership union of government and civil society organisations that keeps the IUCN Red List and other nature data products, and whose members resolved in 2025 to develop a policy on AI in conservation.

name: International Water Management Institute
summary: International research-for-development organisation on water and land management, headquartered in Colombo. In 2020 it began a partnership with Digital Earth Africa to build water management tools from Earth observation data and machine learning.

name: International Waterbird Census
summary: Global annual count of waterbird species, coordinated by Wetlands International, with a database of counts by country and species.

name: International Whaling Commission
summary: International body on whaling, with headquarters in Impington near Cambridge.

name: Internet of Elephants
summary: Company that uses real wildlife data for conservation storytelling through games and interactive experiences, and released its visualisation tool for wildlife movement data as open source.

name: Internet of Turtles
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that uses AI to identify sea and terrestrial turtles from photographs.

name: InterNodes, Inc.
summary: Registered non-profit that is the legal and administrative entity for the Global Forest Biodiversity Initiative. The initiative's site gives a contact address in West Lafayette, Indiana.

name: Inverto Earth
summary: Company offering restoration and monitoring technology, including drones, eDNA, acoustic monitoring, camera traps and radar, with coastal restoration work.

name: IPBES Code of Practice on the Use of Artificial Intelligence
summary: Code of practice for ethical and responsible use of AI in IPBES work, welcomed by the IPBES Plenary, with use cases for common AI types.

name: IPBES Task Force on Knowledge and Data
summary: IPBES task force that supports assessment experts in finding and mobilising knowledge and data and guides the secretariat's data management.

name: IPLC Science Endowment Fund
summary: Endowment that supports Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities to become scientists and leaders in conservation. It was established by the ETH BiodivX team and GainForest with the XPRIZE Rainforest Award and is stewarded by GainForest in Zurich.

name: IRCAI Water Observatory
summary: Set of technological tools for water management and ESG reporting from IRCAI, registered as a UN SDG 6 partnership.

name: ISA Deep Seabed and Ocean Database
summary: Spatial, web-based data system that hosts data on deep-seabed activities, including data collected by contractors during exploration.

name: Island Conservation
summary: Non-profit that restores islands for nature and people, using drones, AI, image recognition and eDNA in its projects.

name: Islas Secas Foundation
summary: Foundation named by Global Fishing Watch as a funder of its work in Panama.

name: ISRIC - World Soil Information
summary: Independent science-based foundation established in 1966 that provides soil information, accredited as the World Data Centre for Soil and producer of SoilGrids.

name: Italian Space Agency
summary: Italian national space agency, party to the Broglio Space Centre agreement with Kenya, whose implementing arrangements cover a regional Earth observation centre and access to Earth observation data.

name: ITU-T work item Y.aiwl on AI-driven wildlife conservation and monitoring
summary: Draft ITU-T standard item on wildlife conservation and monitoring using IoT sensors, cameras and GPS trackers, listed as carried to the next study period.

name: IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology
summary: Classification framework for Earth's ecosystems that integrates functional and compositional features, useful when assessing ecosystems for the IUCN Red List of Ecosystems.

name: IUCN Policy on Artificial Intelligence and Conservation
summary: Work requested by IUCN Resolution 8.140 of 2025, under which a working group is to draft an IUCN policy and guidelines on AI in conservation and on the integrity of digital evidence.

name: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems
summary: Assessments of the risk of collapse of ecosystems under an IUCN protocol, including global assessments of coral reefs and mangroves.

name: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
summary: Global information source on the extinction risk of animal, fungus and plant species, with data on range, population, habitat, threats and conservation action.

name: IUCN Species Survival Commission
summary: Volunteer expert network of IUCN that builds knowledge on the status of species and threats to them, and contributes indicators through the Red List.

name: IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas
summary: IUCN's expert network on protected and conserved areas, which advises policymakers and works on Target 3 of the Global Biodiversity Framework.

name: iWildCam
summary: Camera trap competition data sets run with the FGVC workshop at CVPR, used to test generalisation across cameras and sites; the 2022 edition focused on counting animals.

name: Jane Goodall Institute
summary: Science-driven, community-led conservation organisation founded in 1977. Its research archive is being digitised with AWS and AI.

name: Jane Goodall Institute research archive digitisation
summary: Project funded by $1 million from the AWS Generative AI Innovation Fund to turn 65 years of handwritten notes, films and observations on chimpanzees and baboons into digital formats with language models.

name: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
summary: Japan's space agency, which supplies L-band radar data for forest and wetland monitoring through the ALOS Kyoto & Carbon Initiative and JJ-FAST.

name: Japan International Cooperation Agency
summary: Japanese aid agency that launched the JJ-FAST tropical deforestation monitoring service with the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency in 2016.

name: JASCO Applied Sciences
summary: Underwater acoustics company working on underwater sound and its effects on marine life, with an office in Halifax, Canada.

name: Jeremy and Hannelore Grantham Environmental Trust
summary: US public charity focused on reducing and reversing global environmental degradation, set up alongside the Grantham Foundation. SPUN lists it among its funders.

name: JICA-JAXA Forest Early Warning System in the Tropics
summary: Forest early warning service launched in 2016 by JICA and JAXA that uses ALOS-2 data to report deforestation and forest change in tropical regions, about every 45 days at launch.

name: John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation
summary: Chicago foundation. Its Conservation & Sustainable Development programme funded Amazon Conservation to extend a near-real-time forest monitoring system from Peru across the tropical Andes.

name: Joint Research Centre of the European Commission
summary: European Commission science service that coordinates the global part of the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service and publishes global forest maps.

name: JRS Biodiversity Foundation
summary: Private US foundation that makes grants for biodiversity information in sub-Saharan Africa, including freshwater biodiversity systems, pollinator data and monitoring in protected areas.

name: Justdiggit
summary: Dutch non-profit that helps landowners restore degraded land by regreening, and gives free tailored advice through its Greener.Land app.
