name: Jülich Supercomputing Centre
summary: Supercomputing centre at Forschungszentrum Jülich in Germany that helped develop the Prithvi geospatial foundation model with NASA and IBM.

name: Kanop
summary: Sells satellite and AI measurement of biomass, carbon and land use change for nature-based carbon projects and supply chains.

name: Kartoza
summary: Open source GIS service provider with registered offices in South Africa and Portugal. It builds BIMS, a biodiversity data platform used by South African National Parks.

name: Katam Technologies
summary: Swedish forest data company whose portal is used to process and analyse forest data, with operations in Indonesia.

name: Kayrros
summary: Sells geospatial AI that tracks human activity and its environmental footprint, with products including a forest carbon monitor, an imported deforestation tracker and forestry due diligence.

name: Kayrros Forest Carbon Monitor
summary: Kayrros remote sensing product giving project developers biomass, carbon stock and forest degradation measurements for nature-based projects.

name: Kayrros Imported Deforestation Tracker
summary: Kayrros product for corporate buyers tracking deforestation linked to imports.

name: Kelp Forest Foundation
summary: Non-profit that develops standards, tools and pilot projects for kelp. It runs a global biodiversity project that uses eDNA to study marine life in kelp forests.

name: Key Biodiversity Areas Partnership
summary: Multi-organisation agreement to jointly identify, map, monitor and conserve sites of global importance for biodiversity, under a strategic plan for 2025 to 2030.

name: King's College London
summary: London university whose Department of Geography led the development of Terra-i, a land cover change monitoring system that uses a neural network.

name: Kitzes Lab
summary: University of Pittsburgh group that uses acoustic recorders and machine learning sound classifiers to study rare species, and maintains the OpenSoundscape library.

name: Knowledge Centre for Biodiversity
summary: European Commission knowledge centre that supports biodiversity policymaking by developing tools for the EU Biodiversity Strategy and structuring relevant information.

name: Kumi Analytics
summary: Singapore company combining remote sensing and deep learning to set environmental baselines for conservation projects.

name: Kuva Space
summary: Finnish hyperspectral satellite company that sells deforestation, habitat and carbon monitoring and has a blue carbon mapping project with WWF-Indonesia.

name: Kuyua
summary: Hamburg company with an analytics platform on nature, biodiversity and climate for corporate risk assessment and reporting.

name: Laboratoire d'Océanographie de Villefranche
summary: Sorbonne Université oceanography laboratory in southern France with a plankton ecology team that works on image data.

name: Lacuna Fund
summary: Fund that gives data scientists, researchers and social entrepreneurs in low- and middle-income contexts the resources to produce labelled datasets for machine learning, including remote sensing and land-use data. It says it moved its leadership and management to partners in Africa and Latin America in July 2025.

name: Lake Chad Basin Commission
summary: Commission of six Lake Chad basin states. It runs the Lake Chad Information System, a regional database shown as maps, charts and tables.

name: Lake Victoria Basin Commission
summary: Specialised institution of the East African Community that coordinates management of the Lake Victoria Basin and manages the Lake Victoria Basin Water Information System.

name: Land Life
summary: Builds and manages reforestation projects and says it monitors them in real time and publishes the data.

name: Land Potential Knowledge System
summary: Free mobile apps for recording and looking up soil and land data, started by USDA-ARS with USAID funding and used as a tool for rangeland monitoring and land-use planning.

name: Landler
summary: The Landbanking Group's platform turning remote sensing and field data into risk signals, financial metrics and nature assets.

name: LandMark
summary: Online global platform of Indigenous and community lands, run by a consortium of organisations with a steering group and secretariat.

name: Landsat
summary: Joint NASA and USGS satellite programme that provides the longest continuous space-based record of Earth's land.

name: LandScale
summary: Online assessment tool for measuring and reporting sustainability at landscape level, co-led by the Rainforest Alliance and Conservation International, with Verra among its early development partners.

name: Large Nature Model
summary: Multimodal AI model developed for DATALAND by Refik Anadol Studio. Its developers say it is trained on more than 1.2 billion ecological data points and environmental recordings.

name: LEAD Conservation
summary: Dutch foundation that trains rangers, instructors, leaders and analysts for protected areas across Africa and Asia. An EarthRanger deployment partner.

name: Leibniz Institute DSMZ
summary: Research infrastructure in Braunschweig, Germany, that develops the SILVA ribosomal RNA database and related scientific databases.

name: Lenovo
summary: Technology company that supplied edge servers for AI camera trap analysis to Island Conservation on Robinson Crusoe Island and donated a smart IT system for Yangtze finless porpoise protection.

name: Lens
summary: Remote land monitoring software from Upstream Tech, used in conservation to monitor easements and track land use change.

name: Leverhulme Centre for Nature Recovery
summary: University of Oxford centre on nature recovery, one of whose themes tracks recovery with remote sensing, big data and deep machine learning; a partner of Google Research on the Farmscapes 2020 map.

name: LGND
summary: Company that turns satellite and aerial imagery into queryable datasets using geographic embeddings; its funding release is datelined New York.

name: LifeCLEF
summary: International research initiative in biodiversity informatics that runs data-oriented challenges each year, including BirdCLEF, PlantCLEF, GeoLifeCLEF, FungiCLEF and AnimalCLEF.

name: LifeWatch ERIC
summary: European Research Infrastructure Consortium providing e-Science facilities for biodiversity and ecosystem research, with a main office in Seville and a machine learning tool programme.

name: LILA BC
summary: Repository of labelled data sets for biology and conservation, hosting over ten million labelled images for machine learning work.

name: Limelight Rainforest
summary: Team led from Colorado Mesa University that won XPRIZE Rainforest with a canopy sensor platform, drones and AI models; a partner in Amazon.ia.

name: Lion Identification Network of Collaborators
summary: AI-assisted collaborative database for lion identification and research between organisations, supported by a 2018 Microsoft and National Geographic AI for Earth Innovation Grant to the team at Wildlife Guardians.

name: LIS Laboratory, University of Toulon
summary: Computer science laboratory at the University of Toulon, a TABMON partner, whose team there includes Hervé Glotin on bioacoustics and AI.

name: LiveEO
summary: Sells satellite-based risk intelligence, including TradeAware software for the EU Deforestation Regulation and deforestation analytics.

name: Livelihoods Funds
summary: Investment fund that pre-finances restoration and carbon projects, including Océanium's mangrove project in Senegal, and pays for monitoring them.

name: Liverpool John Moores University
summary: University in Liverpool, England, whose researchers published the Conservation AI platform papers.

name: Living Planet Index
summary: Measure of the state of biological diversity based on population trends of vertebrate species, and an indicator in the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

name: Lobelia Earth
summary: Barcelona company producing observational datasets on air, water, soil and vegetation, including a project detecting marine plastic with SAR and AI.

name: Loggerhead Instruments
summary: United States maker of underwater acoustic recorders and a tool used to observe Sarasota Bay bottlenose dolphins.

name: Lotek
summary: Makes fish and wildlife tracking and monitoring systems, with offices in Canada, the United Kingdom and the United States.

name: LUCAS Land Use/Cover Area Frame Survey
summary: In-situ EU survey run by Eurostat that gives point-level information and harmonised statistics on land use and land cover, publishing microdata for each surveyed point.

name: Lyda Hill Philanthropies
summary: Funds advances in science and nature, and is a named donor to the Audacious Project raise for Global Fishing Watch.

name: Macaulay Library
summary: Scientific archive of natural history audio, video and photographs, rooted in birds, which also holds recordings of amphibians, fishes and mammals.

name: Major TOM
summary: Standard and set of open datasets for curating, sharing and combining large-scale Earth observation data for deep learning, published by ESA Φ-lab contributors.

name: MAMBO
summary: Horizon Europe project of 10 partners that developed and tested biodiversity monitoring tools combining artificial intelligence with remote sensing and sensors, to fill gaps in Europe's biodiversity data.

name: Mammal Diversity Database
summary: Database from the American Society of Mammalogists that tracks taxonomic changes to mammals, recording 6,904 species in version 2.5.

name: MammAlps
summary: Multi-view video behaviour monitoring dataset of wild mammals, recorded in the Swiss National Park with video and audio.

name: ManglarIA
summary: WWF pilot in Mexico that uses AI, drones and sensor networks to monitor mangrove health, with support from Google.org and leadership from local communities.

name: Mangrove Capital Africa
summary: Ten-year programme led by Wetlands International and funded by DOB Ecology to safeguard and restore African mangroves. Its Mangrove Watch Africa strand builds capacity in Earth observation and drones, including in the Saloum Delta.

name: Manomet
summary: Conservation science organisation in Plymouth, Massachusetts, that works on bird migration routes and coasts across the Western Hemisphere and houses the Western Hemisphere Shorebird Reserve Network Executive Office.

name: Manta ID
summary: Prototype underwater camera trap built for the Marine Megafauna Foundation to identify manta rays automatically, which its developer says is no longer being worked on.

name: MantaMatcher
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that uses AI to identify giant mantas and rays from photographs.

name: Map of Life
summary: Global resource on the distributions of species and their change, whose indicators are used to track progress under the Global Biodiversity Framework.

name: Map the Point
summary: Small business offering data management, mapping and visualisation to small and mid-sized organisations, designing pest management programmes, running invasive species removal projects and saying it works wherever needed.

name: MAPAMED
summary: Database of marine protected areas in the Mediterranean, whose 2019 edition covers 1,320 sites, from SPA/RAC and MedPAN.

name: MapBiomas
summary: Multi-institutional network of NGOs, universities and technology companies that produces annual land cover and land use maps from satellite imagery, with a secretariat in Brazil and country networks across Latin America, Asia and Africa.

name: Mapeo
summary: Offline mapping tool used by hundreds of communities to document and defend biodiverse places, built by Awana Digital, with maintenance to end under its October 2024 CoMapeo plans.

name: MarAlliance
summary: Marine conservation non-profit working in five countries, focused on Central America and the Caribbean, that monitors marine wildlife with satellite tags.

name: MARCO-BOLO
summary: EU project that strengthens European coastal and marine biodiversity observation and links it to global efforts.

name: MarCOSouth Western Indian Ocean Coral Bleaching Monitoring Service
summary: Service showing satellite-derived thermal stress on coral in the Western Indian Ocean with bleaching observations from CORDIO East Africa, co-designed by the CSIR under the GMES and Africa programme.

name: Marine Biodiversity Observation Network
summary: GEO BON node that links long-term marine biodiversity programmes into an open record, using methods from satellite data to DNA.

name: Marine Biological Laboratory
summary: Research institution for biological and environmental sciences in Woods Hole, Massachusetts, whose SeaBase project has foundation support.

name: Marine Conservation Institute
summary: Organisation that created the Marine Protection Atlas.

name: Marine Geospatial Ecology Lab
summary: Duke University laboratory named as copyright holder of OBIS-SEAMAP, the marine megavertebrate data system.

name: Marine Life 2030
summary: Programme to build a global system for delivering knowledge of ocean life.

name: Marine Megafauna Foundation
summary: Marine conservation non-profit working on large ocean animals since 2009. It partnered with Wild Me to create MantaMatcher, the Wildbook for mantas and other rays.

name: Marine Protection Atlas
summary: Atlas that integrates science-based assessments measuring progress toward protecting 30% of the global ocean in fully and highly protected areas by 2030.

name: Marine Regions
summary: Standard georeferenced list of marine place names and boundaries, integrating the VLIMAR Gazetteer and the VLIZ Maritime Boundaries Geodatabase.

name: Marine Stewardship Council
summary: International non-profit that runs a fishery certification programme and ecolabel. Its AI page says it uses AI in selected areas, with all output under human review; no AI work on fisheries or ocean data was found.

name: Marine Ventures Fund
summary: Fund set up in 2000 by Tom McMurray that backs conservation work on opening up data, through citizen science apps, aerial mapping and studies. It has funded startups including iNaturalist and The Ocean Foundation.

name: MarineSPEED
summary: Benchmark dataset for marine species distribution modelling, used in a 2017 study from the Flanders Marine Institute.

name: MarSensing
summary: Portuguese company in Faro that took part as an exhibitor in underwater acoustics events and makes a compact autonomous acoustic recorder.

name: MARSPEC
summary: Ocean climate layers for marine spatial ecology.

name: Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg
summary: German university that CORDIS lists as coordinator of EuropaBON, the European biodiversity observation network design project.

name: Marxan
summary: Free software and documentation for conservation planning, used for reserve design and natural resource management on land, in fresh water and at sea.

name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
summary: Private research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts, home of the Beery Lab and a partner in the AI and Biodiversity Change Global Center.

name: Mataki
summary: Described as a cheap, light, reprogrammable GPS tracking and sensing device whose tags share data peer to peer, so data can be retrieved from whole groups of monitored animals.

name: Mathesar Foundation
summary: New York foundation recorded as giving Conservation X Labs $2 million in 2020.

name: MATRIX
summary: AI-driven forest growth model built by Jingjing Liang with funding from WRI, using data from over 1.8 million forest plots, being integrated into FAO's For-Growth work.

name: MAVA Foundation
summary: Swiss conservation foundation founded by Luc Hoffmann in 1994, which ceased grant-making at the end of 2022. It was the main donor of a BirdLife project on monitoring systems for migratory birds along the West African coast and a funder of Mediterranean waterbird counts.

name: Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine in the Helmholtz Association
summary: Berlin research centre in the Helmholtz Association, named with Helmholtz Imaging as a lead of the AqQua aquatic foundation model project.

name: Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry
summary: Max Planck institute in Jena whose groups apply machine learning to Earth system science and which runs the TRY plant trait database.

name: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology
summary: Research institute in Leipzig that runs the Pan African Programme, whose camera trap videos come from chimpanzee sites across Africa.

name: Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior
summary: Max Planck institute that hosts Movebank, the animal tracking data platform, and whose director Martin Wikelski is quoted on the ICARUS tracking system.

name: Max Planck Society
summary: Non-profit association of German research institutes, which gives Movebank long-term funding.

name: Mbaza AI
summary: Open camera trap image classifier built by University of Stirling researchers with Appsilon's machine learning team, for the National Parks Agency in Gabon with support from Panthera.

name: McGill University
summary: Public research university in Montreal that leads the Canadian team in the AI and Biodiversity Change Global Center.

name: McLane Research Laboratories
summary: United States maker of ocean sampling instruments, including the RoCSI eDNA sampler.

name: Mediterranean Wetlands Initiative
summary: Mediterranean wetlands body whose Committee asked for the Mediterranean Wetlands Observatory. Its secretariat moved from Greece to the Tour du Valat in southern France in 2014.

name: Mediterranean Wetlands Observatory
summary: Observatory set up by the Tour du Valat in 2008 at the request of the MedWet Committee, which maps and monitors changes in Mediterranean wetlands with earth observation data.

name: MegaDetector
summary: Open-source AI model that detects animals, people and vehicles in camera trap images so that researchers can skip empty frames; it does not classify species.

name: Meise Botanic Garden
summary: Belgian botanic garden whose biodiversity informatics team manages plant and fungal biodiversity data and coordinates the B-Cubed project.

name: Mekong River Commission
summary: Intergovernmental organisation of Cambodia, Lao PDR, Thailand and Viet Nam for cooperation in the Lower Mekong Basin, which monitors the river and publishes data including the Mekong Atlas.

name: Mercator Ocean International
summary: Implementer of the Copernicus Marine Service, due to become the Mercator International Centre for the Ocean, an intergovernmental organisation, and a partner in the European Digital Twin of the Ocean.

name: Merlin Bird ID
summary: Free app from the Cornell Lab of Ornithology that identifies birds from photos and sounds, using AI-powered photo recognition.

name: MERMAID
summary: Wildlife Conservation Society platform for coral reef survey data, adding machine learning to classify reef photos with support from an AWS Imagine Grant.

name: MERMAID AI
summary: AI feature launched by the Wildlife Conservation Society in June 2025 that classifies benthic photo quadrats inside MERMAID, using a model trained on more than 500,000 public CoralNet images.

name: Meta
summary: Technology company that built global canopy height maps and models with the World Resources Institute, using its DINOv2 and DINOv3 vision models.

name: MGnify
summary: Microbiome sequence data analysis resource at EMBL-EBI.

name: Microsensory
summary: Spanish company that develops devices for locating and studying animals, with tags used on birds of prey and on marine and land mammals.

name: Microsoft
summary: Technology company whose AI for Good Lab builds open biodiversity models and devices, and which runs the Planetary Computer and ran the AI for Earth grant programme.

name: Microsoft AI for Good Lab
summary: Microsoft research lab whose biodiversity work covers MegaDetector, PyTorch-Wildlife, SPARROW, bioacoustics, overhead imagery and sonar detection of ghost nets.

name: Microsoft Planetary Computer
summary: Microsoft platform announced in 2020 to give access to environmental datasets and a computing platform to analyse them, with a paid Azure service, Planetary Computer Pro, for managing geospatial data.

name: Microwave Telemetry
summary: United States maker of animal tracking devices for birds and fish, including solar-powered satellite transmitters, working on these since 1991.

name: MIDORI Reference
summary: Quality-controlled DNA and amino acid reference sequences for taxonomic assignment and metabarcoding of eukaryotic mitochondrial sequences.

name: MiewID
summary: AI model from Wild Me Lab that identifies individual animals from photographs, used as the main matching algorithm in Wildbook.

name: MigraMar
summary: Network of scientists that tracks marine migratory species and researches their populations in the Eastern Pacific Ocean.

name: Mila - Quebec AI Institute
summary: Machine learning research institute in Montreal where David Rolnick's group works on AI for biodiversity and climate.

name: MillionTrees
summary: Benchmark that seeks to collect a million tree locations for machine learning models that predict trees from airborne imagery.

name: Milsar
summary: Makes animal telemetry devices, specialising in GPS loggers with remote download, with an address in Nicosia.

name: Minderoo Foundation
summary: Australian philanthropy that set up the OceanOmics programme in 2020 and funds environmental DNA work in marine protected areas, including AU$3.5 million for UNESCO's eDNA Expeditions Phase II. It is a listed funder of Global Fishing Watch.

name: Missouri Botanical Garden
summary: Botanical garden in Saint Louis, Missouri, and a TDWG institutional member. Wikipedia names it as the producer of the Tropicos plant database.

name: MitoFish
summary: Fish mitochondrial genome resource with the MitoAnnotator and MiFish Pipeline tools, at the University of Tokyo.

name: MLWIC2
summary: Tool for classifying camera trap images and training new image classification models, with pre-trained species and empty-image models, which its maintainer says is no longer maintained and points to WildObserve instead.

name: Modelling of DNA-based survey data
summary: Offers free R packages for modelling qPCR and metabarcoding survey data and lists published work on an RShiny app that accounts for false positives and negatives in eDNA.

name: momentuHMM
summary: Open-source R package for generalised multivariate hidden Markov models, with many features motivated by animal movement data and worked examples using real telemetry data.

name: Monash University
summary: Public research university in Melbourne and a core partner in the AI and Biodiversity Change Global Center.

name: Mongabay
summary: Non-profit environmental news organisation founded in 1999, which regularly reports on conservation technology and AI.

name: Mongabay Reforestation Directory
summary: Global directory of reforestation and tree-planting projects, run by Mongabay, recording 36 criteria in five categories to show how much each project discloses through self-reporting.

name: Monitoring of the Andes Amazon Program
summary: Amazon Conservation programme launched in 2015 that uses satellites, drones and radar to detect deforestation and fires in near-real time across the Amazon.

name: Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute
summary: Ocean research institute that creates technologies to explore and map the ocean, and home of FathomNet.

name: MOOBYF
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project monitoring open-ocean biodiversity with fishers, using echosounders, bioacoustics and underwater video supported by AI.

name: Morgan Stanley Global Impact Funding Trust
summary: Donor-advised giving trust recorded as giving Earth Species Project $3.2 million across nine grants from 2022 to 2024.

name: Motus Wildlife Tracking System
summary: International collaborative research network using automated radio telemetry to track the movement and behaviour of small animals such as birds, bats and insects.

name: Mountain Philanthropies
summary: Philanthropy launched in 2017. The CV4Ecology Workshop names it as a supporter.

name: move
summary: R package that uses Movebank, with functions to access movement data stored there and to calculate dynamic Brownian Bridge Movement Models.

name: MoveApps
summary: Open analysis platform for animal tracking data aimed at movement ecologists and wildlife managers, whose institute page reports 125 apps from 22 developers and over 1,100 registered users.

name: Movebank
summary: Online platform for managing, sharing, analysing and archiving animal tracking data, hosted by the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior.

name: moveHMM
summary: R package for modelling animal movement using hidden Markov models.

name: Movetech Telemetry
summary: Academic partnership producing lightweight GPS tracking devices for studying animal movements, a division of BTO Services Ltd.

name: moveVis
summary: R package that turns movement data and changes in environmental data into video animations, with example data on 15 white storks migrating to Africa and a peer-reviewed paper in Methods in Ecology and Evolution.

name: Mulago Foundation
summary: Foundation listed as a funder of the MapBiomas Project since 2023.

name: Multi-Mission Algorithm and Analysis Platform
summary: Cloud platform that combines data, algorithms and computing to process Earth science data, used by teams working with GEDI, ICESat-2, ESA Biomass and NISAR data.

name: Multimodal Vision Research Laboratory
summary: Washington University in St. Louis laboratory, led by Nathan Jacobs, that builds multimodal models for biodiversity monitoring from natural-world imagery, citizen science and Earth observation.

name: Muon Space
summary: Satellite company with sites in Mountain View and San Jose, California. It builds the FireSat wildfire-detection constellation with Earth Fire Alliance.

name: Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle
summary: Paris natural history museum and research institution. Its Eco-Anthropologie unit is the lead affiliation on DeepForestVision, a camera trap classifier for African tropical forests.

name: Nadar
summary: Sells satellite monitoring of carbon stocks and deforestation-free sourcing for compliance with the EU Deforestation Regulation.

name: NASA Biological Diversity Program
summary: NASA research programme that uses observations and models to understand biological diversity and how and why it is changing.

name: NASA Earthdata
summary: NASA's portal for Earth observation data and tools, including Earthdata Search, Worldview and FIRMS.

name: NASA Ecological Conservation Program
summary: NASA Earth Action programme that moves research into decision support for natural resource managers and conservation.

name: NASA Harvest
summary: NASA-commissioned consortium of agriculture and remote sensing experts, managed from the University of Maryland, that publishes the Presto and Galileo Earth observation models.

name: NatCap Research
summary: London company that identifies and quantifies environmental risk, including water, ecosystem health and biodiversity loss, for businesses and supply chains.

name: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
summary: US space agency that funds research and applications on biodiversity and conservation with Earth observation, and flies missions such as GEDI that supply forest structure data.

name: National Audubon Society
summary: US bird conservation organisation. It sits on the Global Mangrove Alliance steering committee.

name: National Center for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis
summary: Independent research affiliate of the University of California, Santa Barbara, which trains scientists in synthesis and data science and has taken on oversight of DataONE.

name: National Ecological Observatory Network
summary: Continental-scale ecological observation facility in the United States, funded by the National Science Foundation and operated by Battelle. A deep learning tree crown dataset was built from its airborne data.

name: National Geographic Society
summary: Non-profit that has awarded more than 16,000 grants since 1888 and now runs its grants through specific requests for proposals. With Microsoft it launched the $1 million AI for Earth Innovation Grant in 2018.

name: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
summary: US federal agency whose work extends beyond national borders. It runs Coral Reef Watch, which provides near real-time satellite products on coral reef stress, and is a partner of Digital Earth Pacific.

name: National Philanthropic Trust
summary: Grant maker based in Pennsylvania and the largest recorded US funder of Global Fishing Watch, with $16.5 million across four grants from 2020 to 2025. It also appears as a funder of Conservation X Labs and Earth Species Project.

name: National University of Singapore
summary: National public research university in Singapore, home of the Centre for Nature-based Climate Solutions.

name: Nationale Postcode Loterij
summary: Dutch charity lottery that supports 150 charities. It is named as a supporter of Global Mangrove Watch.

name: NaturaConnect
summary: EU project that developed knowledge, tools and training to help Member States build a connected trans-European network of protected areas.

name: Natural Capital Alliance
summary: Collaboration with its global hub at Stanford University that helps decision-makers value nature; renamed from the Natural Capital Project in January 2026 and maker of the InVEST software.

name: Natural Capital Data Hub
summary: World Bank platform connecting users to its datasets on wealth and sustainability, including the Changing Wealth of Nations.

name: Natural Forests of the World 2020
summary: Global 10-metre map of the probability of natural forest in 2020, separating natural forest from planted forest, tree crops and other land cover, to support uses such as the EU Deforestation Regulation.

name: Natural History Museum, London
summary: London museum whose PREDICTS team produced the Biodiversity Intactness Index.

name: Naturalis Biodiversity Center
summary: National museum of natural history and biodiversity research centre in Leiden and a developer of the ARISE species identification infrastructure.

name: Nature Data Lab
summary: Fiscally sponsored project of One Earth Philanthropy. Its main work is the Global Safety Net, which monitors remaining natural land and inland waters and their conservation status.

name: Nature Data Public Facility
summary: Proposed public facility for nature-related data, launched by WWF and the TNFD after a TNFD scoping study.

name: Nature Drones CIC
summary: Coordinates the Global Conservation Tech & Drone Forum and has started a resource on drone rules for conservation.

name: Nature Guardian
summary: Huawei programme with Rainforest Connection that uses bioacoustic sensors, cloud and AI to monitor species and threats, including a smart buoy off the Irish coast with Ireland ORCA.

name: Nature Positive Initiative
summary: Initiative with a secretariat that promotes a global nature-positive goal and publishes State of Nature Indicators and Metrics.

name: Nature Tech Collective
summary: Non-profit alliance of startups, investors, researchers, corporates, policymakers and project developers in nature tech, which began as the MRV Collective. It runs events, sector maps and a Nature Tech Directory.

name: Nature4Climate
summary: Coalition of 31 international organisations working on nature-based solutions. It launched an AI and machine learning policy tracker with Metabolic at COP26.

name: NatureAlpha
summary: Sells nature risk intelligence and biodiversity analytics to investors and companies, with location-based risk for individual assets.

name: Naturebase
summary: Web platform from The Nature Conservancy that identifies where, why and how to carry out nature-based climate projects.

name: NatureFinance
summary: Organisation working on nature in financial systems. It runs NatureAlign, a free assessment tool that uses data to show how finance interacts with nature. Trase lists it among its funders.

name: NatureLM-audio
summary: Audio-language foundation model for bioacoustics that learns from paired audio and text to describe recordings and identify and detect species.

name: NatureMetrics
summary: Sells biodiversity monitoring based on environmental DNA and bioacoustics, with species and habitat reporting and a nature risk screening layer for companies in mining, energy, infrastructure, finance and forestry.

name: NatureServe
summary: Biodiversity data organisation with a network of member programmes in the United States and Canada. It publishes species and ecosystem data through NatureServe Explorer.

name: NatureTech Alliance
summary: Alliance of ERM, Salesforce, NatureMetrics and Planet, formed at Davos, to help companies assess, manage and disclose biodiversity impacts and dependencies on nature. Current status not checked.

name: NbS Policy Tracker
summary: Tracker launched at COP26 by Nature4Climate and Metabolic that uses AI and machine learning to identify legislation and investment plans for nature-based solutions.

name: NCX
summary: Gives landowners forest analytics and market opportunities; ForestSource describes it as a forest carbon marketplace and monitoring platform using satellite-based measurement.

name: Nekton Foundation
summary: Ocean exploration organisation that works with more than 190 partners and co-launched Ocean Census with The Nippon Foundation.

name: Neotropical Waterbird Census
summary: Regional part of the International Waterbird Census, coordinated by a regional office of Wetlands International.

name: New England Biolabs Foundation
summary: Foundation in Ipswich, Massachusetts. Kindora lists grants in Peru, Ghana, Ecuador and Guatemala, and a 2025 grant to MarAlliance for monitoring a marine reserve in Belize.

name: New York Botanical Garden
summary: Botanical garden in the Bronx with a Bezos Earth Fund AI Grand Challenge award to automate plant species identification with computer vision.

name: NewsSerow
summary: Language model pipeline that filters news for conservation relevance from a handful of examples, made for low-resource languages. WWF deployed it for media monitoring in Nepal, by the 2024 paper; no later page was read, so whether it still runs is not known.

name: Nia Tero
summary: Organisation that supports Indigenous Peoples' guardianship of their territories. It runs Guardian Connector, an open-source data and monitoring platform.

name: NICFI Satellite Data Program
summary: Norwegian-funded programme giving free access to monthly high-resolution satellite images of the tropics, with data back to 2015. In January 2025 NICFI said the contract period was ending and that it was developing a new phase.

name: Nile Basin Initiative
summary: Intergovernmental partnership of 10 Nile Basin countries that runs shared databases including a water quality database and lists Earth observation products.

name: NIPS4Bplus
summary: Birdsong audio dataset that its paper presents as richly annotated with species tags and temporal annotations, and suggests using to train models for bird population monitoring and species classification.

name: NISAR
summary: NASA and ISRO radar satellite mission whose data is used to monitor ecosystems and crops, track disasters and study how Earth's surface changes.

name: NOAA Coral Reef Watch
summary: NOAA programme that provides near real-time satellite products for monitoring coral reef stress, including bleaching alert areas.

name: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
summary: Natural history museum in Raleigh, North Carolina, named as a Wildlife Insights partner.

name: North Pacific Marine Science Organization
summary: Intergovernmental marine science organisation of six North Pacific countries, with its Secretariat in British Columbia. It has a joint working group with ICES on deep learning for plankton images.

name: North Star Science and Technology
summary: United States company listed by Argos for bird and land animal transmitters and by Movebank for Globalstar tags.

name: Norway's International Climate and Forest Initiative
summary: Norwegian government funder of tropical forest protection, run through the Ministry of Climate and Environment. It paid for universal free access to high-resolution satellite data of the tropics and funded capacity building in its use.

name: Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation
summary: Norwegian aid agency that manages the civil society call under Norway's International Climate and Forest Initiative for the Ministry of Climate and Environment.

name: Norwegian Institute for Nature Research
summary: Independent Norwegian research foundation in Trondheim; it coordinates the TABMON acoustic monitoring network and takes part in BIG_PICTURE.

name: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
summary: Norwegian university that coordinates the Horizon Europe DiverSea project.

name: Novo Nordisk Foundation
summary: Independent Danish enterprise foundation that supports scientific, humanitarian and social causes; it jointly funds the AEGIS ancient environmental genomics initiative.

name: Nuquantic
summary: Baltimore company that launched a portable environmental DNA sampling device in August 2026, first developed at Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory.

name: NUS Centre for Nature-based Climate Solutions
summary: Research centre under the NUS Faculty of Science that has developed technology-driven methods to estimate forest carbon in Singapore, with an outlook to replicate them for Southeast Asia.

name: NVIDIA
summary: Chip and AI company whose hardware and software are used by conservation groups such as Conservation AI. No dedicated nature programme was found.

name: Oak Foundation
summary: Geneva-based charitable foundation with an environment programme. It is a named donor to the Audacious Project raise for Global Fishing Watch and a past funder of MapBiomas.

name: OBAMA-NEXT
summary: EU project developing a toolbox of marine ecosystem and biodiversity information from new technologies including remote sensing, with AI among the methods.

name: OBIS-SEAMAP
summary: Thematic node of the Ocean Biodiversity Information System on the distribution and ecology of marine mammals, seabirds, sea turtles and other marine megavertebrates.

name: Observatoire des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale
summary: Technical body of the Central African Forest Commission that provides information and analysis tools on Central African forest ecosystems.

name: Observatoire pour la biodiversité et les aires protégées en Afrique de l'Ouest
summary: One of five regional observatories set up by BIOPAMA, covering data and reporting on biodiversity and protected areas in West Africa.

name: Observatoire Satellital des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale
summary: Regional NGO based in Kinshasa that produces land cover products, distributes satellite data and builds remote sensing capacity for Central Africa.

name: OBSGESSION
summary: Project launched in January 2024 and coordinated by the Finnish Environment Institute that integrates Earth observation, in-situ observations and ecological modelling to understand the drivers of biodiversity change.

name: Ocean Biomolecular Observing Network
summary: UN Ocean Decade-endorsed programme to monitor, research and understand ocean life by analysing biomolecules such as DNA.

name: Ocean Data Action Coalition
summary: Coalition of the High-Level Panel for a Sustainable Ocean Economy on ocean data, led by HUB Ocean in partnership with Microsoft and Accenture.

name: Ocean Decade Corporate Data Group
summary: Working group co-chaired by Fugro and IOC/UNESCO that builds frameworks for making privately held ocean science data public. It wrote a bathymetry data sharing guideline.

name: Ocean Genomes
summary: Programme producing reference genomes for representatives of all marine vertebrate families, to support environmental DNA monitoring of marine biodiversity.

name: Ocean Health Index
summary: Framework used to measure ocean health from global to local scale, with a global assessment calculated each year.

name: Ocean Impact Organisation
summary: Australian non-profit running an accelerator and venture fund for start-ups working on ocean health, in the Australia and Asia-Pacific regions.

name: Ocean Instruments
summary: New Zealand maker of the SoundTrap underwater acoustic recorders, based in Auckland.

name: Ocean Ledger
summary: Company with AI geospatial accounting software that quantifies ecosystem extent, condition and value, listed as UK and US by Silverstrand Capital.

name: Ocean Networks Canada
summary: University of Victoria initiative running ocean observatories that collect continuous data from the Pacific, Arctic, Atlantic and Southern oceans.

name: Ocean Risk and Resilience Action Alliance
summary: Multi-sector alliance connecting finance and insurance with governments and civil society on ocean risk, registered in Washington DC. Grantable records $1,581,222 to Global Fishing Watch between 2022 and 2024.

name: Ocean Sonics
summary: Canadian maker of digital hydrophones, with marine mammal monitoring among its uses.

name: Ocean Tracking Network
summary: Global aquatic research, data management and partnership platform headquartered at Dalhousie University, used to track movements and survival of aquatic species.

name: Ocean Twilight Zone project
summary: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution project on the ocean's twilight zone, in which biologists use AI techniques to analyse images of plankton.

name: Ocean+ Habitats
summary: Source of information on the status and conservation of coastal habitats from UNEP-WCMC. The related Ocean+ Data Viewer and Ocean+ Library have been retired, with data moved to the UNEP-WCMC GIS Portal.

name: Oceana
summary: International ocean conservation organisation and one of the three founders of Global Fishing Watch, with SkyTruth and Google.

name: Oceankind
summary: Philanthropy whose stated mission is to improve the health of ocean ecosystems by advancing policy, science and technology. It is a funder of Global Fishing Watch and a partner in the sustainable fisheries initiative of Schmidt Marine Technology Partners.

name: OceanMind
summary: Non-profit data provider that combines satellites, AI and analysts to strengthen fisheries enforcement, stop illegal fishing and report on shipping.

name: OceanOmics
summary: Minderoo Foundation marine genomics programme, set up in 2020 with a lab at the University of Western Australia. It has collected and analysed over 10,000 environmental DNA samples from marine environments.

name: Oceans 5
summary: Global philanthropic collaborative on ocean conservation policy, with a 15-year record of grantmaking. Its project areas include illegal fishing and transparency.

name: OceanX
summary: Ocean exploration nonprofit founded by Ray and Mark Dalio, which uses AI through its SeaSwipe annotation platform for ROV footage and digital twin models.

name: ODE Clay
summary: Team that built the Clay foundation model and works on AI for public-interest uses of Earth data, hosted by Renaissance Philanthropy.

name: Okala
summary: Nature monitoring company that says it uses camera traps, bioacoustics, eDNA and remote sensing with AI analysis, with projects in more than 15 countries.

name: OlmoEarth
summary: Ai2's family of open foundation models for Earth observation and the platform built around them, used for tasks such as mapping land cover change, detecting vessels and identifying deforestation.

name: Omdena
summary: AI delivery company with a global expert network, whose local chapters run projects such as AI coral reef monitoring in Indonesia.

name: Omic Biodiversity Observation Network
summary: Thematic network of GEO BON that coordinates biomolecular observations of genes, transcripts, proteins and metabolites towards a distributed global observatory.

name: OnDeck
summary: Canadian company that automates video monitoring of oceans and fisheries with AI, started in Vancouver as OnDeck Fisheries AI.

name: One Earth Philanthropy
summary: US charitable organisation that fiscally sponsors Nature Data Lab, which works with it on the Global Safety Net map of natural land.

name: One Forest Vision initiative
summary: French-funded scientific initiative following the 2023 One Forest Summit, supporting tropical basin countries in monitoring forest degradation, carbon stocks and biodiversity. It trains conservation staff on the DeepForestVision and DeepForestSound AI tools.

name: Open Acoustic Devices
summary: Designs, supports and deploys open-source acoustic hardware and software for monitoring wildlife; its main product is the AudioMoth recorder.

name: Open Data Cube
summary: Free, open-source software for managing and analysing large amounts of satellite imagery and other Earth observation data.

name: Open Forest Protocol
summary: Runs a blockchain-based platform for monitoring and issuing forest carbon credits for afforestation and reforestation projects.

name: Open Foris
summary: FAO's suite of free and open-source tools for forest and land data collection, analysis and reporting, used for national forest monitoring systems.

name: Open Foris Whisp
summary: Free, open-source FAO tool for plot-level analysis of land use and deforestation risk, using geospatial datasets and satellite information, with AI-generated summaries through Earth Map.

name: Open Geospatial Consortium
summary: Consortium that develops open standards for geospatial data. ISRIC and other nature data bodies are members.

name: Open Ocean Robotics
summary: Canadian maker of autonomous ocean vehicles with edge AI for vision and acoustic detection, with illegal fishing enforcement among its uses.

name: Open Science Conservation Fund
summary: Founded by scientists from the Białowieża Forest, it develops free tools for monitoring wildlife, including the TRAPPER camera-trap data system.

name: Open Tree of Life
summary: Collaborative project to build a comprehensive, digital tree of life by synthesising published phylogenetic trees with taxonomic data.

name: Open-Earth-Monitor
summary: Horizon Europe project of 23 partners led by the OpenGeoHub foundation that is building an open-source AI and machine learning computing engine for environmental information.

name: Open-Insect
summary: Fine-grained insect image dataset and benchmark for detecting unknown species, across Northeastern North America, Western Europe and Central America.

name: OpenCollar
summary: Conservation collaboration on open-source tracking collar hardware and software, initiated by Smart Parks.

name: OpenForests
summary: German company that helps restoration and conservation projects map, monitor and report impact through the explorer.land platform.

name: OpenGeoHub Foundation
summary: Independent not-for-profit research foundation promoting open source and open data in geospatial science, which runs OpenLandMap.

name: OpenLandMap
summary: Web portal for exploring and downloading global environmental layers, including soil, vegetation, climate, land cover and biodiversity data.

name: OpenSoundscape
summary: Free and open source Python library for analysing bioacoustic data, developed by the Kitzes Lab.

name: OPERA Land Surface Disturbance Alert
summary: Satellite-based system that tracks land surface disturbance globally, created and operated by University of Maryland researchers with NASA's OPERA project, using Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel-2 data.

name: Orbify
summary: Sells Earth observation analytics for deforestation risk in supply chains, validation of nature and carbon projects, and vessel movements in LNG markets.

name: Ornitela
summary: Lithuanian maker of OrniTrack GPS transmitters for birds and mammals, with data feeds into Movebank.

name: Ornithokrites
summary: Tool for automatically identifying kiwi calls in low-quality audio recordings, classifying regions of interest in each recording with a support vector machine.

name: OroraTech
summary: Sells wildfire monitoring from its commercial thermal infrared satellites, for teams protecting forests, communities and assets.

name: OSPAR Commission
summary: Mechanism through which 15 governments and the European Union protect the marine environment of the North-East Atlantic, with an online system for the data gathered through its monitoring programme.

name: Overstory
summary: Sells vegetation data made by combining AI with satellite and aerial imagery, mainly for electric utilities managing vegetation around power lines.

name: PACE mission
summary: NASA satellite mission whose products include ocean colour and phytoplankton data.

name: Pachama
summary: Forest carbon measurement and monitoring platform using remote sensing and AI, acquired by Carbon Direct, now Relae, in November 2025.

name: Pacific Blue Foundation
summary: Foundation working on community-led restoration and management in Pacific islands, listed as a supporter of the CoralNet image analysis platform.

name: Pacific Community
summary: Principal scientific and technical organisation of the Pacific region, owned by 27 country and territory members, with work on remote sensing through Digital Earth Pacific.

name: Pacific Data Hub
summary: Portal of thousands of datasets from Pacific Island countries and territories, from the Pacific Community.

name: Pacific GIS and Remote Sensing Council
summary: Council bringing together GIS and remote sensing professionals in the Pacific, which runs the annual Pacific Islands GIS and Remote Sensing User Conference and works with Digital Earth Pacific.

name: Pacific Islands Forum Fisheries Agency
summary: Coordinates regional surveillance against illegal fishing in the Pacific from a surveillance centre in Honiara, using satellite detections among other inputs.

name: Pan African Programme: The Cultured Chimpanzee
summary: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology project that studies many chimpanzee populations across Africa; its camera trap videos are classified by volunteers on Chimp&See.

name: Pan-African Agency of the Great Green Wall
summary: Agency created in 2010 under the African Union to coordinate the Great Green Wall initiative. Its site lists an information system and observatory.

name: Pan-European Common Bird Monitoring Scheme
summary: Project of the European Bird Census Council, started in January 2002, that collects data from national monitoring schemes and calculates European common bird indices and indicators.

name: PANGAEA Benchmark
summary: Global and inclusive benchmark for geospatial foundation models, officially adopted to benchmark TerraMind.

name: Pano AI
summary: San Francisco company selling AI wildfire detection from cameras to fire agencies, utilities and landowners in the United States and Australia.

name: Panthera
summary: Conservation organisation founded in 2006 that works on the world's 40 wild cat species. It built PantheraIDS, which automatically identifies species in camera trap data, and is a core member of the SMART Partnership.

name: PantheraIDS
summary: Panthera's data system for camera trap, telemetry and observation data, which identifies species, animal counts and behaviour automatically.

name: Partenariat Régional pour la Conservation de la zone côtière et Marine en Afrique de l'Ouest
summary: Regional coalition for the conservation of coastal and marine areas in West Africa, with the Géo-PRCM online information portal for the sub-region.

name: Partnership for Observation of the Global Ocean
summary: UK-registered charity founded in 1999 by directors of oceanographic institutions as a forum to promote and advance observation of the global ocean.

name: Patrick J. McGovern Foundation
summary: Philanthropy that funds AI and data work for social impact. Its grants include AI and data projects in conservation, biodiversity monitoring and ocean governance.

name: Paul M. Angell Family Foundation
summary: Family foundation that in 2023 began a five-year partnership with Global Fishing Watch to support its international policy programme.

name: PCP WISE
summary: Horizon Europe pre-commercial procurement, January 2025 to December 2027, for water management solutions using artificial intelligence, satellite observation and early warning systems.

name: Peace Parks Foundation
summary: Southern African foundation that co-manages protected areas and transfrontier landscapes. It integrates sensors, satellite technology and LoRaWAN into EarthRanger in Mozambique.

name: Peace Parks TFCA GIS Database
summary: GIS database of protected area and transfrontier conservation area boundaries in southern Africa, maintained by Peace Parks Foundation and listed on the TFCA Portal.

name: Pelagic Data Systems
summary: Sells vessel tracking hardware and data analytics to fisheries, governments and fishers.

name: Pelagic Size Structure Database
summary: Database of plankton size structure, part of the COPEPOD Project.

name: Pensoft Publishers
summary: Academic publisher founded in Bulgaria in 1992, known for open access biodiversity journals including the Biodiversity Data Journal. It works with Plazi on semantically enhanced publishing.

name: Perch
summary: Open bioacoustics model from Google that identifies species from audio; version 2.0 covers birds, mammals, amphibians and sound from coral reefs and can be adapted to new species and habitats.

name: Permanent Inter-State Committee for Drought Control in the Sahel
summary: Intergovernmental body of thirteen West African and Sahel states. Its AGRHYMET centre in Niamey gives information, training and research services and is linked to SERVIR West Africa.

name: Perona Lab
summary: Caltech laboratory on the computational foundations of vision, whose machine vision systems have applications that include conservation.

name: Pettersson Elektronik
summary: Swedish maker of bat detectors and sound analysis software, including Batsound.

name: PICES/ICES Joint Working Group: Best Practices for Using Deep Learning in Processing Plankton Images
summary: Joint PICES and ICES working group on best practices for deep learning in plankton image processing, set up because a lack of guidelines has caused problems with model generalisability, dataset bias and reproducibility.

name: Picterra
summary: Sells geospatial AI analytics, used by its customers for deforestation risk assessment and for checking land practices.

name: Pinpoint Earth
summary: New Zealand company in Nelson building seafood traceability and vessel monitoring hardware with AI analytics software for the fishing industry.

name: PiVa AI
summary: Computer vision and machine learning research and development organisation led by Lukas Picek, with work on 783-species snake recognition for Geneva's Institute of Global Health and Varroa mite detection.

name: Pivotal
summary: UK company selling primary biodiversity and ecosystem condition data to companies, processed on what it calls an AI-powered platform.

name: Pixxel
summary: Builds hyperspectral imaging satellites and sells the data, with offices in India and California.

name: Pl@ntNet
summary: Citizen science project and app that identifies plants from pictures, governed by a consortium of four French research bodies, and the source of the Pl@ntNet-300K and GeoPlant data.

name: Planet Forest Carbon
summary: Global dataset of aboveground forest carbon, tree height and canopy cover estimates sold by Planet Labs.

name: Planet Labs
summary: Operates Earth observation satellites and sells daily imagery, derived data and analytic feeds, including forest carbon estimates, to governments and companies.

name: Planetary Knowledge Base
summary: Graph of life built by the Natural History Museum, London from collections and literature, intended for global research use. AWS described it as a prototype in 2024.

name: Plankifier
summary: Eawag project on deep learning classification of plankton images, whose models were also compared on ZooScan, Imaging FlowCytobot and ISIIS data.

name: Planktonzilla
summary: Multimodal data set and models for understanding plankton ecosystems.

name: Plant and Fungal Trees of Life
summary: Project at the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, sequencing plant and fungal genera to build their tree of life, with an open data approach.

name: Plants of the World Online
summary: Online taxonomic database of seed-bearing plants published by the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.

name: PlantSearch
summary: Botanic Gardens Conservation International database of plant taxa held in botanic gardens and similar organisations.

name: Plataforma Regional de Monitoreo y Evaluación de la Biodiversidad en Centroamérica
summary: Finished regional project funded by the Inter-American Development Bank to build a system for monitoring and evaluating biodiversity in Central America.

name: Plazi
summary: Not-for-profit organisation in Bern that maintains a repository of digital taxonomic literature and makes taxonomic treatments openly accessible.

name: PlutoF
summary: Online platform for managing biosystematics and ecology data, from fieldwork to molecular records, and the base for public outputs including UNITE and the Estonian biodiversity portal.

name: Polytrack 2.0
summary: Tracks several insect pollinator species and their pollination behaviour in video using YOLOv4 and a background subtractor, and its owner archived the repository on 14 January 2025.

name: Pontificia Universidad Javeriana Cali
summary: Colombian university with authors on AnuraSet, a neotropical anuran call dataset for machine learning.

name: Presto
summary: Lightweight model pre-trained on remote sensing pixel time series, usable for transfer learning or as a feature extractor.

name: Priceless Planet Coalition
summary: Initiative founded by Mastercard to restore 100 million trees, guided by Conservation International and World Resources Institute. TerraMatch is its monitoring platform and its monitoring framework includes remote sensing.

name: Primate Genome Project
summary: Project to generate reference genomes for all extant primate species, affiliated to the Earth BioGenome Project.

name: Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation
summary: Non-profit founded by Prince Albert II of Monaco in 2006 that gives grants on planetary health. It supported the Marine Biological Laboratory's SeaBase project to improve knowledge of marine biodiversity.

name: Prithvi
summary: Open-source geospatial foundation model from NASA, IBM Research and the Jülich Supercomputing Centre, trained on Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 data and used for tasks including flood, fire and biomass mapping.

name: PROBLUE
summary: Multi-donor trust fund administered by the World Bank for sustainable development of marine and coastal resources.

name: Project Centinela
summary: Planet's data grants programme for biodiversity, launched in late 2024, giving scientists, conservationists and stewards at 50 vulnerable sites three-year subscriptions to satellite imagery and analytics.

name: Project CETI
summary: Nonprofit that uses machine learning, robotics and underwater acoustics to understand and translate sperm whale communication, with its field station in Dominica.

name: Project CORaiL
summary: AI-powered system for monitoring coral reef resilience, built by Accenture, Intel and the Sulubaaï Environmental Foundation and deployed in 2019 at Pangatalan Island in the Philippines. Current status not checked.

name: Project Guacamaya
summary: Joint project in the Colombian Amazon that uses AI on satellite imagery, camera trap images and bioacoustics to monitor deforestation and biodiversity.

name: Project Psyche
summary: Multinational project to sequence the genomes of all 11,000 species of moths and butterflies in Europe, affiliated to the Earth BioGenome Project.

name: Prométhée Earth Intelligence
summary: French Earth observation company founded in 2020, which signed a memorandum with Senegal's space agency in January 2024 on a constellation of 5 to 8 satellites for Senegal.

name: Protected Planet
summary: Global source of data on protected areas and other effective area-based conservation measures, used for monitoring Target 3 of the Global Biodiversity Framework.

name: ProtectedSeas
summary: Marine conservation organisation associated with the Anthropocene Institute. It publishes the Navigator map of marine protected and managed areas.

name: ProtectedSeas Navigator
summary: Free interactive map of over 21,000 marine protected and managed areas across 220 countries and territories, with their regulations.

name: Protist 10,000 Genomes Project
summary: International genome sequencing initiative on protists, launched in December 2019 by scientists led by the Institute of Hydrobiology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, with a public data portal.

name: Protist Ribosomal Reference database
summary: Set of interconnected 18S rRNA reference databases for metabarcoding, focused on protists, started in the Plankton Group of the Station Biologique of Roscoff.

name: Pulitzer Center
summary: Organisation that sponsors independent reporting on international issues and runs the Rainforest Investigations Network.

name: Purdue University
summary: Public research university in Indiana, home of the FACAI forest AI laboratory.

name: PyTorch-Wildlife
summary: Deep learning framework and model zoo for conservation from the Microsoft AI for Good Lab. It is no longer maintained; its inference work continues in SPARROW-Engine.

name: Quadrature Climate Foundation
summary: UK charitable foundation that funds the Climate Change AI Innovation Grants and is a listed past funder of MapBiomas. Its site now uses the name Quadrature Charitable Foundation.

name: QUT Ecoacoustics Research Group
summary: Queensland University of Technology group led by Paul Roe that works on ecoacoustics, including recognisers for rare, endangered or invasive species.

name: RADD Forest Disturbance Alert
summary: Alerts that use Sentinel-1 radar imagery to map new disturbances in primary humid tropical forest at 10 m scale in near real time.

name: Radiant Earth
summary: Technology non-profit that runs Source Cooperative for data publishing and the Cloud-Native Geospatial Forum.

name: RAINFOR
summary: Network of long-term forest plots across Amazonia, with data managed through ForestPlots.net.

name: Rainforest Alert
summary: Approach in which Indigenous communities use satellite images and smartphones to detect and act on deforestation. A peer-reviewed study of communities in the Peruvian Amazon reported a 52% reduction in forest loss in the first year.

name: Rainforest Alliance
summary: Certification and sustainability organisation that has published a position on AI, which says AI could lower the cost of verification and bring better evidence to more farmers.

name: Rainforest Connection
summary: Organisation that uses sound and AI to protect rainforests and monitor wildlife, with acoustic devices that detect threats such as illegal logging, and the Arbimon analysis platform.

name: Rainforest Foundation US
summary: US non-profit that works with Indigenous peoples in rainforests. Its Rainforest Alert approach gives communities satellite images and smartphones to detect deforestation.

name: Rainforest Investigations Network
summary: Pulitzer Center initiative that funds journalists for a year to investigate deforestation in the three main tropical rainforest regions, with data and geospatial support. Its reporters have used AI on satellite imagery.

name: Rainforest Trust
summary: Conservation organisation that creates rainforest reserves with partners and tracks threats to them with satellite imagery and custom software. A member of the Key Biodiversity Areas Partnership.

name: Ramboll
summary: Consultancy whose Galago team built a prototype for National Highways that maps landcover and habitats from satellite imagery with machine learning.

name: Ramsar Convention Secretariat
summary: Secretariat of the Convention on Wetlands, based at IUCN in Gland.

name: RanMarine Technology
summary: Rotterdam maker of autonomous robots that clean harbours and waterways and treat blue-green algae, with data services.

name: Rare
summary: Environmental non-profit founded in 1973 that designs community conservation programmes. It publishes a guide to its AI work, which includes turning coastal sensor data into WhatsApp voice alerts for fishers and oyster farmers on the Amazon coast.

name: RAS AI Foundation
summary: Los Angeles grantee of the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation, funded to develop the Living Nature Machine, described as a publicly available generative AI tool for nature data.

name: Re:wild
summary: Conservation organisation and member of the SMART Partnership. It has published work on using machine learning to prioritise IUCN Red List reassessments.

name: Reconyx
summary: Makes camera traps for wildlife biologists, ecologists and field researchers.

name: Red Amazónica de Información Socioambiental Georreferenciada
summary: Consortium of civil society organisations from Amazonian countries that produces and shares geospatial data on the Amazon, including the MapBiomas Amazonía and MapBiomas Agua layers.

name: Red de Bosques Andinos
summary: Long-term monitoring platform of permanent forest plots along the Andes, with demographic data on tree communities and species.

name: Redbioma
summary: Mesoamerican network applying data science to biodiversity conservation, with a focus on building capacity and on women in the region. It runs courses including machine learning applied to biodiversity.

name: Reef Check Foundation
summary: International non-profit that trains volunteer divers to survey coral reefs and kelp forests, with more than 17,000 reef surveys in 102 countries and territories since 1997.

name: Reef Life Survey
summary: Non-profit citizen science programme in which trained divers make standardised visual surveys of reef biodiversity on rocky and coral reefs worldwide.

name: ReefCloud
summary: Digital tool that uses machine learning to extract and share data from images of coral reefs, with coral cover analysis the Australian Institute of Marine Science puts at 80 to 90 percent accuracy.

name: ReefNet
summary: Public coral reef image dataset and benchmark with point labels mapped to the World Register of Marine Species, built from 76 CoralNet sources and a site in the Red Sea.

name: Refik Anadol Studio
summary: Los Angeles media art studio, established in 2014, that built the Large Nature Model and leads DATALAND.

name: refinq
summary: Vienna company selling asset-level climate and nature risk analytics, built on external geodata and models.

name: Reforest'Action
summary: French company that runs forest restoration projects and says it monitors their impact from the field to the satellite.

name: Regional Center for Remote Sensing of North African States
summary: Regional body that encourages member-state institutions to use remote sensing for sustainable development and scientific research. It is a member of the Sahara and Sahel Observatory.

name: Regional Centre for Mapping of Resources for Development
summary: Inter-governmental organisation in Nairobi, established in 1975, that generates and applies geo-information services for its member states.

name: Regional Organization for the Conservation of the Environment of the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
summary: Intergovernmental organisation of seven states, hosted by Saudi Arabia in Jeddah, that coordinates conservation of the marine environment of the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.

name: Regional Organization for the Protection of the Marine Environment
summary: Organisation established in 1979 to implement the Kuwait Action Plan, with a Remote Sensing Unit that monitors its sea area from satellites.

name: Regional Resource Hub for Eastern and Southern Africa
summary: BIOPAMA-established regional observatory for data and reporting on biodiversity and protected areas in Eastern and Southern Africa, hosted by RCMRD.

name: Registry of Open Data on AWS
summary: Catalogue that helps people find and share datasets available through AWS, including collections from NOAA, NASA, Digital Earth Africa and the Amazon Sustainability Data Initiative. Most datasets are provided by third parties.

name: Remote Sensing Centre for Earth System Research
summary: Leipzig centre set up by Leipzig University and the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research, using remote sensing and machine learning on vegetation and Earth system questions.

name: Remote Sensing Foundations
summary: Google's vision transformer backbone for remote sensing, pre-trained on more than 300 million satellite images and part of Google Earth AI.

name: Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
summary: US university in Troy, New York, where Charles Stewart, a co-investigator on Wildbook, works.

name: rePLANET
summary: Develops biodiversity restoration projects, measured with the Wallacea Trust methodology, with projects across seven countries.

name: RESOLVE
summary: Non-profit working on conflict resolution and on people and planet solutions since 1977. It develops the TrailGuard AI camera alert system and works on the Global Safety Net and Ecoregions of the World.

name: Restor
summary: Non-profit platform for nature sites, spun off from the Crowther Lab, which connects restoration and conservation sites, users and organisations.

name: Restoration Barometer
summary: Developed by IUCN and launched in 2016 as the Bonn Challenge Barometer, it tracks restoration targets, with IUCN reporting use by 22 countries and endorsement by over 50.

name: Restore Blue
summary: Irish company supplying real-time biodiversity data and tools to design and monitor nature-inclusive design for offshore wind projects.

name: REV Ocean
summary: Operates a privately owned research and exploration vessel. Data from its missions goes into open systems through HUB Ocean.

name: Rewilding Europe
summary: European rewilding organisation that supports rewilding through its European Wildlife Comeback Fund and took part in the AI for European Wildlife Challenge.

name: Rezatec
summary: ForestSource describes it as a geospatial analytics platform combining satellite imagery and AI to monitor forest health.

name: Richard Lounsbery Foundation
summary: US foundation that supports science and French-American cooperation. POGO says its grants helped establish the Ocean Biomolecular Observing Network, and Kindora lists a 2026 grant for a Lower Hudson River eDNA partnership.

name: Rights and Resources Initiative
summary: Coalition on the land rights of Indigenous Peoples, Afro-descendant Peoples and local communities. It publishes tenure data through the RRI Tenure Tool.

name: Robin Radar Systems
summary: Makes bird and drone detection radar systems.

name: Robotics Cats
summary: Hong Kong company with AI software that detects wildfires early and counts bird populations, according to Silverstrand Capital.

name: Robotto
summary: Danish perception software company for drones and other autonomous systems, listing nature preservation among its markets.

name: Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors
summary: New York philanthropy adviser recorded as giving Global Fishing Watch $4.6 million from 2020 to 2024 and Conservation X Labs $1 million in 2021.

name: Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil
summary: Sets environmental and social standards for certified palm oil, monitors fire hotspots by satellite and publishes members' concession maps through GeoRSPO.

name: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew
summary: UK non-departmental public body and botanical research institution that collaborates on the International Plant Names Index.

name: RTsys
summary: French maker of underwater acoustic and robotic equipment, whose site names marine mammal detection among its uses.

name: Rumah Foundation
summary: Philanthropic arm of a Singapore-based family office, which co-chairs the 30x30 Southeast Asia Ocean Fund and gave pilot funding to Fin Finder, an AI tool for identifying shark and ray fins.

name: Sahara and Sahel Observatory
summary: Regional organisation that hosts AfrikENCA, a geospatial platform on African ecosystem accounts, and took part in CBD COP17.

name: Saildrone
summary: Builds and operates uncrewed surface vehicles that collect ocean mapping and maritime data, sold for defence as well as for seabed survey and environmental observation.

name: Salesforce
summary: Software company that funds nature-based work through its Accelerator for Nature and related grants, including remote sensing and acoustic monitoring projects.

name: Salesforce Accelerator for Nature
summary: Salesforce grant programme announced at COP27 that gave $1 million to four nonprofits to test nature-based solutions; recipients included Rainforest Connection, Island Conservation and GreenWave. Current status not checked.

name: Sall Family Foundation
summary: Foundation listed as a funder of Global Fishing Watch.

name: Samsung
summary: Electronics company that created the Wildlife Watch anti-poaching livestream pilot with Africam.

name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance
summary: Conservation organisation that developed Twiga Walinzi, a community-led giraffe programme in Kenya, per the Giraffe Conservation Foundation.

name: SarVision
summary: Private company founded by Wageningen University researchers that builds automated satellite monitoring systems for forests and natural resources.

name: SatBird
summary: Bird species distribution data set that pairs remote sensing with citizen science data from eBird.

name: SatCLIP
summary: Global, general-purpose geographic location encoder from Microsoft that trains location and image encoders by matching satellite images to their locations.

name: Satelligence
summary: Sells satellite-based deforestation monitoring and supply chain traceability for companies preparing for the EU Deforestation Regulation.

name: Satellite Embedding dataset
summary: Annual embeddings produced by AlphaEarth Foundations and published in Google Earth Engine, at 10 metres per pixel.

name: Satellites for Biodiversity Award
summary: Award from the Connected Conservation Foundation and the Airbus Foundation that gives conservation projects satellite imagery, Earth observation tools and technical support. Its fourth round, in 2026, selected six projects.

name: Satellites on Fire
summary: Argentine company whose software applies AI models to satellite imagery to detect wildfires; The Next Web reports it monitors territory in 21 countries.

name: Satellogic
summary: Earth observation satellite operator selling imagery, with an environment line it says supports conservation and deforestation tracking, alongside defence and energy customers.

name: Satlas
summary: Ai2's open AI-generated geospatial data computed from Sentinel-2 imagery, updated monthly, with foundation models pre-trained on the SatlasPretrain dataset.

name: Satlink
summary: Spanish maker of sustainable fishing devices and supplier of oceanographic information, on the NOAA list of electronic monitoring providers through Satlink US.

name: SatSure
summary: Sells satellite-based intelligence for agriculture and a forest product covering forest health, deforestation and carbon markets.

name: Savannah Tracking
summary: Kenyan company that makes animal tracking collars, including models for Asian, African savannah and forest elephants.

name: Save Our Seas Foundation
summary: Geneva-based foundation that has supported over 300 research, conservation and education projects worldwide since 2003. OpenAlex records it as a funder on published environmental DNA monitoring research.

name: Save the Elephants
summary: Research and conservation organisation founded in 1993 that has worked with Wild Me on training computers to identify individual elephants.

name: Savimbo
summary: United States social enterprise made by and for Indigenous Peoples and local communities, selling Indigenous-led biodiversity and climate credits.

name: SCAR Antarctic Biodiversity Portal
summary: Portal for Antarctic biodiversity records, which began as SCAR-MarBIN. Its home page counts occurrences in the SCAR and OBIS networks and lists tools and identification keys.

name: Schmidt Marine Technology Partners
summary: Schmidt Family Foundation grant programme that funds new ocean technology for sustainable fisheries, ocean monitoring and habitat health. Its $3.5 million sustainable fisheries round went to ten organisations and universities in seven countries.

name: Schmidt Ocean Institute
summary: Set up by Eric and Wendy Schmidt in 2009 as a seagoing research facility operator. It supports oceanographic research and technology development and states a commitment to open sharing of information.

name: Schmidt Sciences
summary: Non-profit founded in 2024 by Eric and Wendy Schmidt to fund science and technology. It runs the Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Scholars initiative.

name: Science Based Targets Network
summary: Civil-society and science-led initiative that sets methods for companies and cities to define science-based targets for nature, and publishes a Natural Lands Map for that target-setting. No AI work was found on its site.

name: Scientific and Technical Advisory Panel of the Global Environment Facility
summary: Seven-member panel giving independent advice to the GEF, which has published an information note on AI across GEF focal areas.

name: Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research
summary: Interdisciplinary body of the International Science Council that coordinates international research in Antarctica, with its Secretariat at the Scott Polar Research Institute in Cambridge. It runs the SCAR Antarctic Biodiversity Portal.

name: Scientific Committee on Oceanic Research
summary: International non-governmental non-profit that convenes interdisciplinary ocean science, and hosts the International Quiet Ocean Experiment pages.

name: scikit-maad
summary: Python package for quantitative analysis of environmental audio recordings, described in its published paper as a toolbox for quantitative soundscape analysis.

name: Scout
summary: Open hardware and open source software from Wild Me for reviewing aerial survey imagery of wildlife, with machine learning alongside human reviewers.

name: Scribe Labs
summary: Small technology company that runs BirdWeather, a library of bird vocalisations, and makes the BirdWeather PUC bioacoustics device.

name: Scripps Institution of Oceanography
summary: School of oceanography and earth science at the University of California, San Diego, whose researchers use machine learning on underwater acoustic data.

name: Scripps Machine Listening Lab
summary: Lab in the Marine Physical Laboratory at Scripps working between oceanography and machine learning on large underwater acoustic datasets.

name: Sea Around Us
summary: UBC-based platform giving reported and unreported fish catches for every country in the world.

name: Sea-Bird Scientific
summary: Maker of CTDs and other sensors for ocean and freshwater measurement used in environmental research.

name: Seabird Tracking Database
summary: BirdLife International's central store of seabird tracking data from around the world, used for seabird conservation work.

name: SeaDataNet
summary: Distributed European infrastructure for marine data, connecting more than 110 national oceanographic and marine data centres from 35 countries.

name: SeadragonSearch
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that uses AI to identify leafy, weedy and ruby seadragons from photographs.

name: Seal Wildbook
