summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that applies AI across several seal species.

name: SeaLifeBase
summary: Global online database on the taxonomy, distribution and ecology of marine species other than finfish.

name: Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity
summary: Secretariat of the UN biodiversity convention, a partner in the UN Biodiversity Lab, whose staff write guidance on the mechanism for sharing benefits from digital sequence information.

name: Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme
summary: Pacific regional environment organisation that launched the Pacific Biodiversity Information Facility.

name: Seiche
summary: British specialist in underwater noise and marine mammal monitoring for offshore marine industries, which also trains marine mammal observers.

name: Semantic AI
summary: San Diego software firm whose graph analytics are used in conservation to map poaching syndicates, with an EarthRanger integration.

name: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research
summary: German biodiversity research society based in Frankfurt; its Jena plant institute applies AI and deep learning to a digitised herbarium, and it is an Ocean Census partner.

name: SenseNet
summary: Canadian company that sells early wildfire detection using sensors, cameras, satellite imagery, weather data and AI, including for forests.

name: Sensing Clues
summary: Dutch non-profit foundation that provides data collection tools and AI-driven analysis for wildlife rangers and area managers.

name: SensorGnome
summary: Automated radio receiver, powered by a Raspberry Pi, that detects and records signals from wildlife tracking tags without anyone present. Its logo is under Major supporters on the Motus site.

name: Sentinel
summary: Conservation X Labs field monitoring product combining a device, AI models and a dashboard, used in eight countries.

name: Sentinel Hub
summary: Cloud service from Sinergise that makes Sentinel, Landsat and other satellite data available to browse and analyse.

name: Sentinel-2 10-Meter Land Use/Land Cover Time Series
summary: Global annual land use and land cover map at 10 metres from Sentinel-2 imagery, produced by Impact Observatory, Microsoft and Esri with a deep learning model trained on human-labelled pixels.

name: SEPAL
summary: Open Foris cloud platform for accessing and processing Earth observation data for forest and land monitoring, connected to Google Earth Engine.

name: SEPPI
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project building a European protocol for monitoring plant-pollinator interactions with time-lapse cameras and deep learning.

name: Sequench
summary: Laboratory in Nelson, New Zealand, that does molecular analysis of environmental samples, including eDNA and eRNA metabarcoding, with a sister site for Sequench Lithuania.

name: Sequoia Climate Foundation
summary: Foundation listed as a funder of the MapBiomas Project in 2023 and 2024.

name: SERVIR
summary: Network of regional hubs that builds Earth observation services with regional institutions. It began as a NASA and USAID partnership and now continues as the SERVIR Global Collaborative, led by independent regional hubs.

name: Sextant Technology
summary: New Zealand company making tracking devices used to study endangered species, listed by Argos for bird, land and marine animal transmitters.

name: SGAT
summary: Software for estimating broad-scale animal movements from archival or satellite tag data, described as solar and satellite geolocation for animal tracking.

name: Shan Shui Conservation Center
summary: Chinese NGO founded in 2007 that works on endangered species such as the snow leopard and giant panda. It took part in a Tencent workshop on the Eye of the Species model.

name: Sharkbook
summary: Wild Me platform that applies AI to photographs of sharks; it uses the skin pattern behind the gills to identify individuals.

name: Shippy
summary: Skylight's AI agent for maritime analysts, which answers plain-language questions about vessels and ocean activity from live vessel-tracking and satellite data and cites its sources. Skylight is Ai2's ocean-monitoring service; Shippy is in early release to vetted users.

name: Silent Cities Dataset
summary: Ecoacoustic dataset of close to 5 terabytes, with a public repository of code that downloads and prepares it, calculates acoustic indices every 10 seconds and tags audio with a pretrained deep learning model.

name: Silicon Valley Community Foundation
summary: Community foundation recorded as giving Earth Species Project $695,169 from 2021 to 2024.

name: SILVA
summary: Quality-checked and regularly updated data sets of aligned ribosomal RNA sequences for all three domains of life, used for taxonomic assignment in environmental DNA work.

name: SilvaCarbon
summary: Interagency technical cooperation programme of the US Government that helps countries measure, monitor and report carbon in forests and other lands. CEOS names USGS among the agencies involved.

name: Silverstrand Capital
summary: Singapore family office that runs the Biodiversity Accelerator+, giving capital, in-kind services and coaching to biodiversity companies. Its 2023 cohort covered biodiversity data collection and analytics, including Arbimon.

name: SimplexDNA
summary: Sells DNA-based biodiversity detection, including water-based environmental DNA services for fish and quagga mussels.

name: Sinay
summary: French maritime data company that monitors ocean and wildlife with cameras, buoys and sensors, with AI video analysis of catch and bycatch.

name: Sinergise
summary: Makes Sentinel Hub, a service that makes Sentinel, Landsat and other satellite data available to browse and analyse.

name: Single.Earth
summary: Estonian company issuing the MERIT nature token; Tech.eu reported that it uses satellite imagery, big data and machine learning to value land such as forests and wetlands.

name: Sinsoma
summary: Austrian spin-off of the University of Innsbruck offering DNA analysis for the environment and food sectors, including environmental DNA, active across Europe.

name: Skoll Foundation
summary: Foundation listed as a funder of the MapBiomas Project since 2021.

name: Skylight
summary: Ai2's maritime monitoring service that uses AI to flag illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing; it is free to government, regional and non-governmental organisations.

name: SkyTruth
summary: Conservation technology non-profit founded in 2001 that uses satellite imagery and AI to expose environmental threats. Its tools include Cerulean and a 30x30 tracker.

name: Smart Parks
summary: Non-profit that develops technology for wildlife protection and park management, including OpenCollar tracking hardware and AddaxAI Connect camera alert systems.

name: SMART Partnership
summary: Partnership of conservation organisations formed in 2011 that develops and supports SMART, software for managing protected and conserved areas. Since 2025 it has worked with EarthRanger through the SMART-EarthRanger Conservation Alliance.

name: SMART Subsea Cables
summary: Initiative to equip transoceanic telecommunications cables with sensors for persistent deep ocean observation, led by a Joint Task Force of ITU, WMO and the IOC.

name: SMART-EarthRanger Conservation Alliance
summary: Alliance announced in October 2025 that brings the SMART and EarthRanger protected area management systems together in one integrated system with training and monitoring standards.

name: Smartfin
summary: Surfboard fin that collects coastal ecosystem data while surfing or paddleboarding, aiming to fill a nearshore data gap and tested with over 100 surfers in San Diego.

name: Smith-Root
summary: United States maker of fisheries equipment, including an eDNA sampler, an autosampler and a citizen scientist sampler.

name: Smithsonian Conservation Biology Institute
summary: Smithsonian unit near Front Royal, Virginia, a named partner in Wildlife Insights.

name: Smithsonian Institution
summary: Group of US museums and research centres created by the federal government, a Phase I grantee of the Bezos Earth Fund AI Grand Challenge.

name: Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute
summary: Smithsonian institute headquartered in Panama City, with research across the tropics and links to the ForestGEO forest monitoring network.

name: SMRU Instrumentation Group
summary: Group within the Sea Mammal Research Unit that designs and produces electronic tags relaying the tracks and behaviour of seals, sharks and turtles.

name: Snail Wildbook
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that uses AI to identify individual snails from photographs.

name: Snapshot Safari
summary: Network whose members use the same camera trapping protocols to collect standardised data from protected areas in Africa, with Snapshot Serengeti as its flagship project.

name: Snapshot Serengeti
summary: Camera trap data set of about 7.1 million images from Serengeti National Park, the flagship project of the Snapshot Safari network, labelled by Zooniverse volunteers.

name: Snow Leopard Trust
summary: Organisation working on snow leopard conservation in Central Asia. It developed an AI system for camera trap images with Microsoft.

name: Sociedad Latinoamericana de Especialistas en Percepción Remota y Sistemas de Información Espacial
summary: Latin American society of remote sensing and spatial information specialists, a regional member of ISPRS, whose symposium has been held across the region.

name: Society for Conservation Biology
summary: Non-profit professional society for the scientific study and conservation of biological diversity. It hosts a Conservation Technology Working Group.

name: Society for Conservation GIS
summary: Non-profit incorporated in 1997 that describes itself as a global community using geospatial technology for conservation, with its 30th conference scheduled for July 2027.

name: Society for the Protection of Underground Networks
summary: Scientific research organisation founded to map mycorrhizal fungal communities and advocate for their protection, publisher of the Underground Atlas.

name: Soil Biodiversity Observation Network
summary: Thematic network of GEO BON working with the Global Soil Biodiversity Initiative to make soil biological and ecosystem observations available.

name: SoilGrids
summary: ISRIC system for global digital soil mapping that uses machine learning to map the spatial distribution of soil properties.

name: soloEO
summary: Small Earth observation consultancy founded in 2009 by Ake Rosenqvist, with offices in Stockholm and Tokyo. It co-leads Global Mangrove Watch with JAXA and Aberystwyth University.

name: Sonotronics
summary: United States maker of ultrasonic transmitters, receivers and hydrophones for tracking animals underwater, founded in 1971.

name: Sony Computer Science Laboratories
summary: Sony research laboratory where Masatoshi Funabashi works on Synecoculture and Augmented Ecosystems, including ecosystem sensing AI.

name: Soundclim
summary: Set of scripts and modules that use machine learning to search field audio recordings for soundmarks.

name: Source Cooperative
summary: Data publishing service that lets organisations and individuals publish geospatial and other data at any scale without running their own infrastructure.

name: South Pacific Regional Fisheries Management Organisation
summary: Inter-governmental organisation for the conservation and sustainable use of South Pacific fishery resources, based in Wellington, which lists public domain data.

name: South Pacific Regional Herbarium
summary: Herbarium established in 1993 as the Fiji Herbarium, now maintained by the University of the South Pacific, whose records are published through GBIF.

name: Southern African Science Service Centre for Climate Change and Adaptive Land Management
summary: Joint initiative of southern African countries and Germany, with a secretariat in Windhoek, whose biodiversity observation network has 47 observatories.

name: Southern Ocean Observing System
summary: International initiative that coordinates the collection and delivery of Southern Ocean observations, with a portal for finding Southern Ocean data.

name: Space Intelligence
summary: Sells nature mapping from satellite data for carbon markets and deforestation-free supply chains.

name: Space Intelligence land cover mapping
summary: Space Intelligence's catalogue of land cover datasets for carbon projects and nature reporting, covering more than 50 countries.

name: Space4Good
summary: Dutch company using remote sensing, GIS and AI for environmental and social impact, with a product called FORESTER.

name: Space4Water Portal
summary: Portal that gives the space and water communities access to data and knowledge on using space technology for water management.

name: SPARROW
summary: Solar-powered edge device from the Microsoft AI for Good Lab that collects camera trap and acoustic data, runs wildlife AI models on site and sends results by low-Earth orbit satellite.

name: Spatial Implicit Neural Representations
summary: Models for global-scale species range estimation, trained with iNaturalist data, from a team that includes iNaturalist staff.

name: Spatial Informatics Group
summary: Geospatial analysis and environmental science firm working with agencies in California and elsewhere on wildfire, forest and agriculture management and ecosystem services.

name: SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog
summary: Community specification that gives a common way to describe and catalogue geospatial data so it can be indexed and found.

name: spcfy
summary: Leipzig company building DNA metabarcoding infrastructure that connects producers and users of biodiversity data.

name: Species 2000
summary: Global partnership that created the Catalogue of Life with the Integrated Taxonomic Information System in 2001.

name: Species Conservation Toolkit Initiative
summary: Partnership funded solely by donations and grants to develop tools for species risk assessment, conservation planning and population management, with tools including Vortex, PMx and Outbreak.

name: Species Threat Abatement and Restoration Metric
summary: Metric that measures the contribution investments can make to reducing species' extinction risk, based on IUCN Red List data and available through IBAT.

name: Species+
summary: Website developed by UNEP-WCMC and the CITES Secretariat that gives a central portal to information on species listed under CITES, CMS and the EU Wildlife Trade Regulations.

name: Species360
summary: International non-profit that brings together zoos, aquariums and wildlife organisations to share data on animals in human care, through the ZIMS record-keeping software.

name: SpeciesNet
summary: Open-source AI model from Google that classifies animal species in camera trap images, first used through Wildlife Insights and released openly in 2025.

name: Specify Collections Consortium
summary: Open source software community of collection institutions, founded in 2018, whose software manages data from biology and geology collections at institutions around the globe.

name: sPlot
summary: Repository of plant community data with more than 2.5 million vegetation plot records, run as a research platform of iDiv.

name: Spoor
summary: Oslo-based company selling AI bird monitoring from video for onshore and offshore wind farms.

name: Spotting Giant Sea Bass
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that uses AI to identify sea bass from photographs.

name: SPYGEN
summary: Provides species inventories for clients and partners using environmental DNA.

name: SSL4EO-S12
summary: Large multimodal, multitemporal data set of Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 patches from 251,079 locations, for self-supervised pre-training in Earth observation.

name: Stand.earth
summary: Environmental organisation with offices in Canada and the United States. It received a McGovern Foundation grant to enhance AI-driven tools for tracking deforestation and fossil fuel financing.

name: Stanford University
summary: Private research university in California whose domain hosts WILDS, a benchmark of distribution shifts in machine learning that includes wildlife monitoring.

name: Star-Oddi
summary: Icelandic maker of data loggers for laboratory, domestic and wildlife animals.

name: STAR.VISION Aerospace
summary: Satellite company that signed a memorandum with Kenya's Directorate of Resource Surveys and Remote Sensing on remote sensing for resource mapping and environmental monitoring.

name: Starling
summary: Satellite deforestation monitoring service for supply chains, developed by Airbus and Earthworm Foundation.

name: Stockel Family Foundation
summary: Family foundation in Santa Monica, California. Kindora lists a $50,000 grant to Rainforest Foundation US for forest monitoring in Brazil.

name: Stockholm Environment Institute
summary: International non-profit research institute headquartered in Stockholm; it co-founded Trase, which tracks deforestation and agricultural commodity trade, and offers the WetSAT-ML wetland monitoring tool.

name: Stockholm Resilience Centre
summary: Collaboration between Stockholm University and the Beijer Institute that published the synthesis report AI for a Planet Under Pressure on AI as a research method in sustainability science.

name: Stream Ocean
summary: Zurich start-up developing underwater cameras with AI analytics that give real-time biodiversity data and video to marine projects.

name: Superorganism
summary: Venture firm that says it is the first dedicated to biodiversity, backing pre-seed and seed startups including remote sensing, genomics and AI companies.

name: Surface Water and Ocean Topography mission
summary: Satellite mission for surface water and ocean measurement, run by NASA and the French space agency CNES.

name: SurfPerch
summary: AI system from Google for finding fish sounds and assessing reef activity in underwater audio, fine-tuned on data from the Calling in Our Corals listening project.

name: Sustainable Ocean Alliance
summary: San Francisco organisation funded by the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation to accelerate tech, AI and data science based ocean solutions.

name: Sustainable Wildlife Management Programme
summary: European Union-funded programme on the conservation and sustainable use of wildlife in forest, savannah and wetland ecosystems; camera trap survey data from its work in Gabon is cited in the DeepForestVision paper.

name: Svarmi
summary: Icelandic geospatial data company with drone data collection and nature reporting, including a digital twin of a magnolia cloud forest in Colombia.

name: Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency
summary: Sweden's development agency, headquartered in Sundbyberg. The Global Forest Watch about page shows it among founding partners.

name: Swift Geospatial
summary: Pretoria company that uses Sentinel-2 and Planet imagery and built forestry monitoring tools for East Africa with Gatsby Africa.

name: Sylvera
summary: Sells independent carbon credit ratings and biomass data for carbon projects, used by companies, investors, developers and governments.

name: Synature
summary: Sells smart microphones and a dashboard that detect species from sound and report acoustic indices.

name: Synecoculture
summary: Sony CSL research on farming dense, mixed plantings based on the self-organisation of ecosystems, with work on ecosystem sensing AI and robotics. It falls within the map as on-farm biodiversity.

name: Syrlinks
summary: French company with an Argos bird transmitter, the MRBA-25G, for wildlife tracking.

name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting
summary: Statistical standard that brings economic and environmental information into one framework. Its Ecosystem Accounting part, adopted by the UN Statistical Commission in 2021, organises data on habitats, ecosystem services and ecosystem assets.

name: TABMON
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project deploying autonomous acoustic sensors across Europe and using AI to turn soundscapes into biodiversity indicators, coordinated by NINA.

name: Tainá
summary: GainForest's Telegram assistant, co-designed with Indigenous and local communities around Manaus, which takes voice recordings, images and video from community members and stores species data and traditional knowledge. GainForest also built a sister language model, Poli.

name: Taking Root
summary: Vancouver organisation restoring forests with smallholder farmers, which built Farm-Trace, a system joining mobile field data, satellite imagery and machine learning to automate forest and carbon reporting.

name: Tank Watch
summary: Programme run by For the Fishes that helps people identify common saltwater aquarium fishes and their origin, and won a USAID Wildlife Crime Tech Challenge prize for its potential to reduce demand.

name: Tara Ocean Foundation
summary: French public interest foundation running scientific expeditions to study marine biodiversity, which says its work has produced the largest open-access database on the planktonic ecosystem.

name: Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures
summary: Market-led, science-based and government-backed initiative that gives organisations tools to act on nature-related issues. It has published recommendations on upgrading the nature data value chain and, with WWF, launched a nature data public facility.

name: TaxonWorks
summary: Web-based workbench for taxonomists and biodiversity scientists to capture, organise, share and publish their data.

name: Teamcore
summary: Harvard research group that advances AI and multiagent systems for social impact in topics that include conservation.

name: TECH4ALL
summary: Huawei's long-term digital inclusion initiative, whose environment work uses AI, cloud and audio monitoring for projects such as bird protection in the Yellow River Delta and wild Atlantic salmon protection.

name: Tech4Conservation
summary: Launched in 2020. It gives conservationists free AI tools through its ArgusWild AI platform, and runs the African Carnivore Wildbook.

name: Tech4Nature
summary: Partnership launched by Huawei and IUCN in 2020 to develop technology for protected and conserved areas. Phase 1 covered China, Mauritius, Mexico, Spain and Switzerland; Phase 2 runs six projects from 2023 to 2026.

name: Tech4Nature Mexico
summary: Tech4Nature project in Dzilam de Bravo State Reserve, Yucatán, that uses audio devices, camera traps and AI to recognise species and protect jaguars; Phase Two began in 2025.

name: Technische Universität Berlin
summary: Public research university in Berlin where the BigEarthNet satellite image benchmark for machine learning is run.

name: Technische Universität Ilmenau
summary: German public research university that leads the Flora Incognita plant identification project with the Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry.

name: Technosmart Europe
summary: Italian maker of miniature GPS devices, accelerometers and magnetometers for tracking birds, mammals and other wildlife.

name: Teledyne FLIR
summary: Thermal imaging maker in Wilsonville, Oregon, whose cameras are used against poaching in Kenya with WWF and to track black-footed ferrets.

name: TelePIX
summary: South Korean satellite company from payload development to AI analytics, working on global mangrove monitoring.

name: Telluray Foundation
summary: US foundation registered in Littleton, Colorado, and named as a supporter by Earth Species Project.

name: Telonics
summary: Makes electronics for wildlife and environmental research.

name: Temple University
summary: Public research university in Philadelphia, listed as an institution behind the TimeTree knowledge base of species divergence times.

name: Tencent
summary: Technology company that built the Eye of the Species camera trap model and a digital detection platform for snow leopards with WWF in Gansu Province.

name: Tencent and WWF snow leopard detection platform
summary: AI digital detection platform in Gansu Province, built by Tencent and WWF, that tracks snow leopards in Qilian Mountain National Park.

name: Terra-i
summary: Satellite forest loss monitor that trains a neural network on normal vegetation greenness patterns, described by CGIAR as open data used by scientists and governments in the tropics.

name: Terraformation
summary: Forest restoration company with a headquarters in Hawaiʻi. It says it develops country restoration platforms in tropical regions and offers Terraware, an open-source platform for managing native restoration.

name: TerraFund for AFR100
summary: Fund for locally led landscape restoration projects in Africa, tracked through the TerraMatch platform, which combines field data with satellite imagery using Land & Carbon Lab methods.

name: TerraMatch
summary: World Resources Institute platform that connects local land restoration groups to finance and tracks funded projects, combining field data with satellite analyses.

name: TerraMind
summary: Multimodal generative foundation model for Earth observation from IBM and ESA Φ-lab, pre-trained with the Jülich Supercomputing Centre and supported by the FAST-EO project.

name: Terramira
summary: Dutch company formed when NEO, eLEAF and 52impact joined forces, which says it combines remote sensing data and AI into products for water, nature and landscape, agriculture and infrastructure.

name: terraPulse
summary: Maps and monitors forests, crops, rangeland, water and wildlife habitat from satellite measurements and sells the results as data, a dashboard and an API.

name: Terrastories
summary: Free, open-source application for Indigenous and local communities to map and share place-based stories.

name: TerraTorch
summary: Python toolkit for fine-tuning geospatial foundation models, built on PyTorch Lightning and TorchGeo. The IBM/terratorch address now serves the torchgeo/terratorch repository.

name: Terrestrial Ecosystem Research Network
summary: Australian ecosystem observatory that measures terrestrial ecosystem attributes and openly provides model-ready environmental data and remote sensing products.

name: TESSERA
summary: Foundation model from the University of Cambridge that processes satellite time series and produces embeddings for uses such as habitat mapping, land classification and canopy height prediction.

name: The Alan Turing Institute
summary: UK national institute for data science and AI, which ran a biodiversity monitoring research programme with the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology, funded by the abrdn Charitable Foundation.

name: The Audacious Project
summary: Giving programme housed within TED that picks a group of projects each year and connects them with donors. It raised $60 million over five years for Global Fishing Watch to apply AI and satellite data to the ocean.

name: The Biodiversity Consultancy
summary: Cambridge consultancy that advises companies on biodiversity risk and has partnered with Okala on chimpanzee monitoring from camera trap data.

name: The Boring Fund
summary: WILDLABS fund, supported by Arm, for the overlooked foundations of conservation technology such as training materials, infrastructure upkeep and curating data. The 2025 round gave $80,000 in grants.

name: The Carl Victor Page Memorial Foundation
summary: California foundation recorded as giving Global Fishing Watch $6 million in 2023 and 2024.

name: The Chicago Community Trust
summary: Community foundation recorded as giving Global Fishing Watch $2 million and Earth Species Project $87,000 in 2025.

name: The Earthshot Prize
summary: Annual prize that awards £1 million to each of five winners across nature, air, oceans, waste and climate. NatureMetrics, which works in environmental DNA, won in the Protect & Restore Nature category in 2024.

name: The Eric and Wendy Schmidt Fund for Strategic Innovation
summary: Parent of Schmidt Sciences, recorded as giving Conservation X Labs $262,500 in 2023.

name: The Landbanking Group
summary: Munich company that sells Landler, nature data infrastructure combining remote sensing and field samples with AI models, for governments, financial institutions and land stewards.

name: The Leona M. and Harry B. Helmsley Charitable Trust
summary: Charitable trust that funds Digital Earth Africa alongside the Australian Government, which gives free Earth observation data and products to users across Africa.

name: The Marisla Foundation
summary: California foundation whose environment programme concentrates on marine and coastal biodiversity. It is a listed funder of Global Fishing Watch.

name: The Nature Conservancy
summary: Global environmental nonprofit working in 86 countries and territories. Its chief executive has described AI on fishing vessels, used through the Tuna Transparency Pledge, as a conservation tool.

name: The Nippon Foundation
summary: Japan-based grant maker founded in 1962. Its ocean work includes the Seabed 2030 seabed mapping project with GEBCO and the Ocean Census with Nekton Foundation.

name: The Nippon Foundation-GEBCO Seabed 2030 Project
summary: Project formed by The Nippon Foundation and GEBCO to produce a complete map of the seabed by 2030 and make it available to all, by gathering bathymetric data from governments, companies and other organisations.

name: The Nippon Foundation-Nekton Ocean Census
summary: Global initiative to discover unknown marine life, launched jointly by The Nippon Foundation and Nekton Foundation as an open network across science, media, academia and business.

name: The Ocean Cleanup
summary: Organisation that removes plastic from oceans and rivers. Its research team uses AI to map plastic density in remote ocean areas.

name: The Ocean Foundation
summary: Washington, DC foundation whose International Ocean Acidification Initiative developed the GOA-ON in a Box monitoring kit.

name: The Ohio State University
summary: Public research university in Columbus, Ohio, where authors of the BioCLIP species image model are based.

name: The Overbrook Foundation
summary: Foundation listed as a funder of the MapBiomas Project since 2024.

name: The Pew Charitable Trusts
summary: US public charity recorded as giving Global Fishing Watch $1.4 million from 2021 to 2024.

name: The Rockefeller University
summary: Biomedical research university in New York City that Google.org funds to rework genome sequencing pipelines with AI, in partnership with Google's genomics work for endangered species.

name: The Rufford Foundation
summary: UK registered charity that funds nature conservation projects, chiefly through the Rufford Small Grants Programme for individuals in developing countries. OpenAlex records it as a funder on published camera trap and bioacoustics research.

name: The Schmidt Family Foundation
summary: Foundation co-founded and led by Wendy Schmidt. It runs Schmidt Marine Technology Partners, which funds ocean technology.

name: The Tilia Fund
summary: Fund for carbon-free energy, energy efficiency and protecting forests and species. Global Nature Watch names it among its founding partners.

name: The Waterloo Foundation
summary: UK grant maker with environment programmes on marine and tropical rainforests. It is a listed funder of Global Fishing Watch.

name: The Wye Foundation
summary: Private foundation in Lighthouse Point, Florida, that sponsors the Fishial.AI fish identification project.

name: Thelma Biotel
summary: Norwegian maker of aquatic animal tracking transmitters, receivers and software.

name: ThreatSearch
summary: Botanic Gardens Conservation International database of known conservation assessments of plants.

name: Timelapse
summary: Software for turning camera trap images into data, with image recognition that can identify empty images and select recognised entities.

name: TimeTree
summary: Public knowledge base on the evolutionary timescale of life, assembled from thousands of published studies, at the Center of Biodiversity at Temple University.

name: TNC edge AI electronic monitoring
summary: Open-source system from The Nature Conservancy that puts AI directly on fishing vessels' electronic monitoring systems to verify longline tuna catch in near real time.

name: TorchGeo
summary: PyTorch library of datasets, samplers, transforms and pre-trained models for geospatial data. The repository at microsoft/torchgeo now redirects to the torchgeo organisation.

name: Tour du Valat
summary: Research institute at Le Sambuc, Arles, for the conservation of Mediterranean wetlands; it runs the Mediterranean Wetlands Observatory.

name: track2KBA
summary: R package that helps identify animal aggregations of potential conservation significance from individual tracking data by estimating and overlaying utilisation distributions to find important areas.

name: TRAFFIC
summary: Wildlife trade research organisation founded by IUCN and WWF, with about 150 experts worldwide. It co-convenes the Coalition to End Wildlife Trafficking Online.

name: TrailGuard AI
summary: Anti-poaching camera that identifies people and vehicles entering nature reserves and alerts rangers, developed by RESOLVE with Intel, the National Geographic Society and the Leonardo DiCaprio Foundation. Current status not checked.

name: trajVis
summary: Free, open source tool, built by Internet of Elephants, that visualises and animates animal GPS movement data and creates videos, with no accounts or downloads.

name: TRANSPONDER
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project on assessing European pondscapes, with sensors, eDNA, remote sensing and AI-aided identification of zooplankton and macroinvertebrates.

name: TRAPPER
summary: Open-source web application for managing camera-trap projects, with AI object detection and species classification.

name: TrapTagger
summary: Web application for processing camera-trap imagery with AI classification and manual annotation, maintained by WildEye Conservation and developed with the Wildlife Conservation Research Unit at Oxford.

name: Trase
summary: Not-for-profit initiative founded in 2015 by the Stockholm Environment Institute and Global Canopy that maps commodity supply chains linked to deforestation.

name: Tree Track
summary: Canadian company in Port Coquitlam with AI-driven aerial seeding, using patented seedpods and drones to reforest.

name: Treeconomy
summary: Builds forest models from satellite imagery and fieldwork that report biomass on every hectare.

name: Treefera
summary: London company that sells satellite and AI monitoring of the first mile of supply chains; TechCrunch reported in 2023 that it began with assessing forest carbon credits.

name: Treemetrics
summary: Sells ForestHQ, a forest management and monitoring platform that brings forestry data together.

name: TreeOfLife-10M
summary: Data set of 10 million biology images covering more than 450,000 species, combined from iNaturalist, BIOSCAN-1M and Encyclopedia of Life.

name: Treevia
summary: Brazilian forest management technology company offering forest inventory and fire risk and detection, which says it works in four countries and more than 16 Brazilian states.

name: Trends.Earth
summary: Tool for monitoring land change and preparing national reports to the UNCCD, produced by Conservation International, Lund University and NASA with support from the GEF.

name: Trillion Trees
summary: The self-described forest protection partnership of BirdLife International and WWF restores forests through its ReForest Fund and lists Makira Natural Park in Madagascar and Kaptagat in Kenya.

name: Trillium Technologies
summary: Company that runs the Frontier Development Lab and Earth Systems Lab, AI research labs. Its listed research includes tree species classification and forest height estimation from satellite radar.

name: Tropical Forest Forever Facility
summary: Forest finance facility with the World Bank as trustee and interim host. IAS Gyan reports that results are to be verified each year using satellite remote sensing data.

name: Tropical Managed Forests Observatory
summary: Pan-tropical network studying the long-term effects of logging on tropical forests, across more than 600 permanent forest plots.

name: Tropical Moist Forests
summary: European Commission Joint Research Centre dataset of forest cover change in tropical moist forests, from 43 years of Landsat time series at 30 m.

name: Tropicos
summary: Online botanical database of taxonomic, bibliographic and specimen data on plants, mainly from the Neotropics, from the Missouri Botanical Garden.

name: Troutspotter
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that uses AI to identify freshwater fish from photographs.

name: TRY Plant Trait Database
summary: Global plant trait database, publicly available under a CC-BY licence, reported by the Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry.

name: Trygg Mat Tracking
summary: Oslo non-profit that gives fisheries authorities and international organisations fisheries intelligence, analysis and training, and keeps a data repository on industrial fishing vessels called FACT.

name: Tryolabs
summary: AI and machine learning consulting firm registered in Montevideo, Uruguay, which shows on-vessel AI for sustainable fishing among its work.

name: TweetyNet
summary: Neural network using hybrid convolutional-recurrent layers to annotate birdsong and other vocalisations by segmenting and labelling spectrograms.

name: Twiga Tracker
summary: GPS satellite tracking study of giraffe led by the Giraffe Conservation Foundation, with over 750 tracking units deployed in 17 African countries.

name: U.S. Geological Survey
summary: United States agency that manages the Landsat programme jointly with NASA. Read through NASA and other pages because usgs.gov refuses this project.

name: U.S. National Science Foundation
summary: US federal research funder that funds the AI and Biodiversity Change Global Center and the Imageomics Institute.

name: UCL People and Nature Lab
summary: Lab based at UCL East that uses environmental DNA, sensors, satellite images and AI to monitor wildlife, including bioacoustics and wildlife disease surveillance.

name: UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology
summary: Independent UK research institute that builds the AMI automated insect camera system, deployed in over 30 countries.

name: UKCEH AMI system
summary: Open-source, non-lethal camera system for monitoring nocturnal insects; nearly 200 have been deployed in over 30 countries.

name: UN Biodiversity Lab
summary: Free, open-source spatial data platform from UNDP, UNEP, UNEP-WCMC and the CBD Secretariat, offering over 400 data layers on nature, climate and development and secure national workspaces.

name: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration
summary: UN programme running from 2021 to 2030, led by UNEP and FAO, to halt ecosystem degradation and restore ecosystems. Its monitoring runs through the Framework for Ecosystem Restoration Monitoring.

name: UN Environment Programme World Conservation Monitoring Centre
summary: UNEP's specialist biodiversity centre, which works with scientists and policymakers on biodiversity data and powers the UN Biodiversity Lab.

name: UN-REDD Programme
summary: Multi-donor programme of UNEP, UNDP and FAO established in 2008 that supports countries on reducing deforestation, with a 2026 to 2030 strategy.

name: UNCCD Data Dashboard
summary: Dashboard of national reporting figures on land degradation, first released in 2023 with data from 126 countries.

name: Underground Atlas
summary: Interactive map and downloadable data of mycorrhizal fungal diversity created by SPUN and colleagues.

name: UNEP-DHI Centre on Water and Environment
summary: Partnership between UNEP and DHI, based in Hørsholm, Denmark. It co-manages Global Lake Watch and maintains the Integrated Water Resources Management Data Portal.

name: UNITE
summary: Database for the eukaryotic nuclear ribosomal ITS region that clusters sequences to about species level and gives each species hypothesis a DOI, used in fungal DNA work.

name: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
summary: UN convention on land degradation whose secretariat in Bonn launched a data dashboard compiling national reports from 126 countries.

name: United Nations Development Programme
summary: UN development agency that is a founding partner of the UN Biodiversity Lab and runs programmes on nature and biodiversity finance.

name: United Nations Environment Programme
summary: UN environment agency whose digital transformation work includes the World Environment Situation Room data platform and environmental AI prototypes.

name: United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs
summary: UN office for outer space affairs, headquartered in Vienna. It runs the Space4Water portal.

name: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime
summary: UN office whose data portal publishes wildlife seizures data. It has a partnership with IUCN on crimes that affect the environment and is a member of the International Consortium on Combating Wildlife Crime.

name: United States Agency for International Development
summary: US foreign aid agency whose operations ceased on 1 July 2025, with remaining foreign assistance moved to the State Department. It ran the Wildlife Crime Tech Challenge.

name: Universidad de los Andes
summary: Private research university in Bogotá and a co-lead of Project Guacamaya, which applies AI to monitoring the Colombian Amazon.

name: University of Amsterdam
summary: Dutch university, a MAMBO participant and co-developer of the ARISE species identification infrastructure.

name: University of Bristol
summary: Public research university in Bristol, a core partner in the AI and Biodiversity Change Global Center, with work on computer vision and animal biometrics.

name: University of British Columbia
summary: Canadian university. Its researchers run Sea Around Us, a platform of reported and unreported fish catch for every country.

name: University of California San Diego
summary: Public university in La Jolla, California, where the CoralNet coral image analysis tool began in the computer science department.

name: University of California, Berkeley
summary: Public research university in California that leads AmphibiaWeb and has hosted the coordination of FLUXNET.

name: University of Cambridge
summary: Research university in Cambridge, England, where the Tessera Earth observation foundation model was developed.

name: University of Cambridge Conservation Research Institute
summary: University of Cambridge institute for interdisciplinary research and teaching on conservation problems, with research themes that include AI Earth observation.

name: University of Copenhagen
summary: Danish public research university whose geosciences and computer science researchers developed deep learning methods for mapping individual trees from satellite images.

name: University of Duisburg-Essen
summary: German university whose Aquatic Ecosystem Research group leads DNAquaIMG, a European project on DNA-based and automated image-based monitoring of freshwater invertebrates and diatoms.

name: University of Edinburgh
summary: Public research university in Edinburgh, a core partner in the AI and Biodiversity Change Global Center through Oisin Mac Aodha's machine learning group.

name: University of Florida
summary: University in Gainesville, Florida, home of the Weecology group, which is behind DeepForest and MillionTrees.

name: University of Geneva
summary: Swiss public research university, a Phase I grantee of the Bezos Earth Fund AI Grand Challenge.

name: University of Guelph
summary: Canadian university that hosts the Centre for Biodiversity Genomics, and whose computer scientists work with the AI and Biodiversity Change Global Center.

name: University of Leeds
summary: English university whose School of Geography hosts ForestPlots.net, the tropical forest plot data network.

name: University of Maryland
summary: US university whose Department of Geographical Sciences hosts the GLAD laboratory, which studies global land surface change, and whose researchers operate the DIST-ALERT monitoring system.

name: University of Oxford
summary: Collegiate research university in Oxford, home of the Leverhulme Centre for Nature Recovery.

name: University of Pisa
summary: Italian university whose Department of Biology leads BIOBOOST+, a European project applying AI to identify and count marine species from images.

name: University of Pittsburgh
summary: Research university in Pittsburgh, home of the Kitzes Lab and a partner in the AI and Biodiversity Change Global Center.

name: University of Plymouth
summary: English university with a Bezos Earth Fund AI Grand Challenge award to develop AI tools that map and protect deep-sea ecosystems.

name: University of Queensland
summary: Australian university whose Remote Sensing Research Centre developed the mapping methods behind the global coral reef maps of the Allen Coral Atlas, using field data and machine learning.

name: University of Southampton
summary: Public research university in Southampton, England, where Open Acoustic Devices, makers of the AudioMoth recorder, started as a research project.

name: University of St Andrews
summary: Scottish university that hosts BioTIME, a database of biodiversity time series.

name: University of Stirling
summary: Scottish university whose researchers built Mbaza AI, an open camera trap image classifier used in Gabon.

name: University of Tartu
summary: Public research university in Tartu, Estonia, named on the governance page of the UNITE fungal DNA database and a participant in the BioDT project.

name: University of the South Pacific
summary: Regional university established in 1968, jointly owned by Pacific governments, and a publisher of biodiversity records through GBIF.

name: University of Victoria
summary: Canadian university of which Ocean Networks Canada is an initiative.

name: University of Washington
summary: Seattle university whose College of the Environment received a Fund for Science and Technology grant for environmental monitoring through field observation and data modelling.

name: University of West Bohemia
summary: Czech university that coordinates BioClima, an EU-China project merging AI with ground and remote sensing data for monitoring land ecosystems.

name: University of Western Australia
summary: Perth university that hosts the OceanOmics laboratory run with the Minderoo Foundation.

name: University of Zurich
summary: Swiss public research university where Jan Dirk Wegner holds the Data Science for Sciences chair and heads the EcoVision Lab.

name: Unseenlabs
summary: French company detecting ships from space by their radio signals, and selling the data to monitor vessels including for illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.

name: Upstream Tech
summary: Sells Lens, which monitors land use and land cover change with satellite imagery and machine learning, and streamflow forecasts.

name: Urbasolar
summary: Solar developer, part of the Axpo Group, that runs an internal chatbot over the biodiversity reports for its solar sites.

name: Urbasolar biodiversity chatbot
summary: Internal chatbot used since March 2025 by Urbasolar's project teams and environmental specialists to ask plain-language questions of the biodiversity reports for its solar sites. Built on Azure OpenAI Service; the account is Microsoft's own.

name: Valhalla Foundation
summary: Foundation with an environmental innovation programme. It is a named donor to the Audacious Project raise for Global Fishing Watch and a listed funder of MapBiomas.

name: Vattenfall
summary: Energy company that ran an AI seabird monitoring trial at its Aberdeen Bay offshore wind farm with Spoor and the British Trust for Ornithology.

name: VECTRONIC Aerospace
summary: Makes GPS collars and related tracking systems for wildlife scientists.

name: Veridi Technologies
summary: Dutch company founded in 2022 using computer vision and automated microscopy to diagnose plant pathogens and measure soil biodiversity, according to Silverstrand Capital.

name: veritree
summary: Runs tree planting for businesses and says it measures and monitors reforestation data before, during and after planting.

name: Verna
summary: Software company calling itself the command centre for nature programmes, which says it uses ecological expertise and AI. Registered at Borehamwood, England.

name: Verra
summary: Operates the Verified Carbon Standard. It piloted a remote-sensing platform from Pachama for measuring forest carbon, and is developing long-term monitoring of agriculture, forestry and land use projects.

name: Versant
summary: Organisation working across metropolitan France that combines GIS layers, species inventories, literature and field observations to reveal a site's ecological stakes, and says AI is central to its method.

name: Vertebrate Genomes Project
summary: International project of the Genome 10K consortium producing high-quality reference genomes of vertebrates, with sequences public in the Genome Ark database.

name: VertLife
summary: NSF-sponsored multi-institutional project to study the biodiversity of all terrestrial vertebrates with near-complete species-level data.

name: VertNet
summary: Provides tools and services for finding, publishing and using biodiversity data.

name: Vigilife
summary: Alliance and observatory that publishes biodiversity data from environmental DNA studies around the world. SPYGEN manages its site.

name: Visipedia
summary: GitHub organisation that publishes the iNaturalist, iNatSounds and iWildCam competition data sets.

name: VITO
summary: Flemish research and consulting centre in Mol, Belgium, and a partner in ESA WorldCover.

name: Vizzuality
summary: Builds digital tools and data visualisation for NGOs, businesses and governments working on environment and sustainability.

name: Vlinder
summary: Austrian company listed by IRCAI for a Mangrove Carbon Verification System, which applies computer vision to satellite and drone images to measure carbon in mangrove forests.

name: Volta Basin Authority
summary: Basin authority listed as a member of the GMES and Africa consortium on wetlands and flood management in West Africa, led by the Centre de Suivi Ecologique.

name: VoucherVision
summary: Tool from University of Michigan researchers that uses language models to turn specimen label text into structured records for natural history collections. It now runs as VoucherVisionGO, and at least one other herbarium reports using it.

name: Wageningen University & Research
summary: Dutch university and research institute whose Laboratory of Geo-information Science and Remote Sensing produces the RADD forest disturbance alerts and which works with WWF on Forest Foresight.

name: Waitt Foundation
summary: Foundation listed as a funder of Global Fishing Watch.

name: Walder Foundation
summary: Foundation shown among the funders of the Centre for Biodiversity Genomics.

name: Wallace
summary: Modular R-based platform for modelling species niches and distributions, funded by the National Science Foundation, free and open source under GPL 3.0, and used in studies informing conservation.

name: Wallacea Trust
summary: Maintains the Wallacea Trust Methodology, an open access framework for measuring biodiversity change, used by Replanet for biodiversity credits.

name: Walmart Foundation
summary: US corporate foundation recorded as giving Global Fishing Watch $1.8 million from 2021 to 2023, and listed as a funder of MapBiomas in 2023 and 2024.

name: Walton Family Foundation
summary: Family foundation in Bentonville, Arkansas, whose giving is mainly in the United States. Grantable lists one 2020 grant to Global Fishing Watch.

name: warbleR
summary: R package for analysing the structure of animal acoustic signals at scale, running a batch pipeline from spectrograms to acoustic measurements and similarity analyses.

name: Washington University in St. Louis
summary: Private research university in Missouri, home of the Multimodal Vision Research Laboratory, which builds models for biodiversity monitoring.

name: Waterbird Populations Portal
summary: Open-access online platform from Wetlands International with size estimates and trends for over 2,500 populations of 870 waterbird species, launched on 29 June 2021.

name: Waterkeeper Alliance
summary: Global network of community clean water groups that partnered with True Elements in 2023 to give member groups AI water quality tools.

name: Waverley Street Foundation
summary: Non-profit investing in climate solutions and community priorities. It gave Earth Species Project a $7 million grant and is a listed funder of MapBiomas.

name: Weecology
summary: Ecology and environmental data science group at the University of Florida, made up of Morgan Ernest's and Ethan White's labs, that publishes open datasets and software and develops AI for monitoring birds.

name: WeForest
summary: Non-profit forest restoration organisation with its head office in Belgium. The Airbus Foundation says it has provided imagery and funding since 2025 to assess reforestation in Ethiopia through machine learning.

name: Wellcome Sanger Institute
summary: Genome research institute at Hinxton, Cambridgeshire, whose Tree of Life Programme produces reference genomes for eukaryotic species.

name: Wellcome Trust
summary: Charitable foundation established in 1936 that supports science on health challenges; it jointly funds the AEGIS ancient environmental genomics initiative and has invested in the Wellcome Sanger Institute since 1992.

name: Wellspring Philanthropic Fund
summary: Fund listed as a funder of the MapBiomas Project from 2019 to 2022.

name: WeRobotics
summary: Organisation that supports the Flying Labs network on drones, data and AI. It took part in the Global Conservation Tech and Drone Forum 2026.

name: West African Science Service Centre on Climate Change and Adapted Land Use
summary: West African intergovernmental organisation with 13 member countries, whose Competence Centre runs a GIS and remote sensing laboratory and a data repository.

name: Western Hemisphere Shorebird Reserve Network
summary: Partnership for protecting shorebird habitat across the Americas, with 119 sites in 20 countries, and the coordinator of the Central American Waterbird Census.

name: Western Indian Ocean Marine Science Association
summary: Science association that promotes interdisciplinary marine and coastal science in the Western Indian Ocean and has launched free cloud ocean data training with HUB Ocean and SeaSketch.

name: Wetlands International
summary: Global network organisation of 18 offices working to safeguard and restore wetlands. It sits on the Global Mangrove Alliance steering committee.

name: WetSAT-ML
summary: Open tool from the Stockholm Environment Institute that uses radar satellite data and machine learning to show when, where and how wetlands change.

name: Whale Seeker
summary: Montreal startup that uses AI to detect marine mammals and birds in imagery, for energy, shipping, government and non-profit customers.

name: Whiskerbook
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that applies AI to photographs of whiskered species.

name: WHOI-Plankton
summary: Benchmark dataset for fine-grained visual recognition of plankton, from a team including the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution.

name: Wild Chimpanzee Foundation
summary: Foundation working on the survival of wild chimpanzees and their habitat, with projects in Côte d'Ivoire, Liberia, Guinea and Sierra Leone; its reports describe monitoring with camera traps.

name: Wild Dolphin Project
summary: Non-profit dolphin research project whose field recordings underpin Google's DolphinGemma model. It runs the CHAT research work on dolphin communication.

name: Wild Me Lab
summary: Lab within Conservation X Labs that builds open software and AI for identifying individual animals from photographs, including Wildbook and MiewID.

name: Wild Moves
summary: Portal for animal tracking data published through GBIF, hosted by GBIF and maintained by WILDLABS and volunteers.

name: WildAid
summary: Wildlife conservation organisation working on illegal wildlife trade and illegal fishing. Its WildAid Marine programme is an EarthRanger deployment partner.

name: Wildbook
summary: Open-source software platform that combines AI and citizen science to re-identify individual animals across images.

name: Wildbook for Lynx
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that uses AI to identify Iberian and Eurasian lynx from photographs.

name: WildDrone
summary: International doctoral training network funded by the EU's Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions that develops autonomous drones for monitoring wildlife, with 13 doctoral candidates.

name: Wilderlab
summary: Reads environmental DNA from water samples to identify the species present, with companies in New Zealand and Australia and an address in the United States.

name: WildEye Conservation
summary: Organisation that applies machine vision to wildlife conservation. It maintains TrapTagger for camera-trap images and runs AI-driven aerial surveys.

name: Wildflow
summary: Organisation using AI to analyse nature data, turning footage into 3D reef models, developing a coral reef foundation model, and working with over 20 research institutions including UCL.

name: WildINTEL
summary: Biodiversa+ funded project that combines camera trapping, citizen science and AI to produce species population and community Essential Biodiversity Variables automatically.

name: WILDLABS
summary: Online community and programme for conservation technology users and makers, launched in 2015. It runs events, research, awards and a technology inventory, and is overseen by four conservation NGOs.

name: WILDLABS Awards
summary: Annual conservation technology grants run by WILDLABS with funding from Arm. The 2026 round funded 16 projects, with eleven awards of $10,000 and five of $50,000.

name: Wildlife Acoustics
summary: Makes acoustic recorders and sound analysis software for biologists, researchers and government agencies.

name: Wildlife Computers
summary: Makes telemetry tags for monitoring animal behaviour and environments.

name: Wildlife Conservation Society
summary: Conservation organisation with a global field programme and four zoos and an aquarium in New York City. It sits on the WILDLABS Steering Committee and is a partner in Wildlife Insights.

name: Wildlife Crime Tech Challenge
summary: USAID prize competition with National Geographic, the Smithsonian and TRAFFIC, for technology against wildlife crime. It selected 16 winners from 300 applicants in 52 countries.

name: Wildlife Cyber Spotter Program
summary: Coalition to End Wildlife Trafficking Online programme that trains citizen scientists to find and report wildlife sales online that AI misses.

name: Wildlife Drones
summary: Canberra company making drone-based radio telemetry for tracking tagged animals, which says its technology is used in eight countries.

name: Wildlife Guardians
summary: Organisation based in Washington, D.C. Microsoft said in 2018 that its team would use an AI for Earth grant to support the Lion Identification Network of Collaborators, an AI-assisted lion identification database.

name: Wildlife Insights
summary: Online platform where people upload camera trap images, have species identified automatically by AI, and share wildlife data. It runs SpeciesNet, and Google is a core partner.

name: Wildlife Protection Solutions
summary: Non-profit that runs wpsWatch, a platform that analyses images from remote cameras with AI and alerts people to what they show.

name: Wildlife Watch
summary: Samsung and Africam pilot that turned Galaxy phones into livestreaming wildlife cameras at Balule Nature Reserve, South Africa, so that viewers could act as virtual rangers for the Black Mamba Anti-Poaching Unit.

name: Wildlife.ai
summary: New Zealand charity that builds open source AI and machine learning tools with grassroots conservation projects, including the Wildlife Watcher smart camera trap.

name: WildlifeDatasets
summary: Open-source toolkit for animal re-identification that gathers wildlife data sets.

name: wildlifeDI
summary: R package for analysing interactions in wildlife telemetry data, calculating dynamic interaction indices between animal pairs and finding contacts in large tracking datasets.

name: WildMon
summary: Non-profit that combines ecoacoustics, camera traps, eDNA and other ecological data, using AI-powered workflows, to report on ecosystem condition. A core partner of Wildlife Insights.

name: WILDS
summary: Curated collection of benchmark data sets for distribution shifts, which includes a camera trap variant of iWildCam and satellite image tasks.

name: WildTrack
summary: Non-profit that identifies endangered animals from their footprints, using data analytics, AI and traditional ecological knowledge.

name: William and Flora Hewlett Foundation
summary: American private foundation based in Menlo Park and a member of the Biodiversity Funders Group.

name: Wings over Wetlands
summary: Four-year project, 2006 to 2010, on the conservation of migratory waterbirds and wetlands in the African-Eurasian flyway region, which produced the Critical Site Network Tool.

name: Wise Ancestors
summary: Scotts Valley nonprofit that co-develops genomic research for biodiversity conservation with Indigenous Peoples and local communities, with projects in Colombia and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

name: WOCAT
summary: Global network launched in 1992 that documents sustainable land management. The UNCCD recognises its Global SLM Database as its primary recommended database.

name: Women in Conservation Technology Programme
summary: Programme launched by the WILDLABS East Africa community in March 2022 to develop women conservation technologists and leaders.

name: Woods & Wayside International
summary: US nonprofit registered in Hopewell, New Jersey. MapBiomas Alerta lists it as a funder from 2023.

name: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
summary: Private non-profit marine science and engineering research institution whose Ocean Twilight Zone project uses AI on plankton imagery.

name: Work for Humankind
summary: Lenovo initiative that gave Island Conservation internet links and edge servers on Robinson Crusoe Island so that camera trap data could be analysed on site to guide removal of invasive coatis.

name: World Bank Group
summary: Development bank group that finances nature work and publishes natural capital data, and says it is working with NASA, ESA and GEO to use AI to measure the nature impact of its work.

name: World Data Centre for Microorganisms
summary: Data centre for the World Federation for Culture Collections, giving a view of culture collections and their holdings.

name: World Database of Key Biodiversity Areas
summary: Global database of Key Biodiversity Areas, the sites that meet a global standard for significance to nature, delivered by the KBA Partnership and its secretariat.

name: World Environment Situation Room
summary: UNEP data platform that aggregates environmental platforms and data. A 2024 UNEP presentation called it a work in progress and listed use cases including an AI language model and natural language data queries.

name: World Flora Online
summary: Open-access database of the world's plant species, a follow-up to The Plant List, conceived in 2012 by four botanical institutions.

name: World Flora Online Consortium
summary: Group of institutions that signed the memorandum of understanding on World Flora Online, opened for signature in January 2013. Thirty-four had signed by the end of July 2016.

name: World Register of Marine Species
summary: Register of marine species names, controlled by taxonomic experts and built on the Aphia database at the Flanders Marine Institute.

name: World Resources Institute
summary: Independent research organisation working on food, land, water, energy and cities. It runs Global Forest Watch, now Global Nature Watch, and has an Applied AI Group inside its Data Lab.

name: World Soil Information Service
summary: Centralised global soil database managed by ISRIC.

name: World Wide Fund for Nature
summary: Global conservation network. Reported AI uses include Forest Foresight, which predicts forest loss, ManglarIA for mangroves, and work on camera trap analysis through Wildlife Insights.

name: WorldClim
summary: Global climate surfaces for land areas, with bioclimatic variables used in species distribution modelling.

name: Worldwide Soundscapes
summary: Project that inventories passive acoustic monitoring data sets targeting biodiversity across all realms, with 351 active collaborators.

name: WRI Data Lab
summary: Data and product unit of the World Resources Institute. It builds and runs WRI's applications and datasets and deploys data science and AI, and its listed staff include people working on Global Nature Watch and Land & Carbon Lab. WRI's Applied AI Group sits inside it.

name: WSL Swiss Federal Research Institute
summary: Swiss research organisation on forests, landscapes, biodiversity, natural hazards, snow and ice, headquartered in Birmensdorf, with researchers on deep species distribution modelling and partners in the BiodivMon projects HiRAD and FunDive.

name: WSP
summary: Engineering consultancy that says its ecology services use AI-driven predictive analytics, remote sensing and AI-powered habitat modelling.

name: Xeno-canto
summary: Online database and sound archive of wildlife recordings shared by a worldwide community, widely used to train bird sound models.

name: Xeno-canto Foundation for Nature Sounds
summary: Dutch foundation that publishes the Xeno-canto wildlife sound collection to GBIF.

name: XeriusTracking
summary: French maker of telemetry systems for wildlife monitoring, including miniaturised GPS, Argos and UHF transmitters from 10 grams.

name: XPRIZE
summary: Foundation that runs large incentive competitions, located in Culver City, California. It ran XPRIZE Rainforest, a biodiversity measurement competition.

name: XPRIZE Rainforest
summary: $10 million competition launched in 2019 for autonomous biodiversity monitoring technology. Six finalist teams competed in the Brazilian Amazon in 2024 and Team Limelight's drone-deployed system won the grand prize.

name: Yaguas AI biodiversity expedition
summary: Conservation International expedition to Yaguas National Park in Peru testing whether AI and new sensors can monitor rainforest biodiversity at scale, with Frankfurt Zoological Society, Okala and Limelight Rainforest.

name: Yale Center for Biodiversity and Global Change
summary: Yale University centre on Earth's biodiversity and tools for its conservation, which with Map of Life publishes the Species Protection Index.

name: Yale University
summary: Private university in New Haven, Connecticut, and home of the Yale Center for Biodiversity and Global Change.

name: Yerevan Tech for Biodiversity Monitoring Hub
summary: Initiative launched at CBD COP17 by the Armenian Presidency to help countries build national monitoring systems and connect them with Earth observation, ecosystem mapping and AI.

name: Zamba
summary: Python package and cloud service from DrivenData that identifies animals, trains custom models and estimates distance from camera trap videos and images.

name: Zebra Wildbook
summary: Wildbook platform from Wild Me Lab that uses AI to identify zebras from photographs.

name: Zonation
summary: Free software for prioritising conservation values from spatial data, used in conservation area and land use planning, and in use in Finland and globally since 2006.

name: ZooBank
summary: Official registry of zoological nomenclature, recording publications, authors and names. zoobank.org refuses the fetcher, so this rests on the ICZN's pages.

name: Zoological Information Management System
summary: Species360's software and shared database of records on animals in human care, covering more than 22,000 species.

name: Zoological Society of London
summary: Charity devoted to the worldwide conservation of animals and their habitats, which runs London Zoo and Whipsnade Zoo. It is a member of the SMART Partnership and a partner in Wildlife Insights.

name: Zooniverse
summary: Platform for people-powered research where volunteers classify data for researchers, including camera trap and wildlife projects used to label data for machine learning.

name: Zoonomia
summary: International collaboration comparing mammal genomes, which created assemblies for 131 species and shares them for human medicine and biodiversity conservation research.

name: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne
summary: Swiss public research university, home of the ECEO laboratory on machine learning for Earth observation and a core partner in the AI and Biodiversity Change Global Center.

name: 1st National Forest Inventory of Andorra
summary: Closed project, run by Andorra Recerca + Innovació from May 2022 to June 2024, that collected standardised data on all Andorran forests, with a database of 194 plots measured in summer 2022.

name: AFOLU land cover maps of Andorra
summary: Active project using Landsat, SPOT and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery to map land cover change and quantify changes in Andorra's sink capacity, with six land use categories following AFOLU classes.

name: Andorra Recerca + Innovació
summary: Private foundation of the public sphere, created by Law 11/2021 from three earlier bodies, that represents Andorra in GBIF and was reported in July 2026 to be leading a pilot testing AI, 3D scanning and drones for forest inventories.

name: Andorran Flora Master List
summary: A 2021 checklist of Andorran flora with conservation status and regulation for each species, covering 1,604 taxa, 309 of them in a threat category, run by Andorra Recerca + Innovació.

name: Butterfly Monitoring Scheme of Andorra
summary: Active programme run by Andorra Recerca + Innovació, monitoring day-flying butterflies since 2004 with ten transects in 2021, and reported by the Madriu-Perafita-Claror valley to feed Catalan and European schemes.

name: Cos de Banders
summary: Andorra's Banders corps, whose 2025 report records continued sample collection for active disease surveillance of wild fauna; Alto (December 2025) reports about 120 wildlife captures a year for disease testing.

name: Evolution of the landscape of Andorra
summary: Project comparing land cover maps at 1:5,000 scale, made from aerial photographs of 1948, 1972, 1995 and 2012, to study landscape change in Andorra, with all maps available in GIS format.

name: Flora d'Andorra
summary: GBIF dataset compiled by CENMA of the Institut d'Estudis Andorrans, containing 60,202 records of flora observed in Andorra, mostly from bibliographic citations, and revised in March 2016.

name: Following of snowbed vegetation
summary: Programme monitoring vegetation in two Andorran and fourteen wider Pyrenean snowbeds yearly with one method since 2011, using temperature loggers and, from 2017, open top warming chambers.

name: GBIF Andorra
summary: Andorra's GBIF country node with voting participation, according to GBIF's registry, to which Andorra Recerca + Innovació says Andorra has contributed around 125,000 records.

name: Llacs sentinella
summary: Active lake monitoring programme, begun in 2017 under the POCTEFA project REPLIM, that takes sediment samples and records water chemistry and continuous temperature at several depths.

name: Metabarcoding of the Andorran Lakes
summary: A project aiming to capture a picture of the microbial biodiversity of six emblematic Andorran lakes, begun as a joint study with the CRG and CREAF, partly government-funded, with Andorra Recerca + Innovació as partner.

name: Ministeri de Medi Ambient, Agricultura i Ramaderia
summary: Andorran government ministry whose 2025 presentation reports brown bear monitoring with 24 deployments and 26 hair samples, and eight bears identified genetically in Andorra that year.

name: Mycological study of Andorra
summary: Project on Andorra's fungi, covering a checklist begun in 2000, a red list, and a climate change study begun in 2018 using 49 plots and soil metabarcoding.

name: Observatori Sentinel
summary: Active long-term interdisciplinary research set-up studying mountain ecosystem dynamics in the Estanyó valley, building on ORCHAMP, with soil DNA measured on 900 square metre plots, according to the Madriu-Perafita-Claror valley.

name: Observatory of Andorran Mountains
summary: Portal set up in 2013 that reports the state and change of Andorra's environment and mountains through scientific indicators, drawn from Andorra Recerca + Innovació follow-up studies and grouped in four themes.

name: Oficina de l'Energia i del Canvi Climàtic
summary: Andorra's Energy and Climate Change Office, created by government decree, which Andorra Recerca + Innovació says funded the first National Forest Inventory.

name: Ornitho Andorra
summary: Active citizen science web application for wildlife observations, started in Andorra in 2015 with a mobile app, NaturaList, and nearly 8,000 records added to GBIF during 2025.

name: Parc Natural de la Vall de Sorteny
summary: Natural park created in 1999, the first of its kind in Andorra and a Ramsar wetland since 2012, where monitoring networks track key species and host the Sentinel Observatory study area.

name: Seguiment d'Amfibis Comuns d'Andorra
summary: A citizen-science project monitoring amphibian populations to estimate long-term trends, using quantified surveys of adults seen or heard, with the Societat Catalana d'Herpetologia and the Government of Andorra collaborating.

name: Seguiment d'Ocells Comuns d'Andorra
summary: Long-term programme tracking common birds in Andorra with volunteer ornithologists since 2011, supplying data to European bird censuses, with 25 transects operating in the 2025 breeding period.

name: Seguiment de l'ós bru a Andorra
summary: Brown bear monitoring programme whose 2025 results, presented on 11 March 2026, show 24 deployments, 26 hair samples and eight individual bears identified genetically, one female and seven males.

name: Seguiment de la papallona del boix a Andorra
summary: Box tree moth monitoring set up in 2019 and part of the Catalan monitoring network since 2021; the 2026 report assesses Fontaneda population dynamics using 2021 to 2025 data.

name: Seguiment de la qualitat biòtica dels rius d'Andorra
summary: A river biotic quality monitoring programme with a 2022 protocol aiming to provide standardised data for the Government of Andorra, following earlier monitoring based on IBGN.

name: Seguiment del seneci del Cap a Andorra
summary: Monitoring of Cape ragwort in Andorra, with ten permanent points installed in 2019; the 2025 study aimed to conduct the third scientific monitoring campaign at those points.

name: Seguiment dels Ocells Comuns a Andorra
summary: Active long-term bird monitoring programme relying on volunteer ornithologists, begun in 2011 with 24 active transects in 2021, and listed by the European Breeding Bird Atlas 2 as Andorra's national data source.

name: SIGMA (Sistema d'Informació Geogràfica mediambiental d'Andorra)
summary: Andorra's environmental GIS platform, begun at the end of 2001, giving downloadable geological, geomorphological, habitat and land cover maps, initially supported by UNESCO with technical advice from CREAF.

name: Vall del Madriu-Perafita-Claror
summary: Valley whose Management Commission hosts yearly monitoring and research projects and keeps biological indicator programmes, while general species and habitat monitoring has been suspended since 2024 pending a new conservation plan.

name: Vertebrats d'Andorra
summary: GBIF dataset compiled by CENMA of the Institut d'Estudis Andorrans, containing 36,836 records of vertebrates observed in Andorra and revised in February 2016.

name: Wildlife in the Andorran Pyrenees (II)
summary: Project listed by CREAF as Earthwatch Pirineu II, monitoring mountain organisms long term to see how climate or land use change affects alpine systems, working closely with CENMA.

name: Abu Dhabi Global Environmental Data Initiative
summary: Initiative run by EAD and UNEP, listed by EAD as including a biodiversity rapid assessment project and an indicator reporting system (IRIS) for sharing state of environment assessments.

name: Abu Dhabi native plant genome sequencing project
summary: Project in which EAD and M42 partner to sequence genomes of important native plants at the Plant Genetic Resource Centre; 12 more species were chosen after the ghaf tree.

name: Abu Dhabi natural terrestrial habitats assessment programme
summary: Project run by EAD with Dendra Co.; EAD said in August 2024 that more than six months of work covered 11,000 hectares as a representative vegetation survey.

name: Abu Dhabi Nature species App
summary: Smartphone app and website launched in October 2022 at GITEX, built and run by EAD, for learning about Abu Dhabi's wildlife and reporting sightings, with a database of over 4,000 species and habitats.

name: Abu Dhabi Red List of Ecosystems
summary: Assessment of Abu Dhabi's terrestrial and marine ecosystems, built by EAD with IUCN and Provita as partners, announced 16 May 2023, finding twelve ecosystems threatened, two of them critically endangered.

name: Abu Dhabi Red List of Wildlife Species
summary: First threat-status assessment of the emirate's terrestrial and marine species, launched by EAD in September 2021 with Provita and the IUCN Species Survival Commission, assessing 244 species and placing 74 in threat categories.

name: Abu Dhabi State of Environment Portal
summary: Programme built by EAD that uses AI and large language models to analyse sensor data and reports and forecast environmental indicators, building on a February 2025 report.

name: Abu Dhabi University
summary: University listed as affiliation of the first author of a 2019 IEEE Access paper on estimating vegetation cover with convolutional neural networks, a deep learning method.

name: ADMI Mangrove Observatory
summary: Digital platform, built by the Environment Agency Abu Dhabi and funded by Dolphin Energy, that consolidates restoration data from 19 active projects across Abu Dhabi using field surveys, satellite imagery and partner-reported data.

name: Adnoc
summary: The National describes it as the Abu Dhabi oil company, which planted its five millionth mangrove seedling in January 2026 towards 10 million by 2030, and reports it uses machine learning to monitor mangroves.

name: Adnoc mangrove planting programme
summary: A programme run by Adnoc, begun in 2023, that uses AI-enabled drones to plant mangroves and machine learning to monitor them, with five million seedlings planted by January 2026 against a 10 million target for 2030.

name: Advanced Technology Research Council
summary: Organisation whose VentureOne unveiled Nabat, a climate tech venture to conserve and restore mangroves with AI and robotics.

name: Al Ain Zoo
summary: Owned by the Zoo and Aquarium Public Institution in Al Ain; The National reported in 2022 that its conservation team had studied wild birds since 2017.

name: American University in Dubai
summary: University listed, with Manchester Metropolitan University, in the first author's affiliations on a 2024 SSRN preprint mapping forests of Golestan Province, Iran, from OLI satellite data.

name: American University of Sharjah
summary: University listed as affiliation on a 2020 paper mapping Northern Emirates mangrove change, 1990 to 2019, with random forest and other models, and a 2024 Bat2Web paper.

name: Arabian Oryx Protected Area aerial survey
