summary: Closed EAD aerial count of oryx, sand gazelle and other species in the Arabian Oryx Protected Area, which reported in June 2021 a 22% oryx increase, with the herd at 946.

name: Arabian Sand Cat Research Programme
summary: Programme run by Al Ain Zoo and funded by Impact by Miral, using eDNA, GPS tracking, camera traps and AI-enabled modelling to study sand cats in Abu Dhabi.

name: Artificial Intelligence Mangrove Monitoring System (UAE, 2017-2024)
summary: Model using UNet++, Sentinel-2 data and hand-labelled training data to monitor UAE mangroves from 2017 to 2024, reporting about 9,142 hectares of dense mangrove in 2024, up about 2,061 hectares on 2017.

name: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani - Dubai Campus
summary: Campus whose Department of Computer Science is the first author's affiliation on a 2021 paper classifying land cover in aerial images with convolutional neural networks.

name: Blue Carbon mangrove rehabilitation project
summary: Project whose second phase planted more than 35,000 mangrove seeds by drone in the Mirfa lagoon with Distant Imagery, following a 2020 pilot that planted about a hectare.

name: Burt Marine Biology Lab
summary: Marine biology lab run by New York University Abu Dhabi, led by John A. Burt, which says it coordinates the Coral Reef Monitoring Program across the ROPME Sea Area.

name: CMS Office – Abu Dhabi
summary: Regional hub established in 2009, according to EAD, which said in February 2020 that an extended agreement would continue its UAE operations for four more years.

name: Collective Artificial Intelligence for Multi-Robot Coral Reef Monitoring and Habitat Enhancement: A comparison across Gulf countries
summary: Project, led by Giulia De Masi, proposing a swarm of bio-inspired robotic turtles with AI and sensors; the AI to be developed runs from computer vision to locating restoration sites.

name: Conservation of the Critically Endangered Emirati Leaf-toed Gecko
summary: Mohamed bin Zayed fund project that aims to survey the gecko's UAE range, model its distribution and sequence its genome, after a 2022 expedition found it in five locations.

name: Dubai Desert Conservation Reserve
summary: Reserve run by the Dubai Environment and Climate Change Authority, which with Biosphere Expeditions completed its ninth annual wildlife survey in January 2020, with camera traps capturing over 6,000 images across 14 points.

name: Dubai Environment and Climate Change Authority
summary: Authority established under Law No. 11 of 2024 that manages eight Dubai nature reserves, conducts wildlife and habitat research, and in 2026 partnered with IUCN's West Asia office on an integrated reserve plan.

name: Dubai Turtle Rehabilitation Project
summary: A turtle rehabilitation project run by Jumeirah and led by Barbara Lang-Lenton, which has returned over 2,000 sea turtles to the sea and, as reported in 2024, fits some with satellite trackers.

name: DubDev Technology
summary: Company whose gazelle feeder, according to Sharjah24, uses computer vision and the internet of things and processes more than 15 million images annually.

name: e& enterprise
summary: Named as an EAD strategic partner developing State of Environment Portal features, whose dashboards use large language models, natural language processing and predictive analytics.

name: EAD AI-based vegetation and pasture monitoring programme
summary: Project run by EAD with Dendra Co. to assess natural terrestrial habitats; in August 2024 EAD said it covered 11,000 hectares over more than six months.

name: EAD annual coral monitoring and assessment programme
summary: Annual programme run by EAD with NYUAD as partner to monitor and assess the health of coral communities in Abu Dhabi's coastal waters.

name: EAD bird monitoring at Al Wathba Wetland Reserve
summary: EAD programme monitoring terrestrial and marine birds at Al Wathba Wetland Reserve since 2002, using satellite tracking of greater flamingos since 2005.

name: EAD marine aerial survey
summary: EAD aerial survey of marine species running since 2004, which reported in June 2025 covering over 8,000 square kilometres and estimated over 3,500 dugongs in 2024.

name: EAD marine turtle nesting monitoring
summary: EAD programme monitoring turtle nesting areas each year, which in a report dated 19 February 2024 recorded 247 hawksbill nests, against 193 in 2022, with 72 per cent hatching success.

name: EAD native tree-tagging programme
summary: Programme run by EAD, begun in November 2023, aiming to tag 100,000 native trees; EAD said in April 2024 it had tagged over 17,000 in the first three months.

name: EAD Osprey breeding survey 2023
summary: Completed 2023 EAD survey of coastal sites and nearby islands in Abu Dhabi, recording 127 breeding Osprey pairs at more than 40 locations, intended to help assess population trends.

name: EAD oyster bed mapping survey
summary: Multi-year EAD survey of the emirate's marine waters, announced 8 July 2026, with fieldwork from 2023 to 2025 assessing 1,088 locations, of which 334 confirmed oyster bed.

name: EAD wildlife assessment and monitoring programme
summary: EAD programme running since 2011 that monitors Arabian tahr on Jabal Hafit with infra-red camera traps, and recorded an Arabian caracal there in 2019, the first since 1984.

name: Emirates Marine Environmental Group
summary: Established in 1996, this Dubai non-profit partnered with EPAA on Sir Bu Nair turtle monitoring from 2010, according to a September 2019 site report.

name: Emirates Nature-WWF
summary: Organisation that says camera traps identified over 1,100 species in Wadi Wurayah, in work with Fujairah Municipality, and that its mangrove monitoring combines field surveys, drones and citizen science.

name: Enviro-portal
summary: A public portal run by EAD, which says it provides the latest environmental data and the distribution of flora, fauna, marine habitats and protected areas in the emirate.

name: Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi
summary: Abu Dhabi environment agency that runs the Enviro-portal and a global environmental data initiative, and launched an AI-based state of environment portal in November 2025.

name: Environment and Protected Areas Authority
summary: Managed Sir Bu Nair and monitored turtles with EMEG from 2010 per a 2019 report, tagged five hawksbills, surveyed ospreys and announced a 2025 seabird debris study.

name: Environment Protection and Development Authority, Ras Al Khaimah
summary: Implements environmental legislation and develops environmental regulation in Ras Al Khaimah; Gulf News reported in August 2024 that it had tagged 475 green turtles with the Emirates Wildlife Society.

name: First eDNA-Based Monitoring of Marine Vertebrates in the Urbanized Marine Ecosystem Abu Dhabi
summary: An eDNA inventory of marine vertebrates at four urban Abu Dhabi sites that detected 83 taxa, holds about 348 GBIF occurrence records, and was funded by Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi.

name: Fish AI
summary: Project using AI to identify fish species in real time and give data on species composition, size, quantity and biomass.

name: Fujairah Environment Authority
summary: Local government agency set up in 2018 that manages Fujairah's reserves including Wadi Wurayah, using volunteers and camera traps, and reportedly co-funded with Mashreq camera traps that recorded Arabian wildcats.

name: Ghaf tree population genomics study
summary: First UAE population genomics study of Ghaf trees, run by EAD with ICBA specialists, announced 28 November 2025, using whole-genome re-sequencing and producing an interactive genomic map.

name: Gulf Green Turtle Conservation Project
summary: Run by Emirates Nature-WWF with EAD and the Marine Research Foundation, this was one of two initiatives Emirates Nature-WWF says satellite tagged 126 turtles over 10 years.

name: HuBot
summary: Robot built by IFHC and Khalifa University of Science and Technology that, according to the Abu Dhabi Media Office, uses AI to recognise houbara behaviour in real time, shown at ADIHEX 2024.

name: Impact by Miral
summary: Platform funding and delivering social and environmental projects across Abu Dhabi, according to Blooloop, with four conservation initiatives approved in May 2026 involving planned research, genomics, AI and monitoring.

name: International Fund for Houbara Conservation
summary: Houbara bustard conservation body that says it has used science for over forty years; OpenAlex lists a 2011 satellite tracking paper and a 2010 Kazakhstan population assessment tied to it or its avian research centre.

name: Jaywun coastal seabed sediment survey off Abu Dhabi
summary: Sediment survey off Abu Dhabi aboard Jaywun, which Khalifa University in December 2024 called the first comprehensive modern one, led by EAD and Khalifa University scientists and begun during the December 2023 expedition.

name: Jumeirah
summary: Its Burj Al Arab and Al Naseem hotels treat rescued turtles and show guests their recovery; The National reported in 2024 that its rehabilitation project began in 2004.

name: Khalifa University
summary: University that says its scientists, with EAD, led the first comprehensive modern sediment survey off Abu Dhabi, and whose Provost says it belongs to EAD's Abu Dhabi Environmental Research Network.

name: Khalifa University Center for Autonomous Robotic Systems
summary: The affiliation of the first author of a 2024 Ecological Informatics paper on HuBot, a biomimicking mobile robot for studying bird behaviour, with houbara bustard and YOLOv9 among its keywords.

name: Khalifa University of Science and Technology
summary: University linked through OpenAlex to a 2024 conceptual review on AI and animal-inspired robots for conservation, and a 2018 remote sensing paper on UAE reef change during the 2015–2016 El Niño.

name: Mangrove Biodiversity Automated Monitoring programme
summary: Research initiative launched under the Abu Dhabi Mangrove Initiative, supporting development of MANTA, which is intended to use AI, monitoring and community science to study natural and restored mangrove biodiversity.

name: Mangrove Monitoring Dashboard
summary: Dataset built by Emirates Nature-WWF that compiles real-time and historical data on mangrove survival and site health, with biodiversity indicators planned.

name: Mashreq
summary: Presents the Notice Nature citizen science wildlife mapping programme with Emirates Nature-WWF, and reportedly co-funded with the Fujairah Environment Authority camera traps in Wadi Wurayah that recorded Arabian wildcats.

name: MAviS-Chat
summary: A multimodal large language model for audio, vision and text, built by Yevheniia Kryklyvets and aimed at fine-grained bird species understanding, introduced alongside a dataset covering over 1,000 bird species.

name: Ministry of Climate Change and Environment
summary: UAE ministry whose Head of Terrestrial Biodiversity Section the CBD lists as the primary national focal point, and whose Director of Biological Diversity it lists as protected areas focal point.

name: Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund
summary: Small grants fund that says it supported 238 projects in 64 countries in 2024, investing 2,231,317 US dollars, and over 3,200 projects across 175 countries overall.

name: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
summary: University affiliated with several authors of MAviS, a 2025 multimodal bird species assistant record that OpenAlex incorrectly lists under Association for Computational Linguistics 2025 as first author.

name: Mubadala Arabian Center for Climate and Environmental Sciences
summary: Centre, run by NYU Abu Dhabi, that says it is building observational and modelling capacity in the marine and atmospheric sector, with coral reefs and plankton dynamics among its topics.

name: Nature X Abu Dhabi
summary: Programme launched at the IUCN World Conservation Congress 2025 to conserve, monitor and restore ecosystems with new technologies and AI tools, built by EAD and the Advanced Technology Research Council.

name: New York University Abu Dhabi
summary: University that says it coordinates the UAE National Coral Reef Monitoring Program, and whose authors published a 2023 paper on identifying heat-resilient corals using machine learning and microbiome data.

name: Notice Nature
summary: Citizen science wildlife mapping movement, run by Emirates Nature-WWF with Mashreq as partner, that aims to collect biodiversity data to build a database and baselines.

name: OceanX United Arab Emirates (UAE) 2023 expedition
summary: Closed expedition run by OceanX in November–December 2023, which OceanX says used eDNA for fisheries assessment and surveyed seafloor, habitats, biodiversity and megafauna across UAE waters.

name: Program MARVEL: Marine Vertebrate eDNA Long-term monitoring, UAE
summary: Project listed among Ocean Institute Projects, running from May 2025 to May 2027, using eDNA metabarcoding of filtered seawater to characterise mobile marine vertebrates in UAE coastal waters.

name: Regional Coral Reef Monitoring Program (ROPME Sea Area)
summary: Coral reef monitoring programme run by the Burt Marine Biology Lab with Mubadala ACCESS Center support, involving eight Gulf states and producing standardised long-term datasets on reef condition, biodiversity and resilience.

name: RoboGenAI
summary: Model built by Khalifa University of Science and Technology that lets underwater robots detect patterns and changes in real time while monitoring marine environments.

name: Rochester Institute of Technology - Dubai
summary: Dubai campus of an institute whose Mechanical and Industrial Engineering Department is listed by the first author of a 2026 Marine Pollution Bulletin paper presenting a deep learning framework for automated coral health assessment.

name: Saadiyat Turtle Patrol
summary: EAD volunteer patrol that, as EAD reported on 20 August 2026, found the first recorded Olive Ridley nest in Abu Dhabi and tracked it through incubation with a solar-powered camera.

name: Sea Turtle Population Tracking Programme
summary: Programme funded by Impact by Miral that uses tracking technologies and rescue data, including GPS tags on juvenile and adult turtles, to map movement and feeding ground hotspots in the Arabian Gulf.

name: Sharjah Marine Science Research Centre
summary: Marine research centre run by the University of Khorfakkan, in Khorfakkan, Sharjah, reporting 12 laboratories, remote sensing and GIS facilities, and planning AI, machine learning and automation for 2026-2030.

name: Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi
summary: Abu Dhabi university campus on Al Reem Island that runs a collective AI multi-robot coral reef monitoring project and is listed in a 2026 PLoS ONE paper on eDNA monitoring of marine vertebrates in mangroves.

name: Technology Innovation Institute
summary: Research body run by the Advanced Technology Research Council, developing an autonomous underwater vehicle with AI-powered cameras to map marine habitats, and listed by the sole author of a 2026 UAV mangrove restoration dataset.

name: UAE National Coral Reef Monitoring Program
summary: Active programme run by New York University Abu Dhabi, which says it coordinates standardised reef surveys in the Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman with environmental authorities, described as the first national-scale coral reef assessment.

name: UAE Space Agency
summary: Government space agency and CEOS member since 2018, associated with the Space Analytics and Solutions programme for downstream satellite applications, including environment monitoring and vegetation health.

name: UAE-wide coral heat stress test study
summary: Closed study that NYU Abu Dhabi said in January 2026 was the first of its kind on both Emirati coasts, using CBASS to test hundreds of field coral colonies for heat tolerance.

name: United Arab Emirates University
summary: University whose Department of Biology in Al Ain is listed by the first author of a 2026 Waterbirds paper estimating a Socotra cormorant breeding population in Bahrain from drone footage.

name: University of Dubai
summary: University whose College of Engineering and IT is listed by the first author of a 2023 IGARSS paper on machine learning for mapping mangroves and shoreline change along an arid coast.

name: University of Khorfakkan
summary: University listed by the first author of a 2026 bioRxiv preprint using passive acoustic telemetry to show migratory connectivity of pelagic predators.

name: University of Sharjah
summary: University listed by first authors of a 2024 machine learning poacher detection paper, from Electrical Engineering, and a 2021 GISTAM paper on remote sensing of invasive Prosopis juliflora in Sharjah.

name: Zayed University
summary: University listed by first authors of a 2024 Landsat 8 mangrove mapping paper for Eastern Lagoon National Park, from Natural and Health Sciences, and a 2019 book chapter on drone-based vegetation assessment.

name: Afghan Geodesy and Cartography Head Office
summary: The Afghan government's national cartographic agency, as described by Wikipedia.

name: Annual land cover for Afghanistan
summary: A 2024 paper recorded in OpenAlex describes annual land cover for Afghanistan derived from Google Earth Engine and Landsat imagery, with a first author listed at ICIMOD in Kathmandu.

name: Conservation of Snow Leopards and their Critical Ecosystems in Afghanistan
summary: GEF-financed project run by the WCS Afghanistan Program, which began in July 2019; UNDP's midterm review suggested a camera-trap AI index as a possible indicator.

name: Conservation Organisation for Afghan Mountain Areas
summary: A non-profit founded in 2010 that, in its April 2013 report to the Rufford Foundation, said it was running the first camera-trap mammal survey of the proposed Shah Foladi protected area.

name: Department of Biology, Faculty of Education, Baghlan University
summary: University biology department whose affiliation appears on a 2025 salamander distribution modelling paper, run in MaxEnt, and on a 2022 OpenAlex-recorded paper estimating emissions and removals from Afghan forest area change.

name: Department of Geography, Parwan University
summary: A university department whose affiliated first author appears on a 2024 paper, recorded in OpenAlex, assessing vegetation in Yakawalang against precipitation using satellite data and remote sensing.

name: Department of Urban Planning, Kabul Polytechnic University
summary: A university department whose affiliated first author appears on a 2022 paper, recorded in OpenAlex, using Landsat imagery to study the Kajaki Dam's effect on vegetation cover in the surrounding basin.

name: Establishing Conservation Management for Paghman Stream Salamander (Afghanodon mustersi)
summary: A closed project on the Paghman River, funded by the Rufford Foundation and dated 28 March 2017, whose November 2018 final report said the salamander was still present in its habitat and elsewhere.

name: Establishing integrated models for protected areas and their co-management in Afghanistan
summary: Closed GEF-financed project run by the WCS Afghanistan Program from April 2014 to April 2019; its terminal evaluation records the snow leopard monitoring target as achieved.

name: Freshwater Biodiversity in Kabul River: Assessment of Fish Diversity, Distribution and Threats to Conservation
summary: A closed project in Kabul, funded by the Rufford Foundation and dated 29 April 2019, that assessed fish diversity at six sampling sites along an altitudinal gradient and planned permanent sampling plots.

name: Integrating Education and Research: A Holistic Approach to Conserving Endangered newt, Afghanodon mustersi in Afghanistan's Fragile Ecosystems
summary: A project in Afghanistan, with an $8,300 grant awarded on 7 July 2025 to a Baghlan University recipient, whose stated objectives include field surveys for new localities and a population monitoring framework.

name: International Waterbird Census in Afghanistan
summary: An active counting programme in which Afghanistan rejoined the International Waterbird Census in January 2026, with counts at six sites along the Kabul River and Amu Darya floodplains recording wintering waterbirds and habitat conditions.

name: Inventory of Frog Diversity and Monitoring for Habitat Conservation in Nangarhar Province
summary: A project on frog diversity inventory and monitoring in Nangarhar Province, listed by the Rufford Foundation under Shahidullah Amn and dated 29 April 2019.

name: Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Livestock (Afghanistan)
summary: Afghan ministry to which, UNDP's 2021 midterm review says, responsibility for funding and carrying out on-the-ground management was delegated; it cooperated with NEPA on the snow leopard project.

name: National Environmental Protection Agency (Afghanistan)
summary: Afghan agency that released its Environment Status Assessment Report in Kabul in May 2026, reporting forest cover below two percent of the country's land.

name: National Statistics and Information Authority (Afghanistan)
summary: Afghan statistics body that, according to Pajhwok, used remote sensing and satellite imagery to report about 1.6 million hectares of forest, 2.54 percent of land area, for solar year 1404.

name: Parwan University
summary: University in Charikar with two OpenAlex-recorded papers: a 2024 satellite remote sensing assessment of vegetation and precipitation in Yakawalang, and a 2022 paper on salamander distribution in Afghanistan.

name: Sayed Jamaluddin Afghani University
summary: Afghan university whose affiliated first author wrote a 2025 paper, recorded in OpenAlex, on vegetation cover in Nuristan Province using remote sensing and GIS.

name: The Islamic Republic of Afghanistan Land Cover Atlas
summary: Land cover mapping dataset covering Afghanistan's 34 provinces and 5 basins, first prepared under a European Commission-funded project with FAO as executing agency, and updated in 2016 with FAO support.

name: Wakhan National Park
summary: National park whose head gave May 2026 survey counts of 77 Marco Polo sheep and 28 reported ibex; local officials reported a decline of over 38 percent.

name: Wildlife Conservation Society Afghanistan Program
summary: Country programme of the Wildlife Conservation Society, listed in CEPF's 2022 assessment for a $250,000 Wakhan National Park grant covering December 2020 to November 2022.

name: Antigua and Barbuda Environmental Information System
summary: National environmental information system reported in November 2021, built by Mona GeoInformatics Institute and Design + Environment Inc., GEF-funded and implemented through the Department of Environment, with visualisation of indicator status for monitoring and reporting.

name: Antigua Marine Conservation Programme
summary: Sea turtle nesting monitoring programme, run and built by the Environmental Awareness Group, which a 2024 presentation says launched in 2021 and counted 43 nests in 2022 and 66 in 2023.

name: Antigua seagrass blue carbon survey (Commonwealth Marine Economies Programme)
summary: National Oceanography Centre project using acoustic surveys and sediment coring on Antigua, with the Department of Environment, intended as the first quantitative assessment of its seagrass meadows' blue carbon potential.

name: Barbuda Benthic Habitat Map for Marine Spatial Planning
summary: Shapefile of Barbuda's benthic habitats for marine spatial planning under the 2013 Barbuda Blue Halo Initiative, classified from 2012 IKONOS-2 imagery using eCognition, and created by Sam Purkis.

name: Blue Halo Barbuda: Sustainable and comprehensive ocean and coastal management initiative
summary: Ocean and coastal management project in Barbuda, registered by the Government of Antigua and Barbuda with the Waitt Institute as partner from February 2013, whose ecological assessment reports fish surveys at 116 sites; no progress reports submitted.

name: Department of Environment (Antigua and Barbuda)
summary: Government environment department within the Ministry of Health, Wellness and the Environment, which a preprint says has the mandate for reporting under biodiversity agreements and undertakes some habitat mapping.

name: Enhancing Management, Monitoring and Enforcement: Nelson's Dockyard National Park's Marine and Coastal Ecosystems
summary: Closed project led by the National Parks Authority, funded by BIOPAMA with a 84,700 euro grant from June 2021 to May 2022, planning a patrol and survey vessel to support marine monitoring.

name: Enhancing Marine Ecosystem Management in the Nelson's Dockyard National Park
summary: Closed project led by the National Parks Authority and funded by the MEPA Trust, aiming to improve marine monitoring and benthic and bathymetry knowledge, and reported complete in March 2023 as a US$80,000 grant.

name: Environmental Awareness Group
summary: Antigua and Barbuda's oldest environmental NGO, founded in 1989, which in 2023 surveyed Antiguan racers on four offshore islands, where CEPF reports a fall from about 1,200 in 2016 to about 400.

name: Jumby Bay Hawksbill Project
summary: In 2005, it was described as Antigua and Barbuda's only sea turtle research project, focused on Pasture Bay Beach and funded by Jumby Bay Island Company.

name: Marine Ecosystem Protected Areas Trust Inc.
summary: Trust established in 2015 and described on its own site as meant to be a core national mechanism for financing local community environmental initiatives, which funded a National Parks Authority marine monitoring project.

name: Ministry of Health, Wellness and the Environment (Antigua and Barbuda)
summary: Includes the Department of Environment; in August 2025, its minister discussed moving the SIRF Fund into the National Conservation Trust Fund with a Caribbean Biodiversity Fund delegation.

name: National Parks Authority (Antigua and Barbuda)
summary: Statutory corporation, self-described as self-sustaining and not-for-profit, whose Environment Unit covers Nelson's Dockyard National Park and which conducted the 2020 mangrove wetland surveys with the Department of Environment.

name: Offshore Islands Conservation Programme
summary: Environmental Awareness Group programme that surveyed racer snakes on four offshore islands, as reported in December 2023, and received a CEPF grant from June 2012 to August 2014 covering 10 islands.

name: The Conservation of the Ferns of Antigua and Barbuda and their Forest Habitats
summary: Project dated 14 February 2011, partnered with the Environmental Awareness Group, which aimed to survey the status of the country's ferns and planned a National Conservation Plan and a National Fern Red List.

name: Advancing Marine Turtle Conservation: A Comprehensive Study of Nesting Habitats and Effective Protection Measures for Caretta caretta in Albania
summary: A closed project, listed by the Rufford Foundation in September 2023, that aimed to identify, map, protect and monitor marine turtle nesting sites in southern Albania, with fieldwork planned for June to November 2024.

name: Advancing Marine Turtle Conservation: A Comprehensive Study of Nesting Habitats and Effective Protection Measures for Caretta caretta in Albania
summary: Rufford-funded project run by PPNEA to map, protect and monitor loggerhead nesting sites in southern Albania; PPNEA reports four of seven Vlora nests succeeded between June and September 2024.

name: Albania National Forest and Pasture Inventory
summary: A continuing national inventory run by the National Forestry Agency, using Open Foris, with 1,100 sampling plot clusters and an eight-year cycle covering a quarter of forest area every two years.

name: Albania-1 and Albania-2 satellites
summary: Two satellites built by Satellogic, reported by bne IntelliNews as launched on 3 January 2023, which the government planned to use against illegal logging and wildfires, with Satellogic to train specialists.

name: Albanian Bird Ringing Scheme
summary: A bird ringing programme in Albania, part of EURING and run by the Albanian Ornithological Society with a national network of ringers, which reported 216 birds of 16 species ringed in one week in October 2023.

name: Albanian Forest Information System
summary: ALFIS, run by the National Forestry Agency, aims to manage geo-information and data on the forest and pasture fund and can publish forest maps and monitoring information, hosted at the National Agency for the Information Society.

name: Albanian Ornithological Society
summary: A self-described national, voluntary, non-profit organisation that partners on a reed-bed project involving faunistic observations and bird banding to develop long-term monitoring of Albanian reed beds.

name: AOS monitoring of breeding waterbirds in Albania's main wetlands
summary: A monitoring programme run by the Albanian Ornithological Society on breeding waterbirds in Albania's main wetlands, continuing work begun in 1995, with 85 Dalmatian pelican pairs counted in one colony in 2020.

name: Artificial Water Reservoirs as Essential Habitats for Tetrapods
summary: Active Rufford-listed study (page dated 10 March 2025) in Shijak, Albania, monitoring tetrapods by birdwatching, audio recording and camera traps, aiming to inform an update of the Territorial Strategy of Shijak.

name: Assessing the Status of Crayfish of Jabllanice National Park, Albania
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project ($19,190, September 2023 to October 2024), with grantee Biologist of Albania, to assess two Jabllanice crayfish species and develop Albania’s crayfish monitoring manual.

name: Atlas of Breeding Birds in Albania
summary: A breeding bird atlas programme run by the Albanian Ornithological Society, under way in the Elbasan region in May 2017 with plans to continue in other regions, to show species distribution and abundance.

name: BioNNA, the Biodiversity National Network of Albania
summary: A national biodiversity database that IUCN reported in May 2019 was used daily by rangers in Albania, and which was the subject of a data paper published in March 2018.

name: Conservation of Critical Habitats of Moustached Warbler (Acrocephalus melanopogon) in Albania
summary: A Rufford Foundation-funded project, listed in April 2016, that aims at a baseline study of Albanian reed beds and their role for migratory birds, especially the moustached warbler.

name: Department of Geography, Faculty of History and Philology, University of Tirana
summary: A university department that OpenAlex links to two 2025 papers on Divjakë-Karavasta National Park, one using GIS and remote sensing for forest health and one on drone use.

name: EcoAlbania - Center for Protection of Natural Ecosystems in Albania
summary: Tirana-based environmental NGO that began CEPF-supported Albanian water frog fieldwork in Vlora Bay in 2019 and reports preliminary analysis of 2026 fieldwork samples at Vjosa Research Center.

name: Effective Conservation and Research of Threatened Sharks, Skates and Rays through Rescue, Rehabilitation, Tagging and Re-Introduction
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project in Vlorë whose November 2022 page planned shark, skate and ray rescue and re-introduction, describing acoustic telemetry as a first for the eastern Adriatic.

name: Establishing a Long-Term Bird Monitoring Scheme in Albania: First International Census Plot 2024
summary: A project on establishing a long-term bird monitoring scheme in Albania, with a first international census plot in 2024, listed on the projects page of the Albanian Ornithological Society, which runs it.

name: Ethnoconservation of the Greek Meadow Viper and sustainable human use of alpine habitats in the Albanian Highlands
summary: A $3,810 grant awarded in April 2015, whose recipient reports data from over 200 vipers across Albania and Greece and a model predicting 90% habitat loss by century’s end.

name: EU4Forests (Albania)
summary: A project run by UNDP and the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation which, UNDP says, will modernise ALFIS through GIS-based monitoring, digital data management and AI-supported wildfire risk assessment.

name: EU4Nature (Albania)
summary: Run by UNDP and the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation, it uses camera traps and drones, UNDP says; ten pilot protected areas averaged 36.53% on METT-4.

name: Exploration of potential nesting sites and design of conservation measures for sporadic nesting in Albania
summary: Closed 2018 to 2019 project run by MEDASSET and funded by the MAVA Foundation that assessed Albanian beaches for turtle nesting using transects and drone images, with drone work continuing afterwards.

name: Faculty of Forestry Sciences, Agricultural University of Tirana
summary: A university faculty listed as the affiliation of three authors of a 2022 paper on remote sensing and GIS for burned areas and severity in Dajti Mountain National Park.

name: ILIRIA – Protection and Social & Environmental Development Association
summary: Albanian association whose specialists prepared a plant monitoring manual describing wide-area monitoring with drones and satellite images; Tour du Valat describes it as an NGO doing reforestation near Divjaka-Karavasta in 2026.

name: International Waterbird Census in Albania
summary: A waterbird count that AOS called Albania’s longest-running monitoring programme in January 2025, with 34 wetland complexes planned for that month.

name: Ministry of Environment (Albania)
summary: The environment ministry in Tirana, which coordinated Albania's 2026 International Waterbird Census with the National Agency of Protected Areas, using 34 monitoring points on 17 and 18 January 2026.

name: National Agency of Protected Areas (Albania)
summary: A protected-areas agency created by a 2015 Council of Ministers decision, which hosts an ILIRIA manual on plant monitoring that covers drones and satellite images, and which helped coordinate the 2026 waterbird census.

name: National Environment Agency (Albania)
summary: An agency with its central office in Tirana that draws up the National Environmental Monitoring Programme every year, whose 2023 edition lists biodiversity monitoring stations and stresses migratory bird monitoring.

name: National Environmental Monitoring Programme (Albania)
summary: Annual programme drafted and run by Albania's National Environment Agency; the 2023 edition covers biodiversity monitoring stations, a migratory bird network and forest genetic resources, using contracted universities and laboratories.

name: National Forestry Agency (Albania)
summary: The agency responsible for the methodology and leadership of the national forest inventory, which runs both the inventory and the Albanian Forest Information System.

name: Nationwide Balkan lynx camera-trap monitoring in Albania
summary: A nationwide camera-trap study run by PPNEA across 20 by 20 km grids, which in 2025 identified two individual Balkan lynx in Shebenik National Park.

name: NaturAL
summary: A closed project that IUCN says began in 2015 to support protected area management and a Natura 2000 network, training around 100 agency staff and giving a preliminary list of 43 proposed sites.

name: Nesting Under Pressure: Addressing Human and Natural Threats to Caretta caretta Nesting Success in Albania
summary: Active Rufford-listed project (page dated 25 August 2025) in the Vlora region, planning patrols, drone surveys and camera traps to record loggerhead nesting and study causes of nest failure, with PPNEA as partner.

name: Observation.org national bird portal for Albania
summary: A national bird data portal for Albania on the Observation.org platform, launched by the Albanian Ornithological Society at Divjaka-Karavasta National Park in 2025, with EuroBirdPortal reporting it was made possible by a LIFE reinforcement project.

name: PPNEA Egyptian vulture monitoring in Albania
summary: PPNEA-run monitoring of Egyptian vulture territories since 2013, using GPS tracking and camera traps; its 2020 to 2021 report says nine territories were occupied in Albania during 2020.

name: PPNEA forest monitoring with remote sensing in Albania
summary: PPNEA-run forest monitoring project that, per its 2023 report, checked field data against Google Earth imagery and Global Forest Watch data and concluded that combining both gives a fuller picture.

name: PPNEA jackal and brown bear monitoring in Albania under 4PETHABECO
summary: An active PPNEA project whose EU Delegation account describes jackal monitoring with playback and camera traps from 4PETHABECO, and a bear tracked over 100 kilometres into North Macedonia.

name: Protection and Preservation of Natural Environment in Albania
summary: A non-governmental organisation founded on 5 June 1991 and BirdLife International's national partner, which runs a nationwide Balkan lynx camera-trap monitoring programme with regional protected-area administrations.

name: Regional Administration of Protected Areas, Fier
summary: Regional protected-areas body created in 2015 that used drone photography to monitor a heron colony in Divjakë-Karavasta National Park within a JICA project and reports drone monitoring of Divjaka beach for turtles.

name: Research Center of Flora and Fauna
summary: A research centre whose experts monitored biodiversity indicators at 16 southern stations in 2015 and worked on Drin and Mat delta monitoring in 2013 for the National Monitoring Program.

name: Setting the foundation for a sustainable future for Buna River Protected Landscape
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project (1 July 2023 to 31 December 2024) run by PPNEA, whose final report says eDNA identified 31 fish species and the method was proposed for later fish monitoring.

name: Site Restricted Endemics of Prespa National Park, Albania: Assessment, Protection and In-situ/Ex-situ Conservation, through the Involvement of Young Professionals
summary: A closed CEPF-funded project from June 2020 to March 2022, aiming to monitor and conserve rare plants in the Dry Mountain and Galičica ranges and collect ten species’ data.

name: Spiny Butterfly Ray (Gymnura altavela) project, southern Adriatic Sea
summary: A project funded by a $6,059 grant that, according to the recipient, recorded five spiny butterfly rays off Vlore, suggesting a nursery area, and held more than 25 workshops for fishermen.

name: State Authority for Geospatial Information
summary: A public geospatial authority in Albania reporting fire maps supporting the National Civil Protection Agency, including a satellite-derived land-cover map for the Selishte fire in August 2026.

name: Support to the management of protected areas in the border region of Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia in monitoring of endangered species
summary: A closed 2019 to 2021 PPNEA project funded by GIZ, planning camera-trap training for regional stakeholders, with a technical report describing a three-country study using 18 cameras.

name: Sustainability, Threats, Presence and Habitat Use of the Mediterranean Monk Seal in Albania
summary: A closed CEPF-funded project from March 2019 to March 2021 to improve knowledge of Albanian coastal monk seal presence and habitat and establish a baseline on threats.

name: University of Tirana
summary: A university with a November 2019 project page on rare plants and invertebrates in Korçë, Berat and Vlorë, and a Department of Geography linked by OpenAlex to a 2025 forest health paper.

name: Wildlife Information Management System (Albania)
summary: A wildlife data system that IUCN reported in May 2019 was in place and used daily by rangers to collect and analyse wildlife data and assess biodiversity in Albania.

name: A.L. Takhtajan Institute of Botany
summary: Botany institute run by the National Academy of Sciences of Armenia; its GBIF record says its herbarium holds over 500,000 specimens and is being digitised.

name: ActiRS4ENV
summary: Project listed by the CENS GIS and remote sensing department, on introducing active remote sensing systems in geoecological research, listed as running from 2023 to 2028.

name: American University of Armenia
summary: University in Yerevan that runs the Acopian Center for the Environment and a GIS and Remote Sensing Lab, which mapped areas hit by the 2017 Khosrov Forest State Reserve fire.

name: Armenian Data Cube
summary: Remote-sensing repository for Armenia's landscapes, being developed by two national institutes and the University of Geneva in 2022, when it held the full Landsat and Sentinel-2 archive.

name: Armenian National Agrarian University
summary: University given as the affiliation of the first author of a 2024 paper assessing changes in NDVI and NDWI values in areas of rare plant species in Armenia.

name: Arpa Environmental Foundation
summary: Reported by Hetq in December 2019 to monitor the Arpa Protected Landscape with trap cameras and drones, with four rangers working daily against poaching.

name: AUA Acopian Center for the Environment
summary: Centre at the American University of Armenia, focused partly on biodiversity and conservation, that runs the Bird Monitoring Atlas to fill gaps in national breeding bird monitoring.

name: AUA GIS and Remote Sensing Lab
summary: Lab set up in 2017 at the American University of Armenia, which used Sentinel-2 data to map the area affected by the August 2017 Khosrov Forest State Reserve fire.

name: Biodiversity Study of Dilijan National Park
summary: NABU Armenia study of fish, birds, plants and large mammals in the park, announced with the Ministry of Environment and the park, meant to show species composition and distribution.

name: Bird Monitoring Atlas
summary: Project run by the AUA Acopian Center for the Environment that divides Armenia into 10 km squares, with field routes set up and a counting method piloted, to feed the European Breeding Bird Atlas.

name: BirdLinks Armenia
summary: Yerevan-based organisation founded in 2014 according to the Sigrid Rausing Trust, leading a project for Armenia's first breeding bird atlas, according to the European Bird Census Council.

name: Birds of Prey Research and Conservation Programme
summary: Within its birds of prey study, NABU Armenia fitted a satellite sensor to a lesser spotted eagle, a first for Armenia, to study local and migratory movements.

name: Cadastre Committee of the Republic of Armenia
summary: State body that lists cadastral, topographic and thematic cartography and a geographic information system among its activities, and says 2014 aerial photography allowed electronic cadastral maps to be made.

name: Caucasian Lynx Conservation and Research in Armenia
summary: Closed project that planned to estimate Caucasian lynx distribution and density by camera trapping on sampling grids along a large-mammal corridor in southern Armenia, with a final report listed in 2017.

name: Center for Ecological-Noosphere Studies of the National Academy of Sciences of Armenia
summary: National Academy of Sciences centre in Yerevan, co-developing the Armenian Data Cube in 2022, with a GIS department data science and machine learning group since 2022.

name: Chair of Cartography and Geomorphology, Yerevan State University
summary: University chair whose authors used Sentinel-2 imagery with NBR, NDVI and NDMI to detect and quantify forest loss in Syunik Region, in a paper published in August 2025.

name: Characterization of Dilijan National Park Forest Ecosystems (ESA EO Clinic EOC0004)
summary: Closed ESA EO Clinic project, run by GeoVille, whose final report delivers land cover maps for eight epochs between 1991 and 2019 to support characterising forest ecosystems in Dilijan National Park.

name: Conservation and Sustainable Management of Land Resources and High Value Ecosystems in Lake Sevan Basin for Multiple Benefits
summary: GEF-supported project, run by the Environmental Project Implementation Unit, that aims to strengthen biodiversity monitoring in Sevan National Park and reports six key biodiversity and bird areas mapped.

name: Conservation of the Leopard in Armenia
summary: Programme launched in 2002 by WWF and the Ministry of Nature Protection, with long-term leopard and prey monitoring; recorded leopards rose from zero or one in 2002 to 2012 to eight adults and two cubs in 2021.

name: Eco-Corridor Fund for the Caucasus (ECF) in Armenia
summary: Run by WWF-Armenia with the Ministry of Environment, the programme includes Gndasar, where WWF-Armenia reports a new leopard recorded on 9 and 13 October 2026.

name: EcoServ (ecosystem services and citizen science in the Hrazdan River basin, Armenia)
summary: Active project on ecosystem services and citizen science in Armenia's Hrazdan River basin, reporting school bioindication work, a July 2025 summer school, and a cultural ecosystem services framework tested in Dilijan National Park.

name: Ecosystem Accounting in Armenia: Setting the Scene
summary: Active project, June 2024 to November 2026 per IOER, aiming to build a prototype of national ecosystem accounting in Armenia to SEEA-EA standards, funded by the German Federal Ministry for the Environment.

name: eDNA Metabarcoding to Advance Funga Research
summary: Closed project applying eDNA metabarcoding to Armenia's fungal biodiversity, with a pilot in Dilijan National Park, where samples of lichens, fungi, soil and bark were collected in October 2025.

name: Environmental Project Implementation Unit
summary: State agency under the Ministry of Environment, associated with the GEF project on land resources and ecosystems in the Lake Sevan basin.

name: Erebuni State Reserve
summary: Established in 1981, covering 118.75 ha and subordinate to the Ministry of Environment, it monitors wild wheat continuously and studies Red Book species, according to Ecolur in June 2026.

name: EU4BiodiversityinSevan: Enhancing Lake Sevan Ecosystem Restoration
summary: Three-year European Union funded initiative, implemented by UNDP from 15 May 2026 to 14 May 2029, expecting digital biodiversity monitoring tools and a forest cover assessment for the Lake Sevan basin.

name: Faculty of Geography and Geology, Yerevan State University
summary: University faculty given as the affiliation of the first author of a 2023 paper assessing floating aquatic vegetation change in Lake Sevan using Landsat imagery and vegetation indices.

name: Forest Guard
summary: Organisation described in 2019 as a smart IoT sensor system for detecting illegal logging, wildfire and illegal transport access, which received a STEP grant in November 2018 to develop a pilot.

name: ForestBerg
summary: Yerevan start-up at beta stage that describes a planned forest smart monitoring system, aimed at deforestation from forest fires and illegal logging.

name: Foundation for the Preservation of Wildlife and Cultural Assets
summary: Foundation whose entry reports AI cameras installed at Twin Lakes and Paruyr Sevak in 2026 to detect movement, smoke, possible fires, poaching and unauthorised entry.

name: GBIF Armenia
summary: Armenia's national node in GBIF, where the country is an associate participant, which has endorsed four data publishers including BirdLinks Armenia NGO.

name: Hydrometeorology and Monitoring Center
summary: State non-commercial organisation under the Ministry of Environment, working with FAO on the National Forest Monitoring and Assessment System project and expected to continue forest monitoring afterwards.

name: Institute for Informatics and Automation Problems of the National Academy of Sciences of Armenia
summary: National Academy of Sciences institute that, according to a 2022 report, was co-developing the Armenian satellite data cube.

name: Khosrov Forest State Reserve SNCO
summary: State reserve that does annual biodiversity research and camera-trap monitoring, and whose 2025 annual report says a leopard has been regularly recorded since January 2018.

name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Armenia
summary: Armenian government ministry with protected areas and agencies, including the Hydrometeorology and Monitoring Center, under it; it is listed as a convener of the Yerevan Tech for Biodiversity Monitoring Hub.

name: ML4GEO
summary: Project from 2020 to 2023, listed by the CENS GIS and remote sensing department, on building capacity to apply machine learning to geospatial data processing in geoecological research.

name: Monitoring Bezoar Goats and Pressure on Forest Ecosystems in Khosrov Forest State Reserve and Dilijan National Park
summary: Closed 12-month project in the Ararat and Tavush regions, funded by the Caucasus Nature Fund, that planned to train rangers to monitor bezoar goats and follow a monitoring plan.

name: NABU Armenia
summary: Organisation that checks camera traps in Ijevan Reserve, Dilijan National Park and Syunik, and is testing AI-powered camera traps with Wildlife Protection Solutions in Yeghegis, where it says they identify bears instantly.

name: National Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Armenia
summary: Armenia's national academy lists the Center for Ecological-Noosphere Studies, whose academy profile describes a spatial data infrastructure giving open access to map data.

name: Publishing the first atlas on breeding birds of Armenia
summary: Active project, led by BirdLinks Armenia and funded by the European Bird Census Council, to produce Armenia's first breeding bird atlas from more than two decades of monitoring data on 242 species.

name: Scientific Center of Zoology and Hydroecology
summary: Armenian research centre, set up by government decision in 2006, that studies Lake Sevan cyanobacteria blooms, is working on an ecological model of the lake from data since 1933, and holds the country's largest entomological collection according to GBIF.

name: SEVAMOD2 - Building up science-based management instruments for Lake Sevan, Armenia
summary: Funded from April 2020 to March 2024, mostly by Germany's research ministry, the project aimed to use satellite remote sensing and eutrophication modelling, with monthly Lake Sevan sampling.

name: Sevan National Park SNCO
summary: Park of about 147,456 hectares whose management requires monitoring of biodiversity, water quality, land use and forests, and whose research head says tools from a partner project are used for monitoring and surveying.

name: Smart Birdwatching: Urban Nature Through the Eyes of Youth
summary: Active project, run by Sunchild NGO with Ucom, in which ten BirdBuddy smart feeder cameras in Armenian schools and communities let students watch birds live and identify species using artificial intelligence.

name: Support the establishment of a National Forest Monitoring and Assessment System in Armenia
summary: Swiss-funded, FAO-run project, agreed on 30 April 2026, that plans to combine field data collection with remote sensing and GIS to produce forest data in Armenia.

name: Ucom
summary: Organisation that supported installing an AI monitoring camera in the Twin Lakes area and provided connectivity and server infrastructure to store data from an AI camera system in Paruyr Sevak.

name: White Stork Project (AUA Acopian Center for the Environment)
summary: Completed project run by the AUA Acopian Center in which villagers recorded stork arrivals, departures and fledglings, over 500 families took part, and 284 nestlings were ringed.

name: White Stork Research and Conservation Programme
summary: Run by NABU Armenia since 2020, the programme holds nest coordinates, counts adults and chicks, records pollution, and reportedly included ringing and satellite sensors in the Ararat valley.

name: Winter Bird Count (AUA Acopian Center for the Environment)
summary: Winter bird count in Yerevan Botanical Garden, organised by the Acopian Center with volunteers, which aims to monitor bird species, numbers and length of stay; the page gives 2005 as its start, with no end date.

name: WWF-Armenia
summary: Conservation organisation that runs a leopard programme; it says its trail cameras detect at least six adult leopards and lists EarthBeat-supported data collection among its activities.

name: Yeghegis AI camera trap and bear deterrent test
summary: Run by NABU Armenia with partner Wildlife Protection Solutions, the Yeghegis bear camera trap and deterrent test could, NABU says, lead to wider use in Armenia if successful.

name: Yerevan State University
summary: University that publishes the Proceedings of the YSU C, which carried a 2025 remote-sensing study of forest change by authors from its Chair of Cartography and Geomorphology.

name: Yerevan Tech for Biodiversity Monitoring Platform
summary: COP17 presidency flagship initiative presented in October 2026 and led by FAO and IUCN; the minister said it aims to help countries strengthen monitoring using technologies from satellites to AI.

name: Angolan giraffe reintroduction to Bicuar National Park
summary: Reintroduction project in Bicuar National Park that has completed its first phase, bringing a founder population of 12 Angolan giraffe from Namibia, all fitted with solar-powered GPS satellite trackers; the Giraffe Conservation Foundation built it.

name: Associação de Conservação do Ambiente e Desenvolvimento Integrado Rural
summary: Self-described locally led NGO based in Menongue, training community wildlife monitors and rangers and facilitating community wildlife data collection mainly at Luengue Luiana National Park.

name: Avifauna do Parque Nacional da Quiçama
summary: Bird dataset of 66 species from Quiçama National Park, drawn from data gathered during a mammal survey by INBAC and the RWCP Angolan team between June and September 2017, with INBAC listed by GBIF as publisher.

name: Bioconserv
summary: Angolan NGO working mainly with wetland birds, which coordinated Angola's 2020 waterbird count and, per EcoAngola, helped identify over 30 sites important to migratory birds; it drew up a management plan for Ilhéu dos Pássaros, awaiting approval in October 2020.

name: Fundação Cuerama
summary: According to RTP, a foundation named after its Cuanza Sul village base, mapping pangolin and trafficking areas, with over 50 pangolins rescued since 2024.

name: Fundação Kissama
summary: Foundation working with World Land Trust and others on Angolan conservation, including forest elephant distribution work from 2019, Projecto Nzau, and Morro do Moco forest conservation since 2022.

name: Gabinete de Gestão do Programa Espacial Nacional
summary: Office established in 2013 under MINTTICS to manage the National Space Programme, launching Observa+ in June 2026, with ANGEO-1 launch attendance reported by Space in Africa.

name: GBIF Angola
summary: Country node for Angola in GBIF, a voting participant, which lists INBAC as a publisher endorsed by the node.

name: Giraffe tagging in Luengue-Luiana National Park, 2025
summary: In 2025, Giraffe Conservation Foundation ran tagging of eight South African giraffe in Angola’s Luengue-Luiana National Park under Twiga Tracker Initiative, sharing GPS data through EarthRanger and Movebank.

name: Impact of Armed Conflict on Angola’s Threatened Mammals and Their Post-Conflict Recovery
summary: Project that plans drone surveys, including thermal imaging where suitable, to detect threatened mammals, combining occupancy and abundance models with spatial layers on conflict legacies such as mine contamination.

name: Instituto de Desenvolvimento Florestal
summary: Public body under the Ministry of Agriculture and Forests that coordinates forest, wildlife and rural policy, and was designated in FAO's 2009 field guide as the coordinating institution for Angola's national forest inventory.

name: Instituto Geográfico e Cadastral de Angola
summary: Government body overseen by the Ministry of Public Works and Territorial Planning, acting as national mapping and cadastre authority and developing the National Geographic Information System, based in Luanda.

name: Instituto Nacional da Biodiversidade e Áreas de Conservação
summary: Public institution under Angola's Ministry of Environment, set up in 2011, that manages the national protected areas network, monitors wildlife and publishes 2017 Quiçama National Park datasets.

name: Instituto Superior de Ciências da Educação da Huíla
summary: Public higher education institute with its seat in Lubango, Huíla province, defined by a 2021 presidential decree, and named as owner of the 2021 vegetation-plot database of Huíla's woody species.

name: Instituto Superior Politécnico Tundavala
summary: Institute whose team, with Wits and Edinburgh, sampled herbaceous vegetation and set up microclimate transects at Bicuar in February 2024, according to a Global Grassy Group post.

name: Inventário Florestal Nacional de Angola
summary: National forest inventory begun in 2009 with FAO support, described in a 2022 decree as Angola's first with national coverage; its first of three phases was completed in 2015, with further data collection planned.

name: Iona NP - Wildlife Collaring
summary: Wild Wonderful World supported wildlife collaring in Iona National Park, where the team collared 8 oryx, 8 Hartmann's mountain zebra and 16 springbok to study desert use.

name: Levantamento de Mamíferos do Parque Nacional da Quiçama - INBAC/RWCP - 2017
summary: Camera-trap dataset from an INBAC survey of large and medium mammals, with field work from June to October 2017; some data is embargoed until fully processed.

name: Ministério do Ambiente
summary: Angola's environment ministry, which supervises INBAC; its minister coordinated a 3 November 2026 commission meeting that recommended doubling the Giant Sable Antelope sanctuary to 80 square kilometres.

name: National Geographic Okavango Wilderness Project
summary: Project funded by the National Geographic Society; Wild Bird Trust says its research has documented more than 50 species new to science, and it underlies Fundação Kissama's internship programme.

name: Otchiva
summary: Mangrove monitoring project across Angola's coastal provinces using satellite and drone imagery; a 2023 paper reports over 65 degradation alerts between July 2020 and June 2022.

name: Parque Nacional do Luengue-Luiana
summary: National park where Peace Parks Foundation reported training 15 rangers and two advisors in SMART and CyberTracker in 2018, and where the Ministry reports 25 animal collars with remote monitoring planned.

name: Portal de Serviços do GGPEN – Aplicações Espaciais
summary: Space applications service portal run by the national space programme office, offering satellite-based land use mapping and change detection using deep learning and machine learning, plus optical and radar services for uses such as farming and deforestation.

name: Programa de Monitorização das Aves Aquáticas e Migratórias
summary: INBAC's regular waterbird and migratory bird monitoring programme, studying distribution, habitat change and population trends to feed Angola's International Waterbird Census report; INBAC's page gives conflicting coastal census totals.

name: Projecto de Conservação da Palanca Negra Gigante
summary: Project begun in 2003 and run by Fundação Kissama, studying surviving giant sable in Cangandala National Park and the Luando reserve; results include GPS and VHF collaring, remote monitoring and six censuses, with 26 animals collared in 2013.

name: Projecto Kitabanga
summary: Project since 2003 run by Agostinho Neto University's biology department; World Land Trust says it works directly on 104 km of coast, about 6% of Angola's coastline.

name: Projecto Nzau
summary: Forest elephant project led by Fundação Kissama, with BIOPOLIS reporting US$1.2 million from the Elephant Crisis Fund for expansion from three to eight provinces where they may persist.

name: Strengthen Management and Climate Change Resilience in Angola's Conservation Areas for Sustainable Development
summary: Project led by Conservation International and run by INBAC, funded by the Global Environment Facility, launched in March 2025 and covering Luengue-Luiana and Iona national parks.

name: Sustainable Human-Wildlife Coexistence
summary: Closed three-year project, started in 2020 and run by Biopolis-CIBIO with TotalEnergies Angola funding, which planned camera traps, genetic monitoring, metabarcoding and GPS tracking to document threatened mammals in Bicuar National Park and Cuatir Private Reserve.

name: Universidade Agostinho Neto
summary: University whose Faculty of Sciences includes a biology department, according to Fundação Kissama's account of Projecto Kitabanga.

name: Vegetation-Plot Database of Woody Species of Huíla
summary: Database of woody species diversity, abundance and diameter (DBH over 5 cm) from Huíla woodlands, described as the first of its kind there and listed in 2021 as AF-AO-001.

name: Wild Bird Trust
summary: Public benefit organisation registered in Johannesburg; its Angola page reports camera trap surveys in the source lake regions confirming four large carnivores, and cites National Geographic Okavango Wilderness Project research documenting over 50 species new to science.

name: Administración de Parques Nacionales
summary: Argentine national parks body with a conservation mission for protected areas, which runs a biodiversity information system receiving national deforestation alerts every two weeks since November 2021.

name: Administración del Parque Provincial Ischigualasto
summary: A self-governing entity of the San Juan provincial government, created by Law 7474, which assigns the coordinator responsibility for the administrative and technical staff, rangers and guides of Ischigualasto Provincial Park.

name: Administración del Área Natural Protegida Península Valdés
summary: A body created in 2001 under Chubut law that says it administers the Península Valdés Natural Protected Area, and implements the management plan jointly with the Ministry of Tourism and Protected Areas.

name: Agencia de Áreas Protegidas de la Provincia de Salta
summary: A Salta provincial agency created by Decree 1849 of 3 May 2010 as the authority responsible for applying Law 7107, which established the Provincial System of Protected Areas.

name: Agencia Provincial de Ordenamiento Territorial (Mendoza)
summary: A provincial land-use planning agency identified as Mendoza’s focal point for the UNDP project in March 2022.

name: AI multi-class fauna classification for camera-trap photos (Tierra del Fuego)
summary: Tierra del Fuego work on AI multi-class fauna classification in camera-trap photos, known from a 2025 preprint listed in OpenAlex, one co-author of which is affiliated with CADIC-CONICET in Ushuaia.

name: ArgentiNat
summary: Argentina's national iNaturalist portal, run by Fundación Vida Silvestre Argentina since 2019, which La Nación reported had reached one million verifiable observations from 16,000 people by April 2023.

name: ArOBIS Centro Nacional Patagónico
summary: Argentine node of the Ocean Biogeographic Information System, according to GBIF's registry, which publishes datasets on GBIF including satellite-tracked locations of southern elephant seals from Península Valdés.

name: Asociación Argentina de Consorcios Regionales de Experimentación Agrícola
summary: Non-profit civil association led by agricultural business owners, working since 1960, which lists InBioAgro as a flagship project and, per GBIF's registry, will train stakeholders in biodiversity monitoring.

name: Asociación de Comunidades Aborígenes Lhaka Honhat
summary: A civil association founded to organise the struggle for recognition of Indigenous communities' territory in Salta, for which the Inter-American Commission in 2012 recommended handing over 400,000 hectares without fragmentation.

name: Asociación Gaia
summary: An association that says it manages and protects the Reserva Natural Quebrada del Agua, has worked since 1991 to regenerate human culture in harmony with living systems, and teaches permaculture.

name: Asociación para la Protección del Patrimonio Natural del Partido del Pilar
summary: An association founded on 19 August 2003 that was ordered by the Honorable Concejo Deliberante to manage the Pilar reserve, and in 2009 obtained its first park ranger.

name: Autoridad de Cuenca Matanza Riachuelo
summary: ACUMAR, a basin authority that states its mission is the comprehensive recovery (recomposición integral) of the Matanza Riachuelo basin.

name: Aves Argentinas
summary: Non-profit founded in 1916 and BirdLife Partner in Argentina, working on the study and conservation of wild birds and their habitats; GBIF's registry records 99 datasets published by it.

name: Big Cat Brother
summary: Project describing itself as a network of low-power connected edge devices built to mitigate the main causes of jaguar deaths, with the site also sharing knowledge on edge computing and tinyML.

name: BioTagLab
summary: Organisation that says it develops, from Argentina, its own technology turning wildlife movements into information, and offers 4G/LTE and satellite trackers configured to weight, environment and scientific objective.

name: Bosques de Agua
summary: An organisation that buys and protects land in the Córdoba Sierras Grandes, with 709 hectares now under its reserve model and an aim to restore 30,000 hectares of native forest and grassland.

name: Campaña de anillado del Playero Rojizo, Bahía de San Antonio
summary: Annual red knot ringing project begun in 2003, whose April 2014 campaign caught 219 birds, 30 of them recaptures, with simultaneous shorebird censuses and Río Negro environment staff taking part.

name: Campaña de monitoreo de cetáceos en el norte del Golfo San Matías
summary: Closed seasonal cetacean monitoring campaign in the north of the Golfo San Matías, started in September 2026 and run by two foundations, following a June campaign that made seven hydrophone recordings at four sites.

name: Censo Binacional de Yaguaretés
summary: Active binational jaguar census; Última Hora reports about 260 camera traps will track jaguars on the border until February 2027, after the 2024 census estimated about 110 jaguars.

name: Centro de Estudios Territoriales, Ambientales y Sociales
summary: Organisation for interdisciplinary socio-environmental research supporting conservation and sustainable development, mainly in northern Argentina, listed as an associated institution of the Red de Bosques Andinos.

name: Centro de Investigaciones del Bosque Atlántico
summary: Civil association listed by CONICET in June 2017 among members of the Subcomisión Selva Paranaense for jaguar conservation.

name: Centro de Investigación Científica y de Transferencia Tecnológica a la Producción
summary: Member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps MapBiomas says are the work of 25 institutions and professionals from across the country.

name: Centro de Investigación y Extensión Forestal Andino Patagónico
summary: Member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps MapBiomas says are the work of 25 institutions and professionals from across the country.

name: CIARA (Argentine Edible Oil Association)
summary: Argentine edible oil association discussed in Dialogue Earth's 2023 report on VISEC, described as a three-year project launched in May 2022.

name: Clementina Patagónica
summary: Programme centralising drone surveys and derived products for comparable environmental monitoring, publishing each survey under a CC-BY 4.0 licence and open formats, applying the FAIR and CARE frameworks.

name: Comisión Nacional Asesora para la Conservación y Utilización Sostenible de la Diversidad Biológica
summary: Advisory commission that reviewed and updated Argentina's National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan in 2023 and 2024, and is compiling information for the seventh national biodiversity report to the CBD.

name: Comisión Nacional de Actividades Espaciales
summary: National space agency that develops its own satellites, completed the two SAOCOM 1 radar satellites launched in 2018 and 2020, and builds and runs the Montes forest monitoring system.

name: Comunidad Mapuche Cayún
summary: A Mapuche community reported in August 2024 as one of seven taking part in co-management of Lanín National Park, whose lonko said it won recognition of its territorial right from National Parks.

name: Comunidad Mapuche Wiritray
summary: A Mapuche community settled on the shore of Lake Mascardi, reported by Río Negro in August 2024 as one of seven taking part in co-management of Nahuel Huapi National Park.

name: Comunidad Mbya Guaraní Ysyry
summary: A Mbya Guaraní community in Misiones for which the vice-governorship reported a special power to issue land deeds, alongside a second community spelt Aguai Poty and Aguay Poty on the same page.

name: Confederación Mapuce de Neuquén
summary: A body representing the Mapuce people that took part in the process leading to Lanín National Park co-management and was represented on the July 2000 committee.

name: Consejo Agrario Provincial de Santa Cruz
summary: A Santa Cruz provincial body that the 2018 management plan names as the authority responsible for applying the plan, and where it lists a Director of Wildlife and Protected Areas.

name: Consejo Federal de Medio Ambiente
summary: Body that chairs the executive committee managing the Federal Protected Areas System, with Juan José Rivera, Chubut's environment secretary, as its president for 2026.

name: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas
summary: Argentine national research council headquartered in Buenos Aires; it announced in June 2018 joint funding with Fundación Bunge & Born for biological collection digitisation, and its researchers coordinate Snapshot Argentina.

name: Convocatoria Preservación y recuperación de colecciones de interés científico de Argentina (2017)
summary: Closed 2017 CONICET call for projects on preserving and recovering collections of scientific interest in Argentina, whose results CONICET published.

name: Copernicus Argentina
summary: Monitoring service for water and land that combines satellites, hydrometric and weather networks and forecast models into dashboards, alerts and reports; it states it is independent of the Copernicus programme and ESA.

name: Corporación Interestadual Pulmarí
summary: A corporation whose own site describes co-management as a forum for decisions on Mapuche territories in Lanín National Park, and which in July 2026 reported signing a concession contract after a public tender.

name: Corredor de los 5 Grandes
summary: Active strategic project promoted by the Río Negro environment secretariat with Fundación Por el Mar to protect marine habitats, with 2025 monitoring campaigns and a deep-water expedition in the Golfo San Matías described in October 2026.

name: Deep learning for large-scale plankton image classification (ICYTE and INIDEP)
summary: Deep learning study on large-scale plankton image classification, listed by OpenAlex as a 2025 paper with co-authors affiliated with INIDEP, Argentina's national fisheries research institute.

name: Deep learning model predicting genetic diversity from satellite imagery (IIMyC)
summary: Deep learning model linked to IIMyC, known from a 2021 paper listed in OpenAlex showing satellite imagery can predict genetic diversity and differentiation; its current status is unknown.

name: Dirección de Ambiente del Municipio de Mar Chiquita
summary: A municipal environment office whose director is named in a 2025 technical report on the reserve's management as representative of the Parque Atlántico Mar Chiquito Biosphere Reserve.

name: Dirección de Parques y Reservas de Corrientes
summary: A Corrientes body that Decree 1440/2009 names Authority of Application for the Iberá Natural Reserve and gives administration of the Parks and Reserves Fund created by Law 4736.

name: Dirección de Recursos Naturales Renovables de Mendoza
summary: A Mendoza provincial directorate whose team includes park rangers and technicians and which, according to IADIZA, signed a 2010 co-management agreement for the Ñacuñán Biosphere Reserve.

name: Dirección Regional Centro de la Administración de Parques Nacionales
summary: A regional directorate of the National Parks Administration which, in the biodiversity information system, has protected areas assigned to it including Talampaya, El Leoncito, San Guillermo, Traslasierra and Ansenuza.

name: Dirección Regional NEA de Conservación, Administración de Parques Nacionales
summary: A regional office of the national parks administration whose technicians, with Proyecto Yaguareté, identified a new male jaguar from camera-trap images in Río Pilcomayo National Park in 2025.

name: Dirección Regional Noroeste de la Administración de Parques Nacionales
summary: A regional directorate of the National Parks Administration which, in the biodiversity information system, has protected areas assigned to it including Calilegua, Copo, El Rey, Los Cardones and Baritú.

name: Dirección Regional Patagonia Austral de la Administración de Parques Nacionales
summary: A regional directorate of the National Parks Administration which, in the biodiversity information system, has protected areas assigned to it including Los Glaciares, Perito Moreno, Monte León and Tierra del Fuego.

name: Dirección Regional Patagonia Norte de la Administración de Parques Nacionales
summary: A regional directorate of the National Parks Administration which, in the biodiversity information system, has protected areas assigned to it including Lanín, Nahuel Huapi, Los Alerces, Lago Puelo and Lihué Calel.

name: Documenta Florae Australis
summary: Dataset developed by IBODA, built by Instituto de Botánica Darwinion, whose data make the Flora Vascular de la República Argentina possible and which the Flora Argentina page links for consultation.

name: eBird Argentina
summary: Argentine portal of eBird, set up in 2013 and run by Aves Argentinas, in which more than 18,800 users have reported 1,062 species in over 817,200 checklists.

name: EcoRegistros
summary: Describes itself as a database of living things started in 2011 holding over 2.5 million records, and says ÉRIA is trained exclusively on its database.

name: Eirú
summary: Founded by Argentine scientists according to Economía Sustentable, which reports initial SF-500 funding of USD 250,000; BCR Innova describes satellite imagery, bioacoustic sensors and AI for biodiversity monitoring.

name: Endangered deer monitoring with UAV imagery and deep learning (Universidad de San Andrés)
summary: Project known from a 2024 paper listed in OpenAlex on monitoring endangered deer with UAV imagery and deep learning, whose first author is affiliated with Universidad de San Andrés.

name: Escudo satelital de bosques (Misiones)
summary: Proposed bill, reported by Canal 12 Misiones as entering the provincial chamber, for a provincial system to detect deforestation, fires and environmental crimes using high-resolution imagery, thermal alerts and open data.

name: Facultad de Agronomía, Universidad de Buenos Aires
summary: University faculty listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps MapBiomas attributes to 25 institutions and professionals nationwide.

name: Facultad de Ciencias Forestales, Universidad Nacional de Misiones
summary: University faculty listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps MapBiomas attributes to 25 institutions and professionals nationwide.

name: Flora Vascular de la República Argentina
summary: Project led by Fernando Zuloaga that compiles information on Argentina's 10,000 vascular plant species, with thirteen printed volumes published covering 80% of recorded species, plus a continually updated electronic version.

name: Fonoteca Zoológica de la Universidad Nacional del Nordeste
summary: Bioacoustic recording archive at the Universidad Nacional del Nordeste, which GBIF's dataset record describes as holding 700 anuran vocalisations.

name: Fundación Bunge y Born
summary: Announced collection digitisation funding with CONICET under the 2017 call and joined the 2026 call, open 14 April–14 May 2026, offering up to 6,000,000 pesos per project.

name: Fundación Cethus
summary: Organisation that, with Fundación Por el Mar, carried out the September 2026 cetacean monitoring in the north of the Golfo San Matías and prepared the report on the June 2026 monitoring.

name: Fundación de Historia Natural Félix de Azara
summary: A foundation that says it is known for creating and putting in place natural reserves, and that its institutional document says has jointly managed the Güirá Oga wildlife centre with the Misiones Ministry of Ecology since 2005.

name: Fundación Federico Wildermuth
summary: A foundation that owns and administers the Federico Wildermuth conservation unit, a Santa Fe provincial reserve under Law 12175 that gained 350 hectares in 2008.

name: Fundación Greenpeace Argentina
summary: Argentine foundation that says its team uses satellite imagery, provincial geospatial data and software to measure clearings, draw polygons of cleared areas and produce annual deforestation reports.

name: Fundación Hábitat y Desarrollo
summary: A foundation founded in 1992 that shares administration of over 25 reserves covering more than 570,000 hectares, according to World Land Trust, and protects the Somuncurá Plateau Reserve with that trust's support.

name: Fundación Inalafquen
summary: Organisation whose Patricia González co-coordinated the red knot ringing project at Bahía de San Antonio, begun in 2003, in April 2014; its members took part in that campaign.

name: Fundación Macá Tobiano
summary: Uses environmental DNA, drones and artificial intelligence, with work including monitoring threatened species in Patagonian freshwater systems through environmental DNA.

name: Fundación Monte Alegre
summary: An NGO since 2024 that began as a project for a 97-hectare private forest reserve in Las Acequias, Córdoba, where a family chose to preserve a portion of Espinal and restore native forest.

name: Fundación Por el Mar
summary: Organisation that, with Fundación Cethus, carried out the September 2026 cetacean monitoring in the north of the Golfo San Matías and prepared the report on the June 2026 monitoring.

name: Fundación ProYungas
summary: According to GBIF, an NGO created in 1999 for conservation and territorial planning that installed 15 camera traps at Finca La Moraleja, Salta, in 2017.

name: Fundación Rewilding Argentina
summary: Foundation created in 2010 to protect and restore ecosystems; MisionesOnline reported in August 2023 that camera traps had confirmed at least 16 free-living jaguars in Iberá.

name: Fundación Temaikèn
summary: Foundation whose maned wolf rehabilitation was reported in July 2026: two wolves spent nine months there and carried GPS satellite collars to monitor their movement, adaptation and survival.

name: Fundación Vida Silvestre Argentina
summary: Argentine foundation associated with WWF that coordinates MapBiomas Argentina, is described by the national parks agency as representing iNaturalist and ArgentiNat, and uses camera traps at its Urugua-í reserve.

name: Fundación Villavicencio
summary: Administers and manages the Reserva Natural Villavicencio, a protected natural area of 60,654 hectares covering monte, cardonal and puna environments.

name: Fundación Williams
summary: Foundation that, with CONICET and Fundación Bunge y Born, announced funding for preserving, recovering and digitising scientific collections in a call open from 14 April to 14 May 2026.

name: Geosimple
summary: Describes using data science and remote sensing for agriculture and natural resources, including land cover mapping and forest carbon stocks, and belongs to the MapBiomas Argentina network.

name: Global Penguin Society
