summary: Organisation that monitors penguin populations, collecting data on population size, trends and breeding parameters, and whose site offers online tracking of penguin migration.

name: Gobierno de Neuquén
summary: Provincial government of Neuquén, which NoticiasNQN reported in December 2025 had 52 active wildlife cameras, 60 more ready to install, a planned total of 150, and an AI species-identification platform launched in 2025.

name: Gobierno de Río Negro
summary: Provincial government that announced satellite wildfire detection and monitoring across the province with OroraTech and GPTech, endorsing it as part of a regional strategy to modernise environmental protection.

name: GP Tech
summary: Company that OroraTech lists as its one local partner in Argentina, linked to two wildfire control centres in Bariloche and El Bolsón centred on OroraTech's Wildfire Solution.

name: Grupo de Estudios Ambientales, Instituto de Matemática Aplicada de San Luis
summary: Research group listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps MapBiomas says are the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: High-resolution acoustic and environmental dataset for monitoring Bombus dahlbomii
summary: 2025 data paper listed in OpenAlex on high-resolution acoustic and environmental data for monitoring Bombus dahlbomii, with Argentine co-authors at INIBIOMA, Universidad Nacional del Comahue and CONICET in Bariloche.

name: IDECOR
summary: Organisation that presented the third edition of Córdoba province's land cover and land use map, for 2022-2023, in December 2023, made from Sentinel-2 images with artificial intelligence classification.

name: Implementing Long-Term Biodiversity Monitoring Through RAPELD Methodology in Central Argentina
summary: A biodiversity monitoring project in central Argentina whose third phase, announced in May 2025, plans to compare vertebrate and invertebrate assemblages across five RAPELD modules and strengthen PPBio.

name: InBioAgro
summary: Active project designing biodiversity management strategies with CREA farmers and researchers; monitoring began on about 30 farms, and its first report in 2025 covered pilot farms in Buenos Aires province.

name: Instituto Argentino de Investigaciones de las Zonas Áridas
summary: Argentine arid-zones institute whose two doctoral fellows, Unidiversidad reports, gave technical support to MapBiomas Argentina Collection 1; specialists said they contributed land cover change analysis for the Monte and High Andes.

name: Instituto Argentino de Investigaciones de Zonas Áridas
summary: Argentine research institute listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps MapBiomas says were the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Instituto Argentino de Nivología, Glaciología y Ciencias Ambientales
summary: Argentine institute that carries out the National Glacier Inventory, coordinated by the Subsecretaría de Ambiente, and was quoted by MapBiomas on its new glacier maps.

name: Instituto de Altos Estudios Espaciales Mario Gulich
summary: Space studies institute created by CONAE and the Universidad Nacional de Córdoba, whose 2020 report lists research in machine learning, computer vision and data fusion, including vessel detection and wetland monitoring.

name: Instituto de Biología Subtropical
summary: Argentine institute whose scientists carried out jaguar monitoring at Iguaçu National Park, reported by CONICET in 2017, and which is a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network.

name: Instituto de Botánica Darwinion
summary: Botanical institute of CONICET and the National Academy of Exact, Physical and Natural Sciences, which developed the Documenta Florae Australis database and is a GBIF-endorsed data publisher.

name: Instituto de Ciencias de la Tierra, Biodiversidad y Ambiente
summary: Argentine research institute listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps MapBiomas says were the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Instituto de Conservación de Ballenas
summary: Whale conservation institute that, according to Meteored in September 2022, recorded 1,420 right whales in its annual photo-identification survey and held a catalogue of over 4,000 southern right whales.

name: Instituto de Ecología Regional
summary: Research institute of the Universidad Nacional de Tucumán and CONICET that reported testing AMI camera traps for moth monitoring in SABIOMA in May 2023.

name: Instituto de Geografía, Historia y Ciencias Sociales, UNCPBA
summary: Institute at UNCPBA listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps MapBiomas says were the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Instituto de Investigaciones en Biodiversidad y Medioambiente
summary: Bariloche institute of CONICET and Universidad Nacional del Comahue, listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network and the affiliation of co-authors of a 2025 Bombus dahlbomii acoustic data paper.

name: Instituto de Investigaciones en Recursos Naturales, Agroecología y Desarrollo Rural
summary: Argentine research institute listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps MapBiomas says were the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Instituto de Investigaciones Fisiológicas y Ecológicas Vinculadas a la Agricultura
summary: Argentine research institute listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps MapBiomas says were the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Instituto de Investigación para el Desarrollo Territorial y del Hábitat Humano
summary: Argentine research institute listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps MapBiomas says were the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Instituto Geográfico Nacional (Argentina)
summary: National mapping body in Buenos Aires that builds a national land cover map using supervised Random Forest classification in Google Earth Engine.

name: Instituto Misionero de Biodiversidad
summary: A biodiversity institute whose technicians, Misiones Online reported in April 2025, supported Proyecto Yaguareté researchers in capturing two jaguars, one fitted with a satellite collar; it belongs to the Selva Paranaense jaguar subcommission.

name: Instituto Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo Pesquero
summary: Argentine fisheries research institute that carried out 17 research campaigns and 252 days at sea in 2021, advises government on fishery resources, and offers satellite-derived environmental data.

name: Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria
summary: Argentine agricultural technology institute and MapBiomas Argentina member whose researchers used deep learning and machine learning to classify satellite images for 2000, 2010 and 2020.

name: Inventario Nacional de Bosques Nativos
summary: Active national programme whose second inventory used systematic sampling across seven forest regions, with permanent plots that can be remeasured and data meant to strengthen national forest monitoring.

name: Inventario Nacional de Glaciares
summary: Glacier inventory carried out by IANIGLA and coordinated by the Subsecretaría de Ambiente, whose first level records the number, location and area of ice bodies and is updated every five years.

name: Inventario Nacional de Humedales
summary: Wetland inventory promoted by the Subsecretaría de Ambiente with other bodies, structured in four spatial levels, with spatial databases and technical reports available on the Integrated Environmental Information System.

name: Laboratorio de Análisis Regional y Teledetección
summary: Remote sensing laboratory in the MapBiomas Argentina network, researching semi-arid Chaco transformations since 1976 and aiming to develop forest monitoring tools.

name: Laboratorio de Ciencias de las Imágenes, Universidad Nacional del Sur
summary: Image science laboratory at the Universidad Nacional del Sur researching AI wildlife surveys in Chubut, with project funding beginning in 2022 and cut at the end of 2023.

name: Land Innovation Foundation
summary: Fund that Dialogue Earth describes as set up by Cargill to seek solutions for deforestation and sustainable livelihoods, funding initiatives in the Gran Chaco.

name: Large-scale coastal marine wildlife monitoring with aerial imagery (Patagonia)
summary: 2025 paper listed in OpenAlex on large-scale coastal marine wildlife monitoring with aerial imagery in Patagonia, with one co-author at the Centro Nacional Patagónico, CONICET, in Puerto Madryn.

name: Mapa Nacional de Cobertura de Suelo (IGN)
summary: Land cover map of Argentina excluding Antarctica for 2021, with 13 categories across six regions, classified by Random Forest on Google Earth Engine at about 83% overall accuracy.

name: MapBiomas Argentina
summary: Network run by Fundación Vida Silvestre Argentina producing open Landsat maps, whose data Unidiversidad reported showed Argentina lost 7.6 million hectares of natural vegetation between 1998 and 2022.

name: Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación Productiva
summary: Argentine ministry that introduced the Sistema Nacional de Datos Biológicos in 2009, which ran until the end of 2020, and is listed in GBIF's registry as a dataset publisher.

name: Ministerio de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo de Río Negro
summary: Río Negro provincial ministry listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps are reported to be the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Ministerio de Ecología y Recursos Naturales Renovables de Misiones
summary: Misiones provincial ministry that runs the Observatorio Ambiental de Datos and organised the presentation of native forest monitoring results showing an 18% fall in deforestation in 2025 against the historical average.

name: Ministerio de Turismo y Áreas Protegidas del Chubut
summary: The provincial ministry created Parque Provincial Patagonia Azul, and in December 2024 Chubut had 46 active wildlife rangers across 16 protected areas and was recruiting more.

name: Modeling Scenarios of Agricultural Land Use Change in the Tropical Forest and Savannah Areas of Brazil and Argentina
summary: Closed project to model agricultural land use change in tropical forest and savannah areas of Brazil and Argentina, funded by a $478,249 Moore Foundation grant awarded in July 2013 to IFPRI.

name: Monitoreo de deforestación en el Chaco Seco
summary: Active joint effort of LART at the University of Buenos Aires, INTA and the Red Agroforestal Chaco Argentina, digitising clearings in the Chaco from Landsat images every year since 2000.

name: MonTeS (Monitoreo Temporal Satelital de los Bosques de Argentina)
summary: Developed by CONAE and BigPear and run by CONAE with IDB funding, the project aimed in November 2022 to map native forest cover and change online using satellite imagery.

name: Municipio de Tigre, Gestión Ambiental
summary: A municipal environmental management body in Tigre, where Monte Blanco Municipal Nature Reserve covers about 20 hectares and has biodiversity and environmental education programmes, an interpretation centre and trails.

name: Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales "Bernardino Rivadavia"
summary: Buenos Aires museum, an implementation unit of CONICET, where CONICET specialists and Argentine GBIF node members developed the national biodiversity data portal, reported in 2024 to hold over 17 million records.

name: Neuquén provincial wildlife camera network
summary: Wildlife camera network built by the Neuquén provincial government; NoticiasNQN reported in September 2026 that 170 cameras had been installed to monitor wild fauna in real time, the first such investment in 20 years.

name: Nodo Argentino de GBIF
summary: Argentine node of GBIF; CONICET reports it developed the Portal de Datos de Biodiversidad de Argentina at the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales with the country's data publishing institutions.

name: Observatorio Ambiental de Datos (Misiones)
summary: Active technical space run by the Misiones environment ministry, presented as centralising, processing and analysing strategic information for provincial environmental management, with the ministry saying it will allow more precise forest tracking.

name: Organismo Provincial para el Desarrollo Sostenible de Buenos Aires
summary: Provincial body that approved an enforcement protocol for Buenos Aires province's protected areas in Resolution 592/2019, after a 2018 resolution set a protocol for audiovisual productions in reserves.

name: Parque Nacional Baritú
summary: A national park where, by 2022, 25 camera traps had been installed for the national parks administration's jaguar monitoring in the Yungas.

name: Parque Nacional Calilegua
summary: A national park that recorded taruca on camera traps in August 2019, after three monitoring campaigns since 2017, and by 2022 had 25 camera traps installed for jaguar monitoring.

name: Parque Nacional Chaco
summary: Protected area among the north-east sites included in the Neotropical Waterbird Census reported in March 2019, carried out in February 2019 by APN rangers, fire crews and technicians.

name: Parque Nacional Ciervo de los Pantanos
summary: A national park hosting a research project that monitors fauna with camera traps, foot transects and drone surveys, and has produced a habitat map and an assessment of burnt areas.

name: Parque Nacional El Impenetrable
summary: Protected area among the north-east sites included in the Neotropical Waterbird Census reported in March 2019, carried out in February 2019 by APN rangers, fire crews and technicians.

name: Parque Nacional Iberá
summary: A national park included in the Neotropical Waterbird Census of north-east protected areas, which national parks rangers, fire crews and technicians carried out in February 2019.

name: Parque Nacional Iguazú
summary: A national park whose staff, as reported in March 2019, had sampled wildlife with camera traps since May 2018, producing more than 430 records from 15 cameras, including jaguar, puma and ocelot.

name: Parque Nacional Lago Puelo
summary: A national park where huemul population-tracking campaigns with camera traps took place in 2022, and whose huemul action plan for 2026-2036 is being updated.

name: Parque Nacional Lanín
summary: A national park whose Department of Conservation and Management carried out the Neotropical Waterbird Census in the park's water bodies in February 2014.

name: Parque Nacional Los Alerces
summary: A national park that ran regular camera-trap monitoring in 2022, particularly in the 21,000-hectare Cerro El Riscoso critical area, created in 2001 to protect a resident huemul population.

name: Parque Nacional Los Glaciares
summary: A national park where 17 camera traps were set on Cerro Polo in 2022 to study huemul home ranges; its updated 2026–2031 action plan was approved in 2026.

name: Parque Nacional Mburucuyá
summary: A national park included in the Neotropical Waterbird Census of north-east protected areas, which national parks rangers, fire crews and technicians carried out in February 2019.

name: Parque Nacional Nahuel Huapi
summary: A park monitoring huemul since 2021, with stations added in 2024, an action plan in preparation, and 14 waterbird sites surveyed within and nearby in February 2025.

name: Parque Nacional Perito Moreno
summary: A national park that extended its camera-trap network by 15 cameras in 2024, doubling the area monitored for huemul, and presented three years of distribution and abundance results in 2025.

name: Parque Nacional Río Pilcomayo
summary: A national park that set up joint camera-trap monitoring with Proyecto Yaguareté and the NEA regional office after jaguar signs were found in March 2024, and recorded a new male jaguar in 2025.

name: Patagonia Azul seabird live video monitoring
summary: Permanent monitoring project in Parque Provincial Patagonia Azul, built and run by CONICET, which Economía Sustentable reports records seabird breeding through live transmission from solar-powered stations with cameras.

name: Patrones espaciales y temporales de la regeneración de bosques en el Parque Chaqueño para el periodo entre 1998 y 2022
summary: A project run by the University of Buenos Aires agronomy faculty, partnered with FAO, planning to map native Chaco forest regeneration for 1998–2022 and design long-term monitoring.

name: Península Valdés aerial marine fauna detection model
summary: Deep learning model using aerial images to detect and count southern elephant seals and sea lions at Península Valdés, based on about 3,000 images from two flights in spring 2023.

name: Pixel
summary: NGO founded by scientists to address environmental problems with quantitative tools, remote sensing and AI, listing projects on Patagonian fires, near-real-time deforestation and wetlands.

name: Plataforma de Monitoreo de Fauna Silvestre (Neuquén)
summary: Wildlife monitoring platform built by the Province of Neuquén, reported by NoticiasNQN as launched in 2025, which identifies species from images sent by agents or citizens.

name: Portal de Datos de Biodiversidad de Argentina
summary: Open Argentine biodiversity portal based on GBIF hosted portals technology, developed with over 60 institutions, reportedly holding over 17 million records at its September 2024 launch.

name: Prefectura Naval Argentina
summary: Argentine maritime authority that says its Coast Guard System detected illegal Vanuatu-flagged fishing vessels in 2025 and 2026, and which uses Skylight, whose analytics Ai2 said helped validate one detection.

name: Programa de Conservación del Monumento Natural Huemul
summary: A huemul conservation programme created in 2002 by the national parks administration, updated in 2021, covering six Patagonian national parks, with shared camera-trap methods and a 2026 staff training course.

name: Proyecto GEF-PNUD 19/ARG/G24 (Mendoza)
summary: A GEF-funded, UNDP-partnered project in Mendoza that in March 2022 was assessing land degradation at a foothills pilot site, with baseline studies by IADIZA-CONICET and INTA and planned wetland inventories.

name: Proyecto monitoreo ecológico del proceso de restauración y recuperación del Iberá
summary: An ecological monitoring project on Iberá's restoration, run jointly by CONICET, APN and Fundación Rewilding Argentina, whose camera traps detected the first wild-born jaguar cub in Iberá in 2021.

name: Proyecto Quimilero
summary: Dry Chaco wildlife organisation active since 2015, whose members surveyed three peccary species over more than 54,000 square kilometres in Chaco, Salta and Formosa.

name: Proyecto Yaguareté
summary: Jaguar conservation programme run by CeIBA, whose 2024 survey with Brazil's Projeto Onças do Iguaçu covered over 570,000 hectares using 267 camera-trap stations.

name: Punta Tombo automated penguin monitoring system
summary: Remote data-logging system at Punta Tombo that, CONICET reported in June 2017, used a microchip-reading mat and a scale to detect and weigh penguins on trips to and from the sea.

name: Red Argentina de Datos y Colecciones Biológicas
summary: Network of institutions sharing primary biodiversity data openly, formed when members of the Argentine GBIF node continued after the Sistema Nacional de Datos Biológicos ended in 2020, and which produces the national biodiversity data portal.

name: Red Argentina de Reservas Naturales Privadas
summary: Network of private reserves and civil society organisations conserving private land, which gained legal status as a civil association in 2019 and, as reported by Ámbito in July 2024, had 111 reserves covering 223,000 hectares.

name: Red Federal Bosque-Clima
summary: Active network described by CONICET's forestry science network as a tool for monitoring forest growth in native forests, with 26 active stations in four areas, co-led by Ricardo Villalba and Ana Srur.

name: Red Subtropical de Parcelas Permanentes
summary: Programme of permanent forest plots studying long-term dynamics of north-western Argentine subtropical mountain forests; a September 2021 page reported 87 plots covering 82.4 ha and over 45,000 trees.

name: Red TICCA Territorios de Vida en Argentina
summary: A network focused on Indigenous conserved territories, whose founding charter was drafted at an October 2021 meeting of members from 33 communities, 14 peoples and 12 provinces.

name: Red Yaguareté
summary: Organisation monitoring jaguars at sites in northern Argentina, mainly where the species is confirmed, using camera traps as a main tool.

name: ReForest Latam
summary: Tucumán startup described by El Ecosistema Startup as combining drones and AI to reforest hard-to-reach areas, reportedly working in seven ecoregions in October 2026.

name: Regenerar Patagonia
summary: El Ecosistema Startup reports plans to restore over 200 hectares of fire-damaged araucaria forest in Lanín National Park during 2026–2027, joining Proyecto Pewen.

name: Remote Sensing Group, Instituto de Astronomía y Física del Espacio
summary: Research group whose 2019 paper used convolutional networks on EVI time series to detect breakpoints for online deforestation monitoring in the Chaco forest, followed by a 2020 lab paper on monthly deforestation prediction.

name: Reserva Natural Educativa Colonia Benítez
summary: Reserve among the north-east protected areas included in the Neotropical Waterbird Census reported in March 2019, carried out in February 2019 by APN rangers, fire crews and technicians.

name: Reserva Natural Estricta San Antonio
summary: Reserve among the north-east protected areas included in the Neotropical Waterbird Census reported in March 2019, carried out in February 2019 by APN rangers, fire crews and technicians.

name: Reserva Natural Formosa
summary: A reserve whose staff, alongside APN’s NEA office and Proyecto Yaguareté, had monitored jaguars since 2022, with 30 camera-trap stations and 18 records of one male by July 2024.

name: Río Negro satellite wildfire detection and monitoring
summary: Satellite wildfire detection and monitoring across 20 million hectares of Río Negro, built and run by GPTech using OroraTech data, with control centres inaugurated on 14 February 2026.

name: SABIOMA
summary: International Argentina–UK collaboration on nature-based solutions to biodiversity loss, climate change and social wellbeing, funded by UKRI; in May 2023 a partner institute reported testing AMI moth traps and planned BirdNET bird-call identification.

name: SAOCOM
summary: Argentine L-band radar satellite, built by national bodies and firms with INVAP as main contractor and run by CONAE, designed in particular to detect soil moisture and part of SIASGE.

name: Secretaría de Ambiente de Tierra del Fuego
summary: Provincial environment body listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps are reported by MapBiomas as the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Secretaría de Ambiente y Cambio Climático de Río Negro
summary: Río Negro provincial secretariat whose environmental rangers, according to a July 2025 government report, periodically carried out a bird census in the Bahía de San Antonio protected area.

name: Secretaría de Biodiversidad y Desarrollo Sustentable de Jujuy
summary: A provincial secretariat whose secretary said in June 2022 that Jujuy was strengthening its protected area system, governed by Law 6080.

name: Secretaría de Medio Ambiente y Desarrollo Sustentable de Ushuaia
summary: Its head said Ushuaia was improving three sites including Laguna del Diablo in February 2022, when municipal guards mainly handled prevention and reporting in Bahía Encerrada Natural Reserve.

name: Sentinel Cloud
summary: Open pilot that detects fire hot spots from space and aims to alert Patagonian municipalities, brigades and producers; its site says it has no published cases with measured results yet.

name: Servicio de Guardaparques del Municipio de San Fernando
summary: Permanent ranger service of the municipality's biosphere reserve, whose rangers guard its natural assets and are based at the Arroyo Borches station on the third section of the islands.

name: Servicio de Parques Provinciales y Recursos Naturales Renovables de Tucumán
summary: Tucumán body named in a summary of Law 5600 as the authority responsible for applying that law, which lists a ranger service among its provisions.

name: Sistema de Administración, Control y Verificación Forestal
summary: Active inter-jurisdictional computer system for federal forest management and control, including traceability of forest products; in July 2019 an official said 20 provinces were working on it and three issued permits.

name: Sistema de Alerta Temprana de Deforestación
summary: Argentine national system processing Sentinel and Landsat 8 imagery every 15 days to detect native forest loss, with alerts received by national parks since November 2021.

name: Sistema de Información de Biodiversidad (APN)
summary: Biodiversity information system of Argentina's national parks agency, which runs it, funded by the GEF and building on a 1994 data bank, offering an online catalogue and spatial data infrastructure.

name: Sistema Federal de Áreas Protegidas
summary: Protected-areas system set up on 20 March 2003 by framework agreement and managed by an executive committee of COFEMA, the national parks agency and the Subsecretaría de Ambiente.

name: Sistema Integrado de Información Ambiental
summary: A platform where much of the information produced by the National Native Forest Monitoring System is published, and which that system uses.

name: Sistema Nacional de Datos Biológicos
summary: Programme introduced in 2009 by the science ministry and active until the end of 2020, funding digitised biological databases that must publish all records through its portal; it is the GBIF Argentina node's homepage.

name: Sistema Nacional de Monitoreo de Bosques Nativos
summary: National system run by the Instituto Geográfico Nacional giving unified information on native forest extent, change, condition and fires, mainly using remote sensing and GIS, with much published on SInIA.

name: Snapshot Argentina
summary: CONICET reports researchers coordinating annual camera-trap mammal monitoring within a network begun in the United States in 2019, with its first campaign planned for early October 2026.

name: Subsecretaría de Ambiente
summary: National authority under the Native Forests Law that began implementing the Deforestation Early Warning System in the Parque Chaqueño and publishes the 2025-2030 biodiversity strategy.

name: Trama Viva
summary: Organisation listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps are reported by MapBiomas as the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Universidad de Buenos Aires
summary: A university that signed an agreement with FAO in 2025 for a Faculty of Agronomy project, under the +Ciencia +Bosques programme, to map native Chaco forest regeneration and design long-term monitoring.

name: Universidad Nacional de Cuyo
summary: University listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps are reported by MapBiomas as the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Universidad Nacional de General Sarmiento
summary: University listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps are reported by MapBiomas as the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Universidad Nacional del Centro de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
summary: University listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps are reported by MapBiomas as the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Universidad Nacional del Comahue, Bariloche
summary: University listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps are reported by MapBiomas as the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: Universidad Nacional del Sur
summary: University listed as a member of the MapBiomas Argentina network, whose Collection 3 maps are reported by MapBiomas as the work of 25 institutions and professionals.

name: VISEC
summary: Closed soy and beef traceability platform for Argentine agro-industry, run by CIARA and funded by LIF; in 2023 reported as a three-year project, launched May 2022, checking deforestation-free status by satellite.

name: WCS Argentina
summary: Active organisation that says it leads the Patagonian Coastal Zone management plan and works with fishers who have tagged over 3,000 sharks, and in January 2023 reported tracking penguins.

name: ÉRIA
summary: Species identification model built by EcoRegistros, designed to identify species from photographs, trained on images validated by its community, and running offline inside the EcoRegistros Android app.

name: ABOL-RefDat
summary: Project aiming to produce at least 5,000 open-access DNA barcodes in the BOLD database for at least 1,500 Austrian animal, plant and fungal species, run by Austrian Barcode of Life and funded by the Biodiversitätsfonds.

name: AgriNatur AT-HU
summary: Closed project with a stated period of January 2019 to February 2022 (the page also says June 2022), covering agrobiodiversity monitoring, a survey of local managers' knowledge and organic arable field trials, led by Vienna's forestry and agriculture department MA 49.

name: AIMBioDat (Austrian Initiative for Mobilizing Biodiversity Data)
summary: Programme run by Umweltbundesamt and funded by the environment department since 2004, with 26 data providers and almost 14 million records on GBIF, where Austria is an observer.

name: Akustisches Monitoring seltener Vogelarten der Österreichischen Bundesforste
summary: Austrian Federal Forests project using AI-assisted acoustic analysis to monitor rare birds; a pilot with the Austrian Research Centre for Forests used 20 recorders in Nationalpark Kalkalpen and confirmed capercaillie from about 200,000 minutes of audio.

name: AlpMon: Schadenserkennung für die Waldwirtschaft
summary: Closed project, 05/2017 to 04/2019, built and run by Joanneum Research, whose AlpMon forest monitoring system maps damaged and felled forest areas within about 0 to 14 days, distinguishing windthrow, clear-cuts and insect damage.

name: Austrian Barcode of Life
summary: Initiative active since 2014 recording Austria's animal, plant and fungal diversity with DNA barcodes, running bioblitzes since 2019 and co-organising a September 2026 metabarcoding symposium that launched an Austrian eDNA interest group.

name: Austrian forest tree species mapping model (BFW, Sentinel-2)
summary: Deep learning model built by BFW that maps 26 forest tree species classes across Austria from Sentinel-2 data, with 55 per cent overall accuracy against National Forest Inventory data.

name: BiKoS – Biodiversität, Kooperation und Synergien in den NÖ Großschutzgebieten
summary: Project funded by the Province of Lower Austria and the EU under the 2023 to 2027 rural development programme, with four protected areas and surveys of indicator species.

name: Bio Forschung Austria
summary: A non-profit research institute outside the universities, based in Vienna, whose earlier Lobau organic field surveys served as the baseline for AgriNatur monitoring.

name: Biodiversity database of the High Tauern National Park
summary: Database run by Haus der Natur Salzburg covering the distribution, biology, ecology and prevalence of animals and plants in the High Tauern National Park's zones and surroundings.

name: Biodiversity Research & Monitoring AT-CZ 2024 - 2028
summary: Cross-border Austria and Czech Republic project, planned for 2025 to 2028 and led by Nationalpark Thayatal, to build a shared biodiversity database and a standardised monitoring protocol for selected species and habitats.

name: Biodiversitäts-Atlas Österreich
summary: Free online portal, online since December 2019, run and built by the Biodiversity Hub, giving access to over 16 million species occurrence records, including citizen science data.

name: Biodiversitäts-Hub Österreich
summary: Organisation set up in autumn 2017 at Danube University Krems as a science-policy-society interface, which runs the Biodiversitäts-Atlas Österreich.

name: Biodiversitätsdatenbank Salzburg
summary: Database run by Haus der Natur with about 3,000,000 records on animals, fungi and plants in Salzburg, part of the GBIF network, using Observation.org for recorded observations.

name: BioDivTech Lab
summary: Project run by the ICEB that received a 2.4 million euro FFG infrastructure grant (2023 call), planning four components combining remote sensing, AI, sensors, robotics and molecular biology, including a mobile biodiversity truck and eDNA lab.

name: Biologische Station Neusiedler See
summary: Office of the Burgenland provincial government's agriculture, nature and environment department, based in Illmitz, which says it has decades of experience monitoring Burgenland's waters.

name: Biosphärenpark Wienerwald
summary: Biosphere reserve organisation that lists research and environmental observation among its aims, publishes data through GBIF and is a partner in the BiKoS project.

name: BirdLife Österreich
summary: Organisation running ornitho.at and Austrian breeding bird monitoring, counting common species since 1998 mainly with volunteers, which developed a woodland bird index with BFW in 2014.

name: Blühendes Österreich
summary: Non-profit BILLA private foundation, according to the University of Innsbruck, whose free butterfly app volunteers use to collect images.

name: Bundesamt für Eich- und Vermessungswesen
summary: Organisation that presented Land Cover, a free high-resolution dataset of vegetation, buildings, soil areas and water bodies, in December 2024, and lists remote sensing among its topics.

name: Bundesamt für Wasserwirtschaft
summary: Organisation based at Scharfling 18, Mondsee, with an institute for aquatic ecology and fisheries and a website listing a fish database, Fischdatenbank Austria.

name: Bundesforschungszentrum für Wald
summary: Organisation serving the federal government as a research, training, information and advisory centre on forests, natural hazards and landscape, which runs Forest Groove and carries out forest inventory work.

name: Bundesministerium für Land- und Forstwirtschaft, Klima- und Umweltschutz, Regionen und Wasserwirtschaft
summary: Federal ministry for agriculture and forestry, climate and environmental protection, regions and water management, which funds AIMBioDat and whose biodiversity unit head chairs the National Biodiversity Commission.

name: Carinthia University of Applied Sciences
summary: University that runs ICEB and operates a field research lab in Metschach, where researchers tested audio sensors, wildlife cameras, drones and eDNA kits between 2023 and 2026.

name: DNA des Waldes
summary: Project run by Innsbruck's applied animal ecology group, funded by Waldfonds Österreich, planning DNA metabarcoding of 500 samples from two forest areas in the Zillertal and Karwendel nature parks.

name: E.C.O. Institut für Ökologie Jungmeier GmbH
summary: Klagenfurt ecology company that worked with the University of Graz, Joanneum Research and the Umweltbundesamt on monitoring ecosystem degradation by combining remote sensing data with reference mapping.

name: Forest Groove
summary: Active Sparkling Science project run by the BFW, studying forest biodiversity with microphones; it plans to record and analyse bird calls and share data through platforms such as iNaturalist.

name: Forschungsbereich für Angewandte Tierökologie, Universität Innsbruck
summary: University of Innsbruck research group that runs DNA des Waldes, which began in May 2022 to test eDNA monitoring of forest biodiversity from forest stream samples.

name: Forschungsinstitut für Wildtierkunde und Ökologie (FIWI)
summary: Wildlife research institute, an extraordinary member of the Österreichzentrum Bär, Wolf, Luchs, commissioned to advise it, act as central point for monitoring and kill assessment, and genetically analyse DNA samples.

name: GeoVille Information Systems and Data Processing GmbH
summary: Company in Innsbruck that says it supplies geospatial data for natural resources and biodiversity, and whose team in AI4Trees, finished by December 2025, aimed to develop a single-tree detection model.

name: Graz University of Technology
summary: University whose researcher Thomas Pock is listed among the authors of a 2023 paper on deep learning tools for mapping and monitoring biological soil crusts.

name: Haus der Natur
summary: Museum running Salzburg’s species database with about 3,000,000 records, mostly workgroup observations, and a High Tauern database, whose distribution data and digitised specimens are available through a GBIF portal.

name: HBLFA Raumberg-Gumpenstein
summary: Institution with a biodiversity and restoration group whose staff surveyed 216 extensively and 183 intensively managed meadow plots for MeadowTypes, according to Joanneum Research.

name: Herpetofaunistische Datenbank Österreichs
summary: Active database of amphibian and reptile distribution records from anywhere in Austria, gathered since 1982 and run by the Natural History Museum Vienna.

name: ICEB – Interdisciplinary Center for Ecosystem Services and Biodiversity
summary: Centre of Carinthia University of Applied Sciences in Villach, awarded a 2.4 million euro infrastructure grant for BioDivTech Lab and reporting field tests of sensors, drones and eDNA kits between 2023 and 2026.

name: Insekten-Bus-Monitoring (IBM)
summary: Active project using DNA analysis to document flying insects in Austria, collected on ÖBB Postbus vehicles, run by Innsbruck's applied animal ecology group and being extended from a 2021 Tyrol pilot to other provinces.

name: Integrated Monitoring Zöbelboden
summary: Long-term ecosystem research programme at Zöbelboden since 1992, led by the Environment Agency Austria on a 90 hectare plot, feeding data to 18 research networks.

name: JOANNEUM RESEARCH Forschungsgesellschaft mbH
summary: Research company with over 500 staff across six sites that coordinated DeerAI, partnered in RestorEO and derives satellite monitoring schemes, with a Sentinel-2 toolbox developed for MeadowTypes.

name: KalkMon
summary: Project led by Nationalpark Kalkalpen and funded by the Biodiversitätsfonds, which from August 2023 to October 2025 extended species monitoring to stepping-stone sites and linked it with neighbouring protected areas' monitoring systems.

name: Land Cover (BEV)
summary: Free dataset built by the Bundesamt für Eich- und Vermessungswesen, with six classes at 20 cm resolution, derived from orthophotos and elevation models and updated every three years.

name: LIFE EUROKITE
summary: Project led by the Mitteleuropäische Gesellschaft zur Erhaltung der Greifvögel, which from 2020 to 2025 fitted GPS trackers to raptors in about 40 areas in 12 countries; its database held 3,306 tagged red kites by December 2025.

name: LIFE Grenzüberschreitender Schutz der Großtrappe in Mitteleuropa
summary: Project run by the Österreichische Gesellschaft Großtrappenschutz from 2016 to 2023, which planned GPS transmitters for 24 adult female great bustards in Austria and Hungary and provided for population and habitat monitoring with GIS analysis.

name: LTER-Austria
summary: Long-term ecological research programme with 39 LTER sites and three LTSER platforms, hosted by a secretariat at Umweltbundesamt GmbH, which Austria launched early among European countries to integrate existing in-situ infrastructures.

name: Machine learning training data: over 500,000 images of butterflies and moths (Lepidoptera) with species labels
summary: Dataset of over 500,000 species-labelled butterfly and moth images, listed by OpenAlex as a 2025 Scientific Data paper with Friederike Barkmann as first author.

name: MeadowTypes
summary: Project that classifies meadow types at a scale of 1:50,000 with a machine learning model on satellite spectral data, trained on 216 extensive and 183 intensive field plots.

name: Mitteleuropäische Gesellschaft zur Erhaltung der Greifvögel
summary: Austrian raptor conservation association, founded for larger cross-border projects using tagging, and coordinating beneficiary of LIFE EUROKITE, which uses telemetry to find human-caused reasons for red kite deaths.

name: MOIST - Erfassung degradierter Moorflächen Österreichs und Beurteilung ihrer Eignung zur Regeneration
summary: Biodiversitätsfonds-funded project, running February 2024 to December 2026 per HBLFA Raumberg-Gumpenstein, to record Austria's peatlands and plans to model peat soil distribution using geostatistics, regression models and machine learning.

name: Monitoring der Brutvögel Österreichs
summary: Programme run by BirdLife Österreich, counting breeding birds at fixed points twice each spring since 1998, and the source of the Farmland Bird Index, which shows indicator species down about 40 per cent over 28 years.

name: Nationale Biodiversitätskommission
summary: Body of ministries, federal states, social partners, universities, federal offices, NGOs and interest groups that agrees national biodiversity reports and advises the responsible minister.

name: Nationalpark Donau-Auen
summary: Floodplain national park of more than 9,600 hectares, founded in 1996, which surveys bats by call recording and mist-netting and takes part in the BiKoS project.

name: Nationalpark Gesäuse
summary: National park that joined a Helsinki-led European research data register pilot from January to October 2025 and participates in eLTER with the University of Graz.

name: Nationalpark Hohe Tauern
summary: The largest Alpine national park, covering 1,856 square kilometres and listed as a GBIF Austria data provider, with a monitoring photo archive reported in a 2022 paper.

name: Nationalpark Kalkalpen
summary: National park protecting Austria's largest continuous forest wilderness, which has monitored lynx since 1998, mostly by camera traps and telemetry, and publishes data through GBIF.

name: Nationalpark Neusiedler See - Seewinkel
summary: Austria's first cross-border national park, covering about 90 square kilometres on Austrian territory, with long-term monitoring of birds, fish ecology and grazing, and frequent monitoring of about 40 saline lakes.

name: Nationalpark Thayatal
summary: National park protecting the Thaya valley with the neighbouring Czech Podyjí National Park, publishing data through GBIF and reporting a research project surveying bats and ground beetles in Lower Austria.

name: naturbeobachtung.at
summary: Citizen science platform for Austrian plants, fungi and animals, run by Naturschutzbund Österreich and science4you, reporting its millionth record and around 60 supporting specialists in August 2024.

name: Naturhistorisches Museum Wien
summary: Vienna natural history museum publishing collection data through DIVINA and research data through its repository, whose staff have gathered Austrian amphibian and reptile records since 1982.

name: Naturschutzbund Österreich
summary: Austrian nature conservation body that has run the naturbeobachtung.at recording platform and app since 2006, announced its millionth record in August 2024, and is listed as a GBIF Austria data provider.

name: Open Scientific Collections Austria
summary: Portal linking natural science museum and university collections in Austria, letting users search collection objects of different institutions from one entry point, and partnered with Naturhistorisches Museum Wien.

name: ornitho.at
summary: Bird observation dataset run by BirdLife Österreich, receiving over a million records a year through its website or the NaturaList app.

name: pentamap GmbH
summary: Graz company developing apps, web platforms and spatial analyses using Earth observation and machine learning, named in 2025 as consortium leader of BioDivAI, with DeerAI and SmartMowAI also announced.

name: Protecting Biodiversity at Lake Neusiedl
summary: Aimed to assess species’ conservation status and ecology in Lake Neusiedl’s reed belt using spectrograms and a convolutional neural network trained on 41 species and song type classes.

name: RestorEO
summary: Earth observation project, finished in August 2025 after starting in September 2022, that aimed to support Austria's National Restoration Plan and reports a nationwide mowing detection system needing no training data.

name: Schmetterlinge Österreichs
summary: Butterfly recording app launched in 2016, run by Blühendes Österreich, with 735,000 observations and 24,000 users in July 2023, and photos that Innsbruck says underpin machine learning research on identification.

name: Seeadler-Monitoring 2022-2024
summary: WWF Österreich project, funded by the Biodiversitätsfonds, which monitored the white-tailed eagle population and fitted ten birds with transmitters, including four young eagles in 2023, to identify distribution and threats.

name: TB Raab GmbH
summary: Company in Deutsch Wagram doing species conservation projects and bird telemetry studies, commissioned to implement LIFE EUROKITE after a pan-European public tender.

name: TU Wien
summary: Vienna technical university whose authors published 2023 papers predicting salt pan inundation in the western Pannonian basin from remote sensing data and classifying Danube biological status with bacterial bioindicators.

name: Umweltbundesamt GmbH
summary: Austrian environment agency, a limited liability company since 1999, that coordinates GBIF Austria, runs AimBiodat, publishes monitoring reports and GBIF datasets, and partners with the European Environment Agency.

name: UNESCO Chair Sustainable Management of Conservation Areas, Carinthia University of Applied Sciences
summary: UNESCO Chair at Carinthia University of Applied Sciences in Villach, listed as a partner of the DNAquaIMG project.

name: University of Graz
summary: Austrian university whose authors published a 2023 paper on deep learning to map biological soil crusts and a 2025 paper on deep learning to distinguish Riccia spores.

name: University of Salzburg
summary: Austrian university whose authors published a 2024 paper on drone-based forest health monitoring with machine learning and a 2022 paper predicting wildlife-vehicle collision risk.

name: University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna
summary: Vienna veterinary university whose authors published a 2025 paper classifying wild boar behaviour from accelerometers and a 2021 paper on video analysis of bird movements and behaviour.

name: University of Vienna
summary: Austrian university whose authors published a 2022 paper on machine learning predictions of global plant diversity and a 2023 paper on reed dynamics at Lake Neusiedl using drones and deep learning.

name: Universität für Bodenkultur Wien
summary: Vienna university of natural resources (BOKU) that publishes data through GBIF, partners with DNAquaIMG and Umweltbundesamt, and has authors on 2023 and 2025 machine learning forest papers.

name: Universität Innsbruck
summary: Austrian university whose Institute of Ecology hosts Viel-Falter monitoring, and whose ecologist trained butterfly identification models on its LEO5 supercomputer, alongside Sentinel-2 forest mapping papers from 2024 and 2026.

name: Viel-Falter
summary: Volunteer butterfly monitoring programme at 480 Austrian sites, based at Innsbruck's Institute of Ecology, nationwide since 2023, with 310 volunteers recording 58,493 butterflies by the end of 2024.

name: WALDATLAS
summary: Free geodata platform on Austria's forests, natural hazards and protected areas, run by the federal ministry, with new tree species (14 classes) and tree height maps described as orientation aids only.

name: Waldrappteam
summary: Describes itself as a company focused on research and species conservation, and monitors wild birds with GPS transmitters.

name: WasserCluster Lunz - Biologische Station GmbH
summary: Austrian research organisation whose authors appear on two OpenAlex-listed papers, from 2021 and 2022, on monitoring fish communities with eDNA methods, including metabarcoding and qPCR.

name: Wasservogelzählung in Österreich
summary: Austrian waterbird counts run by BirdLife Österreich with provincial coordinators, centred on a January midwinter count, with BirdLife's December 2025 article reporting more than 330 participants each year.

name: Wildnisgebiet Dürrenstein-Lassingtal
summary: Holds the Rothwald primeval forest, has UNESCO World Heritage status since 2017 and prioritises long-term monitoring, with a multispectral drone intended to record forest development.

name: Woodland Bird Index (Austria)
summary: Dataset developed in 2014 by BirdLife Österreich with the BFW from 19 indicator species, building on national breeding bird monitoring, and updated in a project finished in 2025.

name: WWF Österreich
summary: Vienna-based conservation association founded in 1963, which reported in August 2023 that it fits young white-tailed eagles with transmitters every year to identify threats and improve cross-border protection.

name: ZOBODAT
summary: Biogeographical database, formerly ZOODAT, founded in 1972 with analysis, documentation and communication facilities, listed on GBIF with Oberösterreichische Landeskultur GmbH/Biologiezentrum as originator.

name: Österreichische Bundesforste AG
summary: Austrian company (ÖBf) that, according to a July 2026 report, uses acoustic survey methods with AI-assisted analysis to monitor rare bird species, and whose 2024 research report covers bioacoustic bird detection.

name: Österreichische Gesellschaft Großtrappenschutz
summary: Association founded in 2004 that held the LIFE project on cross-border great bustard protection (July 2016 to December 2023), which provided for population and habitat monitoring analysed with GIS.

name: Österreichische Mykologische Gesellschaft
summary: Austrian mycological society that manages a mycological database of fungal observations, mainly from Austria and recorded since the 1980s, with experts checking the plausibility of species identifications.

name: Österreichische Vogelwarte
summary: Austrian bird ringing organisation whose ringing centre took over national ringing coordination from the Vogelwarte Radolfzell on 1 January 2016 and documents recoveries through international data exchange.

name: Österreichische Waldinventur
summary: Austrian national forest inventory, run by the Federal Research Centre for Forests, surveying about 11,000 sample plots with expert teams and imagery, with latest results presented in January 2025.

name: Österreichischer Biodiversitätsfonds
summary: Environment ministry funding line for Austrian biodiversity, which the ministry reported on 29 June 2026 had funded 251 projects; a 2026 call has a 5 million euro budget.

name: Österreichischer Brutvogelatlas 2013–2018
summary: Atlas published by BirdLife Österreich in spring 2024, showing distributions of all 235 bird species breeding in Austria in 2013 to 2018, from over 2.1 million citizen science records by more than 2,300 volunteers.

name: Österreichisches Biodiversitäts-Monitoring der offenen Kulturlandschaft
summary: Programme built and run by the Umweltbundesamt, founded in 2017/18 to document long-term biodiversity change in open farmland; its 2023/24 round mapped plants, grasshoppers and butterflies on 200 sites, with analyses starting from remote sensing data.

name: Österreichzentrum Bär, Wolf, Luchs
summary: An association with federal government and Länder voting members, evaluating Länder large carnivore monitoring data nationwide with FIWI support for distribution maps and the wolf status report.

name: 2pi Software
summary: Technology developer partnered with the Centre for Invasive Species Solutions on WeedRemeed.

name: Aak Puul Ngantam
summary: Ranger organisation on Cape York whose rangers use drones and AI analysis of aerial images to monitor turtle nests and feral pig predation.

name: Aboriginal Land Council of Tasmania
summary: Tasmanian Aboriginal body whose statutory functions under the Aboriginal Lands Act 1995 include managing Aboriginal land sustainably, and which established palawa Enterprises to oversee the wukalina Walk tourism venture.

name: ACFR Marine Robotics Program
summary: Marine systems group at the University of Sydney's Australian Centre for Field Robotics, which operates a national autonomous underwater vehicle facility and uses machine learning on seabed imagery.

name: Acoustics for Large Scale Biodiversity Assessment
summary: Australian Research Council Discovery project of $560,082 to James Cook University on using automated acoustic recording to census biodiversity at continental scale.

name: AgriProve
summary: Issues a Deforestation-Free Beef Credential for buyers with deforestation-free commitments, using national datasets, ground cover analysis and satellite alerts, with independent analysis by partner Verterra Ecological Engineering.

name: Agronomeye
summary: Australian technology company whose AgTwin platform is a LiDAR-first digital twin of farm landscapes used for natural capital measurement.

name: AI feral cat control partnership
summary: Bush Heritage Australia partnership with eVorta and Timberscope developing AI-enabled cameras and traps to detect and catch feral cats, with a $1.7 million Game Changers grant.

name: AI for Koalas
summary: Project building a network of 100 connected cameras in South East Queensland to monitor koalas near roads with AI.

name: AI to protect turtle nests from feral pigs on Cape York
summary: NESP hub project using AI and cloud computing to analyse aerial images of the Cape York coast for feral pig damage to turtle nests.

name: AirborneLogic
summary: Company providing remote sensing and spatial analysis, including biodiversity and natural capital measurement.

name: Akula Tech
summary: In August 2024, Swinburne described this Melbourne-based space startup as specialising in Earth observation satellite technology and worked with it on bushfire detection at the XPRIZE Wildfire summit.

name: Alinytjara Wiluṟara Landscape Board
summary: Landscape board that in March 2024 was allocated $450,000 over two years for feral predator management in the Yalata IPA, including satellite-connected Celium traps.

name: Anindilyakwa Land Council
summary: Land council whose Land and Sea Rangers manage a 10,000 square kilometre Indigenous Protected Area of islands, reef and ocean in the Groote Archipelago.

name: AquaWatch Australia
summary: Programme to build a network of Earth observation satellites and ground sensors that monitors water quality in Australia's rivers and coastal and inland waterways.

name: Arabana Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation working with its Arabana Rangers and partners on a management plan for the future care of Jackboot Paddock on Arabana Country.

name: Arafura Swamp Rangers Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Rangers' corporation whose Healthy Country Plan for 2025-2035 includes management strategies for the Arafura Swamp Indigenous Protected Area in north-east Arnhem Land, with a dedication ceremony scheduled for 22 October 2025.

name: Arid Recovery
summary: Reserve in arid South Australia that uses Felixer traps with artificial intelligence, and trap alert systems, in feral animal control.

name: Artificial odds: Using AI to achieve effective threat mitigation
summary: Project linking AI processing of camera images to three new feral animal management devices, including a cat-netting device, covering five Australian jurisdictions, with a grant of $1,675,380.

name: Atlas of Life in the Coastal Wilderness
summary: Volunteer non-profit running an ongoing citizen science project and biodiversity surveys on the south-east Australian coast.

name: Atlassian Foundation
summary: Foundation whose Engage4Good program placed two Atlassian staff on the FrogID project to work on machine identification of frog calls.

name: Aussie Ark
summary: Conservation organisation focused on habitat restoration and species rewilding within the 400-hectare predator-proof Barrington Wildlife Sanctuary in Barrington Tops, New South Wales.

name: AusTraits
summary: National database of Australian plant traits, synthesising data on 500 traits across 30,000 plant taxa.

name: Australian Antarctic Division
summary: Part of the Australian Government climate and environment department, based in Tasmania, which coordinates the Australian Antarctic Program.

name: Australian Antarctic Program
summary: Australian Antarctic research program that uses an automated weighing and recording system to monitor Adélie penguins.

name: Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics and Sciences
summary: Australian Government bureau whose 2013 presentation on forest reporting names a National Forest Inventory manager and covers the national forest cover dataset.

name: Australian Environmental Grantmakers Network
summary: Member organisation for environmental philanthropy with more than 200 foundations, trusts, funds and individuals.

name: Australian Microbiome
summary: Continental-scale project building a publicly accessible database of microbial diversity across Australian land and water ecosystems.

name: Australian Museum
summary: Museum that runs FrogID, a national citizen science project on frog calls, with a beta that identifies the recordings by machine.

name: Australian National Insect Collection
summary: CSIRO collection of over 12 million specimens, the world's largest collection of Australian insects and related groups.

name: Australian National University
summary: University whose Fenner School of Environment & Society published an article on a fuel moisture map that uses a machine-learning model.

name: Australian Ocean Data Network
summary: Portal described as the gateway to Australian marine and climate science data, offering open access to ocean data.

name: Australian Reference Genome Atlas
summary: Genomic atlas intended to let researchers find genomic data for Australian species in one place, listed among the Atlas of Living Australia's current projects.

name: Australian Research Council
summary: Australian Government agency that awards Discovery Projects grants, including one on acoustics for biodiversity assessment.

name: Australian Research Data Commons
summary: National research data infrastructure facility that co-invests in WildObs through its Planet Research Data Commons.

name: Australian Seed Bank Partnership
summary: Partnership whose members' seed collection and germination data are brought together in the Australian Virtual Seed Bank, an open national portal.

name: Australian Space Agency
summary: National space agency of Australia, a member of the International Astronautical Federation since 2011.

name: Australian Temperate Reef Collaboration
summary: Reef monitoring collaboration that contributes survey data to the IMOS National Reef Monitoring Network, with partners across Tasmania, Victoria and Western Australia.

name: Australian Wildlife Conservancy
summary: Conservation organisation that runs wildlife sanctuaries and partnership sites in Australia, and builds AI models that identify animals in camera trap images.

name: Automated Fish Identification
summary: Web-based system that uses computer vision to detect and identify fish and measure their length from underwater video, developed by the Curtin Institute for Data Science with partners.

name: AWC species recognisers
summary: Australian Wildlife Conservancy's AI models for recognising Australian mammals and reptiles in camera trap images, planned for release on a public open-source repository.

name: AWC135
summary: Open species classifier from Australian Wildlife Conservancy with 135 labels for threatened, common and introduced animals in motion-sensor camera images across mainland Australia.

name: Barengi Gadjin Land Council Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Representative body for five Traditional Owner groups under a cooperative management agreement with the State, maintaining the co-management relationship directly with Parks Victoria.

name: Bawinanga Homelands Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation whose Bawinanga Rangers and landowners declared the Djelk Indigenous Protected Area in 2009, covering over 6,700 square kilometres in Arnhem Land.

name: BHP
summary: Mining company named as the funder of Curtin University's eDGES environmental DNA program. Included for that funding only.

name: Biamanga Board of Management
summary: Board with a majority of Aboriginal members that, in partnership with NPWS, is responsible for the care and control of Biamanga National Park in New South Wales.

name: BioCollect
summary: Free field data collection tool for biodiversity science, developed and hosted by the Atlas of Living Australia.

name: Biodiversity Information Office
summary: Western Australian office that developed Dandjoo and reviews all records before publication.

name: Biological Databases of South Australia
summary: South Australian flora and fauna database of specimen and observation records.

name: Bioplatforms Australia
summary: Invests in omics facilities and open genomic data for Australia's biodiversity, including a survey of Australia's Tree of Life.

name: Birdata
summary: BirdLife Australia's online bird monitoring platform, which holds more than 30 million bird sighting records from professional researchers and citizen scientists.

name: BirdLife Australia
summary: Bird conservation organisation that deployed acoustic monitors which found the Eastern Bristlebird in South East Queensland.

name: Blue Carbon
summary: Brisbane climate technology company that uses wave energy to circulate, cool and oxygenate seawater, with real-time ocean intelligence and autonomous systems, and won KPMG's Nature Positive Prize.

name: Botanic Gardens and Parks Authority
summary: Authority responsible for the care, control and management of Kings Park and Botanic Garden, Bold Park, and any other designated lands.

name: Botanic Gardens of Sydney
summary: Sydney botanic gardens body where over 1 million National Herbarium of New South Wales specimens were imaged, and whose scientists worked with UNSW on machine learning for them.

name: Buda-dji Aboriginal Development Association Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation named as host of the Bulmba rangers, who work with Mona Mona and Kuranda communities on traditional fire management and wetland protection on Djabugay Country.

name: Bulimba Creek Catchment Coordinating Committee
summary: Community catchment and Landcare organisation in Brisbane that runs BioBlitz events recording local wildlife.

name: Bundjalung of Byron Bay Aboriginal Corporation (Arakwal)
summary: Reported in May 2019 to have worked for over two decades to sustain Arakwal culture and country.

name: Bunya Peoples’ Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation named as host, on behalf of the Wakka Wakka people, of the Wakka Wakka rangers, who work on Country in the South Burnett Region from a base at Murgon.

name: Bureau of Meteorology
summary: Australian Government agency included here for its national water information services. Its weather work is outside the map.

name: Bureau of Meteorology Water Information
summary: Water information services of the Bureau of Meteorology, providing water data products to the public and to specialist users.

name: Burnett Mary Regional Group
summary: Queensland natural resource manager that worked with EnviroDNA on eDNA detection of threatened freshwater turtles, including the Mary River Turtle.

name: Bush Heritage Australia
summary: National conservation charity that manages reserves and works on AI-linked traps and deterrents for feral cats and foxes.

name: Butchulla Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation named as host of the Butchulla Land and Sea Rangers, who work on conservation on Butchulla country, focused on K’gari (Fraser Island), and has employed a new ranger team through the NIAA expansion.

name: Canberra Birds
summary: Bird group in Canberra that conducts bird surveys, including the COG Gardenbird Survey.

name: Cape York turtle nest AI monitoring
summary: Machine learning analysis of drone and helicopter images of the Cape York coast to find turtle nests, turtle tracks and feral pig tracks, shown to rangers through a dashboard.

name: Carbon AI
summary: AI used on NatureMapr that suggests possible species identifications and directs moderators' attention.

name: Caring for Country program
summary: Indigital and Rio Tinto program helping Indigenous communities in Far North Queensland use AI data analysis, LiDAR and environmental sensors.

name: Carpentaria Land Council Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Land council named as host of the Normanton Land and Sea Rangers, who protect natural and cultural resources on Country in the Lower Gulf of Carpentaria.

name: Central Land Council
summary: Land council whose rangers manage four Indigenous Protected Areas on Aboriginal land in central Australia: Northern Tanami, Southern Tanami, Angas Downs and Katiti-Petermann.

name: Central Queensland University
summary: University with authors leading a 2025 paper comparing YOLO and RT-DETR models for coral bleaching detection and a 2026 paper on drone mapping of invasive rangeland plants.

name: Centre for Biodiversity and Conservation Science
summary: University of Queensland research centre for biodiversity conservation that gave seed money to WildObs.

name: Centre for Invasive Species Solutions
summary: Peak research and development organisation for invasive species, which developed WeedRemeed, WeedScan and FeralScan.

name: Charles Darwin University
summary: University that took part with Warddeken Land Management and CSIRO in research on AI for Indigenous-led wildlife monitoring.

name: Charles Sturt University
summary: Australian university with a Chief Investigator on the Australian Acoustic Observatory, and whose Gulbali Institute is a partner in the Gayini Data Hub.

name: Citizens of the Reef
summary: Conservation group that runs the Great Reef Census, combining reef image collection, AI and volunteer analysis.

name: Climate Friendly
summary: Company offering natural capital and nature repair services that use remotely sensed data and machine learning models.

name: ClimateWatch
summary: Citizen science phenology project in Australia, developed by Earthwatch with the Bureau of Meteorology and the University of Melbourne.

name: Community for Coastal and Cassowary Conservation
summary: Community group that bought Gurrbum Nature Refuge in Wet Tropics with Queensland Trust for Nature in 2019, has owned it since 2024, and is restoring a former banana plantation to cassowary habitat.

name: Coral Sea Foundation
summary: Reef conservation organisation based on Magnetic Island that develops reef monitoring methods, trains Indigenous women in Australia and Melanesia, and works on ReefCloud with the Australian Institute of Marine Science.

name: Cradle Coast Authority
summary: Tasmanian grant recipient training the AI in Felixer traps to recognise Tasmanian devils so that they are not treated as targets.

name: Crown-of-thorns starfish detection model
summary: Machine learning model from Google, CSIRO and the Kaggle community that detects crown-of-thorns starfish in underwater images of the Great Barrier Reef, which Google said it would open source.

name: Curtin Institute for Data Science
summary: Curtin University data science institute that developed the Automated Fish Identification system with partners.

name: Curtin University
summary: University in a three-year collaboration with Mineral Resources on environmental DNA monitoring for biodiversity surveys in remote environments.

name: Dabu Jajikal Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation named as host of the Dabu Jajikal rangers, who care for sea, reef and coastal country around the Bloomfield River and Weary Bay within their TUMRA area.

name: Dambimangari Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation whose Dambimangari Rangers began work on Country in 2012 and manage Land and Sea Country, with seven full-time and ten casual rangers in 2023.

name: Dandjoo
summary: Western Australia's first whole-of-state biodiversity data platform, which curates records from government, industry and research and passes data to the Commonwealth's Biodiversity Data Repository.

name: Darumbal People Aboriginal Corporation RNTBC
summary: Native title corporation named as host of the Darumbal rangers, who look after land and sea country around Rockhampton and Yeppoon, including the Darumbal TUMRA area.

name: Deakin Marine Mapping
summary: Deakin University group that maps the seafloor and coastlines of Victoria with sonar and a drone fleet.

name: Deakin University
summary: University whose authors led a 2022 paper on a smart camera trap and a 2021 paper evaluating machine learning classifiers for smart animal trackers; it hosts Deakin Marine Mapping.

name: Department for Environment and Water
summary: South Australian Government department named as a partner on a project using Kanyini thermal imagery and AI to map surface temperatures.

name: Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions
summary: Western Australian government department for biodiversity conservation, within which the Western Australian Herbarium sits.

name: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
summary: Australian Government department for the environment. It administers grant programmes including Innovative Biodiversity Monitoring, and Parks Australia is one of its divisions.

name: Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action
summary: Victorian Government department, owner and custodian of the state's vegetation data, updated using machine learning on Vicmap imagery.

name: Department of Natural Resources and Environment Tasmania
summary: Tasmanian government department whose website presents the Natural Values Atlas, which holds around 4.7 million plant and animal observations, as an authoritative source on Tasmania's natural values.

name: Department of Water and Environmental Regulation
summary: Western Australian Government department whose WAVE Pilot investigates the potential of machine learning for native vegetation mapping.

name: Dhelkunya Dja Land Management Board
summary: Board that jointly manages and oversees the Dja Dja Wurrung parks, for which a Joint Management Plan is in place.

name: Dhimurru Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation whose rangers manage Yolngu land and sea Country in the Dhimurru Indigenous Protected Area, including threats such as feral animals, invasive weeds and marine debris.

name: Digital Earth Australia
summary: Geoscience Australia programme that makes free and open satellite data products for Australia, including land cover, mangroves, intertidal and fractional cover products.

name: Diversity Arrays Technology
summary: Company that delivers CSIRO's NatureIQ biodiversity assessment tool.

name: Dja Dja Wurrung Clans Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation that manages six parks and reserves on Dja Dja Wurrung Country in Victoria jointly with the Victorian Government under a Recognition and Settlement Agreement.

name: Djabugay Bulmba Rangers
summary: Ranger group in Far North Queensland that set trail cameras on Flaggy Creek and found a platypus among 400,000 images, as part of Eyes on Country.

name: Dudley Peninsula Feral Cat Eradication program
summary: Feral cat eradication program run by the Kangaroo Island Landscape Board, where remote cameras capture around 30,000 images a day, processed by the eVorta AI platform to identify cats and priority native species.

name: Dugalunji Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation named as host of the Lake Eyre Basin Rangers, based at Longreach and Mount Isa, who do natural resource management and cultural heritage protection across Queensland’s channel country.

name: Dulabed and Malanbarra Yidinji Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation named as host of the Jawajawa rangers, who care for traditional country around Gordonvale within the Wet Tropics World Heritage Area.

name: Earth Observation Australia
summary: National association for the Australian Earth observation community.

name: Eastern Australian waterbird survey
summary: Annual low level aerial survey of waterbirds across eastern Australia, operating since 1983 and carried out by the University of NSW.

name: EcoAssets
summary: Atlas of Living Australia project with ARDC that links three national research infrastructures to deliver integrated data for State of the Environment reporting.

name: ECOCEAN
summary: Not-for-profit based in Western Australia that researches and conserves whale sharks and keeps a whale shark photo-ID library.

name: Ecocene
summary: Company specialising in data-driven ecological management for mine closure and ecosystem restoration, with the Ecoda platform, AI camera traps and acoustic monitoring.

name: EcoCommons
summary: Cloud platform for ecological and environmental modelling, giving access to curated datasets, species distribution models and training.

name: EcoDNA
summary: Research and development team translating eDNA technologies for biosecurity and biodiversity in Australia and the Asia Pacific, with a National eDNA Reference Centre at the University of Canberra.

name: Edith Cowan University
summary: University described as a research collaborator with Landgate on MyFireWatch, with authors leading 2023 and 2025 papers on museum specimen collections and recreational fisheries survey trends.

name: eDNA for Biodiversity Action (WA)
summary: Western Australian eDNA project listed among the Biodiversity in Action projects and funded through Landcare Biodiversity in Action.

name: eDNA for Global Environment Studies
summary: Curtin University environmental DNA research program with projects on threatened species, invasive marine species and underground invertebrates.

name: ednaAustralia
summary: Company offering environmental DNA analysis.

name: ENVestigator
summary: Toolkit using Earth observation and machine learning to monitor groundwater dependent vegetation, led by FrontierSI.

name: EOWater
summary: Google Earth Engine toolkit that uses satellite imagery to monitor water surface areas in the Murray-Darling Basin.

name: eReefs
summary: Forecasting and modelling program for the Great Barrier Reef, combining satellite technology, models and machine learning.

name: Esperance Tjaltjraak Native Title Aboriginal Corporation RNTBC
summary: Native title corporation named in the Australian Government's 2024 announcement of 12 new Indigenous Protected Areas as the organisation for the new Wudjari IPA in Western Australia.

name: eVorta
summary: Technology provider on the HAND trap, and developing the Cat Audio Deterrent with Bush Heritage Australia.

name: Ewamian Ltd
summary: Organisation hosting the Ewamian rangers, based at Talaroo Station near Georgetown, who care for savannah lands in the upper Gilbert and Einasleigh River catchments, as listed by the Queensland Government.

name: Eyes on Country
summary: First Nations-led project set up by WWF-Australia with Google.org funding, combining Indigenous Knowledge with trail cameras, Wildlife Insights, eDNA and drones, including platypus monitoring by the Djabugay Bulmba Rangers.

name: Eyre Peninsula Landscape Board
summary: Landscape board that uses solar-powered 4G remote cameras to support recovery of drooping sheoak grassy woodland, in a project funded by the Australian Government Natural Heritage Trust.

name: FAHM Cam
summary: Project, announced in July 2025, that aims to use edge AI herbivore monitoring cameras for proactive kangaroo management in the Gawler Ranges district, funded by the Kangaroo Partnerships Project.

name: Felixer
summary: Automated grooming trap for feral cats. Newer models use a camera and lidar with AI to detect and confirm a cat.

name: Fenner School of Environment & Society
summary: Australian National University school whose researchers helped develop a machine-learning fuel moisture map for Australia from Sentinel-2 imagery.

name: FeralAI
summary: KJR software that identifies and categorises animals by species in thermal drone images.

name: FeralScan
summary: Tool from the Centre for Invasive Species Solutions that records observations of feral animals including cats, foxes, deer, birds, mice and rabbits.

name: Fire Foresight
summary: An active organisation based in Cambridge, Tasmania, that uses a camera network and AI to spot early smoke, with human verification, and reports 3.3 million hectares under monitoring.

name: Fireball International
summary: Queensland company whose sensor system uses satellite and ground sensor data with deep learning to detect bushfires.

name: Fireproofing Koalas
summary: $600,000 project on Minjerribah (North Stradbroke Island) in which Quandamooka rangers find koalas with an AI thermal drone before cultural burns.

name: FireWatch
summary: Landgate satellite products that detect fires and monitor their effect on the land.

name: FishID
summary: AI system for researchers to annotate imagery and train deep learning models to monitor coastal and marine species.

name: Flinders University
summary: University whose Global Ecology author leads a 2023 paper on predicting predator and prey interactions in terrestrial endotherms using random forest.

name: FLINTpro
summary: Nature analytics company assessing agricultural supply chain deforestation risk and biodiversity impacts, with a platform offering preloaded datasets, remote sensing maps and EU Deforestation Regulation reports.

name: FrogID
summary: National citizen science project in which people record frog calls on a smartphone, with expert validation and work towards automated identification.

name: FrontierSI
summary: Not-for-profit research organisation that has built machine learning vegetation mapping for the Murray-Darling Basin Authority and the Victorian Government.

name: Fungimap
summary: Community organisation that records and maps fungi in Australia and keeps the National Australian Fungimap Database.

name: Gaia Resources

name: Greybits Engineering

summary: University named as recipient of an ARC Discovery grant on acoustics for biodiversity assessment, and as a Reef Restoration and Adaptation Program partner.

name: KJR

summary: Regional authority whose Land and Sea Management Unit supports 13 Ranger groups across 14 Torres Strait communities, grown from one group on Mabuiag in 2009, according to its 2024 account.

name: Tracks App
summary: Ecological science app for Aboriginal ranger groups to record animal tracks and other signs, designed by the Indigenous Desert Alliance and developed by the Atlas of Living Australia.

name: Trailing AI Smart-Gate Technology for adaptive macropod management
summary: Project funded by the Kangaroo Partnerships Project, testing AI-powered gates on Kangaroo Island fencing in July 2025 for Tammar wallaby management while aiming to protect other wildlife.

name: Trees For Life
summary: Offers volunteers over 300 established Bush For Life sites in South Australia, each a bushland site regenerated with help from a regional coordinator.

name: Trust for Nature (Victoria)
summary: Conservation trust that owns and manages more than 40 reserves across Victoria, 42 in total with some open to the public, and holds conservation covenants on private land.

name: Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park Board of Management
