summary: Board that makes major policy and management decisions for Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park, while Parks Australia implements its decisions and manages the park day to day.

name: Uncrewed Research Aircraft Facility
summary: Programme working on drone use in environmental monitoring, combining aircraft, sensors and processing techniques, and supporting research, development and training with natural resource managers and government agencies.

name: University of Adelaide
summary: An active university whose School of Biological Sciences hosted the Spatial Sciences Group in 2019, which used GIS and remote sensing.

name: University of Canberra
summary: Australian university whose authors lead papers from 2021 to 2023 on eDNA detection of a cryptic insect and rare native fish, and on generative AI applied to bird bill shapes.

name: University of Melbourne
summary: University whose researchers, writing on AIhub, describe building and testing the Hespi herbarium pipeline. Its main site refused the fetcher.

name: University of New England
summary: Australian university that is a partner in the Australian Acoustic Observatory and Open Ecoacoustics. Its own site refuses this tool, so facts come from partners.

name: University of New South Wales
summary: University collaborating with Nature Foundation on a federally funded project to process audio biodiversity data for monitoring in remote Australia.

name: University of Newcastle
summary: Australian university that the NSW Wildlife Drone Hub names as a research collaborator on real-time AI for thermal detection of koalas.

name: University of Sydney
summary: University whose groups include the ACFR Marine Robotics Program and the Ecosystem Dynamics Lab, which studies AI software for biodiversity monitoring.

name: University of Tasmania
summary: University that created one of the models in the Stickybeak camera trap tool and is Lead Agent for IMOS.

name: University of the Sunshine Coast
summary: Australian university whose authors lead 2025 papers on validating machine learning for classifying animal behaviour from accelerometers and on forest restoration potential using machine learning.

name: University of Wollongong
summary: University whose researchers led the development of MossCam and an AI sensing platform to monitor Antarctic moss beds.

name: Victorian National Parks Association
summary: Victorian nature group that runs NatureWatch, a citizen science programme of spotlighting and camera monitoring, and ReefWatch.

name: Victorian Species Recognition Model
summary: AI model that recognises 212 wildlife and feral animal species in remote camera images, launched by Parks Victoria and Addax in April 2026.

name: WA Vegetation Extent Pilot
summary: Pilot run by the Department of Water and Environmental Regulation showing deep learning on satellite imagery can map native vegetation, though confined to three Western Australian pilot regions.

name: Walalakoo Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation that in May 2017 announced a Healthy Country Plan to protect the Fitzroy River and guide management of the Nyikina Mangala native title area, intended to help the Nyikina Mangala Rangers.

name: Warddeken Land Management
summary: Indigenous land manager in West Arnhem that runs the Mayh camera trap monitoring program and applied the MegaDetector model to its images.

name: Watch on Nature
summary: Wilderness Society platform that uses Sentinel-2 satellite imagery to find deforestation in Australia.

name: Watergum
summary: Community conservation group delivering thermal drone surveys with AI analysis across koala habitat in Kooralbyn.

name: WeedRemeed
summary: Software platform that analyses drone imagery with colour picking, AI and machine learning to locate target native plants and weed species.

name: Wellington Park Management Trust
summary: Management trust that issues permits for activities within Wellington Park, including launching or landing drones and holding wedding receptions with tables or marquees.

name: Western Australian Biodiversity Science Institute
summary: Western Australian institute working on biodiversity data and information management, which runs the Shared Environmental Analytics Facility with the Western Australian Marine Science Institution.

name: Western Australian Herbarium
summary: Collection of more than 845,000 specimens within the Western Australian biodiversity department, with information made freely available through Florabase.

name: Western Sydney University
summary: Australian university whose author leads 2025 computer vision and machine learning research on turtle roadkill; a School of Science author leads 2026 research on platypus behaviour from accelerometry.

name: Western Yalanji Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation that hosts the Western Yalanji rangers, who care for traditional country around Palmerville Station in central-southeastern Cape York Peninsula, as listed by the Queensland Government.

name: Wheatbelt NRM
summary: Western Australian natural resource management group that trained local citizen scientists to run airborne eDNA surveys with EnviroDNA.

name: Wild Echo
summary: Acoustic monitoring product that uses AI to identify Australian species and monitor biodiversity, and also watches hive health.

name: WildCount
summary: New South Wales wildlife survey programme that ran from 2012 to 2021, with a final report published in 2025.

name: Wilderness Society
summary: Environmental organisation that runs Watch on Nature, a platform tracking deforestation in Australia with satellite imagery.

name: Wildlife Observatory of Australia
summary: National platform that stores and analyses camera trap images with AI species classifiers, developed at the University of Queensland with QCIF, ARDC and TERN.

name: Wildlife Preservation Society of Queensland
summary: Named by EnviroDNA as delivering the Resilient Rivers SEQ eDNA monitoring programme.

name: WildObs Camera Trap Tagged Image Repository
summary: Verified, species-labelled camera-trap images from WildObs, published on the Atlas of Living Australia for training and testing computer vision models.

name: WildObs QLD Wet Tropics model
summary: Region-specific computer vision model for wildlife camera-trap images from the Australian Wet Tropics, fine-tuned from SpeciesNet.

name: WildSeek
summary: National program using thermal drones, AI and community surveys to find and protect koalas across eastern Australia.

name: WildSeek Project: Community Wildlife Intelligence Hubs
summary: Network of community hubs that collect drone footage of wildlife for analysis with a QUT algorithm, starting with koalas.

name: WildTracker
summary: Tasmanian Land Conservancy tool that lets private landholders upload, tag and share camera trap images.

name: Wilinggin Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Supports the Wunggurr Rangers and Nyaliga Rangers, both formed in 2020 and working on Wilinggin country in the northern Kimberley; the groups are responsible to the Corporation.

name: Winda-Mara Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation whose Land Management Unit manages over 3,000 hectares of Aboriginal-owned land across more than 10 properties in the Budj Bim National Heritage Landscape, western Victoria.

name: WIRES
summary: Wildlife rescue charity that launched the WildSeek project with Landcare Australia and QUT and made a significant contribution to its funding.

name: Wolli Creek Preservation Society
summary: Community group in Sydney linked to an ongoing bird survey of the Wolli Creek valley running since 1964.

name: Woodlands and Wetlands Trust
summary: Trust established to ensure two Canberra reserves, Mulligans Flat Woodland Sanctuary and Jerrabomberra Wetlands Nature Reserve, are managed to provide rich and diverse environments.

name: Woppaburra TUMRA Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation that hosts the Woppaburra rangers, who work from Rosslyn Bay and Woppa (Great Keppel Island) caring for sea country in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park.

name: Worimi Conservation Lands Board of Management
summary: Board for Worimi-owned Conservation Lands near Port Stephens, New South Wales, leased to the NSW Government for joint management; the lease secures an Aboriginal owner majority on the board.

name: Wreck Bay Aboriginal Community Council
summary: Council that owns Booderee National Park, which is leased to the Commonwealth and jointly managed by Parks Australia and the Wreck Bay Aboriginal community as Traditional Owners.

name: Wunambal Gaambera Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Secured native title over Wunambal Gaambera country in the north Kimberley in May 2011 and declared the first stage of Uunguu Indigenous Protected Area, covering 343,700 hectares.

name: Wuthathi Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation that hosts the Wuthathi Land and Sea Custodians, who look after country at Shelburne Bay on north-eastern Cape York Peninsula and sea country east to Raine Island.

name: WWF-Australia
summary: Australian arm of WWF, which uses Wildlife Insights on camera images, set up the First Nations-led Eyes on Country project and works with Indigenous rangers on AI drone koala surveys.

name: Xylo Systems
summary: Sydney company with an AI-driven platform for biodiversity assessments, used by businesses to track impact and report against frameworks such as TNFD.

name: Yalata Anangu Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation that is the governing body of the Yalata Indigenous Protected Area in South Australia.

name: Yindjibarndi Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation named as the organisation for the new Yindjibarndi Indigenous Protected Area in Western Australia, announced by the Australian Government in 2024 among 12 new such areas.

name: Yorta Yorta Nation Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation through which the Yorta Yorta People were party to a 2004 cooperative management agreement with the State, which established the Yorta Yorta Joint Body to participate in managing the agreement lands.

name: Yorta Yorta Traditional Owner Land Management Board
summary: Board that, under the 2010 Traditional Owner Land Management Agreement, must prepare with the Secretary a Joint Management Plan for Barmah National Park, subject to ministerial approval.

name: Yuku-Baja-Muliku Landowner & Reserves Ltd
summary: Landowner company that hosts the Yuku Baja Muliku Rangers, who care for country at Archer Point near Cooktown, bordering the Great Barrier Reef and Wet Tropics World Heritage Areas.

name: Yuwi Aboriginal Corporation
summary: Aboriginal corporation that hosts the Yuwi Land and Sea Rangers, who work to protect the natural and cultural resource values of their land and sea country around Mackay.

name: Zoos Victoria
summary: Zoo-based conservation organisation that worked with Parks Victoria on AI cameras to monitor seals in Port Phillip Bay, as described in a supplier's report.

name: Azerbaijan National Aerospace Agency
summary: A Baku agency whose affiliated researcher Tabriz Tahmazov co-authored a 2023 paper on estimating forest tree allometric indicators from satellite data, including a biomass formula derived from NDVI values.

name: Azerbaijan Ornithological Society
summary: National NGO and BirdLife International member, listed by IUCN as a member since March 2008.

name: Azercosmos
summary: Azerbaijan space agency, as Report.az calls it, offering satellite-based forest and deforestation monitoring tools, and in March 2025 reporting a Papua New Guinea forest monitoring programme with an AI platform expected to launch.

name: Azercosmos Deforestation Detection
summary: A tool run by Azercosmos that, by its account, detects land-cover change and deforestation patterns linked to logging or land clearing, available as an AI model on GEO360.

name: Baku State University
summary: A university whose Geography Department produced a 2023 paper assessing forest transformation in Eastern Zangezur, using Landsat and AzerSky imagery with GIS and mathematical methods.

name: Bison Reintroduction
summary: A bison release project in Shahdag National Park run by IDEA, the ecology ministry and WWF Azerbaijan, where IDEA says released bison are tracked with GPS collars.

name: Camera-trap monitoring of wild animals in the liberated territories (Azerbaijan)
summary: Camera traps installed by Azerbaijan's Ecology Ministry; AzVision reported in February 2023 that traps at Basitchay reserve recorded porcupine, common pheasant and wild boar over one week.

name: Conservation of Egyptian Vulture in Azerbaijan
summary: Closed 12-month Rufford-listed project under Sevinj Sarukhanova, aimed at filling Egyptian vulture population and distribution data gaps in Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic and Gobustan.

name: Conservation of Egyptian Vulture in Lesser Caucasus within the Territory of Azerbaijan
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project, under Guler Isayeva, that aimed to collect breeding population data on Egyptian vultures in the Lesser Caucasus in Azerbaijan, with a distribution model to guide later conservation.

name: Conserving goitered gazelles in the Azerbaijan–Georgia transboundary region
summary: Closed 2024 to 2025 project under the Fondation Segré Conservation Action Fund initiative, in Azerbaijan and Georgia, with planned gazelle monitoring and equipment provision.

name: Forest Development Service (Azerbaijan)
summary: A body listed by the ministry among those under it and run by it, which a 2025 journal article says supplied report materials on tree and forest cover change and carried out 2018–2021 research on forest ecosystem services in Lankaran and Masalli.

name: Forest drone monitoring against illegal logging (Azerbaijan)
summary: Proposed drone system for monitoring Azerbaijan's forests against illegal logging, with images compared electronically; the minister said in May 2026 that contracts were signed, and Ismayilli forests were chosen for the first stage.

name: Forest Resources Assessment and Monitoring to Strengthen Forest Knowledge Framework in Azerbaijan
summary: A project run by the ecology ministry, funded by the Global Environment Facility and partnered with FAO, which the UN said in February 2018 would help establish a national forest assessment and monitoring system.

name: GEO360
summary: Active cloud-based platform, run by Azercosmos, that brings its AI tools together so users can upload satellite imagery and apply models such as deforestation detection in a browser.

name: Geodesy and Cartography Agency (Azerbaijan)
summary: A public legal entity that Trend reported on 17 March 2025 the ministry had enlisted, under a signed contract, to oversee planned detailed mapping of protected natural areas in territories recently liberated from occupation.

name: Geography Department, Baku State University
summary: University department listed by OpenAlex as the sole affiliation on a 2023 paper analysing forest landscape change in Eastern Zangezur, Azerbaijan, using satellite imagery.

name: IDEA Public Association
summary: A Baku-based association founded by Leyla Aliyeva that runs the bison reintroduction, reports camera-trap evidence of six Caucasian leopards in 2015, and partners with the ecology ministry and Blue Marine Foundation.

name: Increasing representation of effectively managed marine ecosystems in the protected area system (Azerbaijan)
summary: Closed project, run by the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources, that bought monitoring equipment for all coastal and marine protected areas; its monitoring programme was set up less than six months before the end.

name: Institute of Botany, Ministry of Science and Education of the Republic of Azerbaijan
summary: A Baku research centre studying Azerbaijan's flora, whose staff published a paper applying remote sensing and GIS to arid sparse forest vegetation in the Turyanchay State Nature Reserve.

name: Institute of Geography, Azerbaijan National Academy of Sciences
summary: A research institute whose researcher Emil A. Jabrayilov published a 2022 Sentinel-2 study of Shahdagh National Park, and which signed a 2018 protocol of intentions with Azercosmos on forest monitoring, per Azernews.

name: Institute of Living Systems Research
summary: A Baku public legal entity under the Ministry of Science and Education whose authors' 2026 paper reports 257 expeditions on resident Lankaran birds, with data used in the 2023 Red Book of Azerbaijan.

name: Inventory, Reporting and Monitoring Data Management System for Specially Protected Nature Areas of Azerbaijan
summary: A project, per DOTSOFT, to support the ecology ministry in building an integrated protected-area data system, delivering four modules and implementation in two pilot parks, Shirvan and Hirkan.

name: Leopard Project
summary: A joint leopard conservation project run by WWF Azerbaijan, IDEA and the ecology ministry, which WWF Azerbaijan says set up camera-trap monitoring in the Hyrcan Forest and Zangezur.

name: Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources of the Republic of Azerbaijan
summary: Azerbaijan's ecology ministry, which was developing a National Biodiversity Monitoring System with 20 indicators and in May 2026 said it planned AI-based platforms for drone forest monitoring, starting in Ismayilli.

name: Platerra
summary: An AI tool built by Azercosmos that, according to Report.az citing Azercosmos, processes satellite imagery automatically into geospatial data, including detecting forest areas and water body surface area.

name: Rare Plant Conservation in Azerbaijan: Monitoring Threats and Education of Local Community
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project, under Yelena Gambarova, that planned to monitor threats to rare vegetation, such as overgrazing and pipeline construction, by linking GPS-located field plots to satellite images.

name: Rare Vegetation Monitoring in the Gobustan National Park, Azerbaijan
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project under Yelena Gambarova that used satellite image classification and an NDVI comparison to find changes in rare vegetation from 2004 to 2007.

name: Research and Conservation of Imperial Eagle (Aquila heliaca) in Azerbaijan
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project, under Shahin Isayev, that set out to study the number and distribution of imperial eagles in Azerbaijan, with its report and database intended for conservation bodies.

name: Rəqəmsal ekologiya informasiya sistemi
summary: Active ‘Digital ecology’ information system, whose regulation was approved by presidential decree in January 2025, with forest, ecological monitoring and biological diversity subsystems.

name: Tackling the Issues of Little Bustard (Tetrax tetrax) Conservation in Azerbaijan
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project whose early 2023 ten-day survey observed almost 20,000 wintering little bustards and found that hundreds are poached each year despite legal protection.

name: WWF Azerbaijan
summary: A Baku-based branch of WWF International registered in January 2006, which runs the bison reintroduction and says it set up camera-trap leopard monitoring in the Hyrcan Forest and Zangezur.

name: ATRA Climate Explorer
summary: An application presented by ATRA for researching the effects of climate change on the herpetofauna of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

name: Biologer BiH
summary: Active Bosnia and Herzegovina community of the free Biologer biodiversity data software, which its site says has 338 users who have submitted 67,561 observations.

name: Cantonal Public Institution for Protected Natural Areas, Sarajevo Canton
summary: Sarajevo-based body for the canton's protected areas that reported fish monitoring research starting on 7 July 2023 and organised a presentation of the project's results.

name: Center for Karst and Speleology
summary: NGO that was CEPF's grantee for a 2013 to 2015 project to create a network of volunteer bat monitors.

name: Climate smart natural mixed forest (NATMIXFOR)
summary: European Forest Institute-funded project, due to start on 1 April 2025 for 18 months, planning twelve experimental plots in mixed beech, fir and spruce forests as part of the FORWARDS project.

name: Department of Forestry, Faculty of Agriculture, University of East Sarajevo
summary: A forestry department at the University of East Sarajevo, listed as the first author's affiliation on a 2024 paper quantifying forest cover loss from drought and spruce dieback with remote sensing.

name: E-PRIRODA FB&H
summary: A nature conservation information system whose fundamental database, built on the Darwin Core standard, was set up by the GIZ-implemented BIMR sub-project from July 2016 to May 2021.

name: Environmental Protection Fund of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
summary: A fund named as a beneficiary of the protected areas module and of the fundamental database of the Information System for Nature Conservation, and a partner of the Sustainability of Protected Areas project.

name: F.I.R.E.S. (Forefront Initiative for Rapid Early Suppression - Early Warning of Forest Fires)
summary: Pilot that, according to People in Need, gave Jablanica and Konjic their first thermal-camera drones for wildfire detection, after a November 2023 announcement of smoke detectors linked to a cloud system.

name: Faculty of Architecture, Civil Engineering and Geodesy, University of Banja Luka
summary: University of Banja Luka faculty listed as the affiliation of the first author of two papers, a 2025 one on estimating tree biomass with multisource remote sensing and a 2023 one on Sentinel-2 forest assessment at Derventa.

name: Faculty of Forestry, University of Banja Luka
summary: A faculty at the University of Banja Luka, listed as the first author's affiliation on a 2024 paper monitoring vegetation indices with Copernicus data in Republic of Srpska old-growth forests.

name: Faculty of Forestry, University of Sarajevo
summary: University of Sarajevo faculty listed as the affiliation of the first author of a 2025 paper on detecting dry trees using NDVI images taken by a drone.

name: Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics, University of Banja Luka
summary: A faculty in Banja Luka, listed as the first author's first affiliation on a 2025 paper on remote sensing for wildfire monitoring in the Sana River basin.

name: Federal Ministry of Environment and Tourism
summary: A ministry that the 2016 national biodiversity strategy names as the National Focal Point for the Convention on Biological Diversity, and which says the Federation's protected area share rose from 3.7% to 4.6% in 2025.

name: Flora Srpske
summary: A dataset on the vascular flora of the Republic of Srpska, built by the University of Banja Luka's Faculty of Forestry, with a GIS database available as a module of the RS nature conservation information system.

name: FORESTMAP
summary: Closed project that mapped areas at risk of illegal logging across the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, identified protected-area hotspots and held its closing event on 14 May 2026.

name: Forestry and Environmental Action
summary: Sarajevo-based civil society organisation, established in 2007 and accredited by the UNCCD, that runs the FORESTMAP project mapping areas at risk of illegal logging in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

name: Herpetological Association in Bosnia and Herzegovina ATRA
summary: A Bosnian-Herzegovinian herpetological association whose site presents ATRA Climate Explorer and announced in December 2024 that it would carry out the Federation's herpetofauna inventory.

name: Hutovo Blato Nature Park
summary: Nature park managed by a public enterprise in Čapljina, whose management plan includes biodiversity monitoring and whose rangers also took part in bird monitoring reported by a 2015 CEPF final report.

name: Hutovo Blato Nature Park and Mostarsko Blato as Safe Breeding, Stop-Over and Wintering Sites for Birds
summary: A closed CEPF-funded project to set up hunting monitoring at Hutovo Blato Nature Park with EuroNatur and extend it to Mostarsko Blato, with monthly monitoring of birds and illegal activities reported.

name: Improving the Management of Hutovo Blato Nature Park
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project from June 2013 to August 2015 whose final report describes protection monitoring using water birds as indicators, with bird monitoring from October 2013.

name: Institute for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology, University of Sarajevo
summary: University institute whose journal published a 2017 paper describing REBIDA as collating known biological data on Bosnia and Herzegovina's natural resources.

name: International Census Plots scheme in Bosnia and Herzegovina
summary: Long-term bird monitoring programme whose first surveys, in spring 2024, covered seven census plots, each with two 1 km transects, and whose data also support a national breeding bird atlas.

name: Inventory, population and health status of large carnivores and other species in Skakavac Natural Monument
summary: Closed 2017 to 2019 project, run by the University of Sarajevo's Veterinary Faculty, that used camera traps and GPS/GSM collar telemetry on a bear to study large carnivores in Skakavac Natural Monument.

name: Let's Make Better Future for Grey Wolves in Bosnia & Herzegovina: Continuation of Conservation Activities
summary: Closed project whose 2018 Rufford page planned combined field and genetic wolf monitoring to identify conservation management units, following earlier field monitoring, non-invasive sampling and genetic analyses.

name: Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations of Bosnia and Herzegovina
summary: State ministry in Sarajevo whose water, tourism and environmental protection sector lists environmental data collection and monitoring among its competences, and which UNDP says partners on two GEF-funded initiatives launched in July 2026.

name: Ministry of Scientific and Technological Development, Higher Education and Information Society of the Republika Srpska
summary: Republika Srpska ministry which, according to the GIZ BIMR project page, partially funded the Flora Srpske project.

name: Ministry of Spatial Planning, Construction and Ecology of the Republic of Srpska
summary: A Republic of Srpska ministry that UNDP said in June 2024 was expected, with the agriculture and forestry ministry, to adopt the lynx monitoring protocol.

name: Ornithological Society Naše Ptice
summary: A society listed by CEPF as grantee of the Hutovo Blato hunting monitoring project, whose final report says teams monitored three times a month for 13 months.

name: Regional Biodiversity Database (REBIDA)
summary: Open-access, searchable biodiversity platform built by the Institute for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology, described in 2017 with tissue, DNA and digital genetic segments and a mobile app, REBIDA SCANNER, for contributions.

name: Republic Institute for the Protection of Cultural, Historical and Natural Heritage of the Republic of Srpska
summary: A Republic of Srpska institute named as a direct beneficiary of the GIZ BIMR nature conservation database and its protected areas module, and as data source for the RS Red List Index indicator.

name: Safeguarding Unique Biodiversity of Drina Valley Environment
summary: A closed, 18-month project starting July 2019, with €165,179.07 in contracted EU funding, whose activities included remote sensing assessments and procuring drones for mapping Pančić spruce habitats.

name: Second State Forest Inventory of Bosnia and Herzegovina
summary: A national forest inventory described in a University of Sarajevo paper that compares it with the first, from 1964 to 1968; the 2008 paper reports satellite-image interpretation for the Unska district.

name: Support to Implementation of the Birds and Habitats Directives in Bosnia and Herzegovina
summary: Project funded by the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, with a stated budget of 1,429,000, whose listed tasks include a Natura 2000 information system and a Natura 2000 proposal with consultation.

name: Sustainability of Protected Areas
summary: A GEF-funded project run by UNDP Bosnia and Herzegovina with environment ministries and funds; in June 2024, UNDP reported work had begun to establish long-term lynx population monitoring.

name: Sutjeska National Park
summary: A national park whose affiliated author co-wrote a paper on field monitoring of chamois during 2017 to 2020 that used a drone alongside field methods.

name: Una National Park
summary: A national park whose projects page describes a wolf population monitoring and inventory project, and names it an implementing partner in EcoSUSTAIN, which planned satellite-based water quality monitoring from November 2016.

name: Una Science Week 2026
summary: Closed 2026 fieldwork week organised by Riverwatch with two partners, in which, Riverwatch reported, more than 70 scientists and students surveyed 660 river kilometres of the Una basin, including olm populations.

name: University of Banja Luka
summary: A university whose Faculty of Forestry appears on a 2024 Copernicus vegetation index paper and whose Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics appears on a 2025 paper on remote sensing wildfire monitoring.

name: University of East Sarajevo
summary: A university whose Department of Forestry is the first author's affiliation on a 2024 remote sensing paper on forest cover loss from drought and spruce dieback.

name: University of Sarajevo
summary: Sarajevo university whose Faculty of Forestry, it reported in October 2025, signed a grant agreement with the European Forest Institute for NATMIXFOR and planned to use the ICP Forests methodology.

name: Veterinary Faculty, University of Sarajevo
summary: University of Sarajevo faculty named in the Skakavac project brochure as the partner carrying out the project's activities, including the bear telemetry work and laboratory analysis of samples.

name: Assessment and Management of Lionfish and Status of Other Marine Invasive Species of Threat to High Biodiversity-value Reef Ecosystems
summary: A closed GEF-funded project run by CERMES and UWI Cave Hill re-surveyed 10 reefs for one year and found no invasive Halophila stipulacea; final report February 2023.

name: Bajan Digital Creations Inc.
summary: Company that entered the Blue Bot Project in an Oceans Challenge, Export Barbados reported in 2022; its CEO said the project uses locally developed AI on underwater video.

name: Barbados cetacean surveys for the Marine Spatial Plan
summary: Barbados Today reports visual and acoustic whale and dolphin surveys for the Marine Spatial Plan in February, March and November 2025, with the team intending to continue them.

name: Barbados Coral Reef Monitoring Programme
summary: Reef monitoring programme run by the Coastal Zone Management Unit, which a 2024 ICRI member report says collects quantitative data on 47 reef sites across the island.

name: Barbados Environmental Conservation Trust
summary: Charity that funds the Barbados Sea Turtle Project and gives its registered charity number on its site.

name: Barbados Marine Spatial Plan Project
summary: An active marine spatial planning process launched by the Coastal Zone Management Unit in January 2023, which Barbados Today reported in November 2024 had reached about 80 per cent of data collection across 435 marine sites.

name: Barbados National Wetland Inventory
summary: Completed in March 2023, this inventory categorises Barbados's primary, secondary and tertiary wetlands and reports on biodiversity, threats and ecosystem services, focusing on Long Pond, Green Pond, Graeme Hall and Chancery Lane.

name: Barbados Sea Turtle Project
summary: Turtle project funded by the Barbados Environmental Conservation Trust, which says it has worked for over 30 years on monitoring, rescue, genetic analysis and satellite telemetry.

name: Benthic habitat classification scheme and island-wide map for Barbados
summary: A shallow marine habitat map of Barbados to 40 m depth, described in a 2019 CERMES report, using WorldView-2 imagery, LiDAR bathymetry and 361 ground-truthing sites for coastal adaptation.

name: Biodiversity Conservation and Management Section
summary: A section of the Ministry of Environment and National Beautification that leads the government's biodiversity programme and, under the GEF CBER project, surveyed gullies and wetlands for the Critically Endangered Barbados threadsnake, with eDNA follow-up under way in November 2024.

name: BlueBOT
summary: Robot built by Bajan Digital Creations and funded by UNDP, which reports ten public datasets from its images in 2020 and a 2024 award of up to US$40,000.

name: Centre for Resource Management and Environmental Studies
summary: University of the West Indies centre at Cave Hill that runs the Sargassum Outlook Bulletin, with island-scale forecasts for the Eastern Caribbean, and publishes a drone-based sargassum monitoring protocol.

name: Coastal Zone Management Unit
summary: Barbados unit established in 1996, according to its site, which runs the coral reef monitoring programme and says it has monitored corals since 1982 at five-year intervals.

name: Conserving Barbados' Endemic Reptiles
summary: Reptile project funded by GEF, with UNEP and CAB International as partners; a 2025 excerpt says searches of 20 sites in 2024 and early 2025 found only invasive blindsnakes.

name: Coral Reef Restoration Alliance
summary: Non-governmental organisation in a coral restoration project completed in August 2022; GEF SGP says it set up a nursery and two restoration sites in 2018.

name: Department of Biological and Chemical Sciences, The University of the West Indies, Cave Hill
summary: A Barbados department listing turtle conservation and plant database projects, it reported over 1,100 species documented across three campuses during November 2026's UWI Inter-Campus Biodiversity Week.

name: Invasive Predator Control at a Selected Hawksbill Nesting Beach: Bath Pilot Project
summary: A GEF-funded ministry pilot with Mosaic Eco Consult (June 2021–August 2022) reported 75.6% lower nest predation in 2022, possibly following removal of 57 mongooses.

name: Lands and Surveys Department
summary: Department that aims to be the hub of surveying, mapping and geospatial services and the government's national surveying agency, with map layers including vegetation, cultivation and pastures.

name: Long Pond Wetland Restoration Project
summary: Wetland project run by the Walkers Institute for Regenerative Research, Education and Design; partner the Barbados Environmental Conservation Trust says water quality monitoring and continuous probes track wetland health.

name: Ministry of Environment and National Beautification, Blue and Green Economy
summary: Barbados ministry whose biodiversity site lists the Graeme Hall Swamp Monitoring Programme under biodiversity management; the Government of Barbados site gives its current name.

name: National Conservation Commission
summary: Department directed by a Board of Management, per the ministry's biodiversity site, whose operations include a ranger and warden service and a marine reserve.

name: Plants of the Eastern Caribbean
summary: An online plant database and virtual herbarium maintained by the University of the West Indies, with specimens still being scanned and the database updated by a senior technician, per a December 2025 department page.

name: Reef Check Barbados
summary: An active Reef Check programme in Barbados, with 52 surveys recorded on the Global Reef Tracker and Barbados Blue named as its EcoDiver training facility.

name: SargAdapt
summary: A project of the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund Ecosystem based Adaptation Facility, led by CERMES and funded by the International Climate Initiative, planning sargassum research and drone monitoring protocols across five Eastern Caribbean countries over three years.

name: Scylla
summary: Analytic software built by BlueBOT; UNDP's account of 2021 says more classes in BlueBOT's dataset marked a milestone in developing its first version.

name: Sub-regional Sargassum Outlook Bulletin
summary: Programme run by the Centre for Resource Management and Environmental Studies, giving medium-range, island-scale forecasts of sargassum influxes to the Eastern Caribbean, with notes for tourism and fisheries stakeholders.

name: Walkers Institute for Regenerative Research Education and Design
summary: Described in 2019 as a local non-profit, it is associated with Long Pond wetland restoration, whose monitoring includes biodiversity assessments and probes continuously recording pH and conductivity.

name: Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology
summary: Dhaka university whose computer science and engineering department had a researcher lead a 2019 paper on identifying species from DNA barcode sequences using supervised learning methods.

name: Aquatic Bioresource Research Lab, Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University
summary: Lab at Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University that the freshwater portal says generated DNA barcodes it includes, and the marine portal says took the initiative to make marine biodiversity information available.

name: Arannayk Foundation
summary: Dhaka forest and biodiversity non-profit established through a Bangladesh–US government agreement in 2003, with a Rainforest Trust-funded Hararganj project scheduled for November 2026 to May 2029.

name: Bangladesh Environment and Development Society
summary: Self-described community-based non-profit in Khulna; a grantee page reports its White-rumped Vulture project, begun in 2024, tracked four vultures with satellite tags and identified nine active nests.

name: Bangladesh Forest Department
summary: Dhaka-based department under the environment ministry that piloted SMART patrol management in the West Sundarbans Sanctuary, according to a 2016 WCS release, and organised the January 2026 Faunal Red List workshop.

name: Bangladesh Forest Information System
summary: Forest information system run and built by the Forest Department, launched in December 2018 with FAO support and UN-REDD and USAID funding, including a forest cover Geoportal.

name: Bangladesh Forest Inventory
summary: Closed 2016 to 2019 forest inventory run by the Forest Department and built by FAO and SilvaCarbon, which visited 1,781 field plots and surveyed 6,400 households, according to FAO's catalogue.

name: Bangladesh Forest Research Institute
summary: National forest research institute whose 2017–2018 programme planned to maintain 30 permanent sample plots across salinity zones in the Sundarbans and collect regeneration, salinity and siltation data from them.

name: Bangladesh National Herbarium
summary: Herbarium whose site lists field plant surveys and specimen collection, lets applicants examine specimens, and whose records fed a Jagannath University dataset registered with GBIF.

name: Bangladesh Oceanographic Research Institute
summary: Institute established on 8 September 2015 whose 2024 annual report describes a remote sensing study of change in tidal salt marshes and mangroves, and which plans a marine data archive and National Oceanographic Database.

name: Bangladesh Shorebird Tracking Project
summary: Active project run by SCOPE Foundation, led by Sayam U. Chowdhury, using GPS-GSM devices and colour flags; the page says it produced the first high-resolution movement data for wintering shorebirds in Bangladesh.

name: Bangladesh Space Research and Remote Sensing Organization
summary: Government space agency of Bangladesh, according to Wikipedia, using remote sensing in fields including forestry and fisheries; two researchers wrote a 2024 paper on Sundarbans mangrove forest stocking changes.

name: Bangladesh Spoon-billed Sandpiper Conservation Project
summary: Active project run by SCOPE Foundation, started in 2009, with monthly winter shorebird surveys at Sonadia Island since 2009 and January monitoring at 45 to 55 Meghna Estuary sites.

name: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology
summary: Dhaka university whose computer science and engineering researchers wrote a 2021 paper on the accuracy of DNA mini-barcodes for species identification using supervised machine learning.

name: Bats of Bangladesh: Bat Assemblage Structure and Species Responses to Land-Use Change
summary: Aims to describe Bangladesh's bat diversity and forest bats' responses to land-use change, with recordings planned to support a call library; a November 2022 update reported 36 acoustic transects.

name: Begum Rokeya University
summary: Rangpur university whose disaster management researchers wrote a 2021 paper using machine learning to assess risk to riparian wetlands in the Padma River Basin of north-west Bangladesh.

name: BRAC University
summary: Dhaka university whose researchers wrote a 2025 paper comparing the effects of light pollution on moths using machine learning and explainable AI.

name: Camera-trap video dataset for monitoring of wildlife biodiversity and anthropogenic activity in Satchari National Park, Bangladesh
summary: Camera-trap video dataset for Satchari National Park, Bangladesh, recorded by OpenAlex as published in 2026, held on Mendeley Data under a CC BY licence.

name: Center for Environmental and Geographic Information Services
summary: Dhaka non-profit whose researchers wrote a 2023 paper on forest land-use changes in the Madhupur Sal forests, and were among co-authors of a 2019 land cover map overview.

name: Center for Natural Resource Studies
summary: Dhaka-based organisation, formally established in 1994, working on natural resource management and biodiversity conservation, which did a brief baseline wildlife survey in October 2020 with UNHCR support and led biological monitoring for an IUCN Tanguar Haor project.

name: Citizen Science Fishermen Safety Network
summary: Active WCS Bangladesh programme where gillnet fishers record verified catch and sighting data for safety equipment and training, including 234 cetaceans and 96 marine turtles from 2015 to 2024.

name: Conservation and Restoration Initiatives in the Sundarbans Region (CRIS)
summary: Active project launched on 17 November 2025 at the Bangladesh Forest Department, funded by Agence Française de Développement, in which IUCN Bangladesh will lead a faunal inventory and GIS habitat mapping.

name: Creative Conservation Alliance
summary: Bangladesh-based non-profit that Mongabay in 2016 described as training local people as parabiologists, shown setting up camera traps in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

name: Daffodil International University
summary: Active university whose A.B.M Kamal Pasha was principal investigator for the December 2017 to June 2022 drone project, whose team gathered data over Sundarbans forest plots.

name: Department of Environment (Bangladesh)
summary: Department whose Director, Natural Resource Management, is listed by the CBD as Bangladesh's Global Taxonomy Initiative focal point and Cartagena Protocol emergency contact point.

name: Department of Forestry and Environmental Science, Shahjalal University of Science and Technology
summary: Sylhet university department whose authors published a 2023 paper using a deep neural network to identify mangrove and freshwater swamp forest tree species from stomata images.

name: Dolphin Mortality Monitoring Network
summary: Active WCS Bangladesh programme that collects information on the cause, number and distribution of dolphin and porpoise deaths; WCS says it has monitored cetacean deaths since 2007.

name: Drone-based monitoring in the Sundarbans
summary: Drone-based monitoring system adopted in the Sundarbans since March 2021, which a January 2022 report says is useful for covering remote and inaccessible areas, with drone training starting on 19 March 2021.

name: Ecological Monitoring of the Sundarbans
summary: Active project run by CEGIS and Arannayk Foundation, supporting long-term monitoring under the PSMFP by assessing ecosystem health through physical, chemical and biological indicators.

name: Elephant Survey Project
summary: Nationwide elephant survey in Bangladesh, run by Arannayk Foundation, which lists it among its ongoing projects and announced that it would conduct the survey.

name: ESA GDA Forest Management, Bangladesh case study
summary: ESA-run activity supporting a World Bank coastal resilience programme in Bangladesh; ESA says it mapped mangroves across about 52,000 km2 of coast from Sentinel-2, with refinement planned.

name: Freshwater Biodiversity Portal of Bangladesh
summary: Portal claiming an updated freshwater species inventory and GenBank DNA barcodes, built by Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University's Aquatic Bioresource Research Lab and led by Kazi Ahsan Habib.

name: Green University of Bangladesh
summary: Dhaka university whose computer science and engineering researcher led a 2025 paper on acoustic recognition of marine mammals using deep learning.

name: Implementing the Global Land Cover Analysis and Discovery (GLAD) System for monitoring forest and trees outside forests in Bangladesh
summary: Closed 2021 to 2023 project that aimed to improve the Bangladesh Forest Department's forest-monitoring capacity using free US and commercial satellite data, including activity data for REDD+ and UNFCCC reporting.

name: International Islamic University Chittagong
summary: Chattogram university whose computer science and engineering authors wrote a 2025 paper on a ResNet101 deep residual learning framework for automated coral reef health assessment.

name: Khulna University
summary: Bangladeshi university whose researchers co-wrote a 2021 wetland classification paper using machine learning and a 2026 paper, with CSIRO and Monash co-authors, on predicting species abundance from sparse observations.

name: Khulna University of Engineering and Technology
summary: Bangladeshi university whose Department of Urban and Regional Planning authors wrote a 2025 paper mapping forest fire susceptibility in Bangladesh using tree-based machine learning algorithms.

name: Land Cover Map 2015 of Bangladesh
summary: Dataset of unknown status, described in a 2019 paper that overviews the National Land Representation System; OpenAlex gives the first author's affiliation as FAO in Rome.

name: Long-term Monitoring of coastal waterbirds (SCOPE Foundation)
summary: Active SCOPE Foundation project, led by Sayam U. Chowdhury with the Bangladesh Bird Club, surveying 45 to 55 coastal sites yearly and using Sentinel-2 imagery to find new or shifting islands.

name: Marine Biodiversity Portal of Bangladesh
summary: Portal that says it includes DNA barcodes of marine organisms from GenBank, set up on the initiative of Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University's Aquatic Bioresource Research Lab, which built it.

name: Migratory Waterbird Census in Bangladesh
summary: Census run by Prokriti O Jibon Foundation with the Bangladesh Bird Club, which POJF says covers coastal areas, chars, islands and haor basins and is used to assess waterbird status.

name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (Bangladesh)
summary: Government ministry overseeing the Forest Department, whose Acting Secretary is the CBD focal point; its secretary reported the first fully government-funded Faunal Red List update in January 2026.

name: Monitoring Crime-prone Hotspots for Tiger and Deer Poaching in the Sundarbans through Camera Trapping
summary: Active project run by Arannayk Foundation, funded by the Bangladesh Forest Department, using camera traps at 27 pre-defined crime hotspots across four Sundarbans ranges to guide patrol planning.

name: North South University
summary: Dhaka university whose Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering authors published a 2021 paper analysing land cover change in the Sundarbans with machine learning and remote sensing.

name: OdoBD (Odonata of Bangladesh)
summary: Database of the dragonflies and damselflies of Bangladesh, where naturalists contribute sightings, habitat and abundance through a web portal, and biology and occurrence datasets can be downloaded with citation.

name: Parabiologist Initiative (Creative Conservation Alliance)
summary: Active programme run by the Creative Conservation Alliance, training local community members to collect morphometric data, log GPS positions and do telemetry work.

name: Pittachhara Forest & Biodiversity Conservation Initiative
summary: Landscape restoration and conservation project active from 2017, led by Mahfuz Russel and partnering with SCOPE Foundation; seasonal bird monitoring in 2023 and 2024 recorded 60 species.

name: Plant Red List of Bangladesh
summary: Red List launched on 11 November 2024 covering 1,000 plant species assessed against IUCN guidelines, of which 395 are listed as threatened, with funding from the World Bank.

name: Prokriti O Jibon Foundation
summary: Organisation reporting twice-yearly Migratory Waterbird Censuses since 2013 with Bangladesh Bird Club, with each report sent to an organisation it calls Wetland International.

name: Protection of Sundarbans Mangrove Forest Project
summary: Project begun with an emphasis on ecological monitoring and aiming to set up a long-term monitoring system for the Sundarbans, with a February 2025 procurement notice listing the Forest Department and government development budget funds.

name: Red List of Bangladesh 2015
summary: Red List assessing 1,619 animal species in seven groups, of which 390 are listed as threatened, published in seven volumes as an update to IUCN Bangladesh's 2000 edition, funded by the World Bank.

name: Scientific research and conservation measures of the fishing cat (Prionailurus viverrinus) in the inland wetlands of northeastern Bangladesh
summary: Fishing cat project at Hakaluki Haor Wetland led by Dr. Ai Suzuki, with 2024 camera trap surveys planned to mid-December, aiming to monitor breeding with landowners; an October 2026 survey is reported.

name: Shahjalal University of Science and Technology
summary: University whose authors published a 2023 deep neural network study of mangrove and swamp forest tree species and a 2025 machine learning assessment of ecosystem health in Sylhet Sadar.

name: Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University
summary: Active university whose Aquatic Bioresource Research Lab’s marine biodiversity portal for Bangladesh includes DNA barcodes of marine organisms from GenBank.

name: SMART patrolling in the Sundarbans
summary: Project in which, according to a 2016 WCS release, the Forest Department piloted SMART in the West Sundarbans Sanctuary with USAID-funded Bagh project support and planned to extend it to other sanctuaries.

name: Southeast University
summary: Dhaka university whose Department of Computer Science and Engineering researcher was last author of a 2019 paper on identifying species from DNA barcode sequences using supervised learning.

name: Species Conservation and Protection of Ecosystems Foundation
summary: Conservation organisation in Dhaka, described by itself as science-focused and formally established in 2017, that runs coastal waterbird monitoring and shorebird tracking projects.

name: Strengthening National Forest Inventory and Satellite Land Monitoring in Support of REDD+ in Bangladesh
summary: Closed project signed on 18 March 2015, funded by USAID with FAO and SilvaCarbon, to help the Forest Department set up the Bangladesh Forest Inventory and a long-term satellite monitoring system.

name: Strengthening Regional Cooperation for Wildlife Protection (Bangladesh)
summary: Closed World Bank-funded project run by the Bangladesh Forest Department, implemented 2011 to 2016 with Nepal, using SMART; an evaluation reports a camera-trap estimate of 106 Sundarbans tigers.

name: Sundarbans Management Project
summary: Joint German-Bangladesh project under which, according to a 2016 WCS release, SMART training for trainers and frontline staff was organised, run by the German development agency GIZ.

name: Sundarbans Tiger Conservation Project
summary: Project whose director told Mongabay in October 2024 that the 2023-2024 camera-trap survey used 1,210 cameras at 605 spots over 2,240 km2, reportedly finding at least 125 adult Bengal tigers.

name: Survey of Bangladesh
summary: National surveying and mapping agency of Bangladesh, which UN-SPIDER describes as under the Ministry of Defence, headed by the Surveyor General, and responsible for aerial photography and topographic maps.

name: Sustainable Forests and Livelihoods (SUFAL) Project
summary: Closed World Bank-funded project run by the Bangladesh Forest Department, approved October 2018 and ended 31 December 2024, with 175 million dollars committed and a digital surveillance system among its results.

name: Unmanned aerial systems-based assessment of tree cover and deforestation dynamics in Bangladesh
summary: Closed drone project run by Daffodil International University, December 2017 to June 2022, producing canopy surface, height and cover estimates for inventory plots in the Sal and Sundarbans forests.

name: Updating the Faunal Red List of Bangladesh
summary: Project, contracted between the Forest Department and IUCN Bangladesh on 14 January 2026, to review about 2,200 animal species and produce ten volumes and upgraded public databases.

name: WCS Bangladesh
summary: Says it works with the Forest Department on SMART in the Sundarbans, while its SMART coordinator trains, mentors and provides technical support to Bangladesh Forest Department frontline staff.

name: Wetland Monitoring Tool
summary: Tool that SEI says generates annual wetland maps from 1994 for the Meghna and Lower Songkhram River Basins using Landsat archives and machine learning, built and run by the institute.

name: WildTeam
summary: Bangladeshi NGO that Wikipedia says began in 2003 and ran the first Sundarbans tiger population survey, and which IUCN says will keep working with communities and the Forest Department from 2026 to 2028.

name: Agency for Nature and Forests
summary: Agency that says it cares for over 70,000 hectares of nature areas, forests and parks in Flanders, and uses an AI camera detection system on fire towers as a pilot.

name: Agentschap Innoveren en Ondernemen
summary: Flemish agency that VITO says funds SSPIRIT.

name: AI habitat mapping feasibility study
summary: A closed feasibility study, requested and funded by the EEA, that used AI and machine learning on high-resolution satellite data to map habitats, trained on the European Vegetation Archive.

name: AI-assisted wildlife monitoring in the Semois valley
summary: Park-led project funded by WWF Belgium; camera traps captured 260,000 images and videos in 2024, and in September 2025 WWF reported AI had helped detect 104 species since April 2025.

name: Amazon Right Now Climate Fund
summary: An active 100 million dollar initiative for climate resilience and nature conservation that funds Brabantse Wouden National Park.

name: Aquafin
summary: Named by VITO as a partner that executed Internet of Water Flanders, whose sensors, VITO reported in January 2024, continuously measured water quality in wastewater, groundwater and surface water across Flanders.

name: Ardenne & Gaume asbl
summary: Non-profit that says it protects more than 1,000 hectares of natural areas across Wallonia and works for their recognition as nature reserves.

name: ASBL Contrat Rivière Dendre
summary: River contract non-profit that announced in April 2025 summer actions against invasive alien plants along watercourses of the Dendre sub-basin, as in previous years.

name: ASBL Domaine de Bérinzenne
summary: Non-profit that initiated, with the Walloon agriculture and natural resources service, a river and forest restoration project including owner agreements, drain-blocking, side-channel restoration and floodplain pond digging.

name: Avatar Bosland
summary: An AI avatar of unknown status, built by Milan Meyberg with VITO and Bosland as partners, trained on ecosystem data and using habitat maps derived from satellite images.

name: Aves
summary: Active organisation whose 2018 article reports point counts since 1990.

name: Aviation Sans Frontières Belgium
summary: Active organisation within which Conservation From the Sky was created in 2009.

name: Be.DiSSCo-FED
summary: Project funded by the Belgian Science Policy Office that aims to make digitalised data FAIR and open source; its kick-off meeting was on 17 May 2024.

name: BeBirds
summary: Belgium's bird ringing centre, run by the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences.

name: BeeOimpact
summary: Programme run by BeeOdiversity that assesses risks, impacts and state of nature using satellite data, AI and databases, with no site visit required.

name: BeeOmonitoring
summary: Programme run by BeeOdiversity that uses bees to monitor plant biodiversity and pollutants across 700 hectares.

name: Belgian Biodiversity Platform
summary: Science-policy interface body funded by the Belgian Science Policy Office and run by the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences, brokering between policy, science and practice and supporting biodiversity data publishing.

name: Belgian GBIF Node
summary: Team designated by Belgium to coordinate a biodiversity data network, run by the Belgian Biodiversity Platform and hosting a portal of Belgian data shared through GBIF.

name: Belgian Science Policy Office
summary: Federal Public Planning Service Science Policy, whose Space Research and Applications directorate manages the STEREO Earth observation programme, and which funds the Belgian Biodiversity Platform.

name: BioScope
summary: Proposed project led by Nationaal Park Brabantse Wouden, using Waarnemingen.be, that plans new statistical methods and machine learning to produce reports automatically.

name: Bleaf Cam
summary: A proposed AI framework to reuse wildlife camera networks for vegetation monitoring, selected for funding by the Smart Solutions competition in June 2025.

name: Botanical Collections
summary: Online platform which the Brussels Times reported in May 2023 makes 83,000 plants from 25 botanic gardens available, plus herbarium scans of nearly three million specimens, still in development.

name: Brabantse Wouden National Park
summary: A national park joining the Hallerbos, Zoniënwoud, Meerdaalwoud and Dijle valley, with over 10,000 hectares of nature, which awarded 150,000 euros to five organisations in its Smart Solutions contest.

name: Brasschaat - De Inslag forest monitoring site
summary: Operational site run by the Agency for Nature and Forests, with a sensor tower and ICP Forests level II plot, where monitoring will focus on recovery from pollution.

name: Brasschaat forest research drone
summary: Research drone that, from May 2025, was to fly autonomously every day over De Inslag forest with seven instruments, recording tree species, health, water content, drought stress and wildfire risk.

name: Bruxelles Environnement
summary: The Brussels Capital Region's public environment and energy body, founded in 1989 according to GBIF, which drew up the Brussels Forêt de Soignes management plan, revised in June 2019.

name: C3S climate service for biodiversity
summary: A closed project, built by VITO within the Copernicus Climate Change Service, offering current and future bioclimate indicators and interactive applications.

name: CALLISTO
summary: A closed project whose consortium planned to use data fusion and machine learning, and which De Watergroep says studied the water quality of reservoirs.

name: CEBE-MOB
summary: Manages, protects and runs activities at two semi-natural sites, the Moeraske (Evere, Schaerbeek, Haren) and the Hof ter Musschen (Woluwe-Saint-Lambert).

name: CongoFlux
summary: A project of unknown status, built and run by Ghent University and led by Pascal Boeckx, centred on an eddy covariance flux tower at Yangambi.

name: Connecting the Forest
summary: A proposed project, a June 2025 funding winner, that would use energy-efficient wireless sensors across the park to monitor environmental conditions.

name: Conservation From the Sky
summary: An active programme run by the Pairi Daiza Foundation, built by Aviation sans Frontières Belgium, using AI-assisted aerial photography from ultralight aircraft, with a 2025 pilot at Zah Soo National Park.

name: Contrat de rivière Dyle-Gette
summary: River contract non-profit set up on 5 July 2009 by merging two river contracts, whose partners voluntarily commit to an action programme for the Dyle-Gette basin, one of 14 Walloon sub-basins.

name: Contrat de Rivière pour la Lesse
summary: River contract that coordinates and carries out projects to improve water quality, restore natural habitats and strengthen biodiversity in the Lesse basin.

name: Contrat de Rivière Semois-Chiers
summary: River contract that describes itself as a participatory water management tool for the Semois-Chiers sub-basin, with an agreed action programme to restore the functions and uses of water.

name: Contrat de rivière Senne
summary: An NGO described by GBIF as gathering water management stakeholders across Wallonia's Senne catchment, leading invasive alien species surveillance and holding pond and river survey data.

name: Contrat Rivière Haine
summary: River contract whose work is to draw up and carry out a concerted action programme to value water resources of its basin and restore and protect watercourses and their surroundings.

name: CurieuzeNeuzen in de Tuin
summary: Closed citizen science project that sought 5,000 sensor hosts in 2021, transmitted real-time data to the University of Antwerp and continued in 2022 with 3,000 soil sensors.

name: De Watergroep
summary: An active organisation that worked with 16 partners from 8 countries on the CALLISTO project.

name: Department of Economy, Science and Innovation (Flanders)
summary: A Flemish government department that financed the 2020 International Research Infrastructure call.

name: Diatom Group
summary: Marine biodiversity advisory group operating through Diatom Consultancy B.V. and Diatom Blue Tech B.V., designing monitoring programmes that combine bioacoustics, eDNA and AI-powered imaging.

name: Digitaal Vlaanderen
summary: An organisation named as a GEO.INFORMED partner, and listed by VITO among the partners that mapped historical land use.

name: Digital Animal Sound Archive
summary: A Belgian programme collecting animal sounds, currently focused on bats, run by the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences with Natuurpunt and Natagora as partners.

name: Directorate-General for Development Cooperation (Belgium)
summary: Finances the CEBioS programme.

name: DiSSCo Flanders
summary: An official consortium of four partners: Meise Botanic Garden, the Research Institute for Nature and Forest, the Flanders Marine Institute and the Royal Zoological Society of Antwerp.

name: DivGrass
summary: An active project that plans digitally supported grassland monitoring using AI, drone data and apps.

name: DroneMatrix
summary: Limburg-based company with which, according to the University of Antwerp, the Brasschaat forest research drone was developed in collaboration.

name: Département de l'Étude du Milieu naturel et agricole
summary: A department, run by the Service public de Wallonie ARNE, that coordinates and validates invasive alien species surveillance in Wallonia, drawing on online recording systems including OFFH.

name: Département de la Nature et des Forêts
summary: A department of the Service public de Wallonie ARNE that manages public forests and state-owned nature reserves and develops and applies forest and nature conservation policy and regulation.

name: E-BIOM
summary: A Namur-based laboratory and consultancy, according to Solar Impulse Foundation, that uses environmental DNA samples and ecologists' observations to organise biodiversity monitoring indicators.

name: Earth Observation and Ecosystem Modelling lab
summary: A lab run by the University of Liège, responsible for remote sensing research within SPHERES.

name: EarthMapps
summary: An organisation run by KU Leuven and led by Stef Lhermitte, combining satellite observations, models and geospatial AI.

name: ECO-CATCH
summary: An active project with 35 partners from 10 countries, funded by Horizon Europe, aiming to reduce Baltic and North Sea bycatch, with real-time AI detection being developed with fishermen.

name: ECOGraph
summary: An active project funded by Research Foundation Flanders that proposes integrating graph theory and deep learning into species distribution models.

name: EcoSource
summary: An organisation that checks for deforestation by analysing satellite data.

name: eDNA-OPTIMA
summary: A project that will develop automated sampling technologies, with partners at the Flanders Marine Institute, the Flanders Research Institute for Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (ILVO) and KU Leuven.

name: Enabel
summary: An active organisation whose biodiversity sheet mentions ecological monitoring tools, applied research, and ecological surveillance and monitoring.

name: EurOBIS
summary: The European node of the international Ocean Biodiversity Information System, run by the VLIZ Marine Data Center.

name: Federal Public Service Health, Food Chain Safety and Environment
summary: Its page assigns international environmental coordination to the federal government and nature conservation to regions, noting the 2025–2030 biodiversity strategy’s approval on 30 January 2025.

name: Field Research Centre, Hasselt University
summary: Hasselt University research centre in Maasmechelen that collects long-term wildlife data in Hoge Kempen National Park using camera traps, biologgers, trail counters and sensors, and works closely with INBO.

name: Flanders historical land use maps
summary: A project built by VITO and the Research Institute for Nature and Forest, in which AI helped digitise historical maps so land use in 1778, 1873 and 1969 can be compared with today's.

name: Flanders Research Institute for Agriculture, Fisheries and Food
summary: An active institute working on seabed biodiversity and the effects of exploiting the sea, including DNA-based monitoring methods and eDNA work with the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences.

name: Flo.Wer
summary: Organisation that GBIF names as an initiator, alongside INBO and the National Botanic Garden of Belgium, of the Florabank1 database.

name: Florabank1
summary: CC0 dataset whose GBIF description reports about three million vascular plant records from Flanders and Brussels since 1800, while its occurrence count is 6,136,750.

name: Fondation Générations Futures
summary: An active foundation whose site lists River Cleanup, a partner, as an AETHER 2025 laureate.

name: Fonds de la Recherche Scientifique
summary: An active research funder that reports work by a FRIA-FNRS fellow on AI in aerial wildlife surveys and is listed by Biodiversa+ for Wallonia-Brussels.

name: ForEOSt
summary: A closed project run by Spacebel, listed by ESA as a completed demonstration project.

name: FOREST.AI
summary: An active project in which goodforest supplies satellite analysis and AI and Timbtrack supplies the software.

name: Forestimator
summary: An active platform hosting more than a hundred map layers, including stand variables estimated by an AI model trained on over 5,000 inventory plots, according to a 2022 article.

name: GeCoLab
summary: An active organisation run by the University of Liège that provides biodiversity inventories and monitoring of threatened or invasive species.

name: Gembloux Agro-Bio Tech
summary: A part of the University of Liège that developed new map layers for Walloon forests, and a Forest Is Life team there used deep learning on oblique images of African wildlife.

name: GEO.INFORMED
summary: A closed 2020 to 2024 project, built by VITO, INBO, Digitaal Vlaanderen and KU Leuven, that aimed to link deep learning on remote sensing data, including Sentinel-2, with Flemish policy needs.

name: Geosparc
summary: An active organisation based in Destelbergen, part of the Gumption group, specialised in data analysis and AI.

name: Ghent University
summary: Has computational bioacoustics research, a June 2020 announcement of planned AI training on drone footage, and a July 2021 to June 2025 acoustic machine learning project.

name: GINAMO
summary: An active project funded by Biodiversa+ that monitors genetic biodiversity using genetic indicators, with INBO and the Royal Zoological Society of Antwerp as partners.

name: Groendienst Stad Gent
summary: City green service that does the daily management of city-owned parcels in the Bourgoyen-Ossemeersen nature reserve, where the City of Ghent owned 206 of 220 hectares in 2014.

name: Hasselt University
summary: University whose Centre for Environmental Sciences includes a Field Research Centre, and whose projects include a smart ecological monitoring network planned for July 2025 to June 2029.

name: Heliovision
summary: Leuven-based Belgian machine vision company, whose planned BLEAF-CAM is intended to use existing wildlife cameras to monitor vegetation.

name: HerdNet
summary: Point-based CNN architecture inspired by crowd counting, reported in 2023 to reach a global F1 score of 73.6% on oblique aerial images of livestock herds in Ennedi reserve, Chad.

name: INSPIRE
summary: Active project, led by the Flanders Marine Institute and funded by the European Commission, with 25 European partners and one from Thailand, testing plastic monitoring on six rivers.

name: Institut Scientifique de Service Public
summary: Public research organisation that has measured environmental data in situ since 1990, with a Remote Sensing and Geodata Unit studying land cover, land use and change detection.

name: Interdisciplinary Research Project on computer vision and intelligent mowing patterns
summary: A project run and funded by Ghent University which, in June 2020, announced plans to develop automated mowing strategies using computer vision and AI to help conserve pollinator biodiversity in Flanders.

name: Internet of Water Flanders
summary: Closed project, run by VITO, imec and several water and environment bodies, in which VITO reported in January 2024 that 300 sensors measured water quality across Flanders, with raw data public.

name: Inventaire permanent des Ressources forestières de Wallonie
summary: Permanent Walloon forest inventory, run by the Department of Nature and Forests (SPW), which began on 1 February 1994 and gained its own administrative unit in 1996.

name: IoSA
summary: Antwerp-based spin-off from imec, launched in early 2023, reported by eeNews Europe as developing wildlife trackers weighing under a gram, working with over 15 research groups and two zoos.

name: IoTHubspot
summary: Leuven start-up marketing transmitter and tracking technology for finding Asian hornet nests.

name: IPERLITE
summary: Active project led by VITO with ESA, the Belgian Science Policy Office and Aerospacelab, whose CSIMBA hyperspectral camera (20 metre resolution) is entering in-orbit testing, according to VITO.

name: Kempens Landschap vzw
summary: Non-profit founded in 1997 by the Province of Antwerp and about 40 municipalities that buys, manages and opens landscapes to the public, and says it manages more than 1,400 hectares.

name: KU Leuven
summary: University partner in GEO.INFORMED, TRANSPONDER, SEPPI and SSPIRIT, with a Belgian TRANSPONDER contact and a project aiming to develop AI methods for extracting tree density, biomass and biodiversity from imagery.

name: Laboratory of Quantitative Forest Ecosystem Science
summary: A laboratory run by Ghent University that combines field observations, 3D forest reconstructions, process-based modelling and remote sensing, using image processing techniques from AI and computer vision.

name: Les Amis de la Fagne
summary: Association that owns approved nature reserves looked after regularly by volunteers, who also work in the state-owned (domanial) reserves.

name: LIFE Belgium for Biodiversity
summary: Active project running from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2031, in which UGent and Natuurpunt use thermal drones to locate vulnerable bird nests in the Zwarte Beek valley.

name: LIFE SMART IAS
summary: Active project, led by Geokomm, that develops and refines eDNA detection, AI-controlled camera traps, cloud infrastructure and apps for managing invasive species.

name: LifeWatch Belgium
summary: Belgian programme combining regional and federal contributions, one of eight LifeWatch ERIC national nodes, with camera traps and acoustic and genomic observatories, which says AI analyses remote sensing data.

name: LifeWatch Belgium camera trap network
summary: Camera trap network that began in 2017, run and built by LifeWatch Belgium, with images annotated in Agouti by hand or with AI.

name: LifeWatch Belgium fish acoustic receiver network
summary: Belgian network of acoustic receivers on buoys, shipwrecks, reefs and moorings across rivers, estuaries and coast, allowing long-term monitoring of aquatic species, with data recovered at least every six months.

name: LifeWatch Belgium genomic observatories
summary: Programme studying Belgian North Sea habitats and taxa using monthly DNA and eDNA water samples, connected through EMO BON to 16 observatories across Europe and the Mediterranean.

name: LifeWatch Belgium plankton imaging
summary: Programme producing plankton abundance and biomass time series for Belgian marine food webs, classifying ZooSCAN and FlowCAM images semi-automatically with machine learning, with datasets released yearly.

name: LifeWatch bird tracking network
summary: Active network run by LifeWatch Belgium that tracks gulls, waders and birds of prey, using the UvA-BiTS GPS system among two technologies.

name: LifeWatch ecotopes and ecopatches
summary: Dataset built by LifeWatch Belgium, with datacubes at Belgian and European scale that users can download directly.

name: LifeWatch permanent Cetacean passive acoustic sensor network
summary: Active dataset from a permanent sensor network run by LifeWatch Belgium, which uses C-PODs to register harbour porpoise.

name: LifeWatch Wallonia-Brussels
summary: Programme, with unknown status, that provides remote sensing data for ecosystem monitoring and offers an integrated 2 m geographic object database tuned for modelling species habitats.

name: Ligue Royale Belge pour la Protection des Oiseaux
summary: Bird protection league that aims to build a network of nature reserves across Wallonia by buying land or acquiring long-term rights, and is one of nine associations in a Walloon protected area project.

name: Limburgs Landschap vzw
summary: Non-profit that says it manages about 3,000 hectares of nature in Limburg, including its own terrain in Nationaal Park Hoge Kempen.

name: LoFeNix
summary: Organisation selected for Smart Solutions funding in June 2025 for a proposal to monitor environmental conditions across the park using energy-efficient wireless sensors.

name: LTER Belgium
summary: National network of sites doing long-term, site-based ecological and socio-ecological research, with 42 verified member sites listed in DEIMS.

name: Marine sound library
summary: Proposed platform for developing machine learning that detects and classifies underwater biological sounds, launched in 2025 with over 2,000 clips and half a million euros from the Flemish government through VLIZ.

name: Marinemammals.be
summary: Open-access dataset of marine mammal observations and strandings in Belgium, gathered by the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences and built with the University of Liège.

name: MeBioS
summary: Active research group, run by KU Leuven, that combines sensing, imaging and AI to monitor insects.

name: Meetnetten.be
summary: Programme, with unknown status, built by INBO and Natuurpunt, in which monitoring schemes for 65 priority species began in 2016 and volunteers enter counts in the portal.

name: Natagora
summary: Nature organisation protecting nature in Wallonia and Brussels, which coordinates Observations.be, where AI assesses the reliability of observations and supports volunteer validators.

name: Natagriwal
summary: Active organisation whose GBIF record describes biological monitoring of agri-environment and Natura 2000 restoration actions, mainly butterfly and vegetation field data, with Walloon records from 1988 to 2024.

name: Nationaal Geografisch Instituut
summary: Belgium's national cartographic agency, under the Minister of Defence, producing geographic reference data, working with the regions on aerial photographs and building the national geographic information infrastructure.

name: Nationaal Park Bosland
summary: Flemish natural area which VITO describes as among the largest and most diverse, and which is working with VITO on an AI avatar trained on ecosystem data to help monitor biodiversity.

name: Nationaal Park Hoge Kempen
summary: Limburg nature area of more than 12,000 hectares of managed and protected forest and heath across ten municipalities, with a National Park Bureau acting for a 32-partner coalition.

name: Nationaal Park Scheldevallei
summary: Park organisation whose support, with WWF, enabled Regionaal Landschap Schelde-Durme to buy a thermal-camera drone that its nature policy officer says helps map habitats and find wildlife bottlenecks.

name: Natuurpunt
summary: Flanders' largest nature conservation NGO by its own description, which coordinates volunteer observations, runs Waarnemingen.be, uses ObsIdentify, and reportedly received €40,000 from Brabants Woud National Park for AI insect traps.

name: Natuurpunt Leuven AI insect traps
summary: Proposed project in which two insect traps are planned, using AI to identify and count species, funded by Smart Solutions and Brabants Woud National Park.

name: Netcompany S.A.
summary: Belgian company that CORDIS names as coordinator of ILIAD, a project that ran from February 2022 to July 2025 and is now closed.

name: Observations.be
summary: Belgian nature database launched in 2008, run by Natagora and built with Natuurpunt; Natagora reported over 80 million observations in December 2024, checked by AI or volunteers.

name: Orchis vzw
summary: Non-profit that manages ecologically valuable areas in Limburg that it buys or rents, and whose 16-hectare Motmolen area became an officially recognised nature reserve on 7 August 2025.

name: Otter over de Grens
summary: An active project whose work includes buying land, restoring areas and monitoring otters and their prey.

name: Pairi Daiza Foundation
summary: An active foundation that supported testing of a survey method in Zah Soo National Park, Chad, in 2025.

name: Parc national de l'Entre-Sambre-et-Meuse
summary: Park whose project-office nonprofit was created in late 2021 and whose 2023 annual report covers camera trap specifications, bird monitoring, a strategic monitoring plan and an action to acquire 100 hectares for reserves.

name: Parc naturel de l'Ardenne méridionale
summary: Natural park recognised in May 2019, a non-profit of public and private actors across nine municipalities, which was one of two parks that carried the Semois valley national park candidature.

name: Parc naturel des Sources ASBL
summary: Natural park non-profit developing an ecological restoration project on the 63-hectare Bronromme site, for which it sought a Walloon Region subsidy fully funding restoration on the main ecological structure.

name: Parc naturel du Pays des Collines
summary: Natural park that lists protection, management and enhancement of natural heritage as one of its missions, and describes a natural park as a rural territory of high biological interest.

name: Parc naturel Hautes Fagnes-Eifel
