summary: Natural park of 72,000 hectares in eastern Belgium, created in 1971 by the Province of Liège, which manages its territory with protection of natural and landscape heritage as its first mission.

name: Parc naturel Viroin-Hermeton
summary: Natural park of more than 48,000 hectares across three municipalities, recognised by the Walloon Region in 1998, which names nature protection as an essential mission and helps private Natura 2000 owners.

name: Patrimoine Nature asbl
summary: Non-profit that says it has protected 192 hectares of high biological value land, over 135 hectares owned and the rest on long-term lease, and is one of nine associations in a Walloon project.

name: PolliConnect
summary: A project running 2025 to 2029 that plans improved pollinator monitoring, including AI cameras.

name: Profish Technology
summary: An organisation with an address in Assesse, Belgium, whose Wildscan division tracks birds, bats and mammals.

name: Provincie Oost-Vlaanderen
summary: Province that said in April 2023 its publicly accessible forest and nature areas are listed in its guide 'Oost-Vlaanderen natuurlijk!', with 26 reachable by walking or cycling path.

name: RBINS bat sound collection
summary: A dataset of bat occurrences and sounds recorded with bat detectors, including North Sea recordings made to monitor wind farm effects on bat migration routes.

name: Regionaal Landschap Schelde-Durme
summary: A body that, WWF Belgium describes, flies a drone with a thermal camera, giving it new ways to monitor biodiversity in the region.

name: Remote Sensing & Terrestrial Ecology
summary: A group run by KU Leuven and led by Ben Somers, applying deep learning models to forest characterisation and land cover classification.

name: Research Foundation - Flanders
summary: Organised the 2020 International Research Infrastructure call that the Flemish LifeWatch Consortium applied to, and intends to fund Flemish researchers through the Biodiversa+ call launched on 9 September 2026.

name: Research Institute for Nature and Forest
summary: Flemish government research institute that reported in April 2024 that it and three other bodies used AI to digitise historical land use maps of Flanders and Brussels.

name: River Cleanup
summary: A non-profit registered in Oudenaarde that combines drones, AI and citizen participation to identify river pollution hotspots, and reports 125 km of riverbanks mapped in 2025.

name: River Watchers
summary: A project built by River Cleanup and VITO in which smartphone photos of litter map river pollution; it won €125,000 in 2024 under the amai! initiative.

name: Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences
summary: Belgium's designated focal point for the Convention on Biological Diversity, a museum and research institute created in 1846, which runs the Belgian Marine Data Centre.

name: Royal Meteorological Institute of Belgium
summary: An institute that has used weather radars to detect birds for some years.

name: Royal Museum for Central Africa
summary: A museum in Tervuren studying Africa's societies, biodiversity and geology; a 2026 CEBioS booklet says it coordinated research and capacity building in the Yangambi landscape for over two decades.

name: Royal Zoological Society of Antwerp
summary: Zoological society with its own Centre for Research and Conservation, carrying out research in zoos and field stations and managing the De Zegge nature reserve.

name: Sauvons Bambi
summary: Non-profit association working across Belgium and Luxembourg, whose volunteers use drones with thermal cameras before mowing.

name: ScheldeMonitor
summary: Portal for estuarine research results in the Scheldt, active for two decades, with MONEOS as its largest raw data provider and run and built by the Flanders Marine Institute.

name: Seascape Belgium
summary: Marine science coordination organisation set up in 2017, with expertise in ocean observing, marine monitoring, research infrastructures and marine data management, and an address in Brussels.

name: SeaWatch-B
summary: Coastal survey project run by LifeWatch Belgium, which, at VLIZ, trained 80 to 100 citizens at the coast to carry out surveys.

name: Semois Valley AI biodiversity monitoring
summary: Led by Semois Valley National Park with WWF Belgium funding, recording 260,000 photos and videos in 2024; WWF reported AI detecting 104 species between April and September 2025.

name: Semois Valley National Park
summary: Active park, set up in January 2023 according to WWF Belgium, which quotes a biologist saying it covers more than 30,000 hectares, with a public, collaborative observatory for nature data.

name: Service Public de Wallonie Agriculture, Ressources Naturelles et Environnement
summary: Walloon public administration whose officials are among those carrying out surveillance of invasive alien species in Wallonia.

name: Smart Long-Term Ecological Monitoring Network
summary: Active project, running from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2029, that aims to set up an automatic low-cost LoRaWAN monitoring system for biotic and environmental data in Hoge Kempen National Park.

name: Smart Solutions competition
summary: Competition run by Brabantse Wouden National Park and funded by Amazon's Right Now Climate Fund, which Amazon said in June 2025 would back technology for biodiversity monitoring and visitor experience.

name: SmartwoodID
summary: Closed 2021–2024 project led by Hans Beeckman, using deep learning and aiming to automate wood identification for DR Congo timber, with a final report published in 2025.

name: SoilTemp
summary: Global network focused on microclimate data for ecological questions, built by Jonas Lembrechts.

name: Spacebel
summary: Company with offices in Belgium and France offering Earth observation services for forestry and natural resources, which ESA Space Solutions says combine satellite, airborne and field data.

name: SPACETWIN
summary: Project run by Q-ForestLab and led by Kim Calders, building a large open-source 3D digital forest database.

name: SSPIRIT
summary: Three-year project begun in June 2025, led and run by VITO and funded by VLAIO, aiming to identify and quantify plastic litter in the Belgian North Sea and Scheldt estuary using remote sensing and AI.

name: STEREO
summary: Belgian Science Policy Office programme whose fourth phase, running from 2022 to 2029, finances laboratory research projects on priority themes including biodiversity.

name: Studying wildlife behaviour by combining camera traps and biologgers in a human dominated environment
summary: Project planned for October 2023 to September 2027 to study wildlife behaviour in Hoge Kempen National Park using camera traps, biologgers and vegetation surveys, combined in species distribution models.

name: Suivi des Oiseaux Communs en Wallonie
summary: Programme run by Aves monitoring widespread breeding birds in Wallonia, which an article summary dates from 1990.

name: TER-Consult
summary: Belgian company with an office in Liège, founded by five bio-engineers, whose Nature unit surveys species and maps habitats, and which in February 2019 reported supplying remote-sensing expertise as a subcontractor on the iDROC drone project.

name: Terrascope
summary: VITO-run platform launched in 2017 giving access to open satellite data and Copernicus archives, which VITO says has over 38,000 users and whose operations are secured until the end of 2028.

name: Tervuren xylarium Wood Density Database
summary: Wood density dataset holding 13,332 samples from 2,994 species.

name: Timbtrack
summary: Belgian company established in 2014 that offers satellite monitoring technologies; an April 2026 announcement said it would commercialise the SWIFTT platform.

name: Tracking Invasive Alien Species
summary: Belgian project building an open data-driven framework with data mobilisation and risk evaluation components, using GBIF services; its current status is unknown.

name: UCLouvain
summary: University whose Earth and Life Institute hosts a geomatics group and machine learning work on biodiversity monitoring tools, and which has been a named LifeWatch partner since 2013.

name: UCLouvain Geomatics research lab
summary: Research lab at UCLouvain, led by Pierre Defourny, that focuses on land monitoring by satellite remote sensing and land use modelling.

name: University of Antwerp
summary: University whose Vision Lab works on multispectral and hyperspectral image processing for vegetation monitoring with VITO, and which announced IoSA with imec on 24 January 2023.

name: University of Liège
summary: University with work on mapping tree species proportions from Sentinel-2 using a convolutional neural network, and strategic AI and satellite image support to Conservation From the Sky.

name: Vereniging van Botanische Tuinen en Arboreta
summary: Belgian association that the Brussels Times names as coordinator of the shared online platform for the collections of Belgian botanic gardens.

name: Vespa-Watch
summary: Flemish hotline where citizens report possible Asian hornet sightings or nests, with validated records published weekly as open data on GBIF.

name: Vielsalm Terrestrial Observatory
summary: Operational forest observatory whose tower eddy-covariance system has measured carbon dioxide and water vapour fluxes since 1996, and a verified member site of LTER Belgium.

name: Virelles-Nature asbl
summary: Non-profit created by Natagora in collaboration with WWF, with an annually reviewed management plan setting out work to be done on the Virelles pond reserve.

name: Vlaamse Bosinventarisatie
summary: Dataset of forest measurements from VBI1 (1997 to 1999) and VBI2 (2009 to 2019), from a policy-supporting network covering all Flemish forests on a 10-year cycle.

name: Vlaamse Landmaatschappij
summary: Flemish organisation that tests drones with thermal cameras to find nests and chicks in the FARMBIRD project.

name: Vlaamse Milieumaatschappij
summary: Flemish environment agency using sensors, with 100 reported by VMM in January 2024 and over 200 by BEPROACT, which reports machine learning predictions of oxygen-poor conditions.

name: Vlakwa
summary: Organisation that VITO named as a partner that executed Internet of Water Flanders, whose sensors, VITO reported in January 2024, continuously measured water quality across Flanders.

name: VLIZ Marine Data Center
summary: Programme run by the Flanders Marine Institute that serves as a national and international contact point for marine and estuarine data and runs EurOBIS.

name: VLIZ Marine Observation Centre
summary: Programme run by the Flanders Marine Institute covering smart measurement, AI and digital twins, including deep learning for plankton data and a sensor network for underwater sound.

name: VLIZ Marine Robotics Centre
summary: Programme run by the Flanders Marine Institute that manages a number of robotic platforms for marine observations in remote, harsh environments.

name: Vrije Universiteit Brussel
summary: University whose researchers authored two 2024 papers, one fusing PlanetScope and aerial imagery to map urban tree species and one using deep learning to classify mammal vocalisations.

name: vzw Durme
summary: Non-profit that says it protects and manages 12 nature reserves across 12 municipalities, about 600 hectares along the Durme, Moervaart and Scheldt, and is one of three recognised land-managing nature associations in Flanders.

name: Waarnemingen.be
summary: Observation database run by Natuurpunt, which says it collects over 6 million observation records a year.

name: Wallonia forest composition map 2021
summary: Freely accessible map of Walloon forest composition, available through Forestimator, with species predicted by a PointNet++ AI model trained on nearly 315,000 reference trees.

name: Waste Watchers
summary: Closed project, run by River Cleanup and VITO, in which citizen drone imagery from the Scheldt in summer 2023 was analysed with AI to produce a litter map in early 2024.

name: WeForest acoustic biodiversity monitoring
summary: WeForest project with partner Wildmon that piloted acoustic monitoring in Pontal, Brazil from 2021 to 2025, recording 219 species, with Zambia listed as launching in 2026.

name: WWF Belgium
summary: Belgium-registered organisation that, in an April 2026 article, said it uses AI to sort camera-trap images and identify species, and that funds the Semois monitoring project.

name: ZERO-IMPACT
summary: Project with ILVO and the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences that, as described by ILVO in November 2021, aims to develop an automatic method for detecting marine species from eDNA.

name: Assessing recent trend in populations of Critically Endangered Hooded vulture and support for its conservation in Burkina Faso
summary: Dated 15 December 2025, this Rufford-listed project assesses Critically Endangered Hooded vulture trends since 2019, when road counts repeated routes and methods from 1969–1973 and 2003–2004.

name: Base de Données de l'Occupation des Terres (BDOT)
summary: Burkina Faso land cover dataset, built by the national geographic and forest information institute, with 1992 and 2002 national databases at 1:200,000 from Landsat imagery, later reused in forest reference levels and the second national forest inventory.

name: Breeding Status and Reproductive Performance of the White-Backed Vulture Gyps africanus in the Nazinga Ranch, Burkina Faso
summary: Closed Rufford Foundation-listed project, dated 12 September 2023, that planned camera trap monitoring of six occupied White-backed vulture nests and of nest sites across breeding stages, with a final evaluation report dated June 2025.

name: Direction de la Faune et des Ressources Cynégétiques
summary: Government directorate under the Ministry of the Environment that, according to the 2017 CMS national report, organises annual bird counts in which NATURAMA and AVES Burkina have taken part since 1999.

name: Direction Générale des Eaux et Forêts (Burkina Faso)
summary: Its teams reportedly collected data for the 2010–2015 second national forest inventory, which analysed 6,000 circular plots of 25 m radius alongside RapidEye imagery.

name: Département de Biologie Générale, Université Daniel Ouezzin Coulibaly
summary: University department that OpenAlex links to a 2025 paper on yearly variations in large mammal distribution in a West African protected savannah, through its first author's affiliation.

name: Département Environnement, Eaux et Forêts, Université Nazi Boni
summary: University department affiliated with the first and last authors of a 2023 paper on predicting vegetation dynamics in Deux Balé National Park using land change modeler.

name: Effect of Habitats Disturbance on Bats Communities in and Around the Nazinga National Park
summary: Rufford Foundation-listed project, dated 31 March 2026, planning mist netting and acoustic monitoring over 12 months, March 2026 to February 2027, to build a bat diversity database and echolocation library.

name: First camera survey in Burkina Faso and Niger (W-Arly-Pendjari complex)
summary: Closed project, run by Nyeema Harris, that Mongabay reports as the first camera survey in Burkina Faso and Niger, with over one million images from 119 cameras across three dry seasons from 2016.

name: INFLUENCES project
summary: ANR-funded project, started March 2023, studying soil and vegetation regeneration in Burkina Faso; random forest classification of Pléiades images from 2013-14 and 2021 mapped tree cover, grass and bare soil on 64 northern plots.

name: Institut Géographique du Burkina
summary: Public administrative body that UN-SPIDER describes as in charge of designing, implementing and monitoring national mapping policy in Burkina Faso.

name: Institut Supérieur d'Etudes Spatiales et Télécommunications
summary: Institute that says it partnered with OMVS on remote-sensing monitoring of invasive aquatic plants in the Senegal River valley, supported SP/CNDD's land occupation platform, and has belonged to the Group on Earth Observations since July 2017.

name: Laboratoire de Biologie et Ecologie Végétales, Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo
summary: University laboratory in Burkina Faso, listed on a 2022 Dori land cover study that found natural formations fell 16.86% between 1995 and 2015, and on a 2024 paper on Detarium microcarpum distribution under climate change.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de l'Eau et de l'Assainissement
summary: Burkina Faso’s environment ministry coordinates government environment policy, lists wildlife transport authorisation procedures and, Burkina24 reported on 30 December 2025, began biodiversity report preparation through SP/CNDD.

name: NATURAMA
summary: Non-profit NGO created in December 1990, seated in Ouagadougou, reporting about twenty years of ecological monitoring of habitats and birds, and in a 6 November 2026 news item intending to monitor insect diversity under agroforestry.

name: Observatoire National de l'Environnement et du Développement Durable
summary: Ouagadougou observatory attached to SP-CNDD that supports environmental monitoring and evaluation, tracks indicators including forests and Kunming-Montreal framework implementation, and offers a geoportal of interactive maps.

name: Office National des Aires Protégées
summary: Body created by decree 2008-171 of 16 April 2008, seated in Ouagadougou under the protected areas minister's technical supervision, with a mission including sustainable management of state and local authority forests.

name: Projet de gestion participative des forêts classées dans le cadre de REDD+
summary: REDD+ project covering 12 classified forests according to a September 2020 brief, financed by the Forest Investment Program, using Sentinel imagery, testing drones and georeferencing 33,000 planted trees.

name: Second Inventaire Forestier National (IFN 2)
summary: Second national forest inventory, named as project BKF/015, whose data fed the 2025 forest reference level and which also collected herbaceous biomass data in sub-plots.

name: Secrétariat permanent du Conseil national de développement durable
summary: Permanent secretariat with three departments through which, Burkina24 reported on 30 December 2025, the environment ministry had begun preparing the seventh national biodiversity report.

name: Secrétariat Permanent pour la REDD+
summary: REDD+ permanent secretariat that provided technical coordination for the forest reference level submission, whose revision adopted a method based on Collect Earth and uses the second national forest inventory.

name: Space and Society Dynamics Laboratory (LDES), Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo
summary: Laboratory in the Department of Geography at Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo, named as the affiliation of a 2025 paper that modelled woody species habitats in the Centre West region and projects a loss of connection between primary habitats by 2050.

name: Système d'information géoclimatique, agro-écologique et hydrologique du Corridor forestier de la Boucle du Mouhoun et des zones humides du bassin de la mare d'Oursi
summary: Proposed geoclimatic, agro-ecological and hydrological information system whose portal space, ONEDD says, was created on 1 December 2016 under the SP/CNDD-coordinated EBA-FEM project, with information sections under development.

name: ANEMONE PLUS
summary: Active project, led by the Antipa marine research institute with Interreg NEXT Black Sea Basin funding of 1,334,056.99 euros, planning tools such as eDNA, underwater cameras and machine learning to assess Black Sea vulnerability.

name: Annotated Regional Black Sea Phytoplankton Image Dataset
summary: Dataset named in a 2026 conference paper recorded by OpenAlex, whose first listed author is Nina Dzhembekova; no other facts are given.

name: Annual monitoring of the brown bear (Bulgaria)
summary: Programme run by the Executive Environment Agency, announced by the ministry on 20 October 2025 as its 16th annual brown bear monitoring, with 14 cameras planned in the Western Rhodopes and parallel DNA sampling under a pilot.

name: Annual monitoring of the chamois in Bulgaria (NSMSBD)
summary: Annual spring and autumn chamois monitoring under the NSMSBD, run by the Executive Environment Agency, using a route method on predefined routes, with 2022 results given in its 2024 report.

name: Atlas of Breeding Birds in Bulgaria
summary: Dataset of 87,747 breeding bird records covering all 1,240 ten-kilometre UTM squares in Bulgaria for 1996 to 2005, built by the Bulgarian Society for the Protection of Birds and published through GBIF.

name: BALKANI Wildlife Society
summary: An association reporting long-term wolf research and conservation in Bulgaria since its beginning, with a page showing a member fitting a GPS collar on a wolf.

name: Bat occurrences from Bulgaria
summary: Dataset of bat occurrence records in Bulgaria from 1905 to 2025, drawn from literature and unpublished data, with GBIF listing 10,203 records and the National Museum of Natural History as publisher.

name: Bat Research and Conservation Centre (BRCC), National Museum of Natural History
summary: Centre at the National Museum of Natural History that lists bat roost, forest and wetland monitoring, and developing the bat part of the National Biodiversity Monitoring System for 2004 to 2009.

name: Bear Digital Twin (Bulgaria)
summary: Model Nature FIRST says it is developing with Wageningen University and Research, combining Cluey, camera trap and historical data to predict bear movements and behaviour in Bulgaria.

name: Biodiversity Monitoring in Central Balkan
summary: A closed 2017 to 2022 project, led by Rashid Rashid, that monitored species including brown bear, wolf and raptors by camera trapping and GPS telemetry, aiming to update the park's biodiversity database.

name: Black Sea oil slick map, Bulgaria
summary: Map built by Greenpeace Bulgaria with SkyTruth support, showing over 170 twice-confirmed slicks covering 819.1 square kilometres in Bulgarian waters, 6 July 2024 to 26 June 2025.

name: BLACKBOX
summary: Active project led by TUBITAK Marmara Research Center, running 19 March 2026 to 18 July 2028, planning a Black Sea FerryBox network and shared cloud data infrastructure, with Interreg funding of 1,397,178.18 euros.

name: Blue Innovative and Sustainable Management of the Coastal Marine and River Environment and Resources
summary: Active project, running 17 June 2025 to 31 December 2029, aiming to build a distributed research infrastructure for the Black Sea and lower Danube, with a total value of 11.8 million euros.

name: Bulgaria Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: Active monitoring programme, led by Zdravko Kolev, that started in 2020 and began collecting transect and 15-minute count data in 2021, covering over 120 day-flying butterfly species.

name: Bulgarian Barcode of Life
summary: An active programme whose members page lists the Institute of Plant Physiology and Genetics as Bulgaria's representative node of the International Barcode of Life Consortium, alongside four other partner bodies including Pensoft.

name: Bulgarian Biodiversity Foundation
summary: Active organisation conserving biodiversity in Bulgaria and neighbouring countries, which in 2015 presented a free web GIS platform and in 2021 began SaveGREEN wildlife crossing monitoring.

name: Bulgarian National Oceanographic Data Centre
summary: Programme run by IO-BAS, set up in 2002 and the national oceanographic data centre since 2004, according to the IOC ODIS catalogue, which records its data access as fully open.

name: Bulgarian National Science Fund
summary: A funder that supports the Forest Research Institute's pine forest resilience project under its 2025 call for fundamental research by young scientists and postdoctoral researchers.

name: Bulgarian Ornithological Centre
summary: A body that, according to a 2012 paper, coordinates bird ringing schemes in Bulgaria and is described there as a separate department at the Institute of Biodiversity and Ecosystem Research.

name: Bulgarian Society for the Protection of Birds
summary: Sofia-based citizens' society and BirdLife partner that runs SmartBirds, built its database and the breeding bird atlas published through GBIF, and monitors birds.

name: Bulgarian Vegetation Database
summary: Established in 1999, it reportedly used TURBOVEG at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences in 2012 and held 5,901 relevés, mostly grasslands, in September 2010.

name: Central Balkan National Park Directorate
summary: Active directorate for Central Balkan National Park, named by the ministry as a participant in 2025 brown bear field monitoring; staff detained two motorcyclists on a prohibited road on 15 March 2026.

name: Common Bird Monitoring Scheme (Bulgaria)
summary: Volunteer bird count run by BSPB since 2004, with sites visited twice a year, 294 plots analysed for long-term trends, and government funding secured to 2027 as reported by EBCC.

name: Conservation measures for the Lesser Spotted Eagle and its habitats in Bulgaria (LIFE for Eagle's Habitats)
summary: Closed project (2019 to 2025) with BSPB as partner, which satellite-tagged 13 juvenile lesser spotted eagles for the first time in Bulgaria, with an EU contribution of EUR 1,460,260.

name: Conservation of Globally Threatened Diving Ducks Across the Flyway (Diving Ducks LIFE)
summary: An active project, listed on BSPB's projects page, on globally threatened diving ducks, updating population data and studying migration routes and staging areas by GPS telemetry across the Black Sea-Mediterranean Flyway.

name: Conservation of Imperial Eagle and Saker Falcon in key Natura 2000 sites in Bulgaria (BSPB LIFE+ Save the Raptors)
summary: Closed LIFE+ project (2009 to 2013) on imperial eagle and saker falcon conservation in Natura 2000 sites, where satellite telemetry gave new knowledge of imperial eagle migration, wintering grounds and threats.

name: Department of Computer Systems, Technical University of Sofia
summary: University department named as the first author's affiliation on a 2026 paper listed in OpenAlex, Time Series Analysis of the Behavior of Wild Animals Using Camera Traps.

name: Department of Electronics, Nikola Vaptsarov Naval Academy
summary: Naval Academy department in Varna, named as the first author's affiliation on a 2025 conference paper listed in OpenAlex on forest degradation and bird habitat stress using satellite data.

name: Determining the number of brown bears in Bulgaria through DNA analysis
summary: Reported by the ministry in September 2025 as Bulgaria’s first DNA-based bear count, with sampling underway, analysis planned in Slovenia and results expected in early 2027.

name: DiSSCo-BG
summary: Active project run by the National Museum of Natural History and the Institute of Biodiversity and Ecosystem Research, aiming by 2027 to digitise about 2 million items, with data shared to GBIF.

name: Egyptian Vulture New LIFE
summary: A project led by BSPB which, BSPB says, fitted more than 50 Egyptian vultures with GPS transmitters to monitor movements and threats on migration routes, and won the Citizens' Prize at the LIFE Awards 2026.

name: Executive Environment Agency
summary: Active agency administering nationwide automated environmental monitoring and maintaining national and regional databases; a July 2025 ministry announcement said it would administer activities under Bulgaria’s GBIF memorandum.

name: Executive Forest Agency
summary: Active agency whose electronic database holds Bulgaria's forest inventory data, according to the national regulation; its nature parks took part in 2025 brown bear monitoring.

name: Field surveys of breeding bird species and preparation of reports pursuant to Art. 12 of the Birds Directive (Bulgaria, 2024)
summary: Closed 2024 survey of breeding birds for Birds Directive Art. 12 reporting, run by the museum and BSPB, covering 422 sites, 134,415 records and 314 species, completed in September 2025.

name: FireBrigade1
summary: Volunteer wildfire prevention unit by ICDSoft that says it builds observatories using AI to detect fires, with SureSupport staff reviewing alerts; its monitoring page lists every camera as under maintenance.

name: FireScope AI
summary: Active model built by INSAIT and ETH Zurich that combines Sentinel-2 imagery and climate data to produce wildfire risk maps, with the map, paper, code and data released at firescope.ai.

name: Forest Disturbance Inventory using Remote Sensing (FoReS)
summary: ESA PECS-funded project led by the Space Research and Technology Institute, with objectives including Sentinel-1 radar processing, forest disturbance detection and validating a post-fire regrowth product, per an ESA report.

name: Forest Research Institute, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences
summary: Works on forest monitoring, protection and restoration, reports field stations and a monitoring network, and has a Western Rhodopes pine project combining remote sensing with IoT systems.

name: Fortis Visio Ltd.
summary: Sofia-based consultancy covering assessments, permits, biodiversity monitoring and waste management, listing national amphibian, reptile and fish monitoring and 2019 to 2020 hydrobiological surface water data among its projects.

name: Fund for Wild Flora and Fauna
summary: Bulgarian conservation charity based in Blagoevgrad that has used an early warning system tracking vultures with GPS transmitters since 2018, and partnered in BalkanDetox LIFE from October 2020 to September 2025.

name: GBIF Bulgaria
summary: Active national node of GBIF, listed as a voting participant in Europe, after Bulgaria's environment minister signed a memorandum to join in July 2025.

name: GENBUL, genome reference database for Bulgarian biodiversity
summary: Project building a genome reference database for Bulgarian biodiversity, led by Stefaniya Kamenova, which sampled plants in the Ali Botush Reserve in June 2024 and insects in Strandzha.

name: Green Balkans
summary: Environmental association that BTA reports tags lesser kestrels with satellite transmitters weighing 5 grams.

name: Greenpeace Bulgaria
summary: Organisation that recorded over 170 oil and ship-fuel slicks with SkyTruth in Bulgarian Black Sea waters during July 2024 to June 2025, publishing satellite analysis near Burgas in 2026.

name: Hybrid Model for Wild Animals Detection Based on Camera Traps in Bulgarian Mountains
summary: Paper proposing a hierarchical wild animal detector built on YOLOv8n, evaluated on 1,882 annotated camera-trap images from Bulgarian mountains in four classes, listed under COMSCI'2025.

name: Improving the Bulgarian Biodiversity Information System (IBBIS)
summary: A closed project that, according to the Biodiversity Information System for Europe, provided the data collection back-end for all BG03 projects and built IT infrastructure for mapping datasets, volunteer data and database links.

name: Institute for Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Technology
summary: Research institute at Sofia University that, according to the university, developed FireScope AI, and released a public high-resolution long-term fire risk map for Europe.

name: Institute of Biodiversity and Ecosystem Research, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences
summary: Bulgarian Academy of Sciences institute in Sofia that runs DiSSCo-BG, aiming to digitise a significant part of its collections by 2027, and has authors on remote sensing papers listed in OpenAlex.

name: Institute of Oceanology "Fridtjof Nansen", Bulgarian Academy of Sciences
summary: Varna-based Bulgarian Academy of Sciences institute describing itself as a national marine research centre, with an oceanographic data centre, coastal monitoring at Shkorpilovtsi and GBIF data publisher registration.

name: Institute of Plant Physiology and Genetics, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences
summary: A Bulgarian Academy of Sciences institute for plant research that lists DNA barcoding among its strategic orientations, is Bulgaria's iBOL node and is a partner of BIOSCAN Europe.

name: Integrated remote sensing and in-situ studies on the resilience of pine forests in the Western Rhodopes in the context of climate change
summary: An active project, funded by the Bulgarian National Science Fund and running from December 2025 to December 2027, that plans IoT soil moisture sensors on three plots alongside Sentinel-2, drone and LiDAR data.

name: IoT framework for environmental monitoring in Strandzha Nature Park
summary: An IoT framework, introduced in a paper published 22 November 2025, for monitoring environmental parameters including wildlife presence in Strandja Nature Park using sensors, LoRaWAN and cloud analytics, with a reported deployment.

name: LIFE EV Safe Return
summary: Project running from 1 September 2026 to 30 November 2031 on a 6,960,086.76 euro budget, 5,220,065.10 euros of it EU LIFE co-funded, planning GPS/GSM tracking of released birds.

name: LIFE Rhodope Vulture
summary: Project aiming to restore the black vulture population in the cross-border Rhodopes of Bulgaria and Greece, planning GPS tracking to identify poisoning and other threat hotspots.

name: LTER-Bulgaria
summary: Bulgarian long-term ecosystem research network with seven verified member sites on DEIMS, which announced in February 2021 a project to upgrade its distributed scientific infrastructure.

name: Mid-winter census of wintering waterfowl (Bulgaria)
summary: An active waterfowl census organised by the Executive Environment Agency and BSPB, whose January 2025 announcement scheduled its 49th round and planned national monitoring system data entry.

name: Ministry of Environment and Water
summary: Bulgarian ministry whose minister is the national competent authority for GBIF matters, and which runs the National System for Environmental Monitoring.

name: Monitoring of endangered species (BSPB)
summary: BSPB programme, run by the society and using SmartBirds, monitoring vultures, imperial eagles and red-breasted geese, including GPS tags on 32 griffon vultures by 2021 and photo traps at Egyptian vulture nests.

name: National Museum of Natural History, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences
summary: Sofia museum holding nearly one and a half million specimens, which runs DiSSCo-BG and had published over 26,615 records on GBIF by the end of 2024.

name: National System for Environmental Monitoring
summary: Bulgarian monitoring programme run by the Executive Environment Agency, including national networks for land and soils, forests and protected areas, and biodiversity.

name: National System for Monitoring the Status of Biological Diversity (Bulgaria)
summary: An active national monitoring programme encompassing the mid-winter waterbird census, whose field data the environment ministry said in January 2025 would enter its information system after monitoring.

name: Persina Nature Park Directorate
summary: Directorate in Belene that, with BSPB, carried out the pelican monitoring in which the first Dalmatian pelican hatchlings were found (reported 7 April 2023), and a listed partner of the Pelican Way of LIFE project.

name: Pirin National Park Directorate
summary: Directorate controlling compliance with park regimes, named by the ministry in October 2025 as a participant in that year’s national brown bear field monitoring.

name: Preserve key forest habitats of the Lesser Spotted Eagle (Aquila pomarina) in Bulgaria (LIFE for Eagles Forests)
summary: Closed project (2013 to 2019) on lesser spotted eagle forest habitats, which found 73 active nests in 16 Natura 2000 sites and built a habitat distribution model from nests, land use, terrain and climate.

name: Register of protected areas in Bulgaria
summary: Electronic register of protected areas declared under the Protected Areas Act and Natura 2000 zones nominated under the Biological Diversity Act, with data said to be updated regularly.

name: Rewilding Rhodopes
summary: Rewilding Europe reported in September 2025 that reintroduced bison at Zhenda wore GPS collars; the team also ran a 64-camera trap survey there that year.

name: Rewilding Rhodopes Foundation
summary: Bulgarian foundation promoting natural grazing and rewilding in the Rhodopes, which with the BSPB began bringing black vultures back from May 2022, and reports GPS transmitters on five more.

name: Rila National Park Directorate
summary: Body enforcing Rila National Park regimes, named by the ministry in October 2025 as a participant in that year’s national brown bear field monitoring.

name: RiverLIFE, Conservation of the stone crayfish for reviving the river ecosystems
summary: Stone crayfish conservation project, led by Fortis Visio, running 1 June 2025 to 31 May 2032, combining environmental DNA surveys with barrier mapping and planning to remove 30 barriers on the Tundzha and Stryama.

name: Safe Sky for Birds in North-East Bulgaria
summary: Joint initiative of ERP North and the Bulgarian Society for the Protection of Birds, running 2023 to 2027, with objectives including a system for monitoring bird mortality on power lines.

name: Science for Nature Foundation
summary: A Sofia-based organisation that ran a 2017 to 2022 biodiversity monitoring project in Central Balkan National Park and says it has started work on a strategic LIFE project on carbon emissions monitoring.

name: SmartBirds
summary: Biodiversity recording programme with two Android apps, run and built by the Bulgarian Society for the Protection of Birds, which describes it as the largest biodiversity database in Bulgaria.

name: Space Research and Technology Institute, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences
summary: Bulgarian Academy of Sciences institute for space physics and remote sensing, with environmental monitoring as a priority and affiliated authors on 2024 papers on canopy fuels and vegetation productivity.

name: University of Forestry
summary: University whose authors published a 2026 paper monitoring European beech phenology by remote sensing at two long-term ecological research sites, with data collection begun under project NIS-B-1292/2023.

name: VIII International White Stork Census in Bulgaria, 2024
summary: Coordinated by BSPB, it planned nationwide coverage of over 5,000 locations in June–July 2024, requested SmartBirds observations, and had results presented in Sofia, BTA reported in October 2025.

name: WatchReefFish
summary: An active project aiming to build a cross-border, non-invasive fish monitoring network for Black Sea reefs, planning an AI tool to identify reef fish from images and video, led by Karadeniz Technical University.

name: WWF Bulgaria
summary: A conservation organisation that reported in May 2025 installing five cameras with the Northwestern Forest State Enterprise to monitor ecological corridors and confirm connectivity sectors for large predators identified through data and modelling.

name: Animating the Carbon Cycle (Bahrain seagrass)
summary: Nuwat's blue carbon project on Bahrain's seagrass meadows, using field research and modelling to add dugongs' functional roles to ecosystem carbon models; IFAW reports a 2026 Yale and Nuwat study was the model's first marine use.

name: Arabian Gulf University
summary: A university whose staff authored 2022 mangrove and 2025 seagrass remote sensing studies in Bahrain, and which runs a national project with Danat mapping pearl oyster and seagrass habitats.

name: Bahrain elasmobranch DNA reference library
summary: Planned first DNA reference library for Bahrain's sharks and batoids; 329 tissue samples came from market surveys documenting 577 specimens of 30 species, with sequencing still pending in January 2026.

name: Bahrain Institute for Pearls and Gemstones
summary: Mumtalakat-established gemmological laboratory and research centre, founded in 2017 according to Mumtalakat, which has completed marine survey work on pearl oyster beds and seagrass with Arabian Gulf University and the Supreme Council for Environment.

name: Bahrain Space Agency
summary: A national agency that, according to a July 2025 report, took part in the Space for Climate Observatory seminar on monitoring oceans and presented three satellite-based monitoring projects.

name: Botanical Atlas (Bahrain)
summary: A project launched in April 2023, according to a report, by the iGA's Geographic Information Systems Directorate at the Bahrain International Garden Show, offering services on the island's plant life.

name: Centre for Environmental and Biological Studies, Arabian Gulf University
summary: A unit at the Arabian Gulf University in Manama, whose affiliation appears on a 2025 paper estimating below-ground sediment carbon in Bahrain's seagrass habitats using remote sensing.

name: Department of Geoinformatics, Arabian Gulf University
summary: A unit at the Arabian Gulf University in Manama, whose affiliation appears on a 2022 paper assessing change and carbon stock of Bahrain's mangroves using GIS and remote sensing data.

name: Department of Natural Resources and Environment, Arabian Gulf University
summary: Arabian Gulf University department; a doctoral thesis from it used Sentinel-2 imagery and ten spectral vegetation indices to map land cover and compute mangrove area in Ras Sanad, Tubli Bay, between 2016 and 2024.

name: Enhancing the role of local communities in dugong and seagrass conservation (Hawar Islands)
summary: A closed project run by ARC-WH and funded by the CMS Dugong MOU, which surveyed dugongs and seagrass around the Hawar Islands and trained local fishing communities in monitoring, from January 2022 to May 2023 at US$75,000.

name: Exploring the Interactions Between the Globally Sizeable Dugong Herd with Seagrass Meadows Around Hawar Islands: Implications for Climate Change Mitigation and Systematic Conservation Planning
summary: Closed 2020 to 2021 study of dugongs and seagrass meadows around the Hawar Islands, combining surveys, remote sensing and citizen science, and recording a group of 696 dugongs by drone on 15 February 2021.

name: Feasibility assessment of satellite detection of dugong groups around the Hawar Islands
summary: A closed desk-based assessment, led by Christophe Cleguer and funded by ARC-WH, of whether satellite images can detect dugong groups of over 100 around the Hawar Islands, dated February to July 2024.

name: Finsight Bahrain
summary: Citizen science programme run by Nuwat, in which participants join fish market surveys and report sightings on the Tadween platform to generate ecological data on sharks and rays in Bahrain.

name: Information & eGovernment Authority
summary: A Bahraini government authority whose Geographic Information Systems Directorate launched the Botanical Atlas, and whose staff described the 2010 national vegetation survey using 0.41 m satellite imagery and NDVI classification.

name: International Waterbird Census in Bahrain (2017 to 2020)
summary: A closed project in which ARC-WH reports conducting the International Waterbird Census for Bahrain from 2017 to 2020 with the Supreme Council for Environment.

name: Invasive Alien Plant and Animal Species Blacklist project (Bahrain)
summary: A Bahraini project announced in June 2022 to map how invasive alien species arrive and are introduced, run by the Bahrain Institute for Pearls and Gemstones, partnered with the Supreme Council for Environment and funded by the Global Environment Facility.

name: Juthoor
summary: Citizen science programme announced by Nuwat in January 2026 to build baseline biodiversity data on Bahrain's terrestrial ecosystems; 28 people joined the February kick-off, starting with plants and planning insects, birds and mammals.

name: National project to map pearl oyster and seagrass habitats in Bahrain
summary: A national project run by Arabian Gulf University with Danat to map pearl oyster and seagrass habitats in Bahrain's territorial waters, with an eleven-month field survey across 2025 and 2026 covering over 8,000 square kilometres.

name: Nuwat for Environmental Research and Education
summary: Bahrain-based environmental research and conservation think tank, education provider and adviser; it maps sharks, assesses coral reefs, and registered as a GBIF publisher in June 2026 with no datasets published yet.

name: Project for Monitoring Changes and Violations Using Artificial Intelligence
summary: A proposed project by the Survey and Land Registration Bureau to build an AI system monitoring changes in natural and constructed features, to be applied to afforestation, plant health and marine waters, among other areas.

name: Shark and ray baselines using eDNA in Bahrain
summary: A project that reported in September 2025 completing Bahrain's first dedicated eDNA surveys of sharks and rays, aiming to establish distribution, species composition, seasonality and possible nursery areas, after switching from sediment to water eDNA.

name: Supreme Council for Environment
summary: Bahrain's government body in charge of environmental strategy and habitat protection, which issued three wildlife regulatory decisions in 2026, publishes the protected areas dataset and monitors coastal water quality.

name: Survey and Land Registration Bureau
summary: A Bahraini bureau that runs a national 3D mapping programme to modernise mapping production and lists a project for an AI system comparing satellite images over time to monitor changes.

name: Tadween
summary: Nuwat-run platform for recording plant and animal observations, intended to build a regional biodiversity database on Arabian Peninsula wildlife and seasonal change, which it says will be open to everyone.

name: The First Regional Red List Assessment of Selected Species in the Kingdom of Bahrain
summary: National Red List report prepared by the Supreme Council for Environment, finding 16 of 23 evaluated species nationally threatened, with six others unevaluated for lack of data.

name: Tubli Bay ecosystem research project
summary: A University of Bahrain project, led by Haifa bint Ebrahim Al Khalifa, including a study of Ras Sanad mangrove vegetation cover, biomass and carbon stock, within a wider Tubli Bay restoration partnership with UN-Habitat, the Supreme Council for Environment and HSBC.

name: University of Bahrain
summary: A university in Sakhir implementing a research project with UN-Habitat to support restoration of the Tubli Bay ecosystem.

name: Améliorer l'efficacité du système de gestion des aires protégées pour la conservation de la biodiversité au Burundi
summary: UNDP-channelled project, funded by Belgium and the EU, that handed OBPE equipment including a surveillance boat in August 2025 and satellite GPS units and infrared drones in May 2026.

name: Association Burundaise pour la protection de la Nature
summary: Burundian nature association, renamed in September 2013, that has organised waterbird counts since 2005 (interrupted in 2009, resumed January 2013) and held crane conservation workshops with OBPE in late 2025.

name: CHM-Burundi
summary: Burundi's Convention on Biological Diversity clearing-house mechanism, by its own description, whose site lists a meeting of its interinstitutional focal points scheduled for 24 February 2025.

name: Conservation et Communauté de Changement (3C)
summary: Bujumbura-based NGO, born in 2019, that a UNCDF 2024 report names as one of two NGOs hired in the Kibira Forest Sanctuaries Project, where it helped develop a chimpanzee ecological monitoring protocol.

name: Department of Natural Sciences, École Normale Supérieure (Burundi)
summary: Natural sciences department at the École Normale Supérieure in Bujumbura, listed first among the affiliations of the first author of a 2026 Landsat paper on land-cover change in mining landscapes.

name: Drone surveillance of Vyanda Nature Reserve and Mukungu-Rukambasi Protected Landscape
summary: Programme to guard two protected areas with drones, after OBPE received two drones and four GPS units from the association 3C in November 2023, as ABP reports.

name: Département des Sciences de la Terre, Université du Burundi
summary: University of Burundi earth sciences department, within the CRSNE, that is the affiliation of the first author of a 2024 IGARSS paper on drone photogrammetry for land degradation at Mugoboka.

name: GBIF Burundi
summary: Burundi's GBIF node, listed with Burundi as a voting participant and Gitega, Quartier Regideso as the address for its node manager and a staff contact.

name: Institut Géographique du Burundi
summary: Described by Spacehubs Africa as a government agency, created by decree 100/146 on 30 September 1980, offering weather, climate, mapping, photogrammetry and geographic data archiving services.

name: Integrated Approach Pilot – Food Security (IAP-FS) Burundi highlands project
summary: Closed food security pilot project in the Burundi highlands, run from September 2017 to September 2024, that analysed vegetation cover with Collect Earth and trained government staff to monitor impacts.

name: Inventaire forestier national du Burundi
summary: National forest inventory dataset whose results the government validated through OBPE, carried out under the Programme Dukingire Ibidukikije with EU and UNDP support, with equipment handed to OBPE for updating forest data.

name: Kibira Forest Sanctuaries Project
summary: According to UNCDF’s 2024 annual report, this blended-finance project in Kibira National Park has a chimpanzee ecological monitoring and habituation protocol in place.

name: Land cover maps of Burundi, 1990, 2000, 2010 and 2022 (CBIT project)
summary: According to the final report, Burundi’s land cover maps use Landsat composites for 1990, 2000, 2010 and 2022 classified with Random Forests, and show progressive forest land decline.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de l'Agriculture et de l'Elevage
summary: Ministry that, by its own account, designs and carries out national policy on environment, agriculture, livestock, water and land, and with FAO validated a national environment policy and forest strategy on 22 August 2024.

name: Office Burundais pour la Protection de l'Environnement
summary: Public body under the environment ministry, created by decree in 2014, that manages protected areas, runs habitat monitoring in Ruvubu National Park, and received UNDP-supplied equipment in 2025 and 2026.

name: Programme de recherche, échange d'information, sensibilisation et conservation de la biodiversité au Burundi
summary: Under an agreement between OBPE and the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences, this OBPE-run programme collects habitat data in Kibira, Rusizi and Ruvubu, and fire-monitoring data in Ruvubu.

name: Projet d'Appui à la Conservation des Écosystèmes du bassin hydrographique de la Rusizi
summary: Project running from 2023 to 2027, run by OBPE and funded by Enabel, that strengthens biodiversity conservation in Kibira and Rusizi national parks, including vegetation mapping and monitoring of key species' home ranges.

name: Real-time surveillance of Kibira National Park with EarthRanger and InReach
summary: Programme using InReach Mini 2 devices and EarthRanger to monitor Kibira National Park, which OBPE reports transmit information on the park in real time.

name: RUBICOM (Rusizi Plain, Burundi)
summary: Two-year collaborative research project in Burundi's Rusizi Plain, now closed, whose fieldwork included water quality monitoring and a botanical survey of the Rusizi lagoon covering 111 sites, which underpinned a new field guide.

name: Université du Burundi
summary: Public higher education and research institute in Bujumbura, whose six authors of a paper on plant species reported as anti-malaria and mosquito repellents give it as their affiliation, with no GBIF datasets published when read.

name: ACP DOUKPO
summary: Conservation association that manages the Bouche du Roy reserve as the body delegated by local administrations, with about thirty ecoguards under its supervision carrying out surveillance and periodic ecological monitoring.

name: Africa Mobile Nature
summary: Organisation monitoring mammals, birds, freshwater fish, reptiles and woody plants in south-west Benin’s Mono Transboundary Biosphere Reserve, recording biodiversity data in a database.

name: Agence Béninoise pour l'Environnement
summary: Beninese organisation that, according to its GBIF publisher record, handles environmental and social assessments, environmental information and monitoring, and environmental regulation and control.

name: Alerte Biodiversité
summary: Mangrove monitoring programme, run and built by Eco Benin, designed to report illegal exploitation and let users recognise mangrove species and report threats or findings.

name: APASAT ONG
summary: Organisation whose red-bellied monkey project, begun in January 2025 with Stiftung Artenschutz funding, trained ten community members in monitoring by transect, camera traps and GPS mapping.

name: Benin Convention on Biological Diversity Clearing House Mechanism
summary: Benin's Convention on Biological Diversity clearing-house site, which lists a national target to use drones, satellites and remote sensing for biodiversity surveillance by 2030.

name: Benin Environment and Education Society
summary: Organisation that DroneBelow reported in 2018 had held drone mapping workshops on Lake Nokoué fish parks and trained six other environmental associations, in partnership with the Dutch IUCN committee.

name: Benin National Biodiversity Information System
summary: Programme for which JRS funded training by Costa Rica's INBio in 2010 and awarded $150,000 in 2014 to the Université d'Abomey-Calavi's agricultural faculty for implementation, building on GBIF Benin.

name: BID National project BID-AF2015-0065-NAC (Benin)
summary: EU-funded national project under which data were mobilised, with GBIF Benin publishing datasets that came from it.

name: Biodiversité, Recherche et Développement Local ONG
summary: Beninese NGO, created in 2012 and officially founded in 2018, that monitors biodiversity by collecting information on animal and plant species to assess how biodiversity changes.

name: Biomonitoring and Conservation of White-thighed Colobus (Colobus vellerosus) in the Kikélé Sacred Forest
summary: Closed project, funded by the Rufford Foundation, in which camera traps in the Kikélé Sacred Forest identified 35 individual colobus, with a detailed final report filed with the funder.

name: BIOSPHERE
summary: NGO officially created in 2019 and based in Comé, Benin, that collects ecological monitoring data on birds, fish, rays and sharks in the Mono Biosphere Reserve and the Bouche du Roy marine protected area.

name: Centre d'Etudes de Recherche et de Formation Forestières
summary: Public body under the Ministère du Cadre de vie et du Développement Durable that contributes to forest policy and science, holding national inventory data and publishing GBIF datasets including an animal census and a Lama forest plant inventory.

name: Centre d'Innovation pour la Recherche Environnementale et Durable
summary: Registered expertise and training firm in Calavi that lists completed drone and imagery surveillance missions over forest blocks and biodiversity monitoring by geospatial scan.

name: Centre National de Gestion des Réserves de Faune
summary: Public office created on 2 April 1996 to conserve and manage protected areas, publishing wildlife patrol and transect data on GBIF.

name: Centre National de Télédétection et de Suivi Écologique
summary: Body created by Decree 2010-334, replacing an earlier forest cover centre, charged with contributing to forest cover monitoring and offering thematic mapping for ecological monitoring, with its seat in Cotonou.

name: Community-Based Conservation of Red-Bellied Monkeys and Wetland Ecosystems on Agonve Island, Benin
summary: Closed Rufford Foundation-funded project on Agonve Island, Benin, that planned camera-trap monitoring of red-bellied monkeys; its first quarterly report says 15 traps were deployed and retrieved on 10 June 2025, recording four species.

name: Conservation and monitoring of mixed heron, African openbill and cormorant colonies on Ramsar sites 1017 and 1018
summary: Project led by Camille Tchankpan that, per a November 2024 report, counted all identified heronries in August 2024 as a baseline, repeated the count in November, and aimed to train monitors to count breeding pairs by drone.

name: Conserving Colobus vellerosus and Cercopithecus erythrogaster: Integrating Monitoring, Threat Assessment, and Community Engagement in Lokoli Swamp Forest, Benin
summary: Funded by the Rufford Foundation, this active project planned camera traps and drones for primate monitoring in November 2025; its first progress report reports camera trap deployment.

name: CREDI-ONG
summary: Beninese association founded in 2005 that monitors biodiversity, including bio-indicator species in the Vallée du Sitatunga park, and was funded by Fondation Ensemble to study red-bellied monkeys, with about ten individuals observed by 2019.

name: Data Mobilization and Long Term Conservation of Wild Fungi (WEF) in Benin
summary: Funded by a 2022 JRS grant of $65,000 over 30 months, the project aimed to upload fungi records to GBIF and iNaturalist, submit DNA sequences and map conservation priorities.

name: Deuxième Inventaire Forestier National du Bénin
summary: National forest inventory launched on 27 January 2022, following the 2007 one, which in January 2022 was expected to provide data on woody density, forest types and the potential of classified forests.

name: Direction Générale des Eaux, Forêts et Chasse
summary: National directorate under the ministry for the living environment that implements forest policy and manages forests, wildlife and protected areas, and says it has collected biodiversity data, including Pendjari and W animal counts.

name: Eco-Bénin
summary: Organisation promoting ecotourism and eco-development, with an Alerte Biodiversité mangrove monitoring app, which reported a September 2023 student mission aiming to develop a Lac Ahémé monitoring application.

name: GBIF Benin
summary: Benin's GBIF country node, based at the Université d'Abomey-Calavi, led by Jean Cossi Ganglo, which provided the platform for the Benin NBIS and trained members of GBIF Nigeria in December 2018.

name: GeoEnvironment and Biodiversity Conservation
summary: Cotonou-based organisation funded by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, whose grant page reports a camera-trap survey of three monkey species in the Lama Forest Reserve.

name: Institut de Recherches Halieutiques et Océanologiques du Bénin
summary: Beninese public research body for marine, lagoon and lake environments, partnered with RBINS on a 2019 Arduino water-quality sensor project; its GBIF record lists no published datasets.

name: Institut Géographique National
summary: Beninese institute whose statutes were approved by a decree of 30 January 2019, giving it the mission of producing, keeping and distributing basic geographic information, including aerial photographic coverage of the territory.

name: Jeunesse et Emplois Verts pour une Economie Verte
summary: Beninese organisation working with local communities through participatory and action-research approaches, which publishes censuses of animal species (2011 to 2019) and plant species (2004 to 2020) across Benin.

name: JRS Benin project (GBIF Benin data mobilisation)
summary: Data mobilisation project under which GBIF Benin publishes datasets, including data from the Lama Forest reserve.

name: Kpassè Sacred Forest aerial mapping
summary: Completed aerial mapping by Benin Flying Labs in August 2023, requested by Ouidah's municipal authorities, which reportedly found only about five of the forest's original 27 hectares intact.

name: Laboratoire d'Ecologie Appliquée
summary: Laboratory in the Faculty of Agronomic Sciences at the University of Abomey-Calavi, created in 1994, listed as publisher of twenty GBIF datasets, including an inventory of animal species in protected areas.

name: Laboratoire de Biomathématiques et d'Estimations Forestières
summary: Laboratory run by the Université d'Abomey-Calavi, where the Faculty of Agronomic Sciences trains biostatisticians, with research on ecological modelling, forest genetic resources and ecosystem services, and a 2024 paper on random forest variants.

name: Ministère du Cadre de Vie et des Transports, en charge du Développement Durable
summary: Beninese ministry for the living environment and sustainable development, listed by the CBD as home of Benin's primary national focal point, with the protected areas focal point in its forestry directorate.

name: Mobilizing data for Identification, Taxonomy, Socioeconomic Importance and Conservation Assessment of Bryophytes in Benin
summary: Project led by Hospice Dassou, with $249,966 JRS funding over 36 months, aiming to publish bryophyte records on GBIF and iNaturalist; JRS reports no Beninese bryophyte database.

name: Monitoring of wildlife in Benin protected areas
summary: GBIF occurrence dataset of wildlife observations, mainly from camera trapping and direct sightings, in the W and Pendjari biosphere reserves.

name: Naben
summary: Organisation that deployed 15 camera traps on Agonvè island in May 2025 and coordinated a June 2026 bird inventory in Benin.

name: National deforestation risk assessment, Benin and Togo
summary: Project run by Okala, which reports using remote sensing and AI-based land-use analysis in 2024 to assess deforestation risk for EU Deforestation Regulation compliance in Benin and Togo.

name: National Herbarium of Benin
summary: Herbarium funded by the JRS Biodiversity Foundation as grantee of a project on bryophyte data, which plans to train its staff to prepare, publish and access GBIF data.

name: Nature Tropicale
summary: Organisation funded by CEBioS and RAMPAO, reported in October 2022 to be training about twenty ecoguards in Cotonou to record field data on smartphones with SMART instead of paper forms.

name: Numérisation pour la conservation de la Réserve de Biosphère du Mono/site de la Bouche du Roy
summary: Closed project, built by Eco-Bénin and financed by German bodies, which in November 2020 planned to deploy SMART across the Bouche du Roy reserve and train 20 people in charge of it.

name: Observatoire Pilote des Paysages et des Dynamiques Agricoles du Bénin
summary: EU DeSIRA-funded project led by CIRAD and partners, aiming to track Benin’s agricultural and landscape change using high-resolution satellite images; Parakou restitution workshops announced for November 2026.

name: ONG Communautés Nature & Développement Durable
summary: Cotonou-based organisation that reports using camera traps and digital tools for biodiversity monitoring, with a white-bellied pangolin conservation project in the Hlanzoun swamp forest.

name: ONG Rêve Développement
summary: Non-profit working on natural resource conservation that publishes plant species lists for Benin on GBIF, including a gallery forest management plans dataset mobilised in a JRS Biodiversity Foundation project.

name: Organisation pour le Développement Durable et la Biodiversité
summary: Working since 2011 to protect threatened primates and their habitats in Benin, it reports 151 interns and volunteers trained in biodiversity monitoring.

name: Pendjari and W National Parks wildlife collaring
summary: Africa Geographic reports that African Parks ran satellite collaring in Pendjari and W National Parks involving 25 elephants and 14 antelopes, concluding on 12 December 2020.

name: Pendjari leopard camera-trap surveys
summary: Mongabay reports biennial Pendjari leopard surveys from 2017, using 81 camera traps in 2021 and 50 in 2023 across a quarter of the 2021 area.

name: Post-release ecology of white-bellied pangolins rescued from illegal trade in the Dahomey Gap
summary: Closed project that aimed to use camera surveys and radio telemetry to estimate offtake and assess home range and activity of white-bellied pangolins rescued from illegal trade and released.

name: Projet de renforcement de la résilience des communautés locales et de conservation du pangolin à ventre blanc dans la forêt marécageuse de Hlanzoun
summary: Active project run by the NGO CNDD in Hlanzoun and Zogbodomey, with an objective of setting up a camera-trap monitoring protocol for the white-bellied pangolin in the swamp forest.

name: Research Unit of Tropical Mycology and Soil-Plant Fungi Interactions, University of Parakou
summary: Fungi laboratory in the University of Parakou's Faculty of Agronomy, run by the university, which is JRS-funded grantee for a project mobilising data on wild edible fungi in Benin.

name: SOS Biodiversity
summary: Beninese NGO aiming to protect and sustainably manage biodiversity, which publishes a plant census on GBIF and a floristic inventory with permanent plots in Agrimey, Lama and Djigbé forests.

name: SOS Savane-ONG
summary: NGO reported to have launched an environmental education programme near northern Benin's parks, with RBT-WAP support, in which pupils record biodiversity on iNaturalist, aiming for at least 7,200 observations.

name: Sustainable Forest Management and Conservation Project in Central and South Benin
summary: Project in central and southern Benin, funded by the Global Environment Facility and closed on 30 June 2025, with an objective including monitoring carbon stocks and emissions alongside preserving forest cover.

name: Towards Effective Conservation of the Benin Potto: Bridging Ecological and Ethnozoological Knowledge Gaps in the Lama Forest Reserve
summary: Closed Rufford Foundation-funded project in the Lama Forest Reserve that aimed to estimate the Benin potto's population and distribution; its final evaluation report, dated 15 September 2025, describes 24 camera traps run for 10 months.

name: Unité de Recherche en Conservation et Écologie de la Faune
summary: Research unit within the University of Abomey-Calavi's applied ecology laboratory, publisher of a 2020 GBIF dataset of mainly camera-trap wildlife observations in the W and Pendjari biosphere reserves.

name: University of Parakou
summary: Beninese university whose mycology research unit was a JRS grantee for wild fungi data mobilisation in Benin from May 2023 to October 2025, and whose MyTIPS laboratory publishes fungi data on GBIF.

name: Université d'Abomey-Calavi
summary: Beninese university that publishes 62 biodiversity datasets on GBIF, received JRS funding in 2014 to develop Benin's biodiversity portal, and runs a Laboratory of Applied Ecology.

name: Baseline Study of Sun Bears in Brunei Darussalam
summary: A collaborative study of sun bears in Brunei, described by IBER in February 2022, developed to carry out the Sun Bear Conservation Action Plan 2019-2028, run by the Forestry Department, IBER at UBD and Borneo Futures.

name: Camera-trap wildlife study in British Forces Brunei jungle training areas
summary: Camera-trap study in British Forces Brunei’s jungle training areas with Brunei partners, described in an October 2023 DIO post reporting early detection of 30 medium to large mammals.

name: Department of Environment, Parks and Recreation (Brunei Darussalam)
summary: Brunei government department that the ASEAN biodiversity dashboard names, under the Ministry of Development, as the agency overseeing biodiversity and natural resources.

name: Department of Fisheries (Brunei Darussalam)
summary: The Australian High Commission reports ReefCloud training with AIMS for 57 professionals since 2022; AIMS reports about 340,000 coral reef records across 13 coastal sites.

name: Distribution and conservation status of the flat headed cat, Prionailurus planiceps in Brunei Darussalam
summary: A project funded by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, with a grant awarded on 11 January 2018, to determine the flat-headed cat's distribution across Brunei and then develop a conservation action plan.

name: Diversity, Distribution and Conservation Status of Brunei's Freshwater Mussels
summary: Closed project led by the University of Nottingham Malaysia; its November 2017 plan combined fieldwork, molecular barcoding and environmental modelling, with surveys at no fewer than 40 sites across Brunei's major river basins.

name: Forest Monitoring Dashboards (Forest Andulau)
summary: Active browser workspace combining LiDAR, drone, satellite and terrain data for Forest Andulau, with a CanopeAI assistant that queries the data, built by IADA at Universiti Brunei Darussalam and supported by a British Council grant.

name: Forestry Department (Brunei Darussalam)
summary: Brunei government department that, per The Star, was the route for the ministry's 2024 workshop on updating the National Biodiversity Policy, and whose official is listed as a CBD national focal point.

name: Identifying and predicting the spatiotemporal pattern changes and tree species classification in Brunei forest using machine learning techniques and remote sensing imagery
summary: Grant-funded project on forest change patterns and tree species classification in Brunei using machine learning and remote sensing, listed by IADA as a supporting grant for 2022 to 2026 worth BND 56,638.40.

name: Institute for Biodiversity and Environmental Research, Universiti Brunei Darussalam
summary: Research institute at Universiti Brunei Darussalam whose site lists a tropical forest dynamics plot network, long-term rainforest tree monitoring and an acoustic project, and which partners with the ASEAN Centre for Biodiversity.

name: Institute of Applied Data Analytics, Universiti Brunei Darussalam
summary: Institute at Universiti Brunei Darussalam that says it self-hosts the Forest Monitoring Dashboards platform.

name: Ministry of Primary Resources and Tourism (Brunei Darussalam)
summary: Brunei government ministry that, according to The Star, organised the 2024 workshop on updating the National Biodiversity Policy and Strategic Plan of Action through its Forestry Department.

name: Monitoring and quantification of spatial-temporal changes in carbon stocks according to forest types of Brunei Darussalam
summary: Project led by Rahayu Sukmaria Sukri and funded by the Korea Forest Service; in October 2019 IBER said it was setting national forest inventory and baseline data for an MRV framework, using field survey and remote sensing.

name: National Forest Resources Inventory (Brunei Darussalam)
summary: Brunei forest inventory covering 2023 to 2025, managed by Lunima Sdn Bhd with the Forestry Department, and cited by an ERIA report for a figure on the Badas peat swamp forests.

name: Refining guidelines for the release of confiscated Sunda pangolin in Brunei
summary: A project funded by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund (grant awarded 8 June 2015) that used VHF transmitters to monitor released Sunda pangolins and proposed a six-week survey for baseline abundance and distribution data.

name: School of Computing and Informatics, Universiti Teknologi Brunei
summary: An active school at Universiti Teknologi Brunei, formed in 2014, offering undergraduate and postgraduate degrees; its affiliation appears on a 2023 OpenAlex-listed paper on LoRa-based remote sensing of peatland in Brunei.

name: School of Digital Science, Universiti Brunei Darussalam
summary: School at Universiti Brunei Darussalam in Gadong, whose author is the corresponding author on a 2023 OpenAlex-listed paper mapping highway forest cover change in Brunei with deep learning and Sentinel-2.

name: Survey Department (Brunei Darussalam)
summary: Brunei government department that, per the national SDG site, organised the Brunei Darussalam Geospatial Challenge 2024 with NIAT as part of GIS Day 2024.

name: Ulu Temburong National Park mammal camera-trap survey
summary: Camera-trap survey of mammals in Ulu Temburong National Park which, in March 2021, IBER said had run over three years with support from UBD, Panthera and the Robertson Foundation.

name: Universiti Brunei Darussalam
summary: University that hosts the Institute for Biodiversity and Environmental Research and whose School of Digital Science and IBER authors produced a 2023 paper mapping Brunei forest cover change with deep learning and Sentinel-2.

name: Universiti Teknologi Brunei
summary: Brunei university whose researchers started peatland projects in 2016, with plans reported in 2021 for IoT monitoring at Badas, and which runs the School of Computing and Informatics.

name: ABE satellite fire-monitoring platform
summary: Satellite platform updating heat hotspots from Earth-observation data, running around the clock according to the Ministry of Public Works, which instructed ABE to monitor fires in July 2026.

name: Agencia Boliviana Espacial
summary: Bolivian space agency that offers satellite services and images, and which DPL News reported in July 2026 as training users in Tarija and offering free training on the GESAT Beta fire-monitoring platform.

name: AMA
summary: Regional monitoring platform run by RAISG for analysing fires, deforestation, biodiversity and ecosystem services in the Amazon, where users can query, analyse and download maps and data.

name: App BUFEO
summary: Citizen-science app for monitoring Bolivian river dolphins and threats, funded by WWF, with Faunagua reporting public information and daily observations by nine fishers on Amazonian rivers.

name: Asociación Armonía
summary: Bolivian bird conservation organisation reporting past population monitoring of seven threatened species and yearly shorebird monitoring in the Barba Azul Nature Reserve.

name: Autoridad de Fiscalización y Control Social de Bosques y Tierra
summary: Bolivian forest and land oversight authority whose site offers a daily heat-source report, and which reported launching the ABT360 platform unifying forest and agrarian information in December 2025.

name: Autoridad Plurinacional de la Madre Tierra
summary: State body that a UNDP page calls the main one responsible for managing forests and the environment in Bolivia, and which partners on Brazil-nut forest mapping in the Cavineño territory.

name: Bolivia Flying Labs
summary: Drone-focused group that says it concluded a forest-fire prevention project using drones, and which won a WingtraOne GEN II fixed-wing drone in the 2022 Wingtra Earth Day Challenge.

name: Bolivia-Germany forest protection initiative in Pando and Charagua Iyambae
summary: Initiative announced in July 2026 by the Bolivian and German governments, backed by €15 million from KfW, to strengthen forest protection, governance and monitoring systems and reduce deforestation.

name: Boliviana de Innovación Tecnológica Satelital
summary: Offers custom software, geospatial solutions and environmental consultancy, and says it validated and implemented a biodiversity module within Bolivia's SIMB forest monitoring platform in 2019.

name: Brazil-nut forest mapping in the Cavineño territory
summary: Project where UNDP says Bioverse mapped Cavineño Brazil-nut forests with local partners, with satellite maps reported in August 2024 as accessible through a mobile app.

name: Centro de Investigación en Biodiversidad y Medio Ambiente
summary: A research centre whose remote sensing and GIS department studies biodiversity and ecosystems, keeps a Landsat image bank being collected for all of Beni, and is named as editor of a report on a 2024 land cover map.

name: Centro de Monitoreo Territorial de la CICC
summary: A proposed territorial monitoring centre, prioritised by the CICC as an early warning hub, with a planned QGIS geodatabase for Concepción and a protocol due 30 October 2026 setting data flow from monitors to alerts.

name: Centro Geoespacial para la Biodiversidad de Bolivia
summary: Biodiversity platform built by the Noel Kempff Mercado museum with JRS funding, reportedly launched on 19 April 2013, with JRS reporting over 80,000 vertebrate records made public.

name: Conservación Amazónica – ACEAA
summary: Bolivian private non-profit association, established in 2011, that says it uses remote sensing, drones, camera traps and apps for research and monitoring, and runs a portal with real-time fire monitoring for Pando.

name: Conservation of Carnivores in Cerro San Pedro: Ecology and Strategies to Mitigate Anthropogenic Threats in Cochabamba, a Highly Urbanized City
summary: A project on the carnivores of Cerro San Pedro near Cochabamba, which reported in May 2025 that it was using camera traps, faecal diet analysis and small-mammal live trapping.

name: Dirección de Recursos Naturales
summary: Departmental directorate under Santa Cruz's environment secretariat, responsible for forest fire management and SATIF oversight, with a specialised forest firefighters unit created in 2020–2022.

name: Dirección General de Gestión y Desarrollo Forestal
summary: Bolivian forest directorate that depends on the planning and environment ministry and runs SIMB, which the SIMB site calls its official platform.

name: Drontec
summary: Bolivian company that, according to a July 2024 UNDP page, joined a digital forest mapping workshop and uses satellite technology, drones and artificial intelligence to analyse forests and territorial change.

name: Faunagua
summary: Non-profit founded in 2004, based in Cochabamba, reporting research on Bolivian aquatic resources and wetlands and a dolphin citizen-science project aiming to involve fishers, boat owners and tourists.

name: Firehawk Project
summary: Closed drone project, run by Bolivia Flying Labs and funded by WeRobotics, which mapped forest areas to identify high-risk fire zones, flying about 100 hectares each at two sites near Roboré in July 2023.

name: Fundación Amigos de la Naturaleza
summary: Bolivian civil society organisation that lists monitoring platforms including SATRIFO, AMA and MapBiomas Bolivia Collection 1.0, and which RAISG names as its member for Bolivia.

name: Fundación Natura Bolivia
summary: A Bolivian non-profit founded in 2003, based in Santa Cruz and funded by CEPF, that monitors wildlife with 120 camera traps, tests acoustic and environmental DNA tools, and monitors deforestation and fires geospatially.

name: Fundación para el Desarrollo de la Ecología
summary: A CEPF-funded organisation approved for two grants running 23 December 2022 to 30 November 2023: updating Cotapata park and KBA monitoring with bioindicators, and sharing corridor biodiversity data through a web application.

name: Fundación para la Conservación del Bosque Chiquitano
summary: Non-profit founded in 1999 to conserve Chiquitano heritage, monitoring habitats and wildlife, with an observatory receiving fire alerts, reporting leadership of a publication on fire recurrence in the Americas.

name: Fundación Teko Kavi
summary: A CEPF-funded foundation approved in 2023 to assess Andean cat distribution and habitat in the Apolobamba protected area, whose team installed 40 camera traps in July 2025, as reported by ANF.

name: Instituto Boliviano de Investigación Forestal
summary: A non-profit civil entity created on 31 October 2002 that monitors forest landscapes, reports community fire monitoring in TCO Monte Verde and funds a CICC monitoring centre technician.

name: Instituto de Investigaciones Forestales de la Amazonía
summary: Forestry research institute created in 1984 under a university faculty in Riberalta, which says it has monitored a growing number of permanent plots since the 1990s and partners with RAINFOR.

name: Instituto de Investigaciones Geográficas, Universidad Mayor de San Andrés
summary: Geography research institute at the Universidad Mayor de San Andrés, whose affiliation appears on a 2024 paper comparing spectral signatures of asaí, majo and cacao using remote sensors in northern La Paz.
