summary: Brazilian company that uses WhatsApp and AI to turn fishers' and communities' reports into data for research and environmental management, with the São Paulo fisheries institute.

name: Tamo de Olho
summary: Deforestation monitoring programme launched in 2021, run by WWF-Brasil and partners, using satellite data and public geospatial databases to support advocacy and grassroots groups, with a platform ranking cases and offering georeferenced downloads.

name: Terra Intelligence
summary: Abundance Brasil's land platform, which reads rural properties with satellite images, AI and official sources for socio-environmental checks and land valuation.

name: TerraBrasilis
summary: INPE's web platform for reaching, querying and analysing the geographic data from its native vegetation monitoring projects.

name: TerraClass
summary: Joint INPE and Embrapa project that has mapped since 2011 what has replaced deforested land in the Amazon and Cerrado.

name: Terras App Solutions
summary: Technology partner of MapBiomas. Its own site refuses automated reading.

name: Terras do Brasil
summary: Federal land-data platform launched in April 2024, chosen under the AI for Nature and Climate Challenge to use AI to monitor land use in real time and support land regularisation.

name: TideWise
summary: Company that combines autonomous surface vehicles with oceanographic sensors for environmental monitoring and licensing.

name: Tigrinus
summary: Supplier of wildlife monitoring equipment, selling VHF and GPS transmitters and receivers and automatic animal sound recorders, with permanent technical support.

name: Timberflow
summary: Imaflora data platform that joins Brazil's timber control systems, including DOF/Sinaflor and Sisflora Mato Grosso, and publishes technical bulletins.

name: Trapa-Câmera
summary: São Paulo company, founded in 2004, that makes camera traps and radio collars for wildlife research, and developed battery-free tracking with FAPESP support.

name: TREES Research Lab
summary: Research group led by Luiz Aragão, headquartered at INPE, assessing the effects of environmental change on tropical ecosystems with remote sensing and field surveys.

name: Treesistance
summary: Non-profit working with the Indigenous Borarí people on real-time forest protection in the Brazilian Amazon, deploying Hack The Planet's InstantDetect AI cameras, according to IO+.

name: Umgrauemeio
summary: Brazilian company based in Jundiaí, working in Brazil, Paraguay and Spain, whose Pantera platform uses cameras, AI and satellite data to detect wildfire smoke.

name: Universidade da Região de Joinville
summary: University in Joinville, Santa Catarina. It passes the register test because it publishes ZooarchBR, a national database of fish remains from archaeological sites on GBIF.

name: Universidade de São Paulo
summary: University named as a partner in Digitais da Floresta and as the seat of the Brazilian Team in XPRIZE Rainforest.

name: Universidade do Estado do Amazonas
summary: State university in Amazonas where students and its embedded systems laboratory built the Curupira acoustic deforestation device.

name: Universidade Estadual de Campinas
summary: São Paulo state university whose zoology museum holds the Fonoteca Neotropical Jacques Vielliard sound archive.

name: Universidade Estadual de Feira de Santana
summary: University that co-coordinates the Caatinga biome in MapBiomas.

name: Universidade Federal da Bahia
summary: Federal university in Brazil, partner of Censipam on the SIPAM Mar oil slick detection system.

name: Universidade Federal de Goiás
summary: Federal university in Goiânia that runs the Lapig image processing and geoprocessing laboratory, which lists a Goiás vegetation remnants atlas and launched UFG-IA to map the university's use of artificial intelligence.

name: Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso do Sul
summary: Federal university partner, with Cornell and PPBio-Pantanal, on automated AI acoustic monitoring of the Pantanal funded by the Bezos Earth Fund.

name: Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina
summary: Federal university in Florianópolis. It passes the register test because it publishes NONATObase, a polychaete database for the Southwestern Atlantic, and long-term reef monitoring data from Brazil's oceanic islands.

name: Universidade Federal do Pará
summary: Federal university hosting the INCT IAmazônia at its High-Performance Computing and AI Center.

name: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro
summary: Brazilian university whose Department of Meteorology hosts LASA, which teaches and researches remote sensing of the atmosphere and land surface, and which runs that laboratory and is a partner in the SIFAU wetland fire intelligence system.

name: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul
summary: University that co-coordinates the Pampa biome in MapBiomas.

name: UpgradeX
summary: Startup in the technology business incubator at the Federal University of Lavras, maker of Urubu Safe.

name: Urubu Safe
summary: Road safety app from the startup UpgradeX, built on Sistema Urubu data to model the risk of collisions with animals across Brazil's roads.

name: Uso de inteligência artificial para otimizar estimativas regionais dos estoques e fluxos de carbono e água no bioma Caatinga
summary: Project on the OndaCBC network's site assessing machine learning to quantify and monitor carbon and water stocks and flows in the Caatinga biome, with institutions in Brazil and the United States.

name: VEIO
summary: InfoAmazonia platform that combines public records to track gold mining in the Brazilian Amazon, compares what is declared with what is observed and produces a prioritised list of what to investigate.

name: Velozzia
summary: ICMBio's system for monitoring areas hit by fire in federal conservation units. No page read says how it works, so no AI label is claimed.

name: VM9
summary: Brazilian startup behind the IAguas AI project on river water quality with the Fluminense Federal University.

name: Wetlands International Brasil
summary: Organisation that signed a technical cooperation agreement with LASA-UFRJ to expand Pantanal fire monitoring and alerting, and in June 2021 reported providing georeferenced fire occurrence data under it.

name: Wood Chat
summary: Brazilian startup formed in June 2024 with an AI that identifies timber species from photographs and a WhatsApp assistant, Violeta, that teaches forest conservation.

name: WRI Brasil
summary: Brazilian arm of the World Resources Institute, with a project developing remote sensing methods to measure landscape restoration.

name: WWF-Brasil
summary: Brazilian arm of the WWF network, which has a conservation technology line of work covering drones, sensors, camera traps and the SMART patrol tool.

name: Xmobots
summary: Brazilian drone maker that develops vehicles, hardware, software and AI, whose Nauru 500C drone Bioverse uses for forest inventories.

name: Abaco Advanced Landscape and Ecosystem Monitoring Project
summary: A project run by Florida International University, planned for 15 August 2022 to 14 August 2027, using aerial and terrestrial LiDAR to study forest structure and pine regeneration on the Abaco Islands.

name: All about sawfish in the Bahamas: tracking movement, breeding and nurseries
summary: A Save Our Seas Foundation-funded project, centred on Andros, in which each sawfish is tagged and tracked by satellites and acoustic receivers.

name: Andros silky shark acoustic telemetry study
summary: A Save Our Seas Foundation-funded study off Andros that, by a November 2025 blog, had acoustic-tagged 51 silky sharks since 2020, monitored by twelve receivers near the buoy.

name: Bahama Banks Blue Carbon project
summary: A 2025 Blue Carbon International abstract reports mapping 500,000 hectares to 5 cm accuracy and finding up to 30% seagrass loss between 2010 and 2020.

name: Bahama Oriole Project
summary: A collaboration between the University of Maryland, Baltimore County and the Bahamas National Trust; a December 2016 post says a May 2016 field team found previously unknown breeding populations in Andros.

name: Bahama Parrots of Nassau Locator
summary: A Bahamas National Trust citizen science project that asks New Providence residents to help collect basic information on the parrots living in the capital.

name: Bahamas Marine Mammal Research Organisation
summary: A small non-profit in Marsh Harbour, Abaco, which says it has documented marine mammals around The Bahamas since 1991, with over 5,000 sightings, the region's only long-term dataset of its kind.

name: Bahamas Marine Mammal Research Organisation Opportunistic Sightings
summary: A dataset of marine mammal sightings from 1988 to 2011, including public reports, provided by the Bahamas Marine Mammal Research Organisation and published in OBIS-SEAMAP.

name: Bahamas Motus stations
summary: A BirdsCaribbean-run project, funded by the US Fish and Wildlife Service and American Bird Conservancy, which by December 2023 had installed two of four planned Motus radio telemetry stations, both on Grand Bahama.

name: Bahamas National Geographic Information Systems Centre
summary: A unit within the Bahamas Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources that, ZNS reported in December 2024, maps the Bahamian landscape, supplies data to agencies and companies, and uses drones, ATVs and mapping software.

name: Bahamas National Trust
summary: A non-profit managing 33 national parks, with GIS mapping, bird monitoring and a February 2023 Inagua trial using drones and cameras to monitor flamingos and feral hogs.

name: Bahamas National Trust national park bird banding project
summary: A Bahamas National Trust wildlife monitoring project in which, by October 2020, Science Officer Scott Johnson had collected two years of bird data in New Providence national parks using identification bands.

name: Bahamas Protected Areas Fund
summary: A corporate body funding protected area management and ecosystem monitoring, whose director reportedly told The Tribune in August 2026 that nine applicants received about $400,000 that year.

name: Bahamas Shorebird Initiative
summary: An Audubon programme, with the Bahamas National Trust as partner, that identified critical shorebird sites, including ones holding half the Atlantic Piping Plover population, and bands wintering Piping Plovers.

name: Bahamian Hutia conservation project (MBZF grant 242536130)
summary: A conservation project with a $9,300 grant awarded on 22 January 2025 by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, whose first objective is baseline surveys on known hutia islands.

name: Bimini Biological Field Station Foundation
summary: A non-profit on South Bimini, Bahamas, studying sharks and rays; a Save Our Seas Foundation page says its shark lab has run longline surveys for over three decades.

name: Capacity building to enhance management of threats to Rock Iguanas in The Bahamas
summary: A Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund grant of $209,994 for April 2025 to July 2027, under which the University of The Bahamas will develop a Central Bahamian Rock Iguana monitoring plan.

name: Cape Eleuthera Institute
summary: A research and conservation centre in South Eleuthera, with whale acoustic surveys, a 2011 to 2023 turtle tagging initiative, and a 2026 paper on machine learning for turtle breathing.

name: Cape Eleuthera Institute Shark Research Program
summary: A Cape Eleuthera Institute programme that monitors shark populations and habitats to safeguard the Bahamas shark sanctuary, and in 2026 resumed nurse shark mating surveys using drones, observation and captures.

name: Coral Vita
summary: Self-described for-profit reef restoration platform that outplants farmed corals on the south coast of Grand Bahama and launched a thermal resilience programme at its Freeport farm.

name: Department of Environmental Planning and Protection
summary: A department within the Ministry of the Environment and Natural Resources, led by a Director who is the Bahamas' primary CBD focal point, and named as executing partner in a GCF deforestation readiness proposal.

name: Exploration of The Bahamas' Deep Sea Habitats
summary: A deep-sea survey led by Marmoris, with an $80,000 award starting 15 March 2026, to document species and habitats around Long Island, Cat Island and San Salvador using imaging and sensors.

name: Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park annual survey
summary: An annual Bahamas National Trust survey of reefs, mangroves and seagrass; The Tribune reported in August 2017 that it covered 12 sites and was funded by the Global Environment Facility.

name: Exuma Turtle Project
summary: A sea turtle research project in the Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park, which Sea Turtle Conservancy says it began in 2025, to provide long-term trend data to wildlife managers.

name: Forestry Unit
summary: A Bahamas government unit that FAO says it trained in National Forest Inventory data collection using Android devices and the Silva Metricus app in July 2026, and the primary beneficiary of a GCF readiness proposal.

name: Marmoris
summary: A Bahamas non-profit that surveys ocean ecosystems with video and sensor data; a Templeton World Charity Foundation record says it is leading a country-wide deep-sea survey and has gathered nearly 200 hours of imagery.

name: Ministry of the Environment and Natural Resources
summary: A Bahamas ministry that houses the Department of Environmental Planning and Protection in Nassau and is named among the beneficiaries of a GCF deforestation readiness project, after the Forestry Unit.

name: Multi-year monitoring of shorebirds in The Bahamas
summary: A dataset of 2,756 observations of 62 bird species from censuses on 16 islands between 2006 and 2022, built by Audubon, Environment and Climate Change Canada and the USGS.

name: National Forest Inventory of The Bahamas
summary: A forest inventory programme that FAO says will collect biophysical and socioeconomic data from sampling units on Abaco, Acklins and Andros, with training participants having used mobile technology in pine, mangrove and coppice forest.

name: Preparation of Strategic Framework to Reduce Deforestation and Forest Degradation and enhance adaptive capacity in the Bahamas
summary: A GCF-funded readiness project for the Bahamas, approved 2 December 2022 with FAO as the organisation, targeting the lack of a National Forest and Land-Use Monitoring System.

name: Saving the Silver Boa: In Situ and Ex Situ Conservation of the World’s Most Endangered Boa
summary: A project funded by a $13,300 Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund grant awarded on 30 January 2019, which plans a population census, a habitat survey and an ex situ colony of six boas.

name: SMART rollout across Bahamian protected areas
summary: A rollout run by Re:wild of the SMART tool across the whole Bahamian protected area network, so rangers can collect data and respond to illegal fishing and wildlife crime.

name: The Bahamas: a beacon of hope for smalltooth sawfish
summary: A Save Our Seas Foundation-funded project, led by Tristan Guttridge, that plans aerial surveys, side-scan sonar and BRUVs to measure sawfish distribution and abundance at Andros, plus a public sightings network.

name: Tracking Bimini's sharks
summary: A Save Our Seas Foundation-funded project run by the Bimini Biological Field Station, whose director uses a network of receivers to record the movements of great hammerheads and other sharks around Bimini.

name: University of The Bahamas
summary: A university at Oakes Field Campus, Nassau, listed as grantee of a Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund rock iguana project, and reported in November 2024 to have five Wilson Award grantees.

name: Annual Black-necked Crane Count for Bhutan
summary: A winter count of black-necked cranes across all habitats, run by RSPN to track population trends; the 2014 count combined spotting-scope counts, photographs counted on a monitor, and departure counts.

name: Bhutan biodiversity monitoring grid
summary: Biodiversity monitoring grid built by the Department of Forests and Park Services across protected areas and forest divisions; BBS reports 144 of close to 2,500 cells used, recording close to 1,200 species.

name: Bhutan Biodiversity Portal
summary: A consortium-based online biodiversity platform for which the National Biodiversity Centre is secretariat, with citizen-science data planned for publication through GBIF (2020 registration).

name: Bhutan Ecological Society
summary: Bhutan-based organisation listed by UNDP Bhutan as a CSO and NGO partner, whose flagship M3D camera trap project has had support from Explorers Against Extinction since 2026.

name: Bhutan for Life
summary: A programme described by its Fund Secretariat's Executive Director as a financing mechanism, which DoFPS says funded the 2022-2023 national snow leopard survey.

name: Bhutan Forest Fire Detection and Monitoring System
summary: Forest fire detection and monitoring system for Nepal and Bhutan based on MODIS data, built by ICIMOD in 2015 or earlier with both countries' forest departments under SERVIR-Himalaya.

name: Bhutan nationwide rangeland extent and condition assessment
summary: A closed study giving the first nationwide high-resolution multi-temporal map of Bhutan's rangelands, using Google Earth Engine, Sentinel-2 and Random Forest, with training points collected by herders on smartphones.

name: Bhutan snow leopard GPS telemetry project
summary: GPS telemetry project tracking snow leopards in Bhutan's high-altitude landscapes; three have been collared since 2016, and an official says two more are wanted in 2026-2027.

name: Bhutan Tiger Center
summary: Research, education, outreach and policy centre established under the Department of Forests and Park Services; in 2022 its team satellite-collared a tiger responsible for cattle kills, per the Bhutan Foundation.

name: Bhutan Trust Fund for Environmental Conservation
summary: A fund that says it was established in 1991 as the world's first environmental trust fund, and which DoFPS lists among partners supporting snow leopard conservation in Bhutan.

name: Bumdeling Wildlife Sanctuary
summary: A protected area listed by DoFPS, whose rangers were among over 70 completing the 2022-2023 national snow leopard survey, which captured snow leopards from new locations including the sanctuary.

name: College of Natural Resources, Royal University of Bhutan
summary: A college in Punakha hosting Bhutan's first eDNA laboratory, launched on 25 April 2025 with ETH Zurich and WWF-Bhutan support, and the affiliation of a 2026 eDNA and camera-trap paper's first author.

name: College of Science and Technology, Royal University of Bhutan
summary: A Bhutanese college whose Information Technology Department staff wrote a 2025 paper in its journal on a machine learning bird recognition system covering 23 species, fine-tuned from Google's pre-trained vision transformer.

name: Department of Environment and Climate Change (Bhutan)
summary: A department under the Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources that jointly led preparation of the 5th NBSAP, which sets 20 targets, with NBC and with UNDP and GEF support.

name: Department of Forests and Park Services (Bhutan)
summary: Bhutan's forest and park agency reportedly uses SMART patrolling, invests in drone and AI-enabled surveillance, and participated in a Mangdechhu eDNA pilot detecting 201 vertebrate taxa.

name: Divisional Forest Office, Sarpang
summary: BBS quotes its forestry chief on mapping hotspots using GPS collar data and conflict records, and reports 125 officials deployed across 17 areas for Gelephu chorten raising.

name: Divisional Forest Office, Zhemgang
summary: A divisional forest office listed by the forest department, where BBS reported camera traps showed a tigress last seen in 2014 with three cubs, and a tiger report supported by WWF Bhutan and UNDP was expected.

name: eDNA for biodiversity monitoring pilot study, Mangde Chhu river basin
summary: Closed eDNA pilot in south-central Bhutan, run by the Department of Forests and Park Services, testing eDNA for tiger and prey monitoring; The Bhutanese reports it detected 201 unique vertebrate taxa.

name: eDNA Laboratory, College of Natural Resources
summary: Laboratory run by the College of Natural Resources, launched on 25 April 2025; The Bhutanese reports it is Bhutan's first eDNA laboratory, set up with ETH Zurich and WWF-Bhutan support.

name: Enhancing Biodiversity Protection and Building Capacity for Cooperative Research in Bhutan to Address Sustainable Development Goal 15
summary: Running from July 2024 to June 2027 under Naturhistorisches Museum Wien, the project plans forest mapping, uses Google Earth Engine and develops avian malaria sampling.

name: Forest Information Reporting and Monitoring System
summary: An online forest data repository run by Bhutan's Department of Forests and Park Services, developed in 2017, holds human-wildlife conflict reports and poaching records.

name: Forest Monitoring and Information Division (Bhutan)
summary: One of four functional divisions of Bhutan's forest department, set up in the 2023 restructuring, that runs national forest inventories, remote sensing for forest health, cover and carbon, and the FIRMS platform.

name: Jigme Dorji National Park
summary: A protected area listed by DoFPS, whose rangers were among over 70 who completed the 2022-2023 national snow leopard survey.

name: Jigme Khesar Strict Nature Reserve
summary: A protected area listed by DoFPS, whose rangers were among over 70 who completed the 2022-2023 national snow leopard survey.

name: Jigme Singye Wangchuck National Park
summary: A protected area listed by DoFPS, whose rangers were among over 70 who completed the 2022-2023 national snow leopard survey.

name: Jomotsangkha Wildlife Sanctuary
summary: A Bhutanese wildlife sanctuary, formerly Khaling Wildlife Sanctuary and renamed in 2014, whose listed work includes flora and fauna monitoring and where camera traps confirmed species other than the pygmy hog and hispid hare.

name: Mapping and Quantifying Multiple Threats to the Critically Endangered White-bellied Heron and associated waterbird species in Bhutan
summary: Completed RSPN study, funded by the Hong Kong Bird Watching Society's 2024-25 Asia Conservation Fund, that identified, quantified and mapped threats to the White-bellied Heron along the Mangdechhu and Punatsangchhu basins.

name: Monitoring Mountain Mammalian Diversity (M3D)
summary: Camera trap project run by the Bhutan Ecological Society, building on a pilot that documented 20 mammal species, and planning about 150 stations covering around 1,500 square kilometres.

name: National Biodiversity Centre (Bhutan)
summary: A Thimphu-based body set up in 1998 under the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock, serving as national biodiversity information clearing house and secretariat to the Bhutan Biodiversity Portal.

name: National Forest Inventory of Bhutan
summary: Bhutan's first full national forest inventory, run by the Royal Government of Bhutan, was reported complete by UN-REDD in August 2019, with results in two reports.

name: National Forest Monitoring System (Bhutan)
summary: A forest monitoring system named among the outcomes of Bhutan's REDD+ readiness programme, with the department's Forest Monitoring and Information function described as solely responsible for it, and run by the Forest Monitoring and Information Division.

name: National Land Commission Secretariat (Bhutan)
summary: BBS reports it leads a satellite data initiative with the Bhutan Foundation and Planet Labs, and quotes its land use and land cover mapping mandate.

name: National Red Panda Survey of Bhutan 2023
summary: A closed survey by the Department of Forests and Park Services, reported by BBS as the first of its kind, estimating over 300 red pandas across nineteen districts, with highest numbers in three sampling areas.

name: National Snow Leopard Survey of Bhutan 2022-2023
summary: A closed survey run by DoFPS and funded by Bhutan for Life, using 310 camera-trap stations over 9,000 km² and confirming 134 snow leopards, up from 96 in 2016 (announced September 2023).

name: National Tiger Survey of Bhutan 2021-2022
summary: A closed national survey whose 2022 report was launched at Global Tiger Day 2023 in Thimphu, with the Global Tiger Forum reporting tiger numbers rising from 103 in 2015 to 131 in 2022.

name: Nature Conservation Division (Bhutan)
summary: A division of Bhutan's forest department responsible for wildlife surveys, enumerations, assessments and species monitoring, whose grantee affiliation appears on a camera trapping study of domestic dogs and wild cats in protected areas.

name: Pangolin conservation pilot in Royal Manas National Park
summary: A completed Bhutan Foundation pilot with the forest department combining camera traps, burrow surveys, genetic sampling and acoustic monitoring, recording Chinese and Indian pangolins at four of 285 camera stations and no confirmed calls on seven recorders.

name: Royal Manas National Park
summary: A protected area listed by the forest department, where officials used camera traps for a biological corridor survey and where a Bhutan Foundation pangolin pilot built ranger capacity and baseline data.

name: Royal Society for Protection of Nature
summary: A citizen-based NGO established in 1987, reporting a week-long drone study that located a White-bellied Heron nest and plans to introduce AI-powered conservation technologies.

name: Royal University of Bhutan
summary: An education institution in Bhutan, recorded by OpenAlex as the institution of the College of Natural Resources affiliation on a 2026 eDNA and camera-trap paper.

name: Strengthening the long-term persistence of tigers in the high altitudes of Bhutan
summary: A closed 2023 to 2024 project under IUCN Save Our Species' Integrated Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme, planned for five protected areas and five forest divisions, including a long-term tiger population monitoring programme.

name: Wangchuck Centennial National Park
summary: A protected area listed by DoFPS, whose rangers were among over 70 who completed the 2022-2023 national snow leopard survey.

name: White-bellied Heron annual population survey (Bhutan)
summary: Annual survey run by RSPN since 2003 with Department of Forest and Park Services support; BBS reports RSPN's annual report found Bhutan is home to 25 White-bellied Herons.

name: White-bellied Heron landscape biodiversity survey, eastern Bhutan
summary: Undated RSPN-run survey of biodiversity and socio-economic conditions in eastern Bhutan's White-bellied Heron landscape, using drones and camera traps, with eDNA sampling planned for the second round.

name: WildinSync nationwide eDNA biodiversity map of Bhutan
summary: An active project with DoFPS, WWF Bhutan and the College of Natural Resources to make Bhutan's first nationwide eDNA biodiversity map, setting a baseline from around 200 river catchment sampling locations.

name: Aardvark Project (Makgadikgadi)
summary: Active project using camera traps and systematic anthill counts to map aardvark distribution across the CT11 concession in the Makgadikgadi.

name: Aeronautical Solutions
summary: Botswana company whose drone project was funded by the Botswana Innovation Fund, with its unmanned aerial vehicle intended for anti-poaching exercises, security and surveillance.

name: Bird Population Monitoring Programme (Botswana)
summary: Citizen-scientist bird monitoring programme in Botswana, started in 2010 as part of a global effort to monitor terrestrial birds, run by BirdLife Botswana.

name: BirdLife Botswana
summary: Conservation organisation that runs the Bird Population Monitoring programme, and whose corporate profile also lists a nest record scheme, volunteer vulture monitoring and a protected-area monitoring project.

name: Botswana International University of Science and Technology
summary: University established in 2006 whose PhD student reportedly led a drones-and-AI anti-poaching proof of concept validated in Khama Rhino Sanctuary.

name: Botswana National Leopard Survey
summary: Closed SCIF-run survey, with the Department of Wildlife and National Parks, covering 20 sites with over 1,000 trail camera stations from September 2022 to December 2024, used for national leopard maps; final report completed August 2026.

name: Botswana National Museum
summary: Government department mandated to protect Botswana's cultural and natural heritage, with a natural history division that collects specimens and publishes a digitised dataset of its Hymenoptera collection.

name: Botswana Predator Conservation
summary: Programme run by Wild Entrust, researching since 1989, that monitors predators by observation and camera traps, with a hyaena photo database it says has helped train machine learning algorithms.

name: Botswana Wildlife Roadkill Study
summary: A nationwide citizen science project, run by the Okavango Research Institute and the University of New South Wales, asking for photo and location reports on iNaturalist to identify roadkill hotspots and the species most affected.

name: Botswana Wildlife Watch
summary: Proposed project to use remote camera traps to estimate large carnivore and prey populations and distribution in the Northern Tuli Game Reserve, and to identify predictive wildlife corridors and barriers.

name: Camera Trapping, Capacity Building and Lion Monitoring in KAZA
summary: Closed 2021 project that aimed to set baseline lion data in the Linyanti system and Chobe River floodplain through camera trap surveys, and to build local camera trapping capacity.

name: Carnivore population monitoring in Botswana and Zimbabwe
summary: WildCRU-run programme reporting 53 camera-trap surveys across Botswana and Zimbabwe to establish baseline large carnivore densities, classifying images with the AI tool TrapTagger.

name: Cheetah Conservation Botswana
summary: Organisation that in December 2020 reported removing 132 camera-trap units from Ghanzi ranches used for long-term monitoring, and sending photos to Wageningen University to trial automated analysis software.

name: Community-based wildlife monitoring (Round River, northern Botswana)
summary: Active Round River project that since 2013 has helped northern Botswana community trusts carry out wildlife, carnivore sightings and bird monitoring, with data returned each field year to the trusts, ORI and DWNP.

name: Conservation of Natural Ecosystems Trust
summary: Active trust working in Botswana and the Okavango Delta that says it focuses on wildlife monitoring and welfare and community livelihoods, digitising and analysing monitoring data for the Department of Wildlife and National Parks.

name: Department of Forestry and Range Resources (Botswana)
summary: Government department, run by the environment ministry, charged with conserving and managing Botswana's vegetation resources, which OC Global says it assisted in establishing a nationwide forest monitoring system.

name: Department of Surveys and Mapping (Botswana)
summary: Government department in Gaborone from which maps, aerial photographs, digital elevation models and remote sensing data can be obtained, according to the government portal.

name: Department of Sustainable Natural Resources, Botswana International University of Science and Technology
summary: Based at BIUST in Palapye, the department appears as an affiliation in a 2025 paper applying Transformer models to national-scale land cover mapping in Botswana using 30-metre Landsat imagery.

name: Department of Wildlife and Aquatic Resources, Botswana University of Agriculture and Natural Resources
summary: Academic department of the Faculty of Natural Resources at Botswana University of Agriculture and Natural Resources, providing teaching and research, with a 2024 paper by its author on elephant spatial dynamics in the Central Kalahari Game Reserve.

name: Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Botswana)
summary: Government department, run by the environment ministry, responsible for fish and wildlife; its Maun office received donated drones in November 2025, and it was named a partner in a planned EarthRanger project.

name: Developing a Large Scale, Standardized Monitoring Program for Carnivores in Botswana
summary: Closed pilot study, described in April 2013, for a multi-year project seeking a sustainable landscape-scale carnivore monitoring method in Botswana, proposing a comparison of spoor and camera trap surveys.

name: Ecoexist Trust
summary: Organisation using five donated satellite collars, reported in January 2024, that send hourly GPS locations to identify, verify and monitor elephant movement corridors to inform land-use allocation.

name: Elephants for Africa
summary: Charity and Botswana NGO whose Boteti River camera trap network ran from 2014 to April 2017 and which says the data support species monitoring.

name: Elephants for Africa bull elephant collaring (Makgadikgadi)
summary: An active Elephants for Africa project that monitored 10 GPS-collared bull elephants in 2024, fitted with collars since 2022, with seven remaining in the study at year end.

name: Elephants Without Borders
summary: Organisation that says it has flown over 4,000 hours of aerial wildlife surveys since 2001 in four countries, including a 2018 northern Botswana census commissioned jointly with the wildlife department.

name: Kalahari Research and Conservation
summary: An NGO based in Hukuntsi, established by Glyn Maude in 2008 according to Akashinga, which Cheetah Conservation Botswana says organised an August 2023 Kgalagadi district lion survey with partners.

name: Kalahari San Master Tracker Programme
summary: Programme in Namibia and Botswana, run by CyberTracker, whose funding by the Frederick Mulder Foundation is acknowledged on CyberTracker’s supporters page.

name: Kalahari Wildlands Trust
summary: Registered in Botswana in 2016, this non-profit trust says it alone regularly monitors wildlife and patrols NG3, and analysed spoor data to estimate species densities in 2024.

name: Kavango Zambezi Transfrontier Conservation Area Secretariat
summary: Secretariat of the Kavango Zambezi conservation area that runs the KAZA elephant survey, an initiative with the five partner states, and was directed in 2023 to coordinate an elephant action plan.

name: KAZA Elephant Survey
summary: Closed aerial survey, flown August to October 2022 and run by the KAZA Secretariat, which estimated 227,900 elephants and, per the ministers' release, cost nearly USD 3.2 million.

name: Khama Rhino Sanctuary Trust
summary: Community-based wildlife project receiving P100,000 from Botswana Insurance Holdings Limited in December 2014 for rhino notching and genetic management; its chair then reported about 56 rhinos.

name: KPR Wildlife Monitoring
summary: Active monitoring project, partnered with Natural Selection Foundation, in which rangers use tablets to record sightings, patrols and incidents in real time and are trained in population monitoring.

name: Leopard Density Study (Khutse Game Reserve)
summary: Active Leopard Ecology and Conservation survey over more than 4,400 km2 in Khutse and the southern Central Kalahari, run in 2023 and 2025, using TrapTagger and African Carnivore Wildbook and feeding the National Leopard Survey.

name: Leopard Ecology & Conservation
summary: Established in 2000 to preserve Botswana's leopards and lions, this NGO surveyed Khutse and southern Central Kalahari in 2023 and 2025, using TrapTagger with staff checking uncertain identifications.

name: Management Oriented Monitoring System (MOMS), Botswana
summary: Community natural resource monitoring programme built by the Department of Wildlife and National Parks, described by its chief wildlife officer in 2016 as a paper-based tool at community level.

name: Ministry of Environment and Tourism (Botswana)
summary: Government ministry in Gaborone leading management and conservation of natural resources, whose minister said in November 2025 that Botswana was updating its National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan.

name: Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants in Botswana (Chobe National Park MIKE site)
summary: Elephant killing monitoring programme at Chobe National Park, reported in June 2025 as Botswana's only MIKE site, where DWNP trained 74 staff in 2025, raising trained personnel from 13 in 2022 to 87.

name: Okavango Research Institute
summary: University of Botswana institute studying the Okavango Delta, which publishes long-term monitoring datasets through GBIF and used random forest machine learning to predict riparian vegetation areas in an Esri user story.

name: ORBIS: Okavango Repository for Biodiversity Data Planning
summary: Project of the Okavango Research Institute for which the JRS Biodiversity Foundation lists a 2020 grant of $50,000 over six months.

name: Oriental Consultants Global
summary: Consultancy that says it led the team establishing Botswana’s nationwide forest monitoring system.

name: Project for Enhancing National Forest Monitoring System for the Promotion of Sustainable Natural Resource Management (Botswana)
summary: Closed 2013 to 2016 project, run by OC Global, that produced a nationwide forest map, a national inventory method, a GIS database and a national forest monitoring plan.

name: Raptors Botswana
summary: NGO described in a March 2018 interview as focused on vulture conservation in Botswana and southern Africa, which worked with the FitzPatrick Institute to quantify vulture population change over 30 years.

name: Scaling fisheries monitoring in the Okavango Delta with low-cost technology
summary: Project on fisheries monitoring in the Okavango Delta using low-cost technology, funded by the JRS Biodiversity Foundation, which lists a 2017 grant of $180,840 over 24 months.

name: Standardised Wildlife Monitoring Protocol
summary: Protocol launched with a website in Maun in July 2016 by SAREP, piloted around the Okavango Delta that year, with SAREP credited for training concession guides to apply it and record data.

name: University of Botswana
summary: Botswana's first institution of higher learning, established in 1982 and based in Gaborone, whose Okavango Research Institute, set up in 1994, was tasked with monitoring for the Okavango Delta Management Plan.

name: Vulture Monitoring (BirdLife Botswana)
summary: Active BirdLife Botswana programme in which volunteers monitor vultures, including their breeding sites and mortality.

name: Waterbird counts (BirdLife Botswana)
summary: Active BirdLife Botswana programme in which members record bird sightings; the organisation says counts at major water bodies have run twice yearly for nearly thirty years, with two ten-year reviews.

name: Wild Entrust
summary: Organisation that runs Botswana Predator Conservation, a programme monitoring predators through observations and camera-trap surveys, whose data and expertise Tech 4 Conservation says made African Carnivore Wildbook possible.

name: WildCAT Botswana Trust
summary: A trust managed by Dr Jess Isden, according to WildCRU, which says she founded and delivers the Coexistence Programme, established in 2017, whose Community Guardians patrol daily for predators.

name: Wildlife Assessment of Kalahari Ecosystems
summary: Conservation Force-supported project in Botswana's Kalahari regions that plans to test track-based monitoring with local !Xo San trackers and overlap aerial surveys with track transects to estimate visibility correction factors.

name: Wildlife Conservation Research Unit
summary: Research unit in the University of Oxford's Department of Biology, which says it co-developed the AI tool TrapTagger.

name: WildSights Botswana
summary: Dormant project that describes collecting thousands of tourist photographs a month with GPS routes in the Okavango Delta, received through Natural Selection Safaris, and using volunteer tags in models to estimate carnivore densities.

name: AI-Powered Bird Sound Recognition System for Monitoring Avian Biodiversity in Belarus
summary: A 2025 paper describes a deep-learning system for monitoring Belarusian birds by sound, with an annotated dataset of over 2,500 recordings of 116 species, a convolutional neural network and a public platform.

name: ARMOSOFT
summary: Company whose Forest Guardian system, according to Hi-Tech Park, combines machine vision, a server platform, software and a GIS for early fire detection; its main Belarusian clients are forestry bodies and reserves.

name: Belarusian Research Centre "Ecology"
summary: A research centre named in a 2005 ministry regulation (amended 2008) as home of the main information and analysis centre of Belarus's national environmental monitoring system, which collects, processes and stores monitoring information.

name: Belarusian State University
summary: A university with monitoring of three lakes documented since 1978 in a 2024 article and an affiliated abstract assessing overgrowth using Sentinel-2 imagery from 2019 and 2023.

name: Belgosles
summary: Ministry of Forestry enterprise in Minsk focused on forest management planning and national forest condition monitoring, with a remote sensing department that processes drone and satellite data.

name: Bellesozashchita
summary: A state institution that, according to Belgosles, organises forest pest and disease monitoring, done by continuous survey of the forest fund to find dying stands and outbreaks.

name: Belovezhskaya Pushcha National Park
summary: State nature protection institution in Brest region, part of the transboundary Bialowieza Forest World Heritage Site since 2014, whose 2016 to 2020 research plan included species monitoring and forest dynamics.

name: Berezinsky Biosphere Reserve
summary: State nature protection institution in Vitebsk region whose scientific department has 16 staff, 12 of them researchers, and includes a geographic information systems specialist.

name: Braslav Lakes National Park
summary: National park in north-west Belarus, created in 1995, that says it has a local network of 124 observation points for integrated ecosystem monitoring, 55 of them in forests.

name: Central Botanical Garden of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
summary: Minsk institute researching plant resources that publishes GBIF datasets on bat mist-netting, acoustic monitoring and winter hibernation surveys, with the latter covering 2018 to 2024.

name: Department of Geodesy and Aerospace Cartography, Belarusian State University
summary: University department whose lecturer was first author of a 2024 paper mapping a forest fire in the Lelchitsy District from Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 images using two largely automated geoprocessing models.

name: Forest Guardian
summary: Fire monitoring system using machine vision and GIS, reportedly providing full coverage of the Ministry of Forestry’s forest fund in 2024, with about 450 monitoring points by June.

name: Francisk Skorina Gomel State University
summary: Belarusian university that OpenAlex lists as the affiliation of the sole author of a 2022 remote sensing paper on climate change and ecosystem productivity in Belarusian Polesie.

name: G. G. Vinberg Naroch Biological Station, Belarusian State University
summary: A university station whose staff and hydroecology laboratory, according to a 2024 article, monitored three Naroch lakes year-round since 1978, recording hydrochemistry and plankton in an eight-table database.

name: GBIF Republic of Belarus
summary: Country node in GBIF's registry for Belarus, whose participation status is observer, linked as a partner of the Global Biodiversity Information Facility.

name: Geoinformation Systems, National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
summary: Enterprise named in a 2019 UN-GGIM workshop presentation as national operator of the Belarusian space remote sensing system, which lists forest fund monitoring among its tasks; current status unknown.

name: Gorodishche Bird Ringing Station
summary: A bird ringing station in Gorodok District, Vitebsk Region, where a 2026 paper reports 1,475 birds of 51 species caught and ringed in spring migration periods from 2018 to 2024.

name: Informational and Analytical Centre of Vegetation Monitoring
summary: Centre founded in 2000 within the institute that coordinates vegetation monitoring organisations and keeps data banks on vegetation and protected plant populations; it is run by the Institute of Experimental Botany.

name: Institute of Nature Management of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
summary: Minsk institute whose research lines include diagnosing the natural environment with aerospace tools, and which OpenAlex lists on a 2022 satellite mapping paper on the Yaselda river.

name: Ministry of Forestry of the Republic of Belarus
summary: A government ministry that Resolution 949 (as amended in 2024) names as the body carrying out forest monitoring within the national environmental monitoring system.

name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Protection of the Republic of Belarus
summary: Ministry that, according to a BelTA report on the National Legal Internet Portal, will coordinate government bodies and report annually on the national biodiversity plan.

name: Multilevel Belarusian Space System for Remote Sensing of the Earth
summary: A Belarusian satellite remote sensing system, reported to the UN in 2025 as created under the national space programme, with subsystems including monitoring of the land fund and the forest fund.

name: NASBSat-2
summary: A Belarusian satellite launched on 28 December 2025 with two infrared cameras and one optical camera, intended for early detection of thermal anomalies such as forest fires in Belarus.

name: National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
summary: A national academy that Resolution 949 (as amended in 2024) names as carrying out plant and wildlife monitoring, plus complex monitoring of protected-area ecosystems and peatlands, within the national environmental monitoring system.

name: National Environmental Monitoring System of the Republic of Belarus
summary: A national monitoring programme, led and run by the environment ministry, covering plants, forests, wildlife, protected-area ecosystems and peatlands, with the Academy of Sciences and Ministry of Forestry carrying out parts of it.

name: National Peatland Register of Belarus
summary: Planned digital register of Belarusian peatlands, which a 2021 UNDP blog says was aiming for completeness by 2025 with GEF funding, and which then held 420 Brest region peatlands totalling 627,405 ha.

name: Polesie State Radiation-Ecological Reserve
summary: A state nature-conservation research institution at Khoiniki whose radiation-ecological monitoring frames a 2025 paper on Cs-137 in river otters in the Belarusian Chernobyl exclusion zone, studied from 2016 to 2024.

name: Pripyatsky National Park
summary: A national park where, News Mail reports, a badger-monitoring camera trap recorded a European wildcat on 16 June 2025, with more cameras and scratching posts planned to collect genetic material.

name: Remote forest pathology monitoring system using drones and AI (Belarus)
summary: Drone and AI monitoring system for forest pathology, described in a BSTU repository paper that trained five U-Net based networks to segment early weakening of conifer stands, using over 15,000 images collected in 2021 to 2023.

name: Scientific and Practical Center of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus for Biological Resources
summary: Minsk state scientific and production association of the Academy of Sciences that publishes seven GBIF datasets and provides scientific support for the protected-area system and biodiversity assessment.

name: State Cadastre of the Animal World (Belarus)
summary: Electronic database of animals living in Belarus, run by the environment ministry, which a 2016 news item says is open apart from restricted information, with a change to its regulation put to public discussion in 2019.

name: State Cadastre of the Plant World (Belarus)
summary: Electronic database of plants living in Belarus, run by the environment ministry, which a 2016 news item says is open apart from state secrets and other restricted information.

name: Turov Bird Ringing Station
summary: A bird ringing station that, according to a paper by Scientific and Practical Center for Bioresources authors, began work in 1999 and in 2013 studied migration from April to September.

name: United Institute of Informatics Problems of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
summary: Minsk institute affiliated with a 2022 bark beetle forecasting paper using 250 m satellite indices, and covered by 2026 reporting on a bird song recognition app.

name: V.F. Kuprevich Institute of Experimental Botany of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
summary: Minsk institute that is the Academy's head organisation for the national environmental monitoring subprogramme for 2021 to 2025 and is listed on 2022 and 2025 remote sensing and vegetation mapping papers.

name: Yaselda Bird Ringing Station
summary: A bird ringing station in the Sporauski Nature Reserve, Brest Region, established in 2018, where more than 12,000 birds of 101 species were ringed in 2023, used to monitor migratory birds.

name: Acoustic Monitoring of Illegal Hunting in Tropical Forests of Belize
summary: Closed project, led by Evelyn Pina Covarrubias, that planned 40 AudioMoth detectors in Tapir Mountain Nature Reserve to detect gunshots and map illegal hunting; one logger was retrieved in 2021 after two years.

name: Advancing Marine Data Tools and Standards in Belize
summary: Active programme run by the University of Belize Environmental Research Institute, which in 2025 designed two R Shiny tools with TASA for its marine monitoring data and wrote two reef health chapters for the 2024 report card.

name: AI for the Belize National Marine Habitat Map
summary: Project run by the Coastal Zone Management Authority and Institute, funded by Microsoft, that updated the 1997 national marine habitat map using machine learning and satellite imagery, covering 20,538 square kilometres.

name: Belize Audubon Society
summary: Non-governmental organisation that, per ECOMAR, manages Blue Hole National Park and Half Moon Caye Natural Monument, where staff monitor coral bleaching, lobster, conch and seagrass, and held bird banding training in October 2024.

name: Belize Bird Conservancy
summary: Nonprofit, formerly the Belize Raptor Research Institute, that says it conserves birds across Belize through research, education and advocacy, and runs and built the Belize Hawk Watch begun in 2013.

name: Belize Bird Rescue
summary: Belize-registered non-profit organisation at Roaring Creek, Cayo District, whose field teams ran transect surveys in 2024 to repeat the 2016 yellow-headed parrot count, and which says it has returned 162 hand-reared chicks to the wild.

name: Belize Collect Earth/Open Foris Land Use and Land Use Change assessment
summary: Forest Department land use and land-use change assessment using Collect Earth virtual sampling, begun in 2018 with 21,993 plots selected in Google Earth Engine, covering 2000-2019 data with annual updates planned.

name: Belize Fire Monitoring System (National Forest Monitoring System)
summary: Fire monitoring system that a Forest Department speaker, reported in September 2025, described as giving almost real-time wildfire results nationwide and as part of the National Forest Monitoring System.

name: Belize Fisheries Department
summary: Government department that manages five marine reserves and monitors coral health, and in a September 2024 presentation set milestones of 25% of ocean space in Biodiversity Protection Zones by November 2024 and up to 30% by November 2026.

name: Belize Foundation for Research and Environmental Education
summary: Non-profit founded by its director Jacob Marlin, with a 1,153-acre reserve; its rangers use camera traps and record wildlife and weather, and its Agami heron nesting study is in its eighth year.

name: Belize Fund for a Sustainable Future
summary: Independent conservation trust fund managing money from the Blue Bonds project, according to The Nature Conservancy, which reports it gave USD 175,000 to the Sarteneja Alliance for wildlife monitoring and sanctuary management.

name: Belize Hawk Watch
summary: Described by operator Belize Bird Conservancy as Belize's first and only raptor migration monitoring programme, where Nearctic-Neotropical migrants comprised 37% of migratory raptors counted in 2013–2023.

name: Belize Jaguar Program
summary: Active national programme on human-wildlife conflict, led by the Forest Department with the Corozal Sustainable Future Initiative, which collared several jaguars for real-time tracking.

name: Belize Karst Habitat Conservation
summary: Community-based conservation organisation in San Ignacio that launched a research programme in early 2023 to monitor Tapir Mountain Nature Reserve, with 22 bird point count stations surveyed monthly from June 2023.

name: Belize Maya Forest Trust
summary: Organisation that Planet names as one of three bodies in a collaborative initiative monitoring land use change in Belize's Maya Forest Mosaic.

name: Belize National Forest Monitoring System
summary: Forest monitoring system built by the Forest Department, whose Geospatial Monitoring Unit lists its development among its activities, following land use data that also led to Belize's first Forest Reference Level.

name: Belize National Mangrove Cover Map 2020-2024
summary: National mangrove cover map for 2020 to 2024, presented in September 2025 as part of the National Forest Monitoring System, with a university partner reportedly looking at using AI on satellite imagery.

name: Belize Roadkill Project
summary: Citizen science project on iNaturalist, built and run by the University of Belize Environmental Research Institute and launched in March 2025, which aims to map roadkill hotspots and the species most at risk.

name: Belize Zoo and Tropical Education Center
summary: Nonprofit led by Celso Poot that, according to Mongabay in May 2025, paired camera traps with acoustic receivers to study traffic and noise effects on wildlife along the George Price Highway.

name: Biodiversity Data Mobilization and Integration for Policy and Research
summary: Active project led by the University of Belize Environmental Research Institute that plans to digitise, validate and publish Belizean biodiversity datasets on GBIF, working with the National Biodiversity Office on policy use.

name: Biodiversity Monitoring and Assessment for Priority Species in the Maya Mountain Massif
summary: Project that aims to co-develop standardised monitoring protocols for birds, mammals and forest trees with protected area managers, and plans baseline surveys in under-monitored forest reserves.

name: Bird Monitoring Overwinter Survival (MOSI) Program
summary: Bird monitoring programme built by the University of Belize Environmental Research Institute in 2016 using the MoSI protocol, aiming to build a standardised database with at least five years of data per site.

name: Climate Crossroads: Futures for People & Nature in Central Belize
summary: Active project led by the University of Belize Environmental Research Institute and funded by the Swiss Re Foundation, using the InVEST tool to model climate and land-use effects on ecosystem services, with 21 communities.

name: Coastal Zone Management Authority and Institute
summary: Autonomous public statutory body for coastal zone policy in Belize, which maintains national coral reef and water quality monitoring and ran supervised classifications on Sentinel-2 data for its marine habitat map.

name: Connecting Protected Area Monitoring to National Biodiversity Reporting in Belize
summary: Active project run by the University of Belize Environmental Research Institute and funded by Biodiversity Information for Development, intended to feed protected-area records of under-represented taxa into national monitoring and CBD reporting.

name: Coral reef benthic and fish monitoring data from Turneffe Atoll, Belize, 2010-2023
summary: Dataset built by the University of Belize Environmental Research Institute and published on Dryad in 2024, holding benthic, invertebrate, coral and reef fish observations from Turneffe Atoll between 2010 and 2023.

name: Coral reef benthic and fish monitoring data from Turneffe Atoll, Belize, 2010-2025
summary: Coral reef benthic and fish monitoring dataset from Turneffe Atoll Marine Reserve, 2010-2025, collected with MBRS-SMP and AGRRA protocols, run by UB-ERI and published on Dryad in 2025.

name: Corozal Sustainable Future Initiative
summary: Belizean not-for-profit, renamed from Shipstern Nature Reserve (Belize) Ltd, that manages Shipstern Nature Reserve and the North-eastern Biological Corridor under government co-management agreements.

name: Crocodile Research Coalition
summary: Belize-based nonprofit established in January 2016 working on crocodiles across Central America and the Caribbean, which led a Morelet's crocodile population study in Chiquibul Forest from 2016.

name: Ecological Insights into the Central American Red Brocket and Yucatan Brown Brocket Deer Using Camera Trap-Based Occupancy Modeling for Conservation
summary: Active project that plans to use ten years of camera trap data from protected forests in northern Belize to model where two brocket deer species occur and to map them.

name: Enhancing jaguar corridors and strongholds through improved management and threat reduction (Belize)
summary: Forest Department project run in partnership with UNDP that, in November 2021, was expanding camera trapping of jaguars and prey and letting landowners contribute to the national camera trap network as citizen scientists.

name: Environmental Conservation Organization (ECOMAR)
summary: Marine-focused non-governmental organisation in Belize that says it launched the Coral Watch Program in 2008, was secretary of the coral reef monitoring network until 2012, and monitors for coral bleaching with members.

name: Forest Department of Belize
summary: Government body managing five categories of protected areas in Belize, whose Geospatial Monitoring Unit analyses land use change and uses fire hotspot platforms and drones for fire and beetle monitoring.

name: FORMNET-B database
summary: Network of permanent forest plots named as Belize's National Forest Inventory in its April 2026 REDD+ annex, which refers to updating its emission factor database from the permanent sample plots.

name: Friends for Conservation and Development
summary: Non-governmental organisation registered in 2005 that monitors the Chiquibul Forest, including scarlet macaws and camera traps whose data goes to Panthera, and uses the SMART tool.

name: Hol Chan Marine Reserve
summary: Marine reserve whose team was monitoring Ambergris Caye's northern beaches weekly for turtle nests in April 2024, with a season due to run to November 2024; by August 2023 it had found 67 nests.

name: Long-Term Atoll Monitoring Program (Glover's Reef)
summary: Programme run by the Wildlife Conservation Society that began applying the LAMP protocol at Glover's Reef in 2004 with 33 sites, rose to 50 sites in 2010, and was revised in 2015 as LAMP II.

name: Mangrove Research Initiative
summary: Initiative that sets out to quantify mangrove biomass and health, assess biodiversity with eDNA and map bird rookeries, saying this will inform conservation and monitoring of Belize's offshore mangroves.

name: MarAlliance Lighthouse Reef Atoll marine megafauna monitoring
summary: Marine megafauna monitoring run by MarAlliance, which says it has researched Lighthouse Reef Atoll every year since 2007, using longline, baited video and snorkel census to analyse long-term trends in sharks, rays, turtles and finfish.

name: MarAlliance Shark Ray Alley monitoring study
summary: Long-term monitoring study run by MarAlliance, focused on the Shark Ray Alley aggregation through weekly video and photo surveys of individual nurse sharks and rays; MarAlliance says it has studied Hol Chan nurse sharks since 2014.

name: Maya Forest Corridor REDD Project
summary: REDD project run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, with the Maya Forest Corridor Trust as proponent, whose team surveyed 17 camera traps from January to March 2024, yielding 943 trap nights and 3,447 photographs.

name: Ministry of Sustainable Development, Climate Change and Solid Waste Management
summary: Government ministry under which, according to a government press release reprinted by the San Pedro Sun, the National Biodiversity Office sits.

name: Monitoring Mammal Communities Across a Forest-to-Farm Landscape
summary: Camera trap initiative run by UB-ERI and Panthera with Silk Grass Farms, aiming to build a photo-based inventory of individual jaguars, to be identified by coat pattern.

name: National Biodiversity Monitoring Programme (Belize)
summary: Belize government monitoring programme that an IUCN invitation says needs updating into a coherent structure with feasible indicators, roles, data flows and protocol outlines, mentioning coral reefs, mangroves and seagrass.

name: National Biodiversity Office
summary: Office under its parent ministry, established in 2020 according to a government press release; the San Pedro Sun reports it has begun updating protected-area policy and planning.

name: National Coral Reef Monitoring Network (Belize)
summary: Network of marine managers across Belize, reformed in 2008 over a bleaching forecast, that ran coral bleaching surveys from September 2023 to March 2024 using a transect method adapted from AGRRA.

name: National Wildlife Database Platform (Belize)
summary: Wildlife database platform built by the Forest Department, reported in December 2024 as launched with data-sharing agreements on International Jaguar Day and as integrating real-time monitoring data.

name: Programme for Belize
summary: Private Belizean non-profit, established in 1988, that manages the Rio Bravo Conservation and Management Area; in 2022 its rangers monitored 47 parrot nests and were trained in SMART and PAWS.

name: Project Centinela Maya Forest Mosaic site, Belize
summary: Site where, Planet says, a collaboration of three partners monitors land use change in the Maya Forest Mosaic and will use Planet data to strengthen the National Forest Monitoring System.

name: Sarstoon Temash Institute for Indigenous Management
summary: Indigenous NGO whose five founding communities' land was included in Sarstoon Temash National Park; organised forest patrols, trained Maya communities in GIS mapping and became WRI's partner in 2016.

name: Sarteneja Alliance for Conservation and Development
summary: Organisation in Sarteneja researching Corozal Bay Wildlife Sanctuary and Bacalar Chico National Park, monitoring bay water quality, colonial nesting birds and manatees through aerial and drone surveys.

name: SMART in Belize's protected areas
summary: Monitoring system that, according to York University's Dahdaleh Institute, Belize adopted in 2018 as the official system for monitoring its protected area network.

name: Southern Environmental Association
summary: Non-governmental organisation that monitors turtle nesting and coral bleaching and, its about page says, co-managed Gladden Spit and Silk Cayes Marine Reserve and Laughing Bird Caye National Park.

name: Strengthening Coral Reef Resilience at Turneffe Atoll
summary: Project aiming to set a reef health baseline by joining UB-ERI's 10-year monitoring dataset with new reserve surveys, alongside restoration work including treatment of Stony Coral Tissue Loss Disease.

name: Strengthening Seagrass Stewardship in Belize through Scientific Evidence, Capacity Building and Community Engagement
summary: UB-ERI-led project funded by the Canada Fund for Local Initiatives, from September 2026 to February 2027, planning three seagrass monitoring sites, a condition baseline and practitioner training.

name: Toledo Institute for Development and Environment
summary: Organisation in Punta Gorda Town that monitors water quality monthly at 43 sites in the Maya Mountain Marine Corridor and lists coral reef, manatee, mangrove and seagrass monitoring.

name: Turneffe Atoll Sustainability Association
summary: Non-profit established in 2013 and co-manager of Turneffe Atoll Marine Reserve, which runs spawning surveys, coral bleaching assessments and, with UB-ERI, two-yearly AGRRA reef health assessments.

name: Turneffe Reef-Monitoring Data Dashboard
summary: Interactive public platform for TASA's monitoring data, including Fisher Catch and long-term atoll datasets, built in R by TASA and UB-ERI.

name: University of Belize
summary: University whose Environmental Research Institute was inaugurated in January 2010 to address a gap in local capacity for research and monitoring.

name: University of Belize Environmental Research Institute
summary: Research institute, run by the University of Belize and founded in 2010, and the only Belizean organisation registered as a GBIF data publisher, with about 30,000 observations published.

name: Ya'axché annual Land Use/Land Cover Change assessment
summary: Annual land cover change assessment run by Ya'axché Conservation Trust, whose 2025 report classified Sentinel-2 imagery in Google Earth Engine using a supervised Random Trees classifier.

name: Ya'axché Conservation Trust
summary: Organisation in Punta Gorda whose research team collects data on large mammals, birds, bees and trees across the Maya Golden Landscape, and has used camera traps on cacao farms since 2016.

name: Ya'axché wildlife camera trapping in BCEP, BNR and MMNFR
summary: Wildlife camera trapping programme in three protected areas, built and run by Ya'axché Conservation Trust, with a 2024 information brief and monitoring at Boden Creek Ecological Preserve starting in 2024.

name: A.U.G. Signals
summary: Company selected for Canadian Space Agency funding for an AI-powered, satellite-based prototype to detect algal blooms and assess water quality.

name: A/Vian Eco
summary: Wildlife consulting firm using technology-enhanced methods, which rents autonomous recording units, offers bioacoustics courses, and announced in March 2024 a move into AI and machine learning recognizers.

name: AAFC Land Use
summary: Time series that consolidates spatial datasets into a 30 m pixel history of what happened on the land in Canada.

name: Accelerating Wildfire Hazard Mapping Across Canada with AI
summary: Mila and Natural Resources Canada project that built an AI surrogate model emulating the BurnP3+ wildfire simulator, for mapping wildfire hazard regionally and nationally.

name: Adopt-A-Pond Wetland Conservation Program
summary: Toronto Zoo programme begun in 1991, with FrogWatch Ontario, Ontario Turtle Tally and research projects conserving Ontario reptiles and amphibians.

name: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada
summary: Federal department that, with Canadensys and the Canadian Museum of Nature, offers a shared site for sharing occurrence data in Canada, and carries out Earth observation work on land.

name: AI for Forest Linear Disturbance Detection in Forested Denesųłiné Traditional Territories
summary: Hatfield and Ya'thi Néné Lands and Resources are developing an AI method to map linear forest disturbances from satellite data, to monitor woodland caribou habitat in Northern Saskatchewan.

name: Air Sea Ocean Monitoring System
summary: $3.8 million project combining robotic ocean and aerial platforms with AI-enabled sensing, for monitoring such as marine protected areas and also for surveillance.

name: Albert Creek Bird Observatory
summary: Migration monitoring station run by the Southeast Yukon Proper Land Use Society, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Alberta Biodiversity Monitoring Institute
summary: Tracks changes in wildlife and their habitats across Alberta and publishes open data. With the University of Alberta and partners it built WildTrax, and it is investing in machine learning for auto-recognition.

name: Alberta Conservation Association
summary: Alberta conservation body whose 2022/23 annual report records fish surveys on 58 rivers and creeks and 40 lakes and ponds.

name: Alberta Environment and Parks
summary: Provincial ministry responsible for managing all wildlife in Alberta.

name: AltaML
summary: Applied AI company. It worked with Hatfield on the smartWhales detection system and is project lead on GenWhales, which uses generative AI to make synthetic satellite images of right whales.

name: Apoqnmatulti’k
summary: NSERC-funded partnership pairing Mi’kmaw, local and western knowledge to understand valued aquatic species in the Bay of Fundy and Bras d’Or Lake.

name: Archipelago Management Board
summary: Co-management board of the Haida Nation and the Government of Canada that manages Gwaii Haanas, an area of 5,000 km2 of land and sea.

name: Arctic BIOSCAN
summary: Project developing a DNA-based biosurveillance system for the Canadian Arctic with community partners and local field technicians.

name: Arctic Eider Society
summary: Created SIKU with northern communities. With Canadian Space Agency support and University of Waterloo researchers, it used machine learning to detect recurring polynyas for the SIKU ice map.

name: Arctus
summary: Company selected for Canadian Space Agency funding to map coastal ecosystems from satellites in Eeyou Istchee, and contracted on aquatic monitoring and right whale prediction.

name: Ashored
summary: Canadian-owned company addressing whale entanglement in fixed-gear fishing, named as lead of the ROC Fishing System Project, which planned gear coiling fishing line on the seafloor.

name: Assiniboine Park Conservancy
summary: Winnipeg park and zoo body whose zoo researchers created the Beluga Bits citizen science project and used neural networks to filter beluga imagery.

name: Association de conservation du Mont Écho
summary: Conservation group whose members seek to protect natural areas through easements negotiated with private owners, followed by conservation and management plans.

name: Atlantic Bird Observatory
summary: Acadia University-affiliated observatory that has operated regularly on Bon Portage and Seal Islands since 1995, listed as a Canadian Migration Monitoring Network station.

name: Atlantic Canada Opportunities Agency
summary: Federal agency that NB Tech News reports is contributing $714,000 to the first phase of Mother Earth Watcher.

name: Awtij, Indigenous Marine Intelligence
summary: Indigenous-owned business based in Lennox Island First Nation, PEI, that equips working boats with AI-enabled sensor packages.

name: BatCaver
summary: Wildlife Conservation Society Canada programme asking cavers to install acoustic loggers to monitor bat use of caves.

name: BC Hydrophone Network
summary: Hydrophone network built by the North Coast Cetacean Society; by 2025 it had 15 partners and 23 hydrophones on the BC coast, feeding a whale and noise map and dashboard.

name: BC Parks
summary: Provincial body that says it protects the natural environment and cultural values of British Columbia's outdoor areas, and runs a Long-Term Ecological Monitoring Program across protected areas.

name: BC Parks Foundation
summary: Foundation that reported in November 2024 that over 1,800 hectares of critical habitat in northern British Columbia had been protected through its support community's collective effort.

name: BC Parks Long-Term Ecological Monitoring Program
summary: Programme run by BC Parks that aims to monitor ecological change from the marine and intertidal biome to the alpine, with data meant as a resource for land managers.

name: BC Species and Ecosystems Explorer
summary: British Columbia government tool from the Conservation Data Centre that gives information on over 24,000 plants, animals and ecological communities.

name: Beaverhill Bird Observatory
summary: Bird observatory whose station operates from May to October in the Beaverhill Lake Natural Area, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Beluga Bits
summary: Citizen science project on Zooniverse, created and managed by Assiniboine Park Zoo researchers, that classifies images of beluga whales.

name: Binnov
summary: Ocean Idea Challenge participant developing a real-time drone and AI-based solution to detect marine mammals, winter ice and coastal erosion.

name: Bioacoustic Unit
summary: Collaboration between the Bayne Lab at the University of Alberta and ABMI that applies wildlife acoustic data to environmental management and research.

name: Biodiversity Pathways
summary: Non-profit and national affiliate of the Alberta Biodiversity Monitoring Institute that develops monitoring programmes beyond Alberta. The Boreal Avian Modelling Centre has been one of its initiatives since April 2025.

name: BIOSCAN-Canada
summary: Centre for Biodiversity Genomics project that aims to complete a DNA barcode registry of all multicellular life in Canada and track how species respond to environmental change.

name: BioSpace
summary: A joint project of the Canadian Forest Service and the Canadian Space Agency that uses satellite data to collect biodiversity data and track its changes nationally.

name: BIOS² training programme
summary: Computational Biodiversity Science and Services, a training programme funded by NSERC for students and postdoctoral fellows, a joint initiative of Canadian universities.

name: BiotaNB
summary: Survey led and run by the New Brunswick Museum, scheduled in a June 2025 announcement for Black River Protected Natural Area, 25 June to 8 July, with over 60 participants expected.

name: Birds Canada
summary: Canadian bird conservation charity. It develops and maintains the NatureCounts data platform, runs the Motus Wildlife Tracking System, and deploys autonomous recording units with partners across Canada.

name: Boreal Avian Modelling Centre
summary: A project on boreal birds, run for over 20 years through the University of Alberta and Université Laval, that became an initiative of Biodiversity Pathways on 1 April 2025. Its database compiles bird data used in other analyses.

name: Bowen Island Conservancy
summary: Conservancy that owns and manages an 85 ha Nature Refuge on Bowen Island's southwest shore and 2 ha of conservation land elsewhere on the island.

name: Brier Island Bird Migration Research Station
summary: Fall migration monitoring station with more than 20 years of monitoring at the site, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: British Columbia Conservation Data Centre
summary: British Columbia government centre behind the BC Species and Ecosystems Explorer, which covers over 24,000 plants, animals and ecological communities.

name: Bruce Trail Conservancy
summary: Conservancy that adds protected natural areas along the Niagara Escarpment each year and cares for them through a land stewardship programme.

name: C-CORE
summary: Innovation hub in St. John's that supplied the calibration transponder for the European Space Agency's Biomass mission and collaborated on the first national wetland map.

name: Calgary Bird Banding Society
summary: Society associated with migration monitoring at Inglewood Bird Sanctuary since 1992, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Canada Centre for Mapping and Earth Observation
summary: Unit of Natural Resources Canada and Canada's national mapping and Earth observation centre. It produces national land cover maps from satellite imagery.

name: Canada Foundation for Innovation
summary: Funder of research facilities and equipment at Canadian universities, colleges, research hospitals and non-profit research institutions, including the Ocean Tracking Network and Ocean Networks Canada.

name: Canada Landsat Disturbance
summary: A Canada-wide 30-metre record of areas affected by fire or harvest from 1984 to 2015, made from Landsat mosaics.

name: Canada's Ocean Supercluster
summary: National ocean cluster that invests in ocean technology projects, including nine AI projects in a $20 million round and the $4.8 million Species Aware project.

name: Canadensys
summary: A Canada-wide effort, operated from the Université de Montréal Biodiversity Centre, that publishes specimen and other biodiversity data from Canadian collections.

name: Canadian Airborne Biodiversity Observatory
summary: Cross-scale initiative of Canadian biodiversity and remote sensing researchers building a spectral database to forecast ecosystem responses to environmental change.

name: Canadian Biodiversity Information Facility
summary: A Canadian programme in support of the Global Biodiversity Information Facility, decommissioned in 2021 along with its website and species resources.

name: Canadian Biodiversity Observation Network
summary: A proposed Canada-wide network connecting universities, museums, governments, industries, NGOs, community groups and Indigenous organisations to support sustained biodiversity monitoring.

name: Canadian BioGenome Project
summary: Canadian branch of the Earth BioGenome Project, which aims to produce high-quality reference genomes for all Canadian species and share them openly.

name: Canadian Forest Service
summary: Part of Natural Resources Canada. It publishes national forest datasets made with remote sensing and machine learning, and works with the Canadian Space Agency on forest mapping.

name: Canadian Institute of Ecology and Evolution
summary: Institute whose working group proposed the Canadian Biodiversity Observation Network.

name: Canadian Integrated Ocean Observing System
summary: National online platform for sharing, discovering and accessing ocean data in Canada, made up of three regional associations: CIOOS Pacific, the St. Lawrence Global Observatory and CIOOS Atlantic.

name: Canadian Migration Monitoring Network
summary: Partnership of bird observatories, Birds Canada and Environment and Climate Change Canada collecting long-term data on over 200 bird species, with Birds Canada calculating migration count trends every two years.

name: Canadian Museum of Nature
summary: National museum that joined Canadensys and Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada to offer a shared site for occurrence data in Canada.

name: Canadian National Parks Malaise Program
summary: Past collaboration between the Centre for Biodiversity Genomics and Parks Canada that trapped arthropods in 43 national parks and identified them by DNA barcoding.

name: Canadian Protected and Conserved Areas Database
summary: Authoritative national source of spatial and attribute data on marine and terrestrial protected and conserved areas, managed by Environment and Climate Change Canada.

name: Canadian Space Agency
summary: Canada's national space agency. Its smartEarth initiative funds satellite data applications, including 20 biodiversity projects chosen in 2025, and it leads the smartWhales programme.

name: Canadian Wetland Inventory
summary: A database built in 2002 by Ducks Unlimited Canada with Environment Canada, the Canadian Space Agency and the North American Wetlands Conservation Council, supported by more than 150 conservation partners.

name: Canadian Wetland Inventory Map
summary: National 10-metre wetland map of Canada made from multi-source satellite imagery with a random forest classification on Google Earth Engine. Version 3A is the third generation.

name: Canadian Wildlife Federation
