summary: National charity that launched the iNaturalist Canada app with ROM Biodiversity in 2015. Its Sean Brillant is a collaborator on the smartWhales detection paper.

name: Canadian Wildlife Service ARU and point count survey locations
summary: A national map layer of Canadian Wildlife Service autonomous recording unit and point count survey locations, 1993 to 2025. The Service deploys the recorders to monitor migratory birds and other wildlife.

name: CarbonRun
summary: Nova Scotia company headquartered in Dartmouth that says it adds crushed limestone to polluted rivers to reduce acidity, and announced the opening of its West River Pictou project.

name: Carleton University
summary: University whose Sprott School of Business is listed as an affiliation of Diane A. Isabelle, first author of a 2022 review of AI opportunities in conservation.

name: Carte dendrométrique lidar
summary: An open vector product for Quebec that gives forest stand characteristics from lidar data at a finer scale than the ecoforest map, under a CC-BY 4.0 licence.

name: Cartographier pour préserver : l’IA au service des milieux humides du Québec
summary: Mitacs Accelerate project aiming to use deep learning and other AI to improve wetland identification and mapping in Quebec, supervised at Université Laval, with Ducks Unlimited Canada as a partner.

name: Census of Environment
summary: Statistics Canada programme that builds ecosystem accounts covering the extent, condition and services of Canada's ecosystems, with a national register of ecosystems at its base.

name: Central Coast Indigenous Resource Alliance
summary: Alliance created by four Nations to build on their work developing and implementing Nation-level marine use plans for their territories, and it supports their management.

name: Central Okanagan Land Trust
summary: Land trust that stewards the land it holds in trust for the conservation of natural ecosystems in the Central Okanagan.

name: Centre de données sur le patrimoine naturel du Québec
summary: Quebec's biodiversity information system for species at risk, created in 1988 and led by a multidisciplinary working group. It holds more than 14,600 plant and animal occurrences.

name: Centre de géomatique du Québec
summary: Quebec centre whose AI and computer vision project list includes detection of invasive exotic plants and assessment of forest cuts.

name: Centre de recherche en données et intelligence géospatiale
summary: Research centre whose team under Professor Mostafavi partners with Ducks Unlimited Canada on AI mapping of Quebec wetlands, in a Mitacs project.

name: CERFO
summary: Quebec forestry research centre working with the Quebec environment ministry and Université de Sherbrooke on monitoring great blue herons with drones and AI.

name: Clayoquot Biosphere Trust
summary: Trust that stewards the intent of the UNESCO biosphere designation of Clayoquot Sound and manages the endowment supporting education, sustainability research and grants in the region.

name: Coastal Carbon
summary: Company training earth observation AI on satellite data. It curated the SeeFar dataset for geospatial foundation models.

name: Coastal First Nations
summary: Coastal organisation with a Regional Monitoring System, used in the Indigenous Guardians Toolkit as a case on monitoring and data management.

name: CoastConnect
summary: Hakai Institute platform giving First Nations, regulators, communities and scientific organisations free data, tools and methods for coastal monitoring in British Columbia.

name: Comox Valley Land Trust
summary: Land trust that works to protect and conserve ecologically significant land and wildlife habitat in the Comox Valley region.

name: Complex System Inc.
summary: AI company in Alberta. The Canadian Space Agency funded its work on 3D maps and change detection from single satellite images.

name: Conservation des vallons de la Serpentine
summary: Conservation group working to protect in perpetuity the natural areas of the Serpentine stream valleys in Bolton-Est, Eastman and Austin, and helping owners explore conservation options.

name: Conservation Halton
summary: Conservation authority that owns about 10,000 acres of conservation lands in over 500 parcels, including eight conservation parks.

name: Corridor appalachien
summary: Organisation that protects natural areas on private land and reported reaching nearly 19,000 hectares protected in perpetuity in 2025.

name: Council of the Haida Nation
summary: Governing body whose constitution gives it a mandate over Haida Gwaii and surrounding waters, and requires it to regulate access to resources by citizens and other users.

name: Cree Nation Government
summary: Government that, with the Quebec government in May 2021, marked the official designation of 23 territory reserves for protected-area purposes in Eeyou Istchee Baie-James, within the Grande Alliance.

name: Dalhousie University
summary: Canadian university that is the host institution for the Ocean Tracking Network, leads the Ocean Frontier Institute, and houses DeepSense in its Faculty of Computer Science.

name: DataStream
summary: Open-access online platform for sharing water quality data in Canada, with regional hubs for the Mackenzie Basin, the Atlantic provinces, Lake Winnipeg, the Great Lakes and the Pacific.

name: DataStream Initiative
summary: Registered Canadian charity that advances freshwater protection through open data flows and delivers the DataStream hubs. It received charitable status in 2020.

name: De CAF-RRT
summary: Project aiming to develop a wide-area satellite Earth observation tool to support salmon habitat monitoring, funded by SmartEarth.

name: DeepSense
summary: Applied AI research platform housed in the Faculty of Computer Science at Dalhousie University, whose projects with partners include benthic species detection and zebra mussel detection.

name: Dehcho First Nations
summary: First Nations body that passed a Dene law in 2018 to protect 14,249 square kilometres of boreal forest, with the joint Edéhzhíe protected area described as to be co-managed with the Canadian Wildlife Service.

name: Delta Marsh Bird Observatory
summary: Observatory that has monitored fall migration since 1992 and spring and fall since 1995, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Developing Tools to Track Vocalizing Marine Mammals with Long Baseline Hydrophone Arrays
summary: Project aiming to develop automated marine mammal tracking from long-baseline hydrophone data, planned for Squally Channel, with WWF-Canada, Gitga'at First Nation and North Coast Cetacean Society as partners.

name: DIGITAL
summary: Organisation that co-invests in technology projects, including Koonkie's mine restoration monitoring platform and SmartICE sea-ice training.

name: Digital Research Alliance of Canada
summary: Gave Simon Fraser University researchers nearly $1 million in special funding for the HALLO whale forecasting project.

name: Dinnage Lab
summary: University of Alberta lab developing foundation models for biological systems, including NicheFlow.

name: Ducks Unlimited Canada
summary: Non-profit conservation organisation that uses machine learning, satellite data and lidar to map and classify wetlands. In a project supported by RBC Tech for Nature it is mapping about 30,000 square kilometres in Alberta.

name: Earth Sense
summary: Canadian-incorporated satellite monitoring service for land, forests and wildfire, including deforestation detection. The page links it to Agtelligence.

name: Ecopia AI
summary: Toronto company that uses AI to extract vector data from imagery. Its 3D land cover data for 40 Canadian cities includes tree canopy, shrubs, grass, forests and water bodies, made under a contract with the Government of Canada.

name: Elk Valley Regional Land Trust
summary: Land trust formed in 2019 to conserve privately owned lands throughout the Elk Valley.

name: Enoch Cree Nation
summary: First Nation that co-manages Big Island Provincial Park, sharing management through a tri-government partnership.

name: Environment and Climate Change Canada
summary: Federal department that published Canada's 2030 Nature Strategy, its plan for implementing the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. It is named as author of the Canadian Wildlife Service's national layer of acoustic and point count survey locations.

name: Environment and Climate Change, Government of the Northwest Territories
summary: A Northwest Territories government department that invests with partners in grids of remote cameras and sound recorders for biodiversity data, currently within protected areas, and runs the territory's monitoring programme.

name: EO & Indigenous knowledge for bird and community climate resilience
summary: Project aiming to map climate strongholds for migratory birds and assess Hudson Bay Lowlands breeding strongholds using satellite data and Indigenous knowledge, funded by SmartEarth.

name: eOceans
summary: Canadian company founded in 2012, offering a platform for managing ocean monitoring projects and data.

name: Equlantic Aquatic Monitoring
summary: Developer of an autonomous water quality monitoring platform and of an autonomous sensor for carbonate variables. An alumnus of the Ocean Startup Project.

name: Escarpment Biosphere Conservancy
summary: Conservancy established to develop and manage a system of nature reserves in the Niagara Escarpment, Manitoulin, Bruce Peninsula and Saugeen River area, which it owns and manages.

name: Fiducie de conservation Massawippi
summary: Conservation trust working for the perpetual conservation of lands adjacent to Lake Massawippi and its tributaries, and it acquires properties.

name: Fiducie foncière de la vallée Ruiter
summary: Land trust that has established a conservation area of more than 900 acres in the Ruiter Valley and Potton township, which it seeks to expand through acquisition and easements.

name: Fiducie foncière du marais Alderbrooke
summary: Land trust dedicated to protecting the wetlands of the Sutton and Missisquoi river watersheds.

name: Fiducie foncière du mont Pinacle
summary: Land trust that has protected 375.4 hectares (928 acres) in perpetuity around Mont Pinacle by acquiring land and negotiating conservation agreements, and it owns land there.

name: FinShield
summary: Ocean Idea Challenge participant building real-time AI detection of shark finning, using machine learning to flag the behaviour.

name: Fisheries and Oceans Canada
summary: Federal department that monitors marine species. It supplied audio and labels for a machine learning model that detects orcas and gave financial support to the smartWhales detection project.

name: Fisheries and Wildlife Management Information System
summary: Alberta's central repository for fish and wildlife inventory data.

name: Flash Forest
summary: Toronto-based company that uses drones, AI, GIS and plant science to automate reforestation after wildfires.

name: Fluvial Systems Research
summary: Company funded by the Canadian Space Agency on right whale detection from satellite radar and optical imagery, and on Arctic marine mammal monitoring.

name: FluxAtlas
summary: Geospatial monitoring platform for measuring, tracking and forecasting coastal and river erosion. An alumnus of the Ocean Startup Challenge.

name: Foothills Land Trust
summary: Land trust that protects ecologically significant private land in Foothills County, south-west of Calgary.

name: Forest BIOmass measurement from 3D terrestrial LiDAR SCANning
summary: Software from a Laval University team that processes terrestrial laser scans into 3D point clouds to estimate above-ground forest biomass. A final award recipient of the Nature x Carbon Tech Challenge.

name: Forest Resources Inventory (Ontario)
summary: A large-scale survey of Ontario's forests and wetlands, now combining lidar, aerial imagery and field data to generate predictive models of forest attributes.

name: FortisBC
summary: Canadian energy utility that, according to Hack The Planet, sponsors biodiversity monitoring in its operating areas.

name: Fraser Valley Conservancy
summary: Land trust that describes itself as the only locally-based one conserving habitat and protecting wildlife across the Fraser Valley, and it acquires and manages conservation properties.

name: Gabriola Land and Trails Trust
summary: Organisation that protects and restores natural ecosystems on Gabriola and nearby islands.

name: Galiano Conservancy Association
summary: Land trust formed in 1989 for community-based land and habitat acquisition, management and conservation on Galiano Island, which owns and manages land and works in ecological restoration.

name: Generation Water Tech Challenge
summary: WWF-Canada challenge for freshwater technology, which granted $75,000 in total to award recipients and gave each a place in a Climate Ventures accelerator programme.

name: Genome British Columbia
summary: Provincial genomics organisation that lists the iTrackDNA environmental DNA project among its projects.

name: Genome Canada
summary: Canadian genomics funder. Its 2026 natural resources initiative will invest $19 million in driver projects, which may improve biodiversity monitoring.

name: GenWhales
summary: Project led by AltaML with Hatfield that uses generative AI to make synthetic satellite images of North Atlantic right whales, to improve detection in the smartWhales system. It has Canadian Space Agency funding under smartEarth.

name: Georgian Bay Land Trust
summary: Organisation that protects and conserves environmentally significant conservation properties on Georgian Bay.

name: Gitanyow Fisheries Authority
summary: First Nation fisheries body that works on computer vision counting of salmon on the Kitwanga River with the Pacific Salmon Foundation and partners.

name: Global Water Futures Observatories
summary: October 2022 reporting announced continued stations and data management as GWFO, citing the parent programme’s 76 sites, 27 deployable systems and University of Saskatchewan leadership.

name: Grand River Conservation Authority
summary: Conservation authority that owns about 19,900 hectares in 430 parcels in the Grand River watershed.

name: GreenLend
summary: Service for Indigenous and smallholder farmers in British Columbia whose AI reads satellite data to calculate carbon sequestration and generate a Verra document. The page offers a waitlist.

name: Gros Morne National Park Migration Monitoring Station
summary: Migration monitoring station in a spruce and tamarack bog, run by Parks Canada and listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: H2O Geomatics
summary: Research spin-off from the University of Waterloo, at a Waterloo address, that turns Earth observation data into products with physically based and machine learning methods. It was selected to build a dashboard tracking biodiversity and climate variables.

name: Habitat
summary: Company selected for Canadian Space Agency funding to analyse changes in land cover and biodiversity indicators with Earth observation and AI in five watersheds. The list names it as Habitat Inc. (Eco2Urb).

name: Habitat Acquisition Trust
summary: Regional land trust that conserves nature on south Vancouver Island.

name: Hakai Institute
summary: Division of the Tula Foundation that has mapped kelp on British Columbia's Central Coast for about a decade. It developed the public KelpExplorer map and Kelp-O-Matic, a machine learning tool for classifying drone imagery of kelp.

name: Haldimand Bird Observatory
summary: Observatory with three stations at Selkirk Provincial Park, Rock Point and Ruthven Park, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Hamilton Conservation Authority
summary: Organisation dedicated to the conservation and enjoyment of watershed lands and water resources at the western end of Lake Ontario.

name: Harpia
summary: Open-source workflow from the Kanopia team that automates high-resolution drone photography of forest canopies, with AI algorithms delineating tree crowns.

name: Hatfield Consultants
summary: Consulting company in environmental, social and geomatics sciences. It works on the smartWhales detection system with AltaML, and its Hatfield SAVER project aims to use multimodal machine learning to assess ecosystem recovery.

name: HawkEars
summary: Software that identifies bird and amphibian species in audio recordings, trained on species that occur in Canada. It was created by Jan Huus and is being refined with Elly Knight, with support from the Alberta Biodiversity Monitoring Institute.

name: Humans and Algorithms Listening for Orcas
summary: Simon Fraser University project developing an AI system to detect Southern Resident killer whales and forecast their movements in shipping corridors, to inform vessel slowdowns.

name: Huron Tract Land Trust Conservancy
summary: Organisation that helps protect and restore land, water and nature in the Huron Tract area.

name: HydroAware
summary: Project led by Innovasea that received $5 million from Canada's Ocean Supercluster to use AI-powered fish monitoring at hydropower sites.

name: iNaturalist Canada
summary: Canadian site of iNaturalist, launched in June 2015 by the Canadian Wildlife Federation and ROM Biodiversity, for recording wildlife observations with photos. Its own site refused the fetcher, so this rests on the ROM release.

name: Innis Point Bird Observatory
summary: Observatory with spring migration monitoring at two sites and other projects such as MAPS, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Innovatree Carbon Group
summary: Company with proprietary lidar-based software to quantify carbon sequestration in individual trees across large landscapes, according to a Mitacs project page.

name: Insectarium de Montréal
summary: Insect museum in Montréal where, AFP reports, some of the data collection for the Antenna AI insect monitoring project happens.

name: Institut National de la Recherche Scientifique
summary: Quebec City institute named as the affiliation of Acacia Markov, first author of a 2026 paper using multi-scale classification models to study Quebec saltmarsh communities.

name: Island Nature Trust
summary: Prince Edward Island land trust that worked with Korotu Technology to create and pilot LandSteward, using remote sensing and AI analysis to monitor hayfield mowing and to assess forest carbon on its properties.

name: Islands Trust Conservancy
summary: Organisation that has protected 115 properties totalling over 1,380 hectares in the Islands Trust Area, through covenants and nature reserves.

name: iTrackDNA
summary: Pan-Canadian project on environmental DNA, budget about $12 million, building standards, kits and capacity to track biodiversity, with Indigenous groups across the country. Caren Helbing of the University of Victoria co-leads it.

name: IVADO
summary: Institute for Data Valorization, a joint initiative of Université de Montréal, Polytechnique Montréal and HEC Montréal. It granted $6 million to five AI research programmes in 2022, one of which covers biodiversity and climate change.

name: IVADO biodiversity and climate change research programme
summary: One of five AI research programmes funded by IVADO in 2022. Etienne Laliberté, Anne Bruneau, Christopher Pal, David Rolnick and Oliver Sonnentag explore biodiversity and climate change.

name: Kanopia
summary: Research collective and open platform making drone imagery and AI available to researchers, local communities and conservationists for forest monitoring.

name: Kawartha Land Trust
summary: Land trust that in May 2026 reported 50 protected properties comprising 9,100 acres in total.

name: Kelp-O-Matic
summary: Open-source machine learning tool and data pipeline from the Hakai Institute that automates classification of drone imagery of kelp forests. It is used by First Nations, agencies, universities and NGOs.

name: KelpExplorer
summary: Public interactive map of kelp forests on the British Columbia coast, combining observations from satellites, aircraft and drones, and part of the CoastConnect open data tools.

name: Ketos
summary: Software package for acoustic data analysis with neural networks, developed for detection and classification tasks in underwater acoustics.

name: Kitasoo Xai'xais Stewardship Authority
summary: Stewardship authority whose biologist supports the Kwakwa River weir, where salmon are counted with AI.

name: Kitasoo/Xai’xais Nation
summary: First Nation that announced the Gitdisdzu Lugyeks (Kitasu Bay) Marine Protected Area in June 2022, where its Watchmen were reported to have taken on monitoring and enforcement.

name: Kiyooka Land Trust Foundation
summary: Foundation that holds lands in trust in the Robson Valley region to conserve wildlife habitat and protect ecological integrity.

name: Koonkie
summary: Biological data analytics company working with large-scale DNA and biodiversity data. It leads a DIGITAL-funded platform integrating eDNA, soil health and remote sensing for mine restoration.

name: Korotu Technology
summary: Company behind LandSteward, a platform that monitors nature from satellites, drones and ground sensors. It was selected for Canadian Space Agency funding to map biodiversity in agricultural landscapes.

name: Land Cover of Canada
summary: A 30-metre land cover map of Canada made from satellite imagery, part of the North American land cover series for 2010, 2015 and 2020.

name: LandSteward
summary: A platform using remote sensing data and AI analysis tools to monitor changes in the landscape. It was created with Island Nature Trust and is sold by Korotu Technology.

name: Last Mountain Bird Observatory
summary: Observatory with a migration monitoring station active in spring and autumn, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Living Lakes Canada
summary: Organisation that describes the Columbia Basin Water Monitoring Framework as NGO-led and collaborative, lists the Columbia Basin Water Hub among its programmes, and runs iTrackDNA.

name: Long Point Bird Observatory
summary: A migration monitoring station that has been a local programme of Birds Canada since 1998 and is listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Mackenzie Nature Observatory
summary: Organisation associated with a Canadian Wildlife Service joint migration monitoring project operating since 1995, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Mamalilikulla First Nation
summary: First Nation that declared the Gwaxdlala/Nalaxdlala (Lull Bay/Hoeya Sound) area of Knight Inlet an Indigenous Protected and Conserved Area on 29 November 2021, aiming for collaborative governance and ecosystem management.

name: Manitoulin Streams Improvement Association
summary: Association focused on large-scale, community-based efforts to rehabilitate aquatic ecosystems on Manitoulin Island, including restoration of named waterways.

name: Marine Environmental Observation, Prediction and Response Network
summary: Network that funded a CAD$100,000 award for an AI-based ocean solution and hosted a workshop on using AI to understand and predict the ocean.

name: Matawa First Nations Management
summary: Not-for-profit Tribal Council in Northern Ontario whose Four Rivers Environmental Services group uses drones for environmental monitoring, according to the drone maker Wingtra.

name: Mayne Island Conservancy
summary: Organisation that works with the community to conserve the ecology of Mayne Island and its surrounding waters.

name: McGill Bird Observatory
summary: A Migration Research Foundation project with a migration monitoring station on McGill-owned land, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Meewasin Valley Authority
summary: Single agency through which three partners manage the Meewasin Valley in the South Saskatchewan River Basin, under statute.

name: Memorial University of Newfoundland
summary: University whose Marine Institute was training an open-source AI model in 2024 to detect fish and coral in underwater video.

name: MERIDIAN
summary: Consortium of ocean researchers, computer scientists and data managers building a Canadian data infrastructure for underwater acoustic and vessel tracking data.

name: Metaspectral
summary: Vancouver-based company with an AI platform for hyperspectral imagery. It was selected for Canadian Space Agency funding to detect and monitor the invasive plant leafy spurge from satellite imagery.

name: Metro Vancouver Regional Parks
summary: Organisation that manages a system of regional parks, greenways, park reserves and ecological conservancy areas.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs
summary: Quebec's environment ministry. A directorate of the ministry publishes the annual report of the Centre de données sur le patrimoine naturel du Québec.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Protection de la biodiversité, de la Faune et des Parcs
summary: Quebec provincial environment ministry. Its mandates include protecting ecosystems and biodiversity, and it runs the Quebec Biodiversity Monitoring Network.

name: Ministère des Ressources naturelles et des Forêts
summary: Quebec ministry listed as the source of the open Carte dendrométrique lidar, a map of forest stand characteristics derived from lidar.

name: Mission Control Space Services
summary: Ottawa company developing an AI wildfire detection system with Canadian Space Agency smartEarth support. Its FireBAN machine learning algorithm is to run on board its Persistence satellite.

name: MistyWest
summary: Vancouver engineering firm that designed a low-power Argos tracking device for polar bears at the request of WWF and IDEO, and published the design files as open source.

name: Mitacs
summary: Organisation reporting government funding and stating that its Accelerate programme provides leveraged funding of 15,000 Canadian dollars per research internship lasting four or six months.

name: Mi’gmawe’l Tplu’taqnn Inc.
summary: Organisation that a March 2023 article reports protects lands through its Land Trust and works towards creating Indigenous Protected and Conserved Areas in New Brunswick.

name: Mother Earth Watcher
summary: Indigenous-owned environmental monitoring system of Pabineau First Nation pairing sensors and AI with Elders' knowledge to track land, water, air and wildlife. NB Tech News reports a pilot planned for 2027.

name: Motus Audio
summary: Collaboration between the University of Windsor and Birds Canada that has deployed 100 acoustic recorders to capture nocturnal bird migration across Canada.

name: Multi-lens Ecological Restoration Monitoring and Forecasting
summary: Koonkie-led AI platform combining eDNA, mobile soil analysis and remote sensing to monitor mine restoration and biodiversity, funded by DIGITAL.

name: National Capital Commission
summary: Body that manages Gatineau Park, the largest natural area in the National Capital Region, with its conservation at the heart of its mandate.

name: National Deforestation Monitoring System
summary: Canadian Forest Service system designed to give Canada the information to report on deforestation under the UN climate convention.

name: National Digital Platform for Biodiversity Conservation
summary: A platform proposed in a Chief Science Advisor report: a national repository of biodiversity data with AI tools for analysis, prediction and forecasting. The sources describe recommendations, not a working system.

name: National Forest Information System
summary: Web tools for discovering, integrating and displaying information on Canada's forests. The Canadian Council of Forest Ministers agreed the need for it in August 2000.

name: National Forest Inventory
summary: Collaborative federal, provincial and territorial inventory monitoring twenty thousand sampling points across Canada to report on forest state and change.

name: Native Bee Society of BC
summary: British Columbia society that started the BC Bee Atlas with Oregon State University, with over 60 volunteer surveyors as of August 2025.

name: Natural Heritage Information Centre
summary: Ontario government centre managing data on species, plant communities and wildlife concentration areas, published as a 1-kilometre grid.

name: Natural Resources Canada
summary: Federal department that publishes national forest and land cover data, through the Canadian Forest Service and the Canada Centre for Mapping and Earth Observation.

name: Natural Resources Initiative
summary: Genome Canada initiative aiming to strengthen use of genomics, data science and AI in natural resources management and biodiversity protection. Regional centres such as Genome BC advertise it.

name: Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada
summary: Federal research funder. It funds the BIOS² training programme in computational biodiversity science through its CREATE programme.

name: Nature Conservancy of Canada
summary: Conservation charity that uses AI-powered tools to identify priority conservation areas. It worked with Carleton University on the Sites planning tools.

name: Nature Manitoba
summary: Organisation whose Habitat Conservation Committee members had cared for 880 acres of tall grass prairie for many years, and in December 2019 recommended transferring title of its prairie preserves to the Nature Conservancy of Canada.

name: Nature Trust of British Columbia
summary: Organisation that secures, restores and manages ecologically significant lands in British Columbia.

name: Nature Trust of New Brunswick
summary: Organisation that has conserved over 14,700 acres in more than 100 nature preserves, which it owns or holds legal interests in and manages in perpetuity.

name: Nature United
summary: Canadian affiliate of The Nature Conservancy, headquartered in Toronto. It supports Indigenous Guardian programmes, including through a Guardians toolkit and technical team.

name: Nature x Carbon Tech Challenge
summary: WWF-Canada challenge that tested technologies for community-led carbon measurement of nature-based climate solutions in Canada, with $100,000 contracts to three final recipients.

name: NatureCounts
summary: Data and technology platform developed and maintained by Birds Canada for collecting, managing, interpreting and sharing biodiversity data from Canada and beyond.

name: New Brunswick Museum
summary: A museum that announced in June 2025 it would lead the 14th annual BiotaNB field project that summer in Black River Protected Natural Area.

name: NextGen Environmental Research
summary: Company selected for Canadian Space Agency funding for a satellite platform to monitor the Prairies, and earlier for lake ice mapping with machine learning.

name: Niagara Peninsula Conservation Authority
summary: Conservation authority that manages 43 Conservation Areas within the Niagara Peninsula watershed, held in public trust, under its provincial mandate.

name: NicheFlow
summary: Described by the Dinnage Lab as one of the first true foundation models for ecology.

name: Nisg̱a’a Lisims Government
summary: Nisg̱a’a nation government that jointly manages Nisg̱a’a Memorial Lava Bed Park with British Columbia.

name: North Coast Cetacean Society
summary: Self-described non-profit whale research organisation on British Columbia’s northern coast, with four Squally Channel hydrophones and software classifying whale calls to species.

name: Northern Hardwoods Research Institute
summary: Institute selected for Canadian Space Agency funding for an AI-powered system to monitor biodiversity and ecosystem change in New Brunswick. It leads a project locating old forests.

name: NorthStar Earth and Space
summary: Company selected for Canadian Space Agency funding to map plant species from hyperspectral satellite data, and earlier to develop a forest species mapping system using deep learning.

name: Northwest Territory Métis Nation
summary: Métis organisation that co-manages Thaıdene Nëné, sharing operational decisions and care of the area with Łutsël K’é Dene First Nation, Parks Canada and the GNWT.

name: Nottawasaga Valley Conservation Authority
summary: Conservation authority with conservation areas, most of them wilderness or natural lands, covering about 13,000 acres according to the page.

name: Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources
summary: Provincial department that designated 11 sites under the Provincial Parks Act in November 2025, all already managed as parks, bringing the province to 136 designated parks.

name: Nova Scotia Nature Trust
summary: Land trust that takes on properties as Conservation Lands, which it owns, and commits to protecting them in perpetuity.

name: Nunatsiavut Government
summary: Inuit government whose Department of Lands and Natural Resources applies resource-development provisions of the Labrador Inuit Land Claims Agreement and manages Labrador Inuit Lands, including Specified Materials Lands and Water Lots.

name: Nunavut Marine Innovation and Research
summary: Iqaluit nonprofit and Qikiqtaaluk Corporation subsidiary that supports Qikiqtani Inuit communities in acquiring marine knowledge, and leads the Qikiqtani Community Marine Innovation Expansion Project.

name: Nunavut Parks and Special Places Division
summary: Territorial division that manages Nunavut's parks under a mandate, planning and managing each jointly with a community joint planning and management committee.

name: NWT Biodiversity Monitoring Program
summary: A community-based, collaborative programme using cameras for medium and large animals and sound recorders for soundscapes, run by the Northwest Territories environment department with several partners.

name: OBIS Canada
summary: Canadian regional node of the Ocean Biodiversity Information System, managed by Fisheries and Oceans Canada.

name: Observatoire d'oiseaux de Tadoussac
summary: An observatory operating since 1993, first on hawk and owl migration with a songbird programme from 1995, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Ocean AID
summary: Victoria, BC marine technology company using AI vision and edge computing, which says it has detected shoreline plastics and underwater ghost gear.

name: Ocean Diagnostics
summary: Victoria company that makes environmental DNA samplers and microplastics sampling technology for freshwater and marine monitoring.

name: Ocean Frontier Institute
summary: Interdisciplinary ocean research and training collaboration led by Dalhousie University, which manages large research programmes and has a Research Implementation Unit that supports ocean observing.

name: Ocean Riot
summary: Company that uses AI models with autonomous submarines to inventory aquatic organisms and map benthic habitat. A DeepSense project page describes its work.

name: Ocean Wise
summary: Vancouver-based non-profit that runs the Whale Report Alert System, which alerts mariners to whales using reports, partner data and automated hydrophone detections.

name: Office of the Chief Science Advisor
summary: Federal science advice office. It convened a 2024 roundtable on a National Digital Platform for Biodiversity Conservation and published recommendations for a data repository with AI tools.

name: Okanagan Nation Alliance
summary: Alliance of Syilx members whose Natural Resources Committee guides stewardship of the Syilx territory (tmxʷulaxʷ), with technical resource management.

name: Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources
summary: Ontario ministry that tested the MegaDetector AI model on camera trap images from its Multiple Species inventory and monitoring programme, and runs the province's Forest Resources Inventory using lidar.

name: Ontario Nature
summary: Owns 27 nature reserves totalling 3,226 hectares (7,971 acres) as part of its nature reserve programme.

name: Ontario Parks
summary: Provincial parks body managing over 330 parks under provincial mandate, with an operating mandate that includes maintaining the ecological integrity of the parks system.

name: ONTOLOGY
summary: Platform for DNA barcoding and metabarcoding with software, consumables and results, developed by the Innovation Unit at the Centre for Biodiversity Genomics.

name: Orcinus Technologies Inc.
summary: Newfoundland and Labrador company behind TerraXWildlife, a platform mapping wildlife presence with satellite data and AI. The Canadian Space Agency funded its moose traffic system.

name: Outreach Robotics
summary: Sherbrooke company spun out of the local university in 2019 that sells insect monitors, offers rainforest sensor stations, camera traps and drones, and reports helping win XPRIZE Rainforest.

name: Pabineau First Nation
summary: Mi'gmaq community in northern New Brunswick building Mother Earth Watcher, a monitoring system it owns and governs. NB Tech News reports this.

name: Pacific Salmon Foundation
summary: Salmon charity whose Salmon Watersheds Program builds AI tools using computer vision, with the Wild Salmon Center and First Nations, to monitor wild salmon.

name: Parc d’environnement naturel de Sutton
summary: Nature park that manages more than 70 km of hiking trails and works to protect biodiversity and threatened species habitats in the Sutton mountains.

name: Parks Canada
summary: Federal agency that protects and presents national parks, national historic sites and national marine conservation areas, and is Canada's protected-area agency. It uses RADARSAT data to track the state of national parks.

name: Parks Division of Tourism, Culture, Arts and Recreation (Newfoundland and Labrador)
summary: Provincial division committed to the conservation and management of a network of 32 provincial parks, under its provincial mandate.

name: Parks New Brunswick
summary: Provincial parks body that manages New Brunswick's provincial parks under provincial mandate, for example Mount Carleton Provincial Park.

name: Pender Islands Conservancy Association
summary: Registered land trust on the Pender Islands, committed to conservation through land acquisition and covenants.

name: Pimachiowin Aki Corporation
summary: Corporation described in a June 2021 article as taking part in implementing community-led plans to protect the Pimachiowin Aki World Heritage Site.

name: Polar Bear Tracker
summary: Ear-mounted tracker for WWF and the US Fish and Wildlife Service with timed release and six-month maximum battery life, sent to Winnipeg Zoo for trials, with further testing planned.

name: PrairieDNA
summary: Prairies North environmental DNA monitoring network using genomics tools in rivers, lakes and municipal waters, connecting researchers and Indigenous communities.

name: Prince Edward Point Bird Observatory
summary: A migration monitoring station established in 1995 that monitors in spring and fall and is listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Qikiqtani Community Marine Innovation Expansion Project
summary: $15 million project to trial low-impact technologies for Inuit-led inshore monitoring in Qikiqtani, Nunavut, including eDNA sampling from vessels and the shore.

name: Qikiqtani Inuit Association
summary: Inuit association party to the August 2019 Inuit Impact and Benefit Agreement with the Government of Canada, which established Tallurutiup Imanga National Marine Conservation Area and ensured Inuit governance of the protected areas.

name: Quantitative Biodiversity Lab
summary: McGill University lab modelling and forecasting global biodiversity change, with a stated interest in AI and citizen science.

name: Quebec Centre for Biodiversity Science
summary: Research centre co-directed by Andrew Gonzalez of McGill University, according to his statement on a Beaty Biodiversity Museum page.

name: RADARSAT Constellation Mission
summary: A Canadian system of three synthetic aperture radar satellites launched in June 2019. Canadian agencies use its data for forest, wetland, park and coastal monitoring.

name: Raincoast Conservation Foundation
summary: British Columbia conservation science organisation that works with Earth Species Project on killer whale communication, combining drone footage, underwater recordings and behavioural observations.

name: RBC Foundation
summary: Funder behind RBC Tech for Nature. It gave $200,000 to expand the Pacific Salmon Foundation's AI salmon counting and funded Island Nature Trust's LandSteward project.

name: RBC Tech for Nature
summary: RBC Foundation programme, established in 2019, that supports partner organisations on environmental research and technology, including wetland mapping and salmon counting projects in Canada.

name: Real-time wolf monitoring during denning season
summary: 2026 project near Vancouver that placed 20 Instant Detect cameras running an AI wolf recognition model, in partnership with the Tsleil-Waututh Nation, with the science led by Zoetica Environmental.

name: Regional Monitoring System
summary: Coastal First Nations digital monitoring tools: the CoastTracker mobile app, a central database on Canadian servers and the CoastViewer web system.

name: Retide Labs
summary: Company that uses AI and robotics to measure, map and verify plastic pollution across oceans, beaches and rivers. An alumnus of the Ocean Startup Challenge.

name: Robonotic
summary: Designs autonomous technologies for aquatic invasive species. With DeepSense it developed AI models to detect and monitor zebra mussels.

name: Rolnick Lab
summary: Research group applying machine learning to climate change problems including biodiversity and remote sensing, reported by McGill in February 2025 as scaling up biodiversity and forest monitoring.

name: Royal Botanical Gardens
summary: Botanical garden in Burlington, Ontario, that has monitored fish moving into Cootes Paradise Marsh for three decades.

name: Royal Ontario Museum
summary: Toronto museum of natural history and world cultures, an agency of the Government of Ontario. ROM Biodiversity launched iNaturalist Canada with the Canadian Wildlife Federation.

name: Réseau de suivi de la biodiversité du Québec
summary: Quebec government monitoring network that measures more than 20 biodiversity indicators to assess the effects of climate change. It has surveyed more than 500 sites, using standard field protocols including camera inventories of mammals, and makes its data available.

name: Sailbotix
summary: Developer of compact autonomous surface vessels for long-duration ocean monitoring. An alumnus of the Ocean Startup Challenge.

name: Salish Sea orca sound detection
summary: Google, Fisheries and Oceans Canada and Rainforest Connection used deep neural networks to monitor Southern Resident killer whales in the Salish Sea from audio at 12 locations.

name: Salmon Computer-Vision Project
summary: Collaboration of the Wild Salmon Center, Pacific Salmon Foundation, Simon Fraser University, First Nations and government agencies that develops computer vision models to identify and count salmon from video and sonar. The model is also called Salmon Vision.

name: Salt Spring Island Conservancy
summary: Conservancy that protects the natural values of Salt Spring Island and its surrounding waters by acquiring land or covenants.

name: SatCaribou
summary: A project that aims to develop an AI and satellite-based tool for mapping boreal caribou habitat in the Uashat Mak Mani-Utenam community, funded by SmartEarth.

name: SCANFI: Spatialized Canadian National Forest Inventory data product
summary: Raster layers predicting vegetation attributes and tree species distribution across Canada, generated with machine learning from remote sensing, climate and environmental data, from the Canadian National Forest Inventory.

name: SeafarerAI
summary: New Brunswick company whose technology underlies Mother Earth Watcher, as reported by NB Tech News. Its earlier work is maritime.

name: SeaHawk Robotics
summary: Developer and operator of UAV-based ocean observation systems, and a partner in the Air Sea Ocean Monitoring System project.

name: SednaLink Marine Systems
summary: Iqaluit company that aims to integrate sensors into telecommunication cables to monitor marine environmental conditions in the Arctic.

name: SeeFar
summary: Collection of multi-resolution satellite images from public and commercial satellites, curated for training geospatial foundation models.

name: Sensor Technology
summary: Collingwood, Ontario company that leads the WhisperLoop acoustic monitoring project.

name: SENSR
summary: Part of Biodiversity Pathways, offering environmental sensor services using acoustic recorders and remote cameras.

name: SentinAILE
summary: Ecological surveillance network for seabirds of the St Lawrence using AI, being set up under the initiative of David Pelletier of Cégep de Rimouski with several partners.

name: Sigma Eight Inc.
summary: Newmarket, Ontario maker of wildlife radio telemetry transmitters and receivers.

name: SIKU Ocean AI Tools Project
summary: $4.3 million project led by the Arctic Eider Society, with SmartICE, to add data analysis, fisheries monitoring and ice navigation tools to the SIKU platform.

name: SIKU: The Indigenous Knowledge App
summary: A free mobile and web platform created by the Arctic Eider Society and northern communities, where users share observations of ice, wildlife and weather and see satellite-based sea ice maps. It has over 34,000 users.

name: Simon Fraser University
summary: University whose researchers work with the Pacific Salmon Foundation and First Nations fisheries on deep learning for automated salmon counting.

name: Sites
summary: Digital conservation planning tool using AI software and prioritisation algorithms, developed by Carleton University's Bennett Lab with the Nature Conservancy of Canada and Environment and Climate Change Canada.

name: Skeena Fisheries Commission
summary: Fisheries commission named as a partner in developing computer vision models to identify and count salmon in British Columbia.

name: SkyWatch Space Applications
summary: Company selected for Canadian Space Agency funding to deliver on-demand Earth observation tools for biodiversity monitoring on its cloud platform.

name: smartEarth
summary: Canadian Space Agency funding initiative for applications of satellite data. In 2025 it selected 20 companies for biodiversity projects, each receiving $250,000.

name: Smartforests Canada
summary: A national-scale research network of regional investigators who run forest monitoring plots, described in a 2022 book chapter.

name: SmartICE Sea Ice Monitoring & Information Inc.
summary: Operates sea-ice monitoring tools that combine traditional knowledge with sensors and Earth observation mapping, and trains Inuit community members in their use.

name: smartWhales
summary: Canadian Space Agency programme funding companies to use satellite data to detect and monitor North Atlantic right whales in Canadian waters, with Fisheries and Oceans Canada and Transport Canada.

name: smartWhales Space-Based Detection System
summary: Project by Hatfield Consultants and AltaML that uses AI on satellite imagery to detect North Atlantic right whales, with financial support from the Canadian Space Agency and Fisheries and Oceans Canada.

name: Société de protection foncière du lac Montjoie
summary: Land protection society that protects 20 hectares of natural areas, part of which is recognised as a private nature reserve.

name: Southern Alberta Land Trust Society
summary: Land trust that works with private landowners to protect open landscapes in Alberta.

name: Southern Interior Land Trust
summary: Land trust that aims to protect and conserve sensitive fish and wildlife habitats in the southern interior of British Columbia.

name: Species Aware Ocean AI Project
summary: $4.8 million project led by Innovasea to add automated fish species identification to its HydroAI platform for hydropower sites.

name: Species Aware Project
summary: $4.8 million project led by Innovasea with two Canadian power companies, adding automated fish species identification to its HydroAI platform for hydropower sites.

name: Squamish Nation
summary: Indigenous nation that signed two park management plans with BC Parks in February 2012, guiding protection of almost 13,000 hectares, and whose Xay Temíxw land use plan protects its territories and Wild Spirit Places.

name: Statistics Canada
summary: Canada's statistics agency. It runs the Census of Environment, which builds ecosystem accounts and a national register of ecosystems.

name: STREAM (Sequencing the Rivers for Environmental Assessment and Monitoring)
summary: River monitoring project launched in 2019 in which trained volunteers collect samples that the University of Guelph analyses by eDNA.

name: Superwake
summary: Drone wildlife survey company that says it surveyed moose, elk and deer over 3,300 square kilometres of Riding Mountain National Park.

name: SWAG (Ships, Whales, Acoustics in Gitga’at Territory)
summary: Bio-monitoring project in northern British Columbia in which four hydrophones in Squally Channel record whales, with AI-based detection telling species apart.

name: Tailgate eDNA sequencing for near-real-time biodiversity monitoring
summary: Genome Canada project bringing eDNA monitoring from the lab to the field using a portable lab setup and a portable DNA sequencer.

name: Taku River Tlingit First Nation
summary: First Nation whose Clan Directors Council and Clan Leaders declared the T’akú Tlatsini Indigenous Protected and Conserved Area in January 2024, governed under its own law.

name: TerraSphere
summary: SeafarerAI platform that NB Tech News says powers Mother Earth Watcher and runs on site without depending on the public internet.

name: Tesera Systems
summary: Calgary company combining analytics and machine learning to produce forest inventories, which says it has delivered inventories across 2 million acres of natural and managed forests.

name: Thaıdene Nëné Xá Dá Yáłtı
summary: Operational management board for Thaıdene Nëné, taking part in operational decisions about the area.

name: The Couchiching Conservancy
summary: Conservancy that protects more than 15,600 acres in the Orillia region through ownership, partnerships and conservation easements.

name: The Gordon Foundation
summary: Philanthropic charity with a commitment to protecting Canada's water. It developed DataStream, which became its own charity in 2020.

name: The Land Conservancy
summary: Charitable land trust that protects habitat and heritage properties throughout British Columbia.

name: Thunder Cape Bird Observatory
summary: An observatory that has operated in spring and fall since a pilot migration monitoring project in 1991, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Parks
summary: Tla-o-qui-aht initiative that exists to promote Indigenous care and reciprocity and strengthen the abundance of its lands for future generations.

name: Tommy Thompson Park Bird Research Station
summary: A research station whose core activity is a daily spring and fall Migration Monitoring Program, listed as a station of the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Toronto and Region Conservation Authority
summary: Conservation authority working to conserve, restore and manage natural resources in nine watersheds, with almost 18,000 hectares of its own land per the City of Toronto, acting under the Conservation Authorities Act since 1957.

name: Toronto Zoo
summary: A zoo that runs the Adopt-A-Pond programme, including FrogWatch Ontario and Ontario Turtle Tally, and reports radio-tracking 22 translocated eastern massasauga rattlesnakes with Wildlife Preservation Canada.

name: Transport Canada
summary: Federal department that commissioned the Boundary Pass underwater listening station and collaborates on the smartWhales programme.

name: TreeTrack Intelligence
summary: British Columbia company combining seedpods, drone deployment and AI-powered monitoring, reporting about 200 hectares treated in documented deployments between 2023 and 2026, including a 2026 post-wildfire deployment at Selbaie, Quebec.

name: Tr’ondëk Hwëch’in
summary: An organisation that jointly manages Tombstone Territorial Park with the Yukon Government, as a co-manager.

name: Tsleil-Waututh Nation
summary: Coast Salish Nation on Burrard Inlet in the Greater Vancouver region, which Hack The Planet works with on biodiversity monitoring technology.

name: Tula Foundation
summary: Foundation of which the Hakai Institute is a division.

name: University of Alberta
summary: University whose staff collaborate on the HawkEars audio classifier and whose Erin Bayne lab works with the ABMI in the Bioacoustic Unit.

name: University of Calgary
summary: University where Saul Greenberg, an emeritus professor of computer science, created Timelapse, software for turning camera trap images into data.

name: University of Manitoba
summary: University with a Centre for Earth Observation Science. A professor there lists work on satellite-based sea ice classification using machine learning.

name: University of New Brunswick
summary: A university whose Saint John researcher Kimberley T. A. Davies led a 2025 paper testing semi-automated right whale detection in very high resolution satellite imagery.

name: University of Saskatchewan
summary: University whose School of Environment and Sustainability has a professor exploring AI and machine learning methods for predictive modelling in environmental systems.

name: University of Toronto
summary: A university whose Mississauga researcher Matthew Noonan led a 2025 paper estimating green and dead vegetation cover in rehabilitated ecosystems using drone imagery and random forest regression.

name: University of Western Ontario
summary: University in London, Ontario, whose researchers work with Birds Canada on migration data and the Motus tracking system.

name: Université de Montréal Biodiversity Centre
summary: University of Montreal centre from which Canadensys, a national network for biological collection data, is operated.

name: Université Laval
summary: Canadian university whose team develops BioScan3D forest biomass software, and a partner in the Transforming Climate Action ocean research programme.

name: Vanderkooij Consult
summary: Company selected for Canadian Space Agency funding to develop cost-effective radar monitoring tools for Northern Canada's ecosystems with government and Indigenous partners.

name: Vaseux Lake Migration Monitoring Station
summary: A migration monitoring station run by the Okanagan Similkameen Conservation Alliance from 2001, listed in the Canadian Migration Monitoring Network.

name: Vecterra Spatial Analytics
summary: Develops automated interpretation for forest inventory data used in Canadian climate, biodiversity and sustainable forest management reporting.

name: Viridis Terra International
summary: Organisation that states it restores degraded lands, with projects listed in Burkina Faso, Canada, Haiti and Peru, where it reports 450 hectares restored and operates a Pucallpa nursery able to produce a million seedlings a year.

name: Water Rangers
summary: Non-profit social enterprise founded in 2015 that gives people water test kits and an open-data platform for citizen science on local waterways.

name: West Africa Blue
summary: Organisation co-founded by Solon Capital Partners that says it has mangrove protection and restoration projects in Sierra Leone and Guinea, with a Sierra Leone project area of about 93,400 hectares.

name: Whale Report Alert System
summary: Ocean Wise's real-time warning system for mariners, drawing on data from users, partners and automated detection technologies. It has been integrated into Trelleborg's SafePilot Pro navigation software.

name: WhisperLoop
summary: $6.5 million dual-use project for an AI-powered underwater acoustic monitoring system using a towed hydrophone array on uncrewed vessels. Its stated uses include marine mammal protection and defence.

name: Wild + Pine
summary: The company, which described itself as a Certified B Corporation in May 2024, designs forest restoration projects including StoneWoods, an afforestation project opened in 2022 targeting 3,700 acres.

name: Wilder Institute
summary: An organisation whose 2025 annual report describes monitoring habitat for a butterfly its genome analysis showed to be a separate species, and which fitted translocated fishers with transmitters.

name: WildFireSat
summary: Government of Canada wildfire satellite programme. A February 2025 release described seven microsatellites launching in 2029. SpaceQ later reported that the federal government terminated the $72-million contract with Spire Global.

name: Wildlife Cameras for Adaptive Management
summary: Named with the Alberta Remote Camera Steering Committee as an author of remote camera survey guidelines for Western Canada, which cover AI classification with MegaDetector.

name: Wildlife Coexistence Lab
summary: University of British Columbia lab, led by Cole Burton, using camera traps as a main survey tool for research supporting wildlife conservation and human-wildlife coexistence in Canada and elsewhere.

name: Wildlife Conservation Society Canada
summary: Conservation organisation that runs a wolverine research project, established to live-trap and monitor wolverines over 6,500 square kilometres of northern Ontario.

name: Wildlife Preservation Canada
summary: Canadian conservation organisation with a Bumble Bee Recovery Program that runs annual population surveys.

name: WildTechDNA
summary: Company whose field-ready kit is intended for conservation and wildlife enforcement, among other uses, and whose screening test it says can confirm species on site.

name: WildTrax
summary: Online platform for storing, managing, processing and sharing data from environmental sensors such as autonomous recording units, remote cameras and point counts. It offers public data discovery and is developing machine learning auto-recognition.

name: WSP Canada
summary: Company selected for Canadian Space Agency funding to develop an AI and satellite-based tool for boreal caribou habitat mapping in the Uashat Mak Mani-Utenam community.

name: WWF-Canada
summary: Canadian conservation charity whose Living Planet Technology Hub holds its conservation technology projects, including eDNA river monitoring.

name: Wyvern
summary: An Edmonton space company described by Emissions Reduction Alberta as using three hyperspectral satellites, which says its imagery improved tree species classification accuracy by up to 45% in a Tesera study.

name: Ya'thi Néné Lands and Resources
summary: Indigenous organisation working with Hatfield to co-develop AI monitoring of woodland caribou habitat condition in Northern Saskatchewan.

name: Łutsël K’é Dene First Nation
summary: First Nation that established Thaıdene Nëné using its Dene law and shares responsibility for operational decisions and care of it.

name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands coral reef eDNA metabarcoding survey
summary: A closed coral reef eDNA metabarcoding survey, with water samples taken at 42 sites in April 2017 and processed at Curtin University's TrEnD Laboratory, whose records on GBIF set a new baseline for monitoring reef fauna.

name: Open-ocean wildlife monitoring of Cocos (Keeling) Islands
summary: Grant-funded project planning to build local capacity to monitor tunas, billfishes and sharks using midwater baited underwater video, with two surveys planned; by February 2024 the equipment was awaiting shipment.

name: Pulu Keeling National Park
summary: A Commonwealth reserve under the EPBC Act, managed by the Director of National Parks, mainly for scientific research and environmental monitoring, including continuous bird counts, weed mapping and coral and fish health checks.

name: Pulu Keeling National Park Island-wide Survey
summary: Recorded on Pulu Keeling in 2009, 2012 and 2017, the survey aimed to monitor native and non-native species and map invasive weeds.

name: Pulu Keeling National Park Island-wide Survey (IWS) Waypoint Survey
summary: Completed dataset from the park's Island-wide Survey, held in November 2009 and March 2012, recording yellow crazy ant and scale insect distribution at 132 random waypoints, built by Parks Australia.

name: Satellite-Derived Bathymetry and Seafloor Habitat Classification Mapping of Cocos (Keeling) Islands Marine Park
summary: Closed dataset of 2 m satellite-derived bathymetry and seafloor habitat maps for the marine park's shallow waters, acquired in 2023 and 2024, giving baseline information for long-term monitoring, built by EOMAP.

name: The Status of Resident Sea Turtles at Cocos (Keeling) Islands
summary: Grant-funded project planning to document the population and health of the islands' green and hawksbill turtles amid seagrass loss, with monitoring by Scott Whiting recorded as planned for six months in 2024.

name: Applied Community-Based Approach and ICT Tool for Kahuzi Biega National Park Elephant Preservation
summary: Closed project led by Dieudonne Shukuru Wasso that aimed to protect Kahuzi-Biega forest elephants by GPS and GIS mapping, with an August 2025 report on MaxEnt habitat modelling and a January 2026 final evaluation.

name: Atlas Forestier Interactif de la RDC
summary: Interactive forest atlas for the DRC, built by WRI with the environment ministry, which aims to bring all major land use categories onto one platform to strengthen forest management and land use planning.

name: Bonobo Diversity Project
summary: Active collaborative research network documenting bonobo diversity and sympatric species across 30 sites in the DRC, using a 25 km2 grid monitored for 12 months per site, and partnering with ICCN.

name: Centre de Surveillance de la Biodiversité
summary: Kisangani biodiversity monitoring centre, created by University of Kisangani decision in January 2011, specialising in field research, holding Boyekoli Ebale Congo 2010 collections and registered as a GBIF data publisher.

name: Centre National de Télédétection
summary: National remote sensing institution in the DRC that signed an agreement with Japanese company Solafune in December 2025 on satellite images and artificial intelligence.

name: Combating illegal wildlife trade - Greater Virunga Landscape
summary: IFAW-run project against illegal wildlife trade in the Greater Virunga Landscape, funded by a US bureau, which IFAW says created an intelligence and crime analysis team and engaged 20 community wildlife monitors.

name: Congo Biotropical Institute
summary: Environmental association, as described by Wilder International, that works on tropical ecosystems and biodiversity, launched a survey of two undocumented sites in Tshuapa and North Kivu, and partners with Wilder International.

name: Direction de Développement Durable
summary: Ministry directorate through which the ministry organised, with the COMIFAC coordination, a 20 May 2026 workshop to validate the seventh national biodiversity report for adoption and submission to the CBD secretariat.

name: Direction des Inventaires et Aménagement Forestiers
summary: Forest inventory directorate listed on the environment ministry's site, named in a 2014 TerraCongo presentation as a cooperation partner of FAO and INPE on monitoring forest area change.

name: Ecole Régionale Postuniversitaire d'Aménagement et de Gestion intégrés des Forêts et Territoires tropicaux
summary: A UNESCO category 2 postgraduate school on the University of Kinshasa campus, linked to a Sentinel-2 mangrove mapping paper, student drone training and the Yangambi flux tower.

name: Era-Congo
summary: Forest concession operator in Maï-Ndombe province, described as a DRC subsidiary of US company WWC, with elephants and bonobos reported by the Congolese press agency in May 2025 to have returned.

name: Etate Research Station
summary: Base of the Salonga Conservation Initiative in Salonga National Park, with 13 resident staff, run by that initiative, which says it has re-surveyed about 30% of the park since 2020.

name: Fonds National REDD+ de la RDC
summary: National REDD+ fund whose 2023 report lists 25 programmes approved since 2016–2017 and $252,781,204 mobilised, 99% directly from CAFI.

name: Garamba National Park
summary: A 5,127 km2 park managed by African Parks, according to a 2020 JRS grant page that reports satellite tracking of elephants and giraffes and community chimpanzee monitoring, which COVID-19 had halted for primate research.

name: ICEYE and Jane Goodall Institute SAR deforestation monitoring in the Congo Basin
summary: Partnership between ICEYE and Jane Goodall Institute USA to deploy radar-based deforestation monitoring across Congo Basin corridors, starting in eastern DRC, aiming at near real-time awareness for patrols.

name: Institut Congolais pour la Conservation de la Nature
summary: State protected-area body in the DRC, named as planned manager of the 2024 Okapi census and partner in Salonga ranger training and Upemba National Park management.

name: Institut Géographique du Congo
summary: Public agency in charge of mapping and geographic information in the DRC, created in December 1949, whose director general said in October 2026 that it works with drones and GPS.

name: Institut National pour l'Étude et la Recherche Agronomiques
summary: An agronomic research institute that ERAIFT says co-manages the Yangambi Biosphere Reserve with the ministry’s Man and the Biosphere programme, with its director quoted in October 2020.

name: Itombwe Génération pour l'Humanité
summary: A non-profit based in Bukavu, Democratic Republic of Congo, that has run community monitoring of chimpanzees and gorillas in the Itombwe Mountains since 2014, analysing monthly patrol data with SMART.

name: Itombwe Nature Reserve
summary: A reserve run by ICCN that, with Primate Expertise, set up camera-trap and transect biomonitoring, reporting Grauer's gorillas recorded regularly by camera traps in September 2026.

name: Jane Goodall Institute and Bezos Earth Fund Congo Basin conservation project
summary: Jane Goodall Institute project announced in February 2024 with a $5 million Bezos Earth Fund grant over three years, covering areas in the DRC and Republic of the Congo, including satellite and mobile monitoring.

name: Let's Be Transformed (MAGUFINA)
summary: Community organisation that Global Nature Watch said in July 2026 trained monitors who documented illegal logging and unauthorised mining across 450,000 hectares of Indigenous lands, with a planned Forest Watcher training and dashboard.

name: Maï-Ndombe REDD+
summary: REDD+ project run by Era-Congo that uses camera-trap images to confirm wildlife return, with large mammal monitoring as an objective for assessing conservation status under the CCB standard.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement, Développement Durable et Nouvelle Économie du Climat
summary: DRC government ministry responsible for environmental policy and biodiversity preservation, with DIAF, ICCN and the Fonds Forestier National among its bodies, and organiser of the October 2026 land tenure plan launch workshop.

name: Moabi DRC
summary: Collaborative mapping initiative on resource issues in the DRC, built on customised OpenStreetMap, whose management passed in 2013 to an IIASA-led project, with no current operator identified.

name: Observatoire de la Gouvernance Forestière
summary: A Congolese independent forest monitoring NGO created in September 2012 that Global Forest Watch says used alerts and trained monitors from 25 organisations in 2023 and 2024.

name: Okapi Conservation Project
summary: Programme run by Wildlife Conservation Global, partnering with ICCN, whose 2025 highlights report camera-trap deployment near Epulu and an informer network of 50 people guiding eco-guard patrols.

name: Parc Marin des Mangroves
summary: Park in the DRC whose staff and volunteers made a 2023 waterbird count, and whose Pierre Mavuemba is listed by Wetlands International as the DRC's International Waterbird Census coordinator.

name: Parc National de Kahuzi-Biega
summary: National park that runs a research and biomonitoring programme, which a April 2026 report says uses geospatial data daily, with staff then being trained in GPS, camera traps, SMART Conservation and QGIS.

name: Permanence of bonobo guards and ranger patrols at and around the expedition camp in the Lomako Yokokala Faunal Reserve
summary: A closed project run by the Royal Zoological Society of Antwerp, reported by IUCN Save Our Species (2019 to 2024 grants) as producing monthly SMART ranger reports and counting bonobo and elephant sightings on patrols.

name: Primate Expertise
summary: NGO for primate research and conservation in the DRC that says it leads biomonitoring work in the Itombwe Nature Reserve, and whose founder is listed as its late executive director.

name: Programme d'Appui aux Aires Protégées (PARAP)
summary: Protected areas support programme which, according to the Kisangani centre's GBIF record, works with WWF and aims to inventory protected areas and strengthen their conservation.

name: Programme de Recherche et Biomonitoring du PNKB
summary: Programme run by Kahuzi-Biega National Park, partnering with the Université Evangélique en Afrique, which began a five-day ecological monitoring training on 13 April 2026 covering GPS, camera traps, SMART Conservation and QGIS.

name: Programme Système National de Surveillance des Forêts (FONAREDD)
summary: National forest monitoring programme with FAO as executing agency, approved in October 2016, started in January 2017 and listed by FONAREDD's 2023 report as closed in 2021.

name: Protecting the Ngamikka-Luama Landscape by Establishing Infrastructure and Capacity
summary: Closed CEPF-funded Wildlife Conservation Society project (June 2014 to December 2016) that developed a SMART-based monitoring system in Kabobo-Luama, built two monitoring stations, and reported 20 local monitors still active in 2017.

name: RFUK community forest monitoring programme in the DRC (2026 phase)
summary: A three-year programme of community-led forest monitoring in the DRC, announced on 30 July 2026, run and built by Rainforest Foundation UK, with partners trained on ForestLink and ForestEye for four provinces.

name: Salonga National Park
summary: Its co-management programme receives WWF Germany and USAID funding, and an April 2020 interview describes 160 cameras surveying 743 locations across 17,127 km2 of its southern block.

name: Sea Turtle Monitoring and Protection along the Muanda Shoreline, Muanda Mangrove National Park
summary: A closed project funded by the Rufford Foundation, which in January 2017 planned daily nesting-beach patrols to quantify nesting activity and follow year-to-year trends; the final report lists daily monitoring.

name: Solutions for Wildlife
summary: A grassroots association supporting communities and indigenous peoples in wildlife and forest management, which deployed camera traps, SongMeters and eDNA water sampling in Yangambi and Weko forests from September to November 2025.

name: Supporting the long-term survival of okapi
summary: A closed 2022 to 2023 project under the IUCN SOS African Wildlife Initiative, run by Fauna & Flora International, aiming to improve law enforcement coverage, wildlife monitoring and community support for conservation.

name: Sustainable Wildlife Management Programme in the Okapi Wildlife Reserve
summary: Active wildlife management programme in the Okapi Wildlife Reserve, run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, which used camera trap monitoring to estimate wildlife abundance and works with communities in Epulu, Eboyo and Bapukeli.

name: Technologies innovantes pour la lutte contre l'exploitation illégale du bois : mise à l'échelle des plateformes d'identification et de transparence du bois
summary: A NORAD-funded project, run by OGF and FLAG, on transparent forest resource management in the DRC; in mid-2025 it trained GASHE community workers in Mbandaka to enter monitoring reports on the Open Timber Portal.

name: Terra Congo
summary: Presented in February 2014 as the DRC's satellite land monitoring system, a national forest monitoring system aimed at estimating forest carbon stocks and changes in forest area, with FAO support under UN-REDD.

name: University of Kolwezi
summary: A university, also headed Université de Kolwezi, linked through OpenAlex to a 2026 paper on information loss in forest compositional mapping in Lualaba Province, shared with the University of Lubumbashi.

name: University of Lubumbashi
summary: A university with OpenAlex papers from 2020 and 2025 using remote sensing to study Miombo woodland change in the Lufira reserve, land cover classification methods, and land cover change on Idjwi Island.

name: Université Catholique de Bukavu
summary: A university in Bukavu, listed by OpenAlex with a 2019 paper by a first author there on land use and land cover change around forests of Kabare and Idjwi.

name: Université de Kinshasa
summary: A DRC university listed in the GERNAC water and natural resources consortium, hosting OSFAC's GIS lab, with OpenAlex papers on forest degradation and deforestation detection and insect data published on GBIF.

name: Université de Kisangani
summary: A public higher education and research institution in Tshopo province, which runs the Centre de Surveillance de la Biodiversité, created in January 2011, with OpenAlex papers on forest mapping and peat carbon.

name: Université Evangélique en Afrique
summary: A university located in Panzi, Bukavu, linked through OpenAlex to a 2023 paper on mapping small inland wetlands in South Kivu with optical and SAR data.

name: Université Officielle de Bukavu
summary: A university in Bukavu with two 2024 OpenAlex papers on land use and land cover change modelling in eastern DR Congo, and a research centre, CREGET, managing a herbarium founded in 2021.

name: Virunga National Park
summary: Its team monitors habitats with satellite imagery, planned 65 camera traps by the end of 2022, and reported drones assisting rangers after a 2021 project launch.

name: WCS DR Congo
summary: The DRC programme of the Wildlife Conservation Society, which includes a research and biomonitoring pillar, says it is leading wider use of SMART and EarthRanger, and co-manages two protected areas with ICCN.

name: Yangambi flux tower
summary: A Yangambi tower studying forest greenhouse gas exchange, built by ERAIFT, CIFOR-ICRAF and Ghent University, which ERAIFT says has operated since October 2020 and promises open data.

name: Atlas Forestier Interactif de la République Centrafricaine
summary: Interactive mapping platform and WRI report (version 1.0, data page dated 1 August 2010) gathering information on the Central African Republic forest sector, with GIS layers on conservation, habitat and vegetation, built by WRI and the Ministry of Water, Forests, Hunting and Fishing.

name: Bangui and Surrounding Areas PES Project
summary: PES project funded by CAFI with USD 10,000,000 and run by UNDP, aiming to conserve 20,000 hectares through community forests, with payments conditional on verified results.

name: Camera Trapping in Dzanga Sangha Protected Areas
summary: A closed master's thesis project that, as planned in January 2018, would use camera trapping on 36 transects of 2 km, with two cameras each for about 165 days, to assess large mammals in two zones.

name: Camera traps in Chinko
summary: Long-running camera trap work in Chinko Nature Reserve, over 12 years, where images are processed at a Swiss lab and volunteers' tags train an AI to recognise species.

name: Centre pour l'Information Environnementale et le Développement Durable
summary: Civil society organisation that Fern reported in October 2021 carries out mandated independent forest monitoring in the Central African Republic, with access to company records and joint field missions.

name: Dzanga Forest Elephant Project
summary: Started by Andrea Turkalo and run by the Elephant Listening Project, it reportedly combines behavioural observation with acoustic monitoring; 27 years’ data identified over 4,000 forest elephants.

name: Dzanga-Sangha Protected Areas
summary: Protected areas run by WWF and the water, forests, hunting and fishing ministry, with biomonitoring including wildlife inventories, camera traps, a zoonotic disease field lab and remote-sensing mapping.

name: Dzanga-Sangha Wildlife Inventory
summary: Five-yearly large-mammal inventory run by WWF Central African Republic and Dzanga-Sangha Protected Areas; the 2025 round used 186 line transects and collected 990 eDNA leaf swabs.

name: EarthRanger deployment at Dzanga-Sangha Protected Areas
summary: Active use of EarthRanger, run by Dzanga-Sangha Protected Areas, to combine patrol, researcher and satellite data in real time, with historical soundscapes being uploaded to build a baseline.

name: Elephant Listening Project acoustic monitoring in Dzanga-Sangha
summary: Acoustic monitoring run by the Elephant Listening Project across almost 1,200 square kilometres, recording elephant sounds and gunshots, with recorded shots evaluated to plan anti-poaching patrols.

name: Forest elephant tracking collars, Dzanga-Sangha Protected Areas
summary: A 2022 appeal for tracking collars for Critically Endangered forest elephants, reporting that two years of monitoring showed collared elephants avoided moving north and west, and aiming to collar 10 more.

name: Freshwater Biodiversity Data Collection System (FBDC) for the Northeast Protected Area Complex, Central African Republic
summary: A $250,000 JRS-funded project, July 2023 to June 2026, led by Felin Twagirashyaka, to fill freshwater biodiversity knowledge gaps in the Northeast Protected Area Complex and set up long-term monitoring of the upper Chari river.

name: GBIF Central African Republic
summary: Country node of GBIF in the Central African Republic, with associate participant status, based at CERPHAMETA in Bangui; the registry lists no publishing organisations in the country.

name: M'Baïki permanent sample plots forest dynamics data (1982-2022)
summary: Data from three control plots near M'Baïki record girth, mortality and recruitment monitored almost annually from 1982 to 2022; the paper carries a CC BY 4.0 licence.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement et du Développement Durable
summary: Environment ministry that UNDP says will co-chair the BIOFIN national steering committee launched in September 2025, and that CAFI lists as a partner of the Bangui PES project.

name: Ministère des Eaux, Forêts, Chasse et Pêche
summary: Ministry described by FAO in 2010 as applying government policy on forest, wildlife and fisheries resources; it runs Dzanga-Sangha Protected Areas and is listed by WCS as a supporter.

name: REDD+ integrated program in the forest region in the South-West of the Central African Republic
summary: Completed REDD+ programme in south-west Central African Republic, from June 2015 with an estimated end of June 2019, with 6.5 million euros total financing, including a baseline scenario and monitoring system component.

name: Service de la Cartographie et de la Télédétection (Central African Republic)
summary: The Central African Republic's national geospatial information authority according to the UN SALB country page, with a postal address in Bangui.

name: Système national de vérification de la légalité du bois
