summary: National timber legality verification system, intended to ensure exported timber meets legal standards, which the EU delegation says is housed in a new APV-FLEGT building the ministry officially received on 27 February 2026.

name: WCS camera-trap surveys in North-Eastern Central African Republic
summary: In August 2025, WCS reported its north-eastern Central African Republic surveys had documented a lioness for the first time in six years; a later release reported cubs.

name: WCS Central African Republic
summary: Run by the Wildlife Conservation Society; under a 25-year public-private partnership signed in December 2018 it is responsible for the 11.5 million hectare Northeastern Protected Area Complex.

name: WWF Central African Republic
summary: Carries out the Dzanga-Sangha wildlife inventory every five years with DSPA, including 2025 eDNA leaf swabs, and relies on ongoing donor support for programme development.

name: Agence Congolaise de la Faune et des Aires Protégées
summary: Public administrative body created by a 2012 law to implement national policy on wildlife, protected areas and anti-poaching units, and tasked with setting up an information system for them.

name: Atlas Forestier Interactif du Congo
summary: A forest information system for Congo, hosted in the forestry ministry, whose 2012 report gave National Forest Estate land-use allocation and land cover as of 31 December 2011, built by WRI and the ministry.

name: CAAPP-Faune
summary: A closed PPECF-funded project, running January 2024 to May 2025 in three Olam Agri-managed forest units in the Republic of Congo, to develop acoustic, camera trap and eDNA methods for monitoring logging's impact on animals.

name: Carte de changement du couvert forestier en République du Congo 2000-2012
summary: Forest cover change map for the Republic of the Congo, 2000 to 2012, built by CNIAF from FACET, GAF and Global Forest Change data as a base for REDD+.

name: Centre National d'Inventaire et d'Aménagement des Ressources Forestières et Fauniques
summary: National forest and wildlife inventory centre that, according to a September 2015 report by its MRV cell, produced the 2000 to 2012 forest cover change map with FAO technical assistance through UN-REDD.

name: Cercle d'Appui à la Gestion Durable des Forêts
summary: Organisation that, according to a WRI report, was created in 2009 and began leading independent forest monitoring in the Republic of the Congo in 2013.

name: Comptoir Juridique Junior
summary: Organisation founded by young lawyers that, RFUK reported in August 2019, was deploying ForestLink at two pilot sites in Likouala and Lékoumou, with 14 community observers and 8 leaders trained.

name: CongoPeat
summary: Five-year project led by Simon Lewis and funded by the UK's Natural Environment Research Council, bringing together six UK universities and five Congolese organisations to study the peatland ecosystem.

name: Conkouati-Douli National Park management partnership
summary: Twenty-year partnership, signed by Noé with the Congolese government in April 2021, to manage the park, including monitoring of its habitats and wildlife; Noé reports relative stability in megafauna monitored since 2013.

name: Conkouati-Douli National Park terrestrial ecological inventory
summary: Terrestrial ecological inventory of the park using line transects, reconnaissance walks and camera traps, with 42 people in eight teams, and the previous inventory more than ten years earlier.

name: Dénombrement international des oiseaux d'eau au Congo
summary: Congolese part of the international waterbird census, which a January 2017 flyway report says was coordinated nationally by Jérôme Mokoko Ikonga, with a park staff member joining counts at Bas-Kouilou.

name: Elephant Listening Project
summary: Acoustic monitoring project begun in 1999 at Cornell University that has worked in Nouabalé-Ndoki National Park since 2017, using 50 recording units to locate poaching and track forest elephants.

name: ESI Congo
summary: A Congolese association, active since 2009 on great apes and Congo Basin biodiversity, whose inventories between Conkouati and Dimonika showed western lowland gorillas, and which is funded by the Fonds Français pour l'Environnement Mondial.

name: ForestLink
summary: Rainforest Foundation UK programme that lets communities send real-time alerts of illegal forest activity, even without connectivity, and has been deployed in the Republic of Congo among other countries.

name: Goualougo Triangle Ape Project
summary: Begun in 1999 and directed by its co-founders, it uses passive field cameras and aims to assess logging effects on apes using timber inventory data and satellite imagery.

name: HELP Congo
summary: Congolese association created in 1990 to protect chimpanzees and conserve biodiversity in Conkouati-Douli National Park, with activities including censuses and planned work on environmental DNA and camera placement.

name: Jane Goodall Institute Congo
summary: Run by the Jane Goodall Institute, it began drone training with Conservation Drones in 2015; 30 camera traps were installed at the institute-managed Tchimpounga reserve in 2019.

name: Lac Télé Community Reserve research and biomonitoring
summary: Ecological monitoring programme in a community reserve, with an annual waterbird census since 1997 that WCS describes as central Africa's longest bird data series, a three-yearly hippo census, and camera traps and acoustic devices.

name: Marien Ngouabi University
summary: A Brazzaville university that co-leads the CongoPeat research programme with Kisangani and Leeds, co-researched a 2024 to 2025 peatland protection report, and whose field school used the Pl@ntNet app offline in April 2024.

name: Mbeli Baï Study
summary: Long-term research site in a 13-hectare swamp forest clearing, studied since 1994, monitoring four flagship species continuously and using video, sound recordings and camera traps for short-term projects, run by the WCS Congo Programme.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement, du Développement Durable et du Bassin du Congo
summary: Ministry whose Direction Générale du Développement Durable staff are listed by the CBD as the country's primary and secondary national focal points, with another member as clearing-house focal point.

name: Ministère de l'Économie Forestière
summary: Ministry responsible for Congo’s forest resources and the regulatory framework for wildlife, forests and sustainable development, supervising ACFAP and CNIAF.

name: Mondika research site
summary: Research site created in 1995 that monitors human-habituated gorilla groups daily, studying their social dynamics, habitat use, response to environmental change and emerging diseases.

name: Ndoki-Likouala wildlife survey
summary: Five-yearly survey estimating large mammal density and abundance across more than 34,000 square kilometres of protected areas and logging concessions, with four surveys in 20 years, the latest in 2022.

name: Nouabalé-Ndoki Foundation
summary: Foundation formed through a WCS and forestry ministry partnership, reporting SMART analysis of patrol data and EarthRanger equipment in Nouabalé-Ndoki National Park’s operations room.

name: Projet de Gestion des Écosystèmes Périphériques au Parc
summary: Collaboration established in 1999 between the forest ministry, CIB and WCS in the buffer zone of Nouabalé-Ndoki National Park, with a 2024 report describing an ecological monitoring team and SMART use.

name: Renatura Congo
summary: Congolese association created in Pointe-Noire in 2005 that studies and protects marine species, monitoring turtle nesting beaches by tagging and GPS recording from September to March.

name: Système Informatique de Vérification de la Légalité
summary: Forest administration tool for recording legality and traceability data, designed around the APV-FLEGT; a March 2020 guide says national roll-out was starting with the tax module.

name: Système National de Mesure, Notification et Vérification
summary: Says it monitors Congo's forests and greenhouse gas emissions, with satellite mapping, run by the forest inventory centre and being operationalised through an FAO project since 2022.

name: The Aspinall Foundation
summary: A 2021 IUCN article describes BIOPAMA equipment enabling wider reserve patrols and monitoring, and says the foundation raised orphaned gorillas and returned them to the wild.

name: Tracking Large Carnivores in Congo
summary: Finished two-year project begun in May 2020, supported by IUCN Save Our Species and run by the Aspinall Foundation, using camera traps and local staff observations to establish leopard and lion presence in Lésio-Louna Reserve.

name: WCS Congo Programme
summary: Programme of the Wildlife Conservation Society in the Republic of the Congo, active for over 30 years, which runs the Elephant Listening Project and uses EarthRanger, SMART patrol data and Okala for monitoring.

name: WWF Republic of Congo
summary: Funded by WWF Belgium and partnering with the Congolese wildlife agency, this WWF organisation is associated with Ntokou-Pikounda, where WWF Belgium reports elephant and great ape inventories have begun.

name: A biodiversity dashboard for Switzerland
summary: An active project led by Philipp Brun, with Info Flora and Info Fauna, building a web application around machine learning species distribution models.

name: A global satellite-derived coral bleaching dataset (2016–2025)
summary: Dataset of monthly predicted coral bleaching at about 1 km resolution across the global tropics for 2016 to 2025, from a neural network, embargoed until 1 December 2027.

name: ADELE
summary: A deep learning model, run by the Federal Statistical Office, that automates part of the aerial image interpretation for Swiss area statistics, in use since 2022 after a 2017 to 2021 project.

name: AeroecologyCam AC1
summary: An optical monitoring system for birds, insects and other flying objects, built by Swiss Birdradar Solution.

name: Agroscope
summary: Swiss agricultural research centre, affiliated with the Federal Office for Agriculture, that builds ALL-EMA and aims to develop biodiversity recording with remote sensing, AI, insect radar and acoustic ecology.

name: Akustik zum Monitoring schwer nachweisbarer Arten
summary: A project run by the Swiss Ornithological Institute that uses acoustic monitoring for rare, secretive forest birds, with loggers able to record autonomously for several months.

name: Ala, Schweizerische Gesellschaft für Vogelkunde und Vogelschutz
summary: Swiss society for ornithology and bird protection, whose journal in 2009 listed the protected areas it looked after at that time, with their sizes.

name: ALL-EMA
summary: Swiss agricultural biodiversity monitoring programme, built and run by Agroscope for federal offices, recording species and habitat diversity in 194 survey squares since 2015.

name: Alpine POLLinator Observatory
summary: A closed 2022 pilot towards automated vision-based insect monitoring in the Swiss Alps, led by Anne Kempel.

name: Amphibienmonitoring Kanton Zürich
summary: Canton-wide long-term amphibian monitoring in Zurich, set up with BirdLife Zürich and info fauna, in which volunteers recorded 21,300 adult amphibians in 2025.

name: Amt für Landwirtschaft und Natur, Canton of Bern
summary: Bernese cantonal office whose 2024 nature promotion report lists 245 cantonal nature reserves covering 39,625 hectares, alongside spending on their upkeep.

name: AquaGen
summary: A closed project, December 2019 to March 2020, run by ID-Gene ecodiagnostics, that combined environmental genomics and machine learning to predict aquatic ecosystem quality.

name: AQUASCOPE
summary: A project partnered with Eawag that uses statistical models and machine learning to forecast plankton dynamics and water quality, with a camera imaging planktonic microbes without disturbing them.

name: Artenmonitoring in Naturwaldreservaten der Schweiz
summary: Project planned for September 2021 to November 2024 to survey saproxylic beetles and fungi in Swiss beech and spruce-fir forests, comparing natural reserves with managed forests.

name: Ask Your Forest
summary: A model built by Operal that analyses satellite and LiDAR data on demand, including swisstopo canopy height data.

name: AskEarth
summary: Swiss geospatial AI start-up and ETH spin-off making satellite images accessible for environmental and climate monitoring, which closed a CHF 2.26m seed round in 2025.

name: Association de la Grande Cariçaie
summary: Association that has managed the Grande Cariçaie natural heritage since 1982, which comprises 9 cantonal nature reserves and protected zones in Vaud, Fribourg and Neuchâtel covering nearly 3,000 hectares.

name: Association Parc naturel régional Gruyère Pays-d'Enhaut
summary: Association whose stated aims are creating and managing a regional nature park, under federal and cantonal law.

name: Association Parc naturel régional Jura vaudois
summary: Association whose statutes of 2010 state its aim as the creation and management of a regional nature park.

name: Associazione Parco Val Calanca
summary: Association whose statutes state its purpose as managing a regional nature park that is in its establishment phase.

name: Automated detection of invasive alien plants along highways
summary: A closed project, led by Michael Nobis, that used a deep learning mapping approach to detect invasive alien plants along highways.

name: Automated Monitoring to Evaluate and Inform Conservation Actions
summary: A proposed project, led by Philipp Brun, that plans to combine UAVs, camera traps and automated species identification in 2027 to 2028.

name: Barry Callebaut
summary: Company that, FoodIngredientsFirst reported in May 2021, launched an indicative High Carbon Stock map for Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines with EcoVision Lab.

name: BatScope
summary: A model built by the WSL Swiss Federal Research Institute that handles BATLOGGER data and automatically recognises the calling bat species.

name: BeaverWatch
summary: Non-profit association for beaver monitoring in Switzerland, mainly active in western Switzerland, doing population monitoring and field surveys, with a mandate for the Canton of Vaud since 2010.

name: Belle robot fish
summary: Robot fish built by ETH Zurich that, Euronews reports, was designed to collect data in a minimally invasive way.

name: Bern University of Applied Sciences
summary: University of applied sciences whose HAFL work includes a toolkit creating forest stand maps from remote sensing data, a planned 2019 to 2022 Togo forest monitoring project and FINT-CH.

name: BioAIRad
summary: An in-progress project, started 7 May 2025 and led by Silke Bauer with four partners, aiming to advance radar biodiversity monitoring with a focus on insect identification.

name: BioDetect
summary: A closed 2020 to 2022 project, led by Catherine Graham, on open-source computer vision and deep learning tools for biodiversity monitoring.

name: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Index
summary: A dataset built by Swiss Re that lets governments and businesses compare the state of local ecosystems.

name: Biodiversity Digital Academy
summary: A programme for which, in June 2023, ten participants (seven Swiss early-stage start-ups, three non-profits) had been selected for six months of support, resources and mentorship; digitalswitzerland built it.

name: Biodiversity Estimation from Satellite Images
summary: A completed project run by the Institute of Geodesy and Photogrammetry that combined dense satellite imagery with in-situ data from Swiss institutions, including Agroscope.

name: Biodiversity Indicator and Reporting System
summary: Biodiversity assessment system built by Holcim and IUCN, which Holcim used to set its 2024 baseline and plans to use to measure improvement in its quarries.

name: Biodiversity Monitoring Switzerland
summary: A long-term observation programme, run by the Federal Office for the Environment, surveying species diversity in select plants and animals on a three-network sampling grid, with over a hundred biologists collecting data for FOEN.

name: Biodiversity Sensor Project
summary: Sensor built by Syngenta Group that uses machine learning to locate and count bee pollinators in real time, identifying four species with over 90% accuracy.

name: Biolovision Sàrl
summary: An active organisation that developed the NaturaList app.

name: BioMonI
summary: An active project, funded by Biodiversa+ and partnered with the Université de Neuchâtel, that plans to provide tested methods combining long-term monitoring with environmental DNA and remote sensing.

name: Biosfera Val Müstair
summary: Public-law institution since 2017, led strategically by a 14-person commission, for a regional nature park covering 199 km2, the whole territory of the municipality.

name: BirdLife Zürich
summary: Organisation on whose behalf annual breeding bird counts are carried out across Zurich canton, with over 100 volunteer specialists surveying between March and July.

name: BirdScan bat classifier
summary: An AI classifier, built by Swiss Birdradar Solution, that discerns between birds and bats from wing beat activity.

name: BirdScan MR1
summary: Compact radar for long-term quantitative monitoring of birds and bats, which uses wing-flapping patterns to exclude insect echoes, and is listed under the maker's legacy systems.

name: BirdScan reference data repository
summary: A dataset run by Swiss Birdradar Solution, with several thousand labelled echoes, used to validate the classification modules.

name: BLOSSOM
summary: An ongoing project (1 January 2026 to 31 December 2028), run by FiBL, exploring modern technologies to monitor ground beetle diversity in cherry orchards with non-lethal, cost-effective methods.

name: Canton of Aargau, Abteilung Landschaft und Gewässer
summary: Cantonal department that has monitored species diversity in the ordinarily used landscape through the LANAG programme since 1996 and is the fact sheet's named contact.

name: CAPTAIN
summary: An open-source package, built by Daniele Silvestro, that integrates biodiversity data, conservation budgets, human pressures and climate change.

name: cargoscreen
summary: Organisation that builds digital tools to screen containerised cargo for illegal wildlife, uses machine learning to improve shipment risk scores, and received a Microsoft AI for Earth grant in April 2019.

name: ChirpNet
summary: A closed project (June 2024 to May 2025), led by Matthias Nyfeler and funded by the ZHAW Digital Futures Fund, that developed a deep learning model for classifying grasshopper sounds recorded on smartphones.

name: ChirpScan: Monitoring grasshopper biodiversity with an AI-driven mobile app
summary: An active project, run by the Zurich University of Applied Sciences and led by Tobias Peter, that develops a mobile app using AI to identify grasshopper species.

name: CitizenBees
summary: Company in Neuchatel, Switzerland, offering rooftop urban beekeeping with sensors and webcams linking hives to the internet, plus biomonitoring that treats the bee as a sampler of its environment.

name: Copernicus Technologies
summary: An active organisation that its The Things Network profile describes as a Swiss start-up focused on wildlife tracking.

name: Crowther Lab
summary: Research group studying global ecosystems for biodiversity and climate, which founded the open restoration data platform Restor and lists a November 2023 publication on global natural forest carbon potential.

name: CSEM
summary: An active organisation that published the announcement of the neophyte radar.

name: Curbing Illegal Logging Patterns using Sound-Based Detection Techniques
summary: A project funded by Climate Change AI, listed on its innovation grants page with five named researchers.

name: Dalle Molle Institute for Artificial Intelligence
summary: A joint institute of USI and SUPSI, which partners with ALP-AI and supplies its project manager and deputy.

name: Datalakes
summary: Platform for searching, visualising and downloading data on Swiss lakes, described by Eawag as a data platform for modelling and forecasting, with the Swiss Data Science Center.

name: Decentlab
summary: A Swiss company providing wireless sensor devices and services for distributed monitoring, listed on the TreeNet about page.

name: DecodeNAture
summary: An active organisation whose products are FloraDecode and AquaDecode, two portable DNA platforms for identification in the field.

name: DeepDive
summary: An open source model, free to use, that learns from synthetic fossil record datasets to estimate global biodiversity patterns through time, with a 2024 paper listed by OpenAlex.

name: Digital Botanical Gardens Initiative
summary: Open science pilot run by the Earth Metabolome Initiative, using mass spectrometry to profile the chemistry of botanical garden plants and integrate the data into an open, searchable atlas.

name: digitalswitzerland
summary: Organisation that launched the Biodiversity Digital Academy in May 2023.

name: DIMPEO
summary: Completed project run by the Swiss Data Science Center, started 1 February 2024, that developed a neural-network vegetation model using Sentinel-2 imagery to detect anomalous forest browning.

name: Direction générale de l'environnement, Canton of Vaud
summary: Vaud environment directorate that held an August 2026 information session on protecting the haute-Versoix marshes; the canton presented its first biodiversity monitoring in October 2025.

name: DNAi
summary: Completed project run by the Swiss Data Science Center, started 1 September 2022, that developed machine learning approaches to process raw eDNA metabarcoding data at high throughput.

name: DNAir
summary: Zürich company (DNAir AG) capturing environmental DNA from air with automated sensors; an investment profile describes arrangements with ETH and WSL collaborators to validate its air sampler.

name: Drone for biodiversity identification in dense forest
summary: Drone developed by WSL and ETH Zurich to identify biodiversity in forests, with its current status unknown.

name: Earth Metabolome Initiative
summary: Open, collaborative effort built by Pierre-Marie Allard to document the world's chemodiversity, aiming to create reusable standards, software and data services, with DBGI as a pilot.

name: ecospat
summary: Programme offering an R package for spatial analyses and modelling of species niches and distributions, built by Antoine Guisan and run by the University of Lausanne.

name: Ecosystems and Landscape Evolution group
summary: Group run by ETH Zurich that combines biological monitoring, eDNA metabarcoding, remote sensing and field sampling, analysed with statistical and process-based models.

name: Einwohnergemeinde Diemtigen
summary: Municipality that its park regulation names as the managing body (Trägerin) of the Diemtigtal regional nature park.

name: Empa
summary: Dübendorf organisation described in a November 2020 Greater Zurich Area report on drones that attach sensors to trees to help monitor environmental and ecological changes in forests.

name: EnviDat
summary: Portal run and built by the WSL Swiss Federal Research Institute that gives managed access to environmental monitoring and research data and can host and publish data sets.

name: ETH Swiss GeoLab
summary: ETH Zurich programme led by Verena Griess that opened at Root near Lucerne on 16 October 2026, with an AI-based geoinformation platform planned.

name: ExoLabs
summary: Zurich-registered company linked to planned development of SILVA with WSL and ETH EcoVision Lab, whose classifiers support the Swiss government on 99 land use and land cover categories.

name: Exploiting the full potential of Copernicus Sentinel data for countrywide tree species mapping
summary: A closed project, dated 2019 to 2023, led by Lars Waser and funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation, on using Copernicus Sentinel data for countrywide tree species mapping.

name: Fachstelle Naturschutz, Canton of Zurich
summary: Zurich cantonal nature conservation office, within the Amt für Landschaft und Natur, whose staff look after reserves of more than communal importance, with rangers in most larger ones.

name: Federal Office for the Environment
summary: Federal authority for biodiversity and landscape that runs Switzerland's landscape and biodiversity monitoring programmes and announced a November 2025 conference in Bern on AI in environmental observation.

name: Federal Office of Topography
summary: Switzerland's geoinformation centre, which runs the National Point of Contact for Satellite Images and held a December 2024 colloquium on large language models and geodata.

name: Federal Statistical Office
summary: Runs Swiss land use statistics and ADELE, which Netzwoche calls a deep learning model; the office reports automatic classification of about a quarter of sample points from 2022.

name: FHNW University of Applied Sciences and Arts Northwestern Switzerland
summary: University whose Institute of Geomatics participated with ExoLabs in an August 2018 to October 2020 pilot involving a software prototype based on deep neural networks and random forests.

name: FINT-CH
summary: Project led by Luuk Dorren that aimed to develop a method for large-area characterisation of forest structures, planned for October 2018 to December 2021.

name: Fishlab
summary: Valais start-up at the Energypolis campus in Sion that used machine learning models to recognise and identify fish species.

name: FlorID
summary: Model that identifies Swiss plant species from photos, location and date, trained on almost 1.5 million photos of 3,076 species, built by Philipp Brun and WSL with Info Flora as partner.

name: Fondation Valery
summary: Non-profit founded in 2018 in Lausanne for environmental protection, ecological values and renewable energy, whose portfolio includes pages on autonomous and airborne eDNA monitoring.

name: Fondazione del Monte San Giorgio
summary: Foundation that a 2023 news article names as the managing body (ente gestore) of the Swiss part of the transnational Monte San Giorgio World Heritage site.

name: Fore[st]cast
summary: Project that aims to develop a platform reporting the current and predicted condition of trees, building on the TreeNet network at WSL, listed as in progress.

name: Forest mix rate NFI
summary: Dataset using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data at 10-metre resolution and machine learning, building on Sentinel-2.

name: Foresta
summary: Project that turns LiDAR point clouds into inventories of individual trees, built by Schweiz3D and funded by Gebert Rüf Stiftung.

name: FORESTS
summary: Closed project, run from March 2024 to March 2025 and led by Idiap, that aimed to improve alpine forest mapping and apply it to aerial imagery of Valais dating back to the 1940s.

name: Fotofallenmonitoring Reh & Gämse im Kanton Bern
summary: Camera-trap monitoring of roe deer in several Bernese areas over two years, and of chamois in the Napf area, which started in February 2026.

name: FutureSpecies.CH: Which species will enter Switzerland under climate change? Implications for law, policy and practice
summary: Project that will compile lists of newcomer species expected to find suitable conditions in Switzerland by 2035 and 2060, then refine forecasts to identify likely entry points.

name: FuturProof
summary: Project run by Eawag, part of National Research Programme 82, that uses eDNA in rivers and groundwater to deliver indicators for authorities.

name: Förderverein Region Gantrisch
summary: Association that is the managing body (Träger) of the Gantrisch regional nature park.

name: GAMMA Remote Sensing
summary: Organisation based in Gümligen, Switzerland, that builds ESA CCI+ Biomass and has the technical lead on it, including generation of the global biomass products.

name: GBIF Swiss Node
summary: Swiss node of GBIF, which provides maintenance infrastructure and technical support for SwissNatColl.

name: Gebert Rüf Stiftung
summary: Foundation that approved CHF 25,000 for Schweiz3D's Foresta project on 22 June 2026.

name: Gemeindeverband UNESCO Biosphäre Entlebuch
summary: Municipal association of seven municipalities that forms the Biosphere Entlebuch, a UNESCO biosphere reserve of 396 km2.

name: Geoembeddings of Switzerland
summary: Annual TESSERA-based Swiss geoembeddings provided by the Swiss Data Cube team, with December 2025 reporting full 2024 and partial 2017–2023 coverage, and completion planned for 2026.

name: GeoFusion Swiss
summary: Organisation whose remote sensing services include forest density and species level forest mapping, and land use and land cover mapping for environmental applications.

name: Geospatial AI × Biodiversity
summary: Eawag-run project that plans an open-source geospatial model for ecology and biodiversity prediction, and names a multimodal AI framework.

name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility Switzerland
summary: Swiss GBIF programme under the Federal Office for the Environment’s aegis, aiming in the long term to register all specimens in Switzerland’s botanical, palaeontological and zoological collections.

name: GRID-Geneva
summary: Organisation which the Swiss Data Cube team page says jointly develops and manages the data cube.

name: Grün Stadt Zürich
summary: City department that carries out care and maintenance in the supra-municipal protected areas at Katzensee, Wehrenbach and Uetliberg.

name: Habitat Map of Switzerland
summary: Closed 2019 to 2021 project, led by Bronwyn Price and funded by the Federal Office for the Environment, that used remote sensing to develop a semi-automated habitat mapping method that can be rerun on updated data.

name: HES-SO University of Applied Sciences and Arts Western Switzerland
summary: Western Switzerland university of applied sciences whose schools are named on Hungry Mills with Earthworm Foundation, and which is named on MoBiKo.

name: Hintermann & Weber AG
summary: A Swiss organisation that coordinates all Biodiversity Monitoring Switzerland activities on behalf of the Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN).

name: Holcim
summary: Company that says it assessed its biodiversity baseline in all active and non-active quarries in 2024 using BIRS, and plans to measure again by 2030.

name: Hungry Mills
summary: A closed project, scheduled to finish by September 2026, that aimed to predict deforestation risks linked to palm oil production.

name: HUVI.GUARDIAN
summary: An early-warning tower for remote forests using vision and edge AI, built and run by HUVI.SWISS, partnered with a Zurich university of applied sciences and funded by Innosuisse.

name: HUVI.SWISS
summary: A company in Kölliken, Switzerland, developing autonomous AI-based wildfire detection systems; its HUVI.GUARDIAN tower has had prototype field tests and Innosuisse has funded a two-year project since 2026.

name: ID-Gene ecodiagnostics
summary: A Swiss start-up in Geneva, founded in 2014 as a University of Geneva spin-off, offering environmental DNA and genetic tests for biodiversity assessment and environmental monitoring.

name: Idiap Research Institute
summary: A research institute in Martigny that the Swiss Confederation recognises as an institute of national importance.

name: IMAGINE
summary: An active project run by Agroscope that develops domain-specific models, including for biodiversity assessment, and names reinforcement learning.

name: IMPACT
summary: A Biodiversa+-funded project that plans to merge traditional monitoring techniques with eDNA technologies to support parasite biodiversity monitoring in aquatic ecosystems.

name: info fauna
summary: The national data and information centre on Swiss fauna, which publishes free 5 by 5 km distribution maps of animal species and is a member of Info Species.

name: Info Flora
summary: A non-profit foundation with offices in Geneva, Bern and Lugano, serving as the national data centre for Swiss wild plants, with FlorApp for reporting observations.

name: InfoSpecies
summary: An association acting as umbrella for Switzerland's national species data centres, whose databases hold more than 15 million records and which shares data through GBIF.

name: Innosuisse
summary: A funder that has been supporting a two-year HUVI.SWISS innovation project since 2026.

name: Institute Land-Nature-Environment, HES-SO
summary: An institute at HES-SO in Jussy that is named as a project partner of TRANSPONDER.

name: Institute of Geodesy and Photogrammetry
summary: An ETH Zurich institute whose core competences include photogrammetry, image analysis and remote sensing, and which completed a project on automating biodiversity estimation with deep learning and overhead imagery.

name: Integrating comprehensive species data into biodiversity assessments
summary: A SIB-led, Swiss National Science Foundation-funded project developing models combining occurrence data, genomics, traits and taxonomic changes, with AI-assisted text mining planned for traits.

name: Jörg G. Bucherer-Foundation
summary: A foundation that, ETH Zurich announced in July 2025, would give the university 10 million Swiss francs a year for ten years to establish an Earth observation centre.

name: KORA
summary: A foundation based in Ittigen that monitors wolves, lynx and wildcats, including camera trap monitoring in four reference areas in winter 2025/2026.

name: KORA Monitoring Centre
summary: A programme whose public data are generally shown with a delay of at least three months.

name: Künstliche Intelligenz für die Arealstatistik der Schweiz
summary: A closed pilot project, August 2018 to October 2020, built by FHNW and Denis Jordan, that developed a prototype workflow to classify area-statistics sample points with machine learning.

name: Lac Léman Exploration
summary: Joint project of Eawag, EPFL and the universities of Lausanne and Geneva, with a ten-year platform on Lake Geneva combining in-situ, remote sensing and modelling data.

name: LANAT 3: Preventing biodiversity loss in waterbodies despite climate change
summary: Project led by Ole Seehausen that has developed an Explainable AI approach to identify which environmental factors make a habitat good or bad for a species.

name: Langfristüberwachung der Artenvielfalt in der Normallandschaft des Kantons Aargau
summary: Aargau programme, run by the canton, that measures species diversity from counts of breeding birds, butterflies, snails and plants, and maps species richness using statistical models.

name: Living Switzerland
summary: A project described as building a digital twin of the environment with satellite data and AI, built by the University of Geneva, delivering 10 m land cover maps and time series since 2018.

name: Long-term Forest Ecosystem Research
summary: An active programme, run by the WSL Swiss Federal Research Institute, with 19 permanent monitoring sites measured regularly since 1994.

name: Maphilindo High Carbon Stock map
summary: A dataset identifying forests with high conservation value, built by Barry Callebaut and Ecovision Lab, with its current status unknown.

name: METAPLANTCODE
summary: An active project running from 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2027 with a grant of about 2.5 million euros, aiming to harmonise plant metabarcoding practice.

name: MIMAS: Machine-learning-based Insect Monitoring and Analysis System
summary: An active insect monitoring project commissioned by FOEN's Biodiversity and Landscape Division, built by Info Fauna with WSL, with its implementation phase running 2025 to 2028.

name: MoBiKo
summary: An active project, selected in the SDSC national calls to start in 2025, that proposes extracting mountain biodiversity knowledge from literature into a graph database.

name: Monitoring Common Breeding Birds
summary: An active bird survey run by the Swiss Ornithological Institute, which Agroscope names as a partner programme for birdlife.

name: MoSTFun
summary: An active project, funded by Biodiversa+, that aims to include aquatic fungi in routine biodiversity monitoring at continental scale.

name: Mountain Invasion Research Network
summary: A programme whose MIREN survey records of vascular plants along mountain roads, observed between 2007 and 2023, are held on Zenodo; its current status is unknown.

name: Mountain Research Initiative
summary: An active organisation that co-leads GEO Mountains.

name: National Point of Contact for Satellite Images
summary: An active programme serving as Switzerland's national contact point for satellite data users, which sells images and created free Sentinel-2 mosaics of Switzerland for 2017 to 2020.

name: National Research Programme 82
summary: A research programme run and funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation, supporting 15 projects with 11.2 million francs to seek practical solutions for biodiversity and ecosystem services.

name: National Surface Water Quality Monitoring Programme
summary: An active programme run by the Federal Office for the Environment, whose TREND network studies rivers and streams at about 140 sites.

name: Natural History Museum of Geneva
summary: Switzerland's largest natural history museum, holding fauna, minerals and fossils, which is closed for renovation with public reopening planned for 2028.

name: NaturaList
summary: An active programme built by Biolovision and funded by the Swiss Ornithological Institute, whose data are shared with partner databases run by nature conservation organisations.

name: Naturvielfalt.ch
summary: An active portal for recording flora, fauna and mushrooms in Switzerland.

name: Neophyte radar
summary: A research project of unknown status, described in August 2024 as aiming to detect invasive plants from the air using drones and AI.

name: NOCTUA
summary: A fixed-wing UAV with hydrogen fuel cell power and onboard AI for real-time detection, with missions including anti-poaching, wildfire detection and forest health.

name: Office cantonal de l'agriculture et de la nature, Geneva
summary: Geneva cantonal office named in the landscape, habitat and flora protection regulation as the competent authority, which must start a protection procedure where lasting site protection is planned.

name: Operal
summary: An active organisation that builds Ask Your Forest, which a case note describes as satellite AI in plain language.

name: OPPAL
summary: An organisation whose volunteers watch over flocks on mountain pastures at night, and whose video dataset is the basis for WolfCam.

name: ORDNA
summary: A model for deep learning ordination of raw eDNA samples, listed by OpenAlex with a 2025 paper.

name: OST Eastern Switzerland University of Applied Sciences
summary: University of Applied Sciences that builds VegEye, made at its ILF institute, with a 2021 student algorithm for finding invasive plants in drone images developed with its AI centre.

name: Otterspotter
summary: A closed otter survey run and built by WWF Bern/Solothurn and Pro Lutra, covering Bern and Solothurn rivers in winter 2017/2018; its 2019/20 round budget was 27,000 francs.

name: PanEco Foundation
summary: A foundation whose rangers work in the Thurauen floodplain almost daily and check compliance with the protection ordinance.

name: Porini Foundation
summary: A Swiss charity building a bridge between technology and conservation, and a partner of Tech4Nature.

name: Pro Lutra
summary: A competence centre for the otter in Switzerland, with over 20 years of research on the species, which carried out the Otterspotter survey with WWF Bern/Solothurn in 2017/2018.

name: Pro Natura
summary: A Swiss nature conservation organisation, based centrally in Basel, which in a 2020 internship notice planned an effect check of ponds from its 2013–2015 amphibian campaign.

name: Pro Natura Thurgau
summary: Nature organisation whose members' magazine has a reserve care section and names its reserve caretakers (Reservatspfleger) as leading its work days.

name: Research Institute of Organic Agriculture
summary: Research institute that describes itself as a leading institute in organic agriculture and is project manager of BLOSSOM.

name: rrreefs
summary: Zurich-registered reef restorer founded as an association in 2020 that installed 820 3D-printed terracotta modules in Pujada Bay, Philippines, and monitors reefs six-monthly for three years.

name: Safora
summary: An active project building real-time electric fence monitoring for conservation and agriculture, which reports logging over 500 alerts including poaching attempts.

name: sarmap
summary: A company in Caslano, Switzerland, founded in 1998 as a spin-off of the University of Zurich and Polytechnic of Milan, with a mission on Earth observation for land cover information.

name: School of Engineering and Management of Vaud
summary: Vaud engineering and management school which a 2012 King's College London release names as a collaborator, with CIAT, The Nature Conservancy and King's, on Terra-i.

name: Schweiz3D
summary: An organisation that builds Foresta, which aims to provide tree-level forest inventories from LiDAR using AI.

name: Service des forêts et de la nature du canton de Fribourg
summary: Cantonal service whose page on nature reserves says Fribourg has eight cantonal nature reserves, including the south shore of Lake Neuchâtel, the Singine gorges and Lake Pérolles.

name: SGS
summary: Certification and verification body that selected Meridia as technology partner for worldwide EUDR assurance, and says it was the first body accredited to the FSC EUDR Regulatory Module.

name: SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics
summary: A national organisation for biomedical and biological data, with an Environmental Bioinformatics Group led by Robert Waterhouse, which in September 2021 reported joining a reference genome sequencing pilot through the Swiss node of the European Reference Genome Atlas.

name: Sihlwald biodiversity and forest structure project
summary: Closed project, run by Bern University of Applied Sciences from July 2016 to December 2021, that studied links between forest structure and the biodiversity of several taxonomic groups in the Sihlwald.

name: SILVA: Satellite-Based Inspection of Large Vegetated Areas
summary: A project funded by the Swiss Space Center, with EcoVision Lab and WSL, that aims to detect forest disturbances in near real time with daily updates at 20-metre resolution.

name: SmartHabitat
summary: A project led by Philipp Brun and funded by the Swiss Data Science Center, developing algorithms that semi-automatically identify plant communities from videos.

name: Space Exchange Switzerland
summary: A closed national platform whose 2021 to 2024 mandate aimed to help Swiss bodies use earth observation data.

name: Spatial sustainable finance: Satellite-based ratings of company footprints in biodiversity and water
summary: An active project, run by Zurich University of Applied Sciences with the University of Zurich, aiming to rate companies on their contribution and exposure to environmental degradation using satellite data.

name: SPEEDMIND
summary: A completed project run by the Swiss Data Science Center, started in December 2017, that proposed data mining and iterative machine learning to improve biodiversity models, with Swiss floristic data as a pilot.

name: State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation
summary: A federal body whose Space Division, the Swiss Space Office, is the competence centre for space matters, and which funds the National Point of Contact for Satellite Images at the University of Zurich.

name: Stiftung Bannriet
summary: Foundation whose purpose, per a foundation directory entry, is the lasting preservation and ecological enhancement of the Bannriet protected area, and which may acquire property.

name: Stiftung Fledermausschutz
summary: Foundation that uses a light barrier at roost entrances to count bats entering and leaving, to monitor colony numbers more precisely, and partners with Zoo Zurich and a bioacoustics group.

name: Stiftung Reusstal
summary: A foundation acting on behalf of Aargau and Zürich in the Reusstal decree area south of Bremgarten and adjoining areas in Zürich.

name: Stiftung UNESCO Welterbe Schweizer Alpen Jungfrau-Aletsch
summary: Foundation whose purpose is the sustainable development of the UNESCO World Heritage site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch.

name: Swiss Academy of Sciences
summary: An academy serving science and society, leading SwissCollNet and housing national park research commission management, which the Swiss Parks Network says hosts its FOEN-mandated research coordination office.

name: Swiss Area Statistics
summary: A dataset run by the Federal Statistical Office giving detail on land use and land cover and their change, with four surveys up to 2018 reported as each using 4.1 million sample points.

name: Swiss Bat Bioacoustics Group
summary: An active group of Swiss bat bioacoustics experts, partnering with the Federal Office for the Environment, aiming to establish bioacoustic methods and write validation guidelines.

name: Swiss Biodiversity Dashboard
summary: An active project, led by Philipp Brun and built and funded by WSL, designed as permanent modular infrastructure for species models using citizen science data and deep learning.

name: Swiss Biodiversity Forum
summary: A programme that describes itself as the scientific competence centre for biodiversity and ecosystem services in Switzerland.

name: Swiss Birdradar Solution AG
summary: A Winterthur company whose radar systems detect, classify, track and report aerial biomass in real time, sold to researchers collecting data on birds, bats and insects, and reported by it as deployed worldwide.

name: Swiss Data Cube
summary: A dataset of Landsat and Sentinel-2 data, run by several bodies including the University of Geneva and built by it and GRID-Geneva, meant to support Swiss government environmental monitoring and reporting.

name: Swiss Data Science Center
summary: A national data science and AI research infrastructure in the ETH domain, created in 2017 by EPFL and ETH Zurich, whose environment work includes deep learning for biodiversity detection.

name: Swiss Landscape Monitoring Program LABES
summary: An active programme, run by WSL and the Federal Office for the Environment, in which physical aspects of the landscape are analysed from partner data or remote sensing data.

name: Swiss Mosquito Network
summary: A programme funded by the Federal Office for the Environment to monitor invasive mosquitoes, running nationwide surveillance of entry points and sending validated data to InfoFauna.

name: Swiss National Assessment of Lake Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
summary: Active project, led by Anita Narwani and funded by NRP 82, that will develop biodiversity monitoring methods and make the first nationwide assessment of more than 200 Swiss lakes.

name: Swiss National Forest Inventory
summary: A WSL-run programme collaborating with the Federal Office for the Environment, in its fifth inventory during 2018–2026, with field teams collecting data on about 6,500 sample plots.

name: Swiss National Park
summary: Switzerland's only national park, committed to strict protection and research, which a 2023 University of Zurich release said holds about 1.5 million camera trap images and was working on AI to analyse them.

name: Swiss National Park Data Center
summary: A dataset that links projects, publications and geographical data sources for the Swiss National Park.

name: Swiss National Science Foundation
summary: A funding body that launched the call for National Research Programme 82, on a Federal Council mandate, seeking practical solutions for biodiversity and ecosystem services, and is the Swiss partner in Biodiversa+.

name: Swiss Ornithological Institute
summary: A private non-profit foundation based in Sempach that monitors the populations of all bird species in Switzerland, with over 2,000 volunteers and an Aeroecology group using radar on birds, bats and insects.

name: Swiss Parks Network
summary: An organisation whose research page describes coordination of research across parks.

name: Swiss Re
summary: An organisation whose institute developed the BES Index.

name: Swiss Space Office
summary: The federal government's competence centre for space, within the State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation; most Swiss space activity is carried out with the European Space Agency.

name: Swiss Wildlife Company
summary: An organisation that develops low-power devices to record wildlife.

name: SwissAIM
summary: A programme built by the WSL Swiss Federal Research Institute that aims to combine established forest monitoring procedures with remote sensing and eDNA, with field trials planned for 2022 and further tests in 2023.

name: SwissCollNet
summary: A programme led by the Swiss Academy of Sciences that works to improve access to natural history collections and was granted a two-year extension in December 2023.

name: SwissEnvEO
summary: A dataset repository of ready-to-use national products derived from satellite data, building on the Swiss Data Cube.

name: SwissForestLab
summary: A research platform and infrastructural network for forest research in Switzerland, with its coordination office at WSL and the Federal Office for the Environment as a partner.

name: SwissFungi
summary: A dataset of distribution maps of fungi recorded in Switzerland, excluding lichenised species, forming part of the Info Species national data centre.

name: SwissLichens
summary: The national data and information centre for Swiss lichens, funded by the Federal Office for the Environment and WSL, and partnered with Info Species.

name: SwissNatColl
summary: A programme whose portal offers open access to specimen data from collections preserved in Switzerland, and which is listed among the GBIF node's publishers.

name: Syngenta Group
summary: Basel-based company whose Biodiversity Sensor Project aims for a low-cost, solar-powered prototype that uses a machine-learning model, trained on GBIF, iNaturalist and field data, to identify and count insects.

name: TerraSpectrum
summary: A Swiss start-up founded in 2023 and headquartered in Geneva, working on nature-based solutions and ecosystem monitoring, which says it uses AI-driven tools to measure carbon stocks, biodiversity and ecosystem services.

name: Tierpark Bern
summary: Zoo that reintroduces stag beetles and monitors which structures they colonise fastest, and has joined Stadtgrün Bern and the Natural History Museum to upgrade rare beetle habitats along the Aare.

name: Tool-Explore
summary: A closed 2022 to 2023 project, led by Catherine Graham and funded by WSL, that developed a low-power alpine camera system, recorded over 3,000 hours of footage, and field-tested it at the Furkapass in summer 2023.

name: TOPODRONE
summary: A Swiss designer and maker of surveying equipment for UAVs, headquartered in Montreux, with forest monitoring among its application areas.

name: TreeNet
summary: An international network analysing automated stem radius measurements from point dendrometers, with sub-networks TreeNet Switzerland and TreeNet Europe, run by WSL and ETH Zurich and funded by the Federal Office for the Environment.

name: TubeCam
summary: A project built by the Zurich University of Applied Sciences, where a September 2017 release describes low-maintenance prototypes that automatically upload images, with the system still in testing.

name: UNEP/GRID-Geneva
summary: An organisation described by the Geneva Environment Network as a partnership of UNEP, FOEN and the University of Geneva, whose scientists it says process satellite imagery and model geospatial data.

name: University of Applied Sciences and Arts of Southern Switzerland
summary: A university whose Institute of Microbiology is a partner of MoSTFun.

name: University of Applied Sciences and Arts Western Switzerland
summary: A university named as a partner of METAPLANTCODE.

name: University of Basel
summary: University represented in OpenAlex-listed 2026 papers on Sentinel-2 peatland mapping and a Swiss butterfly index, and a Zenodo dataset predicting coral bleaching with a neural network.

name: University of Bern
summary: A university that hosts the Global Mountain Biodiversity Assessment's International Project Office, and is linked to a paper on AI bioacoustic wolf monitoring and to the DIMPEO and MoBiKo projects.

name: University of Fribourg
summary: A university where a team led by Daniele Silvestro trained the CAPTAIN software (reported April 2022), and whose AI-based tools were reported in December 2022 to have supported a review of Madagascar's biodiversity.

name: University of Lausanne
summary: A university whose members wrote the ecospat R package for species niche and distribution modelling, and which co-hosts the Global Mountain Biodiversity Assessment's International Project Office and lists the N-SDM platform.

name: Université de Neuchâtel
summary: A university whose conservation biology laboratory member Delphine Clara Zemp is listed on a sound-based illegal logging detection project among the Climate Change AI Innovation Grants 2023.

name: UPSCALE: Novel avenues to forest monitoring
summary: Active project led by Verena Griess, partnered with ETH Zurich and funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation, that aims to build a web platform giving real-time information on forest health.

name: ValPar.CH
summary: Active project studying the status and the ecological, economic and social value of ecological infrastructure in four Swiss regional nature parks.

name: VegCHange: A toolbox to investigate anthropogenic changes in the Swiss flora and vegetation
summary: Active project, started in November 2025 and funded by NRP 82, that aims to quantify changes in Swiss flora and vegetation using large, varied data sources and modern statistics.

name: VegEye
summary: Project led by Jasmin Joshi and run by OST that developed drone image analysis, combining RGB and multispectral imagery, to identify invasive goldenrod stands; its page reports late goldenrod on 10% of the Kaltbrunner Riet.

name: Verein Jurapark Aargau
summary: Supporting association (Trägerverein) of the Jurapark Aargau, which held its 36th general meeting in Wittnau on 11 June 2025.

name: Verein Landschaftspark Binntal
summary: Association responsible for implementing and developing the charter of the Binntal regional nature park since the label was awarded in 2011.

name: Verein Lebens- und Erlebnisraum Pfyn-Finges
summary: Association that is the sponsoring body (Trägerschaft) of the Pfyn-Finges nature park, with municipalities, clubs, companies and private persons as members.

name: Verein Naturpark Beverin
summary: Association that a directory page names as the supporting organisation (Trägerorganisation) of the Beverin nature park, which covers nine municipalities.

name: Verein Parc Ela
summary: An association concerned with the Parc Ela regional nature park under the federal nature and heritage law.

name: Verein Region Thal
summary: Association that has been the supporting association (Trägerverein) of the Naturpark Thal since 2010.

name: Verein regionaler Naturpark Chasseral
summary: Association whose statutes of 2024 name it the executing body for the Chasseral regional nature park project.

name: Verein Regionaler Naturpark Schaffhausen
summary: Association organising a park whose first operating phase runs from 2018 to 2027, per a municipal proposal of 9 March 2026, with 15 municipalities connected in that phase.

name: Virtual Forest
summary: Active project, led by Stefan Holm, that creates realistic digital twins of existing forests.

name: Vogelwarte passive acoustic monitoring of rare forest species
summary: Planned nationwide programme, run by the Swiss Ornithological Institute, to monitor rare forest species with volunteers from 2026, at least 100 sites in 2026 and 180 from 2027.

name: Waldmonitoring für Togo's REDD+ Programm
summary: A project, with Bern University of Applied Sciences and the World Bank as partners, that developed satellite methods to derive forest area change (forest meaning at least 30% canopy cover); Togo submitted its reference level to the UNFCCC in 2020 based on the work.

name: Webfauna
summary: Active mobile application, updated in 2025, that is used by Info Fauna.

name: Wild bee nest detection with camera drones
summary: Completed pilot study run by Agroscope, reported in February 2026, testing deep learning on drone images to tell bee nest mounds from other soil deposits, tested on a 120 square metre area.

name: WildAI
summary: Active project run by the Environmental Computational Science and Earth Observation Laboratory, partnered with the Swiss National Park, that aims to model wildlife habitats and wildlife-environment interactions using AI, drone images and camera traps.

name: WildinSync
summary: Active non-profit initiative by WSL and ETH Zurich researchers promoting eDNA for long-term monitoring, with 91 sampling sites in around 30 countries as of August 2025 and data freely available on EnviDat.

name: Wildlife@Campus Grüental
summary: Project run by ZHAW and led by Roland Felix Graf, from April 2020 to December 2021, that set out to develop a three-module monitoring system including automatic image interpretation.

name: Wildnispark Zürich
summary: Park organisation whose foundation supports research and monitoring of the Sihlwald as a natural forest reserve, with a long-term monitoring concept that has recorded rare species such as the lichen Rinodina polyspora.

name: Wildtier Schweiz
summary: Organisation that, according to its 2025 annual report, does applied research and monitoring of native wildlife, including Swiss-wide wildcat monitoring on behalf of FOEN, and lists a polecat monitoring.

name: Wirkungskontrolle Biotopschutz Schweiz
summary: Active long-term monitoring programme built by the Federal Office for the Environment and WSL, acting as an early warning system for the federal government and cantons.

name: WolfCam
summary: Active project, partnered with Oppal and the Idiap Research Institute, that aims to build an AI system detecting wolves from thermal images.

name: WSL multispecies deep learning plant model
summary: Active predictive tool built by WSL, described by its lead author as a deep learning approach, for where plant species occur in Switzerland now and in future.

name: WWF Bern/Solothurn
summary: Organisation whose address a Solothurn government decision of 20 August 2019 gives as 3011 Bern, and which launched the Otterspotter project with Pro Lutra.

name: Wyss Academy for Nature
summary: Organisation whose Bern Hub has operated since 2020 on climate, biodiversity and land use, with an aquatic biodiversity project reporting an Explainable AI approach to habitat suitability.

name: Zoo Zurich
summary: Organisation that, in a February 2024 article, says it initiated an eDNA collection research project with ETH Zurich in its Masoala rainforest.

name: Zurich University of Applied Sciences
summary: Organisation whose wildlife group develops small-mammal detection methods, with work including a tube camera trap, the ChirpScan app and planned acoustic recognition of Orthoptera.

name: Action pour la Conservation de la Biodiversité en Côte d'Ivoire
summary: Ivorian NGO created by researchers in October 2007, working on fauna and flora surveys and ecological monitoring, including a 2017-2019 camera-trap inventory of fauna in the Tanoé-Ehy swamp forest.

name: Addressing Illegal Gold Mining in Taï National Park, Côte d'Ivoire
summary: A CEPF-funded project, dated May to November 2026, to help park authorities detect and dismantle mining sites inside Taï National Park using satellite-based alerts and a web monitoring system.

name: AI-powered Monitoring of Mangrove Biomass and Carbon Stocks (Côte d'Ivoire)
summary: A mangrove biomass and carbon monitoring pilot at Fresco and Sassandra, led and built by data354, using satellite imagery and machine learning calibrated with 300 field plots, now expanding to Senegal.

name: AINTELLIGENCE
summary: Ivorian single-member limited company, registered in Abidjan Marcory, whose EUDR module combines satellite data, optional drone imagery and WDPA inputs with forest-change baselines for deforestation screening and certificates.

name: Akatia
summary: Ivorian NGO, founded in 2017 by its own account, that follows wild chimpanzees in Yapo-Abbé forest and, since 2026, has begun camera-trap, transect and flora monitoring in two concessions under a ten-year EticWood project.

name: Behavioural Ecology of the Common Hippopotamus, amphibius linnaeus, 1758 and Risk Factors for Human-Hippopotamus Conflict in Central Côte d'Ivoire
summary: Project dated February 2024 that planned reconnaissance surveys, camera traps and community interviews to study common hippopotamus behaviour and human conflict risk, aiming to determine their range along the Bandama River.

name: Centre d'Information Géographique et du Numérique (BNETD-CIGN)
summary: According to African Sustainability Matters, Côte d’Ivoire’s national geospatial authority will contribute technical expertise to the ministry’s October 2026 agreement with TerraKora AI.

name: Centre National de Floristique
summary: A biodiversity information and research centre in Abidjan with an arboretum and a herbarium of about 60,000 specimens, publishing 37 datasets through GBIF and run by Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny.

name: Centre Suisse de Recherches Scientifiques en Côte d'Ivoire
summary: A research centre studying biodiversity and nature-based solutions, with a primate station at Taï and a herbarium dataset on GBIF containing 8,896 records.

name: Centre Universitaire de Recherche et d'Application en Télédétection
summary: A remote sensing research centre that receives training in the Comoé drone monitoring project and belongs to two GMES and Africa consortia on wetlands and coastal areas.

name: Chimpanzee research and conservation at Comoé National Park
summary: Chimpanzee research and conservation project at Comoé National Park, with 20 camera traps over 900 km2 in 2014 to 2015 and a planned second phase working with OIPR.

name: Comité National de Télédétection et d'Information Géographique
summary: A national remote sensing and geographic information body that presented a land monitoring geoportal in December 2017, reported as developed with C2D support through the French development agency AFD.

name: Conservation des Espèces Marines
summary: A local non-profit whose members have worked on sea turtle conservation since 2010, using local eco-guards for field work and helping create a voluntary nature reserve since 2016.

name: Côte d'Ivoire BNETD 2020 Land Cover Map
summary: A yearly land cover map at 10 metre pixel size, made by the Ivorian government's geographic centre with EU funding, noted as relevant to checking forest status against the EUDR 2020 cut-off.

name: data354
summary: An organisation listed by ITU as lead partner on a mangrove biomass and carbon monitoring use case in Côte d'Ivoire, responsible for AI model development, field integration and remote sensing.

name: Direction de Zone Nord-Est (OIPR)
summary: OIPR directorate in charge of Comoé National Park, whose director and head of ecological monitoring co-authored the AI-assisted survey paper, and which presented its use of SMART in October 2026.

name: Direction de Zone Ouest (OIPR)
summary: Western zone directorate of the Office Ivoirien des Parcs et Réserves, whose staff were reportedly trained in June 2026 in satellite monitoring, and which reported about 496 elephant camera-trap observations at Mont Péko in 2025.

name: Direction de Zone Sud-Ouest (OIPR)
summary: OIPR directorate whose ecological monitoring and GIS service processed phase 12 SMART data with working group support in 2018, following annual Taï monitoring described in 2016.

name: Dispositif de surveillance sanitaire de la faune sauvage en Côte d'Ivoire
summary: Wildlife health surveillance system launched at Bouna in November 2024 with electronic data collection tools, and backed by a September 2026 ministerial memorandum giving OIPR a monitoring and reporting role in protected areas.

name: Distribution and Conservation Status of Medium and Large Mammals in Residual Forests of South-Eastern Region of Côte d'Ivoire
summary: Closed project whose July 2020 description planned camera traps, agent training and GIS maps of mammal distribution in residual forests of south-eastern Côte d'Ivoire.

name: Distribution and Viability of an Endangered Primate Species, the White-Naped Mangabey in Comoé National Park
summary: Closed project proposed in June 2021 to map the distribution of white-naped mangabeys in Comoé National Park and the factors shaping it, using reconnaissance surveys and camera traps.

name: Drone-based wildlife monitoring in Comoé National Park
summary: A GIZ-commissioned project for 2025 to 2026 developing drone-based wildlife monitoring in Côte d'Ivoire, with a machine learning image analysis workflow and training for OIPR and CURAT.

name: Dénombrement International des Oiseaux d'Eau (DIOE), Côte d'Ivoire
summary: Côte d'Ivoire's annual participation in the International Waterbird Census, run by the Ministry of Water and Forests, which counted 49,305 waterbirds of 68 species at 38 sites in 2026.

name: Détection des pertes d'arbres dans la forêt de Bossématié par drone
summary: Closed drone study by Nitidæ's team, published in Drones, that detected 107 tree losses, about 2 ha, between November 2018 and April 2019 with 97% overall accuracy.

name: EAFI migratory bird monitoring in the Ehotilé Islands
summary: Citizen science project run by SOS-Forêts with BirdLife under the East Atlantic Flyway Initiative, which since 2022 trained 26 volunteers to monitor migratory birds in the Ehotilé Islands.

name: Fondation pour les Parcs et Réserves de Côte d'Ivoire
summary: A foundation that funds the Office Ivoirien des Parcs et Réserves, reported to have signed a 700 million CFA franc agreement for Taï and Comoé parks in 2017.

name: GFA Consulting Group
summary: A consultancy supporting the GIZ drone wildlife monitoring project in 2025 to 2026 with flight planning, survey design and a semi-automated AI image processing workflow.

name: Harnessing Environmental DNA for Mangrove Conservation and Sustainable Management in Côte d'Ivoire's Parc National d'Azagny
summary: A project on environmental DNA for mangrove conservation in Azagny National Park, listed with Nature Metrics Ltd. on CEPF's Guinean Forests of West Africa hotspot page.

name: Improving Freshwater Biodiversity Conservation in Côte d'Ivoire Using DNA-based Monitoring
summary: A closed project, run by NatureMetrics and funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund, that ran from February 2021 to July 2022 and, per its final report, set up Côte d'Ivoire's first miniature barcoding lab.

name: Influence of Climate Variability and Human Activities on the Common Hippopotamus Distribution in the Comoe National Park
summary: Project page from March 2024 describing planned work on hippo distribution, abundance, habitat use and movement in Comoé National Park, using field surveys, camera traps and spatial modelling to improve park monitoring.

name: Institut Botanique Aké-Assi d'Andokoi
summary: A botanical institute whose GBIF dataset reports 7,054 herbarium occurrence records from specimens collected in 1905–2018, with a publisher record describing a collection of about 10,000 West African specimens.

name: Inventaire aérien photographique de la grande faune du Parc national de la Comoé assisté par l'intelligence artificielle (2022)
summary: Closed 2022 field trial in Comoé National Park, run by OIPR, in which the HerdNet model processed 148,239 aerial photographs and deep learning cut human processing effort by 98%.

name: Inventaire Forestier et Faunique National (IFFN)
summary: Closed national forest and wildlife inventory, presented in Abidjan on 29 June 2021, which inventoried 578 taxa and delivered its data to the Ministry of Water and Forests.

name: Mangrove Biomass and Carbon Stocks in Côte d'Ivoire
summary: A CC-BY 4.0 dataset of 300 observations of mangrove biomass and carbon at Sassandra and Fresco, covering January to May 2025, with Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 bands and Lacuna Fund backing.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Transition Écologique (Côte d'Ivoire)
summary: Ivorian environment ministry that, per African Sustainability Matters, signed a 24-month framework agreement with TerraKora AI on 2 October 2026 on ecosystem monitoring, and which oversees the Office Ivoirien des Parcs et Réserves.

name: Ministère des Eaux et Forêts (Côte d'Ivoire)
summary: Ivorian ministry in Abidjan-Plateau that received national inventory data and mapping and satellite monitoring equipment donated by IDH in 2023.

name: National Office of Technical Studies and Development
summary: BNETD, whose geographic and digital information centre is reported as Côte d'Ivoire's national geospatial authority and is to contribute technical expertise to the ministry's agreement with TerraKora AI.

name: Notre Forêt Notre Avenir
summary: Ivorian conservation NGO based in Guiglo, whose forest protection work includes independent observation missions, and which the Wild Chimpanzee Foundation names as its key local partner for independent monitoring.

name: ObservaTerra
summary: Civil-society association observing land, agrarian and forest dynamics, which publishes downloadable forest cover change maps for 2000, 2016 and 2020 for sites including Marahoué, Bayota, Sassandra-Dagbégo and Fresco.

name: Office Ivoirien des Parcs et Réserves
summary: Ivorian body created in 2002 to manage parks and reserves, now covering 19 protected areas, which carries out ecological monitoring including camera traps and, per AIP, recorded about 496 elephant observations in Mont Péko in 2025.

name: OIPR deforestation alert and monitoring system for the Mabi-Yaya Nature Reserve
summary: Deforestation monitoring system used by OIPR, with Mabi-Yaya as its test case; Nitidæ reports training about fifteen agents in late 2022 and verifying seven alerts in the field.

name: Programme de Recherche et Actions pour la Sauvegarde des Primates en Côte d'Ivoire
summary: Primate conservation programme that identified the Tanoé-Ehy swamp forest as high conservation value in 2004, with surveillance and ecological monitoring documented in 2023 and tree-top cameras in 2022.

name: Projet Satelligence de surveillance satellitaire de la déforestation (SIFCA)
summary: Satellite deforestation monitoring run by the SIFCA group since 2021 across its palm oil, rubber and sugar supply chain in Côte d'Ivoire and Liberia, extended to Ghana from 2023.

name: Recent History, Ecology and Conservation of the Liberian Mongoose Liberiictis Kuhni (Hayman, 1958): A Vulnerable Species
summary: Closed project dated March 2024 in Taï National Park, aiming to map the Liberian mongoose's abundance and distribution and assess threats, using camera traps and naive occupancy in its second quarterly report.

name: SIG MINEF
summary: Ministry geographic information system, presented in December 2021 as a decision-support and surveillance tool based on forest, wildlife and water data, which the ministry said would allow transparent data sharing.

name: SNVLT (Côte d'Ivoire)
summary: Presented by BoisLégal as a decision-support tool for forests, with an application and an Android download.

name: Société de Développement des Forêts
summary: Ivorian government forest agency that, per Earthworm Foundation, signed an agreement to keep using Starling to monitor the Cavally Forest Reserve until the end of December 2019.

name: SOS-Forêts
summary: Ivorian organisation seated at the Centre National de Floristique, which lists building a natural resources database among its aims and received a $27,125 CEPF grant for biological surveys in 2004–2005.

name: Station d'Écologie de Lamto
summary: Ecology station in Lamto Scientific Reserve, run by Université Nangui Abrogoua, with savanna research since 1961 and a 100-hectare plot protected from fire since 1962.

name: Suivi écologique des Parcs nationaux et Réserves naturelles de Côte d'Ivoire
summary: Ecological monitoring programme for Ivorian national parks and nature reserves, with an OIPR-written implementation manual recommending monitoring methods suited to each park's type, context and management objectives.

name: Suivi écologique du Parc national de Taï
summary: Annual ecological monitoring of Taï National Park, run by OIPR's South-West directorate, with systematic sampling improved in 2015 and use of the SMART tool marking phase 12.

name: Système National de suivi spatial des forêts et d'alerte précoce de la déforestation
summary: National forest spatial monitoring and deforestation early-warning system, which the Initiative Cacao et Forêts reported piloting in some priority zones in October 2023 with IDH funding.

name: Taï Chimpanzee Project
summary: Research and conservation project led by Roman Wittig that has carried out non-invasive work on wild chimpanzees and other primates in Taï National Park since 1979.

name: TerraKora AI
summary: Based in Abidjan and Toronto, the company reportedly signed a 24-month environment ministry agreement on 2 October 2026, with mapping and carbon work expected.

name: Tripartite Methodological Approach for Data Collection to Develop Long-Term Conservation Strategies of Vultures in the Comoé National Park
summary: Closed project proposed in February 2021 to combine field observations, vulture tracking and ethnozoological surveys, aiming to generate data on vulture populations, habitats and movements in Comoé National Park.

name: UNDP drone forest surveillance support to the Ministry of Water and Forests
summary: Support in which UNDP handed twelve drones with paired smartphones to the Ministry of Water and Forests in February 2021, intended to make its special surveillance and intervention brigade more effective against illegal logging.

name: Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny
summary: University whose Centre National de Floristique held an April 2026 workshop on a continuing training programme in biodiversity conservation, and whose biosciences faculty GBIF describes as housing biological science laboratories.

name: Université Nangui Abrogoua
summary: According to NatureMetrics’ January 2023 report, a barcoding laboratory was established within the university’s Freshwater Ecosystem Lab during the February 2021–July 2022 project.

name: WCF biomonitoring in Côte d'Ivoire
summary: Biomonitoring of species distribution and frequency, run by the Wild Chimpanzee Foundation since 2004 with the Ministry of Water and Forests and OIPR, now in Taï National Park and Cavally Nature Reserve.

name: 1000 Genomas Chile
summary: Project led by the Instituto Milenio Centro de Regulación del Genoma, which the UC news service says aims to decipher the genetic heritage of Chile's plants, animals, fungi and algae.

name: ACOT Systems
summary: Organisation that Descubre VC says develops Firecatch, a forest fire early detection platform combining AI and computer vision.

name: Actualización de la Estrategia Nacional de Biodiversidad de Chile
summary: Closed project run by Chile's environment ministry to update its national biodiversity strategy, with GEF funding and UNDP as partner; the strategy says it contributes to the Kunming-Montreal framework.

name: Agencia Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo
summary: Asked by the science ministry to fund post-wildfire research in 2023–2024, and funded COPAS and University of Chile ocean acoustic AI work through Fondecyt.

name: AgroPlan
summary: Organisation whose technical manager, according to CONAF, is Andrés Gómez Hernández.

name: Anglo American Chile
summary: Organisation that Pacto Global Chile's site calls the first mining company in Chile to use the technology.

name: Apoyo a los esfuerzos de Chile para promover la innovación en la agenda de biodiversidad
summary: Closed project, funded by the Inter-American Development Bank, that aimed to develop instruments and provide institutional support to strengthen the national framework.

name: Arauco
summary: Forestry company headquartered in Chile that uses OroraTech and Lemu-Atlas; the first stage covers more than 91,500 hectares of its land in 20 conservation zones.

name: Arauco Ventures
summary: Organisation that Lemu reported in February 2023 was the sole investor in the first close of Lemu's Series A round.

name: Armada de Chile
summary: Organisation that uses Global Fishing Watch, which says it assists the Navy with fisheries intelligence for pre-patrol activities.

name: Asociación de Comunidades Indígenas Hualaihué
summary: A Chilean Indigenous association designated by a 2023 maritime destination decree to administer the Mañihueico Huinay coastal marine space for Indigenous peoples.

name: Asociación de Comunidades Indígenas Huicha Pucatué
summary: A Chilean Indigenous association designated by a November 2021 maritime destination decree to administer the Huicha coastal marine space for Indigenous peoples.

name: Asociación de Comunidades Indígenas Mapu Lahual
summary: Nine Huilliche communities set aside 2,250 hectares in 2005 to establish the Mapu Lahual park network, and their community network spans almost 60,000 hectares.

name: Asociación de Comunidades Indígenas Purra Lof Inchin Taiñen Lafken
summary: A Chilean Indigenous association designated by a March 2022 maritime destination decree to administer the 29,522.81-hectare Manqueche coastal marine space for Indigenous peoples.

name: Association of Mapuche Winkulmapu Communities of Kurarewe
summary: A Mapuche association that, under a framework agreement signed on 3 December 2024, is to have representatives on the council governing the Puesco Lanín sector of Villarrica National Park.

name: Atlas
summary: Lemu's platform, built and run by Lemu, with LemuRank and Biorarity indicators, used by Banco Central de Chile, Codelco and Conexión Kimal Lo Aguirre.

name: BASE Millennium Institute Research Data Portal
summary: An active research data portal, built and run by the BASE Millennium Institute, integrating datasets published since 2022 in open repositories such as GBIF, Zenodo and GenBank.

name: Biodata
summary: Programme run by the Instituto de Ecología y Biodiversidad and led by Pablo Guerrero, integrating biological collections, herbaria and databases on Chile's flora, fauna and ecosystems.

name: Bitácora Electrónica de Pesca
summary: Programme built by WWF and used by Servicio Nacional de Pesca y Acuicultura; WWF reported in July 2020 that the system was being implemented in Ecuador and Chile.

name: Biósfera LAB
summary: Organisation that describes advanced biosphere research with aerospace tools and AI, and places itself within the University of Chile.

name: Bloom Alert
summary: Chilean start-up that Descubre VC says uses satellite imagery, machine learning and AI to detect extreme oceanographic events; Google included it in its May 2025 AI for Nature cohort.

name: Bosquentrama
summary: Network of civil society organisations formed from 2024, funded by the European Union, that carries out collaborative monitoring of native forests.

name: Business For Conservation
summary: Organisation that says it uses bioacoustics as a tool for monitoring fauna in environmental consulting.

name: Catastro Vegetacional
