summary: Camera-trap project run by Panthera Costa Rica in the Barbilla Destierro sub-corridor, monitoring since 2009 with cameras from 2012; data fed a jaguar habitat use model.

name: Monitoring of sharks and rays with baited remote underwater video in the Costa Rican Pacific
summary: Study reported by Delfino in October 2020, in which UCR scientists and SINAC monitored sharks and rays with underwater cameras over four years, described as the country's first broad study using this method.

name: Monteverde Institute
summary: Non-profit educational organisation founded in 1986, whose history reports 553 people monitoring 35 local streams through Adopt-a-Stream in 2025.

name: Museo Nacional de Costa Rica
summary: Endorsed GBIF publisher that publishes its national zoology collection under CC BY 4.0, plus a herbarium dataset and a Flora Costa Rica metadata record.

name: NaturalistaCR
summary: Costa Rican name for iNaturalist, run by CONAGEBIO, whose community can help identify species from uploaded photographs, as Delfino reported in July 2026.

name: Ocean Prediction for Costa Rica
summary: Project begun in 2025 and run by Mercator Ocean International, whose first phase produced a Cocos Island dashboard and whose second phase, to December 2026, is to plan an ocean prediction service centre.

name: Osa Camera Trap Network
summary: Community wildlife monitoring network built by Osa Conservation, whose 2023 page reported 30 members and plans to join Talamancas camera trap projects as the AMISTOSA Camera Trap Network.

name: Osa Conservation
summary: Southern Costa Rica nonprofit with camera-trap and acoustic data from the 2020 and 2021 Ridge to Reef Megasurvey and Spotter platforms in Golfo Dulce since April 2025.

name: Panthera Costa Rica
summary: Organisation that says it has focused on consolidating the Jaguar Corridor Initiative in Costa Rica and lists camera trap monitoring and jaguar genetics projects.

name: Programa Nacional de Monitoreo Ecológico
summary: Inter-institutional programme within SINAC, created by Decree 39747-MINAE to produce and share information on biodiversity status and trends, which held its first network meeting at CATIE in 2025.

name: Programa Restauración de Tortugas Marinas
summary: Costa Rican marine conservation non-profit that says it was founded in 1997 and builds Cocos Island monitoring and research, with expeditions co-led with STRP since March 2009.

name: Rainforest Eyes and Ears
summary: Trial run by Osa Conservation, described in 2023, to let SINAC rangers respond to illegal activity alerts in real time, with alerts sent within a minute.

name: Remora
summary: San José organisation that Schmidt Marine lists as developing the Smart Scale for fisheries data, piloted on the Osa Peninsula, and FishWise says works on seafood traceability.

name: SERVIR Central America
summary: Hub of the SERVIR network for Central America, implemented by CATIE in Costa Rica.

name: Sistema de Información de Recursos Forestales de Costa Rica
summary: Costa Rica's integrated forest information management system, run by SINAC, covering themes such as forest cover and illegal logging and including the national forest inventory and the SIPLAMA system.

name: Sistema Nacional de Información Ambiental
summary: Platform launched by MINAE in June 2019 for environmental indicators and reports; its update was developed by INCO, supported by the French Development Agency and Costa Rica Por Siempre.

name: Sistema Nacional de Monitoreo de la Cobertura y Uso de la Tierra y Ecosistemas
summary: Land cover and land use monitoring system set up by Executive Decree 42886-MINAE-MAG-JP, made up of MINAE, MAG and IGN, with 2025 working groups including FONAFIFO, SINAC and INTA.

name: Sistema Nacional de Áreas de Conservación
summary: Environment ministry body created under the 1998 Biodiversity Law, split into eleven conservation areas, whose staff have collected ecological monitoring data under official protocols since 2017.

name: Strengthening the Prevention, Protection and Control programme of the Área de Conservación Marina Coco
summary: Funded by Fondo Azul Costa Rica and run by WildAid and Amigos Isla del Coco, the project uses EarthRanger and supported training to strengthen ACMC’s protection and control programme.

name: TapirVet Project
summary: A September 2025 Rufford page naming its director describes plans for national health surveillance of Baird’s tapirs in Costa Rica with communities, SINAC and national laboratories.

name: The Crystal Floor
summary: Photogrammetry project built by Innoceana, launched in 2020 per Earth.Org, making 3D models of coral to assess health; a CoralNet source says it monitors Cocos Island reefs with SINAC.

name: Thermal drone monitoring of sea turtles in Costa Rica
summary: Project in Costa Rica, reported by Auckland Zoo in March 2026, using thermal drones and AI models to record sea turtle abundance, sex ratios and behaviour, with expansion planned for the 2025/2026 nesting season.

name: Tortuguero sea turtle monitoring and research project
summary: Sea turtle monitoring project run by Sea Turtle Conservancy, which says it is the world's longest continuous one, continuing nesting and growth monitoring begun in the 1950s using tagging and track surveys.

name: Two decades of annual landscape-scale tree growth and dynamics in old-growth tropical rainforest in the CARBONO Project, La Selva Biological Station, 1997-2018
summary: Dataset of 21 years of annual tree, palm and liana growth and dynamics across 18 half-hectare plots at La Selva, built by Deborah Clark, with data used in remote-sensing studies.

name: Universidad de Costa Rica
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2025 paper on self-supervised learning for camera trap species classification.

name: Universidad Estatal a Distancia
summary: Distance university (UNED) whose affiliated authors appear in OpenAlex for a 2022 conference paper on automated bird acoustic detection and a 2018 paper on Guanacaste land cover classification.

name: Universidad Nacional
summary: Costa Rican university whose ICOMVIS contributed to passive acoustic bellbird detection, and whose Jaguar Program research, reported by the Tico Times, flagged declining jaguar records.

name: Área de Conservación Guanacaste
summary: Costa Rican protected area hosting over ten long-term scientific projects, with a research programme envisaged in 1986 and listed camera trap, acoustic, reef and satellite fire monitoring.

name: Área de Conservación Marina Coco
summary: Marine conservation area that uses EarthRanger; MINAE reported in 2026 that, through SINAC and ACMC, it was implementing the tool and training staff to use it.

name: Acoustic Monitoring as a Non-Harmful Tool to Monitor Natalus primus, a Critically Endangered Bat Species from Cuba
summary: Closed Rufford-funded project in Guanahacabibes National Park that planned automatic recording of critically endangered Natalus primus, with grant use from December 2014 to October 2015.

name: Acuario Nacional de Cuba
summary: Cuban aquarium and local partner of TNC, whose March 2026 newsletter reports A. cervicornis colonies spawning at its nursery, and whose staff joined manatee monitoring expeditions in southern Cuba.

name: Aplicación de un enfoque regional al manejo de las áreas protegidas marinas y costeras en los Archipiélagos del Sur de Cuba
summary: A GEF-funded project, implemented by UNDP and executed by the Centro Nacional de Áreas Protegidas from 2010 to 2014, which its report says set up nine monitoring programmes in 26 marine protected areas.

name: Assessing the Prevalence of a Lethal Fungus on Populations of an Endangered Cuban Amphibian: Rising Awareness and Developing Conservation Efforts
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project, dated 23 March 2016, that planned to assess the prevalence of a fungus in natural P. longinasus populations and train rangers in species identification and sensing techniques.

name: Biodiversidad Cubana
summary: A database of native Cuban species with advanced search tools, said to be validated by experts, with a home page count of 36940 species and 91766 occurrence records.

name: Bird Ecology Group, University of Havana
summary: A bird research group at the University of Havana, led by Dr. Martin Acosta Cruz in 2021, which BirdsCaribbean reported had surveyed Piping Plover wintering coastline yearly since 2016.

name: Bird watching and citizen science project in Cuba (Betty Petersen Conservation Fund grant)
summary: A project funded by a 2023 Betty Petersen Conservation Fund grant to Yaro Rodríguez and Nils Navarro, giving binoculars and training to community leaders to share bird data through eBird Caribbean.

name: Bojeo a Cuba
summary: Closed expedition of 18 July to 9 September 2023, led by the Centro de Investigaciones Marinas, covering nearly 2,000 nautical miles of coast to assess Cuba's coral reefs and marine life.

name: Centro de Estudios Ambientales de Cienfuegos
summary: A Cuban research centre on watershed and coastal marine environmental problems, which Prensa Latina reports led a Sentinel-2 coastline study with ENEA, as part of the ECOATLAS project.

name: Centro de Investigaciones de Ecosistemas Costeros
summary: Coastal ecosystems research centre run by CITMA, which a 2012 report places alongside the Centro Nacional de Áreas Protegidas, and whose staff took part in seagrass monitoring at Jardines de la Reina and other marine protected areas.

name: Centro de Investigaciones del Medioambiente de Camagüey
summary: Cuban environmental research centre attached to CITMA, reported in April 2025 to be assessing seagrass meadows periodically, with 15 new stations added on Camagüey's north coast, and a partner in mangrove monitoring.

name: Centro de Investigaciones Hidráulicas, Universidad Tecnológica de La Habana José Antonio Echeverría
summary: Hydraulics research centre at a Havana university, whose affiliated researcher is first author of a 2026 paper, listed in OpenAlex, on remote sensing for mangrove monitoring on the south coast of Artemisa and Mayabeque.

name: Centro de Investigaciones Marinas, Universidad de La Habana
summary: Marine research centre run by the University of Havana, whose researchers followed two manatees released with satellite transmitters in 2012 and which supplied coordinators for the manatee and seagrass monitoring programmes.

name: Centro de Investigaciones y Servicios Ambientales Ecovida
summary: A Cuban government institution placed at Guanahacabibes National Park in a 2025 predator video survey paper, whose first and corresponding author is affiliated with the centre.

name: Centro Nacional de Áreas Protegidas
summary: Founded in 1995, the lead centre of Cuba's National System of Protected Areas reviewed 24 protected-area management plans in 2022.

name: Centro Oriental de Ecosistemas y Biodiversidad
summary: Cuban budgeted unit under CITMA, based in Santiago de Cuba, reportedly involved in monthly bird banding for twelve years by May 2023 and responsible for areas with mangrove monitoring.

name: Conservation and educational activities for Eleutherodactylus symingtoni (Symington's Robber Frog)
summary: Project funded by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund that aims to start long-term monitoring of Symington's Robber Frog, studying calling phenology and testing for chytrid fungus.

name: Cuerpo de Guardabosques de Cuba
summary: Forest ranger corps under MININT, listed in the annex for operational monitoring of forest disturbances, fires, illegal logging and forest degradation.

name: Dirección del Servicio Estatal Forestal
summary: Forest sector authority under MINAG, coordinating the national forest monitoring system, using Collect Earth Online and cited as the source of the 2019–2023 forest emissions balance.

name: Dung Beetles as Indicators for Evaluating and Monitoring Conservation Areas in Cuba
summary: Rufford project page dated 17 September 2018, planning a dung beetle catalogue and reference collection and data on spatial community change in the Sierra del Rosario Biosphere Reserve, related to land use.

name: Effects of Hurricanes on Bat Populations in the Sierra del Rosario Biosphere Reserve, Cuba: A Long-Term Monitoring Study
summary: Closed Rufford project, dated 19 June 2009, planning to compare bat abundance at three hurricane-affected sites in the Sierra del Rosario reserve, where long-term bat monitoring began in the mid-1990s.

name: Empresa Nacional para la Protección de la Flora y la Fauna
summary: Cuban enterprise in the Flora y Fauna system for conserving protected-area resources, which in 1999 created a nesting-record programme for sea turtles and partners with turtle and crocodile monitoring programmes.

name: GBIF Cuba
summary: The GBIF country node for Cuba, listed in GBIF's registry with observer status, using the environment ministry's address, with a record created and last modified on 3 May 2010.

name: Increasing conservation capacity on behalf of the endangered Greater Caribbean manatee in Zapata Swamp
summary: Awarded US$12,000 by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund in February 2025, the project reports combining boat, drone and fishing-guide surveys in 2025, with drones detecting nine manatees.

name: Instituto Cubano de Biodiversidad
summary: A Cuban body formed in 2025 by joining the Instituto de Ecología y Sistemática and the national natural history museum, publishing amphibian and Lepidoptera checklists through GBIF.

name: Instituto de Ciencias del Mar
summary: Marine science institute founded on 17 February 2017 by merging CEBIMAR and the Instituto de Oceanología, subordinate to CITMA's Environment Agency, according to FAO AGRIS.

name: Instituto de Geografía Tropical
summary: A Cuban institute producing geographical, environmental and geomatics solutions, which publishes 15 species checklists through GBIF, including 2,285 names of fishes recorded for the Cuban archipelago and its exclusive economic zone.

name: Instituto de Investigaciones Agro-Forestales
summary: Research institute in the Ministry of Agriculture, named in the annex as scientific and methodological support of the MRV system, developing forest inventory methods, emission factors and biomass and carbon models.

name: IUCN SSC Cuban Plant Specialist Group
summary: A regional IUCN Species Survival Commission group with 63 members and collaborators, producing Cuban plant Red List assessments since 1998 and publishing checklists and occurrence data through GBIF.

name: Juan Cristóbal Gundlach Bird Banding Station
summary: A bird banding station in the Siboney Juticí Ecological Reserve, described by BirdsCaribbean in May 2023 as Cuba's longest running, which hosted part of Cuba's first banding workshop in 2022.

name: Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología y Medio Ambiente
summary: Cuba's ministry of science, technology and the environment, which lists environmental planning and protected areas among its functions and whose address is used for the GBIF Cuba node.

name: Monitoring of Bat Maternity Colonies during Birthing Season in Two Hot-Caves
summary: Closed project, on a Rufford page dated 26 May 2015, that planned to study bat populations in two caves with automatic recording units and infrared cameras, identifying species from echolocation calls.

name: National Survey and Action Plan for the Bats of Cuba: Generating a Long-Term Strategy for Conservation
summary: Closed Rufford project, dated 10 August 2015, planning to combine mist-netting, acoustic surveys and cave counts and to produce an updated, geo-referenced catalogue of the main bat caves.

name: Nos vemos pronto cocodrilo
summary: Proposed initiative, from an alliance including FANJ, ECOCIENZAP and UNDP Cuba, to raise funds for buying and fitting satellite tags to track the movements of Cuban crocodiles.

name: Parque Nacional Cayos de San Felipe
summary: Protected area in Pinar del Río with a named person responsible for iguana monitoring; the UNDP report says its iguana population is recovering after heavy unsustainable use in earlier decades.

name: Parque Nacional Ciénaga de Zapata
summary: Protected area in Matanzas that the UNDP reports list as having a person responsible for manatee monitoring and as taking part in the crocodile monitoring programme.

name: Parque Nacional Desembarco del Granma
summary: Protected area in Granma with two people responsible for iguana monitoring, where the UNDP report finds low iguana density in two populations and lists it in manatee monitoring.

name: Parque Nacional Guanahacabibes
summary: Cuban national park whose coral reef research, monitoring and management over ten years is presented in a paper, with a monitoring programme created under its first management plan for 2004–2008.

name: Parque Nacional Jardines de la Reina
summary: Protected area in Ciego de Ávila and Camagüey with two people responsible for iguana monitoring; the UNDP report says 2011 and 2012 results there and at Cayos de Ana María show stable metapopulations.

name: Programa de Monitoreo de Cocodrilos
summary: A UNDP report covering 2012 and part of 2011 described crocodile monitoring in four protected areas on Cuba’s south coast and reported an established system for both species.

name: Programa de Monitoreo de Iguana
summary: Iguana monitoring programme in six protected areas on Cuba's south coast, begun in 2011, measuring population density per hectare twice a year, according to the UNDP report.

name: Programa de Monitoreo de Manglares
summary: A UNDP report recorded 68 permanent mangrove plots by December 2012, citing 14 protected areas in results but 13 elsewhere, with remote sensing among its monitoring goals.

name: Programa de Monitoreo de Pastos Marinos
summary: Seagrass monitoring programme that, per the UNDP report, began in ten marine protected areas in 2011–2012 to set a baseline, using 12 fixed quadrats along 50 m transects.

name: Programa de Monitoreo de Tortugas Marinas
summary: National sea turtle monitoring programme, created through a group formed in 2009 with a standard protocol and national database, whose project areas recorded 8,275 nests from 2010 to early 2012.

name: Programa de Monitoreo de Vegetación de Costa Arenosa
summary: Sandy-shore vegetation monitoring programme on eight beaches in three protected areas on Cuba's south coast, begun in 2011, using two permanent 100 square metre plots per beach, per the UNDP report.

name: Programa de Monitoreo del Manatí Antillano
summary: Manatee monitoring programme that, per the UNDP report, had reached five of seven selected protected areas, recorded 14 manatee mortality events in 2011 and 2012, and released two satellite-tagged manatees in 2012.

name: Protecting Natalus primus by updating its current status using ecological data collection, acoustic monitoring and social actions
summary: Funded by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, the project aims to assess bat habitat occupancy acoustically and reports a management plan included in Guanahacabibes’ 2023–2025 strategy.

name: Refugio de Fauna Delta del Cauto
summary: Wildlife refuge in Las Tunas and Granma that sent six crocodile monitoring participants and hosted initial training at Monte Cabaniguán, reportedly Cuba’s largest American crocodile population in 2011–2012.

name: Servicio Hidrográfico y Geodésico de la República de Cuba
summary: A Cuban hydrographic and geodetic service created by a 1997 decree law, which in a UN congress presentation described full national topographic mapping coverage and a land cover map of Cuba.

name: Sistema de Monitoreo de la Biodiversidad (Archipiélagos del Sur de Cuba)
summary: Biodiversity monitoring system run by CNAP, for which the UNDP final evaluation reports ten key species and ecosystems selected, twelve protocols developed and over 280 specialists trained.

name: Sistema Nacional de Monitoreo Forestal
summary: Cuba's national forest monitoring system, which FAO says the agriculture ministry is strengthening with FAO technical help and Green Climate Fund support, including drones with imaging systems.

name: Starting the First Long-Term Acoustic Monitoring Program of Amphibians in Cuba
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project, dated 11 May 2015, with the goal of starting Cuba's first long-term acoustic monitoring programme of amphibians using automatic recorders, with work planned in Sierra del Rosario Biosphere Reserve.

name: Status and Conservation Strategy of Diurnal Raptors of a Wetland in Cuba
summary: Closed Rufford-funded project in a Cuban wetland, run over three phases from 2011, whose first phase road transects registered 11 diurnal raptor species and whose third phase planned citizen science and nesting-area modelling.

name: Universidad de La Habana
summary: Cuban university whose Centro de Investigaciones Marinas researchers followed two manatees released with satellite transmitters in 2012, and which OpenAlex lists as the Cuban institution with the most works.

name: Vector model of the Cuban archipelago coastline from Sentinel-2
summary: A vector model of the Cuban archipelago coastline made from Sentinel-2 imagery, reported by Prensa Latina to reach 94 per cent overall accuracy at 1:25 000 scale, within ECOATLAS.

name: Watershed Conservation in Cuba: Bio-monitoring, Training and Environmental Education
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project with three phases dated 2011–2014 in the Sierra Maestra, whose third phase planned community comparisons of freshwater fauna using a Cuba-adapted BMWP index.

name: Associação Lantuna
summary: Organisation funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund; its project covered seabird breeding monitoring and ringing, GPS tagging of shearwaters in 2023 with University of Coimbra support, and website development.

name: Associação Projecto Vitó
summary: Organisation whose technical team, per an August 2026 Inforpress report, did local fieldwork for the Ilhéu de Cima turtle campaign (15 June to 15 October 2026), which recorded 281 nests and 535 tracks in June and July.

name: Baseline BRUV Surveys, Eastern Cabo Verde
summary: A MarAlliance project that, since 2015, has used baited remote underwater video around Boavista, Maio and Sal to build a baseline of shark, ray and large finfish abundance and distribution.

name: Biflores, Associação de Conservação da Biodiversidade
summary: Local biodiversity conservation association for Brava's terrestrial ecosystems, established in 2016, whose botanical inventory work under a CEPF grant is to underpin a protected area proposal prepared with Projecto Vitó.

name: Bioindicadores de Resiliência Climática
summary: Active project, run by Instituto do Mar and funded by LuxDev, that studies corals, seagrasses and microalgae as bioindicators, with a 2025 board deliberation providing team allowances for sea sampling campaigns.

name: BIOS.CV
summary: Turtle conservation NGO on Boa Vista, funded by CEPF, which Inforpress reports recorded 9,737 nests and 19,432 hatchling releases in September 2025.

name: Biosfera 1 – Associação Para a Defesa do Meio Ambiente
summary: Environmental association, funded by CEPF, that says it has worked since 2006 on coastal and marine biodiversity, mainly through monitoring and conservation on Santa Luzia, Raso and Branco.

name: Birds of Sal
summary: A bird field study programme on Sal, launched in 2017 per its page, collecting nesting, feeding and migration data; its 2018 data led University of Barcelona scientists to identify Sal as likely a key tropicbird breeding site.

name: Cabo Verde Natura 2000
summary: Turtle conservation NGO on Boa Vista that, according to Inforpress, registered 16,721 of the more than 35,000 nests monitored on the island in September 2025.

name: Coastal Ecosystem Monitoring in Cabo Verde
summary: A MeerWissen project from 2019 to 2023 that developed standards for coastal ecosystem monitoring around Cabo Verde, where no systematic observations existed, and which GEOMAR says local researchers can operate and extend.

name: Conservation of Key Shark Habitats and Development of a Stepping Stone for a Long-Term Monitoring System of Local Shark Communities in Cape Verde
summary: Closed Rufford-supported project, reported in 2014, that aimed to use genetic methods on shark bycatch samples, collected with the local community, to get first abundance and population data around a Cape Verde island.

name: Conservation Status for Sea Turtles Caretta caretta in Santa Luzia Island (Cabo Verde)
summary: Closed Rufford-supported project, completed by December 2015, continuing work begun in 2011 on nesting sea turtles at the Santa Luzia marine reserve through daily beach patrols, nest relocation and marking of females.

name: Direção Nacional do Ambiente
summary: National environment directorate that coordinated the 2026 seabird conservation plan, which provides for integrated seabird monitoring, and is listed as executing agency for GEF-funded projects on biodiversity governance and the blue and green economy.

name: Estabelecendo a Gestão Cooperativa da Área Marinha Protegida para Conservar a Área Chave para a Biodiversidade da Ilha do Sal, Cabo Verde
summary: A CEPF-funded project run by Project Biodiversity from May 2019 to November 2023, monitoring birds, plants, reptiles and nesting turtles (with drones) at Costa Fragata, and starting fisher-led megafauna monitoring.

name: Fundação Maio Biodiversidade
summary: Non-profit established in 2010 on Maio, authorised by the government to monitor and protect all turtle nesting beaches, with a 2023 programme listing an ongoing study of drones for monitoring nesting.

name: Fundação Tartaruga
summary: Non-profit protecting Boa Vista’s sea turtles since 2008, with detection dogs, proposed BIOPAMA-funded drone use and 8,607 nests reported by Inforpress for September 2025.

name: GISCV.ORG
summary: Independent open-access geospatial data repository for biologists and ecologists, presented in a 2026 Zoologia Caboverdiana paper by Nuno de Santos Loureiro and organised into eight sections at launch.

name: Guardians of the Sea (Cabo Verde)
summary: A community monitoring programme in which fishers record illegal activities and marine megafauna sightings, begun on Maio in 2016; Mongabay reported in July 2026 that around 190 fishers take part on seven islands.

name: Instituto do Mar
summary: Marine institute formerly INDP, hosting Ocean Science Centre Mindelo, collaborating with GEOMAR on an ocean observatory since 2004 and forming a climate bioindicators team in 2025.

name: Instituto Nacional de Gestão do Território
summary: State body of Cabo Verde responsible for organising the national territory, with domains including cartography, geodesy and the national Spatial Data Infrastructure (IDE-CV), based in Plateau, Praia.

name: Instituto Nacional de Investigação e Desenvolvimento Agrário
summary: A Cabo Verdean state agrarian research service, seated on Santiago, whose researchers have used satellite imagery and Random Forest classification to study land use change on Maio between 1957 and 2021.

name: Monitoring and Environmental Education to Support Conservation of Endangered Species in an African Shark Nursery
summary: A project to monitor juvenile sharks in a multi-species nursery on Boa Vista; an October 2024 update reported 771 sharks sampled that year to date, mostly milk sharks.

name: Nursery Area Monitoring Boavista, Cabo Verde
summary: MarAlliance project that identified Baía de Sal Rei as a shark nursery area in 2015 and began monitoring in 2016, using standardised scientific fishing with local fishers, focused on scalloped hammerheads.

name: Parque Natural do Fogo
summary: Described in a CEPF final report as Cabo Verde's main terrestrial protected area, with one ecological monitoring technician at baseline and a vegetation monitoring plan drawn up and awaiting approval by the DNA.

name: Project Biodiversity
summary: NGO in Santa Maria, Sal, that began with its sea turtle programme and monitors and protects the island's turtle population, patrolling all beaches weekly for nesting and poaching.

name: Protected Areas Programme (Maio)
summary: A Fundação Maio Biodiversidade programme that monitors plants, birds, reptiles and legal and illegal human activities in Maio's protected areas, aiming to improve the monitoring system through a six-front action plan.

name: REFLOR-CV
summary: Closed project, run by the Food and Agriculture Organization, signed in July 2017 and finished in April 2022, which strengthened land cover monitoring and produced six forest inventories in 2020 and land cover statistics for nine islands.

name: Sea Turtle Conservation Programme (Maio)
summary: A Fundação Maio Biodiversidade programme with daily beach monitoring during the June to October nesting season, using drones, GPS and satellite tracking, and counting hatchlings to assess reproductive success.

name: Sharks of Sal
summary: A Project Biodiversity programme using baited video surveys, tagging and sampling to monitor sharks and rays on Sal, whose long-term monitoring led to Parda Reef being recognised as an Important Shark and Ray Area.

name: TAOLA, Rede Nacional de Proteção das Tartarugas Marinhas de Cabo Verde
summary: Cabo Verde's national sea turtle conservation network had met annually since 2009 and developed standardised data protocols by 2022; a non-profit association named TAOLA+ was constituted in 2023.

name: Terrimar – Ambiente e Desenvolvimento Sustentável
summary: A Santo Antão NGO, CEPF-funded for sea turtle and vulture conservation, whose 2023 campaign recorded 2,029 turtle nests and which plans two forest conservation projects over three years, per a December 2025 report.

name: Towards Co-management of Protected Areas on Maio Island, Cabo Verde
summary: A CEPF-funded project run by Fundação Maio Biodiversidade from April 2021 to November 2023, monitoring species and human activities in all seven protected areas of Maio, which produced two scientific publications.

name: A. G. Leventis Foundation
summary: Funder that paid for the setting up of Terra Cypria in 1992 and says its funding lets Terra Cypria monitor six Natura 2000 sites.

name: AP Marine Environmental Consultancy Ltd
summary: A private SME offering marine research, survey and consultancy services, with past work on offshore cetacean surveys, benthic habitat mapping and Natura 2000 biodiversity assessments.

name: BIOMON: Using passive acoustic monitoring methods to survey bird communities in biodiverse agricultural farmlands in the EU
summary: Project coordinated by Frederick University and funded by the EU Horizon ERA Fellowships programme, which in November 2022 aimed to develop AI methods using acoustic sensors to monitor birdlife in ecologically important rural areas of Cyprus.

name: BirdLife Cyprus
summary: Non-profit nature conservation organisation in Cyprus that runs and built a bird trapping surveillance programme with the RSPB, ongoing since 2002, and holds data on bird distributions and habitats.

name: BirdLife Cyprus Griffon Vulture counts
summary: Monitoring of the small wild Griffon Vulture population in Cyprus, built by BirdLife Cyprus from 2011, with counts on one spring day and one late autumn day each year.

name: BirdLife Cyprus raptor migration counts
summary: Monitoring programme for migrating birds of prey, run by BirdLife Cyprus since 2003, with autumn counts mostly by volunteers; it identified the Akrotiri Peninsula as an Important Bird Area.

name: BirdLife Cyprus surveillance programme on illegal bird trapping
summary: Ongoing programme run by BirdLife Cyprus and built with the RSPB, visiting random 1 km² squares by day to detect mist netting across Larnaca and Famagusta.

name: BirdLife Cyprus wetland bird monitoring programme
summary: Wetland bird programme run by BirdLife Cyprus since 1982, now monthly monitoring, feeding the International Waterbird Census; in January 2025, 36 volunteers surveyed 72 sites and counted 21,592 waterbirds.

name: Checklist of introduced taxa in Cyprus
summary: Public domain (CC0) dataset of 1,500 introduced taxa in Cyprus, run by The Cyprus Institute, usable for invasion research and management and for alien species registries.

name: Climate change monitoring programme at Cavo Greco MPA
summary: Monitoring programme at Cavo Greco MPA in Cyprus, run by AP Marine as the next phase of MPA4Change, which in March 2025 reported temperature loggers, fish census surveys and sponge mortality surveys.

name: Common Birds Monitoring Scheme (Cyprus)
summary: Volunteer scheme run by BirdLife Cyprus, piloted in 2006, covering 70 to 100 one-kilometre squares, whose data supported 2013 Article 12 reporting and the Farmland Bird Index.

name: Cyprus Bird Surveys Project
summary: Funded by the EBCC Small Grant Fund and launched in 2024 with KUŞKOR to fill field monitoring gaps in northern Cyprus; thirteen volunteers made 49 surveys that year.

name: Cyprus Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: Butterfly monitoring scheme that began collecting transect and 15-minute count data in 2019, led by Elli Tzirkalli and supported by Near East University, according to the eBMS page.

name: Cyprus Database of Alien Species
summary: Database that aims to be a single source on alien species in Cyprus, built by RIS-KY, collecting occurrence records through two iNaturalist projects.

name: Cyprus Herp Atlas
summary: The first attempt to collect and organise all existing data on Cyprus's herpetofauna, from books, databases, volunteers, the public and social media; last updated 31 July 2025.

name: Cyprus monk seal monitoring programme
summary: Led by Charalambos Nicolaou, the programme has monitored all monk seal caves since 2011, uses cameras and maintains a national seal activity database, Cyprus Mail reports.

name: Cyprus nationwide tree-level biomass and carbon inventory
summary: Reported by Politis as Cyprus's first nationwide tree biomass and carbon inventory, it was developed by The Cyprus Institute, combining AI with Department of Forests field measurements.

name: Cyprus Roadkills Observation System
summary: Intended to record citizens' and volunteers' observations of dead wild animals on the island's roads, with species, location and photographs; funded by the Open University of Cyprus.

name: Cyprus University of Technology
summary: University that runs and co-funds the ERATOSTHENES Centre of Excellence, which describes itself as a centre of the university in Limassol.

name: Department of Computer Engineering, Cyprus International University
summary: University department given as the affiliation of both authors of a 2025 OpenAlex-listed paper on binary classification of coral reefs using deep learning.

name: Department of Electronic Communications (Cyprus Space Office)
summary: Government department acting as the Cyprus Space Office by Council of Ministers decision, tasked with formulating and implementing the national space strategy, including EU, ESA and EUSPA participation.

name: Department of Environment (Cyprus)
summary: Cyprus government department, run by the agriculture and environment ministry, that hosts the primary CBD national focal point and coordinates LIFE IP Physis for the Natura 2000 network.

name: Department of Fisheries and Marine Research (Cyprus)
summary: Cyprus department monitoring sea caves for monk seals since 2011; it is a LIFE IP Physis participant and, per Terra Cypria, collaborates on turtle nest protection.

name: Department of Forests (Cyprus)
summary: Cyprus department overseeing fire protection in state forests and a two-kilometre buffer; it introduced drones in August 2022, and its head said they gave a real-time picture.

name: Department of Lands and Surveys (Cyprus)
summary: Part of the Ministry of Interior, it announces drone mapping flights, links to the INSPIRE Geoportal and calls its data its most important strategic asset.

name: e-FORESTER
summary: EU-funded Cyprus, Italy and Poland collaboration, launched on 18 November 2024 and led by Space Systems Solutions, to develop an autonomous robotic vehicle for monitoring forests using robotics and AI.

name: EarthView Cyprus
summary: Initiative reported launched in June 2026, bringing together ERATOSTHENES and Cyta around a station receiving satellite data in near real time, with wildfire, marine and coastal monitoring uses stated.

name: Eastern Mediterranean University Underwater Imaging and Research Center
summary: Eastern Mediterranean University centre that carried out a satellite-tracking study of loggerhead turtles in summer 2025, with an August 2025 report saying two turtles were being tracked.

name: Ecoacoustic dataset collected on the island of Cyprus
summary: Ecoacoustic dataset from Cyprus, described in a 2025 paper listed in OpenAlex, with first author Christos Mammides of Frederick University's Nature Conservation Unit and a co-author affiliated with BirdLife Cyprus.

name: eDNA-LEV
summary: Project running December 2024 to November 2027 with 200,000 euros, aiming to compare coastal eDNA biodiversity assessments in Cyprus and Israel and establish a bioinvasion early warning system.

name: EFFECTIVE
summary: Horizon Europe project running from June 2023 to May 2027 to build guidance for managing Mediterranean blue natural capital, planning a digital twin tool and a Cape Greco sensor pilot.

name: Enalia Physis Environmental Research Centre
summary: A non-profit non-governmental organisation based in Cyprus, active since 2009, whose core activities include marine and terrestrial biodiversity monitoring; it also lists a monk seal protection project.

name: ERATOSTHENES Centre of Excellence
summary: Centre of the Cyprus University of Technology in Limassol, aiming to be an Earth observation hub for the eastern Mediterranean, with AI methods for forest species and land cover classification.

name: FORSAT: A satellite processing platform for high resolution forest assessment
summary: Closed project led by GeoImaging that aimed to move forest cover mapping to satellite-based monitoring, developing a 3D forest information platform and a Saittas fire deforestation case study using 2001 and 2014 data.

name: Frederick University
summary: University in Cyprus running a Nature Conservation Unit studying local flora, fauna and habitats, which led the 2020 State of Environment Report and preparation of the Cyprus Biodiversity Strategy.

name: Game and Fauna Service (Cyprus)
summary: Cyprus service responsible for conserving all wild birds and their Special Protection Areas under the Birds Directive, with research including annual population, monthly waterbird and hunter harvest surveys.

name: GeoImaging Ltd
summary: Described by EOmag in March 2015 as a Cyprus SME established in Nicosia in 2002 offering geo-informatics and remote sensing, it coordinated FORSAT.

name: Geosfire: Geospatial Earth Observation System for Fire Intelligence and Real-time Evaluation
summary: Active project, funded by TechIsland, that aims to develop a satellite-based, machine-learning fire detection and alert system for Cyprus, which Cyprus Mail (23 July 2026) reports was presented by a Cyprus Institute researcher.

name: Green-HIT: A Green - Holistic IoT platform for Forest Management and Monitoring
summary: Project led by Andreas Konstantinidis that aims to design an IoT platform for forest management and monitoring, planning to use machine learning, Earth observation, sensors and UAVs.

name: Herpetological Society of Cyprus
summary: Non-governmental organisation based in Cyprus promoting protection, conservation and education on reptiles and amphibians, whose EU-Citizen.Science profile lists the Cyprus Herp Atlas among its projects.

name: Holistic Fire Surveillance System (Cyprus)
summary: Proposed Cyprus fire surveillance system for which the President approved EUR 28,513,593 in May 2026; its second phase is planned over three years across 338,000 hectares of forest land.

name: Karpaz Bird Ringing Station
summary: Bird ringing station whose 2025 paper reports regular ringing from autumn 2024, with 1,436 birds of 39 species ringed, and titles it the first ringing station in Cyprus.

name: KUŞKOR
summary: Non-governmental organisation working to protect Cyprus's birds and nature since 1988, through education, research, monitoring and lobbying in northern Cyprus; its volunteers joined the January 2025 wetland survey.

name: LIFE IP Physis
summary: Integrated project led by the Department of Environment, running July 2019 to October 2029 with a budget of about 17 million euros, aiming to provide a geospatial database and web GIS tool for Natura 2000.

name: LIFE with Vultures
summary: Four-year project, 2019 to 2023, against the main threats to Griffon Vultures in Cyprus, coordinated by BirdLife Cyprus, with a EUR 1,375,861 budget, 60% co-funded by the EU LIFE programme.

name: Mediterranean Turtle Research and Conservation Society
summary: Established in 2022, the NGO began satellite tracking of two turtles nesting at Lara Bay, one green and one loggerhead, according to Politis (29 July 2026).

name: Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment (Cyprus)
summary: Cyprus ministry that, according to the CBD, houses the Department of Environment with the national focal points and the Conservator of Forests, focal point for plant conservation.

name: Nature Conservation Unit, Frederick University
summary: Established in 2005 to study, monitor and conserve Cyprus's flora, fauna and habitats, the unit is the first author's affiliation on a 2025 bird acoustic indices paper.

name: Open University of Cyprus
summary: Organisation whose TEMLab project page says it funds the Cyprus Roadkills Observation System and also describes the Cyprus Herp Atlas.

name: PUREEF-Y
summary: EU-funded project running from July 2024 to June 2027, led by the Cyprus Marine and Maritime Institute, to assess the health of shallow benthic and planktonic habitats and propose management plans.

name: PyroGuard AI
summary: AI fire detection system which Sigmalive reported in August 2026 had detected dozens of fires in two years, using a network of 65 stations with over 100 planned by end of 2026.

name: Raptors for LIFE
summary: Project reported by Politis as due to begin in October 2026, with 60% EU LIFE co-financing and BirdLife Cyprus as lead partner, planning GPS tagging of birds and scientific evidence for wildlife poisoning prosecutions.

name: RELIONMED
summary: Described by Plymouth in July 2021 as a €1.6 million EU-funded project aiming to assess Cyprus's lionfish invasion, it involved divers and citizen scientists in removals and surveys.

name: Remote Sensing and Geo-Environment Lab, Department of Civil Engineering and Geomatics, Cyprus University of Technology
summary: Affiliated with the first author of the 2025 OpenAlex-listed paper Seagrass Mapping in Cyprus Using Earth Observation Advances, the lab belongs to Cyprus University of Technology.

name: Report on Conservation Status of Habitats and Species (Cyprus)
summary: Six-yearly Article 17 Habitats Directive report on conservation status, with habitat and species distribution and range shapefiles, covering 2013 to 2018 under CC BY 4.0 and listed under the Department of Environment.

name: Research and Innovation Foundation
summary: Cyprus body that says it is the national authority for supporting research and innovation, founded in 1996 as the Research Promotion Foundation and renamed after an October 2018 decision.

name: Researching Invasive Species of Kýpros
summary: Project launched in April 2017 on invasive alien species impacts in the Sovereign Base Areas, funded by the Darwin Initiative, with a Darwin Plus successor scheduled until March 2021.

name: Society for the Protection of Turtles (North Cyprus)
summary: Northern Cyprus turtle protection group that worked with EMU-SAGEM in summer 2025 to attach satellite transmitters to two released loggerhead turtles, one of which had been tagged before.

name: Space Systems Solutions (S3) Ltd
summary: Cyprus-based company, established in 2016 as a spin-off of the Cyprus Space Exploration Organisation, described as developing space technologies and applications and leading e-FORESTER.

name: Taşkent Nature Park
summary: Nature park described by a minister in 2023 as a non-profit charitable institution, reported to have a Karpaz donkey protocol and host the Cyprus Marine Life Centre's turtle work.

name: Terra Cypria, the Cyprus Conservation Foundation
summary: Educational NGO established in 1992 with A. G. Leventis Foundation funding, which the foundation says enables monitoring of six Natura 2000 sites.

name: Terrestrial Ecosystems Management Lab, Open University of Cyprus
summary: Open University of Cyprus lab whose research includes spatial analysis for species and habitat modelling, and whose projects include the Cyprus Herp Atlas and CyROS, a database of roadkill observations.

name: The Cyprus Bycatch Project: Understanding multi-taxa bycatch of vulnerable species and testing mitigation
summary: Closed project led by BirdLife Cyprus and funded by the MAVA Foundation; its first phase, 2017 to 2020, found turtles and elasmobranchs bear the heaviest toll from fishing operations.

name: The Cyprus Institute
summary: Non-profit research and educational institution, according to GBIF, which runs the checklist of introduced taxa in Cyprus, covering 1,500 introduced taxa.

name: 3Lynx
summary: Interreg Central Europe project that ran from July 2017 to June 2020 with a 2,318,784 euro allocation, aiming to coordinate lynx monitoring in three isolated populations using camera traps and winter snow tracking.

name: ALKA Wildlife
summary: Czech non-profit founded in 2007 that studies and protects selected wild mammals and birds; in 2019 it reported manually processing about 100,000 camera-trap photos and had a grant for an AI project still in development.

name: AMSrv
summary: Free suite that the Czech Society for Ornithology says automatically converts recordings into spectrograms, now developed voluntarily under member Ivo Hertl, with a link showing funding from the Nature Conservation Agency.

name: Analýzy prostorových dat jako praktický nástroj ochrany druhů a biotopů alpínského a subalpínského bezlesí pod vlivem globálních změn
summary: Technology Agency-funded project, March 2025 to February 2028, combining remote sensing, ecological modelling and AI tools to develop monitoring methods for alpine and subalpine treeless areas in the Jeseníky and Krkonoše.

name: Avif
summary: Bird observation database run by the Czech Society for Ornithology, which calls it the largest such data source in the country; in 2025, 3,072 people entered 594,503 observations.

name: BioLog
summary: Programme developed by the Nature Conservation Agency of the Czech Republic in 2013, and one of the routes for entering data into the nature conservation finds database.

name: Biology Centre of the Czech Academy of Sciences
summary: Czech research body whose helminthology laboratory is listed as an IMPACT partner and whose soil biology institute is a MONITANT partner, a project Biodiversa+ says will test semi-automated remote sensing monitoring.

name: Blue Cat Team
summary: Forest ecology department of the Landscape Research Institute in Brno that collects forest structure, soil and biodiversity data, including metabarcoding records, and in October 2026 held a BioReMo partner workshop on habitat monitoring.

name: CarniTrack
summary: Mobile app for large carnivore mappers, recording GPX routes, signs and photographs, enhanced by Hnutí DUHA Šelmy from the original Shelmon app.

name: Czech National Phytosociological Database
summary: Database of vegetation plots, described in GBIF's publisher record for the department and run by Masaryk University.

name: Czech Office for Surveying, Mapping and Cadastre
summary: Provides open data under CC BY 4.0; since July 2023, the Land Survey Office has published ZABAGED, Czech orthophotos and the state map series free.

name: Czech Technical University in Prague
summary: University listed by Biodiversa+ as a FunDive partner through its Department of Cybernetic, Faculty of Electronic Engineering.

name: DendroNetwork
summary: National network for biomonitoring of forest ecosystems with real-time data, which a 2023 Czech Academy of Sciences release says included NetFor's automatic dendrometers recording stem size changes every 30 minutes.

name: Detekce, identifikace a monitoring živočichů pokročilými metodami počítačového vidění
summary: Technology Agency-funded project, 2022 to 2024, on computer vision for camera-trap data to support species reporting under the Habitats Directive; the funder's evaluation says it produced a public identification library and models.

name: FlowerChecker
summary: Company that began as an academic project and builds the Plant.id AI; a January 2023 article reported about 309 companies in 56 countries used its product and that it planned to identify insects.

name: Fotomonitoring rysa ostrovida v NP a CHKO Šumava
summary: Šumava administration programme of long-term camera-trap monitoring of Eurasian lynx, with Bavarian Forest National Park, drawing on 16 years of data; in 2025 cameras stayed out all year at 28 of 56 sites.

name: Genetický monitoring vlka
summary: Technology Agency-funded project, running April 2024 to December 2026, to develop genetic monitoring of wolves and determine population structure, abundance and viability in Czechia, with 10,871 thousand CZK of state support.

name: Global Change Research Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences
summary: Czech Academy of Sciences institute (CzechGlobe) working on remote sensing, airborne data and forest monitoring, which in 2023 helped set up an oak vitality network and reported first National Forest Inventory results in October 2026.

name: Grantová agentura České republiky
summary: State organisational unit and the country's only institution giving targeted public support to basic research projects, which funded the Pladias project, creator of the database of Czech flora and vegetation, from 2014 to 2018.

name: Hnutí DUHA
summary: Self-described largest Czech environmental organisation, which organises field monitoring of lynx, wolves and bears through its Wolf and Lynx Patrols.

name: Hnutí DUHA Šelmy
summary: Olomouc-based branch association of Hnutí DUHA that has organised field monitoring of large carnivores through its Wolf and Lynx Patrols since 2002, reaching almost the whole country.

name: Hydrologický ústav AV ČR
summary: Public research institution set up by the Czech Academy of Sciences, whose site lists hydrological monitoring and wetland hydrology.

name: Institute of Botany of the Czech Academy of Sciences
summary: Self-described largest Czech botanical research centre in Průhonice, which builds Pladias, administers the shared Pladias GBIF publisher for PlantBank and partners in ForBioMon.

name: Institute of Microbiology of the Czech Academy of Sciences
summary: Czech Academy of Sciences institute in Prague 4, listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of the GlobalFungi paper.

name: Institute of Vertebrate Biology of the Czech Academy of Sciences
summary: Brno institute researching free-living vertebrates, whose GBIF record describes biological collections including the IVB Genetic Bank, with data regularly published through GGBN.

name: Jednotný program sčítání ptáků
summary: Long-term programme run by the Czech Society for Ornithology that tracked annual trends in common breeding birds and ran until 2024, alongside the Lineal Species Census.

name: JUICE
summary: Software for vegetation classification, as listed on the department's site, with no further detail given.

name: Katedra geoinformatiky, Fakulta životního prostředí UJEP
summary: Department at the UJEP environment faculty that researches GIS and remote sensing for landscape change, including the cross-border Czech-Saxon Switzerland region, and has drones with thermal and multispectral cameras.

name: Kočka divoká
summary: Plans camera-trap and genetic monitoring of wildcats in 2025 and 2026, plus an online database of project photographs of wildcats, domestic cats and hybrids.

name: Kroužkovací stanice Národního muzea
summary: Part of the National Museum, founded in 1934, it coordinates bird ringing in the Czech Republic and holds over 5 million records, and it partners with EURING.

name: Lineal Species Census
summary: Long-term citizen science bird monitoring programme run by the Czech Society for Ornithology, in which volunteers record each bird's position and behaviour on Android mobile devices.

name: LTER-CZ
summary: Network of 24 research sites for long-term ecosystem research, four of them part of an LTSER platform, governed by a Czech ILTER committee led by Jakub Hruška.

name: Masaryk University
summary: A Czech university that runs the Czech National Phytosociological Database, builds Pladias, and is listed by Biodiversa+ as a partner in DNAquaIMG through its Department of Geography.

name: Mendelova univerzita v Brně
summary: University whose forestry faculty reports a three-year urban wildlife study using more than 150,000 camera-trap images, and which is one of five partners in the Czech-Slovak wildcat project.

name: Mezinárodní sčítání vodních ptáků v ČR
summary: Waterbird count in the Czech Republic that has run without a break since January 1966, monitoring numbers and their changes, and is coordinated by the Czech University of Life Sciences Prague.

name: Ministry of the Environment of the Czech Republic
summary: The Czech ministry with main responsibility for implementing the national biodiversity strategy and monitoring progress, and listed by Biodiversa+ as a Czech partner.

name: Ministry of Transport of the Czech Republic
summary: A Czech ministry that the National Space Plan 2026-2032 names as coordinating state, industry and academia in Czech space activities, which include Earth observation data for environmental and climate protection.

name: Monitoring evropsky významných druhů šelem ve vybraných lokalitách soustavy Natura 2000
summary: Closed project run by Hnutí DUHA that mapped wolf, brown bear, lynx and wildcat with camera traps and genetic methods, covering 241 squares (6,025 square kilometres) from July 2015 to June 2016.

name: Monitoring sýčka obecného na Moravě
summary: Closed project run by ZO ČSOP Nový Jičín that used sound recordings, call playback and camera traps, checking 631 sites and confirming little owls at 15.

name: Moravský ornitologický spolek
summary: Non-governmental non-profit and Czech Society for Ornithology branch since 2005, whose members monitor breeding success of selected species at Filena through CES and terns on artificial islands.

name: National Biodiversity Portal
summary: A Czech portal run by the Nature Conservation Agency that, according to GBIF's publisher record for the agency, holds data about species and habitats.

name: Nature Conservation Agency of the Czech Republic
summary: Czech governmental body established in 2015 that runs the Nature Conservation Finds Database and National Biodiversity Portal and is registered as a GBIF data publisher.

name: NetFor
summary: A project, described in a November 2023 press release, to move to automatic real-time monitoring of pedunculate oak vitality in Danube-region floodplains, led by Marko Stojanović.

name: Nálezová databáze ochrany přírody
summary: A Czech database run by the Nature Conservation Agency that collects available species occurrence data for conservation authorities and for public use, including research.

name: Národní inventarizace lesů
summary: A Czech independent survey of the state and development of forests, whose second inventory estimated forest land at 2,904.2 thousand hectares, 36.8 per cent of the country.

name: Národní lesnický institut
summary: State administrative authority under the Ministry of Agriculture from 1 January 2026, formerly ÚHÚL, which runs the National Forest Inventory combining field plots with remote sensing and holds powers under the EU deforestation regulation.

name: Ostravská univerzita
summary: University whose project list includes the completed January 2015 to April 2017 monitoring of carnivore species in Natura 2000 sites, which planned genetic analysis of non-invasively collected DNA samples.

name: Pladias Database of the Czech Flora and Vegetation
summary: A database of Czech flora and vegetation, built by Masaryk University, the Institute of Botany and the University of South Bohemia, funded by the Czech Science Foundation from 2014 to 2018 and still updated.

name: Plan4all
summary: A Czech organisation registered at the Regional Court in Plzeň, listed by CORDIS as a Czech participant in BioClima.

name: Plant.id
summary: A model built by FlowerChecker, for which a January 2023 cc.cz article reported that the FlowerChecker project helped identify about 30 million plants a year.

name: PlantBank
summary: A Czech consortium of four members that jointly operates an e-infrastructure for curated plant and vegetation data, and runs Pladias, according to GBIF's publisher record.

name: Refugium
summary: Private Czech company, not a non-profit or state agency, that invests in damaged natural sites to restore natural processes, funded by philanthropic investors, corporate partnerships and grants.

name: Rings Online
summary: Digital bird ringing database launched in autumn 2016 that allows direct entry of ringing and recovery locations, within a station database of over 3.5 million records and 300,000 recoveries.

name: Spolek Ametyst
summary: Association with branch associations whose 2024 annual report says its nature conservation section monitored the spring black grouse lek in 2024, alongside management plans and biological surveys.

name: Správa Krkonošského národního parku
summary: Based in Vrchlabí, it processes data using GIS and databases; its 2024–2025 project aimed to monitor protected species, with a planned black grouse acoustic monitoring pilot.

name: Správa Národního parku Podyjí
summary: State contributory organisation in Znojmo whose contracts register lists monitoring of fish migration, beavers, golden jackal and Aesculapian snake, and which is to take over the monitoring system developed by the BioReMo project.

name: Správa Národního parku České Švýcarsko
summary: Park administration whose stated research directions include comprehensive monitoring of the natural environment, and which reported placing camera traps to monitor wild animals in November 2023.

name: Správa Národního parku Šumava
summary: Park administration that has run forest biomonitoring in non-intervention areas since 2008, monitored lynx since the 1990s including telemetry and camera traps, and monitored peatlands in detail since 2005.

name: System for cyanobacteria monitoring in water reservoirs using remote sensing and artificial intelligence methods
summary: Finished Technology Agency-funded project that, per the funder's evaluation, combined remote sensing and in-situ sampling to calibrate an AI-based model built into publicly accessible software for monitoring cyanobacteria in reservoirs.

name: T. G. Masaryk Water Research Institute
summary: A Czech state environmental institute whose research areas include aquatic biodiversity protection, groundwater protection and assessment of the status of waters, and whose site lists online water quality monitoring on the Bečva river.

name: Technology Agency of the Czech Republic
summary: A Czech agency that announced preparations for the third call of its Prostředí pro život 2 research programme, with biodiversity and landscape as a topic, and is listed by Biodiversa+ as a partner.

name: Tilia Impact Ventures
summary: An investor that, according to an August 2026 cc.cz article, led Flox Intelligence's three-million-dollar Seed+ investment round in 2026.

name: University of South Bohemia
summary: A Czech university that builds Pladias and is listed by Biodiversa+ as a partner in FunDive and SEPPI, through its Faculty of Science and Department of Biology of Ecosystems.

name: Využití nástrojů biologgingu a volně dostupných datových zdrojů pro hodnocení kvality habitatu, existenčních rizik a efektivní plánování ochrany u ptáků ohrožených úbytkem vody v krajině
summary: Technology Agency-funded project, recorded as closed, that aims to link in-situ data on two model bird species with satellite data and observation databases, then extrapolate results to the Czech Republic.

name: Víceúrovňová datová analýza pro správu ekosystémů říčních toků s využitím automatizovaných nástrojů
summary: Technology Agency-funded project, June 2025 to May 2028, planning AI-based freshwater degradation analysis and testing in Brazil, the Czech-Polish border region and Spain.

name: Výzkumný ústav lesního hospodářství a myslivosti
summary: Czech research institute (VÚLHM) whose site lists forest condition monitoring, an online forest protection service and a national bank of seed and explants of forest trees.

name: Výzkumný ústav pro krajinu
summary: A Czech state environmental research institute, listed by the Nature Conservation Agency, whose site shows biomonitoring, forest ecology and spatial ecology departments.

name: ZO ČSOP Nový Jičín 70/02
summary: Basic organisation of the Czech Union for Nature Conservation, registered as a branch association, whose little owl monitoring project used sound recording for computer analysis, call playback and camera traps at sites where owls were heard.

name: Česká botanická společnost
summary: Non-governmental non-profit association of professional and amateur botanists, founded in 1912, whose Vratička floristic database for plant records held 167,145 records by 4 December 2024, according to its 2024 report.

name: Česká informační agentura životního prostředí
summary: Subsidised Ministry of the Environment organisation that provides validated environmental data and mapping services, and has led the national GEO/Copernicus secretariat since 1 January 2020.

name: Česká společnost ornitologická
summary: Scientific bird organisation founded in 1926 that says it is BirdLife International's Czech partner, runs the Avif database and Lineal Species Census, and counted a record 1,269 volunteers in its 12th white stork count.

name: Česká zemědělská univerzita v Praze
summary: University whose work includes planned bird and satellite data linkage, wolf genetic monitoring, wildlife GPS telemetry and coordination of the Czech waterbird census.

name: Advanced Identification Methods
summary: Company spun out of the Bavarian State Collection of Zoology that offers DNA metabarcoding of environmental samples as a service to research institutes, authorities and companies, and is building the spcfy data platform.

name: AI Lab at the German Environment Agency
summary: Lab at the German Environment Agency that builds AI and big data applications for federal environment agencies, including species protection and environmental monitoring.

name: AI National Park
summary: Monitoring system with camera traps, audio loggers and climate loggers, supported by AI, being installed in 13 German national parks and two wilderness areas from 2025 to 2027.

name: AI-BioDynamics
summary: German-Korean research collaboration from 2025 to 2029 building an AI monitoring platform that combines satellite imagery, radar and citizen science observations.

name: AI-Klima
summary: Interreg project that uses AI and remote sensing to monitor forest health in the Bavarian Forest and Šumava national parks.

name: AI-REEFSHIELD
summary: KI-Leuchtturm project to monitor offshore marine habitats with AI in a way that spares reefs and reduces crewed ship trips.

name: AI4Forest
summary: Develops AI methods to monitor forests from radar and optical satellite imagery and to build high-resolution global maps of canopy height, biomass and disturbance.

name: AI4Wildlife
summary: University of Bayreuth research on wildlife and visitor activity in the Veldensteiner Forest, using camera traps since 2020 and an active learning tool to classify images, with the Bavarian State Institute of Forestry and LMU.

name: AI4WildLIVE
summary: BiodivKI project developing an analysis portal for monitoring data from citizen science and sensors.

name: AMMOD
summary: German project described by Microsoft as a kind of weather station for biodiversity. The project's own page could not be read.

name: Animal Sound Archive
summary: Bioacoustic collection at the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin, with around 120,000 recordings of birds, mammals and other animals and a database of over 40,000 audio files.

name: Archaster Labs
summary: Brings satellite, biodiversity, water and forest data together with AI for users without a geodata team.

name: ArtenFinder
summary: Citizen science platform and app for reporting animals, plants and fungi, run in Rhineland-Palatinate and Berlin, with data passed to nature conservation authorities and a web service interface.

name: ArtenFinder RLP
summary: Reporting platform for sightings of animals, plants and fungi in Rhineland-Palatinate. Reports are checked by experts and feed the state's official data.

name: Artenglück
summary: Helps companies in German-speaking countries plan and monitor their own nature projects, using soil, water and plant samples and sensors with AI.

name: ASMSpotter
summary: AI tool for detecting artisanal mining from public Sentinel-2 data, built by dida Datenschmiede; its demo case study reports increased deforestation in Brokopondo, Suriname since 2017, and it won the Microsoft AI Award 2020.

name: Audi Stiftung für Umwelt
summary: Foundation that the LBV names as partner in its pilot with listening boxes for acoustic monitoring. Its own site refused the fetcher.

name: Baden-Württemberg Stiftung
summary: Foundation with an Earth observation programme for research projects at the interface of Earth observation, AI data analysis and decision support.

name: bAImo
summary: bayklif2 project building an AI-supported, model-based insect monitoring system for Bavaria.

name: Barcoding Fauna Bavarica
summary: DNA barcoding project for Bavarian animal species, begun in 2009 at the Zoologische Staatssammlung München, according to an article by Axel Hausmann.

name: Bavarian Forest National Park
summary: German national park that has used camera traps since 1997, and runs joint biodiversity monitoring with Berchtesgaden National Park since 2021.

name: Bavarian State Institute of Forestry
summary: Bavarian state forestry institute that studies AI and remote sensing for crown damage in the ForstEO project and works with the University of Bayreuth on AI4Wildlife.

name: Bavarian State Ministry of Food, Agriculture, Forestry and Tourism
summary: Bavarian state ministry whose Board of Forestry Research funds AI4Wildlife.

name: Bavarian State Ministry of Science and the Arts
summary: Bavarian state ministry that funds the bayklif2 research network, including its AI biodiversity monitoring projects.

name: Bayerisches Landesamt für Umwelt
summary: Bavarian state environment agency, which publishes the BayWAT-AI project on modelling river temperature.

name: bayklif2
summary: Second Bavarian climate research network, funded by the Bavarian science ministry, with six projects including AI-based biodiversity monitoring.

name: BaySenseAI
summary: Bavarian project on a scalable biodiversity observation and prediction platform based on community sensors and AI, led by Florian Hartig and funded by the Bavarian science ministry.

name: BayWAT-AI
summary: Process-based and AI modelling of water temperatures in Bavarian rivers, including LSTM network approaches, as tools for water management.

name: bbe Moldaenke GmbH
summary: Makes water quality instruments and software, including algae spectrofluorometers and toximeter warning systems; its managing director says SIMON enables sensor adaptation for autonomous underwater vehicles.

name: Bee friendly UG
summary: German company in Wiesloch that makes a solar-powered AI camera trap for counting and classifying insects, creates habitat on customers' land, and combines local insect data with remote sensing data.

name: BeeVision
summary: University of Hohenheim project from January 2024, planned for two years, on a camera and AI system that recognises pollinator groups from their flight patterns, without harming the insects.

name: Behörde für Umwelt, Klima, Energie und Agrarwirtschaft
summary: Hamburg environment and agriculture authority, partnered with SIMON, which says more than 10% of Hamburg's land is nature reserve.

name: BenthicAI
summary: Helmholtz Imaging project that combines underwater cameras and acoustic sonar with AI to reveal seabed life such as worms and clams.

name: Berchtesgaden National Park
summary: German national park that runs biodiversity monitoring on 54 permanent plots, including DNA sequencing of fungi, jointly with Bavarian Forest National Park since 2021.

name: Bergwaldprojekt
summary: German conservation organisation that has worked with thousands of volunteers a year for over 35 years on forests, moors and open biotopes, and on 13 November 2026 planted 2,500 broadleaf trees at Hangelsberg.

name: Berliner Hochschule für Technik
summary: Berlin university of applied sciences named with Umweltbildungszentrum Listhof on the KInsecta citizen science project.

name: BExIS
summary: Data management system of the Biodiversity Exploratories, with a growing set of freely available datasets.

name: Bi-O-Ton
summary: Classifies the biodiversity of meadows with machine learning, using citizen science sound recordings and satellite images.

name: Bio-O-Ton
summary: BiodivKI project linking sound recordings from the public with satellite data to assess biotopes.

name: BioCASe
summary: Service network giving access to data on biological collections, with its secretariat at the Botanic Garden and Botanical Museum Berlin.

name: BioConsult SH
summary: Named as a research partner in the SeaMe project on marine monitoring in offshore wind farms.

name: BiodivDetect
summary: Funding initiative of the federal research ministry for technologies and methods that record and assess little-studied aspects of biodiversity in Germany. Submissions are open until 26 November 2026.

name: Biodiversity Exploratories
summary: Long-term open research platform in three German regions on how land use affects biodiversity and ecosystem processes, with more than 40 projects and a public data portal, BExIS.

name: Biodiversitätsmonitoring NRW
summary: North Rhine-Westphalia's state biodiversity monitoring, which observes the state and development of biological diversity under the state's nature conservation law.

name: BiodivKI
summary: German federal research funding measure for AI methods in biodiversity research, with nine consortia in a three-year main phase since May 2025.

name: BioFresh
summary: EU-funded project, from November 2009 to April 2014, on the status and trends of freshwater biodiversity. It built an information platform on freshwater biodiversity data, coordinated by the Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries.

name: BioIntAkt
summary: BiodivKI project using acoustic sensors to recognise species.

name: Biologische Station Mittlere Wupper
summary: Biological station for Remscheid, Solingen and Wuppertal, the three cities of the Bergisches Städtedreieck, whose main tasks are nature reserve care, contract nature conservation advice and education.

name: Biologische Station Zwillbrock
summary: NRW biological station that celebrated 40 years in 2026 as one of the network's pioneers; such stations are non-profit associations caring for over half of the state's nature reserves.

name: BioMe
summary: Modular UFZ infrastructure for biodiversity monitoring projects, first used by Tagfalter-Monitoring Deutschland.

name: biometrio.earth
summary: Saarbrücken company that reported on biodiversity in nature-based projects from camera trap, audio and satellite data using AI. A co-founder's page says it decided not to continue the business.

name: BioMLAgrar
summary: BiodivKI project studying AI-based strategies for biodiversity-friendly farming.

name: Biosphärenreservatsverwaltung Niedersächsische Elbtalaue
summary: Administration of the Elbtalaue biosphere reserve, reporting to the Lower Saxony environment ministry, covering land use, nature and genetic resource protection, research, monitoring and education, and acting as lower nature conservation authority in part C.

name: Biosphärenreservatsverwaltung Oberlausitzer Heide- und Teichlandschaft
summary: Administration of a UNESCO-recognised reserve that Sachsenforst has been responsible for since 2008, combining conservation authority, forestry and ranger tasks over 30,102 hectares as of 1 January 2018, seated in Malschwitz.

name: BioWaWiKI
summary: BiodivKI project using AI to safeguard biodiversity in areas used for water management.

name: BirdNET Live
summary: Smartphone app that identifies animal sounds with AI on the device, with no internet connection. It is a development of BirdNET.

name: BirdRecorder
summary: Combines stereo cameras with machine learning to detect and identify bird species sensitive to wind energy near turbines. The models were trained on about 680,000 images.

name: BirdVision GmbH & Co. KG
summary: Makes a camera system that detects birds near wind turbines, with an AI check that a detected object is a bird.

name: Botanic Garden and Botanical Museum Berlin
summary: Berlin botanical institution that GBIF Germany lists as responsible for coordination and for the plants and protists node.

name: BoTiKI
summary: KI-Leuchtturm project developing an efficient, low-cost AI system to study soil fauna.

name: Bund für Umwelt und Naturschutz Deutschland
summary: German environmental association that runs wildcat monitoring with the lure stick method.

name: BUND Naturschutz in Bayern
summary: Conservation association that has bought about 2,750 hectares of valuable land in Bavaria to secure it long term and has rented a further 750 hectares.

name: Bundesforst
summary: Body that looks after about 30,000 hectares of national natural heritage land staying in federal ownership, on behalf of the federal environment ministry.

name: Bundesministerium für Landwirtschaft, Ernährung und Heimat
summary: German federal agriculture ministry. It coordinates the national forest inventory and funds forest projects such as SENSURE Wald.

name: Bundesministerium für Verkehr
summary: German federal transport ministry. It funds ForestPulse and co-finances the national CODE-DE-Lab Earth observation platform.

name: Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft und Energie
summary: German federal economics ministry, named as funder of the Wildlife Disease Warning System through its SME innovation programme, and under its earlier name of KIHBA.

name: Bundeswaldinventur
summary: Germany's national forest inventory, a joint federal and state project coordinated by the agriculture ministry, with the Thünen Institute for Forest Ecosystems as inventory lead.

name: Carl von Ossietzky Universität Oldenburg
summary: A 2021 article names this university as one of three ChESS AI project partners and identifies ICBM as its institute.

name: Carl-Zeiss-Stiftung
summary: German foundation named as the funder of the BeeVision pollinator monitoring project.

name: ChESS
summary: Closed project in which, in 2021, DFKI, Oldenburg University and Jade Hochschule were developing an AI method to detect unusual changes in sensor data, planned to run to 2024.

name: Christian-Albrechts-Universität zu Kiel
summary: University in Kiel, listed as a funding recipient for the KIMMCO, SEAGUARD and DeepBirdDetect AI projects.

name: ci-tec GmbH
summary: Karlsruhe company and consortium member of the Bi-O-Ton project on machine learning from citizen science sound recordings and satellite images.

name: CODE-DE-Lab
summary: National platform for providing and processing Earth observation data in Germany, financed by the federal transport and research ministries.

name: Cognitive Weeding
summary: Finished KI-Leuchtturm project that used AI to keep as many arable weeds as possible alongside crops, for on-farm biodiversity.

name: Copernicus Netzwerkbüro Wald
summary: German network office on forests that surveys and promotes the use of remote sensing data and products by forest users.

name: Custom Animal Tracking Solutions (CATS)
summary: Company founded in 2012 making animal tracking products for conservation science, including the CATS Diary multi-sensor tag and CATS Cam video recorder, and reporting a first suction-cup video tag deployment on a false killer whale in March 2023.

name: Dachverband Deutscher Avifaunisten
summary: German federation of bird recorders that organises and coordinates national bird monitoring programmes and runs the ornitho recording platform.

name: DatKI4BKG
summary: Project of the Federal Agency for Cartography and Geodesy and DLR to build a remote sensing data management system and develop AI methods that support the German land cover model LBM-DE. Listed as running from October 2021 to April 2024.

name: Dawn Chorus
summary: International citizen science and art project recording birdsong. Since 2022 it has been run jointly by Naturkundemuseum Bayern/BIOTOPIA Lab and the LBV, to document bird diversity over the years through acoustic biomonitoring.

name: DBU Naturerbe GmbH
summary: Non-profit subsidiary of the Deutsche Bundesstiftung Umwelt, founded in 2007 in Osnabrück, that by 2024 had taken over 66 natural heritage areas of about 70,000 hectares in ten federal states.

name: deadtrees.earth
summary: Open database for accessing, sharing, analysing and visualising tree mortality data based on remote sensing, listed among the forest AI projects by the University of Freiburg.

name: Deeeper Technology GmbH
summary: Company listed by CopWald as active in forest remote sensing, with a stated field of AI and automated analysis of geodata.

name: Deep Learning Applied to Animal Linguistics
summary: Research project applying deep learning to underwater recordings of killer whales, to help marine biologists interpret their sounds.

name: DeepBirdDetect
summary: AI system for detecting bird species at risk from wind energy, from recordings of bird sound with deep learning. Funded with about 2.2 million euros from 2023 to 2025 and listed as finished by ZUG.

name: DeepTrees
summary: AI framework from the UFZ, based on deep learning and convolutional networks, used by Saxony's mapping office to analyse official digital orthophotos of forests.

name: Detection of Illegal Online Wildlife Trade
summary: Prototype tool that combines image classification and rule-based text analysis to detect illegal online wildlife trade, built by the German Environment Agency's AI Lab for the Federal Agency for Nature Conservation.

name: Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft
summary: German research funder that supports the Biodiversity Exploratories as an infrastructure priority programme (SPP 1374).

name: Deutsche Wildtier Stiftung
summary: German wildlife foundation that fits wildcats in the Altmark with GPS collars and follows them with camera traps in a study running since 2020.

name: Deutscher Jagdverband
summary: German hunters' association, whose WILD monitoring collects counts and surveys from hunting districts through an online portal.

name: dida Datenschmiede GmbH
summary: Berlin-based company whose ASMSpotter project uses AI and Sentinel-2 data to detect artisanal mining.

name: Dieing GmbH
