summary: Company listed as a funding recipient for the DraAuF reforestation project.

name: Digital.Natur.Landschaft
summary: Funding initiative of the German Federal Environmental Foundation for digital tools that measurably help environmental protection in land use, including biodiversity.

name: Distance Estimation and Animal Tracking for Wildlife Camera Trapping
summary: Open-source MIT-licensed pipeline built by Peter Johanns that uses MegaDetector to find animals in camera-trap video, then estimates their distance and tracks them without reference footage, for density estimation.

name: Distance Estimation Toolbox
summary: Code and graphical interface built by Timm Haucke on MegaDetector 5.0, based on 2022 research proposing automatic camera-to-animal distance measurement that reduced manual effort more than twenty-onefold.

name: Diversity Workbench
summary: Software for biodiversity information, developed since 2006 at the Bavarian Natural History Collections with the SNSB IT Center.

name: DLR-Wildretter
summary: DLR work, between 1990 and 2020, on remote sensing methods and prototypes to detect fawns and ground-nesting birds in meadows before mowing.

name: Dokumentations- und Beratungsstelle des Bundes zum Thema Wolf
summary: Federal documentation and advice centre on wolves, which publishes the official monitoring data for each monitoring year, with maps of occurrence.

name: DraAuF
summary: KI-Leuchtturm project on drone-supported automated reforestation, using AI to pick planting spots.

name: Dromni GmbH
summary: Company developing early detection of tree stress with drones and AI in the GreenView research project with EXCIT3D GmbH.

name: DVGW Deutscher Verein des Gas- und Wasserfaches
summary: Named on the federal research ministry's project sheet as coordinator of the IQ-Wasser project on AI for biodiversity research.

name: Earth Observation Center
summary: Germany's centre for Earth observation at DLR, formed by the German Remote Sensing Data Center and the Remote Sensing Technology Institute.

name: Earth Observation Services Jena GmbH
summary: Spin-off of the remote sensing chair at Friedrich Schiller University Jena, founded in 2012. Thünen's CopWald list names it for mapping forest biomass from microwave remote sensing.

name: ecoBay
summary: Joint LMU and TUM project using robotic sampling, eDNA and eRNA monitoring and AI to assess Bavarian lakes, funded with about 1.37 million euros over five years through the Bavarian Climate Research Network.

name: Edaphobase
summary: Open access data warehouse for soil biodiversity, combining data on soil animals, their distribution and habitats, developed and hosted by the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History Görlitz.

name: Emschergenossenschaft
summary: Public-law corporation converting the Emscher river system, with wastewater to be moved into closed sewers and the river and tributaries progressively restructured into near-natural waterways, described as an intergenerational project.

name: EnMAP
summary: German hyperspectral satellite mission that measures variables on the status and evolution of land and water ecosystems.

name: Entovia
summary: Develops AI monitoring of insects, plants and their interactions with ordinary smartphones.

name: enviaM
summary: Company listed by the CopWald service as active in forest remote sensing, offering Forest Health, a drone-flight vitality analysis to detect forest damage.

name: EO Wald
summary: Free DLR web service with interactive maps of forest canopy cover loss across Germany, monthly since September 2017 at 10 metre resolution, based on satellite data.

name: EO4Nature
summary: National portal for monitoring and applications in nature conservation and natural climate protection, which uses AI methods to supply information for planning and monitoring.

name: Erlebnis-Zoo Hannover
summary: Zoo that takes part in research with AI software that recognises ungulates on video and sorts their behaviour into categories.

name: explorer.land
summary: Geospatial platform built and run by openforests for mapping, monitoring and sharing restoration and conservation work, which says more than 2,000 projects worldwide use it.

name: Fachagentur Nachwachsende Rohstoffe
summary: Project management agency of the federal agriculture ministry, founded in 1993. It manages funding for forest projects such as SENSURE Wald.

name: Faszination nächtlicher Vogelzug
summary: LBV pilot that uses AI to make night-time bird migration audible and visible, with the aim of better protecting endangered species.

name: Federal Agency for Cartography and Geodesy
summary: Federal mapping agency. Pages from DLR and the German Environment Agency show it co-coordinating the Copernicus land service and moving AI methods for remote sensing into its land cover work.

name: Federal Agency for Nature Conservation
summary: Germany's federal scientific authority for nature conservation, responsible for federal observation of nature and landscape, and host of the National Monitoring Centre for Biodiversity at its Leipzig site.

name: Federal Institute of Hydrology
summary: German federal institute that runs a joint transfer lab with DFKI on AI for federal waterways, covering hydrological, ecological and other processes.

name: Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency
summary: German higher federal authority whose site lists a marine environmental monitoring network and the MARNET monitoring network.

name: Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space
summary: German federal ministry that leads on space and funds AI biodiversity research through the BiodivKI measure and technology for biodiversity assessment through BiodivDetect.

name: Firetail
summary: Desktop application built by Schäuffelhut Berger for visualising and annotating tagged animal movement data, with a machine learning behaviour-labelling module, connecting to Movebank and described by its developers as successor to the Movebank Acceleration Viewer.

name: FiVe3D
summary: DBU-funded project on remote sensing methods for monitoring forest structure.

name: FloraWeb
summary: Federal Agency for Nature Conservation information service on the distribution, threat, protection and ecology of Germany's wild plants.

name: FluBioKI
summary: Finished project on insect monitoring from a drone, using fluorescence and AI image recognition.

name: FNEWs
summary: Forest damage monitoring from Sentinel-2 imagery. A factsheet says implementation started at the Thünen Institute of Forest Ecosystems from 2024, extending the method to all of Germany.

name: FOGS
summary: Reference database and data portal of genetic markers that helps authorities assign confiscated wildlife material to species and populations, built by the LIB.

name: ForestChangeAI
summary: AI system for updating forest management data automatically from remote sensing analysis.

name: ForestPulse
summary: Forest monitoring project at Thünen that derives forest structure from airborne laser scanning at Bundeswaldinventur plots and tree crown segmentation.

name: ForestWatch
summary: Free nationwide service from LUP that monitors loss of forest vitality in Germany from a Sentinel-2 time series.

name: Forschungsinitiative zum Erhalt der Artenvielfalt
summary: German federal research initiative on biodiversity, part of the FONA sustainability research framework, which funds dozens of projects across Germany, including an AI funding line.

name: Forschungsinstitut für Bergbaufolgelandschaften
summary: German research body named by FEdA as home of the lead of FluBioKI.

name: Forschungsverbund Berlin
summary: Named on the federal research ministry's project sheet as coordinator of the SmartPatrol project on AI for biodiversity research.

name: ForstEO
summary: Research project from 2023 to 2026 of the Bavarian State Institute of Forestry and partners on detecting forest crown damage with AI and remote sensing.

name: Forstliche Versuchs- und Forschungsanstalt Baden-Württemberg
summary: Forest research institute of Baden-Württemberg. Its remote sensing unit develops methods for biodiversity monitoring, tree species and damage recognition and forest inventory.

name: Fraunhofer FKIE
summary: Fraunhofer institute that develops the analysis tools for AMMOD, using AI for sensor data fusion.

name: Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits
summary: Fraunhofer institute that co-develops the GAIA animal tags carrying on-board AI, a camera and satellite communication with the Leibniz Institute for Zoo and Wildlife Research.

name: Fraunhofer-Institut für Digitale Medientechnologie IDMT
summary: Fraunhofer research institute for digital media technology. It built the TrapScan camera-trap analysis tool with WWF Germany.

name: Fraunhofer-Institut für Graphische Datenverarbeitung IGD
summary: Fraunhofer institute working on AI for nature and marine monitoring, including the KIMoPa peatland vegetation project and plankton image analysis.

name: Freie Universität Berlin
summary: German university named on a published map of tree species in Germany made with Sentinel-2 time series and the SITS-BERT model.

name: Freshwater Information Platform
summary: Website launched in 2015 that brings together information and findings from freshwater ecosystem research.

name: Friedrich Schiller University Jena
summary: German research body named by FEdA as home of the lead of LEPMON.

name: Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg
summary: German university whose researchers apply deep learning to underwater recordings of killer whales in the Deep Learning Applied to Animal Linguistics project.

name: GAF
summary: Munich geoinformation company whose site lists forestry and land services and which heads a consortium for the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service High Resolution Layers for 2025 to 2028.

name: GAIA initiative
summary: Research on animal tags with on-board AI, a camera and satellite communication, developed by Leibniz-IZW and Fraunhofer IIS and tested on vultures at Tierpark Berlin and in Namibia as an early warning of ecological change.

name: GBIF Germany
summary: Germany's GBIF node system, in which eight nodes at German museums and collections mobilise biodiversity data, each for a range of taxonomic groups.

name: GEBIKI
summary: BiodivKI project combining genomic data with remote sensing to record biodiversity.

name: Geo Engine
summary: Start-up from the University of Marburg's database group with a cloud platform for spatio-temporal data whose results can feed machine learning. It grew from the GFBio and Natur 4.0 biodiversity projects.

name: Georg-August-Universität Göttingen
summary: University listed as a funding recipient for the KI-Recover forest project.

name: German Aerospace Center
summary: Germany's aerospace research centre, which gives specialist support to the federal ministry leading on space. Its Earth Observation Center builds satellite forest monitoring services for Germany.

name: German Barcode of Life
summary: Genetic reference library of Germany's fauna and flora.

name: German Environment Agency
summary: Germany's main environmental protection agency. It shares national coordination of the Copernicus land service and is responsible for the national CORINE Land Cover dataset.

name: German Federal Environmental Foundation
summary: German environmental foundation that funds digital tools for biodiversity, climate adaptation and soil protection through its Digital.Natur.Landschaft initiative.

name: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence
summary: German AI research centre that develops the autonomous underwater vehicle DeepLeng for marine monitoring in SeaMe and runs a joint transfer lab with the Federal Institute of Hydrology.

name: Gesellschaft für Biologische Daten
summary: German association of people and institutions that generate biological and environmental data, and a coordinating partner in NFDI4Biodiversity.

name: GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences
summary: German research body named by FEdA as home of the lead of MikroKIez.

name: GhostNetZero.ai
summary: Online platform from WWF Germany, Microsoft and Accenture on which sonar recordings of the seabed are donated and analysed by AI to mark likely positions of lost fishing nets.

name: GIZ chatbot for Open Foris Whisp
summary: Chatbot developed by GIZ that connects directly to Open Foris Whisp, according to an FAO blog on AI in forest monitoring.

name: Global Nature Fund
summary: Nature organisation that works with ZALF on KICS-Zert, an AI tool for monitoring biodiversity on certified farmland, and brings companies' needs into its development.

name: Gorilla Tracker
summary: Hasso Plattner Institute project that identifies individual gorillas on zoo video with deep learning and follows them over long periods.

name: green account
summary: Bielefeld start-up offering digital tools to record, assess and market ecosystem services, which also plans and develops restoration projects and documents results in annual impact reports.

name: greeNature
summary: Company that says it has more than 10,000 hectares of its own land across Germany and offers compensation sites, species protection measures, replacement afforestation and in-house GIS mapping.

name: GreenView
summary: Research project on early detection of tree stress from multispectral and RGB drone data with AI, funded by the EU and North Rhine-Westphalia.

name: GRÜNBLICK
summary: DLR Earth Observation Center project on an AI system for forest monitoring that estimates forest biomass from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data. Listed as running from August 2024 to February 2026.

name: Hamburg Port Authority
summary: Public-law port body that launched and builds the SIMON project, announced in February 2026, to test sensor-equipped autonomous underwater vehicles in the tidal Elbe, with federal funding.

name: Hamburg University of Technology
summary: University whose Smart Sensors Group partners in BioIntAkt-2, responsible for developing the intelligent acoustic sensor system and hardware accelerators for embedded AI on the sensor.

name: Hasso-Plattner-Institut
summary: Computer science institute whose AI and intelligent systems group built the Gorilla Tracker with zoo video.

name: Heinz Sielmann Stiftung
summary: Foundation that since 2012 has looked after about 4,000 hectares in the south of the former Wittstock training area, securing it as national natural heritage.

name: Helmholtz Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Unit
summary: Helmholtz unit named as a collaborator on the AqQua aquatic foundation model.

name: Helmholtz Foundation Model Initiative
summary: Helmholtz initiative that funds the team building AqQua, a foundation AI model for pelagic imaging.

name: Helmholtz Imaging
summary: Helmholtz platform named as a collaborator on the AqQua aquatic foundation model.

name: Helmholtz Institute for Functional Marine Biodiversity
summary: Marine biodiversity institute at the University of Oldenburg and a research partner in SeaMe.

name: Helmholtz Munich
summary: German research body named by FEdA as home of the lead of GEBIKI.

name: Helmholtz-Zentrum Potsdam - Deutsches GeoForschungsZentrum GFZ
summary: Named on the federal research ministry's project sheet as coordinator of the MikroKIez project on AI for biodiversity research.

name: Hessisches Landesamt für Naturschutz, Umwelt und Geologie
summary: Hessian state agency for nature, environment and geology, with a remote sensing topic covering sensors on satellites, aircraft and drones.

name: Hochschule Anhalt
summary: University of applied sciences behind the MeineWaldKI citizen forest monitoring project.

name: Hochschule für angewandte Wissenschaften Kempten
summary: University of applied sciences listed as a funding recipient for the DraAuF reforestation project.

name: Hochschule für angewandte Wissenschaften München
summary: University of applied sciences listed as a funding recipient for the DraAuF reforestation project.

name: Hochschule Weihenstephan-Triesdorf
summary: German university named on the bayklif2 site as home of project leads of SmartReForest.

name: Hochschule Zittau/Görlitz
summary: University of applied sciences listed as a funding recipient for the BoTiKI soil fauna project.

name: IABG mbH
summary: Company listed by the CopWald service as active in forest remote sensing, offering satellite land-use classification, change analyses, storm damage studies and biomass estimation.

name: iForest
summary: Finished project that combined drone, Flora Incognita, iNaturalist and remote sensing data with AI to derive forest biodiversity.

name: Insector
summary: Solar-powered AI camera trap built by Bee friendly that counts and classifies insects and uploads data over LTE; in October 2024 Bee friendly reported testing it with Fraunhofer IBP on green facades.

name: Institut für Hygiene und Umwelt
summary: Hamburg institute presenting the city's nine-station water quality monitoring network, and, per Hamburg's environment senator, bringing sensor and measurement expertise to SIMON.

name: Institute for Chemistry and Biology of the Marine Environment
summary: Oldenburg marine research institute that, according to a 2021 article, operates the Spiekeroog Coastal Observatory.

name: Institute of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology
summary: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology institute that runs Bio-O-Ton, named as the project's management.

name: IQ-Wasser
summary: BiodivKI project on methods for forecasting biodiversity and water quality in reservoirs.

name: ISOE Institute for Social-Ecological Research
summary: Research institute contributing to Bio-O-Ton by working with stakeholders on biodiversity indicators and the questions put to a tool combining user-submitted audio with satellite images.

name: Jade Hochschule Wilhelmshaven/Oldenburg/Elsfleth
summary: University of applied sciences that in 2021 was working to develop and evaluate software architectures for the AI methods in ChESS.

name: Johann Heinrich von Thünen-Institut
summary: German federal research institute for rural areas, forests and fisheries, based in Braunschweig. Its forest ecosystems institute leads the national forest inventory and coordinates national forest monitoring. Its main site refused the fetcher, so facts come from its project sites and partners.

name: Julius Kühn-Institut
summary: Research institute whose Institute for Plant Protection in Field Crops and Grassland is named as a close cooperation partner in BioIntAkt-2.

name: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology
summary: German research body named by FEdA as home of the lead of Bio-O-Ton, BioWaWiKI.

name: KI-gestützte InsektenMonitoring-Station
summary: Insect monitoring station with AI from the Umwelt-Campus of Hochschule Trier, which received 24,500 euros from the Prototype Fund Hardware in November 2024.

name: KI-Lab am UBA
summary: Applied AI and big data laboratory at the German Environment Agency. It serves as an innovation space for the authorities of the environment ministry and has 25 staff.

name: KI-Leuchttürme
summary: German federal environment ministry funding programme for AI projects on environment, climate and nature, with 53 projects and about 70 million euros across its first two rounds. Its third round sought AI projects for nature-based climate action and biodiversity.

name: KI-Recover
summary: KI-Leuchtturm project on AI for choosing climate-resilient tree species and managing reforestation in national parks, protected areas and forest authorities.

name: KI4Forst
summary: Project listed by the University of Freiburg that detects forest areas and their changes from Copernicus Sentinel data with deep learning and shows them on maps.

name: KIBA-D
summary: Eighteen-month FEdA project that trains large language models on the Faktencheck Artenvielfalt data to keep an assessment of German biodiversity up to date from text sources.

name: KIBI
summary: Simplifies the mapping of protected plant communities with machine learning on satellite and aerial images.

name: KICS-Zert
summary: BiodivKI project using AI and citizen science to test how effective biodiversity projects are.

name: KIForst
summary: Competence centre at the University of Göttingen that strengthens the use of AI and machine learning in forest science.

name: KIHBA
summary: Researches a deep learning method for tree species classification across Bavaria from high-resolution remote sensing data. Funded from May 2021 to November 2023.

name: KIMERA
summary: Three-year project developing an AI to make predictive maps for spatial planning in the deep sea, supporting the designation of marine protected areas.

name: KIMMCO
summary: KI-Leuchtturm project developing AI-supported monitoring of phytoplankton in the German coastal Baltic Sea.

name: KIMoPa
summary: Joint project that uses drones and AI to recognise and classify peatland vegetation on rewetted moors, and to build a digital monitoring platform.

name: KInsecta
summary: Open source project of the Technische Hochschule Berlin and the Listhof environmental education centre in Reutlingen on low-cost AI insect monitoring with a camera and an optical wing beat sensor.

name: KIWA
summary: Project on using unmanned drones with cameras and AI to assess forest and land fires, funded by the environment ministry from 2023 to the end of 2025.

name: Landesamt für Geobasisinformation Sachsen
summary: Saxony's state mapping office. With M.O.S.S. it ran a pilot that analyses official high-resolution geodata of forests automatically with AI.

name: Landesamt für Natur, Umwelt und Klima Nordrhein-Westfalen
summary: North Rhine-Westphalia state office that runs the Eifel National Park administration, which the KI-Nationalpark list gives as a participating area.

name: Landesamt für Umwelt Brandenburg
summary: Brandenburg state agency that says it manages the region's nature parks and biosphere reserves, and lists collecting, analysing and providing nature data among its tasks.

name: Landesanstalt für Bienenkunde, Universität Hohenheim
summary: Bee research institute at the University of Hohenheim, which leads the BeeVision insect monitoring project.

name: Landesbetrieb für Küstenschutz, Nationalpark und Meeresschutz Schleswig-Holstein
summary: State enterprise in Husum whose national park administration, seated in Tönning, was in October 2024 one of six departments, covering the 4,380 square kilometre Schleswig-Holstein Wadden Sea National Park.

name: Landesbund für Vogel- und Naturschutz
summary: Bavarian nature conservation association that runs the Dawn Chorus birdsong recording project jointly with Naturkundemuseum Bayern/BIOTOPIA Lab.

name: Landschaftspflegeverband Mittelfranken
summary: Association describing itself as service provider for nature, landscape and climate protection in Middle Franconia since 1986; a 9 March 2026 item reports 20 volunteers cared for sandy grassland under its guidance.

name: Lebendiger Atlas der Natur Deutschlands
summary: Biodiversity portal for Germany put together by NFDI4Biodiversity and hosted by GBIF, gathering national and regional occurrence datasets.

name: Leeana
summary: Berlin-registered company that began by helping sustainability teams run site-level checks on protected areas, species sensitivity and water risk, and offers a plain-language workspace with its own database of protected areas.

name: Lehrstuhl für Global Change Ecology, Universität Würzburg
summary: University of Würzburg chair that hosts the ecological modelling part of the bAImo insect monitoring project.

name: Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research
summary: German research body named by FEdA as home of the lead of KICS-Zert.

name: Leibniz Centre for Tropical Marine Research
summary: Bremen marine research centre, a partner in the MOOBYF open-ocean monitoring project and in NFDI4Biodiversity. Its own site did not answer.

name: Leibniz Institute for Baltic Sea Research Warnemünde
summary: Leibniz institute for Baltic Sea research that offers ODIN 2, an online search of its measurement database with over 90 million records since 1877.

name: Leibniz Institute for the Analysis of Biodiversity Change
summary: Institute with a Bonn site that holds GBIF Germany's vertebrate node.

name: Leibniz Institute for Zoo and Wildlife Research
summary: Berlin research institute on the adaptability of wildlife, which co-develops AI animal tags for the GAIA initiative with Fraunhofer IIS.

name: Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries
summary: Berlin freshwater research institute, a partner in the TRANSPONDER pond monitoring project and in NFDI4Biodiversity.

name: LEPMON
summary: BiodivKI project from 2023 to 2027 developing an automated recorder for nocturnal insects (ARNI) that photographs moths at night, with AI to identify them, for use across Germany.

name: Local Cosmos
summary: Non-profit, open-source software project that lets institutions and small local groups build apps and websites for species identification, monitoring and education without programming.

name: Loki Schmidt Stiftung
summary: Foundation that by June 2022 reported over 40 years of buying, designing and caring for nature protection land in Hamburg and across Germany, and then leased meadows in Rahlstedt needing volunteers for scything.

name: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
summary: Munich university that runs ecoBay with the Technical University of Munich and is a partner in AI4Wildlife.

name: Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
summary: Munich university that models river temperature in BayWAT-AI and cooperates on AI-Klima.

name: LUP - Luftbild Umwelt Planung GmbH
summary: Remote sensing company that maps biotopes and land use and monitors Habitats Directive sites with very high resolution satellite data. It runs the free ForestWatch service and is a recipient in KI-Recover.

name: Machine Learning Kaiserslautern-Landau
summary: University initiative on machine learning for sustainable production and the environment, using sources such as satellite images and biological monitoring data to predict environmental impacts.

name: Marine Dateninfrastruktur Deutschland
summary: Shared marine data infrastructure of German authorities responsible for coasts and seas. The Federal Agency for Nature Conservation currently holds its project lead and budget.

name: MeineWaldKI
summary: Research project of Hochschule Anhalt that tests how citizens' photos and purpose-built AI models can improve forest condition surveys, in Halle and the Karstlandschaft Südharz biosphere reserve.

name: Melchionna - Remote Sensing
summary: Company listed by the CopWald service as active in forest remote sensing, with a stated field of satellite-based thematic maps of deforestation, vegetation and forest fire.

name: Mellumrat
summary: Association that looks after the islands of Mellum and Wangerooge, the Minsener Oog structure and an inland nature reserve, with state of Lower Saxony funds for its care work.

name: Michael Succow Stiftung
summary: German foundation working on peatlands, near-natural forests and land use. At the Karrendorfer Wiesen site, continuous monitoring documents changes in vegetation and water balance.

name: MikroKIez
summary: Finished project on observing and predicting soil microbial diversity with AI.

name: Mission to Marsh gGmbH
summary: Non-profit company developing a satellite monitoring service for peatlands with the European Space Agency's Kick-Start initiative.

name: mundialis
summary: Company founded in 2015 to make satellite information available to customers. The Thünen CopWald list says it works with free geodata and free software in remote sensing.

name: Museum für Naturkunde Berlin
summary: Integrated research museum in the Leibniz Association, in Berlin, that runs the Naturblick app, whose AI recognises species, and holds GBIF Germany's nodes for insects and fossils.

name: NABU
summary: German nature conservation association. Its federal association has been a strategic partner of the naturgucker observation portal since 2016.

name: NABU-Bodenseezentrum
summary: Centre that looks after 28 valuable protected areas, including the 774 hectare Wollmatinger Ried - Untersee - Gnadensee nature reserve.

name: NABU-Stiftung Nationales Naturerbe
summary: Foundation that buys conservation land across Germany, with an undated NABU overview reporting over 16,200 hectares in its care and another source about 27,400 hectares in over 450 areas, including Südharz forest bought in 2025.

name: NABU|naturgucker
summary: Biodiversity portal and social network for nature observers that went online in February 2008 as a digital field book, with the NABU federal association as a strategic partner since 2016.

name: National Monitoring Centre for Biodiversity
summary: Federal centre opened in Leipzig in March 2021 at the Federal Agency for Nature Conservation, set up to make biodiversity monitoring data better available and to link the bodies that collect it.

name: Nationale Naturlandschaften
summary: Alliance of all German national parks, nature parks, biosphere reserves and wilderness areas, and project coordinator of AI National Park.

name: Nationales Biodiversitätsmonitoring im Wald
summary: Planned national biodiversity monitoring of forests in Germany, being worked out by a group of federal and state forestry and nature conservation representatives.

name: Nationalpark Harz
summary: National park taking part with twelve other parks and two wilderness areas in KI-Nationalpark, having installed 120 camera traps and 52 audio recorders whose data is analysed with AI.

name: Nationalpark Unteres Odertal
summary: National park listed as a participating area in KI-Nationalpark, where a 2022 report says camera-trap monitoring had already been carried out before a federal wildlife monitoring project.

name: Nationalpark- und Forstverwaltung Sächsische Schweiz
summary: Park and forest administration listed as a participating area in KI-Nationalpark, run by Staatsbetrieb Sachsenforst, with staff trained on site and involved in setting up monitoring.

name: Nationalparkamt Hunsrück-Hochwald
summary: National park authority listed as a participating area in KI-Nationalpark, where a 2022 report says camera-trap monitoring had already been carried out before a federal wildlife monitoring project.

name: Nationalparkamt Kellerwald-Edersee
summary: National park authority listed as a participating area in KI-Nationalpark, where a 2022 report says camera-trap monitoring had already been carried out before a federal wildlife monitoring project.

name: Nationalparkamt Müritz
summary: National park authority listed as a participating area in KI-Nationalpark, in the camera programme, with staff trained on site and involved in setting up the monitoring.

name: Nationalparkamt Vorpommern
summary: National park authority listed as a participating area in KI-Nationalpark, in the camera programme, with staff trained on site and involved in setting up the monitoring.

name: Nationalparkverwaltung Eifel
summary: National park administration listed as a participating area in KI-Nationalpark, run by the Landesamt für Natur, Umwelt und Klima Nordrhein-Westfalen, with staff trained on site.

name: Nationalparkverwaltung Hainich
summary: National park administration listed as a participating area in KI-Nationalpark, where a 2022 report says camera-trap monitoring had already been carried out before a federal wildlife monitoring project.

name: Nationalparkverwaltung Niedersächsisches Wattenmeer
summary: National park administration listed as a participating area in KI-Nationalpark, in the camera programme, with staff trained on site and involved in setting up the monitoring.

name: Nationalparkverwaltung Schwarzwald
summary: National park administration listed as a participating area in KI-Nationalpark, where a 2022 report says camera-trap monitoring had already been carried out before a federal wildlife monitoring project.

name: Naturblick
summary: Free app from the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin for recognising and recording urban species, with around 120,000 users, whose observations also go to research on Berlin's biodiversity.

name: Nature 4.0
summary: University of Marburg project funded by the Hesse LOEWE programme on a networked environmental monitoring system that uses animals and plants as carriers of sensors and cameras, tested in the university forest at Caldern.

name: NatureAI
summary: Finished project on automatic detection of biodiversity in German national nature landscapes with deep learning.

name: Naturkundemuseum Bayern
summary: Bavarian natural history museum that started the Dawn Chorus citizen science and art project on birdsong.

name: Naturpark Südschwarzwald e.V.
summary: Association carrying the Südschwarzwald nature park, with 115 member municipalities in 2017, when the park's 394,000 hectares were called the largest of Germany's 104 nature parks.

name: Naturschutz Berlin-Malchow
summary: Association whose Naturschutzstation Malchow, per the Berlin environment senate, cares for the Falkenberger Rieselfelder reserve, where it has run a grazing project since 1998, and which operates two environmental education centres.

name: Naturstiftung David
summary: Foundation that owns 182 hectares in the Hohe Schrecke, part received in 2012 as national natural heritage, and works on its long-term securing, development and care.

name: Naturwald Akademie
summary: Non-profit forest research organisation that develops satellite forest monitoring, joining Earth observation data with AI analysis, and co-published the Waldmonitor Deutschland.

name: Netzwerk Phytodiversität Deutschland
summary: German botanical network that runs Deutschlandflora, a national portal and app for collecting plant records.

name: Next Wave Carbon
summary: Company that uses AI on geospatial imagery, and aerial and underwater drones with computer vision, to estimate biomass and carbon stock in blue carbon ecosystems.

name: NFDI4Biodiversity
summary: German national research data infrastructure consortium that provides services and tools for managing biodiversity, ecology and environmental data.

name: Niedersächsischer Landesbetrieb für Wasserwirtschaft, Küsten- und Naturschutz
summary: Lower Saxony state agency whose protected-area documentation has centrally recorded and analysed all available protected-area data for over 25 years, with six nature stations looking after protected areas.

name: Niedersächsisches Ministerium für Wissenschaft und Kultur
summary: Lower Saxony ministry that, according to a 2021 article, funded ChESS with about 700,000 euros from the Niedersächsisches Vorab of the Volkswagen Foundation.

name: Nordwestdeutsche Forstliche Versuchsanstalt
summary: Forest research institute for north-west Germany, a partner in SENSURE Wald, which uses AI to improve the resolution of satellite data for finding forest damage.

name: north.io
summary: Company developing KIMERA, an AI tool that makes predictive seabed maps for deep-sea spatial planning.

name: NRW-Stiftung Naturschutz, Heimat- und Kulturpflege
summary: Foundation that by its 2024 milestone had bought 7,500 hectares for nature conservation in North Rhine-Westphalia, the largest being the 1,050-hectare Brachter Wald nature reserve.

name: ocell
summary: Forest management software company whose Forest Intelligence product uses AI models to analyse forest stands down to the individual tree.

name: OekoFor
summary: Maker of the ecoPi:Bird automated acoustic recorder for bird monitoring, with a neural network being developed to recognise target species.

name: OGF GmbH
summary: Forestry planning company developing ForestChangeAI, an AI system that updates forest inventory data from remote sensing.

name: ORCA-SPOT
summary: Toolkit that uses deep learning to detect killer whale sounds in underwater recordings.

name: ornitho.de
summary: Internet portal for bird observation and population surveys in Germany, whose verified records go to scientific evaluation and nature conservation.

name: OXO Earth
summary: Company that uses machine learning on ground and remote sensing data to quantify forest carbon, working with German forest owners on carbon removal projects, all in Germany.

name: PANGAEA
summary: Open repository that archives and publishes georeferenced data from Earth and environmental research, including ecology, fisheries and biological classification, jointly operated by the Alfred Wegener Institute and MARUM.

name: Pina Earth
summary: Sells carbon certificates from local forests in Europe, and builds a digital twin of each forest from a current inventory to quantify and show project progress.

name: PlanBlue
summary: Bremen start-up, spun out of the Max Planck Institute for Marine Microbiology, that brings new seafloor monitoring technology to market, including the DiveRay underwater camera.

name: Projektträger Jülich
summary: Project management agency that handles the BiodivKI funding measure for the federal research ministry, including project funding and communication.

name: Prototype Fund Hardware
summary: Fund for open hardware, which supported the Umwelt-Campus AI insect monitoring station.

name: RangerSound
summary: DBU-funded project in which the BirdNET Live app was developed.

name: RAPID
summary: Open-source, modular model built by the University of Stuttgart and WildCap that re-identifies known individual animals in real time from coat patterns, tested on six datasets.

name: Remote Sensing Solutions GmbH
summary: Company that published the first satellite forest monitor for Germany with the Naturwald Akademie, including AI mapping.

name: Rhineland-Palatinate University of Technology Kaiserslautern-Landau
summary: German university that launched the Machine Learning Kaiserslautern-Landau initiative, covering prediction of environmental impacts from satellite images and biological monitoring data.

name: RIFCON
summary: German scientific consultancy for agrochemical registration, with an environmental planning arm. It says it uses eDNA sampling, remote sensing and drones in wildlife field studies.

name: RiMoDi
summary: Satellite data project, reported by DLR, for monitoring deforestation-free supply chains. It gives authorities land use data so that the Federal Office for Agriculture and Food can check goods.

name: RobbenBlick
summary: WWF Germany pilot from 2025 on AI monitoring of grey seals in the Baltic.

name: Rote-Liste-Zentrum
summary: Coordinating office for Germany's national Red Lists of animals, plants and fungi, working on behalf of the Federal Agency for Nature Conservation, with a species search engine for Red List data.

name: RWE
summary: Energy company that leads and finances the SeaMe project on marine biodiversity monitoring in offshore wind farms, with tests in its Kaskasi wind farm.

name: RWE Offshore Wind GmbH
summary: Offshore wind company that runs the SeaMe environmental monitoring research project at its Kaskasi wind farm.

name: Schutzstation Wattenmeer
summary: Independent association since 1962 that looks after two thirds of the Schleswig-Holstein national park through a network of 18 stations from Friedrichskoog to Rantum on Sylt.

name: Schäuffelhut Berger GmbH
summary: Company in Unterhaching, Germany, founded in 2013 by Matthias Berger and Friedrich Schäuffelhut, whose work includes Firetail, an animal tracking tool with machine learning for behaviour labelling.

name: SEAGUARD
summary: KI-Leuchtturm project that uses AI on remote sensing data and measurements to identify suitable sites for seagrass meadows.

name: SeaMe
summary: RWE-led and funded project from summer 2024, planned for three years, on monitoring marine ecosystems in offshore wind farms, including an autonomous underwater vehicle with AI video to recognise fish and marine mammals.

name: SENSURE Wald
summary: Develops AI models that raise the resolution of Sentinel-2 data so that small areas of forest damage can be found in Hesse.

name: Shazam4Nature
summary: Low-cost acoustic sensor idea from Felix Govaers at Fraunhofer FKIE, reported by Microsoft as a 2019 recipient of its AI for Earth programme.

name: SIMON
summary: Develops 4D environmental monitoring of the Port of Hamburg with an autonomous underwater drone, sensors and AI analysis on board.

name: SKYLAB
summary: Hamburg company that applies remote sensing and AI to forestry and forest carbon, including a Forest Health Monitor.

name: SLU Sachverständigenbüro für Luftbildauswertung und Umweltfragen
summary: Provider listed by the CopWald service as active in forest remote sensing, with services including mapping, classification and monitoring of land cover and land use.

name: SmartForestFire
summary: Develops an AI early warning system that detects forest fires automatically.

name: SmartPatrol
summary: Finished project on real-time AI analysis of biodiversity and patrol data to plan ranger patrols against snaring, especially in South-East Asia.

name: SmartReForest
summary: bayklif2 project on resilient reforestation in Bavaria, which uses multispectral satellite data and AI image processing to map damaged forest.

name: Spiekeroog Coastal Observatory
summary: Observatory run by the Institute for Chemistry and Biology of the Marine Environment, with stations, one recording oceanographic, meteorological and biochemical data, plus groundwater monitoring on the island.

name: Staatliche Naturwissenschaftliche Sammlungen Bayerns
summary: Bavarian state natural history collections, whose IT centre runs the Diversity Workbench biodiversity data software.

name: Staatsbetrieb Sachsenforst
summary: Saxon state forest enterprise under which the KI-Nationalpark list places the Saxon Switzerland park administration, and whose researchers prepared forest monitoring there in 2020 with Eberswalde University.

name: Stiftung Ausgleich Altenwerder
summary: Foundation that buys or takes over near-natural land for long-term conservation and cares for these compensation areas, with planned measures focused on the tidal Elbe around Hamburg.

name: Stiftung KulturLandschaft Günztal
summary: Foundation that has worked for over two decades on biodiversity in the Günz catchment and on 20 June 2024 signed a habitat-network partnership with the Bavarian conservation administration, its first private partner.

name: Stiftung Lebensraum Elbe
summary: Foundation founded by Hamburg in 2010 for Lower Elbe biodiversity and the tidal Elbe's ecological state, which had a stone barrier removed at Wrauster Bogen and fully financed bank protection lowering at five places at Juelssand.

name: Stiftung Natur und Umwelt Rheinland-Pfalz
summary: Rhineland-Palatinate foundation whose ArtenFinder platform takes species sightings that feed the state's official data after checking.

name: Stiftung Naturlandschaften Brandenburg
summary: Brandenburg foundation that secures former military training areas as wilderness and is recruiting to develop systematic species and habitat monitoring, including AI-based methods.

name: Stiftung Naturschutz Berlin
summary: Non-governmental foundation that runs ArtenFinder platforms, partners with Stiftung Natur und Umwelt Rheinland-Pfalz, and hosts the Berlin ArtenFinder observations, 6% of the records.

name: Stiftung Naturschutz Schleswig-Holstein
summary: Conservation foundation that describes itself as the largest nature conservation organisation in Schleswig-Holstein, and runs renaturation projects for moors, meadows, woods and waters plus a state moor-rewetting programme.

name: Stiftung Naturschutz Thüringen
summary: Thuringian foundation under public law, independent and legally capable since new statutes of 14 March 2019, whose woodland programme guides management of its forest, part of which is left to develop on its own.

name: Stiftung NaturSchutzFonds Brandenburg
summary: Brandenburg foundation under whose roof the Naturwacht rangers have worked since 1997, covering 15 protected landscapes on about 9,750 square kilometres and testing automated analysis of bat ultrasound recordings.

name: Tagfalter-Monitoring Deutschland
summary: Citizen science project that assesses the status and trends of butterfly populations in Germany, and the first use of the UFZ's BioMe infrastructure for biodiversity monitoring.

name: Technical University of Munich
summary: Munich university that runs ecoBay with LMU Munich and where Xiaoxiang Zhu is Professor of Data Science in Earth Observation.

name: Technische Hochschule Berlin
summary: Berlin university of applied sciences behind the KInsecta insect monitoring project, with the Listhof environmental education centre.

name: Technische Hochschule Ostwestfalen-Lippe
summary: German research body named by FEdA as home of the lead of BioMLAgrar.

name: Technische Universität Clausthal
summary: German research body named by FEdA as home of the lead of BioIntAkt.

name: TERENO
summary: Long-term research programme involving six Helmholtz Association centres, with four observatories studying terrestrial ecosystems and providing observation data to researchers, stakeholders and decision makers.

name: Thünen Institute
summary: German federal research institute. A factsheet names its Institute of Forest Ecosystems as the place where the forest damage monitoring system is being implemented from 2024.

name: Tierfund-Kataster
summary: German register of animals found dead, focused on conflicts between animals and traffic, operated by the Deutscher Jagdverband.

name: Tierpark Berlin
summary: Berlin zoo that is a cooperation partner of the GAIA animal tag consortium; keepers and GAIA scientists tagged two white-backed vultures there.

name: TransparenC
summary: Measures and monitors nature-based asset projects with automated Earth observation data and AI. The Future Forest list of start-ups names it.

name: TrapScan
summary: AI tool that analyses camera-trap videos, finds animal movement and classifies species, developed by Fraunhofer IDMT with WWF Germany and used on the Middle Elbe since January 2026.

name: Tree species map of Germany (Koeltzow, FU-Berlin, SITS-BERT)
summary: Map of tree species across Germany from Sentinel-2 time series and SITS-BERT, published on Zenodo with training code on GitHub.

name: TreeAI Global Initiative
summary: Initiative listed by the University of Freiburg to identify and monitor tree species and tree mortality in support of biodiversity and conservation.

name: TREEO
summary: Digital monitoring, reporting and verification provider endorsed for the Global Tree C-Sink standard, which cross-checks its app data with satellite images and reports over two million tree measurements recorded.

name: TreeSat AI
summary: Project listed by the University of Freiburg that applies AI to Earth observation and other geodata for infrastructure, nature conservation and forest monitoring.

name: TreeScatter
summary: Flies drones over forests and delivers a 3D digital twin with tree-level detail. The Future Forest start-up list says it uses LiDAR and AI.

name: TZW: DVGW-Technologiezentrum Wasser
summary: German research body named by FEdA as home of the lead of IQ-Wasser.

name: UFZ-Waldzustandsmonitor
summary: Satellite-based monitor of forest condition in Germany, shown as maps at 20 metre resolution, from a research team coordinated by the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research.

name: Umwelt-Campus Birkenfeld
summary: Campus of Hochschule Trier that develops an AI insect monitoring station.

name: Unabhängiges Institut für Umweltfragen
summary: Berlin research institute and registered non-profit on democracy and education in environmental protection, a partner in KIBA-D and NFDI4Biodiversity.

name: unique land use
summary: Provider listed by the CopWald service as active in forest remote sensing, with services including forest inventories, forest management information systems and bark beetle monitoring.

name: University of Bayreuth
summary: German university whose AI4Wildlife site describes camera trap research on wildlife and visitors in a Bavarian forest.

name: University of Freiburg
summary: German university whose Chair of Wildlife Ecology and Wildlife Management is a partner in AI National Park, and whose computer centre stores the project's data and trains its AI systems on it.

name: University of Hohenheim
summary: German university whose Landesanstalt für Bienenkunde develops the BeeVision camera system for recognising pollinators.

name: University of Kassel
summary: German research body named by FEdA as home of the lead of NatureAI.

name: University of Marburg
summary: German university where the Nature 4.0 monitoring project is based and whose database group produced the Geo Engine platform.

name: University of Regensburg
summary: German university named on the bayklif2 site as home of project leads of BaySenseAI, bAImo.

name: University of Würzburg
summary: German university named on the bayklif2 site as home of project leads of bAImo.

name: Universität Marburg
summary: University whose open-source AI model classifies species in the TrapScan camera-trap tool.

name: Universität Stuttgart
summary: University whose flight robotics group is led by Aamir Ahmad.

name: Universität zu Lübeck
summary: University whose Institute of Technical Computer Science head says SIMON builds on its autonomous underwater vehicle work, aiming to add intelligent sensor concepts and embedded computing.

name: Verein Jordsand
summary: Association that has protected landscapes on the German North Sea and Baltic coasts since 1907 and now looks after about 20 protected areas there and in the Hamburg area.

name: Verein Naturschutzpark Lüneburger Heide
summary: Association founded in 1909 that has worked to preserve and develop the Lüneburger Heide heathland, and which says the reserve would not exist without it and its foundation.

name: Vision Impulse GmbH
summary: Company that Thünen's CopWald list of forest remote sensing providers names for geodata analysis with AI.

name: Waldmonitor Deutschland
summary: Satellite forest monitor for Germany, showing forest condition, damage statistics by state and AI mapping, from a long Sentinel-2 time series.

name: Wasserwirtschaftsamt Landshut
summary: Water management office that opened a newly built Isar section with side arm at Ettling in February 2025 as ecological compensation, creating shallow-water spawning zones and land for floodplain woodland.

name: Wildcap
summary: Closed project, run by the University of Stuttgart and funded by the Cyber Valley Research Fund, that aimed to observe threatened wildlife using AI, a drone and an airship between May 2021 and April 2026.

name: Wildlife Disease Warning System
summary: Develops an early warning system that detects animal disease with camera sensors, using African swine fever as the example.

name: Wildtier-Informationssystem der Länder Deutschlands
summary: National monitoring programme that records the presence, density and trends of wildlife in Germany, with data collected by hunting district holders since 2001.

name: Wood Krew
summary: Provider listed by the CopWald service for forest remote sensing, offering drone flights and satellite image analysis to map and mark trees affected by bark beetle.

name: WWF Germany
summary: German member of the WWF network. Its annual report describes AI used to find lost fishing nets through the GhostNetZero.ai platform and to train an algorithm on forest elephant camera images.

name: WWF Germany Space + Science
summary: WWF Germany programme with a remote sensing and AI analyst that describes using geospatial technologies for ecosystem conservation, spanning vegetation, coral reefs, seagrass, mangroves and deforestation.

name: Zentrum für Sonnenenergie- und Wasserstoff-Forschung Baden-Württemberg
summary: Energy research centre whose wind test field at Stötten supplied images for training the BirdRecorder AI models.

name: ZERBIS Geo-IT GmbH
summary: Provider listed by the CopWald service for forest remote sensing, working on integrated fire management and offering firemaps.net, burnt area mapping and fire emission estimates.

name: Zoo Berlin
summary: Berlin zoo and animal park, which have worked with GAIA-Initiative researchers since 2022 and collect lion data for an AI behaviour recognition project.

name: Zoologische Staatssammlung München
summary: Bavarian state zoological collection in the Staatliche Naturwissenschaftliche Sammlungen Bayerns, and home of the Barcoding Fauna Bavarica DNA barcode project.

name: Zukunft - Umwelt - Gesellschaft
summary: Project management agency responsible for the federal environment ministry's KI-Leuchttürme funding programme.

name: Zuse-Institut Berlin
summary: Berlin research institute whose optimisation and learning lab publishes the AI4Forest forest monitoring project.

name: Zweckverband Naturpark Bergisches Land
summary: Special-purpose association named on the website as the body behind the Bergisches Land nature park, which stretches from Cologne to the Sauerland and from the Wupper to the Sieg.

name: Öko-Institut
summary: German institute named among the bodies carrying out the KIBA-D biodiversity assessment.

name: Ökologische Schutzstation Steinhuder Meer
summary: Station founded in 1991 by local conservation groups, based in a former farm in Winzlar, working with nature authorities on wet meadows and moors at the Steinhuder Meer and recording plants and monitoring selected animals.

name: Association Djibouti Nature
summary: A membership-based not-for-profit established in Djibouti in 1999, formerly the Wildlife Protection Organization, reporting field studies and completed raptor counts, with a $10,000 Djibouti francolin grant.

name: Centre d'Etudes et de Recherche de Djibouti
summary: A public scientific and technological establishment attached to Djibouti's Ministry of Higher Education and Research, under whose supervision ORREC was created in 2022, according to HCERES.

name: Coral Reef Monitoring of Djibouti (CRMD)
summary: Proposed project to monitor Djibouti's coral reefs with a scientific and technological solution, including training local scientists and setting up permanent monitoring sites, in partnership with three named bodies; the page says no proper monitoring system exists.

name: Djibouti camera-trap biodiversity survey 2021-2022
summary: Closed biodiversity survey in Djibouti, contracted by the World Bank in 2021 as reported by GroundUp, whose camera trapping on the Digri Plateau in March 2022 confirmed a cheetah.

name: DJIVES2 project
summary: Marine inventory project in Djibouti whose second mission, reported by CERD, ran from 5 to 21 November 2025 to extend surveys of macroalgae and sponges, funded by ISblue and CERD.

name: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (Djibouti)
summary: Listed on the CBD’s Djibouti national focal point page, this ministry’s AMP2 activities included creating and running a management unit, according to UNDP.

name: Mitigating key sector pressures on marine and coastal biodiversity and further strengthening the national system of marine protected areas in Djibouti (AMP2)
summary: Running August 2018–April 2025, this completed Djibouti ministry-run project had GEF and Japanese funding, with activities including building surveillance sites and three additional marine protected areas.

name: Monitoring of juvenile whale sharks in the Gulf of Tadjoura, Djibouti
summary: Closed, archived project led by David Rowat and funded by the Save Our Seas Foundation in 2011, monitoring juvenile whale sharks in the Gulf of Tadjoura, with 350 sharks photo-identified by 2011.

name: Observatoire Régional de Recherche sur l'Environnement et le Climat
summary: Regional environment and climate research body, created in 2022 under CERD's supervision according to HCERES, and named as affiliation on a 2026 paper on mangrove dieback and recovery at Godorya.

name: Transnational Red Sea Center scientific mission in Djibouti (September 2022)
summary: Closed September 2022 mission, run by the Transnational Red Sea Center with partners and reported by ICRI, using 3D mapping, machine learning segmentation and eDNA; no bleaching was found at the six sites studied.

name: 15. Juni Fonden
summary: Organisation that the Danish Technological Institute names as the supporter of VIBES, and that says it works for more and better nature.

name: Aabenraa Municipality
summary: Danish municipality whose nature officer, quoted on Koordinat's site, says it reviews changes in protected nature with the VERNA tool and uploads them to Miljøportalen.

name: Aage V. Jensen Naturfond
summary: Danish nature foundation whose purpose is preserving nature and protecting wild animals; Lex says it owned about 19,300 hectares in 2024.

name: Aalborg University
summary: University whose researchers report using thermal drones since 2022, with AI analysing recordings, and which CORDIS lists as AquaINFRA coordinator.

name: Aalborg Zoo
summary: Zoo listed as a participant in a project on an intelligent camera system for zoo animals, and a partner of Aalborg University.

name: Aarhus Kommune
summary: Danish municipality whose 2013–2030 nature quality plan states a duty to maintain the protected natural areas it owns, totalling 371 hectares.

name: AI for Climate & Conservation
summary: Programme run by the Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence, led by Ankit Kariryaa, Joakim Bruslund Haurum and Nico Lang, aiming to bring researchers and practitioners together.

name: AI for Marine Perception
summary: Programme run by the Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence from 2026 to 2028, seeking collaboration among researchers and practitioners in AI, marine science and underwater robotics.

name: AMI trap monitoring in nature national parks
summary: Proposed project, run by the Danish Centre for Environment and Energy, providing for two AMI traps in each nature national park, though the trap concept is still development work.

name: Anemo Robotics
summary: Danish start-up, as Ecowende describes it, making underwater cameras with AI analysis for marine monitoring; it says it has built and deployed over 120 cameras.

name: AnemoHub
summary: Proposed fish detection software for marine research teams, built and run by Anemo Robotics, with a launch planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

name: Animal Detect
summary: Copenhagen-registered company that says it turns wildlife camera footage into species-level data, offers a wildlife image recognition API, and lists Danish public bodies and Aalborg University as supporters.

name: Arter.dk
summary: Species records database that says it holds 53 million verified records and shares data with GBIF; a 2026 abstract says it integrates AI to validate citizen observations.

name: Atlas Flora Danica
summary: Closed dataset run by Dansk Botanisk Forening, begun in 1992 and ended with publication in December 2015, with data it says are available on GBIF.

name: Atlas of Danish Fungi
summary: Fungal records database that calls itself Denmark's official one, reports over 700,000 user observations and offers AI image-based identification suggestions.

name: Atlas Survey of the Butterflies of Denmark
summary: Closed survey of butterflies in Denmark, carried out from 1989 to 1994, built by Michael Stoltze and published under a CC-BY 4.0 licence.

name: B-USEFUL
summary: Project led by DTU Aqua, with dates given as 2022 to 2026 and status unknown.

name: BIO-DRONE
summary: Project using drone technology and image recognition to aim at controlling giant hogweed through drone monitoring, with a MUDP grant and partners Cellari and Scout Robotics.

name: BIOCHANGE
summary: Organisation founded in August 2017 on a VILLUM Investigator grant, funded by Villum Fonden and built by Jens-Christian Svenning.

name: Biodiversitet Nu
summary: Closed research project on the state of Danish nature, 2015 to 2020, in which more than 27,000 people registered over a million observations with the NaturTjek app.

name: Biodiversitetskort for Danmark
summary: Dataset giving a spatial priority ranking of nature areas by importance for Danish biodiversity, built by Aarhus University and the University of Copenhagen.

name: BITCue
summary: A project that, in 2018, was examining Arctic flowers and pollinators using surveillance cameras, automatic image recognition and machine learning, led by Toke Høye and funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark.

name: Blåvand Bird Observatory
summary: Bird observatory at Blåvandshuk that has collected migration data since August 1963 and, since 1984, has ringed migrating small birds more systematically for nature monitoring.

name: Bornholms Regionskommune
summary: Danish regional municipality that manages nature on privately and municipally owned protected areas on Bornholm, where protection declarations give a management right or obligation, and draws up management plans with owners and others.

name: Brabrand-Årslev Kogræsser- og Naturplejeforening
summary: Local cattle-grazing and nature management association whose purpose is managing meadows protected under section 3 of the Nature Protection Act along Brabrand Sø and Aarslev Engsø by grazing.

name: Bugbase
summary: A dataset run by the Lepidopterologisk Forening, published under a CC-BY-NC 4.0 licence, where only society members can enter records.

name: Carlsbergfondet
summary: A foundation that announced, in September 2026, DKK 150 million for three interdisciplinary centres marking its 150th anniversary, one of them on landscapes and ecosystem recovery.

name: Cellari
summary: An organisation whose chief executive says its algorithms are working for nature in a project funded by MUDP.

name: Center for Macroecology, Evolution and Climate
summary: A centre run by the University of Copenhagen that took part in Svampeatlas 2.0.

name: Center for Marin Naturgenopretning
summary: A centre whose stated main task is to gather and analyse knowledge to advise authorities and private bodies on marine restoration and monitoring, supported by the Velux foundation and the environment ministry.

name: Christiansø Administration
summary: Local authority of the Ministry of Defence, responsible for maintenance and operation of Christiansø, part of the state-owned Ertholmene archipelago.

name: Clarity
summary: Project developing a platform intended to combine AI-based species models, climate scenarios to 2100, rainwater management and soil balance optimisation, with a MUDP grant of DKK 2,447,426.

name: Copenhagen Zoo
summary: A zoo in Frederiksberg that contributes biodiversity monitoring in Danish forests and monitors species by satellite tracking in Baluran, funded by the Hempel Foundation.

name: DanBIF
summary: Denmark's GBIF participant node, listed for a voting country, which is named as endorsing the Lepidopterological Society as a data publisher.

name: Danish Agency for Climate Data
summary: An agency that says it maps Denmark.

name: Danish Bird Ringing Administration
summary: Programme at the Natural History Museum of Denmark that administers recoveries of ringed wild birds, each giving knowledge of migration routes, lifespans and causes of death.

name: Danish Facility for Museomics
summary: A proposed project, led by Natasha de Vere and funded by a Villum Foundation grant, that is to enable Denmark's first research laboratory for museomics.

name: Danish Fishermen's Producers Organization
summary: An organisation that DTU Aqua calls a major end-user of TEFIMO.

name: Danish Mycological Society
summary: A fungi community founded on 1 October 1905, based in Hillerød according to Biodiversa+, named as a partner in Svampeatlas 2.0 and listed in 2021 on the species council advising Arter.

name: Danish National Research Foundation
summary: A research funder that lists a DKK 59909600 grant to TreeSense and supports centres including ECONOVO.

name: Danish Pelagic Producers Organisation
summary: An organisation that said in July 2024 that over half of Danish catches were monitored using CCTV, AI and sensors through a system it says it owns.

name: Danish Roadside Dataset for Camera-Assisted Monitoring of Invasive Plant Species
summary: Dataset of 14838 high-resolution images taken along Danish roadsides, designed to evaluate and benchmark image classification and object detection methods.

name: Danmarks Jægerforbund
summary: Organisation in Rønde doing citizen science with Danish hunters, aiming for a statistically robust, validated dataset on larger nocturnal mammals in Denmark.

name: Danmarks Miljøportal
summary: Public partnership owned by the state, municipalities and regions, by its own and KL's description, which says it is working to make its data more usable by AI.

name: Danmarks Naturfond
summary: Landowning foundation in Denmark that owns 772.9 hectares spread over 17 nature areas.

name: Danmarks Naturfredningsforening
summary: Copenhagen organisation that was a partner in Biodiversitet Nu, which investigated Danish nature in 2015–2020 with university researchers; the campaign was renamed Det store Naturtjek soon after starting.

name: Danmarks Skovstatistik
summary: A sample-based inventory of Danish forests, built on a nationwide 2 by 2 km grid according to a 2019 report, and described in a 2009 article as having about 7500 measuring points.

name: Danmission
summary: Organisation that stands behind an EU-funded project with the University of Copenhagen and local organisations supporting the monks, and says drones make forest monitoring more effective and safer.

name: Dansk Botanisk Forening
summary: Danish flora organisation whose eastern branch is developing a citizen science project where volunteers monitor sites for rare plants, with one aim of making the data freely available.

name: Dansk Ornitologisk Forening
summary: Danish partner in BirdLife International, a Copenhagen NGO of about 16,000 members that runs DOFbasen and in May 2024 reported developing a point count recording app.

name: DaSSCo
summary: National programme to digitise all of Denmark's natural history specimens, led by Statens Naturhistoriske Museum, whose consortium's collections hold 19 million specimens and artefacts.

name: DCE - Danish Centre for Environment and Energy
summary: A central Aarhus University unit carrying out some NOVANA monitoring, which published 2026 notes on AI image recognition for moth traps and alternative data sources.

name: Den Danske Naturfond
summary: Foundation that says it is an independent, private non-profit and that it buys, protects and restores nature across Denmark.

name: Den Danske Rødliste
summary: A dataset giving an overview of about 13,900 Danish species, with assessments that can be exported to a file.

name: Department of Chemistry and Bioscience, Aalborg University
summary: Unit based in Aalborg and Esbjerg with 230 employees as of 1 March 2026, where Microflora Danica was carried out.

name: Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University
summary: Aarhus University unit responsible for national monitoring of waterbirds, coordinating marine mammal monitoring and developing automated localisation from sound.

name: Digital ecological site prioritisation
summary: Closed project built by peatz and Teknologisk Institut, developing a proof of concept combining more than 45 ecological data layers with rule-based methods and early AI models.

name: Digitalt Skovkort
summary: Map of Danish forests made with machine learning and satellite data, using a model trained on data that agency forestry staff drew from orthophotos.

name: DOFbasen
summary: Online database of bird observations in Denmark, started in 2002 according to a 2017 agreement, run by Dansk Ornitologisk Forening, with records shared through GBIF.

name: Dronningborg Kogræsser- og Naturplejeforening
summary: Local cattle-grazing and nature management association whose purpose is nature management in Torup Dal through half-year grazing with cattle.

name: DTU Aqua
summary: Technical University of Denmark institute developing eDNA methods; Cyprus Mail reports an AI pipeline matched fish correctly 90.43 per cent of the time in tests on six similar-looking species.

name: DTU Space
summary: Lyngby institute that calls itself Denmark's largest space research institute, lists geodesy and Earth observation, and partnered in the eelgrass mapping project of June 2019 to May 2023.

name: Earth Surveillance
summary: Copenhagen organisation that combines satellites, field measurements and AI to measure land condition.

name: Environmental Technology Development and Demonstration Programme
summary: Ministry of Environment programme supporting environmental technology development and full-scale testing, which in its 2025 grant list funded HabiSense, VILD and NatureSeNSS under a wild nature and biodiversity theme.

name: EOatDHI
summary: Formerly DHI GRAS, run by DHI, it works on satellite image and data processing and offers deep learning for satellite imagery; DHI said its activities would transfer to DHI A/S from 1 July 2022.

name: evolito
summary: Company formerly called FaunaPhotonics, registered under the new name from 27 June 2025, whose sensors capture insect wingbeat signatures and use AI to calculate insect metrics.

name: Fangstjournalen
summary: Catch journal developed by DTU Aqua in which anglers share trip and catch records for research and fisheries management, funded from fishing licence income with Tips- og Lottomidlerne support.

name: Fanø Kommune
summary: Danish municipality that manages nature on Fanø through partnerships with landowners, foundations, national funding programmes and volunteers.

name: Fisheries and Maritime Museum
summary: Museum, part of Museum Vest, that says it has long worked on monitoring marine mammals and takes part in the national response for stranded marine mammals on Danish coasts.

name: Fiskeatlas
summary: Active project that began the national mapping of Danish fish in 2006 and still collects data, in partnership with the Natural History Museum Denmark and DTU Aqua.

name: Fjord&Bælt
summary: Kerteminde organisation that collaborated with the University of Southern Denmark on the Fyn finder marsvin citizen science project, for which the public could report porpoise sightings in 2020.

name: Foreningen Sdr. Resen Borgerhus og Naturpark
summary: Association that owns the nature park, with a board responsible for keeping to the park's purpose and volunteers and village caretakers maintaining the facilities.

name: Forests of the World
summary: Danish organisation founded in 1983 that describes satellite-based rainforest protection in local hands and hosted two technical workshops with DHI GRAS.

name: Fugleværnsfonden
summary: Foundation that owns and manages 26 nature reserves of just over 1,300 hectares with over 300 volunteers, set up by Dansk Ornitologisk Forening in 1966 and with its own board and secretariat since 2006.

name: Fully Documented Fishing
summary: Programme run by the Danish Pelagic Producers Organisation that documents fishing activity on member vessels with sensors, AI and CCTV cameras, for use in science, management and traceability.

name: Fyn finder marsvin
summary: Project run by the University of Southern Denmark that in 2020 invited people to report porpoise observations through the Marine Tracker app.

name: Gedser Bird Observatory
summary: Bird observatory that opened officially in 2001, with activity in the area since the 1970s, and rings birds in spring and autumn; DOF names it one of three main observatories.

name: Geopark Det Sydfynske Øhav
summary: Geopark whose secretariat carries out, on behalf of four South Funen municipalities, a project to build new stone reefs at Drejø to restore sea nature.

name: Ghost Net Zero
summary: AI model that analyses existing sonar data and, according to WWF, spots ghost nets with 90 per cent accuracy.

name: Gismap
summary: Start-up that describes itself as working on computer vision and GeoAI for biodiversity in property and construction, with an AI model that maps areas to support work on urban nature.

name: Greenland Ecosystem Monitoring
summary: Long-term programme funded by the Danish Environmental Protection Agency that says it provides free and open access to all data collected.

name: HabiSense
summary: Aims to automate marine data collection and analyse sensor and camera data from small autonomous vessels with AI; DHI A/S is lead applicant, with a DKK 2,347,565.80 MUDP grant.

name: HabitatVision
summary: Company that says it monitors terrestrial habitats and species diversity in the national NOVANA programme and has its own sound laboratory for bat, amphibian and insect recordings.

name: Hempel Fonden
summary: Foundation that in 2023 bought just under 800 hectares of the former Lungholm Inddæmning on southern Lolland to restore biodiversity by rewilding, as Saksfjed Vildmark.

name: Herd Tracking
summary: Model built and run by Robotto that integrates AI-trained elephant detection, trained on more than 5,000 images and videos.

name: Independent Research Fund Denmark
summary: Funder that gave BITCue DKK 2.6 million in 2018 and is named as funder of the Limfjord underwater AI project.

name: Innovationsfonden
summary: Funder that Koordinat says funds its team, and whose site lists the Biodiversa+ 2026 BiodivFuture call.

name: Insektmobilen
summary: Dataset from a national citizen science and DNA metabarcoding survey of flying insects carried out in June 2018 and 2019.

name: Integrated Marine Monitoring Denmark
summary: DHI-led project that uses deep-learning classification models to turn satellite imagery into habitat maps, mapping submerged vegetation across Denmark at 10 by 10 metres.

name: InvaDrone
summary: University of Southern Denmark project that aims to teach computers to recognise individuals of focal species and to apply this to early detection of invasive species.

name: IT University of Copenhagen
summary: University whose research portal lists the SeagrassFinder dataset, and whose DASYA lab and Maritime Hub announced a SenseBoat workshop for 21–22 April 2026.

name: Klimadatastyrelsen
summary: Danish Climate Data Agency, which says it is Denmark's mapping authority and publishes most of its data free; Lex says it is to merge with DMI on 1 December 2026.

name: Kongernes Nordsjælland National Park
summary: Independent state foundation registered in Græsted, established to develop the national park within statutory rules, owning no land in the park and carrying out projects with landowners.

name: Koordinat
summary: Copenhagen start-up, founded in 2024 according to The Hub and funded by the Danish Innovation Fund, which says it builds AI tools helping authorities use Earth observation data.

name: KYRA Robotics
summary: Copenhagen-based company, status unknown, whose drone platforms for environmental monitoring are described by Clean.

name: Lensor
summary: Company that Copenhagen Capacity says provides habitat intelligence from satellite imagery, LiDAR scanning and AI analysis, and has set up its headquarters in Denmark.

name: Lepidopterologisk Forening
summary: Danish society that is the publisher and rights holder of Bugbase.

name: Leveraging genomics and deep learning for biodiversity conservation
summary: 2024 Emerging Investigator project, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation with a DKK 10,999,214 grant, that aims to identify species most at risk of extinction.

name: Lille Vildmose Naturfond
summary: Foundation owning almost 900 hectares of the Mellemområdet in Lille Vildmose, whose protected area totals 7,700 hectares, plus 20 hectares of Paraplymosen and the Gulhøj grassland.

name: Long-Term Ecosystem Research in Denmark
summary: Joint research infrastructure of the University of Copenhagen, Aarhus University and DTU, built from existing long-term ecosystem monitoring platforms and linked to the eLTER network.

name: Lystrup Kogræsser- og Naturplejeforening
summary: Local cattle-grazing and nature management association whose purpose is nature management in Hovmarksparken by cattle grazing.

name: Læsø Natura 2000 Lodsejerforening
summary: Landowners' association that administers nature management on Læsø with Læsø Kommune and Naturstyrelsen, in a cooperation covering about 2,600 hectares of natural land and representing 120 members.

name: Microflora Danica
summary: A finished project that Aalborg University calls the world's first national atlas of environmental microorganisms, with 10,683 samples collected, run by its chemistry and bioscience department and funded by the Poul Due Jensen Foundation.

name: Miljøministeriet
summary: Danish ministry with an address on Frederiksholms Kanal in Copenhagen, which says nature conservation, environmental concern and the green transition are core tasks; Altinget reports a 2026 split of environment and nature portfolios.

name: Miljøstyrelsen
summary: A national agency under the environment ministry, headquartered in Odense, which DCE says has overall responsibility for NOVANA and which in 2023 said a new University of Copenhagen map base could support better forest management.

name: Ministeriet for Natur og Dyrevelfærd
summary: Danish ministry created on 3 June 2026, which Lex describes as mainly a continuation of the Ministeriet for Grøn Trepart, and which runs the Danish Nature Agency and the agency for green land use and aquatic environment.

name: Mols Bjerge National Park
summary: National park foundation in Rønde, an independent body within the state administration, which owns no land in the park and carries out projects on it with landowners.

name: Monitor Songbird Lab
summary: Active project built by Copenhagen Zoo and led by Simon Bruslund, with Species360 and the University of Southern Denmark as partners, which contributed to a dataset on the global songbird trade.

name: MOSAR
summary: Closed project led by ReefCircular that ran from June 2024 to June 2025 in Hundested, Denmark, studying artificial reefs through continuous monitoring and data gathering.

name: Moth Classification and Counting
summary: A deep learning algorithm for the moth trap, built by Kim Bjerge, with its current status unknown.

name: MycoKey
summary: Fungal identification key resource in Tirstrup, built by Jens H. Petersen and Thomas Laessoe, which offers an AI trained on its pictures and Danish fungal atlas images, though it stopped updating its key program around 2020 and calls it obsolete.

name: Nation-wide mapping of submerged coastal vegetation in Denmark
summary: Closed project, described as the first nation-wide mapping of submerged coastal vegetation in Denmark, using satellite data, machine learning and radiative transfer modelling in 2018–2019, run by eoatdhi.

name: Naturbasen
summary: Active citizen science project calling itself Denmark’s largest, reporting nationwide atlas surveys and offering adult butterfly image recognition, with photographs requested for observations identified using AI.

name: NatureSeNSS
summary: Project aiming to develop a constellation of steerable stratospheric balloons for persistent high-resolution nature monitoring, intended to improve Natura 2000 data, with a MUDP grant of DKK 2,754,192.

name: Naturhistorisk Museum Aarhus
summary: Aarhus natural history museum, named as a partner in Arter and in a planned three-year mammal monitoring project, which lists faunistics and bioacoustics among its research areas.

name: Naturpark Lillebælt
summary: Nature park run as a partnership formed by three municipal councils that adopted its plan, with an executive committee taking the overall decisions on development and operation.

name: Naturpark Mølleåen
