summary: Nature park run as a collaboration between Egedal, Furesø, Frederikssund and Allerød municipalities and Naturstyrelsen, with a secretariat run by three of the municipalities handling daily operation.

name: Naturpark Nissum Fjord
summary: Nature park established and operated by the Nissum Fjord Netværket and Lemvig and Holstebro municipalities, approved as a nature park by Friluftsrådet in December 2018.

name: Naturpark Åmosen
summary: Self-owning nature park institution that receives yearly operating grants from Kalundborg, Sorø and Holbæk municipalities and was the first certified under Friluftsrådet's Danske Naturparker scheme.

name: Naturstyrelsen
summary: Agency in the Ministry of Nature and Animal Welfare that reported managing about 212,000 hectares in 2025 and commissioned the 2026 DCE note on AMI traps.

name: Nflection
summary: Company named in the 2025 MUDP grant list as lead applicant for Clarity, a project developing what it describes as Denmark's first digital platform for real-time biodiversity assessment.

name: NIRAS
summary: Organisation that says it maps biodiversity with eDNA and works with Danish research institutions on DNA methods.

name: NIVA Danmark
summary: Active firm that says it is an independent research and consultancy company on the water environment, working in streams, lakes, fjords and open sea.

name: NORDECO
summary: Danish-based social enterprise founded in 1990 and wholly owned by a non-profit foundation, which lists monitoring and evaluation among its services.

name: NordiQ Consulting
summary: Consultancy that says it turns open satellite data into evidence for EUDR supply chains and peatland rewetting, and offers a peatland and wetland monitoring service line.

name: NOVANA
summary: National monitoring programme for water and nature, currently running 2023 to 2027, supporting Denmark's EU monitoring obligations and run by DCE, the environmental protection agency and the agency for green land use and aquatic environment.

name: Odense Kommune
summary: Danish municipality that maintains its own natural areas, over 400 hectares, by grazing and hay cutting.

name: OWESOME
summary: Active project described by DTU Aqua, dated 2025 to 2028, with DTU Aqua as partner and TotalEnergies as funder.

name: PEATZ
summary: Organisation that describes its platform and has a listed address in Frederiksberg, according to Clean.

name: Pilotnaturpark Nordfyn
summary: Pilot nature park set up by Nordfyns Kommune with all its landowners, and run day to day by the municipality with the landowners and the nature park council.

name: Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence
summary: Organisation named alongside the AI for Marine Perception programme on aicentre.dk.

name: Plature
summary: Vejle-founded organisation that says it is built on one of Denmark's largest continuous trail-camera networks, with an AI pipeline that classifies species automatically and GBIF and Darwin Core compatible export.

name: Preferred by Nature
summary: Organisation that pioneered a voluntary Geospatial Data Sharing Protocol for harvest sites and is developing, with WWF, a Traceability Tool Navigator, whose first test platform was expected in early 2026.

name: Race for Oceans Technology
summary: Impact start-up in Løkken, founded in March 2023, which says its own AI models identify, classify and map visible microplastics and other pollutants down to 2 mm in complex land environments.

name: Redoxa
summary: Organisation that Clean says combines nature-based solutions with sensors and monitoring, listed in Kongens Lyngby, and whose own site offers live data for restoration decisions.

name: Ringsted Municipality
summary: Danish municipality whose nature officer, quoted on Koordinat's site, says it uses the VERNA tool to review aerial photographs for unwanted changes in nature.

name: Roadside invasive plant monitoring
summary: Project using a network of vehicle-mounted cameras with AI algorithms to identify invasive alien plants, built by Trifork and Develco, with Trifork saying it is expanding to monitor roadkill.

name: Roskilde Municipality
summary: Danish municipality whose nature officer, quoted on Koordinat's site, says it maintains its register of §3 protected nature with the VERNA tool.

name: Roskilde University
summary: University with authors on a 2023 paper comparing earthworm biodiversity estimated by DNA metabarcoding and by morphology, whose first author is affiliated with it and Aarhus University.

name: Sensemakers
summary: Maritime start-up developing uncrewed sensor boats, whose SenseVision platform uses AI, worked with DHI during November 2025–February 2026 on AI mapping of eelgrass and seabed types.

name: Skagen Bird Observatory
summary: Very active ringing site, per the Natural History Museum, which rings by day and at night; DOF describes a station at Det Grå Fyr from 2017, led by Simon S. Christiansen.

name: Skamlebæk butterfly monitoring
summary: Project built by Ericsson and TDC NET that, according to a TDC NET and Ericsson release, automatically records butterflies at Skamlebæk, using solar-powered field units, AI and 5G per Welcome.AI.

name: Skjoldungernes Land National Park
summary: National park foundation, an independent body within the state administration, whose board is responsible for establishing and developing the park; its site lists threatened species plans and Roskilde Fjord projects.

name: Smart seabed monitoring: AI in underwater images
summary: Closed project, run and built by Sensemakers and DHI from November 2025 to February 2026, that aimed to develop a seabed and habitat segmentation model, with a budget of 200.000 (currency not stated).

name: Spaceline Labs
summary: Company whose 2024 MUDP pre-project, ended in 2025, planned stratospheric balloons at 20 km and aimed to investigate classifying habitat types from frequent high-resolution optical and hyperspectral data.

name: Statens Naturhistoriske Museum
summary: Danish natural history museum, run by the University of Copenhagen, responsible for the national collections and their digitisation, with a new DNA laboratory announced in a 22 October 2026 release and a new museum due to open on 6 March 2027.

name: Stevns Kommune
summary: Danish municipality named in the 2023 to 2026 management plan for Stevns Klint as responsible for managing the World Heritage site, one of three responsible parties.

name: Styrelsen for Grøn Arealomlægning og Vandmiljø
summary: Agency within the Ministry for Nature and Animal Welfare, set up in September 2024, which monitors fjords, coasts and open sea, and whose policy adviser is listed as Denmark's CBD national focal point.

name: Sund & Bælt
summary: Organisation that says it wants to share its data with the public so that researchers and environmental organisations can use it.

name: SustainScapes
summary: Project-like organisation started on 1 March 2021, which Aarhus University's listing says aims partly at scalable tools for understanding biodiversity and land use change, including machine learning on animal sound recordings.

name: TDC NET
summary: Organisation that says it uses 5G, AI and cameras with Ericsson to gather butterfly information, which Welcome.AI says is part of its heathland restoration programme.

name: TDC NET and Ericsson butterfly monitoring
summary: Butterfly monitoring project built by Ericsson and TDC NET, which Welcome.AI says uses two models and replaced manual surveys.

name: Technical University of Denmark
summary: Denmark's largest technical university and DaSSCo technical partner for 3D imaging and processing, with Cyprus Mail reporting an OptiFish AI pipeline tracking fish on conveyor belts.

name: Technologies for Ecosystem and Fisheries Monitoring
summary: Active project, led by Valentina Melli and funded by the Danish Maritime Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme, researching AI and eDNA for monitoring commercial fish and ecosystem components, with a planned automated species detection and length measurement pipeline.

name: Tecology
summary: Aarhus-based start-up housed in The Kitchen at Aarhus University, partnering with Nationalpark Thy and using AI cameras to monitor insects, with Atlas measuring insects according to Clean.

name: Teknologisk Institut
summary: Taastrup organisation that says it uses AI for species recognition and camera traps; its VIBES project, January 2026 to October 2028, aims to test sensors and AI-based species recognition.

name: The Bat Group, Aarhus University
summary: Programme run by Aarhus University, working on automating identification of bat calls and on image recognition of species.

name: The Brackish Dataset
summary: Underwater image dataset presented as the first public European one with bounding box annotations of marine organisms, holding 89 annotated videos recorded in Limfjorden, Aalborg.

name: Thy National Park
summary: National park in Nørre Vorupør that tested insect monitoring with Tecology in 2024 and uses BeeSee stations, which its biologist says could simplify insect monitoring.

name: Toke T. Høye Lab
summary: Research group, led by Toke Høye, studying how species and communities respond to climate and land use change, developing image-based monitoring tools and running the PollinatorWatch insect project on Zooniverse.

name: TreeSense
summary: Centre hosted by the University of Copenhagen's Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, led by Rasmus Fensholt, aiming to improve tree monitoring with satellite remote sensing and deep learning, running April 2025 to March 2031.

name: Trifork
summary: Company reporting an AI-driven solution for monitoring invasive plants for the Danish Road Directorate.

name: Trusted A/S
summary: Based in Silkeborg, the company was approached by Savannah Tracking in 2012 to develop wildlife tracking devices for endangered species in Africa, leading to a partnership.

name: Uddannelses- og Forskningsministeriet
summary: Danish ministry responsible for coordinating Danish space activities and authority cooperation, and which shares responsibility for Denmark's Copernicus interests with the climate ministry.

name: Underwater AI in the Limfjord
summary: Project with three underwater cameras installed at the Limfjord bridge, aiming to develop a system that analyses underwater conditions automatically, funded by Danmarks Frie Forskningsfond.

name: University of Southern Denmark
summary: Odense university that leads the WildDrone network and coordinates it, with a UAS Center combining robotics and computer vision expertise and a drone centre listing InvaDrone for detecting invasive plants.

name: Varde Kommune
summary: Danish municipality that administers Naturpark Vesterhavet.

name: Vejdirektoratet
summary: Organisation described by Trifork as having a project to identify and mitigate invasive plants, using technology along roads in Denmark, Sweden and Iceland.

name: VELUX FOUNDATION
summary: Foundation in Søborg that says it aims to contribute to a healthy marine environment and is named as a supporter of the centre.

name: VERNA
summary: Model built by Koordinat that runs several deep-learning architectures side by side on aerial, near-infrared, LiDAR, elevation and Sentinel data; Koordinat says it found over 2000 potential changes and 2500 potential new ponds and lakes across 15 municipalities.

name: VIBES
summary: Project led by Machteld Verzijden, running January 2026 to October 2028, that will assess whether sensors and AI can measure rewilding and regenerative farming effects, testing audio recorders and camera traps in six areas.

name: VILD
summary: Project aiming to use camera traps and autonomous drones, with AI turning images into animal counts and heatmaps, mainly for red and fallow deer at Ovstrup Hede; MUDP awarded DKK 4,259,838 in 2025.

name: Vildmarken
summary: Programme built by the Hempel Foundation, where Aarhus University researchers tested an AI camera light trap station for moths at Saksfjed Wilderness in 2024, alongside a 2024 airborne DNA project.

name: Villum Fonden
summary: Foundation in Søborg supporting technical and natural science research and environmental purposes, which says it gave about DKK 1,820 million in 2025.

name: Vordingborg Kommune
summary: Danish municipality with management responsibility for both the Møns Klint UNESCO World Heritage site and the UNESCO biosphere reserve on Møn and Nyord.

name: Wadden Sea National Park
summary: Organisation on Rømø that WildDrone describes as a Danish state foundation and that partners with WildDrone.

name: WINDNA
summary: Project led by DTU Aqua with Ørsted, running 2023 to 2027 per DTU Aqua, testing an underwater robot for monitoring biodiversity around wind farms, with Horns Rev 2 as the case study.

name: WWF Verdensnaturfonden
summary: Organisation that in February 2025 described a WWF Germany AI tool for mapping lost fishing gear and advocated its use in Denmark, and in July 2025 described international WWF AI work on whales, deforestation and nature crime.

name: Yggdrasil
summary: Project that exists to generate reference genomes, represented by Tom Gilbert and partnering with the Earth BioGenome Project.

name: Ægir
summary: Environmental information portal that Sund & Bælt says has served the construction area since 2020, with measuring stations sending data to it round the clock.

name: Ørsted
summary: Funder of Spoor, which Offshorewind.biz reported in June 2022 it would help test and commercialise at its wind farms, and of BIOREEF with WWF, per DTU Aqua.

name: Assessing post-hurricane status and hybridization threat in the last remaining Iguana delicatissima stronghold (MBZF grant 182518984)
summary: Project in Dominica funded by a $7,000 Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund grant awarded 1 December 2018, aiming to assess iguana health through nesting, road mortality and invasive iguana surveys.

name: Dominica baseline marine environmental and topographic survey
summary: Closed survey, reported in April 2022, in which NOC scientists and the fisheries department filmed the seabed at 5 to 100 metres in fishing and diving areas, under the UK's Commonwealth Marine Economies Programme.

name: Dominica National Conservation Trust Fund
summary: Conservation funder, set up in 2022 with the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund, which with that partner awarded over US$93,000 to two projects, one being coral reef restoration and monitoring at Soufriere Scotts Head.

name: DSWP long-term sperm whale sightings database
summary: Long-term sperm whale sightings database, run by the Dominica Sperm Whale Project, combined with AIS vessel data to study whale, shipping and fish-aggregating device interactions off Dominica; the project's page says this facilitated national shipping lanes.

name: Environmental Coordinating Unit
summary: Unit within the environment ministry, founded by Cabinet decision in 1999, which serves as the focal point for executing multilateral environmental agreements and is run by the ministry.

name: Forestry, Wildlife and Parks Division
summary: Forestry service established in 1949, run by the environment ministry, with parrot, national park, mountain chicken and Black-capped Petrel monitoring work, including song meters in 2016.

name: Georgia Aquarium/DomSeTCO Leatherback's of Dominica (OBIS-SEAMAP dataset 1174)
summary: Completed telemetry dataset, held at OBIS-SEAMAP as dataset 1174, summarising locations per species per 1-degree cell from 19 May 2014 to 17 March 2015, with DomSeTCO listed as creator.

name: Kalinago community forest monitoring pilot
summary: Proposed pilot, with UNDP, of community monitoring in the Kalinago territory, which UNDP says could use drones for MRV and still needs further financial and technical support.

name: Lands and Survey Division
summary: Government mapping division which, according to Natural Resources Canada, now uses supplied hardware and a customised AI segmentation model for high-resolution imagery to map in near real time.

name: Ministry of Environment, Rural Modernisation, Kalinago Upliftment and Constituency Empowerment
summary: Government ministry through which, according to a 2026 contract notice, Dominica acts on the GEF-financed, World Bank-channelled project on eco-tourism for biodiversity protection.

name: National Database of Land Use, Land Use Changes and Disturbances (Dominica)
summary: National databases of land use, land-use changes and disturbances for 2000 to 2021, produced by Saint Lucia and Dominica experts using satellite imagery, which Dominica will use to draft its REDD+ results technical annex.

name: Nature Island Dive
summary: Local dive operation based in Soufriere which, according to Alert Diver (Q3 2025), monitors reefs and hand-treats corals with stony coral tissue loss disease.

name: Oceans Forward
summary: Non-profit established in 2014 and registered in Dominica and the USA, facilitating community-led marine habitat monitoring and due to implement a funded coral reef restoration and monitoring project at Soufriere Scotts Head.

name: Sea Turtles of Dominica (OBIS-SEAMAP dataset 1386)
summary: Completed satellite-tracking dataset, held at OBIS-SEAMAP as dataset 1386, covering 29 May 2016 to 4 August 2018, meant to show habitats and migratory routes of nesting leatherbacks in Dominica's waters.

name: Sea Turtles of Dominica (OBIS-SEAMAP dataset 890)
summary: Closed OBIS-SEAMAP dataset of 5,720 satellite-tag sea turtle records from 30 April 2011 to 10 July 2013, provided and owned by the Dominica Sea Turtle Conservation Organization.

name: Strengthening Community Resilience in the Kalinago Territory
summary: US$1 million project launched in December 2024 by Dominica's government, UNDP and India through the India-UN Development Partnership Fund, covering reforestation, water retention and community-based ecosystem monitoring.

name: The Dominica Sperm Whale Project
summary: Research programme founded by Shane Gero in 2005, studying sperm whale acoustics, genetics and social networks, and working with governments and NGOs on conservation.

name: WildDominique
summary: Non-profit formed by local ecologists and others in Dominica, doing research and population assessments on the mountain chicken frog and invasive Cuban treefrog, and listed as a Mountain Chicken Recovery Programme partner in 2023.

name: Adaptación de los índices BMWP e IBF para la República Dominicana
summary: Project adapting the BMWP and Family Biotic Index to monitor freshwater quality in the Dominican Republic, with a GBIF dataset of macroinvertebrates from Cordillera Central rivers, funded by MESCyT.

name: Airborne reef mapping of the Santuario Marino Arrecifes del Sureste
summary: Closed project in which, Mongabay reported in July 2019, Asner and Martin's aircraft flew over the sanctuary for a month to map it for a management plan.

name: Biomonitoreo acuático participativo en la cuenca del río Yaque del Norte y humedales de San Antonio de Guerra
summary: A project by Ruth Bastardo Landrau on aquatic biomonitoring in the Yaque del Norte basin and San Antonio de Guerra wetlands, approved by FONDOCYT in 2024 and reported by Diario Libre in July 2025 to have received over 4 million pesos.

name: Black-capped Petrel acoustic survey, Valle Nuevo
summary: A closed 2015–2016 acoustic survey run by Grupo Jaragua, in which seven sensors were deployed and petrel calls were reported detected at four of 14 exploratory Valle Nuevo sites.

name: Black-capped Petrel nest monitoring (Grupo Jaragua)
summary: An active nest monitoring programme run by Grupo Jaragua, which in 2024–2025 used cameras at Valle Nuevo and Loma del Toro to determine nest use and fate.

name: Centro de Investigaciones de Biología Marina Idelisa Bonelly de Calventi
summary: A university marine research institute founded in 1962 and run by UASD, with coral disease, humpback whale and manatee projects, and partnerships with the Red Arrecifal Dominicana and Monitorea.

name: Centro para la Conservación y Ecodesarrollo de la Bahía de Samaná y su Entorno
summary: A Dominican non-profit based in Santa Bárbara de Samaná which, with FUNDEMAR, monitored humpback whales in 2023 through photo-identification; its director reported a catalogue of over 2,000 individuals.

name: Expediciones científicas del Santuario de Mamíferos Marinos Bancos de La Plata y La Navidad
summary: Closed scientific expeditions to a marine mammal sanctuary, led by the Dominican environment ministry; February and March 2026 findings were presented in April 2026, with 644 humpback whale sightings over three days reported on Navidad Bank.

name: Fondo Nacional para el Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales
summary: Dominican national environment fund created by Law 64-00 to finance conservation and research projects, which manages technically and financially the Caribbean Engagement project whose expeditions studied the Silver and Navidad Banks sanctuary.

name: Fundación Cap Cana
summary: Non-profit created in 2016 in Cap Cana that monitors coral reef health twice a year and coral disease three times a year, and began a one-year manatee drone project in 2023.

name: Fundación Dominicana de Estudios Marinos
summary: Reports AGRRA monitoring in SAMAR and a 2019 monitoring plan; Diario Libre reports its 2022 agreement for a national manatee census using drones and aircraft.

name: Fundación Eco-Bahía
summary: A foundation that Acento reports uses drones to monitor Antillean manatees at El Portillo, Samaná, and says nest poaching fell from 89 to 29.6 per cent between 2024 and 2025.

name: Fundación Propagas
summary: A foundation that, per Acento, has monitored reefs with Reef Check República Dominicana since 2015 to set biodiversity baselines, and is listed as a founder of the Red Arrecifal Dominicana.

name: GBIF Dominican Republic
summary: Dominican Republic's GBIF associate participant node, managed by José Alberto Melendez Juan, which has endorsed five data publishers including Grupo Jaragua.

name: Grupo Jaragua
summary: Dominican non-profit incorporated in 1989 that monitors turtle nests, juveniles and rock iguanas, fitted 18 satellite transmitters between 2008 and 2019, and uses iNaturalist.

name: HISPABIOTA MARINA
summary: Long-term project, run by Programa EcoMar since 2001, to create the first inventory of the coastal and marine biota of Hispaniola.

name: Hispaniolan species checklist and occurrence database (PEER project 7-434)
summary: A closed project led by Yolanda León that compiled Hispaniolan checklists and created two iNaturalist projects reported to hold over 3,000 and over 50,000 observations.

name: Instituto de Investigaciones Botánicas y Zoológicas Prof. Rafael M. Moscoso
summary: University research unit in Santo Domingo holding the first Dominican herbarium of some 10,000 specimens, with 13 GBIF datasets, including macroinvertebrate data used to calibrate water-quality indices.

name: Instituto Geográfico Nacional "José Joaquín Hungría Morell"
summary: Dominican national body that says it makes geographic, cartographic and geodetic data on the country available to the public, and lists supplying cartographic information among its services.

name: Instituto Tecnológico de Santo Domingo
summary: University that El Inmobiliario reports is pursuing QuisqueyaSat-1, the first nanosatellite designed in the country, with an IILA-donated ground station on its campus.

name: Manatee photo-identification project (FUNDEMAR)
summary: An active project run and built by FUNDEMAR, partnered with the environment ministry, that began in June 2023 using drones to photograph manatees; identification was manual, with matching software only a planned partnership.

name: Ministerio de Educación Superior, Ciencia y Tecnología
summary: Dominican ministry that El Inmobiliario reports gave QuisqueyaSat-1 its main local backing through FONDOCYT research funds.

name: Ministerio de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales
summary: Dominican environment ministry that launched a 30x30 protected-area strategy in 2023, held eight workshops in 2025 to update the National Biodiversity Strategy, and partners with UNDP.

name: Modelación de los servicios ecosistémicos del socioecosistema Laguna de Cabral o Rincón
summary: A project approved by FONDOCYT in 2024 that models ecosystem services of the Laguna de Cabral using AI techniques, with RD$5,761,326.70 in funding reported by Diario Libre in July 2025.

name: Monitorea: integrando la evaluación de ecosistemas costeros y marinos
summary: A closed programme, built by FUNDEMAR and launched in 2023 with French government funding of half a million euros, which Acento reported found over 70 per cent of 64 assessed reefs had under 10 per cent live coral.

name: Monitoreo de la Deforestación (DO0068)
summary: Proposed Open Government Partnership commitment, led by the environment ministry, to use satellite imagery and artificial intelligence to identify deforestation patterns in real time by June 2027.

name: Monumento Natural Saltos de la Damajagua
summary: According to a January 2024 Presidencia release, the monument had led solenodon monitoring since 2018, and camera traps had been installed there to study the animals' behaviour.

name: Museo Nacional de Historia Natural "Prof. Eugenio de Jesús Marcano"
summary: Autonomous natural history museum attached to the environment ministry, holding 160,000 zoological specimens, with six GBIF datasets, and partnering with Grupo Jaragua and Durrell.

name: Piloto nacional de seguimiento de tortugas marinas en Bahía de las Águilas
summary: Active national sea turtle tracking pilot at Bahía de las Águilas, built by the environment ministry, using EarthRanger to follow patrols, nesting and strandings in real time; three female leatherbacks were recorded.

name: Programa de Monitoreo y Protección de Tortugas Marinas de Miches
summary: An active sea turtle monitoring and protection programme in Miches, run by the environment ministry and Promiches, which began 2024 nesting season monitoring at La Vacama and partners with FUNDEMAR and CEBSE.

name: Programa EcoMar, Inc.
summary: Non-profit scientific and educational institution constituted by presidential decree in 2001, publishing two GBIF datasets, including benthic marine macroalgae records from the Dominican Republic and Haiti.

name: QuisqueyaSat-1
summary: Proposed nanosatellite INTEC runs and plans to build with MESCyT funding for real-time sargassum monitoring; August 2025 reporting described assembly, funding needs and launch expected in 2026.

name: Red Arrecifal Dominicana
summary: National alliance of government, private sector, academia and communities for coral reef management, whose Coral Disease Commission, formed in June 2019, prepared a plan with a monitoring protocol for coral disease and bleaching.

name: Reef Check República Dominicana
summary: Coral reef conservation foundation and member of the Red Arrecifal Dominicana, which El Imparcial reports has monitored reefs with Fundación Propagas since 2015 and presented a 2025 reef resilience report.

name: Ridgway's Hawk recovery project (Dominican Republic)
summary: A programme run by The Peregrine Fund whose biologists, per a July 2013 release, were monitoring the remaining wild hawks in Los Haitises National Park and banded and radio-tagged a chick; current status is unknown.

name: Sigeo RD
summary: A public geographic information system, built by the Dominican Republic's environment ministry, which its 2025-2026 balance says integrates 19 layers, including protected areas, biodiversity and water resources, and makes the information available to the public.

name: Sistema Nacional de Monitoreo Forestal
summary: National forest monitoring system of unknown status, listed in the national REDD+ strategy among legal measures, with the strategy assigning it monitoring of emission reductions.

name: Site selection for coral reef restoration using airborne imaging spectroscopy (Bávaro)
summary: A closed study, built by Steve Schill, that used airborne imaging spectroscopy to pick coral outplant sites in Bávaro; it reports over 76 per cent of 1,722 fragments survived after 11 months.

name: SOH Conservación
summary: A conservation organisation whose final report on a CEPF-funded project (May 2013 to October 2015) lists a biological monitoring programme drawn up with the environment ministry and a presence-absence map from species monitoring data.

name: Universidad Autónoma de Santo Domingo
summary: A university in Santo Domingo that runs the IIBZ, a research unit in its Facultad de Ciencias with 13 published datasets listed on GBIF.

name: Uso sostenible de la microbiota asociada a esponjas marinas para la innovación biotecnológica y el monitoreo de la salud de ecosistemas marinos
summary: A project by Jhon Noel Guerrero Aybar on marine sponge microbiota, approved by FONDOCYT in the 2024 call, with funding of RD$10,915,300.00 reported by Diario Libre in July 2025.

name: Áreas Esenciales para el Soporte de la Vida (ELSA) República Dominicana
summary: Project described in a science brief as an ELSA map and online web tool for the Dominican Republic, centred on protection, management and restoration actions, using the prioritizr library in R.

name: Agence Nationale pour la Conservation de la Nature
summary: A national nature conservation agency formed under Decree 91-33 from the museum created in 1985, named in a 2017 review among sources of bird observations since the 1970s.

name: Agro Biotechnology and Nutrition Laboratory in Semi-arid Zones, University of Tiaret
summary: University of Tiaret laboratory whose authors wrote a paper whose title names monitoring of vegetation cover trends in western Algeria's steppe region using MODIS imagery.

name: Algerian Cultural Parks Programme
summary: A cooperation project between the Algerian government through the Ministry of Culture, UNDP and the GEF, led by Salah Amokrane, whose director announced the 2020 camera-trap record of the Saharan cheetah in the Ahaggar.

name: Algerian Space Agency
summary: A UN-SPIDER Regional Support Office established in 2002, reportedly partnering with the forest directorate in 2018 and able, according to TSA in August 2022, to supply fire-location satellite imagery.

name: Algerian Wildlife Watching Association
summary: An active wildlife watching association whose members, according to MaghrebOrnitho, documented the first live Pale Fox in Algeria by camera trapping in 2024 and a species new to Algeria in November 2023.

name: Artificial Intelligence Laboratory for Embedded Systems, Advanced Telecommunications, and Telemedicine (LIS2T), University of Mascara
summary: A university laboratory for embedded systems, telecommunications and telemedicine, and the affiliation of the first author of a paper whose title covers deep learning for real-time fire and smoke detection in forests.

name: ASAL forest fire detection system
summary: According to TSA in August 2022, ASAL engineers installed this pilot forest fire detection system at the DGF’s request, combining satellite-image GIS data, forest inventories and weather information.

name: Association de Réflexion, d'Échanges et d'Actions pour l'Environnement et le Développement
summary: An organisation that CEPF lists as grantee of a December 2013 to April 2017 project for a participatory protected area in the Massif de Babor, covering inventories, mapping and zoning of about 3,000 hectares.

name: Association Environnement sans frontières
summary: Association that, according to its president as reported by L'Écho d'Algérie, agreed to cooperate with the park on Posidonia monitoring with local diving clubs, and recorded the start of flowering on the Jijel coast.

name: Association Nationale Algérienne d'Ornithologie
summary: A national ornithology NGO created in 2013 to study Algerian birds, which led waterbird monitoring in Algeria within a North African project, with field visits scheduled for 2014.

name: Basseer
summary: According to Algérie Eco in November 2023, an Algerian start-up with an artificial intelligence forest fire sensor project tested at two Tizi-Ouzou sites, selected for a green-economy programme.

name: Basseer and DGF forest fire early detection pilot
summary: Built by Basseer, an artificial intelligence pilot reportedly tested with the DGF at two Tizi-Ouzou sites from August 2023, with results presented that November to seek wider deployment funding.

name: Bureau National d'Études pour le Développement Rural
summary: A public establishment founded in 1976 under the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, whose completed work includes the National Forest Inventory and a national land-cover map, and which offers database and GIS services.

name: CDTA forest fire detector
summary: Forest fire detector built by the CDTA that scans the horizon with invisible light pulses to locate smoke and alert civil protection; the CDTA says it aims to cut alert time to one to five minutes.

name: Centre de Développement des Technologies Avancées
summary: Public scientific and technological establishment under the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, based in Baba Hassen, Algiers, which builds the remote forest fire detector inspected in Médéa in October 2024.

name: Centre de Recherche en Aménagement du Territoire
summary: A research centre named as the lead affiliation of the first author of a paper whose title covers remote sensing data and machine learning for forest fire hazard assessment in Jijel.

name: Centre National de Développement des Ressources Biologiques
summary: A centre in Algiers whose stated mission is to centralise inventories of fauna, flora, habitats and ecosystems, listed by the CBD among institutions the environment ministry created between 2000 and 2002.

name: Centre National de Recherche et de Développement de la Pêche et de l'Aquaculture
summary: A fisheries and aquaculture research centre in Tipaza whose authors reported in 2020 that its long-term cetacean and sea turtle stranding monitoring project began in 1997, using a protocol.

name: Department of Agronomic and Veterinary Sciences, Ziane Achour University of Djelfa
summary: A university department named as the lead affiliation of the first author of a paper whose title covers remote sensing for monitoring deforestation in the Djelfa forests.

name: Department of Biology and Plant Ecology, Faculty of Natural and Life Sciences, Ferhat Abbas University Sétif 1
summary: Sétif 1 university department affiliated with the author of a paper whose title names a geospatial modelling approach to land surface temperature and vegetation cover change in the Mount Babor forest area.

name: Department of Earth Sciences, Institute of Architecture and Earth Sciences, University Ferhat Abbas of Sétif
summary: University of Sétif earth sciences department affiliated with the first and corresponding author of a paper whose title names forest cover change detection with NDVI in the Oued Bouhamdane watershed.

name: Department of Mathematics and Computer Sciences, University of Ahmed Draia
summary: A university department that is the affiliation of the first and corresponding author of a paper whose title covers a deep learning model and Sentinel-2 data for classifying burned forest areas in Algeria.

name: Ferhat Abbas University Setif 1
summary: University whose affiliated authors studied vegetation and land surface temperature at Mount Babor in 2024 and vegetation and water dynamics in semi-arid watersheds using remote sensing in 2025.

name: Forest Fire Detection and Monitoring System for Algeria (Omdena local chapter project)
summary: A completed Omdena local chapter project, run from 15 April to 15 June 2023, that planned a convolutional neural network to detect forest fires in satellite imagery.

name: General Directorate of Forests (Algeria)
summary: Within Algeria’s agriculture ministry, it presented a forest fire detection pilot in 2023 and partners with ASAL and Tour du Valat.

name: Higher National School of Forests
summary: A forestry school named as the lead affiliation of the first author of a paper whose title covers GIS and remote sensing for assessing vegetation dynamics in the Ouled Yagoub forest from 1994 to 2025.

name: Institut National de Cartographie et de Télédétection
summary: A public industrial and commercial body under the Ministry of National Defence, created in 1967, whose missions include producing and disseminating geographic information, according to Spacehubs Africa.

name: Laboratory "Biodiversity, Biotechnology and Sustainable Development", University of Batna 2
summary: A university laboratory named as the lead affiliation of the first author of a paper whose title covers remote sensing for evaluating changes in the Sebkhet of Aurès wetlands and their importance for Anatidae.

name: Laboratory for Improvement of Agricultural Production and the Protection of Ecosystems in Arid Zones, University of Batna 1
summary: University of Batna 1 laboratory affiliated with the authors of a paper whose title names characterising plant cover evolution in the Aurès using Landsat imagery.

name: Laboratory of Biodiversity and Biotechnological Techniques for the Valorisation of Plant Resources (BBT_VPR), University of M'sila
summary: University of M'sila laboratory affiliated with the first author of a paper whose title names long-term dynamics of remote sensing indicators for monitoring arid and semi-arid ecosystems.

name: Laboratory of Functional Ecology and Environment, Larbi Ben M'hidi University of Oum El Bouaghi
summary: Oum El Bouaghi university laboratory affiliated with the first author of a 2025 paper assessing Zouagha Forest vegetation dynamics from 2000 to 2020, with NDVI among the indices analysed.

name: Laboratory of Urban and Environmental Analysis, Badji Mokhtar-Annaba University
summary: University laboratory with affiliated first authors of two 2024 papers on El Kala National Park, covering forest monitoring with Landsat data and the remote sensing ecological index.

name: Laboratory of Water Resources and Environment, University of Saida Dr. Tahar Moulay
summary: A university laboratory named as the lead affiliation of the first author of a paper whose title covers remote sensing and clustering for managing green oak forests in western Algeria.

name: LabRI-SBA Laboratory, École Supérieure en Informatique de Sidi Bel Abbès
summary: A laboratory at a computer science school that is the affiliation of the first author of a paper whose title covers deep transfer learning for forest fire detection.

name: LITIO Laboratory, University of Oran 1
summary: University of Oran 1 laboratory affiliated with the first and corresponding authors of a paper whose title names mapping and monitoring of desertification patterns in Algeria's arid transition zone.

name: Ministry of Environment and Quality of Life (Algeria)
summary: Algeria's environment ministry, whose minister said in May 2026 that the country had launched its national biodiversity strategy and action plan 2025-2030, aligned with the Kunming-Montreal framework.

name: Mohamed Boudiaf University of M'sila
summary: University whose affiliated authors wrote 2024 and 2025 papers on remote sensing of vegetation in Algeria, covering climate effects in 25 watersheds and NDVI-based vegetation change in M'sila from 1990 to 2023.

name: Office National du Parc Culturel de l'Ahaggar
summary: According to MaghrebOrnitho, its scientific team installed cameras that filmed a Saharan cheetah in March 2020; the PPCA director said the work produced over 230,000 photos.

name: Parc National d'El Kala
summary: National park in El Tarf province that, La Nation reports, launched its winter count of migratory waterbirds in January 2026, described as an annual count.

name: Parc National de Taza
summary: National park whose director, as reported by L'Écho d'Algérie, said its 9,602-hectare marine reserve was classified in 2022 and that it works with associations and clubs on Posidonia monitoring.

name: Parc National du Gouraya
summary: Park in Béjaïa whose staff poster describes a seabird inventory of its coast and Lake Mézaïa from September 2021 to August 2022, using transects, point counts and colony counts.

name: Réseau National des Observateurs Ornithologues Algériens
summary: A network of bird observers created by ministerial order in 2011 and active from December 2012, which by 2017 had over 500 volunteer members and was used for the May 2017 national breeding bird count.

name: Réseau opérationnel pour le suivi des échouages de cétacés sur le littoral algérien
summary: A network for monitoring cetacean strandings on the Algerian coast, run by the national fisheries and aquaculture research centre and funded by ACCOBAMS; a 2022 document describes it as being set up, with formalisation listed as not yet implemented.

name: Saharan cheetah camera-trap survey in the Ahaggar Cultural Park
summary: Camera-trap survey of Saharan cheetah and large fauna in the Ahaggar Cultural Park, run by the park office; in May 2020 Algérie Eco reported 40 cameras and over 230,000 photos under study.

name: Space Techniques Center (CTS), Earth Observation Department, Algerian Space Agency
summary: Earth observation centre of the Algerian Space Agency, at Arzew, Oran, affiliated with the first author of a paper whose title names land cover change mapping of western Algeria for SDG indicator 15.3.1.

name: Suivi des Oiseaux d'eau en Afrique du Nord
summary: A closed waterbird monitoring project funded by CEPF, scheduled from July 2013 to June 2015, with national NGOs in Algeria, Libya, Morocco and Tunisia and regional coordination by Tour du Valat.

name: Université Badji Mokhtar d'Annaba
summary: University listed by CEPF as grantee of a project to protect and monitor rare endemic plants in the El Kala Key Biodiversity Area, including Erica numidica, and a member of the Mediterranean Alliance for Wetlands.

name: Université Mustapha Stambouli de Mascara
summary: A university that is the affiliation of the first author of a paper whose title covers optical and radar remote sensing for monitoring wetland dynamics in western Algeria.

name: Écocirta
summary: An association describing a participatory environmental monitoring cell for the Rocher de Constantine, with institutional and local partners and public reporting through an online form.

name: Agencia de Regulación y Control de la Bioseguridad y Cuarentena para Galápagos
summary: Galápagos authority for controlling the risk of introducing exotic organisms; in August 2026 the ministry reported AI X-ray scanners at two airports, planned for Baltra, saying AI would not replace staff.

name: Alianza Ceibo
summary: Organisation of Indigenous people from four Ecuadorian Amazon nationalities that trains community guards and cartographers to monitor and map territory; it reports over 200 guards covering 500,000 hectares and a 2026 Gulbenkian Prize.

name: Asociación 21 de Mayo de Puerto Roma
summary: Association of 230 crab fishers that, with the Cooperativa 4 de Octubre, cares for 3,000 hectares of mangrove at Puerto Roma.

name: Asociación de Pesca Artesanal Puerto Buena Vista
summary: Artisanal fishing association that had taken part in the Auscem programme for 11 years as of September 2025, with 450 hectares of mangrove under its protection.

name: Aves y Conservación
summary: Ecuadorian bird conservation organisation listing participatory research, monitoring and Christmas bird counts, which BirdLife quotes describing itself as Ecuador’s oldest bird conservation and research organisation.

name: Base Nacional de Datos de Biodiversidad
summary: Ecuadorian national biodiversity database run by the national biodiversity institute, which Lexis reported in March 2026 was established by ministry rule as the single, official, compulsory system for biological information.

name: BioAmazonia
summary: Proposed database from Ikiam for biological resource information and monitoring of Amazon biodiversity.

name: Biocultural Jaguar Credits
summary: Project built by Fundación Pachamama and Regen Network whose monitoring combines local land change monitoring, satellite monitoring and community smartphones, with jaguar numbers to be monitored by cameras.

name: Bioparque Amaru
summary: Ecuadorian park organisation whose amphibian conservation centre held 25 species in July 2022, according to El Mercurio, which also reported a plan with three lines of work.

name: Bioweb Ecuador
summary: Online repository of Ecuadorian biodiversity, built by Pontificia Universidad Católica del Ecuador and Santiago Ron, with fauna, fungi and flora sections, a frog sound database and a REST API.

name: Capuchin Corridor bioacoustic monitoring
summary: Sound monitoring programme built by Third Millennium Alliance, which deployed over 50 AudioMoths across nine transects, producing more than two million recordings, with calls identified by a convolutional neural network.

name: Carnivore Lab, Universidad San Francisco de Quito
summary: Active USFQ programme led by Rebecca Zug, which BearID reported in July 2024 it was helping speed up camera-trap analysis with AI, with a server planned.

name: Centro Cofán Zabalo
summary: Community organisation that, in December 2024, held 128,000 hectares in custody in Sucumbíos province after 88,000 hectares there were added to Socio Bosque II.

name: Centro de Investigación de la Biodiversidad y Cambio Climático (BioCamb)
summary: Biodiversity and climate change research centre built by Universidad Indoamérica, created by university resolution in July 2011, which offers DNA sequencing and molecular identification of species.

name: Centro Jambatu de Investigación y Conservación de Anfibios
summary: Amphibian research and conservation centre in San Rafael, Ecuador, whose site lists an environmental DNA study detecting a low-density population of a threatened harlequin frog.

name: Centro Shuar Kiim
summary: Shuar community centre that gained title to about 5,500 hectares in Ecuador's Tiwi Nunka reserve, described in a 2022 report as the country's first nature reserve held by an Indigenous community.

name: CIDIS, Escuela Superior Politécnica del Litoral
summary: Research centre at Escuela Superior Politécnica del Litoral focused on intelligent technologies such as computer vision, robotics and machine learning, with a project assessing dry forest scale insects using sensors, satellite images and AI.

name: Cloud based Early Warning System for forest disturbances in Ecuador
summary: Project in which GAF announced in August 2018 a six-month effort, started 1 July, to design a deforestation early warning system using free Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 data, funded by KfW.

name: Community Monitoring Program of Junín
summary: Community camera-trap monitoring programme in Junín that INABIO lists among those confirming a jaguar between November 2023 and January 2024, and which partners with Defensa y Conservación Ecológica de Intag.

name: Comuna Kichwa Sani Isla
summary: Kichwa community that has conserved more than 20,000 hectares of its territory, choosing conservation and tourism over oil.

name: Comuna Marcos Pérez de Castilla
summary: Community holding title to its ancestral land, where 8,604 hectares were declared in 2019 the second community protected area in the national system, with commitments to ban farming and cattle.

name: Comunidad Achuar de Mashientz
summary: Achuar community that, with the Tinkias community, keeps in custody 65,000 hectares of forest incorporated into the Socio Bosque II project.

name: Comunidad Agua Blanca
summary: Community with a 9,201-hectare territory zoned for resource use and conservation, shared in governance with Machalilla National Park, where residents patrol as community park rangers.

name: Comunidad de Chilco
summary: Community that owns 275 hectares of páramo and has restored more than 47 hectares of it.

name: Comunidad de Playa de Oro
summary: Community that has held the rights to protect its forest since 1995 and has strengthened its efforts to protect the territory.

name: Comunidad Kichwa 24 de Mayo
summary: In 2020, some Kichwa farmers worked through Ally Guayusa on conservation across 6,000 hectares reportedly better protected from illegal logging, mining and poaching by the community’s presence.

name: Comunidad Kichwa Añangu
summary: Kichwa community named after Lake Añangu that cares for the area around the Napo Wildlife Center and has given up hunting entirely to preserve the forest's species.

name: Consejo de Gobierno del Régimen Especial de Galápagos
summary: Constitutional public-law body that, by its own account, administers, plans and manages resources in Galápagos province to conserve the state's natural heritage.

name: Consejo Provincial de Tungurahua
summary: Provincial council that promoted the Fondo de Páramos programme, which has supported Cocap's páramo management plan since 2008 to help safeguard water sources serving Tungurahua province.

name: Conservación Internacional Ecuador
summary: Ecuador branch of Conservation International, working there since 2001, which Galapagos Conservation Trust names as a partner in training Galápagos National Park rangers as drone operators.

name: Consorcio Taita Imbabura
summary: Formed in 2018 by Imbabura’s provincial government and local municipalities to protect 3,717.48 hectares at Taita Imbabura, the consortium would handle its management plan, according to its president.

name: Cooperativa 4 de Octubre de Puerto Roma
summary: Cooperative of 86 crab fishers that, with the Asociación 21 de Mayo, cares for 3,000 hectares of mangrove at Puerto Roma.

name: Cooperativa de Desarrollo de la Comunidad Jima Ltda
summary: Community development cooperative that owns and manages the Tambillo Community Protected Area.

name: Cooperativa Ichubamba Yasepan
summary: Cooperative whose 24 members own the Ichubamba Yasepan protected area, over 4,790 hectares of páramo in Chimborazo province declared protected on 30 July 2020.

name: Corporación Chakra
summary: Tena-based body representing five Kichwa producer associations, partnering with Rainforest Foundation UK, whose August 2026 announcement proposed bringing ForestLink and ForestEye to Ecuador’s Kichwa communities.

name: Corporación de Organizaciones Campesinas de Pilahuín
summary: Peasant organisations' corporation whose members in the Fondo de Páramos initiative work to conserve 110 hectares of páramo.

name: Corporación Ecopar
summary: Ecuadorian organisation working on research, training and conservation of fragile ecosystems, doing participatory mapping with GIS and remote sensing, and funded by Global Nature Watch to train community monitors on alerts.

name: Corporación Ecuatoriana para el Desarrollo de la Investigación y la Academia
summary: Ecuadorian research body whose Fondo I+D+i, formerly CEPRA, funds member-institution research projects through an annual call; its 2024 call accepted the CIDIS scale insect proposal, and CEPRA XVI awarded 23 projects.

name: Corporación Microempresarial Yunguilla
summary: The community organisation and Cooperativa Santa Lucía carried out a CEPF-funded project in 2017–2018 that reportedly consolidated Yunguilla–Santa Lucía conservation work and updated the area’s management plan.

name: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Quito
summary: Quito fire service which, Expreso reported in August 2024, was trialling three optical and thermal cameras with early forest fire alert sensors to map green areas, as AI joined its tools that year.

name: Data-Driven Conservation Initiative for high Andean ecosystems in the Antisana Natural Reserve
summary: Project tracking change in high Andean ecosystems of the Antisana reserve with drones, computer vision and AI, in partnership with Escuela Politécnica Nacional and KU Leuven.

name: dataZone
summary: Data access platform that the foundation describes as giving access to all the scientific information stored in several of its databases.

name: DeepARC Research Group
summary: Research group whose paper proposes mobile application technology and AI for L. fulica, and which gives its affiliation in that paper.

name: Detección y Monitoreo de Bosques Andinos del Cantón Cuenca con Drones y Sar
summary: Project of unknown status whose 2023 page proposes applying machine learning to drone data to detect forest species locally in Cuenca canton.

name: Dirección del Parque Nacional Galápagos
summary: Body managing the two Galápagos protected areas, including research and monitoring, with satellite vessel monitoring and THEMIS; its rangers received drone training.

name: Empresa Pública Metropolitana de Agua Potable y Saneamiento
summary: Quito’s public water and sanitation company, which Quito Informa said in May 2022 maintained the country’s most robust hydrometeorological network, with 89 stations.

name: Equilibrio Azul
summary: Non-profit working since 2004 that monitors seabird colonies on Isla de la Plata, and which had 12 years of nesting data when SWOT described its 2019 grant.

name: Escuela Politécnica Nacional
summary: University named as Esteban Valencia’s location on KU Leuven’s project page; OpenAlex lists a 2022 paper on forecasting Amazon deforestation using a hybrid machine learning model.

name: Escuela Superior Politécnica del Litoral
summary: Guayaquil university whose authors and posters cover deep learning for bird audio, animal biodiversity and marine wildlife, plus land cover classification around Guayaquil, with CIDIS as a research centre.

name: Estación Científica Yasuní
summary: Research station founded in 1994 inside Yasuní National Park, run by PUCE, which says it has supported more than a hundred research projects and sustains long-term monitoring.

name: Estación de Biodiversidad Tiputini
summary: Research station in the Yasuní Biosphere Reserve, run by Universidad San Francisco de Quito and led by Gonzalo Rivas-Torres, who Mongabay Latam says leads or joins drone projects there.

name: ETAPA EP
summary: Cuenca's municipal company, reported in January 2020 to have recorded spectacled bears mating on a camera trap in Cajas National Park, with about 50 camera traps beside the park collecting data for about ten years.

name: Evaluación del estatus de conservación de especies de peces bandera-sombrilla y sus ecosistemas en las cuencas del bajo Pastaza y Aguarico de la Amazonía Ecuatoriana
summary: Project of unknown status, led by Fundación Futuro Ecuador with WWF, expected to contribute environmental DNA databases and ecosystem health indicators for the lower Pastaza and Aguarico basins.

name: Federación de Centros Awá del Ecuador
summary: Federation whose Territorio de Vida brings together 21 Awá communities working to strengthen territorial security and conserve biodiversity.

name: Federación Interprovincial de Centros Shuar
summary: Shuar federation that signed the 2021 agreement beginning the Tarímiat Pujutaí Nunka Reserve process, and which a Shuar author describes as a pioneer in defending Shuar territory.

name: Floreana Island Ecological Restoration Project
summary: Active restoration project on Floreana Island that Island Conservation says is led by the Galápagos park directorate together with the biosecurity agency.

name: Fondo Biocorredor Amazónico
summary: Fund that has presented its first call for grants, according to the ministry, and says it is evaluating 51 full proposals, with a board intended to have nine directors.

name: Fondo de Inversión Ambiental Sostenible
summary: A financial mechanism intended to manage environmental cooperation resources, with REM III administration planned and a Páramos sub-account reported established for Socio Bosque in April 2020.

name: Fondo de Páramos Tungurahua y Lucha contra la Pobreza
summary: Commercial trust formed in June 2008 by the prefecture, the province's main Indigenous movements and public water and energy companies, beginning with 7,000 hectares of páramo under management plans.

name: Fondo para la Protección del Agua
summary: Water protection fund that Quito Informa said in February 2025 was created 25 years earlier, and through which Epmaps reportedly recovered 70,000 hectares of páramo since 2000.

name: Fortalecimiento Cooperativo del Sistema de Control y Vigilancia para la Reserva Marina Hermandad y la Reserva Marina Galápagos
summary: Active project funded by the Galápagos Life Fund, with the park directorate as partner, whose expected results include remote monitoring covering 100% of the Hermandad reserve, according to the fund's director.

name: Fortalecimiento de las capacidades locales para el monitoreo participativo de aves playeras en áreas de custodia de manglar
summary: Project funded by the Iniciativa Humedales Costeros in which Aves y Conservación partnered with three crab-gatherer associations to set up waterbird monitoring to international standards, training and assessing more than 50 members in workshops.

name: Fuerza Aérea Ecuatoriana
summary: Air force which, Teleamazonas reports, took over space programme coordination under Executive Decree 143 and is to carry out applied Earth observation and remote sensing research with the military geographic institute.

name: Fundación Cambugán
summary: Foundation whose Tesoro Escondido reserve Rainforest Trust describes as part of a proposed Canandé expansion that would form the largest private reserve network in the Ecuadorian Chocó.

name: Fundación Charles Darwin
summary: International non-profit working in the Galápagos since 1959, with a Research Station in Puerto Ayora, that uses drones, geospatial analysis and machine learning and shares data through its dataZone.

name: Fundación Contamos Contigo Ecuador
summary: An Ecuadorian sea turtle conservation foundation whose camp had achieved 80% hatching success by January 2023, according to Vistazo, which also reported its 2026 leatherback rescue at Crucita.

name: Fundación Cóndor Andino
summary: Conservation organisation that says it tracks Neotropical vertebrates by satellite and runs camera-trap stations, activating more than 100 monitoring stations each year in seven provinces.

name: Fundación EcoCiencia
summary: Ecuadorian private non-profit scientific body, a partner of RAISG and the Waorani, which Primicias says presented the fourth MapBiomas Ecuador collection on 14 October 2026.

name: Fundación EcoMinga
summary: Ecuadorian non-profit protecting areas of high endemism through private reserves, which says its camera-trap monitoring in two areas has been permanent since 2022 and also monitors water quality at Manduriacu.

name: Fundación Futuro (Ecuador)
summary: A foundation using camera traps and recorders in Mashpi, partnering with Rainforest Connection and WCS Ecuador, and reporting planned environmental DNA research with WWF-Ecuador in 2022.

name: Fundación Jocotoco
summary: Ecuadorian conservation NGO founded in 1998 that uses camera traps, audio recorders and AI tools, and which Mongabay Latam reports collected over two million recordings between 2023 and 2025.

name: Fundación Maquipucuna
summary: Ecuadorian non-profit conservation NGO, created in 1988 by its own account, with a listed partnership with Space4Good.

name: Fundación Megafauna Marina del Ecuador
summary: Quito-based conservation organisation aiming at community monitoring of the Ecuadorian coast and Galápagos, whose Proyecto Mantas Ecuador led a study described in an Oregon State University release.

name: Fundación Pachamama
summary: A foundation which, according to Pachamama Alliance, launched a programme with the Sharamentsa Achuar community and Regen Network on 12 March 2024.

name: Fundación Pachaysana
summary: Ecuadorian non-profit operating since 2015 that runs Humans for Abundance, restores ecosystems with Indigenous and rural communities and helps Amazon and Andes families restore forests.

name: Fundación para la Conservación de los Andes Tropicales
summary: Rainforest Trust’s local partner aims to safeguard 398 acres of Chocó rainforest and link two protected areas, and promotes conservation in Mache-Chindul through research, education and community development.

name: Fundación para la Conservación e Investigación JaPu
summary: A scientific team researching Chongón Colonche since 2020, using camera traps and claiming the most complete biodiversity database for its tropical dry forest, published on GBIF.

name: Fundación Pro-Bosque
summary: Foundation created among private actors to administer the Cerro Blanco dry forest at Guayaquil, with offices there; the reserve grew from 2075 hectares in 1989 to 6078 hectares.

name: Fundación RACSE
summary: Non-profit based in Manta, working since 2021, which the GBIF publisher record says promotes applied research and field monitoring of marine and coastal ecosystems, including sea turtle nesting.

name: GAD Cantonal de 24 de Mayo
summary: Cantonal government whose ordinance created the 24 de Mayo Conservation and Sustainable Use Area, a municipal protected area declared to protect almost 15,000 hectares of ecosystems.

name: Galapagos Conservation Trust
summary: An organisation funding the Galápagos National Park Directorate, including drone training, which reports that partners such as Island Conservation use Sentinels on Floreana.

name: Galapagos Geoportal
summary: Online geoportal, run by the Charles Darwin Foundation, where users can explore maps and download data.

name: Galapagos Science Center
summary: A centre run and built by Universidad San Francisco de Quito, with a data science laboratory, Galápagos Data Hub initiative and genomics laboratory listing environmental DNA samples.

name: Galapagos Species Database
summary: Open database run by the Charles Darwin Foundation sharing its Natural History Collections, which comprise more than 135,000 specimens from more than 7,500 species.

name: Galapagos Whale Shark Project
summary: A Jonathan Green-led research project using spot patterns to identify whale sharks, with an expedition reported in April 2022 placing five satellite tags on large females.

name: GalNEMO
summary: Dataset built by the Charles Darwin Foundation and the Smithsonian Environmental Research Center, launched according to a release of 12 December 2022, creating a baseline of introduced marine species in the Galápagos Marine Reserve.

name: Galápagos Azul: Gestión Pesquera Sostenible para el Futuro de Galápagos
summary: Fisheries project run by WildAid with Universidad San Francisco de Quito, aiming to upgrade the monitoring platform, digitise the fishing register and create a public repository.

name: Galápagos Conservancy
summary: Organisation that has placed over 100 camera traps on Wolf Volcano, uses satellite-reporting GPS trackers, and says NASA-supported satellite data is being used to plan tortoise rewilding.

name: Galápagos Life Fund
summary: Fund created to manage the debt-for-nature swap money, which delivered a 6 million dollar grant and signed a contract for 2,000 vessel monitoring devices for real-time satellite tracking.

name: Galápagos Wildlife Project
summary: Organisation that uses autonomous recording units to track petrel activity and says the Government of Ecuador legally recognises it.

name: GBIF Ecuador (SIB-EC)
summary: Active national GBIF node run by the ministry, dating to 2010, with an INABIO address and a site listing a capacity project selected in GBIF’s 2023 call.

name: Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado del cantón de El Chaco
summary: Cantonal government that established the El Chaco Municipal Reserve by ordinance in July 2017, to conserve more than 67,000 hectares, about 20 percent of the canton.

name: Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Provincial de Manabí
summary: Provincial government whose 2024 ordinance establishes a provincial system of Conservation and Sustainable Use Areas, defines what counts as one, and lets the provincial government initiate their creation.

name: Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Provincial de Napo
summary: Provincial government whose ordinance declares a 41,888.55 hectare Conservation and Sustainable Use Area, and requires it to update the management plan every six years, subject to a prior Pueblo Kichwa Rukullakta resolution.

name: Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Provincial de Pastaza
summary: Provincial government that, by ordinance, established the Pastaza Ecological Area of Sustainable Development, covering more than 2.5 million hectares, to conserve forest and water sources.

name: Gobierno Provincial de Morona Santiago
summary: Provincial government that signed an agreement with four Indigenous nationalities on 9 November 2021, beginning the process of creating the Tarímiat Pujutaí Nunka Reserve, covering 1,237,395 hectares of forest.

name: Gobierno Provincial del Carchi
summary: The provincial government backed the Cordillera Oriental de Carchi conservation area, established to protect montane forest and covering 16,800 hectares of cloud forest and mountains.

name: Grupo La Fabril
summary: Palm oil company which, Earthworm reported in November 2018, used satellite monitoring of land use around its plantations in an Airbus Starling pilot.

name: Humans for Abundance
summary: Programme that pays local families in the Amazon and Andes of Ecuador to restore degraded land, funded by monthly subscriptions and donations, and run by Fundación Pachaysana.

name: Implementación de SMART en el Sistema Nacional de Áreas Protegidas del Ecuador
summary: Programme led by WCS Ecuador since 2014 to implement SMART across Ecuador's protected areas, now used in 26 areas, with WCS training rangers to support MAATE's surveillance.

name: Iniciativa Regional de Monitoreo Hidrológico de Ecosistemas Andinos
summary: Network of organisations, partnered with Universidad de Cuenca and CONDESAN, aiming to strengthen knowledge of Andean hydrology and to generate and manage information with common standards.

name: Innovación verde: tecnologías vanguardistas para el manejo sostenible de la cochinilla en bosques secos y zonas de conservación en la costa ecuatoriana
summary: Proposed project, funded by CEDIA, to determine scale insect incidence in Ecuadorian coastal dry forest using high-resolution images, environmental variables and AI, with a planned 25 sensor nodes.

name: INNOVAPESCA: Fishing with Science, from Ocean to Table
summary: Project funded by the Galápagos Life Fund, with partners including the Allen Institute for AI and ShellCatch, promoting sustainable fishing through electronic monitoring and traceability, aiming to fit every participating vessel.

name: Instituto de Geografía, Universidad San Francisco de Quito
summary: An institute listed on the Universidad San Francisco de Quito research portal, which a community environmental monitoring site says carried out the Monitoreo Comunitario Ambiental project.

name: Instituto Geográfico Militar (Ecuador)
summary: Ecuador's national cartography body, responsible under law for national cartography and the geographic data archive, which kept thematic geoinformation after Decree 143 and created a space research directorate under Decree 714.

name: Instituto Nacional de Biodiversidad (Ecuador)
summary: A public biodiversity institute in Quito, created in 2016, that holds biological collections, publishes herbarium data to GBIF, promotes citizen science, and partners with international-barcode-of-life and alianza-aguas-amazonicas.

name: Instituto Nazca
summary: An organisation that recorded fish, invertebrates and benthic communities by visual census in an April 2008 study of Puntilla de Santa Elena.

name: Instituto Público de Investigación de Acuicultura y Pesca
summary: A public aquaculture and fisheries research institute that is developing a community early warning and monitoring system for coastal impacts, and lists a participatory mangrove monitoring project in El Oro and Guayas.

name: Jocotoco bioacoustic monitoring, Narupa and Kichwa communities
summary: A Fundación Jocotoco project in which, Mongabay Latam reports, smart acoustic monitors have processed sound in real time at Narupa since October 2025, with AI models retrained on local data.

name: Jocotoco smart acoustic monitors at Narupa
summary: A Fundación Jocotoco project that, Mongabay Latam reports, has had smart acoustic monitors installed at Narupa since October 2025, each with an internal computer running trained AI models.

name: ManglArt AI
summary: A model, built by Universidad Espíritu Santo, that uses unsupervised machine learning to interpret biosignals taken from mangroves by dendrometric sensors.

name: MANGLEE
summary: A mangrove mapping and monitoring tool in Google Earth Engine, whose second module uses Random Forest to classify mangrove and non-mangrove areas, with its paper listed in OpenAlex.

name: Mapa Interactivo Ambiental
summary: An environmental map dataset built by the environment ministry, listed with 73 geographic layers in a 2023 consular note.

name: Mapas de susceptibilidad a incendios forestales
summary: A project by Universidad Nacional de Loja and Universidad Técnica Particular de Loja in which specialists develop predictive wildfire susceptibility models using machine learning and satellite data.

name: MapBiomas Ecuador
summary: A collaborative land mapping initiative using satellite images and geospatial analysis, led by Fundación EcoCiencia, whose fourth collection was reported by Primicias as presented on 14 October 2026.

name: Mapping Galapagos Invaders with Drones and Machine Learning
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project (4 January 2024) that planned to map vegetation in the Galapagos rural zone and protected area using drones and machine learning; its final report gives about 13.8 square kilometres flown.

name: Mashpi Lodge
summary: Lodge that says it began species inventories and installed camera traps across its reserve, and that its resident biology team has described 26 new species.

name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía (Ecuador)
summary: Ecuador's environment ministry, which held the November 2025 workshop for the seventh national biodiversity report, and which the president ordered merged with the energy and mines ministry in 2025.

name: Minkafab
summary: Organisation offering remote biodiversity monitoring in natural areas, based in Quito since 2019.

name: Monitoreo Comunitario Ambiental
summary: Project run by Instituto de Geografía USFQ and Todos los Ojos en la Amazonía, using drones and applications with 24 monitors to gather information on environmental liabilities and deforestation.

name: Monitoreo Comunitario de agua y biodiversidad acuática
summary: Community monitoring project run by the Pueblo Kichwa de Rukullakta, which The Nature Conservancy says young Kichwa people lead.

name: Monitoreo Inteligente de fauna en hábitats naturales mediante Deep Learning y Redes de Sensores
summary: Project run by CIDIS-ESPOL that aims to develop a wildlife monitoring system using deep learning and smart sensor networks.

name: Monitoreo satelital de condor andino en Ecuador
summary: Dataset built by Fundación Futuro Ecuador, holding data from satellite trackers placed on Andean condors.

name: Municipio de Loja
summary: Municipality that installed eight camera traps in a municipal conservation area, and partners with Naturaleza y Cultura Internacional and Universidad Técnica Particular de Loja.

name: Municipio Intercultural de Cañar
summary: Municipality whose "La Fauna Vive" unit has led camera-trap monitoring in Sangay National Park and two páramos, with April to November 2025 results confirming spectacled bear, deer and páramo fox.

name: Museo de Ballenas
summary: Organisation that explains humpbacks can be identified individually from the tail, and whose researchers and partners formed a team to assess climate change's impact on humpbacks.

name: Nacionalidad Sápara de Pastaza Ecuador
summary: Sápara Indigenous nationality whose 376,300 hectares in Pastaza were demarcated as its territory in 2009; a Puyo court returned disputed land to the Sápara in October 2021.

name: Nacionalidad Waorani del Ecuador
summary: Organisation representing 87 communities in three Amazonian provinces, based in Puyo, with the Kengiwe territorial monitoring programme dating from 2020.

name: Naturaleza y Cultura Internacional
summary: Organisation whose page describes rangers and forest guards in the corridor strengthening camera-trap monitoring, with the information to inform conservation decisions.

name: Observatorio Copernicus Ecuador
summary: Initiative to strengthen national capacity in research and strategic use of satellite data, giving access to high-performance computing for Sentinel data.

name: Observatorio Forestal UTN
summary: Programme whose deforestation platform joins geospatial tools, simulators and an AI assistant trained on all of Ecuador's forest rules, with primary forest loss alert viewers, using Google Earth Engine.

name: Pontificia Universidad Católica del Ecuador
summary: Quito university that Primicias reports shares its scientific collections free of charge, and whose site hosts Museo QCAZ pages with reptile, amphibian, mammal and invertebrate divisions.

name: Prefectura de Cotopaxi
summary: Provincial prefecture that in 2025 chose Quinticusig in Sigchos canton for páramo restoration support through its Lulú Reforesta campaign, announcing 500 native plants for the first phase after fire damage.

name: Programa de Monitoreo Territorial Kengiwe
summary: Programme run by Nacionalidad Waorani del Ecuador, whose monitors record threats on digital forms; Global Nature Watch says a 2026 grant will strengthen its capacity to use its tools.

name: Programa Integral Amazónico de Conservación de Bosques y Producción Sostenible
summary: Programme led by the environment ministry and funded by the Green Climate Fund and GEF, which Corresponsables says centres on the six Amazon provinces and southern dry forests.

name: Programa Paisaje Yasuní
summary: Programme funded by the Legacy Landscapes Fund, whose aims include strengthening the park's monitoring and environmental control.

name: Proyecto Corredores de Conectividad Amazónicos
summary: Active project run by Ecuador's environment ministry, funded by the Global Environment Facility and partnered with WWF, which monitors with ten camera traps and, Youtopía says, uses an AI tool to classify photos formerly sorted manually.

name: Proyecto Mantas Ecuador
summary: Project run by Fundación Megafauna Marina del Ecuador and led by Michel Guerrero, partnered with the Marine Megafauna Foundation; its head said in 2019 it began in 2011 and held around 2,500 individuals in its database.

name: Proyecto Paisaje Jaguar
summary: Jaguar conservation project run by WCS Ecuador and funded by the Global Environment Facility, which placed over 120 camera traps at 62 Esmeraldas stations in late 2023 and trained Yasuní staff in July 2025.

name: Pueblo Kichwa de Rukullakta
summary: Indigenous people who, according to The Nature Conservancy, drive an initiative together with the Kichwa Nationality of Pastaza.

name: Pueblo Originario Kichwa de Sarayaku
summary: Indigenous Kichwa people whose territory is Kawsak Sacha, the Living Forest, declared for its sustainable preservation and conservation, and registered by them in the ICCA Registry.

name: Pueblo Shuar Arutam
summary: Shuar people with a territory of about 233,170 hectares across 6 associations and 47 communities; joined Socio Bosque in 2008, and a 2020 case study reported an agreement covering 83,915 hectares.

name: Reassembly research unit
summary: Active research unit led by Nico Blüthgen, which Ecoticias reports is at the Canandé reserve documenting forest recovery after clearing, with team members having set up 62 monitoring plots.

name: REDD for Early Movers Ecuador
summary: Programme whose first agreement in June 2018 was worth about 50 million dollars, acknowledged in the ministry's forest report and said by a German-funded monitoring project to rest on its foundations.

name: ReforesTree
summary: Benchmark dataset covering six sites in Ecuador, whose authors show a deep learning model estimating carbon stock from drone imagery.

name: Registro de trampas cámara del monitoreo a escala de paisajes
summary: Camera trap dataset from a landscape management project in the national protected area system, which the record says the ministry published on 25 April 2023.

name: Rivas-Torres Lab
summary: Active lab, partnered with Amazon IA, that says it combines field ecology, drones, remote sensing, sensors, AI and local knowledge, and produced field-validated vegetation maps for the Galápagos.

name: Sacred Headwaters site, Project Centinela
summary: Project site with Fundación Pachamama, the Amazon Sacred Headwaters Alliance and Regen Network as partners, where Planet said in June 2025 the partners would use its imagery and analytics to monitor deforestation.

name: Segunda Evaluación Nacional Forestal del Ecuador Continental
summary: Active dataset whose GBIF description says the evaluation aims to provide updated data on tree species diversity and composition across forest strata in continental Ecuador.

name: SELVATEK
summary: Ecuadorian company that Limelight describes as owned by Indigenous and local people from Napo, with a mission of biomonitoring and research enhanced by AI, robotics, drones, imaging and acoustic recognition.

name: Sistema de Monitoreo de Bioindicadores Amazónico
summary: Project using remote sensing, drone information and chemical and biological parameters, described as the first system programmed in open source for the Ecuadorian Amazon.

name: Sistema Nacional de Indicadores Ambientales y Sostenibilidad
summary: Active national dataset of environmental statistics and indicators by theme, run by the environment ministry and listed under its Strategic Information Directorate.

name: Sistema Nacional de Monitoreo de Bosques (Ecuador)
summary: Active national forest monitoring programme run by the environment ministry, using SEPAL for map processing since the 2018 coverage and generating early warning alerts every 15 days in its first phase.

name: Smart Island Monitoring, Floreana
summary: Active Island Conservation project, part of the Floreana restoration project, combining IoT, AI camera traps and smart traps, which it reports reviewed over 81,000 images in about two months and cut manual monitoring by 98%.

name: Support of the national forest monitoring
summary: Closed project funded by the International Climate Initiative, whose page reports an open-source monitoring system for carbon emissions accounting and foundations for the REDD Early Movers programme.

name: Tayunts Association
summary: Association representing 7 Shuar communities, whose 47,500 acres of forest entered Socio Bosque in 2013, with government payments of over $70,000 a year described for 20 years of protection.

name: The Leatherback Project
summary: Nonprofit describing itself as a 501(c)(3) protecting leatherback sea turtles and other endangered marine species, reporting nests monitored under Proyecto Yaug Galu, with a GBIF publisher record listing Jaramijó, Manabí.

name: Third Millennium Alliance
summary: Organisation reporting a 2,000-acre rainforest purchase for a reserve, with bioacoustic monitoring and a neural network trained to identify wildlife vocalisations.

name: Todos los Ojos en la Amazonía
summary: Active programme implemented by a coalition of more than 30 organisations, led by COICA, Hivos and Greenpeace.

name: Tu Amazonía
