summary: Active non-profit describing itself as Amazonian, Indigenous and intercultural, listing territorial monitoring systems among its lines of action, funded by Global Nature Watch and partnered with the Waorani nationality.

name: Un poco del Chocó
summary: Small nature reserve and biological research station at Las Tolas, Gualea, Pichincha, focused on local birds, with a bird observatory and biodiversity inventories.

name: Universidad de Cuenca
summary: University linked to a 2023 LSTM runoff forecasting paper, a reported agreement for a satellite, drone and AI tool, and a laboratory listing freshwater biomonitoring research.

name: Universidad de Las Américas
summary: Quito university whose SI2Lab has the last author of a 2022 paper on forecasting Amazon deforestation with a hybrid machine learning model.

name: Universidad de las Fuerzas Armadas ESPE
summary: University whose department lists a 2020 to 2021 project on early forest-fire detection using machine learning and visible-spectrum classification algorithms.

name: Universidad del Azuay
summary: University whose 2023 project proposed applying machine learning to drone data from the Cuenca Forest Inventory to detect forest species locally.

name: Universidad Espíritu Santo
summary: University whose BIO-SOS programme spans 2021 to 2050 and which reports that ManglArt AI uses unsupervised machine learning.

name: Universidad Indoamérica
summary: University with papers on forest change drivers using random forests (2019) and species distribution modelling using deep learning (2026), whose first author gives a Quito affiliation.

name: Universidad Nacional de Loja
summary: University that reports a pilot project with UTPL on wildfire susceptibility maps.

name: Universidad Regional Amazónica Ikiam
summary: University with an author on a 2018 paper classifying long-term forest dynamics in the Ecuadorian Amazon, and which proposes an open-source relational database management system.

name: Universidad San Francisco de Quito
summary: Quito university whose researchers published deep learning work on sharks, sea lions, Amazon animals and ladybird beetles, and which reports research, teaching and conservation at three scientific stations.

name: Universidad Técnica del Norte
summary: University reporting collaboration with the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona and the national risk management secretariat on a fire monitoring platform.

name: Universidad Técnica Particular de Loja
summary: University that Naturaleza y Cultura Internacional says taught a camera-trapping course to rangers, and which is party to a joint wildfire pilot project.

name: Uso del UN Biodiversity Lab para apoyar el mapeo del Marco Global de Biodiversidad Kunming-Montreal en Ecuador
summary: Active project launched on 11 June 2025 to strengthen spatial data and biodiversity mapping use, built by Ecuador's environment ministry, funded by the Moore Foundation, and using the UN Biodiversity Lab.

name: WCS Ecuador
summary: Active organisation whose site reports twenty years of wildlife monitoring on the Maxus road in Yasuní and ten years of manatee monitoring, with SMART reported in ten protected areas in 2020.

name: WildAI
summary: Project of unknown status whose poster describes a web observatory showing images already classified by its AI and proposes a species classification system based on deep learning.

name: WWF-Ecuador
summary: Active organisation which Primicias reported in February 2022 planned a study with UDLA using environmental DNA to detect river fauna, and which partners with Fundación Futuro Ecuador.

name: Yachay Tech University
summary: University in Urcuquí, Ecuador, listed with its School of Mathematical and Computational Sciences and the DeepARC Research Group in the affiliation of a paper on AI detection of the giant African snail.

name: Yakuwarmi
summary: Active local organisation, described by Mongabay Latam as 80% women, which reportedly used AI-processed biodiversity reports to help conserve more than 5,000 hectares through two protected areas.

name: Zamora Chinchipe Provincial Government
summary: Provincial government that worked with Nature and Culture International and nine municipal governments to establish the Zamora Chinchipe Provincial Reserve, which in 2019 was said to protect 1,098,611 acres.

name: Zancudo Cocha community camera-trap monitoring
summary: Project of unknown status in which El Oriente says the community was trained in biological monitoring with camera traps, partnered with WWF-Ecuador.

name: 5D Vision
summary: Organisation mentioned alongside the Eagle Club in a source describing the BirdMap portal at birdmap.5dvision.ee.

name: Arbonics
summary: Founded in early 2022, this forestry company says it monitors forests using remote sensing and over 50 data layers and launched Impact Forestry in Estonia in September 2024.

name: Aves OÜ
summary: Company that carried out the 2017 Pärnu Bay and 2016 Pakri bird area inventories, with breeding counts and spring and autumn migration counts for Pärnu Bay.

name: Biodiversity Informatics and Taxonomy Research Strand
summary: Active research strand that builds the PlutoF platform and the eElurikkus portal, led by Urmas Kõljalg, and whose PlutoF team includes an AI engineer.

name: Biodiversity Programme (Swiss-Estonian cooperation)
summary: Four-year programme launched in 2024 with 6.93 million Swiss francs to improve Estonian wildlife monitoring and protected-area effectiveness; eDNA, mobile 3D bird radar and AI are to be tested.

name: BirdMap
summary: GPS tracking portal for migratory birds, operating since 2006, with over 160 birds of 12 species monitored and more than 850,000 fixes stored; the Environmental Investment Centre funded its upgrade.

name: Cape Põõsaspea autumn migration monitoring
summary: Autumn migration monitoring run by Viron Lintuseura ry. in 2004, repeated in 2009 and 2014; 2004 and 2009 counts reached 10 to 60 per cent of several flyway populations.

name: EAGLELIFE
summary: Closed project that ran from April 2004 to May 2009 with a total eligible budget of 846,618 euros, using GPS/satellite tracking and webcams and registering over 230 new nest sites.

name: ECOGRID
summary: Built and run by the University of Tartu Landscape Biodiversity Group, with soil geochemistry, carbon and DNA sampled at about 170 areas to validate maps and tools.

name: eElurikkus
summary: Active public portal on Estonian biodiversity, built on PlutoF, which says it holds over 7 million records and 45,580 species, including DNA-based and sound observations.

name: ELME project
summary: Estonian monitoring project whose 2023 methods report covers camera traps, drones, acoustic recorders and DNA, and says it bought Kaleidoscope Pro 5 and planned to test BirdNET.

name: Endangered Wildlife OÜ
summary: Tallinn-based company describing itself as ESG software and consulting that values biodiversity in monetary terms, offering a species database and SnapTi, a gamified citizen science app for tourists.

name: Environmental Investment Centre (Estonia)
summary: Estonian body that says it was founded in 2000, belongs to the Ministry of Climate's administrative area, and has been the central funder of the country's environmental projects.

name: EstBatLIFE
summary: Closed bat conservation project that ended on 31 December 2021 with an EU contribution of €583,437, led by the Estonian Fund for Nature, with monitoring planned to continue afterwards.

name: ESTHub
summary: Active programme, run by the Land and Spatial Board, that stores Sentinel data covering Estonia, free to all users, and received €430,000 from the EU Structural Fund.

name: Estonian bird and bat ringing scheme
summary: Active ringing scheme in which ringers report the birds they ring and the data go to an international database; a birdwatcher quoted by ERR put it at about 100 ringers and 60,000 to 80,000 birds a year.

name: Estonian breeding bird atlas 2025-2030
summary: Fieldwork for a new breeding bird distribution atlas began in 2025, run by the Estonian Ornithological Society, with nearly 700 volunteers entering records in the first year.

name: Estonian breeding bird point count monitoring
summary: Point count monitoring operating since 1983, run by the Estonian Ornithological Society, with counts on 61 routes in 2025, its 43rd counting season.

name: Estonian Environment Agency
summary: Active agency that carries out the national environmental monitoring programme and data exchange, and in its ELME report planned a 2023 procurement to develop camera-trap species identification.

name: Estonian Environment Information Centre
summary: Registered GBIF data publisher whose one listed dataset is the Estonian Nature Observations Database.

name: Estonian Environmental Board
summary: Active government agency within the Ministry of Climate's area, which says its task is to implement state policy on environmental use, nature conservation and radiation safety.

name: Estonian Fund for Nature
summary: Non-governmental conservation organisation founded on 1 February 1991 by 41 naturalists and experts, based in Tartu, which leads the EstBatLIFE project.

name: Estonian game population monitoring
summary: Monitoring of game species, for which the Environment Agency published a 2026 report with hunting recommendations; it uses trail cameras and a track-count index, and reported 650 to 800 lynx in autumn 2025.

name: Estonian Land and Spatial Development Board
summary: Estonian public body that says the national satellite data centre ESTHub, which processes and distributes Copernicus Sentinel data, was established under it, and it runs ESTHub.

name: Estonian Marine Institute
summary: Data creator of a public dataset of benthic flora biomass and coverage from Estonian national coastal sea monitoring, 1997 to 2016, published under a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence.

name: Estonian mid-winter waterbird count
summary: Mid-winter waterbird count run by the Estonian Ornithological Society, one of 17 monitoring works it carried out in 2025 under the state biodiversity and landscape monitoring sub-programme.

name: Estonian Naturalists' Society
summary: Active society that says its network of trustees across Estonia supports observations, and whose GBIF dataset holds citizen science observations, monitoring data and Atlas of Estonian Flora data.

name: Estonian Nature Information System
summary: Dataset where the Environmental Board enters protected bird species sites and sets buffer zones; ERR reported in October 2026 close to 100,000 records, over 14,000 revised the previous year.

name: Estonian Nature Observations Database
summary: Active observations database on GBIF, mostly of butterflies, birds, vascular plants and mammals, published under CC BY 4.0 with the Estonian Environment Information Centre named as publisher.

name: Estonian Ornithological Society
summary: Active society, a BirdLife International partner, that carried out the 2021 breeding bird point counts for the national monitoring programme and uses PlutoF for observations.

name: Estonian Research Council
summary: Funder of the 7 million euro FutureScapes centre of excellence, alongside the Ministry of Education and Research; February 2024 article reports it co-organised a Brussels biodiversity digital twin seminar.

name: Estonian University of Life Sciences
summary: University whose Institute of Agriculture and Environmental Sciences is the first author's affiliation on a 2024 paper mapping coastal meadow plant cover from Sentinel-2 and UAV data.

name: Estonian winter bird count
summary: Winter bird count run by the Estonian Ornithological Society using transect counts of unlimited width, with 2024/25 being its 38th season.

name: Forest resource accounting with remote sensing methods
summary: Run by Reach-U, September 2018 to July 2020; a November 2020 presentation described mapping tree species with satellite images and machine learning, said to enable annual 10 metre maps.

name: GBIF Estonia
summary: Active programme listed in GBIF's registry as the voting country node for Estonia, with the eElurikkus portal as its homepage, and partnered with GBIF.

name: Geokuup data cube for Estonia
summary: Active data cube for Estonia, built on Sentinel-2, combining Sentinel, Landsat and airborne LiDAR data, which a FOSS4G 2025 talk says aims to advance biodiversity and carbon research.

name: Greenmeter
summary: Application, built by the University of Tartu Landscape Biodiversity Group, that calculates how good a location within a 500 metre radius is for biodiversity and gives recommendations.

name: Institute of Agriculture and Environmental Sciences, Estonian University of Life Sciences
summary: Institute named as the first author's affiliation on a 2024 paper mapping coastal meadow plant fractional cover from Sentinel-2 and UAV data; address Kreutzwaldi 5, Tartu.

name: Kabli Bird Centre
summary: Bird centre in Kabli village, Pärnu county, run by the Estonian Environment Agency; a 17-metre mesh net is put up each autumn for ringing, ongoing over 50 years.

name: KappaZeta
summary: Active company specialising in synthetic aperture radar satellite imagery, which told Tehnopol it aims to launch its 3d-SAR mission in 2028 and lists national governments among customers.

name: Kotkaklubi
summary: NGO named alongside 5D Vision Ltd in a source about BirdMap, whose data cover over 160 GPS-tracked birds of 12 species.

name: Lake Võrtsjärv automated buoy station
summary: Automated buoy station run by the Estonian University of Life Sciences, deployed in 2010 to gather meteorological and water quality data, renewed in 2021 and recorded as operational.

name: Landscape Geoinformatics Lab, University of Tartu
summary: University of Tartu research group whose stated background spans land cover, water quality and geospatial machine learning, with members working on biodiversity prediction and detecting landscape elements in farmland using deep learning.

name: LIFE Mires Estonia
summary: Closed project that ran from September 2015 to December 2021 with a 2,815,576 euro eligible budget, restoring hydrology on 7,900 hectares and using drones and Random Forest classification for vegetation mapping.

name: LIFE-IP ForEst&FarmLand
summary: Ministry of the Environment-led project running 2020 to 2029 at a total cost of €19,561,784, planning to restore 3,500 ha of wet forest and 500 ha of dry forest and develop a new IT system.

name: Linnuekspert
summary: Company that conducted the 2017 Väinameri reedbed bird aerial counts for the Estonian Ornithological Society, with a report describing drone photo-mapping using DJI Phantom 4 Pro.

name: Lutreola Foundation
summary: Non-profit foundation registered in Estonia, named as responsible for a planned 2001–2004 EU LIFE European mink recovery project, with earlier release and radio-tracking work on Hiiumaa.

name: mereRITA
summary: Closed project run by the Estonian Marine Institute to develop monitoring and assessment methods for Estonian marine waters, testing Sentinel-3 models and machine learning for seabed habitat mapping, and producing 20 thematic reports.

name: Metsa võtmepuuliikide geneetilise mitmekesisuse vähenemise varajase prognoosimise ja seire süsteem
summary: Active 2025 to 2028 project led by Vytautas Magnus University to build a cross-border genetic diversity monitoring system for four key forest tree species, with a 1.915 million euro budget.

name: Mid-winter waterfowl count, Estonian national monitoring 1991-2016
summary: Dataset of waterfowl counts in monitoring sectors in Estonian territorial waters from 1991 to 2016, shared under a CC-BY licence, with 2,800 seabird records held in OBIS-SEAMAP.

name: Ministry of Climate (Estonia)
summary: Estonian ministry that says it carries out conservation management with the Estonian Environmental Board, and was named the Ministry of the Environment until 30 June 2023, according to Wikipedia.

name: My Naturesound
summary: Ongoing project, active since August 2015, using an app to record animal sounds, moderate them and publish observations to GBIF through PlutoF; its dataset holds about 2,956 occurrences.

name: NATARC
summary: Programme on the Estonian research infrastructure roadmap, funded by the European Regional Development Fund, within which PlutoF was developed in 2015 and which, with DiSSCo, is the main focus of PlutoF's current development.

name: National Environmental Monitoring Programme (Estonia)
summary: Estonian national programme, set by ministerial regulation, with sub-programmes including biodiversity and landscape, forest and marine monitoring; the Estonian Environment Agency is reported to be responsible for managing and implementing it.

name: Natural History Archives and Common Data Space
summary: Project that, according to Research in Estonia, aimed to make Estonian biodiversity and geological data accessible in a unified data space and develop AI-based analysis solutions, and supported upgrades to PlutoF.

name: Nature Observation Marathon
summary: Citizen science BioBlitz initiative run by the University of Tartu Natural History Museum and Botanical Garden, whose ninth marathon in June 2026 produced 10,199 observations from nearly 200 observers.

name: Naturum
summary: Company that compiled the 2015 Luitemaa bird area inventory report, with monitoring commissioned by the Estonian Ornithological Society as coordinator of a KIK project.

name: NutriLoopWorks
summary: Project funded by the European Regional Development Fund, with one goal of a remote sensing tool for algae levels in selected water bodies; it has six named partners.

name: Pro Mare
summary: NGO named as co-creator of the dataset of grey seal aerial counts and breeding success from Estonian national monitoring, 2000 to 2016.

name: Pärandkoosluste Kaitse Ühing
summary: Organisation that began a nationwide project in 2021 on dry and paludified meadows; support was granted to inventory 2,000 hectares, and management was recorded on 1,472 hectares of semi-natural grassland.

name: Reach-U
summary: Company founded in 1990, described in 2014 as working in mapping, geospatial data, GIS and mobile positioning; main contractor for 2018 to 2020 forest inventory remote sensing software project.

name: Satiladu
summary: Open web map of Estonian land use and land cover data, released by the Estonian Land Board in February 2021, also offering Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 imagery with NDVI filters.

name: Seire ja liigituvastus pildituvastuse abil (tehisintellekt)
summary: Estonian Environment Agency's ELME report says an AI-based software prototype was completed in 2021 to identify animal species in photos and semi-automatically estimate REM density parameters, but needs more work on accuracy and usability.

name: Single.Earth Digital Twin
summary: Model built and run by Single.Earth that, it says, monitors forest canopy on its platform every two weeks using Sentinel-1 data and machine learning, and covers land use, land cover and ecosystem parameters.

name: Single.Earth EUDR Tool
summary: Tool run by Single.Earth that, it says, uses its Digital Twin model of the world's forests to track sites for deforestation and forest degradation.

name: State Forest Management Centre
summary: Estonian forest management body that describes itself as the country's largest doer of nature conservation work, supporting protected species and restoring habitats and fish stocks, with 102,856 euros of a forest tree genetic diversity monitoring budget.

name: Statistical Forest Inventory
summary: Sample-based forest inventory, continuous in Estonia since 1999, with about 5,500 systematic-grid point observations a year and plots re-measured every five years at the same GPS-located places.

name: Sõrve Bird Observatory
summary: Bird station organisation (MTÜ Sõrve Linnujaam) that conducted the 2020 Mullutu-Loode inventory, reportedly using standardised methods, and whose 2001–2010 migration records are analysed in Hirundo.

name: Tartu Observatory
summary: Estonian research body whose authors, per OpenAlex, appear on papers about Sentinel-2 water quality retrieval and validation and on GLORIA, a global hyperspectral water dataset.

name: Tartu Observatory remote sensing support for Ukrainian forest and water-body monitoring
summary: In May 2024, Tartu Observatory reported cooperation with Ukrainian institutions on forest and water-body monitoring, using Estonian datasets for forest height, wood volume and carbon estimates.

name: The Center of Excellence for Sustainable Land Use (FutureScapes)
summary: Seven-year project, 2024 to 2030, with 7 million euros, planning to link biodiversity and carbon fluxes with satellite data in machine learning models and upscale to regional level.

name: University of Tartu Landscape Biodiversity Group
summary: Group that collected soil DNA and habitat data at about 170 ECOGRID test areas and launched a nationwide cowslip citizen science survey.

name: University of Tartu Natural History Museum and Botanical Garden
summary: Holding over a million specimens, it publishes a GBIF DNA and environmental sample dataset, was developing PlutoF in September 2022 and shares the GBIF Estonia node’s address.

name: Vaibla Bird Observatory
summary: Estonia's only inland bird station, founded in 1987 and run by volunteers as a non-profit at Vaibla village, Viljandi county, which mist-nets small passerines and can serve as a base for research data collection and ringer training.

name: Academy of Scientific Research and Technology
summary: Egyptian academy whose president, Mahmoud Sakr, launched a unified national database of wild plant herbarium specimens hosted by the Academy on 16 June 2021, as reported by Sada Elbalad.

name: Ain Shams University
summary: University listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of Nourhan K. ElBahnasy, first author of a 2025 paper on litterfall forecasting with tree-based ensemble models.

name: Al-Azhar University
summary: University listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of Emad El-Aydi, first author of a 2026 work on how many reefs and seasons a coral-bleaching model needs for the Red Sea.

name: Alexandria University
summary: University listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of Madiha Moustafa, first author of a 2025 paper on monitoring coral reefs near Hurghada using remote sensing and acoustic data.

name: Annual coral reef monitoring programme in the Red Sea (Egypt)
summary: Annual Red Sea coral reef monitoring programme announced in September 2025 and run by Red Sea Protectorates, in which reserve specialists and university researchers use standardised surveys to measure coral cover and stress factors.

name: Assessment of the Presence of Dugongs in the Suitable Habitats in the Egyptian Red Sea
summary: A closed project that, per its page, followed earlier dugong habitat prediction maps by planning a citizen science programme with 100 trained volunteers, 1,000 sightings, and habitat maps and an individual catalogue for the Ministry of Environment.

name: Assiut University
summary: University listed by OpenAlex among the affiliations of Ragab Khalil, first author of a 2024 paper on supervised NDVI composite thresholding for mapping arid region vegetation.

name: Beni-Suef University
summary: University listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of Asmaa A. Attwa, first author of a 2026 paper classifying coral bleaching with convolutional and transformer networks.

name: BleachWatch Egypt
summary: Coral monitoring programme, derived from an Australian Great Barrier Reef community scheme, that began in Hurghada, Safaga, El Quseir and Marsa Alam, with workshops, trainings and a September 2024 report, per HEPCA.

name: Cairo University
summary: University listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of Ahmad K. Hegazy, first author of a 2024 paper on Avicennia marina populations in South Sinai using satellite radiometric indices.

name: Center for Applied Research on the Environment and Sustainability
summary: Research centre at AUC’s School of Sciences and Engineering running MERS, which launched a mangrove GIS platform and reports restoring about 15 hectares by April 2026.

name: Centre for Environment and Development for the Arab Region and Europe
summary: Intergovernmental not-for-profit organisation founded in 1992 and based in Cairo, whose water programme lists applying AI, GIS, remote sensing and decision support tools, plus periodic State of the Water reporting.

name: Chamber of Diving and Water Sports (Egypt)
summary: Egyptian body founded by the Ministry of Tourism in 2007 for diving standards and Red Sea protection; it built the CDWS ECO Monitoring app for uploading marine species photos and videos.

name: Coastal Survey Project (HEPCA)
summary: HEPCA project begun in 2010 and built and run by HEPCA, aiming at the first quantitative survey of Red Sea natural resources, especially coral reefs, with sensitivity maps and a monitoring database.

name: Conservation of Nubian Ibex (South Sinai)
summary: A closed South Sinai project, funded by the GEF Small Grants Programme with US$13,720, planned camera-trap monitoring, ibex records and monitoring training for protected-area researchers; SGP lists it as completed satisfactorily, December 2009 to November 2012.

name: Coral Reef Image Classification Dataset for Deep Learning and Marine Biodiversity Monitoring
summary: Dataset for deep learning and marine biodiversity monitoring, listed by OpenAlex in 2025, with first author M.B. Badawi affiliated to King Salman International University.

name: Damietta University
summary: University listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of Hesham M. El Asmar, first author of a 2025 paper on deep learning monitoring of mangrove cover change in Tarout Bay, Saudi Arabia.

name: Desert Research Center
summary: Says it explores Egyptian desert resources and reports a remote sensing and GIS unit opened in 1988 and a gene bank storing 2,500 rare wild medicinal plants.

name: DroneTech
summary: Company that, according to Egypt Independent, signed a cooperation agreement with the ministry to implement its drone surveillance system, and is linked as a partner of the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency.

name: Eco Monitor
summary: App that the ministry's 2024 report says was prepared with the Chamber of Diving and Water Sports so diving operators can help monitor endangered marine species, with the Green Sharm project.

name: Effective Management of Wadi El-Rayan and Qarun Protected Areas
summary: Closed GEF-funded project in Egypt, run by IUCN, that surveyed biodiversity to update Key Biodiversity Areas and assessed management effectiveness at both protected areas; its closing ceremony was on 21 December 2025.

name: Egypt Mangrove GIS Knowledge Platform
summary: An active GIS platform, built by the Mangrove Ecosystem Restoration Solution project, giving data on mangrove distribution, health, biodiversity indicators and restoration site monitoring, with story maps, decision-support dashboards and downloadable datasets.

name: Egypt National Waterbird Monitoring Programme
summary: Run by Nature Conservation Egypt with EEAA and Nature Conservation Sector collaboration, the programme surveys wetlands and, NCE says, seeks long-term trend analysis using field observations and remote sensing.

name: Egypt smart aerial surveillance system
summary: Drone surveillance system, reported by Egypt Independent to integrate AI and geospatial analysis and to detect encroachment on state land or natural protectorates, built and run by the environmental affairs agency.

name: Egyptian Clearing House Mechanism for biodiversity
summary: Described in a 2018 document as a national biodiversity page updated in 2015, with no maintenance staff and two earlier versions no longer online.

name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency
summary: Described in a 2018 CBD document as Egypt's central environmental protection body, responsible for protectorates management and leading preparation of the national biodiversity strategy.

name: Egyptian Space Agency
summary: Egyptian space agency whose chief executive said in March 2025, as reported by Masrawy, that it was developing capacity in remote sensing through specialised satellites and applications.

name: Egyptian Survey Authority
summary: Egyptian mapping authority whose head of central administration for maps gave a presentation naming a national base map, built on its existing digital maps, as an aim of the spatial data infrastructure.

name: Elba Protectorate
summary: Protected area of 36,000 km² in Egypt’s Eastern Desert; a 2009 Oryx paper describes an author’s responsibility for monitoring dorcas gazelle, lappet-faced vulture and Egyptian vulture populations.

name: Fayoum University
summary: University listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of Ali G. Mahmoud, first author of a 2022 paper on land use and cover change in Al-Jouf, Saudi Arabia, using Google Earth Engine.

name: Galala Bird Observatory
summary: Bird migration count station on Galala Mountain, run by Nature Conservation Egypt, monitoring northbound soaring birds in spring, with 2,467 observation hours over five years to 20 April 2026.

name: Healthy Ecosystems for Rangeland Development
summary: Closed project, funded by the Global Environment Facility, on rangeland rehabilitation in Egypt and Jordan, whose listed results include a natural and rangeland database for research and decision makers.

name: Hurghada Environmental Protection and Conservation Association
summary: An NGO registered in the Red Sea Governorate that says it aims, with the dive community, to monitor coral reefs throughout the Egyptian Red Sea.

name: King Salman International University
summary: University that OpenAlex gives as the first author's affiliation on a 2025 coral reef image classification dataset work for deep learning and marine biodiversity monitoring.

name: Mangrove Ecosystem Restoration Solution (MERS)
summary: An active 2021 to 2026 mangrove restoration project with the communities of Hamata and Safaga, carried out with HSBC's Climate Solutions Partnership, which had restored about 15 hectares as of April 2026.

name: Marine Turtles Monitoring Programme in the Red Sea and Mediterranean (Egypt)
summary: According to Egypt's NBSAP 2015-2030, monitoring recorded four turtle species at 15 beaches, and green turtle satellite tracking began in Wadi El Gemal National Park in 2012.

name: Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation
summary: Ministry listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of Ahmed Y. Abed, first author of a 2026 paper on land cover change in the Bahr El Jebel Basin using remote sensing.

name: NAFCOAST
summary: A closed project funded by GMES and Africa and run by NARSS, studying North African coastal Earth observation services, including fishing zone mapping and Sentinel-1 oil spill detection.

name: National Authority for Remote Sensing and Space Sciences
summary: An Egyptian body that ran NAFCOAST, was selected for GMES and Africa in 2017, and organised a November 2023 course scheduled to cover vegetation monitoring with AI.

name: National Institute of Oceanography and Fisheries
summary: Egyptian institute listed among the members of the Partnership for Observation of the Global Ocean, and the first author's affiliation on a 2020 paper on GIS and remote sensing in lakes and coastal areas.

name: National Research Centre
summary: Research centre in Giza that OpenAlex gives as an affiliation of the first author of a 2021 paper using machine learning to track microeukaryotes in a Chinese watershed.

name: Nature Conservation Egypt
summary: Founded in 2005, it is BirdLife International's partner in Egypt and an IUCN member, and reports recording 379,033 birds at Galala in one spring season.

name: Nature Conservation Sector (Egypt)
summary: Described in a 2018 CBD document as Egypt's central protected areas and biodiversity institution, which the ministry's 2024 report says received a Siwa gazelle monitoring report.

name: Port Said University
summary: University that OpenAlex lists among the first author's affiliations on a 2024 paper on automated machine learning tools to distinguish two killer whale ecotypes.

name: Protecting Endangered Marine Turtles (Bir El Abd)
summary: Marine turtle project run by the Development and Environment Protection Association in Bier El Abd, from June 2010 to June 2012, recorded as satisfactorily completed, monitoring egg hatching in over 70 field visits.

name: Red Sea annual coral reef assemblage monitoring programme (Egypt)
summary: According to Egypt's 2023 ICRI report, an EEAA-used programme running from 2000 to 2019, stopped by COVID-19, with 24 sites evaluated annually from 2015 to 2019.

name: Red Sea Dolphin Project
summary: A closed project, run by HEPCA, whose 2010 to 2013 monitoring plan set twelve weeks a year at sea, combining visual observation, towed hydrophone acoustic monitoring and photo-identification.

name: Red Sea Islands Breeding Waterbirds Project (Egypt)
summary: A closed project, run by the Nature Conservation Sector and Nature Conservation Egypt and funded by the AEWA Small Grants Fund, which from 2011 to 2014 sought better breeding waterbird data and set up a database with historical counts.

name: Red Sea Protectorates (Egypt)
summary: Egyptian Ministry of Environment conservation body whose scientific team leads the Red Sea coral reef monitoring programme announced in September 2025; surveys at several Northern Islands sites found no bleaching in 2025.

name: Red Sea Sharks (HEPCA)
summary: Research programme built and run by HEPCA, which says it gathers data on shark population structure, ecology and behaviour, using diver sightings and photo-identification, including of oceanic whitetip sharks.

name: Reef Check Egypt
summary: Survey programme whose Egypt page records 702 surveys, including 12 in 2025 and 20 in 2024, with all data available on the Global Reef Tracker.

name: Saint Katherine Protectorate
summary: In June 2021, its director reported instructions to increase biodiversity patrols and identify violations, alongside South Sinai plans for patrols identifying species close to extinction.

name: Senghor University
summary: University that OpenAlex lists among the first author's affiliations on a 2026 remote sensing study of mangrove landscape change in Coubalan, Casamance, Senegal.

name: Sensitivity Atlas of Migratory Soaring Birds in Egypt
summary: A document, listed on Nature Conservation Egypt's publications page, that proposes a sensitivity map of migratory soaring birds in Egypt based on distribution and migration data.

name: Suez Canal University
summary: University that OpenAlex gives as the first author's affiliation on a 2017 paper presenting a new approach to estimating mangrove canopy cover from Landsat 8 imagery.

name: Suez University
summary: University that OpenAlex gives as the first author's affiliation on a 2026 paper assessing Lake Nasser's optical and thermal variability with MODIS data from 2005 to 2025.

name: Tanta University
summary: University that OpenAlex lists among the first author's affiliations on a 2026 paper using Google Earth Engine remote sensing to assess vegetation dynamics in Bavaria's protected areas.

name: The Development and Environment Protection Association in Bier El Abd
summary: Non-governmental organisation in Bier El Abd that was grantee of an SGP marine turtle project from June 2010 to June 2012, which monitored egg hatching along 100 km of Mediterranean coast.

name: Thermal resilience of corals in the Egyptian Red Sea
summary: Administered by Port Said University with HEPCA and NYU Abu Dhabi as partners, the project reported coral microbiome genomics and planned heat-stress experiments in December 2022.

name: TurtleWatch Egypt
summary: Citizen science programme on endangered marine turtles in the Egyptian Red Sea, started in 2011, with a photo-identification database and, from February 2025, a team member leading development of an AI identification system.

name: Unified national database of Egyptian herbarium plant specimens
summary: Reported by Sada Elbalad as launched on 16 June 2021, hosted by the Academy and coordinated by Cairo University, with data and images available to everyone.

name: Wadi Gemal Protected Area
summary: Protected area covering 7,000 km² in Egypt’s Eastern Desert; a 2009 Oryx paper describes camera monitoring of ibex waterholes and a biologist’s responsibilities for bird, gazelle and ibex surveys.

name: Conservation Management of Eritrea's Coastal, Marine and Island Biodiversity
summary: A GEF-funded project run by the Ministry of Marine Resources, aimed at setting up conservation areas, species programmes and an operational information system, and listed by GEF as closed on 13 September 2016.

name: Eritrea Land Degradation Monitoring and Assessment 2018
summary: A map service dataset described as land degradation monitoring and assessment products developed with RUSLE.

name: Eritrea Wetlands Monitoring and Assessment
summary: Map service covering Debarwa wetlands in Eritrea for 1990, 2000 and 2019, tagged with status maps, change maps, Sentinel-2 and Landsat, with credited bodies’ roles unspecified.

name: Forestry and Wildlife Authority (Eritrea)
summary: An active Eritrean authority reported in 2022 to monitor wildlife every three months, and credited in 2019 with research that led to the 2016 rediscovery of the Eritrea side-neck turtle.

name: Integrated Semenawi and Debubawi Bahri Protected Area System for Conservation of Biodiversity and Mitigation of Land Degradation Project
summary: A closed GEF and UNDP funded project (GEF ID 4559), run by the Forestry and Wildlife Authority, located mainly in the Northern and Southern Red Sea zobas, with wildlife monitoring surveys as an outcome indicator.

name: Mai Nefhi College of Science
summary: Eritrean college which, with the Ministry of Marine Resources, is assessing coral reefs and has started a coral monitoring programme, using line transect surveys to measure bleached coral, according to the 2026 to 2030 biodiversity strategy.

name: Massawa College of Marine Science and Technology
summary: Public Eritrean Massawa college created in 2006 which a 2019 national report says established reef monitoring sites, surveyed bleaching and jointly conducted preliminary surveys with the marine resources ministry.

name: Ministry of Agriculture (Eritrea)
summary: An active Eritrean ministry which, a 2022 UNDP evaluation reported, was given authority by proclamation to establish protected areas, and which a 2019 report names as the CITES focal point.

name: Ministry of Land, Water and Environment (Eritrea)
summary: Described by UNDP in 2022 as Eritrea's GEF focal point, this ministry reportedly helped train 25 experts in GIS and remote sensing in February 2026.

name: Ministry of Marine Resources (Eritrea)
summary: An active Eritrean ministry that, per a 2019 national report, has funded marine turtle nesting survey and tagging work and was conducting a rapid assessment ecological survey.

name: National Database of Fauna and Flora (Eritrea)
summary: Database of the Ministry of Agriculture's Regulatory Services Department, which Eritrea's updated NBSAP cites for 2,508 identified plant species in 48 orders and 202 seaweed species reported by its aquatic group.

name: ACCIONA
summary: Infrastructure and energy company that monitors birds of prey and bats at wind farms with radar and a camera-based detection system.

name: Acció Ecologista-Agró
summary: Environmental group whose management of the Tancat de la Pipa reserve, owned by the Confederación Hidrográfica del Júcar, runs through an agreement with that body and SEO/BirdLife.

name: AEMS-Ríos con Vida
summary: Association with which part of the Palancia river's management is agreed, running ecosystem restoration and education activities there.

name: Agencia Espacial Española
summary: Spain's national space agency, based in Seville. With the European Space Agency it launched a national call for Earth observation applications after the wildfires that affected Spain's land and ecosystems.

name: Agencia Estatal de Investigación
summary: Spain's state research funding agency. It funds nature AI projects including PLOME.

name: Agforest
summary: Company offering AG4EUDR, an AI tool combining satellite analysis and geospatial data to automate due diligence statements under the EU deforestation regulation.

name: Agresta
summary: Spanish worker cooperative in forestry consulting, founded in 2000, that uses remote sensing and runs the ForestMap automatic forest inventory service.

name: AgroForChange
summary: R software that analyses 20 years of Landsat and Sentinel data with Random Forest to detect abandoned farm plots turning into other land uses.

name: Aguas de Murcia passive bioacoustic bird monitoring
summary: Passive acoustic monitoring of birds at water utility sites in Murcia, with audio sent to the cloud where neural networks identify species.

name: Agència Menorca Reserva de Biosfera
summary: Agency through which the Consell Insular de Menorca manages the Menorca Biosphere Reserve, which covers 70,093.66 ha of land and 448,936.45 ha of sea, according to the ministry's page.

name: AI-based fish detections at OBSEA Underwater Observatory
summary: Open dataset of fish detections from a YOLOv8 model run on OBSEA camera images.

name: AI-CENSUS
summary: Wildlife census in Doñana National Park that identified mammal species in photo-trapping images with a convolutional neural network, with volunteers checking images on Zooniverse.

name: AI4SEA
summary: Project developing AI-embedded multi-robot systems for autonomous mapping, monitoring and restoration of underwater habitats, with Posidonia meadows as the main use case.

name: AIMA
summary: AI algorithm in Mosquito Alert that identifies invasive species in citizens' images in under five minutes and alerts health authorities to detections in new areas.

name: AIR Institute
summary: Private foundation and technology centre in Salamanca for AI and computing research. It leads the RetechFOR forest data space.

name: Ajuntament de València
summary: City council that developed València-BioSoundScape with iTEAM and coordinated the sensors through its Urban Sandbox service.

name: Alnitak
summary: Organisation whose surveys in the Alboran Sea from 1990 to 2006 recorded 3,712 cetacean and 306 sea turtle sightings, published as an open dataset on OBIS-SEAMAP.

name: Anthos
summary: Information system on the plants of Spain, built from distribution data extracted from the literature at the Real Jardín Botánico.

name: APEXS
summary: i2CAT project for a camera trap prototype with on-board AI, communications and a deterrent system.

name: Artificial Vision Air Detection
summary: Maker of an AI bird detection system for wind farms and critical infrastructure, also installed at Endesa's Rocío substation in Doñana.

name: Artikode Intelligence
summary: Company that developed the BioSoundScape online platform for València's acoustic biodiversity project.

name: Asociación de Desenvolvemento Rural Mariñas - Betanzos
summary: Rural development association named by the ministry as managing entity of the Mariñas Coruñesas e Terras do Mandeo Biosphere Reserve in A Coruña (114,359.57 ha land, 2,866.45 ha sea).

name: Asociación de Naturalistas del Sureste
summary: Conservation association founded in 1973, based in Murcia. It runs field monitoring in south-east Spain, including bottlenose dolphin monitoring with a photo-identification catalogue.

name: Asociación Herpetológica Española
summary: Spanish herpetological society that developed SIARE, a server of data on Spanish amphibians and reptiles, and runs monitoring networks.

name: Asociación Hippocampus
summary: NGO in the Region of Murcia that studies and monitors the long-snouted seahorse in the Mar Menor through volunteer underwater censuses.

name: Asociación para la Defensa de la Naturaleza y los Recursos de Extremadura
summary: Extremaduran nature association that owns about 350 ha of biological reserves, built up by buying and leasing estates since 1984, and says it pioneered land stewardship in the region.

name: Asociación para o Desenvolvemento do Medio Rural da Reserva da Biosfera Área de Allariz
summary: Association of four municipalities that the ministry's biosphere reserve page gives as the management and administration body of the Allariz biosphere reserve.

name: Asociación Quercus Sonora
summary: Association in Ulloa (Lugo) that, according to a February 2021 El Salto article, took over management of some estates from FUNDEM and also bought land in its areas.

name: Asociación Reserva de la Biosfera Valle del Cabriel
summary: Association of local action groups and the Asociación de Municipios Ribera del Cabriel, named by the ministry as managing entity of the 421,797.77 ha Valle del Cabriel Biosphere Reserve, seated in Enguídanos (Cuenca).

name: Asociación Salmantina de Agricultura de Montaña
summary: Association (ASAM) named by the ministry as managing entity of the Sierras de Béjar y Francia Biosphere Reserve in Salamanca, covering 199,203.76 ha and 88 municipalities.

name: Asociación Tyto Alba
summary: Association that SEO/BirdLife's reserves page says manages the 969 ha reserve in the Montes Aquilianos.

name: Asociación Zerynthia
summary: Spanish butterfly association with monitoring programmes, listed by the European Butterfly Monitoring Scheme as one of four networks in Spain.

name: AtalaIA Detection Technologies
summary: Company applying AI to monitoring and management of the maritime environment, with its OJOS project and a recreational fishing system built with IMEDEA.

name: Atos Spain
summary: Spanish arm of Atos, which coordinated the EO4wildlife platform for wildlife monitoring with Copernicus and ARGOS data.

name: Ayama
summary: Spanish company that, by its own account, designs and makes GPS and radio-tracking systems for wild animals entirely in Spain, aimed at biology, conservation, ecological studies and wildlife management.

name: Ayuntamiento de La Pola de Gordón
summary: Town council named by the ministry as managing entity of the Alto Bernesga Biosphere Reserve (33,385.08 ha), which covers La Pola de Gordón and Villamanín in León.

name: Ayuntamiento de Madrid
summary: City council that deployed a network of 15 AI acoustic sensors to follow birds and bats in two Madrid parks.

name: AZTI
summary: Technology and research centre that built an AI model telling small pelagic fish species apart from their acoustic echo-traces.

name: Balearic Islands Coastal Observing and Forecasting System
summary: Spanish scientific infrastructure that runs a multi-platform marine observation and forecasting system in the western Mediterranean, with open data through a certified repository.

name: Baliera Global SL
summary: Spanish company that coordinates PCP-WISE, a European project on water management from space.

name: Banc de Dades de Biodiversitat de Catalunya
summary: Biodiversity data bank of Catalonia, hosted at the University of Barcelona and registered as a GBIF publisher.

name: Banco de Datos de la Biodiversidad de la Comunitat Valenciana
summary: Regional platform of the Generalitat Valenciana that gathers and publishes expert-validated distribution records of wild species, with a mobile app.

name: Banco de Datos de la Biodiversidad en Aragón
summary: Unit of the Aragón government's biodiversity service that gathers, organises and publishes data on Aragonese biodiversity for managers and the public.

name: Banco de Datos de la Naturaleza
summary: The environment ministry's data bank on nature, with downloads including habitats of community interest and a map server.

name: Basoinsa
summary: Environmental consultancy founded in 1985 in the Basque Country. It developed EEIKO, a multi-platform tool for recording and controlling invasive plants.

name: Big Mosquito Bytes
summary: Mosquito Alert project coordinated by Frederic Bartumeus at CEAB-CSIC and supported by the "la Caixa" Foundation.

name: Bioacústica Física y Multi-sensores Distribuidos
summary: University of La Laguna research group that built a neural network and low-cost smart node to classify orca sounds.

name: BIOCAN
summary: The Canary Islands government's biodiversity information system, which brings together its species databases and tools.

name: Biodiversidad Virtual
summary: Citizen science platform that gathers species distribution data for Iberia, the Balearics and the Canaries through georeferenced digital photographs. Data upload now runs through observation.org.

name: Biogenoma
summary: Catalan genome project associated with the European Reference Genome Atlas, which is building an atlas of Europe's biodiversity genome.

name: Biotfy
summary: Company selling automated biodiversity monitoring with expert advice, for decision-making and auditing.

name: Bird Song Detector
summary: Deep learning detector of bird song segments for audio from Doñana, used before a fine-tuned BirdNET classifier. Set out in a 2025 preprint.

name: BIRDeep
summary: Birdsong monitoring project in Doñana that uses deep learning on recorder audio to follow bird species abundance and changes to migration periods.

name: BIRDeep Audio Annotations
summary: Open dataset of bird vocalisations from Doñana National Park, annotated for training and testing detection and classification models.

name: Blanes Bay Microbial Observatory
summary: Marine microbe monitoring programme studying genomic, functional and species diversity, with monthly sampling since March 2001 and microbial data going back to 1992.

name: BLUESTOCK
summary: Project on Posidonia oceanica blue carbon, developing a non-destructive way to quantify carbon stocks with geoacoustics, autonomous vehicles, drones and satellite images.

name: Cabildo de Fuerteventura
summary: Island government named by the ministry's biosphere reserve page as managing entity of the Fuerteventura Biosphere Reserve (166,139.40 ha land, 188,675.85 ha sea).

name: Cabildo de Gran Canaria
summary: Island government that, through its Servicio de Medio Ambiente, is named by the ministry as managing entity of the Gran Canaria Biosphere Reserve (65,994.42 ha land, 37,600.14 ha sea).

name: Cabildo de Lanzarote
summary: Island government named by the ministry's biosphere reserve page as managing entity of the Lanzarote Biosphere Reserve (84,467.62 ha land, 40,488.07 ha sea).

name: Cabildo de Tenerife
summary: Island government whose environment, sustainability and water area is named by the ministry as managing entity of the Macizo de Anaga Biosphere Reserve (16,717.17 ha land, 33,208.82 ha sea).

name: Cabildo Insular de El Hierro
summary: Island government that, through its environment, waste and recycling department, is named by the ministry as managing entity of the El Hierro Biosphere Reserve (26,871 ha land, 31,731 ha sea).

name: CAMELE
summary: Deep learning framework that maps Posidonia oceanica and other seabed habitats from satellite imagery, trained on PlanetScope images and 19 years of Balearic government habitat data.

name: CarbonX Engineering Solutions
summary: Company leading the Silvatech forest monitoring tool under RetechFOR.

name: CARTIF
summary: Technology centre foundation in Castilla y León. It is a member of the VALOR AQUA consortium in PCP-WISE and a RetechFOR partner.

name: Catalan Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: Network launched in 1994 that monitors butterfly abundance on fixed transects, with 240 stations having provided data by 2023 across much of Catalonia, the Balearic Islands and Andorra.

name: CatLC
summary: A set of aerial and satellite images from 2018 for creating the Catalan land cover map with AI techniques.

name: CDTI Innovación
summary: The innovation agency of Spain's science ministry. Its NEOTEC programme supported COOLX Earth's deforestation platform.

name: Centre d'Estudis Avançats de Blanes
summary: CSIC research centre that coordinates the Mosquito Alert citizen science platform and worked with IFISC on the CAMELE seagrass mapping model.

name: Centre de Ciència i Tecnologia Forestal de Catalunya
summary: Catalan forest research centre whose Conservation Biology Group built the PyrVision camera-trap model, and a partner in the Spanish phase of Tech4Nature.

name: Centre de Visió per Computador
summary: Computer vision centre at the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona that worked with CTFC on the PyrVision camera-trap model.

name: Centro Nacional de Información Geográfica
summary: Spanish public body whose download centre distributes the PNOA-LiDAR point clouds and derived products.

name: Cesefor
summary: Foundation for forest services and industry in Castilla y León. It leads the region's continuous forest inventory and forest data portal under RetechFOR.

name: CIRCE
summary: Organisation that researches cetaceans in the Strait of Gibraltar and took part in the first acoustic description of the Iberian orca's dialect with a broadband buoy.

name: COMBUS-IA CYL
summary: AI platform that produces dynamic high-resolution maps of forest fuels in Castilla y León from LiDAR and satellite data.

name: Comisión de Gestión del Parque Nacional de los Picos de Europa
summary: Management commission named by the ministry as managing entity of the Picos de Europa Biosphere Reserve (63,642.31 ha), which spans Asturias, Cantabria and León.

name: Comisión Mixta OAPN-Comunidad Autónoma de Castilla-La Mancha
summary: Joint commission of the national parks agency and Castilla-La Mancha that, according to the agency, manages Cabañeros and Las Tablas de Daimiel national parks, which remain with the State.

name: Complex System Group, Universidad Politécnica de Madrid
summary: Research group at the Technical University of Madrid and a partner in the ANTENNA pollinator monitoring project.

name: Comunidad de Bardenas Reales de Navarra
summary: Traditional local body formed three centuries ago by 22 entities with use rights, named by the ministry as managing entity of the 39,285.30 ha Bardenas Reales de Navarra Biosphere Reserve.

name: Comunidad de Madrid
summary: Regional government whose environment department is named as managing entity of the Sierra del Rincón Biosphere Reserve (15,233.23 ha) and which pays 70% of basic management of Cuenca Alta del Manzanares Regional Park in 2023–2027.

name: CON-DATA
summary: Project that recovers, sorts and opens biodiversity data gathered by Fundación Global Nature over decades, running since October 2025.

name: ConBoSer
summary: Project using underwater robots and deep learning to assess the conservation status of seagrass and Cystoseira forests on the Balearic coasts and the role of marine reserves.

name: Confederación Hidrográfica del Júcar
summary: River basin authority that owns the Tancat de la Pipa reserve area in the Albufera Natural Park, managed through an agreement with SEO/BirdLife and Acció Ecologista Agró, and often recovers riparian forest under agreement with Fundación Limne.

name: Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas
summary: Spain's state agency for scientific research. Its centres include the Doñana Biological Station, the Institute of Marine Sciences and the Spanish Institute of Oceanography.

name: Consorci de les Gavarres
summary: Consortium that, in a November 2024 announcement, was to coordinate planned thinning and clearing on 30 ha of public and private estates in the Gavarres massif, prioritising sectors and obtaining owners' authorisations.

name: Consorci del Parc de l'espai d'interès natural de Gallecs
summary: Consortium set up on 22 November 2006 by the Generalitat and six municipalities to manage, protect and conserve the 774 ha Gallecs site and its ecological values.

name: Consorcio de Administraciones de la Reserva de la Biosfera La Palma
summary: Consortium of administrations named by the ministry's biosphere reserve page as managing entity of the La Palma Biosphere Reserve (70,701.21 ha land, 16,550.06 ha sea).

name: Consorcio de la Reserva de la Biosfera de los Ancares Leoneses
summary: Consortium of four municipalities and the Consejo Comarcal de El Bierzo, named by the ministry as managing entity of the Ancares Leoneses Biosphere Reserve (56,742.14 ha).

name: Consorcio de la Reserva de la Biosfera Ordesa-Viñamala
summary: Managing entity of the Ordesa-Viñamala Biosphere Reserve, which covers 117,264.99 ha across 11 municipalities in Huesca, according to the ministry's reserve page.

name: Consorcio para la Gestión y Administración de la Reserva de la Biosfera de Babia
summary: Managing entity of the Babia Biosphere Reserve, which covers 38,107.60 ha in the municipalities of Cabrillanes and San Emiliano, León, according to the ministry's reserve page.

name: COOLX Earth
summary: Málaga startup, founded in 2022, building a platform on satellite observation, AI and blockchain so that companies can check where raw materials come from and comply with the EU Deforestation Regulation.

name: Cos d'Agents Rurals
summary: Rural agents body whose AI system for identifying Pyrenean bears from camera-trap images is reported by Lleida Diari as under development, alongside monitoring with cameras and hair traps.

name: DC Technology
summary: Company that will supply acoustic instruments to SofiaNet.

name: DECAPIN-IA CYL
summary: Deep learning early warning system that maps the decline of maritime pine in Castilla y León from satellite and drone data.

name: Detección automatizada de fuentes de humo con modelos de IA
summary: AI tool that detects smoke in real time on any forest surveillance camera in the Castilla y León monitoring network.

name: DETECPOS
summary: Coordinated UIB and IMEDEA project that automates geolocated multilayer maps of Posidonia, other algae and associated fauna with underwater robots and deep learning.

name: Diputació de Barcelona
summary: Provincial government of Barcelona, which manages a network of natural parks and is the local authority in the Tech4Nature Spain partnership.

name: Diputació de Girona
summary: Provincial body named by the ministry, together with the Diputación de Barcelona, as managing entity of the Montseny Biosphere Reserve, a natural park of 50,346.32 ha.

name: Diputación Provincial de Lugo
summary: Provincial body named by the ministry as managing entity of the Terras do Miño Biosphere Reserve, which covers 365,869.42 ha across 26 municipalities in Lugo.

name: DNASense
summary: Biodiversa+ project developing environmental impact assessment tools for marine biodiversity from eDNA and remote sensing, with the University of Barcelona as the Spanish beneficiary listed by Fundación Biodiversidad.

name: DTBird
summary: Spanish company whose system detects birds near wind turbines and warns of collision risk, with units in several countries. Developed by three Spanish biologists.

name: EEIKO
summary: Multi-platform application for controlling invasive exotic plants, fed by records from the public that a technical team validates.

name: EIDOS
summary: A database of official information on wild species present in Spain, gathered by the environment ministry and structured on the Plinian Core standard.

name: EMPHATIC
summary: Biodiversa+ BiodivMon project, listed in Fundación Biodiversidad's award resolution, using eDNA, drone photogrammetry and blow sampling, with indicators planned for a policymaker monitoring tool.

name: Endesa
summary: Spanish energy company whose biodiversity work includes camera trap and acoustic surveys at its sites, and AI bird detection at a substation in Doñana.

name: Eoforest
summary: GMV's catalogue of forestry geoinformation products from Earth observation, for sustainable management of forest resources.

name: Espacio de Datos Forestal RETECHFOR
summary: Federated forest data space for Castilla y León, built on International Data Spaces Association and Gaia-X specifications, for public bodies, research centres and companies.

name: Estación Biológica de Doñana
summary: CSIC research station at Doñana. Its researchers work on AI for camera traps with the Seville microelectronics institute and on the BIRDeep birdsong model with U-tad.

name: EXOCAT
summary: CREAF information system and database on exotic species in Catalonia.

name: FAPAS
summary: Spanish wildlife NGO that says it keeps up its own census of female brown bears, with camera traps.

name: FireTwin
summary: AI digital twin that combines multi-sensor satellite data and weather to assess vegetation state and fuel moisture, one of eight projects backed by AEE and ESA InCubed.

name: Fonoteca Zoológica
summary: Bioacoustic collection of the Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales that gathers, classifies and stores recordings of amphibians, birds, insects, mammals and reptiles.

name: ForestGPT
summary: AI assistant that lets forest technicians in Castilla y León query the region's forest documents in natural language, with answers tied to the official documents.

name: ForestMap
summary: Web service that calculates forest inventories automatically from national aerial LiDAR and forest inventory plots, for selected Spanish provinces.

name: Fotografía y Biodiversidad
summary: Spanish non-profit association set up in 2010 to manage Biodiversidad Virtual, a citizen science platform that gathers species distribution data from georeferenced photographs. It also runs butterfly monitoring.

name: Fototrampeig Mamífers Catalunya
summary: Camera-trap project in Catalonia, led by the FELIS-ICHN group with Fundació Barcelona Zoo, that aims to be the reference portal for collecting such data.

name: FRIAS
summary: Global compilation of more than 3,800 freshwater non-native species from 94 online sources, built by automated extraction, web scraping and manual download.

name: Fundació Assut
summary: Valencian foundation that runs OBEREK, a sensor monitoring project in L'Albufera.

name: Fundació Barcelona Zoo
summary: Zoo foundation whose 2020 report describes in situ research, including 5,800 euros for ICHN wildcat monitoring, a 216-camera-trap network, and the first camera-trap record of an otter on the Besòs.

name: Fundació Catalunya-La Pedrera
summary: Foundation that, according to a February 2021 El Salto article, had absorbed the Fundació Territori i Paisatge, which then owned more than 8,000 ha of high natural value sites in Catalonia.

name: Fundació Emys
summary: Foundation working to protect natural heritage through land custody, mainly of forest, agricultural and wetland areas, and which has restored the rural estate Can Moragues in Riudarenes as its centre.

name: Fundación "la Caixa"
summary: Spanish foundation that funded the Big Mosquito Bytes project of Mosquito Alert.

name: Fundación ANSE
summary: Foundation through which ANSE announced in April 2020 its purchase of the Cabo Cope estates, about 270 ha covering almost all the cape's mountainous land, including regional park and bird protection designations.

name: Fundación BBVA
summary: Foundation of the BBVA bank that supports research in five areas including environment, and runs the Premios Biodiversidad awards and the Prismas y Problemas applied research programme.

name: Fundación Biodiversidad
summary: Spanish foundation of the environment ministry that works to reverse biodiversity loss and funds projects, including a deep-learning wildlife census in Doñana.

name: Fundación CBD-Hábitat
summary: Spanish conservation foundation, winner of a Fundación BBVA biodiversity prize, that works with landowners and follows Iberian lynx with camera traps.

name: Fundación CTIC
summary: Technology foundation in Asturias that lists SCOUT, a non-intrusive wildlife monitoring device using computer vision and machine learning.

name: Fundación Endesa
summary: Endesa's foundation. It offers grants for protecting emblematic species and works with CBD-Hábitat on Iberian lynx monitoring with camera traps.

name: Fundación Enrique Montoliu
summary: Foundation whose main mission, according to a February 2021 El Salto article, was buying estates for conservation, with more than 350 ha acquired, mainly in the Valencian Community and some managed directly.

name: Fundación Global Nature
summary: Spanish foundation running CON-DATA, which recovers decades of its biodiversity records and publishes them through open repositories such as GBIF España.

name: Fundación Internacional para la Restauración de Ecosistemas
summary: Private non-profit ecosystem restoration and conservation foundation with over 20 stewardship agreements, managing about 370 ha at La Nava del Conejo with IRIAF under concession since October 2021.

name: Fundación Laciana Reserva de la Biosfera
summary: Managing entity of the Valle de Laciana Biosphere Reserve, which covers 22,846.67 ha in the municipality of Villablino, León, according to the ministry's reserve page.

name: Fundación Limne
summary: Stewardship body running ecosystem restoration and education activities, with which the Júcar basin authority often works under an agreement to recover riparian forests.

name: Fundación Lurgaia Fundazioa
summary: Land stewardship body that acquires land by donation, purchase or cession agreements, says it manages about 700 hectares, and runs a programme restoring native forests on that land.

name: Fundación Naturaleza y Hombre
summary: Foundation that says it has more than 20 reserves of its own, run with public bodies, and whose work began at the Marisma de Alday wetland.

name: Fundación Oceanogràfic
summary: Foundation involved in satellite tracking of loggerhead turtles, including five turtles to be tracked after release in April 2017, and author of the LIFE IP INTEMARES report on 12 trawl-caught turtles.

name: Fundación Oso Pardo
summary: Spanish NGO working on the Cantabrian brown bear, whose Bear Patrols monitor the species and act against poaching.

name: Fundación para la Conservación del Quebrantahuesos
summary: Spanish foundation that tracks bearded vultures by satellite and publishes each bird's location on a map on its site.

name: Fundación Repsol
summary: Foundation that promotes the Motor Verde reforestation programme with its investee company Sylvestris Group.

name: Future Oceans Lab
summary: Research lab at the University of Vigo and a partner in the CAMBioMed Mediterranean monitoring project.

name: FöcoCyL
summary: Web application that simulates the probability of ignition and the severity of a forest fire and recommends forestry treatments to reduce its impact.

name: Föra Forest Technologies
summary: Forest technology company in Soria offering research and tools for forest management, including the FöcoCyL wildfire simulation application.

name: Galicia remote sensing system for forest harvesting
summary: A Xunta de Galicia system that uses Sentinel images and an algorithm built for Galicia to detect ground changes caused by forest harvesting.

name: GBIF Spain
summary: Spain's national node of the Global Biodiversity Information Facility, a distributed infrastructure with a coordination unit at CSIC that runs the national biodiversity data portal.

name: GBIF Spain Biodiversity Data Portal
summary: National portal through which GBIF Spain shares biodiversity records from Spanish institutions under a common standard.

name: GBIF.ES Biodiversity Data Portal
summary: Spain's national biodiversity data portal, holding records from Spanish data providers under a common standard and open-access licences.

name: Generalitat de Catalunya
summary: Catalonia's regional government, which funds the Catalan Butterfly Monitoring Scheme and whose Fauna Service gave camera-trap images for training PyrVision.

name: GeoAI-Cubes
summary: Spatial and temporal database from several Earth observation sensors, aligned by pixel and labelled with the Land Cover Map of Catalonia, for training AI models.

name: GMV
summary: Space and technology company whose remote sensing division worked on the MySustainableForest project and presented its forest diversity product.

name: Gobierno de Aragón
summary: Regional government whose protected-area pages list the Moncayo natural park decree and an ecological monitoring plan for the Laguna de Gallocanta nature reserve covering 2020 to 2024.

name: Gobierno de Canarias
summary: Regional government that runs BIOCAN, the Biodiversity Service's information system integrating its biodiversity databases, which include BIOTA, the Canary Islands biodiversity data bank.

name: Gobierno de Navarra
summary: Regional government whose website describes the protected areas network (RENA) covering 8% of Navarra, and which approved a management plan for the Montes de la Valdorba conservation area on 22 November 2023.

name: Gobierno Vasco
summary: Regional government of the Basque Country. It runs the Sistema de Información de la Naturaleza de Euskadi, which publishes monitoring datasets through GBIF.

name: Govern de les Illes Balears
summary: Regional government that manages and conserves the Balearic protected natural areas through its Natural Areas Service.

name: GRAFCAN
summary: Canary Islands mapping company that develops AI for territorial analysis, including automatic detection of environmental features and crops from orthophotos.

name: Graniot
summary: Satellite remote sensing company offering services including EUDR deforestation compliance and tree inventories.

name: GreenNet
summary: Project building a multiscale tool to assess ecological connectivity in Cantabrian estuaries, combining numerical modelling, AI and advanced remote sensing.

name: Grumets Research Group
summary: Research group on methods and applications in remote sensing and GIS, coordinated by Xavier Pons of the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona. It develops MiraMon and the SatCat image server.

name: Grup Balear d'Ornitologia i Defensa de la Naturalesa de Menorca
summary: Menorca branch of GOB, seated at the Molí del Rei in Maó, whose agrarian stewardship programme reported over 2,800 ha, 4% of the island, in June 2023.

name: Grup d'Integració d'Observacions de la Biodiversitat
summary: CREAF research group that coordinates, integrates and jointly analyses biodiversity data, mainly in Catalonia and also at European scale.

name: Grup de Recerca en Carnívors de Catalunya (FELIS-ICHN)
summary: Carnivore research group in Catalonia, part of ICHN, that leads the Fototrampeig Mamífers Catalunya camera-trap project.

name: Grupo de Rehabilitación de la Fauna Autóctona y su Hábitat
summary: Spanish wildlife association, founded in 1981, that recovers species and follows populations by telemetry, ringing and nest watching, including GPS tagging of cinereous vultures in its Monachus project.

name: Grupo Sylvestris
summary: Madrid-based forest restoration company founded in 2013 by two forest engineers, which restores burnt areas, brought in Hispasat as technology partner in 2022, and builds Motor Verde.

name: Grupo Tragsa
summary: Spanish public works and technical services group. Its Tragsatec arm helps the environment ministry follow ecosystems with Sentinel imagery, big data and AI.

name: Hisdesat
summary: Owner and operator of the PAZ radar satellite, whose listed uses include environmental control and protection of natural resources.

name: Hispasat
summary: Satellite operator that joined the Repsol Foundation to supply satellite technology to the Motor Verde reforestation programme.

name: Hydro-Forest
summary: University of Vigo research group, set up in June 2024, applying remote sensing and AI to land and freshwater ecosystems.

name: i2CAT
summary: Research centre taking part with IEEC and ICGC in the PCP-WISE use case on water management in southern Europe.

name: IA4BIRDS
summary: Project designing an explainable AI platform to guide environmental planning of future wind farms and protect birds, funded through Fundación Biodiversidad.

name: IAS Tracker
summary: Crowdsourced project with a geoportal and mobile app for reporting locations of invasive alien species.

name: IberArthro
summary: Database of the distribution of Ibero-Balearic arthropods in ten taxonomic groups, with 1,006,768 records on a 10 km grid.

name: IC5Team
summary: Group of five Barcelona researchers in geoinformation who built IAS Tracker, a crowdsourced project to locate invasive alien species. The domain in its GBIF record now carries unrelated content.

name: ICATMAR
summary: Catalan institute for research on governing the sea. It monitors recreational and commercial fishing along the Catalan coast and shares the data through viewers and a repository.

name: ICTIOSCREW
summary: EDP research project using underwater cameras and AI to detect and identify fish at hydroelectric plants in Asturias.

name: ICTS Doñana
summary: Scientific infrastructure that runs environmental and biodiversity monitoring protocols in Doñana, producing time series published in annual reports and fed to LTER-Europe and LifeWatch.

name: Identificació individual d'ossos bruns amb IA al Pirineu
summary: System rolled out by Catalonia's Rural Agents that combines camera-trap images, recognition algorithms and genetic data to follow individual brown bears in the Pyrenees.

name: IFCA Advanced Computing and e-Science
summary: Research computing group that lists iMagine, on AI image analysis for aquatic science, among its projects.

name: IHCantabria
summary: Cantabrian environmental hydraulics institute. Its marine science programme uses AI and machine learning.

name: III Atlas de las Aves
summary: SEO/BirdLife atlas of breeding birds in Spain for 2014 to 2018, with species sheets on habitat, distribution and occupied area.

name: Image Processing Laboratory, Universitat de València
summary: University of València Earth observation laboratory, directed by José Antonio Sobrino since 2023. Its ISP group is already on the global layer.

name: iMagine
summary: Project providing image datasets, AI image analysis tools and best practice documents for aquatic science.

name: Institució Catalana d'Història Natural
summary: Catalan natural history body that runs the FELIS carnivore group and had an agreement with Fundació Barcelona Zoo covering development of the Catalan wildcat monitoring project.

name: Institut Cartogràfic i Geològic de Catalunya
summary: Mapping and geology body of Catalonia. It publishes the Land Cover Map of Catalonia and GeoAI-Cubes, a dataset for training geospatial AI models.

name: Institut Català d'Ornitologia
summary: Catalan bird science NGO whose main activity is monitoring bird populations. It runs the Ornitho.cat portal and the SOCC common bird scheme.

name: Institut d'Estudis Espacials de Catalunya
summary: Catalan space research foundation in the public sector of the Government of Catalonia. It takes part in PCP-WISE on water management from space.

name: Institut de Ciències del Mar
summary: CSIC marine research institute that promotes the MINKA citizen science platform and coordinates the SMART-ME deep-sea monitoring project.

name: Institut Mediterrani d'Estudis Avançats
summary: CSIC and University of the Balearic Islands institute using AI on images to monitor recreational boats and coastal fish.

name: Institute for Cross-Disciplinary Physics and Complex Systems
summary: Joint CSIC and University of the Balearic Islands institute whose researchers developed the CAMELE seagrass mapping model with CEAB-CSIC.

name: Institute for Game and Wildlife Research
summary: Wildlife research institute in Ciudad Real linked to CSIC, the University of Castilla-La Mancha and the regional government. It is a partner in the BIG_PICTURE camera trap project.

name: Institute of Telecommunications and Multimedia Applications
summary: Institute at the Universitat Politècnica de València that developed València-BioSoundScape with the city council and is developing AI models for detecting the city's common bird species.

name: Instituto de Ciencias Marinas de Andalucía
summary: CSIC marine institute whose researchers led a study mapping the seabed from satellite images, tested on Posidonia at Cala Millor.

name: Instituto de Investigaciones Marinas (IIM-CSIC)
summary: CSIC marine research centre, run by the Spanish National Research Council, that leads EMPHATIC's coordination, data collection and development of population-level health indicators.

name: Instituto de Investigación Marina, Universidad de Cádiz
summary: University of Cádiz marine institute whose team built an AI system to detect cetacean whistles in the Strait of Gibraltar from passive acoustic recordings.

name: Instituto de Microelectrónica de Sevilla
summary: Joint centre of CSIC and the University of Seville whose hardware researchers, with the Doñana Biological Station, proposed processing images inside smart camera traps.

name: Instituto Español de Oceanografía
summary: Spanish oceanography institute, now part of CSIC. Its research cruises use the iOBSERVER electronic observer, which identifies catch species with AI.

name: Instituto Geográfico Nacional
summary: Spain's national mapping agency. It is the national reference centre for land cover and use and, with the National Geographic Information Centre, coordinates the National Land Monitoring Plan.

name: Instituto Pirenaico de Ecología
summary: CSIC research institute at Jaca. It publishes FRIAS, a global dataset of freshwater non-native species, and a checklist of freshwater non-native species for Spain.

name: Instituto Tecnológico de Castilla y León
summary: Private technology centre in Burgos. Under RetechFOR it builds autonomous forest robots with computer vision for field data capture and seed dispersal.

name: Instituto Universitario de Investigación en Gestión Forestal Sostenible
summary: University of Valladolid forest management institute based in Palencia, building digital tools and AI for forestry through projects such as Small4Good.

name: Inventario Español del Patrimonio Natural y de la Biodiversidad
summary: The national inventory of Spain's natural heritage and biodiversity, made up of components, a system of indicators and an annual report.

name: Inventario Forestal Continuo de Castilla y León
summary: Digital infrastructure combining satellite images, LiDAR and field data to keep a continually updated picture of forests in Castilla y León.

name: Inventario Forestal Nacional
summary: Spain's continuous national forest inventory, built from repeated field plots with the same measurements repeated every 10 years across the country, published as tables, maps and databases.

name: isardSAT
summary: Partner of Lobelia Earth in the MIREIA project on detecting marine litter with radar and AI.

name: ITAGRA
summary: Agricultural and agri-food technology centre in Palencia that built the AgroForChange land change software.

name: Junta de Andalucía
summary: Andalusia's regional government. Its environmental portal publishes the REDIAM environmental information network, and it forms the Sierra Nevada Global Change Observatory with the University of Granada.

name: Junta de Castilla y León
summary: Regional government of Castilla y León. It coordinates the RetechFOR forest technology network and co-finances tools built under it.

name: Junta de Comunidades de Castilla-La Mancha
summary: Regional government that GBIF's record for IREC names as one of the institute's three founders.

name: Junta de Extremadura
summary: Regional government whose procedure for protected natural areas regulates uses needing authorisation, licence or concession, based on Extremadura's 1998 nature conservation law.

name: Junta Directiva de la Reserva de la Biosfera Valles de Leza, Jubera, Cidacos y Alhama
