summary: Managing entity, regulated by La Rioja Decree 31/2006, of a 121,827.83 ha biosphere reserve in south-east La Rioja, according to the ministry's reserve page.

name: Khaos Research Group
summary: University of Málaga group that built a tool to classify forests from satellite images with AI, within the EnBiC2-Lab project.

name: Kreios Space
summary: Space company in a consortium with Aistech Space and Telespazio Ibérica on detecting forest fires from Very Low Earth Orbit.

name: Laboratory of Applied Bioacoustics
summary: Unit of the Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya that processes acoustic data for environmental monitoring in water and air. It led the LIDO deep-sea listening project and the PROVIDENCE PLUS team in XPRIZE Rainforest.

name: Land Cover Map of Catalonia
summary: Land cover map of Catalonia published by ICGC. The 2022 version was updated by photointerpretation of recent orthophotos, and the 2009 version derives from one prepared by CREAF.

name: LandGriffon
summary: Programme built by Vizzuality and funded by the European Commission that helps companies measure agricultural supply chain impacts using an open scientific methodology and satellite data.

name: Leolia
summary: Technology company at the Asturias Technology Park, founded in 2022, building software for environmental sustainability, including EcoCustodIA algorithms for monitoring.

name: LIFE Agroestepas Ibéricas
summary: EU LIFE project coordinated by SEO/BirdLife to halt the decline of threatened farmland birds, which built an AI tool on thermal drone data to detect nests in crops.

name: LIFE Iberconejo
summary: LIFE project coordinated by WWF on managing European wild rabbit across Iberia, with 15 partners and use of SMART for field monitoring.

name: LIFE IP INTEMARES
summary: Aims at effective management of marine Natura 2000 sites, using research, with a work package covering tagging and remote tracking of 12 accidentally trawled loggerhead turtles.

name: LIFE+Iberlince
summary: Project to recover the historic distribution of the Iberian lynx in Spain and Portugal, whose office advised on and supplied images for Magtel's computer vision system.

name: LifeWatch Alborán
summary: Málaga project that uses big data and AI to gather and analyse data for conserving land and sea ecosystems around the city, co-financed with ERDF funds.

name: Listening to the Deep Ocean Environment
summary: International project led by the Laboratory of Applied Bioacoustics that applies passive acoustic monitoring to cabled deep-sea platforms and moored stations.

name: Loro Parque Fundación
summary: Foundation linked to the Loro Parque zoo in Tenerife that leads work on orca acoustics, including a broadband acoustic buoy tested in Tenerife and deployed near Barbate in 2025.

name: Luce Innovative Technologies
summary: Technology company in Valladolid that built the ForestGPT forest management assistant under RetechFOR.

name: Lynx
summary: Computer vision project to detect, identify and follow individual Iberian lynx automatically in the Guadiamar green corridor, using a camera trap that recognises lynx patterns and sends data to a remote centre.

name: Madrid bird and bat sensor network
summary: Madrid City Council network of 15 AI sensors in Madrid Río and Valdebebas that recognise bird song and bat ultrasound in real time.

name: Magtel
summary: Spanish company whose R&D area built the Lynx project, a computer vision system to detect, identify and follow Iberian lynx in the Guadiamar green corridor.

name: Mammals – Camera Trap Surveys – Spain – MOMAT Project
summary: Camera trap detections of wild and invasive land mammals from more than 1,700 sites across mainland Spain, 2014 to 2026.

name: Mancomunidad de Municipios Sierra de las Nieves
summary: Association of municipalities named by the ministry, with the Andalusian Consejería de Agricultura, Ganadería, Pesca y Desarrollo Sostenible, as managing entity of the 93,227.51 ha Sierra de las Nieves Biosphere Reserve in Málaga.

name: Mancomunidad del Alto Turia
summary: Association of municipalities named by the ministry as managing entity of the Alto Turia Biosphere Reserve, which covers 67,082.36 ha in Valencia and Cuenca.

name: Marilles Foundation
summary: Non-profit foundation that funds marine conservation projects in the Balearics, including a study of sharks by Shark Med.

name: Microsoft and Generalitat de Catalunya AI sustainability projects
summary: Three AI projects on environmental sustainability agreed between Microsoft and the Generalitat de Catalunya, one aimed at monitoring species with the Cos d'Agents Rurals.

name: Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades
summary: Spain's science ministry, which co-governed and part-funded the Plan Complementario de I+D+I en Biodiversidad.

name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico
summary: Spain's environment ministry. It is listed on the Convention on Biological Diversity's country profile for Spain and publishes the national inventory of natural heritage and biodiversity.

name: MINKA
summary: Citizen science infrastructure for biodiversity data where anyone can contribute photographs and sound recordings, launched in 2021 and promoted by ICM-CSIC.

name: MiraMon
summary: Free GIS and remote sensing software developed in Catalonia. CREAF says it has more than 200,000 users in 37 countries and distributes most official Catalan cartography.

name: Miranatura
summary: Camera monitoring specialist named in the Tech4Nature Spain partnership.

name: MIREIA
summary: Lobelia Earth project that tested Synthetic Aperture Radar and AI for detecting plastic litter in marine environments, with isardSAT and the Oceanographic Institute of the Balearic Islands.

name: MOMAT
summary: Monitoring plan for Spain's terrestrial mammals that lack their own programmes, now run with volunteers using camera traps, owl pellets and sign surveys.

name: Mosquito Alert
summary: Citizen science platform that detects invasive mosquitoes from photographs sent by the public, using an AI algorithm to identify species and trigger alerts.

name: Motor Verde
summary: Reforestation programme for offsetting CO2 emissions in Spain, promoted by the Repsol Foundation and Sylvestris Group, using satellite monitoring from Hispasat.

name: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales
summary: Spanish natural history museum that coordinates the national node of DiSSCo, the European infrastructure for natural science collections.

name: Museu de Ciències Naturals de Granollers
summary: Natural sciences museum that coordinates the Catalan Butterfly Monitoring Scheme.

name: MySustainableForest
summary: H2020 project offering forest services based on satellite, statistical, sonic and LiDAR data, including forest condition, biomass and ecosystem vulnerability products.

name: Naturgy
summary: Energy company that built a predictive AI model with NTT Data and Ingecid to protect birds at wind farms.

name: Natusfera
summary: Open platform for biodiversity monitoring inspired by iNaturalist, available in English, Spanish, Catalan, Galician and Basque, whose research-grade observations are published to GBIF.

name: OBEREK
summary: Fundació Assut project in L'Albufera that combines environmental sensors, continuous water quality monitoring and digital platforms.

name: OBSEA
summary: Cabled seafloor observatory 4 km off Vilanova i la Geltrú in a fishing protected area. It sends sensor and camera data to shore in real time.

name: OBSEA fish detector AI model
summary: Open YOLOv8 model trained to detect fish in underwater pictures taken at the OBSEA observatory in the north-west Mediterranean.

name: Observatori del Patrimoni Natural i la Biodiversitat de Catalunya
summary: Official Catalan network that gathers, integrates and shares information on the state of nature. It was created by decree in 2023 and offers distribution and trend viewers.

name: Observatorio de Cambio Global de Sierra Nevada
summary: Observatory created some 20 years ago to study climate change effects on Sierra Nevada's ecosystems. Press reports say it has had no agreement regulating it since November 2024.

name: OCEANSENTINEL
summary: Project using high-resolution coastal cameras and AI to monitor short-finned pilot whales and vessels in the Teno-Rasca Marine Strip Special Area of Conservation off Tenerife, with a public web portal.

name: ODISEC
summary: Project to digitise and standardise monitoring data on red deer, roe deer and red-legged partridge, adapting the LIFE Iberconejo workflow.

name: Organismo Autónomo Parques Nacionales
summary: Spain's national parks agency, which works on the national parks network and leads the monitoring of global change across the parks.

name: Ornitho.cat
summary: Online bird records portal among the web portals of the Institut Català d'Ornitologia.

name: ornitho.eus
summary: Citizen science portal that gathers and shares naturalist records for the Basque Country.

name: Parés&Bosch
summary: GPS specialist named in the Tech4Nature Spain partnership.

name: Patronato de la Reserva de la Biosfera de Urdaibai
summary: Managing entity of the Urdaibai Biosphere Reserve in Bizkaia, which covers 21,774.78 ha of land and 269.24 ha of sea, according to the ministry's reserve page.

name: PETRI-MED
summary: Project developing satellite-based indicators of marine microbial biodiversity in the Mediterranean, using omics and AI.

name: Plan Complementario de I+D+I en Biodiversidad
summary: National research programme, co-governed and co-funded by the science ministry and seven regions, on monitoring biodiversity and assessing global change. It closed in January 2026 after mobilising more than 66 million euros.

name: Plataforma Oceánica de Canarias
summary: Canary Islands ocean platform that has developed tools identifying vessels and cetaceans at sea with AI and real-time alerts, and leads the Teno-Rasca camera monitoring project.

name: PLOME
summary: Project building an underwater platform to monitor marine ecosystems in real time, led by the University of Girona with ICM-CSIC and others.

name: PNOA-LiDAR
summary: Spanish national airborne LiDAR programme covering the whole country in three cycles from 2009 to 2025. The third cover uses AI-based classification, and FAO cites it as an example of open forest data.

name: Portal de Datos Forestales de Castilla y León
summary: Digital platform that brings together forest, environmental and socio-economic data for Castilla y León, with map viewers and reports supported by AI.

name: Principado de Asturias
summary: Regional government whose Consejería de Agroganadería y Recursos Autóctonos the ministry names as managing entity of the Somiedo (29,061.55 ha) and Muniellos (56,948.12 ha) biosphere reserves.

name: Programas de seguimiento de avifauna de SEO/BirdLife
summary: SEO/BirdLife's bird monitoring programmes, in which registered volunteers submit data.

name: Pyrenean bear identification with AI
summary: System in development by the Agents Rurals to identify Pyrenean bears from camera trap images with AI, according to Lleida Diari.

name: PyrVision
summary: Open-source AI model that detects up to 17 kinds of animals, including humans, and motor vehicles in camera-trap images from the Pyrenees.

name: Real Jardín Botánico
summary: CSIC botanical garden and research institute in Madrid, with the MA herbarium. Its Mycology Department is a partner in the FunDive project.

name: Red Cambera
summary: Non-profit association working on nature conservation in Cantabria since 2010, which, according to an October 2019 ministry page, stewards the Camesa river surroundings under a 2014 agreement with the Confederación Hidrográfica del Duero.

name: Red de Información Ambiental de Andalucía
summary: Andalusia's environmental information network, with a data catalogue, satellite observation of the territory and a drought monitoring system.

name: Red de Seguimiento del Cambio Global en la Red de Parques Nacionales
summary: Monitoring network for global change in Spain's national parks, begun by four institutions and set within the monitoring plan of the national parks network.

name: Red de sensores acústicos de biodiversidad de Madrid
summary: Network of 15 acoustic sensors in Madrid Río and the Valdebebas-Felipe VI forest park that identify birds and bats in real time with AI without keeping recordings, with data fed to a digital twin.

name: Red Española de Investigación Ecológica a Largo Plazo (LTER-Spain)
summary: Spanish long-term ecological research network, begun in 2008 and part of ILTER and eLTER, which keeps a monitoring catalogue and lists the Blanes Bay observatory among its nodes.

name: Redeia
summary: Parent of Spain's grid operator Red Eléctrica, which with the Balearic government used 14 underwater robots to monitor Posidonia oceanica meadows.

name: Repsol
summary: Energy company that ran an environmental DNA biodiversity monitoring pilot at Kinteroni in Peru in 2019.

name: RetechFOR
summary: Spanish regional network for forest monitoring and reducing environmental disasters, led by Castilla y León with the Canary Islands. It funds and publishes digital and AI tools for forest management.

name: Rewilding Spain
summary: Rewilding organisation that runs camera trap and transect monitoring in the Iberian Highlands.

name: Ridimoas
summary: Galician association founded in 1988 in O Ribeiro, Ourense, described in a February 2021 El Salto article as the oldest buying estates to protect native forest, owning about 400 ha and managing another 100 ha.

name: SARTI Research Group
summary: Research group at the Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya that builds remote data acquisition and ocean instruments and runs the OBSEA seafloor observatory.

name: SatCat
summary: Catalonia Satellite Image Server, a public bank of Landsat images of Catalonia from 1972 onwards, prepared with MiraMon.

name: SATLANTIS
summary: Earth observation small-satellite company with its headquarters in Spain, offering solutions for sectors including energy and environment.

name: SEAGHOSTS
summary: Project listed in the BiodivMon award resolution as covering storm petrel spatial ecology and conservation across the Mediterranean and North East Atlantic.

name: SEAMPHONI
summary: Horizon Europe project building a smart acoustic platform to monitor the ocean, with 23 partners from 12 European countries.

name: Secretaría de Estado de Digitalización e Inteligencia Artificial
summary: Spanish government office that organised the Soluciones GenAI para la Biodiversidad hackathon under the Programa Nacional de Algoritmos Verdes.

name: Seguiment d'Ocells Comuns a Catalunya
summary: Common bird monitoring programme for Catalonia, promoted by the Institut Català d'Ornitologia and the Catalan government's environment department.

name: SEO/BirdLife
summary: Spain's oldest environmental NGO, founded in 1954. It coordinates the LIFE Agroestepas Ibéricas project, which built an AI tool on thermal drone data to find nests, and the SACRE common bird monitoring programme.

name: Servicios IA
summary: PLOCAN project building AI services for the sea, including identifying vessels and cetaceans and generating real-time alerts.

name: Servidor de Información de Anfibios y Reptiles de España
summary: Online system built by the Asociación Herpetológica Española to follow amphibians and reptiles in Spain and detect biodiversity loss.

name: Silvatech
summary: Digital solution for monitoring forest stands with 3D laser scanning, SLAM and AI, producing three-dimensional models that measure height, diameter, density and biomass.

name: SilvIA Earth
summary: Madrid startup combining Earth observation with a predictive AI model to anticipate wildfire risk for land managers.

name: SIMANFOR
summary: Open and collaborative forest management simulator developed by the University of Valladolid. It combines growth and yield models with optimisation algorithms.

name: Sistema de Información de la Naturaleza de Euskadi
summary: Basque Government system for nature data, rebuilt with search tools, downloads, an API, and publication to GBIF and OpenData Euskadi.

name: Sistema de Información sobre Ocupación del Suelo en España
summary: Spain's national land cover and land use information system, part of the National Land Monitoring Plan.

name: Sistema REMOTE
summary: A semi-automatic system that analyses satellite data to follow ecosystem functioning, such as primary productivity, in Spain's national parks.

name: Smart Ecomountains
summary: Sierra Nevada mountain ecosystems centre tied to LifeWatch, with a work package on deep learning for classifying images of traits, species and ecosystems.

name: SMART-ME
summary: Project funded by Spain's science ministry to set up a permanent, intelligent system for real-time ecological monitoring of the deep Mediterranean, centred on the OBSEA-DEEP observatory at 400 metres off the Catalan margin.

name: SOCEME
summary: Society for the Conservation and Study of Butterflies in Spain, which coordinates a butterfly monitoring network.

name: Sociedad de Ciencias Aranzadi
summary: Non-profit science society in Donostia-San Sebastián. It runs biodiversity monitoring programmes, the ornitho.eus citizen science portal and a bird ringing scheme.

name: Sociedad Española para la Conservación y Estudio de los Mamíferos
summary: Spanish mammal society that publishes open camera trap data from its MOMAT project through GBIF.ES.

name: Sociedad Ibérica de Ictiología
summary: Iberian society for the study of fish. It lists the Carta Piscícola, a knowledge base on the biology and distribution of Iberian fish, among its projects.

name: Sociedade Galega de Historia Natural
summary: Non-profit Galician natural history society founded in 1973. It has counted wintering waterbirds in Galicia every January since 1974.

name: SofiaNet
summary: Planned acoustic monitoring network for cetaceans in the Strait of Gibraltar, promoted by Loro Parque Fundación, with a three-year roadmap.

name: Soluciones GenAI para la Biodiversidad
summary: Generative AI hackathon on biodiversity held in Madrid under Spain's Programa Nacional de Algoritmos Verdes. BioCeltas-IA won, and a third-placed team built an autonomous agent for the environment ministry.

name: Sound Earth Legacy
summary: Organisation that aims to record and preserve earth's sounds that could disappear because of climate change, and helps fund and share knowledge on related scientific projects.

name: Spanish component of the Atlantic Constellation
summary: Eight Spanish Earth observation satellites in the Atlantic Constellation promoted by Spain and Portugal, intended for uses including environmental management and coastal surveillance.

name: Submon
summary: Conservation organisation on the Catalan coast. It uses drones with LiDAR and AI to study interactions between bottlenose dolphins and fishing in the Alt Empordà.

name: SUMHAL
summary: CSIC project co-financed by ERDF within LifeWatch ERIC on the sustainability of Mediterranean biodiversity hotspots in Andalusia.

name: Systems, Robotics & Vision Group
summary: Research group at the University of the Balearic Islands whose site presents the ConBoSer underwater robotics and AI project.

name: TAXUS Medio Ambiente
summary: Environmental company whose genetics laboratory developed eDNA primers and probes for detecting five invasive aquatic species in Iberia, in the invADN project.

name: Tech4Nature Spain
summary: The Spanish part of the IUCN and Huawei Tech4Nature partnership, monitoring eagles, bats and climbers in Sant Llorenç del Munt i l'Obac and visitors and wetlands in Sierra Nevada with cameras, recorders and AI.

name: Telespazio Ibérica
summary: Satellite services company working with the Andalusian government to monitor firebreaks and forest infrastructure with remote sensing and AI.

name: TerraTwin
summary: Horizon Europe project, January 2026 to December 2028, building a digital twin of ecosystems that links marine, land, soil and atmospheric systems using AI and machine learning.

name: Tracasa Global
summary: Company in the WI4EURECA consortium of the PCP-WISE project. Its own site refused the fetcher, so this rests on a consortium notice.

name: TRAGSATEC
summary: Company that designed the MOMAT land mammal monitoring plan with SECEM in 2024 and 2025, as a MITECO commission funded by NextGenerationEU.

name: TropiCam-AI
summary: Algorithm that automatically identifies arboreal mammals and birds in camera trap images from Neotropical forests.

name: Tursiops
summary: Marine research body in the Balearic Islands that studies cetaceans, with photo-identification surveys and hydrophone monitoring of coastal noise.

name: ULTIMATE
summary: Project under Spain's Recovery Plan in which IMSE-CNM and Doñana Biological Station researchers proposed AI for camera traps in places with little communications infrastructure.

name: Universidad Autónoma de Madrid
summary: University where biologist Diego Llusia of CIBC-UAM contributed bioacoustics to the Brazilian Team in XPRIZE Rainforest in June 2023, where AI algorithms classified recordings by species.

name: Universidad de Alicante
summary: University whose Department of Computer Technology and Computation hosts first author David Mulero-Pérez of a 2026 paper on predicting Mediterranean wetland bird observations with deep learning.

name: Universidad de Almería
summary: University credited in the REMOTE user manual for its participation and advice, and linked as a partner of the REMOTE system.

name: Universidad de Cantabria
summary: Spanish university named as coordinator of GreenNet on Fundación Biodiversidad's project page, which develops hybrid methods combining numerical modelling and AI, validated with multispectral sensors.

name: Universidad de Castilla-La Mancha
summary: Spanish university linked to IREC, a joint institute with CSIC and the regional government, whose author led a 2026 paper on how camera height affects camera-trapping rates.

name: Universidad de Cádiz
summary: Spanish university whose Institute of Marine Research is the affiliation of the first author of a 2026 paper on iterative deep learning for detecting cetacean whistles in the Strait of Gibraltar.

name: Universidad de Córdoba
summary: Public university in Spain. It curates the BIRDeep Audio Annotations dataset with the Estación Biológica de Doñana.

name: Universidad de Granada
summary: Spanish university that forms the Sierra Nevada Global Change Observatory with the Andalusian government.

name: Universidad de Huelva
summary: Spanish university that ran the AI-CENSUS deep-learning wildlife census in Doñana National Park.

name: Universidad de La Laguna
summary: Spanish university whose Department of Industrial Engineering is the first author's affiliation on a 2026 paper describing an edge AI pipeline for real-time detection and classification of killer whale vocalisations.

name: Universidad de Málaga
summary: Spanish university named as the research body in the Lynx project, which proposes developing algorithms to detect Iberian lynx in images taken in their habitat.

name: Universidad de Oviedo
summary: Spanish university whose Biodiversity Research Institute, shared with CSIC and the Principality of Asturias, is the first author's affiliation on a 2024 paper applying the random encounter model to camera-trap data.

name: Universidad de Sevilla
summary: Spanish university whose Department of Statistics and Operations Research is the first author's affiliation on a 2023 paper on re-identifying individual undulate skates with few-shot deep learning.

name: Universidad Politécnica de Madrid
summary: Spanish technical university whose Center for Automation and Robotics, shared with CSIC, is the first author's affiliation on a 2023 paper on detecting fin whale pulses with deep neural networks.

name: Universidad Rey Juan Carlos
summary: Spanish university whose Area of Biodiversity and Conservation is the first author's affiliation on a 2023 paper comparing non-invasive DNA sampling and camera trapping in the red fox.

name: Universidade de Santiago de Compostela
summary: Spanish university whose CiTIUS centre is the first author's affiliation on a 2024 paper presenting ResNeTS, a ResNet for Sentinel-2 time series used to predict grassland plant biodiversity.

name: Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona
summary: Its Genetics and Microbiology department is the first author's affiliation on a 2025 metabarcode denoiser benchmarking paper; a 2013 page describes a professor coordinating GRUMETS.

name: Universitat de Barcelona
summary: Spanish university whose Department of Evolutionary Biology, Ecology and Environmental Sciences is the first author's affiliation on a 2023 paper on semi-supervised hidden Markov models for inferring animal behaviour.

name: Universitat de Girona
summary: Spanish university leading the development of autonomous underwater systems for the SMART-ME deep-sea monitoring project.

name: Universitat de les Illes Balears
summary: Spanish university that runs a computer vision and robotics group, whose DETECPOS project (2020 to 2023) planned to automate Posidonia mapping with underwater robotics and deep learning; it is also a SEAGHOSTS beneficiary at 90,750 euros.

name: Universitat de València
summary: Spanish university that runs an Image Processing Laboratory, whose author is first author of a 2025 paper on generative networks for gap filling of Sentinel-2 reflectances.

name: Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya
summary: Technical university in Catalonia, home of the SARTI research group and the OBSEA seafloor observatory.

name: Universitat Politècnica de València
summary: Spanish technical university that runs iTEAM, which developed València-BioSoundScape with Valencia City Council; a 2017 account also describes it helping fit satellite tags to five sea turtles.

name: University of León
summary: Spanish university. Its corvid researchers partner with the Earth Species Project on AI analysis of crow calls, and it is a RetechFOR partner.

name: University of Valladolid
summary: Spanish university that developed SIMANFOR and is a RetechFOR technology partner.

name: Urban Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: Citizen observatory of urban butterflies run from CREAF and listed by the European Butterfly Monitoring Scheme.

name: València-BioSoundScape
summary: Project that monitored bird activity in València's Turia Garden and the Devesa of l'Albufera with acoustic recorders and AI, and built a public platform of species and biodiversity indicators.

name: Vexiza
summary: Spanish company making GIS and emergency management tools. Under RetechFOR it built AI smoke detection for forest surveillance cameras.

name: WWF España
summary: Spanish association in the WWF network, registered in Madrid. It is the beneficiary of ODISEC, a project digitising monitoring of game species.

name: WWF Spain
summary: National WWF organisation in Spain, named as a partner in the AI for European Wildlife Challenge.

name: Xeocode
summary: Galicia's internal fire management platform, which identifies smoke from 241 surveillance cameras with convolutional neural networks.

name: Xunta de Galicia
summary: Galicia's regional government, which has built AI smoke detection on surveillance cameras into its Xeocode fire management platform.

name: Zunibal
summary: Marine technology company in Biscay that makes tools for tropical tuna fisheries and bought the hydroacoustic software company Echoview.

name: A Spatiotemporal Analysis of Poaching Patterns and Human-Elephant Interactions in Babile Elephant Sanctuary, Eastern Ethiopia
summary: Project page dated 17 October 2025 saying it will use GIS and remote sensing to map poaching patterns, and analyse multi-year poaching and elephant movement data for temporal peaks, in Babile Elephant Sanctuary.

name: Adama Science and Technology University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2024 paper on deep learning to identify Ethiopian indigenous medicinal plant species.

name: Addis Ababa Science and Technology University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2022 paper on random forest and support vector machine classifiers for regional land cover mapping.

name: Addis Ababa University
summary: University with the most Ethiopian works since 2021 tagged with both machine learning and ecology in OpenAlex (137), and listed by GBIF as a data publisher in Ethiopia.

name: Africa Centre of Excellence for Water Management
summary: Centre at Addis Ababa University, listed as one affiliation of the first author of a 2026 paper on Bi-LSTM deep learning and Sentinel-2 water quality monitoring.

name: Arba Minch University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2026 paper using explainable machine learning to assess eutrophication in Lakes Ziway and Langano.

name: Arsi University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2026 systematic review of deep learning for monitoring forest dynamics and degradation in Ethiopian agroforestry.

name: AWF wildlife and habitat monitoring in Simien Mountains National Park
summary: Wildlife and habitat monitoring project built by the African Wildlife Foundation in Simien National Park; AWF says 2025 monitoring revealed concerning walia ibex trends, prompting a community data-collection programme.

name: Bahir Dar University
summary: University with authors on OpenAlex-listed papers on machine learning for water quality and Lake Tana water hyacinth, including a 2026 paper on predicting hyacinth expansion.

name: Bale Mountains Ecological Threat Monitoring
summary: Programme run by Frankfurt Zoological Society, partnered with the Ethiopian Wolf Conservation Programme, monitoring key park ecosystem components in wet and dry seasons through counts and surveys.

name: Bale Mountains National Park Operations Room
summary: Operations room using EarthRanger, which Chengeta Wildlife says combines patrol tracking, GPS collars and camera traps in one system in Bale for the first time.

name: Biodiversity and Forestry Programme (BFP)
summary: Closed programme run by the Ethiopian Wildlife Conservation Authority in three phases, 2015 to 2024, commissioned by BMZ; it introduced digital monitoring tools and a digital forest inventory solution.

name: BIOME (Biodiversity Monitoring Ethiopia)
summary: Project run by GIZ that, E.C.O. says, tests technologies and trains staff, setting up a system to monitor large wild animals, vegetation and land use in Nechisar National Park.

name: BioRES (Biodiversity potential for resilient livelihoods in the Lower Omo)
summary: Active project that aims to fill biodiversity data gaps in the Lower Omo by combining scientific monitoring with local knowledge, and donated 53 camera traps to Arba Minch University, which hosted an October 2025 workshop.

name: Collaborative Monitoring for Sustainable Development of Lake Tana UNESCO Biosphere Reserve
summary: Project from 2021 to 2023, budget 20,000 euros, coordinated by Carinthia University of Applied Sciences, that planned to combine Sentinel remote sensing with SMART surveys to monitor water hyacinth.

name: Community Coexistence for Endangered Ethiopian Wolves in the Bale Mountains National Park, with AI-driven Settlement Mapping
summary: Case study using Mask R-CNN, trained on manually annotated satellite imagery, to map settlements in Bale Mountains National Park, reporting a rise from 387 in 2019 to 3,506 in 2024.

name: Community-based wetland ecosystem health assessment for the sustainability of Lake Tana UNESCO Biosphere Reserve
summary: Africa-UniNet lists this Lake Tana wetland health project, involving Carinthia University of Applied Sciences and Bahir Dar University, without marking it completed.

name: Conservation and spatial ecology of Beisa Oryx in Ethiopia
summary: Project run by Melkam Getachew Gebru that aims to study beisa oryx in Awash and Omo National Parks using GPS telemetry, with collars planned for 20 adults.

name: Conservation Status of Endangered Hartebeest and Critically Endangered Black Rhinoceros in Ethiopia
summary: Closed survey that, according to a July 2016 page, planned to use transects, questionnaires, camera traps and pellet counts to check whether hartebeest and black rhinoceros persisted at historical sites near three borders.

name: Conservation-Oriented Mapping and Threat Assessment of the Critically Endangered White-Backed Vulture in the Gambella Region
summary: Project listed by the Rufford Foundation in January 2026, proposing surveys, drone roost monitoring, Landsat and interviews for the first spatially explicit distribution model of white-backed vultures in Agnuak.

name: Debark University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2026 systematic review of AI and remote sensing for freshwater quality monitoring.

name: Debre Berhan University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2026 paper on semi-supervised spatial graph convolutional networks for early detection of soil erosion.

name: Debre Markos University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2025 paper on deep learning to identify indigenous fish species in Lake Tana.

name: Debre Tabor University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2020 review of deep learning methods for land cover and land use classification in remote sensing.

name: Digital community monitoring in the Kafa Biosphere Reserve
summary: Smartphone-based monitoring in which, according to NABU's page, rangers in the Kafa Biosphere Reserve collect forest and biodiversity data monthly, a system the page says is now used across Ethiopia.

name: Dilla University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2026 paper using Google Earth Engine and machine learning to assess vegetation cover change in Nech Sar National Park.

name: Dire Dawa University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2023 paper on machine learning to model forest canopy height and cover in north-western Ethiopia.

name: Distribution, Abundance and Breeding Success of the Critically Endangered Hooded Vulture in Addis Ababa and Surrounding Towns
summary: Closed survey of Critically Endangered hooded vultures in Addis Ababa and nearby towns, which an October 2018 page said would find nests using high-resolution satellite images and assess breeding success with camera traps.

name: EarthRanger in Ethiopia
summary: Project funded by the Darwin Initiative, in which EPIF says it has supported EarthRanger implementation with equipment and EWCA staff training, and is working with EWCA on operations rooms.

name: EBI Spatial Decision Support System
summary: Platform used by the Ethiopian Biodiversity Institute, which runs it, for spatial biodiversity conservation, management and utilisation, built on the GeoNode geospatial content management system.

name: Enhanced Management and Enforcement of Ethiopia's Protected Area Estate
summary: Closed GEF-funded project run by the Ethiopian Wildlife Conservation Authority; 1.5 million hectares came under enhanced management and average METT scores rose from 23.4 to 70.4.

name: Estimating Carbon Footprint, Forest Coverage, and Biomass in Menagesha Suba Forest in Ethiopia using field data and Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI)
summary: Africa-UniNet lists this project, involving BOKU and Bahir Dar University, on estimating carbon, forest cover and biomass in Menagesha Suba Forest using GeoAI, without marking it completed.

name: Ethiopia annual waterbird census
summary: Annual census of waterbirds in Ethiopia; the 2019 count visited 27 wetlands, giving full coverage of the major wetlands, in a report headed Ethiopian Wildlife Conservation Authority.

name: Ethiopia digital wildlife monitoring platform
summary: Platform that ATTA reports is being piloted across 106 protected areas, first deployed in Bale Mountains National Park and Senkele sanctuary, combining satellite data, geospatial tools and unmanned systems.

name: Ethiopia National Forest Monitoring System
summary: System described in a 2014 presentation as including satellite monitoring and a forest inventory designed with 630 sampling units; an FAO summary reports one inventory completed with 539 units.

name: Ethiopian Biodiversity Institute
summary: Institute responsible under national legislation for implementing the biodiversity conventions Ethiopia has joined; it has seven biodiversity centres, two botanical gardens and a duplicate gene bank.

name: Ethiopian Forestry Development
summary: Autonomous federal institution established by Proclamation No. 1263/2021, with duties including compiling information on forest cover and carbon balance, and linked to the SEPAL platform.

name: Ethiopian Wildlife Conservation Authority
summary: Government body responsible for Ethiopia's wildlife, national parks and protected areas, based in Addis Ababa; the Elephant Protection Initiative Foundation says it plans to scale EarthRanger to 20 protected areas by 2030.

name: Ethiopian Wildlife Crime Database System
summary: Active database funded by the US Fish and Wildlife Service, which AWF's 2023 call said was meant to let EWCA collect, collate and analyse Ethiopian wildlife crime data.

name: Ethiopian Wolf Conservation Programme
summary: Conservation programme founded in 1995 and run by the Wildlife Conservation Research Unit, which monitored 41 wolf packs at 17 locations across six populations from April 2024 to March 2025.

name: Forest Fire Early Warning Bulletin
summary: Forest fire bulletin run by Ethiopian Forestry Development, produced three times a week, CIMA says, from RISICO Ethiopia forecasts validated for 2023 to 2024 against 75,961 MODIS hotspots.

name: GBIF Ethiopia
summary: Country node of GBIF with associate participation status, whose head of delegation is listed as Karta Kaske Kalsa.

name: Great Rift Valley Renaissance
summary: Restoration initiative led by WeForest, which says over 23,000 hectares of degraded land are under restoration; the UN recognised it as a World Restoration Flagship on 29 October 2026.

name: Haramaya University
summary: University that OpenAlex lists as the affiliation of the first author of a 2025 paper on machine learning predictions of climate change effects on a near-threatened bird's habitat.

name: Hawassa University
summary: University that OpenAlex lists as the affiliation of the first author of a 2026 paper on cloud-based machine learning to predict land use and land cover change in the Gidabo watershed.

name: Improving Ethiopian Wolf Monitoring
summary: Closed JRS-funded grant ($64,600, 2012 to 2015) run by the Ethiopian Wolf Conservation Programme to improve monitoring data with tablets and training, reported as integrated into its wolf monitoring.

name: Insect Pollinator Diversity under Different Land Uses in and around Kafa Biosphere Reserve and Bale Mountains National Park
summary: JRS-funded Hawassa University project on insect pollinator diversity; the team uploaded over 1,300 occurrence records to GBIF in 2025, and it was entering its final year in January 2026.

name: Jethi Software Development PLC
summary: Space in Africa reports an Axelspace MoU under which Jethi will lead a local satellite data framework and Axelspace will provide data, including for forest conservation.

name: Jimma University
summary: University that OpenAlex lists as the affiliation of the first author of a 2026 paper on machine learning algorithms for land cover image classification in south-west Ethiopia.

name: Jinka University
summary: University that OpenAlex lists as the affiliation of the first author of a 2025 paper on machine learning algorithms for land use and land cover change in the Abelti watershed.

name: Kotebe University of Education
summary: University that OpenAlex lists as the affiliation of the first author of a 2024 paper on machine learning models to assess and project land use and land cover change in the Guder watershed.

name: Landscape Change Tracking System
summary: Digital system built by Wondo Genet College, piloted in 20 woredas in and around Bale with Royal Norwegian Embassy funding; a scale-up workshop was held on 28 March 2026.

name: Mammal and Herpetofauna Diversity of the Gera Forest Priority Area, Ethiopia
summary: Closed survey of mammals and herpetofauna in the Gera Forest, which a February 2014 page said would combine camera traps and live trapping across forest patches until December 2014.

name: Mekdela Amba University
summary: University that OpenAlex lists as the affiliation of the first author of a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis on AI-based prediction of mycorrhizal colonisation in seedlings and afforestation systems.

name: National REDD+ MRV Capacity Consolidation and Strengthening project (Ethiopia)
summary: FAO-led project, supported by the Government of Ethiopia, to strengthen forest emissions monitoring, reporting progress on a National Forest Monitoring System, forest inventory, mapping and change detection.

name: Nechisar National Park
summary: National park in southern Ethiopia, listed by EWCA, which an EWCA officer wrote in 2026 is one of two parks using SMART, and which is the pilot site for planned phased EarthRanger integration.

name: Oromia Forested Landscape Program
summary: Programme under which Ethiopia signed a February 2023 agreement with the BioCarbon Fund ISFL, unlocking up to $40 million, which the World Bank says will be paid for verified emission reductions.

name: Oromia Forested Landscape Program - Emission Reduction Project
summary: Project run by Ethiopian Forestry Development to generate verified emission reductions from reduced deforestation and degradation in Oromia, including an MRV system; active, closing at the end of 2028.

name: Salale University
summary: University that OpenAlex lists as the affiliation of the first author of a 2025 paper on explainable machine learning and cloud-based remote sensing for monitoring terrace degradation and restoration.

name: Shade-Coffee Plantations as Reservoirs of Large Mammal Biodiversity in the Tropical Rain Forest of Ethiopia
summary: Closed study of shade-coffee plantations and large mammals in Ethiopian rain forest, which a September 2016 page said would place 30 infrared camera traps per habitat and verify pellet species by DNA sequencing.

name: Simien Mountains National Park
summary: National park in the Amhara Region, listed by EWCA, which uses the SMART desktop application per a 2026 EWCA officer, has AWF's TRACTS Sites tool deployed, and had EarthRanger training reported in April 2026.

name: SMART in Ethiopian protected areas
summary: Active use of SMART in Ethiopia, where an EWCA officer wrote in April 2026 that only Nechisar and Simien Mountains use the desktop application, and a first SMART Connect attempt was not fully implemented.

name: Space Science and Geospatial Institute
summary: Ethiopian government institute for space science and geospatial work, set up in 2022 by merging two bodies; ENA reports it inaugurated satellite data stations in December 2025, and Fana reports free high-resolution data.

name: Terra-i Ethiopia
summary: Customised for near real-time forest loss warnings in Ethiopia, with a Sentinel-1 alert prototype at 10 m resolution; a 2024 record describes piloting in Bench Maji Zone.

name: University of Gondar
summary: University with a listed 2023 paper, by first author Getahun Sisay, on a neural network and cellular automata model of land use and land cover change in the Goang watershed.

name: Wachemo University
summary: University with a listed 2026 work, by first author Teshale Tirulo, on remote sensing and machine learning for land use and land cover change detection and climate model bias correction.

name: Water and Land Resource Centre
summary: Centre whose site lists research stations, observatories and learning watersheds; it says its Executive Director presented progress on the Ethiopian Basin Information System in July 2026.

name: WeForest Ethiopia reforestation impact assessment (Airbus Foundation)
summary: Active project in which the Airbus Foundation says it has provided satellite imagery and funding to WeForest since 2025 to assess reforestation impact in Ethiopia through machine learning.

name: Wildlife monitoring in Ethiopia. Expanding the national monitoring programme in the Chebera Churchura National Park
summary: 2019 project aiming to roll out the national wildlife monitoring strategy in Chebera Churchura National Park using remote sensing and transects, for client GIZ, adapting a SMART database sheet.

name: Wolaita Sodo University
summary: University with a listed 2026 dataset record, by first author Alefu Chinasho, combining geostatistics and machine learning to predict soil organic carbon in lakeside wetlands of southern Ethiopia.

name: Woldia University
summary: University with a listed 2024 paper, by first author Alemu Eshetu Fentaw, using Google Earth Engine and random forest to map land use and land cover change in the Upper Tekeze basin.

name: Wollega University
summary: University with a listed 2026 paper, by first author Gedefa Adugna Tamene, using machine learning to predict forest cover change and carbon stock under the Green Legacy Initiative.

name: Wollo University
summary: University with a listed 2020 paper, by first author Abebe Mohammed Ali, using machine learning to retrieve plant traits of a mixed mountain forest from Sentinel-2 data.

name: Wondo Genet College of Forestry and Natural Resources
summary: Founding college of Hawassa University with GIS, remote sensing and drone equipment, which has served as a national MRV capacity centre and organised training for 15 experts in Oromia.

name: Aalto University
summary: University whose listed connections include a remote sensing review co-authored by Miina Rautiainen, coordination of the ESA BIC Finland programme (per its Startup Center page), and a water and environmental engineering group hosting Digital Waters.

name: Aalto University Remote Sensing Research Team
summary: A research team focused on methods for monitoring vegetation from space, which lists ARTISDIG among its projects, with Rautiainen as principal investigator of the Research Council of Finland funding for 2022 to 2024.

name: Advances in Soil Information
summary: Closed project that was part of the Catch the Carbon climate action programme, led by Natural Resources Institute Finland and funded by the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry.

name: AI Vesi360
summary: Completed project, listed as running from 2018 to 2025, that studied AI in the water sector for forecasting and counselling, and automatic categorising of citizen observations from images.

name: ALFAwetlands
summary: Project whose work package 1, according to a Natural Resources Institute Finland release, developed a machine learning approach for mapping land use and land cover from satellite imagery.

name: Alg@line
summary: Syke-led monitoring network, which Syke says has operated for over thirty years, with ferryboxes on ships collecting seawater data automatically.

name: Anicare
summary: Organisation based in Oulu that makes NanoTrack devices for tracking the location and behaviour of wild and domestic animals.

name: Aquaspace Finland
summary: Consortium led by Sitowise, with Aalto University, University of Turku, National Land Survey and Finnish Meteorological Institute as partners, selected as one of five consortia for the first phase of PCP WISE.

name: Archipelago Research Institute
summary: Research institute that has monitored the environment and marine conditions on Seili Island since 1966, producing datasets over 50 years long, including seawater and plankton time series; run by the University of Turku.

name: Arctic Space Centre
summary: Programme run by the Finnish Meteorological Institute that focuses on calibration and validation of Earth observation satellite data.

name: ARTISDIG
summary: Closed project, run from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2024, that aimed to monitor boreal forests by applying AI-based algorithms to satellite data, led by VTT and funded by the Research Council of Finland.

name: Assessing the success of peatland restoration (SOINTU)
summary: Active University of Oulu project, led by Aleksi Räsänen, that develops satellite image analysis methods for post-restoration change and will analyse monitoring data with supervised machine learning.

name: AUTOGAME
summary: Closed project, run by and funded by Natural Resources Institute Finland, that aimed to develop game camera trapping protocols and analysis tools for large image data sets.

name: Baltic Sea Action Group
summary: Ran SAARI water quality mapping in the Gullkrona marine protected area with Pro Litore in 2023–2024, and partners with BiodiverSea LIFE IP.

name: BiodiLogDef
summary: Project run and led by the University of Eastern Finland, funded by Business Finland, that aims to improve measurement of forest biodiversity indicators using sensors and AI, with several research and company partners.

name: Biodiversea LIFE IP
summary: Project running from 2021 to 2029, led by Metsähallitus with ministry, Syke and Natural Resources Institute Finland partners, which uses VELMU.

name: BioSounds
summary: Proposed eighteen-month project, from 1 December 2026, led by Otso Ovaskainen and funded by the European Research Council, to develop AI-based real-time acoustic monitoring, with a goal of a network in 20 Madagascar national parks.

name: BirdLife Finland
summary: National bird conservation and birdwatching organisation, part of BirdLife International, whose 2025 annual report says it carried out national bird monitoring with the Finnish Museum of Natural History and continued its eagle transmitter tracking project.

name: BitApps
summary: Organisation whose platform combines GIS and AI services with web and mobile solutions, and which builds WoodsApp as the first solution on that platform.

name: Business Finland
summary: Funding body that gave BiodiLogDef over 2.7 million euros in Co-Innovation funding and, it says, funded CollectiveCrunch through its New Space Economy programme.

name: Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment
summary: Bodies of unknown status that Metsähallitus says use its Uljas protected area systems.

name: City of Espoo
summary: City authority whose environmental protection service maintains several nature spatial datasets, mostly open to view on its WFS interface, and which introduced a nature information system in 2024-2025.

name: City of Helsinki
summary: City authority that tested AI on satellite data in summer 2025 to identify overgrown lawns and invasive plants, and has used Crowdsorsa since 2024.

name: City of Hämeenlinna
summary: The city owns about 5,800 hectares of forest, about 600 classed as protected, with reserves including Sibelius's forest at Aulanko (2018) and Annala (2019).

name: City of Jyväskylä
summary: A city that owns nature reserves protected under section 24 of the Nature Conservation Act on its own land, totalling 118.6 hectares.

name: City of Kouvola
summary: A city whose technical board approved a proposal in September 2020 to protect about 2.4 hectares, which the city said would bring the protected share of its forests to about six per cent.

name: City of Kuopio
summary: A city owning about 780 hectares of nature reserves, sharing ownership of the Puijo reserves, with other major protected old forests at Kolmisoppi-Neulamäki (230 ha) and Vanuvuori (125 ha), both in Natura 2000.

name: City of Lappeenranta
summary: A city whose strategy aims to set up new nature reserves on its land, with a reserve on Naurissaari in preparation alongside existing ones such as Hämmäauteensuo, Pappilanniemi, Tiuruniemi and Uus-Lavola.

name: City of Oulu
summary: A city that reported in June 2024 that the North Ostrobothnia ELY Centre had approved its application for a 24.22-hectare private nature reserve at Tuppisuo in Muhos, which would add to protected city-owned land and waters.

name: City of Porvoo
summary: In October 2026 the city reported Uusimaa's regional centre established Virvik at its request, its largest reserve on city land, raising protected city forest to about 11%.

name: City of Raasepori
summary: A city whose page on its forests and waters gives about 4,350 hectares of city forest and reports 260 hectares of statutory nature reserves.

name: City of Rovaniemi
summary: In 2024 the Lapland ELY Centre decided to establish Pöyliöjärvi reserve on the city's 55.24-hectare Erkkilä property, and the city lists about 300 forest hectares protected from forestry operations.

name: City of Tampere
summary: A city that at the end of 2025 owned 29 of Tampere's 62 nature reserves, the other 33 being private, and whose 2026–2040 programme identifies further city-owned land and water areas for protection.

name: City of Turku
summary: In November 2026 the city reported preparing its first reserve programme (2026–2038), proposing 39 sites covering about 1,060 hectares within Turku, where 18 statutory reserves cover 603 hectares.

name: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Laboratory
summary: Active laboratory run by LUT University, working on Saimaa ringed seal re-identification and plankton recognition, whose researchers construct a neural network to recognise individual seals.

name: Conservation Biology Informatics
summary: University of Helsinki group led by Heini Kujala that develops methods and software for conservation and land use planning and developed the Zonation spatial planning software.

name: Crowdsorsa
summary: Tampere-based start-up, according to the City of Helsinki, whose game has been used in seven countries and in which players search for invasive species on a map.

name: Digital Geography Lab
summary: Active laboratory run by the University of Helsinki that develops spatial analysis frameworks combined with machine learning; one project proposed using social media data to study illegal wildlife trade.

name: Digital Waters Flagship
summary: Active programme running 2024 to 2030 according to Syke, led by the University of Oulu and funded by the Research Council of Finland, aiming to secure water resources with digital twins.

name: EarthCape
summary: Organisation of unknown status offering a biodiversity database platform and collection management for research groups and natural history museums, with an address in Helsinki.

name: eDNA-monitor
summary: Closed project listed as running 2022 to 2024, aimed at testing, developing and validating DNA methods for assessing water status and species diversity, and using Hertta.

name: eDNA-tiekartta
summary: Closed project listed as running from 2021 to 2022, whose result is a national roadmap.

name: EnVision
summary: Completed project, 2017 to 2018, led by Jari Silander, that aimed to evaluate machine vision with drones for identifying species and listed deep learning among its methods.

name: ESA Phi-Lab Finland
summary: Active programme offering 4.4 million euros of funding between 2025 and 2030, with seed funding of 200,000 to 500,000 euros for each selected project.

name: ESA/FMI Arctic-Boreal Earth Observation Supersite
summary: Active programme launched by ESA and FMI at Sodankylä, built by both, aiming to provide reference data to validate satellite sensors.

name: Etelä-Karjalan virkistysaluesäätiö
summary: A foundation that bought about 32 hectares along the Hiitolanjoki river and took ownership of its power plants in 2017 to 2019, allowing generation to stop, dams to be removed and the river to reopen to Ladoga salmon and trout.

name: European Forest Institute
summary: Active organisation that says it brings science, policy, practice and society together on forests; its EFINET report describes a neural network used to predict forest height metrics.

name: FAO and Finland forest resources and data management project
summary: Project of unknown status: a January 2022 report says FAO and Finland signed an agreement on forest resources and data management, especially in Africa, with an initial 2.3 million dollars toward a planned 7 million dollar, four-year project.

name: FASTVISION-plus
summary: Completed project, 2021 to 2025, led by Sanna Suikkanen and run by the Finnish Environment Institute, that aimed to develop plankton species recognition using automated imaging devices and machine learning.

name: FEO RI
summary: Active programme led by the Finnish Environment Institute and Natural Resources Institute Finland, building on the Finnish Ecosystem Observatory, with Syke describing its goal as a digital research and monitoring infrastructure.

name: FinBIF-FIRI2021
summary: Active project running 2022 to 2026, led by the Finnish Environment Institute, applying AI to enrich FinBIF data and offer automated species identification from DNA, image or sound data.

name: FINMARI
summary: Active programme that describes itself as a distributed interdisciplinary marine research infrastructure, with tools including research vessels, gliders and Argo floats.

name: Finnish Biodiversity Information Facility
summary: Run by Luomus, it was established in 2012 according to Syke and reported about 47,000 species and 50 million occurrence records in its CoreTrustSeal application.

name: Finnish bird sound identification model
summary: Active model built by the University of Jyväskylä on the BirdNET neural network, which knows 263 Finnish bird species and is also used in the Muuttolintujen Kevät app.

name: Finnish Breeding Bird Atlas
summary: Closed fourth Finnish bird atlas (2022–2025) that aimed to record bird distribution and breeding certainty across 3,859 ten-kilometre squares, taking observations through the Finnish Biodiversity Information Facility's and BirdLife Finland's services.

name: Finnish Cultural Foundation
summary: Active organisation that funds VesiMon together with the Ministry of the Environment.

name: Finnish Ecosystem Observatory
summary: Closed project, 2020 to 2024, led by Peter Kullberg, that assessed biodiversity and ecosystem monitoring in Finland, including remote sensing and eDNA methods.

name: Finnish Forest Centre
summary: Says it collects and shares forest information and monitors forest laws; a staff member reported six-year nationwide inventories to Esri, and it partners with KOKO Forest.

name: Finnish Geospatial Research Institute
summary: Research and expert institute for spatial data infrastructures, run by the National Land Survey of Finland, named as a BiodiLogDef research partner; deep learning on dense laser scanning identified nine tree species at 92% average accuracy.

name: Finnish Lepidopterological Society
summary: Society that coordinates the National Butterfly Survey of Finland and publishes its annual results in the journal Baptria.

name: Finnish Long-Term Ecosystem and Socio-Ecological Research
summary: Programme that brings Finnish research sites and scientists into one coordinated research infrastructure, and partners with the International Long-Term Ecological Research Network.

name: Finnish Meteorological Institute
summary: Meteorological institute whose Arctic Space Centre is described as Finland's primary infrastructure for Earth observation data use, calibration and validation, and which has an extensive monitoring network according to ICOS Finland.

name: Finnish Museum of Natural History
summary: Independent research institution under the University of Helsinki, responsible for national natural history collections, and it coordinates most Finnish bird monitoring with BirdLife Suomi.

name: Finnish national moth monitoring scheme
summary: Active moth monitoring scheme, part of the Finnish Biodiversity Research Programme and coordinated by the Finnish Environment Institute, which gives quick information about environmental change.

name: Finnish Nature Information Hub
summary: Website, built by the Finnish Ecosystem Observatory, which Syke says gives an overview of Finland's biodiversity and ecosystem monitoring, alongside other data services.

name: Finnish peatland site type dataset
summary: Dataset covering all Finnish peatlands, funded by the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry and using CSC, that classifies site type, fertility and land use at 10 by 10 metre pixels using machine learning and remote sensing.

name: Finnish Wildlife Agency
summary: Independent public-law institution established in 2011 that runs and builds Oma riista, and is responsible for maintaining it.

name: Fishheart
summary: Its fishway, created in Lapland in 2016, uses AI for fish detection and real-time imaging; four Fishheart units and one Satelliteheart unit operated in summer 2025.

name: Forestry Thematic Exploitation Platform
summary: Online cloud service built by VTT that turns satellite and other data into maps, with VTT saying it uses machine learning algorithms, and it partners with the European Space Agency.

name: Forgis Oy
summary: Company that, according to PEFC, led a project supported by its 2014 Collaboration Fund to develop an online platform monitoring sustainable forest management in Finland using open-source satellite imagery.

name: Forum Virium Helsinki
summary: Describes itself as the City of Helsinki's innovation company, and says it made the Helsinki AI and satellite data pilot of summer 2025 possible.

name: GBIF Finland
summary: Programme under which GBIF lists Finland as a voting participant, partnering with the Global Biodiversity Information Facility and led by Will Morris.

name: Geological Survey of Finland
summary: Research institution governed by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment, which published news of Finland's first nationwide open spatial dataset on peatland site types.

name: Global Ecosystem Health Observatory
summary: Interdisciplinary research team, led by Samuli Junttila, that develops remote sensing algorithms for forest health and maps global tree mortality.

name: Government of Åland
summary: Regional government responsible for supervising and managing Åland's nature reserves, which has drafted a decision and management plan for a Storskär-Kalhära reserve in Kökar and partners with BiodiverSea LIFE IP.

name: Helsinki Lab of Interdisciplinary Conservation Science
summary: A University of Helsinki team spanning conservation and computer science; a February 2023 article reports university scientists trained 24 neural-net models to identify online wildlife trade.

name: Hertta
summary: Open database run by the Finnish Environment Institute, which Syke describes as its own.

name: Husö biological station
summary: Åbo Akademi University station at Bergö in the Åland Islands that holds long-term databases on marine environmental change.

name: Hydrology LIFE
summary: Closed project that ran from 2017 to 2023, in which the University of Oulu developed drone monitoring methods.

name: IBC-Carbon
summary: Closed project, 2018 to 2023, led by Martin Forsius and funded by the Strategic Research Council, aiming to produce forest value information from modelling and varied data.

name: ICOS Finland
summary: Programme of 18 stations studying boreal ecosystems, focused on coniferous forests and peatlands, partnering with the University of Helsinki and the Finnish Meteorological Institute.

name: Indufor
summary: Uses its Dwell platform, remote sensing and AI for satellite-based monitoring of forest and land-use change, and says governments, industry and investors use it.

name: Jamk University of Applied Sciences
summary: A university of applied sciences that will develop an energy management solution for BioSounds equipment.

name: Jane and Aatos Erkko Foundation
summary: A foundation named by the University of Jyväskylä as a funder of Muuttolintujen kevät, which awarded 2.44 million euros to the Research Centre for Ecological Change for 2023 to 2027.

name: Jurmon osakaskunta
summary: A shareholder body of Jurmo which, Baltic Sea Action Group reported in October 2026, decided to enter a three-year agreement with the Southwest Finland regional centre to protect more than 23,000 hectares of sea around Jurmo.

name: Kasviatlas
summary: Plant distribution atlas based on the Kastikka database, begun in the mid-1960s, which held about 7.8 million plant observations by October 2022, with maps online since 2007.

name: Kelluu
summary: A Joensuu-based Finnish company that, per a 2023 AgEagle release, operates autonomous airships for environmental and infrastructure monitoring, and says researchers used one to study forest damage in Koli national park.

name: Kerttu
summary: An app for which a January 2021 release describes birdwatchers producing machine learning teaching material, built by the Finnish Museum of Natural History and LifePlan, in partnership with BirdLife Finland.

name: Kevo Subarctic Research Station
summary: Research station, run by the University of Turku, that combines long-term environmental monitoring and mapping with experiments, including monitoring of environmental change and reindeer grazing effects.

name: Kilpisjärvi Biological Station
summary: Biological station with its own long-term monitoring, including a rodent scheme running annually since 1946 and bird counts along four line transects every year since 1979.

name: KOKO Forest
summary: A company that started operating in spring 2023, using satellite imagery, AI and remote sensing to monitor forest health, and offering geospatial estimates of Nature Value Hectares.

name: Kone Foundation
summary: A Helsinki foundation awarding grants for academic research and the arts and funding Zonation, which reports awarding over EUR 66 million in 2025.

name: Korkeasaari Zoo
summary: A zoo that monitors bird populations on its island year-round, uses a zoological information management system, and partners with LIFEline4Fennicus.

name: Kuopio Natural History Museum
summary: A natural history museum whose collections are being digitised into FinBIF.

name: Kuopion Luonnon Ystäväin Yhdistys
summary: An association that owns land at the summit of Pisa in Nilsiä, at Korkeakoski in Maaninka, and at Kokkokallio and Tyyrinvuori in Rautalampi.

name: Kuusinkijoki kuntoon ry
summary: An association that has started a project on the Kuusinkijoki river in Kuusamo to free the trout's route to spawning areas above the Myllykoski power station, and keeps raising funds for the work.

name: Kuva Space and Syke algae monitoring pilot
summary: A pilot announced by Kuva Space in July 2025 to test hyperspectral satellite data and AI on algae blooms in Finnish lakes and coastal waters, with Kuva Space and Syke developing the models.

name: LajiGIS
summary: A national species information database used by the environmental authorities and run by Metsähallitus.

name: Lammi Biological Station
summary: Biological station whose six MONIMET cameras have photographed the same locations every 30 minutes since 2013, with all images freely available.

name: Lapland Regional Council
summary: A regional council named as a co-funder of NorthDIVeRSITY.

name: Lauhanvuori – Hämeenkangas Geopark ry
summary: An association that administers the Lauhanvuori–Hämeenkangas UNESCO Global Geopark, working with Metsähallitus, the Natural Resources Institute Finland and member businesses and associations.

name: LIFEline4Fennicus
summary: An EU-funded project led by Metsähallitus that will develop an AI-based tool to process a growing number of images, with monitoring overseen by the Natural Resources Institute Finland.

name: Linda Forest
summary: An AI platform for predicting forest inventory, as described in a 2019 Metsähallitus release.

name: Linda Planet
summary: A biodiversity and carbon tracking tool launched in April 2023, built by CollectiveCrunch.

name: Long-term bird breeding time-series (UTUBirds)
summary: Active long-term bird breeding dataset run by the University of Turku, with time series starting in the 1940s and a plan for a new multiuser database.

name: Luonnonperintösäätiö
summary: A foundation that had nearly 200 nature reserves covering more than 5,000 hectares at the end of 2023.

name: Luonnontila
summary: A system for disseminating information on the state and development of biodiversity in Finland, run and built by the Finnish Environment Institute.

name: Luontoa
summary: A Finnish biodiversity consultancy working on nature-based solutions and biodiversity markets, which says it helps companies understand their biodiversity impact and partners with CollectiveCrunch and Koko Forest.

name: Lupa- ja valvontavirasto
summary: National agency created by Finland's 2026 reform to gather state permit, guidance and supervision tasks; the City of Helsinki says it approves nature reserve management and use plans.

name: LUT University
summary: A university in Lappeenranta whose computer vision group has worked on Saimaa ringed seal identification since 2015, and which Syke credits in the FASTVISION-plus consortium.

name: Maa- ja vesitekniikan tuki ry
summary: An organisation that Syke says made it possible to start the AI Vesi360 work.

name: Maj and Tor Nessling Foundation
summary: Foundation that mainly funds solution-oriented environmental protection research, and granted EUR 95,485 to Mariana Verdonen's postdoctoral project on multisensor permafrost mapping in palsa mires.

name: Metsä Group
summary: A forest industry group partnering with CollectiveCrunch, whose nature value map for owner-members calculates biodiversity value for 16 by 16 metre squares.

name: Metsä Group nature value map
summary: A map built by Metsä Group, based on open spatial data, that calculates biodiversity value by 16 by 16 metre grid square within its Metsäverkko service for owner-members.

name: Metsähallitus
summary: A state-owned enterprise managing state land and water across Finland, including most conservation areas, and training staff in AI.

name: Metsäliike
summary: An organisation running forest watch activity over natural forests threatened by logging, where watchers follow logging notifications and satellite images remotely and visit forests.

name: Metsään.fi
summary: A portal run and built by the Finnish Forest Centre that gives open access to government forest inventory data, updated from laser scanning, aerial photography, plot measurements and site visits.

name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland
summary: A ministry whose March 2026 release cites an evaluation finding 6.7 million hectares of forest protected, restored or sustainably managed in 2010 to 2024 with Finnish support, with biodiversity objectives included only from 2023.

name: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry of Finland
summary: A ministry that funded the MaaTi project behind the peatland site type dataset, and, according to Copernicus, the Government's logging detection project, and funds the 2025 to 2028 individual tree data project.

name: Ministry of the Environment (Finland)
summary: A ministry hosting Finland's primary national focal point for the Convention on Biological Diversity, which funds Zonation and uses Metsähallitus's Uljas protected area systems, according to Metsähallitus.

name: Mittausguru
summary: An organisation providing real-time environmental monitoring for industrial and research uses, with off-grid stations measuring water flow, quality, ground and weather conditions.

name: ML4DRONE
summary: A project proposing a methodology that combines drones, hyperspectral imaging and machine learning for forest health monitoring.

name: MONIMET
summary: Camera network across Finland maintained by four institutes, run by the Finnish Meteorological Institute, the Finnish Environment Institute and the University of Helsinki, with images accessible online.

name: MONITOR 2020
summary: A closed programme, led by the Finnish Environment Institute, that set targets for gathering, storing and using environmental data up to 2020.

name: Multi-Source National Forest Inventory of Finland
summary: A forest inventory dataset offered under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, with a product for the year 2023 published on 22 October 2025.

name: Multifolia
summary: A project run by the Natural Resources Institute Finland that combines drone and satellite data with AI-driven analysis to build a 3D replica of forest ecosystems.

name: Multisensor mapping of permafrost in North European palsa mires
summary: An active project funded by the Nessling Foundation uses multisensor remote sensing and field data to model palsa mire dynamics and aims to develop monitoring methods supporting conservation.

name: Muuttolintujen kevät
summary: A mobile app built by the University of Jyväskylä that records bird song and uses AI to identify 263 Finnish species, reported in April 2025 as downloaded over 300,000 times in Finland.

name: National Butterfly Survey of Finland
summary: Research project coordinated and run by the Finnish Lepidopterological Society, with observations recorded in the Finnish Museum of Natural History's database.

name: National Forest Inventory of Finland
summary: A forest inventory in Finland, conducted since the 1920s, which one April 2017 description says measured almost 60,000 sample plots and 500,000 trees on forestry land over five years.

name: National Land Survey of Finland
summary: Carries out national laser scanning and aerial photography and announced a joint 2025 to 2028 project with the Finnish Forest Centre on individual-tree forest data using AI.

name: Natural Resources Institute Finland
summary: A Finnish renewable natural resources research organisation running Multifolia and Autogame, deriving forest statistics from the National Forest Inventory, and reporting environmental DNA capabilities from sampling to genetic analysis.

name: Networked Environmental Monitoring and Evaluation System for Intelligent Surveillance
summary: A project running from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2028, led by Turku University of Applied Sciences, that combines land and sea sensors, autonomous platforms and a data hub across the Archipelago Sea.

name: NORPPA
summary: A method for identifying seals from their pelage pattern, extracted with a U-net encoder-decoder, using content-based image retrieval, and built by Ekaterina Nepovinnykh.

name: Norppagalleria
summary: A photo dataset, built by WWF Finland and run by the University of Eastern Finland, mostly from researchers' trail cameras, in which fur patterns identify individual Saimaa ringed seals.

name: Norppalive
summary: A live camera on the Saimaa ringed seal, run by WWF Finland.

name: NorthDIVeRSITY
summary: A project led by Natural Resources Institute Finland, funded by UPM and Lapland Regional Council, developing eDNA tools for monitoring fish and forest species.

name: Novia University of Applied Sciences
summary: University of applied sciences listed as Stefan Heinänen's affiliation in a 2020 paper on satellite telemetry and aerial surveys of red-throated divers near offshore wind farms.

name: Oma riista
summary: A service run and built by the Finnish Wildlife Agency whose field app records catch and observations; AI identification of game animals is a future vision, not yet in place.

name: Oulanka Research Station
summary: Run by the University of Oulu in Kuusamo, it monitors climate and environmental change; decades of monitoring data helped it join the eLTER network.

name: Our Saimaa Seal LIFE
summary: A closed project led by Metsähallitus during September 2020–December 2025, costing 6.96 million euros, that developed population monitoring and photographic identification of individual seals.

name: PEAT-GENIE
summary: A project led by the Geological Survey of Finland during September 2026–August 2030, planning AI-based predictive models, two generative AI interfaces and extended digital twin components for peatlands.

name: Peatland site type dataset of Finland
summary: Finland's first nationwide open spatial dataset on peatland site types, classified at 10 by 10 metre pixels, with accuracy improved by combining remote sensing data and machine learning.

name: Pohjois-Karjalan biosfäärialue
summary: A biosphere reserve administered by the Ministry of the Environment and the Eastern Finland regional centre, with the North Karelia ELY Centre identified on the page as the former local centre.

name: Pohjolan Voima
summary: Has used the Fishheart fishway at Raasakka on the Iijoki River since 2023, saying it supports its efforts to promote biodiversity.

name: Priodiversity LIFE
summary: An ongoing project led by Metsähallitus, listed as running from 2024 to 2031, that develops monitoring methods including remote sensing and environmental DNA with several Finnish partners.

name: Pro Litore
summary: Organisation that carried out the SAARI water quality measurements using the Coastrider method, an automatic moving system that needs no samples.

name: Puro Analytics
summary: A Finnish organisation, based at Otakaari 7, that offers eDNA-based biodiversity tracking and reporting.

name: Päijänteen Luonnonperintösäätiö
summary: A foundation that reported in December 2014 buying its fourth protected area, the 26-hectare Kuminansalo farm on Kumina island in Korpilahti, Jyväskylä, on Lake Päijänne.

name: REC database
summary: A collection of datasets with long-term species observations, built and run by the Research Centre for Ecological Change, for the exclusive use of its researchers.

name: Remote sensing Northern Lapland
summary: A closed project run by Metsähallitus and the Finnish Environment Institute that surveyed nearly three million hectares in 2020 to 2023, with AI that Metsähallitus says was trained to identify habitat types.

name: Replacing human eye with AI
summary: A closed project run by Natural Resources Institute Finland from December 2020 to December 2022, funded by the Ministry of Finance, on automating monitoring of migratory fish, seals, white-tailed deer and large carnivores.

name: Research Centre for Ecological Change
summary: A centre established in 2018 to coordinate analysis of long-term ecological data, run by the University of Helsinki and funded by the Jane and Aatos Erkko Foundation.

name: Research Council of Finland
summary: Described by Digital Waters as a Finnish education ministry agency, funds all research fields and 2026–2031 biodiversity digital twinning, with its renaming announced in June 2023.

name: RESONATE
summary: Project running from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027 that aims to combine remote sensing and AI to monitor forest tree mortality precisely, led by the Natural Resources Institute Finland.

name: Riistakolmiot
summary: Finnish wildlife triangle count pages reporting summer, winter and Upper Lapland willow grouse results, nationally and by game management area, with 2026 hare, squirrel and fox track densities nearly halved.

name: SAARI
summary: Closed project, run by the Baltic Sea Action Group and Pro Litore, that measured water quality at about 3,000 points in 2023 and 2024 using the automatic, moving Coastrider method.

name: Saimaa Geopark ry
summary: An association whose stated mission is to look after the geology, nature and culture of the Saimaa Geopark area, a UNESCO Global Geopark since spring 2021.

name: SALMUS
summary: Closed project, implemented from 2019 to 2022, that used eDNA in river water samples to detect the mussel.

name: Satelliittilinnut
