summary: Programme run by the Finnish Museum of Natural History, offering a public platform to follow bird tracking projects that use satellite transmitters and other positioning devices.

name: Seeing Biodiversity from Space
summary: Active project that aims to develop a biodiversity monitoring method combining aerial imagery, very-high-resolution satellite data, laser scanning and field observations with AI and machine learning, built by Luontoa and KOKO Forest.

name: Simsonar
summary: Oulu company founded in 2009 that develops fish surveillance technology using machine learning, computer vision and cloud computing, with government agencies and research institutions among its customers.

name: SingleTree
summary: Active project that uses data capture and AI to monitor individual tree attributes, health and biodiversity, with KOKO Forest, Kelluu and the University of Eastern Finland as partners.

name: Sitowise
summary: Nordic technical consulting and digital solutions company that offers the Foresta forest management system, and whose presentation refers to an AI-based forest growth model it developed.

name: Skärgårdshavets Biosfärområde
summary: The Archipelago Sea biosphere reserve has an office managed by the city of Pargas, the municipality of Kimitoön and the Southwest Finland ELY Centre, with a steering group responsible for planning and carrying out its activities.

name: Snowchange Cooperative
summary: Finland-based non-profit with members across the Arctic, reported to own 8,500 hectares of recovering lands and leading the Landscape Rewilding Programme, where each site is to be inventoried.

name: Spectral Imaging Laboratory
summary: University of Jyväskylä laboratory, led by Ilkka Pölönen, that combines hyperspectral imaging with modelling, simulation and machine learning and publishes open spectral data on Zenodo.

name: SPORELIFE
summary: Active project, funded by the Research Council of Finland, that develops airborne DNA methods and automated spore recognition instruments for monitoring.

name: SpringDNA
summary: Helsinki-based company that says it offers biodiversity detection and monitoring using environmental DNA, and that regular sampling enables long-term ecosystem monitoring.

name: Stora Enso
summary: Company whose Precision Forestry project, according to Forest.fi, uses AI to identify insect damage and remains in an observational phase.

name: Strategic Research Council
summary: Body whose granted funding is reported in the Research Council of Finland's dashboards.

name: Suomen luonnonsuojeluliiton Pirkanmaan piiri
summary: The district says it honoured Aili Kyllikki Jalava's bequest wishes, and Vuohisaari in Vilppula and the neighbouring Kotiranta properties in Kuorevesi became a statutory nature reserve.

name: Suomen Luonnonsuojelun Säätiö
summary: A foundation that owns protected areas acquired according to donors' wishes, including three bog and forest areas in Muhos and Siikajoki acquired in 2017.

name: Suomen Riistanhoito-Säätiö
summary: A foundation that coordinates restoration of former peat production areas on land it does not own, and whose EPKA project, launched in late 2025, aims to rewet about 110 hectares.

name: Tampere University
summary: University whose Faculty of Information Technology and Communication Sciences is the affiliation of Fahad Sohrab, first author of a 2020 paper on identifying rare benthic macroinvertebrate taxa.

name: Tarkka
summary: Active dataset that gives the latest satellite observations.

name: Taxa Identification with Machine Learning Enhanced by DNA Metabarcoding
summary: Completed project from 2020 to 2024, led by Jenni Raitoharju and funded by the Research Council of Finland, that proposed combining DNA metabarcoding and optical machine learning for automated aquatic biomonitoring.

name: Terramonitor
summary: Satellite and remote sensing data company, based in Helsinki, that says it uses AI and machine learning, and was a subcontractor in the ESA-funded, VTT-led Forest Digital Twin Component project.

name: Thematic Network on Terrestrial Biodiversity Monitoring
summary: Active thematic network, led by Stefan Prost, that aims to harmonise monitoring methods and support Indigenous-community-led monitoring and data sovereignty.

name: Tiira
summary: National bird observation system described as used by practically all birdwatchers, with two million observations logged in 2025.

name: Towards sustainable coexistence of seals and humans
summary: Project of unknown status in which, according to a LUT article, a seal identification method is being developed.

name: Trestima
summary: Private software company founded in 2012 whose forest inventory system recognises tree species from pictures automatically, using location data, machine learning and mobile technology.

name: Turku University of Applied Sciences
summary: Higher education institution that leads the NEMESIS consortium and gives its address as Joukahaisenkatu 3, Turku.

name: Tvärminne Zoological Station
summary: Marine station at the entrance to the Gulf of Finland, run by the University of Helsinki, that carries out environmental monitoring as well as research.

name: University of Eastern Finland
summary: University that coordinates BiodiLogDef, and was reported in September 2023 to have a postdoctoral researcher awarded a 1.81 million euro ERC Starting Grant for tree mortality research.

name: University of Helsinki
summary: University whose researchers developed methods using open aerial imagery to identify aspens and dead trees, and an algorithm to identify wildlife trade images, and which builds Zonation.

name: University of Jyväskylä
summary: University that builds the Muuttolintujen kevät app and runs a spectral imaging laboratory, and received €150,000 of ERC Proof of Concept funding for BioSounds.

name: University of Oulu
summary: University that coordinates the Digital Waters Flagship and the SOINTU project, and whose Center for Machine Vision and Signal Analysis is listed as a Digital Waters host unit.

name: University of the Arctic
summary: Organisation based in Rovaniemi whose Thematic Network on Terrestrial Biodiversity Monitoring aims to connect researchers across its institutions.

name: University of Turku
summary: University with a 1.02 million euro share of BiodiLogDef's Business Finland funding, long-term breeding bird datasets and indoor experimental aquaria, according to FINMARI.

name: UPM
summary: Company that says it participates in NorthDIVeRSITY.

name: Velmu
summary: Programme led by the Finnish Environment Institute and the Ministry of the Environment that collects data on Finland's underwater marine habitats and species, using video and diving, and publishes results through a map service.

name: VesiMon
summary: Active project investigating new monitoring methods in nine Finnish lakes between 2022 and 2026, funded by the Finnish Cultural Foundation and the Ministry of the Environment.

name: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
summary: Research centre that builds Forestry TEP, says it specialises in forestry applications of satellite image analysis, and led Forest Flux, which ran from December 2018 to November 2021.

name: WildForestReindeerLIFE
summary: Closed project run by Metsähallitus from 2016 to the end of 2023, which monitored wild forest reindeer with GPS collars.

name: WoodsApp
summary: Programme built by Bitapps that, according to Forest.fi, turns satellite data into maps helping forest owners spot damage and plan forestry work remotely.

name: WWF Finland
summary: Independent foundation within the WWF network that builds and runs Norppagalleria, says it is responsible for the southern Saimaa seal census, and partners with Priodiversity LIFE.

name: Ylä-Lapin luonnon kaukokartoitus
summary: Closed remote sensing project run by Metsähallitus and the Finnish Environment Institute, which a Metsähallitus presentation says began in their 2020 to 2023 joint project.

name: Åbo Akademi University
summary: University named as a partner in the NEMESIS consortium.

name: Aquatic biodiversity records at The University of the South Pacific
summary: Occurrence records for specimens in the USP Marine Collection in Suva, mostly from Fiji with records from other South Pacific island countries, published through GBIF and updated regularly.

name: Artificial Intelligence Fiji Pte Limited
summary: Company in Suva whose site sets out plans for an AI research centre on sustainability, marine conservation and climate resilience. The site names no projects, people or partners.

name: Automated CNN based coral reef classification
summary: 2021 paper with University of the South Pacific authors on classifying coral reef images with a convolutional neural network and image augmentation. No page read says who holds or runs the model.

name: Barotu village
summary: Village that became one of the leading communities in restoring its mangrove forest with Conservation International, replanting and nursing mangroves over three years.

name: Biodiversity Clearing House Mechanism Fiji
summary: Portal for exchanging information on Fiji's biodiversity under the Convention on Biological Diversity, with its focal point in the Department of Environment.

name: Biome Health Project, Great Sea Reef
summary: Reef monitoring work on Fiji's Great Sea Reef that plans photogrammetry, video transects and novel acoustic sensors, with WWF Pacific and the Wildlife Conservation Society as partners.

name: Blockchain Supply Chain Traceability Project
summary: WWF project, started in Fiji, to track tuna from vessel to supermarket on a blockchain, with ConsenSys, Traseable and Sea Quest Fiji.

name: Blue Carbon Condition Index and Tool for Fiji
summary: 18-month pilot, known as B-CABONI, to quantify the condition of Fiji's mangrove and seagrass carbon stores and build a monitoring tool.

name: Blue Carbon Fiji Project
summary: Conservation International project funded by Australia's DFAT to protect and restore Fiji's mangroves and find financing for them, with drone surveys of selected villages in the mangrove deltas.

name: Blue Prosperity Fiji
summary: Fijian Government programme with the Waitt Institute on marine spatial planning, blue economy and fisheries. It ran Fiji's first nationwide marine survey in 2023.

name: Blue Prosperity Fiji Interactive Map
summary: Online map of data layers from the 2023 ocean science expedition, published to support Fiji's marine spatial plan.

name: Boarding and Inspection Tool
summary: Web portal and offline Android app built by Traseable Solutions that replaces paper fishing vessel inspection forms for Fiji's fisheries officers.

name: Bose Vanua of Kubulau
summary: District council of chiefs for Kubulau that set up a district fisheries committee and, by 2005, had established the Kubulau Resource Management Committee.

name: Building Coastal Resilience through Nature-based and Integrated Solutions (Fiji)
summary: Asian Development Bank technical assistance for seawalls with mangrove restoration in Fiji, for which ADB used AI on satellite imagery to choose sites, as reported by PINA from an ADB report.

name: Catch Accountancy System
summary: Web platform built by Traseable Solutions for Fiji's Ministry of Fisheries to track and reconcile landed offshore catch.

name: CommonSensing
summary: A UK Space Agency programme that supports Fiji, the Solomon Islands and Vanuatu to use satellite Earth observation data, including on deforestation and land degradation. UNOSAT hosts a CommonSensing mangrove map of Fiji's five main islands.

name: Community Centred Conservation (Fiji)
summary: A non-profit registered in Fiji that, per the Fiji Global Fund for Coral Reefs 2025 report, screened 30 locally managed marine areas, chose 10 and completed baseline biodiversity monitoring involving over 200 community members.

name: Coral Bleaching Extent Detection
summary: Method using Copernicus Marine data and Sentinel-2 to monitor the 2026 marine heatwave in Tonga and Fiji. The preprint is restricted, so only its title could be read.

name: Coral Gardeners Fiji
summary: Fiji branch of Coral Gardeners on Malolo Island, restoring corals with Six Senses Fiji. Its team tracks coral growth and health with the Reef App on an underwater iPhone.

name: CoralNet Image Analysis for Lau Province
summary: Joint project of the Khaled bin Sultan Living Oceans Foundation and Pacific Blue Foundation testing machine learning on reef photographs from Lau Province through CoralNet.

name: Developing Base Maps of Tropical Aquatic Resources in the Pacific
summary: University of Fiji project with the University of South Florida, funded through USAID, that mapped reefs around Votua and Komave.

name: Endangered Species of Fiji
summary: A 2007 NatureFiji-MareqetiViti resource that a UN data flows report treats as the equivalent of a national red list for Fiji.

name: Envirotech Solutions Pacific
summary: Suva environmental consultancy that measures air, water and noise and offers a water quality map of Fiji. The Fiji Times reports a partnership with Google on AI.

name: F-Net
summary: Hybrid explainable convolutional neural network for telling bleached from healthy coral reefs, published in 2026 with a University of the South Pacific co-author.

name: Fiji Carbon Fund Emission Reduction Program
summary: National REDD+ programme that pays for measured forest emission reductions in Fiji, with a measurement, reporting and verification system.

name: Fiji Flying Labs
summary: Local hub in the Flying Labs network that trains and supports drone, data and AI use in Fiji, including for environmental management. It continues the work of South Pacific Flying Labs.

name: Fiji Geospatial Information Management Council
summary: Fiji's government council on geospatial data. Its member agencies feed the Vanua GIS platform, and it identified the need for a nationally authorised land cover dataset.

name: Fiji longline electronic monitoring
summary: Electronic monitoring of Fiji's longline fleet under an agreement between the Ministry of Fisheries and the Fiji Fishing Industry Association, with on-board cameras, computers and software. RNZ reported 28 vessels fitted in 2017 and 22 more planned.

name: Fiji LULC
summary: National annual land use and land cover maps of Fiji at 10 m resolution, made by a random forests model from Sentinel-2 and topographic layers. Maps for 2019 to 2022 are open on the Pacific Data Hub.

name: Fiji mangrove mapping for coastal resilience
summary: Fiji's Ministry of Waterways and Agriculture used satellite imagery to build mangrove maps for nature-based seawall planning, with support from Earth Observation for Sustainable Development and the Asian Development Bank.

name: Fiji Meteorological Service
summary: Fiji's weather service, included here for its ocean and coral data: it issues Coral Bleaching Outlooks and a Fiji Ocean Outlook.

name: Fiji National Forest Monitoring System
summary: National forest monitoring and measurement, reporting and verification system, developed in 2017 and upgraded in 2021 through the Forestry Information Management System.

name: Fiji National University
summary: Fijian university with authors on machine learning papers about rivers and groundwater. It was a partner on the forest monitoring project for Fiji's forestry ministry.

name: Fiji ocean accounts
summary: National ocean accounting work in Fiji, begun as a pilot by the Global Ocean Accounts Partnership Secretariat with the University of the South Pacific.

name: Fiji offshore Electronic Monitoring System
summary: Ministry of Fisheries system with cameras on selected fishing vessels and a trained team of data analysts. Its first phase is complete and more funding has been allocated.

name: Fiji Petrel Sightings Database
summary: A database of sightings of the endemic Fiji Petrel, fed by sightings forms from boaters. The page read does not name who holds it.

name: Fiji Sea Turtle Monitoring Protocol and Priority Maps
summary: Draft national sea turtle monitoring protocol, operating procedures and priority maps under review in 2026, led by the Ministry of Fisheries and WWF-Pacific to make conservation data more consistent.

name: Fiji Tuna Blockchain Traceability Pilot
summary: WWF-led 2018 pilot that traced tuna from a Fijian longline fishery through the supply chain with blockchain, with Traseable Solutions and Sea Quest Fiji.

name: Fijian seagrass dataset with soil carbon, geomorphic variables and seagrass probability map
summary: Dataset published through CSIRO in 2026 with 135 soil cores from 47 sites and a 10 m seagrass probability map for Fiji from Sentinel-2.

name: Forest invasive species mapping in Fiji
summary: Machine learning work on Digital Earth Pacific to map invasive trees such as African tulip in Fiji, using field surveys, Sentinel-2 and a random forest classifier.

name: Forest Reference Level and MRV System for Fiji's National REDD+ Programme
summary: University of Hamburg project for Fiji's forestry ministry, April 2017 to February 2019, to develop a forest reference level and a national forest monitoring system.

name: Great Fiji Shark Count
summary: A national citizen science count of sharks by Fijian dive operators and their guests. From 2012 to 2016, 39 operators recorded 146,304 shark observations from 30,668 dives at 592 sites.

name: Hydrological Information System and Turbidity Forecasting Model in Fiji
summary: A UNSW project with the Water Authority of Fiji to store hydrological data and forecast river turbidity in the Waimanu and Sigatoka catchments, using remote sensing to track river flow and water quality where ground measurements are lacking.

name: iKatch Coastal Catch Data System
summary: Coastal catch data system with a fisher app and an officer portal, built by Traseable Solutions for Conservation International Fiji and piloted on six islands in the Lau Group.

name: Integrated Satellite-Underwater Drone System for Coral Reef Monitoring and Climate Resilience
summary: Tupu Pacific Research Grant project led by Dr Utkal Mehta of the University of the South Pacific, with partners at the University of Fiji and Charles Sturt University.

name: iTaukei Land Trust Board
summary: Fijian land board whose drones carry LiDAR. It used one to map a boundary in the Seaqaqa rainforest for a forest certification project.

name: Kahuto Pacific
summary: Fiji aerial mapping company behind Moana Data Services. It flies LiDAR and imaging surveys of terrain, and ran a LiDAR survey for flood modelling in the Penang River catchment.

name: Korolevu-i-Wai qoliqoli fishing rights owners
summary: Customary fishing rights owners of the Korolevu-i-Wai/Koro-i-Nasau qoliqoli, supported to manage and conserve their locally managed marine area, with Namada one of four villages set to benefit.

name: Kubulau Resource Management Committee
summary: Committee that WCS works with, alongside dive operators and the Coral Alliance, on management plans for the marine reserve.

name: Lau CoralNet benthic image automation
summary: Joint project of the Khaled bin Sultan Living Oceans Foundation and Pacific Blue Foundation to train CoralNet on annotated reef images from Lau Province, Fiji.

name: Leadership Fiji's Community Fund
summary: Fiji fund that manages money from past Leadership Fiji groups, donors and philanthropists, and paid for the National Trust of Fiji's monitoring drone.

name: MACBLUE: Management and Conservation of Blue Carbon Ecosystems
summary: Project linked to GIZ that mapped seagrass and mangroves in Fiji, Vanuatu, Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands from local knowledge, GIS and satellite imagery.

name: Macuata Qoliqoli Management Committee
summary: Committee in Macuata, where resource management committees were established in 2004 (as in Kubulau), thanked by WCS for its commitment to marine protected area work.

name: Mamanuca Environment Society
summary: A non-profit society formed in 2002 and registered in 2003, whose projects include water quality monitoring and Reef Check surveys, with 37 dive sites surveyed through a network formed in 2004.

name: Manta Project Fiji
summary: Affiliate project of the Manta Trust that studies manta and devil rays in Fiji. It set up the first nationwide reef manta database and deployed the first tags on reef mantas there.

name: Marine Atlas for Fiji
summary: A 2019 atlas that compiles more than a hundred marine and coastal datasets for Fiji as maps, data layers and raw data, to support marine spatial planning. Published by GIZ, IUCN and SPREP.

name: Marine Ecology Consulting
summary: Fiji company doing coastal and marine ecology assessments. AIMS names it among the partners that developed the ReefCloud reef image analysis tool, and its principal coordinates the Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network in Fiji.

name: Mataqali Nadicake
summary: Landowning group pressured to lease its forest for logging, with WCS taking a 99-year conservation lease in partnership with the iTaukei Land Trust Board.

name: Mataqali Waisali
summary: Landowning group that owns the 120-hectare Waisali Forest Reserve in Waisali Village, Cakaudrove, Vanua Levu, which the National Trust of Fiji is entrusted to care for.

name: Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways, and Sugar Industry
summary: Fiji's agriculture and waterways ministry. It has used satellite tools for coastal resilience and mangrove maps, and sent staff to the national land cover monitoring workshop.

name: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change
summary: Fiji's environment ministry. It launched the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2026 to 2030 and leads Fiji's Seventh National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity.

name: Ministry of Fisheries
summary: Fiji's fisheries ministry. It runs an offshore electronic monitoring system with cameras on vessels and the Catch Accountancy System.

name: Ministry of Forestry
summary: Fiji's forestry ministry. Its staff work on the National Forest Monitoring System, and it organised the 2024 country-led planning workshop on that system.

name: Ministry of Lands and Mineral Resources
summary: Fiji's lands ministry, endorsed through the Fiji Geospatial Information Management Council to centralise government spatial data on one platform, the Vanua GIS Portal.

name: Moana Data Services
summary: Geospatial data service from Kahuto Pacific that sells LiDAR and imagery of Fiji, starting with 1,000 square kilometres in the Central and Western divisions.

name: Monitoring Heat-Tolerant Algae Living Inside Corals
summary: CORDAP project developing portable bio-optical tools and models to predict coral bleaching, tested in Fiji and Guam.

name: Nadi land cover classification and change detection
summary: Study of land use change in Nadi, Fiji, from 2013 to 2024, using Landsat-8, Google Earth Engine, k-means clustering and convolutional neural networks.

name: Nadogo Development Committee
summary: Committee representing Nadogo's 22 tribes that, alongside the Tui Nadogo, led communities in declaring Nukuvadra and Katawaqa islands community protected areas and turtle sanctuaries.

name: Nagilogilo clan
summary: Clan that traditionally owns Vatu-i-Ra Island and has monitored and managed it for invasive species since 2007, with BirdLife International's support.

name: Naidiri village
summary: Village whose community-led marine protected area has revived local fish populations, growing from a 1,200 square metre no-take area set up in 2009 into the Naidiri Marine Biodiversity Park.

name: Naisisili village
summary: Village that, with Navotua, planted more than 8,000 Rhizophora mangroves and whose headman reports two mangrove areas, Tukusaga and Mamada.

name: Nanuca village
summary: Village whose leaders set up two tabu reserves in 2012, which protect more than 1,300 acres of ocean and mangrove areas.

name: Nasilai village
summary: Village whose people, the traditional fishermen of the Tui Nakelo, closed their traditional fishing ground as a tabu for five years.

name: National Fisheries Surveillance and Operations Centre
summary: Fijian centre that receives real-time data from cameras and sensors on fishing vessels to help combat illegal fishing.

name: National Geographic Pristine Seas Fiji expedition
summary: Two-month survey of Fiji's reefs, lagoons and deep sea, using submersible dives, seabed cameras and environmental DNA sampling.

name: National Landcover Monitoring Working Group
summary: Fiji's cabinet-endorsed working group on national land cover monitoring, set up in 2023 to produce a common, nationally authorised land cover classification and dataset.

name: National Trust of Fiji
summary: Body that manages protected places in Fiji, including Sigatoka Sand Dunes National Park, where it was given a drone for monitoring and management.

name: NatureFiji-MareqetiViti
summary: Fiji's domestic conservation NGO. It runs Endangered Species of Fiji, which a UN report treats as the national red list equivalent.

name: Navotua village
summary: Village that, with Naisisili, joined a mangrove restoration initiative planting more than 8,000 Rhizophora mangroves, as part of locally led efforts to protect its coastline.

name: Navukavu Qoliqoli Committee
summary: Committee whose chairman asks people using the fishing ground to catch only what they need and to stay out of the taboo area.

name: Qoliqoli Cokovata Management Committee
summary: Committee set up by traditional owners to manage and care for the Qoliqoli Cokovata site on the north coast of Vanua Levu, where local communities retain custodial ownership of fishing grounds.

name: Raviravi village
summary: Village that has planted mangroves to rehabilitate its shoreline and, according to its chief, met its target of 20,000 trees with help from the Kiwa Initiative, IUCN and C3 Fiji.

name: Real-time fish recognition on an underwater drone
summary: Deep learning fish recognition for low-quality images on an underwater drone, published in 2024 by authors at the University of the South Pacific.

name: Reef Explorer Fiji
summary: Fiji-based research and development company founded by coral reef ecologist Victor Bonito to support community marine conservation. It is a partner on a project building bio-optical tools to predict coral bleaching.

name: Sea Turtle Nesting Beach Database
summary: A database of sea turtle nesting beaches in Fiji, fed by forms from boaters. The page read does not name who holds it.

name: Serua traditional leaders
summary: Traditional leaders of Serua who banded together to put a province-wide tabu on fishing along the coast.

name: Site-Specific Water Quality Map of Fiji
summary: Envirotech Solutions Pacific's map of water quality across Fiji, covering marine and freshwater sites over 10 years.

name: South Pacific Flying Labs
summary: WeRobotics-backed drone group hosted at the USP Geospatial Unit in Suva. It worked on coral reef mapping and forest degradation until it moved to Papua New Guinea on 1 January 2021.

name: Sovi Landowners Committee
summary: Committee of five villages, Naivucini, Delailasakau, Nadakuni, Naseuvou and Nukusere, with which the National Trust of Fiji co-manages the Sovi Basin.

name: Spatial Intel
summary: Pacific dealer of drones, geospatial software and satellite Earth observation products, with offices in Suva and Brisbane. It lists GeoAI analytics for environmental intelligence among its partner products.

name: Stepping Stone Drone Surveys
summary: Fiji-based geospatial provider of drone mapping and remote sensing for environmental monitoring and other projects, using open-source tools.

name: Strengthening Capacities in the use of Geospatial Information for Improved Resilience in Asia-Pacific and Africa
summary: NORAD-funded UNITAR and UNOSAT project building geospatial skills, including AI-based methods, in agencies working on natural resources. Fiji's environment ministry is a partner.

name: Traseable Solutions
summary: Fiji-based company, founded in 2017, that describes itself as AI-enabled and builds fisheries traceability and data systems for Pacific governments, the Forum Fisheries Agency and NGOs.

name: Trees of Fiji app
summary: Mobile app to identify tree species in Fiji, based on the book Trees of Fiji and paid for through a project of Germany's International Climate Initiative.

name: Triton's Spear Coastal Vessel Monitoring Pilot
summary: Pilot of the solar-powered TS3 vessel monitor for small coastal fleets in Fiji, explored by the fisheries ministry with UN-SPIDER.

name: University of Fiji
summary: University at Saweni, Lautoka. Its School of Science and Technology publishes machine learning work on floods, rivers and water, and mapping of mangroves and reefs.

name: USP AI Reef Monitoring Underwater Vehicle
summary: University of the South Pacific master's project putting machine learning on a remotely operated underwater vehicle to capture and analyse images of Fiji's coral reefs.

name: USP Geospatial Science Laboratories
summary: Four geospatial labs at the University of the South Pacific, one of which holds a drone fleet and has housed South Pacific Flying Labs.

name: VanuaGIS
summary: Government web portal and repository for Fiji's geospatial information, managed by the lands ministry.

name: Vatu-i-Ra Conservation Park Management Committee
summary: Management committee of the Vatu-i-Ra conservation park, which received a patrol boat to launch monitoring and surveillance of the no-take zone.

name: Vatuvara Foundation
summary: Foundation working on marine resource management in Fiji's Northern Lau group. Its own article in EXPLORE Fiji says it added the ReefCloud AI tool to its reef monitoring with the Australian Institute of Marine Science.

name: Votua and Maui Bay reef mapping and monitoring
summary: A USAID Pacific American Climate Fund grant to the University of Fiji to map and monitor reefs around Votua and Maui Bay, with land and marine habitat maps from regional satellite imagery.

name: Wailevu East and West Resource Management Committees
summary: Two committees, Wailevu East and West, that jointly hold copyright of the 2013 ecosystem-based management plan with WCS and make decisions needing approval from the Bose Vanua.

name: Waitabu Marine Park Committee
summary: Committee whose consent was needed before a group cleared crown-of-thorns starfish from the tabu area.

name: Water Authority of Fiji
summary: The statutory body for clean water and wastewater services across Fiji. It is the client and key stakeholder on a UNSW hydrological information system and river turbidity forecasting project.

name: Watershed Interventions for Systems Health in Fiji
summary: Fijian project on risks to people and ecosystems in five watersheds. Its paper proposes Bayesian Belief Networks to quantify the combined effect of interventions.

name: WCS Fiji
summary: Fiji programme of the Wildlife Conservation Society, based in Suva. Its marine scientists use MERMAID to store Fiji's reef monitoring and bleaching data.

name: Whale & Dolphin Sightings Database
summary: A national database of whale and dolphin sightings in Fiji, fed by sightings forms from boaters. The page read does not name who holds it.

name: WWF-Pacific
summary: WWF's Pacific programme, with offices in Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands and Fiji and a regional hub in Suva. WWF's Fiji office was a partner in the Pacific tuna blockchain traceability project.

name: Yadrava na Vanua
summary: A team from Suva that won the 2022 Space for Planet Earth Challenge. It used machine learning on Planet satellite images, with field measurements, to refine land cover and carbon stock data across Fiji.

name: Yavusa Burenitu, Nabukelevu
summary: Mataqali of Nabukelevu and the wider yavusa Burenitu, who are custodians of hundreds of acres of dense forest and whose forefathers stayed to protect the ancestral mound.

name: Aerial mapping survey of Yap's coral reefs (2026)
summary: A Yap Marine Resources Management Division aerial survey of the state's coral reefs, announced for 10 to 13 November 2026 using the Global Airborne Observatory aircraft, with results going to Yap's Department of Resources and Development.

name: Blue Prosperity Micronesia
summary: Programme the FSM government calls its flagship for developing and protecting marine resources, which partnered with National Geographic Pristine Seas on a nation-wide marine science expedition.

name: College of Micronesia-FSM
summary: Active college that, with the FSM government, co-established the FSM Clearing-House Mechanism.

name: Conservation Society of Pohnpei
summary: Non-governmental organisation that, per The Nature Conservancy's 2024 report, gathered coral reef monitoring data as a programme partner, and has monitored fish in a Nahtik Island no-take zone and used GPS in forest monitoring.

name: Department of Environment, Climate Change and Emergency Management
summary: Active FSM government department through which the government plans to strengthen sustainable land and coastal management to secure ecosystem services, partnering with the United Nations Development Programme.

name: Department of Resources and Development
summary: Active FSM department whose Secretary is the CBD primary national focal point, listed by the CBD Secretariat, and which the National Association of State Foresters names as the forestry agency.

name: Federated States of Micronesia Ridge to Reef Project
summary: Closed GEF-funded project run by DECEM, whose terminal evaluation, dated 31 December 2022, reports that post-planting monitoring of rehabilitated areas was completed in 2022.

name: FSM Clearing-House Mechanism
summary: Information exchange mechanism for the CBD, set up by the FSM government and the College of Micronesia-FSM with the four states, built by the college and funded by the Global Environment Facility; current status unknown.

name: FSM Protected Areas Network
summary: A national protected areas framework adopted by the FSM Congress in 2018, with a coordinator post advertised from 3 March 2026 to hold monitoring data and update the World Database on Protected Areas.

name: Kosrae Conservation and Safety Organization
summary: Active Kosrae nonprofit, funded by CEPF, that was grantee of the Protecting Kosrae's Upland Forest project and, as reported, took part in a ReefCloud training workshop in April 2026.

name: Kosrae Island Resource Management Authority
summary: Active semi-autonomous agency of the Kosrae State Government, in the Federated States of Micronesia, with five units that monitor and inform policy on protecting the island's resources.

name: Loosiep Island restoration, Ulithi Atoll
summary: Restoration project on Loosiep Island where Island Conservation reported removing feral pigs with the community in 2019, planning rat removal for March 2020 and working towards removing monitor lizards.

name: Mangrove Species Dominance Map of Pohnpei
summary: Dataset published in 2022 as a public US Geological Survey data release, modelling mangrove species dominance on Pohnpei with k-nearest neighbour and random forest models.

name: Micronesia Conservation Trust
summary: Active Pohnpei-based trust with US 501(c)(3) status that says it became the dedicated financial mechanism for the Micronesia Challenge and, per NOAA, co-coordinates the Pacific Islands Marine Protected Areas Community.

name: National Geographic Pristine Seas and Blue Prosperity Micronesia expedition
summary: Closed expedition, run by Blue Prosperity Micronesia and National Geographic Pristine Seas, that studied 11 remote atolls, surveying 62 sites with 531 dives and 11 FSM scientists and divers.

name: Protecting Kosrae's Upland Forest
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project run by the Kosrae Conservation and Safety Organization from December 2011 to November 2012, beginning with a plant inventory survey and reporting data on invasive-species-affected areas.

name: Ulithi Marine Turtle Program
summary: Community conservation project on Ulithi Atoll, Federated States of Micronesia, which by 2014 had tagged and monitored nearly 3,000 nesting green turtles with the Falalop community since 2005, largely funded by NOAA.

name: Yap Marine Resources Management Division
summary: Active Yap body that, according to Island Times in November 2023, provided preliminary fish surveys and reported Ngulu Atoll data indicating recovery from coral bleaching.

name: Faroese Marine Ecosystem Observing Study (FAMEOS)
summary: Closed project that, per 2017 slides, aimed to build an observing system in Faroese waters integrating DNA-based estimates, and whose results Havstovan combined with historical records in a January 2024 phytoplankton diversity registry.

name: Føroya Fuglafrøðifelag
summary: Faroese ornithology association that invited public participation in Global Big Day in May 2023 and organised a research evening in Perlan after establishing the Kenneth Williamson bird fund.

name: GloBECC: Gelatinous Lifeforms in Faroese waters: Biodiversity, Regional Connectivity, and Capacity building
summary: Running in 2024–2026 with Faroese Research Council funding, aims to establish Faroese jellyfish surveillance and a database using data from existing Havstovan, Firum and Bakkafrost sea surveys.

name: Granskingarráðið
summary: Its marine research programme committee awarded DKK 14 million to four projects in 2021 from Danish government funds; it also funded BlueCea, which aims at AI-based seafloor imagery identification.

name: Havstovan
summary: Independent advisory institution under the Ministry of Resources and Industry that researches Faroese marine life, with reported work on dolphin GPS tagging, grey seal censuses since 2018, and eDNA compared with trawl data.

name: Hunters' Self-Monitoring in the Faroe Islands
summary: Hunters' self-monitoring of shot mountain hare, which an INTAROS report of 30 November 2020 says the University of the Faroe Islands had organised since 2012, with data held in a Faroese web database.

name: Koltur Research Station
summary: Research station owned by Tjóðsavnið that provides historical biodiversity records, climate data and recent soil temperature data, and which the museum says will be expanded for scientists.

name: Koltur species inventory
summary: Closed Tjóðsavnið project that inventoried Koltur's plants, birds and invertebrates from 2019 to 2024, recording 519 species as a baseline for monitoring, backed by a DKK 2 million three-year grant.

name: MeDNA - Tracking spatial and temporal distribution of marine mammals in the Atlantic Arctic with environmental DNA
summary: Active project, led by Anni Djurhuus and funded by Granskingarráðið in the round announced on 8 September 2025, on tracking marine mammals in the Atlantic Arctic with environmental DNA.

name: R250 Bird Surveys Faroe Islands
summary: Dataset of standardised R250 bird point counts from surveys across the Faroe Islands, including annual monitoring at Skúvoy and Koltur, with its metadata saying annual updates follow each field season.

name: The Metadatabase of Environment and Nature in the Faroe Islands (MENFO)
summary: Metadata catalogue for Faroese nature and environment data, established on 1 January 2025 according to its registration guide, which asks organisations to document archived and recent data and plans a map display.

name: Tjóðsavnið
summary: Faroe Islands National Museum, established in 2018 by merging the culture and natural history museums, which publishes eight GBIF datasets and leads a 2025 paper on a 2019 to 2024 Koltur species inventory.

name: Tjóðsavnið freshwater monitoring scheme
summary: Active regular freshwater monitoring scheme run by Tjóðsavnið, using chironomid pupal exuviae collection, which gave at least seven new Faroese species records from lakes sampled in 2025.

name: Umhvørvisstovan
summary: Authority and data institution under the Ministry of Environment, whose 2023 annual report says it has begun organising nature and environmental data and is building a structured data foundation for nature management.

name: University of the Faroe Islands
summary: University whose researcher leads the MeDNA eDNA project on marine mammals, and whose affiliated researcher co-authored an eDNA versus trawl paper on the Faroese Plateau.

name: ADEME
summary: French public body that operates France 2030 funding, including the funding of the Psi-Biom project.

name: ADENA
summary: Association at Agde that manages the Bagnas National Nature Reserve, runs scientific monitoring there, and hosted AI insect and pollinator monitoring tests as a MAMBO pilot site.

name: ADENO
summary: National PatriNat programme to study dragonfly and damselfly communities through environmental DNA.

name: ADNeIA
summary: A University of Montpellier and SPYGEN industrial chair that combines environmental DNA and AI to monitor marine biodiversity, with 1.28 million euros over 48 months.

name: Agence de l'eau Rhône Méditerranée et Corse
summary: French water agency that supports the TEMPO Posidonia monitoring network.

name: Agence nationale de la recherche
summary: The French agency that funds research by project. It runs the Challenge IA-Biodiv with AFD and funds AI for forest monitoring and eDNA research.

name: Agence Régionale de la Biodiversité Bourgogne-Franche-Comté
summary: Regional biodiversity agency presenting an observatory with indicators, the Sigogne geoservices platform of maps and dashboards, and a large predators mission monitoring livestock protection trials with automatically triggered cameras.

name: AI4Forests
summary: A French and German research project building high-resolution AI maps of European and other large forest biomes, down to individual trees, with an ANR grant of about 1.05 million euros.

name: AIME
summary: A Franco-African consortium in the Challenge IA-Biodiv working to improve marine biodiversity indicators with AI.

name: AIonWetlands
summary: A project using satellite image time series and AI to map Mediterranean wetland habitats and follow their change, with its geoportal still in development.

name: Alliance pour la Renaturation des Villes
summary: Alliance of five companies, created in 2023, that offers cities urban renaturation services around the Ecoteka tool.

name: Andromède Océanologie
summary: Company partnered with MARBEC at the University of Montpellier on methods for studying underwater ecosystems.

name: ARB Occitanie
summary: Leads the Occitanie Regional Biodiversity Observatory, which tracks the state of biodiversity and its pressures using indicators designed from shared expertise.

name: ARBRE
summary: Association on La Réunion that monitors marine and land biodiversity there and in the Indian Ocean, and led an environmental DNA inventory of sharks and rays.

name: Argaly
summary: French company in Sainte-Hélène-du-Lac whose managing director, Aurélie Bonin, also leads its research and development. Directories describe it as an environmental DNA firm.

name: Association de gestion de la réserve naturelle de Saint-Martin
summary: Management association of the Saint-Martin nature reserve, whose manager presented a plan in mid-September 2023 to restore Tintamarre islet, part of which lies in the reserve.

name: Association des Amis de la Réserve Naturelle du Lac de Remoray
summary: Association created in 1984 that carries out management of the Lac de Remoray national nature reserve on behalf of the State.

name: Association Finocchiarola pour la gestion des espaces naturels de la Pointe du Cap Corse
summary: Association that manages the Finocchiarola islands nature reserve, created in 1987, off the Cap Corse.

name: Association pour la protection des animaux sauvages
summary: Wildlife protection association whose 2022 annual report states that 1,306 hectares acquired through purchases and donations were fully protected and labelled Réserves de Vie Sauvage.

name: Asters, Conservatoire d’espaces naturels de Haute-Savoie
summary: Conservation body that is the sole manager of the nine national nature reserves of Haute-Savoie.

name: ATLASea
summary: French research programme co-led by the CNRS and the CEA to sequence the genomes of 4,500 marine species, funded by France 2030 for eight years.

name: Autowing
summary: Project started in 2021 with OFB funding that builds an AI to recognise the age and sex of a bird from a photo. It sits inside ChassAdapt, the hunting federation's bag reporting app.

name: AVES Wind
summary: Real-time bird detection and identification system for wind farms, sold by Biotope Technologies and based on a system developed by ProTecBird.

name: AXA Climate
summary: AXA's climate business, listed by CORDIS as a French coordinator of the Horizon Europe project SWIFTT on AI forest monitoring.

name: Aéro Biodiversité
summary: French non-profit that runs standardised biodiversity surveys on airports and airfields and supports operators in managing those sites.

name: BD Forêt v3
summary: The third version of IGN's forest map of mainland France, published as a beta test dataset in June 2026. IGN aims to cover the whole of mainland France within one year.

name: BioEOS
summary: Space for Climate Observatory project developing observation tools for coastal biodiversity, with its first demonstrator in the south-west Indian Ocean.

name: BIOINDIC-IA
summary: ANR project on automatic classification by deep learning for biological indication of aquatic environments from image analysis, coordinated by Martin Laviale.

name: BioLit
summary: A national citizen science programme on coastal biodiversity, launched in 2010, in which participants photograph shore species and share the observations.

name: BioPhonia
summary: Company that uses passive acoustics to give site managers data for understanding and monitoring biodiversity.

name: Biotope
summary: Environmental consultancy in ecology and biodiversity that works in France and abroad. It is part of the consortium mapping biodiversity in Occitanie.

name: Birdz
summary: The French IoT subsidiary of Veolia. With the Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle it co-developed Leko, which detects bats and other animals from sound with an algorithm.

name: BLOOM
summary: French marine conservation association that runs TrawlWatch monitoring to detect industrial vessels in coastal waters.

name: Bretagne Vivante
summary: Nature protection association in Brittany, which has become the regional Conservatoire d'espaces naturels. Its site lists regional observatories of birds, reptiles and amphibians, invertebrates and mammals, and an observatory of change on the shore.

name: BSB Marine
summary: Company that developed the OSCAR navigation aid and, with the Parc national de Port-Cros, the EYESEA AMP surveillance system for marine protected areas.

name: CAIRN
summary: Tool from the Écrins National Park for monitoring visitor numbers in natural areas by AI analysis of images, built on open-source software.

name: Canopée
summary: French forest NGO that publishes L'Observatoire des coupes rases, a satellite-based tracking of clear-cuts built on FORMS-T deep learning products.

name: CarHab
summary: National predictive map of natural habitats that supports the national biodiversity strategy. It covers 91% of mainland France and Corsica and reached La Réunion in February 2026.

name: Carte d'occupation des sols OSO
summary: Automatic 10 metre land cover maps of mainland France made from Sentinel-2 by the Theia land cover expert group.

name: Carte de couverture du sol par intelligence artificielle
summary: IGN's land cover map made with artificial intelligence, from deep learning models that analyse aerial images.

name: CARTOVEGE
summary: Space for Climate Observatory project on vegetation mapping that lists machine learning classification and drone monitoring among its tools.

name: CASSIA Technologies
summary: French company whose Cassia technology analyses drone, aircraft or satellite images of vegetation with learning algorithms to map ecosystems.

name: CDC Biodiversité
summary: Subsidiary of the Caisse des Dépôts that developed the Global Biodiversity Score, a tool that lets companies and financial institutions measure their biodiversity footprint.

name: CEN Nouvelle-Aquitaine
summary: Regional conservation body that develops, administers and hosts the open-source Kollect recording system.

name: Centre d'Ecologie Fonctionnelle et Evolutive
summary: Ecology research centre on the CNRS campus at Montpellier, and the affiliation of Simon Chamaillé-Jammes, who co-leads DeepFaune.

name: Centre de synthèse et d'analyse sur la biodiversité
summary: The FRB's synthesis centre in Montpellier. It runs a five-day course, AI for ecologists, that teaches early-career researchers AI concepts and tools.

name: Centre national d'études spatiales
summary: The French space agency. It describes itself as supporting public policy that depends on space, and it presents national Earth system data hubs including Theia, Odatis and the biodiversity data hub PNDB.

name: Centre national de la recherche scientifique
summary: French national research centre, which funds the DeepFaune camera-trap AI project, co-leads the ATLASea marine genome programme and is a member of the Pl@ntNet consortium.

name: Cerema
summary: French public expert body on planning. Its REAUZOH project uses field data, satellite imagery and AI to map potential wetlands.

name: CESBIO
summary: Research unit that produces the OSO land cover map of France from Sentinel-2 images.

name: Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives
summary: French research body whose LSCE laboratory works on forest deep learning and which co-leads the ATLASea marine genome programme.

name: Communauté de communes Frasne-Drugeon
summary: Local authority grouping that manages the Tourbières de Frasne-Bouverans regional nature reserve, with the Bourgogne-Franche-Comté Region as supervising and classification authority.

name: Compagnie Nationale du Rhône
summary: Concession holder and manager of the Rhône from the Swiss border to its delta, on which the Vigilife environmental DNA methods for large rivers were tested and validated.

name: Conservatoire botanique national de Bourgogne-Franche-Comté - Observatoire régional des Invertébrés
summary: National botanical conservatory covering the flora and habitats of Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, which also inventories butterflies, dragonflies and molluscs.

name: Conservatoire d'espaces naturels de Bourgogne
summary: Association under the 1901 law, founded in 1986, that manages natural sites with local partners and, with the Franche-Comté conservatory, managed 400 sites covering 9,468 hectares at the end of 2025.

name: Conservatoire d'espaces naturels de Franche-Comté
summary: Conservation body that, with the Burgundy conservatory, managed 400 sites covering 9,468 hectares at the end of 2025, and is listed as a partner of the Thalera moth identification project.

name: Conservatoire d'espaces naturels de Guyane
summary: Conservatory of natural spaces in French Guiana, founded in 2008, that leads the network of protected areas, co-manages one reserve and runs the RIO project.

name: Conservatoire du littoral
summary: French public body created in 1975 that buys land to protect natural areas and landscapes on sea and lake shores for good.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels Allier
summary: Regional conservation body working on the knowledge, preservation, management and enhancement of natural heritage in the Allier department and neighbouring areas.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels Auvergne
summary: Conservation body working to preserve landscapes and biodiversity across the Puy-de-Dôme, Cantal and Haute-Loire, listing 307 managed natural sites.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels de Corse
summary: Non-profit association approved for environmental protection, created in 1972 to preserve the natural heritage and biodiversity of Corsica.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels de Lorraine
summary: Conservation body that since 1984 has preserved natural sites in Lorraine by buying them or renting them for long periods.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels de Normandie
summary: Conservation body responsible for the knowledge, protection, management and enhancement of 217 natural areas in Normandy.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels de Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur
summary: Conservation body working for a balance between people and nature and to maintain natural heritage in Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur, listing the natural sites it manages.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels de Savoie
summary: Conservation body that aims to safeguard and manage natural areas of recognised natural value in the Savoie department.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels des Hauts-de-France
summary: Conservation body that works to preserve, restore or develop natural heritage on the natural sites where it operates in the Hauts-de-France region.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels des Pays de la Loire
summary: Conservation body whose stated purpose is the knowledge, protection, management and enhancement of biodiversity and natural heritage in the Pays de la Loire.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels du Centre-Val de Loire
summary: Conservation body created in 1990 that protects natural areas in the Centre-Val de Loire region for their biodiversity and landscape or geological quality.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels d’Alsace
summary: Conservation body with a regional network of nearly 400 protected natural areas in Alsace, preserved by its team and volunteers.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels d’Occitanie
summary: Conservation body whose staff and volunteers work to preserve natural sites across the Occitanie region through collective actions.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels d’Île-de-France
summary: Conservation body that since 1988 has preserved natural areas in the Paris region through protection, management, knowledge and enhancement.

name: Conservatoire d’espaces naturels Isère
summary: Conservation body whose main purpose is restoring and managing natural sites, either for itself or in support of local authorities.

name: Cosma
summary: French deep tech company founded in 2022 that maps seabed ecosystems with swarms of autonomous underwater robots and algorithms that recognise habitats and species. Hosted at Ifremer in La Seyne-sur-Mer.

name: Cosmeo
summary: France 2030 programme supported by CNES that turns Earth observation data into services on coastline, coastal habitats, water quality and sea states for government bodies and coastal managers.

name: CREA Mont-Blanc
summary: Research centre at Chamonix that studies high-altitude ecosystems, with nine citizen science programmes on its SPOT platform and an online Atlas du Mont-Blanc.

name: darwin
summary: Start-up that helps consultancies and software platforms assess companies' biodiversity impact and risk, using AI to process data, aligned with SBTN and TNFD.

name: Data Terra
summary: French research infrastructure for Earth system data, organised around data clusters for atmosphere, ocean, solid earth and land surfaces, with some thirty partner organisations.

name: DataPhonia
summary: BioPhonia's tool for managing, storing and using sound data from environmental monitoring, co-funded by the European Regional Development Fund.

name: DEAL Réunion
summary: Funded IRRAE (2021 to 2023), launched in August 2021, with BIORECIF, the Université de Mayotte and GLOBICE as partners.

name: Dinamis
summary: A French access scheme for satellite imagery, listed by CNES among its data hubs. Its open data initiative makes SPOT-6/7 imagery freely available.

name: Disaitek
summary: Paris company founded in 2017 that combines satellite data and AI for environmental risk and regulatory compliance, including deforestation analysis.

name: DNA EcoTrace
summary: LDgenX research and development project that aims to automate and simplify biodiversity monitoring by environmental DNA.

name: Département de la Haute-Corse
summary: Departmental authority in charge of the Étang de Biguglia nature reserve (1994), according to the Corsican environment office page.

name: EAR (ecoacoustics research project)
summary: Ecoacoustic research site from members of a Paris institute at the Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle and CNRS, offering open-access tools such as scikit-maad and running the sonosylva project.

name: ECO-MED Ecologie & Médiation
summary: Ecological consultancy founded in 2003, part of the consortium mapping biodiversity in Occitanie.

name: EcoSecrets
summary: Open source web application for monitoring with autonomous sensors such as camera traps, from Natural Solutions.

name: Ecoteka
summary: Open source web and mobile platform for urban tree inventories and renaturation, with AI inventories from satellite or LiDAR.

name: EDF Pulse Ventures
summary: Corporate venture capital arm of the EDF group, which invests in the biodiversity measurement start-up NatureMetrics.

name: EFREI
summary: French engineering school listed as a partner in the Farmbird farmland bird monitoring project.

name: Envolis
summary: Consultancy of scientists and environmental experts on water, soil and biodiversity, part of the consortium mapping biodiversity in Occitanie.

name: EQUIPONANT
summary: A project awarded funding in the first EQUIP call of PEPR SOLU-BIOD in 2025, intended for low-cost underwater cameras and sensors at four sites, and planning drone tests to map Spartina alterniflora.

name: EUROPAM
summary: European research project that compares passive acoustic monitoring of marine megafauna across the Mediterranean, the Azores and Norway, using Bombyx sonobuoys and AI on marine soundscapes.

name: EVERGREEN
summary: Inria project team at Montpellier, with INRAE and CIRAD, that designs machine learning for Earth observation data, including tree dieback mapping and country-scale canopy height.

name: EYESEA AMP
summary: An automated surveillance system for marine protected areas that uses computer vision to recognise floating objects, analyse visitor numbers, and flag unauthorised anchoring or suspected harm to marine species. Pilot at Port-Cros.

name: Farmbird
summary: Interreg North-West Europe project that develops drone, satellite and AI monitoring of farmland birds at breeding sites in five regions, led by the Province of Fryslân with the OFB as the French partner on monitoring.

name: Faune-France
summary: French online citizen science portal for sharing animal observations, created in 2017 and administered by the LPO, with more than 100 million records.

name: FISH-PREDICT
summary: A French consortium in the Challenge IA-Biodiv working on predicting reef fish biodiversity.

name: FLAIR
summary: IGN's AI challenges and benchmark datasets for land cover mapping from aerial and satellite sensors. FLAIR-HUB covers over 2,500 square kilometres of France with 63 billion hand-annotated pixels.

name: fold ecosystemics
summary: French simplified joint-stock company (SAS) of data scientists working with forestry professionals, offering continuous solar-powered bioacoustic monitoring of birds and bats and training detection algorithms for other species.

name: Fondation de France
summary: French philanthropic foundation that hosts the Fondation Ginkgo pour l'environnement, which supports the ADENO eDNA programme, and has supported research at the Tour du Valat.

name: Fondation François Sommer
summary: French foundation for wildlife and habitat conservation that supports research at the Tour du Valat on restoration and water management.

name: Fondation Inria
summary: Foundation that has supported the Pl@ntNet consortium since January 2026, in succession to Agropolis Fondation.

name: Fondation pour la Nature et l'Homme
summary: French foundation on ecological transition. The DeepForestVision paper thanks it for supporting the work.

name: Fondation pour la recherche sur la biodiversité
summary: French foundation that brings together biodiversity researchers and society. Through its synthesis centre, Cesab, it trains ecologists in AI and funds synthesis projects.

name: FORMS-T
summary: France-wide forest height, wood volume and biomass maps from 2018 onwards, made with a deep learning framework on Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and GEDI data.

name: FORMSpoT
summary: A decade-long map of forest canopy height for mainland France at 1.5 metre resolution from 2014 to 2024, with yearly disturbance polygons, derived from SPOT-6/7 images with a transformer model trained on airborne laser data.

name: Fédération des Conservatoires d’espaces naturels
summary: Federation whose 2022 dashboard, using data as of 1 January 2021, reports its conservatories network managing 3,800 sites covering more than 145,000 hectares.

name: Fédération des Réserves Naturelles Catalanes
summary: Organisation that manages nine national nature reserves in the Pyrénées-Orientales together with local managers.

name: GAIA PREDICT
summary: A project presented to Occitanie's regional geographic information committee, with parts on mapping natural and semi-natural habitats, potential species distribution, and data sharing.

name: Gardiens du Haut-Maroni
summary: A three-year project in French Guiana that gives local people tools such as camera traps to follow forest health. Thirty camera traps around Taluen recorded more than 30 species in two months.

name: GBIF France
summary: The French node of the Global Biodiversity Information Facility, which passes biodiversity data collected by French bodies to the international network, drawing on the SINP, Récolnat and the PNDB.

name: GEODES
summary: The CNES portal for Earth observation space data, run by the French space agency, whose environment catalogue lists a service for near real-time tracking of tropical deforestation.

name: GeoNature
summary: Open source software for entering, managing and publishing fauna and flora data, developed by the French national parks and Natural Solutions.

name: GeoNature-atlas
summary: Open source tool developed by the Parc national des Écrins for publishing naturalist observations, free for other bodies to reuse on top of the national INPN references.

name: GeoPl@ntNet
summary: Maps of biodiversity from deep learning models trained on remote sensing, climate and occurrence data, which predict species assemblages and derive indicators. Developed by the Pl@ntNet team.

name: Ginco
summary: Open source ministerial web application that serves as a regional or thematic platform of the SINP, co-developed by the ministry, the IGN and the Muséum.

name: GIP Réserve Nationale Marine de La Réunion
summary: Public interest group managing La Réunion's marine reserve, which coordinates reef monitoring run since 1998 across 14 sentinel stations and has monitored the reserve effect since 2007.

name: Global Biodiversity Score
summary: Tool developed by CDC Biodiversité and launched on 12 May 2020 that measures the biodiversity footprint of companies and financial institutions.

name: GlobeEye
summary: Company that says it combines satellite data and AI for environmental monitoring, with a CarbonEagle platform for REDD+ sites and a partner role in the Horizon Europe project ThinkingEarth.

name: GlobEO
summary: A Toulouse-based organisation created in 2018 that develops environmental monitoring services from Earth observation data, mainly Sentinel imagery.

name: Globice
summary: NGO founded in 2001 for cetacean science and conservation in La Réunion, whose humpback photo-identification catalogue held 3,200 individuals by 2023, and which uses Happywhale.

name: Goodforest
summary: French deep tech start-up, winner of the i-Lab 2026 competition, that monitors forests with satellite remote sensing and AI.

name: Groupe Chiroptères Océan Indien
summary: Bat group in the Indian Ocean behind Vigie-Chiro-RUN, standardised recording of bat calls on La Réunion over at least five years to follow population trends.

name: HYDROSTREA
summary: A project awarded funding in the first EQUIP call of PEPR SOLU-BIOD, intended for continuous hydrological monitoring of oyster ecosystems with a multiparameter probe, with plans to feed national research infrastructures.

name: Hytech Imaging
summary: French spectral imaging company that developed SolarStormm, a solar drone system for monitoring marine biodiversity at offshore wind farms.

name: i-Sea
summary: French firm that maps natural habitats and coastlines from satellite and aerial images. Its Biocoast service applies machine learning to Pléiades images and field records.

name: Initiative Française pour les Récifs Coralliens
summary: French coral reef initiative whose fifth programme has seven themes, including observation networks monitoring reef, seagrass and mangrove health, with a shared portal listing monitoring stations across three oceans.

name: INPN Espèces
summary: Mobile app and national citizen science programme on wild species in France, developed by PatriNat.

name: Institut national de l'information géographique et forestière
summary: The French public mapping agency, which also runs the national forest inventory. It develops open source AI models for geospatial information, including the Maestro foundation model and the FLAIR land cover datasets.

name: Intelligent Acoustics
summary: Project from doctoral work at the University of Toulon on embedded AI and bioacoustics, building autonomous sensors that analyse terrestrial or underwater sound in real time. The incubator said in January 2026 that the company would be created in late February 2026.

name: Inventaire forestier national
summary: France's national forest inventory, run by IGN. Results are published every year and the raw field data can be viewed and downloaded.

name: Inventaire national du patrimoine naturel
summary: France's national natural heritage inventory, managed by PatriNat. It acts as the national platform of the SINP, and species observation data are available through its OpenObs tool.

name: IRRAE
summary: Inventory of sharks and rays around La Réunion from environmental DNA, launched in August 2021.

name: Kermap
summary: Company founded in 2017 in Cesson-Sévigné that uses AI to analyse satellite and aerial images and supplies information on urban, agricultural and natural land.

name: Kinéis
summary: Satellite operator founded in 2019 that inherited CNES and CLS expertise from the Argos system. It connects devices that collect data from oceans and wildlife.

name: Kollect
summary: Open-source system with a web portal and mobile app for recording and managing naturalist observations, developed, run and hosted by the Conservatoire d'espaces naturels Nouvelle-Aquitaine.

name: La Rochelle Université
summary: University whose Pelagis Observatory is listed as part of it among the EMPHATIC partners.

name: Lab-STICC
summary: French research laboratory with an AI and Ocean division working between AI and ocean and maritime subjects, including marine ecology.

name: Laboratoire d'Ecologie Alpine
summary: Ecology laboratory at Chambéry, named as the affiliation of Vincent Miele, who co-leads DeepFaune. Its own site refused the fetcher with a bot challenge, so nothing here comes from it.

name: Laboratoire d'informatique, de robotique et de microélectronique de Montpellier
summary: Montpellier computing and robotics laboratory, which collaborates with the ZENITH team and is a partner in the SMART-WING marine drone project.

name: Laboratoire de Biométrie et Biologie Evolutive
summary: Research laboratory named as the affiliation of Gaspard Dussert, who co-leads DeepFaune, and home of the PRABI-LBBE data centre. Its own site refused the fetcher, so nothing here comes from it.

name: Laboratoire national de métrologie et d'essais
summary: Leads the operational consortium of the Challenge IA-Biodiv, which evaluates the AI systems and builds the shared datasets.

name: Laboratory for Sciences of Climate and Environment
summary: CEA laboratory that works with INRAE on deep learning estimates of forest height at 10 metres from Sentinel and GEDI data, and on the One Forest Vision remote sensing work for the Congo basin.

name: Lacoscope
summary: Citizen science project that monitors plankton in Alpine lakes with the PlanktoScope portable microscope, and collects samples to help train an AI that recognises species.

name: LDgenX
summary: French genomics company working on environmental DNA, sequencing and bioinformatics. Its DNA EcoTrace project aims to automate biodiversity monitoring by environmental DNA.

name: Leko
summary: Bioacoustic biodiversity monitoring from Birdz. Since January 2023, seven buses in the Rouen Normandie metropolis have carried sensors that count bats, birds and grasshoppers.

name: LIFE BIODIV'FRANCE
summary: EU co-funded project coordinated by the OFB with 30 participants that supports the national biodiversity strategy, including tools for monitoring and evaluating protected area management.

name: LIFE SeaDetect
summary: Project funded by the EU LIFE programme that develops and demonstrates ways to reduce collisions between ships and marine mammals.

name: Ligue pour la Protection des Oiseaux
summary: French bird conservation charity. It runs Vol de Nuit, a citizen science programme that studies night migration by standardised acoustic monitoring.

name: Maa Biodiversity
summary: French start-up, according to ESCP's Choice magazine, that combines ecological science, forest management and environmental finance, and measures forest health with satellite imagery, soil samples and acoustic sensors.

name: MADE IN France
summary: A PEPR FORESTT project building a modelling toolbox for forest managers, starting from an application by the French forestry development institute and adding AI.

name: Maestro
summary: A geographic foundation model built by IGN from aerial and satellite images with a time dimension, released as open source and aimed first at the third version of the French forest database.

name: MARBEC
summary: Joint research unit of IRD, CNRS, Ifremer and the University of Montpellier. It works on environmental DNA for marine fauna with SPYGEN and coordinates the ADNeIA project.

name: MASSIF
summary: PEPR FORESTT project on automated monitoring and intelligent surveillance of insect biodiversity in French forests, coordinated by INRAE and led by Carole Kerdelhué.

name: MEDTRIX
summary: Mapping platform that publishes results of coastal water and ecosystem monitoring in the Mediterranean, from Andromède Océanologie.

name: MIA-Paris
summary: AgroParisTech research unit of statisticians and computer scientists working on statistical and machine learning modelling for biology, ecology and the environment.

name: Ministère de la Transition écologique, de la Biodiversité et des Négociations internationales sur le climat et la nature
summary: The French environment ministry. It published the national biodiversity strategy for 2030 and filed it with the Convention on Biological Diversity under the Kunming-Montreal framework.

name: MIRACETI
summary: French cetacean association that runs photo-identification and population monitoring in the Mediterranean, including the TURSMED 2 monitoring of bottlenose dolphins with the OFB.

name: Mission BioDivMed 2023
summary: 2023 campaign to map marine biodiversity along the French Mediterranean by environmental DNA, from the coast to the Pelagos sanctuary.

name: MONITOR
summary: Six-year project of the PEPR FORESTT programme, led by Jérôme Chave and Sylvain Schmitt, developing a high-resolution national forest monitoring system for France and its overseas territories.

name: MORFO
summary: French company founded in 2021 that restores tropical forests with drones that sow seed capsules, using drone and satellite imagery with computer vision to choose species and follow biomass, biodiversity and carbon.

name: MORINGA
summary: Open source platform for automatic land cover classification from multi-sensor imagery, started in 2015 within the THEIA hub's land cover expertise centre.

name: Mycelium
summary: Assistant inside Ecoteka for managers of urban trees and green space, built with Mistral AI on field data and scientific sources.

name: Natural Solutions
summary: Marseille company that has built digital tools for biodiversity since 2008, including GeoNature with the French national parks, the EcoSecrets camera-trap manager and the Ecoteka urban tree platform.

name: Naturalia Environnement
summary: Ecological consulting and engineering company founded in 1998, part of the consortium mapping biodiversity in Occitanie.

name: Naturefrance
summary: French public service portal on biodiversity policy, with indicators from the Observatoire national de la biodiversité.

name: Nausicaá
summary: French aquarium where the start-up VISIOON tests the PICTUM AI species recognition tool in the Californian tank.

name: Netcarbon
summary: Bordeaux-based start-up founded in 2022 that makes simulation and monitoring software for land use, carbon storage and biodiversity. VINCI Autoroutes has tested it on its land.

name: NEXVISION
summary: Company that designs the optical detection of cetaceans for the LIFE SeaDetect project, using deep learning algorithms on purpose-built electro-optics.

name: Nocturnal Bird Migration
summary: A collaborative project with more than 200 people, organised as an association, building a tool that detects and classifies the calls of birds migrating at night.

name: Noé
summary: French nature protection NGO created in 2001, with biodiversity programmes in France and Africa, including Parcs de Noé, which uses EarthRanger.

name: OBSCAMe+
summary: French programme that puts cameras on gillnetters and trawlers in the Bay of Biscay to study accidental captures of marine mammals and other protected species.

name: Observatoire de l'activité minière
summary: Observatory pooling survey and satellite data, including ONF Sentinel-2 alerts, to track gold mining and forest clearance in French Guiana over nearly twenty years, built by the ONF and run by EMOPI.

name: Observatoire des forêts françaises
summary: A forest observatory listed on IGN's institute page, with a site, map data and a resource catalogue.

name: Observatoire national de la biodiversité
summary: French multi-partner observatory that provides indicators on the state of biodiversity, the pressures on it and its interactions with society.

name: Observatoire Pelagis
summary: Marine mammal observatory at La Rochelle University, a partner in the EMPHATIC project on cetacean monitoring by eDNA and a scientific partner of OBSCAMe+.

name: OCAPI
summary: Web platform from TerrOïko for annotating camera-trap data, with automatic detection and identification of species.

name: Occitanie biodiversity mapping programme
summary: A three-year programme to build a dynamic map of natural habitats across nearly 72,000 square kilometres of the Occitanie region, combining Sentinel satellite data, about 700 field days by botanists and a frugal AI approach.

name: Occitanie regional biodiversity habitat mapping programme
summary: Three-year programme in the Occitanie region that combines satellite data, field ecology and a frugal AI approach to make a dynamic map of natural habitats over nearly 72,000 square kilometres.

name: Occupation du sol à grande échelle
summary: National large-scale land cover and land use reference, led by IGN, which uses AI object detection on aerial images to speed up production.

name: ODATIS
summary: French ocean data hub whose eight data and service centres assemble, harmonise and give access to marine datasets.

name: Office de l’Environnement de la Corse
summary: Organisation that directly manages three Corsican nature reserves: Bouches de Bonifacio, îles Cerbicales and Tre Padule de Suartone.

name: Office français de la biodiversité
summary: Public body created in 2020 to protect and restore biodiversity in mainland France and the overseas territories, under the joint oversight of the environment and agriculture ministries. National parks are attached to it.

name: Office national des forêts
summary: The public body that manages public forests in France, with 8,200 staff. It has a research, development and innovation department that has presented on operational uses of remote sensing.

name: Office pour les insectes et leur environnement
summary: French insect association founded in 1969 that carries out insect inventories for clients and takes part in the French Bugs Matter programme.

name: Oiseaux.net
summary: Volunteer-run website describing the birds of the world, with a photo identification tool for European species.

name: ORCHAMP
summary: Collaborative observatory of Alpine biodiversity and climate relations, led by Wilfried Thuiller of the Laboratoire d'Ecologie Alpine, with academic bodies, protected area managers and associations.

name: OSO land cover map
summary: Land cover map of France produced by automatic classification of Sentinel-2 image time series by CESBIO, within the Theia hub.

name: Parc amazonien de Guyane
summary: French Guiana national park that, with the gendarmerie, armed forces and ONF, contributes to the Observatoire de l'activité minière.

name: Parc national de forêts
summary: National park that runs 28 camera traps in its core area and analyses the images with CNRS's DeepFaune software to identify species.

name: Parc national de la Vanoise
summary: National park body that looks after the Vanoise park's core, which covers 53,300 hectares under special protection.

name: Parc national de Port-Cros
summary: French national park that worked with BSB Marine on EYESEA AMP, an AI vision system for automated surveillance of marine protected areas.

name: Parc national des Cévennes
summary: National park body that looks after the Cévennes national park, whose core covers 937 square kilometres.

name: Parc national des Pyrénées
summary: National park body that looks after the Pyrenees national park, which has a core zone of 45,707 hectares along the Spanish border.

name: Parc national des Écrins
summary: French national park that developed the open source GeoNature-atlas tool behind its Biodiv'Écrins atlas, and tested camera traps with AI classification for monitoring visitor numbers.

name: Parc national du Mercantour
summary: French national park with a framework agreement with Université Côte d'Azur on using AI to analyse audio and visual data on the park's animals.

name: Parc naturel régional de Corse
summary: Regional nature park that manages the Scandola nature reserve, the oldest of Corsica's reserves, dating from 1976.

name: Parc naturel régional de la Brenne
summary: Regional nature park whose identity page gives an area of 200,000 hectares.

name: Parc naturel régional de la Martinique
summary: Regional nature park covering about 63,000 hectares and 32 of Martinique's 34 communes.

name: Parc naturel régional de Lorraine
summary: Regional nature park extending over nearly 210,000 hectares and 183 communes.

name: Parc naturel régional des Vosges du Nord
summary: Regional nature park whose presentation page gives an area of 127,666 hectares, of which 15,955 hectares are protected areas.

name: Parc naturel régional du Morvan
summary: Regional nature park covering 133 communes in the four Burgundy departments since 2020, plus three partner towns.

name: Parc naturel régional du Vercors
summary: Regional nature park whose page on perimeter and key figures gives an area of 227,621 hectares, 70 percent of it forest.

name: Parc naturel régional d’Armorique
summary: Regional nature park whose identity page gives an area of 125,000 hectares and 44 member communes in Finistère.

name: Parc naturel régional Loire-Anjou-Touraine
