summary: Regional nature park covering 129 communes of Maine-et-Loire and Indre-et-Loire, protecting their natural and cultural heritage with member authorities and partners.

name: Parc naturel régional Périgord-Limousin
summary: French regional nature park that has run a programme since 2024 to identify old forests in the Dronne catchment, using an AI method developed by i-Sea.

name: Parcs de Noé
summary: Programme of the NGO Noé, listed by EarthRanger among its partners.

name: PatriNat
summary: Expertise and data centre on French natural heritage, working for the Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle, OFB, CNRS and IRD. It manages the national inventory INPN for those bodies.

name: Pelagic
summary: A research project funded by the FRB through its synthesis centre. Work partly from it used social media and deep learning to detect rare marine megafauna in video surveys.

name: PelaObs
summary: Open online tool listing the marine megafauna observations Pelagis has collected since 2003 on aerial and oceanographic surveys.

name: PEP BIOccIA
summary: An Occitanie project that uses AI to give a high-resolution map of natural habitats and predict the distribution of land species, updated yearly, with data free to use.

name: PEPR DynaBIOD
summary: Eight-year national research programme launched in June 2026 under France 2030, co-led by the national museum and the CNRS, to document and predict the dynamics of land biodiversity.

name: PEPR FORESTT
summary: A French France 2030 research programme on the socio-ecological transition of forests in temperate, Mediterranean and tropical zones, with a challenge on monitoring systems.

name: PEPR SOLU-BIOD
summary: French research programme funded under France 2030 with 44.2 million euros over 2023 to 2032, whose EQUIP action targets sensor networks, environmental DNA, drones and AI tools.

name: PICTUM
summary: AI tool from the start-up VISIOON that detects and names fish in aquarium footage. It has been tested at Nausicaá in Boulogne-sur-Mer, where a camera feeds a visitor screen.

name: PIXSEA
summary: Group of companies that collects aerial imagery of marine life and builds neural networks to detect and identify marine species and human activities.

name: Pl@ntBERT
summary: Language model for plants, trained on more than a million European vegetation plots, that predicts plant species assemblages and helps map natural habitats.

name: Planète Mer
summary: French association that runs BioLit, a national citizen science programme on coastal biodiversity.

name: Plastic Origins
summary: A citizen science project in which volunteers filmed river banks and an AI algorithm detected, counted, located and classified waste. It ended in 2025 after six years.

name: Programme national LiDAR HD
summary: IGN programme producing and releasing a 3D lidar map of the whole of France's ground and what stands on it.

name: Projet RIO
summary: A project run by CEN Guyane to develop tools and methods for assessing forest and aquatic ecosystems in French Guiana's protected areas, considering camera traps, acoustic recorders, eDNA, lidar and remote sensing.

name: Psi-Biom
summary: France 2030 project that links connected sensors, automated species recognition and ecological modelling into one chain of biodiversity data processing. Coordinated by TerrOïko.

name: PUR
summary: Landscape restoration company founded in 2008, reporting nature-based solutions across 400,000 hectares in 30 countries and listing rainforest protection and tree planting projects in Peru.

name: PureForest
summary: IGN lidar dataset on forest tree species, with 135,000 images covering 449 forests in 40 French departments.

name: Pôle national de données de biodiversité
summary: The biodiversity part of the Data Terra research infrastructure, created in 2018 with 17 partners.

name: REAUZOH
summary: Research project to inventory and map potential wetlands around Béthune with a method combining field data, satellite imagery and AI.

name: Recognition and Spatio-temporal Modeling of Animal Species in the Mercantour National Park Thanks to AI
summary: Completed project between the Mercantour National Park and Université Côte d'Azur that used AI to analyse photo and video trapping data on the park's animal species.

name: Reef Pulse
summary: Company offering coral reef monitoring and restoration through acoustics and AI since 2021, recording reef soundscapes with hydrophones.

name: Récolnat
summary: French national research infrastructure for natural history collections, led by the Muséum, with a portal of nearly 11 million images and data from over 80 institutions.

name: Région Bourgogne-Franche-Comté
summary: Regional authority that gave 20,000 euros to Réserves naturelles de France for the Thalera project.

name: Région Occitanie
summary: French regional authority that is using satellite data and AI to map natural habitats across its territory.

name: Réseau des Zones Ateliers
summary: Network of research sites chosen for ecological and socio-economic importance, covering forests, mountains, coasts, farmland and urban areas, where researchers run long-term monitoring.

name: Réseau Initiatives des Eco-Explorateurs de la Mer
summary: Association and participatory marine science network, created in 2011, which the GBIF registry says observes and monitors marine biodiversity and the Morbihan coast.

name: Réserves naturelles de France
summary: The association of French nature reserves. It runs the Thalera moth monitoring test, in which identification is partly automated with AI.

name: SEAS Guyane
summary: A satellite reception station opened in Cayenne in early 2006 to build an imagery bank from Envisat radar and SPOT optical images, built by IRD with CNES funding.

name: Seatizen Monitoring
summary: Marine monitoring site on an Ifremer host that uses autonomous surface vehicles and AI to map lagoon habitats and detect coral.

name: seewave
summary: R package for sound analysis and synthesis, with functions for ecoacoustic analyses, built by the EAR ecoacoustics research project.

name: SENSEAFR
summary: French small company developing sensors and services for monitoring ecosystem health. Its Pi-Sigma platform uses AI and neural networks, with a web portal that gives results to users.

name: SEPANLOG
summary: Organisation that has managed the Étang de la Mazière national nature reserve since its creation, leads four Natura 2000 sites and co-manages another national reserve.

name: Service hydrographique et océanographique de la marine
summary: French national hydrographic service, which collects and distributes official information for maritime navigation.

name: SMART-BIODIV
summary: A French consortium in the Challenge IA-Biodiv that uses machine learning to fill gaps in coastal marine biodiversity data and build indicators, drawing on plankton images.

name: Société Française pour l'Etude et la Protection des Mammifères
summary: French mammal study and protection society. Its 2024 report describes 24 sites monitored by camera traps.

name: Société nationale de protection de la nature
summary: Organisation that manages three national nature reserves in wetlands, including the Camargue and Grand-Lieu reserves.

name: SonoChiro
summary: Software that automatically analyses bat ultrasound recordings and identifies 111 bat species.

name: SONOSYLVA
summary: French project led by the OFB and the Muséum to monitor forest biodiversity in protected areas by acoustics, recording 110 sites across mainland France from 2024 to 2026.

name: Sorbonne Université
summary: University that, with the CNRS, hosts the research units at the Station Biologique de Roscoff, which it runs.

name: Station Biologique de Roscoff
summary: Marine station in Brittany whose Plankton Group work led to the PR2 reference sequence database, and where ATLASea has run sampling campaigns.

name: SUivi des FOrêts par SATellites
summary: Near-real-time map of clear-cuts in mainland French forests, made from Sentinel-1 radar data and distributed through the Theia data centre.

name: Surfnet
summary: AI model developed by Surfrider to count litter on river banks from video. Open source, within the Plastic Origins project.

name: Surfrider Foundation Europe
summary: Non-profit that protects lakes, rivers, the ocean and the coast. Its volunteers built Plastic Origins, a citizen science programme that used AI to detect waste on river banks, which ended in 2025.

name: SWIFTT
summary: Horizon Europe project coordinated by AXA Climate that combines Copernicus satellite data and machine learning so foresters can map dieback and windthrow.

name: Symbiose
summary: Deeptech company using AI, remote sensing and high-performance computing to monitor forests, according to a Station F job listing.

name: Syndicat mixte de gestion des milieux naturels
summary: Joint authority that manages three national nature reserves in the Landes, including the Marais d'Orx.

name: Syndicat mixte de gestion du Parc naturel régional du Luberon
summary: Joint authority for the Luberon regional nature park, which decides the park's actions together with its deliberative assemblies.

name: Syndicat mixte de la Grande Dune du Pilat
summary: Joint authority that manages the public lands of the Dune du Pilat Grand Site, in particular those entrusted by the Conservatoire du littoral.

name: Syndicat mixte de l’EPTB Seine Grands Lacs
summary: River basin public establishment responsible for four reservoir lakes in the Seine basin, with a stated purpose that includes preserving and restoring aquatic ecosystem and wetland biodiversity.

name: Syndicat mixte des espaces littoraux de la Manche
summary: Joint authority whose sea missions, including management, awareness-raising and scientific monitoring, were listed as a presentation topic for 14 August in the summer 2025 Chausey programme.

name: Syndicat mixte du Grand Site Cap d’Erquy – Cap Fréhel
summary: Public establishment created in 1992 to protect biodiversity and landscapes and welcome visitors at the Cap d'Erquy – Cap Fréhel Grand Site, and operator of the terrestrial zone of its Natura 2000 site.

name: Syndicat mixte du Parc naturel régional des Grands Causses
summary: Joint authority that leads territorial policies for the Grands Causses regional nature park.

name: Syndicat mixte du Parc naturel régional du Marais poitevin
summary: Joint authority for a regional nature park covering 88 communes in three departments over 200,000 hectares.

name: Syndicat mixte d’aménagement et de gestion du Parc naturel régional des Landes de Gascogne
summary: Joint authority whose page gives the Landes de Gascogne regional nature park 53 communes in Gironde and Landes over 360,000 hectares.

name: Syndicat mixte d’aménagement et gestion des étangs et rigoles
summary: Joint authority that manages the Étangs et rigoles d'Yveline national nature reserve.

name: Syndicat mixte Eden 62
summary: A joint public body that manages the sensitive natural areas of the Pas-de-Calais, owned by the Département, the Conservatoire du littoral or communes.

name: Syndicat mixte pour la protection et la gestion de la Camargue gardoise
summary: A joint public body that, according to its own 2024 internship advert, manages more than 1,700 hectares of natural areas owned by the Département and others.

name: Système d'information de l'inventaire du patrimoine naturel
summary: French national network that shares natural heritage data among the environment ministry, the OFB, the Muséum, associations, local authorities and other bodies under common rules.

name: Système d'information sur la biodiversité
summary: French system that federates data from 31 public policies on biodiversity and gives open access to it, through services including Naturefrance and the INPN.

name: Tadarida
summary: Open software for sound identification, with a sonotype classifier that has been retrained for bats in the Republic of Congo.

name: TAXREF
summary: France's national taxonomic reference, which lists the scientific and common names of all living things on French territory, developed by PatriNat since 2003.

name: TEMPO
summary: Network that monitors Posidonia meadows along the whole French Mediterranean coast, operated since 2011 by Andromède Océanologie with the support of the Agence de l'eau Rhône Méditerranée et Corse.

name: Terres australes et antarctiques françaises
summary: The territory administration, under a prefect, that covers biodiversity preservation in the French Southern and Antarctic Lands, whose southern islands form France's largest national nature reserve.

name: Territoires, Environnement, Télédétection et Information Spatiale
summary: French remote sensing research unit named as the collaborating unit of the EVERGREEN machine learning team.

name: TerrOïko
summary: French company founded in 2012 by two ecologists that builds digital tools for processing, analysing and modelling biodiversity data, including the OCAPI camera-trap annotation platform.

name: Thalera
summary: A test of the EU pollinator monitoring scheme's moth protocol on 16 sites in Bourgogne-Franche-Comté and 2 in the Pyrénées-Orientales, with identification partly automated by AI.

name: Theia
summary: The land surface data and services hub of the Data Terra research infrastructure, covering cryosphere, continental waters, land cover, agrosystems and biodiversity, and imagery.

name: TotalEnergies Monitoring Toolbox
summary: Tools used by TotalEnergies researchers at the Jean Féger centre in Pau for large-scale species inventories in the Béarn region, including acoustic ecology and AI analysis of sound and images.

name: TropiSCO
summary: A deforestation detection platform, online and open since 27 June 2022, that uses Sentinel-1 radar images to detect deforestation 6 to 12 days after the event, depending on the area.

name: Tēnaka
summary: Paris-registered coral reef and mangrove restoration company whose underwater station collects reef data in marine protected areas, with machine learning applied to 360-degree photographs for impact reports.

name: UMR AMAP
summary: Montpellier research unit whose BIAS theme develops automatic methods, notably deep learning, to identify and quantify biological structures, including for species distribution models.

name: UMR LETG
summary: French joint research unit in coastal environment, remote sensing and geomatics, which runs the D2T drone and remote sensing platform.

name: Université Côte d'Azur
summary: French university that signed a framework agreement with the Parc national du Mercantour on using AI to study the park's biodiversity.

name: Université de Bretagne Occidentale
summary: An institution listed for EQUIPONANT, a laureate of the first PEPR SOLU-BIOD equipment call.

name: Université de Montpellier
summary: French university, a founding member of Vigilife and the listed affiliation of the MARBEC coordinator of FISH-PREDICT.

name: Université de Toulouse
summary: A university that runs CESBIO, a joint research unit making heavy use of satellite remote sensing to study the land biosphere, and is one of its parent bodies.

name: Veolia Connected Solutions
summary: Unit of Veolia that developed Leko, an acoustic device for identifying animal species, with the national natural history museum.

name: Vigie-Chiro
summary: A French acoustic monitoring programme running since 2006 for bats, bush-crickets and other sound-making animals, identified by the Tadarida software.

name: Vigie-Nature
summary: A French citizen science programme of volunteer observers, founded by the Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle.

name: VISIOON
summary: Start-up founded by marine ecologist Delphine Mallet, specialising in image and video processing of marine life. It developed PICTUM, an AI fish recognition tool.

name: Vol de Nuit
summary: A citizen science programme on the LPO site that studies the night migration of birds by standardised acoustic monitoring.

name: WIPSEA
summary: French small company at Lancieux, Brittany, listed by CORDIS as a participant in the WildDrone project, with its participation marked as ended.

name: WWF France
summary: The French office of WWF. Its team in French Guiana coordinates the Gardiens du Haut-Maroni project, in which local people use camera traps to monitor forest health.

name: ZENITH
summary: Inria scientific data management team, with the CNRS and the Université de Montpellier, whose work covers machine learning for biodiversity and the Pl@ntNet platform.

name: Équipe IROKO
summary: Research team at LIRMM in Montpellier that applies and improves data science for environmental science, including human-in-the-loop machine learning on citizen science data.

name: Établissement public du Marais poitevin
summary: Public body that coordinates water and biodiversity management on the Marais poitevin wetland and its feeding catchments, an intervention area of 639,000 hectares.

name: États Sauvages
summary: Organisation that acquired more than 5 hectares of forest in 2021 through a public campaign and in March 2022 appealed for donations to buy a four-hectare Vosges parcel.

name: AfriSAR
summary: A 2016 NASA campaign with ESA, DLR and AGEOS, flown in Gabon from 27 February to 8 March, collected lidar canopy and biomass data at five sites, with field plot data from the Mondah Forest used to train models.

name: Agence Gabonaise d'Etudes et d'Observations Spatiales
summary: Gabon's publicly funded space agency in Libreville, set up in 2010 to collect and analyse Earth observation data, which maintains a USGS Landsat ground station and completed a 2018 forest cover map.

name: Agence Nationale des Parcs Nationaux
summary: Gabon's national parks agency, which runs a wildlife genetics laboratory, uses Skylight and EarthRanger, and is reported to have worked with partners on AI wildlife monitoring and camera trap and acoustic deployments.

name: ANPN and Olam Palm Gabon human-elephant conflict study
summary: A planned three-year study in Ngounié and Moyen-Ogooué, covered by a cooperation agreement signed on 27 June 2022, would count forest elephants using DNA and track them with GPS collars and camera traps.

name: Assessing defaunation in Ivindo National Park
summary: Combines camera traps, acoustic recorders and terrestrial LiDAR to estimate species occupancy and abundance in Ivindo; a 2023–2024 Bass Connections team tested combined data using Bayesian models.

name: Atlas Forestier Interactif du Gabon
summary: A pilot public atlas of Gabon's forest sector, described by WRI in 2009, which WRI reported in 2012 was combining forestry, mining and conservation land-use data under two ministries.

name: Aventures Sans Frontières
summary: A non-governmental organisation whose experts, with ANPN eco-guards, were reported in March 2026 to watch turtle nests at Pongara National Park around the clock.

name: Brainforest
summary: A Gabonese organisation whose president, Marc Ona, described it to EIA as specialised in the independent monitoring of timber flows.

name: Cartographie de l'occupation du sol du Gabon 2010 et 2015
summary: Land cover maps for 2010 and 2015 and a change map, made by AGEOS under the OSFACO programme and described as the first national reference map, showing forests at 89% of Gabon in 2015.

name: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique et Technologique
summary: A national research centre created in 1976, including IRET, which One Forest Vision says co-organised October 2026 Libreville training on DeepForestVision and DeepForestSound through IRET.

name: Centre National des Données et de l'Information Océanographiques
summary: Active Gabonese oceanographic data centre, created on the initiative of the IOC-UNESCO ODINAFRICA project, that holds the Gabon Marine Turtle Partnership's sea turtle database and manages oceanographic data collection, processing and distribution.

name: Conservation of Biodiversity in Tropical Forest through Sustainable Coexistence between Human and Wild Animals
summary: A finished Kyoto University and IRET project established an IRET laboratory and aimed to study Moukalaba-Doudou ecosystems and genetic diversity and habituate gorillas and chimpanzees.

name: Drone mapping of the Bas-Ogooué wetlands
summary: A Nature Conservancy drone survey of 30 wetland transects in and outside the Bas-Ogooué Ramsar site, reported in September 2016, gathered 2-centimetre imagery to identify 15 habitat types for checking NASA radar data.

name: Dénombrement des oiseaux d'eau au Gabon
summary: A national waterbird count, reported in January 2022 as running for twenty years through a network of amateur and professional ornithologists, covering Akanda, Pongara and Cap Lopez with 3,000 to 6,000 birds counted annually.

name: Eramet-Comilog ecological monitoring pilot with Mozaic Earth and Gentian
summary: A closed ecological monitoring pilot on five plots at Eramet-Comilog sites, tested by Mozaic Earth and Gentian with the Fondation Lékédi Biodiversité from September to December 2025.

name: Etude de la mégafaune aquatique de la lagune Iguela et la lagune Banio pour une conservation et une gestion durable
summary: Small grant project on aquatic megafauna in Iguela and Banio lagoons, with IRAF as the entity, requesting and receiving 49,769,400 FCFA from FPBG; its status is unknown.

name: Fondation Lékédi Biodiversité
summary: A foundation established jointly by Comilog and Eramet, whose executive director said in April 2022 that its camera traps had filmed giant pangolins and spotted otters.

name: Fonds de Préservation de la Biodiversité au Gabon
summary: Active fund that describes itself as an international non-profit (501c3) for biodiversity conservation and sustainable development in Gabon, with board-approved small grants totalling 763,596,149 FCFA.

name: Forest Ecosystem Research and Monitoring
summary: A CAFI-funded project, run by The Nature Conservancy from October 2022 to March 2027 with $2,492,310 listed, to strengthen SNORNF and support long-term ecological monitoring sites.

name: Forest Foresight in Gabon
summary: A Forest Foresight deployment in Gabon, extended from some areas to the whole national territory after the government and WWF signed a governance agreement on 20 December 2024.

name: Gabon Biodiversity Collection
summary: A zoological reference collection described as the largest known in Central Africa, with 123,000 specimens, from which four datasets are published on GBIF, one with a title and description that disagree.

name: Gabon Convention on Biological Diversity Clearing House Mechanism
summary: Gabon's national Convention on Biological Diversity clearing-house website, with sections on biodiversity facts, national targets and implementation, and a page on ANPN published on 2 February 2022.

name: Gabon Environnement
summary: NGO of unknown current status that, according to the Programme de Petites Initiatives, completed a seven-month turtle conservation project in Mayumba National Park under a 15 December 2006 agreement, including daily monitoring of 17 km of beach and Argos tracking of leatherbacks.

name: Gabon marine biodiversity atlas
summary: A marine biodiversity atlas compiling marine, biological, extractive industry and political data, built by WCS Gabon and the University of Exeter, which WCS says has been invaluable for government marine protected area planning.

name: Gabon national forest elephant survey
summary: A closed national survey that reported in November 2021 an estimate of 95,000 forest elephants in Gabon, based on 4,058 dung samples from 18 sites, and used ANPN's genetics laboratory.

name: Gabon: Developing a National Land Use Plan and a Forest Monitoring System
summary: A closed CAFI-funded project run by AFD, with $18,428,689 listed for 2018–2025, aiming to finalise SNORNF, which CAFI reports produced maps validated with 908 villages.

name: GABONX
summary: A five-week DLR-led airborne measurement campaign in Gabon, reported complete in August 2023, flew seven tropical rainforest areas and built on AfriSAR flights from 2016 to compare biomass loss or regrowth.

name: Global Fishing Watch in Gabon
summary: A collaboration run by Global Fishing Watch with Gabon since 2020, including a June 2025 memorandum of understanding on sharing fisheries data for monitoring, control and surveillance.

name: Herbier National du Gabon
summary: Gabon's national herbarium, created in 1984 within a CENAREST institute, which publishes six GBIF datasets including the Gabon Vascular Plant Occurrences dataset under CC BY 4.0.

name: IBONGA-ACPE
summary: Active Gabonese NGO whose main marine programme monitors and protects turtles as ecosystem bio-indicators, with permanent patrol camps and objectives including collecting coastal activity and habitat data.

name: Institut de Recherche en Écologie Tropicale
summary: A research institute created in 1985 and run by CENAREST, which studies Gabon's ecosystems and, CAFI reports, now monitors 24 forest plots transferred from Duke University.

name: Institut de Recherches Agronomiques et Forestières
summary: A public institution under three ministries that holds Gabon's largest fish collection, about 10,000 specimens, and publishes a 2,784-record ichthyology dataset through GBIF, with FPBG small-grant funding for lagoon megafauna study.

name: Inventaire des Ressources Naturelles
summary: A dataset attributed to ANPN by a CNC official, with SalvaTerra reporting 338 permanent plots measured and 81 being defined for 2025 for CAFI and the CNC.

name: Ipassa research station
summary: A research station rehabilitated and made operational with $313,966 of CAFI support to IRET, where historical transects were restored and 24 forest plots transferred from Duke University are now monitored.

name: Laboratoire de Génétique de la Faune de l'ANPN
summary: A wildlife genetics laboratory run by ANPN, inaugurated on 11 March 2021 and reported as the first of its kind in Central Africa, funded by the World Bank and AFD.

name: Laboratoire de Géomatique, de Recherche Appliquée et de Conseil
summary: Active laboratory in the Department of Geographical, Environmental and Marine Sciences at Université Omar Bongo, whose funded projects include remote sensing of forest degradation risk (MORIDEF, 2013 to 2014) and mangrove monitoring and modelling.

name: Langoué Bai monitoring
summary: A WCS Gabon programme at Langoué Bai, the organisation's longest-term bai monitoring project in Central Africa, collecting data on elephants, gorillas and buffalo.

name: Loango western gorilla long-term research project
summary: A long-term western gorilla study in Loango National Park begun in 2005 by Martha Robbins of the Max Planck Institute, whose field site added camera traps in 2009, including 45 traps over 60 km² in 2009 to 2010.

name: Lopé long-term tree phenology monitoring
summary: A 2017 DataSTORRE dataset reports monthly crown observations of leaf, flower and fruit phenology for 88 plant species at Lopé National Park since 1984.

name: Mandrillus Face Database
summary: Active dataset with Projet Mandrillus affiliation, containing 29,495 wild mandrill portraits from 2012–2021 at 224 × 224 pixels, field-identified by assistants and licensed under CC BY 4.0.

name: Mandrillus Project
summary: A field project founded in 2012 in Lékédi Park, built by Marie Charpentier, which has recorded tens of thousands of observation hours on more than 300 habituated mandrills.

name: Ministère des Eaux et Forêts, de l'Environnement, du Climat, chargé du Conflit Homme-Faune
summary: Gabon's ministry for water, forests and the environment, which supervises and coordinates public policy on those areas and organised the launch of data collection for the seventh CBD national report in February 2026.

name: National Natural Resources and Forestry Observation System
summary: Gabon's national forest monitoring system, supported by CAFI since 2018, which CAFI reports sent 18,370 deforestation alerts to authorities, 508 of them followed by field operations.

name: Nsombou Abalghe-Dzal Association
summary: A local NGO supporting about twenty villages in Ogooué-Ivindo with sustainable hunting management, which installed camera traps in the Massaha area in 2023 and supports the Massaha community's proposed 11,300-hectare conserved area.

name: Ozouga Chimpanzee Project
summary: An active study of a chimpanzee population in Gabon's rainforest since 2005, using camera traps shared with Chimp&See and faecal genetics that identified seven communities, led by Simone Pika and Tobias Deschner.

name: Pacific co-existence between humans and elephants
summary: A CAFI-funded project run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, with $10,000,003 listed for 2025 to 2027, which CAFI reports piloted elephant early-warning systems and installed 1,608 mobile electric fences by 30 June 2026.

name: Panthera camera-trap monitoring and lion restoration in Plateaux Batéké National Park
summary: A Panthera-run camera-trap programme in Plateaux Batéké National Park, which Panthera says showed a 99.5% fall in poacher capture rates between 2001-2003 and 2017-2018, alongside a 2020–2022 lion restoration project.

name: Partenariat pour les Tortues Marines du Gabon
summary: A Gabonese sea turtle conservation network that WCS says it created with governmental and non-governmental partners since 2005, monitoring conservation status through research along the whole coastline.

name: Pl@ntNet field training in Gabon, 2025
summary: A closed five-day Pl@ntNet field training in May 2025, run between CENAREST and the Arboretum Raponda Walker, which was the first in Gabon and tested the app in real conditions.

name: Planification Nationale de l'Affectation des Terres et Système National d'Observation des Ressources Naturelles et des Forêts
summary: A closed five-year programme begun in March 2019 with 18.4 million US dollars from CAFI, covering national land-use planning and natural resource observation, including mapping of 117 villages in 2022.

name: Projet de développement d'un système d'inventaire des ressources forestières nationales
summary: A JICA-run forest inventory project in Gabon that presented results in February 2018 after five years of field work, producing stratification maps and a database, with 299 of 688 planned plots inventoried by end 2017.

name: Projet de surveillance environnementale au Gabon
summary: A Gabonese environmental monitoring project funded by the Direction Générale du Trésor, whose aircraft made its inaugural flight on 5 June 2024 to monitor mangrove destruction, fishing, poaching and gold panning.

name: Protectrice des Grands Singes de la Moukalaba
summary: A July 2020 report describes a Gabonese conservation NGO established in 2004, working near Moukalaba-Doudou National Park on honey production, gorilla tracking and ecotourism.

name: Real-time alerts from AI-enabled camera traps, Lopé National Park pilot
summary: A closed pilot in Lopé National Park, led and built by the University of Stirling and Hack the Planet, in which five AI camera systems recognised elephants with 82% accuracy and alerted rangers within seven minutes on average.

name: Sharks ADNe
summary: A project aiming to characterise shark and ray communities along Gabon's coast by detecting elasmobranch DNA in seawater, mapping important areas and exploring patterns over two hydrological seasons.

name: Smithsonian Gabon Biodiversity Program
summary: A programme publishing four GBIF datasets from a 123,000-specimen collection described as the largest zoological reference collection known in Central Africa.

name: Soutenir la surveillance indépendante des forêts via le portail Open Timber
summary: A Brainforest project, being implemented in June 2023, supports independent forest monitoring through the Open Timber portal, with a June 2023 workshop aiming to adopt an observation strategy and set up a report review committee in Gabon.

name: Station d'Études des Gorilles et Chimpanzés
summary: A research station at Lopé National Park that hosted October 2026 work to harmonise and validate environmental and wildlife data collection protocols.

name: SUMAG
summary: Closed project, run by the Laboratoire de Géomatique, de Recherche Appliquée et de Conseil, to build a platform for monitoring and managing Gabon's mangroves, which received the SCO label in March 2024.

name: Système National de Traçabilité du Bois du Gabon
summary: Gabon's national timber traceability system, built by EIA and Code4Nature, which ATIBT reported in October 2023 had to be adopted by the whole forest sector within six months.

name: TRACER Nkok
summary: A dormant due diligence service on log suppliers to the Nkok special economic zone, in place since October 2018, whose activities the forest administration ordered suspended on 7 March 2023.

name: Université Omar Bongo
summary: A university whose LAGRAC laboratory sits in its Department of Geographical, Environmental and Marine Sciences and has funded projects including SUMAG-1, a platform for characterising and monitoring Gabon's mangroves.

name: Utilisation des images satellitaires pour accompagner les processus de cartographie participative des ressources forestières
summary: Closed project, run by Brainforest and listed in its 2024 archive, that used satellite images to support participatory mapping of forest resources, following its 2009 to 2011 Congo Basin mapping project that used basic methods.

name: WCS Gabon
summary: Active programme run by WCS, whose Gabon page describes Central African monitoring, including long-term work at Langoué Bai, and acoustic assessment of bais with the Elephant Listening Project.

name: WWF-Gabon
summary: Its national director described Forest Foresight as detecting illegal deforestation about six months ahead, while Gabonreview reports WWF signed a government governance agreement in December 2024.

name: 1000 Rivers eDNA Project
summary: Non-profit citizen science project led by NatureMetrics with the University of Hull, using eDNA to record fish in UK rivers.

name: 2Excel Geo
summary: Airborne hyperspectral survey company supporting environmental applications, including tree condition analysis.

name: 2Excel woodland mapping initiative
summary: UK Space Agency highlighted project exploring new satellites to assess woodland condition. The blog names 2Excel but not which 2Excel company runs it.

name: A deep learning model for global camera trap labelling
summary: Completed Brunel project, with a co-investigator from the Zoological Society of London, on automating species labelling of camera trap images.

name: AAC Clyde Space
summary: Glasgow satellite company building THICKET, a habitat mapping tool for farmers.

name: Aberdeen Bay Spoor seabird AI trial
summary: Trial by Vattenfall, Spoor and the British Trust for Ornithology using AI to record the 3D flight of seabirds around offshore wind turbines.

name: Abriachan Forest Trust
summary: Community trust managing the forest at Abriachan, aiming to improve and sustain biodiversity through sensitive land and forest management.

name: ACCURATE project
summary: Project to synthesise knowledge on acoustic cue rates and cue stability for marine mammal density estimation, led by CREEM at the University of St Andrews and funded by the US Navy.

name: Acua Ocean
summary: Early-stage UK business designing autonomous, hydrogen-fuelled surface vessels, a partner in the MOBI project.

name: ADAS
summary: Named as a partner in River Deep Mountain AI, which builds open models for river health.

name: Additive Catchments
summary: Company offering Catchment Monitoring as a Service, which tracks nature recovery in river catchments.

name: Aderyn
summary: Online biodiversity information and reporting database for Wales, developed by the four Local Environmental Records Centres.

name: Advanced Research and Invention Agency
summary: UK government research funding agency. Its £81 million Forecasting Tipping Points programme funds TiMBER, which studies tipping points in marine ecosystems.

name: Agri-Food and Biosciences Institute
summary: Northern Ireland research institute with an author on a review of machine learning in marine ecology.

name: Agtelligence
summary: Company combining satellite data and AI into risk and compliance intelligence, with a FarmScore service giving farm-level deforestation risk and land-use change views for coffee farms; registered in England and Wales.

name: AgZero+
summary: UK programme under which the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology installs automated camera traps and bioacoustic equipment on farms to assess agri-environment schemes.

name: AI and Autonomous Systems for Assessing Biodiversity and Ecosystem Health
summary: University of Southampton research project on AI and autonomous systems for assessing biodiversity and ecosystem health.

name: AI classification of wildflower seeds
summary: Earlham Institute study using machine learning on over 145,000 flatbed scanner images to classify native wildflower seeds used in restoration.

name: AI for Climate & Nature (University of Cambridge)
summary: University of Cambridge research community developing AI that brings together datasets on climate and biodiversity, with projects on a conservation chatbot, forest monitoring and land use.

name: AI for Earth Observation, British Antarctic Survey
summary: BAS project developing AI tools to detect icebergs, sea ice, ice floes and wildlife from satellite imagery.

name: AI for environmental science
summary: NERC funding call with a total of £4.8 million and awards of £200,000 to £400,000. Its terrestrial ecology area covers AI for insight into ecosystem and biodiversity change.

name: AI for Forest Monitoring (University of Cambridge)
summary: Cambridge project using AI and drones to turn laser scans of European forests into individual trees and ecological measures for carbon and biodiversity accounting.

name: AI Librarian for Ecological Archives
summary: Exeter project with Natural Resources Wales on a verifiable AI assistant that turns environmental documents into citable planning evidence.

name: AI to detect pollutants harmful to lake biodiversity
summary: University of Birmingham AI analysis of water and biofilm samples from 52 English lakes that links pollutants to biodiversity loss.

name: AI-Hab: Using artificial intelligence for automated habitat assessment
summary: NERC award to the University of Lincoln for automated habitat assessment using AI.

name: AI-INTERVENE: AI for Unlocking Datasets for Biodiversity Assessment and Prediction
summary: NERC award to the University of Reading for AI to unlock datasets for biodiversity assessment and prediction.

name: AI4Peat
summary: Natural England tool that maps upland peat drainage and damage in England with deep learning on aerial imagery.

name: Aigas Community Forest
summary: Community body that had acquired the 270 hectare Aigas Forest in Strathglass by 2018 and has developed it since.

name: Albatross Drones
summary: Environmental consultancy using drones, GIS and mapping software to survey and monitor protected species and habitats across the UK. No AI is shown on the page read.

name: AMBER project
summary: Research programme of the Alan Turing Institute and UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology, funded by the abrdn Charitable Foundation, that deploys automated sensors with AI to monitor insects, bats and birds.

name: AMBER: Automated Monitoring of Biodiversity via eDNA Recovery
summary: Project to process marine eDNA in near real time on lab-on-a-chip technology, won by Platform Kinetics and Intuitiq. No page read says which of the two leads.

name: Amelia Space Technologies
summary: Company with a geospatial AI platform whose projects include satellite detection of harmful algal blooms in the UK's largest freshwater lake.

name: Amphibian and Reptile Conservation
summary: UK amphibian and reptile conservation charity that publishes species datasets on GBIF.

name: Amphibian and Reptile Groups of the UK
summary: Network of volunteer groups that runs the Record Pool online recording service and the ARGWEB survey toolkit.

name: Ancient Tree Inventory
summary: Woodland Trust inventory where people add and search records of ancient trees.

name: Anglian Water
summary: Water company named as a partner in River Deep Mountain AI, which builds open models for river health.

name: APEM
summary: Environmental consultancy whose remote sensing team uses satellites and aerial surveys to model land use, condition and type. It says its work is a benchmark for aerial survey design in the UK for offshore wind.

name: Applied Genomics
summary: UK DNA ecology laboratory and consultancy that says it uses machine learning on biodiversity data. Supplier on a JNCC benthic eDNA trial.

name: Aquaread
summary: UK designer and maker of multiparameter water quality instruments, on a 2012 trade page. Current status not read.

name: ARBOR
summary: Artificial intelligence plugin for forest monitoring, developed by OSINFOR and the University of Sheffield and trained on drone data from the Peruvian Amazon.

name: Arts and Humanities Research Council

name: Autospray Systems
summary: Company with an Innovate UK award for nature recovery at scale with long-range drone operations.

name: Auyan

summary: Welsh university with authors on machine learning and remote sensing for forest biomass and land cover.

name: Beachwatch

name: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust

name: Better Biodiversity Data project
summary: Project to improve access to biodiversity data in Scotland, first delivered between 2023 and 2025.

name: Biodiverse Landscapes Fund
summary: UK government fund that aims to protect and restore nature, tackle climate change and reduce poverty.

name: British and Irish Bryological Society
summary: Society that publishes bryophyte records for Great Britain and Ireland on GBIF.

name: British Hedgehog Preservation Society
summary: Wildlife charity that co-leads the National Hedgehog Monitoring Programme.

name: British Lichen Society

name: British Mycological Society
summary: Society that publishes the Fungal Records Database of Britain and Ireland on GBIF.

name: British Trust for Ornithology

name: Broads Authority

name: Brunel University London
summary: University whose Intelligent Data Analysis group ran a deep learning project on labelling camera trap images.

name: Buglife

summary: Company that, with Caerphilly County Borough Council, created a geospatial land assessment tool for investment in natural capital.

summary: NERC-funded study at the University of Plymouth.

name: Harnessing AI to catalyse biodiversity recovery
summary: Royal Society University Research Fellowship of Thomas Frederick Johnson at the University of Sheffield, announced in 2026.

name: Harper Adams University
summary: Shropshire university running the Green Box bird monitoring project with smart sensors and AI.

name: Hawk and Owl Trust
summary: Charity that creates and manages nesting, roosting and feeding habitats for owls and birds of prey, and runs wildlife reserves.

name: Hebridean Whale & Dolphin Trust
summary: Charity that has collected sightings and photographs of whales and dolphins in the Hebrides for 30 years and is scoping AI photo identification.

name: Hedgehogs in Focus
summary: Planned PTES initiative combining citizen science and AI with a nationwide camera trap network on hedgehogs, at development grant stage.

name: Hello Lamp Post
summary: Company whose AI conversation platform underlies the Environment Agency's WaterWatch and BluePrint public reporting tools.

name: Hemsworth Farms
summary: Farm partnership with an Innovate UK award for continuous biodiversity monitoring.

name: Herefordshire Wildlife Trust
summary: Wildlife trust that says it cares for a network of nature reserves in Herefordshire.

name: Heriot-Watt University
summary: University with an author on species classification from DNA barcodes with deep learning.

name: HiDef Aerial Surveying
summary: Digital aerial offshore wildlife survey company, part of the BioConsult SH group. No page read shows AI.

name: Highlands & Islands Environment Foundation
summary: Scottish funder that made a grant for AI in marine mammal research.

name: Highlands and Islands Enterprise
summary: Scottish regional development agency that part-funded a commercial marine eDNA laboratory in Argyll.

name: Highlands Rewilding
summary: Scottish rewilding company that treats its estates as open-air natural capital laboratories, monitoring them with thermal drones, eDNA, camera traps and BIOSCAN insect sampling, and aims to publish the research and data openly.

name: Howden

name: Howden biodiversity risk monitoring tool
summary: UK Space Agency funded project in the Howden Resilience Laboratory, with PCI Geomatics, to monitor biodiversity risk on land sites from satellite data and AI. The fact comes from Insurance Business.

name: HR Wallingford
summary: Oxfordshire organisation leading EO4Biodiversity.

name: HumBug II: enabling large-scale acoustic monitoring for invasive insect species
summary: Listed in the March 2024 Innovation in Environmental Monitoring announcement with Dr Yunpeng Li of the University of Surrey, addressing acoustic monitoring for invasive insect species.

name: HydroSurv Unmanned Survey (UK)
summary: Maker of robotic survey vessels that led a project on subtidal seagrass survey with the University of Plymouth.

name: Ignite Labs: Space for Nature & Biodiversity
summary: Innovate UK programme with NatWest helping businesses and financial institutions use satellite data, AI and cloud computing for biodiversity. The Satellite Applications Catapult published the case study and took part.

name: Improving Observation Capabilities of Biodiversity in UK Waters
summary: £2.1 million two-phase Innovate UK and Defra competition, part of the marine Natural Capital and Ecosystem Assessment, funding machine learning and eDNA tools. No page read says which body runs it.

name: Indicia
summary: Open source toolkit for building online biological recording websites, which the Biological Records Centre says it helped create.

name: Informed Solutions
summary: Company that built InformedDECISION, an AI planning decision support platform first used by NatureScot.

name: InformedDECISION
summary: Planning decision support platform that combines mapping, data analytics, satellite imagery and AI to answer land management questions, first used by NatureScot.

name: Innovate 4 Nature
summary: UKCEH-led, Defra-funded programme that gathers evidence on what low and middle income countries need to adopt biodiversity monitoring technologies, including AI.

name: Innovate UK
summary: UK innovation agency that awarded £2 million to six AI projects on environmental monitoring and investment in nature.

name: Innovation in Environmental Monitoring
summary: A programme announced in March 2024 by UKRI, with £12 million from NERC, Defra and Innovate UK for new environmental sensing systems, including projects using artificial intelligence, airborne DNA and audio monitoring.

name: Integrated Land Management
summary: Corby-based company supplying off-site biodiversity units from a nationwide network of registered habitat banks, saying it runs the whole process from habitat design to ongoing management, with 30 years of habitat management.

name: Integrating Finance and Biodiversity for a Nature Positive Future
summary: Seven million pound programme co-led by NERC and Innovate UK to embed the value of biodiversity in financial decisions, including grants for data and AI projects.

name: Intelligent Earth Centre
summary: Oxford centre announced in 2023 at the meeting of AI and environmental science, with a £12 million UKRI grant to train almost 100 PhD students. Oxford's own site refuses automated readers, so this comes from the student newspaper Cherwell.

name: Intuitiq
summary: Leeds-registered company named with Platform Kinetics as a winner of a Defra and Innovate UK award to build an automated marine eDNA monitoring system.

name: iRecord
summary: UK website for entering wildlife records, with verification and record checks and data sharing.

name: Isle of May Bird Observatory
summary: A bird observatory founded in 1934, administered by a Scottish charitable trust and staffed by visiting volunteers between March and November, who record and ring birds moving through the island.

name: Isles of Scilly Wildlife Trust
summary: Charity that looks after around half of the Isles of Scilly.

name: iSpot
summary: Citizen science identification project developed and run by The Open University, whose website has closed; its British Isles observations remain on GBIF.

name: Jacobs
summary: Consultancy listed in the CIEEM 2024 Best Practice Innovation award for radio tracking with remote data collection.

name: James Hutton Institute
summary: Scottish research institute with machine learning staff, peatland remote sensing work and a commercial eDNA metabarcoding service.

name: JET Engineering System Solutions
summary: Company with an award for natural capital monitoring through 5G multi-sensor integration.

name: John Ellerman Foundation
summary: UK grant-making foundation that gave the National Biodiversity Network Trust £120,000 for organisational resilience.

name: John Muir Trust
summary: Organisation that says it owns, and works in partnership to care for, wild places including Ben Nevis, Schiehallion and Sandwood Bay.

name: Joint Nature Conservation Committee
summary: The statutory nature adviser to all four countries of the UK. Its site carries the UK's 7th National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity, which assesses progress against targets aligned with the Kunming-Montreal framework.

name: Keen AI
summary: Technology firm that built, with UKCEH, AI software identifying plants beside railway lines from train cameras.

name: Kent Wildlife Trust
summary: County conservation charity in Kent that runs the Bugs Matter insect recording app with Buglife.

name: Knepp Estate
summary: Estate that describes itself as a 3,500-acre rewilding project in Sussex.

name: Knoydart Foundation
summary: Foundation under whose community ownership about 7,000 hectares on the Knoydart peninsula, a National Scenic Area, is held.

name: Lake District National Park Authority
summary: Authority responsible for conserving and enhancing the natural beauty, wildlife and cultural heritage of the Lake District.

name: Lancaster City Council
summary: District council in Lancashire testing AI habitat mapping for Local Plan biodiversity assessments.

name: Lancaster University
summary: University with authors on deep learning for satellite monitoring of large mammal populations.

name: Land InSight digital twin
summary: UKCEH digital twin of UK soils that combines observations and process models with machine learning to predict soil moisture and soil carbon.

name: Landguard Bird Observatory
summary: A bird observatory carrying out daily bird counts and ringing, with moth trapping from March to December and data compiled into annual reports and shared with other organisations.

name: Landscape Observatory
summary: AI mapping project for England's Protected Landscapes, with a core team at the Peak District National Park working with Cranfield University. Facts come from the Landscape Institute because the project's own hosts refuse us.

name: Langland Conservation
summary: UK-registered charity using data and low-code deep learning on satellite imagery, including habitat study of Nyakweri Forest in Kenya with The Pangolin Project.

name: Laurence De Clippele's Research Group
summary: University of Glasgow group using machine learning to study how marine biodiversity and ecosystem functions change, on habitats such as cold-water coral reefs.

name: Lee Valley Regional Park Authority
summary: Authority governed by the Lee Valley Regional Park Act 1966, whose remit includes nature conservation and protecting and enhancing the natural environment in the park.

name: Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust
summary: Wildlife charity that manages over 35 nature reserves covering over 1,300 hectares in Leicestershire and Rutland.

name: LepiSense
summary: UKCEH AI-enabled system that captures images to identify and monitor moths and other nocturnal insects, licensed to Wilder Sensing in 2026.

name: LERC Wales
summary: The four Local Environmental Records Centres in Wales, which developed the Aderyn biodiversity database and a recording app.

name: Leverhulme Trust
summary: UK research funder that gave £10 million to the Leverhulme Centre for Nature Recovery at Oxford.

name: Lifer
summary: Bird identification app that names birds from sound or photographs and offers its records to GBIF.

name: Linckia
summary: Environmental technology company selling tools for biodiversity net gain survey and data management, using Ordnance Survey land cover data.

name: Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust
summary: Wildlife charity that manages almost 100 nature reserves in Lincolnshire and helps protect roadside nature reserves, marine protected areas and local wildlife sites.

name: Living England
summary: Natural England's map of broad habitats across England, predicted with a random forest model from Sentinel satellite imagery, lidar and field survey labels.

name: Living Map of Northern Ireland
summary: NIEA project developing habitat mapping from satellite data, to improve evidence on habitat extent and change.

name: Living Wales
summary: Aberystwyth University project, funded by the Welsh Government, whose data underlies the Natural Resources Wales map of Wales' eight broad ecosystems.

name: Loch Lomond and The Trossachs National Park Authority
summary: Authority whose first statutory aim, set by the National Parks (Scotland) Act 2000, is to conserve and enhance the park's natural and cultural heritage.

summary: University where a team led by Josh Wolstenholme used AI on aerial images to map hedgerows and their gaps as part of work on nature-based flood management.

name: Loughs Agency

name: Mac Aodha Group
summary: Research group on computer vision and machine learning, including biodiversity monitoring, led by Oisin Mac Aodha, whose listed papers include deep learning tools for detecting bat calls.

name: Machine Listening Lab, Queen Mary University of London
summary: Queen Mary University of London lab developing machine learning for natural and everyday sounds and recorded music.

name: Make it Wild
summary: North Yorkshire rewilding company using AgriSound's AI listening devices to monitor pollinators on its land.

name: Making Earth Observation Work for UK Biodiversity
summary: Four-phase project that addressed UK habitat monitoring and surveillance needs with Earth observation, from which JNCC's current approaches originated.

name: MammalWeb
summary: Durham University citizen science platform for camera trap images, used by the National Hedgehog Monitoring Programme.

name: Manchester Metropolitan University
summary: University with an author on deep learning for land use and land cover mapping.

name: Manchester Museum
summary: University museum that publishes its botany collection records on GBIF.

name: Map Impact
summary: Company combining Earth observation with its own datasets to report climate and biodiversity risk for assets. No page read says it uses AI.

name: Mapping Ancient Woodland Image Segmentation Model
summary: Welsh Government image segmentation model that predicts areas of woodland on historic OS maps, with the resulting shapefiles published for others to use.

name: MappingForRights
summary: Tools and methods from the Rainforest Foundation UK for forest communities in the Congo Basin to map, monitor and protect their land.

name: Marine Alliance for Science & Technology for Scotland
summary: Scottish marine research alliance of over 900 researchers across 17 partner institutions, with a forum on marine artificial intelligence.

name: Marine Biological Association of the United Kingdom
summary: Registered charity that conducts and supports research into life in the sea, and a partner in Darwin Tree of Life.

name: Marine Biology Research Group, University of Portsmouth
summary: University of Portsmouth group studying marine biodiversity, including a machine learning project decoding sound in the deep ocean.

name: Marine Conservation Society
summary: UK ocean charity that runs the Good Fish Guide and the Beachwatch litter survey, whose 30-year dataset it shares under data sharing agreements. No page read shows AI.

name: Marine Directorate
summary: Scottish Government directorate for marine affairs. A Scottish Government reply lists fish scale identification among its uses of AI, and a 2020 post describes a study of AI for marine images.

name: Marine Environmental Data and Information Network
summary: Open partnership of government departments, research institutions and private companies that promotes sharing of, and access to, UK marine data.

name: Marine Management Organisation
summary: Executive non-departmental public body sponsored by Defra, created by the Marine and Coastal Access Act 2009. With Defra and Cefas it is introducing remote electronic monitoring on UK fishing vessels.

name: Marine MEGAfauna Lab
summary: Newcastle University lab led by Per Berggren, on porpoises, dolphins, whales, sharks, rays and seals; its publications include deep learning classification of dolphin clicks.

name: Marine Technology Research Unit
summary: University of Essex group of computer science, AI, engineering and life sciences researchers developing computer vision methods for rapid marine surveying and coral reef conservation.

name: MARLIN
summary: Underwater AI system from the University of Southampton and RS Aqua, funded by Innovate UK, that monitors sound to spot illegal fishing and protect marine mammals.

name: Marwell Wildlife
summary: Zoo and conservation charity working with the University of Surrey on AI to monitor animals at night.

name: MASTS Marine Artificial Intelligence Research Forum
summary: Forum for knowledge exchange and networking on AI methods for problems in the marine environment.

name: Maynard Lab
summary: UCL group studying ecological communities with computational, theoretical and statistical methods, including deep learning on forest resilience.

name: Merman Conservation Expeditions Ltd
summary: UK environmental consultancy and conservation company that lists an AI advisory agent and publishes raw project data openly.

name: MESOSCAN
summary: Forest Research project developing a machine learning dataset and tool for automatically identifying soil mites and springtails.

name: Migrate Technology
summary: Family business near Cambridge, UK, that designs and manufactures miniature light-level loggers (geolocators) for tracking birds, and says they have also tracked seals.

name: Molendotech
summary: Company with an Innovate UK award to validate an AI early warning system for river contamination.

name: Montgomeryshire Wildlife Trust
summary: Wildlife charity that describes 18 nature reserves across Montgomeryshire as its own.

summary: Bumblebee Conservation Trust project on which the University of Cambridge is building AI-powered species distribution models for the moss carder bee.

name: Mossy Earth
summary: UK private social venture with rewilding hubs and over 30 partnership projects, aiming to design monitoring strategies for each and using drone mapping, eDNA and bioacoustics.

name: MothSense
summary: Wilder Sensing tool, built on UKCEH's LepiSense, that captures images to identify and monitor moths at scale for biodiversity reporting.

name: Mott MacDonald
summary: Consultancy listed for the CIEEM 2026 Best Practice Innovation award for habitat suitability and connectivity modelling.

name: Mourne Heritage Trust
summary: Charity whose stated public benefits include habitat protection and enhancement in the Mournes, through habitat management plans and invasive species control.

name: Mozaic Earth
summary: Company building a nature risk system that joins data collection, AI analysis, expert verification and reporting.

name: MSeis
summary: Company building dual thermal and optical camera platforms, working with the University of Plymouth on AI detection of marine mammals.

name: National Biodiversity Network Trust
summary: UK partnership for sharing wildlife data, with over 200 members. It runs the NBN Atlas and is the UK node for GBIF.

name: National Botanic Garden of Wales
summary: Botanic garden in Carmarthenshire that led the DNA barcoding of the native flowering plants and conifers of Wales and keeps the Barcode UK reference collection.

name: National Centre for Earth Observation
summary: NERC-funded UK centre at Space Park Leicester that studies the Earth system with data from satellites, aircraft and ground instruments, including the carbon content of forests.

name: National Forest Company
summary: Company leading the transformation of the 200 square mile National Forest in central England, where forest cover has risen from 6% to more than 26% since 1991.

name: National Forest Inventory
summary: Great Britain's woodland map and inventory, published by the Forestry Commission and updated each year. It covers woodland over 0.5 hectare with at least 20% canopy cover.

name: National Highways
summary: Client of the Intelligent Environmental Estate project, which tracks biodiversity on land along the strategic road network.

name: National Highways Intelligent Environmental Estate
summary: Prototype that maps landcover and habitats across the strategic road network from satellite images and machine learning, built by Galago at Ramboll.

name: National Lottery Heritage Fund
summary: UK heritage funder whose awards include £96,800 to NatureHack, a project exploring technology for monitoring nature.

name: National Museums Scotland
summary: Museum group that co-leads the DiSSCo UK project in Scotland, creating over 700,000 digital records of specimens.

name: National Oceanography Centre
summary: UK ocean research centre and a partner in the TiMBER project on marine ecosystem tipping points.

name: National Parks Partnerships
summary: Partnership body for the UK National Parks, named as a partner with Vodafone UK on AI habitat mapping.

name: National Plant Monitoring Scheme
summary: UK plant survey run by BSBI, JNCC, Plantlife and UKCEH, with a mobile recording app.

name: National Tree Map
summary: Bluesky dataset of trees in Great Britain and the Republic of Ireland that are 3 metres and taller, with height, location and canopy extent.

name: National Trust
summary: UK conservation charity and lead on a NERC award on restoring resilient ecosystems.

name: National Trust for Scotland
summary: Publishes the National Trust for Scotland Species Records dataset on GBIF.

name: National Woodland Bat Survey
summary: Acoustic survey of bat populations in England's woodlands, listed among Forest Research's projects under the Natural Capital and Ecosystem Assessment.

name: Natural Apptitude
summary: UK software company specialising in citizen science data collection apps that runs Coreo and built the Dawn Chorus app, partnering with BirdNET to add AI species suggestions.

summary: Government science programme set up to survey England's land, freshwater and coastal ecosystems and produce a baseline assessment of natural assets by 2029.

name: Natural England
summary: The UK government's adviser for the natural environment in England. It produces the Living England habitat map using satellite imagery, field survey and machine learning.

name: Natural Environment Research Council
summary: UK Research and Innovation council that funds environmental science, including a £4.8 million call on AI for environmental science that covers ecosystem and biodiversity change.

name: Natural Resources Wales
summary: Environment body for Wales. Its State of Natural Resources Report 2025 maps Wales' eight broad ecosystems from Living Wales satellite data.

name: Nature Equity
summary: Company with an AI-enabled natural capital platform that classifies habitats to UK Habitat level 4 and links them to valuation models.

name: Nature's Calendar
summary: Woodland Trust project that collects data for the UK Phenology Network. Its records are used in research on seasonal shifts.

name: Naturebytes
summary: Small maker of a Raspberry Pi wildlife camera kit, launched on Kickstarter with support from the Raspberry Pi Foundation and Nesta.

name: NatureHack
summary: Project in York exploring new technology for monitoring nature, led by the Yorkshire and Humber Ecological Data Trust with a 2018 National Lottery Heritage Fund award.

name: NatureScot
summary: Scotland's nature agency, working to improve the natural environment in Scotland.

name: NatureScot RR1356 peatland surface motion condition data
summary: Open spatial data that class about 680,000 hectares of peatland by condition from satellite surface motion, distributed by NatureScot.

name: NatureSpot
summary: Community wildlife recording website for Leicestershire and Rutland, which takes records through the iRecord app.

name: NatureSpy
summary: Conservation social enterprise that sells wildlife cameras and runs conservation projects, including the Yorkshire Pine Marten Project.

name: NBN Atlas
summary: UK wildlife records portal, built on the Atlas of Living Australia platform, with separate atlases for Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland and the Isle of Man.

name: NC-UK
summary: UKCEH programme running events on UK environmental monitoring over five years, source of the report arguing for a UK Biodiversity Observation Network.

name: NERC Environmental Omics Facility
summary: NERC-funded facility provided by the Universities of Liverpool and Sheffield and managed by the British Geological Survey. It has trained Natural England staff in eDNA research.

name: Nesta
summary: UK innovation charity whose Scotland AI for Good programme, a £105,000 prize fund, funded the Riverwoods satellite mapping project.

name: Network Rail

name: Network Rail dormouse monitoring with ZSL and Google Cloud
summary: Collaboration of Network Rail, the Zoological Society of London and Google Cloud monitoring dormice beside railway lines, training algorithms on images, video and audio.

name: Network Rail lineside biodiversity AI
summary: Trials using AI to identify trees and other plants from on-train camera photographs of railway lineside vegetation.

name: Network Rail lineside vegetation AI
summary: UKCEH and Keen AI work with Network Rail on software that identifies invasive plants and at-risk trees beside railway lines from on-train camera images.

name: New Forest National Park Authority
summary: Authority responsible for conserving and enhancing the natural beauty, wildlife and cultural heritage of the New Forest.

name: New Gradient
summary: Company working with Caledonian Climate Partners on AI technologies funded by Innovate UK. Its founder and managing director is Ewan McMillan.

name: New Gradient woodland monitoring tool
summary: Machine learning tool for woodland monitoring, backed by the UK Space Agency, that assesses individual trees for health, height, biomass, carbon and species.

name: Newark and Sherwood District Council
summary: District council working with Lancaster City Council and AiDASH on an AI biodiversity assessment pilot.

name: Newcastle University
summary: University building ALGAE-Watch, a low-cost cyanobacterial sensor and Earth observation analytics for Lough Neagh.

name: Norfolk Ornithologists' Association
summary: A registered charity at Holme next the Sea that collects information to monitor birds and wildlife year to year, publishes results in annual reports, and has had Shannon Clifford as warden since January 2026.

name: Norfolk seal drone and AI survey
summary: Two-year Natural England pilot that used drone images and instance segmentation to count grey seals and pups at Winterton-on-Sea, Norfolk.

name: Norfolk Wildlife Trust
summary: Wildlife charity that cares for more than 60 nature reserves in Norfolk.

name: North Devon Biosphere Birdsong
summary: Project recording bird calls in North Devon parks and reserves and identifying species by artificial intelligence.

name: North Harris Trust
summary: Community trust set up in 2002 to manage the North Harris Estate on behalf of the community.

name: North Ronaldsay Bird Observatory
summary: A bird observatory on North Ronaldsay where, according to a Visit Orkney article quoting its assistant warden, staff run a daily census across six zones and ring chicks in July.

name: North Wales Wildlife Trust
summary: Wildlife charity that manages 35 nature reserves in North Wales, covering over 950 hectares.

name: North West Mull Community Woodland Company
summary: Community company set up to manage the Langamull and West Ardhu woodlands, 675 hectares in the north west of the Isle of Mull.

name: North York Moors National Park Authority
summary: Authority responsible for conserving and enhancing the natural beauty, wildlife and cultural heritage of the North York Moors.

name: Northern Ireland Water
summary: Water company named as a partner in River Deep Mountain AI, which builds open models for river health.

name: Northumberland National Park Authority
summary: Authority responsible for conserving and enhancing the natural beauty, wildlife and cultural heritage of the Northumberland uplands.

name: Northumberland Wildlife Trust
summary: Wildlife charity that manages over 70 nature reserves and works with partners to create wildlife-rich landscapes and seas.

name: Northumbria University
summary: University leading a project using machine learning to study urban kittiwakes on the River Tyne.

name: Northumbrian Water
summary: Water company that leads the River Deep Mountain AI project on open-source models for river health.

name: Nottingham Trent University
summary: University partner in the National Hedgehog Monitoring Programme.

name: Nottinghamshire Wildlife Trust
summary: Wildlife trust that says it has nature reserves across Nottinghamshire.

name: Nucbarcoder
summary: Company with an Innovate UK award to build a database for species identification.

name: NUUV
summary: Company leading a project on river water quality monitoring with sensors and AI.

name: Ocean AI
summary: Company with an Innovate UK award for monitoring and forecasting seawater visibility with remote sensing and AI.

name: Ocean Conservation Trust
summary: Charity that led the cultivation and restoration element of the LIFE Recreation ReMEDIES seagrass project and reports 8 hectares of subtidal seagrass planted.

name: Ocean Ecology

name: Ocean Science Consulting
summary: Scottish marine consultancy doing environmental monitoring for offshore industry, applying AI to identify marine organisms in monitoring data.

name: Oceanos Earth
summary: Marine biodiversity company, trading as OceanOS, using satellite data and AI to map marine habitats and species for regulators and offshore wind.

name: Ofwat
summary: Runs the Water Breakthrough Challenge, which funds River Deep Mountain AI.

name: Online Oceans Robotics
summary: Company with an Innovate UK award for automating marine mammal monitoring during offshore wind consenting.

name: Open Cosmos
summary: Satellite company at Harwell building the UK pathfinder satellite for the Atlantic Constellation, described on its page as using AI to improve environmental management.

name: Open-source UK mammal camera trap detection model
summary: Open-source object detection model for 31 classes, including 28 common UK mammal and bird species, released in a June 2026 preprint.

name: Open-source UK mammals camera trap model
summary: Open-weights object detector for 31 classes, 28 of them common UK mammals and birds, released with a 2026 preprint from the Conservation AI and Trap Tracker work.

name: Ordnance Survey

name: ORG.one
summary: Programme set up by Oxford Nanopore Technologies for local endangered species sequencing, with EMBL-EBI ENA uploads within six weeks and over 150 species reportedly sequenced.

name: Oshen
summary: Company with an award for autonomous wind-driven devices for acoustic and visual sensing at sea.

name: Oxford Nanopore Technologies
summary: Maker of real-time DNA and RNA sequencing devices, with a registered office in Oxford, UK, that set up ORG.one to support sequencing of endangered species.

name: PAMGuard
summary: Application software for passive acoustic detection, classification and localisation of animal sounds, used worldwide for marine mammals.

name: Pathtrack
summary: Otley company whose miniature GPS tags are named in a UK nightjar tracking dataset.

name: Peak District AI land cover map
summary: Project by the Peak District National Park Authority with Cranfield University and the Alan Turing Institute that used deep learning on Bluesky aerial photographs to make a detailed land cover map.

name: Peak District National Park
summary: National park whose staff form the core team of Landscape Observatory, according to the Landscape Institute. Its own site refuses us.

name: Peatland ACTION
summary: A programme run by NatureScot which, with NERC, funded methods using satellite radar measures of peatland surface motion to map peatland condition, aiming to support monitoring of restoration investment in Scotland.

name: Peersonic
summary: Maker of low-cost full-spectrum bat recorders and detectors.

name: Pembrokeshire Coast National Park Authority
summary: Authority managing the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park under two statutory purposes, the first being to conserve and enhance its natural beauty, wildlife and cultural heritage.

name: People's Postcode Lottery
summary: Lottery whose players funded the £1.25m Space4Nature award.

name: People's Trust for Endangered Species
summary: Wildlife charity that co-leads the National Hedgehog Monitoring Programme, which uses AI image sorting.

name: Plankton Analytics
summary: Maker of high-speed imaging instruments that photograph plankton in water for ecological surveys.

name: Plant Ecology Beyond Land
summary: Community interest company leading the PEBL-FLOW project on detecting debris at floating offshore wind devices in the Celtic Sea.

name: Plantlife
summary: Charity for wild plants and fungi that helps run the National Plant Monitoring Scheme and publishes survey records on GBIF.

name: Plants for Purpose
summary: Five-year RHS programme from 2025 developing, with the University of Nottingham, a deep learning tool to find useful traits among UK plant cultivars.

name: Plastic-i
summary: Company with an award for mapping marine plastic pollution with satellites and AI.

name: Platform Kinetics
summary: Company with an award for real-time molecular biodiversity monitoring of the marine water column.

name: Plymouth Marine Laboratory
summary: Marine research body with NERC awards for decentralised learning in biodiversity monitoring and for valuing marine biodiversity.

name: Policy Support Systems
summary: Free, open access software and hardware for conservation planning, environmental risk assessment and monitoring, co-developed by Mark Mulligan and reportedly used by over 3,500 organisations in over 180 countries.

name: Pollenize
summary: Organisation that makes the Nest Sweeper bait station for Asian hornets, with an AI identification app built with Capgemini's Applied Innovation Exchange.

name: PollenTrace
summary: Forthcoming app that identifies insects and pollinators from a photograph and turns sightings into data on Britain's pollinators.

name: Pollinatework
summary: Company with an Innovate UK award for Sensibee, autonomous pollinator monitoring and identification.

name: Ponterra

name: Portland Bird Observatory and Field Centre
summary: A bird observatory and field centre at Portland Bill studying bird migration and the natural history of the Isle of Portland, which reported 300 volunteers and 12 trustees for 2025.

name: PRECISE
summary: UKRI-funded project to predict the effects of conservation interventions at specific sites, with researchers at the University of Southampton, UKCEH and the Norwegian Institute for Nature Research.

name: Proforest

summary: Wildlife charity that describes its nature reserves in Wiltshire as its own and open to visit.

name: Woodland Trust
summary: The UK's largest woodland conservation charity, which runs the Ancient Tree Inventory.

name: Worcestershire Wildlife Trust
summary: Wildlife charity that owns and manages more than 75 places for wildlife in Worcestershire.

name: WRc
summary: Named as a partner in River Deep Mountain AI, which builds open models for river health. The page does not say what WRc does.

name: WWF Conservation Technology
summary: Free peer-edited guidance, run by WWF UK, on using technology for conservation, covering camera trapping, acoustic monitoring and lidar remote sensing.

name: WWF-UK
summary: A UK registered charity and company limited by guarantee that gives free, peer-edited guidance on conservation technology.

name: Wye & Usk Foundation
summary: Charity concerned with restoring the habitat, water quality and fisheries of the rivers Wye and Usk.

name: Yorkshire and Humber Ecological Data Trust
summary: Applicant for the 2018 NatureHack award from the National Lottery Heritage Fund.

name: Yorkshire Dales National Park Authority
summary: Authority responsible for conserving and enhancing the natural beauty, wildlife and cultural heritage of the Yorkshire Dales.

name: Yorkshire Water
summary: Water company that says it was the first in the UK to join the 1000 Rivers eDNA Project.

name: Yorkshire Wildlife Trust
summary: Wildlife charity that manages and restores 115 nature reserves across Yorkshire.

name: Zulu Ecosystems
summary: Company that, with Severn Trent, developed land use optimisation tools modelling nature-based solutions, applied to the River Idle catchment, under an Innovate UK award.

name: At the Water's Edge (Grenada)
summary: Project run and led by The Nature Conservancy in the Greater Grenville Area of Grenada, using ecosystem-based adaptation against coastal erosion and flooding, with pilot reef structures in Grenville Bay monitored quarterly by TNC scientists and monthly by local partners.

name: Critically Endangered Nesting Sea Turtles Conservation, Mangrove Ecosystem Restoration and Youth Environmental Education & Conservation Activities in Carriacou
summary: Closed Rufford Foundation-funded project, run by KIDO Foundation and led by Marina Fastigi, that planned hawksbill and leatherback nesting monitoring on Carriacou and, per its final report, trained and employed five local guides.

name: Fisheries Division (Grenada)
summary: Grenadian fisheries body that implemented a UNEP-CEP/CaMPAM mid-size grant for a national MPA structure, supplying equipment including a patrol boat, and was described in 2026 as using Woburn Bay MPA as a demonstration site.

name: Forestry Department (Grenada)
summary: Department within Grenada's Ministry of Agriculture, Lands and Forestry that, Now Grenada reported in March 2021, had begun gathering data to protect the Grenada Dove and other birds at Mt Hartman Bird Sanctuary.

name: Grenada Coral Reef Foundation
summary: NGO working to restore and conserve corals, described as implementing an MPAConnect project on Stony Coral Tissue Loss Disease preparedness, which aims to improve reef monitoring and set up monitoring and response teams.

name: Grenada Dove Conservation Programme
