summary: Grantee of a 2010 Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund grant for Grenada Dove nest, breeding and population monitoring and outreach, developed at the Government of Grenada's request in 2007, with NGO incorporation then in progress.

name: Grenada land cover and forest formations map (IITF_CJS44_grenada_landcov)
summary: Raster map of Grenada's land cover and forest formations, made by decision tree classification of cloud-cleared Landsat imagery, mostly from November 2001, and funded by USAID and the International Institute of Tropical Forestry.

name: Grenada seabed habitat maps
summary: Seabed habitat maps around Grenada, covering habitats such as coral reefs and seagrass beds, which a 2018 programme case study says Cefas and the National Oceanography Centre had produced to inform marine conservation.

name: Grenada Sustainable Development Trust Fund
summary: Trust fund founded in 2016 by the Government of Grenada, community and private sector to give long-term funding for conserving ecosystems in Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique, and a partner of Our Bay, Our Future.

name: Habitat Requirements, Threats and Community Conservation of the Critically Endangered Grenada Dove
summary: Closed Rufford Foundation-funded project, covering 2012 to 2013, that aimed to establish Grenada Dove habitat requirements and threats, and per its final report trained Forestry Department staff to use tracking tunnels and camera traps.

name: KIDO Foundation
summary: Local NGO on Carriacou that, per Seacology, has restored mangroves, and which the Grenada Tourism Authority lists as monitoring nesting sea turtles, with a stated aim of preserving island ecosystems through conservation, research and youth education.

name: Land Use Division (Grenada)
summary: Named in a 2019 presentation as responsible for GIS and land cover mapping in Grenada; its 2010 map used 5 m Ikonos imagery, and it planned a new map from 2017 LiDAR.

name: Management Strength Drives Ecological and Social Outcomes in Marine Protected Areas in Grenada (datasets)
summary: Open Zenodo deposit, under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence, of ecological and social survey datasets behind a paper on management strength in Grenada's marine protected areas, including abundance and parrotfish biomass tables.

name: Mangrove species suitability maps for Grenada
summary: Species suitability maps for Grenada’s Mangrove Innovation Hub use survey plot and landscape-scale environmental data, with terrain layers from a 2017 LiDAR elevation model.

name: Ministry of Climate Resilience, the Environment and Renewable Energy
summary: Grenadian ministry listing biodiversity conservation among its portfolios; in February 2026 its Environment Division and UNDP, its partner, held a workshop reviewing draft national biodiversity targets under the Convention on Biological Diversity.

name: Moliniere-Beausejour Marine Protected Area
summary: Marine protected area on Grenada's south-west coast, designated on 28 December 2001, managed primarily by the Fisheries Division and monitored through Reef Check, with a 2014 paper documenting benthic cover and fish populations from 2008 to 2012.

name: Ocean Spirits
summary: Volunteer-reliant non-profit that describes its leatherback nesting research at Levera beach, collecting data since 2000, as Grenada's longest running sea turtle survey, with volunteers tagging turtles and relocating nests on night patrols.

name: Our Bay, Our Future
summary: Project launched in January 2026 at Woburn Bay Jetty by the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund with the Grenada Sustainable Development Trust Fund, funded by Global Affairs Canada, covering marine protection, habitat restoration and livelihoods.

name: Population genetics of green and hawksbill turtles in Grenada
summary: Closed 2022 to 2024 project using DNA analyses to identify possible origins and migration corridors of Grenada's hawksbill and green turtles, alongside nesting monitoring, run by the University of Plymouth and Ocean Spirits.

name: Sandy Island Oyster Bed Marine Protected Area
summary: Marine protected area on Carriacou whose wardens took a Reef Check training course in February 2011, collecting data by snorkelling and SCUBA and certifying as EcoDivers to monitor reef stressors using a standard protocol.

name: St. George's University
summary: University in Grenada whose faculty page lists Stephen Nimrod as a research scientist in coral reef monitoring since 2007, and which is the first creator's affiliation on a 2026 Zenodo deposit of marine protected area survey datasets.

name: Agency of Protected Areas of Georgia
summary: Public-law agency for Georgia's protected areas, reported by CBW to have launched SMART Survey, a biodiversity monitoring module, with bear monitoring planned as a pilot in Machakhela National Park.

name: Bats in the Vineyards of Georgia: Diversity, Activity and Conservation Implications
summary: Rufford Foundation-listed project, dated 11 March 2026, that plans to place acoustic detectors in an organic and a conventional vineyard from May to November 2026, with roost guano to be metabarcoded.

name: Batumi Shota Rustaveli State University
summary: University which keep.eu names as CARE SEA lead partner; it bought a drone and monitoring devices for the project, fieldwork produced GIS habitat maps of the Chorokhi River Delta.

name: Biodiversity monitoring plan for Georgia's protected areas, 2020 to 2029
summary: Biodiversity monitoring plan for 2020 to 2029, built by the environment ministry and run by the Agency of Protected Areas, reported in July 2026 to cover 11 protected areas.

name: CARE SEA: Cooperation and Awareness for Pollution-free and Environmentally Sustainable Black Sea
summary: Interreg Black Sea Basin project led by Batumi Shota Rustaveli State University, aiming to raise pollution awareness and protect biodiversity; fieldwork produced GIS habitat maps of the Chorokhi River Delta.

name: Caucasus Leibniz Biodiversity Research Center
summary: Research centre set up by Ilia State University's Academic Council in Tbilisi on 30 April 2024, aiming to analyse and model biodiversity and its changes.

name: Cave Biodiversity of Transcaucasia
summary: An open-access database, version 1.0, counting 660 species and 214 caves, with a footer copyright to Ilia State University's Institute of Zoology for 2019 to 2020.

name: Centre for Biodiversity Conservation and Research
summary: Tbilisi organisation whose Conservation Research Programme team ran the first radiotelemetry study of the East Caucasian tur and surveyed bezoar goat populations in Pshav-Khevsureti and Tusheti in 2021.

name: Conservation Actions of Cetaceans in the Georgian Black Sea
summary: A closed Rufford Foundation project under Temur Shvelidze that aimed to assess core cetacean areas, evaluate and mitigate by-catch using pingers, and develop a stranding network and online database.

name: Conservation of Cave-Dwelling Bat Communities in West Georgia
summary: A closed Rufford Foundation project under Sophio Maglakelidze used an ultrasound detector to identify cave-dwelling bats in Georgia, where data are scarce; its final report dates from November 2024.

name: Define the Presence and Distribution of Endangered Species on Egrisi Ridge and Promote the Planning of Appropriate Conservation Activities on the Area
summary: Closed 2019 survey of Egrisi Ridge in which 28 camera traps were placed, detecting the target West Caucasian tur and Caucasian chamois, with data held in CTAP software.

name: EfxINNOs: Establishing and Operating an Innovative Marine Technology Transfer Network for Enhancing the Transition to a Sustainable Blue Economy in the Black Sea Basin
summary: Black Sea marine monitoring network project with partners in Bulgaria, Romania, Turkey and Georgia, in which Ilia State University deployed a sensor buoy in the Poti Port area on 29 April 2025.

name: Electronic Timber Resource Management System
summary: Active system for timber resource management, run by the National Forestry Agency; a ministerial order of 19 August 2026 approved its operating rules and repealed a 2014 instruction.

name: Enhancing Financial Sustainability of the Protected Areas System in Georgia
summary: Closed project, completed in May 2025, that launched a 10-year biodiversity monitoring programme, put SMART into twelve protected areas and set up a Biodiversity Monitoring Council.

name: Establishment of participatory monitoring system for endangered and vulnerable species at Borjomi National Park
summary: Closed Small Grants Programme project run by NACRES to set up endangered species monitoring in Borjomi National Park and involve NGOs, guides and students; its plan includes drones.

name: Faculty of Informatics and Control Systems, Georgian Technical University
summary: Faculty at Georgian Technical University in Tbilisi, listed as the affiliation of the first author of a 2024 paper on hybrid AI models for identifying trees in UAV forest images.

name: Forest Information and Monitoring System (Georgia)
summary: Forest monitoring programme in Georgia, including the first National Forest Inventory, which unique land use says it supported during 2019 to 2022.

name: Fostering the conservation and recovery of threatened sturgeons in Georgia
summary: Closed 2024 project, listed by IUCN SOS under the Fondation Segré Conservation Action Fund, that aimed to show acoustic telemetry could aid Georgian sturgeon recovery, with fish tagging planned in the Rioni.

name: Friends' Association of Lagodekhi Protected Areas
summary: Non-governmental organisation that was grantee of two completed Small Grants Programme projects in 2014 and 2015 at Lagodekhi, one covering biodiversity and poacher monitoring with online maps.

name: GBIF Georgia
summary: Georgia's GBIF country node, an associate participant, to which GBIF moved endorsement of existing Georgian publishers, including Ilia State University's Institute of Ecology, in August 2025.

name: Georgian Biodiversity Database
summary: Database of species from different taxonomic groups ever recorded in Georgia's terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems, arranged by taxonomy and run by Ilia State University's Institute of Ecology.

name: Georgian Technical University
summary: University at 77 Kostava Street, Tbilisi, given by both authors of a 2024 paper on hybrid AI models for identifying trees in forest UAV images, according to OpenAlex.

name: Grasslands Monitoring Programme for Protected Areas
summary: An active programme commissioned by the Caucasus Nature Fund to set a grassland baseline, with the Kazbegi assessment planned to produce a habitat distribution map and a pasture biodiversity database.

name: Ilia State University
summary: University that Georgia's AEWA national report for 2021 to 2024 says monitors waterbirds in Javakheti under the International Waterbird Census guideline and trained Kolkheti National Park representatives in 2018.

name: Institute of Ecology, Ilia State University
summary: Ilia State University institute in Tbilisi that implements the Quantitative Ecology Programme (2010 to 2028) and runs the Georgian Biodiversity Database, though GBIF shows no datasets published by it.

name: Institute of Zoology, Ilia State University
summary: Described by GBIF as Georgia's oldest zoological research organisation, it publishes GBIF datasets on bats (1835 to 2022), rodents (1900 to 2018) and insectivores, plus a wetland plant checklist.

name: Integrated Forest Fire Monitoring and Early Warning System in Borjomi-Kharagauli National Park
summary: Completed project, listed by the Agency of Protected Areas, to implement an integrated forest fire monitoring and early warning system in Borjomi-Kharagauli National Park using remote sensing technologies.

name: Mapping Forest Fire Risks in Georgia
summary: An active NACRES project, funded by the US Forest Service, aiming to create a forest fire risk model, piloted in Borjomi National Park from 2021 and since expanded to three other protected areas.

name: Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia
summary: Georgian ministry in Tbilisi whose agencies include the Agency of Protected Areas and the National Forestry Agency, and which GIZ names as a partner of the ECO.Georgia forestry reform project.

name: Monitoring of Eurasian lynx in Vashlovani PAs
summary: A closed NACRES monitoring report, following a February 2022 agreement with the Caucasus Nature Fund, which identified 11 lynx from camera traps and estimated 9 to 14 in Vashlovani protected areas.

name: NACRES Community Ranger Program
summary: Programme run by NACRES in which participants spend almost a year setting up camera traps and mapping key species sightings; begun in 2020, it had trained 43 community rangers.

name: NACRES leopard camera-trap survey in Tusheti and Khevsureti
summary: A NACRES camera-trap study, supported by the WWF Caucasus Programme Office, that photographed a leopard in Tusheti in August 2021, the first evidence in Georgia in nearly 12 years.

name: National Agency for Sustainable Land Management and Land Use Monitoring
summary: Agency responsible for state monitoring of land use, thematic land use maps and a unified agricultural land database; its news reports pasture monitoring finding ploughed pastures and lease violations.

name: National Agency of Public Registry
summary: Agency that coordinates the geoportal of Georgia's National Spatial Data Infrastructure, presented in July 2025 and planned to carry maps, orthophotos and land parcel boundaries.

name: National biodiversity monitoring platform of Georgia
summary: Proposed national platform for biodiversity data collection and coordination; Georgia's AEWA report says it is under development, with a Biodiversity Monitoring Division set up to implement it.

name: National Environmental Agency
summary: Agency reporting up to 200 seawater and seabed samples from Gonio to Anaklia in October 2021, running an EU-funded Black Sea project planning AI-based forecasting.

name: National Forest Inventory of Georgia
summary: Closed national forest inventory reported in November 2022 as carried out across the country, using a methodology developed under a Georgia-Germany memorandum; run by the environment ministry and GIZ.

name: National Forestry Agency
summary: Agency whose Forest Use Management Division makes the electronic information system available to users and gives them methodological help.

name: National Wildlife Agency
summary: Agency reporting brook trout monitoring and restoration, and reporting in September 2025 that two of its red deer farm's 40 camera traps recorded a Persian leopard.

name: Nekton Consulting Ltd
summary: Limited company that says it has worked on water ecology, fisheries and aquatic biodiversity monitoring for 12 years, and lists sturgeon monitoring around the Rioni delta for 2026.

name: PSOVI Environmental Association
summary: NGO that, with Ilia State University, has monitored waterbirds in Kolkheti since 2012 to 2013 per Georgia's AEWA report; EuropaBON lists it for the International Waterbird Census.

name: Radiotelemetry study of the East Caucasian tur in Lagodekhi Nature Reserve
summary: A closed NACRES study, the first radiotelemetry of East Caucasian tur in Lagodekhi Nature Reserve, with GPS collars from March 2019 giving up to six locations a day until June 2022.

name: Scientific-Research Center of Agriculture
summary: Public law entity whose Agroforestry Research Division led a project creating an electronic database, with distribution maps, of rare and relict forest species.

name: Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation of Georgia
summary: Public law entity under Georgia's Ministry of Education, Science and Youth, based in Tbilisi, which supports science and innovation and funded the rare and relict forest species database project.

name: Study of Rare and Relict Species of Georgian Forests and Creation of an Electronic Database
summary: Closed, SRCA-run and Rustaveli-funded project studying 18 rare and relict forest species, whose leader reports creating a database in Georgian and English and compiling distribution maps.

name: Supporting biodiversity at Lagodekhi protected area by supporting eco-tourism development at Ninigori community
summary: Closed Small Grants Programme project on biodiversity and poaching monitoring at Lagodekhi; the Agency of Protected Areas reportedly replicated it with GSM trail cameras in ten protected areas.

name: Supporting the Conservation of Velvet Scoter at Lake Tabatskuri by Determining the Direct Causes of the Scoters’ Poor Reproductive Success
summary: A closed Rufford Foundation project under Nika Paposhvili that planned camera traps, breeding pair counts and brood monitoring to find causes of poor breeding success in Lake Tabatskuri's isolated Velvet Scoter population.

name: Ungulate monitoring in Adjara protected areas
summary: A closed camera-trap study of chamois and roe deer, with 61 traps installed from December 2020 in Adjara protected areas and 15,368 camera trap days of data collected across three areas.

name: Agence territoriale de la biodiversité de Guyane
summary: A proposed agency for French Guiana, meant to help the territory know, protect and promote its biodiversity; a convention preparing it was signed on 20 April 2026.

name: Association Kwata
summary: An association founded in 1994 and approved for environmental protection, whose 2024 season was its 27th of sea turtle monitoring on nesting beaches.

name: Association Trésor
summary: Based in Cayenne and named maître d’œuvre of the Anomaloglossus blanci study, the association’s monitoring protocol trial began in 2018, according to a 2021 report.

name: CAT-TRIN Project
summary: Permanent camera-trap grid launched by the La Trinité reserve, set up in 2022 in the Aya zone, with photographs placed on an AI recognition platform and 16 stations by 2024.

name: Collectivité Territoriale de Guyane
summary: An organisation whose president signed a convention on 20 April 2026 preparing French Guiana's territorial biodiversity agency; its COP30 assises report proposes extending the Bio-Plateaux water and biodiversity observatory.

name: Comptages Wetlands des oiseaux d'eau en Guyane
summary: An active French Guiana waterbird counting programme run by GEPOG within the Neotropical Waterbird Census, with local counts restarted in 2022 and coordinated counts described in its 2025 report.

name: Conservation ecology study of the Giant Snipe in French Guiana
summary: Conservation ecology study of the Giant Snipe in French Guiana, run by GEPOG and the MNHN from March 2023 to June 2025 in three phases, using GPS tags and sound detections, as ecological compensation funded by ArianeGroup.

name: Direction générale des territoires et de la mer de Guyane
summary: An organisation that became the DGTM from the DEAL on 1 January 2020, steers the SINP arrangement in French Guiana and chairs the platform's regional monitoring committee.

name: ESPEECE
summary: A closed project whose 2024 report, credited to Association Kwata, says a wide network of bodies was asked to pool time-series datasets from late December 2021, before delays led to administrative closure in 2022.

name: Etude sur la détection d'Amphibiens de Guyane à partir de l'ADN environnemental
summary: A closed study led by Association Trésor, funded by the Collectivité Territoriale de Guyane and DGTM Guyane, on detecting French Guiana amphibians from environmental DNA, sampled from December 2021 to January 2022 with SPYGEN analysis.

name: Faune-Guyane
summary: A collaborative site gathering naturalist data for French Guiana, set up under BIODIV'OM and run by GEPOG; a new challenge is announced for 14 and 15 November 2026.

name: GEPOG
summary: An association that coordinated setting up STOC-EPS in French Guiana under LIFE+ CAPDOM, per a 2014 protocol, and lists common bird and savanna species monitoring among its work.

name: Guiana Dolphin long term survey by deep learning
summary: A survey that, per a March 2025 abstract, has used hydrophones and deep learning since 2021 to detect Guiana dolphin vocalisations automatically; one author is affiliated with GEPOG.

name: Guyafor network of permanent plots
summary: A research platform of permanent forest plots covering 300 hectares across 17 sites, run by CIRAD, CNRS and ONF and available to scientists.

name: Guyomique
summary: A genomics platform for Amazonian biodiversity, inaugurated on 22 April 2026 at the Institut Pasteur de la Guyane campus, shared between CNRS, IRD and the University of French Guiana, and led by CNRS and IRD.

name: Hydreco Guyane
summary: Based in Kourou and identified as a SARL in 2019, it describes itself as a tropical hydrobiology research firm covering fish taxonomy, ecology, fishing protocols and eDNA.

name: Labex CEBA (Centre d'Etude de la Biodiversité Amazonienne)
summary: CNRS-run research programme in French Guiana on tropical biodiversity, supported by the French state with close to 18 million over 15 years, using camera traps, eco-acoustics and environmental DNA.

name: Laboratoire Ecologie, Evolution, Interactions des Systèmes amazoniens
summary: A Cayenne laboratory on the Montabo campus, created in January 2016 from CNRS, University of French Guiana and Ifremer staff, which leads the MESH mangrove monitoring project and whose site is being rebuilt.

name: MESH
summary: An active project led by LEEISA that sets up plots and monitoring points in estuaries and seafront mangroves, including a Montabo pontoon instrumented for continuous salinity, current and sedimentation measurements.

name: Office de l'eau de la Guyane
summary: Public-law body in Cayenne attached to the Collectivité Territoriale de Guyane, partner in Bio-Plateaux, that tendered 2025 Water Framework Directive monitoring including eDNA sampling and phytoplankton, and urban stream monitoring in 2026.

name: Paracou Forest Experimental Research Station
summary: A series of permanent forest plots of around 120 ha monitoring growth of around 70,000 trees, run by EcoFoG and part of networks including Guyafor and RainFor-ForestPlot.

name: Phénologie de l'activité de chant d'Anomaloglossus blanci par l'utilisation de la bioacoustique
summary: A closed project, run by Association Trésor and funded by DGTM Guyane, that ran from late 2023 to early 2025 and, per its report, built an annotated database to train a neural-network acoustic detector.

name: Plateforme Guyane du SINP
summary: A French Guiana platform run by the DGTM to encourage exchange of geolocated data; its charter provides for open-data dissemination, subject to legal exceptions and restrictions on sensitive data.

name: Réserve naturelle des Nouragues
summary: A nature reserve co-managed by ONF and GEPOG, whose 2021 report lists monitoring of amphibians, STOC-EPS bird counts, NOE and DARKSOUND, an acoustic project installed in December 2021.

name: Réserve naturelle nationale de Kaw-Roura
summary: National nature reserve in French Guiana whose monitoring supplies black caiman data, including river transects and size estimates carried out with Association Kwata, according to Kwata's 2024 ESPEECE report.

name: Réserve Naturelle Nationale de l'Ile du Grand-Connétable
summary: French Guiana’s first reserve, created in 1992 and managed solely by GEPOG since 2016, reports frigatebird and dolphin monitoring and a turtle protocol developed in 2019.

name: Réserve naturelle nationale de La Trinité
summary: A national nature reserve in French Guiana, managed by ONF since its creation in 1996, whose 2024 report lists monitoring of forest cover by mapping, birds under STOC-EPS, botanical plots and Pléiades aerial photographs.

name: Réserve naturelle régionale Trésor
summary: A regional nature reserve run by Association Trésor under a renewed management agreement, which has monitored diurnal amphibians since 2014, keeps four databases and enters records in Faune Guyane, per its 2021 report.

name: STOC-EPS Guyane
summary: A common bird monitoring programme in French Guiana, built and run by GEPOG, which per a July 2014 protocol coordinated its setting up with LPO and MNHN under LIFE+ CAPDOM.

name: UMR EcoFoG (Écologie des Forêts de Guyane)
summary: A joint research unit created in 2002 that studies tropical forest biodiversity and publishes datasets through GBIF.

name: Étendue de la mangrove 2025 - Guyane française
summary: A dataset of mangrove extent along the whole French Guiana coast in 2025, made by visual analysis of Pléiades 1B images from SEAS-GUYANE, partly for the DGTM-funded mangrove observatory.

name: A Rocha Ghana
summary: Environmental NGO working in more than 20 communities across six regions, which in its 2023 annual report describes community monitoring with SMART and eDNA biodiversity assessment at Atewa.

name: A.G. Leventis Foundation threatened species project
summary: Active project run by the Ghana Wildlife Society and funded by the A.G. Leventis Foundation, which confirmed six new Picathartes nesting sites in 2024 and updated the national distribution map.

name: Advanced Virtual Fire Information System
summary: A near-real-time satellite wildfire detection and alert system, run by the Earth Observation Research and Innovation Centre, that issues alerts within 15 minutes of satellite scans and covers fire hotspots in West Africa.

name: Application of Technology to Enhance Monitoring of the Forest in Offinso Forest District
summary: A closed project, funded by WRI through the GFW Small Grants Programme, to modernise forest monitoring in Offinso Forest District; its close-out presentation reported satellite-based alert systems and community training.

name: Artisanal Small Scale Gold Mining Monitoring Portal
summary: Built and run by CERSGIS with USAID and NASA support under SERVIR West Africa, this portal maps galamsey in Ghana’s high forest zone according to its code repository.

name: Assessment of Habitat Preferences and Distribution Patterns of Leopard in Mole National Park; A Baseline for their Conservation
summary: A closed study that aimed to examine leopard habitat preferences and distribution patterns in Mole National Park, with a camera trap shown on its project page.

name: Aya Data
summary: Company that says it operates across Africa, Europe and Asia and collected multispectral drone data of Oko Environmental's forests for a dashboard tracking forest growth and illegal deforestation.

name: Bolgatanga road eDNA biodiversity survey
summary: Closed project in which, NatureMetrics says, eDNA sampling along the Bolgatanga road detected 59 species from ten water samples, feeding the impact assessment and Biodiversity Action Plan.

name: Centre for Biodiversity Conservation Research
summary: A University of Ghana centre, formerly the Centre for African Wetlands, set up in 2000 with Dutch funding, which began the 2026 International Waterbird Census in Ghana with the Wildlife Division.

name: Centre for Coastal Management, University of Cape Coast
summary: A University of Cape Coast centre established in 1995 to monitor coastal ecosystem health, recognised by the World Bank in 2019 as an African Centre of Excellence, which runs the Regional Oceans & Coastal Data Hub.

name: Centre for Remote Sensing and Geographic Information Services
summary: Non-profit that began in 1990 as a University of Ghana remote sensing laboratory, runs the SERVIR-West Africa programme, and lists monitoring portals for small-scale gold mining and charcoal production among its projects.

name: Charcoal Production Site Monitoring Service
summary: A web platform run by CERSGIS showing where charcoal production sites are, to support monitoring of savannah woodland degradation in Ghana, with information updated alongside national partners and communities.

name: Coastal Mangroves (Coast Man)
summary: An active project listed as running from December 2024 to December 2027, aiming to create a decision support system for mangrove restoration that identifies degraded mangrove areas.

name: Cocoa deforestation monitoring system trial in the Juabeso-Bia Hotspot Intervention Area
summary: Built by Satelligence, this system was trialled in Juabeso-Bia, an area of about 243,500 ha, according to SNV in March 2019, distinguishing cocoa types and detecting illegal farms.

name: Cocoa Deforestation Risk Assessment
summary: Harmonised method, built by WRI, the World Cocoa Foundation and Climate Focus, for assessing cocoa-linked deforestation risk; recent forest loss strongly influenced results, and the note says it will be public and updated annually.

name: Conservation Alliance International
summary: Not-for-profit environmental organisation which, JRS Biodiversity Foundation says, led the Ghana team that published 23,362 biodiversity records to GBIF and won the 2019 African Biodiversity Challenge.

name: Conservation and sustainable management at the Keta Lagoon Complex Ramsar Site, Ghana, for birds and community climate resilience
summary: An active project, partnering with A Rocha Ghana, that aims to produce updated habitat maps and bird lists; a February 2025 field trip caught 63 birds of 35 species and counted 894 birds at nine sites.

name: Conservation of White-necked Rockfowl at Nyameben Bepo Forest
summary: A Ghana Wildlife Society project whose 2023 annual report says an inventory of nesting and roosting sites documented 10 nesting rocks, with a camera trap image of the bird at a roost.

name: Coordinating and Supporting the Implementation of Ghana's Threatened Trees Conservation Action Plan
summary: Project funded by Fondation Franklinia and run by the Forestry Research Institute of Ghana, which says it will carry out botanical surveys and phenology monitoring for 20 targeted species.

name: Council for Scientific and Industrial Research
summary: National science and technology institution, by its own description, that lists the Forestry Research Institute of Ghana and the Water Research Institute among its research institutes.

name: CSIR-Forestry Research Institute of Ghana
summary: Describes a threatened trees project planning botanical surveys for 20 species and a biodiversity information portal for 39 priority species over three years.

name: Dase
summary: According to Global Voices, this EJF-built and maintained app captures illegal fishing evidence in real time, launched first in Ghana and has been used in Liberia and Senegal.

name: Department of Environmental Management, University of Energy and Natural Resources
summary: Department at the University of Energy and Natural Resources in Sunyani, listed as the first author's affiliation on papers on land use and land cover change, and on vegetation loss using machine learning and remote sensing.

name: Documenting Bat Roosts, Threats and Knowledge of People for Urban Bat Conservation in the Greater Tamale Area, Northern Region, Ghana: Phase I
summary: An active phase I project aiming to document bat roosts, threats and local knowledge in Greater Tamale using mist netting, acoustic monitoring, GIS and social surveys, with a progress update dated March 2026.

name: Earth Observation Research and Innovation Centre
summary: A centre at the University of Energy and Natural Resources, off the Sunyani-Fiapre Road, that offers a near-real-time satellite wildfire alert system and announced remote sensing training in March 2025.

name: Enhanced Land Use Land Cover Map of Ghana
summary: According to the UK Space Agency blog, this Forestry Commission and KNUST land cover map distinguishes monocropped from agroforestry cocoa, with overall accuracy of about 90 per cent.

name: Enhancing Community-based Forest Management of Biologically Important Rainforest in Southwest Ghana
summary: One-year CEPF-funded project in the Takoradi Forest District, begun in 2024, that aims to equip community forest monitoring teams with spatial monitoring technologies and real-time deforestation alerts in two GSBAs.

name: Forestry Commission (Ghana)
summary: Government body whose Wildlife Division administers 16 wildlife protected areas and five coastal Ramsar sites, and which uses EarthRanger, with a World Bank-reported pilot at Mole National Park.

name: Ghana Biodiversity Information Facility
summary: Ghana's GBIF country node, with observer status and hosted by the University of Ghana's Department of Botany, which JRS Biodiversity Foundation says supported the 2019 African Biodiversity Challenge win.

name: Ghana Clearing-House Mechanism
summary: A biodiversity information project whose content Ghana moved to the Bioland tool in 2024, with its coordinator saying the new platform maps the country's biodiversity hotspots.

name: Ghana Cocoa Forest REDD+ Programme
summary: Programme run by the Forestry Commission and COCOBOD, which GNA reports began in 2019, is expected to end in 2027, and covers 5.9 million hectares and over 140,000 cocoa farmers.

name: Ghana Flying Labs
summary: Organisation that, in a December 2020 post, says it used drones, including night flights with a thermal camera, to count hippos at Bui for the Tyndall Centre.

name: Ghana Forest Compliance Service for Export Commodities
summary: A service run by the Forestry Commission and Ecometrica using the enhanced land cover map, which in September 2021 the UK Space Agency blog said could give cocoa-sourcing companies government certification.

name: Ghana Herbarium
summary: Described by GBIF's registry as the largest herbarium in Ghana, it publishes the dataset "Plants of Ghana" through GBIF.

name: Ghana Instinct
summary: An organisation that advertised a 2024 to 2025 volunteer turtle programme with Escape3Points Ecolodge at Cape Three Points, involving night and morning beach patrols to monitor nesting sites.

name: Ghana Land Use Project
summary: Run by the University of Florida with CERSGIS and the University of Ghana, this project reports a 2023–2025 NASA grant for detecting artisanal mining and charcoal production risks.

name: Ghana Landscape Restoration and Small-Scale Mining Project
summary: Joint World Bank and Government of Ghana project that aims to strengthen natural resource management in degraded savannah and cocoa landscapes and, the World Bank says, supports Wildlife Division monitoring.

name: Ghana National Forest Monitoring System
summary: FAO reports NFMS assessment and an October 2023 review of Ghana's forest monitoring, plus improved deforestation data using a sample grid assessed in Collect Earth.

name: Ghana Space Science and Technology Institute
summary: Research institute under Ghana's Atomic Energy Commission and environment and science ministry, whose site reports Cabinet approval for a future transition into the Ghana Space Agency.

name: Ghana Wildlife Society
summary: Non-profit conservation organisation belonging to BirdLife International, which runs a threatened species project and says its Important Bird Areas work has informed national programmes and policies.

name: Ghana Wood Tracking System
summary: A programme run by the Forestry Commission, operated by its Timber Validation Department, that maintains a database intended to include legal documents confirming timber consignments comply with the Timber Legality Matrix.

name: Herp Conservation Ghana
summary: With a Kumasi postal address, this conservation organisation helps seven communities manage 5,720 ha of Onepone Endangered Species Refuge and, according to Synchronicity Earth, monitors frogs in Atewa.

name: Hɛn Mpoano
summary: A Ghana-based nonprofit in Takoradi that GFW reports used community monitoring teams and GFW tools in March 2024, including for mangrove and freshwater swamp monitoring in a US Forest Service-funded project.

name: Implementing the Participatory Management Plan for Primate Conservation in Cape Three Points
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project run by Hen Mpoano, from 1 September 2021 to 28 February 2022, that created forest monitoring teams in seven communities and, the report says, increased monitoring coverage and frequency.

name: Improving capacity for protected area management in Ghana
summary: A closed four-year project led by the Centre for Biodiversity Conservation Research, aiming for multi-taxa monitoring in at least four sites by December 2024, which introduced camera traps at Ankasa/Nini Suhien and Digya, per a November 2025 report.

name: Integrated Land and Water Management of the Greater Amanzule Wetland System
summary: A three-year research initiative launched in Beyin on 18 February 2025 to analyse 30 years of ecosystem service change, with Hɛn Mpoano planned to provide GIS and remote sensing for habitat mapping.

name: International Waterbird Census in Ghana
summary: A waterbird count run by the Centre for Biodiversity Conservation Research and the Wildlife Division, begun in January 2026 and extended from coastal to inland wetlands, with data meant to feed national and global databases.

name: Knowledge for World Conservation
summary: A not-for-profit in Kumasi that ran WRI-funded ATEM-OFD, onboarded all nine Offinso District ranges to GFW Forest Watcher in September 2024 and contracted a wood-tracking developer in 2026.

name: Kwahu acoustic monitoring of nature recovery
summary: Project in which, according to Oriel College in March 2025, Bawa Suleman was deploying audio recorders across Kwahu and planned to use an AI model to measure biodiversity trends.

name: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology
summary: University whose Faculty of Renewable Natural Resources, MyJoyOnline reports, executed a Ghana land cover map project with the Forestry Commission's Resource Management Support Centre.

name: Lands Commission (Ghana)
summary: Public body whose Survey and Mapping Division says it directs trigonometric, hydrographic and topographical surveys and coordinates photogrammetric surveys such as aerial photography and orthophoto mapping.

name: Local Community Training to Implement SMART Ecological Monitoring to Ensure Long Term Survival of Highly Endangered Primates in a Community Rainforest in Ghana
summary: Closed project, on a Rufford page dated 14 March 2014, that aimed to implement SMART monitoring in the community-owned Kwabre Rainforest and establish baseline data on three endangered primate species.

name: Marine and Coastal Areas Management in North and West Africa
summary: University of Ghana-led GMES & Africa consortium covering 18 coastal countries, which GMES & Africa says provides Earth observation information for managing marine and coastal resources.

name: MineWatch
summary: A programme using satellite imagery to detect illegal artisanal gold mining in Ghana's forests, monitoring six regions with updates every five days, with national expansion under way and a mobile app for citizen reports.

name: Ministry of Environment, Science and Technology (Ghana)
summary: Ministry responsible for environmental management, science and technology policy; GNA reports its minister said Ghana needed satellite imagery, drones and AI together, which is a stated aim, not a deployed system.

name: Mole National Park wildlife monitoring
summary: A Wildlife Division programme in which, the World Bank reported in February 2024, analysts staff a 24-hour control room tracking real-time sightings, with the division deciding to pilot EarthRanger.

name: Monitoring of Marine Mammals and Sea Turtles Offshore and Inshore of Ghanaian Waters
summary: A project run by the Ghana Wildlife Society which, by its own account, carried out with partners the first shipboard monitoring of marine mammals and sea turtles in Ghanaian waters.

name: National Monitoring Support Initiative (Ghana)
summary: GNA reports a 2025–2030 project planning a national biodiversity monitoring plan and data platform, built by the environment ministry and funded by the International Climate Initiative.

name: Population Status and Conservation of the Critically Endangered Western Chimpanzee in the Krokosua Hills Forest Reserve, Ghana
summary: Closed project, on a Rufford page dated 15 July 2020, that set out to determine chimpanzee abundance and distribution in Krokosua Hills Forest Reserve and provide threat data to guide patrol and monitoring.

name: Prime Initiatives Organization
summary: A Sunyani non-profit formed in 2015 and registered in August 2017, involved in a two-year Bui conservation project launched in 2023 with Forestry Commission collaboration, patrols and GIS.

name: Protecting Atewa Critical Ecosystem (CEPF project)
summary: This closed CEPF-funded project ran under A Rocha Ghana in 2021–2022, using SMART, recording species new to Atewa through eDNA and combining acoustic, biodiversity and water monitoring data.

name: Reference Dataset for Land Use Change Mapping in Ghana's Cocoa Landscape (2024–2025)
summary: Produced by CERSGIS with Lacuna Fund support, it holds 21,031 cocoa farm portion polygons and 20,035 other land use features collected September 2024 to March 2025.

name: Regional Oceans & Coastal Data Hub
summary: A data hub run by the University of Cape Coast's Centre for Coastal Management, which has published 24 datasets on it, including phytoplankton and lagoon water quality, all reusable under CC BY 4.0.

name: Resource Management Support Centre
summary: Technical wing of the Forestry Commission, based in Kumasi, whose functions include monitoring and reporting on the state of Ghana's forest and wildlife resources.

name: Save Ghana Frogs
summary: Founded in 2011 and renamed in 2020, this amphibian nonprofit has undertaken species monitoring since 2013 and works with the Forestry Commission searching for a lost species.

name: Saving the White-Bellied Pangolin: Research and Community Action for Conservation in Onepone Endangered Species Refuge
summary: An active project that plans line transect, camera trap and visual encounter surveys to gather baseline data on white-bellied pangolin presence, distribution and threats in Onepone Endangered Species Refuge, with a November 2025 update.

name: SERVIR West Africa
summary: SERVIR's West Africa hub, run by CERSGIS, CSE and ICRISAT, whose initial phase CERSGIS says focuses on Burkina Faso, Ghana, Niger and Senegal.

name: SKT Live
summary: According to MarcoPolis, this company provides forestry monitoring and satellite deforestation detection in Ghana; its CEO describes a drone or satellite alert platform used against illegal mining.

name: SpotGalamsey
summary: A platform that describes itself as using AI and satellite imagery to detect and track illegal mining across Ghana, with automated reports sent to the NAIMOS Taskforce for enforcement.

name: Thermal Drone Survey of Wildlife in Avu Lagoon Community Protected Area
summary: A thermal drone survey at the Avu Lagoon catchment, run by the Centre for Coastal Management with the Wilder Institute, which a March 2024 report says first captured images of a sitatunga, monkeys and birds.

name: Transfer Learning To Detect Natural, Monoculture, and Agroforestry Tree-Based Systems in Ghana
summary: Model built by Jessica Ertel that classifies natural, agroforestry, monoculture and other land from Sentinel imagery, demonstrated in 26 priority Ghanaian districts as a 10-metre map for 2020.

name: UN Biodiversity Lab Global Biodiversity Framework Mapping Project in Ghana
summary: A closed project in which, a January 2026 UNDP report says, Ghanaian institutions used UNBL and ELSA for biodiversity data and reporting, producing Ghana-specific priority and opportunity maps.

name: University of Cape Coast
summary: A university that runs the Centre for Coastal Management, a research and training institute on coastal resources.

name: University of Ghana
summary: University in Ghana whose GBIF node supported the Ghana team in the 2019 African Biodiversity Challenge; CERSGIS began there as a 1990 remote sensing laboratory, and it leads the MarCNoWA consortium.

name: University of Ghana Department of Marine and Fisheries Sciences
summary: Department of the University of Ghana, listed by POGO as its member institution in Ghana.

name: Upscaling Mangrove Restoration for Coastal Hazard Reduction in a Deltaic Environment: Prioritizing Restoration Efforts for Nature-based Solutions in the Volta Delta
summary: Ongoing 36-month, US$312,183 project, started 23 March 2022 and funded by IUCN, that has completed four rounds of drone LiDAR mangrove monitoring at five sites and aims to build a web-based EbA ranking tool.

name: West Africa Cocoa Dataset
summary: Database of mapped cocoa plot locations compiled from data collected by 19 companies, to be distributed as a heat map rather than plot boundaries, to respect farmer privacy.

name: West Africa Forest Degradation Data system
summary: A system a paper in the University of Ghana repository says was developed for the Forestry Commission of Ghana, with authors reporting it was built entirely in Google Earth Engine, with annual maps and summaries in a web app.

name: Wildlife Division of the Ghana Forestry Commission
summary: Run by Ghana’s Forestry Commission, this Mole National Park manager had decided to pilot EarthRanger by February 2024 and reportedly used SMART, drones and camera traps that year.

name: Acoustic Monitoring of Marine Mammals in a Changing Arctic
summary: Research programme using seafloor-moored acoustic recorders to monitor marine mammals and surrounding noise, some projects running multi-year to track changes in species composition and distribution, run by the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources.

name: BioBasis Nuuk
summary: A programme run by the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources and Aarhus University, one of five NuukBasic subprogrammes, collecting data at Kobbefjord since 2008, with a freely accessible dataset.

name: Community Based Monitoring for Arctic marine climate change, noise pollution and impacts on marine living resources
summary: A project led by Malene Simon that plans to co-create a marine climate and noise monitoring service with four north-west Greenland communities; sensors were reported deployed with local hunters in January 2022.

name: Data Centre for Nature and Environment (Greenland)
summary: Jointly run by the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources and DCE, it includes NatureMap, with services financed particularly by the Environmental Agency for the Mineral Resource Activities.

name: Disko Bay LIVE!
summary: Active project to install what it describes as the first permanent Arctic underwater acoustic station for marine mammals and noise; a 23 April 2024 press release says it was live, recording all year, run by the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources.

name: Environmental Oil Spill Sensitivity Atlas (Greenland)
summary: Active atlas dataset showing wildlife, fishing, hunting and archaeological sites sensitive to oil spills, with coast classified in roughly 50 km segments, built by Aarhus University's Department of Ecoscience; newest parts published in 2022.

name: GINR Benthic Monitoring Programme
summary: A programme run by the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources since 2015, recording seafloor photos and video down to 1,600 m, with imagery feeding projects that aim to apply AI identification.

name: GPS tracking and diet study of white-tailed eagles in South Greenland
summary: Active project run by the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources, fitting solar-powered GPS transmitters to white-tailed eagle chicks in South Greenland; per Arctic Hub, the DNA diet study ends in 2026 while movement tracking continues.

name: GPS tracking of muskoxen in the Sisimiut–Kangerlussuaq hunting area
summary: Research project run by the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources, which fitted GPS collars to 49 muskoxen in late 2025 to compare their landscape use with reindeer, with Copenhagen Zoo and Aarhus University as partners.

name: Greenland humpback whale photo-identification catalogue
summary: Photo-identification catalogue being built and used by Greenland Institute of Natural Resources, combining citizen, tourist, whale-watching operator and researcher photographs for comparison with other North Atlantic catalogues.

name: Greenland in Focus: Infrastructure for Real-Time Phytoplankton Monitoring
summary: Project given a 2025 Carlsberg Foundation research infrastructure grant of DKK 1,400,000, which says it will use CytoSense technology and AI to monitor plankton in near real time and enable early warnings of harmful algae blooms.

name: Greenland Institute of Natural Resources
summary: Researches Arctic ecosystems, monitors living resources and advises Greenland’s government; its researchers co-authored a 2025 paper on a YOLO V5 model trained on Greenlandic seafloor images.

name: Greenland Red List
summary: Second regional red list of threatened Greenland animals and plants, after a 2007 list, evaluating 602 taxa and populations with IUCN criteria and finding 22% of the evaluated species red listed.

name: MarineBasis Nuuk
summary: Long-term marine monitoring programme in Nuup Kangerlua, begun in 2005 and run by the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources, with data used by Arctic Council working groups and funding from DANCEA and Danish ministries.

name: Ministry for Nature and Environment (Greenland)
summary: Issued Greenland’s 24 September 2025 National Park access advisory and was designated to receive comments on a proposed West Greenland national park during December 2025–March 2026.

name: Monitoring Greenland's Benthic Ecosystems
summary: A project led by Nadescha Zwerschke, funded with DKK 17.2 million from the EU and Greenland Green Growth programme, to map and monitor seafloor communities over an intensified four years.

name: PISUNA
summary: A project funded by the European Commission in which, per a January 2017 account, local resource councils chose what to monitor and community observations were stored in the public PISUNA-net web application.

name: PISUNA-net
summary: Public database and website recording and sharing indigenous and local knowledge on natural resources on Greenland's western and northern coasts, covering 2009 to the present, with NORDECO as a partner.

name: RemoteID: Identification of Atlantic walrus at haul-out sites using high-resolution satellite images
summary: Closed pilot project run by the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources testing satellite images for observing Arctic mammals; its report finds 0.5 m resolution sufficient to detect walrus by visual inspection.

name: South Greenland Peregrine Falcon monitoring programme
summary: Peregrine Falcon monitoring in South Greenland since 1981, covering over four decades, done by volunteers or in limited research time until 2023, with nest cameras from 2017 to 2024.

name: South Greenland Regional Environmental Baseline Assessment for mining activities
summary: Closed assessment run by the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources and DCE, compiling baseline data for South Greenland mining and producing a 10 by 10 metre Sentinel-2 vegetation map with five types, published in 2023.

name: Biological Records Centre (The Gambia)
summary: Reported by The Point as launched in Fajara in August 2014, this programme was built by the Wildlife and Conservation Trust to computerise species records and cross-reference habitat data.

name: Department of Forestry (The Gambia)
summary: Government forestry body in The Gambia, run by the environment ministry, which FAO reported in July 2025 was leading preparation of the next national forest inventory with FAO support.

name: Department of Lands and Surveys (The Gambia)
summary: Banjul-based department responsible for surveying and mapping, according to East View Geospatial, which says it has published topographic and cadastral maps.

name: Department of Parks and Wildlife Management (The Gambia)
summary: Department run by the environment ministry, with a mandate over eight reserves and national parks and 14 community-based conservation areas, according to the CBD country profile.

name: Gunjur Conservationists and Ecotourism Association
summary: A community organisation formed by 2021 to unite Gunjur's local conservation groups; in August 2026 its Turtle Committee head reported over 50 volunteers, and members found the first green turtle nest of the 2026 season.

name: Gunjur Environmental Protection and Development Group
summary: Voluntary community-based organisation, described by Access Gambia's NGO directory as established in 1992 and headquartered in Gunjur, whose current status is unknown.

name: Integrated Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Management (The Gambia)
summary: A GEF-funded project run by the Department of Parks and Wildlife Management to conserve coastal, marine and wetland biodiversity, closed on 1 September 2008; a 2009 official said its second phase would expand the marine species monitoring system.

name: Landscape Planning and Restoration to Improve Ecosystem Services, and Livelihoods, Expand and Effectively Manage Protected Areas (GEF-6 Land/Seascape project, The Gambia)
summary: An active GEF-funded project run by the National Environment Agency, approved in March 2020, which in July 2026 handed surveillance equipment, including binoculars, cameras and telescopes, to 35 trained officers for monitoring Indigenous and Community Conserved Areas.

name: Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resources
summary: Ministry that says it leads on environment, climate change and natural resources in the Gambia and has overall responsibility for coordinating related policies and programmes.

name: National Environment Agency (The Gambia)
summary: A Gambian environment ministry agency whose officer presented its GIS work, including updating land use and land cover maps, according to a 2019 UN workshop report.

name: National Forest Inventory of The Gambia
summary: Forest inventory being prepared in 2025, led by the Department of Forestry with FAO, using satellite imagery, Collect Earth Online and Open Foris tools; field deployment had not yet begun in July 2025.

name: Smile for Life The Gambia
summary: Describes itself as a community-based turtle conservation non-profit registered in 2011 and reports no nests or tracks at monitored sites from 1 June to 11 September 2022.

name: Tesito forest mapping and monitoring project
summary: According to Dodo, this active project aims to map forests interactively in Gambia, Senegal and Guinea-Bissau, with Gambian officials learning GRASS GIS and receiving QGIS training in 2025.

name: The Gambia Environmental Monitoring Systems
summary: Reported by The Point in December 2021 as nearing completion, the project collected River Gambia biodiversity data and, according to GREAT’s director, involved school students in citizen science.

name: Wildlife and Conservation Trust (The Gambia)
summary: A charitable organisation, registered in 2010 according to The Point's 2014 report, that launched The Gambia's first Biological Records Centre and received a UNDP GEF Small Grants Programme grant that year.

name: Biology Laboratory, Department of Biology, University of Kindia
summary: University laboratory named as the affiliation of the lead author of a 2025 paper that used Landsat images to analyse land use around the Mount Gangan classified forest between 1995 and 2024.

name: Biotope Guinée
summary: Guinean subsidiary established in January 2021 after Biotope projects there since 2016, holding species observation data and involved in Atlantic humpback dolphin conservation.

name: CCC camera-trap biomonitoring, Haut Niger National Park
summary: Camera-trap biomonitoring in Haut Niger National Park, run by the Chimpanzee Conservation Center; a 2026 paper reports a 2025 Mafou survey with 53 cameras recording 30 taxa.

name: Centre d'Observation de Surveillance et d'Information Environnementales
summary: Central directorate of Guinea's environment administration that publishes three datasets on GBIF, including plant inventories, and hosts the datasets published from Guinea, including the national herbarium's.

name: Checklist of the Vascular Plants of the Republic of Guinea
summary: GBIF dataset listing vascular plants known to occur naturally in Guinea, generated from Kew-maintained databases, reviewed by 41 specialists, and reported by the National Herbarium to include 3,505 native species.

name: Chimpanzee biomonitoring and other large mammals in the 15 km buffer zone of the Simandou railway
summary: WCF biomonitoring project on chimpanzees and other large mammals in the 15 km Simandou railway buffer zone, funded by Winning Consortium Simandou, with a listed period of May 2025 to October 2026.

name: Chimpanzee Conservation Center
summary: Organisation in Guinea that takes in and rehabilitates chimpanzees victims of poaching; its 2023 report says 49 camera traps were deployed, covering about 42,000 ha of a 54,400 ha protected zone.

name: CHM/Guinée, Guinea's biodiversity clearing-house website
summary: Guinea's clearing-house website under the Convention on Biological Diversity, run by the environment ministry, which announced a launch workshop for its new Bioland website from 5 April 2024.

name: COHAB, identification of solutions for cohabitation between chimpanzees and local communities in the Fouta Djallon
summary: Closed three-year project on cohabitation between chimpanzees and communities in the Fouta Djallon, run by Biotope and funded by the Arcus Foundation, with a closing workshop on 1 December 2022.

name: Community Conservation of Sea Turtles, Tristao Archipelago
summary: Closed community project (March 2021 to June 2024) on Katrack Island, run by Chelonee and the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, involving beach patrols and relocating nine nests, with 150 green turtle hatchlings in February 2022.

name: Conservation des arbres menacés en Guinée Maritime
summary: Project run by the Herbier National de Guinée, with Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, and funded by Fondation Franklinia, covering 13 threatened tree species in three TIPAs, with a second phase planning community conservation committees.

name: Coordination Nationale REDD+ (Guinea)
summary: Guinea's national REDD+ coordination body, run by the environment ministry, which according to Guinea's UNFCCC reference level submission consolidates the data, prepares the reference level and coordinates the national MRV system.

name: COPERNICEA in Guinea
summary: Guinea's part of a regional ecosystem natural capital accounting initiative launched in 2020 across six countries and run by the Sahara and Sahel Observatory, with national workshops in Conakry in February 2024 and September 2025.

name: Direction Générale des Conservateurs de la Nature
summary: Guinean directorate under the Minister of Environment, Water and Forests, responsible for monitoring forest, wildlife and environment regulations, and listed by Wetlands International as home of Guinea's International Waterbird Census coordinator.

name: Direction nationale des Eaux et forêts
summary: Guinean water and forests directorate whose GBIF record describes conservation programme design, coordination of forest and wildlife inventories, and responsibilities for national bushfire programmes.

name: Département de Biologie, Université Gamal Abdel Nasser de Conakry
summary: Biology department at the Université Gamal Abdel Nasser de Conakry, listed as one affiliation of the first author of a 2026 remote sensing paper on land cover change in Ziama Biosphere Reserve, 2000 to 2024.

name: Département de Biologie, Université Julius Nyerere de Kankan
summary: University biology department named as the affiliation of first authors on a 2022 Landsat study of sacred forests in the upper Niger basin of Guinea and a 2026 paper on fire dynamics in the Bonama protected forest.

name: Enhancing data access to transform Guinea's capacity to identify and protect its threatened plant species
summary: JRS-funded project with Kew and the National Herbarium of Guinea that published floristic survey data on GBIF and, according to the herbarium, led to five new species being described.

name: Enhancing Data Access to Transform Guinea's Capacity to Identify and Protect its Threatened Plants
summary: JRS-funded project with Kew, awarded $274,721 over 36 months in 2022, aiming to add 6,000 Guinean records to GBIF and train botanists for Red Listing.

name: Gamal Abdel Nasser University of Conakry
summary: University in Conakry that hosts the National Herbarium of Guinea, which became a university research centre in 2011.

name: GBIF Guinea
summary: Guinea's GBIF country node has associate status, a Conakry postal address and no listed homepage; GBIF lists ten publishers registered in Guinea.

name: Guinea biodiversity monitoring partnership with GEO BON (BON in a Box)
summary: Partnership announced at COP16 between Guinea's environment ministry and GEO BON, with Habitat and UPA Développement International, under which GEO BON is to implement BON in a Box for protected area indicators.

name: Guinea's gentle giants: African manatee research and conservation
summary: A conservation project managed by the MBZ fund with the African Aquatic Conservation Fund, which in 2022 reported baseline work on African manatees and sightings recorded by trained fellows along two rivers.

name: Guinée Écologie
summary: Non-profit NGO created in 1989 that publishes 18 datasets on GBIF, including mining-concession biodiversity inventories, and in 2024 reported training 39 conservators in SMART and KoboToolbox.

name: Herbier National de Guinée
summary: Guinea's national herbarium, set up in 2009, which publishes plant data on GBIF and announced a verified checklist of 3,505 native vascular plant species.

name: Improved surveillance and monitoring of mitigation measures in the future Pinselli-Soyah-Sabouyah National Park
summary: Current WCF project in Guinea on surveillance and monitoring of mitigation measures in the future Pinselli-Soyah-Sabouyah National Park, funded by Rio Tinto from July 2025 to July 2027.

name: Institut de Recherche en Environnement de Guinée
summary: Research institute named as the affiliation of the lead author of a 2026 Landsat study in Maritime Guinea, which found wooded or shrub savanna and open forest lost 47.4% and 45.7% of area between 2002 and 2024 in Damakhania.

name: Institut de Recherche Environnementale de Bossou
summary: Institute mainly studying primates which Guinéenews reported in October 2024 had launched a Nimba chimpanzee census, with a primatologist reporting over a hundred available camera traps.

name: Institut Géographique National (Guinea)
summary: Guinean mapping institute that a January 2023 decree, reported by Guinéenews, made responsible for the national geographic information system, base mapping and technical standards for geodesy and imaging.

name: Laboratoire d'Enseignement et de Recherche en Energétique Appliquée
summary: Applied energetics research and teaching laboratory, given as the first author's affiliation on a 2025 paper on monitoring above-ground woody biomass in Forest Guinea's classified forests from satellite imagery.

name: Laboratoire de Recherche Appliquée en Géosciences et Environnement, Institut Supérieur des Mines et Géologie de Boké
summary: Laboratory at the Institut Supérieur des Mines et Géologie de Boké, named as the first author's affiliation on a 2026 paper using Landsat imagery and GIS to assess bauxite mining impacts in Malapouyah between 2011 and 2024.

name: Mapping of high conservation value areas in Moyen-Bafing National Park (Femmes pro-Forêts)
summary: A closed mapping project for Moyen-Bafing National Park, built by Habitat, whose 2024 report identifies high conservation value areas using Sentinel-2 land cover classification and species distribution models.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement et du Développement Durable (Guinea)
summary: Guinea's environment ministry, listed by InforMEA as a biodiversity contact, named as a partner of Natura Guinée and as a collaborator in Wild Chimpanzee Foundation biomonitoring.

name: National inventory of chimpanzees and large mammals in Guinea, 2009 to 2012
summary: Closed national inventory of chimpanzees and large mammals, run by the Wild Chimpanzee Foundation and Guinea's national parks office, covering all of Guinea and highlighting the Moyen-Bafing area.

name: Natura Guinée
summary: EU-funded project under NaturAfrica, run by the Wild Chimpanzee Foundation, which held a first-year review in February 2025 and began camera-trap biomonitoring with 150 cameras in Badiar in May 2024.

name: Natural Resources, Mining and Environmental Management Project (Guinea)
summary: A Guinea project funded by the World Bank, which approved $65 million from IDA in May 2021, and which uses SMART and plans camera trap monitoring, according to a November 2025 mission aide-mémoire.

name: Office Guinéen des Parcs Nationaux et Réserves de Faune
summary: Guinea's national parks office, listed as a biodiversity contact and WCF collaborator; Max Planck reports their joint chimpanzee and large mammal inventory from 2009 to 2012.

name: Population Status and Conservation Issues of the Common Hippopotamus in Upper Niger National Park, Guinea
summary: Project in Guinea that aims to use local ecological knowledge, boat counting and camera trapping to fill gaps in knowledge of hippopotamus status; the Rufford page lists an April 2026 progress report.

name: Réserve de biosphère de Ziama
summary: Guinean biosphere reserve where, in May 2024, its chief conservator reported nine foot patrols, a camera-trap team and real-time position collars on three elephants, within a forest of 119,019 hectares.

name: Scaling Up Pangolin Research and Conservation in West Africa – Identification of Priority Hotspots in Guinea
summary: Project that plans to use species distribution modelling to identify sensitive areas for Guinea's three pangolin species, then validate each model with field checks in three unexplored areas; a February 2026 update is listed.

name: Simandou primate monitoring programme
summary: Rio Tinto programme which, by its own account, found western chimpanzees concentrated on the Simandou range's western side and has tracked one female since September 2024, sampling her faeces for genetics.

name: SMART patrol monitoring in Guinea's protected areas
summary: Use of the SMART patrol monitoring tool, run by OGPNRF, which a 2026 evaluation says covers most of its sites while it also analyses other tools such as EarthRanger.

name: Study and conservation of the Atlantic humpback dolphin in Guinea
summary: Project on the Atlantic humpback dolphin in Guinea, whose first boat survey in June 2022 in Boké waters used line transects and fin photo-identification to build a catalogue of individuals.

name: Sylvatrop Consulting
summary: Environmental and community development consultancy based in Conakry and accredited in Guinea, France and Senegal, listing ecological monitoring, fauna and flora inventories, mapping, GIS and LIDAR among its work.

name: Technical assistance to Guinea's National Forest Monitoring System (SNSF)
summary: Closed technical assistance project, led by IGN FI and funded by the World Bank, on a national forest monitoring system, with SalvaTerra reporting work from June 2023 to May 2025.

name: Tropical Important Plant Areas of Guinea
summary: Darwin Initiative-funded project launched in Conakry in June 2016; the herbarium reports 22 Tropical Important Plant Areas, nine threatened habitats and over 200 Red List assessments.

name: University of Labé
summary: University given as the first author's affiliation on a preprint on machine learning models for subnational climate forecasting and forest ecosystem monitoring across Guinea's 34 prefectures.

name: WCF biomonitoring in Guinea
summary: Repeated species surveys focused on chimpanzees, conducted by WCF in Guinea with the environment ministry and national parks office in Moyen-Bafing, proposed national parks and other areas.

name: WCF support for law enforcement in Guinea
summary: WCF support for community eco-guards who patrol two proposed national parks, collect SMART data and report illegal activities and animal densities, done with the environment ministry and the national parks office.

name: Amigos de la Naturaleza y del Desarrollo de Guinea Ecuatorial
summary: Equatoguinean non-governmental organisation whose CEPF final project report says its park inventory found a great diversity of habitats and lists a rapid fauna appraisal among its outputs.

name: Biodiversity Initiative
summary: International conservation NGO, formerly the Equatorial Guinea Bird Initiative, working mainly in Equatorial Guinea; it has run camera-trap surveys in Oyala since 2015 and runs a mammal camera-trapping project.

name: Bioko Biodiversity Protection Program
summary: Academic and research partnership between Drexel and UNGE on Bioko Island, reported by Drexel in March 2020 as having started in 1998 and employing Equatoguineans.

name: Bioko wild meat market survey data
summary: Wild meat survey data from Bioko public markets, counted as carcasses visible on sale, collected by market monitors from 1998 to 2021 and curated by Bioko Biodiversity Protection Program staff, according to a 2024 article.

name: Enhancing Equatorial Guinea's institutional and technical capacity in the agriculture, forestry and other land-use sector for enhanced transparency under the Paris Agreement
summary: GEF-funded forest data project launched in Bata in June 2021 with USD 1,400,138, aiming to improve inventories, with INCOMA and INDEFOR-AP assigned responsibility for execution.

name: Equatorial Guinea Mammals
summary: Studies human impact on mammal diversity in Equatorial Guinea, with an enforcement plan developed by Biodiversity Initiative and INDEFOR-AP to get conservadores deploying camera traps in protected areas.

name: Flora of Equatorial Guinea project
summary: A 2023 paper describes a botanical project begun by Real Jardín Botánico, CSIC, in 1997, collecting 6,800 specimens with Spanish cooperation funding, later Spanish science ministry support.

name: Human-wildlife coexistence around Monte Alen National Park
summary: Bristol Zoological Society reports monitoring crop foraging in 15 Monte Alén villages using camera traps and surveys, and setting up elephant-deterrent Rapid Response Units in October 2024.

name: Instituto Nacional de Conservación del Medio Ambiente
summary: National environmental conservation institute whose director was identified in a June 2021 announcement as the GEF focal point in Equatorial Guinea, and which was to help execute the GEF forest data project.

name: Instituto Nacional de Desarrollo Forestal y Manejo del Sistema de Áreas Protegidas
summary: Public body based in Bata, with administrative and financial autonomy, responsible for sustainable forest use and the National System of Protected Areas, with departments covering the national herbarium, cartography and computing.

name: Interactive Forest Atlas of Equatorial Guinea
summary: Open data platform that WRI describes as the country's first for the forest sector, combining remote sensing, GIS and ground-truthing; version 1.0 holds 15 years of land use allocation data, and WRI built it.

name: Ministerio de Agricultura, Ganadería, Bosques, Pesca y Medio Ambiente
summary: Equatorial Guinea's ministry for agriculture, forests and environment, which held multi-sector consultations with UNDP on a long-term low-carbon strategy in April 2025 and is credited in the June 2025 strategy.

name: Moka Wildlife Center
summary: Run by Bioko Biodiversity Protection Program, Moka's research station was called nationally unique for continuous operation in 2020, with laboratory, training and climate monitoring reported in 2008.

name: Monitoring Drill Populations in the Ureca-Moka Corridor (Southern Bioko)
summary: Rufford Foundation project page (December 2025) describing a plan for twenty camera traps along a 20 km Ureca-Moka transect, with occupancy and density models and training for INDEFOR-AP technicians.

name: Monte Alén great ape monitoring programme
summary: Bristol Zoological Society programme begun in 2019, described in June 2020 as using cameras, bioacoustics, surveys and invertebrate DNA, with 20 cameras by August 2019 and more planned.

name: Nivel de Referencia de Emisiones Forestales de Guinea Ecuatorial
summary: Equatorial Guinea's forest reference emission level submission, presented by the environment directorate of the then agriculture and forestry ministry, using Collect Earth with Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery and listing forest monitoring capacity as a need.

name: Passive acoustic monitoring of hunting in the Gran Caldera de Luba Scientific Reserve
summary: Closed study, described in a 2022 article, that used acoustic sensors and an automatic gunshot detection algorithm to monitor hunting, with 10 monitored areas in the Gran Caldera de Luba Scientific Reserve on Bioko.

name: Rio Campo Nature Reserve mammal camera-trap survey
summary: Closed camera-trap survey run by INDEFOR-AP at 66 sites in Rio Campo Nature Reserve in 2017 and 2019, with hurdle models relating mammal presence and abundance to human impact and habitat.

name: Rio Campo, Equatorial Guinea - Assessing One of Africa's Globally Important Forest Refugia for Bat Conservation
summary: Closed project, with a page dated 28 November 2022, that aimed to survey the little-studied bats of Rio Campo Natural Reserve and contribute data to GBIF and IUCN Red Listing.

name: The Drill Project
summary: Nonprofit registered in the US as a 501(c)3 and in Equatorial Guinea, which says it has run a camera-trap study of drill behaviour and social dynamics since 2012.

name: Tortugas Marinas de Guinea Ecuatorial
summary: Turtle project described in a 2011 tracking dataset as managed by INDEFOR under ministry oversight, with telemetry funded by Darwin Initiative, Wallace Research Foundation and Marine Turtle Conservation Fund.

name: Agricultural University of Athens
summary: A Greek university established in 1920 as the Highest Agricultural School of Athens, with laboratories working on microbiology, environmental biotechnology and biodiversity data, and a partner in FunDive.

name: AgriHUB
summary: Research group within the Beyond Centre of Earth Observation Research at the National Observatory of Athens, run by that centre, working on big Earth data and AI, with open GitHub repositories of datasets for Copernicus-based AI.

name: AKOMM Psiloritis Development Agency
summary: A development agency that established the Psiloritis Geopark as an informal nature park in 2001, since a UNESCO Global Geopark from 2015, and continues the initiative promoting stakeholder cooperation there.

name: AMVRADIA
summary: A closed 2023–2024 project with a 194,515.95 euro budget that aimed to develop machine vision for bird monitoring using thermal cameras and drones at Amvrakikos and Kerkini wetlands.

name: Antikythira Bird Observatory
summary: Long-term bird monitoring programme on Antikythira and the surrounding sea, run by the Hellenic Ornithological Society; a 2023 abstract reports over 72,100 birds ringed and over 32,900 migratory raptors observed from the early 2000s to 2022.

name: APOLLO - Greek Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: An active programme, run by the University of Ioannina's Biodiversity Conservation Lab and led by Vassiliki Kati, that aims to set up Greece's national voluntary butterfly monitoring scheme.

name: ARCHELON, the Sea Turtle Protection Society of Greece
summary: A Greek sea turtle conservation society that has recorded loggerhead nesting every summer since 1983 and, with partners, had fitted 150 satellite and GSM tags by March 2025.

name: Archipelagos Institute of Marine Conservation
summary: A marine conservation institute monitoring cetaceans, monk seals and sea turtles with hydrophones and research vessels, which has partnered with the Norwegian University of Life Sciences.

name: ARCTUROS
summary: A wildlife organisation founded in 1992, according to Greek News Agenda, that has identified and monitored 250 bears, used infrared cameras and studies bear behaviour with GPS collars.

name: Aristotle University of Thessaloniki
summary: A Thessaloniki university that coordinated SAT4FOREST, which it says produced Greece’s first national satellite-based forest monitoring system, with 61 OpenAlex works matching specified AI and biodiversity-related tags since 2021.

name: Athanasios K. Laskaridis Public Benefit Foundation
summary: A foundation that, ProtoThema reports, pledged 13 million euros in April 2024 over five years for marine environment projects, including 1.5 million euros for Saronic Gulf studies.

name: Athena Research and Innovation Center in Information, Communication and Knowledge Technologies
summary: A research centre whose 2024 report describes AMVRADIA work on bird monitoring with thermal cameras and drones at the Amvrakikos Gulf and Lake Kerkini wetlands.

name: Athens University of Economics and Business
summary: A university whose ReSEES laboratory lists DiverSea, a marine observation and monitoring technology project including DNA-based identification, in which its research centre is a participant according to CORDIS.

name: BEYOND Centre of Earth Observation Research & Satellite Remote Sensing
summary: An operational unit of the National Observatory of Athens, according to the European Commission, combining Earth observation, AI and high-performance computing for public authorities and running FireHUB’s fire forecasts.

name: BEYOND Centre of Excellence for Earth Observation Research and Satellite Remote Sensing
summary: A programme, run by the IAASARS institute, that its 2024 annual report says maintains satellite antennas and computing infrastructure and published a deep learning method for detecting grassland mowing.

name: Biodiversity Conservation Lab, University of Ioannina
summary: A University of Ioannina laboratory that coordinates the APOLLO butterfly monitoring scheme and lists 2022-2023 coypu and dormouse monitoring projects naming the Natural Environment and Climate Change Agency.

name: BLUECOAST
summary: Closed project that planned a combined biotic and abiotic monitoring solution, day and night, with stations in Albania and a cross-border observatory, running from April 2018 to November 2020.

name: Breeding Bird Atlas of Greece
summary: Ongoing Greek breeding bird atlas work, listed by the European Bird Census Council with a 2013 to 2020 census period and a 10 x 10 km grid method.

name: Callisto
summary: A non-profit established in 2004 in Thessaloniki conserving large mammals, which used DNA sampling, camera trapping and distribution models, and radio-collared and monitored nine brown bears in one project.

name: Cave Fauna of Greece database
summary: A free online database run by the Hellenic Institute of Speleological Research, holding 8,880 records on more than 980 cave species and more than 780 caves across all 14 regions.

name: Comp-Biodiv-GR
summary: An active project, running 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2027 at FORTH under Horizon Europe, that aims to set up a Biodiversity Computing Group and reports using machine learning to speed up biodiversity data analysis.

name: Cyclades Preservation Fund
summary: Funder of local initiatives in the Cyclades and other Aegean islands, including fieldwork such as research and monitoring, with grants that it says typically average 5,000 to 7,000 euros.

name: DeepOtolith
