summary: A web-based system using convolutional neural networks to return fish age from otolith images, presented in a 2022 paper as open source, built by Greek and Norwegian research institutes.

name: Democritus University of Thrace
summary: University taking part as a project partner in LIFE RECLOAK, through a department based in Orestiada.

name: Department of Environment, University of the Aegean
summary: University department that, according to its GBIF publisher record, was the first environmental sciences department in Greece, founded in 1986, with an address in Mytilene.

name: Department of Forestry and Natural Environment, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki
summary: Forestry department of the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, according to its GBIF publisher record, which runs a laboratory of forest management and remote sensing.

name: Dryads
summary: Project using multimodal sensing and 3D forest models for early wildfire detection and forecasting; it has completed its final technical review, demonstrating AI models for wildfire and smoke detection.

name: Early forest fire detection pilot, Syggrou Forest
summary: Huawei pilot in Syggrou Forest combining 5G, drones and AI that analyses drone images in real time to locate possible fires, alongside ground sensors for carbon dioxide and temperature.

name: EL-BIOS
summary: LIFE-funded Greek national biodiversity information system, run by the Natural Environment and Climate Change Agency and the Green Fund, whose database holds 681,929 entries from 16 existing databases.

name: Environmental DNA methods for monitoring biodiversity in Natura 2000 areas (Aegean wetlands)
summary: A project on environmental DNA monitoring of Natura 2000 areas in Aegean wetlands, hosted by the University of Athens with a 27,000 euro budget, listed by ELIDEK.

name: FireFly
summary: Active Interreg Greece-North Macedonia project, scheduled from August 2025 to August 2027, whose tools include an AI fire detection system of smart cameras using machine learning.

name: FireHUB
summary: An automated forest fire management system built and run by BEYOND, offering risk forecasting, detection and burnt area mapping, with the mapping covering Greece from 1984 to the present.

name: FLOGA (Forest wiLdfire Observations for the Greek Area)
summary: Machine learning ready dataset of satellite imagery from before and after wildfires in the wider Greek region, built by Maria Sdraka, with a proposed deep learning model for burnt areas.

name: Forest Research Institute (ELGO-DIMITRA)
summary: One of 11 ELGO-DIMITRA agricultural research institutes, founded in 1961, which lists acoustic monitoring and satellite image processing as services and says 18 recorders ran in Rodopi in 2019 and 2020.

name: FORTH Institute of Applied and Computational Mathematics
summary: FORTH institute, run by the Foundation for Research and Technology Hellas, whose staff profile lists coastal satellite remote sensing, environmental mapping and species distribution modelling.

name: FORTH Institute of Computer Science
summary: FORTH institute, run by the Foundation for Research and Technology Hellas, which ELGO-DIMITRA names as a partner in its protected-area fauna monitoring project.

name: Foundation for Research and Technology Hellas
summary: Research foundation listed by CORDIS as coordinator of Comp-Biodiv-GR, which aims to set up a Biodiversity Computing Group at its Institute of Computer Science.

name: General Secretariat for Research and Innovation
summary: Greek body listed by Biodiversa+ as Greece's partner and a funder in the 2025 to 2026 BiodivConnect call, with 1,000,000 euros provisionally reserved.

name: General Secretariat for Research and Technology
summary: Greek research body which, according to the GTIS paper, funded GREFAUN from 1998 to 2001.

name: Geosystems Hellas
summary: Athens company that was co-prime on the completed SAT4FOREST project, covering Natura 2000 monitoring services, and is prime contractor for the National Satellite Space Project's land monitoring service.

name: Goulandris Natural History Museum
summary: Private non-profit museum founded in 1964, holding 357,000 specimens according to GBIF, which runs the Greek Biotope/Wetland Centre and runs and builds a portal for nature and biodiversity.

name: Greek Biotope/Wetland Centre
summary: Branch of the National Museum of Natural History Goulandris, named under a joint ministerial decision as the competent body for monitoring the ecological status of Greek waters.

name: Greek National Satellite Space Project
summary: Programme funded by the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility, under which ESA signed six contracts for services monitoring agriculture, forests, water, land, and safety and security.

name: Greek National Small Satellite Programme
summary: Programme intended to comprise 13 satellites, some already operational, funded by Greece through the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility, with disaster response and environmental monitoring among its aims.

name: Greek Taxon Information System
summary: LifeWatchGreece initiative, described in a 2016 paper, to compile a complete checklist of species reported from Greece, with 35,000 valid species and subspecies assembled from earlier sources.

name: Green Fund
summary: Greek institution reorganised under Law 3889 (2010) to manage environmental funds, and coordinating beneficiary of the LIFE EL-BIOS project, which ran from October 2021 to March 2025.

name: GREFAUN
summary: Closed project (1998 to 2001) which the GTIS paper says first attempted to list all terrestrial and freshwater animal species reported from Greece, covering about 23,000 taxa.

name: Ground optical and acoustic sensors for monitoring fauna and human activities in Greek protected areas
summary: A project, named by ELGO-DIMITRA, to monitor fauna and human activities in Greek protected areas with ground optical and acoustic sensors, led by Systada with university and research partners.

name: Gyaros marine protected area remote surveillance system
summary: Closed project (2018 to 2020) continuing remote surveillance of the Gyaros marine protected area against illegal activity, using radar, an infrared camera and a drone.

name: Harokopio University of Athens
summary: University whose Department of Informatics and Telematics is listed as the affiliation of two authors of the 2023 FLOGA paper.

name: Hellenic Bear Register
summary: Programme monitoring brown bears genetically, using their habit of rubbing on electricity poles, and reporting on its site a recent genetic recovery in Greece.

name: Hellenic Bird Ringing Centre
summary: Scientific organisation that describes itself as coordinating and managing wild bird ringing in Greece, represents Greece in EURING, and works closely with the Zoological Museum of the University of Athens.

name: Hellenic Cadastre
summary: Greek body which, Neos Kosmos reports, cooperates in making forest maps and provides a search engine for owners to check whether land is classed as forest.

name: Hellenic Centre for Marine Research
summary: Greek governmental research organisation for studying and monitoring marine and fresh waters, which coordinated the LifeWatch Greece research infrastructure through its Institute of Marine Biology, Biotechnology and Aquaculture.

name: Hellenic Common Bird Monitoring Scheme
summary: Ongoing bird monitoring scheme using point counts, started in 2007 and listed by PECBMS as providing data in its 2025 update.

name: Hellenic Fire System
summary: Wildfire-monitoring system of four thermal infrared satellites, a ground station in Greece and OroraTech's platform, whose launch OroraTech announced in May 2026.

name: Hellenic Foundation for Research and Innovation
summary: Independent research funding body established in 2016, which ran a 2022 call for field studies of endangered species and lists a project developing eDNA methods for monitoring Natura 2000 areas.

name: Hellenic Institute of Speleological Research
summary: Non-profit scientific organisation based in Crete, established in 2001, whose Cave Fauna of Greece database holds 8,880 records on more than 980 species and more than 780 caves.

name: Hellenic Military Geographical Service
summary: Greek mapping body which, according to the 2015 UN-GGIM report, carried out the main cartography in Greece for over 110 years and took the legal mapping mandate in 1962.

name: Hellenic National Oceanographic Data Centre
summary: National oceanographic data centre established in 1986 in the IOC IODE network, with online access to marine data including physical, chemical and biological water-column parameters; run by HCMR.

name: Hellenic Ornithological Society
summary: Greek BirdLife partner whose data manager said in 2021 she coordinated all national voluntary monitoring schemes and the national Important Bird Areas programme.

name: Hellenic Space Center
summary: Greece's space agency, a non-profit public body supervised by the Ministry of Digital Governance, which joined CEOS as an associate member in 2025.

name: High Technology for protection of Biodiversity through early fire detection in high significance protected forest areas
summary: Closed Interreg project, led by the Municipality of Soufli, that aimed to install two fire detection systems with a 15 km range across 141,300 hectares in Greece and Bulgaria, from 2017 to 2021.

name: iNaturalistGR
summary: Programme managed by iSea with support from the Goulandris Natural History Museum; a March 2024 iSea invitation said the obSERVING NATURE project aimed to strengthen its results on protected species.

name: Industrial Systems Institute
summary: Institute named as beneficiary of the AMVRADIA project, which the Athena 2024 report says develops computer vision for remote bird monitoring using thermal cameras and drones.

name: Information Technologies Institute
summary: Institute whose MKLab publication list includes papers on wildfire analysis, including change detection, wildfire event detection from social media and Earth observation data, and the SILVANUS wildfire platform.

name: Institute for Astronomy, Astrophysics, Space Applications and Remote Sensing
summary: Institute whose remote sensing and machine learning group, per its 2024 report, works on image processing and products for monitoring sensitive ecosystems and natural disasters such as forest fires.

name: Institute of Communication and Computer Systems
summary: Research institute listed on its I-SENSE group's page as a partner in GUARDEN (2022–2025), whose partners planned deep learning, Earth observation and hybrid modelling for predictive biodiversity and ecosystem indicator models.

name: Institute of Marine Biology, Biotechnology and Aquaculture
summary: One of three HCMR institutes, run by the Hellenic Centre for Marine Research, which hosts LifeWatchGreece and lists DNA metabarcoding and eDNA biodiversity assessment among its research lines.

name: iSea
summary: Thessaloniki-based organisation founded in 2016, registered as a GBIF data publisher, with a 2024-2029 plan setting targets for citizen scientists' marine reports.

name: Laboratory of Forest Management and Remote Sensing, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki
summary: A Thessaloniki university laboratory working on vegetation dryness, forest fire modelling and biodiversity monitoring with remote sensing, and a LandShift partner providing Earth observation expertise and AI for forest management.

name: LIFE EL-BIOS
summary: Closed LIFE project (October 2021 to November 2025, 2,571,132 euros eligible budget) that tested Earth observation, remote sensing and wireless sensor monitoring in two Greek national parks.

name: LIFE MareNatura
summary: LIFE project run by HCMR from 2023 to 2029, with a budget of almost 11 million euros, planning satellite telemetry, eDNA and an early warning system for marine protected areas.

name: LIFE RECLOAK
summary: LIFE Nature and Biodiversity project on restoring resilient holm oak forests, led by Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche, with a monitoring framework spanning proximal sensing, soil quality and metabarcoding.

name: LIFE-IP 4 NATURA
summary: Integrated LIFE project running December 2017 to May 2029 with a 17 million euro budget, led by the Ministry of Environment and Energy, including Natura 2000 ecosystem mapping and decision-support tools.

name: LifeWatchGreece Research Infrastructure
summary: Greek national node of LifeWatch ERIC, run and built by HCMR and funded by a Greek research secretariat, offering e-services and virtual labs for biodiversity data.

name: LTER-Greece
summary: National chapter of LTER Europe, listed as comprising eight observatories (though the page lists nine), producing high-frequency and long-term biotic and abiotic measurements under a central management committee.

name: MADOS
summary: Open-access Sentinel-2 dataset of 15 classes including oil spills and marine debris, built from 174 scenes (2015 to 2022) with about 1.5 million annotated pixels, by Katerina Kikaki.

name: Management Body for the Prespa National Park
summary: A public sector body established in 2003 to manage Prespa National Park, declared in 2009 and covering two Natura 2000 sites, and abolished in 2022 in favour of management units.

name: Management Body of Chelmos-Vouraikos
summary: A closed management body for Chelmos-Vouraikos whose site carries a geopark section and which was incorporated into OFYPEKA by a ministerial decision of 9 February 2022.

name: Management Body of Mount Parnon and Moustos Wetland
summary: The closed body's archived site names it for Mount Parnon and Moustos Wetland and records the 8 February 2022 OFYPEKA incorporation decision for Parnon, Moustos, Mainalon and Monemvasia.

name: Management Body of the Dadia-Lefkimi-Soufli National Park
summary: A closed management body for the Dadia-Lefkimi-Soufli National Park, incorporated into OFYPEKA by a ministerial decision of 6 December 2021.

name: Management Body of the National Marine Park of Alonissos, Northern Sporades
summary: A management body whose park operations page describes it as responsible for managing the National Marine Park of Alonissos, Northern Sporades, and running its daily operations; its current status is unknown.

name: Management Unit for the Prespes National Park and Protected Areas of Western Macedonia
summary: An active management unit that manages Prespa National Park, one of the management units set up in February 2022 under NECCA.

name: Management Unit of Protected Areas of Southern Peloponnese
summary: An active management unit for protected areas of Southern Peloponnese, to which the former Parnon, Moustos, Mainalo and Monemvasia management body's website now points.

name: Management Unit of the Chelmos-Vouraikos National Park and Protected Areas of Northern Peloponnese
summary: An active management unit for the Chelmos-Vouraikos National Park and Northern Peloponnese protected areas, to which the former Chelmos-Vouraikos management body's site now points.

name: Management Unit of the National Parks of Nestos Delta, Vistonida, Ismarida and Rodopi
summary: Management unit run by the Natural Environment and Climate Change Agency, with a white stork monitoring programme since 2012 and eight telemetric stations monitoring rivers, lakes and lagoons.

name: Management Unit of the National Parks of the Evros Delta and Dadia
summary: An active management unit for the national parks of the Evros Delta and Dadia, to which the former Dadia management body's site now points.

name: Management Unit of the National Parks of Zakynthos and Ainos and Protected Areas of the Ionian Islands
summary: Management unit run by the Natural Environment and Climate Change Agency, which monitors loggerhead nesting with ARCHELON and plans monitoring using unmanned vehicles, video cameras and hydrophones.

name: MARIDA
summary: Sentinel-2 marine debris dataset of 1,381 patches of 256 by 256 pixels with pixel-level annotations, built by Katerina Kikaki, with train, validation and test splits.

name: Marine Remote Sensing Group, University of the Aegean
summary: University of the Aegean group, run by the university, researching satellite and UAV coastal data since September 2014, including seagrass mapping, oil spill detection and machine learning for floating litter.

name: MariNeXt
summary: Deep learning segmentation framework built by Katerina Kikaki, whose authors report beating all baselines by at least 12 per cent in F1 and mIoU on the MADOS test set.

name: MEDASSET, Mediterranean Association to Save the Sea Turtles
summary: Not-for-profit sea turtle association, founded in 1988 in England and 1993 in Greece, whose 2017–2020 Mediterranean project work included Albanian nesting monitoring and a stranding protocol and database.

name: Mediterranean Monk Seal monitoring pilot, Greece
summary: Pilot that installed two autonomous camera prototypes near possible monk seal caves on Greek Ionian islands in early 2018, with footage to be analysed by AI, built by the Octopus Foundation.

name: Midwinter Waterbird Counts in Greece
summary: Midwinter waterbird counting programme in Greece, run by the Hellenic Ornithological Society with many bodies and hundreds of volunteers; a January 2021 article reports 33 years of counts at Lake Great Prespa.

name: Ministry of Digital Governance and Artificial Intelligence
summary: Greek ministry that OroraTech's release says has space among its main competencies, and through which Hellenic Fire System data reaches the Greek fire services.

name: Ministry of Environment and Energy
summary: Greek ministry that sets protected-area policy, is named in Greece's CBD reports as responsible for the biodiversity strategy, and leads LIFE-IP 4 NATURA as coordinating beneficiary.

name: MOm, Hellenic Society for the Study and Protection of the Monk Seal
summary: Non-profit monk seal society that set up a sightings network in 1991 with more than 4,500 sightings, and says it was first in the Mediterranean to use remote monitoring in seal caves.

name: Municipality of Soufli
summary: Local authority in Soufli listed by keep.eu as lead partner of the closed Interreg Greece-Bulgaria fire detection project, with a project budget share of 562,422 euros.

name: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
summary: Athens university that CORDIS lists among the participants in the DiverSea project.

name: National Lakes Monitoring Network of Greece
summary: Greek lakes monitoring network set up under the Water Framework Directive, which EKBY has operated without interruption since 2012.

name: National Observatory of Athens
summary: Greek research centre founded in 1842 with three institutes, including astronomy and remote sensing, whose BEYOND unit combines Earth observation and AI and lists fire monitoring services.

name: National system for the permanent monitoring of species and habitat types and the surveillance of protected areas (Sub3)
summary: Planned national monitoring system in Greece's Recovery and Resilience Plan, with uniform protocols for species and habitats and surveillance plans for all 446 protected sites.

name: National Technical University of Athens
summary: University listed on Source Cooperative as owner of MARIDA, a Sentinel-2 dataset for marine debris segmentation.

name: Natural Environment and Climate Change Agency
summary: Greek protected-area agency created by Law 4685/2020, with 24 management units covering the 446 Natura 2000 sites, which monitors species and habitats and funded a 330,000 euro research programme, as reported by CNN Greece.

name: Natural History Museum of Crete
summary: University of Crete museum operating since 1980, holding over 2 million specimens, with bird surveillance and genomic projects and staff research estimating Cretan wildcat abundance using camera traps.

name: Nature Conservation Consultants
summary: Greek consultancy established in 2010 that identifies fauna from photographs, video and audio using AI and uses BirdWeather with recording stations along an Aegean migratory corridor.

name: Nature Guardian project, Aoos Gorge
summary: Project that deployed acoustic sensors linked to cloud AI in the Aoos Gorge to detect poachers' gunshots; Huawei reported in August 2021 more than five gunshots recorded since April.

name: Navarino Environmental Observatory
summary: Collaboration between Stockholm University, BRFAA and TEMES, with a Costa Navarino field station, water monitoring stations and planned fish, benthic and bird monitoring.

name: Naxos Wildlife Protection
summary: Non-profit volunteer organisation on Naxos, funded by the Cyclades Preservation Fund, which says it has identified more than 130 individual loggerhead turtles.

name: NESTS
summary: Active Interreg Greece-Italy project that held its kick-off meeting in October 2025, with partners discussing shared monitoring standards, data tools and a future cross-border biodiversity observatory.

name: NMNHG-EKBY Geoportal
summary: Geoportal giving access to geospatial data and maps on Greek nature and biodiversity, built and run by the Greek Biotope/Wetland Centre.

name: NOUS Stratoni seahorse monitoring
summary: Pilot seahorse monitoring installation, still in testing, built by NOUS; the proposed system would use machine learning on images and sound spectrograms to observe artificial habitats made by the Hippocampus Marine Institute.

name: nvisionist
summary: Greek AI company founded in 2021, associated with nvbird, an edge-based bird detection and deterrence platform for wind farms with over 300 installations, according to PES Wind.

name: OFIDIA2
summary: Interreg Greece-Italy funded project to prevent wildfires in Epirus and Apulia, using forecasting, real-time monitoring, HD cameras, wireless sensor networks and drones.

name: OHB-Hellas
summary: Company whose Satellite-as-a-Service platform includes on-board fire detection using U-NetV2 and Sentinel-2 data, with stated uses in forest monitoring, agricultural fire control and governmental risk assessment.

name: Planetek Hellas
summary: Company contracted by ESA to deliver the data hub for Greece's planned Earth observation satellites, and prime contractor for a safety and security service including wildfire analysis.

name: Portal for Nature and Biodiversity
summary: Greek web portal for nature and biodiversity data, with a web map and OGC and INSPIRE-compliant catalogue, run and built by the Goulandris Natural History Museum, with a 2026 upgrade funded by the Recovery and Resilience Facility.

name: Region of Attica
summary: Regional authority with a 2 million euro share of the LIFE-IP 4 NATURA budget, whose listed actions include an interactive WebGIS for visualising and monitoring ecosystem services.

name: Samaria National Park and Western Crete Management Body
summary: A closed management body whose responsibilities under Article 15 of Law 2742/1999 included managing public land given or rented to it, and which issued a press release on Samaria Gorge visits on 3 May 2022.

name: SAT4FOREST
summary: Closed project, run from August 2024 to June 2026 by Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, delivering national forest type, fuel and Natura 2000 monitoring from multispectral, hyperspectral and radar satellite data.

name: SCAN Laboratory, National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
summary: Informatics and telecommunications group at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, partnering with Dryads, whose site says the project demonstrated AI models for wildfire and smoke detection.

name: Scidrones
summary: University of the Aegean spin-off founded in 2021 on Lesvos that develops machine learning for drone-based research and monitoring, and won a CASSINI Maritime Prize for marine litter work.

name: Society for the Protection of Biodiversity of Thrace
summary: Thracian conservation group that says it monitors birds of prey with binoculars, telescopes, tags and satellite transmitters, and searches for dead birds under power lines and turbines.

name: Society for the Protection of Prespa
summary: Conservation society with long-term waterbird monitoring using drone photography, Pelican Watch and Follow the Pelican apps, and funding from MAVA and the Aage V. Jensen Charity Foundation.

name: Stavros Niarchos Foundation
summary: Funder that says it has committed nearly 4 billion dollars to over 3,100 grantee-partners since 1996, including a 2017 grant to the Hellenic Ornithological Society's Important Bird Areas programme.

name: TYTO - Association for the Management and Conservation of Biodiversity in Agricultural Ecosystems
summary: Association that says it has installed 120 barn owl nest boxes across about 1,500 square kilometres of Thessaly farmland since spring 2019, as a monitored pilot.

name: University of Crete
summary: University listed among the 16 partners of the DiSSCo Transition project (2023 to 2025), within whose School of Sciences and Engineering the Natural History Museum of Crete operates.

name: University of Ioannina
summary: University whose Department of Biological Applications and Technology includes the professor who heads the Biodiversity Conservation Lab.

name: University of Patras
summary: Its plant biology section researches species and habitat conservation mapping and monitoring, while an assistant professor lists GIS, telemetry and remote sensing for habitat monitoring.

name: University of the Aegean
summary: Hosts the Marine Remote Sensing Group, partners in BioBoost+ and ANTENNA, and has a marine sciences department using neural networks for fisheries research and underwater acoustics.

name: University of Thessaly
summary: Its team installed LIFE EL-BIOS sensors in Northern Pindos National Park; OpenAlex lists 43 works since 2021 combining machine or deep learning with ecology or biodiversity.

name: WILD LIFE FOR EVER
summary: Closed project, ending in November 2021, whose planned outputs included a Natura 2000 risk assessment model, flying surveillance equipment, a telematic network and a biodiversity database for decision making.

name: WWF Greece
summary: NECCA reports its 2015 Gyaros surveillance installation; it reports satellite imagery use for fire assessment, published Oikoskopio land cover maps and coordinates the Greek Wildlife Alliance.

name: Zoology Museum of the University of Athens
summary: University of Athens museum, described in its GBIF record as about 160 years old, that runs grefaun and whose animal reference database is cited in the GTIS paper.

name: Acciones de conservación y restauración en el Refugio de Vida Silvestre Punta de Manabique
summary: Closed 13-month project in the Punta de Manabique wildlife refuge, funded with EUR 396,000 by the EU, which set up a Copernicus-based marine-coastal monitoring centre and trained 25 people.

name: AI bioacoustic detection of environmental crime in the Maya Biosphere Reserve
summary: Proposed project, as reported by Mongabay, to install bioacoustic devices in the Maya Biosphere Reserve using AI models trained to detect chainsaws and gunshots, with testing planned for 2026.

name: Asociación Balam
summary: Guatemalan civil society organisation constituted in 2001, with citizen science jaguar monitoring; with WWF, it gave CONAP a Maya Biosphere Reserve monitoring manual in April 2022.

name: Asociación de Comunidades Forestales de Petén
summary: Community forestry association whose young monitoring network trained in 2018 on drones; Mongabay reported in 2025 that youths from 13 concessions were trained in drones, satellite data analysis, camera traps and biological monitoring.

name: Asociación de Proyectos Evaluados Raxmu
summary: Guatemalan non-profit, non-governmental organisation for nature conservation and sustainable development whose bird monitoring programme focused on Mesoamerica, with emphasis on Guatemala.

name: Asociación Forestal Integral Cruce a la Colorada
summary: Mongabay reports a CONAP concession contract and spending on drones, camera traps and species apps; WCS reported personnel receiving SMART training in February 2024.

name: Asociación Rescate y Conservación de Vida Silvestre
summary: Guatemalan wildlife organisation (Arcas) that runs crawl count surveys at nine Pacific coast sites and sea turtle research, and says its counts show olive ridley numbers in Guatemala are increasing.

name: Autoridad para el Manejo Sustentable de la Cuenca del Lago de Atitlán y su Entorno
summary: Authority for Lake Atitlán basin, based in Panajachel, whose research department is to assess water quality systematically using sampling equipment and a laboratory, and whose 2025 report tracks cyanobacteria densities.

name: Autoridad para el Manejo Sustentable de la Cuenca y del Lago de Amatitlán
summary: Authority for the Lake Amatitlán basin whose monitoring division checks water periodically and assesses biodiversity through fish and bird health, and which publishes a March 2023 to March 2024 bird report.

name: Censo Centroamericano de Aves Acuáticas en Guatemala
summary: Volunteer waterbird count at chosen wetlands using site and count forms, run by FUNDAECO, which Wetlands International lists as Guatemala's coordinating organisation.

name: Centro de Estudios Biológicos y Sociales de Guatemala
summary: Small company in Mixco researching biodiversity, environmental economics and social sustainability; its 2025 El Triunfo dataset estimated mammal abundance from camera traps in oil palm, riverside and broadleaf forest areas.

name: Centro de Estudios Conservacionistas, Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala
summary: University of San Carlos centre, based in Guatemala City, that GBIF records as holding three institutional biological collections, including a botanic garden and the Centro de Datos para la Conservación.

name: Centro de Monitoreo y Evaluación del CONAP
summary: CONAP programme producing outlooks before each dry season; WCS reported in February 2024 that it and CEMEC had trained about 48 rangers and field technicians in SMART.

name: Closing Distribution Gaps of C. acutus Across the Caribbean Slope and Central Guatemala
summary: Active project aiming at a national survey of American crocodiles; a 2021 Caribbean slope survey found 2.13 crocodiles per kilometre over 56.3 km in Izabal.

name: Consejo Nacional de Áreas Protegidas
summary: Public body responsible, per the CBD secretariat's draft profile, for implementing Guatemala's biodiversity policy; it runs CEMEC, hosts the GBIF node's homepage and led a national forest monitoring roadmap workshop.

name: Estación Biológica Las Guacamayas
summary: Biological station with bird and participatory biodiversity monitoring in Laguna del Tigre, administered by Asociación Balam in 2008, which joined the MoSI network through work with WCS Guatemala.

name: Forestry Management and Protection (FMAP) Guatemala
summary: Project the UK Space Agency said in 2017 it would fund with £5.3 million over three years, using satellite data and GNSS apps to improve timber traceability and reduce deforestation causes.

name: Fundación Defensores de la Naturaleza
summary: Guatemalan conservation foundation listed by GBIF as publishing camera-trap records from managed reserves, whose publisher record reports nearly 40 years’ conservation work and protection of approximately 5% of Guatemala.

name: Fundación para el Ecodesarrollo y la Conservación
summary: Guatemalan conservation and community development organisation, established in 1990, that partners with Panthera on remote cameras for wild cats and, per World Land Trust, has monitored birds for 32 years.

name: Geoportal Comunitario
summary: A community GIS and geoportal that ACOFOP says it developed, offering a biological monitoring dashboard and heat-point maps for information produced under its community monitoring area.

name: Gremial de Palmicultores de Guatemala
summary: A good-practice compilation describes a business organisation established in 2008, providing near real-time Satelligence satellite monitoring from 2020 across 37,770 km² of Guatemala, including members' oil palm plantations.

name: Grupo Interinstitucional de Monitoreo de Bosques y Uso de la Tierra
summary: Working group of Guatemalan government and university bodies with a steering council, under whose coordination by INAB the forest cover change reports and 2020 forest and land use map were produced.

name: Instituto Geográfico Nacional de Guatemala
summary: Technical and scientific body of the agriculture ministry (MAGA), tasked with national geographic information system administration and producing, publishing and distributing official geographic information.

name: Instituto Nacional de Bosques
summary: Guatemala's forestry authority, which runs the forest fire monitoring system, maps fire scars with Landsat 8 imagery and forest cover change, and publishes forest biodiversity data to GBIF.

name: Instituto Privado de Investigación sobre Cambio Climático
summary: Non-profit climate research institute founded in 2010 by sugar sector companies, which monitors aquatic fauna twice a year and breeds and releases three native fish species in four south coast rivers.

name: Mapa de bosques y uso de la tierra, República de Guatemala 2020
summary: Forest and land use map for Guatemala, led by INAB within GIMBUT and cited as a data source for the forest indicator of the national development priorities.

name: Mapa de Cobertura Vegetal y Uso de la Tierra 2025 de Guatemala
summary: Land cover and land use map of Guatemala at 1:50,000, described by the agriculture ministry's catalogue as a 2025 MAGA update through DIGEGR, validated in all 22 departments.

name: Ministerio de Agricultura, Ganadería y Alimentación
summary: Guatemala's agriculture ministry, which builds the 2025 vegetation cover and land use map at 1:50,000, described in its catalogue as validated in all 22 departments.

name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Recursos Naturales
summary: Government ministry named by FAO's GFOI news among institutions at a CONAP-led workshop on the national forest monitoring roadmap; it has a Director of Geospatial Analysis and Climate Change.

name: Monitor de Incendios Forestales en Tiempo Real
summary: ACOFOP's surveillance and early warning system, built and run by ACOFOP, uses NASA FIRMS data to detect heat points and, it says, protects over 15 management units and concessions in the Maya Biosphere Reserve.

name: National Forest Monitoring System of Guatemala
summary: Guatemala's national forest monitoring system, which GFOI reports government institutions have worked on jointly since 2024, producing a nationally owned roadmap reviewed at a 2026 workshop of CONAP, MARN, MAGA and INAB.

name: Passive acoustic monitoring of the resplendent quetzal in the Biotopo Universitario para la Conservación del Quetzal
summary: A closed study, reported by La Hora, that used passive acoustic monitoring and BirdNET to describe resplendent quetzal vocal activity and habitat use over a full year in a Purulhá biotope.

name: Programa de Aves de WCS Guatemala
summary: Run by WCS Guatemala, the programme uses Motus tracking in Tikal and Laguna del Tigre; Marcial Córdova was identified as coordinator at a September 2024 festival.

name: Programa de Monitoreo de Aves de PROEVAL RAXMU
summary: Closed bird monitoring programme run by PROEVAL RAXMU that assessed local avifauna and threatened species; Eisermann & Avendaño Bird Studies say they did most of its studies until 2018.

name: Promoviendo territorios sostenibles y resilientes en paisajes de la cadena volcánica central en Guatemala
summary: Closed project run by Guatemala's environment ministry and funded by the Global Environment Facility, covering 32 municipalities and reporting in May 2023 that monitoring had recorded 175 bird, 44 mammal and 38 amphibian species.

name: Proyecto Gobernanza Forestal: Nuestra Tierra, Nuestros Bosques
summary: EU-funded forest governance project run by ACOFOP and ICCO Cooperación, which in September 2018 was reported to have held a drone workshop for community forest monitoring and fire early warning.

name: Quetzal-1
summary: Guatemala's first satellite, built by Universidad del Valle de Guatemala and handed to JAXA for launch in November 2019, with a mission to measure cyanobacteria chlorophyll in Lake Atitlán.

name: Red de Monitoreo Comunitario
summary: A network run by ACOFOP, created to involve young people from member communities, using camera traps for fauna monitoring and photogrammetry flights to monitor degraded areas in recovery.

name: Sierra Caral combined SMART patrol and passive acoustic monitoring
summary: Closed study combining passive acoustic recording from 2017 to 2021 with 273 SMART patrols in La Firmeza between September 2017 and December 2021.

name: Sistema de Monitoreo Forestal Multipropósito del Ecosistema Manglar
summary: Active mangrove monitoring system based on permanent plots, used by INAB to set technical criteria for incentives, restoration and management, with remote sensing also used for updated cover maps.

name: Sistema Integral de Información para la Gestión de Fuego en Guatemala
summary: Fire information platform, built and run by INAB, that La Hora reports records forest fires and area burnt, monitors heat points by satellite, helps coordinate field response and is open to public consultation.

name: Sistema Nacional de Información sobre Diversidad Biológica de Guatemala
summary: National biodiversity information system, SNIBgt, listed by GBIF as the GBIF Guatemala node and as a data publisher, with Guatemala an associate participant.

name: Standardized Biodiversity Monitoring to Assess the Impact of Climate Change in the Selva Maya
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project in El Mirador National Park, dated 14 December 2020, that aimed to train and equip CONAP staff for monitoring and to trial acoustic surveys of birds and bats.

name: Support for the Monitoring of Biodiversity and Climate Change in the Selva Maya
summary: Concluded project run by GIZ from August 2016, led by CCAD, implementing SMART in Guatemala, Belize and Mexico and reporting information from 52 Petén plots.

name: Uaxactún and Mirador-Río Azul camera-trap survey
summary: Closed WSU and WCS camera-trap survey across about 1,500 square kilometres over two dry seasons, recording 26 species, with similar richness across community-managed forest and neighbouring protected areas.

name: Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala
summary: University whose Centro de Estudios Conservacionistas, according to its GBIF publisher record, is part of the university and holds a conservation data centre.

name: Universidad del Valle de Guatemala
summary: Privately managed Guatemalan university that GBIF lists as a data publisher, hosting three sets of biological collections and handing the satellite Quetzal 1 to JAXA for launch in 2019.

name: WCS Guatemala Program
summary: Programme run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, active in Guatemala since 1992 on the Maya Biosphere Reserve, which published a 2024 GBIF dataset of frog detections from recording units in Laguna del Tigre National Park.

name: Wildlife Conservation Society Guatemala Program
summary: Conservation organisation working in Guatemala since 1992 on the Maya Biosphere Reserve, producing fire information with CONAP's CEMEC, reported by Mongabay in April 2026 as using acoustic devices for about three years.

name: 3D coral reef mapping of Guam's priority reefs
summary: Project run by the University of Miami and University of Guam that, as of July 2022, was producing centimetre-scale 3D maps of Guam's priority reefs, with imagery collected in 2022 still to be processed.

name: Coral Inventory at War in the Pacific National Historical Park
summary: Open-format National Park Service Inventory and Monitoring data package, issued 31 January 2024, recording a 2022 survey of stony corals, coral habitat and stressor evidence at the park's Hågat and Asan units.

name: Eyes of the Reef Marianas
summary: Active programme that, according to Public Radio Guam, teaches local water users to identify and report threats to Guam's coral reefs, supporting long-term reef health data, and resumed in-person training in March 2025.

name: Guam Division of Aquatic and Wildlife Resources
summary: Its Aquatic Section has surveyed offshore and inshore waters since the early 1970s, informing Marine Preserve Area proposals, while freshwater monitoring aims to support watershed management.

name: Guam Environmental Protection Agency
summary: Guam agency whose Monitoring Program carries out the Guam Water Quality Monitoring Strategy to protect fresh and marine waters and monitors damage incidents to the marine environment.

name: Guam Forestry and Soil Resources Division
summary: Forestry division in Mangilao conserving Guam’s forests and requiring permits for live tree removal except tangantangan on government land; UOG reports it led southern reforestation drone monitoring in 2026.

name: Guam Long-term Coral Reef Monitoring Program
summary: Reef monitoring project, run by the University of Guam Marine Laboratory and funded by NOAA, that has surveyed benthic, fish and invertebrate populations at high priority Guam reef areas since 2010.

name: Guam NSF EPSCoR E-RISE
summary: Research project run by the University of Guam and funded by the National Science Foundation, with stated objectives to assess biodiversity across scales and integrate natural resource assessments with advanced data analytics.

name: Guam Plant Extinction Prevention Program
summary: US Forest Service-funded programme working to prevent extinction of Guam's rarest plants, those with fewer than 200 wild individuals, through regular field monitoring of wild and outplanted plants and habitat surveys.

name: Ko'ko' for Cocos Project
summary: Project run by the Division of Aquatic and Wildlife Resources, with several funders and partners, aiming to establish six breeding pairs of Guam rails on Cocos Island, with planned radio telemetry and reported trail camera monitoring.

name: Micronesian Area Geospatial Information Center
summary: University of Guam research hub that leads five grant-funded programmes, including NASA Guam EPSCoR and the UOG Drone Corps, and aims to maintain an online hub of geospatial datasets for Micronesia.

name: NASA Guam EPSCoR
summary: Grant-funded programme led by the Micronesian Area Geospatial Information Center, whose freshwater and coral project collected reef imagery at four Guam sites and processed 1989 to 2021 satellite data for the Northern Guam Lens Aquifer.

name: Research and Environmental Education Fellowship
summary: Ongoing undergraduate fellowship, run by the UOG Center for Island Sustainability and Sea Grant, in which 2026 fellows used AI on CoralNet to analyse reef sites in Yap and Kosrae, all showing steady coral decline.

name: University of Guam
summary: A U.S. Land Grant and Sea Grant university with assistants trained for forest inventory in 2024, second place in a 2026 DARPA challenge and reported reef imaging work.

name: University of Guam Marine Laboratory
summary: A university laboratory running the Guam Long-term Coral Reef Monitoring Program, affiliated with the first author of a 2024 paper on photoquadrat analyses and underwater hyperspectral imaging validation.

name: UOG Center for Island Sustainability and Sea Grant
summary: University of Guam centre that runs the UOG Sea Turtle Monitoring Program, in which visiting Guam Green Growth Conservation Corps members spotted turtle tracks, marked nests and carried out nest inventories during a week of fieldwork.

name: UOG Drone Corps
summary: University of Guam programme that runs drone missions with local agencies for imagery and geospatial data, and had certified 64 remote pilots since 2021 by its sixth cohort in 2026.

name: UOG Reef Flat Monitoring Program
summary: University of Guam Marine Laboratory programme led by Laurie Raymundo that tracks coral communities on Guam's shallow reef flats, with semi-annual collection at five sites as of the 2023 report and Tumon Bay data since 2009.

name: UOG Sea Turtle Monitoring Program
summary: Active sea turtle project, run by the UOG Center for Island Sustainability and Sea Grant and funded by the Department of the Navy for Joint Region Marianas, involving spotting tracks, marking nests and nest inventories.

name: CAJU - Cashew in West Africa: socio-economic and environmental challenges of an expanding cash crop
summary: Concluded research project, begun in 2012 and lasting three years, combining ecological surveys, ethnographic studies and remote sensing to examine cashew expansion effects on livelihoods, ecosystem services and biodiversity across 21 villages in eastern Guinea-Bissau.

name: CARBOVEG
summary: National programme that, according to Guinea-Bissau's 2019 forest reference emission level submission, used satellite imagery for country-wide forest cover maps and supplied field inventories from 2007 and 2009; current status unknown.

name: Consolidation of sea turtle conservation in Guinea-Bissau
summary: Closed MAVA-funded project dated 2018 to 2020 by CE3C, which said most funds would support managing two marine protected areas for green turtles, including surveillance and monitoring.

name: Guinea-Bissau Convention on Biological Diversity Clearing House Mechanism
summary: Active site presenting itself as Guinea-Bissau's Convention on Biological Diversity Clearing House Mechanism, which reports a March 2023 capacity-building workshop on the national mechanism.

name: Guinea-Bissau National Forest Monitoring System
summary: Forest monitoring programme run by the Instituto da Biodiversidade e das Areas Protegidas, which a 2019 submission says was being piloted, with a safeguards system, across the roughly 750,000-hectare terrestrial protected areas network.

name: Guitarfish satellite tagging in the João Vieira–Poilão Marine National Park
summary: Closed project in which, PRCM reported in May 2025, six adult guitarfish were satellite-tagged to track movements for eight months, led by experts from IBAP, INIPO and Wageningen University.

name: Impacts of Climate Change on West African Green Turtles and Marine Turtle Conservation in Guinea-Bissau
summary: Rufford-funded turtle conservation project (grant £9,989) that planned community monitoring at a Cacheu nesting beach; a November 2018 update reports 142 green turtle nests found across seven beaches from August to October 2018.

name: Instituto da Biodiversidade e das Áreas Protegidas
summary: Mandated to manage Guinea-Bissau’s biodiversity and protected areas, it uses Global Mangrove Watch; reports describe GPS-based turtle monitoring in 2021 and ad-hoc mangrove monitoring in 2022.

name: Mapping Cashew Orchards in Cantanhez National Park (Guinea-Bissau)
summary: Project described in a 2022 paper that develops an automatic cashew orchard detection procedure using machine learning and Sentinel-2 images, as a case study in Cantanhez National Park and a step towards operational monitoring.

name: Poilão Island sea turtle monitoring and tracking
summary: Active project run by IBAP in which, Mongabay reported in 2021, local staff count nests on Poilão and follow adult turtles, with 45 females satellite-tagged between 2018 and 2020 with ISPA.

name: Protecting the critically endangered western chimpanzee in Guinea-Bissau
summary: Born Free-supported project, reported in January 2018 as led by Maria Joana Ferreira da Silva, developing a country-scale primate conservation strategy using modelling, surveys and DNA analysis, and monitoring the primate meat trade.

name: Proteção e Restauração de Mangais e Paisagem produtiva para fortalecer a segurança alimentar e mitigar as mudanças climáticas
summary: Mangrove restoration project in Guinea-Bissau, funded by the Global Environment Facility and dated July 2016 to January 2025, whose January 2023 mission planned drone mapping of restored areas and a 2024 guide covers drone monitoring.

name: Securing the ecological integrity of the Bijagós archipelago as a key site for waders along the East Atlantic Flyway
summary: Closed project, dated 2018 to 2020 on the CE3C page, covering applied ecological research on wintering shorebirds and local research and monitoring capacity, led by Teresa Catry of CESAM and funded by the MAVA Foundation.

name: Seeking people-primate coexistence: endangered primate responses to anthropogenic activities and land transformation in Guinea-Bissau
summary: Primate study in Cantanhez and Dulombi National Parks, awarded $12,000 in June 2015, which planned camera trap surveys and occupancy models to study distribution, with an Oxford Brookes University research group as recipient.

name: To Plant or Not to Plant Guinea Bissau, Phase 2
summary: Active 2026 to 2030 restoration project in the Cantanhez and Cacheu landscapes, run and built by Wetlands International, combining annual field monitoring with remote sensing to track restored sites.

name: Vultures in Guinea-Bissau: developing monitoring tools, assessing conservation status, and raising awareness concerning their provision of ecosystem services
summary: Its final report records Rufford grant use from December 2015 to December 2016, a field-tested vulture monitoring method, and a nationwide census of all species including the Bijagós archipelago.

name: Caiman House
summary: Village-run research station on the Rupununi River, self-described, where Yupukari's citizen scientists have studied black caiman since 2005 and river turtles since 2011, including a long-term mark-recapture caiman study.

name: Conservation and Sustainable Resource Use in Guyana's Kanuku Mountains Protected Area (camera-trap monitoring)
summary: Camera-trap project run by the Protected Areas Commission using 14 cameras, which captured over 130,000 images in six months, documented 39 species, and showed declining black curassow occupancy using Wildlife Insights.

name: Conservation International Guyana
summary: Guyana office of Conservation International, working there since 1989 on species and protected areas, whose eDNA analysis of 70 samples reported 494 vertebrate species, some identified only to family level.

name: eDNA as a Tool for Biodiversity Baselines in Region 1 and 9
summary: Project that collected 70 eDNA water samples across Regions 1 and 9 using NatureMetrics kits, with 25 local community members trained, and samples shipped to the UK for analysis.

name: Environmental Management Consultants Inc.
summary: Guyanese consultancy, established in 2005 and incorporated in 2020, which says it carries out biodiversity assessments, monitoring and management plans for clients, with flora and fauna specialists.

name: Environmental Protection Agency (Guyana)
summary: Guyana's biodiversity convention focal point according to GBIF's publisher record, which also describes its project to strengthen management of biodiversity data and widen access to it.

name: Faculty of Earth and Environmental Sciences, University of Guyana
summary: University of Guyana faculty at Turkeyen Campus, whose member is first author of a 2024 paper on mangrove ecosystems and hydrological regimes in coastal Guyana using remote sensing, as listed by OpenAlex.

name: GBIF Guyana
summary: Guyana's country node in GBIF, listed with voting participation status, created in the directory in May 2026, led by Yohan Parmanand and based on Ganges Street, Georgetown.

name: Guyana Forestry Commission
summary: Runs Guyana's MRVS, whose 2020 report describes deforestation mapping largely using Sentinel-2 imagery, and was reported by Esri to be developing an ArcGIS deforestation dashboard.

name: Guyana Lands and Surveys Commission
summary: Guyana's national mapping agency according to Ordnance Survey, which says it worked with the Commission to restore its national network operations centre and eight-site reference station network.

name: Guyana Mangrove Information System (GuyMIS)
summary: Web application for monitoring mangrove extent and change in Guyana, built and run by SERVIR and used by NAREI, with Random Forest maps from optical and radar imagery for 2010, 2015 and 2020.

name: Guyana Marine Conservation Society
summary: Non-governmental organisation that describes itself as Guyana's oldest and only marine-focused NGO, and which ran a sea turtle monitoring programme with community rangers from 2000 to 2010.

name: Guyana National Biodiversity Monitoring Initiative
summary: Programme launched by President Irfaan Ali in July 2025 to standardise biodiversity monitoring nationally, using the NBIS so a consortium can consolidate existing data and develop shared collection systems.

name: Guyana REDD+ Monitoring, Reporting and Verification System
summary: Forest monitoring system run by the Guyana Forestry Commission and funded by Norad, tracking forest cover change since 1990, with a GGGI project planned from February 2025 to March 2027 to add mangrove mapping.

name: Guyana Sea Turtle Telemetry Project
summary: Ongoing project with the Turtle Conservancy and Environmental Management Consultants Inc. to study distribution and migration of four turtle species nesting at Shell Beach, including satellite tagging in May 2023.

name: Guyana Wildlife Conservation and Management Commission
summary: Agency established in 2017 and designated CITES Management Authority for Guyana, which conducts research on species status and threats to wildlife and partners with Iwokrama.

name: Integrated Ecosystem Assessment and Biodiversity financing in Guyana's new Acarai-Rupununi Corridor (ARC) Conservation Forests
summary: Proposed GEF-funded project, partnered with Conservation International, to set up a National Biodiversity Information System and monitoring framework for Guyana and pilot biodiversity valuation and financing; concept listed as approved 28 April 2026.

name: Iwokrama International Centre
summary: Established in 1996, this non-profit manages 371,000 hectares of rainforest and uses remote sensing, field surveys, ecological indicators and Indigenous knowledge in monitoring.

name: Kanashen Village Council
summary: Village Council of Kanashen, a body corporate under Guyana's Amerindian Act and sole management authority of the Kanashen Amerindian Protected Area since its 2017 declaration, employing rangers for monitoring, patrols and data collection, with Protected Areas Trust funding.

name: National Agricultural Research and Extension Institute
summary: Guyanese agricultural research institute, established in 2011, which took on mangrove restoration and management in 2014, offers mangrove forest monitoring, and held a January 2020 radar monitoring workshop.

name: National Biodiversity Information System (Guyana)
summary: Platform for managing, visualising and analysing biodiversity data, built on Map of Life, forming the data foundation of Guyana's national monitoring initiative, with a border-to-border system planned by 2030.

name: Protected Areas Commission
summary: Operational since 2012, this statutory body has a mandate covering the National Protected Areas System and partners with Iwokrama.

name: Protected Areas Trust (Guyana)
summary: Describes itself as Guyana's only national environmental trust fund, and issued its first grant, for turtle monitoring at Shell Beach, in 2017.

name: Rapid Inventory 32, Acarai-Rupununi Corridor, Guyana
summary: Closed Field Museum rapid inventory of the 1.5 million hectare Acarai-Rupununi Corridor, fieldwork in November 2024 with Guyanese government, Indigenous experts and scientists, finding dozens of undescribed species; report published July 2025.

name: Red Siskin Research and Conservation (South Rupununi)
summary: Project run by the South Rupununi Conservation Society which, after long monitoring and data gathering, works with five communities to monitor a community-based conservation management zone for the red siskin.

name: Rupununi Wildlife Research Unit
summary: Self-described collaboration involving a University of Florida academic and Rupununi communities, ranches and conservation organisations, reporting over 100 researchers trained since 2011, with camera-trap work and jaguar research.

name: Shell Beach sea turtle monitoring
summary: Turtle monitoring run by the Protected Areas Commission and funded by the Protected Areas Trust, which reports 92% of nests relocated to hatcheries in 2024 and patrol hours down 58% from erosion.

name: Sophia Point Rainforest Inc
summary: Guyana Times reports it is a UK-registered charity and Guyanese not-for-profit; it uses camera traps and bioacoustic recorders, and in spring 2026 its rangers were collecting eDNA for a programme with CNRS and the University of Guyana.

name: South Rupununi Conservation Society
summary: Society registered in 2002, according to Mongabay, that trains and pays local residents to research and protect wildlife, including camera-trap work on giant anteaters and armadillos.

name: South Rupununi District Council
summary: Representative body of the elected Toshaos of 21 Wapichan communities in southern Guyana, according to Rainforest Foundation US, and a co-creator of the Earth Defenders Toolkit.

name: South Rupununi giant anteater research and conservation project
summary: Two-year giant anteater research and protection project run by SRCS, announced in late 2020 with GEF Small Grants funding, which placed 40 camera traps on a 1 km grid in October 2021.

name: South Rupununi giant armadillo research and conservation project
summary: Camera-trap study, running since August 2023 across the titled land of three communities, of giant armadillo population, range and behaviour; SRCS says Guyana had no specific giant armadillo study before 2023.

name: South Rupununi wildfire research and monitoring
summary: Research project, with South Rupununi Conservation Society as partner, studying how land and fire use changes affect fire regimes and wildfire management in the South Rupununi savannas.

name: SWM Programme biodiversity monitoring pilot, Rupununi
summary: Biodiversity monitoring pilot in the Rupununi, run by CIFOR-ICRAF and funded by the European Union; Guyana Times reported in October 2025 that 28 Indigenous monitors from seven communities had used camera traps, acoustic devices and eDNA since March 2025.

name: The Guiana Shield in the Face of Global Change, Advancing Environmental Genomics for Biodiversity Monitoring in Amazonia
summary: CNRS-funded project involving the University of Guyana that uses nanopore sequencing; its team has run eDNA training across Guyana, French Guiana and Brazil, with bioinformatics training planned.

name: University of Guyana
summary: Guyanese university affiliated with all four authors of a 2024 mangrove remote sensing paper, whose graduate research school appears in a 2023 logging roads mammal paper.

name: Yellow-spotted Amazon River Turtle Community Monitoring and Head-start (Yupukari)
summary: Ongoing village project run by Caiman House, founded in 2011 by a Caiman House intern, aiming to reduce annual losses of adults, hatchlings and nests and to found a community-based management strategy.

name: 114°E Hong Kong Reef Fish Survey
summary: Reef fish survey run by Bloom Association, designed to give baseline data on Hong Kong's reef fish diversity (species number, qualitative abundance, distribution), with non-scientist recreational divers helping collect the data underwater.

name: AFCD baseline ecological monitoring programme for the Ramsar Site
summary: Long-term baseline ecological monitoring programme for the Ramsar Site, which AFCD's 2017-2018 annual report says it had implemented since 2001, covering benthic communities and wetland habitat condition.

name: AFCD long-term marine mammal monitoring
summary: Marine mammal monitoring study funded by the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department, whose 2023-24 surveys recorded 163 groups of Chinese white dolphins, with acoustic monitoring also funded from 2017 to 2024.

name: AFCD long-term monitoring programme of Hong Kong mammals
summary: Monitoring programme of Hong Kong mammals that AFCD launched in 2002 to estimate species numbers, abundance and distribution; its 2008 to 2018 camera trap survey recorded porcupine, wild pig and red muntjac at over 60% of traps.

name: AFCD territory-wide ecological survey programme
summary: Territory-wide ecological survey programme that AFCD's 2017-2018 annual report says it had conducted since 2002 to maintain a Hong Kong ecological database, which held over 311,400 species records by March 2018.

name: Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department
summary: A Hong Kong government department that patrols and enforces against illegal wildlife feeding, and whose AI CCTV trial at two Kam Shan Country Park car parks led to 13 successful prosecutions.

name: AI butterfly identification system (Fung Yuen Butterfly Reserve)
summary: Funded by the Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme, this system at Fung Yuen could identify 10 butterfly species in early 2025, with plans for 245 within two years.

name: Archireef
summary: Marine restoration spin-out from the University of Hong Kong that deployed Reef Tiles at Hong Kong marine parks, using eDNA for species detection and photogrammetry to track coral growth.

name: Citizen Science Programme for Subtidal Habitats in Hoi Ha Wan Marine Park
summary: Two-year citizen science programme in Hoi Ha Wan Marine Park, run by AFCD and described in the past tense in its 2025 feature, which included monitoring coral coverage and composition.

name: Clear Robotics
summary: Start-up founded by four university students in March 2020 that reports a Hong Kong headquarters and builds the AI-powered open-source Open Ocean Camera for research, conservation and citizen science.

name: Constructing the First DNA Barcode Reference Library of Hong Kong Moths
summary: Project to build the first DNA barcode reference library of Hong Kong moths, listed by the HKU Faculty of Science as an Environment and Conservation Fund award of HK$1,318,639.

name: Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme
summary: A funding scheme launched in October 2019 and run by the Countryside Conservation Office; 50 projects had been approved by the end of 2024 with about $270 million, including the Fung Yuen AI butterfly system.

name: Countryside Conservation Office
summary: A body set up in 2018 under the Environment and Ecology Bureau to co-ordinate sustainable development of remote countryside areas, which runs the Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme.

name: Department of Biology, Hong Kong Baptist University
summary: University department that led 2024 papers on a DNA barcode reference database for Hong Kong marine animals and on refining environmental DNA sampling for fish diversity assessment.

name: Department of Mechanical and Automation Engineering, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
summary: Department at the Chinese University of Hong Kong involved in a horseshoe crab survey pilot described by its CityU co-investigator as using AI deep learning.

name: Department of Science and Environmental Studies, The Education University of Hong Kong
summary: University department that led a 2024 paper on AI-assisted environmental DNA metabarcoding and underwater imaging, and whose staff also authored a 2024 paper on eDNA and RNA metabarcoding of marine fishes.

name: EcoMatcher
summary: Hong Kong-headquartered tree-planting company that says it develops its TreeTech in-house to make planted trees and their impact visible and traceable, and enables planting through vetted local partners.

name: eDNA & eEcology Lab, School of Biological Sciences, The University of Hong Kong
summary: University of Hong Kong lab that led a study using environmental DNA to measure human impacts on marine biodiversity, collecting 240 water samples over seven months from 12 mesocosms.

name: Environment and Conservation Fund
summary: Statutory trust fund operating since August 1994 that funds nature conservation projects, including a Lingnan University amphibian and reptile specimen collection from 2019 to 2021.

name: Environment and Ecology Bureau
summary: A Hong Kong government bureau that runs the Countryside Conservation Office, which sits under it.

name: Environmental Association
summary: Charitable institution managing Fung Yuen Butterfly Reserve that launched a 2024 AI butterfly recognition programme and built an identification system, with countryside conservation funding received.

name: Environmental Protection Department
summary: Government department whose Hong Kong Environmental Database won the International Association for Impact Assessment’s 2025 Corporate Initiative Award.

name: Green Power
summary: Tax-exempt charity whose Butterfly Survey, launched in 2008 and conducted by citizens, recorded 184 species in 2024–2025, about 70% of Hong Kong’s total, and which lists Lantau dragonfly results.

name: HKBirds: Birds of Hong Kong
summary: App for observing, identifying, recording and sharing bird records, built by HKU's School of Biological Sciences and the Hong Kong Bird Watching Society under a Knowledge Exchange Fund-supported project, with HKU Computer Science technical support.

name: Hong Kong Biodiversity Information Hub
summary: Biodiversity data hub launched in 2022, built by the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department, whose mapping system launched in January 2025 held over a million local species occurrence records.

name: Hong Kong Environmental Database
summary: Mapping database built by the Environmental Protection Department, integrating over 100 types of baseline survey data, with an AI application using large language models planned in March 2025.

name: Hong Kong Herbarium
summary: Herbarium run by the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department that collects, identifies and curates Hong Kong flora specimens and compiles the Check List of Hong Kong Plants.

name: Hong Kong Marine Life Stranding Online Database
summary: Public online database run by OPCFHK, with data collected under an agreement with AFCD to investigate cetacean stranding cases in Hong Kong.

name: Hong Kong Plant Database
summary: Database run by the Hong Kong Herbarium recording more than 3,300 Hong Kong plants, based mainly on herbarium specimen records, with over 11,700 high-resolution images.

name: Hong Kong Reef Check
summary: AFCD-run reef survey involving over 1,150 divers across 33 sites in 2023 and over 1,170 in 2024, first held by Hong Kong Reef Check Foundation in 1997.

name: Hong Kong Register of Marine Species
summary: Database led by the Swire Institute of Marine Science and funded by the Environment and Conservation Fund, aiming to provide globally accessible taxonomic information on Hong Kong marine species.

name: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
summary: University whose staff authored a 2025 coral reef image labelling tool paper and who, from June 2018, worked with the Drainage Services Department on AI cameras counting egrets, per a 2019 government report.

name: Hong Kong Wetland Park
summary: Park run by AFCD that carries out continuous ecological monitoring of wildlife and water quality, with bird surveys along fixed routes showing 300 bird species recorded at the Wetland Reserve as of 2025.

name: Hong Kong Wildtracks
summary: Database of over 60,000 local ecological entries, including wildlife sounds, bird distribution and species abundance, built by the Hong Kong Bird Watching Society with a website developed by Hong Kong Baptist University's library.

name: Horseshoe crab UAS and AI survey pilot programme (Ha Pak Nai)
summary: Two-year pilot at the Ha Pak Nai mudflat using drones and AI for horseshoe crab surveys, built by a CUHK department, which by June 2025 identified juveniles with accuracy above 90%.

name: International Black-faced Spoonbill Census
summary: Annual January census run by the Hong Kong Bird Watching Society, whose 2024 count across 11 regions recorded 6,988 Black-faced Spoonbills with over 200 experts and volunteers.

name: Kadoorie Farm and Botanic Garden
summary: Private nature reserve of about 148 hectares reporting camera captures of all Hong Kong’s medium-to-large terrestrial mammals and analysis of 131 years of otter records.

name: Ocean Park Conservation Foundation, Hong Kong
summary: Charitable trust established in 1995 that has funded 560 research projects since 2005.

name: OPCFHK horseshoe crab population survey
summary: Horseshoe crab population survey run by OPCFHK, which as of June 2025 had surveyed breeding and nursery mudflats since 2014 and collected data at four monitoring stations.

name: Open Ocean Camera
summary: Underwater camera system built by Clear Robotics that records for up to a month at depths to 400 metres, with AI software that identifies and counts animals and a public code base.

name: School of Biological Sciences, The University of Hong Kong
summary: School within the University of Hong Kong involved with the Hong Kong Bird Watching Society in the HKBirds iOS app for observing, identifying, recording and sharing bird records.

name: Science Unit, Lingnan University
summary: University unit that, with the Hong Kong Bird Watching Society, quantified 20-year waterbird population trends in Deep Bay, and began a 2019 to 2021 specimen collection funded by the Environment and Conservation Fund.

name: Seahorse Survey and Tagging Project
summary: Project run by OPCFHK to document seahorse numbers, species, size, sex and distribution in shallow Hong Kong coral communities, with tagging begun in 2013 to track survival, growth and home range.

name: State Key Laboratory of Marine Pollution
summary: Laboratory, named in an author affiliation as part of City University of Hong Kong, that is the corresponding institution on three 2024 studies using eDNA and marine indicators.

name: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
summary: University that is the corresponding institution on studies from 2022 to 2025 covering mangrove change in the Greater Bay Area, coastal wetland bird habitat and remote sensing for mangrove valuation.

name: The Hong Kong Bird Watching Society
summary: Charitable organisation whose 2020 report describes its coordination of waterbird monitoring carried out since 1998, and which initiates the International Black-faced Spoonbill Census each January.

name: The Swire Institute of Marine Science
summary: A University of Hong Kong marine research facility at Cape d'Aguilar that is compiling a marine biodiversity database, with a first planned upload from a rocky shore survey recording over 412 species.

name: The University of Hong Kong
summary: University that runs the Swire Institute of Marine Science and is corresponding institution on studies from 2024 to 2026 on eDNA metabarcoding, satellite monitoring of migration and otter persistence.

name: WWF-Hong Kong
summary: A non-profit conservation organisation that uses IoT, AI and real-time monitoring in its work, and has deployed over 100 IoT devices across Mai Po since 2022.

name: WWF-Hong Kong smart conservation at Mai Po
summary: A WWF-Hong Kong programme started in 2022 to apply technology at Mai Po, with over 100 IoT devices deployed and a July 2024 'Smart Wetland 2.0' project using AI-assisted mammal identification.

name: Alerta Bosque
summary: According to La Prensa’s sponsored article, ICF developed this forest alert verification app with EU funding, initially for technical staff, with public versions planned, inspired by GFW’s Forest Watcher.

name: Asociación Amigos de los Arrecifes de Tela
summary: Non-profit legally recognised since 12 July 2017, co-managing the Tela Bay Marine Wildlife Refuge, with coral reef research and monitoring partly funded by Coral Reef Alliance sub-grants.

name: Asociación Cuerpos de Conservación Omoa
summary: A self-described non-governmental, non-profit environmental organisation in Cuyamel, Omoa, that co-manages three protected areas and lists habitat monitoring and community night watches of turtle nesting beaches among its work.

name: Asociación Hondureña de Ornitología
summary: Bird association, now known as Aves de Honduras, which El País reported in February 2023 had run a new waterbird census, part of monitoring done since 2012, with forty members taking part.

name: Bay Islands Conservation Association
summary: A private non-profit founded in 1990 with chapters on Utila, Roatán and Guanaja, which monitors reefs, seagrass, mangroves and water quality and tracks stony coral tissue loss disease to decide where to treat.

name: BICA seagrass and sediment carbon monitoring in the Bay Islands (CariCAS)
summary: A 2025 seagrass and sediment monitoring programme on Utila, Roatán and Guanaja, run by BICA under the CariCAS method, with 15 sites sampled from May to July to set a carbon baseline.

name: Centro de Estudios Marinos
summary: Honduran NGO established in 2006 to build technical capacity in applied research for managing marine biodiversity, and named in a July 2025 UNAH article as carrying out reef monitoring with the natural resources ministry and others.

name: Dirección General de Biodiversidad
summary: A unit of the environment ministry, run by it, which a 2016 leaflet calls the national body regulating biodiversity and which was created in 1997 by Executive Decree 008-97.

name: Eagle ray photo-ID, Bay Islands
summary: A citizen-science project in which divers and snorkellers submit photos of spotted eagle rays, identifiable by their markings, to study movements and seasonality around the Bay Islands and Mesoamerican Reef.

name: Facultad de Ingeniería, Universidad Tecnológica Centroamericana
summary: A San Pedro Sula engineering faculty named, according to OpenAlex, as the affiliation of all three authors of a 2022 IEEE paper on coral detection with neural networks at Cayo Blanco.

name: Five Great Forests of Mesoamerica in La Moskitia, Honduras
summary: An EU-funded project that, according to a February 2026 WCS article, has supported conservation in La Moskitia, including community camera trapping, track identification and SMART threat recording, with WCS and ICF as partners.

name: Fundación Cayos Cochinos
summary: Its website reports sea turtle studies under Honduras Coral Reef Fund management since 1998 and coral restoration nurseries holding over 500 Acropora cervicornis fragments.

name: Fundación Cuero y Salado
summary: Foundation aiming to conserve the natural resources of the Barras de Cuero y Salado wildlife refuge, with a research programme that monitors ecosystem health, wildlife populations and biological and physical indicators.

name: Fundación Islas de la Bahía
summary: Private non-profit recognised by the Honduran government, which cares for the Iguana Research and Breeding Station, researches Ctenosaura bakeri and invasive species, and breeds and releases the Critically Endangered Utila spiny-tailed iguana.

name: Fundación para la Investigación y Conservación de los Ecosistemas y la Biodiversidad
summary: Foundation whose Apu Pauni project researches and conserves macaws in Honduras, with a GBIF record reporting Miskito community patrols cut nest looting by 80 per cent.

name: Fundación para la Protección de Lancetilla, Punta Sal y Texiguat
summary: A Honduran NGO that co-administers Punta Izopo National Park and, in a MAR Fund project planned for August 2025 to June 2028, would study mangrove cover with drones and train staff in monitoring.

name: Geoportal ForeSIG
summary: Geoportal publishing 110 geographic layers on Honduras for consultation, analysis and download, covering forest, hydrological, energy and administrative data, and run by the Universidad Nacional de Ciencias Forestales.

name: Honduras Mesoamerica Forest IP Project: Conserving the Intact Forests of the Honduran Moskitia
summary: A full-size GEF-8 project in Honduras approved on 22 October 2024 to improve conservation of Moskitia ecosystems, with IUCN's design request planning acoustic monitoring and remote sensing for fire detection.

name: ilili Honduras
summary: A non-profit working on sharks and rays in Honduras through research, education and collaboration, including a citizen-science project on eagle rays in the Bay Islands.

name: Instituto de Investigación en Ciencias Biológicas del Norte de Honduras
summary: Research institute with permanent water quality monitoring in Barras de Cuero y Salado, flooded forest carbon assessments and Honduras’s first seagrass carbon sequestration validation.

name: Instituto de la Propiedad
summary: A Honduran body whose creation, according to a 2020 report to SIRGAS, merged the national geographic institute and cadastre directorate, with functions that include coordinating the country's cartographic and geodetic system.

name: Instituto Nacional de Conservación y Desarrollo Forestal, Áreas Protegidas y Vida Silvestre
summary: Honduras's forest and protected areas institute, which by law must keep the national forest and biodiversity inventories updated and runs the forest monitoring information system and SMART-FIRE.

name: Kanahau Utila Research and Conservation Facility
summary: Registered NGO on Utila whose long-term research on the Utila spiny-tailed iguana, dating to 2012, estimates populations by mark-recapture and also uses camera trapping, habitat surveys and radio telemetry.

name: Mapa Nacional de Cobertura Forestal y Uso de la Tierra 2024
summary: A national land cover map with 23 categories showing 51.6% of Honduras under forest, led by ICF's Forest Monitoring Unit with FAO Honduras funding and technical help, according to ICF's minister.

name: MarAlliance marine megafauna research and monitoring in Honduras
summary: A MarAlliance-run project reporting Honduras's first North Coast shark and ray study, seventeen fishers trained in standard monitoring methods and a 2017 Bay Islands baseline survey.

name: Mesa Nacional de Monitoreo Biológico
summary: A national body that, according to a November 2024 Pew article, was charged by a 2018 agreement with knowledge management of environmental resources and was reviewing national mangrove and seagrass monitoring methods.

name: MOPAWI (Agencia para el Desarrollo de la Mosquitia)
summary: A non-profit working with Indigenous and mestizo peoples of the Mosquitia, which IUCN says helped develop territorial monitoring plans and trained Indigenous monitors in technological tools through VOCES.

name: Panthera Honduras
summary: Panthera's Honduras programme, active since 2009, which used camera traps to document jaguars and now focuses on ranger teams and SMART patrols, reporting a fall in poaching in some areas.

name: Proyecto Conecta+
summary: A SERNA project funded by the GEF through UNDP, with FAO as an executing partner, described in an October 2023 UNDP article as having equipped community forest protection crews.

name: RMP iPatrol
summary: Roatan Marine Park's mobile app, through which users report environmental impact within the park to local authorities, and which is part of the park's community patrol training.

name: Roatan Institute for Marine Sciences
summary: A marine science institute at Anthony's Key Resort, Sandy Bay, which began a long-term reef monitoring project in 1996 and says it has built a substantial database on Roatan's reefs.

name: Roatan Marine Park
summary: A community-based non-profit conserving Roatán's protected marine area, which uses SMART for patrols, monitors spawning sites, offers a public reporting app, and in 2026 began mapping sargassum.

name: Secretaría de Recursos Naturales y Ambiente
