summary: Honduras's environment ministry, formerly called MiAmbiente, which runs the Conecta+ project and whose approved 2026 budget targets preparing and presenting the seventh national biodiversity report.

name: Shark Sightings Database for the Bay Islands of Honduras
summary: According to ilili, it established this Bay Islands shark sightings database with Roatan Marine Park, the Whale Shark Oceanic Research Center and Sea Leucas, inviting public reports.

name: Sistema de Información de Biodiversidad CHM Honduras
summary: A biodiversity information system for which the approved 2026 budget of the environment ministry sets a target to update it and includes a record of visits.

name: Sistema de Información para la Gestión y Monitoreo Forestal
summary: ICF's official forest sector information platform, made so by Acuerdo 002-2019, which monitors forest cover and draws on other ICF systems including SIRMA, the national forest inventory and an ODK collector.

name: Sistema Informático para Rastreabilidad de la Madera
summary: The timber traceability information system, SIRMA, which a 2019 ICF agreement lists among the systems already established within ICF.

name: SMART-FIRE
summary: A free monitoring system based on geospatial data analysis and hosted on Google Earth Engine, which came out of the Conecta+ project and is built and run by ICF, with FAO also a builder.

name: Universidad Nacional Autónoma de Honduras
summary: Its CURLA presentation covers 2015–2018 reef and seagrass monitoring in Trujillo Bay and Laguna de Guaimoreto; a 2018 agreement lists its national biological monitoring board membership.

name: Universidad Nacional de Ciencias Forestales
summary: University whose GIS volunteer group, ForeSIG, gathers the information published on the ForeSIG geoportal of Honduran geospatial data.

name: Universidad Tecnológica Centroamericana
summary: A Honduran university whose engineering faculty affiliates all authors of a 2022 coral detection paper at Cayo Blanco, which presented Earth Observation Centre products in September 2026.

name: Universidad Zamorano
summary: Founded in 1942, this university protects the 907-hectare Uyuca Biological Reserve; its 2020 report mentions a biodiversity centre, GBIF, citizen science and 8,074 biodiversity monitoring records on its properties.

name: Utila Whale Shark Project
summary: Completed study by the Marine Megafauna Foundation, which says it analysed over a decade of sightings with Utila Whale Shark Research and identified 95 individual whale sharks, published in 2013.

name: WCS Honduras
summary: Programme run by the Wildlife Conservation Society that, in October 2025, reported installing 14 camera traps and six acoustic recorders in Montecristo National Park with the Biodiverse Landscapes Fund, and has begun supporting reef monitoring.

name: Whale Shark & Oceanic Research Centre
summary: A registered Honduran non-profit on Utila that says it has gathered whale shark data since 1997, holds the only research permit for them in Honduras, and maintains a coral nursery.

name: Adriatic Dolphin Project
summary: Programme run by the Blue World Institute that has tracked Adriatic dolphins through dorsal fin photo-identification for more than 35 years.

name: Association BIOM
summary: Croatian civil society nature conservation organisation, working since 2006 according to its own account, with offices in Zagreb and Sinj, which published a GBIF dataset of at-sea seabird surveys from the LIFE Artina project (2019 to 2021).

name: Atlas bioraznolikosti Hrvatske (BioAtlas)
summary: Described by the ministry as Croatia’s first national open biodiversity data system, it uses Living Atlases and holds a 2025 Učka dataset under CC BY 4.0.

name: Biodiversity Monitoring in Kopački Rit Nature Park
summary: Project with Rainforest Connection and partners that, it says, recorded at 95 sites in the park in April to June 2023, reporting 75 species detected and training a neural network on spectrograms.

name: Biom
summary: Organisation based in Zagreb that says it tested MegaDetector on about 70,000 photographs and videos from LIFE Artina seabird nests, and whose 2025 report describes GPS-transmitter bird monitoring.

name: Bioportal
summary: Web portal of the Information System for Nature Protection, run and built by the Institute for Environment and Nature, whose GBIF page describes consolidating local data.

name: Bioterra
summary: NGO of researchers, as described by NatureSpy, who monitor wolves, lynx, bears, wildcats and other mammals in the Velebit Mountains and Biokovo, largely with trail cameras, over 40 donated by NatureSpy.

name: Blue World Institute of Marine Research and Conservation
summary: Based in Veli Lošinj and incorporated in 1999, it organises research, education and conservation work, tagging loggerheads since 2006 and, reportedly in June 2025, an Adriatic bottlenose dolphin.

name: Center for Marine Research, Ruđer Bošković Institute
summary: Interdisciplinary oceanographic research centre in Rovinj, run by the Ruđer Bošković Institute, listing the MIRAMAR cumulative-impacts monitoring project as active until December 2027.

name: Centre of Excellence MARBLE
summary: Zagreb limited company that says it receives Horizon Europe funding and offers acoustic sensing systems detecting underwater events, vessels and fish, with three Adriatic pilot sites.

name: Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts
summary: Zagreb-based academy with a natural sciences class and a scientific council for nature and environmental protection; its Institute of Ornithology is Croatia's bird ringing centre.

name: Croatian Agency for SMEs, Innovations and Investments
summary: Croatian agency that, according to Oikon, co-funds the GEOAI4ESRSE4 project through the Eurostars programme.

name: Croatian Forest Research Institute
summary: Jastrebarsko-based institute whose ecology division lists ICP Forests damage monitoring and Krka National Park work, and which partners in the FORBEECH beech forest monitoring project.

name: Croatian Natural History Museum
summary: Zagreb museum with 1.34 million collection items that runs the Virtual Herbarium; Dnevnik.hr reported in June 2025 that its researcher led Adriatic bottlenose dolphin satellite tagging.

name: Croatian Nature Protection Information System
summary: Set of databases, applications and web services for data on biodiversity, geodiversity, landscape diversity and nature protection in Croatia, with Bioportal as its web portal.

name: Development of the System for Monitoring the Status of Species and Habitat Types
summary: Project whose Group 3 developed bird monitoring programmes and gathered new abundance and distribution data on 80 bird species of EU interest, using the proposed methods to test them for long-term monitoring.

name: Društvo istraživača mora 20000 milja
summary: Zadar-based society of marine biology researchers that in 2016 and 2017 surveyed infralittoral fish in proposed no-take zones by underwater visual census, producing a monitoring protocol, with funding from the Environmental Protection and Energy Efficiency Fund.

name: DVOKUT-ECRO d.o.o.
summary: Company that gave Brijuni National Park expert support from December 2024 to December 2025, under the Interreg GREW project, by monitoring aquatic ecosystems in the Veliki Brijun wetlands, and also monitored invasive alien species for the Pelješac bridge project.

name: eDNA Labs (Labena d.o.o.)
summary: Zagreb company, Labena d.o.o., that carries out environmental DNA analysis from sample collection to bioinformatics, detecting selected species by PCR and assessing whole communities by next-generation sequencing.

name: Enhancing FORest monitoring of BEECH forests in South-East Europe
summary: Project running from 1 February 2026 to 31 August 2027 that aims to link terrestrial and airborne measurements of beech forests in South-East Europe and supply near-real-time data to the FORWARDS platform.

name: Environmental Protection and Energy Efficiency Fund
summary: Co-financed CroSpeleo’s upgrade with HRK 4.6 million after almost HRK 2 million for development; Ruđer Bošković Institute reports national co-financing for marine habitat mapping.

name: Faculty of Agrobiotechnical Sciences Osijek
summary: University faculty in Osijek whose project lead told Dnevnik.hr in January 2026 that bioacoustic monitoring and machine learning had identified over 70 animal species in two years.

name: Flora Croatica Database
summary: National plant database owned by the Faculty of Science, University of Zagreb, described in a 2020 review as thirty years old, with 175 tables and a geoportal for spatial data.

name: ForFungi DNA
summary: Closed project, hosted by the Ruđer Bošković Institute from October 2018 to September 2022, that aimed to study fungal diversity in Croatian forests using DNA barcoding and morphological taxonomy.

name: GBIF Croatia
summary: Croatia's country node in GBIF's register, with voting participation status and a node manager based in Zagreb.

name: Geonatura d.o.o.
summary: Zagreb company, founded in 2008, offering species and habitat monitoring and distribution mapping, which monitored hibernating bats around Krka National Park in January 2026 and summer bat colonies in June 2026.

name: Hrvatsko društvo za zaštitu ptica i prirode
summary: Non-governmental organisation named in the 2022 waterbird census guide as the source of the national coordinator who sends Croatia's data, for a count running since 1982.

name: Hrvatsko herpetološko društvo – Hyla
summary: Zagreb-based society whose 2025 work included 23 of 31 projects monitoring target species, with 368 field days and 5,066 species records entered through Biologer, plus reptile monitoring in Krka National Park.

name: Institute for Environment and Nature
summary: Croatia's GBIF node, run by the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Green Transition, coordinating biodiversity data publication and running and building the Croatian Bioportal.

name: Institute of Oceanography and Fisheries
summary: Marine research institution in Split that, Dnevnik.hr reported, hosted the National Marine Habitat Map launch in January 2024 and leads the North Adriatic soundscapes project.

name: Institute of Ornithology, Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts
summary: Croatia's bird ringing centre, run by the Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts, which has organised ringing since 1910 and digitises and analyses data from about sixty ringers.

name: Integrated Geospatial Information System (GIS), Earth Observation (EO) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) toolbox for European Sustainability Reporting Standards on Biodiversity and Ecosystem (ESRS E4)
summary: Project begun on 1 October 2025, lasting 18 months with a EUR 730,879 budget, planning pilots in the food industry, renewable energy and public utilities for biodiversity reporting tools.

name: Javna ustanova Nacionalni park Brijuni
summary: National park where, in February 2026, fieldwork with BIOM ornithologists counted the breeding European shag population and recorded active nests on 11 uninhabited islands, funded through the Competitiveness and Cohesion Programme 2021 to 2027.

name: Javna ustanova Nacionalni park Sjeverni Velebit
summary: National park institution that has carried out more than 120 research projects since 2002 and is setting up monitoring programmes, with its 2018 programme listing large carnivore monitoring and yearly stag beetle monitoring by its own staff.

name: Javna ustanova Natura Viva
summary: Karlovac-based public institution whose staff ran monitoring of bee-eaters (July 2026), bats in Vrlovka cave (March 2026) and freshwater crayfish (October to November 2025).

name: Javna ustanova Park prirode Biokovo
summary: Public institution cited for a 2025 BioAtlas dataset on stag beetle and great capricorn beetle monitoring in a Biokovo Natura 2000 site, covering 33 one-kilometre squares in one ten-day June 2025 field trip, with traps in 14.

name: Javna ustanova Park prirode Medvednica
summary: Public institution that by 2019 had commissioned and carried out 110 research and monitoring studies in the park, holds all results in its database, and has monitoring protocols for Natura 2000 target species and habitats.

name: Javna ustanova Park prirode Učka
summary: Public institution whose 2025 project monitored target animal species and lichens in the nature park and its Natura 2000 sites, including large carnivores and chamois by camera traps and tracks, with a dataset released under CC BY 4.0.

name: Javna ustanova Park prirode Vransko jezero
summary: Public institution that has organised bird ringing at Vransko Lake with the HAZU Institute of Ornithology since 2021, ringing about 6,000 birds a year to collect data on the lake's role on migration routes.

name: Javna ustanova Priroda Primorsko-goranske županije
summary: In 2025, this county institution monitored all Kvarner griffon vulture colonies, tracked large carnivores using camera traps and tracks, and added field data to its information system using Mergin.

name: Javna ustanova za upravljanje prirodnim vrijednostima Grada Zagreba
summary: Public institution for protected nature of the City of Zagreb, listed by the ministry; a July 2019 page by Javna ustanova Maksimir described research, monitoring and supervision in the city's protected areas.

name: Javna ustanova za upravljanje zaštićenim dijelovima prirode Bjelovarsko-bilogorske županije
summary: Public institution for protected nature in Bjelovar-Bilogora County, listed by the ministry, which in February 2022 reported yearly white stork monitoring at 316 addresses in 130 settlements.

name: Javna ustanova za upravljanje zaštićenim dijelovima prirode Brodsko-posavske županije - Natura Slavonica
summary: Public institution for protected nature in Brod-Posavina County, listed by the ministry, which in May 2026 reported monitoring pollinator number changes on selected grasslands using Flower-Insect Timed Counts.

name: Javna ustanova za upravljanje zaštićenim dijelovima prirode Dubrovačko-neretvanske županije
summary: County public institution in Dubrovnik that, with the ornithological society Brkata sjenica, monitored selected bird species in the Neretva Delta area HR1000031 in 2019 using total counts and song listening.

name: Javna ustanova za upravljanje zaštićenim dijelovima prirode i ekološkom mrežom Virovitičko-podravske županije
summary: Public institution founded in 2002 by the Virovitica-Podravina County Assembly, which manages protected areas including the Mura-Drava regional park and whose activities include monitoring species and rescuing injured animals.

name: Javna ustanova za upravljanje zaštićenim dijelovima prirode na području Krapinsko-zagorske županije
summary: Public institution managing protected areas in Krapina-Zagorje County that monitors many bird, bat, insect, orchid and fish species, and has counted the snake's-head fritillary with primary schools for twelve years running.

name: Javna ustanova za upravljanje zaštićenim dijelovima prirode Sisačko-moslavačke županije
summary: Public institution managing protected areas in Sisak-Moslavina County, based in Petrinja, for which species population monitoring is a main task and which currently monitors 14 protected species.

name: Javna ustanova za upravljanje zaštićenim dijelovima prirode Varaždinske županije
summary: County public institution in Varaždin whose staff monitored invasive alien plants at ten locations in the Drava park forest in August, as part of the EU project LIFE RESTORE for MDD.

name: Javna ustanova za upravljanje zaštićenim dijelovima prirode Vukovarsko-srijemske županije
summary: Public institution managing protected areas in Vukovar-Srijem County that finished monitoring the white-tailed eagle's presence, behaviour and breeding success in April 2026, and lists common farmland bird monitoring among its activities.

name: Javna ustanova za upravljanje zaštićenim područjima i drugim zaštićenim dijelovima prirode na području Ličko-senjske županije
summary: Public institution for protected areas in Lika-Senj County whose report on its 2025 annual programme records camera-trap monitoring and bear population monitoring that registered 66 bears.

name: Javna ustanova za zaštitu prirode Osječko-baranjske županije
summary: Public institution that in 2025 monitored riverbank-nesting birds on the Drava and Danube under the Danubeparks-funded Riparia project with the Drava natural history society, and monitored the thick-shelled river mussel on the Breznica in September.

name: Javna ustanova Zeleni prsten Zagrebačke županije
summary: Zagreb County public institution coordinating the planned 2026 to 2029 ReNatura project, which includes environmental DNA surveys of mudminnow, LiDAR imaging of Žutica forest and monitoring of target species and habitats.

name: Jeste li ih vidjeli?
summary: Public recording programme, organised by the Institute for Environment and Nature since 2015, in which people report saproxylic beetle sightings with a photograph for validation by the Institute's experts.

name: Josip Juraj Strossmayer University of Osijek
summary: University that runs the Faculty of Agrobiotechnical Sciences Osijek; two of its faculties were named on the November 2022 to November 2025 WatchOut project, as coordinator and partner.

name: Karte osjetljivosti prostora Hrvatske na razvoj solarnih i vjetroelektrana
summary: Sensitivity maps for solar and wind energy development in Croatia, built by the ministry and The Nature Conservancy, presented in December 2024, using about a million animal observations to model distributions for more than 350 species.

name: LIFE Artina – seabird conservation network in the Adriatic
summary: Closed seabird conservation project in the central Adriatic, led by BIOM, which collected over 300,000 camera-trap photographs and videos; BIOM reported testing MegaDetector on about 70,000 of them in December 2025.

name: LIFE SUPport: Securing a future for Griffon Vultures in Croatia
summary: Active project led by BIOM, with the Vulture Conservation Foundation, to improve conditions for Croatia's last griffon vultures on the Kvarner Islands, using GPS transmitter data in an electrocution hotspot analysis.

name: Mapping of coastal and benthic marine habitats in the Adriatic Sea under national jurisdiction
summary: Project run by the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development, completed with the January 2024 launch of a map covering 51 per cent of Croatia's Adriatic seabed, of which 82 per cent was modelled.

name: Međimurska priroda - Javna ustanova za zaštitu prirode
summary: County public institution for protected nature in Međimurje County, listed by the ministry, whose 2025 yearbook reports its staff carried out their first moth monitoring.

name: Ministry of Environmental Protection and Green Transition
summary: Croatian ministry whose staff include Croatia's primary CBD national focal point and which has published bird observations and saproxylic beetle records through GBIF.

name: Monitoring of the mixed bird colony in the Krapje Đol ornithological reserve (2025)
summary: Closed 2025 monitoring of the mixed bird colony in the Krapje Đol ornithological reserve, counting breeding spoonbills and colonial herons from drone images filmed at 20 to 30 metres to avoid disturbing nesting birds.

name: Monitoring čestih vrsta ptica poljoprivrednih staništa u Hrvatskoj
summary: Monitoring system built for field data collection, data entry and checking, and index calculation for common farmland birds in Croatia, with a database of bird observations and habitat features from 2014 to 2016.

name: More efficient management of speleological objects in the Republic of Croatia through maintenance and upgrade of the CroSpeleo system
summary: Project to maintain and upgrade the CroSpeleo cave database within the Nature Protection Information System, valued at HRK 5.7 million with 80 per cent from the Fund, as announced in May 2022.

name: Nacionalni park Risnjak
summary: Since 2014, its large carnivores have been followed with camera traps and GPS collars, while transects and baseline data were prepared for future monitoring of four bird species.

name: Natura Histrica
summary: Pula-based institution with a CC BY 4.0 Palud bird dataset covering 2025 and WASTEREDUCE partner that commissioned satellite-based marine pollution monitoring used in Lim Bay in 2024.

name: New Age Solutions
summary: Listed by OroraTech as its one local partner in Croatia, with a June 2024 report saying training for the Zadar OroraTech pilot began in cooperation with it.

name: Oikon Ltd. – Institute of Applied Ecology
summary: Applied ecology institute in Zagreb, established 1997, leading the GEOAI4ESRSE4 consortium, which says it will develop GIS, Earth observation and AI tools for ESRS E4 reporting.

name: Ornitološko društvo Brgljez kamenjar
summary: Ornithological association that coordinated the 2015 ringing camp at Vransko jezero with licensed amateur and professional ringers; the nature park took over organising the camp in 2021.

name: OroraTech satellite wildfire detection pilot, Zadar County Operations Centre
summary: Pilot of the OroraTech satellite fire detection platform, described in a 24 June 2024 report as the first of its kind in Croatia, with county operations centre staff training begun and two weeks of summer use planned.

name: Paklenica brown bear collar tracking
summary: According to Total Croatia News, five brown bears had tracking collars by June 2026 in a Paklenica research project with the University of Zagreb’s Faculty of Veterinary Medicine.

name: Prirodoslovno društvo Drava
summary: Natural history association whose members marked 20 years of bird monitoring on the last 256 km of the Drava in 2024, counting from a slow-moving boat, and which partners with WWF Austria and the Osijek-Baranja institution.

name: Public Institution Kopački rit Nature Park
summary: Public institution at Mali Sakadaš 1, Kopačevo, Bilje, whose site lists the WatchOut project on wetland and wildlife monitoring with technology and acoustics.

name: Public Institution Krka National Park
summary: Public institution whose staff and a BIOM volunteer ornithologist counted winter waterbirds on 15 and 16 January 2022, recording 33 species and over 1,900 birds.

name: Public Institution Lonjsko Polje Nature Park
summary: Public institution whose 2021 annual report tabulates its species and habitat monitoring, including spoonbill and otter monitoring.

name: Public Institution Plitvice Lakes National Park
summary: Its general manager said in 2023 that it had monitored lynx for seven years and that camera traps recorded a female with two cubs at the end of 2022.

name: Ruđer Bošković Institute
summary: Zagreb institute that says it leads SMART-Water, developing AI and satellite water quality monitoring, and that runs the Center for Marine Research.

name: SMART-Water
summary: Project led by the Ruđer Bošković Institute that aims to assess water quality at lakes in Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro by analysing satellite and sensor data with AI.

name: Soundscapes in the North Adriatic Sea and their impact on marine biological resources
summary: Project led by the Institute of Oceanography and Fisheries that ran from January 2019 to November 2021 and planned nine hydrophones to assess underwater noise in the Northern Adriatic.

name: State Geodetic Administration
summary: Body whose 2022 annual report says it has the coordinating role in establishing Croatia's national spatial data infrastructure and refers to digital orthophoto maps.

name: Udruga za prirodu, okoliš i održivi razvoj Sunce
summary: Split-based association that, for 2025, planned its eighth consecutive monitoring of Posidonia meadows in Telašćica Nature Park, commissioned by the park's public institution.

name: Udruga ZEUS
summary: Association that, according to a 2026 Parkovi Hrvatske article, coordinates the International Waterbird Census in Croatia together with BIOM, and is listed in the 2025 Croatian volunteer guide for the census.

name: Virtual Herbarium CNHM
summary: Online herbarium, run by the Croatian Natural History Museum, showing data and photos of inventoried specimens from two of its herbaria, updated as specimens are processed.

name: Wetland and Wildlife Monitoring Using Technology and Acoustics
summary: Closed Tech4All project, November 2022 to November 2025, that aimed to develop a neural network for selected or protected species and assess habitats using drone and satellite data.

name: WWF Adria
summary: Croatian nature conservation association, listed on Keep.eu as partner in RESTORIVER and Carnivora Dinarica, which installed five camera traps in a Stara planina Nature Park pilot area to monitor bears, wolves and lynxes.

name: 2024 Census of the American Flamingo (Phoenicopterus ruber) in Haiti
summary: Aerial census run by Haiti National Trust, which surveyed 19 wetland sites by fixed-wing aircraft in February 2024 and, by its account, detected an estimated 1,333 American flamingos at five sites.

name: Agence Nationale des Aires Protégées
summary: Haitian national protected areas agency that, per the Haiti National Trust, renewed in December 2025 a five-year management delegation contract for Grand Bois National Park, and which UNEP supported in 2016 on management plan methodology.

name: Assessing the Status of Rock Iguanas (Cyclura spp.) and Integrating Community Outreach and Education in Massif la Hotte and Massif la Selle Conservation Corridors, Haiti
summary: Closed June 2014 to July 2015 project, funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund and held by the International Iguana Foundation, that set out to assess rock iguana status in the Massif de la Selle, with 77 surveys in July 2014.

name: Building Local Management Capacity and Conservation Plans to Save Endangered Frogs in Four High Priority Key Biodiversity Areas in Hispaniola
summary: Closed 2012 to 2015 grant to the Zoological Society of Philadelphia, funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund, whose planned components included baseline ecological field work such as determining the presence of chytrid fungus.

name: Centre National de l'Information Géo-Spatiale
summary: Haitian geospatial information centre that UNDP names as technical coordinator of a November 2025 training on mapping national biodiversity strategy targets, which covered remote sensing with Landsat and Sentinel imagery.

name: Ecosystem Approach to Haiti Cote Sud
summary: GEF-funded project in Haiti's south coast whose results brief reports trained environmental agents, equipped marine monitoring teams, a decree for a 5,835 hectare marine area and 750 hectares of mangroves rehabilitated.

name: Ecosystem Threat Assessment and Protected Area Strategy for the Massif de la Hotte Key Biodiversity Area, Haiti
summary: Closed project, run from November 2014 to November 2015 by Temple University's Center for Biodiversity with CEPF funding, which used forest cover analysis of remotely sensed data and field work to identify sites later declared national parks.

name: ELSA Haïti (Essential Life Support Areas, "cartes de l'espoir")
summary: UNDP-run programme, described in March 2021, to map nature for people and planet, listing Haiti as a pilot country; its scientific dossier says the Haiti analysis uses the Prioritizr R package.

name: Establishing a conservation evidence-base for Hispaniolan Solenodon in Haiti's Massif de la Hotte (MBZF grant 142510195)
summary: Awarded $13,300 by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund on 6 February 2015, this Haiti project's recipient describes plans for the solenodon's first quantitative ecological study.

name: Flora of Haiti
summary: Naples Botanical Garden reported a nationwide plant survey launched on 22 January 2021, led by William Cinea, enlisting residents through iNaturalist to provide baseline data for plant conservation.

name: Fondation pour la Protection de la Biodiversité Marine
summary: Non-governmental foundation established in 1992, based in Port-au-Prince, whose 2014 newsletter reports a mangrove assessment estimating 22,740 hectares and coral reef and fish monitoring starting in Caracol Bay.

name: Grand Bois National Park
summary: Park of 370 hectares in the Massif de la Hotte, run by the Haiti National Trust, with patches of primary forest and endemic species and daily patrols by rangers recruited locally.

name: Haiti Agriculture: Utilizing NASA Earth Observations to Evaluate the Success of Reforestation Practices in Haiti
summary: A 2022 Spring DEVELOP technical report describes a Google Earth Engine vegetation tool and a 1984 to 2021 enhanced vegetation index series using Landsat and Sentinel-2.

name: Haiti National Forest Inventory Project
summary: Active project launched by the Directorate of Forests and Renewable Energy with MARNDR, CNIGS and FAO support, which expects to complete the National Forest Inventory and update mapping data on Haitian forests.

name: Haiti National Trust
summary: Haitian conservation body, both a US 501(c)(3) and a Haitian foundation, which runs Grand Bois National Park, saw its management delegation renewed in December 2025 and reports a February 2024 aerial flamingo census.

name: Haiti Ocean Project
summary: Active Haitian nonprofit funded by New England Aquarium, BIOPAMA and National Fish and Wildlife Foundation, reporting co-management of Baraderes-Cayemite MPA and 22 confirmed marine megafauna species there.

name: ISTEAH Department of Mathematics
summary: Mathematics department in Cap-Haïtien that is the first author's affiliation on a 2024 paper, recorded in OpenAlex, predicting deforestation of the Forêt-des-Pins with parametric and neural network techniques.

name: Jardin Botanique des Cayes
summary: Botanical garden and NGO in Les Cayes that keeps floristic inventories, maps and databases and has an MOU with ANAP for research, but says it has been closed by force for over eight months.

name: Measuring and Monitoring Ecosystem Services in Protected Areas of the Southern Peninsula of Haiti
summary: Closed technical cooperation funded by the Inter-American Development Bank and approved on 1 June 2017, aiming to provide up-to-date methodology, data and tools for assessing and managing ecosystem services in the Southern Peninsula's protected areas.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement
summary: Haiti's environment ministry, whose Director of Biodiversity is the CBD primary national focal point, and which organised with UNDP a November 2025 mapping training and March 2026 workshops to update the biodiversity strategy.

name: Observatoire National de l'Environnement et de la Vulnérabilité
summary: Observatory through which, according to HaitiLibre, the ministry launched SIE-Haïti in March 2021.

name: Participatory/ Multi-stakeholder development of a Locally Managed Marine Area (LMMA) for Caracol Bay, Lagons du Nord-est Key Biodiversity Area in Haiti
summary: Closed project, run by FOPROBIM and funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund, which ran January 2013 to September 2014; over 200 stakeholders took part in participatory GIS mapping, and the community data-verified map component is marked complete.

name: Population Biology of a Hispaniola-Endemic Bird Species, the La Selle Thrush (Turdus swalesi): Applications to the Management and Conservation of the Species
summary: Rufford-listed project in La Visite National Park, Haiti, dated 7 January 2022, covering thrush demography, genetic differentiation and habitat selection in relation to deforestation over the last 30 years.

name: Reef Check survey of Haiti's coral reefs
summary: Reef Check project described in March 2011 as the first attempt at a complete survey of Haiti's coastal reefs, with a first round covering 120 km of coast and over 100 km surveyed by manta tow.

name: Société Audubon Haïti
summary: Haitian foundation, called a sister foundation by the Haiti National Trust, which co-holds the Grand Bois management delegation renewed in December 2025 and runs a restoration programme there with long-term monitoring.

name: Strengthening of coastal zone management initiatives for the Three Bays Marine Managed Area, Haiti
summary: Closed BIOPAMA small technical grant of 92,597.25 euros, led by FoProBiM from September 2020 to September 2021, whose main activities included monitoring and patrol equipment for the Three Bays Marine Managed Area.

name: Supporting a Local Community in Creating a Municipal Wildlife Habitat for the Conservation of Ricord's Iguanas in Anse-a-Pitres, Massif de la Selle Conservation Corridor, Haiti
summary: Closed 2011 to 2015 project, funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund and held by the International Iguana Foundation, that monitored Haiti's last Ricord's iguana population with local NGO Jenes Ansapit and trained local people in habitat monitoring.

name: Système d'Information Environnementale d'Haïti
summary: Online platform launched by the Ministry of the Environment through ONEV on 25 March 2021, described by HaitiLibre as intended to collect environmental data to assess, inform and monitor Haiti's environment.

name: Actio Hungarica
summary: Hungarian bird migration research network, run by MME, that collects migration data at research camps using constant-effort sampling sites and standard measurements, with the Ócsa observatory a member from the start.

name: Aggtelek National Park Directorate
summary: Hungarian state national park directorate, one of ten covering the whole country, based in Jósvafő, listed among OpenBioMaps contributors; a staff member operated WWF Hungary's camera traps for LECA large carnivore monitoring.

name: AI based Fusion of Satellite/Airborne data for Biodiversity Change Characterization
summary: Project that ran from November 2023 to October 2025, built by HUN-REN SZTAKI and Lechner Tudásközpont, planning machine learning and deep neural networks to characterise biodiversity change from satellite and airborne data.

name: Balaton-felvidék National Park Directorate
summary: Hungarian state national park directorate, one of ten covering the whole country, based in Csopak, responsible for conservation management and research, and listed among OpenBioMaps contributors for 2015 to 2026.

name: Beavermap
summary: Programme run by the HUN-REN Centre for Ecological Research that aims to involve the public in monitoring beaver distribution and landscaping, alongside field surveys of beaver effects.

name: BIOTIKA projekt
summary: Hungarian project running from 1 October 2024 to 30 September 2029, with a 970 million forint grant, to review the National Biodiversity Monitoring System and create the planned BÁRKA biotic data store.

name: Bódva-völgyi Madárgyűrűző Állomás
summary: Bird ringing station whose migration research and conservation camp began its 30th season in 2015, organised by MME's Gömör-Torna local group and Aggtelek National Park Directorate, and listed in the 2024 ringing report.

name: Bükki Nemzeti Park Igazgatóság
summary: Hungarian state national park directorate based in Eger, one of ten; in its area 60 cameras, mostly managed by its ranger staff, collected large carnivore data during LECA.

name: Chernel István Madártani és Természetvédelmi Egyesület
summary: Bird and nature conservation association that set up the Tömörd bird observatory in 1997, where ringing takes place at weekends and school holidays from May to November, and which MME described in 2013 as its Vas County group.

name: CLIMANATRES
summary: Project run by the HUN-REN Centre for Ecological Research, planned for April 2025 to March 2028 with 1,983,340 euros under Interreg Danube, aiming to produce habitat suitability models, maps and restoration decision tools.

name: Debreceni Egyetem
summary: A university whose researchers have published on deep learning in conservation biology, with 2024 abstracts describing neural camera-trap analysis of large game and AI prediction of tiger mosquito occurrence.

name: Department of Hydrobiology, University of Pécs
summary: University of Pécs department, run by the university, that studies stream invertebrate communities, especially in intermittent streams, using integrative taxonomy, DNA barcoding and metabarcoding, and indoor flume experiments.

name: Duna-Dráva National Park Directorate
summary: Hungarian state national park directorate, one of ten covering the whole country, based in Pécs, responsible for conservation management and research, and listed among OpenBioMaps contributors for 2015 to 2026.

name: Duna-Ipoly National Park Directorate
summary: Hungarian state national park directorate, one of ten covering the whole country, based in Budapest, responsible for conservation management and research, and listed among OpenBioMaps contributors for 2015 to 2026.

name: Dávodi Madárgyűrűző Állomás
summary: Bird ringing station operated jointly by the Duna-Dráva National Park Directorate and Gébics Nature Conservation Association, with specialists working there continuously since 2010.

name: Ecosystem Map of Hungary
summary: Dataset built by Lechner Tudásközpont, described in a 2021 paper as a high-resolution country-level ecosystem map compiled to support environmental policy.

name: Envirosense Hungary Kft.
summary: Company whose engineer, in a 2024 presentation, showed tree species mapping from hyperspectral, PlanetScope and Sentinel-2 imagery and a LiDAR timber volume estimate, with forestry products in development.

name: Erdőrezervátum Program ER HTV adatbázis
summary: Research database for long-term monitoring data from permanent sampling points of the Forest Reserve Programme, holding about 243,000 records from 4,566 points, with baseline surveys done in 32 of 63 reserves.

name: Eötvös Loránd University
summary: Budapest university whose Department of Plant Anatomy partners in FunDive; a 2025 paper first-authored there describes PyEOGPR, a Python package for mapping vegetation traits from Earth observation data.

name: Farmosi Madárvárta
summary: Bird observatory at Farmos, described in 2019 and 2020 as collecting breeding and passage data throughout the year, and reported renovated in 2022.

name: Fecskeles adatbázis
summary: Open online bird-monitoring database launched by MME in 2010 as its fourth, taking nesting data for swallows, the common swift and the bee-eater, and holding earlier records of 4,252 nesting sites and 4,886 counts.

name: Fenékpuszta Madárgyűrűző Állomás
summary: Bird ringing station listed in the Bird Ringing Centre's 2024 report, where a 2019 MME magazine article said ringing has gone on since 1985 under a local group's organisation.

name: Ferencmajori Madárvárta
summary: Bird observatory run by Száz Völgy Természetvédelmi Egyesület, operating since 1991 and founded as Ferencmajori Madárvárta in 2013, with ringing programmes including Constant Effort Site and Actio Hungarica.

name: Fertő-Hanság National Park Directorate
summary: Hungarian state national park directorate, one of ten covering the whole country, based in Sarród, responsible for conservation management and research, and listed among OpenBioMaps contributors for 2015 to 2026.

name: Forest Research Institute
summary: Hungarian research institute with which the first author of a 2024 paper on forest disturbance monitoring and a 2025 forest health survey, both using Sentinel-2 imagery, is affiliated.

name: Foundations for the strategic planning of ecosystem services-based green infrastructure developments supported by regularly updated datasets
summary: A project planned for 2025 to 2028, funded by the Hungarian Development Centre with 1.35 billion forints, of which 363 million go to the HUN-REN ecological research centre.

name: Fészek adatbázis
summary: Database completed in 2025 that continues the register of artificial nest-box colonies and nest-box checks, with more than 5,000 nest boxes and 35,000 checks to be moved from the old ODÚ database.

name: Fővárosi Állat- és Növénykert
summary: Municipal zoo in Budapest reporting transmitter implants in over 100 meadow vipers by its vets and participation in the 2019 to March 2025 LIFE HUNVIPHAB project.

name: Gébics Természetvédelmi Egyesület
summary: Nature conservation association associated with the Dávod bird ringing station.

name: Gólyales adatbázis
summary: White stork nest database launched by MME in 2005, renewed and operating since summer 2022, holding over 10,000 nest records, 118,000 breeding results, 55,000 observations and 67,000 photos.

name: Herman Ottó Intézet Nonprofit Kft.
summary: Nonprofit company wholly owned by the Ministry of Agriculture, described as its environmental and nature conservation administration body, taking part in national biodiversity monitoring tasks and partnering with two related programmes.

name: Hortobágyi Nemzeti Park Igazgatóság
summary: Hungarian state national park directorate based in Debrecen, one of ten, whose 2015 report gives its operating area as 1,747,744 hectares.

name: Hortobágyi Vonuláskutató Állomás
summary: Songbird migration research station, built by the Hortobágy National Park Directorate within an EU-funded project, where songbirds are mist-netted and ringed to study population change and migration strategies.

name: HUN-REN Balatoni Limnológiai Kutatóintézet
summary: According to Infostart, this institute’s environmental DNA method maps Balaton’s fish fauna without catches; an affiliated co-author contributed to a 2025 machine learning bioacoustics paper.

name: HUN-REN SZTAKI
summary: Hungarian research institute whose Machine Perception Research Laboratory was associated with a 2023 to 2025 project proposing AI analysis of remote sensing data for biodiversity change.

name: HUN-REN Ökológiai Kutatóközpont
summary: Research centre studying aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, mosquito and animal sound recognition, and public monitoring, with OpenAlex listing 801 ecology and conservation works since 2018.

name: Hungarian Mycological Society
summary: Hungarian scientific and professional society, established in 1992, which according to its GBIF publisher record maintains a national data-collection network for protected fungi.

name: Hungarian Natural History Museum
summary: Hungary’s largest museum by its account and a DiSSCo partner, with GBIF reporting over 11 million specimens, 12.7% databased and 0.6% fully digitised.

name: Institute of Ecology and Botany
summary: Institute with nearly 80 researchers organised in research groups, carrying out public-interest monitoring and applied research alongside basic research.

name: izeltlabuak.hu
summary: Citizen science web application, run by Közösen a Természetért Alapítvány, where users upload arthropod photos with place and date for expert identification, with open data exportable in Darwin Core.

name: KISKUN LTER
summary: A research infrastructure with a farmhouse research station, weather station and experimental area at Fülöpháza, where researchers study dry grasslands and wetlands; the centre says Hungary is not a full eLTER member.

name: Kiskunság National Park Directorate
summary: A national park directorate based in Kecskemét, one of ten state bodies covering the whole country with conservation management and research tasks, and listed as an OpenBioMaps contributor for 2015 to 2026.

name: Kiskunsági Madárvédelmi Egyesület
summary: Association founded in 2000 to operate the Kolon-tó bird observatory, which ringed 7,891 birds over 88 days of the standard migration period in 2017.

name: Körös-Maros National Park Directorate
summary: A national park directorate with an address in Szarvas, one of ten state bodies covering the country with conservation management and research tasks, and listed as an OpenBioMaps contributor for 2015 to 2026.

name: Közösen a Természetért Alapítvány
summary: A foundation with a Budapest address, named in GBIF's publisher record as the maintainer of the izeltlabuak.hu website.

name: Külgazdasági és Külügyminisztérium
summary: A ministry to which, according to the national space strategy, government direction of Hungary's space sector passed in May 2018, when it set up a department for space research and activities.

name: LECA
summary: A large carnivore project, funded by Interreg Central Europe, that WWF Hungary reports closed in March 2026, having placed over 560 camera traps across 37,000 square kilometres.

name: Lechner Tudásközpont
summary: A background institution of the Prime Minister's Office whose remote sensing work dates to the FÖMI centre of 1980, now using machine learning in mapping and helping develop an Earth observation information system.

name: LIFE IP GRASSLAND-HU
summary: EU LIFE-supported project whose action D.1 monitors species and habitats, with Herman Ottó Intézet, MME and nine national park directorates as the beneficiaries responsible.

name: LIFE Safeheaven
summary: EU LIFE project run by MME for 2025 to 2031 to restore four salt lakes, with planned AI software to detect indicator bird nests from thermal camera night flights.

name: Madáratlasz Program
summary: A bird database created in 2015 by MME’s Monitoring Centre, serving Hungarian data collection for the European Breeding Bird Atlas published in 2020, with 60,766,444 records.

name: Madárgyűrűzési Központ
summary: Bird Ringing Centre run by MME, hosted since 1976, which archives ringing data; its databank held 8,461,207 records on 31 January 2025, with 312 active ringers in 2024.

name: Magyar Agrár- és Élettudományi Egyetem
summary: A university whose researchers first-authored a 2023 paper estimating reed bed cover in Hungarian fish ponds using an NDVI-based remote sensing technique.

name: Magyar Denevérgyűrűzési Központ
summary: Bat ringing centre established in early 2007 with institutional support from the Hungarian Natural History Museum, offering tables for submitting TIR-compatible data and ringing and recovery data.

name: Magyar Madártani és Természetvédelmi Egyesület
summary: A bird and nature conservation association whose Monitoring Centre’s work includes common breeding bird surveys from 1998 and the Madáratlasz Program database from 2015.

name: Mekszikópusztai Madárvárta
summary: Waterbird ringing observatory which MME's Sopron local group described in its account of 2025 as the longest-established such station, alongside weekly counts on the Mekszikópuszta floodings for over two decades.

name: Mindennapi Madaraink Monitoringja
summary: A common bird monitoring programme using five-minute counts at 15 points per square, which a 2025 presentation reports holds 59.5 million records from 1,320 squares and 1,300 surveyors.

name: MTA–ELTE Lendület Collective Behaviour Research Group
summary: Research group whose members András Zábó and Máté Nagy developed the RAPID algorithm with Aamir Ahmad of the Max Planck Institute and the University of Stuttgart.

name: Nemzeti Biodiverzitás-monitorozó Rendszer
summary: A national biodiversity monitoring system built from 1997, with field surveys since 1998, coordinated regionally by national park directorates and supported professionally by the Herman Ottó Intézet.

name: Nemzeti Földügyi Központ
summary: A background institution of the Ministry of Agriculture which, per a 2024 presentation, has a 108-person forestry department and handles forest inventory and monitoring alongside remote sensing developments.

name: Nemzeti Kutatási, Fejlesztési és Innovációs Hivatal
summary: A research funding office listed by the HUN-REN Centre for Ecological Research as funder of a 310 million forint grassland restoration project running from 2022 to 2027.

name: Obuda University
summary: A university whose researchers first-authored a 2024 paper classifying land cover from Sentinel-2 time series with machine learning, and a 2025 paper on first experiences with AlphaEarth Foundations.

name: OpenBioMaps
summary: An open-source biodiversity data management platform founded in Hungary in 2011, reported by Interreg Europe in 2019 to be used by six national parks and about 20 research projects.

name: RAPID (Real-time Animal Pattern re-Identification on Edge Devices)
summary: Open source model, built by the MTA–ELTE group, András Zábó and the University of Stuttgart, which ELTE says recognises individual patterned animals in real time, including from drone footage.

name: RTM adatbázis
summary: Breeding bird database built and run by MME's Monitoring Centre staff, holding over four million uploaded records and, since 2013, data summarised for 2.5 by 2.5 km UTM squares.

name: SATELLITETRACKING.EU
summary: Site built by MME with EU LIFE and European Regional Development Fund funding, aiming to collate regional satellite bird-tracking results and restricting sensitive locations when coordinators deem necessary.

name: Sumonyi Madárvonulás-kutató Állomás
summary: Bird migration research station listed in the 2024 Bird Ringing Centre report, with a ringing series labelled as starting in 1981 and MME reporting in 2010 that it had ringed its 300,000th bird.

name: Száz Völgy Természetvédelmi Egyesület
summary: Nature conservation association describing Constant Effort Sites ringing at Ferencmajor and Szőny, and sand martin ringing at breeding colonies, with up to 250 birds per occasion.

name: TermészetLesen
summary: Public data-collection programme of five simple schemes, run by MME through the Turdus app and created with LIFE NGO4GD support, covering feeder birds, spring wildlife, swallows, storks and dead animals.

name: Természetvédelmi Információs Rendszer
summary: Nationwide conservation database with a purpose-built GIS application, supporting national park directorates and authorities, linked to an interactive map within the OKIR public service module.

name: Tringa (T-Ring Application)
summary: Online application for managing Hungary’s bird ringing databank, launched in 2014 and built by MME, with 1.4 million ringing and recovery records entered by March 2018.

name: Turdus
summary: Field data-collection app for Android and iOS, built by MME, which serves the MAP, MMM and TermészetLesen programmes and lets data be uploaded directly to the databases.

name: Tömördi Madárvárta
summary: Bird ringing and migration research station whose staff published a study in 2018 for its twentieth anniversary, giving ringing data for 133 species, rare catches and foreign recoveries.

name: University of Pécs
summary: A university whose Department of Hydrobiology applies DNA (meta)barcoding to aquatic macroinvertebrates, according to the department's GBIF publisher record.

name: University of Sopron
summary: A university linked to papers by the same first author on Sentinel-2 forest disturbance monitoring with machine learning (2024) and Sentinel-2 forest health surveys (2025).

name: University of Szeged
summary: A university whose researchers first-authored papers on mapping wetland water cover from Sentinel-1 (2020) and monitoring plants with drone imagery (2023 and 2026).

name: Vadonleső Program
summary: A volunteer-based nature observation programme open to anyone, described by the state nature conservation site as one of Europe's largest, operating within the national biodiversity monitoring framework and offering a mobile app.

name: Viability improvement of Hungarian meadow viper populations and habitats in the Pannonian region (LIFE18 NAT/HU/000799)
summary: Closed LIFE project led by MME on Hungarian meadow viper populations, which ran from August 2019 to March 2025 with a 4,162,182 euro budget, 75% EU-funded, and tracked released vipers with radio-telemetry transmitters.

name: Vízimadár adatbázis
summary: Waterbird database built and run by MME's Monitoring Centre staff, aiming at current data on waterbird numbers and distribution in Hungary from monthly counts, set up under a cross-border project.

name: WWF Magyarország
summary: Hungarian branch of the international WWF foundation, active since 1991, which says it used AI to help process LECA camera trap data and monitored lynx in Slovak Karst National Park from 2023 to 2026.

name: Életképes ürgeállomány fennmaradásának biztosítása a Pannon régióban
summary: Ground squirrel conservation project running from 1 December 2025 to 1 March 2033, budgeted at €9,791,425 with €7,343,568 EU support, planning colony records, health assessments and threat maps.

name: Élő Környezetért Felelős Minisztérium
summary: Hungarian ministry described on the state nature conservation website as the top body of state nature conservation, whose deputy state secretariat directs the national park directorates; it partners with OpenBioMaps.

name: Ócsai Madárvárta Egyesület
summary: Association working in the northern Ócsa Landscape Protection Area, with research and monitoring there since 1983 by its forerunners, and a member of the Actio Hungarica network.

name: Őrség National Park Directorate
summary: A national park directorate with an address in Őriszentpéter, one of ten state bodies covering the country with conservation management and research tasks, and listed as an OpenBioMaps contributor for 2015 to 2026.

name: AI assessment of restored coral reefs at Bontosua
summary: Study led from IPB University that used AI to compare the beauty of restored and healthy coral reefs around Bontosua Island, South Sulawesi. It was published in Scientific Reports.

name: AI Coral Monitoring
summary: AI application from Universitas Syiah Kuala that measures coral transplant growth and percentage coral cover, launched in Banda Aceh in 2023.

name: AI Karhutla
summary: AI application developed by the weather modification centre at BPPT to indicate forest and land fire threat from hydrometeorological data, to guide peat wetting by weather modification.

name: AI-Driven Coral Reef Restoration and Monitoring in Indonesia
summary: Omdena local chapter project to build AI models for satellite and underwater imagery to assess reef health and identify restoration priorities.

name: AI-powered Seagrass Mapping for Blue Carbon Monitoring
summary: Global Green Growth Institute pilot with Indonesia's fisheries ministry and Spatial Informatics Group that used machine learning and remote sensing to map and assess seagrass beds in Bali Province.

name: Alam Sehat Lestari
summary: NGO that began a reforestation programme in Gunung Palung National Park in 2009, employing one hundred villagers from a village of 764 households between 2009 and 2013 in nursery, planting, day labour and fire protection work.

name: APRIL
summary: Pulp and paper group in Riau that monitors fire risk in its concessions from NASA satellite data, with ground crews checking each hotspot.

name: Auriga Nusantara
summary: Indonesian foundation that publishes annual deforestation data and maps, and started MapBiomas Indonesia in 2017.

name: Badan Informasi Geospasial
summary: Indonesia's national mapping agency, which runs the One Map geoportal and is discussing a forest and elevation mapping campaign with NASA.

name: Badan Meteorologi, Klimatologi, dan Geofisika
summary: Indonesia's meteorology, climatology and geophysics agency. In April 2026 it signed a memorandum with the Ministry of Forestry on sensors and data integration for fire prevention.

name: Badan Pengelola Ciletuh-Palabuhanratu UNESCO Global Geopark
summary: Management body under the Sukabumi district government that, as of August 2021, managed the geopark's tourist areas, which had 64 featured attractions across eight sub-districts.

name: Badan Pengelola Gambut dan Mangrove Nasional
summary: National peat and mangrove agency formed by decision of President Prabowo in 2026 to strengthen fire prevention and manage peat and mangrove ecosystems.

name: Badan Pengelola Hutan Desa Setulang
summary: Forest management body chosen by villagers, reported in September 2014 to manage the Setulang reserved forest (tana' ulen), designated by a 2013 ministerial decree as 4,330 hectares of village forest.

name: Badan Pengelola Toba Caldera UNESCO Global Geopark
summary: Management body for the Toba Caldera geopark, which a geoscientist says was formed after the 2013 acceleration team, and which is abbreviated BP TCUGG.

name: Badan Restorasi Gambut dan Mangrove
summary: Former peat and mangrove restoration agency, wound up on 31 December 2024 according to Mongabay. Earlier, as BRG, it built the Sipalaga peat water level monitoring platform.

name: Badan Riset dan Inovasi Nasional
summary: Indonesia's national research and innovation agency. Its head says it works with the Ministry of Forestry on hotspot detection and will update this with AI; its researchers use LiDAR drones on mangroves.

name: Balai Besar KSDA Jawa Barat
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 46 conservation area units.

name: Balai Besar KSDA Jawa Timur
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 26 conservation area units.

name: Balai Besar KSDA Nusa Tenggara Timur
summary: State conservation office run by the forestry directorate; RRI reported in April 2026 that it had deployed 12 camera traps across East Manggarai to monitor Komodo dragon movements near settlements.

name: Balai Besar KSDA Papua
summary: State conservation office run by the forestry directorate; WWF Indonesia reported a September 2025 memorandum with it on biodiversity conservation, and a June 2025 workshop where it presented bird survey techniques and SMART patrols.

name: Balai Besar KSDA Papua Barat Daya
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 27 conservation area units.

name: Balai Besar KSDA Riau
summary: State conservation office run by the forestry directorate; Metro TV reported it set two camera traps in Siak in December 2025 to monitor a tiger suspected of killing livestock.

name: Balai Besar KSDA Sulawesi Selatan
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 15 conservation area units.

name: Balai Besar KSDA Sumatera Utara
summary: State conservation office run by the forestry directorate; Mongabay reports it and Yayasan Ekosistem Lestari surveyed Tapanuli orangutans in 2021 to 2023 on 5 by 5 km transects, to provide baseline data for policy.

name: Balai Besar Taman Nasional Bromo Tengger Semeru
summary: Park authority that announced in October 2026 that the Penanjakan sunrise viewing area on Mount Bromo would be closed.

name: Balai Besar Taman Nasional Gunung Gede Pangrango
summary: Park authority whose head said in August 2026 that it was still investigating the cause of fires at Kawah Wadon and Surya Kencana, adding that Kawah Wadon is a core zone not meant for tourism or climbing.

name: Balai Besar Taman Nasional Lore Lindu
summary: Park management body for Lore Lindu National Park, whose own zoning page says zoning organises the park into management zones.

name: Balai Kawasan Konservasi Perairan Nasional Kupang
summary: Indonesian technical unit for national marine protected areas, according to the ministry's SeaPark page.

name: Balai Kliring Keanekaragaman Hayati Indonesia
summary: National biodiversity clearing house introduced by the environment ministry as a centre for national biodiversity data and knowledge.

name: Balai KSDA Aceh
summary: State conservation office run by the forestry directorate; RRI reported GPS collars fitted to wild elephants in West Aceh in July 2026, and Metro TV reported camera traps used to identify a tiger after a May 2026 attack.

name: Balai KSDA Bengkulu dan Lampung
summary: State conservation office run by the forestry directorate; VOI reports its then head saying camera traps and patrols from 2020 to 2025 showed 42 tigers in three landscapes.

name: Balai KSDA Jakarta
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 4 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Jambi
summary: State conservation office run by the forestry directorate; RRI reported in September 2026 that it had fitted GPS collars to five elephant groups in the Bukit Tigapuluh landscape and tracked them by satellite.

name: Balai KSDA Jawa Tengah
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 34 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Kalimantan Barat
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 13 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Kalimantan Selatan
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 16 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Kalimantan Tengah
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 10 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Kalimantan Timur
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 8 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Maluku
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 28 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Nusa Tenggara Barat
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 16 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Sulawesi Tengah
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 18 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Sulawesi Tenggara
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 12 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Sulawesi Utara
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 13 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Sumatera Barat
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 22 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Sumatera Selatan
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 11 conservation area units.

name: Balai KSDA Yogyakarta
summary: Indonesian conservation body whose ministry page says it manages 5 conservation area units.

name: Balai Pengelolaan Daerah Aliran Sungai dan Hutan Lindung Indragiri-Rokan
summary: Watershed and protection forest unit that rehabilitated 410 hectares of mangrove forest in Riau in the four years to February 2021, and ran a labour-intensive mangrove programme across five regencies in late 2020.

name: Balai Pengelolaan Daerah Aliran Sungai dan Hutan Lindung Krueng Aceh
summary: Watershed and protection forest unit whose head said in 2021 that about 264,900 of its five million hectares of working area were damaged, and that it plants trees yearly in critical areas.

name: Balai Pengelolaan Kelautan Denpasar
summary: Marine management body whose own profile lists protecting, conserving and using conservation areas among its tasks.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Alas Purwo
summary: Park management body whose own profile says its work area is divided into two park management sections and six resorts.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Bukit Baka Bukit Raya
summary: Park management body that, according to the ministry's profile, changed from a unit to a Balai in 2002.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Bukit Duabelas
summary: Park authority whose head said in 2018 that signing the inscription committed it, for the government, to combining Orang Rimba customary rules with government rules in managing the park.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Bunaken
summary: Park authority that, in a 2018 article, was urged by an observer to patrol, inspect and guide boat operators more, while its head set out reef rules for divers and snorkellers.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Gunung Ciremai
summary: Park management body for Gunung Ciremai National Park, which the ministry's profile says carries out the mission set for the park.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Gunung Merbabu
summary: Park management body that the ministry's profile describes as a type B unit with two management sections.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Gunung Rinjani
summary: Indonesian national park management body whose organisation, according to the ministry's profile, was set up by a 2002 decree.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Karimunjawa
summary: Indonesian national park management body; the ministry's profile cites a decision by its head setting priority species for Karimunjawa National Park.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Kayan Mentarang
summary: Management body of Kayan Mentarang National Park in Indonesia, established in 2007 according to its own page.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Kepulauan Seribu
summary: Indonesian national park management body; its own zoning page says the park's space is managed through a zoning system.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Kepulauan Togean
summary: Indonesian body formed in 2007, according to the ministry's profile, as an organisational unit to manage the Togean Islands National Park.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Manusela
summary: Park authority whose head said in October 2026 that about 26 hectares of conservation area at Pasahari, North Seram, had burned and that the authority was investigating.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Rawa Aopa Watumohai
summary: Indonesian national park management body that, a ministry news page dated 7 November 2018 reports, presented the park's long-term plan (RPJP) to stakeholders.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Siberut
summary: Park authority whose head confirmed in a January 2022 report that it had reported unlicensed transport of non-timber forest products out of Siberut National Park.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Tanjung Puting
summary: Park authority which, with partners, carried out ecosystem restoration in areas including Pondok Ambung and Pondok Tanggui, totalling 6,500 hectares from 2018 to 2021 by its data, 1,729.25 hectares of it by partners.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Tesso Nilo
summary: Indonesian national park management body that, according to the ministry's profile, plans to carry out collaborative management of Tesso Nilo National Park with the community and related parties.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Wakatobi
summary: Park authority whose head said in 2022 that it records capture fisheries monthly and bans catching and selling Napoleon wrasse in the park's waters.

name: Balai Taman Nasional Wasur
summary: Park authority whose office head said in 2022 that community participation in managing and guarding the park allows the nature of each village within the conservation area to be kept.

name: Baluran National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; JPNN reported in December 2018 that it used camera traps and, with Copenhagen Zoo, had GPS collars on six banteng, with leopard and dhole collars planned.

name: Batang Gadis National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; a November 2025 forestry directorate news item reports its office's camera traps recording 25 wildlife species.

name: Berbak and Sembilang National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; Koran Jakarta reports that camera traps recorded two Sumatran tigers during its 2025 monitoring in a small part of the Berbak tiger habitat.

name: Biodiversitas Nusantara
summary: A free web portal showing GBIF records for Indonesia by province and taxon, with open source code. It says a volunteer team runs it and names no operator.

name: Biodiverskripsi
summary: Open database of Indonesian biodiversity records taken from student theses, published through GBIF under a CC BY 4.0 licence.

name: BIONESIA
summary: Bali nonprofit working on Indonesian biodiversity science; publishes a Savu Sea eDNA dataset to GBIF. The website listed for it now shows an unrelated casino.

name: Birdpacker Indonesia
summary: Indonesian group behind the Burungnesia bird recording app and the Kupunesia butterfly app, which funds its work partly by selling merchandise.

name: BISA Indonesia
summary: Indonesian organisation whose executive director coordinates the five-country Locally-led East Asian Flyway Acoustics project on migratory birds.

name: Blue Alliance Indonesia Foundation
summary: Foundation that in February 2026 agreed with the Maluku Provincial Government to set up long-term co-management across 1.5 million hectares of ocean, with Hero Ohoiulun as national manager.

name: BlueCarbon AI
summary: University team platform for mangrove and blue carbon monitoring using Sentinel-2, drones and computer vision, a grand finalist at BRIN AIDeaNation 2026.

name: Bogani Nani Wartabone National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; WCS Indonesia says its collaboration since 2001 includes SMART-supported patrols, camera traps for anoa and babirusa, and five maleo nesting sites managed jointly with the park office and communities.

name: BombDetect
summary: Machine learning system trained on underwater audio to identify bomb fishing blasts, used to quantify blast fishing in Indonesia's Spermonde Archipelago.

name: Borneo Atlas
summary: Map from Center for International Forestry Research researchers of the location and ownership of 467 palm oil mills on Borneo, built to help buyers check that palm oil does not harm forests.

name: Borneo Futures
summary: Environmental consultancy that runs KehatiKu, paying villagers in West Kalimantan for wildlife photos and recordings through an app with an AI system for checking observations.

name: Borneo Nature Foundation
summary: Not-for-profit conservation and research organisation working in Borneo's peat swamp forest; publishes two datasets to GBIF.

name: Bukit Barisan Selatan National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; WCS Indonesia says it supports camera trap monitoring over 492 square kilometres, SMART patrols, and the Way Canguk Research Station it helped set up in 1995.

name: Bukit Tigapuluh National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; Metro TV reports that camera trap monitoring from September to December 2025, using 40 cameras across 20 plots, recorded four different Sumatran tigers.

name: Burungnesia
summary: Citizen science application for recording wild birds in Indonesia, whose records were the main data for the Indonesian bird atlas.

name: C-SERM Universitas Nasional
summary: Research centre at Universitas Nasional, developing bioacoustic biodiversity studies with YAYORIN in Lamandau, Central Kalimantan.

name: CarbonAtlas
summary: Jejakin's monitoring platform for nature-based projects, using satellites, IoT sensors and mobile apps.

name: CarbonEthics
summary: Jakarta-based ecosystem restoration company developing blue carbon and other nature-based carbon projects, with digital monitoring.

name: Center for Regional System, Analysis, Planning and Development, IPB University
summary: IPB research centre whose authors applied deep learning to high-resolution satellite images to map smallholder oil palm.

name: Center for Remote Sensing, Institut Teknologi Bandung
summary: Research centre at ITB whose authors publish on decision tree and random forest classification for mangrove mapping.

name: Central Kalimantan gibbon acoustic monitoring
summary: Study using eight recording units and a pretrained deep learning detector to follow Bornean white-bearded gibbon calls over 18 months in Central Kalimantan.

name: CORA(i)L
summary: Université Côte d'Azur research project on AI image recognition for coral health, with fieldwork partners at Raja Ampat and Bali.

name: Coral Triangle Center
summary: Bali-based organisation listed as a partner in the CORA(i)L coral health AI project.

name: Dashboard Lancang Kuning
summary: Android app launched by the Riau regional police for fire task force staff to monitor and report forest and land fires by phone, using remote sensing for hotspots. It was used to detect a hotspot in February 2026.

name: Data Science and Artificial Intelligence Research Group, Universitas Hasanuddin
summary: Thematic research group at Universitas Hasanuddin that names biodiversity conservation among its fields. It has worked on detecting medaka fish species and on estimating seaweed biomass from drone imagery.

name: DBP metabarcoding pipeline
summary: Integrated tool for eDNA analysis of nanopore data against an Indonesian marine fish database, published from Diponegoro University in 2026.

name: Department of Geography, Universitas Indonesia
summary: University department whose authors published a machine learning classification of coral reefs at Derawan Island over two decades.

name: Desa Adat Tenganan Pegringsingan
summary: Customary village described as the only one in Bali controlling customary forest as village custom, with a 2019 ministerial decree listing its forest at about 591 hectares in Manggis, Karangasem.

name: Desa Butong
summary: Village that, according to Kalaweit's project page, manages the community-protected forest next to the Dulan reserve.

name: Desa Kao
summary: Village whose 400 hectares of mangrove forest the North Halmahera government designated an essential ecosystem area, then the only one in Maluku and North Maluku, per an August 2020 report.

name: Dinas Lingkungan Hidup dan Kehutanan Aceh
summary: Aceh provincial agency that, per an August 2026 report, manages the Pocut Meurah Intan grand forest park, a nature conservation area of about 6,220 hectares in Aceh Besar.

name: Direktorat Jenderal Konservasi Sumber Daya Alam dan Ekosistem
summary: Directorate general of the Ministry of Forestry responsible for protected flora and fauna and conservation areas.

name: Early detection information system for human-elephant conflict in Bukit Tigapuluh
summary: Universitas Gadjah Mada project in Jambi that combines elephant sound detection by machine learning with a web map and mobile app, to warn of human-elephant conflict.

name: Earthqualizer
summary: Non-profit that works with companies on commodity-driven deforestation in Southeast Asia and the Pacific.

name: East Ventures
summary: Investor named by Jejakin among the backers of its US$2.7 million funding round in 2024.

name: Elasmobranch Institute Indonesia
summary: Indonesian institute in a collaboration that developed an environmental DNA method for detecting the walking shark endemic to Raja Ampat.

name: Enhancing Sumatran tiger conservation efforts in the Berbak Sembilang landscape
summary: Project listed by IUCN SOS under its Integrated Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme, running 2025 to 2028 in Indonesia and run by KKI Warsi, with planned tiger and prey monitoring using SMART patrols, camera traps and bioacoustics.

name: Eyes on the Forest
summary: Coalition of Indonesian environmental NGOs, founded in Riau in 2004, that investigates forest clearing and publishes satellite and GIS analyses of plantations in forest areas.

name: Fairatmos
summary: Carbon project developer in Jakarta that uses AI and geospatial data for blue carbon and peatland restoration projects in Southeast Asia.

name: Fakultas Kehutanan Universitas Gadjah Mada
summary: Forestry faculty entrusted in 2016 with managing roughly 11,000 hectares of Getas-Ngandong forest; Wanagama became a conservation and education forest under the university’s management.

name: Fakultas Kehutanan Universitas Mulawarman
summary: Forestry faculty using a 299.03 hectare education forest designated in 2020; an April 2025 report says the university reported at least 3.26 hectares cleared for coal mining.

name: Find Your Turtle AI
summary: AI tool from Marine Conservation Indonesia that helps identify species and individuals from turtle photos.

name: FishFace
summary: AI-powered tool that uses smartphone cameras to identify fish species and record catch data automatically, developed by YKAN in Indonesia.

name: Forest Watch Indonesia
summary: Bogor-based organisation that monitors forests through databases, field checks and satellite imagery analysis, and offers spatial forestry data and image interpretation.

name: Forum Bintoro
summary: Forum through which Maskur and colleagues ran self-funded mangrove replanting, reported in December 2024 to bring together 11 groups in nine villages covering half of Demak's 58 km coastline.

name: Forum Konservasi Leuser
summary: Aceh organisation that runs SMART patrols and drone missions in the Leuser Ecosystem with Global Conservation's support.

name: Geo AI and Big Data Research Group, Universitas Gadjah Mada
summary: Research group at Universitas Gadjah Mada using geospatial AI and big data for coastal wetlands, mangroves, deforestation, fires, seagrass and benthic habitats.

name: GEOMIMO
summary: A satellite imagery application from BRIN, which BIG and BRIN's Geoinformatics Research Centre discussed joining up with Piksel in August 2026.

name: Geoportal Kebijakan Satu Peta
summary: Public geoportal of the One Map Policy with thematic maps, version 2.0 presented by BIG in 2024.

name: Global Ocean Innovation Challenge in Indonesia
summary: Initiative of The Nature Conservancy, YKAN and Newlab. In 2026 it began trials in the Sawu Sea of blueOASIS AI underwater acoustic stations and Havoc uncrewed surface vessels.

name: Golden Agri-Resources and Arkadiah forest carbon monitoring in West Kalimantan
summary: Five-year project reported by Forestry Tech Landscape, deploying digital monitoring in West Kalimantan with satellite data, LiDAR and AI modelling to build 3D digital twins of forest areas.

name: Green of Borneo
summary: North Kalimantan civil society group and member of the MapBiomas Indonesia network. No page read shows work of its own beyond network membership.

name: Ground Truthed.id
summary: Forest monitoring platform that gathers field evidence and geolocation data to document environmental violations, as a bottom-up complement to satellite systems.

name: Gunung Halimun Salak National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; Mongabay reports that two camera traps set in February 2025 recorded two Javan leopards in 28 frames, alongside more than 5,000 frames of visitor activity.

name: Gunung Leuser National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; WCS Indonesia says it works with the Ministry of Forestry on management, with camera trap population monitoring a key component, and supports routine SMART patrols.

name: Gunung Naning biodiversity impact monitoring
summary: WildMon and Planet Indonesia project in West Kalimantan using paired acoustic recorders and camera traps at 100 sites, analysed by AI pipelines, for 60 priority species.

name: HAkA
summary: Community group in Aceh that uses Global Forest Watch alerts and the Forest Watcher app to monitor deforestation in the Leuser Ecosystem.

name: Halo Robotics
summary: Indonesian drone and AI company with an environmental conservation service, mapping land cover, vegetation and wildlife habitats and supporting carbon projects.

name: Hasanuddin University
summary: University in Makassar; its authors co-wrote work on machine learning for marine soundscapes at the Mars restoration site.

name: HCSA Forest Plot Data 2023
summary: Forest field plot inventory data from Indonesian provinces, collected as validation and training data for large-scale indicative High Carbon Stock maps, published on Hugging Face under a CC BY-SA 4.0 licence with access conditions.

name: Herbarium Bogoriense
summary: Herbarium under BRIN, described by GBIF as the largest in South East Asia, with seven published datasets.

name: Hotama Technologies
summary: West Kalimantan technology developer that gave the province a free AI system mapping forest and land fire risk up to 24 months ahead.

name: Hutan Harimau
summary: Sumatran tiger conservation organisation that installs real-time cameras in Aceh and West Sumatra, sending tiger images to a phone app within 60 seconds to manage conflict with people.

name: Hutan Kemasyarakatan Kibuk
