summary: Community forestry group on Mount Dempo holding an HKm permit for 420 hectares of protected forest, whose secretary said in January 2022 that endemic plant ecotourism helps protect the forest from illegal logging, fire and change of use.

name: Hutan Kita Institute
summary: South Sumatran civil society group and member of the MapBiomas Indonesia network. In 2015 it was part of a coalition that mapped fires from Landsat imagery.

name: i-Mangrove Blue Carbon Dashboard
summary: Mangrove climate solutions mapping tool described in a 2026 report published by the Center for International Forestry Research and World Agroforestry at Bogor.

name: Indicative HCS forest mapping in Indonesia
summary: FAIR Forward-backed project collecting forest field plots in Sumatra, Kalimantan and West Papua to build open-source, field-validated indicative High Carbon Stock forest maps of all Indonesia using satellite data and AI.

name: Indonesia Biru Foundation
summary: NGO in Lombok working on coral reef research and restoration; it installed live underwater cameras and tested AI classification of reef restoration sites.

name: Indonesia vessel monitoring system data
summary: Indonesia's national fishing vessel monitoring data, made public through Global Fishing Watch in 2017. The pages read do not show whether it continues.

name: Indonesian Biodiversity Information Facility
summary: GBIF national node for Indonesia, listed with Observer status and an address at Cibinong Science Center. GBIF's record names no current host.

name: Indonesian Coral Reef Foundation
summary: Indonesian coral reef foundation behind Remap Coral, described by the BISA innovation programme as using AI-driven monitoring and GIS for reef rehabilitation.

name: Indonesian Peat Prize
summary: Two-year US$1 million contest run by Indonesia's Geospatial Information Agency to find the best method of measuring the country's peatlands, won in 2018 by the International Peat Mapping Team.

name: InklusiGeo
summary: Central Java geospatial company offering geo AI change detection of forest clearance for park rangers, plus WebGIS dashboards and training.

name: Integrated Forest Crime Alert System
summary: Forest monitoring and enforcement system built by YIARI and expanded across protected forests in Lampung and West Kalimantan.

name: Integrated Maritime Intelligent Platform
summary: Indonesian fisheries ministry platform that monitors vessel movement through VMS and AIS and flags violations automatically with a geofencing feature.

name: IPB University
summary: University in Bogor whose repository holds machine learning work on peat fire vulnerability from water table height; its centres also map oil palm by deep learning.

name: Jaringan Kerja Pemetaan Partisipatif
summary: Indonesian network of participatory mapping groups that collected forest field plots for AI-based indicative High Carbon Stock maps with the High Carbon Stock Approach.

name: Jejakin
summary: Jakarta-based company whose platform tracks tree planting, carbon and nature projects using satellite imaging, sensors and AI.

name: JERAT Papua
summary: Papua civil society group and member of the MapBiomas Indonesia network, named as contributing to data collection and validation.

name: Kalaweit
summary: An association that describes its work as protecting wildlife through forest conservation, and that co-manages the 2,546.9 hectare Dulan reserve in Central Kalimantan and reports a 306.5 hectare Pararawen reserve.

name: Kampung Manggroholo
summary: A village, split from Kampung Sira, that a March 2017 report says received a village forest of 1,695 hectares in 2014.

name: Kampung Merabu
summary: A village that was the first in Berau to receive village forest recognition, through a January 2014 forestry ministry decree setting the working area at 8,245 hectares.

name: Kampung Sira
summary: A village that received the right to manage its own 1,850 hectare village forest in 2014, whose forests a March 2017 report says belonged to the Sremere and Kladit clans within Knasaimos customary territory.

name: Kaoem Telapak
summary: Indonesian environmental NGO behind the Ground Truthed.id forest monitoring platform.

name: Kapikan
summary: Company behind a platform that predicts fishing zones in real time for fishers from AI and satellite data, trialled with the fisheries ministry's revolving fund.

name: Kasepuhan Cibedug
summary: A customary community that received a 2022 decree recognising 1,268 hectares of customary forest, out of 2,138 hectares applied for, with the decree stating the forest is no longer state forest area.

name: Kasepuhan Karang
summary: A customary community whose 486 hectare customary forest the President recognised on 30 December 2016, of which a 2018 article says 462 hectares lie in Gunung Halimun Salak National Park.

name: KehatiKu
summary: Programme paying people in nine West Kalimantan villages for photos or recordings of wildlife, producing data on distribution and population change. An AI system helps humans verify observations.

name: Kelompok Jaka Kencana
summary: A group formed with West Java forestry service facilitation in 2004, which a 2019 article reports planted api-api and bakau mangroves in Pabean Udik village, Indramayu.

name: Kelompok Parit Segagah
summary: A group whose founders made a 14 hectare mangrove area a restoration and protection area from 2012, and which has designed a rehabilitation of 35 hectares along the Kelapapati shore.

name: Kelompok Pengelola Hutan Adat Depati Kara Jayo Tuo
summary: Customary forest management group of Rantau Kermas village that Mongabay reports received a 2019 Kalpataru award.

name: Kelompok Restorasi Ekosistem Terumbu Karang dan Konservasi Penyu Desa Birawan
summary: A seven-member village group for coral reef restoration and turtle conservation in Birawan, which transplants corals taken from a small island in front of the village.

name: Kelompok Tani Hutan Makmur
summary: A forest farmers' group that, according to a 2023 article, has restored 70 hectares of mangrove forest at Teluk Pangpang, Banyuwangi, since its founding in 1999.

name: Kelompok Tani Hutan Perempuan Batang Nilo
summary: A women's forest farmers' group whose chair says members replanted at least 30 hectares of the national park, and which was entrusted in 2018 with about 100.4 hectares of traditional zone.

name: Kelompok Tani Hutan Rahayu Jaya
summary: A forest farmers' group that signed a cooperation agreement with Balai TN Way Kambas, and which the park's head said in 2022 was the only group with a conservation partnership.

name: Kementerian Kehutanan
summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Forestry. Its site links the SIMONTANA forest monitoring system and the SIPONGI fire system, and it is promoting drones for forest surveillance.

name: Kementerian Kelautan dan Perikanan
summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries. It runs a command centre for integrated sea monitoring and made its vessel monitoring data public through Global Fishing Watch.

name: Kementerian Lingkungan Hidup / Badan Pengendalian Lingkungan Hidup
summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Environment and Environmental Control Agency. It launched the IBSAP 2025-2045 biodiversity plan and introduced the national biodiversity clearing house.

name: Kementerian PPN/Bappenas
summary: Indonesia's national development planning ministry; part of the consortium behind the national status of biodiversity publications. Its own site refused the fetcher, so this rests on the environment ministry's page.

name: Kepolisian Daerah Riau
summary: Regional police of Riau province, which launched the Dashboard Lancang Kuning fire monitoring app.

name: Kerinci Seblat National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; RRI reports a team from its second management area monitors tigers with systematically placed camera traps, which the ministry says underpin tracking of numbers, breeding and cub survival.

name: Kerukunan Balai Adat Datu Kandangan
summary: A community covering nine Dayak Meratus balai adat in Ulang village, one of four the regional government recognises, managing a customary territory of 2,712.32 hectares.

name: Kesatuan Pengelolaan Hutan Berau Barat
summary: A forest management unit that, according to a 2018 article quoting a conservation worker, holds authority over the Lesan protected forest and reports to the provincial forestry service head.

name: Kesatuan Pengelolaan Hutan Lindung Batutegi
summary: A protected forest management unit whose head confirmed encroachment and illegal gold mining in Batutegi forest and, with the provincial forestry service, ordered joint patrols in 2018.

name: Kesepuhan Pasir Eurih
summary: Customary community whose Hutan Adat was the site where, a news page says, the Ministry of Forestry handed over forest adat decrees covering 1,175 hectares in total on 6 June 2026.

name: Ketemenggungan Adat Tae
summary: A customary area in Sanggau district that received a 2,189 hectare customary forest designation in September 2018, the largest government-set customary forest at that time.

name: Kewang Laut Negeri Liang
summary: A proposed revival of the Kewang Laut and sasi tradition by residents of Negeri Liang, Central Maluku, which in 2026 a Saniri Negeri Liang deputy head described as supervising sasi laut and acting against bombs and poison.

name: Kewang Negeri Haruku
summary: A kewang that enforces sasi laut rules at Haruku as a local police force, and established the Foundation of Haru-Ukui Kalesang to empower kewang in Maluku and coordinate sasi laut on Haruku Island.

name: KKI Warsi
summary: Environmental group in Sumatra that worked with Rainforest Connection to place acoustic monitoring devices in four West Sumatra villages.

name: Koltiva
summary: Agricultural traceability company whose system, according to a coffee industry article it reposted, uses deep learning and machine learning on satellite data for deforestation checks.

name: Komite Gabungan Mitigasi dan Penanganan Interaksi Negatif Gajah Sumatra di TNWK
summary: Joint committee for elephant conflict at Way Kambas National Park, developing an AI command centre to identify individual elephants and watch for fires and poaching.

name: Komodo National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; CNBC Indonesia reports the ministry citing monitoring with Yayasan Komodo Survival Program, including Padar island population estimates, with 2025 data still being analysed.

name: Komodo Survival Program
summary: Foundation that CNBC Indonesia reports carried out Komodo monitoring with the park office, cited by the forestry ministry for Padar island population estimates with confidence intervals.

name: Komunitas Adat Yano Akrua
summary: A customary community in Papua that received a forest designation from the forestry ministry on 18 October 2022, with five other communities, and says it will manage it as ecotourism despite an overlapping palm oil land-use right.

name: Konservasi Indonesia
summary: Indonesian conservation organisation, funded by the Hempel Foundation, that took part in developing an environmental DNA method to detect the Raja Ampat walking shark.

name: Koperasi Tani Hutan Maju Bersama Desa Santong
summary: A forest farmers' cooperative in Santong village that, per a 2015 article, had about 1,258 members across Kayangan and Bayan under the HKm programme, on land described as barren shrubland 18 years earlier.

name: Kupunesia
summary: Citizen science mobile app for identifying and recording butterflies across Indonesia, free on Google Play since November 2022.

name: Kutai National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; RRI reported in June 2026 that its managers had introduced thermal drones and camera traps, and quoted its head saying 324 fauna species had been recorded.

name: Kuva Space and WWF-Indonesia blue carbon monitoring
summary: Partnership announced in December 2025 using hyperspectral satellite data and AI to track mangrove and seagrass growth for Indonesia's blue carbon work.

name: Lembaga Pengelola Dana Pendidikan
summary: Indonesian government education and research fund. Its RISPRO scheme funded the OPTIMAL-IPB deep learning model for mapping oil palm.

name: Lembaga Pengelola Hutan Desa Depati Junjung
summary: A village forest management body, created by a 2011 village regulation, for a 995-hectare working area in Kepahiang, Bengkulu; a 2017 article reports it coordinated planting about 67,000 trees.

name: Lembaga Pengelola Hutan Desa Haratai
summary: A village forest management body listed in a 2026 Mongabay Indonesia article as a scheme covering 762 hectares in the Meratus mountains.

name: Lembaga Pengelola Hutan Desa Tangkahen
summary: A village forest management body in Pulang Pisau, Central Kalimantan, whose forest received a 162-hectare permit under a December 2016 ministerial decree and which began ecotourism in 2017.

name: Lembaga Pengelola Hutan Desa Ulang
summary: A village forest management body listed in a 2026 Mongabay Indonesia article as a scheme covering 1,405 hectares in the Meratus mountains.

name: Lembaga Pengelola Hutan Nagari Sungai Buluh
summary: A nagari forest management body that received a management right decree for 780 hectares from the Governor of West Sumatra in December 2014.

name: Listening to the Wild
summary: Bioacoustic conservation research in Central Kalimantan by C-SERM UNAS and YAYORIN, building a machine learning model first trained on gibbon calls.

name: LKKPN Pekanbaru
summary: Technical unit for national marine protected areas, as described on the ministry's SeaPark page.

name: Locally-led East Asian Flyway Acoustics
summary: International project started by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology that uses passive acoustic monitoring of migratory birds in Cambodia, Taiwan, the Philippines, Malaysia and Indonesia, with devices in Aceh, Gorontalo, Banyuwangi and Yogyakarta.

name: MangroveAI
summary: AI app from Tanamin that uses Sentinel-2 satellite data to monitor mangrove condition and show which areas need restoration.

name: MapBiomas Indonesia
summary: Civil society network mapping Indonesian land cover change year by year. Collection 1.0 covered 2000 to 2019; its fire product uses deep learning.

name: Marine Conservation App
summary: Free web app from Marine Conservation Indonesia for planning reef surveys and recording benthic, fish, coral health, coral growth and turtle data.

name: Marine Conservation Indonesia
summary: Indonesian non-profit based on Gili Air, Lombok. It runs a free reef monitoring web app with AI photo suggestions, and uses AI to identify turtles, sharks and rays from photos.

name: Mars Coral Reef Restoration Project
summary: Reef restoration project in Indonesia whose recordings were used to train an algorithm that told healthy from degraded reefs by sound.

name: Masyarakat Adat Ammatoa Kajang
summary: An indigenous community in Bulukumba district whose customary forest recognition letter was handed over by the President in December 2016, listed as 313 hectares, though another source reports 314.

name: Masyarakat Adat Dayak Wehea
summary: An indigenous Dayak community whose head of custom, per a 2017 article, decided to fight to keep the Wehea forest, which a local official praised as 38,000 hectares preserved.

name: Masyarakat Adat Iban Sungai Utik
summary: A Dayak Iban community that has preserved more than 6,000 hectares of old-growth rainforest within its 9,450-hectare customary forest, using customary rules on hunting, harvest, fire and cropping.

name: Masyarakat Adat Knasaimos
summary: An indigenous community whose customary territory of 97,441 hectares across Saifi and Seremuk districts was recognised by a South Sorong regent's decree in June 2024.

name: Masyarakat Adat Puyang Kedung Samad
summary: A customary community of 234 households that, according to a 2019 article, manages the 336-hectare Mude Ayek Tebat Benawa customary forest, the first in South Sumatra recognised by the government.

name: Masyarakat Adat Wabula
summary: An indigenous community that regulates access to coral reefs, seagrass beds and mangroves under its Kaombo system, with a monitoring group supported by Destructive Fishing Watch Indonesia.

name: Masyarakat Kampung Folley
summary: A village community that dedicated sea sasi areas within the East South Misool marine conservation area, reported as about 82 hectares in 2013 and 297 hectares in 2018.

name: Medaka fish species detection and classification
summary: Research project on detecting and classifying two medaka fish species with YOLOv8, with the trained model built into a mobile application for use in the field. A Universitas Hasanuddin group reports it.

name: Mempawah Mangrove Conservation
summary: A mangrove planting group formed on 14 December 2011 by Fajar and two colleagues, whose planted area across seven villages in Mempawah district reached 28 hectares by 2018.

name: MERANTI
summary: Norway-supported project with the Ministry of Forestry and FAO to strengthen the National Forest Inventory 2.0 and advance SIMONTANA, paired with the AIM4Forests programme.

name: Meru Betiri National Park
summary: National park run by the forestry directorate; VOI reported in September 2024 that it installed 32 camera traps in its Regional II Ambulu section, after setting cameras in rotating zones since 2017.

name: Misool Foundation
summary: Foundation at Sorong, Indonesia, listed as a partner in the CORA(i)L coral health AI project.

name: Mnukwar
summary: West Papua group founded by environmental and social justice activists, working through film, and a member of the MapBiomas Indonesia network. No data work of its own read beyond membership.

name: MonMang
summary: Mobile mangrove monitoring application developed by BRIN for citizen scientists, reported as used in 27 countries; version 3.0 is being developed with Blue Ventures Indonesia.

name: Mukim Beungga
summary: A customary community unit in Aceh whose head said it proposed 10,900 hectares of customary forest and was granted 4,060 hectares following a September 2023 decree handover.

name: Nagari Paru
summary: A nagari that, according to a 2021 article, guarded 4,500 hectares of rimbo larangan, designated nagari forest in 2014, alongside 17,000 hectares of state forest.

name: Ngata Toro
summary: An indigenous community with an 18,360-hectare customary forest divided into traditional zones, lying inside the Lore Lindu National Park area that the government had claimed without discussion with residents.

name: npnameyrapp
summary: Open R application for processing camera-trap data from national parks and producing standard ecological metrics and reports. It was released in December 2025.

name: Nusantara Atlas
summary: Web platform for monitoring deforestation, fires, peatland degradation and forest regeneration in Equatorial Asia, combining satellite images, RADD and GLAD alerts and concession data.

name: Ocean Big Data
summary: A marine data system planned by Indonesia's marine ministry, using radar, water sensors, underwater and aerial drones and nanosatellites with AI to map marine activity and habitats.

name: Ocean Monitoring System (KKP)
summary: A marine monitoring system the marine ministry is procuring under its World Bank-backed LAUTRA project. A first phase collects drone data at Gili Matra and the Sawu Sea, with AI development among the deliverables.

name: OPTIMAL-IPB
summary: Deep learning model from IPB University that detects individual oil palms in high-resolution satellite imagery, funded by LPDP and used to delineate smallholder plantations.

name: Orangutan Information Centre
summary: Medan orangutan organisation that Conservation Drones lists as a partner using its drones in Indonesia.

name: Panglima Laot Aceh
summary: A customary sea institution in Aceh that leads customary fishing practice, including setting fishing grounds and mooring, settling disputes, and applying customary sea law on area limits, closed days and conservation.

name: Pantau Gambut
summary: Online platform set up by a civil society alliance in 2017 with information on peat restoration progress in Indonesia, including a restoration activity map and commitment tracking.

name: Papua Watch
summary: Interactive story map published by Nusantara Atlas, showing satellite monitoring of land clearing at 13 locations in West Papua.

name: Perhimpunan Burung Indonesia
summary: Indonesian bird conservation organisation founded on 15 July 2002 which, with BirdLife International and RSPB, founded Yakehi so that PT REKI could hold Hutan Harapan licences covering 52,170 hectares in South Sumatra and 46,385 in Jambi.

name: Piksel
summary: National platform for processing and analysing satellite data, launched by Badan Informasi Geospasial in August 2026 and developed with Geoscience Australia and Auspatious.

name: Planet Indonesia
summary: Nonprofit working with communities in West Kalimantan on ecosystem governance; partner in a WildMon acoustic and camera-trap monitoring project at Gunung Naning.

name: Politeknik Statistika STIS
summary: Statistics polytechnic in Jakarta whose Department of Statistical Computing publishes on satellite machine learning for oil palm area detection.

name: PT Alam Bukit Tigapuluh
summary: A company holding an ecosystem restoration licence to protect and restore degraded forest near Bukit Tigapuluh in Sumatra, set up by WWF, Frankfurt Zoological Society, The Orangutan Project and Rainforest Trust.

name: PT Eka Lestari Persada
summary: Bogor consultancy in IT, forestry and GIS that combines cloud, AI and big data for survey data.

name: PT Informasi Geo Sistem
summary: Company that signed a partnership with Indonesia's marine ministry on developing a marine monitoring and evaluation system model.

name: PT Restorasi Ekosistem Indonesia
summary: Company that, according to an independent monitoring firm's project page, manages the Hutan Harapan concession, referred to there as PT REKI.

name: PT Restorasi Habitat Orangutan Indonesia
summary: A company founded by Yayasan BOS on 21 April 2009 to manage forest for rehabilitated orangutans, holding a restoration permit; a 2025 article says it manages 86,593 hectares in East Kalimantan.

name: PT Rimba Makmur Utama
summary: Company that, according to its 2020 communication on progress, develops and manages the Katingan Mentaya Peatland Restoration and Conservation Project, covering 149,800 hectares of relatively intact peat swamp forest.

name: PT Sustainability Tech Indonesia
summary: Company making IoT sensors and software for monitoring large forest, wetland and plantation areas, with offices in Jakarta and Bali.

name: PT Techno GIS Indonesia
summary: Yogyakarta geospatial start-up working on natural disasters, forest degradation and land mapping, offering geospatial AI.

name: PT Terra Drone Indonesia
summary: Drone survey company, formerly PT Aero Geosurvey Indonesia. A Terra Drone team gathered images of elephants for the AI system at Way Kambas National Park.

name: Remap Coral
summary: TERANGI initiative for reef rehabilitation and mapping using AI monitoring, GIS and community involvement. BISA's page says Komodo National Park adopted its rehabilitation plan.

name: Research Center For Biology, Indonesian Institute of Sciences
summary: GBIF publisher under the former Indonesian Institute of Sciences (LIPI). It is the largest Indonesian publisher in the GBIF registry by dataset count.

name: Sampan Kalimantan
summary: West Kalimantan civil society group and member of the MapBiomas Indonesia network. No page read shows data work of its own beyond network membership.

name: Sangga Bumi Lestari
summary: Organisation behind the Bentarum Landscape site in West Kalimantan. It teaches Dayak youth to monitor forests with satellite imagery, drones, acoustic sensors and camera traps.

name: SATUDATA KemenLH
summary: The environment ministry's official open data portal, covering environmental quality, biodiversity and climate change.

name: Save Our Borneo
summary: Central Kalimantan civil society group and member of the MapBiomas Indonesia network, named as contributing to data collection and validation.

name: Saveforest.ai
summary: Prototype AI forest and land fire detector built by a Universitas Gadjah Mada student team, using gas sensors and a thermal camera carried on a drone. It sends data to a web dashboard.

name: Sawu Sea ocean monitoring pilots
summary: Global Ocean Innovation Challenge pilots in the Sawu Sea, East Nusa Tenggara, testing autonomous surface vessels and solar-powered AI acoustic stations that detect marine mammals and vessels.

name: Sebangau National Park
summary: Indonesian national park whose staff describe using AI-equipped thermal drones for forest and wildlife monitoring.

name: Sharks & Rays ID AI
summary: AI tool from Marine Conservation Indonesia that helps identify species and individuals from shark and ray photos.

name: SIGAP Kehutanan
summary: The forestry ministry's geospatial portal for standardised forestry data, developed and managed by its inventory and monitoring directorate.

name: SIHATI Kaltim
summary: East Kalimantan's provincial biodiversity information system, promoted by the province's environment agency.

name: SIMONTANA
summary: Indonesia's national forest monitoring system, used for land cover maps, deforestation figures and the national greenhouse gas inventory.

name: Simontini
summary: Public information system on land cover and permits in Indonesia, with maps and deforestation data. GoodStats reports that the 2025 Auriga deforestation figure came from analysis on this platform. No page read states who operates it.

name: Sipalaga
summary: Real-time platform for peat water level, soil moisture and rainfall from sensor stations, developed by the peat restoration agency to anticipate fires.

name: SIPASHUT
summary: Ministry of Forestry information system on forest concession business plans and reports, upgraded with UNDP support. One press article says it includes AI algorithms for detecting forest clearing.

name: SiPongi+
summary: Forest and land fire monitoring site from the forestry ministry's fire control directorate, publishing hotspot data for the public.

name: Sistem Informasi Taman Kehati
summary: National platform under the environment ministry for inventories and data exchange across Indonesia's biodiversity parks, linking local governments, BRIN and academics.

name: Smart Forest Guardian, West Bali National Park
summary: AI forest-monitoring project announced in 2020 for West Bali National Park with Huawei Indonesia and the environment ministry. The pages read do not show whether it went ahead.

name: SONGKET
summary: South Sumatra's WebGIS system for early detection of forest and land fires, launched in May 2021, with hotspot data, wind and routing to the nearest fire post and smoke cameras on Telkom towers.

name: SPARTAN
summary: BMKG early warning system that estimates the danger and spread of forest and land fires.

name: SSRS Indonesia Biodiversity Hub
summary: Technical unit of the SSRS Institute that aims to act as an open public Indonesian biodiversity database, and lists species detection using AI among its services.

name: Suku Klesi
summary: Customary community that committed to protect its forest by designating part of its territory in 11 villages a customary conservation forest, and asks the Jayapura government for a legal basis.

name: Sumatran Orangutan Conservation Programme
summary: Conservation programme for Sumatran and Tapanuli orangutans, implemented mainly by Yayasan Ekosistem Lestari, and a listed user of Conservation Drones.

name: Sumatran Tiger Project
summary: A UNDP-supported, GEF-financed project which, the GEF reported in March 2018, supported a standard scientific monitoring protocol for tigers, prey and forest habitat and produced a SMART patrolling training module.

name: Swandiri Institute
summary: Pontianak research institute that has built low-cost drones since 2011 for observing forests and river basins.

name: Taka Bonerate National Park
summary: A national park run by the Directorate General KSDAE, where WCS Indonesia says it supports routine SMART patrols with the park office to strengthen monitoring and enforcement.

name: Tambora Muda Indonesia
summary: Network of young Indonesian conservationists. With the Indonesian Biodiversity Information Facility it started Biodiverskripsi, a database of biodiversity records from student theses.

name: Tanamin
summary: Indonesian company developing MangroveAI, an AI app for monitoring mangroves from satellite data.

name: TFCA-Sumatera
summary: Grant programme for forest and species conservation in Sumatra, administered by Yayasan KEHATI. Its eleventh grant cycle supports camera trap procurement for species work.

name: TheTreeMap
summary: Technology and consultancy company focused on insular South East Asia, which designed Nusantara Atlas. Its EU lobby register entry gives an address in France.

name: TMAT Gambut
summary: Monitoring and reporting system for the water table in peatland, by province, from the peat ecosystem directorate of the environment ministry.

name: TREEO Indonesia
summary: Digital monitoring, reporting and verification provider for forest carbon projects in Indonesia, combining farmer-led field data with satellite remote sensing, and building its own mapping drones.

name: Udayana University
summary: Indonesian university listed as a partner in the CORA(i)L coral health AI project.

name: Ujung Kulon National Park
summary: A national park run by the forestry ministry, which reported camera traps recording a Javan rhino mother and calf in January 2026 and planned technology-based population monitoring.

name: Universitas Gadjah Mada
summary: University in Yogyakarta whose geography and forestry faculties publish on machine learning for mangrove mapping and peat subsidence.

name: Universitas Indonesia
summary: University in Depok whose Department of Geography has studied 20 years of change on Derawan's coral reefs by machine learning classification, and where Prof. Rokhmatuloh has lectured on remote sensing and AI for forests.

name: Universitas Nasional
summary: A Jakarta university which runs the C-SERM centre; in July 2026 it said C-SERM and YAYORIN were developing a bioacoustic biodiversity study in Lamandau, Central Kalimantan, analysing recordings for species presence.

name: Universitas Syiah Kuala
summary: Banda Aceh university whose marine and fisheries research centre has an AI application for measuring coral transplant growth and coral cover.

name: University of Palangka Raya
summary: University in Central Kalimantan whose authors, with WWF Central Kalimantan, trained YOLOv5 to detect Bornean orangutan nests in drone imagery.

name: University of Papua
summary: Papuan university listed as a partner in the CORA(i)L coral health AI project.

name: UPT Taman Hutan Raya Ngurah Rai
summary: Park management unit with an office at the park's entrance in Suwung, Denpasar, which a 2019 article says manages the forest area, taken back from JICA in 2013.

name: UPT Taman Hutan Raya Raden Soerjo
summary: Technical unit within the East Java provincial forestry service for the Raden Soerjo grand forest park, which a 2019 article reports covers about 27,000 hectares across five regencies.

name: UPTD Tahura Ir. H. Djuanda
summary: Public service agency with flexible budgeting, referred to in a West Java regulation in connection with its BLUD strategic plan.

name: UPTD Tahura Provinsi Jambi
summary: Technical unit inside the Jambi provincial forestry service, formed by a regulation of the Jambi governor.

name: UPTD Taman Hutan Raya Wan Abdul Rachman
summary: A park management unit whose head said in 2020 that social forestry was possible in the park, with its data listing managed tourist sites.

name: Wakatobi Dive Resort
summary: A dive resort which, according to an October 2024 Divernet feature, had started a reef health assessment programme with an in-house marine biologist and an eDNA survey inside its private marine preserve.

name: Way Kambas Integrated Surveillance System
summary: AI-based monitoring network of 360-degree CCTV cameras, drones and 38 camera traps run from a command centre, which tracks Sumatran elephant movements at Way Kambas National Park.

name: Way Kambas National Park
summary: National park in East Lampung that runs an AI-based surveillance system along its 167-kilometre boundary.

name: WCS Indonesia
summary: Indonesian programme of the Wildlife Conservation Society, which recruits SMART patrol and SMART database staff for the Leuser landscape.

name: West Bali National Park
summary: Indonesian national park whose head welcomed a planned Huawei and Rainforest Connection AI forest sound monitoring pilot in 2020.

name: West Sumatra forest acoustic monitoring
summary: Rainforest Connection Guardian devices in four West Sumatra villages, using TensorFlow to send forest sounds to rangers' phones, with KKI Warsi.

name: West Sumatra forest guardians
summary: Installation of Rainforest Connection Guardian sound sensors, which alert rangers to chainsaws, in community forests in Solok and Solok Selatan, West Sumatra.

name: Wetlands International Indonesia
summary: The Bogor-based Indonesian programme of Wetlands International, which runs the Asian Waterbird Census in Indonesia, coordinating the annual count with the forestry ministry's nature conservation directorate for waterbird management planning.

name: Wildlife Laboratory, Faculty of Forestry, Universitas Gadjah Mada
summary: University laboratory that studies wildlife management, including camera trap distance sampling of Sumatran tiger prey, and publishes to GBIF.

name: WRI Indonesia
summary: World Resources Institute's Indonesian office, implementing partner of the Indonesian Peat Prize and on the drafting team of Pantau Gambut. Its own site refused the fetcher, so facts come from other pages.

name: Yayasan Adudu Nantu International
summary: Foundation that worked with Rainforest Trust on a plan to add 15,346 acres to Nantu Wildlife Sanctuary by lease and small purchase, marked protected in 2022.

name: Yayasan Badak Indonesia
summary: Foundation formed in 2008 by merging Yayasan Suaka Rhino Sumatera, set up in 1997, with other bodies; its predecessor managed the Sumatran Rhino Sanctuary in Way Kambas National Park.

name: Yayasan Bhakti Alam Sendangbiru
summary: Foundation whose ecotourism initiative, Clungup Mangrove Conservation Tiga Warna, managed six beaches in 2021, with a main aim of conserving protected forest, mangrove and coral reef.

name: Yayasan Borneo Orangutan Survival Foundation
summary: Foundation that founded PT RHOI in 2009 to manage Kehje Sewen forest in East Kalimantan for rehabilitated orangutans, with a 2025 report saying the forest's release capacity has reached its maximum.

name: Yayasan EcoNusa
summary: Indonesian foundation that has trained indigenous communities in West Papua to record and manage forest data with the SMART Patrol app.

name: Yayasan Ekosistem Lestari
summary: Sumatran conservation foundation and main implementer of the Sumatran Orangutan Conservation Programme, building a predictive AI platform that links environmental degradation with disaster risk.

name: Yayasan Generasi Biologi Indonesia
summary: Indonesian biology foundation offering research services including microbiome and eDNA analysis and DNA sequencing.

name: Yayasan Genesis Bengkulu
summary: Bengkulu foundation and member of the MapBiomas Indonesia network. It investigates overlaps between forest land and mining and plantation use.

name: Yayasan Hutan Wakaf Bogor
summary: Foundation whose wakaf forest in Bogor had grown by 2026 to 2.6 hectares at seven locations in two villages, after it bought a 1,200 square metre plot in 2019.

name: Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia
summary: Indonesian foundation with offices in Bogor and Ketapang that built the Integrated Forest Crime Alert System for protected forests in Lampung and West Kalimantan.

name: Yayasan Keanekaragaman Hayati Indonesia
summary: Indonesian biodiversity foundation that makes grants. It administers TFCA-Sumatera and TFCA Kalimantan, and backs conservation technology such as camera traps, drones and environmental DNA for rhinos.

name: Yayasan Kompas Peduli Hutan
summary: Central Sulawesi environmental group and member of the MapBiomas Indonesia network. It has calculated land lost to nickel mining.

name: Yayasan Konservasi Alam Nusantara
summary: Indonesian conservation foundation that developed FishFace, which uses smartphone cameras and AI to identify fish species and record catch data, with the Swedish company Refind.

name: Yayasan Orangutan Indonesia
summary: Orangutan conservation foundation in Central Kalimantan working with C-SERM at Universitas Nasional on passive acoustic monitoring and a machine learning model for primate calls.

name: Yayasan Palung
summary: An organisation which in September 2020 reported over a year of orangutan surveys in Gunung Palung National Park, comparing ground counts with a drone method, with its nest data assisting Serge Wich's AI nest-detection work.

name: Yayasan Pendidikan dan Sosial Ma'arif Sidoarjo
summary: Foundation that a June 2026 article says held 2.4 hectares of wakaf forest land on two plots, including 1.6 hectares on Mount Anjasmoro, with the second plot planned as productive forest.

name: Yayasan Perhimpunan Penempuh Rimba dan Pendaki Gunung Wanadri
summary: A 2022 article describes its joint management with BBKSDA of Masigit Kareumbi’s roughly 12,420.70 hectares and a tree-guardian programme covering 600 hectares across three locations.

name: Yayasan Pro Natura
summary: A 2023 article names the foundation as Sungai Wain protected forest’s manager in Balikpapan, whose manager described primary forest and secondary forest planted after the 1997 fires.

name: Yayasan Pusat Informasi Lingkungan Indonesia
summary: Indonesian NGO that holds a Global Nature Watch small grant to turn routine patrols in a West Kalimantan community forest into an alert-driven monitoring and enforcement system.

name: Yayasan WWF Indonesia
summary: Indonesian conservation foundation working with Kuva Space on hyperspectral AI mapping of blue carbon habitats, and running camera trap and acoustic training in Papua.

name: Biological Q Results
summary: River quality dataset run by the EPA, with records dating back to 1971 and a Q-value assigned to each river station; the latest listed update is 19 January 2023.

name: BirdWatch Ireland
summary: Irish conservation organisation, established in 1968 by its own account, which runs the Countryside Bird Survey, involving volunteers, NPWS rangers and staff.

name: Botany Discipline, School of Natural Sciences, Trinity College Dublin
summary: Trinity College Dublin academic unit, listed as an affiliation of the first author of an abstract applying random forest to predict water tables in selected Irish peatlands.

name: CeADAR
summary: Ireland's centre for applied artificial intelligence, according to ThinkBusiness in April 2023, which reported it led a €200,000 project in the National Challenge Fund and partners with AI2Peat.

name: Centre for Robotics and Intelligent Systems, University of Limerick
summary: University of Limerick research centre, listed as the affiliation of the first author of a paper on automating data analysis in digital aerial surveys for offshore wind.

name: Countryside Bird Survey
summary: Breeding bird survey run by BirdWatch Ireland and funded by NPWS, in which over 200 volunteers and staff walk 1 km squares each summer, producing the Common Bird Index.

name: Department of Geography, Trinity College Dublin
summary: Dublin department listed as the lead affiliation on 2023 papers using Landsat and Google Earth Engine to assess peatland land use change and using drones to map coastal dune habitats.

name: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage
summary: Irish government department whose Heritage Division includes NPWS, which manages national parks and nature reserves and designates protected sites, according to NPWS.

name: Discipline of Geography, School of Natural Sciences, Trinity College Dublin
summary: Trinity College Dublin academic unit, the sole affiliation of the authors of a national assessment of peatland land use change from 1989 to 2020 using Landsat and Google Earth Engine.

name: Earth and Life Sciences, School of Natural Sciences, University of Galway
summary: University of Galway academic unit, affiliation of the first author of the BioIntertidal Mapper paper on satellite NDVI intertidal habitat mapping; version 2.0 of the software appeared in 2026.

name: Environmental Protection Agency
summary: Independent public body established under the Environmental Protection Agency Act 1992, based in Wexford, providing environmental evidence and funding Explore Your Shore!, according to the Centre.

name: Hamilton Institute, Maynooth University
summary: Maynooth University research institute, listed as the affiliation of the first author of "NEAL: an open-source tool for audio annotation".

name: Hy-Res Research Group, University of Galway
summary: University of Galway research group, affiliation of the first and corresponding authors of a paper using remote sensing and machine learning to observe variability within peatlands.

name: Inland Fisheries Ireland
summary: Irish body that protects, manages and conserves inland fisheries and sea angling resources under the 2010 Act, and has deployed an AquaWatch float with five water quality sensors.

name: Irish Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: Volunteer transect scheme run by the National Biodiversity Data Centre since 2008, whose index of the 15 commonest species shows a 65% decline in 2025 compared with 2008.

name: Irish Wetland Bird Survey
summary: Winter waterbird survey run by BirdWatch Ireland and funded by NPWS, with counts from September to March and a database covering about 25 years, publishing species and site trends.

name: Irish Wildlife Trust
summary: Irish conservation group that develops citizen science projects combining awareness raising, training and species surveying, with past projects including the National Reptile Survey and the National Smooth Newt Survey.

name: MaREI, the Research Ireland Centre for Energy, Climate and Marine
summary: Research centre at University College Cork whose completed 13-year funded programme was coordinated by the Sustainability Institute; its site cites over 220 researchers, and a 2023 paper by a listed author compared F-POD and C-POD porpoise loggers.

name: Marine and Freshwater Research Centre, Atlantic Technological University
summary: Galway research centre listed as the lead affiliation on papers about passive acoustic monitoring, including a glider-mounted SoundTrap, seals in the Malin Sea (2024) and beaked whales off west Ireland (2025).

name: Marine Institute
summary: Irish state agency for marine research and innovation, which co-led the 2017 to 2019 SeaRover reef survey with INFOMAR and runs INFOMAR seabed mapping jointly with Geological Survey Ireland.

name: National Biodiversity Data Centre
summary: Waterford-based charity, registered in November 2025, which is Ireland's node to GBIF, runs the Irish Butterfly Monitoring Scheme, and says it has spent 20 years making biodiversity data freely available.

name: National Forest Inventory
summary: Forest Service report undertaken every four years, according to Hometree, which said the 2022 inventory found 5,000 hectares converted from forest to other uses since 2017.

name: National Parks and Wildlife Service
summary: Part of the Heritage Division of the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage, it manages national parks and nature reserves, designates protected sites, and surveys Irish seals and habitats.

name: Ocean Research and Conservation Association Ireland
summary: Cork-based non-profit running Smart Whale Sounds, whose website describes an AI-enabled smart buoy and use of deep learning models to identify cetacean species from vocalisations.

name: Polliknow
summary: Company funded by Enterprise Ireland, charging fees, with solar-powered AI sensors monitoring pollinator numbers and species richness for four to six weeks, according to November 2025 Irish Times reporting.

name: Ryan Institute, University of Galway
summary: Galway institute listed as an affiliation on a 2022 paper mapping peatland soil with machine learning and a 2023 paper monitoring intertidal golden tides with Sentinel-2 imagery.

name: School of Computer Science and Statistics, Trinity College Dublin
summary: Dublin school listed as the first and corresponding authors' affiliation on a paper presenting a hidden Markov model framework for species behaviour changes under disturbance in acoustic time series.

name: School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, University College Dublin
summary: Dublin school listed as the lead affiliation, for both first and last authors, on a 2024 paper about the quality of IoT sensor data in peatland environmental monitoring networks.

name: SeaMonitor
summary: Marine research project around Ireland, Western Scotland and Northern Ireland, led by the Loughs Agency and funded with 4.6 million euros from EU INTERREG VA, which planned spatial models and an extended acoustic receiver network.

name: SeaRover
summary: Closed Marine Institute-led deep-water habitat assessment that mapped 154 locations in Ireland's marine territory over three surveys in 2017 to 2019, funded by the National Parks and Wildlife Service.

name: Smart Whale Sounds
summary: Project run and built by ORCA Ireland that uses AI to classify cetacean sounds from a buoy launched off Ireland's south coast on 18 March 2021; Rainforest Connection reports 98% accuracy.

name: SmartBay Ireland
summary: Describes itself as Ireland's national marine and ocean energy observation and validation facility, publishing real-time sea temperature and salinity data from its cabled observatory in Spiddal.

name: Taighde Éireann – Research Ireland
summary: Ireland’s national research funding agency, established on 1 August 2024 by merging SFI and Irish Research Council activities, which funds AI2Peat, an AI-enhanced peatland monitoring platform.

name: Tailte Éireann
summary: Independent government agency, established in December 2022 under the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage, providing national mapping and surveying alongside property registration and valuation.

name: The Heritage Council
summary: Listed among the National Biodiversity Data Centre’s state body partners, with a December 2022 page stating that the new company was subject to its oversight.

name: AgmoNET
summary: A completed piece of research on long-term monitoring of bird vocal activity, building a deep learning bird-call classifier from more than two years of recordings at two stations, with no further development planned.

name: AI platform to predict wildfire spread with remote sensing (Ben-Gurion University, KKL-JNF grant)
summary: Project to predict wildfire spread with AI and remote sensing, funded by KKL-JNF with NIS 299,970 in its 2025 research call.

name: AI4Biodiversity
summary: Active project developing new methods, with conservation agencies, to assess the state of nature, using transfer-learned YOLOv5 and MegaDetector on camera images, and proposing satellite mammal detection for two gazelle species.

name: Albo Systems
summary: Organisation that, according to KrASIA in January 2021, measured carbon sequestration in nature-based projects, used deep learning to predict CO2 proxies, and had signed Finnish forestry company Wuudis.

name: Animal Flight Group (University of Haifa)
summary: Active University of Haifa research group that published a fully automated deep-learning algorithm to identify, count and map breeding seabirds, with university-linked papers on bat and bird radar detection.

name: ATLAS reverse-GPS wildlife tracking system
summary: Reverse-GPS wildlife tracking system built by Ran Nathan and Sivan Toledo, which a 2020 report says collected over 18 million localisations of 172 Egyptian fruit bats across four years.

name: Automated deep-learning monitoring of seabird breeding colonies (Atlit)
summary: Active deep-learning model, built by Inbal Schekler, using YOLOv8 on remote camera images of seabird colonies, with counts within 2% of manual counts on average and over 90% species accuracy for nesting birds.

name: Ben-Gurion University of the Negev
summary: Active university that is the grantee for the AI wildfire-spread platform in KKL-JNF's 2025 call, with 2021 papers led by its authors on random forests and insect deep learning.

name: BioGIS - Israel Biodiversity Information System
summary: Active open-access GIS database of Israel's flora and fauna distribution, led by Eyal Ben-Hur and built by Ronen Kadmon, which publishes eight datasets to GBIF.

name: BMSapp
summary: A citizen science app designed and developed by Israel Pe'er (GlueCAD) for the Israeli Butterfly Monitoring Scheme, in use since 2015 across more than 400 transects and alerting observers to out-of-range or out-of-season records.

name: Coral Monitoring Station (Gulf of Aqaba)
summary: A real-time, open-data installation in the Gulf of Aqaba that continuously records the reef environment and coral response, with an underwater camera tracking coral pigmentation and reef fish activity.

name: Dead Sea and Arava Science Center
summary: Active organisation where an author led a 2025 paper using remote sensing to assess vegetation dynamics in the Arava valley.

name: Delphis
summary: An association that conducted 82 dolphin surveys in 2024, collected over a year of continuous cave camera data at Rosh Hanikra, and began training volunteer surveyors with University of Haifa researchers.

name: GBIF Israel
summary: Active programme listed by GBIF as the country node for Israel with observer status, whose registry home page is the BioGIS site.

name: GlueCAD
summary: Organisation supporting voluntary butterfly data collection, storage, validation and analysis associated with the Israeli Butterfly Observations Portal.

name: HaMaarag - Israel's National Ecosystem Assessment Program
summary: Active national ecosystem assessment programme founded in 2006 with four partners, monitoring terrestrial biodiversity using trail cameras, with remote sensing work and GBIF dataset publishing.

name: Hebrew University of Jerusalem
summary: Active university holding the National Natural History Collections, with BioGIS staff listed there, researchers reported in 2020 to use ATLAS on wild bats, and papers on machine learning in 2021 and 2024.

name: Holon Institute of Technology
summary: Active institute where an author led a 2022 paper correcting a bias in behavioural time budgets based on supervised learning.

name: Hula monitoring program
summary: A programme led by Idan Barnea that has monitored abiotic and biotic changes in the Hula Project ecosystem every year for 20 years, funded by the National Water Authority, KKL and Peat convention farmers.

name: Hula Research Center
summary: A joint venture of Tel-Hai College and KKL-JNF whose ringing station has identified and ringed more than 10,000 birds of about 100 species, alongside motion-triggered cameras recording wildlife across the Hula Valley.

name: INPA - Observations
summary: A GBIF dataset of Israel Nature and Parks Authority observations, with about 2.4 million occurrence records covering Israel, the Palestinian authority, Sinai and the Mediterranean Sea, maintained continually under a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence.

name: Interuniversity Institute for Marine Sciences in Eilat
summary: Marine research institute in Eilat, where authors led a 2026 annotated plankton image dataset and a 2024 dataset of 3D artificial reef models, both from the northern Red Sea.

name: Israel Center for Citizen Science
summary: Programme says it was set up at the Steinhardt Museum in early 2022 to promote public participation in biodiversity research, and says it launched a data collection website in February 2025.

name: Israel Citizen Science Center
summary: Citizen science organisation whose technical lead is building infrastructure to collect and process data on a local Living Atlas installation, and which the AI4Biodiversity project names as a partner.

name: Israel Long-term Ecological Research Network
summary: Long-term ecological research network founded in 1997, with 13 sites across Israel's climate and demographic gradients, aiming to harmonise data collection for cross-site research.

name: Israel Marine Mammal Research and Assistance Center
summary: An Israeli association that began a cetacean database in 1993, runs surveys of common bottlenose dolphins and staffs a national 24/7 network for reports of distressed marine mammals.

name: Israel Nature and Parks Authority
summary: Statutory body established under a 1963 Knesset law, protecting habitats and species and publishing GBIF observations, named alongside the ministry in 2022 as the biodiversity targets centre.

name: Israel Oceanographic and Limnological Research
summary: Non-profit governmental research corporation established in 1967 that lists three institutes and says it has monitored Israel’s Mediterranean coast and marine area for over 50 years.

name: Israel Space Agency
summary: State body within the Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology that coordinates Israel's civil space activity and, per CNES, shared responsibility for the VENµS mission, which ended in August 2024.

name: Israeli Butterfly Observations Portal
summary: Portal launched in 2011 that handles public and citizen-science butterfly sighting reports and digitises older records, and was built by Gluecad.

name: Israeli Lepidopterists’ Society
summary: Society whose GBIF record says it aims to study and monitor Israel's butterflies, and whose members set up the Israeli Butterfly Monitoring Scheme in April 2009 using fixed transect walks.

name: ISRAMAR
summary: Marine data centre set up in 2001 at the National Institute of Oceanography, holding physical, chemical, biological and geological data from the Mediterranean, Red Sea and Dead Sea.

name: ISRAMAR - Israel Marine Data Center
summary: Israel's marine data centre, listed among the knowledge centres of Israel Oceanographic and Limnological Research, which runs it.

name: Jerusalem Bird Observatory
summary: Bird-ringing and migration monitoring site housing Israel's national ringing centre, run by the Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel, with migration data collected and analysed in a database.

name: Keren Kayemeth LeIsrael - Jewish National Fund
summary: Forestry body whose 2024 report, published in March 2025, describes five long-term ecological monitoring stations, and whose 2025 research call funded 23 of 73 proposals.

name: Kinneret Limnological Laboratory
summary: Lake Kinneret monitoring since January 1969 has built a database used for operational decisions and policy, now including four online sampling platforms and satellite imaging.

name: Migal - Galilee Technology Center
summary: Research centre whose author led a 2026 paper using deep learning on drone imagery to detect crane mortality hotspots during an H5N1 outbreak.

name: Ministry of Environmental Protection (Israel)
summary: Ministry and founding partner of the 2006 National Ecosystem Assessment Program; the State Comptroller's May 2022 report said Israel missed 14 of 19 national biodiversity targets.

name: Morris Kahn Marine Research Station
summary: Marine research station that says it monitors the eastern Mediterranean and offers free data, and whose partnership deck says it uses machine-learning image recognition to detect lionfish and is piloting AI tools for ships.

name: Morris Kahn Marine Research Station database
summary: A downloadable long-term ecological research dataset from the Morris Kahn Marine Research Station, split into five sub-divisions and including moored acoustic records of dolphin and toothed whale presence along Israel's Mediterranean coast.

name: National Butterfly Monitoring Programme (Israel)
summary: Citizen science project listed by the Israel Center for Citizen Science, whose databases and software a team member manages, and which a team member supports in moving onto BioCollect.

name: National Center for Aquatic Ecology
summary: Israel's national knowledge centre for inland water ecology, founded in 2015 at the Steinhardt Museum of Natural History, which sets biological standards for assessing streams and publishes basin monitoring reports.

name: National Monitoring Program of the Gulf of Eilat
summary: Monitoring programme led and run by the Interuniversity Institute for Marine Sciences in Eilat, which has built extensive databases over 20 years, some available online.

name: National Terrestrial Biodiversity Monitoring Program (Israel)
summary: Long-term programme, operated by Hamaarag, that monitors terrestrial biodiversity to track effects of development and climate change, including mammals monitored with trail cameras.

name: Nexus Israel Mediterranean Monitoring
summary: A CoralNet source affiliated with NEXUS, University of Haifa, for which a classifier was trained in December 2024 using EfficientNet (default) as the feature extractor.

name: Open Landscape Institute
summary: Applied, policy-relevant centre at the Steinhardt Museum that, per KKL-JNF, has run over thirty GIS-based land surveys and developed vegetation mapping methods and a model of open-space fragmentation.

name: Ramat Hanadiv
summary: A public benefit company whose research aims to build a long-term database, listing gazelle, partridge and roadkill monitoring, with nature park land privately owned by Yad Hanadiv.

name: Ramat Hanadiv Long-Term Ecological Research Station
summary: Long-term ecological research station set up at Ramat Hanadiv in September 2003, monitoring gazelles, partridges, songbirds, butterflies and vegetation, with data to be collated into an online database.

name: Salamander population monitoring (SPNI and Yarok Balev)
summary: According to AI4Biodiversity, SPNI and Yarok Balev monitor salamanders through expert identification from annual winter images, while AI4Biodiversity proposes an automated identification algorithm.

name: Sami Shamoon College of Engineering
summary: Engineering college whose affiliated first author wrote a 2022 paper on urban plant classification using deep learning on a new dataset.

name: Sea-Thru
summary: An active project described by Schmidt Marine as a lidar-based platform being developed to image real colours underwater in real time.

name: Shamir Research Institute
summary: A research hub in Katzrin, Golan Heights, describing over 40 years of work, with University of Haifa sponsorship and research into mushroom monitoring and griffon vulture decline.

name: Sharks in Israel
summary: A non-profit that, according to Menasim's project page, has collected sightings of sharks and rays in the Mediterranean and Red Sea for over a decade, with a database of around 12,000 sightings.

name: Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel
summary: An active organisation that, with Yarok Balev, tracks salamander population size from images collected in annual winter monitoring.

name: Steinhardt Museum of Natural History
summary: A museum at Tel Aviv University and Israel's national biodiversity centre, holding over 6 million specimens, over 600,000 digitised, with an open database and data published to GBIF.

name: Survey of Israel
summary: Agency whose regulations set quality requirements for geospatial products including maps, elevation models and ortho imagery, and which published a new national aerial capturing standard in 2019.

name: Tatzpiteva
summary: Project collecting data on the Golan's fauna and flora through public observation, using an application built on iNaturalist, with more than 25,000 observations recorded since January 2016.

name: Technion – Israel Institute of Technology
summary: An active organisation; a 2023 paper whose first author is affiliated with it concerns estimating biodiversity from environmental drivers using machine and deep learning.

name: Tel Aviv University
summary: An active university that hosts the Steinhardt Museum, with affiliated papers on AI for climate change biology and bat tracking, and a 2024-reported vulture study using 15 years of GPS data from 142 birds.

name: Tel Hai Academic College
summary: An active college; a 2024 paper whose first author is affiliated with it concerns continuous annual soundscape monitoring using a deep learning system in Agmon Hula Lake Park.

name: Terra Space Lab
summary: Remote sensing company using existing satellites that describes an AI platform, forest inventory uses for tree counts and composition, and fire intensity estimates.

name: The Bat Lab for Neuro-Ecology
summary: Active lab describing miniature technologies for tracking bats, the Vesper sensor, Batalef sound-analysis software, and monitoring of Egyptian fruit bats in the laboratory and wild.

name: The Coral Reefs of the Gulf of Eilat
summary: Active project, run by Deep Voice, that says it fine-tunes an AI model on Gulf of Eilat acoustic data, using manual annotations to identify fish calls and other low-frequency biological sounds.

name: The National Natural History Collections
summary: Collections at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem that it says are the most extensive biological collections in the Middle East, with twelve datasets listed on GBIF.

name: Urban LTER Israel
summary: Long-term urban monitoring programme in Haifa and Beer Sheva, for which the Israel Center for Citizen Science names a community coordinator handling citizen science communities and monitoring tools.

name: VENµS
summary: A closed French-Israeli vegetation monitoring mission, launched in 2017 and run by the Israel Space Agency and CNES, which imaged more than 110 areas from 2017 to 2024.

name: Vulture GPS monitoring and alert system (Israel Nature and Parks Authority)
summary: Vulture tracking programme run by the Israel Nature and Parks Authority, with slightly more than 100 GPS-tagged vultures, nearly half the population, and an alert system that Tel Aviv University says flags stopped or endangered birds.

name: Weizmann Institute of Science
summary: An active organisation; a 2022 paper whose first author is affiliated with it concerns separating soil, shade and tree canopy contributions to satellite vegetation indices in a sparse dry forest.

name: Yad Hanadiv
summary: An active organisation whose marine protected areas initiative supports management, enforcement tools and research, and whose Environment Programme aims at ecosystem health and resilience; it partners with the Israel Nature and Parks Authority.

name: Yarok Balev
summary: An association registered in 2014 that has led a salamander protection project in Haifa since 2017, covering research, awareness and policy, with public help on patrols and field reports.

name: Ballaugh Curragh wallaby drone survey
summary: Closed survey run by Manx Wildlife Trust in January 2023, using a consultant with a drone-mounted thermal camera; two nights over 400 hectares gave an average count of 568 red-necked wallabies.

name: Calf of Man Bird Observatory
summary: Bird observatory programme on the Calf of Man, owned by Manx National Heritage, where wardens carry out daily bird census counts and ringing, alongside seabird breeding monitoring and colour ringing studies; run by Manx Wildlife Trust.

name: Calf of Man Seal Survey
summary: Active seal monitoring programme run by Manx Wildlife Trust since 2009, with the 2025 survey recording 111 pups using camera traps and a thermal drone, in partnership with the Department of Environment, Food and Agriculture.

name: Coan
summary: Environmental AI research and consultancy company, named Coan Ltd on its site, which says it is Isle of Man based and lists a 10 m island habitat baseline and a Defra wet woodland map for England.

name: Curlew Country (Isle of Man)
summary: Active Manx Wildlife Trust curlew project whose 2025 report records 45 breeding pairs north of the central valley and 20 south of it.

name: Cypris marine monitoring station
summary: Active monitoring station about two nautical miles off Port Erin, run by the Department of Environment, Food and Agriculture, where a buoy deployed in 2023 measures water variables and fortnightly samples are analysed.

name: Department of Environment, Food and Agriculture (Isle of Man)
summary: Isle of Man government department that holds a wildlife records database and mapping system, develops biodiversity policy and strategy, and works to conserve scarce species and habitats; GBIF lists the Manx Biological Recording Partnership at its address.

name: Isle of Man island-wide seal monitoring
summary: Island-wide seal monitoring run by Manx Wildlife Trust, which the 2024 Seal Biodiversity Action Plan says has been carried out since 2016, including a survey in October and November 2017.

name: Isle of Man marine nature reserve camera surveys
summary: Reported in December 2019, underwater camera surveys of marine nature reserves use a towable sledge to provide fisheries data, species records and habitat monitoring.

name: Isle of Man marine strandings programme
summary: Active programme run by Manx Wildlife Trust, which attends dead marine megafauna strandings for the Department of Environment, Food and Agriculture, feeds a national database, and lists annual reports for 2013 to 2025.

name: Isle of Man rocky shore indicator species time series
summary: Part-funded by the Isle of Man government since 2008, this time series combines Manx data with up to 80 UK shores, monitoring up to 60 indicator species.

name: Isle of Man Seabird Census 2017-18
summary: Closed census project that surveyed seventeen seabird species from April to June 2017 using JNCC protocols, validated counts with high-resolution photography, and captured 10,000 records; run by Manx BirdLife.

name: Isle of Man Small Shark Tagging Programme
summary: Operating since May 2013, the Manx Wildlife Trust programme partners with DEFA, had trained 111 anglers by the end of 2025 and tagged 123 individuals in 2025.

name: Isle of Man upland peat survey
summary: Active Manx Wildlife Trust survey mapping peat depth and extent, measuring depth every 150 m, with about half of the upland area needing survey mapped by the end of 2020.

name: Manx Bat Group
summary: Registered charity number 443 maintains Isle of Man bat records and says it has recorded nine bat species through surveys, bat walks and record keeping.

name: Manx Biological Recording Partnership
summary: Partnership led by the Department of Environment, Food and Agriculture and Manx Wildlife Trust that collates terrestrial and marine Isle of Man data, has 11 datasets listed on GBIF, and supports NBN Atlas Isle of Man.

name: Manx BirdLife
summary: A Manx bird conservation charity that conducted the 2017–18 seabird census and, Manx Lottery Trust reports, received £28,618 in 2026 to recruit a warden supporting the National Ornithological Database.

name: Manx Blue Carbon Research Project
summary: Closed four-year project led by the Department of Environment, Food and Agriculture on carbon storage in Manx seas; Manx Radio reports it mapped 50,000 hectares of offshore muddy seabed, 196 hectares of seagrass and 7.4 hectares of saltmarsh.

name: Manx Eelgrass Group
summary: Active programme built by Manx Wildlife Trust that plans to map eelgrass beds around the Manx coast using cameras, divers and baited video, linked to a Blue Carbon Project and supported by KPMG.

name: Manx Lottery Trust
summary: Independent Isle of Man charitable trust that administers the Dormant Asset Fund for the Treasury, and whose 2026 funding for a Manx BirdLife warden includes help with data management.

name: Manx National Heritage
summary: Described by Wikipedia as a statutory heritage agency and charity, publishes Calf of Man occurrence data (1959–2004) and is a core Manx Biological Recording Partnership partner.

name: Manx Whale and Dolphin Watch
summary: Reports Manx marine mammal work since 2006, keeps licensed photo-identification catalogues, receives Manx Lottery Trust funding and partners with Manx Wildlife Trust and Manx Biological Recording Partnership.

name: Manx Wildlife Trust
summary: Isle of Man registered charity and company, one of three main data providers to the partnership's Recorder 6 database, which runs the Small Shark Tagging Programme that tagged 809 small sharks from 2013 to the end of 2025.

name: Nature Recovery Network (Isle of Man)
summary: Launched in June 2023 by Manx Wildlife Trust and UNESCO Biosphere Isle of Man, this programme maps land managed for nature, with participants able to opt out of publication.

name: NBN Atlas Isle of Man
summary: Wildlife data atlas for the Isle of Man, supported by the Manx Biological Recording Partnership, which Manx Wildlife Trust says lets everyone access the island's wildlife data.

name: Seasearch Isle of Man
summary: Volunteer diver and snorkeller recording scheme, coordinated on the island by Manx Wildlife Trust with the Marine Conservation Society since January 2021, with 2025 priorities including mapping the Bulgham eelgrass bed.

name: Taxa Genomics
summary: Manx Radio reports a globally operating Douglas company offering £1,000–£5,000 biodiversity testing grants in May 2026; its presentation suggests abundant European eel from 2024 internal research samples, warranting investigation.

name: Western Irish Sea Mud Belt BRUV survey
summary: Manx Wildlife Trust survey of unknown status that drops baited underwater video units inside temporary closed areas and in open areas outside them, then records and counts species on the footage.

name: 7WEAVES
summary: Community-led bio-cultural material system in the Indo-Burma and Eastern Himalaya regions. Its Biodiversity and Geospatial Lab runs long-term ecological monitoring, including an annual bird monitoring programme at Deepor Beel.

name: A Rocha India
summary: Indian charity in the Bannerghatta-Hosur landscape with an Asian Elephant Conservation Program and a monitoring and surveys pillar of work.

name: Aadax Data Science
summary: Data science firm that built a central India camera-trap species recognition model with the Wildlife Conservation Trust.

name: Aaranyak
summary: A conservation organisation with a Geo-spatial Technology and Application Division that runs training in remote sensing, GIS and GPS.

name: Abhai
summary: An Indian company building drones and AI for early detection and prediction of forest fires.

name: Acoustic Detection of Owls
summary: IISER Tirupati project recording primary data and developing detection algorithms on acoustic data for common owls in the Tirupati landscape.

name: Acoustic early warning system for human-elephant conflict
summary: Centre for Wildlife Studies and Rainforest Connection project for real-time AI acoustic monitoring at pilot sites in India, to warn communities of elephants.

name: Adavi Alert Foundation
summary: The body behind an AI elephant detection camera project at Bandipur, according to Deccan Chronicle.

name: Advitiya Labs
summary: The technology partner building a prototype AI model for elephant detection at Bandipur, according to Deccan Chronicle.

name: All India Tiger Estimation
summary: Four-yearly national assessment of tigers, co-predators, prey and habitat, using camera traps. Species sorting for the 2022 round used the deep learning module in CaTRAT.

name: Amrabad Tiger Reserve AI surveillance system
summary: Approved AI surveillance system for Amrabad Tiger Reserve in Telangana that is to identify at least 20 animal species from live video on towers.

name: Anavaran Deforestation Alert System
summary: Satellite and machine learning system that the Forest Survey of India used to send states deforestation alerts every 15 days from January 2024. Civilsdaily reports the alerts stopped and the portal has not been updated since November 2025.

name: Andaman Nicobar Environment Team
summary: A field station in the Andaman Islands that hosts long-term monitoring of coral reefs, seagrass, sea turtles and reef fish.

name: ANIDERS Sundarbans pilot
summary: Solar-powered motion-sensing units with trap cameras, installed in the Raidighi Range to warn of tigers before they enter villages in the Sundarbans.

name: Applied Environmental Research Foundation
summary: Pune NGO conserving forests and mangroves in the northern Western Ghats and coastal Maharashtra through agreements with communities, with annual biodiversity surveys and forest monitoring by trained rangers.

name: Arcturus.Inc
summary: A company started by ecologist Abhijit Kumar that builds radio collars for wildlife, according to Mongabay India.

name: Artificial Intelligence for Monitoring in Wildlife Conservation
summary: Core Research Grant project led by Saket Anand whose software is to be integrated with the systems the Wildlife Institute of India uses for the national tiger census.

name: ATREE Ecoinformatics Lab
summary: Lab at the Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment that assembles and analyses ecological and spatial data from active and passive remote sensing, and aims to be an open hub of environmental geospatial data.

name: Auroville Forest Group
summary: A group that a September 2023 article reported had nurtured 1,250 acres of Auroville's forests and green spaces for more than four decades.

name: Bandipur AI elephant detection cameras
summary: AI camera systems to detect and track elephants at Bandipur, taken up by Adavi Alert Foundation with Advitiya Labs and Nikon India, reported by Deccan Chronicle.

name: Bat Conservation India Trust
summary: Research and conservation organisation on India's bats, which keeps a database of roost sites and monitors their populations.

name: Bhadra Tiger Conservation Foundation
summary: Foundation formed in 2011 to mobilise and manage revenues from eco-tourism in the tiger reserve.

name: Bhadra Tiger Reserve
summary: In 1974, the Government of Karnataka declared Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary with an area of 492.46 square kilometres.

name: Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics
summary: An Indian geo-informatics institute that signed a memorandum with the Forest Survey of India on geospatial and AI tools for forest fire management and wildlife conservation.

name: BHlab
summary: Bilal Habib's lab at the Wildlife Institute of India, a collaborator on MegaDetector that publishes SpSeg, a machine-learning tool for sorting camera-trap images by species.

name: Bhoonidhi
summary: ISRO's Earth observation data hub, through which registered users get satellite data including NISAR S-band products.

name: Bhuvan
summary: Geo-platform of the Indian Space Research Organisation.

name: Big Butterfly Month
summary: Annual citizen science butterfly count across India each September, launched in 2020, with 30-minute counts recorded through its own app and published on GBIF.

name: Biodiversity Collaborative
summary: Network of Indian institutions and individuals behind the preparatory phase of the National Mission on Biodiversity and Human Well-Being, which calls for integrating India's biodiversity data.

name: Biodiversity Conservation Society of the Great Himalayan National Park
summary: Autonomous society created by the state in 1999 to manage the Great Himalayan National Park through ecodevelopment with neighbouring communities, sharing responsibility with state and central governments.

name: Biodiversity of West Bengal
summary: Open online citizen science atlas of West Bengal's flora and fauna, launched in 2019, holding images, audio, video and species names.

name: Bird Count India
summary: Partnership of groups that collates birdwatchers' lists to build knowledge of bird distribution and populations in India.

name: BlueMAP-India
summary: Continuing compilation of India's marine habitats and species, with a map of marine protected areas notified by the government, published on the WCS-India site.

name: Bombay Natural History Society
summary: Indian conservation research society that holds records from over 2 million tagged birds and is transcribing its handwritten ringing sheets with AI.

name: Botanical Survey of India
summary: Indian government botanical survey under the environment ministry.

name: Brahmaputra flood plain human-elephant conflict ensemble
summary: Multi-scale ensemble machine learning framework for assessing human-elephant conflict in Assam, from a paper led by authors at the North East Regional Centre of the G. B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment.

name: Bruksha O Jeevara Bandhu Parishad
summary: Organisation reported in June 1992 to have mobilised community management of 16,000 ha of common property resources, such as forests and pastures, through 13 related organisations.

name: Care Earth Trust
summary: Trust that restores wetlands feeding the Pallikaranai marsh, including removing silt, strengthening the bund and clearing invasive flora at Narayanapuram.

name: CaTRAT
summary: Software that sorts camera-trap photographs by species with neural network models, used in India's national tiger assessment.

name: Centre for Ecological Sciences, Indian Institute of Science
summary: Ecology department at the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru, with authors on MOTHe, a method for tracking animals in field videos. Found by Europe PMC while OpenAlex was out of budget.

name: Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology
summary: Kochi centre under India's Ministry of Earth Sciences that runs the IndOBIS marine biodiversity node and acts as nodal agency for it.

name: Centre for Wildlife Studies
summary: Indian wildlife research and conservation centre that runs the Wild Incubator Tech Program and is building an AI acoustic early warning system for elephants with Rainforest Connection.

name: Chhattisgarh Elephant Tracking and Alert app
summary: App that takes reports from elephant trackers and patrol teams and uses AI to alert villagers within ten kilometres of a herd. It began as a pilot around Udanti Sitanadi tiger reserve.

name: Chilika Development Authority
summary: Odisha government agency created in 1992 to restore and develop the Chilika lagoon and conserve its ecology, which received the Ramsar Wetland Award in 2002.

name: ChutkiAI
summary: Farmers for Forests' multilingual WhatsApp chatbot, which shares updates with farmers, collects feedback and supports enrolment.

name: Climitra Carbon
summary: Indian company in the first Google DeepMind Accelerator for Asia-Pacific, which Google describes as using Geo-AI to verify the removal of invasive species and turn them into biochar.

name: Coastal Conservation Foundation
summary: A marine research and conservation nonprofit based in Mumbai, which runs Marine Life of Mumbai.

name: CommonsTech Foundation for Participatory Technologies
summary: Host organisation of CoRE Stack, a digital public good for natural resource management in rural India.

name: Composite Landscape Assessment & Restoration Tool
summary: GIS-based Android tool in the India Observatory suite for planning region-specific soil and water conservation measures.

name: Coral Reef in situ Observation Network
