summary: Long-term monitoring of coral reef health, calcification and ocean acidification, using data buoys and automatic weather stations at Indian reef sites.

name: Corbett Tiger Reserve AI wildlife alert trial
summary: Trial of connected camera traps at two sites in Corbett Tiger Reserve, whose images go to a server where AI identifies wildlife and raises an alert.

name: CoRE Stack
summary: Open-source digital public good for climate adaptation and natural resource management in rural India, with land-use, hydrology and vegetation layers built from satellite data and machine learning.

name: CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology
summary: CSIR research centre in Hyderabad whose LaCONES laboratory developed a method for assessing total biodiversity from environmental DNA.

name: CSIR-National Institute of Oceanography
summary: Oceanography institute whose scientists matched fish sounds off Goa with AI algorithms, using passive acoustic recordings.

name: Dakshin Foundation
summary: Indian not-for-profit whose Marine Flagships programme has tracked India's sea turtles for 16 years with the Indian Institute of Science and state forest departments.

name: Dalamariang
summary: Association founded in the winter of 1997–98 to coordinate the Thaiang project, which reforested a former sacred grove.

name: Darukaa Earth
summary: Mumbai company offering digital monitoring and credit simulation for carbon and biodiversity projects, with AI, drones and machine learning for wildlife detection and forest monitoring.

name: DeCaTron
summary: An AI tool launched by Telangana's emerging technologies wing that processes forest camera-trap images and identifies animal movements, reported by the Times of India.

name: DeepDATA
summary: A mobile platform of verified deep sea species records, developed under a Deep Ocean Mission vertical on automated identification of marine species with neural networks.

name: Delhi Ridge Management Board
summary: Board constituted by gazette notification of 10 June 2026 as the apex authority for protecting, restoring and regulating activities within the Delhi Ridge and the Morphological Ridge.

name: Department of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Arunachal Pradesh
summary: State government department that describes itself as existing for more than 50 years and as engaged in preservation and conservation.

name: Development of National Framework for Electronic People's Biodiversity Registers in India
summary: Active project, run by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit and funded by the International Climate Initiative, supporting a national electronic People's Biodiversity Register framework, then implementation in two states.

name: DigiNetra
summary: AI surveillance system with cameras and IoT sensors that monitors animal movements and detects poachers. The only source is its maker's startup listing; no deployment was confirmed.

name: Digitisation of Bird Ringing Data
summary: Bombay Natural History Society project with a Wild Incubator grant to transcribe over 40,000 handwritten bird ringing sheets with AI into a validated migration database.

name: Dorbar Shnong Mawpen Community Reserve management committee
summary: Management committee for a community reserve recognised in 2024, to be led by a chairperson and seven members, with the Divisional Forest Officer as Member Secretary.

name: Dudhwa Tiger Reserve
summary: Tiger reserve whose field director told PTI it combines thermal drones, AI-enabled cameras and M-STrIPES with patrolling, and uses M-STrIPES.

name: Earth Pulse
summary: A network of hyperlocal environmental observatories starting at Baner Hill, Pune, which records air quality, weather, bird sound and plants as open data, using BirdNET for acoustic detections.

name: Earth Systems Science Organisation
summary: Indian agency listed as a member of the Committee on Earth Observation Satellites since 2012.

name: Earthwise
summary: A Bengaluru company that uses drones for land and forest monitoring, with wildlife and forestry among its focus areas.

name: Ecological Forest Records Entry System
summary: Web portal for the Himachal Pradesh Forest Department, launched in beta on 30 July 2024, that records forest compartment data and tracks forestry operations and conservation work.

name: Endemic Plants of the Western Ghats
summary: Mobile app from the Naoroji Godrej Centre for Plant Research on endemic plants of the Western Ghats, for iOS and Android.

name: eNetra
summary: Sells a forest monitoring system that uses satellite data and machine learning to detect deforestation and land cover change, and says it is deployed with state forest departments.

name: Environmentalist Foundation of India
summary: Non-profit that mobilises thousands of volunteers for lake and pond restoration across the country, with work spanning 460+ water bodies by 2025.

name: EyeROV
summary: Kochi marine robotics startup founded in 2017. NITI Aayog reports that its AI underwater robots support coral reef surveys in the Andaman and Lakshadweep islands.

name: Farmers for Forests
summary: Pune social enterprise that helps smallholders move to agroforestry and developed the TreeLens drone tree detection model.

name: Faunterra
summary: Describes itself as a wildlife and conservation company working on ecological education, biodiversity intelligence, marine conservation and technology systems.

name: Forest AI Grand Challenge
summary: A challenge launched by the Telangana Artificial Intelligence Mission with Capgemini for AI in wildlife conservation, reported by Telangana Today.

name: Forest Cover Change Alert System
summary: Satellite surveillance system in Karnataka that detects forest cover change and unauthorised land use and alerts officials. Deccan Herald reports AI and satellite imagery behind it.

name: Forest Forward
summary: Work reported by BMZ Digital.Global that uses AI and geospatial insights from Vertify.earth to support forest planning in Goa.

name: Forest Stack proof of concept, Rajasthan
summary: A proof of concept by JICA DXLab and the Rajasthan Forest Department to develop a digital forest health monitoring system.

name: Forest Survey of India
summary: Indian government body under the environment ministry that maps forest cover and publishes the India State of Forest Report. It ran the Anavaran deforestation alerts.

name: Forest Survey of India forest fire alert system
summary: Near real-time forest fire alerts issued by the Forest Survey of India from hotspot data processed by the National Remote Sensing Centre, currently based on six satellite passes a day.

name: Foundation for Ecological Security
summary: Indian foundation that leads India Observatory, a data platform on social, economic and ecological parameters.

name: French Institute of Pondicherry
summary: Research institution under France's foreign ministry and CNRS, in the core group of the India Biodiversity Portal, which publishes its herbarium on GBIF. Its site refused the fetcher.

name: G. B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment
summary: Institute whose North East Regional Centre authors published an ensemble machine learning framework for human-elephant conflict in Assam. Found by Europe PMC while OpenAlex was out of budget.

name: Gadoli and Manda Khal Wildlife Conservation Trust
summary: Trust created to manage several hundred acres of family-owned forestland in the Himalayan foothills, focused on conservation and scientific research.

name: Gajraj elephant detection system
summary: Fibre optic and AI sensor system that detects elephants along 400 km of track and 30 corridors on Indian Railways' East Coast network, under a contract won by Sensonic.

name: Garudalytics
summary: A Hyderabad AI company that took part in the Forest AI Grand Challenge, according to Telangana Today.

name: GBIF India
summary: India's entry in the GBIF registry, listed with observer status and the Wildlife Institute of India's Dehradun address.

name: GEF project 11784 on implementing India's National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan
summary: Global Biodiversity Framework Fund project to improve biodiversity management, monitoring and financing under India's national biodiversity plan, approved for implementation on 3 September 2026.

name: Ghora Aabhe
summary: Group of village elders and women's self-help groups from villages around Pakke, reported in December 2010 to have adopted stringent norms and imposed penalties on offenders.

name: Gir railway AI intrusion detection system
summary: AI intrusion detection system for monitoring animal movement near railway lines in the Gir forest, reported in a reply to a parliamentary question.

name: Global Tiger Forum
summary: A forum that promotes technology for tiger conservation and protection across tiger range countries.

name: Gubbi Labs Research Foundation
summary: Not-for-profit research collective in Karnataka working on ecosystems and cities, with expertise in geospatial science. Its Project Ashoka sets up long-term ecological monitoring stations with citizen science.

name: Gudalur AI camera network
summary: Network of 44 solar-powered AI cameras across six zones of the Gudalur Forest Division in Tamil Nadu, with a control centre at the Nadukani Gene Pool Garden.

name: Gujarat Forest Department
summary: State forest department that uses SIMBA, AI photo-identification software for Asiatic lions, and led a lion census with AI across 11 districts.

name: Haldwani Forest Acoustic Surveillance System
summary: An AI acoustic system demonstrated by the Haldwani Forest Division in Uttarakhand to detect illegal logging, poaching and human intrusion, reported by The New Indian Express.

name: Haldwani Forest Division
summary: A forest division in Uttarakhand that demonstrated an AI forest acoustic surveillance system in 2026.

name: Haldwani forest division AI acoustic bird monitoring
summary: Haldwani forest division deploys wildlife acoustic recorders in forest areas and analyses the bird calls with machine learning and deep learning.

name: Haritarium
summary: Digitised plant taxonomic database from the Naoroji Godrej Centre for Plant Research, documenting more than 80 endemic and threatened plant species.

name: Haryana Forest Department
summary: State forest department that says Haryana hosts two national parks, eight wildlife sanctuaries, two conservation reserves and eight community reserves.

name: HAWK
summary: Digital incident reporting and surveillance app for wildlife crime, used by forest departments in Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

name: HCLFoundation
summary: Runs the HCLTech Grant, whose environment category became biodiversity from the 2026 financial year.

name: Hima Mawphlang
summary: Traditional authority under which the Lyngdoh clan manages the central, most sacred section of the Mawphlang sacred grove, nearly forty hectares.

name: Himachal Pradesh Forest Department
summary: State forest department whose Wildlife Wing and the Nature Conservation Foundation prepared a Spiti management plan, and whose snow leopard project, accepted from 2010-11, aimed at India's first comprehensive radio-collaring.

name: Himalayan Nature and Adventure Foundation
summary: Volunteer conservation organisation in Siliguri, West Bengal. Its GBIF record says it has coordinated the Asian Waterfowl Count across twelve wetlands for over three decades. Its own site refused the fetcher with a bot challenge.

name: Hosur AI elephant early warning system
summary: AI-triggered early warning system in the Hosur Forest Division that shows alerts on elephant movement on screens along the Chennai-Bengaluru highway.

name: ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute
summary: Marine fisheries research institute in Kochi. Its MARLIN@CMFRI app gathers citizen photographs of marine fish to feed an AI identification system.

name: IIT Indore wetland monitoring tool
summary: Digital tool from IIT Indore that uses satellite images and cloud computing to follow wetland water quality indicators in near real time.

name: India Biodiversity Portal
summary: Open portal that aggregates biodiversity data for India, with species pages, citizen observations, maps and documents. Its own site refuses automated reading, so this comes from Strand Life Sciences.

name: India Ecoacoustics Network
summary: Community of about 400 academics, practitioners, officials and naturalists working to build a centralised bioacoustics database for India.

name: India Observatory
summary: Data platform with datasets on social, economic and ecological parameters for any state, district or block in India.

name: India open-access ecoacoustic biodiversity dataset
summary: Crowdsourced open-access dataset reported at 518 species and 5,815 minutes of recordings from 25 states and union territories. Only secondary reports were found; no repository or DOI.

name: India Roadkill Monitoring Project
summary: Citizen science platform and mobile app that maps wildlife killed on India's roads and railways, with an open dataset on GBIF.

name: India Sand Watch
summary: Open platform crowd-sourcing information on sand mining in Indian rivers, built by Veditum with Rainmatter Foundation's support.

name: India State of Forest Report
summary: Biennial report of the Forest Survey of India on forest cover in India and how it changes.

name: Indian Biodiversity Information System
summary: Group of free, searchable citizen-science portals on Indian birds, mammals and flora, an initiative of the Foundation for Ecological Security.

name: Indian bird species visual-acoustic fusion classifier
summary: Method that combines images and sound to classify Indian bird species, from a paper by authors at Vellore Institute of Technology.

name: Indian Institute of Science
summary: Research institute that runs the QUEST Lab, in Bangalore's Department of Computational and Data Sciences, which applies agent-based modelling and machine learning to conservation and lists an elephant habitat random forest analysis.

name: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Tirupati
summary: Public science institute with an ecology and evolution programme. Its groups work on bird acoustics, including detection algorithms for owl calls, and curate the Squirrels of South Asia Database.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
summary: Institute whose Centre for Atmospheric Sciences authors presented a machine learning fire danger framework for Indian forests.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Indore
summary: Institute whose researchers developed a satellite tool to monitor wetland health.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur
summary: Indian technology institute listed among the partners of the AI and Biodiversity Change Global Center.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Madras
summary: Institute whose Department of Engineering Design published deep learning for real-time biodiversity analysis on mobile robots. Found by Europe PMC while OpenAlex was out of budget.

name: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services
summary: Indian ocean information centre whose coral reef service lists reef monitoring and early warning on coral bleaching among its objectives.

name: Indian Railways AI-enabled Intrusion Detection System
summary: An AI system that uses distributed acoustic sensors along railway lines to detect elephants and alert loco pilots, station masters and control rooms.

name: Indian Space Research Organisation
summary: India's space agency. Its Bhuvan portal and National Remote Sensing Centre supply satellite data on land cover and forests.

name: Indian Virtual Herbarium
summary: Database of digitised herbarium specimens with label data, searchable by barcode, family, genus, species, collector and place, described on the Botanical Survey of India's site.

name: IndiaSAT
summary: An open pixel-level land cover dataset for India, for training classifiers on Landsat 7, Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 imagery.

name: Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology, Delhi
summary: University in Delhi whose computer vision group built CaTRAT with the Wildlife Institute of India and works on AI monitoring for the national tiger census.

name: Integrated Forest Management Toolkit
summary: Forest management planning tool in the India Observatory suite, for officers in state forest departments preparing working plans.

name: International Big Cat Alliance
summary: An alliance that plans a series of knowledge products on conservation technologies with the Wildlife Institute of India.

name: Internet of Birds
summary: Platform built by Accenture Labs in Bangalore for the Bombay Natural History Society that identifies Indian bird species from photographs with machine learning and computer vision.

name: IORA Ecological Trust
summary: Trust that a November 2026 announcement says will implement a three-year project, with the Karnataka Forest Department, aiming to restore around 600 hectares of native forest in Nandi Hills.

name: Jabarkhet Nature Reserve
summary: Private forest reserve of 100 acres whose owners developed it as a company rather than a charity.

name: Jardhar Van Suraksha Samiti
summary: Village forest protection committee described in a July 2008 report as having its own enforcement mechanism, within a community conserved area of about 650 hectares of forest.

name: Jeevitnadi Living River Foundation
summary: Section 8 company in Pune working on river revival through citizen participation, which maps biodiversity on its adopted river stretches and publishes the surveys on GBIF.

name: Ka Lum Thangbru Khloo Kynrien Community Reserve management committee
summary: Management committee for a community reserve recognised in 2024, to be headed by a chairperson with four members and the Divisional Forest Officer as Member Secretary.

name: Kalasalingam Academy of Research and Education
summary: University named by OpenAlex as the affiliation of K. Madhav Varma, first author of a 2026 paper on vision-based elephant behaviour and posture recognition.

name: Kali Tiger Reserve
summary: Tiger reserve that says it comprises Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary (475.018 sq km) and Anshi National Park (339.866 sq km).

name: Kanchendzonga Conservation Committee
summary: Committee registered and recognised by the Government of Sikkim on 19 February 1997, with a participatory monitoring programme for the national park trekking trail, as described in October 2014.

name: Kapikaat
summary: Solar-powered bioacoustic system built by Katidhan that switches on when a sensor detects a monkey, is available only for pilots and tests, and was tested in several Indian states.

name: Karnataka Forest Department
summary: State forest department that uses AI and satellite imagery against encroachment, and surveyed leopards by camera trap with the Nature Conservation Foundation.

name: Karnataka leopard camera-trap study
summary: Six-year camera-trap study of leopards across Karnataka by the Nature Conservation Foundation and the state forest department, which used machine learning to identify 363 individuals from 1.5 million images.

name: Karnataka wildlife Command and Control Centres
summary: Centres that use AI cameras and thermal drones to map wildlife movement and alert villages when animals are near.

name: Kashmir Himalaya above-ground forest biomass dataset
summary: Multi-temporal forest inventory and above-ground biomass record for the Kashmir Himalaya, made from field observations, remote sensing and machine learning, by authors in the University of Kashmir's Department of Geoinformatics.

name: Katidhan
summary: Indian maker of the Parabraksh solar animal deterrent light and the Kapikaat monkey-repelling sound system, presenting its products as managing human-wildlife conflict and listing WWF as a client.

name: Kawnpui-I Village Council
summary: Village council that owns 620 hectares of forest at Zotlang Ngaw and, with the Kawnpui Young Mizo Association, put forward Mizoram's first community reserve.

name: Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve
summary: Park and tiger reserve that runs Kaziranga drone surveillance; the Assam Tribune reported its 2024 report counted 148 adult tigers using camera traps, and a 2025 director account of daily technology use.

name: Kaziranga National Park drone surveillance
summary: Drones used since 2017 at Kaziranga National Park in Assam to protect rhinos, catch poachers and track animals during floods.

name: Kerala AI elephant surveillance pilot
summary: Pilot costing 5 crore rupees with cameras at forest edges that detect elephants and send alerts over LoRaWAN, part of Kerala's Mission Real-Time Monitoring.

name: Kerala Biodiversity Monitoring Network
summary: Community collective in Kerala for biodiversity monitoring and citizen science, which holds moth monitoring events for National Moth Week.

name: Kerala Dinesh
summary: A worker-owned cooperative in Kerala that launched the Wild Watch AI surveillance system.

name: Kerala elephant intrusion alert pilot
summary: A pilot of AI cameras and LoRaWAN alerts for elephant movement, by the Kerala forest department with Tata Motors, reported by The New Indian Express.

name: Kerala Forest Department
summary: State forest department piloting AI cameras that detect elephants at forest boundaries, with two Tata companies.

name: Khonoma Village Council
summary: Nagaland village council whose authority under the Nagaland Village Council Act to devise forest resource management allowed the Khonoma sanctuary to be declared.

name: Koola Wild Foundation
summary: Not-for-profit wildlife conservation foundation in Amravati, Maharashtra, which publishes the India Roadkill Monitoring Project dataset on GBIF.

name: KSCSTE Malabar Botanical Garden and Institute for Plant Sciences
summary: A botanic garden and plant science institute in Kozhikode. A researcher there developed the NeophyteID invasive plant tool.

name: Laboratory for the Conservation of Endangered Species
summary: CCMB laboratory in Hyderabad that developed a lysis and PCR-free method for reading environmental DNA, tested in Chilika Lagoon.

name: Leopard Tech Labs
summary: Kerala company founded by Allen Shaji and Sobin Mathew that built HAWK, software for forest departments to record wildlife crime.

name: Loktak Development Authority
summary: Authority constituted by the Government of Manipur in 1986 for the overall improvement and management of Loktak Lake.

name: Long-Term Ecological Observatories
summary: Environment ministry programme, with several partner institutions, on climate change impacts on Indian ecosystems, with work planned at six index landscapes and a planned Andaman marine monitoring theme.

name: Luzaphuhu Village Students' Union
summary: A village students' union that, in 1983, resolved to conserve a 500 ha patch of forest above the village as a watershed.

name: M-STrIPES
summary: Mobile phone application used in India's national tiger assessment to record field data and geotag photo evidence by GPS.

name: Machine learning based fire danger assessment framework for Indian forests
summary: Country-scale forest fire risk framework by Barik and Baidya Roy, presented at EGU 2024, using vegetation indices, topography and population data, and meant as a step towards an operational system for India.

name: Madhya Pradesh AI forest alert system
summary: Pilot in Madhya Pradesh that runs a custom model on satellite data in Google Earth Engine to flag forest change, with field feedback by phone used to retrain it.

name: Madhya Pradesh Forest Department
summary: State forest department piloting an AI forest alert system built on satellite images and field feedback.

name: Madukkarai AI elephant surveillance system
summary: Thermal cameras on twelve towers and an AI command centre along two railway lines in the Madukkarai forest range, Coimbatore, which alert railway staff to elephants near the track.

name: Maharao Pragmulji Nature Conservation Trust
summary: A trust formed in 2021 to ensure the long-term protection and preservation of Chadva Rakhal as an area of biodiversity.

name: Maharashtra Forest Department
summary: State forest department that runs AI early warning for big cats near Pench, with Nagpur Rural Police.

name: Maharashtra Remote Sensing Application Centre
summary: State-run space technology body, described by Mumbai Live, which reports it was tasked with a two-year satellite assessment of mangroves in seven coastal districts, with INR 4.36 crore planned.

name: Maharashtra Research and Vigilance for Enhanced Law Enforcement
summary: A Maharashtra government-owned body that builds AI tools for law enforcement. It signed an agreement with the state forest department for AI cameras and sirens near tiger reserves.

name: Manas Maozigendri Ecotourism Society
summary: A community-based conservation society established in December 2003, named as behind the efforts that revived Manas National Park.

name: Mangrove Cell, Maharashtra Forest Department
summary: A unit of the Maharashtra Forest Department that a July 2019 report called India's only unit specialising in mangrove protection, and whose head said it planted around 2 million seedlings in 2018.

name: Manipal Academy of Higher Education
summary: University named by OpenAlex as the affiliation of K. A. Yashaswini, first author of a 2025 paper on deep learning for animal sensing systems in habitat monitoring.

name: Mankulam AI wildlife monitoring
summary: AI surveillance cameras and an AI butterfly identification app used by the Kerala Forest Department in the Mankulam forest division.

name: Marine Life of Mumbai
summary: A citizen science community that documents Mumbai's coastal and intertidal biodiversity, with an open database on iNaturalist of over 14,000 observations.

name: Marine Mammal Research and Conservation Network of India
summary: Website and network with an online database of marine mammal sightings, strandings and historical records from Indian waters.

name: MARLIN@CMFRI
summary: Mobile app for the public to upload photographs of marine fish. The images are to feed an AI system that identifies species and estimates landings.

name: Mediomix
summary: A Bangalore genomics company whose JeevAadhar platform uses environmental DNA to report on soil health, biodiversity and water quality.

name: Mendha Lekha Gram Sabha
summary: In September 2009, the assembly reportedly awaited Forest Rights Act management rights over 1,832 hectares; Devaji Tofa said it already managed village forest resources.

name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (India)
summary: India's environment ministry. It prepared the country's seventh national report to the Convention on Biological Diversity, and bodies such as the Wildlife Institute of India sit under it.

name: MOTHe
summary: Method for detecting and tracking animals in videos taken in natural settings, from a paper whose lead authors are at the Centre for Ecological Sciences, Indian Institute of Science.

name: Mynzo Carbon
summary: A company that uses AI, satellite data and field data for forest, carbon and biodiversity monitoring.

name: Nagarahole Tiger Conservation Foundation
summary: A foundation listed on the reserve's site, which cites section 38-X, under which the state establishes such a foundation to support management of a tiger reserve.

name: Nagarahole Tiger Reserve
summary: A tiger reserve of 843.96 sq km (core 643.392, buffer 200.57) spanning Mysuru and Kodagu districts.

name: Nagpur and Pench AI early warning system
summary: AI early warning system tracking big cats at three sites near Pench Tiger Reserve in Nagpur's rural belt, planned to reach 40 sites, run by the forest department and Nagpur Rural Police.

name: Naoroji Godrej Centre for Plant Research
summary: Not-for-profit plant research centre in Maharashtra working on Western Ghats plants, with the Haritarium digital plant database and a mobile app on endemic plants.

name: National Biodiversity Authority
summary: Statutory body set up in 2003 to implement India's Biological Diversity Act. It gave technical coordination for the seventh national report to the Convention on Biological Diversity.

name: National Centre for Biological Sciences
summary: Indian research centre running a master's in wildlife biology, a partner in State of India's Birds and Bird Count India.

name: National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management
summary: A national centre under India's environment ministry, whose outputs include a mangrove community zonation atlas of India.

name: National Information System for Climate and Environment Studies
summary: Multi-institution programme and gateway for Earth and climate data products, with ISRO centres and other national bodies taking part; its site is hosted by NRSC.

name: National Remote Sensing Centre
summary: Centre under India's Department of Space. Its forestry and ecology work maps forest types, canopy density and land cover for biosphere reserves and forest working plans.

name: National Tiger Conservation Authority
summary: India's statutory tiger authority under the Wildlife (Protection) Act. Its national tiger assessment sorts camera-trap photographs by species with AI.

name: Nature Conservation Foundation
summary: Indian public charitable trust for wildlife research and conservation. It runs SeasonWatch and surveyed leopards with the Karnataka Forest Department, using machine learning on camera-trap images.

name: Nature Environment and Wildlife Society
summary: An organisation that, with Livelihoods and local communities, restored 5,011 hectares of Sundarbans mangroves from 2011, planting more than 16 million mangroves.

name: Nature Mates-Nature Club
summary: Kolkata conservation society that runs biodiversity surveys in West Bengal and elsewhere, ran a lesser cat survey with camera traps in the Sundarbans, and publishes the national Monitor Lizard Count on GBIF.

name: NatureDots
summary: Company that says it engineered an aquatic foundation model and builds digital twins from it, reporting deployment across 625,000 hectares and coverage in at least seven countries.

name: Nawegaon Nagzira Tiger Reserve Conservation Foundation
summary: A foundation whose trust deed lets it receive and maintain government grants for managing Nawegaon-Nagzira Tiger Reserve, declared in 2013 with an area of 653.67 sq km.

name: NeophyteID
summary: A photo identification tool for invasive plants across Kerala and the Western Ghats, using a YOLOv11 model, with interfaces in several Indian languages.

name: NRSC land use and land cover mapping
summary: National Remote Sensing Centre mapping of land use and land cover for India, annual at 1:250,000 and every five years at 1:50,000.

name: Odisha Forest Department
summary: State forest department that buys and installs the AI cameras at Similipal Tiger Reserve.

name: Odraix
summary: Builds multi-sensor edge AI nodes that combine acoustic, gas and night-vision signals for forest monitoring.

name: Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park
summary: Zoo whose genetic biobank, established in June 2024, worked with CCMB and held 21 DNA samples from nine species by December 2024, according to Indian Masterminds.

name: Palamau Tiger Reserve
summary: A tiger reserve of 1,129.93 square kilometres under the administrative control of the Chief Conservator of Forest and Field Director, Palamau Tiger Reserve.

name: Palghar AI leopard surveillance
summary: AI surveillance machines supplied to the forest department for Mokhada and Dahanu talukas, Palghar district, to track leopards and alert residents; the first camera is installed.

name: Parabraksh
summary: Solar-powered animal deterrent light, built by Katidhan, that switches on automatically at night to reduce animal attacks on cattle and crops, with 50 or more reported installations across India.

name: Pardus Wild-tech
summary: Indian startup that makes trail cameras and sensors for Indian conditions and is expanding into GPS trackers and thermal cameras.

name: Pathanga
summary: A phone app that identifies Indian butterflies from photographs by AI and logs sightings reviewed by experts.

name: Pathanga Suchaka
summary: Online portal launched in 2019 that uses AI to identify about 800 butterfly and 500 moth species in India from uploaded photographs.

name: Pitchandikulam Forest
summary: An environmental organisation and community in the green belt of Auroville, whose team works to restore the indigenous forest.

name: Project Anāhitā
summary: Farmers for Forests' open-source AI suite, made up of TreeLens, an impact dashboard and a forest protection dashboard.

name: Project Ashoka
summary: Gubbi Labs' long-term ecological research initiative estimating biodiversity outside protected areas on the Deccan Plateau, through monitoring stations with a citizen science interface.

name: Puttenahalli Neighbourhood Lake Improvement Trust
summary: A trust co-founded in 2010 that, after municipal rejuvenation of the lake, co-managed it, restoring wetlands, planting trees and protecting habitat.

name: QUEST Lab, Indian Institute of Science
summary: A lab at the Indian Institute of Science that applies agent-based modelling and machine learning to conservation problems, including Asian elephant crop-raiding.

name: Rainmatter Foundation
summary: Indian non-profit founded in 2019 that says it has committed $200 million to organisations working on climate and the environment, including forests, water and ecology.

name: Rajasthan Forest Department
summary: The forest agency of Rajasthan, partner with JICA DXLab on a digital forest health monitoring proof of concept.

name: Rajasthan forest health monitoring proof of concept
summary: Proof of concept to develop a forest health monitoring system for Rajasthan, announced by SatSure with the Rajasthan Forest Department, JICA DXLab and Boston Consulting Group.

name: Real-time biodiversity analysis on mobile robotic platforms
summary: Deep learning method for biodiversity analysis on mobile robots, from a paper by authors in the Department of Engineering Design, Indian Institute of Technology Madras.

name: Remote Sensing and Machine Learning-Based Detection of Floating Offshore Plastic Debris in Coastal Goa
summary: WWF-India project with a Wild Incubator grant that uses Sentinel-2 images and machine learning to map floating plastic off Goa.

name: Research and Action in Natural Wealth Administration
summary: Small Pune NGO that documents plants and animals in western Maharashtra and has carried out ecological surveys and biodiversity assessments.

name: Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies
summary: Indian philanthropy with conservation and adaptation among its themes. Bird Count India acknowledges its support.

name: RootIQ Labs
summary: A New Delhi AI company that worked with forest officer Pushpendra Rana to develop WhereToPlant Bot, as reported by Mongabay India.

name: Rupa Rahul Bajaj Centre for Environment and Art
summary: Environmental education centre in Pune's Empress Botanical Garden that runs seasonal biodiversity surveys of the garden, with records uploaded to iNaturalist, and is a SeasonWatch partner.

name: Sahya Digital Conservation Foundation
summary: A non-profit that promotes open data, open-source software, open knowledge, biodiversity and citizen science.

name: SAI Sanctuary Trust
summary: Described in April 2017 as a registered not-for-profit trust associated with a Kodagu sanctuary reportedly grown from 55 acres bought in 1991 to 300 acres.

name: Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve
summary: A tiger reserve formed on 15 March 2013 when the whole 1,40,840 hectare Sathyamangalam Sanctuary was declared one, and which reports 54 anti-poaching camps.

name: Science and Engineering Research Board
summary: Indian government research funder listed as the funder of the AIM-Wildlife Conservation project.

name: Sciurid Lab
summary: Research group in the Biology Department at IISER Tirupati studying squirrels and other small mammals, which builds and curates the Squirrels of South Asia Database.

name: SeasonWatch
summary: Citizen science project across India that follows the leaf, flower and fruit timing of more than 130 common trees.

name: Sendenyu Village Council
summary: A village council that resolved to set aside an area of about 1,000 hectares.

name: Sieora
summary: Company, with an office in Perungudi, Chennai, whose monitoring system uses AI on camera-trap, thermal and drone feeds to detect animals in real time and alert forest officers, farmers or loco pilots.

name: Sigur Nature Trust
summary: A trust with a private reserve in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve that has protected 30 acres of land for the past 50 years.

name: Sikkim Forest and Environment Department
summary: A government department mandated to control and manage forests, environment and wildlife, including creating and managing national parks and wildlife sanctuaries.

name: SIMBA
summary: AI photo-identification software for Asiatic lions, housed in the Gir Hi-Tech Monitoring Unit at Sasan-Gir.

name: Similipal AI camera surveillance
summary: AI camera surveillance in Similipal Tiger Reserve in Odisha, which the state decided to extend to Satkosia and Debrigarh sanctuaries, reported by The New Indian Express.

name: Similipal Tiger Reserve AI surveillance
summary: About 900 AI cameras across Similipal Tiger Reserve in Odisha, used against poaching and to detect forest fires, with more than 500 more being installed.

name: Siruthuli
summary: An organisation reported in August 2025 as chaired by Vanitha Mohan and as having spent two decades restoring the Noyyal river's chain of tanks and lakes.

name: Sky N Land Insights
summary: A Mumbai-based company that uses satellite data and AI to track ecosystem health, including forest change and carbon stocks.

name: Snow Leopard Population Assessment in India
summary: A national snow leopard survey coordinated by the Wildlife Institute of India, with camera traps at 1,971 locations, reported by the Press Information Bureau.

name: Space Applications Centre
summary: Centre in Ahmedabad that runs the VEDAS website, which lists the National Wetland Inventory and Assessment Atlas, and is run by the Indian Space Research Organisation.

name: SpSeg (Species Segregator)
summary: Machine-learning tool built by BHLab on MegaDetector that sorts camera-trap images into 36 species or classes in Maharashtra's Eastern Vidarbha Landscape, trained for the Central Indian landscape.

name: Squirrels of South Asia Database
summary: Occurrence records for all 34 squirrel species of South Asia from museums, literature, field records, citizen science and social media, covering 1766 to 2022.

name: SRM Institute of Science and Technology
summary: University named by OpenAlex as the affiliation of Sakthi A, first author of a 2026 paper on elephant detection in thermal imagery using YOLOv8n.

name: Strand Life Sciences
summary: Company whose biodiversity informatics team has built open-source platforms since 2008, including the India Biodiversity Portal.

name: Strofes Technologies
summary: Kottayam company that makes DigiNetra, an AI surveillance system for forest protection and wildlife conservation, according to its Kerala Startup Mission listing.

name: Study of Ganges River Dolphins and Gharials Using Drones
summary: Drone work by India Flying Labs on the banks of the Gandak in Bihar, documenting habitats for Gangetic river dolphins and gharials and training the Bihar Forest Department.

name: Sundarban Biosphere Reserve
summary: A reserve constituted by the Government of India in 1989 and recognised by UNESCO's Man and Biosphere Programme in November 2001, named under the West Bengal Directorate of Forest.

name: Survey of India
summary: India's national survey and mapping organisation under the Department of Science and Technology, according to the re3data registry. Its own site refuses automated reading.

name: Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve AI camera alerts
summary: AI-enabled cameras at villages around Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra, with a published list of villages, cameras and alerts.

name: Tadoba-Andhari AI tiger alert system
summary: AI camera system at Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra that alerts people in nearby villages by phone when tigers move close.

name: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve
summary: Tiger reserve in Chandrapur, Maharashtra, that installed an AI camera system to warn villagers of tiger movement.

name: Tamil Nadu Forest Department
summary: State forest department that runs an AI camera system to keep elephants off the railway lines at Madukkarai in Coimbatore.

name: Tata Chemicals
summary: Company that, in an April 2010 release, described the Whale Shark Conservation Project as a joint venture with Gujarat Forest Department and Wildlife Trust of India, and said it supported the research.

name: Tata Power
summary: Company whose 2025-26 annual report says its Gaja Sanrakshana Project deployed 15 early warning systems and 75 proximity sensors in Odisha, and sets a 2030 no net biodiversity loss target.

name: Tech for Conservation
summary: WWF-India programme using GIS, remote sensing, modelling and digital platforms for conservation analysis, including fire hotspots, floating plastic detection and support for radio-collaring.

name: Technology for Wildlife Conservation (WildTech)
summary: Wildlife Conservation Trust project that develops low-cost, open-source tools for conservation, including boat tracking, railway alerts and hydrology sensors.

name: Technology for Wildlife Foundation
summary: Goa not-for-profit that collected conservation data from satellites, fieldwork and its own aerial and underwater robots. Its site says it has paused operations and now serves as an archive.

name: Telangana AI Mission
summary: State AI mission that invited startups to the Telangana Forest AI Grand Challenge.

name: Telangana Forest AI Grand Challenge
summary: Call to Indian startups for AI solutions to monitor wildlife in Telangana's forests, with a pilot and up to INR 20 lakh for the winner.

name: Telangana Forest Department
summary: State forest department that joined the Telangana Forest AI Grand Challenge and approved AI surveillance at Amrabad Tiger Reserve.

name: Terai Elephant Reserve AI early warning system
summary: AI cameras in the Terai Elephant Reserve that track elephant movement and notify forest officials and villagers, run by WWF-India with support from NTT DATA.

name: The Corbett Foundation
summary: Indian charitable trust working on wildlife and communities around tiger reserves and other sites. It runs waterbird monitoring and nesting surveys of Indian vultures, and assists a satellite telemetry study of birds in Gujarat.

name: The Habitats Trust
summary: Indian trust that makes grants for lesser-known species and habitats, and a partner in State of India's Birds.

name: The Shola Trust
summary: Non-profit in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, based in Gudalur, that monitors forest with drones and bioacoustics and has built an app for recording elephant sightings.

name: TraceX Technologies
summary: Bengaluru agrifood and climate tech startup with an agentic AI tool that helps Indian exporters comply with the EU Deforestation Regulation.

name: TreeLens
summary: Open tree detection model built on Detectron2 that maps tree crowns in aerial orthomosaics and estimates crown width, height and biomass.

name: TRST01
summary: Supply chain traceability company whose platform maps farms by drone and runs deforestation analysis for Indian and other exporters of coffee, rubber and soy under the EU Deforestation Regulation.

name: University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru
summary: University whose School of Ecology and Conservation developed the Pathanga Suchaka butterfly and moth identifier.

name: University of Kashmir
summary: University whose Department of Geoinformatics published an above-ground biomass dataset for the Kashmir Himalaya. Found by Europe PMC while OpenAlex was out of budget.

name: Uttarakhand Forest Department
summary: State forest department trialling AI alerts from camera traps at Corbett Tiger Reserve. Its Haldwani division uses AI on acoustic recorders to monitor birds.

name: Uttaranchal University
summary: University named by OpenAlex as the affiliation of Nimesh Kumar, first author of a 2025 paper on wildlife conservation using image recognition with AI.

name: VanNetra
summary: The Better India describes it as an AI platform launched by Telangana's government to sort camera-trap images from Amrabad and Kawal tiger reserves by species.

name: Varaha
summary: Company that generates carbon credits from nature, with a monitoring platform built on remote sensing and machine learning, across India, Bangladesh, Nepal and Kenya.

name: VEDAS
summary: An Earth observation data system of the Space Applications Centre of the Indian Space Research Organisation, with a page on space-based observation of Indian wetlands.

name: Veditum
summary: Kolkata not-for-profit on environmental and social justice that runs India Sand Watch, an open platform on sand mining.

name: Vellore Institute of Technology
summary: Institute whose authors published a visual and acoustic classifier for Indian birds. Found by Europe PMC while OpenAlex was out of budget.

name: Visual Analytics for Wildlife Monitoring
summary: A project at IIIT Delhi with the Wildlife Institute of India to identify species and individuals in camera-trap images.

name: Wayanad AI wildlife fencing
summary: AI-supported wildlife fencing tested at Chelakolly and to be extended over 10 km at Pulpally in Wayanad, a Rs 5.5 crore project.

name: WCT and Google Research India human-wildlife conflict models
summary: Project from 2020 by the Wildlife Conservation Trust and Google Research India that designed AI models to predict human-wildlife conflict in central India.

name: WCT and Google Research India human-wildlife conflict prediction
summary: AI models to predict human-wildlife interactions in Maharashtra, built in a collaboration between the Wildlife Conservation Trust and Google Research India's AI Lab.

name: WCT and Google Research India human-wildlife interaction models
summary: Collaboration between the Wildlife Conservation Trust and Google Research India's AI lab on AI models to predict human-wildlife interactions in Chandrapur district, Maharashtra. Described in a May 2021 article.

name: WCT Central India species recognition model
summary: Open-source camera-trap model that recognises 40 classes of wild animals in central India, built by the Wildlife Conservation Trust with Aadax Data Science on 1.1 million images.

name: West Bengal Forest Department
summary: State forest department in a JICA pilot of technology against human-elephant conflict.

name: West Bengal human-elephant conflict technology pilot
summary: Proof of concept by JICA and the West Bengal Forest Department that tests RESOLVE's technology against human-elephant conflict.

name: Wetlands International South Asia
summary: New Delhi organisation, established in 1996, that jointly coordinates the Asian Waterbird Census in India with the Bombay Natural History Society, and says the data is available to agencies and NGOs.

name: Wetlands of India Portal
summary: A knowledge repository on Indian wetlands, developed under an Indo-German project implemented with the environment ministry.

name: Whale Shark Conservation Project
summary: Joint venture of the Gujarat Forest Department, Tata Chemicals and the Wildlife Trust of India that studies whale shark population and migration, including by photo-identification against a global database.

name: WhereToPlant Bot
summary: A chatbot that predicts the survival probability of saplings at a given location, developed by forest officer Pushpendra Rana with RootIQ Labs, reported by Mongabay India.

name: Wild Incubator Tech Program
summary: Grants of Rs 20 lakh for one year to five Indian NGOs building wildlife technology such as IoT, AI, open data and remote sensing.

name: Wild Seve
summary: Centre for Wildlife Studies programme launched in 2015 that gives timely help to people affected by human-wildlife conflict around wildlife reserves.

name: Wild Watch
summary: An AI surveillance system from the Kerala Dinesh cooperative for human-wildlife conflict in Palakkad and Wayanad, reported by The New Indian Express.

name: Wildernest Nature Resort
summary: An October 2022 report described its 900-acre private sanctuary, Swapnagandha Valley, eight-acre resort and a newly created Mhadei Research Centre with over 100 acres of protected forest.

name: WildEye
summary: The CSR Journal describes a Mumbai startup using AI camera traps and sensors to monitor wildlife. No other source was found.

name: Wildlife Conservation Society - India
summary: Indian non-profit company working on wildlife conservation with governments and communities. It publishes BlueMAP-India, a resource on India's marine habitats and protected areas.

name: Wildlife Conservation Trust
summary: Indian conservation trust whose Conservation Behaviour team applies AI to conservation projects, including models with Google Research India to predict human-wildlife conflict.

name: Wildlife Information and Nature Guide Society
summary: Non-profit in Durgapur, West Bengal, that surveys local wildlife and powers the Biodiversity of West Bengal citizen science portal.

name: Wildlife Institute of India
summary: Autonomous institute of the environment ministry in Dehradun. GBIF lists its address as the contact for GBIF India, and it works with IIIT-Delhi on AI for the national tiger census.

name: Wildlife Protection Society of India
summary: Organisation that runs a Wildlife Crime Database of over 33,300 cases involving more than 400 species, using i2 software, and says national and international agencies rely on it.

name: Wildlife SOS
summary: An Indian wildlife rescue and conservation organisation that uses drones and camera traps to study elephants, leopards and sloth bears.

name: Wildlife Technology Laboratory
summary: Laboratory at the Wildlife Institute of India that works with camera traps, telemetry, acoustic recorders and drones, and develops machine learning models for species identification in camera-trap images.

name: Wildlife Trust of India
summary: Indian conservation NGO that worked with Leopard Tech Labs on the HAWK crime reporting app and runs an early warning pilot against tigers in the Sundarbans. Its own site refuses automated reading.

name: WildTales Foundation
summary: Not-for-profit foundation in New Delhi working on butterflies and biodiversity clusters, which publishes the Big Butterfly Month Counts 2021 on GBIF. Its website did not resolve on 31 October 2026.

name: WPSI Wildlife Crime Database
summary: A database of wildlife crime cases and criminals, with records of over 33,300 cases, published by WPSI.

name: WRI India
summary: Indian knowledge organisation working on food, land and water, energy and cities, which uses geospatial data and analytics, including on long-term ecological trends and landscape restoration.

name: Wular Conservation and Management Authority
summary: An authority constituted in September 2012 to conserve and manage Wular Lake, a Ramsar site, where a drone survey was underway in October 2025 to monitor the boundary.

name: WWF-India
summary: Indian conservation NGO that works by landscape, seascape and river basin. It runs an AI early warning system for elephants with NTT DATA and built a machine learning tool that maps floating plastic off Goa.

name: zetawave
summary: Maker of ROAR, an AI acoustic system for wildlife protection and biodiversity monitoring, which says it runs on a processor from CDAC, an Indian government research body.

name: Zoological Survey of India
summary: Indian government faunal survey under the environment ministry. Roundglass Sustain reports that it planned to use eDNA to study and monitor wildlife.

name: American University of Iraq, Sulaimani
summary: University named by BGCI as one of three partners in a 2021-2023 oak woodland conservation project, and reported by Rudaw in 2019 as housing the Kurdistan Botanical Foundation's herbarium in a basement.

name: Applied Remote Sensing and GIS Center, University of Zakho
summary: University of Zakho centre in Duhok that completed a project mapping vegetation coverage in the Kurdistan Region and, in May 2025, organised a session to coordinate a GIS mapping workshop.

name: Birds of Peramagroon
summary: An identification app covering the 133 bird species of Peramagroon Mountain, released as part of an Iraqi Darwin Initiative project for education, training and monitoring, and available for iOS devices.

name: Center for the Restoration of Iraqi Marshes and Wetlands
summary: Iraqi body that Nature Iraq names as part of the Ministry of Water Resources, whose Design and Study Department contracted the national wetland atlas.

name: Civil Engineering Department, University of Technology - Iraq
summary: Civil engineering department at the University of Technology, Iraq, listed by OpenAlex as lead affiliation on remote sensing and GIS studies of Al-Dalmage Marsh (2025) and Al-Hawizeh Marsh (2022).

name: Conservation of Persian leopards in West Asia
summary: Nature Iraq says it partners with Future4Leopards Foundation on Persian leopard conservation and monitoring across Iraq and Iran, with a systematic camera-trap baseline survey as an objective.

name: Conservation Planning of Goitered Gazelle (Gazella subgutturosa) in the Garmian Area of Kurdistan, Iraq: Collecting Data, Mapping Distribution, and IUCN Red List Assessment
summary: Closed Rufford-funded project, listed 9 November 2017, which aimed to create baseline data on goitered gazelle in Garmian, using spring and summer field surveys and a handheld GPS.

name: Department for Space and Communications (Iraq)
summary: Iraqi department through which, according to the Space Security Portal, the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research is responsible for the country's space objectives.

name: Department of Biology, College of Education, University of Sulaimani
summary: Biology department at the University of Sulaimani's College of Education, the sole affiliation on a 2025 MaxEnt distribution model of Phragmites australis in Iraq, per OpenAlex.

name: Department of Biology, College of Science, University of Sulaimani
summary: Biology department at the University of Sulaimani's College of Science, listed by OpenAlex as lead affiliation on a 2023 paper predicting the distribution of the Persian leopard.

name: Department of Forestry, College of Agricultural Engineering Sciences, Salahaddin University-Erbil
summary: A forestry department at Salahaddin University-Erbil, lead affiliation on a 2026 preprint forecasting the Enhanced Vegetation Index with deep learning and a 2024 paper mapping forest cover with RapidEye indices and terrain variables.

name: Department of Forestry, College of Agricultural Engineering Sciences, University of Duhok
summary: Forestry department at the University of Duhok, listed by OpenAlex as lead affiliation on a 2025 remote sensing assessment of forest degradation and environmental stress in Amedi District.

name: Department of Forestry, College of Agriculture and Forestry, University of Mosul
summary: Forestry department at the University of Mosul, listed by OpenAlex as lead affiliation on a 2023 paper determining canopy gaps in Atrush forest from remote sensing data.

name: Department of Geography, College of Art, Salahaddin University-Erbil
summary: Geography department at Salahaddin University-Erbil, listed by OpenAlex as lead affiliation on a 2025 paper on monitoring biodiversity in Erbil Governorate using remote sensing data.

name: Department of Spatial Planning, College of City and Regional Planning, University of Duhok
summary: A University of Duhok planning department listed among the lead author's affiliations on a 2024 paper that applies deep learning to estimate forest vegetation cover.

name: Directorate of Forests and Range in Duhok
summary: A forestry directorate under the Kurdistan Region's agriculture ministry, named as lead affiliation, with a University of Duhok department, on a 2024 paper on deep learning for estimating forest vegetation cover.

name: Forests and Desertification Control Department (Ministry of Agriculture, Iraq)
summary: According to Kalima on 19 June 2026, its director general said the department adopted a desertification assessment method using vegetation cover and water indices.

name: Hasar
summary: An NGO based in Erbil province which, according to 964media in January 2024, unveiled a tool measuring shade trees, mountain tree population change over seven years, and changes in water bodies.

name: Iraq Convention on Biological Diversity Clearing House Mechanism
summary: Iraq's Convention on Biological Diversity clearing-house website, built with the Bioland tool, which publishes national biodiversity targets to 2032 and hosts marsh management plans calling for a water quality monitoring database.

name: Iraq Darwin project (Peramagroon Mountain)
summary: Nature Iraq project funded by the Darwin Initiative, run from April 2012 to March 2015, that trained Iraqis in botany, ornithology and conservation and found five previously undescribed plant species.

name: Iraq LD Monitor
summary: Describes itself as Iraq’s national land degradation monitoring platform, combining satellite, field and GIS data, offering a 2000–2020 land cover product, with handover scheduled for early 2026.

name: Iraq Natural History Research Center and Museum
summary: University of Baghdad centre that held a field trip to Al-Dubouni District, Wasit Governorate, on 1 May 2026 to collect specimens and help establish a biodiversity database for Iraq.

name: Iraqi Green Climate Organization
summary: This Iraq-based environmental NGO focuses on climate change and biodiversity and reports finding a new blind cavefish population during a joint survey on 10 August 2026.

name: Iraqi Ministry of Environment
summary: Iraqi government ministry whose site covers natural preserves, an environmental information system page and CITES certificate requests, and reports handing an endangered Eurasian otter to Al-Zawraa Park.

name: Knowledge University
summary: A private university in Erbil, established in 2009, whose listed 2025 study modelled Duhok border forest dynamics for 2015 to 2024 using Sentinel-2 and machine learning, finding canopy cover fell from about 630 to 577 km2.

name: Kurdistan Biodiversity
summary: Platform built by the Kurdistan Foundation and run by Climate.KRD that documents Kurdistan Region wildlife in three languages, giving 844 animal and 1,408 plant species recorded, with public sightings reviewed before publication.

name: Kurdistan Botanical Foundation
summary: Reported by Rudaw in 2019 as a nonprofit founded in 2013 with some 60,000 herbarium samples, and described by BGCI as a 2021-2023 oak survey partner.

name: Kurdistan Foundation
summary: Reported by Kurdistan24 as founded by Areen Masrour Barzani and as launching a biodiversity project documenting 2,252 plant and animal species and 19 ecological hotspots.

name: Kurdistan Organization for Animal Rights Protection
summary: A volunteer non-profit animal welfare NGO in the Kurdistan Region, founded in 2009 and registered with the regional government in May 2013, which says it monitors local wildlife and habitats and reports on hunting and disease.

name: Kurdistan Region Environmental Board
summary: Kurdistan Region body that Kurdistan24 reports says 45 of Iraq's 82 identified protected areas lie in the region, and which partners with Nature Iraq.

name: Leopards Beyond Borders
summary: Described by Mongabay as a nonprofit founded by Hana Raza, and reported by Kurdistan Chronicle as established in 2022 with footage recording Iraq's first leopard prey caching.

name: Mapping and Estimating Vegetation Coverage in Iraqi Kurdistan Region
summary: Closed project run by the University of Zakho's remote sensing centre, started in 2015 and reported complete in December 2018, that aimed to map and estimate planted forest area across the Kurdistan Region.

name: Marine Data Bank (Marine Science Centre, University of Basrah)
summary: A data bank run by the University of Basrah's Marine Science Centre, described as Iraq's first for collecting, documenting and distributing marine environmental data, holding measurements of various environmental variables.

name: Marine Science Centre, University of Basrah
summary: University centre in Basrah that says it organised a field trip to the Al-Mashab Marshes on 6 October 2026 to monitor them and assess their biological and ecological status.

name: Ministry of Environment (Iraq)
summary: Iraqi ministry whose Deputy Minister is the national CBD focal point, and which is executing agency with the UNEP West Asia Office for GEF project 10672 in the Middle Euphrates.

name: National Atlas of Marshes and Wetlands of Iraq
summary: Nature Iraq says CRIMW’s Design and Study Department contracted SGI Studio Galli Ingegneria, with Nature Iraq subcontracting, to develop this closed wetland atlas to Ramsar Convention requirements.

name: Nature Iraq
summary: Founded in 2003 by Azzam Alwash and, according to OSME, published the Key Biodiversity Areas of Iraq in 2017 with the Ministry of Health and Environment.

name: Nature Iraq Key Biodiversity Areas Project
summary: Surveys in 2005–2012 collected biodiversity, water quality and soil data, with nine bird species added to Iraq’s list and 55 breeding bird species discovered or confirmed.

name: Recovering the Wild: Conservation of imperiled oak woodlands in Kurdistan, Iraq
summary: National Geographic Society-funded partnership from 2021 to 2023 of the Kurdistan Botanical Foundation, AUIS and BGCI that surveyed remnant oaks and built stocks of over 10,000 seedlings, planting about 1,200 in its last year.

name: Remote Sensing Unit, College of Science, University of Baghdad
summary: Remote sensing unit at the University of Baghdad's College of Science, established by ministerial order in 1999, linked to papers on Iraqi marshes, including Landsat soil-use and Al-Hammar Marsh studies.

name: Sustainable Land Management for Improved Livelihoods in Degraded Areas of Iraq
summary: GEF-funded project run by FAO with the Ministry of Environment, building national land degradation monitoring capacity, with 16 field monitoring packages handed over on 7 July 2026, as FAO reported.

name: University of Baghdad
summary: University with a Natural History Research and Museum Center, whose May 2026 field trip aimed to enrich its Iraqi specimen collection and establish a biodiversity database of Iraq.

name: University of Duhok
summary: Founded in 1992 in Duhok, in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region, this university has a botanical garden with a citizen-science network on wild plants.

name: University of Duhok Botanical Garden
summary: Botanical garden at the University of Duhok that runs a citizen-science network, in which volunteers use its standard protocols and tools to gather plant population, distribution and health data.

name: University of Duhok Botanical Garden Citizen-Science Network
summary: Citizen-science network, run by the University of Duhok Botanical Garden, in which participants record wild plant populations, distribution and health across the Kurdistan Region, using a mobile app for photos and locations.

name: University of Sulaimani
summary: Iraqi university whose professors reportedly launched a wildlife water and camera monitoring project by November 2024, and whose authors wrote a 2026 Penjween wildfire and deforestation assessment.

name: Water sources for wildlife with camera monitoring, Sulaymaniyah
summary: Active project in which two professors and local residents have set up water sources for wildlife in remote Sulaymaniyah areas since 2021, monitored by camera traps, as reported in November 2024.

name: Waterkeepers Iraq
summary: Became an independent NGO registered in the Kurdistan Region in December 2014, after starting as a Nature Iraq programme in 2011.

name: Aerovision
summary: Company that says it was established in Iran in 2018 and combines AI, multispectral sensors and 3D analytics, including LiDAR tree volume estimation for forest management.

name: Agricultural Research, Education and Extension Organization
summary: Organisation in Iran, headed by a deputy minister, whose authors appear in OpenAlex on 2023 and 2026 machine learning papers on Hyrcanian forest biodiversity.

name: AI population estimate of the yellow-spotted mountain newt
summary: Active project run by Iran's Department of Environment with Razi University, which Koohestun reports uses AI to recognise individual newts by spot and colour patterns in habitat photographs and estimate their population.

name: Alborz Provincial Department of Environment
summary: The director general told Mehr News that vegetation in some managed natural areas in southern Alborz was damaged, along with the provincial wildlife museum and office building.

name: Anzali Wetland Ecological Management Project
summary: Completed project, run by the Department of Environment, whose completion report lists five outputs including monitoring procedures, and a monitoring manual revised after training and trial.

name: Anzali Wetland Management Committee
summary: Cross-sectoral committee for environmental management of the wetland, which a 2012 JICA completion report says was formed and approved the project outputs, meeting the project's purpose.

name: Arasbaran National Park and Protected Area
summary: National park and protected area whose head reported that rangers on patrol spotted a fire, which was put out with rangers and local communities.

name: Ardabil Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Provincial environment department whose director said in September 2022 that it managed 174,000 hectares of protected areas and 282,000 hectares of no-hunting areas.

name: Arta Sanjesh Negar
summary: Company that says it combines remote sensing, AI and local knowledge to help government bodies and private companies monitor land and resources, including forest, rangeland and water.

name: Assistance to Strengthening the Resilience of Zagros Forests to Oak Decline and Caspian Forests to Boxwood Blight and Development of National Forest Monitoring System in Iran
summary: Closed FAO-run project (TCP/IRA/3502) that aimed to build a national forest monitoring system to assess dieback in Zagros and Caspian forests, using Collect Earth.

name: AvayeBoom Bird Conservation Society
summary: Iranian NGO founded in Isfahan in 2015, with more than 310 volunteers by its own account, which says it conducts bird and waterbird surveys and publishes three datasets on GBIF.

name: Bamu National Park
summary: National park 15 km from Shiraz, reported by Tasnim in 2024 to cover 48,000 hectares, where its head said night-vision cameras helped rangers arrest two groups of repeat poachers.

name: Bushehr Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Provincial environment office whose director general said a count of summer-visiting breeding birds in Nakhiloo Marine National Park began with its experts and the area's rangers.

name: Central Committee for Revitalizing the Naghadeh Wetlands
summary: With UNDP Small Grants Programme support, local organisations formed this committee to coordinate Naghadeh wetland restoration, which expanded to 1,500 to 1,600 hectares and involved seven communities.

name: Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Provincial environment office whose director general said in May 2024 that a small building in the Tang-e Sayad complex was being completed, and that all agencies must help the national park project succeed.

name: Cheetah in Iran: A Country-Scale Assessment
summary: Closed final report of the Iranian Cheetah Society covering cheetah sightings from December 2011 to November 2013, with monitoring across nine reserves.

name: Collar4Conservation
summary: Programme run by Future4Leopards Foundation that, by its description, fits GPS satellite collars to Persian leopards in north-eastern Iran, sending 8 to 24 points a day.

name: Conservation of Asiatic Cheetah Project
summary: Closed project run by the Department of Environment to reverse Asiatic cheetah decline; UNDP says GEF co-funded Phase I in 2001 to 2008 and lists Phase II as completed.

name: Department of Environment (Iran)
summary: Body headquartered in Tehran, overseeing protected areas according to Wikipedia; IMNA reported October 2024 plans for AI systems to manage and protect natural areas.

name: Department of Environment AI assistant
summary: An AI assistant built by Tarbiat Modares University for Iran's Department of Environment, connecting a large language model to varied data including satellite data to generate reports; its first phase is in pilot operation.

name: Divar wildlife advert screening
summary: Programme in which Divar, per its report, uses AI to recognise wildlife images in adverts and block them, and agreed to work with the Department of Environment's protection unit.

name: DNA barcoding of Iran's vertebrates
summary: Department of Environment project that Mehr News reported covered, in its first phase, reptiles and birds of the south, bats of the west, amphibians, and rodents of the north-east, to update species lists and maps.

name: Effects of anthropogenic pressure on large mammals in the Hyrcanian forest, Iran
summary: Closed Erasmus Mundus Action 2 project, 2015 to 2017, studying distribution, co-occurrence and population dynamics of four large mammal species in the Hyrcanian forest using non-invasive surveys and occupancy modelling.

name: Farrokhvand tribe of the Bakhtiari tribal confederacy
summary: A 2015 report describes this Bakhtiari tribe across three provinces, its revival of a 500-hectare ICCA and the creation of its Council of Elders and Sustainable Livelihood Fund.

name: Fars Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Provincial environment department whose director said in June 2025 that 386 staff, including 199 rangers, were responsible for 3 parks, 2 wildlife refuges, 9 protected areas and 21 no-hunting zones.

name: Forests, Range and Watershed Management Organization
summary: Body responsible, per Wikipedia, for Iran's forests, rangelands and watersheds; Tehran Times reported in June 2023 that its head said the Khayyam satellite was used against land grabbing and forest clearing.

name: Future4Leopards Foundation
summary: Non-profit foundation, begun as a project in 2013, working in several Iranian reserves, which says satellite GPS collars and camera traps are its two main field tools.

name: Gavkhouni Wetland Biodiversity Website
summary: Website built by AvayeBoom with the Isfahan Department of Environment, launched on World Wetlands Day 2023, holding Gavkhouni International Wetland biodiversity checklists for birds, reptiles and mammals.

name: Gilan Hyrcanian forest leopard identification programme
summary: A programme run by the Gilan directorate, begun on 21 Ordibehesht 1405 in Amlash county with camera traps, which will tell individual leopards apart by comparing spot patterns in new and older images.

name: Gilan Provincial Directorate of Environmental Protection
summary: A provincial directorate that named identifying the leopards of Gilan's Hyrcanian forests as a main programme for 1405, carried out by its wildlife affairs office with county experts and rangers.

name: Golestan National Park
summary: National park that Mehr News describes as Iran's first registered national park and a listed UNESCO biosphere reserve; Iran International reported a ranger died on patrol in its Kuyler area.

name: Golestan Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Provincial environment office whose acting head told Mehr News in March 2025 that patrols in Golestan National Park had roughly doubled and staff were stationed along busy stretches of the park road.

name: Gorgan University of Agricultural Sciences and Natural Resources
summary: Iranian university whose authors appear in OpenAlex on two machine learning papers, from 2023 on rangeland species mapping and 2025 on habitat suitability for the herb Salvia leriifolia.

name: Hamadan Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Provincial environment department whose director said in July 2022 that the province had six protected areas covering 62,351 hectares, about 3 percent of its area.

name: Hamuleh tribe of the Bakhtiari tribal confederacy
summary: Tribe of the Bakhtiari confederacy, counted at 500 households in 2008, said in a workshop report to have managed its area under customary laws for centuries; CENESTA facilitated an ICCA revival workshop.

name: Hormozgan Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Provincial environment office whose director said in June 2021 that it managed 19 areas, including five international wetlands, all on the coastal strip and islands.

name: Ilam Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Provincial environment office whose director general said 143,000 hectares of the province's natural areas, including four protected areas and two national natural monuments, are under its management.

name: Ilam University
summary: Iranian university whose authors appear in OpenAlex on two machine learning papers, from 2021 on medicinal plant leaf recognition with a neural network classifier and 2024 on forest restoration from satellite images.

name: Information Technology Organization of Iran
summary: Iranian body described by Tasnim as technical lead of the Land Management Single Window; Tasnim also reports a spatial content platform providing government GIS services.

name: Iran Biodiversity Database
summary: Database that Mehr News reported was launched by the Department of Environment's national museum and genetic resources office, with its system in operation and a support phase planned.

name: Iran Birds Checklist
summary: Checklist of all bird species recorded and confirmed in Iran, with names, conservation statuses and biological information, published on GBIF by AvayeBoom under CC BY 4.0, currently version 1.3.

name: Iran Land Cover Map v1 13-class (2017)
summary: 13-class land cover map of Iran for 2017 at 10-metre pixel size, made from Sentinel imagery in Google Earth Engine with an object-based random forest method, by the KNTU lidar lab.

name: Iran winter waterbird census
summary: Run by Iran's Department of Environment, the census began in 1967; a 1393 report described 1.7–2 million birds counted annually and planned coverage of 30 provinces.

name: Iran_v1
summary: Camera-trap model identifying 14 species or higher taxa in Iran, trained on about one million images and designed, per its model card, to speed up Iranian Cheetah Society monitoring.

name: Iran_v1 camera-trap species model
summary: Camera-trap species model for Iran covering 14 species or higher taxa, trained on about one million images; its model card says accuracy was not tested on out-of-sample data.

name: Iranian Cheetah Society
summary: Tehran-based non-profit registered in 2001, with the Asiatic cheetah as flagship species, running camera-trap monitoring in northern and southern Iranian reserves since 2012.

name: Iranian National Center for Ocean Data
summary: Programme established in 1995 as Iran's national node of the IODE programme, run by the national oceanography institute, managing oceanographic data from cruises, coastal monitoring, remote sensing and modelling, accredited in 2017.

name: Iranian National Institute for Oceanography and Atmospheric Science
summary: Tehran-based institute under the Ministry of Science, founded in 1992, that publishes eight datasets on GBIF as the PEGO-OBIS node and monitors Iranian seas using cruises, drones and satellites.

name: Iranian Space Agency
summary: Iranian agency that UN-SPIDER lists as national focal point for space research and remote sensing, with Khayyam reported in July 2023 to have started land use monitoring, and Pars 2 only planned.

name: IranVeg, the Vegetation Database of Iran
summary: National vegetation database of Iran whose 2024 paper reports an updated version with 13,411 plots, 3,919 plant species and 64 authors, first authored by Soghra Ramzi.

name: Isfahan Provincial Department of Environment
summary: In June 2023, its director dated the Qamishlou National Park castle deed acquisition to 25 years earlier and said the Kolah Ghazi motorway protection proposal awaited Supreme Council approval.

name: Isfahan University of Technology
summary: Iranian university whose authors appear in OpenAlex on two papers, from 2021 on Ferula ovina habitat using machine learning and 2023 on species distribution model parameterisation.

name: K. N. Toosi University of Technology
summary: Iranian university whose authors appear in OpenAlex on two machine learning papers, from 2022 on mangrove mapping with neural networks and 2026 on wetland classification in arid coastal environments.

name: K. N. Toosi University of Technology LiDAR Lab
summary: A university lab associated in the Earth Engine Data Catalog with Iran Land Cover Map v1, made using an object-based random forest classifier trained on reference samples.

name: Kerman Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Provincial environment office whose director reported in May 2025 the discovery of a natural cave in Khabr National Park, Baft County, where a team including environmental experts recorded the entrance.

name: Kermanshah Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Iran Daily reports that the department manages the Zaleh-Zard Wildlife Refuge of over 40,000 hectares and that Kermanshah has over 240,000 hectares of protected areas under environmental management.

name: Khayyam satellite monitoring system
summary: A satellite monitoring system that Tasnim reports can detect illegal construction, forest grabbing and resource destruction, with Khayyam imagery also supplying part of the Land Management Single Window's land-monitoring subsystem.

name: Khuzestan Provincial Department of Environment
summary: The provincial environment director said crews had largely contained the Khaiz fire and the office would keep supplying water, food and equipment until it was fully under control.

name: Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Provincial environment office whose director said in December 2013 that 80 rangers protected seven areas covering 290,000 hectares, and in August 2019 that 73 rangers protected 312,466 hectares.

name: Kolah Ghazi drone wildlife census
summary: A closed pilot drone wildlife census in Kolah Ghazi National Park, run by Iran's Department of Environment, reported in December 2025, with AI analysis of the data planned and extension to other areas intended.

name: Kurdistan Provincial Department of Environment
summary: Provincial environment office whose acting head said in December 2024 that mammal population estimates were underway in the Shahu and Kosalan protected area, which came under it by government decision in Iranian year 1387.

name: Lake Urmia National Park
summary: National park of about 102 islands, protected in 1967 and made a National Park in 1976; in August 2019 its then head said rainfall had saturated island reservoirs.

name: Land Management Single Window
