summary: Italian non-profit that surveys biodiversity and, with CSQA, proposed the Biodiversity Friend certification for farming.

name: WWF Italia
summary: Italian WWF organisation. With Huawei it ran the Guardiani della natura project, using AI sound recognition in reserves it manages.

name: XNatura
summary: Nature intelligence division of 3Bee, launched in March 2025, that uses AI, IoT sensors, satellites and cloud computing for managing impacts and risks on nature, biodiversity and climate.

name: Ziboni Technology
summary: Company in Costa Volpino, Bergamo, that offers GPS and VHF telemetry collars, geolocators, camera trapping and sound recorders for wildlife research, and has a partner link to Ecotone Telemetry.

name: A Jamaican Path from Hills to Ocean
summary: Closed six-year project run by the Planning Institute of Jamaica, whose seagrass study combined drone and satellite imagery, field validation and geospatial modelling to map seagrass beds.

name: Adaptive Management for Mangrove Conservation in Trelawny, Jamaica
summary: Active mangrove monitoring project at two sites in Trelawny, Jamaica, reporting three years of data from permanent 10 by 10 metre plots, with a September 2025 plot check showing further mangrove removal.

name: Advancing Jamaican Biodiversity Data Products and Information Services (BID-Jamaica)
summary: Project led by the Institute of Jamaica from September 2017 to January 2019, which created datasets on mosses, fungi, some flowering plants, insects, birds and selected invasive species.

name: Alligator Head Foundation
summary: Active foundation that, TBA21 says, was created and endowed by Francesca Thyssen-Bornemisza to support Portland fishing communities; a partner's October 2022 blog reported staff monitoring beaches for sea turtle nesting.

name: Bluefields Bay Fishermen’s Friendly Society
summary: Sea turtle monitoring programme begun in 2006 to cut poaching of nesting females and eggs; a 2019 profile reports nightly beach patrols, tagging and data sharing with NEPA, and a 2019 grant was to continue it.

name: Caribbean Coastal Area Management Foundation
summary: A nongovernmental organisation with 2012–13 baseline surveys and a US$388,483.53 CEPF grant proposed for July 2022–June 2025, including participatory monitoring of Portland Bight Protected Area.

name: Centre for Marine Sciences, University of the West Indies, Mona
summary: University of the West Indies centre in the Department of Life Sciences that runs the Caribbean Coastal Data Centre and coordinates Jamaica's Reef Check reef surveys, alongside mangrove carbon research.

name: Coral Reef Health Index monitoring (Jamaica)
summary: NEPA-run reef monitoring institutionalised in 2007 uses a health index, described as the main tracking method, measured triennially at 20 sites according to Jamaica’s 2023 ICRI report.

name: Department of Life Sciences, The University of the West Indies, Mona
summary: First affiliation in a 2026 mangrove paper assessing 1,681 trees in 49 plots and identifying sediment pH as a carbon-stock predictor; a lecturer received acoustic equipment.

name: Environmental Foundation of Jamaica
summary: Foundation that, the Gleaner reports, awarded about $85 million in grants in 2022, $60 million of them from the Forest Conservation Fund, whose themes include research and monitoring.

name: Establishment of Mobile Emergency Rapid Response Team and Utilisation of Technological Solutions to support Enforcement and Monitoring in Forest Protected Areas
summary: Closed 2024 project, led by Jamaica's Forestry Department and funded by BIOPAMA with a 99,927.30 euro grant, that planned a small ranger team and drone training for enforcement around Mount Diablo, St Ann.

name: Field Assessment of Selected Critically Endangered Species
summary: Ongoing Natural History Museum of Jamaica project, run by the museum, in which fieldwork supported by The Red List Project monitors populations of several critically endangered species.

name: Forestry Department (Jamaica)
summary: Government agency that says it manages about 117,000 hectares of forest; its 2013 to 2023 land use assessment found forest cover rose from 40 to 47.9 per cent.

name: Forestry Department GIS Portal (Jamaica)
summary: Active Jamaican Forestry Department web portal, run by the department, that offers featured maps and apps, including one on monitoring forest ecosystems, and links to ArcGIS Online and staff dashboards.

name: Implementing Critical Conservation Actions for the Jamaican Rock Iguana in Hellshire Hills, Jamaica
summary: CEPF-funded conservation project running from December 2024 to March 2027, covering ecological monitoring of invasive and native species in the Hellshire Hills and improvements to the Hope Zoo headstart facility.

name: Institute of Jamaica
summary: Agency of the Ministry of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sports that runs the Natural History Museum of Jamaica and led the BID-Jamaica biodiversity data project.

name: Jamaica Clearing-House Mechanism
summary: Serving as Jamaica’s biodiversity information network and run by the Natural History Museum of Jamaica, this programme coordinated the Biodiversity Information for Development Jamaica project.

name: Jamaica Conservation and Development Trust
summary: Delegated management of the Blue and John Crow Mountains National Park by the Natural Resources Conservation Authority; the park’s pages report stream monitoring at 12 sites.

name: Jamaica Coral Reef Monitoring Network
summary: Local arm of the Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network, launched in June 2003 by the Caribbean Coastal Data Centre and run by UWI Mona's Centre for Marine Sciences.

name: Jamaica Environment Trust
summary: Non-profit membership environmental organisation in the Kingston and St. Andrew area that has trained communities in Portland, St. Elizabeth and Westmoreland to monitor sea turtle nesting, with data going to NEPA.

name: Jamaica Invasive Species Database
summary: Database launched on 14 October 2015, described then as the island's first comprehensive portal of its kind, covering how invasive species arrived, where they were and how far they had spread.

name: Jamaica mangrove and seagrass mapping and carbon stock project
summary: Mapping and carbon stock work run by The Nature Conservancy and UWI's Centre for Marine Sciences, with data to be given to the Jamaican government, according to Pew.

name: Land Use-Land Cover Change Assessment (Jamaica)
summary: Ten-yearly land use and land cover assessment built by the Forestry Department; the 2013 to 2023 round reported 88 per cent overall accuracy from 396 sample points.

name: Long-term Monitoring of Jamaican Bats
summary: Proposed project, with a USD 25,000 three-year grant awarded to Damion Whyte by Jamaica Conservation Partners, aiming to set up island-wide monitoring of bat population trends, habitat use and threats.

name: Ministry of Water, Environment and Climate Change (Jamaica)
summary: Jamaican ministry set up to lead work on safe water, environmental sustainability and climate mitigation, adaptation and resilience, with the National Spatial Data Management Division among its agencies.

name: Mona GeoInformatics Institute
summary: University of the West Indies institute awarded Google’s 2023/2024 Geo for Good Impact Award for KHEAM geospatial work around Kingston Harbour; uses Google Earth Engine for nature conservation.

name: National Environment and Planning Agency
summary: Lead government agency for environmental protection, land use and spatial planning, which the Jamaica Observer reports received monitoring equipment under the Hills to Ocean project.

name: National Forest Monitoring System (Jamaica)
summary: Forest monitoring system run by the Forestry Department, piloted in 2022 and reported as operational, which uses permanent sampling plots: a ten-year target of 200, with over 400 sample plots established.

name: National Spatial Data Management Branch
summary: Jamaican government branch that, as its acting principal director said in November 2023, coordinates the local geospatial sector, represents Jamaica at geospatial forums, and gave the National Land Agency training and technical support.

name: Natural History Museum of Jamaica
summary: Division of the Institute of Jamaica that runs the Jamaica Clearing-House Mechanism and holds Jamaica's main repository of biological specimens; its zoology department contributes data to GBIF.

name: Planning Institute of Jamaica
summary: Active Jamaican body at 16 Oxford Road, Kingston 5, which coordinated the Hills to Ocean project, started in 2020.

name: The spatial ecology and behavior of the Jamaican Rock Iguana (Cyclura collei)
summary: Post-release monitoring study that radio-tracked 19 Jamaican iguanas, 13 of them released from captivity, between February and June 2018; analyses were reported as still in process.

name: Windsor Research Centre
summary: Conducts natural sciences research for Cockpit Country conservation, with bird-banding mark-recapture and avian health studies planned under an EFJ grant for September 2003 to September 2005.

name: Al-Hussein Technical University
summary: University reported by Al Defaiya in July 2025 as funding the Al-Rhim Sat project.

name: Al-Rhim Sat
summary: Proposed CubeSat, reported to be designed to track endangered wildlife in remote Jordan using LoRa, in preliminary design review in July 2025 with launch planned for late 2026.

name: Al-Zaytoonah University of Jordan
summary: University that Jordan News reported in September 2022 as sponsoring and funding a forest fire detection project using wireless sensor networks and machine learning.

name: Aqaba Bird Observatory
summary: Reports 271 recorded bird species, over 61% of Jordan’s recorded species, while Ayla’s June 2026 release plans continued bird monitoring and an environmental database.

name: Aqaba Marine Reserve
summary: Jordanian marine reserve designated by Royal Decree in June 2020 and established by Cabinet in December 2020, with a 2022-2026 management plan, Norwegian-supported monitoring and a GIS-based marine database from 2022 to 2024.

name: Aqaba Special Economic Zone Authority
summary: Authority established in 2000 according to the University of Jordan, whose environment commissioner the Global Fund for Coral Reefs named as patron of August 2025 reef-monitoring training.

name: Assessment of Status of Seagrass Beds along the Jordanian Coast in Aqaba
summary: A closed project, run by ASEZA and UNDP within the Global Fund for Coral Reefs, that surveyed most seagrass-dominated coastal areas of Aqaba, mapped bed distribution and health, and ended with a remote sensing and GIS training workshop for Aqaba Marine Reserve staff.

name: Ayla bird monitoring programme
summary: Programme, run by the Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature and Ayla Oasis Development Company, monitoring migratory and resident birds in Ayla, with spring and autumn 2026 seasons planned and an environmental database in development.

name: Ayla lagoons marine monitoring programme
summary: A programme under a two-year agreement, renewed with the Marine Science Station according to Ayla, monitoring marine life, water quality and sediment in Ayla's lagoons, with AI-based coral reef monitoring planned.

name: Biodiversity Information Management System and Monitoring Program (Jordan)
summary: National biodiversity information and monitoring system described by RSCN as planned on a GIS platform integrated with protected-area and partner databases.

name: Biodiversity Information Management System and National Monitoring Programme
summary: Closed RSCN project, run and built by the society, to develop a national biodiversity monitoring and information system, listed in its 2014 report for 2014 to 2016 and covering three sites.

name: Coral Reefs Conservation and Blue Economy – Jordan
summary: Project funded by UNDP Jordan, with IUCN ROWA assigned key technical tasks, covering three Aqaba coral reef sites and aiming to produce baselines, assess climate refugia and strengthen monitoring through training and citizen science.

name: Department of Horticulture and Crop Science, University of Jordan
summary: A university department in Amman, lead affiliation on 2022 and 2025 remote sensing papers covering small forest fires, Arabian oryx reintroduction sites and forest moisture, using Sentinel-2 and Landsat data.

name: Developing a national monitoring and information system specialized in biodiversity
summary: Closed RSCN project, 2014 to 2016, to develop a national biodiversity monitoring and information system, which also lists studies of tourism's effect on Dibeen Forest Reserve.

name: Eco Consult (Jordan)
summary: A renewable energy advisory in Jordan which, according to Euronews in April 2020, used a bird observer to watch for collision risks at power lines and wind turbines, calling the team to stop turbines.

name: Enhancing the Capacity of the Forestry Sector to Control and Manage Forest Fires in Jordan
summary: Closed project, built by FAO and Jordan's Ministry of Agriculture from October 2021 to December 2023 with USD 99,620 from FAO, that set up a fire early warning system and gave rangers digital reporting tablets.

name: Gulf of Aqaba Resilient Reefs Programme
summary: Programme covering three priority Aqaba reef sites, with a GFCR budget of USD 1,628,754 in its 2025 annual report, UNDP Jordan convening, and activities including citizen science monitoring and environmental DNA training.

name: Jordan BirdWatch
summary: Amman-based endorsed GBIF publisher whose programmes include bird monitoring, research and a database, and which expected in 2020 to publish data on invasive or introduced birds.

name: Jordan forest inventory using space technology and AI
summary: Proposed initiative, reported in September 2024, to assess forest types, density and soil using direct and satellite monitoring within the National Plan for Sustainable Agriculture.

name: Jordan national online database on bird collisions and electrocution at energy infrastructure
summary: A national online database, reported by the Renewables Grid Initiative as established by RSCN, to monitor and mitigate migratory bird collisions and electrocution at energy infrastructure, alongside 116 wind shutdowns at the time of writing.

name: Jordan University of Science and Technology
summary: University departments are lead affiliations on a 2022 satellite deforestation paper and 2024 and 2025 papers on grassland leaf area index and rangeland biomass.

name: Mainstreaming Plant Key Biodiversity Areas into Jordan's National Conservation Planning Framework
summary: Closed project funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund, running from November 2018 to May 2022, that aimed to identify plant Key Biodiversity Areas in Mediterranean Jordan and include them in national land-use planning.

name: Marine Science Station, Aqaba
summary: Part of the University of Jordan’s Aqaba branch, whose coral laboratory describes long-term reef monitoring with ASEZA to assess reef status along Jordan’s coast.

name: Ministry of Agriculture (Jordan)
summary: Ministry reported in September 2024 as signing an agreement to inventory forest assets using space technologies and AI, and whose Forestry Department specimens the Royal Botanic Garden digitised (2,207).

name: Ministry of Environment (Jordan)
summary: Jordan's environment ministry, whose Minister the CBD Secretariat lists as the national focal point for the Convention on Biological Diversity, with a Nature Protection Directorate and a Biodiversity Division.

name: National Monitoring Program for the Gulf of Aqaba
summary: Programme begun in 2001 to record baseline coral cover, reef health and fish abundance, which the University of Jordan page (updated 2017) says ASEZA committed to finance and manage.

name: Nature Conservation Monitoring Center
summary: RSCN programme, run and built by the society, with flora, fauna and bird survey teams and a GIS unit; its 2019 report records eight ecological studies and reserve monitoring.

name: Protecting Marine Biodiversity in Aqaba
summary: Project funded by Global Affairs Canada and partnered with UNDP, listed as operating from 4 March 2025 to 31 December 2027, with baseline biodiversity surveys begun by March 2025.

name: Royal Botanic Garden (Jordan)
summary: With headquarters in Khalda, Amman, says its herbarium gained national registration in 2017 and it has collected over 2,600 plant tissue samples for DNA study since 2015.

name: Royal Jordanian Geographic Centre
summary: Jordanian mapping body that a University of Jordan research group says provides aerial photography, topographic maps, national geospatial datasets and satellite imagery used for land cover classification.

name: Royal Marine Conservation Society of Jordan
summary: A Jordanian non-profit, which says it was the country's first specialised marine conservation NGO in 1995, listing Coral Watch, Reef Check and Aqaba Marine Park monitoring, and calling for citizen scientists.

name: Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature
summary: Jordanian conservation society that says it has established ten protected areas covering over 4,656 square kilometres, and whose site lists a monitoring centre and a national biodiversity database.

name: Sustainable World Software Technology Company
summary: Software company whose general manager was reported by Jordan News in September 2024 as saying it aimed to use space and AI-driven geospatial technology for the ministry's forest management.

name: System for detecting, predicting and monitoring forest fires using wireless sensor networks and machine learning
summary: Project of unknown status, reported in September 2022 as an early fire-detection experiment in Ajloun's Barqash plantations using temperature and humidity sensors, with artificial intelligence expected later.

name: The Conservation Programme of the Houbara Bustard in Jordan
summary: Closed RSCN project, 2014 to 2017, which reported 500 Houbara released in two areas and monitored using GPS devices and 100 radio transmitters.

name: The University of Jordan
summary: Jordanian university whose geography research group says it obtains satellite imagery from the Royal Jordanian Geographic Center for land cover classification.

name: Virtual Herbarium of the Royal Botanic Garden (Jordan)
summary: Active electronic library of digital samples of wild Jordanian plants, including scanned specimens from three named institutions, run by the Royal Botanic Garden.

name: Advancement of Technologies for Utilizing Big Data of Marine Life
summary: MEXT-funded and MEXT-run commissioned marine research programme led by Tomonari Akamatsu, approved as an Ocean Decade Action in November 2025, pairing marine biologists with information scientists.

name: AdvanSentinel Inc.
summary: Osaka-based organisation listed as a partner of Kobe University.

name: AI biologging device for seabirds
summary: Seabird camera device built by Takuya Maekawa and Ken Yoda; an October 2020 release reported it automatically detected and filmed wild seabirds' foraging, calling it a world first.

name: AI video bio-logger for wild seabirds
summary: Bio-logger for wild seabirds built by the University of Osaka, described in its release as the first to use AI for this task, with 76 five-minute videos collected.

name: AIST SAR foundation model for Japan
summary: SAR foundation model for Japan, built by the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology from JAXA Daichi-2 data on AIST's ABCI system.

name: Akame Satoyama Wo Sodateru Kai
summary: A non-profit that, according to the Ministry of the Environment's page on the Akame satoyama, carries out satoyama conservation, including managing a dragonfly pond.

name: Akaya Project Regional Council
summary: A council formed by local residents that, per the Forestry Agency, launched the Akaya Project in 2004 with the Kanto Regional Forest Office and the Nature Conservation Society of Japan to restore biodiversity across six forest zones.

name: Akkeshi Marine Station, Field Science Center for Northern Biosphere, Hokkaido University
summary: Hokkaido University field station that has recorded air and water temperature and other weather and ocean data at its pier continuously since 1950, and is listed for the Akkeshi JaLTER core site.

name: Akkeshi Waterfowl Observation Center
summary: Education, research and surveillance base at Ramsar-listed Akkeshi Lake and Bekambeushi, counting and mapping ducks, especially whooper swans, and surveying birds and mammals mainly with observation cameras.

name: Amami Wildlife Conservation Center
summary: Base for research on rare wildlife and public education, surveying the Amami rabbit, Amami thrush and Amami woodcock, the woodcock across three islands twice a year.

name: Amami-Oshima, Tokunoshima, Northern Okinawa Island and Iriomote Island World Natural Heritage Regional Liaison Council
summary: A council whose charter tasks it with coordinating among government agencies to help conserve and manage the heritage area, with a subcommittee for each of four islands or island areas.

name: ANEMONE DB
summary: Open fish biodiversity database for eDNA surveys, opened 2 June 2022 with data from over 4,000 surveys at 861 locations, run by Michio Kondoh and the ANEMONE Consortium.

name: ANEMONE Global
summary: Described as the initiative to expand the ANEMONE network worldwide.

name: Animal Portal
summary: Cloud-based wildlife service that Biologging Solutions says it operates, and which the company says research institutions, national parks and local governments use.

name: Asahata Retarding Basin Conservation and Use Promotion Council
summary: A council named by the Ministry of the Environment as applicant for Asahata retarding basin in Shizuoka, listed among certified nature symbiosis sites, a certification the Ministry began in fiscal 2023.

name: Asama Sanroku International Nature School
summary: A non-profit that the Ministry of the Environment designated on 11 March 2008 as park management body for the Asama area of Joshinetsu-kogen National Park.

name: Asaza Fund
summary: An organisation named by the Ministry of the Environment as applicant for the Ushiku water-source satoyama in Ushiku, Ibaraki, listed among certified nature symbiosis sites, a certification begun in fiscal 2023.

name: Aso Grassland Restoration Council
summary: A council that the Ministry of the Environment says was set up so many parties could help pass on Aso's grasslands, with five sub-committees including rangeland management.

name: Aso Green Stock
summary: A foundation named as applicant for its trust lands in Aso, Kumamoto, a certified nature symbiosis site, and designated a park management body for Aso-Kuju National Park on 2 December 2003.

name: Atmosphere and Ocean Research Institute, The University of Tokyo
summary: University of Tokyo institute whose mission includes primary research on the oceans and atmosphere, and which analyses data and considers responses in the Nippon Foundation project.

name: Automatic vegetation identification by deep learning (KAKEN 18H03357)
summary: Closed research project, 2018 to 2022, led by Takeshi Ise, that aimed to advance non-contact vegetation observation using deep learning.

name: Axelspace
summary: Organisation that says satellite observation can track tree growth and forest area change, and names vegetation health and biodiversity monitoring in its Maldives Space Research Organisation partnership.

name: Biodiversity Center of Japan
summary: Run by the Ministry of the Environment, it surveys and monitors Japan's vegetation, species, rivers, lakes, tidal flats and coral reefs, and runs Monitoring Sites 1000.

name: Biodiversity Impact Assessment Tool for solar power plants
summary: Biodiversity impact assessment tool for solar power plants, built by Think Nature and UPDATER, with a joint demonstration announced in July 2026 and planned for June to September 2026.

name: Biodiversity Visualisation System
summary: Map system built and run by Japan's environment ministry showing protected areas, nature symbiosis sites and conservation-effective places; a later release says all first planned functions are built.

name: Biologging intelligent Platform
summary: Cloud platform for standardising and sharing biologging data, built by Biologging Solutions and developed under the Sato theme of the education ministry's marine big data programme.

name: Biological Information System for Marine Life
summary: Web-based biodiversity information system run by JAMSTEC, serving as the system of J-OBIS and the Japan node of OBIS.

name: Biome app and BiomeDB
summary: Citizen species-identification app and database from Biome Inc., released April 2019, covering about 100,000 Japanese species; the company reports 1.3 million downloads, and BiomeDB record counts differ between sources.

name: Biome Inc.
summary: Kyoto company, established 31 May 2017, that builds and runs the Biome app, which names species from photos; in April 2026 it said it was stepping up overseas work.

name: BiomeBoard
summary: Programme built and run by Biome Inc., whose beta launched on 21 October 2026 after 23 companies tried the demo.

name: BiomeSurvey
summary: Survey support programme built and run by Biome Inc. covering planning, execution, data collection and management, with organism photos sent to species identification AI; open beta released December 2022.

name: Biosphere Informatics Lab, Kyoto University
summary: University lab that uses large-scale geographic, satellite and DNA database data and develops environmental DNA methods for analysing biological communities.

name: BioWM
summary: Mapping service built by the National Institute for Environmental Studies, offering GBIF occurrence records and the institute's biodiversity data, downloadable by dataset as Darwin Core Archives.

name: Bird Note
summary: Bird record database run by the Japan Bird Research Association, usable on smartphones, tablets and computers.

name: Blakiston's fish owl voice recognition software
summary: Voice recognition software for Blakiston's fish owl, built by Fujitsu; a report says Fujitsu provides technology to the society's work protecting the owl.

name: Blue carbon Data Archive System
summary: Archive built by Japan's land ministry and Port and Airport Research Institute; a June 2026 release announced public WebGIS maps of modelled seaweed beds, with drone uploads planned for early August.

name: BlueArch
summary: Described in one report as an association using drones and AI for blue carbon surveys, and by Kanagawa Prefecture as an underwater vehicle maker and collaborator.

name: C.W. Nicol Afan Woodland Foundation
summary: A foundation named by the Ministry of the Environment as applicant for the north area of Afan Woodland in Shinano, Nagano, listed among certified nature symbiosis sites, a certification begun in fiscal 2023.

name: CanopyScope
summary: Programme analysing ALOS radar data, high-resolution optical images and drone data, and using generative AI to make project development and monitoring reports more efficient.

name: Center for Biodiversity Science, Ryukoku University
summary: Research centre set up in the 29th year of Heisei that uses eDNA analysis as its main technology and aims to provide high-resolution biodiversity data for conservation and policy.

name: Center for Ecological Research, Kyoto University
summary: Kyoto University centre that continues the monthly Lake Biwa regular observation begun in 1965, keeps plankton and benthos samples, and is named for the Lake Biwa JaLTER associate site.

name: Center for Environmental Remote Sensing, Chiba University
summary: Chiba University centre established in 1995 for remote sensing research; a university release says a study led from it made a refined land cover map for Siberia.

name: Central Research Institute of Electric Power Industry
summary: Organisation that says it uses stereo vision to observe bird flight and work out wind power collision effects, and is developing automatic AI processing of the footage.

name: Chiba University
summary: University that runs the Center for Environmental Remote Sensing; its news release reports a land cover map for Siberia made with machine learning.

name: Chubu Regional Forest Office
summary: A regional forest office that reorganised its protected forests between fiscal 2015 and 2017, and whose page gives 86 sites covering 112,345 hectares as of 1 April 2024.

name: Circuit Design
summary: Seller of GPS collars and related equipment with a drop-off mechanism, whose pages also describe the ANIMAL MAP wildlife damage control platform and a 1 g beacon for following forest green tree frogs.

name: Coral distribution survey, Ryukyu and Ogasawara Islands
summary: Ministry of the Environment survey, run from 2017 to 2021, that combined satellite image analysis with field surveys to assess coral distribution and cover in the Ryukyu and Ogasawara Islands.

name: DAI Labs
summary: Organisation that says its CanopyScope platform combines satellite data and AI.

name: DeepForest Technologies
summary: Kyoto-based company, described as a Kyoto University spin-out, that develops forest analysis technology from drone and other remote sensing data, raised 200 million yen in a Series A in June 2024, and builds DF Scanner.

name: DeepHL
summary: Deep learning method named in a paper title, with no further details given and its status unknown.

name: DeepLitterAI
summary: System built by JAMSTEC to detect and count deep seafloor litter from video, tested on footage from 860 to 5,600 m around Japan, with AI counts differing from expert counts by about 10%.

name: DF Scanner
summary: AI tool built by DeepForest Technologies that detects trees, identifies species and estimates stem volume from drone orthoimages and point cloud data, and includes a crown-species diversity assessment.

name: DGPU
summary: Four-step method (Detect, Group, Promote, Union) built by Biologging Solutions on an audio foundation model tuned to ocean sound, tested so far only on existing recordings.

name: DNA Data Bank of Japan
summary: Nucleotide sequence database run by the National Institute of Genetics as an INSDC member, providing data freely and exchanging released data daily with ENA/EBI and NCBI.

name: Dugongs' EYE
summary: Biodiversity visualisation app, as Think Nature describes it, run by Think Nature.

name: Earthwatch Japan
summary: Organisation whose briefing scheduled fish eDNA fieldwork for 20 June–20 August 2026, with a 2022 release planning citizen surveys at 50 sites, then 100.

name: Ecosystem Conservation Society-Japan
summary: Environmental protection group that says it works with citizens, companies and government, and whose JHEP method assesses sites using habitat suitability (HSI) and regional vegetation character (VEI).

name: Edge AI Bioacoustics for Invasive Species Detection
summary: Project in Japan listed among the WILDLABS Awards 2026 grantees, funded by the WILDLABS Awards, on edge AI bioacoustics for invasive species detection.

name: Environmental Restoration and Conservation Agency
summary: Agency that took over project calls, review, allocation and contracts of a fund from October 2016, and has current projects on seabird counts using drones, biologging and deep learning, and on fish community monitoring by image analysis.

name: Estuary Research Center, Shimane University
summary: Continued monthly ecosystem monitoring of Lake Shinji, Lake Nakaumi and Honjo in 2022, and is listed for the Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi JaLTER core site.

name: FAMOST
summary: Programme that the Forestry Agency says it built to identify felled sites from free satellite data using Google Earth Engine, with a fiscal 2025 technician manual published alongside the source code.

name: Fisheries Agency of Japan
summary: Government agency whose site hosts a report describing the use of an AI deep learning model for coral classification.

name: FishPass Inc.
summary: Company based in Sakai, Fukui Prefecture, established October 2016, whose business is the FishPass online fishing permit app and environmental DNA surveys.

name: Forest Culture Association
summary: An association named by the Ministry of the Environment as applicant for Tsukuba Expo Forest in Tsukuba, Ibaraki, listed among certified nature symbiosis sites, a certification begun in fiscal 2023.

name: Forest Ecosystem Diversity Basic Survey
summary: Forestry Agency survey, begun in fiscal 1999 and in its sixth five-year round since fiscal 2024, using 0.1 ha plots on a nationwide 4 km grid, with data used for forest carbon uptake calculations and Montreal Process reports.

name: Forest Inventory Management
summary: Synspective solution for forestry companies, listed as run by Synspective.

name: Forest Research and Management Organization
summary: Tsukuba-based body whose statutory work covers forest research and surveys, and whose 2024 annual report lists projects on tropical forest biodiversity from satellite images, wildlife monitoring methods and AI-based land-use change detection; it runs the REDD-plus centre.

name: Forest Research Station, Field Science Center for Northern Biosphere, Hokkaido University
summary: Hokkaido University research station that monitors sika deer, raptor nesting and ground beetles over the long term, with its Tomakomai Research Station listed for a JaLTER core site.

name: Forestry Agency of Japan
summary: Government agency that runs the national forest ecosystem diversity survey, whose 4 km plot mesh it describes and whose first to fifth round data, including tree-level records, are published through a help desk site.

name: GBIF Japan
summary: Japanese country node listed in the GBIF registry with observer participation and a Tsukuba address, partnering with the Global Biodiversity Information Facility.

name: Geoinformatics Team, RIKEN Center for Advanced Intelligence Project
summary: RIKEN team working on image processing and machine learning to understand Earth from images, with a listed paper on OpenEarthMap, a global high-resolution land cover benchmark dataset.

name: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan
summary: Japan’s only national administrative body for surveying and maps produced the GSI Dataset through fiscal 2018–2022 research on automatic feature extraction with AI.

name: Gifu University
summary: A 2019 university press release describes a ResNet-based model estimating animal presence, species and count in camera trap images.

name: Graduate School of Life Sciences, Tohoku University
summary: A Japan Science and Technology Agency news item names Dr Michio Kondoh of this Sendai graduate school among those who released ANEMONE DB.

name: GSI Dataset
summary: A machine learning dataset for extracting features from 20 cm aerial photographs by semantic segmentation, with classes including natural vegetation such as broadleaf and coniferous forest.

name: High-Resolution Land Use and Land Cover Map of Japan
summary: A land use and land cover map of Japan, version 25.04, covering 2020, 2022 and 2024 from Sentinel-2, Landsat-8 and ALOS-2, intended as base information for ecosystem assessment and disaster response.

name: Hiroshima Nature School
summary: An organisation named by the Ministry of the Environment as applicant for its site in Kitahiroshima, Hiroshima, listed among certified nature symbiosis sites, a certification begun in fiscal 2023.

name: Hiruzen Nature Restoration Council
summary: A council that the Ministry of the Environment says was set up on 20 January 2022 to restore the natural environment of the Hiruzen area, whose grasslands depend on burning and other upkeep.

name: Hokkaido Regional Forest Office
summary: The Forestry Agency lists the Shiretoko Forest Ecosystem Reserve under this office and identifies forest ecosystem reserves as the protection measure for Shiretoko's World Natural Heritage site.

name: Hokkaido Research Organization
summary: Its fiscal 2024 forestry list includes projects developing satellite methods for natural forest information in 2022–2025 and implementing single-tree measurement AI and CLAS-LiDAR resource estimation in 2023–2025.

name: Hokkaido Seabird Center
summary: Base in Haboro for public education, recovery work and research on Hokkaido's seabirds, monitoring common murre and other seabird populations and using decoys under the murre recovery plan.

name: Hokkaido University
summary: A saved OpenAlex query groups 60 works since 2021 with Japanese affiliations and primary topic T10199 under it; university research applies remote sensing, GIS and machine learning.

name: HRLULC-Japan 2024 with Detailed Vegetation
summary: A land use and land cover dataset reflecting Japan in 2024, apart from some outlying islands, released in March 2026.

name: Hylable
summary: A company that says it has analysed conversations in noisy spaces since its 2016 founding, with a registered business in media signal processing and communication products.

name: Hyogo Prefectural Government
summary: APN lists it among its financial donors and says it gives significant in-kind contributions.

name: Hyomon-modoki Conservation Area Council (Mihashidani Biotope)
summary: Council named by the Ministry of the Environment as applicant for Mihashidani Biotope in Mihara, Hiroshima, on its list of sites certified under the nature symbiosis scheme begun in fiscal 2023.

name: IDEA Consultants
summary: A consultancy whose September 2019 technical newsletter describes its environmental DNA work and lists AI species identification and counting among its survey methods.

name: IHI Corporation
summary: A Tokyo-headquartered company that announced in February 2023 the establishment of NeXT FOREST as a joint venture with Sumitomo Forestry.

name: Ikimono Eye
summary: According to BIMedia, AI processes continuous footage to record birds, covering 42 species in January 2026, with 60 bird and 15 mammal species planned during 2026.

name: Ikimono-log
summary: An online system that collects and provides information on living things, run by the Ministry of the Environment of Japan.

name: Innoqua
summary: A Japanese government magazine describes its AI image analysis for coral health and says its technology uses IoT and AI to control aquarium conditions.

name: Institute of Industrial Science, The University of Tokyo
summary: A Tokyo institute whose Takeuchi laboratory says it extracts ecological parameters from satellite data, and hosts a paper comparing machine learning models for mangrove above-ground biomass.

name: Iriomote Wildlife Conservation Center
summary: Base set up in 1995 for education, recovery programmes and research on Iriomote, collecting Iriomote cat data with automatic cameras, radio tracking and clinical tests, working with universities.

name: ITOCHU Technology Ventures, Inc.
summary: Named by Think Nature as its lead investor.

name: J Blue Credit
summary: A credit certified and issued after independent committee review by the Japan Blue Economy Association, which created and runs the scheme.

name: J-BMP
summary: A Japan biodiversity mapping project operated by Think Nature, whose marine maps cover Japan's waters from coast to deep sea and whose coastal maps cover 14 taxonomic groups on a 10 km mesh.

name: J-Litter
summary: A dataset built by the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology holding 12,029 original images, of which 4,197 contain seafloor litter.

name: JAMSTEC E-library of Deep-sea Images
summary: A dataset of images of deep-sea organisms and seafloor, run by the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology.

name: Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology
summary: National ocean research and development agency in Yokosuka that runs BISMaL, through its Data and information Technology Development Group, and is listed by POGO as a member from Japan.

name: Japan Biodiversity Observation Network
summary: Organisation aiming to promote biodiversity and ecosystem observation in Japan, use of the data and international cooperation, with partner links to GEO BON and the Asia-Pacific network.

name: Japan Bird Research Association
summary: Nonprofit for bird research and conservation that uses BirdNET; its October 2024 blog reports AI classifying 83 species from 23,229 sound files from one monitor.

name: Japan Blue Economy Association
summary: Body that created the J Blue Credit scheme and runs it as scheme administrator.

name: Japan Breeding Bird Atlas
summary: Breeding bird atlas run by the Biodiversity Center of Japan and the Japan Bird Research Association; its 2016 to 2021 round surveyed 2,344 sites and mapped 278 species.

name: Japan Fisheries Research and Education Agency
summary: Agency reporting stock surveys; a ministry evaluation of its fiscal 2024 work reports DINO as the most accurate model for detecting harmful bloom plankton in training images.

name: Japan Initiative for Biodiversity Information
summary: Programme for GBIF-related activity in Japan, funded by the education ministry through the National BioResource Project, with three institutions working together since fiscal 2022 according to the IUCN Japan committee.

name: Japan Integrated Biodiversity Information System
summary: A system built and run by the Biodiversity Center of Japan to digitise and manage survey results, publish them online and offer a Web-GIS of those results.

name: Japan International Research Center for Agricultural Sciences
summary: Research centre that published a 2020 research result on models for estimating mangrove aboveground biomass.

name: Japan Long Term Ecological Research Network
summary: A network of ecological monitoring sites for long-term ecological studies, established in November 2006 and partnered with the International Long Term Ecological Research Network.

name: Japan national goose and duck census
summary: Annual census run by the Ministry of the Environment Japan with prefectures since 1970; the 56th, in January 2025, covered about 8,700 sites with about 3,600 counters.

name: Japan National Trust Association
summary: After supporting local trusts, the association began acquiring land in 2007 and is saving for threatened species' habitats, while a notice reports joint land buying with Tsurui Village, Hokkaido.

name: Japan Nature Park Foundation
summary: A foundation that the Ministry of the Environment's list shows was designated a park management body on 14 July 2005 for Shiretoko National Park and 14 other parks.

name: Japan Science and Technology Agency
summary: Agency that implements SATREPS with JICA and AMED; the environmental project list includes a finished blue carbon ecosystems project in the Coral Triangle.

name: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science
summary: KAKENHI grants supported tropical forest biodiversity mapping from satellite images in 2019 to 2023; a KAKENHI report describes deep learning detection of wild Japanese macaques in video.

name: Japan Wildlife Research Center
summary: Foundation for research, policy support and public education on conserving nature, which the Wild Bird Society of Japan says is contracted with Bird Research for forest core sites.

name: JAXA and NTT seaweed bed monitoring research
summary: Research in which JAXA and NTT combine satellite images and AI to reduce seaweed bed monitoring work; JAXA says the AI's estimates still have to be validated.

name: Kagoshima University
summary: University whose news item reports an AI image recognition system for naming plant species, reaching 96.4% correct answers across 2,171 taxa.

name: Kajima Corporation
summary: Company that has a case study listed under its name by Deep Forestry, which it is linked to as a user.

name: Kamakura Scenic Preservation Society
summary: A society that, according to a Ministry of the Environment report, owns three green spaces in Kamakura of about 1.5, 1.2 and 5 hectares, acquired between 1966 and 2006.

name: Kami-Sarobetsu Wetland Nature Restoration Council
summary: A council whose rules give its purpose as discussing the matters needed to promote the nature restoration of Kami-Sarobetsu.

name: Kan-Hakusan Protection and Use Management Association
summary: An association that the Ministry of the Environment designated a park management body for Hakusan National Park on 16 December 2021, with work including conservation and maintenance of visitor facilities.

name: Kanagawa blue carbon autonomous underwater drone demonstration
summary: Proposed demonstration with BlueArch; in May 2026 the prefecture announced support and planned a kelp measurement trial at Jogashima in July 2026.

name: Kanagawa Prefectural Government
summary: Government body that says its method was the first in Japan to be recognised for J Blue Credit.

name: Kanagawa Prefecture
summary: Prefecture whose autonomous underwater drone method produced a credit certified in December of the year before a May 2026 release.

name: Kanagawa Trust Midori Foundation
summary: The foundation says it campaigns and drove Koajiro Forest conservation with citizen groups, while the prefecture owns the green spaces acquired through purchase or donation.

name: Kanagawa underwater drone seaweed bed monitoring
summary: Project run by the prefectural government with BlueArch and a Keio laboratory; an AI model for seaweed cover was reported in December 2025 and 9.6 t of credits certified.

name: Kanto Regional Forest Office
summary: The Forestry Agency lists the Ogasawara Islands Forest Ecosystem Reserve under this office and describes forest ecosystem reserves as the protection measure for the Ogasawara World Natural Heritage site.

name: KEEP Association
summary: Japanese environmental education foundation which, according to a Ministry of the Environment profile, works across Japan and took on management of Nasu Heisei no Mori in Nikko National Park in 2011.

name: Keidanren Nature Conservation Fund
summary: Fund supporting private conservation projects in developing regions, mainly the Asia-Pacific, at about 160 million yen annually; its 2016 overview dates council support to 1993.

name: Kinki-Chugoku Regional Forest Office
summary: Regional forest office which says that, as of April 2026, it has designated 81 protected forests covering 22,247 hectares in its area.

name: Kiritappu Wetland National Trust
summary: Trust which, according to a Ministry of the Environment case study, buys land in Kiritappu Wetland, protecting it from development, and is based in Hamanaka town, Akkeshi district, Hokkaido.

name: Kobe University
summary: University with a laboratory developing environmental DNA analysis and leading surveys; OpenAlex groups 65 Japanese-affiliated works since 2022 in topic T12640 under it.

name: Kobe University Research Center for Inland Seas
summary: Kobe University centre that, according to its 2019 guide, operates two seaweed bed sites for Monitoring Sites 1000 and acts as the Awajishima JaLTER core site.

name: KoeTurri
summary: Programme built by Hylable that identifies animal calls around the clock with waterproof IoT microphones and AI, and said in September 2026 it could identify 151 species.

name: Kokusai Kogyo Co., Ltd.
summary: Company that runs the Mimamori forest information service and Mimamori Global, and analysed forest change on about 254,000 ha of company forest using its Mimamori service.

name: Kubokawa Iihatov Nature Restoration Council
summary: Council named by the Ministry of the Environment as applicant for the Kubokawa Iihatov site in Ichinoseki, Iwate, listed under the ministry's nature symbiosis site certification begun in fiscal 2023.

name: Kushiro Wetland Nature Restoration Council
summary: Council which, according to the Hokkaido Regional Development Bureau, was set up to bring residents, NGOs, local governments, agencies and experts together to agree and carry out restoration work at Kushiro Wetland.

name: Kushiro Wetland Wildlife Center
summary: Ministry-run facility with a public exhibition and research on rare bird care, using remote cameras on birds in rehabilitation and, says the ministry's guide, wetland monitoring and wildlife surveys.

name: Kyoto University
summary: University with 14 OpenAlex-listed works since 2021 in Ecology under a Japanese affiliation, ranking second among listed Japanese institutions, and a staff profile listing dugong drone-image and sound detection papers.

name: Kyushu Regional Forest Office
summary: The office says its protected forests are designated to conserve ecosystems and protect valuable species, and describes national forest land generally as lying mainly in remote mountains.

name: Kyushu University
summary: University whose forest planning laboratory lists monitoring and assessment of forest resources by ground survey and remote sensing.

name: Lake Biwa 100-point eDNA survey
summary: Project planned to detect fish at 100 points on the lake shore, run by Ryukoku University's biodiversity centre and held yearly as a citizen survey across Shiga since fiscal 2021.

name: Lake Biwa Branch Office, National Institute for Environmental Studies
summary: National Institute for Environmental Studies branch office that develops Lake Biwa monitoring methods using remote sensing, including satellite, fixed-camera and drone images of aquatic plants, and points to a specimen database.

name: Leave a Nest
summary: Organisation whose stated strength on the platform is developing the next generation and local conservation systems.

name: Maeda Ippoen Foundation
summary: Foundation described in a Japan Tourism Agency text prepared in fiscal 2018 as managing roughly 3,600 hectares around Lake Akan, conserving natural forests and tending planted forests.

name: Mapry
summary: Organisation that announced the mapry AI concept.

name: mapry Map
summary: Programme run by Mapry that automatically produces forest resource figures and draft plans.

name: Mie University
summary: University whose research profile says satellites and drones monitor the state and change of farmland and forests, with machine learning as a listed keyword.

name: MiFish primers
summary: Set of universal PCR primers for metabarcoding environmental DNA from fishes, built by Masaki Miya.

name: Mimamori forest information service
summary: Programme run by Kokusai Kogyo that analyses forest measurements to show tree distribution and numbers efficiently.

name: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, Japan
summary: Japanese ministry commissioning the marine life big data programme, endorsing the running of BI-DDBJ, and listed with JAXA as a CEOS member agency.

name: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, Japan
summary: Japanese ministry whose Ports and Harbours Bureau promotes blue infrastructure, including seaweed beds and tidal flats, across Japan.

name: Ministry of the Environment, Japan
summary: Japanese ministry that runs the Biodiversity Center of Japan and Ikimono-log, funds the Asia-Pacific Network for Global Change Research, and certified 610 private conserved areas by end of June 2026.

name: MiteMiru Forest
summary: Programme run by PASCO Corporation that uses satellite images and AI interpretation to monitor logging and reforestation areas, adopted by 53 municipalities as of October 2024.

name: Mitsubishi Electric
summary: Company that says it developed ALOS-2 and that its ME Innovation Fund invested in Archeda, which it funds.

name: Mitsui & Co. Environment Fund
summary: A programme run by Mitsui & Co., which decided the fund's 2017 research grants.

name: Mitsui & Co., Ltd.
summary: Company headquartered in Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, that decided the 2017 research grants of its Environment Fund.

name: Miyagi Izunuma and Uchinuma Environmental Conservation Foundation

summary: Project led by the University of Exeter on scalable ecosystem monitoring in Kenya, using vibrational sensing for soil health and human-wildlife coexistence.

name: Atlas
summary: Twende Green Planet's platform of maps and analysis, with an AI analyst that answers plain-language questions.

name: AZ Forest Kenya
summary: AstraZeneca reforestation project in six counties of western Kenya, pledging up to six million trees over more than 3,500 hectares, that plans to use a deep learning model on drone and satellite images to monitor tree growth and carbon.

name: Bahari Hai
summary: Organisation based in Watamu, Kenya, that works with fishing communities, government agencies and the private sector on marine awareness, with programmes on sea turtle nest monitoring, photo identification and bycatch mitigation.

name: Big Life Foundation
summary: Conservation organisation in the Amboseli area of Kenya that uses thermal drones to reduce conflict between elephants and people, according to Mongabay.

name: Bioacoustic approaches for ecosystem monitoring and conservation
summary: DSAIL project that shrinks the Perch bird-classification model to run on low-cost edge devices, with a prototype deployed at the DeKUT Conservancy that reports over LoRaWAN.

name: Biodiversity Atlas of Kenya
summary: Web portal of Kenyan biodiversity data for decisions at national and county level, built by the African Conservation Centre with JRS funding.

name: BirdPy
summary: Software from the Kenya Bioacoustics Project that studies acoustic indices of biodiversity and recognises bird species from calls and songs, using the bob toolkit.

name: Boma and cattle detection in the Maasai Mara
summary: Microsoft AI for Good work that detects livestock enclosures and cattle in satellite imagery of the Maasai Mara, to help NGOs such as the Kenya Wildlife Trust target predator-proof bomas.

name: Borana Conservancy
summary: 32,000-acre conservancy in Laikipia that, per The Star, tracks wildlife in real time with EarthRanger.

name: Building Community Capacity to Conduct Biodiversity Assessments integrating Indigenous Knowledge with Technology
summary: JRS-funded project, with a 2025 grant of 99,900 US dollars over 18 months to NMK and Earth Acre, for community biodiversity assessments combining indigenous knowledge with technology.

name: Carbon-Eye
summary: Tool estimating above-ground biomass and carbon stock across Kenya's 47 counties from satellite and environmental data with a machine-learning ensemble in Google Earth Engine.

name: Centre for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, Dedan Kimathi University of Technology
summary: Research centre at Dedan Kimathi University of Technology that builds computer vision and acoustic tools for wildlife and forest monitoring in Kenya.

name: Centre for Ecosystem Restoration Kenya
summary: Kenyan restoration organisation and an award winner in the Masai Mara Satellite Sandbox, which supplied high-resolution satellite imagery.

name: Centre for Transformative Research and Development
summary: Charitable trust in Nanyuki that runs the Social and Hydrological Information Platform and other GIS and remote sensing tools for the Ewaso Ng'iro basin.

name: Chehe Community Forest Association
summary: Volunteer group that, since 2009 and working with the Kenya Forest Service, has restored 43 hectares of forest while protecting the remaining Afromontane forests of the Chehe block on Mount Kenya.

name: Chepkitale Indigenous People Development Project
summary: Partner of Forest Peoples Programme in community-based biodiversity monitoring on Mount Elgon; in October 2023 five of its staff were trained to train community monitors, with eight villages planned.

name: Cheptongei Community Forest Association
summary: One of six community forest associations in the Cherangani Hills running tree nurseries for restoration; its nursery produced more than 160,000 seedlings.

name: Cherangani Community Forest Association
summary: One of six community forest associations in the Cherangani Hills running tree nurseries; together their seedlings were planted over 290 hectares to restore degraded areas inside state forests.

name: Chesoi Community Forest Association
summary: One of six community forest associations in the Cherangani Hills running tree nurseries; together their seedlings were planted over 290 hectares to restore degraded areas inside state forests.

name: Chuka University
summary: Kenyan university whose computer scientists publish on deep learning for wildlife identification.

name: Co-designing Kenyan-Danish AI and Robotics for Sustainability and Impact
summary: Seed project to build an education and innovation base for drones, robotics and AI in East Africa, following the WildDrone network's work on conservation in Kenya.

name: Community Forest Association of Vanga, Jimbo and Kiwegu
summary: Community forest association that runs the Vanga Blue Forest project with the Kenya Forest Service and is involved in restoring 460 hectares of the mangrove forest's original 4,428 hectares.

name: ConservaCam
summary: Maker of solar-powered camera traps with on-device AI, which it has deployed in Nairobi National Park.

name: Conservancy Analytics and Dashboard
summary: Dashboard giving conservancy managers in northern Kenya analysis-ready Earth observation data, built with Digital Earth Africa data and infrastructure.

name: Conservancy Management and Monitoring System
summary: Simple system for monitoring wildlife, attitudes and vegetation trends in conservancies, used by Northern Rangelands Trust, whose 2014 to 2019 key species population trends are based on its Wildlife CoMMS abundance index.

name: CORDIO East Africa
summary: Non-profit marine research organisation registered in Kenya that works across the Western Indian Ocean and runs a data and information portal.

name: Cottar’s Wildlife Conservancy Trust
summary: Trust that co-manages Olderkesi Conservancy with the Olderkesi Wildlife Community Trust, renting the land from its Maasai owners.

name: Curbing Illegal Logging Patterns Using Sound-based Detection Techniques
summary: Project that puts IoT devices with AI in Kenyan community forests to detect the sound of cutting tools and send alerts, with carbon stock measurements of the effect.

name: Dakatcha Woodland Conservation Group
summary: Group through which local communities, together with the Kamale Mazingira community-based organisation, manage Kamale Nature Reserve, whose forest block measures 1,800 acres.

name: Database of Bioacoustics Monitoring in Smallholder Agroecosystems, Kenya
summary: Dataset of bioacoustics monitoring on Kenyan smallholder farms, with authors at the International Center for Tropical Agriculture.

name: Dawida Biodiversity Conservation Group
summary: Group taking part in an adopt-a-forest scheme to restore degraded forest landscapes in the Taita Hills key biodiversity area.

name: Dedan Kimathi University of Technology
summary: University in Nyeri, Kenya, home of the Centre for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence.

name: Developing a Freshwater Biodiversity Information System for the Tana River Basin, Kenya
summary: JRS-funded project led by Siro Masinde that, per a September 2018 announcement, planned to mobilise and publish biodiversity data to assess the basin's status; a mid Tana fish occurrence dataset was created for its portal.

name: Digital Radio Network and Early Fire Video Detection (Kenya Forest Service)
summary: Kenya Forest Service and France 22 million euro project for forest fire detection by video and digital radio in the Mau, Aberdare and Mount Kenya ecosystems.

name: Directorate of Resource Surveys and Remote Sensing
summary: Kenyan government remote sensing body in Nairobi, listed as an author affiliation on a random forest land cover map of the Greater Masai Mara.

name: Directorate of Surveys
summary: Kenya's official government agency for land surveying and mapping, within the State Department for Lands.

name: DSAIL Porini
summary: Annotated camera-trap images from a Kenyan conservancy covering six categories of grazing mammals.

name: DSAIL-Annotate
summary: Application in development at DSAIL, with Mugie Conservancy, that processes large sets of camera trap images and reports species statistics.

name: Earth Observation Innovation Laboratories
summary: Kenya Space Agency programme of laboratories providing a cloud environment for satellite data and turning research into products and services.

name: EarthAcre
summary: Nature asset company working on Kenyan community lands, which quantifies nature outcomes and pays landowners directly; JRS funded its biodiversity surveys using indigenous knowledge and data technology.

name: EarthRanger deployment at Maasai Mara National Reserve
summary: Adoption of EarthRanger at the Maasai Mara National Reserve, launched by Narok County in 2024 with 51 Degrees.

name: East African Wild Life Society
summary: JRS reported in February 2023 that this funded advocacy organisation had worked for over 60 years and was undertaking a project providing biodiversity information on Lake Ol Bolossat.

name: Eburu Forest biodiversity monitoring
summary: Project run by Wilder Institute with Rhino Ark and the Bongo Surveillance Project; in January 2023 it aimed to monitor biodiversity, focused on mountain bongo habitat, after a 2019 camera study with 50 cameras.

name: Eco-consult
summary: Kenyan ecosystem science consultancy whose services include sensor networks, remote monitoring, machine learning and decision-support systems.

name: EcoScope
summary: Open-source module for analysing EarthRanger data, developed by the Mara Elephant Project according to Nawiri Group.

name: Egerton University
summary: Kenyan university with an author using geospatial and machine learning methods to simulate ecosystem services.

name: Elephant Drone Behavior Tracking
summary: Collaboration between the Colossal Foundation and Save the Elephants, from November 2023 to May 2026, that used drones and machine learning to track elephant movements and social interactions.

name: ElephantBook
summary: Mara Elephant Project software that uses machine learning to identify individual elephants from features such as tusks and ear shape.

name: Elgeyo Community Forest Association
summary: One of six community forest associations in the Cherangani Hills running tree nurseries; together their seedlings were planted over 290 hectares to restore degraded areas inside state forests.

name: EMANCIPATE
summary: Proposed project led by Kenyan marine biologist Levy Otwoma to use third-generation sequencing of environmental DNA to detect fish biodiversity in African waters.

name: Enarau Conservancy
summary: Conservancy covering 866 hectares, established to expand conservation areas, restore degraded farmland and protect threatened habitats.

name: Enonkishu Conservancy
summary: Conservancy of 5,928 acres at the northernmost point of the Greater Mara Ecosystem, with 42 landowners and two tourism partners.

name: Estimating Wildlife Populations with AI Software
summary: Project at Mpala Research Centre applying AI and machine learning to wildlife population estimates from image-based data, led from the University of Arizona.

name: Ewaso Lions
summary: Kenyan lion conservation group that uses GPS collars and a customised SMART app with its Warriors and Lion Governors.

name: Eyes in the Courtroom
summary: Partnership between WildlifeDirect and the Judiciary Training Institute that collects wildlife crime case data from Kenyan courts.

name: Forest Alert
summary: Rapid deforestation monitoring system based on Copernicus Sentinel-2 images, co-developed by the University of Leicester and the Kenya Forest Service.

name: Forest Restored A.I
summary: Kenyan-based startup using AI as an early warning system for deforestation, wildfires and charcoal burning, with solar-powered devices in forests. Its wording closely matches M-Situ's and the link between the two is not stated.

name: Friends of Dunga Swamp
summary: Group that restores degraded swamp areas by planting papyrus, runs conservation awareness activities, and owns and manages a boardwalk over the swamp.

name: Friends of Karura Forest
summary: Community forest association co-managing Karura Forest Reserve with the Kenya Forest Service under a 2021 to 2041 agreement; it led replanting that raised indigenous cover from 25% in 2009 to over 40%.

name: Friends of Kinangop Plateau
summary: Group that leads conservation efforts on the Kinangop Grasslands and has been instrumental in habitat conservation and restoration.

name: Gatsby Africa Geospatial Forestry Platform
summary: GIS platform for farm and plantation forestry, developed by Gatsby Africa, with remote sensing data, site and species matching, and carbon monitoring.

name: GBIF Kenya
summary: Kenya's national node in the GBIF network, listed by GBIF with observer status and a Nairobi postal address.

name: GeoSense Solutions
summary: Nairobi startup building AI geospatial tools from satellite and drone data to monitor coasts and inland water, and mapping wildlife habitats.

name: Global Rangelands Data Platform
summary: Data platform led by ILRI to consolidate information on the world's rangelands, shown before launch in November 2025.

name: Gr8 Cheetah Census
summary: Photo-based census of individual cheetahs in Kenya, complementing the National Cheetah Survey.

name: Great Grevy's Rally
summary: Citizen science photographic census of Grevy's zebra across Kenya, first run in 2016, which identifies individuals by their stripe patterns.

name: Green Belt Movement
summary: Organisation running watershed-based ecosystem restoration across Kenya, partnering with the Kenya Forest Service on the Mount Kenya and Aberdare water towers, with more than 5,000 community nursery groups.

name: Grevy's Zebra Trust
summary: Conservation organisation for Grevy's zebra that publishes the Great Grevy's Rally photographic census.

name: Hirola Conservation Programme
summary: Conservation programme that in 2025 expanded giraffe monitoring through its Somali Giraffe Project, with 29 giraffes collared according to its annual report, and used camera traps to study behaviour.

name: I&M Foundation
summary: Foundation that partners with the Kenya Community Development Foundation on the Young Innovators Challenge, which funded M-Situ.

name: ID PES aerial survey of Laikipia and Isiolo
summary: Aerial survey over 18 days in March 2025 under the Wyss Academy's ID PES project, producing more than 10 terabytes of imagery of about a quarter of Laikipia County and parts of Isiolo.

name: Il Ngwesi Community Conservancy
summary: Community conservancy that was one of the first two established in northern Kenya.

name: International Livestock Research Institute
summary: Livestock research institute that publishes rangeland work including a study using AI and remote sensing to detect invasive Prosopis juliflora in Baringo County.

name: International Training Centre for Environmental Research
summary: Non-profit in Siaya County, western Kenya, that monitors biodiversity through geo-referenced photographs and shows them in its public Macrobiome Image Archive.

name: Isaaten Conservancy
summary: Conservancy of 2,600 hectares of protected land in the eastern Maasai Mara, where landowners lease land for conservation.

name: Isiolo County Conservancies Association
summary: Association of community conservancies in Isiolo County that uses Earth observation analytics on a dashboard built on Digital Earth Africa data.

name: Isiolo County Government
summary: County government recorded as managing the Samburu, Buffalo Springs and Shaba National Reserves, which cover about 620 square kilometres combined.

name: Jazamiti
summary: Kenyan government mobile app that documents, tracks and monitors tree planting and growth, as part of the 15 billion trees target.

name: Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology
summary: Kenyan university whose authors use machine learning and geospatial data to predict forest cover change and carbon stocks.

name: KABR
summary: Open CC0 dataset of drone video of giraffes, plains zebras and Grévy's zebras, filmed at Mpala Research Centre in January 2023, for animal behaviour recognition.

name: Kakamega Environmental Education Programme
summary: Programme that works closely with government agencies to conserve Kakamega Forest and involves local residents in participatory forest management.

name: Kakamega Forest Community Forest Association
summary: Community forest association that works closely with government agencies to conserve Kakamega Forest and involves local residents in participatory forest management.

name: Kamale Mazingira Community-based Organization
summary: Community-based organisation through which local communities, together with the Dakatcha Woodland Conservation Group, manage Kamale Nature Reserve, whose forest block measures 1,800 acres.

name: Kapyego Community Forest Association
summary: One of six community forest associations in the Cherangani Hills running tree nurseries; together their seedlings were planted over 290 hectares to restore degraded areas inside state forests.

name: Kasigau Corridor REDD+ Project
summary: REDD+ project of 500,000 acres of dryland forest in the Tsavo ecosystem, monitored with rangers, camera traps and Sensing Clues tools.

name: KEFRIApp
summary: Web and mobile platform giving a guide to matching tree species to sites for sustainable tree growing.

name: KenGen
summary: Kenyan power company that uses drones and GIS to track its environmental restoration work, per its foundation's site.

name: KenGen drone and GIS restoration mapping
summary: Geospatial mapping by KenGen with drones and GIS to track forest restoration at its Ngong Wind Power Station and other conservation work.

name: Kenya Afforestation Decision Support Tool
summary: Web tool that simulates the effects of climate change on forest growth to guide forest planning in Kenya, developed by SEI, Colorado State University and the Kenya Forestry Research Institute.

name: Kenya Bird Map
summary: Citizen science atlas documenting the distribution and status of all birds across Kenya, on a grid of pentads of about 9 km by 9 km.

name: Kenya Bird of Prey Trust
summary: Organisation named by the Peregrine Fund as a research partner providing expertise and mentorship for capturing and tagging raptors, and which trains vulture liaison officers, scouts and rangers around the Maasai Mara and Amboseli.

name: Kenya Bird Trends
summary: Online platform launched in August 2024 by the Tropical Biology Association that tracks changes in the range of Kenya's birds on interactive maps.

name: Kenya Community Development Foundation
summary: Kenyan foundation that implements the Young Innovators Challenge, which funded the AI forest monitoring startup M-Situ.

name: Kenya Conservancies Fund
summary: Small grant facility for Kenyan conservancies, whose 2025 call covered ecological monitoring among other themes.

name: Kenya Flying Labs
summary: Kenyan drone group, a local partner in the WildDrone project and involved in a pilot of drones for forest monitoring in Kirisia, Samburu County.

name: Kenya Forest Service
summary: Kenya's forest agency, which houses the National Forest Monitoring System and is piloting an AI early warning system at Ngong Forest.

name: Kenya Forestry Research Institute
summary: Kenya's forestry research institute, named by the Global Forest Observations Initiative among bodies with experience in forest inventories and remote sensing.

name: Kenya Mangrove Portal
summary: Application on Kenya's National Forest Monitoring System platform for mangrove information.

name: Kenya Marine and Fisheries Research Institute
summary: Kenyan marine research institute, a collaborator in the Tech4Nature AI reef monitoring project at Kisite-Mpunguti.

name: Kenya Marine Mammal Network
summary: Network established in 2011 by government and non-governmental agencies for consistent marine mammal data collection on the Kenyan coast; a 2021 paper described more than 100 contributors, with reports going to Watamu.

name: Kenya national coffee geo-mapping
summary: National exercise that maps coffee farms from satellite imagery and field checks to show coffee is grown on non-deforested land, for the EU Deforestation Regulation.

name: Kenya Natural Resource Atlas and Geoportal
summary: National atlas and online geoportal that maps and documents Kenya's natural resources, launched by the National Land Commission and FAO. Counties were asked to use it as a baseline for their own atlases.

name: Kenya Ocean Biodiversity Information System
summary: Kenya's national node of the Ocean Biodiversity Information System, run by the Kenya Marine and Fisheries Research Institute.

name: Kenya sovereign LoRa Network Server
summary: National LoRaWAN cloud platform for wildlife tracking data, launched by Kenya Wildlife Service with Connected Conservation Foundation, Actility by Netmore and Konza Technopolis. It keeps tracking data in Kenya under KWS control.

name: Kenya Space Agency
summary: Kenya's space agency, which leads Project Centinela on mountain bongo habitat and ran a spaceborne AI programme for university students.

name: Kenya Water Towers Agency
summary: Agency that looks after Kenya's water towers. Its chairperson wrote that it uses GIS, GPS and drones to map forest cover and monitor degradation.

name: Kenya Waterbird Counts
summary: Annual count of waterbirds in wetlands as an indicator of wetland health, run by National Museums of Kenya, Kenya Wildlife Service and Nature Kenya; January 2023 counts included Lake Naivasha and Lake Baringo.

name: Kenya wetland mapping with Earth observation
summary: Training on wetland mapping with Earth observation for Kenyan agencies, run by the Regional Centre for Mapping of Resources for Development with NEMA and supported by Digital Earth Africa.

name: Kenya Wildlife Conservancies Association
summary: National membership body for Kenya's conservancies, which published the National Wildlife Conservancies Map and manages the Kenya Conservancies Fund.

name: Kenya Wildlife Service
summary: Kenya's wildlife agency, which runs AI-enabled thermal cameras, drones and the EarthRanger platform in its protection work.

name: Kenya Wildlife Trust
summary: NGO named by Microsoft as a user of its satellite-based boma and cattle detection in the Maasai Mara.

name: Kenyatta University
summary: Kenyan university, a local partner in the WildDrone project on autonomous drones and computer vision for wildlife monitoring.

name: Kessup Community Forest Association
summary: One of six Cherangani Hills community forest associations running tree nurseries; its nursery raised over 400,000 seedlings in Kessup forest, one of thirteen fragments of the Cherangani Hills Forest.

name: Kifaru Rising Project
summary: Collaboration between FLIR Systems and WWF to deploy thermal imaging against rhino poaching at 10 locations in Kenya. FLIR pledged $3 million in technology, engineering help and training.

name: Kirisia forest drone monitoring pilot
summary: Pilot by FAO Kenya with the Kenya Forest Service and Kenya Wildlife Service to use drones to monitor forest health in Kirisia, Samburu County.

name: Konza Technopolis
summary: Kenyan government technology city that hosts the national LoRaWAN platform for wildlife tracking data and a pilot of M-Situ's AI forest devices. It co-hosted the 2026 conservation tech forum.

name: Kuruwitu Conservation and Welfare Association
summary: Association that established a 30-hectare no-take sanctuary in 2006, one of Kenya's earliest community-driven locally managed marine areas, which the Kuruwitu CBO manages.

name: Kutuma
summary: Natural State's application for taking in and sorting field data, mainly using remote sensors or AI.

name: Laikipia Conservancies Association
summary: Association of conservancies in Laikipia whose Data Hub initiative brings member data from SMART, EarthRanger and other monitoring tools together.

name: Lamu mangrove alert command centre
summary: Kenya Forest Service centre in Lamu, set up with Wetlands International, that checks satellite mangrove alerts from Global Mangrove Watch before sending patrols.

name: Lamu Marine Conservation Trust
summary: Local community-based organisation that set out to create a 741-acre community-managed marine protected area at Kiweni; by December 2009 members had mapped and demarcated 3 square kilometres, and scouts had confiscated illegal fishing gear.

name: Land Degradation Index Map
summary: Land degradation map products handed to Kenya's Directorate of Resource Surveys and Remote Sensing by RCMRD under the GMES and Africa project, used to guide tree planting across the 47 counties.

name: Lekurruki Conservancy Trust
summary: Conservancy of the Mukogodo Maasai, recorded in the Global ICCA Database as 800 hectares within an 11,953 hectare group ranch, used for wildlife conservation and tourism.

name: Lemek Conservancy
summary: Conservancy of 17,350 acres and 350 landowners, formed by members who left the Koiyaki Lemek Community Wildlife Trust and registered in 2009.

name: Lewa Wildlife Conservancy
summary: Private conservancy in northern Kenya, one of the reserves on the Northern Rangelands Trust's IoT conservation network.

name: Lion early warning at Loisaba Conservancy
summary: Project with Lion Landscapes and partners at Loisaba Conservancy using GPS collars, alarm systems and mobile apps to prevent lion attacks on livestock.

name: Lion Guardians
summary: Kenya-based lion conservation group that launched the LINC facial recognition database of lions in 2015, per Scientific American.

name: Lion Landscapes
summary: Organisation working on lion conservation that, with The Nature Conservancy and partners at Loisaba, uses collars and mobile apps to warn herders of lions.

name: Local Ocean Trust
summary: Organisation formed in 2002 out of Watamu Turtle Watch, which started in 1997; a newsletter reported over 15 years of nest monitoring, a research database and a hatching model for predicting nest emergences.

name: Loisaba Conservancy
summary: 58,000-acre conservancy in northern Laikipia that works with Connected Conservation Foundation on mapping the invasive Opuntia cactus with high-resolution satellite imagery and machine learning.

name: Loita Hills Community and Wildlife Conservancy
summary: Trust-registered conservancy covering 2,500 hectares, established in 2023.

name: Lolldaiga Conservancy Trust
summary: Trust established at the closing of the purchase of Lolldaiga Hills Ranch in Laikipia to secure the land's long-term conservation; the ranch also has a wildlife conservation easement.

name: Ltome-Katip
summary: Project with Samburu and Shuar communities labelling animal sounds to build datasets for machine learning on human-wildlife conflict, at Namunyak Conservancy in Kenya and in Ecuador.

name: M-Situ
summary: Kenyan startup making solar sensors with machine learning that detect illegal logging and charcoal burning and alert the Kenya Forest Service.

name: m-Twiga
summary: AI and IoT camera system from Safaricom, Vodafone and WWF that detects animals and alerts rangers, tested at Mara Siana Community Conservancy.

name: Maasai Mara boma and structure mapping
summary: Kenya Wildlife Trust and Microsoft work using AI to map structures in the Maasai Mara, including livestock enclosures.

name: Maasai Mara LoRaWAN deployment
summary: Sensor network in the Maasai Mara used with EarthRanger at the Maasai Mara Conservation Centre to monitor wildlife, patrols and tourism.

name: Maasai Mara University
