summary: Kenyan university whose authors publish on ecoacoustics for ecosystem monitoring and machine learning for wetland restoration.

name: Maasai Moran Conservancy
summary: Conservancy of 15,000 acres with 250 landowners, run by a committee and sharing 20 rangers with two neighbouring trusts.

name: Macrobiome Image Archive
summary: Public archive of geo-referenced biodiversity photographs from the ITCER site in Ng'iya, western Kenya.

name: Mangrove Forest Alerts System
summary: Kenya Forest Service system that uses satellite imagery, sensor data and machine learning to flag mangrove degradation, with community scouts trained to report on alerts.

name: Mara Conservancy
summary: Not-for-profit company set up to manage the 510 square kilometre Mara Triangle, starting operations on 12 June 2001; its management agreement passed to Narok County Government, with a ten-year agreement signed in 2016.

name: Mara Elephant Project
summary: Conservation organisation in Kenya's Maasai Mara that uses drones, some with thermal imaging, to manage human-elephant conflict and monitor herds.

name: Mara Naboisho Conservancy
summary: Conservancy next to the Maasai Mara National Reserve, covering over 52,000 acres contributed by 636 landowners.

name: Mara North Conservancy
summary: Not-for-profit entity set up in 2009 as a partnership between tourism partners and 783 Maasai landowners, looking after over 29,170 hectares bordering the Maasai Mara National Reserve.

name: Mara Predator Conservation Programme
summary: Kenya Wildlife Trust's long-term predator programme, which publishes lion identification catalogues and collects field data with customised Cybertracker applications.

name: Mara Ripoi Conservancy
summary: Conservancy of 24,500 acres, run as a partnership between landowners and two tourism camps.

name: Mara Siana Conservancy
summary: Self-described not-for-profit organisation, originally established in 2004, that employs 50 local rangers.

name: Masai Mara Satellite Sandbox
summary: Connected Conservation Foundation and Airbus Foundation initiative giving local teams a 30 cm Pléiades Neo mosaic to apply Earth observation and AI in the Masai Mara, from pangolin habitat to invasive species and elephant geo-fences.

name: Mbokishi Mara Conservation Area
summary: Conservation area established in September 2021 next to Enonkishu Conservancy, comprising 600 families, with five communities committing their land to wildlife conservation.

name: Mida Creek Conservation and Awareness Group
summary: Nature Kenya Site Support Group that, at an event held with ASFADA, saw over 200 people plant 6,000 mangrove seedlings to restore degraded parts of Mida Creek.

name: Mijikenda Council of Elders
summary: Body of elders formed to promote the protection and conservation of the sacred kaya forests of the Mijikenda in Kilifi County.

name: Mikoko Pamoja
summary: Community-led mangrove restoration and conservation project of the Gazi community, covering 117 of the 615 hectares of mangrove in Gazi Bay.

name: Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Forestry (Kenya)
summary: Kenya's environment ministry, which oversees the Kenya Forest Service and KEFRI and holds the national focal point for the Convention on Biological Diversity.

name: Mirema Community Forest Association
summary: Community forest association whose reforestation prompted Kenya Forest Service support; according to Aloo, at least 405 hectares are restored, and the service expects full restoration by 2027.

name: Miti360
summary: Multi-modal machine learning dataset from DSAIL at Dedan Kimathi University of Technology, built from a 770-hectare reforested stand in Kieni Forest in the Aberdare ecosystem.

name: MothNet
summary: Lightweight model from DSAIL's Project AMI, built to identify moths on a microchip inside an insect trap. Field trials at the DeKUT Conservancy are planned.

name: Mount Elgon Conservation and Heritage Initiative
summary: Organisation working to restore degraded landscapes and conserve biodiversity in the Mount Elgon ecosystem, including reforestation, with a Nairobi address.

name: Mount Kenya Trust
summary: Non-profit in Nanyuki working on Mount Kenya's environment, wildlife and communities, which uses SMART and EarthRanger for patrols and monitoring.

name: Mount Kenya Wildlife Conservancy
summary: Conservancy at Mount Kenya that People Daily reports uses AI-powered cameras to identify individual mountain bongos, and a partner in Project Centinela.

name: Mount Suswa Conservancy
summary: Conservancy started in 2008 as Mount Suswa Conservation Trust, with a board of trustees drawn from eight cluster villages on and around the mountain.

name: Mpala Live
summary: Live field cameras at Mpala in Laikipia for watching wildlife in real time.

name: Mpala Research Centre
summary: Research centre in Laikipia, Kenya, that hosts AI wildlife estimation work and the WildDrone hack-a-thon.

name: Mt. Kenya Biodiversity Conservation Group
summary: Site Support Group for the Mount Kenya Forest KBA that operates three tree nurseries and worked with others to restore the Nanyuki River with indigenous trees and gabions.

name: Mugie Conservancy
summary: Conservancy in Laikipia working with DSAIL on an application that processes camera-trap images, and supplying images for Grévy's zebra work.

name: Mukutan Conservancy
summary: Self-described expansive conservancy in Laikipia on the edge of the Great Rift Valley, with a stated mandate to conserve biodiversity and natural resources.

name: Mumoni Site Support Group
summary: Local community group working to conserve, protect and restore biodiversity in Mumoni Hill Forest Reserve, including biodiversity monitoring.

name: Murguiywet CBO
summary: Nature Kenya Site Support Group that has led restoration work in North Nandi Forest since launching in 2010, including recruiting community scouts to patrol the forest.

name: Mutitu Community Forest Association
summary: One of two community forest associations in a 2026 to 2031 participatory forest management plan with the Kenya Forest Service, covering 13,000 hectares overall, including 1,958 hectares in Mutitu Hill Forest Reserve.

name: Muumoni Community Forest Association
summary: One of two community forest associations in a 2026 to 2031 participatory forest management plan with the Kenya Forest Service, covering 13,000 hectares overall, including 11,031 hectares in Mumoni Hill Forest Reserve.

name: Mwaluganje Elephant Sanctuary
summary: Sanctuary established in 1993 on land leased by about 4,000 farmers and landowners, with its chairman helping run the reserve.

name: Namunyak Community Conservancy
summary: One of the first two community conservancies established in northern Kenya, described as a local institution run for and by indigenous people to manage community-owned land.

name: Narok County Government
summary: County government that adopted EarthRanger for the Maasai Mara National Reserve and is part of a LoRaWAN deployment there.

name: Nashulai Maasai Conservancy
summary: Maasai-founded, directed and run conservancy that protects a migratory corridor, covering 10,000 acres with 195 landowners.

name: National Drought Management Authority
summary: Kenyan authority whose drought monitoring rests on satellite vegetation condition data, using a processing chain set up with BOKU in Vienna.

name: National Environment Management Authority
summary: Kenyan environment authority that hosts the National Biodiversity Clearing House Mechanism pages, with national biodiversity reports.

name: National Forest Monitoring System (Kenya)
summary: Kenya's national framework for monitoring forests and forest emissions, with satellite land monitoring, a national forest inventory and a forest information platform.

name: National Land Commission
summary: Kenyan commission that launched the Kenya Natural Resource Atlas and Geoportal with FAO and partner institutions.

name: National Museums of Kenya
summary: Kenya's national museum body, a GBIF data publisher and a joint runner of the Kenya Bird Map through its Ornithology Section.

name: National Recovery and Action Plan for the Mountain Bongo 2026–2030
summary: National plan that combines AI-enabled cameras, camera traps and GPS tracking with breeding and habitat restoration to rebuild the mountain bongo population.

name: National Wildlife Census (Kenya)
summary: Kenya's national count of wildlife, carried out by the Wildlife Research and Training Institute with partners, mainly by hand with planes and helicopters.

name: National Wildlife Conservancies Map (Kenya)
summary: Map published by the Kenya Wildlife Conservancies Association in 2016 showing 119 of Kenya's 160 conservancies.

name: National Wildlife Database
summary: Kenya's national repository of wildlife conservation data, holding species and census records, developed and maintained by the Wildlife Research and Training Institute.

name: Natural State
summary: Restoration organisation with a research centre at the base of Mount Kenya, which deploys camera traps and AudioMoths and validates BirdNET output for African birds.

name: Nature Kenya
summary: Conservation society whose Bird Committee is a joint runner of the Kenya Bird Map.

name: Ndege Zetu
summary: More than 20 hours of recordings from the Mount Kenya ecosystem annotated by expert ornithologists, published by DSAIL.

name: Ngare Ndare Forest Trust
summary: Trust registered in 2004 to sustain conservation of Ngare Ndare forest and develop surrounding communities, with a concession management agreement finalised with the Kenya Forest Service in 2009.

name: Northern Rangelands Trust
summary: Organisation working with community conservancies in northern and coastal Kenya, which runs a landscape-wide IoT conservation network and tracks rangelands with satellite data.

name: NRT IoT conservation network
summary: LoRaWAN sensor network across 22 community conservancies and four private reserves in Kenya, built by the Northern Rangelands Trust with the Connected Conservation Foundation.

name: Nyekweri Kimintet Community Forest Conservation Trust
summary: Community-based organisation formed in 2004 and registered, concerned with community forest conservation.

name: Ogiek Peoples’ Development Program
summary: Programme whose Nakuru county volunteers work with Kenya Forest Service rangers in the eastern Mau Forest blocks and have planted more than 60,000 native trees in four blocs.

name: Ol Choro Oirouwa Conservancy
summary: Conservancy established in 1991 as a wildlife trust, described as among the first in East Africa, which protects southern white rhinos under ranger and Kenya Wildlife Service surveillance.

name: Ol Jogi
summary: Private reserve in the sensor and communication network that the Connected Conservation Foundation describes across northern Kenya.

name: Ol Kinyei Conservancy
summary: Conservancy of 18,641 acres, set up in 2005 as a partnership between 177 landowners and GameWatchers Safaris/Porini Safari Camps, and green-listed by IUCN for 2018 to 2023.

name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy
summary: Wildlife conservancy of about 90,000 acres in Kenya with a Digital Operations Room built around EarthRanger, thermal cameras and sensors.

name: Ol Pejeta Conservation Tech Lab
summary: Lab opened at Ol Pejeta with Fauna & Flora, Liquid Telecom and Arm to research and test technology for conservation, including Sigfox tracking. Fauna & Flora dates it to 2017; no page read gives its current state.

name: Olare Motorogi Conservancy
summary: Conservancy of about 33,386 acres combining Olare Orok and Motorogi, acting as a buffer zone for the Maasai Mara National Reserve through a partnership with 288 landowners.

name: Olderkesi Wildlife Community Trust
summary: Maasai body that owns Olderkesi Conservancy and co-manages it with Cottar's Wildlife Conservancy Trust.

name: Olerai Conservancy
summary: Conservancy of 2,020 hectares formed in 2017 when 23 landowners leased their parcels.

name: Oloisukut Conservancy
summary: Conservancy of 23,000 acres along the Siria Escarpment, 16,000 of them leased for 25 years, serving as an elephant corridor linking the Mara areas to the Nyakweri Forest.

name: Oloolua Forest EcoTourism CFA Group
summary: Community forest group authorised by the Kenya Forest Service to provide information, scouts and guides in Oloolua Forest, with entry fees going to trails, security and scouts.

name: Pardamat Conservation Area
summary: Wildlife conservation area of 26,000 hectares, legally registered by its 850 landowners.

name: Pate Marine Community Conservancy
summary: Conservancy of 10 villages on Pate Island, a Northern Rangelands Trust member, whose rangers patrol an octopus closure area.

name: Project Centinela at Mount Kenya Wildlife Conservancy
summary: Kenya Space Agency project with Mount Kenya Wildlife Conservancy and Planet Labs that uses high-resolution satellite imagery to monitor and restore bongo habitat on Mount Kenya, the Aberdares and in Kakamega Forest.

name: Rangelands Atlas
summary: Atlas of the world's rangelands from ILRI and partners, published in 2021, which also records gaps in rangeland data.

name: Rangelands Decision Support Tool
summary: Web tool built by SERVIR-Eastern and Southern Africa at the Regional Centre for Mapping of Resources for Development, which makes downloadable maps of vegetation condition from MODIS NDVI for Kenyan rangelands.

name: Regional Centre of Excellence for Biodiversity, Forests and Seascape Ecosystems Management
summary: RCMRD programme for 2024 to 2028 covering 24 countries in Eastern and Southern Africa, with a cloud geospatial platform of biodiversity, forest and protected-area data. It is part of the EU-funded ArcX programme.

name: Rhino Ark Kenya Charitable Trust
summary: Kenyan conservation trust leading the reintroduction of eastern black rhinos to the Aberdares, where it piloted an AI system to detect and deter hyenas, according to IPS.

name: Rhions Lab Limited
summary: Maker of Xoome, a wildlife camera trap with AI and Internet of Things, which won Kenya's National Innovation Award.

name: Ringing Scheme of Eastern Africa
summary: Programme begun in the early 1960s that coordinates bird ringing in East Africa by issuing rings, curating data and tracking recoveries, and is linking with SAFRING to coordinate ringing data for Africa under AFRING.

name: Safaricom
summary: Kenyan telecoms company, a partner with Vodafone and WWF in the m-Twiga AI wildlife alert system.

name: Satellite-based drought monitoring in Kenya
summary: Operational processing chain that maps drought across Kenya from MODIS vegetation data, set up by BOKU in Vienna with the National Drought Management Authority.

name: Sea Turtle Photo ID (Bahari Hai)
summary: Programme run by Bahari Hai that identifies individual sea turtles from facial scales, aiming to use the data to study turtle populations in Kenya's coastal habitats and later other marine protected areas.

name: Segera
summary: A 50,000-acre eco-retreat on the Laikipia Plateau that uses EarthRanger with AI-powered camera management software, according to Fortune.

name: Sera Community Conservancy
summary: Conservancy in Samburu County that set up East Africa's first community-based rhino sanctuary in 2015, working with the Northern Rangelands Trust and receiving rhinos relocated from Lewa Downs.

name: Serengeti-Mara wildebeest satellite survey
summary: Study that counted wildebeest in the Serengeti-Mara from high-resolution satellite images with two deep learning models, as described by its authors in Capital FM.

name: Sheldrick Wildlife Trust
summary: Kenyan conservation trust working with the Kenya Wildlife Service in Tsavo. Connected Conservation Foundation says it is putting in LoRaWAN networks and runs an operations room that combines aerial patrol, vehicle and camera trap data.

name: Shompole Community Trust
summary: Trust recorded in the Global ICCA Database as owning a 10,000 hectare conservancy on Shompole Group Ranch, with a formal management plan and rules of use.

name: Signvita
summary: Nairobi company selling digital monitoring systems for carbon projects, including mangrove restoration, REDD+ forest conservation and reforestation.

name: Social and Hydrological Information Platform
summary: Open platform sharing water, soil and land data for the Ewaso Ng'iro basin.

name: Solio Game Reserve
summary: Rhino sanctuary in Kenya that received AI-enabled FLIR thermal cameras from the Kenya Wildlife Service and WWF.

name: Soundscape as a Land Degradation and Ecosystem Restoration Monitoring Tool in Savannah Ecosystems
summary: Study led by Consolata Gathoni Gitau testing passive acoustic monitoring as a measure of land degradation and restoration in the northern Maasai Mara.

name: Space for Giants
summary: Conservation charity with a postal address in Nanyuki, working in nine African countries, which tracks elephants in Kenya with collars reporting through EarthRanger.

name: Spaceborne AI Algorithm Rideshare Programme
summary: Kenya Space Agency and STAR.VISION programme in which 58 students from 14 Kenyan universities deployed AI algorithms on an Earth observation satellite.

name: Spatial Intelligence and Environmental Analytics Lab
summary: Lab at JKUAT applying automated imagery analysis and biodiversity measurement to Kenya's mangroves and coastal waters, building on its director's work on seafloor classification.

name: State Department for Environment and Climate Change
summary: Kenyan government department for environment and climate change. It convened the review of the updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2026-2030, which is aligned with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

name: State Department for Forestry
summary: Kenyan government department for forestry. It hosts the national REDD+ site, which describes the National Forest Monitoring System.

name: Stawisha Mau Charitable Trust
summary: Public-private partnership of more than sixteen stakeholders, announced to help restore and conserve 60,000 hectares of the South West Mau Forest by 2030.

name: Strathmore University
summary: Nairobi university whose researchers publish on bioacoustic feature extraction and machine learning for insect sounds.

name: Taita Research Station
summary: Established by the University of Helsinki in 2011 in Wundanyi, Taita Taveta County, this station holds a geospatial database including airborne laser scanner, hyperspectral and satellite data.

name: Taita Taveta County Government
summary: County government that has led development of forest management plans for the Chawia and Vuria forest fragments and was the first county to sign a forestry devolution agreement with national government.

name: Tech4Nature project at Kisite-Mpunguti Marine Park and Reserve
summary: Three-year project launched in January 2025 by IUCN, Huawei and the Kenya Wildlife Service, using underwater cameras and AI species recognition to monitor coral reefs.

name: Technical University of Kenya
summary: Nairobi university whose authors model potential fishing zones in Kenya's exclusive economic zone with machine learning and satellite data.

name: TechnoServe
summary: Development organisation whose TechnoServe Labs built TerraTrac, a free app for mapping farms, used by Kenyan coffee cooperatives to show deforestation-free supply.

name: TerraTrac
summary: Free Android app from TechnoServe Labs for collecting farm GPS data for the EU Deforestation Regulation, piloted with Kenyan coffee cooperatives.

name: TerraVerge Solutions
summary: Mombasa company developing mangrove monitoring from satellite and field evidence, starting in Lamu, and a coastal climate programme with fishing communities in Kilifi County.

name: The Pangolin Project
summary: Project protecting giant ground pangolins in Nyekweri Forest with telemetry, thermal scopes and camera traps. Langland Conservation uses deep learning on satellite imagery to map degradation of its landscape.

name: The Safari Collection Footprint Trust
summary: Trust in a collaboration deploying LoRaWAN for wildlife conservation and tourism in the Maasai Mara.

name: The Wildlife Foundation
summary: Foundation under whose stewardship a land lease programme has operated for two decades, enrolling landowners in the Sholinke area of the Nairobi National Park wildlife dispersal area.

name: Tsavo Trust
summary: Kenyan not-for-profit field conservation organisation that, in a May 2024 report, described monitoring of black rhino, hirola, Grevy's zebra and large carnivores with WRTI and KWS, and flew rhino and collared elephant monitoring flights.

name: Twende Green Planet
summary: Restoration organisation working on the Kenyan coast and in forests, with Atlas, an evidence platform for Africa's nature and climate that includes an AI analyst.

name: Twiga Walinzi
summary: Community-led giraffe conservation programme in northern Kenya that monitors giraffes and manages camera traps, developed by San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance and local partners.

name: Uhai WashWise
summary: Kisumu group using AI to monitor and predict water quality in communities around Lake Victoria.

name: uKweli
summary: Natural State's impact monitoring portal, a dashboard of trends in biodiversity, carbon and human wellbeing.

name: United States International University Africa
summary: Nairobi university with authors of a review of automated bioacoustics classification.

name: University of Embu
summary: Kenyan university whose authors use machine learning on tree survival and published spatial data on Kenya's grassland and rangeland extent.

name: University of Nairobi
summary: Kenyan university whose Department of Geospatial and Space Technology co-authored deep learning land-cover mapping of Kenya, and a host of the Earth Observation Innovation Labs.

name: Unlocking Biodiversity Data to Facilitate Designation of Lake Ol Bolossat as a 7th Ramsar Site in Kenya
summary: East African Wild Life Society project, led by Jabes Okumu with a JRS grant of 272,136 US dollars over 36 months from 2022, aiming to gather biodiversity information to support Ramsar designation of the lake.

name: Upande
summary: Kenyan social enterprise that builds spatial data systems, including one for the Biodiversity Atlas of Kenya, and runs IoT sensor work.

name: Vihiga County Government
summary: County government in western Kenya that monitors forest degradation with Sentinel satellite imagery, according to a report on its governor's data work.

name: VirtualRanger
summary: AI-powered WhatsApp chatbot for communities in the Masai Mara to report human-wildlife conflict to nearby NGOs, built by Will May of AI Edge.

name: Watamu Marine Association
summary: Organisation whose Watamu office hosted the KMMN data centre for marine mammal sightings, according to a 2021 study, which also describes teams of KWS and WMA members deployed to reported strandings.

name: Water Resources Authority
summary: Kenyan water authority upgrading its monitoring stations to send real-time data to a central server.

name: Wildlife Crime Kenya Dataset
summary: Published dataset of 1,099 wildlife crime court cases from Kenyan magistrate courts, from cases registered in 2018 and 2019.

name: Wildlife Research and Training Institute
summary: Kenyan state institute for wildlife research and training, which carried out the national wildlife census and is building a national wildlife database.

name: Wildlife Works
summary: Runs the Kasigau Corridor REDD+ project in Kenya, with rangers and camera traps, and uses Sensing Clues tools there.

name: WildlifeDirect
summary: Kenyan non-profit behind the Eyes in the Courtroom monitoring of wildlife crime trials, whose court data are published as the Wildlife Crime Kenya Dataset.

name: Wildwatch Kenya
summary: Zooniverse citizen science project on camera trap images of reticulated giraffe and other wildlife, begun at Loisaba and Namunyak conservancies.

name: WWF-Kenya
summary: Kenyan office of WWF, which supported AI-enabled thermal cameras at rhino sites and tested the m-Twiga wildlife alert system.

name: Wyss Academy for Nature East Africa Hub
summary: East Africa hub of the Wyss Academy for Nature, which ran a 10-terabyte aerial survey of Laikipia and Isiolo rangelands and shared the data with communities.

name: Xoome
summary: Wildlife camera trap using AI and Internet of Things to identify people, wild animals, rangers and vehicles, previously known as WildEye.

name: Yala Ecosystem Site Support Group
summary: Group that restored 66.7 hectares of wetland with papyrus within Yala Swamp’s Indigenous and Community Conserved Area and planted 69,622 indigenous trees along the lower Yala River.

name: Besh-Aral State Nature Reserve
summary: The April 2023 CEPF report describes the reserve as the project’s primary beneficiary and partner, reporting increased monitoring and patrolling, equipment use and initial camera trap results from 2021.

name: Building capacity to protect Besh Aral's meadows, marmots and megafauna, Kyrgyzstan
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project run by Fauna & Flora from November 2020 to February 2023, which coordinated field surveys with the reserve and gave its rangers initial camera trap monitoring results.

name: CAMP Alatoo Public Foundation for Sustainable Development of Mountain Regions
summary: Public foundation in Bishkek for sustainable development of mountain regions; its 2023 annual report lists a pasture data collection tool, and the Sigrid Rausing Trust says it and Ilbirs trained local hunters and fishermen to monitor the Baibosun reserve.

name: Capacity Enhancement for Better Wildlife Conservation and Monitoring in Kyrgyzstan (Rufford 13476-1)
summary: Closed Rufford-funded project, reported for November 2013 to December 2014, whose sensor camera training enabled Naryn reserve rangers to record the reserve’s first snow leopard photos and videos.

name: Central-Asian Institute for Applied Geosciences
summary: Registered in May 2004, it researches Earth system processes affecting society in Central Asia and lists the National Database of Wildlife of Kyrgyzstan among its projects.

name: Clarifying conservation status of Pallas's cat in Kyrgyzstan (MBZF grant 172515422)
summary: Pallas's cat project in Kyrgyzstan that received a $6,830 MBZ Fund grant on 7 June 2017 and planned camera trapping in the west and a national database of records.

name: Comprehensive assessment of the snow leopard population in Kyrgyzstan
summary: Closed four-year camera trap study, reported by 24.kg in December 2024, covering over 125,000 km2 with more than 875 cameras and estimating 234 to 349 snow leopards in Kyrgyzstan.

name: Conservation of globally important biodiversity and associated land and forest resources of Western Tian Shan mountain ecosystems (GEF 6958)
summary: GEF-funded project on biodiversity, land and forest resources in Kyrgyzstan's Western Tian Shan, which a 2020 report says supports a snow leopard monitoring database and a population monitoring methodology.

name: Department of Biodiversity Conservation and Specially Protected Natural Areas
summary: Government department, run by the Ministry of Natural Resources, which 24.kg reports is to coordinate protected natural areas, help create and enlarge reserves, keep state biodiversity databases and help keep the Red Book.

name: Directorate of the Biosphere Territory "Issyk-Kul"
summary: Directorate of the Issyk-Kul biosphere territory which, MTS.kg reported on 27 January 2026, organised the winter waterbird count at Lake Issyk-Kul and Orto-Tokoy reservoir with the Institute of Biology of the National Academy of Sciences.

name: Earth Observation Support for Forest Management in Kyrgyzstan (ESA GDA Forest Management)
summary: Earth observation project with the ADB that produced land cover, forest type and change maps (2019, 2024) covering about 8,558 km2 of Jalal-Abad walnut-fruit forests, which the page says national agencies now use.

name: Engaging communities to safeguard rural livelihoods and cultivate conservation partnerships in Kyrgyzstan
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project run by Panthera, with a $150,000 grant from December 2020 to June 2023, in which the Ilbirs Foundation provided staff for surveys and camera trapping.

name: Environmental Impacts of Infrastructure Development on Macro-Invertebrate Biodiversity in Freshwater Ecosystems in Kyrgyzstan's Mountains
summary: Rufford-listed project (September 2021) at Issyk Kul Lake that planned to collect macroinvertebrate, turbidity, velocity and chemical data for a public webpage, with a monitoring strategy open to schools.

name: Eurasian otter field research in Chon-Alay district (Ilbirs Foundation, GEF Small Grants Programme)
summary: Closed field study in Chon-Alay district, run by the Ilbirs Foundation with UNDP support, using camera traps and water analyses, which found no stable breeding Eurasian otter population in Kyrgyzstan at that time.

name: Ilbirs Foundation
summary: Kyrgyz NGO that launched a community anti-poaching project with NABU in 2021; Mongabay reported in May 2025 that it supported 10 community conservancies in nine districts with GPS, camera traps and patrol gear.

name: Integrated Community-based Management of High Value Mountain Ecosystems in Southern Kyrgyzstan for Multiple Benefits
summary: GEF-funded project approved on 22 October 2022 to safeguard Pamir-Alai biodiversity and restore degraded land; CAMP Alatoo reported IFMIS modernisation under way in January 2026.

name: Introducing SMART in the Khan-Tengri Corridor, Kyrgyzstan
summary: Closed CEPF-funded grant of $156,723.02 (June 2021 to May 2023), run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, to introduce SMART for patrol and wildlife monitoring at two pilot sites.

name: Kan-Achuu State Nature Park
summary: Nature park that in July 2020 planned an October to December winter wildlife count and had received winter tents and sleeping bags from the UNDP-GEF Western Tian Shan project.

name: Khan-Tengri National Park
summary: Protected area that was one of two SMART pilot sites, where SMART patrol data showed patrol days rising from 12 to 69 between the first quarters of 2022 and 2023.

name: Kyrgyz Data Cube
summary: Open-access dataset of satellite imagery and 18 years of data on pastures, snow and drought across Kyrgyzstan, according to the Central-Asian Institute for Applied Geosciences, credited to eOsphere and partners under the SIBELIUs name.

name: Kyrgyzstan CITES electronic database
summary: Records wildlife smuggling cases to help agencies spot patterns and share information; in August 2025, finalisation and handover to Kyrgyzstan’s natural resources ministry were planned by September 2025.

name: Ministry of Natural Resources, Ecology and Technical Supervision of the Kyrgyz Republic
summary: Kyrgyz ministry that, per MTS.kg, prepared the country's seventh national report to the Convention on Biological Diversity, and which 24.kg reports took part in a September 2025 camera trap survey of snow leopards in Shamshy-Tuyuk reserve.

name: NABU and Ilbirs community SMART anti-poaching project, Kara-Kujur
summary: Community-based anti-poaching project by NABU and Ilbirs whose main goal, the CMS Central Asian Mammals Initiative says, was implementing SMART; a model was customised for Kara-Kujur and mobile devices given to local participants.

name: Naryn State Nature Reserve
summary: Reserve run by the ministry which, Economist.kg reports, monitors wild animals with OSI-Panthera, uses continuous camera traps and active monitoring since 2026 to estimate population sizes, and feeds the data into Red Book updates.

name: National Database of Wildlife of Kyrgyzstan
summary: Wildlife database for Kyrgyzstan built on PostgreSQL with 36 tables and a web site, loaded with checked observation card data, with support listed from the EU's FLERMONECA, GIZ and the World Bank.

name: Sarychat-Ertash snow leopard density study
summary: Snow Leopard Foundation Kyrgyzstan and Snow Leopard Trust study described in a March 2019 field blog as Kyrgyzstan's first long-term snow leopard density study, running since 2013, with a plan for 35 camera traps over three months.

name: Sarychat-Ertash State Nature Reserve
summary: Protected area that was one of two SMART pilot sites, where the June 2023 report said patrol volume and coverage had not increased and teams could reach only a small part of the reserve.

name: Saving snow leopards and their prey species in Kyrgyzstan
summary: Closed snow leopard and prey project run by the Snow Leopard Trust under IUCN SOS, with a grant budget of 142,747 CHF, where 26 working camera traps and a prey survey gave a baseline.

name: Scaling up Wildlife Monitoring and Protection in the Inner Tien-Shan Mountains of Kyrgyzstan
summary: Rufford-listed project, dated 29 March 2023, that planned a Naryn State Nature Reserve management plan and extension to Salkyn-Tör Nature Park, building on rangers already able to run sensor cameras independently.

name: Second National Forest Inventory of Kyrgyzstan
summary: Covered Kyrgyzstan’s forests from 2020 to 2023 within a Forest Service project funded by a World Bank and GEF grant and loan, with results presented in October 2023.

name: Snow Leopard Foundation in Kyrgyzstan
summary: Public foundation registered in Bishkek on 14 May 2012 according to Statsnet; in March 2019, the Snow Leopard Trust reported joint Sarychat-Ertash camera-trap density research since 2013.

name: State Agency for Land Resources, Cadastre, Geodesy and Cartography under the Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic
summary: State agency that presented Kyrgyzstan's position at the 2025 UN-GGIM workshop, with stated five-year goals of a shared national geospatial data portal and encouraging start-ups and research using satellite imagery, drones and AI.

name: Tabiyat kenchi
summary: Biodiversity app, launched in February 2023 in Kyrgyz and Russian and both built and run by CAMP Alatoo, that lets users record and identify species and send data to experts for confirmation.

name: Underground Habitats as a Unit for Conservation of Vulnerable Bat Communities in South-Western Kyrgyzstan
summary: Closed Rufford project that surveyed caves in Osh and Batken regions during June to September 2018 expeditions, according to its final report, and identified 12 bat species.

name: Upscaling Use of the Spatial Monitoring and Reporting Tool (SMART) in Kyrgyzstan
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, a $155,370 grant for April 2023 to March 2025, to promote use of the SMART tool in two protected areas in eastern Kyrgyzstan.

name: Cambodia Environment Management Information System
summary: A system the Ministry of Environment is developing, with UNDP technical assistance, to collect, store, integrate, display and share environmental data, including near real-time data, from Cambodia's protected areas.

name: Cambodia National Forest Monitoring System
summary: A national system developed largely alongside REDD+ readiness over the past decade, supporting forest monitoring, emissions estimation and UNFCCC reporting; Cambodia joined GFOI’s Country-Led Planning process in 2025.

name: Cambodia Protected Area Alerts System
summary: A tool that monitors near real-time forest changes and threats such as deforestation, fires and floods in Prey Lang Wildlife Sanctuary, and is said to help prioritise patrol planning.

name: Cambodia Vulture Conservation Project
summary: A vulture conservation partnership set up in 2004 between government agencies and NGOs, led by WCS Cambodia, whose page says vulture restaurants make monitoring vulture populations easier.

name: Central Cardamom REDD+ project
summary: REDD+ project launched in 2021, for which a camera trap survey, reported by Mongabay as supported by the Ministry of Environment, USAID and Conservation International, helped set an initial biodiversity baseline.

name: Centre for Biodiversity Conservation, Royal University of Phnom Penh
summary: A centre in the Department of Biology at the Royal University of Phnom Penh, supporting biodiversity management through research and monitoring, with completed elephant, crocodile and gibbon projects and bat work current since 2019.

name: Conservation International-Cambodia
summary: The Cambodia programme of Conservation International, active there since 2001, which according to an AFP report trained a machine-learning model on gibbon calls from 10 Cardamom Mountains sites and published a camera-trap survey in 2024.

name: Department of Biodiversity, General Secretariat of the National Council for Sustainable Development
summary: A department run by the Ministry of Environment, named in a 2018 report as responsible for Cambodia's Clearing House Mechanism under the CBD, with a roadmap to add national biodiversity status data.

name: Establishment of a National Forest Monitoring System for REDD+ Readiness in Cambodia
summary: A closed FAO project (June 2016 to December 2019) that built Cambodia's National Forest Monitoring System, trained staff in Open Foris tools, and completed a 2016 forest cover assessment endorsed by government in October 2017.

name: Fishing Cat Ecological Enterprise
summary: Cambodian organisation conserving threatened wetland carnivores and restoring mangroves, with CEPF funding for SMART patrolling and monitoring; IUCN reports 22 camera traps installed at Koh Kapik.

name: Forest Disturbance Alert Platform (Cambodia)
summary: A platform built by Open Development Cambodia that sends forest disturbance alerts through Telegram, using GFW, JJ-FAST and SERVIR-SEA data, generally 12 to 15 days after detection, and does not monitor wildlife.

name: Forestry Administration (Cambodia)
summary: A government body under the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries that tested monitoring tools including SMART in a 2016 to 2019 FAO project and jointly collected Keo Seima wildlife survey data with WCS from 2010 to 2016.

name: GBIF Cambodia
summary: Cambodia's country node of GBIF, listed in the GBIF registry with associate participation status, with most contacts based at the Morodok Techo Building in Phnom Penh.

name: General Department of Cadastre and Geography
summary: A department of the Ministry of Land Management, Urban Planning and Construction which, according to its own 2023 paper, is responsible under a sub-decree for surveying and producing base maps.

name: General Directorate of Administration for Nature Conservation and Protection
summary: Part of Cambodia's Ministry of Environment whose MRV team, with the Forestry Administration, prepared the 2016 and 2018 land use and land cover maps from Landsat imagery cited in the forest reference level submission.

name: Khmer Earth Observation (KHEOBS) Laboratory
summary: Laboratory at the Institute of Technology of Cambodia set up to use Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and aerial imagery, with processing chains meant to produce five-day water and vegetation time series and Tonle Sap land cover maps.

name: Long-term monitoring of primate, bird, and ungulate populations 2010-2022 for protected area management, Keo Seima Wildlife Sanctuary, Cambodia
summary: A GBIF dataset of 13 key species over 12 years from standardised line-transect surveys in Keo Seima Wildlife Sanctuary, built by WCS Cambodia, the Forestry Administration and the Ministry of Environment for protected area management.

name: Mapping Drivers of Habitat Loss and Fragmentation in Seasonally Dry Tropical Forest Landscape
summary: A closed project that planned time-series land cover maps and a camera-trap survey, whose November 2022 final report describes mapped natural forest types with uncertainty estimates.

name: Marine Conservation Cambodia
summary: A community-based NGO working since 2008 on Cambodia's marine ecosystems, monitoring seagrass at fixed sites, with a 2025 paper reporting a 39% fall in Kampot seagrass cover between 2013 and 2023.

name: Ministry of Environment
summary: Cambodia's environment ministry, which SERVIR Southeast Asia says launched the Protected Area Monitoring Platform and is developing an environmental information system with UNDP, and which houses the national Clearing House Mechanism department.

name: NatureLife Cambodia
summary: A CEPF-funded grantee for a 2020 to 2022 Stung Sen Ramsar Site project, in which 11 rangers completed 312 patrols using SMART Mobile and received SMART training.

name: Open Development Cambodia
summary: A private non-profit open data and open knowledge media group that built the Forest Disturbance Alert Platform, which a post dated 9 July 2026 says launched officially on 24 June 2026.

name: Prek Toal large waterbird monitoring
summary: Monitoring programme in which WCS staff and Ministry of Environment rangers protect endangered waterbird nesting colonies at Prek Toal, giving yearly population estimates, with reports listed for 2001 to 2007, 2009 and 2011.

name: Prey Lang Community Network
summary: Network of local forest activists who, with University of Copenhagen scientists, used the Prey Lang App in patrols, producing 4,560 validated entries on forest resources and illegal logging from February 2015 to January 2017.

name: Protected Area Monitoring Platform
summary: A platform launched by the Ministry of Environment that, according to SERVIR Southeast Asia, integrates ground-based and remotely sensed data to improve law enforcement and conservation.

name: Royal University of Phnom Penh
summary: Cambodia's oldest and largest public university, according to its site, co-launched the Cambodian Journal of Natural History in 2008 and was a CEPF grantee for a 2012 to 2013 hog deer survey.

name: The Role of Waterholes in Structuring Insectivorous Bat Assemblages in the Dry Dipterocarp Forests of Northern Cambodia: A Multi-Scale Analysis
summary: Rufford Foundation project dated July 2025 in Kulen Promtep Wildlife Sanctuary, which plans acoustic bat monitoring to identify priority waterholes and a species classifier from Cambodian echolocation recordings, to be made freely available.

name: WCS Cambodia
summary: Reports using drones, remote sensing, SMART and EarthRanger to track threats, camera traps and acoustics to track species, and describes Keo Seima REDD+ as its flagship REDD+ project.

name: WCS Cambodia camera trap occurrence data
summary: A GBIF-funded dataset of selected WCS Cambodia camera-trap records from 2001 to 2018, covering 101 species, described as the first GBIF publication of occurrence data by a Cambodian organisation.

name: Wildlife Alliance
summary: An international non-profit founded in 1995 as the Global Survival Network, working to protect Cambodia's Cardamom Rainforest, which reports drone and camera-trap monitoring from 2021 and a 2023 tiger prey camera-trap survey.

name: WWF-Cambodia
summary: Uses photo identification, camera traps, eDNA, drones and annual bird censuses to monitor species, including 311 white-shouldered ibises recorded in 2024.

name: Biodiversity and Conservation Unit
summary: A unit run by the Environment and Conservation Division that, per MELAD's page, handles the Convention on Biological Diversity, World Heritage and Ramsar Conventions, and implements turtle monitoring and mangrove mapping projects.

name: Climate and Biodiversity Smart Marine Spatial Planning (CabSmart)
summary: A closed project funded by NZ MFAT, which Earth Sciences New Zealand said in March 2026 was helping move the Phoenix Islands Protected Area to an integrated spatial plan using species forecasts.

name: Environment and Conservation Division
summary: Kiribati government division within MELAD, which runs it, with reported work in 2022 and 2023 on turtle tagging, seagrass and mangrove monitoring, and littering enforcement, and the executing role for GEF project 5130.

name: Holding the Lines, Restoration of the Northern Line Islands, Kiribati
summary: A closed project run by the Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme, funded by CEPF with a USD 165,000 grant from October 2009 to December 2012, with Eco Oceania coordinating technical assistance on bird monitoring, predator management and ant surveillance.

name: Integrating Global Environmental Priorities into National Policies and Programmes in Kiribati
summary: Closed GEF-funded project, run by the Environment and Conservation Division, that aimed to improve information management and compliance monitoring, with an environmental management information system and an indicators and compliance monitoring system as its two planned outcomes.

name: Kiritimati coupled socioeconomic and ecological coral reef monitoring programme
summary: Rufford-funded programme led, by Julia K. Baum's account in 2015, combining socioeconomic and ecosystem monitoring on Kiritimati, with data from 2007 to 2013 and a fifth field season planned for 2015.

name: Kiritimati Island Conservation Protected Area Project
summary: A closed project, 15 September 2020 to 14 March 2023, led by MELAD and funded by BIOPAMA, which planned patrol and monitoring equipment for seabird sites; the grant figure differs between sources.

name: Land Management Division
summary: A ministry division whose activities include boundary mapping and map and site plan sales, described alongside the Kiribati Land Information System in a 2018 presentation.

name: Marine Atlas: Maximizing Benefits for Kiribati
summary: Atlas published in 2019 by GIZ, IUCN and SPREP, covering Kiribati's marine ecosystems from coral reefs to deep-sea trenches, with map layers including benthic species richness across the EEZ.

name: Marine Turtle Monitoring Project (Kiribati)
summary: An active turtle monitoring and tagging project run by the Biodiversity and Conservation Unit, funded by SPREP, with monitoring ongoing in Tarawa, North Tarawa and Kiritimati according to MELAD.

name: Ministry of Environment, Lands and Agricultural Development
summary: A Kiribati government ministry based in Bikenibeu, Tarawa, whose Environment and Conservation Division has the mandate to safeguard the natural environment and protect human health, and which hosts Kiribati's CBD national focal points per InforMEA.

name: Ministry of Fisheries and Marine Resource Development
summary: A Kiribati ministry at Bairiki, Tarawa, whose Fisheries Division partnered on 2018 surveys at 16 reef sites and whose Research Unit worked with Simon Donner installing loggers from 2014.

name: Research and Monitoring Unit, Coastal Fisheries Division
summary: A unit of the Coastal Fisheries Division whose team, a 2018 press release says, spent almost a month on Abemama surveying coral cover, finfish and invertebrates and assessing climate change impacts.

name: Seagrass restoration and protection in Kiribati (Kiwa Initiative local project)
summary: An active locally led project under MELAD, one of 15 launched by IUCN Oceania through the Kiwa Initiative, which IUCN says builds local capacity in seagrass monitoring and restoration.

name: Tarawa and Abaiang coral reef surveys
summary: A closed project in which a team carried out SCUBA surveys at 16 outer reef sites in Tarawa and Abaiang in April and May 2018, building three-dimensional reef models from overlapping images, in partnership with the fisheries ministry.

name: The influence of local and global stressors on coral reef ecosystems (Kiritimati)
summary: A Mitacs-listed project that plans to use underwater acoustic and imagery surveys to measure coral, fish and habitat change on Kiritimati in the four years after a bleaching event, and to test acoustics for assessing reef health.

name: Wildlife Conservation Unit
summary: A unit of the Kiribati environment ministry, run by it, which a 2013 CEPF report says led on-the-ground activities, including bird and rat monitoring on Kiritimati, with staff trained in bird surveys.

name: Association d'Intervention pour le Développement et l'Environnement
summary: Organisation named AIDE in a 2021 CEPF final report, which records participatory reef monitoring at five sites and 43 people trained in socio-economic and ecological monitoring; CORDIO met it in 2026.

name: Association pour le Développement Socio-Economique d'Itsamia
summary: Non-profit from Itsamia, created in 1991 to protect sea turtles, whose members began beach patrolling in 1998 and, per a 2019 IOSEA sheet, tagged nesting females and reported poached turtles during track counts.

name: Comoros Convention on Biological Diversity Clearing House Mechanism
summary: Website presenting itself as the Comoros Convention on Biological Diversity Clearing House Mechanism, hosting the country's 2016 national biodiversity strategy and action plan.

name: Dahari
summary: Comorian NGO, funded by CEPF, with GPS tracking of two flying foxes in 2019, a Livingstone's fruit bat survey with Durrell, a GBIF publisher role, and a 2030 aim of fisher-managed reef reserves.

name: Dahari forest programme
summary: Forest restoration programme run by Dahari on Anjouan and Grande Comore, funded by JRS to evaluate the Moya conservation agreements using satellite imagery and to support forest mapping in La Grille KBA, with Oxford.

name: DAYIMA
summary: Described by IUCN NL as a Comorian NGO, it enhanced a mobile app through a completed CEPF-funded capacity-building project, with species data already used by community groups.

name: Direction Générale de l’Environnement et des Forêts
summary: UNDP reported in 2020 that this directorate acquired a specialised mapping drone with UNDP and GEF support, alongside online mapping of biodiversity and protected area boundaries.

name: First Descent: Comoros
summary: Run by Nekton and R-POC, the 6 October–14 November 2025 expedition found evidence of healthy reefs below 30 metres and deep-water sharks; its release reports Comorian data ownership.

name: Identifying and Monitoring Terrestrial Conservation Priorities in the Comoro Islands
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, running June 2015 to August 2019, that aimed to map remaining Comoro Islands forests, study deforestation drivers and define conservation plans for Livingstone's fruit bat and the mongoose lemur.

name: Laboratory of Marine and Coastal Sciences
summary: At this University of the Comoros laboratory, two 2025 expedition researchers interned; in September 2026, one reported organising data towards a descriptive Comorian marine species database.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement chargé du Tourisme
summary: Active Comorian ministry listed among the CBD national focal points' affiliations, and placed by CORDIO in 2026 as the ministry over Comoros National Parks.

name: Mohéli National Park coral reef monitoring (CORDIO, R-POC)
summary: CORDIO-run reef monitoring in Mohéli National Park, part of the R-POC programme, with sites monitored since 2010 and three sites surveyed in 2026 with park eco-guards.

name: Parc National de Mohéli
summary: Comorian protected area described by UNDP in 2024 as the country's first and a leading sea turtle nesting site, with 30,000 landings a year, and named in 2024 as a RECOS pilot site.

name: Parcs nationaux des Comores
summary: Agency managing the Comoros protected area system, whose database UNDP reported as operational on ArcGIS Online in 2020, alongside monitoring that counted 8,550 mongoose lemurs on Ndzuani.

name: Renforcement de la Protection des Océans aux Comores
summary: Under this initiative, described by Nekton as government-led, partners announced systematic ocean exploration to 900 metres in October 2025 to inform Marine Protected Areas.

name: RNAP 2 (Réseau national des aires protégées des Comores, phase 2)
summary: Co-financed by the Comorian government, UNDP and GEF, this active protected area project supported eco-guards at Bazimini and Mont Ntringui, where tools and training were reported in August 2025.

name: University of Comoros
summary: Listed for ecological monitoring, remote sensing, biomass estimation and marine ecosystem study and protection, it supplied the scientist named as co-chief scientist of the 2025 First Descent mission.

name: C.A.R.E. SKN (Coral Reef Assistance, Restoration and Education in St. Kitts and Nevis)
summary: NGO registered in 2021 that began a coral nursery pilot in June 2022, partners with Reef Check, hosted a 2022 EcoDiver course certifying ten divers, and in April 2025 was reported to be implementing a PROCARIBE+ community project.

name: Center for Conservation Medicine and Ecosystem Health, Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine
summary: A Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine centre in Basseterre that says it does applied Caribbean research on marine species health, population ecology and non-native island species, with affiliated studies on eagle rays and green monkeys.

name: Conserving biodiversity and reducing habitat degradation in Protected Areas and their areas of influence (St Kitts and Nevis)
summary: A closed GEF-funded project run by the Department of Environment, whose terrestrial and marine inventories were reported incomplete at terminal evaluation, with the marine inventory not accepted by the Department of Marine Resources.

name: Coral Reef Early Warning Station, Paradise Reef (St Kitts)
summary: Buoy first deployed in April 2018 at Paradise Reef, Sandy Point, with NOAA and Environmental Mooring Institute support; in May 2020 an officer said it measures sea temperature, salinity and algae to help predict coral bleaching.

name: Department of Environment (St Kitts and Nevis)
summary: Government department, run by the sustainable development ministry, overseeing biodiversity, pollution, waste, coastal and marine protection; SKNIS reported in May 2026 it had begun the Seventh National Report on biodiversity with UNDP help.

name: Department of Marine Resources (St Kitts and Nevis)
summary: Government body responsible for the Marine Management Area declared in 2016 and federal waters under the 2016 Act, reported to have led marine inventory work for a UNDP-GEF project and to run the 2018 marine ecological assessment.

name: Department of Physical Planning (St Kitts)
summary: Government department under the Ministry of Sustainable Development whose GIS Unit marked GIS Day in November 2024, when it was reported to be leading GIS integration across government sectors.

name: Department of Physical Planning and Environment (Nevis)
summary: Nevis department responsible for managing, administering and enforcing the resolution establishing Nevis Peak National Park and Camps River Watershed as protected areas, as reported on 29 April 2025.

name: Improving Environmental Management through Sustainable Land Management in St. Kitts and Nevis
summary: An active GEF-funded project run by IUCN, scheduled for May 2020–June 2028; IUCN reports mapping degraded lands digitally and training over 50 farming groups and cooperatives.

name: Marine ecological assessment of the St. Kitts and Nevis Marine Management Area, 2018
summary: Closed assessment run by the Department of Environment, led by Envision Mapping consultants, planned for June and August 2018 at the conservation zones in Keys, Sandy Point and the Narrows.

name: Marine Spatial Planning in St. Kitts and Nevis (BioTA marine zoning exercise)
summary: Under BioTA, The Nature Conservancy collaborated with the St Kitts and Nevis Maritime Administration in 2010–2012 on marine zoning using Marxan, producing a draft Marine Spatial Plan.

name: Ministry of Sustainable Development, Environment, Climate Action and Constituency Empowerment
summary: Government ministry in Basseterre, St Kitts, which its page says brings together sustainable development, environment, climate action and constituency empowerment.

name: Nevis hawksbill sea turtle migration study
summary: Study of hawksbill turtles nesting on Nevis, begun in August 2006 according to the Sea Turtle Conservancy; a 2026 press release says over 20 years it has satellite-tracked more than 30 turtles.

name: Nevis Turtle Group
summary: Non-profit in Gingerland, Nevis, that began night patrols and turtle tagging in 2003, reportedly monitored over 150 sea turtles by 2011, and builds the Nevis hawksbill migration tracking project.

name: Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine
summary: Veterinary school in Basseterre whose conservation medicine centre researches sea turtles, birds, marine mammals, corals, fish and introduced species, and which reported a USD 55,000 US Fish and Wildlife Service grant in December 2018.

name: St. Kitts Sea Turtle Monitoring Network
summary: Programme led by Kimberly Stewart whose main goal, per an August 2019 Ross Vet news item, was to look after nesting sea turtles on St Kitts.

name: A Checklist of North Korean Vascular Plants
summary: GBIF dataset record for a checklist of native and naturalised vascular plants recorded in North Korea, cited as version 1.7 of 2024 by Chang C S, TB Lee Herbarium.

name: Faculty of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Kim Il Sung University
summary: Faculty of Kim Il Sung University in Pyongyang, listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of both authors of a 2023 paper on estimating chlorophyll a from MODIS data in Sinpho Bay.

name: Joint Shorebird Survey of the Onchon County Coast of DPRK
summary: Closed joint survey, run by the Nature Conservation Union of Korea and the Pūkorokoro Miranda Naturalists' Trust, that counted 20,635 shorebirds of 31 species at three sites on 5-7 May 2015.

name: Kim Il Sung University
summary: Pyongyang university that OpenAlex gives as the affiliation for a 2023 neural-network chlorophyll a paper from MODIS data and a 2024 ensemble-learning paper on forest aboveground biomass.

name: Ministry of Land and Environment Protection
summary: Government ministry named in an April 2024 article among bodies researching bird reserves and surveying waterbirds, and said in the CBD country profile to promote firewood forests.

name: Nature Conservation Union of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea
summary: National NGO and IUCN member since January 1963, which in 2014 agreed with the Pūkorokoro Miranda Naturalists' Trust to hold shorebird surveys along the West Sea coast from 2015.

name: Rason bird surveys
summary: Closed set of four short surveys in the Rason Special Economic Zone, proposed and funded by the Hanns Seidel Foundation, reported in August 2018 to have found 228 bird species, 12 globally threatened.

name: State Academy of Sciences
summary: Academy that the draft CBD country profile says carried out the NBSAP update, dated to 2012, and that a 2024 article names among bodies researching bird reserves and surveying waterbirds.

name: 5th National Natural Environment Survey vegetation data
summary: Spatial dataset built and run by the National Institute of Ecology from the vegetation results of the 5th National Natural Environment Survey (2019 to 2020), using field surveys and imagery; the institute says it is pursuing ongoing updates.

name: AI Challenge for Biodiversity
summary: A closed 2022 contest run by SK hynix used ten years of Earth Love Explorers records; a January 2023 report says six teams shared 26 million won.

name: AI ecologist
summary: A project described in a December 2020 talk abstract, developing deep learning to analyse wildlife images, said to identify a dozen mammal species and several crane species around the Korean DMZ.

name: AI harmful cyanobacteria automatic analysis
summary: Model built by the National Institute of Environmental Research and E-Solutions that counts cyanobacteria cells from grid images, trained on 15,080 images, cutting analysis from about four hours to about one.

name: AI-Hub wildlife activity video data
summary: A dataset covering 11 species, with 500 hours of raw video and over 270,000 annotated images, supplied with a YOLOv5 object detector as its model.

name: AI기반 국립공원 변화탐지 모니터링 플랫폼 구축
summary: CC0-licensed national park land cover training dataset built by Sundosoft from drone and satellite imagery, used for segmentation and change detection models, including a SegFormer-based segmentation model.

name: Alchera
summary: A company that a 2023 report calls a face recognition AI firm which commercialised Fire Scout.

name: Anseong Stream ECOSEE programme
summary: SK hynix defines this programme as monitoring the Anseong stream river ecosystem alongside youth environmental education, with citizen scientists recording findings in the ECOSEE app during an April 2023 event.

name: Aquatic Ecosystem Health Map
summary: A dataset built by the National Institute of Environmental Research from 2016 to 2021 assessments of river life and riverside conditions, which a January 2023 report says anyone could view online.

name: Argosdyne
summary: A company whose forest disaster response system is described in a 2023 report, which says it was demonstrated in forest surveillance pilots at Wonju and Andong.

name: Asian Forest Cooperation Organization
summary: A Seoul-headquartered organisation describing itself as a treaty-based intergovernmental body that runs community forest data portal training for ASEAN member states.

name: Baekdudaegan National Arboretum
summary: An organisation named as the collector of the specimens.

name: Baekdudaegan species distribution mapping
summary: A project mapping the distribution of 989 species across the range using nine machine-learning models, with officials expecting results to inform conservation priorities and other effective area-based measures.

name: Bandal Lens AI
summary: A model built by the Korea National Park Service, announced in October 2026 as able to identify 17 mammal species in camera-trap footage at over 90% accuracy, with field use and public release planned.

name: Biodiversity in the Korean Peninsula
summary: A dataset built by the National Institute of Biological Resources, which CBD-CHM Korea describes as a database of native species, specimens, distribution and genetic information.

name: Birds Korea
summary: An organisation whose partner profile gives its founding and aims, and whose field surveys, including counts of shorebirds and seabirds, are listed on a funder page.

name: CAS500-4
summary: A satellite launched on 7 July 2026 for forest management and monitoring of forest cover change, with full agriculture and forestry observation due to begin in 2027.

name: CBD-CHM Korea
summary: A biodiversity information sharing system, run by the National Institute of Biological Resources, that describes itself as Korea's representative clearing-house mechanism and lists the National Species List of Korea.

name: Changnyeong County
summary: According to a 2007 National Archives account, a county that handled land purchase, wardens and enforcement at Upo Wetland (1,278,285 sq m) under Nakdong River Basin Environmental Office oversight.

name: Cheorwon DMZ Crane Ecotourism Council
summary: Council for the ecotourism area designation and development programme at the Cheorwon DMZ migratory bird area; it says local residents have led its work conserving crane habitat there.

name: Chollian-2 Satellite Integrated Utilization Consortium
summary: A cooperation body of four centres, including the National Institute of Environmental Research and KIOST, whose products include a red tide index from the GOCI-II ocean payload.

name: Chollipo Arboretum Foundation
summary: Public-interest foundation listed in the national biodiversity register as a biodiversity management institution at Sowon-myeon, Taean; its arboretum page gives seven management areas and 589,429 sq m in total.

name: Chungnam National University
summary: University whose industry-academic cooperation foundation led a 2020–2022 Korea Forest Service research project aimed at AI recognition of trees damaged by pine wilt disease.

name: Citizen Scientist Biodiversity Monitoring Project
summary: A programme run by the National Institute of Biological Resources with about 100 citizen scientists each year, which an August 2026 report says has built up more than 400,000 biological records.

name: Compact Advanced Satellite 500
summary: A five-satellite research and development mission run by the Korea Aerospace Research Institute, intended to support crop, water, marine and land uses and domestic public sector Earth observation demand.

name: DeepCOI
summary: A 2025 paper describes this as a large language model-driven framework for fast and accurate taxonomic assignment in animal metabarcoding.

name: Developing Data Portals for Community Forest Data in ASEAN Member States
summary: A closed training project run by the Asian Forest Cooperation Organization and funded by the Korea International Cooperation Agency, held on 5 to 16 December 2022.

name: Dong-A Science
summary: Organisation that a January 2023 SK hynix report says runs Earth Love Explorers and provided ten years of ecological records for the AI Challenge, after a September 2022 sponsorship announcement.

name: E-Solutions
summary: Described as a specialist in measurement and analysis instruments, and linked as a builder of the AI harmful cyanobacteria automatic analysis model.

name: Earth Love Explorers (지구사랑탐사대)
summary: Citizen science programme run by Dong-A Science, whose data a January 2023 SK hynix report gives as 200,000 photographs and videos over ten years, with records from about 20,000 citizen scientists.

name: EarthPaper
summary: Described in a partner's release as a proprietary geospatial platform, run by Nara Space Technology, carrying GRUS-1 imagery and showing analysis of the 2026 Gwangyang wildfire.

name: Eastern Regional Forest Service
summary: Forest service whose 2018–2027 plan covers 384,891 ha under seven national forest offices and reports 103,073 ha of Baekdudaegan protection area, 39.3 percent of the national designation (2018 data).

name: ECO Korea
summary: Organisation that runs ecological surveys and research, including ecosystem monitoring, through its PGA Ecological Institute, and whose site has a citizen ecological monitoring group.

name: Eco.AI
summary: Camera-trap image classifier built by the National Institute of Ecology and Sphere AX, with a KAIST team improving the algorithm; in March 2025 it sorted seven categories, was used first for goral research, and a public release was planned.

name: EcoBank
summary: Ecological information portal run by the National Institute of Ecology, stating 3,054,010 data items and 90 Open API services, with research data searchable by DOI.

name: Endangered Species Restoration Center, National Institute of Ecology
summary: The National Institute of Ecology’s centre had released or translocated 14 endangered species since 2018 by October 2022, using transmitters and radio or satellite tracking for mammals and birds.

name: Environmental Geographic Information Service
summary: Programme that serves land cover maps, thematic maps, land use regulation maps and individual spatial systems as map layers.

name: Fire Scout
summary: Detects smoke and other anomalies in real time from mountain cameras, and a 2023 report says California uses it on about 1,000 cameras.

name: FIREWATCHER
summary: A May 2025 report describes plans for a forest fire watch project in Da Nang using this system with GTEL drones, forest CCTV and Mobifone's network.

name: Forest and Sharing Foundation (숲과나눔)
summary: A foundation that a January 2023 SK hynix report says supplied ecological observation data to the AI Challenge for Biodiversity, with a grant supporting grassroots NGOs.

name: Gochang County
summary: County authority handling on-site management of Gochang Getbol, a marine protected wetland, while the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries holds management authority, per the site's flyway network information sheet.

name: GOCI-II
summary: Ocean observation satellite payload that KARI describes as having 250 m resolution and 13 channels, intended in a February 2020 pre-launch report to succeed GOCI and observe red and brown tides.

name: Green Asia Network
summary: Network carrying out afforestation in response to climate change and desertification, with its afforestation page showing a site at Baanuur.

name: Green Wave
summary: Project run by Shinsegae I&C with InvaLab and Green Foundation Korea as partners, whose method is described in a press report.

name: Gyeongsang National University
summary: University that led a 2021–2023 Korea Forest Service research project aimed at combining sensors, AI and drones for early wildfire prediction and detection.

name: Hallyeohaesang roadkill prevention and monitoring pilot
summary: Roadkill pilot run by Korea National Park Service with partner POSCO DX, announced on 25 October 2023 for the following day on roughly 350 metres in Hallyeohaesang National Park.

name: Hanyang University
summary: University where OpenAlex lists the first author of the DeepCOI paper, and lists the paper as having Hanyang University authors.

name: Honam National Institute of Biological Resources
summary: Environment ministry institute, opened in 2021 for island and coastal biological resources, which a August 2025 report says has confirmed a list of 22,084 native species on Korea's islands.

name: Image data of confirmed specimens of native plants
summary: Image dataset of confirmed specimens covering 40 native plant species, with computer vision plant recognition training data listed among its expected uses.

name: Intelligent agriculture and forestry satellite operating system
summary: Proposed system, to be built by the National Institute of Forest Science, planned to sort cloudy images and pick out wildfire and pest signs for specialists, with development planned through to 2030.

name: InvaLab
summary: Company founded in September 2023 by CEO Wonhyeop Shin that builds NatureBlitz and NatureX and completed a seed investment round in November 2024.

name: IT·ET·BT 융합 유입 외래생물 분포·확산 탐지모델 개발 연구
summary: Research project announced in April 2021 to combine spatial information technology and eDNA to model alien species distribution and spread, with 1.636 billion won of funding planned over three years.

name: IUCN GET ecosystem map of the Republic of Korea
summary: Ecosystem map of Korea built by Seonyoung Park on Landsat, with 36 Korea-specific classes and overall accuracy of about 85%, using machine learning and deep learning.

name: Jeju Gotjawal Trust
summary: Non-profit foundation set up in 2007 to protect Jeju's Gotjawal; in 2026 it reported 115.7 ha bought and permanently conserved, aiming for 165 ha by 2030.

name: Jeju Intensive Ecological Research Site
summary: Regional intensive ecological research site on Jeju, opened in November 2017 according to the National Institute of Ecology, with a researcher post covering its operation and bird monitoring from 2018 to 2024.

name: Jeju Special Self-Governing Province World Heritage Headquarters
summary: Provincial headquarters whose 2020 audit listed conservation, management and use of the Jeju World Natural Heritage among its functions and showed the Hallasan National Park management office under it.

name: Jeombongsan Intensive Ecological Research Site
summary: Terrestrial intensive ecological research site opened in April 2016 at Jeombongsan, with a real-time link system for automatic ecological sensors built that year and observation results in a 2025 report.

name: Jigu Sarang Tamsadae
summary: Programme run by Dong-A Science, which a September 2022 announcement describes as having 200,000 photographs and videos accumulated over ten years and records from about 20,000 citizen scientists.

name: K-water
summary: Korean water body whose research covers satellite and drone monitoring of rivers, dams and algae, and which a June 2026 report says would apply its chlorophyll-a technology on the Nakdong River.

name: K-water Research Institute
summary: Research institute run by K-water, in Daejeon, whose AI lab lists raw water quality prediction, agentic AI for water management and physics-informed AI among its work.

name: KAIST Center for Anthropocene Studies
summary: Centre run by KAIST, where a December 2020 talk notice identifies Myung-Ae Choi as an assistant professor and researcher.

name: Kangwon National University
summary: University that leads a Korea Forest Service project including the development of forest carbon monitoring algorithms based on multi-source satellite imagery and AI.

name: Kookmin University
summary: University whose authors appear on a 2026 forest monitoring paper and a 2025 deep learning mangrove mapping paper listed in OpenAlex.

name: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology
summary: University that builds Eco.AI Korea, with a team led by Kim Changick that improved the Eco.AI algorithm, presented at AAAI 2025.

name: Korea AeroSpace Administration
summary: Korean space agency that announced the CAS500-4 launch with the Rural Development Administration and Korea Forest Service, with the two satellites to pass to its National Satellite Operation Center after initial operations, a 2026 report says.

name: Korea Aerospace Research Institute
summary: Daejeon-based institute that runs CAS500 and operates Korea's national satellites, and says it combines high-resolution satellite data with AI for applications such as land cover classification.

name: Korea Arboreta and Gardens Institute
summary: Sejong-based institute, founded in 2017 according to a July 2026 report, that runs the National Baekdudaegan Arboretum and is named as publisher of native plant specimen image data.

name: Korea Biodiversity Observation Network
summary: Programme built by the National Institute of Biological Resources in 2012, which works with 22 private groups on nationwide monitoring of climate change bioindicators and uses Naturing.

name: Korea Database on Protected Areas
summary: Dataset built by the Korea Environmental Conservation Institute that covers 3,392 protected areas of 30 types under 14 laws and is also used to submit records to the World Database on Protected Areas.

name: Korea Environment Institute
summary: Institute listed by THE VC as lead institution on BiodivAID.

name: Korea Environmental Conservation Institute
summary: Institute that builds the Korea Database on Protected Areas, and whose page describes the 30×30 Alliance to protect 30% of national territory and restore 30% of damaged areas.

name: Korea Environmental Industry and Technology Institute
summary: Institute whose listed AI commercialisation programme includes aquatic ecosystem monitoring, with 17 gram tracker research conducted under a public technology development programme.

name: Korea Forest Service
summary: Government forest agency that runs CAS500-4 and says it plans to use AI, drones and satellites against pine wilt, with 2024 plans to expand AI-camera wildfire monitoring.

name: Korea Forestry Promotion Institute
summary: Organisation whose page describes forest management certification and which is named as client of a 2025 UAV survey with AI analysis.

name: Korea Institute of Ocean Science and Technology
summary: Busan-based institute leading tidal-flat monitoring, which a June 2026 report says collects ocean climate data from research vessels, stations and overseas bases.

name: Korea International Cooperation Agency
summary: Agency whose CIAT programme funded training linked to a community forest data portal in ASEAN.

name: Korea Marine Environment Management Corporation
summary: Organisation that publishes survey data, with no further detail given.

name: Korea National Arboretum
summary: Arboretum in Pocheon that builds Bioblitz Korea, publishes a national vascular plant checklist through GBIF, and per a press report started a citizen plant phenology app in September 2025.

name: Korea National Park Service
summary: Park agency under the ministry that builds Bandal Lens AI, which it said in October 2026 would identify 17 mammal species in camera-trap footage at over 90% accuracy.

name: Korea Network for River and Watershed
summary: Network whose 50 member organisations joined citizen migratory bird monitoring at 60 sites in February 2022, following its February 2021 start, EAAFP reported in April 2022.

name: Korea phenological forest-type maps
summary: Dataset of national forest-type maps for 2019 to 2021, made with a U-Net on Sentinel-2 data and reaching 83.13 percent overall accuracy.

name: Korea Society of Forest Environment Research
summary: Society conducting UAV pine wilt surveys since 2018, expanding into AI image analysis, and listing a 2025 AI survey for the Korea Forestry Promotion Institute.

name: Korea University
summary: University whose team, a vendor case study says, mapped national forest types with a U-Net, and which OpenAlex ranks second for Korean deep learning and ecology works since 2021.

name: Korean Biodiversity Information Facility
summary: Korea's GBIF country node with voting status, run by the National Science Museum of Korea, where its secretariat was set up in January 2008.

name: Korean Bioinformation Center
summary: Daejeon-based national centre for managing biological data, according to a 2018 abstract, which runs the Korean Bioresource Information System linking biodiversity and bioresource data.

name: Korean Bioresource Information System
summary: Dataset run and built by the Korean Bioinformation Center, which collects, processes, analyses and distributes bioresources data.

name: Korean National Trust
summary: Trust set up in 2000 to conserve donated heritage permanently; a May 2026 release reported eight sites held, including the Ganghwa Maehwamarum colony and an Imjin River crane habitat.

name: Korean Natural History Research Information System
summary: Korean biodiversity information system run by the National Science Museum of Korea; its home page reported 14,717 species, 598,812 specimens and 711,523 observations on 2 November 2026.

name: Korean Society for Environmental DNA
summary: Academic body studying environmental DNA analysis, applied to monitoring and endangered species.

name: KT
summary: Company that says it will build long-term ecological monitoring by linking ICT and automatic weather stations.

name: Kwangwoon University
summary: University named as one of five partners in the AI-BioDynamics project, with its School of Information Convergence listed on an EGU 2026 abstract.

name: Leaf Engineering
summary: Organisation whose page describes YOLO and CNN deep learning for detecting endangered wildlife in unmanned camera and drone images.

name: MBRIS
summary: System run by the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea, whose spatial service opened fully in December 2021, offering 425,396 quality-checked records covering 8,860 registered species.

name: Migratory Birds Center, National Park Research Institute
summary: Bird ringing centre of the National Park Research Institute, reported in 2017 to run year-round surveys from Heuksando and Taean, and said in 2015 to have ringed about 50,000 birds in ten years.

name: Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment
summary: Korean ministry that designates species under the Integrated Wildlife Management System; its Nature and Ecology Policy Division has a deputy director listed as CBD primary national focal point.

name: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (Republic of Korea)
summary: Korean ministry that runs the National Marine Ecosystem Survey, held since 2015 per its March 2024 statement, and announced in March 2026 plans to support 20 AI commercialisation projects.

name: Ministry of Science and ICT
summary: Korean ministry named as funder of AI-BioDynamics.

name: Moonsoft
summary: Organisation listed in Seoul on an EGU 2026 abstract and named as a project partner of AI-BioDynamics.

name: Nakdong River Basin Environmental Office
