summary: Office given overall charge of Upo Wetland (1,278,285 sq m) and its monitoring, including at least quarterly water checks, in a 2007 National Archives account.

name: Nakdonggang National Institute of Biological Resources
summary: Institution listed by Korea's CBD clearing house among the environment ministry's institutions; its site links a freshwater biodiversity information portal.

name: Nara Space Technology
summary: Company described by a partner's release as Seoul-based, which runs EarthPaper and builds EP-Agent; a trade report says it uses its own small satellites and AI analysis.

name: National Ecosystem Survey
summary: Programme whose second to fourth round data, covering 1997 to 2018, were cleaned, and whose citizen strand began in 2019 with about 730 participants so far, as reported in 2023.

name: National Forest Satellite Information Technology Center
summary: Centre run by the National Institute of Forest Science that works on detecting forest resource changes and monitoring forest disasters from satellite imagery.

name: National Geographic Information Institute
summary: Land ministry affiliate in Suwon that sets the geodetic reference system, produces geospatial information including the National Base Map, and runs the National Land Satellite programme.

name: National Institute of Biological Resources
summary: National Biodiversity Center in Incheon that prepares Korea's CBD report and says its biodiversity AI model supports searches for species, specimen and image data.

name: National Institute of Ecology
summary: Institute in Seocheon under the environment ministry that runs EcoBank, which it also built, and per a 2025 report built Eco.AI with Sphere AX.

name: National Institute of Environmental Research
summary: Institute in Incheon that runs an algal bloom forecast and real-time algal bloom monitoring; on 3 May 2026 it announced AI forecasts for summer blooms starting 4 May.

name: National Institute of Fisheries Science
summary: Fisheries institute that says it is releasing a photograph-based marine mammal identification service, linked as builder of NIFS whale photo identification AI.

name: National Institute of Forest Science
summary: Seoul forest institute run by Korea Forest Service that reportedly developed LiDAR tree classification AI and made a national forest carbon map using machine learning.

name: National Land Satellite
summary: Satellite programme run by NGII and built by Korea Aerospace Industries; a 2026 report says CAS500-2 launched on 3 May, twin to the 2021 satellite.

name: National Land Satellite Center
summary: Centre established within NGII on 1 November 2019, whose history lists CAS500-1 image service in December 2021 and regular service of three CAS500 products in February 2024.

name: National Long-Term Ecological Research
summary: Programme run by the National Institute of Ecology, with a disclosed period of March 2014 to December 2025, observing community dynamics, phenology and carbon uptake in major ecosystems to analyse climate change impacts.

name: National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea
summary: Institute in Seocheon-gun that runs MBRIS, has a Biodiversity & AI Office, and in 2024 ran a spatial analysis course for marine researchers using MBRIS and OBIS data.

name: National Nature Trust (Korea)
summary: Trust set up under the 2006 National Trust Act to acquire and permanently conserve natural assets, targeting the Baekdudaegan, islands and coast, the DMZ and sensitive areas such as Gotjawal.

name: National Park Core Genetic Resources Database
summary: Proposed database of genetic information on national park wildlife; in May 2026 the Korea National Park Service announced a 22 May web release of 13,555 items, including genetic resources from 50 endangered species.

name: National Science Museum of Korea
summary: Museum that runs NARIS, the Korean Biodiversity Information Facility and a natural history research information system, and acts as GBIF's Korean secretariat; GBIF lists 244 published datasets for it.

name: National Species List of Korea
summary: Inventory of Korean species, run by the National Institute of Biological Resources, which a January 2024 government release says reached 60,010 species at the end of December 2023.

name: NatureBlitz
summary: Service built by Invalab that combines drones, AI and spatial information technology as a one-stop offering.

name: NatureOne
summary: Company that, according to a July 2021 Newsis report, signed a non-exclusive licence with the National Institute of Ecology for a wildlife monitoring system and method patent.

name: NatureX
summary: Proposed software-as-a-service digital twin platform built by Invalab, which the company aims to perfect and fully launch.

name: Naturing Inc.
summary: Seoul company running Naturing, an online platform where users record species, run bioblitzes and share results, described by GBIF as South Korea's first citizen science platform for biodiversity.

name: NIER algal bloom forecast
summary: Algal bloom forecast run by the National Institute of Environmental Research, combining an AI model with a numerical model for seven days of information, with twice-weekly publication reported for May to October through Mulmoa.

name: NIFoS LiDAR tree species classification
summary: LiDAR tree species classification model built by the National Institute of Forest Science, reporting 99% accuracy for coniferous versus broadleaved forest, with plans to extend it to more species.

name: NIFS whale photo identification AI
summary: Photo identification model built by the National Institute of Fisheries Science for ten marine mammal species common in Korean seas, trained on 20 years of survey images, with a location-based monitoring system planned.

name: OJEong Resilience Institute
summary: Korea University institute led by Woo-kyun Lee that studies global ecosystem resilience, using satellite data and AI analysis in tipping point research, and was established from an alumnus donation.

name: ONEOMICS
summary: Company whose listed environmental DNA purposes include biodiversity surveys and early detection of invasive species.

name: POSCO DX
summary: Company partnering on the national park roadkill prevention pilot, whose engineers used its own Vision AI to optimise the system for reading wildlife.

name: Pyeongchang pine wilt helicopter AI survey
summary: Proposed survey, reported in August 2026, in which AI and specialists would analyse helicopter imagery to locate suspected pine wilt trees, called by the Korea Forest Service the first wide-area precision survey of its kind.

name: Saemangeum Shorebird Monitoring Program
summary: Shorebird monitoring programme run by Birds Korea, with a funder page giving its third year as April to May 2008.

name: Sangmyung University
summary: University whose authors appear on a 2022 paper listed in OpenAlex.

name: Seoul Metropolitan Government
summary: City government that, as of March 2025, had designated 18 ecological and landscape conservation areas totalling 5,244,318 sq m, with district and project offices patrolling them on site.

name: Seoul National University
summary: University whose authors produced work including a 2024 mapping of 24 mammal species with random forest models and a 2026 paper detecting marine species sounds with YOLO.

name: Seoul National University of Science and Technology
summary: University named as a project partner of AI-BioDynamics, with its Applied Artificial Intelligence department listed on the EGU 2026 abstract.

name: Shinsegae I&C
summary: A company that runs the Green Wave project, which a press report describes as its conservation activity.

name: SI Analytics
summary: A company described as using imagery to provide AI geospatial analysis, with tools that classify land types.

name: SI Imaging Services
summary: Daejeon company responsible for worldwide commercial satellite imagery supply, whose site says SpaceEye-T launched in March 2025 and operates under it.

name: Sinpyeong-ri Village Association
summary: Village association named in a 2024 provincial evaluation report as contractor for Jeju Gotjawal Provincial Park management and operation, 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2024.

name: SK hynix
summary: Company running Yongin biodiversity work that held the September 2022 AI Challenge and June 2024 forum, aiming, it says, to apply AI to about 60,000 Korean species.

name: Sphere AX
summary: An AI company, led by Park Yoon-ha according to a May 2025 trade report, that builds Eco.AI and Eco.AI Korea and lists deep learning wildlife detection among its products.

name: Supgwa Nanum Foundation
summary: A foundation named in a September 2022 announcement as co-organiser of the planned AI Challenge for Biodiversity, whose director spoke at the 2024 forum.

name: UNIST
summary: The cited IRIS Lab description says it integrates remote sensing, GIS modelling and AI.

name: University of Seoul
summary: A university with authors on a 2024 paper and a 2026 paper that uses tabular transformers to assess river health.

name: Urban wild boar AI monitoring system
summary: A model built by the National Institute of Biological Resources that uses deep learning on drone and camera footage to detect boar within 3 km, which the ministry planned to offer local governments from November 2026.

name: Water Resources Satellite
summary: A proposed satellite that K-water calls the world's first dedicated water resources satellite, planned for launch in 2027.

name: Waterbird Network Korea
summary: An organisation named as an organiser of the 2024 Black-faced Spoonbill study, which ran nationwide monitoring four times.

name: Winter Waterbird Simultaneous Census (Korea)
summary: A March 2024 report says the National Institute of Biological Resources announced results from its winter bird census covering 200 wetlands nationwide since 2015.

name: Wondong Wetland biodiversity conservation
summary: A proposed project that chose Wondong Wetland as its first site, which is home to otters and the only natural site of a threatened plant.

name: Wonju Regional Environmental Office
summary: Regional environmental office whose own site describes Daeamsan Yongneup as a high-moor wetland protected area designated in August 1999 and managed as such.

name: WWF-Korea
summary: An organisation that SUNCOM names as a partner in its pilots.

name: Yeonsu District Office, Incheon
summary: District office named on Incheon City's ocean page (last updated November 2019) as managing authority of the 6.11 sq km Songdo Getbol wetland protected area, tidal flats inhabited by black-faced spoonbills.

name: Yongin Semiconductor Cluster Biodiversity Project
summary: A project run by SK hynix that records biodiversity change around the Yongin cluster through citizen science, uses AI based on Microsoft Azure, and has seven main tasks.

name: ㈜선도소프트
summary: Company that was lead contractor for the AI Hub national park change detection monitoring dataset, and is named in a Ministry of Education listing alongside a satellite-based carbon sink time series.

name: ㈜아이지아이에스
summary: Company whose listing names a Korea Forest Service drone image big data management system and ecological restoration monitoring for the Korea Forest Service.

name: 갯벌 공간정보 변화 모니터링 기술개발
summary: A tidal flat spatial information monitoring technology project led by the Korea Institute of Ocean Science and Technology and Juhyoung Yoo, costing about 20 billion won in total over two stages.

name: 네이처렌즈
summary: Wishket describes photographic AI species identification and hazard judgement; a 2026 project upgraded its model, pursuing integration with National Institute of Biological Resources species data, weather and specialist AI.

name: 땡스카본
summary: A company that says it developed the nature-tech platform Terre, and is recorded as its builder.

name: 떼르
summary: An AI-based biodiversity monitoring and project proposal platform, according to its abstract, built by Thanks Carbon.

name: 산림탄소 흡수·저장 기능 증진을 위한 임분과 경관 수준의 산림 관리 기술 개발
summary: Korean project running April 2024 to December 2026 that includes developing and validating forest carbon monitoring algorithms using multi-source satellite imagery and AI, and building a database.

name: 산불 초기 예측 및 능동적 대처를 위한 다중 드론 기반 이동형 센서 데이터 획득 및 운용 핵심 기술 개발
summary: Gyeongsang National University project, April 2021 to December 2023, aimed at combining sensors, AI, drones and AR for early wildfire prediction; its record lists a 2023 licence for an AI-based prediction method.

name: 스마트 산림보호 플랫폼 개발
summary: Chungnam National University project, April 2020 to December 2022, aimed at drone and aerial image identification of trees killed by pine wilt disease and hyperspectral monitoring of street tree growth and water stress.

name: 주식회사 썬컴
summary: A Busan company that says it developed an AI video analysis platform through electronic monitoring pilots from 2020, identifying species and measuring length and height.

name: 카이스트 생태연구센터
summary: Ecology research centre run by KAIST, whose research fields are given in KAIST's centre directory.

name: 한국지능정보사회진흥원
summary: Organisation named alongside the Ministry of Science and ICT on AI-Hub's page.

name: 한국환경생태연구소
summary: Korean environmental ecology institute whose research team a 2017 government briefing associates with a 17 gram wildlife tracker using mobile networks.

name: 해양수산과학기술진흥원
summary: Organisation designated as the managing body of a programme, with no further detail given.

name: A Remote Sensing Based Early Warning System for Algal Blooms in Kuwait Bay and Coastal Waters
summary: Closed project that aimed to test satellite methods for identifying algal blooms in Kuwait's waters and build a database and web platform, run by the Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research and Western Michigan University.

name: Beatona
summary: Kuwait's official environmental portal, run by the Environment Public Authority and built by it and eMISK, with one map application for making environmental maps and another for downloadable research maps.

name: Department of Geography, Kuwait University
summary: Kuwait University department, given as the affiliation of the first author of a 2025 paper modelling urban expansion effects on Kuwait's land ecosystems with random forest and cellular automata.

name: Environment Public Authority
summary: Kuwaiti authority whose remit includes defining and managing protected areas, and which lists among its achievements a database of more than 250 geographic layers and satellite images.

name: Environmental Monitoring Information System of Kuwait
summary: Programme initiated by the Environment Public Authority to build a geo-environmental database of Kuwait, holding over 250 geographic layers, nationwide satellite images and more than twenty years of monitoring data.

name: Hayat Team for Wildlife Conservation
summary: Volunteering group that runs a research project, listed as ongoing since 2018, monitoring and recording seasonal changes in Failaka Island's flora.

name: Kuwait Dive Team
summary: Part of the Voluntary Environmental Foundation; Al Jarida reported it monitored coral reefs south of Umm Al-Maradim in June 2020 and fitted 35 moorings at Kubbar island in October 2026.

name: Kuwait Environment Protection Society
summary: NGO using eBird for field data, with Arab Times reporting winter bird counts since 2012 and a nationwide count covering 1–17 January 2026.

name: Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research
summary: Partially independent government research institute, according to its then director general, which funded a past project with Western Michigan University on satellite mapping of algal blooms in Kuwait Bay.

name: Kuwait University
summary: University whose Department of Geography is the affiliation of a 2025 paper's first author, and which Times Kuwait reported in June 2025 as a partner in a national sea turtle monitoring project.

name: Kuwaiti Environmental Lens
summary: Programme of the Environment Public Authority that, Times Kuwait reported in August 2022, tracked eagle migration using solar-powered devices with KFAS support and supervision.

name: Monitoring and Documentation of Biodiversity in Kuwait
summary: Project to document Kuwait's biodiversity and help establish a national database, funded by the Environment Public Authority and run by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.

name: Monitoring and Documenting of Native Flora in Failaka Island
summary: Project, listed as running from 2018 and ongoing, to observe and record changes in Failaka Island's flora across several seasons, run by the Hayat Team for Wildlife Conservation.

name: Public Authority for Agriculture Affairs and Fish Resources
summary: Authority responsible, per the CBD's draft country profile, for national parks and combating desertification, and said by the Environment Public Authority to supervise the Sulaibikhat Bay marine reserve.

name: A.N. Bukeikhan Kazakh Research Institute of Forestry and Agroforestry
summary: Research institute whose site lists monitoring of forest ecosystem condition as a main line of its forest protection sector, and a laboratory of ecological monitoring.

name: Aerospace Committee of the Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development of the Republic of Kazakhstan
summary: Government committee within Kazakhstan's Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development; its page says the KazEOSat-1 and KazEOSat-2 system fully supplies the country with remote sensing data.

name: Aksu-Zhabagly State Nature Reserve
summary: Founded in 1926 as the country’s first reserve according to UNDP, it had 25 camera traps installed by July 2021, used for biodiversity monitoring according to Qazinform.

name: Akzhaiyk State Nature Reserve
summary: Protected area where staff monitor daily, found dead birds on Shalyga island on 16 July 2025, and where the regional akimat says three fixed towers with thermal imagers and cameras allow round-the-clock watch.

name: Alakol State Nature Reserve
summary: A state nature reserve that lists scientific monitoring among its four main lines of work and partners with the Institute of Zoology, including on GPS-tracking of pelicans and gulls.

name: Altyn Dala Conservation Initiative
summary: Steppe conservation programme working since 2005 or 2006 (sources differ) across 75 million hectares, led by ACBK and built by FZS and ACBK, using aerial surveys and saiga tracking.

name: Altyn-Emel State National Nature Park
summary: National park whose listed tasks include biodiversity conservation methods and ecosystem monitoring under the Chronicle of Nature programme; it takes part in an annual winter census of argali, kulan and goitered gazelle (2025).

name: Assessment of impact linear infrastructure construction on Saiga populations and actions to reduce damage species and its ecosystems in Kazakhstan
summary: A closed 2023–2025 project led by Nazerke Bizhanova, with objectives including ground, aerial and satellite migration tracking, that studied saiga behaviour using camera traps near artificial railway crossings.

name: Association for the Conservation of Biodiversity of Kazakhstan
summary: Conservation body active since 2004, tracking saiga with satellite collars since 2009 and publishing to GBIF, whose specialist reports developing AI counts of saiga, kulan and goitered gazelle.

name: Astana International University
summary: University whose NatureLaB laboratory studies Kazakhstan's flora, and which publishes through GBIF a checklist of native vascular plants covering 5,883 taxa.

name: Bayanaul State National Nature Park
summary: National park where camera traps operate in the forests through joint work of park staff and doctoral students from Toraighyrov University, its partner.

name: Beeline Kazakhstan
summary: Telecoms company which, according to VEON, deployed the Orman-AI monitoring system with the Kostanay regional natural resources department.

name: Biodiversity Conservation Fund of Kazakhstan
summary: Established by Kazakh environmental NGOs in 2007, this grant-giving fund reported in December 2022 that it was running a four-year, $1.2 million AFoCO-funded forest inventory and software pilot.

name: Biodiversity Research and Conservation Center (Kazakhstan)
summary: Non-governmental, non-profit organisation, established in 2020 according to the Rufford Foundation, whose biologists have monitored Egyptian vultures since 2022 and ringed 27 over three seasons, 13 in 2025.

name: Bird Ringing Research Centre, Institute of Zoology
summary: Centre run by the Institute of Zoology, described on its August 2020 page as Kazakhstan's only laboratory of its kind for marking birds, which processes ring records and has written programs to check migration data.

name: Burabay State National Nature Park
summary: National park that counts animals each February to March, using camera traps and drone filming to record movements and estimate numbers, with results reported by its chief game manager Yuri Zelinsky.

name: Cadastre of wild animals of the arid territories of the Balkhash–Alakol Basin with assessment of threats to their conservation and sustainable use
summary: Closed 2023 to 2025 project, led by Marina Chirikova, that aimed to create an electronic cadastre of the Balkhash–Alakol Basin's fauna by building a digital database of available information.

name: Central Asian Mammals Migration and Linear Infrastructure Atlas
summary: Open-access tool, as described by FZS, into which saiga movement data feeds.

name: Charyn State National Nature Park
summary: National park whose wildlife-monitoring camera traps recorded roe deer, which the park presents as a result of its conservation and research work, with monitoring continuing.

name: Checklist of Native Vascular Plants of Kazakhstan
summary: Open dataset, licensed CC BY 4.0 and published by Astana International University, documenting the whole country's native vascular flora: 5,883 taxa in 978 genera and 128 families.

name: Chokpak Ornithological Station
summary: Field station of the Institute of Zoology that says over 1.7 million birds of 236 species have been ringed on the Chokpak pass, over 70 per cent of Kazakhstan's ringed birds, and 12 species tagged with GPS/GSM transmitters.

name: Conservation and management of the brown bear (Ursus arctos) population in the Kazakh part of the Altai
summary: A programme that ran from 2020 to 2025, led by Sanzhar Kantarbayev, with tasks including adapting population assessment methods for the Kazakh Altai and counting and monitoring bears.

name: Conservation and Sustainable Management of Key Globally Important Ecosystems for Multiple Benefits
summary: Closed UNDP project, run with the Kazakh government from 2018 to 2024, which UNDP says installed 294 camera traps in 14 pilot protected areas and eight forestry enterprises, and piloted SMART patrolling in 2019.

name: Creating of Supplemental Feeding Sites for the Conservation of Vulture's Population in Ustyurt State Nature Reserve, Kazakhstan
summary: A closed project that planned vulture feeding sites monitored with hides and camera traps in 2016, with 2018 camera-trap results that also recorded a Persian leopard.

name: Development of a system for sustainable use of the Betpak-Dala and Ustyurt saiga populations
summary: Active 2024 to 2026 programme, code BR23591114, aiming to map saiga ranges, calving areas and migration routes with collar tracking, and to build a forage database from satellite vegetation indices.

name: Development of an information system for maintaining the cadastre of wild animals of the Western Tien Shan
summary: Run by the Institute of Zoology and led by Aydyn Eszhanov in 2024–2026, the programme plans a GIS-linked fauna database, promising free access for agencies, universities and environmental NGOs.

name: Early forest and steppe fire detection system (Kazakhstan)
summary: Programme piloting AI-based early detection of forest and steppe fires in the Semey Ormany reserve with 37 cameras over 510,000 hectares, planned to cover the most fire-prone areas of 24 parks and reserves by July 2026.

name: Ertis Ormany State Forest Natural Reserve
summary: Forest nature reserve whose science department found a golden eagle nest during fauna monitoring, and where a camera trap recorded roe deer, elk, wild boar and raccoon dog.

name: Forest Fire Early Detection System (Kazakhstan)
summary: Kazakh project whose specification, the environment minister said, provides for AI hardware and software, with the system introduced in Ertis Ormany and Kokshetau in 2023.

name: Forest Hero
summary: Company still developing its product in November 2024, whose platform, according to Digital Business, uses AI to advise tree planting locations and help monitor forest condition.

name: Forestry and Wildlife Committee of the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources of the Republic of Kazakhstan
summary: Government committee, run by the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources, that implements, controls and supervises forestry, wildlife and specially protected natural territories.

name: GIS and Remote Sensing Department, Institute of Zoology
summary: Run by the Institute of Zoology, the department aims to develop geo-information technology for research, with priorities including remote-sensing monitoring and species niche modelling.

name: Ile-Alatau State National Nature Park
summary: National park that says it monitors snow leopards with 35 camera traps, including 20 donated under the UNDP programme, and has given 22 leopards an ID code.

name: Ile-Balkhash State Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve where, the ministry says, animals are monitored round the clock from a control centre, each released tiger is to wear a satellite GPS collar, and prey numbers including wild boar rose.

name: Institute of Botany and Phytointroduction
summary: Research institute under the forestry and wildlife committee, whose site lists digital maps, a Taraz green space database and a cadastre of Almaty region higher vascular plants.

name: Institute of Zoology of the Republic of Kazakhstan
summary: Research institute and GBIF publisher in Almaty whose Snow Leopard Monitoring Centre scientists collected data to train a neural network, according to Yandex Cloud.

name: International Waterbird Census in Kazakhstan
summary: Waterbird count run by ACBK in Kazakhstan; the January 2025 count recorded 22,839 birds of 34 species, with data sent to Wetlands International.

name: Karaganda National Research University named after academician Ye.A. Buketov
summary: University in Karaganda that publishes 29 datasets through GBIF, including a national earthworm checklist, White-headed Duck records and a Karkaraly park flora inventory.

name: Karatau State Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve whose staff and PO Okhotzooprom counted argali on 25 to 29 September 2023, putting the endemic population at 1,309, reported as 15% more than the year before.

name: Katon-Karagai National Park
summary: National park where, per Tengrinews quoting the Forestry and Wildlife Committee in February 2025, camera traps were installed in the Altai forestry area to track wild animals.

name: Kazakh Forest Management Enterprise
summary: State forest inventory organisation, named in ministry rules as a republican state enterprise covering forest resource accounting and state forest monitoring, which includes use of Earth remote sensing data.

name: Kazakh-British Technical University
summary: University whose third-year students, mentored by Yandex Cloud experts, built a snow leopard neural network trained on thousands of images, which Yandex Cloud says analyses millions of camera-trap images an hour.

name: Kazakhstan Earth Remote Sensing Space System
summary: Two-satellite system, KazEOSat-1 and KazEOSat-2, with ground complexes; a ministry page reports all forest land digitised in 2018 and daily monitoring of felling, burnt spots and fire hazard.

name: Kazakhstan Gharysh Sapary
summary: Company that Bizmedia reported in June 2023 was named by a ministry order as national operator of the Earth remote sensing space system and the satellite navigation system.

name: Kolsai Kolderi State National Nature Park
summary: National park reporting 16 snow leopards in July 2021; in January 2020, the Institute of Zoology reported camera-trap guidance and responsibility for staff training in snow leopard monitoring.

name: Korgalzhyn State Nature Reserve
summary: A state nature reserve whose scientific staff, Informburo reported in 2018, counted animals and birds by air once a year and from the ground several times a year.

name: Kyzylsay State Regional Natural Park
summary: Regional natural park where 38 cameras, the first installed in 2021, had taken about 17,000 images by February 2024, according to its director Mynbergen Karatauov.

name: Laboratory of Theriology, Institute of Zoology
summary: Laboratory run by the Institute of Zoology that says it uses camera traps, satellite telemetry and drones to study rare mammals, and that four snow leopards were fitted with satellite collars in 2021 and 2022.

name: Markakol State Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve where a camera trap set by inspector Krasnopeev recorded lynx, sable, squirrel and hare, as reported by NewTimes.kz on 16 February 2022.

name: Merke Department for Protection of Forests and Wildlife
summary: Local forest and wildlife protection department that UNDP says received 11 GEF-funded camera traps, which recorded a snow leopard family in 2021, and was credited for protection measures in Zhambyl region.

name: Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources of the Republic of Kazakhstan
summary: Kazakh ministry that, according to UNDP, published the Seventh National Biodiversity Report in 2025 with UNDP support, and in July 2026 reported funds directed to fire detection and drones.

name: Monitoring of Specially Protected Species of Birds of Prey and Mammals Using Camera Traps at Feeding Sites in the Ustyurt State Nature Reserve, Kazakhstan
summary: Closed 2022 Rufford-listed project in Karakiya, Kazakhstan, that planned camera-trap monitoring of predators at feeding sites and an assessment of overhead power line impacts on raptors in Mangistau region.

name: National Centre of Geodesy and Spatial Information
summary: Astana-based body whose site describes topographic, geodetic, aerial survey and cartographic work, including digital maps for GIS, and lists the national spatial data fund and Kazakhstan's open spatial data portal.

name: Naurzum State Nature Reserve
summary: Scientists reportedly ringed just over fifty young rooks to study migration by July 2023, and a camera trap recorded a moose in the reserve in 2025.

name: Orman-AI
summary: Wildfire detection programme in which, VEON says, Beeline tower cameras feed an AI engine trained to recognise smoke; VEON reports 34 cameras gave early alerts for 50 fires in testing.

name: Pallas’s Cat in Kazakhstan: From Investigation to Conservation – Phase 2
summary: A closed second-phase project, listed on Rufford in April 2017, that aimed to gather new data on Pallas's cat and its threats through camera traps and interview surveys.

name: Pilot project on inventory of unaccounted forests in Kostanay and North Kazakhstan regions and automation of information collection on forestry
summary: AFoCO-funded pilot, with a memorandum signed in March 2022, to inventory unaccounted forests in two regions; by March 2023 a contractor was chosen for an information system on the state forest fund.

name: PO Okhotzooprom
summary: Organisation that ACBK says organised the 2026 saiga aerial count on the Forestry and Wildlife Committee's instruction, and that held a contract with ACBK in 2025 covering saiga calving observation and monitoring.

name: Population and Conservation Status of the Turkestan Lynx in the Kazakh Part of the Northern Tien Shan
summary: A closed project led by Nazerke Bizhanova with a 2019 Rufford Small Grant, using camera traps in three protected areas, with a reported effort of 8,278 camera-days.

name: Safe Passage for Saiga: Studying Migration to Reduce Human-Wildlife Conflicts in Ustyurt
summary: Rufford Foundation-listed project, dated 19 February 2026, that plans GPS satellite tags on saiga and camera traps to study migration on the Ustyurt plateau, with recommendations to be developed with the Committee for Forestry and Wildlife.

name: Sairam-Ugam National Park
summary: Protected area where UNDP reported in July 2021 that SMART patrol systems were in active use, and says a GIS database of the SMART system was created for it.

name: Semey Ormany State Forest Natural Reserve
summary: Forest nature reserve where the early fire detection system was piloted, with operations centres in all ten branches across seven districts of Abai region, and a general director named Kazbek Ametov.

name: Snow Leopard Foundation (Kazakhstan)
summary: Foundation whose director said in 2019 that researchers set up camera traps in Trans-Ili Alatau gorges and collected genetic samples, and which Yandex Cloud says joined its 2024 snow leopard neural network project.

name: Studying Rare and Hunting Species of Geese and Branta in the North of Kazakhstan and Creation of Monitoring System and Set of Actions for their Protection
summary: A closed project that planned to tag nesting and migrating geese with satellite transmitters, rings and collars, and to work out migration routes and key areas from the data.

name: Syrdarya–Turkestan State Regional Natural Park
summary: Regional natural park whose science department monitors animal and plant life continuously with camera traps, drones and other technology, and which has more than 350 staff.

name: Toraighyrov University
summary: University publishing a GBIF dataset of camera-trap monitoring of terrestrial mammals in northeastern Kazakhstan, the first release of a long-term monitoring programme, alongside research in biology, ecology and biodiversity conservation.

name: Ulytau State National Nature Park
summary: National park in which camera traps were installed to count animals, follow their movements and protect the natural environment, as part of strengthened wildlife monitoring using modern technology.

name: Unified database of rare and endangered animal species of Kazakhstan
summary: The Institute of Zoology built this database during its Red Book update and reports 2,959 records, promising rapid analysis and population monitoring.

name: Ustyurt State Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve where camera traps on its territory recorded a Persian leopard, and where staff continue to monitor the animal's movements.

name: Wildlife Without Borders
summary: Conservation group that a CEPF review says installed up to 50 camera traps to study snow leopards; it launched an IUCN-backed project near Almaty in 2020 and co-organised a 2025 snow leopard monitoring training.

name: Wings - Animal and Plant Conservation and Protection Fund
summary: Fund publishing GBIF data, including a five-country Central Asian mammal checklist and citizen-science photo records of migrating birds in Kazakhstan, with environmental monitoring in Kazakhstan among its listed goals.

name: Yandex Cloud snow leopard neural network
summary: Neural network built by Yandex Cloud that, the company says, reviews up to 8 million photos an hour and recognises individual snow leopards; Alexey Grachev is quoted saying it helped find about 20 in Altyn-Emel.

name: Zhasyl Damu JSC
summary: State company wholly owned by the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources; in July 2026 the ministry said 16.9 billion tenge was allocated to fire detection systems, drones, video surveillance and data transfer.

name: Zhongar-Alatau State National Nature Park
summary: National park that has worked since 2020 to install permanent camera traps for Turkestan lynx, and which counted 70 to 80 of the animals in its forest belts.

name: Assessing the Status of Northern White-Cheeked Crested Gibbon
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, May 2014 to May 2015, that aimed to improve information on the northern white-cheeked gibbon in and around Phou Den Din National Protected Area.

name: Association Anoulak
summary: French-registered association, registered in September 2014, working on biodiversity conservation in Laos; its 2019 partnership with Nakai-Nam Theun National Park closed in May 2025, and from 2026 it emphasises education and capacity-building.

name: Biodiverse Landscapes Fund Lower Mekong camera trap and acoustic monitoring in Lao PDR
summary: Active camera trap and acoustic monitoring work within the DEFRA-funded Biodiverse Landscapes Fund Lower Mekong project, run by FFI and IUCN, which has trained government staff and community members since 2023.

name: Conservation Initiative for Indochinese Silvered Leaf Monkey in Dong Phouvieng National Protected Area of Savannakhet Province, Central Lao PDR
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, June 2012 to March 2013, aiming to survey the Indochinese silvered leaf monkey in Dong Sakee Sacred forest and strengthen local conservation and monitoring capacity.

name: Conservation of Lao Langur (Trachypithecus laotum) in Phou Hin Poun National Protected Area, Khammouane Province, Laos
summary: Closed project in Phou Hin Poun National Protected Area that set out a field monitoring programme for the Lao langur and expected to train protected area staff in wildlife mapping and surveys.

name: Department of Forest Inspection
summary: Lao forest agency under the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, which GIZ says developed the Provincial Deforestation Monitoring System jointly with the Department of Forestry, with JICA support, and which implements F-REDD 2.

name: Department of Forestry (Lao PDR)
summary: According to JICA, its official forest maps support REDD+ MRV; WWF-Laos says it will lead implementation of the National Tiger Recovery Action Plan.

name: Environment and Forest Protection Fund
summary: Government-established fund in Vientiane, founded in 2005 as financially autonomous, which Vientiane Times reported in March 2021 would provide over 7.9 billion kip for conservation in six provinces.

name: Exchange and training on the SMART system for national protected areas, Lao PDR (2024)
summary: Closed training on the SMART monitoring tool held 17 to 21 June 2024, reported by SNRD Asia, for 36 staff from four national protected areas.

name: Faculty of Forest Science, National University of Laos
summary: Academic faculty named as the first author's affiliation on two 2026 papers, one mapping 2015 to 2025 forest cover change with Random Forest and Planet NICFI imagery, one on restoration site suitability.

name: Fourth National Forest Inventory of Lao PDR
summary: Closed national forest inventory run by the Department of Forestry, launched October 2024 with preliminary results in September 2025, collecting data on forest resources and biodiversity, with World Bank, GIZ and JICA funding.

name: GCF REDD+ emission reduction programme in Lao PDR (GIZ)
summary: GCF-funded REDD+ programme in Laos, run by GIZ, which uses a cloud database from 2020 for real-time forest monitoring and has produced over 240 village forest management plans.

name: Integrated nature conservation and sustainable resource management in the Hin Nam No region
summary: Closed GIZ project, December 2013 to August 2018, funded by BMZ, during which GIZ reported regular use of SMART in protected area management and training of 110 recognised village rangers.

name: Ministry of Agriculture and Environment
summary: Lao ministry that endorsed the NBSAP 2026-2030 and the 7th National Report on 17 August 2026, with its Department of Environment as implementing partner of the UNDP project.

name: Nakai-Nam Theun camera-trap wildlife monitoring programme
summary: Closed camera-trap programme built by Association Anoulak, whose second survey ran February to August 2020 with 133 stations across three priority zones, after systematic surveys in 2018 and 2019.

name: Nakai-Nam Theun National Park
summary: National park designated in February 2019, covering 4,270 square kilometres in Khammuan and Borikhamxay; Vientiane Times reported that a camera-trap monitoring programme was established there in 2020.

name: Nam Et-Phou Louey National Park
summary: Protected area managed under the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry with Wildlife Conservation Society support since 2003, monitoring wildlife with camera traps, transects, listening posts and SMART threat analysis.

name: Nam Poui livestock-wildlife camera trap assessment
summary: Active WWF camera trap assessment, with the Nam Poui Management Authority, in and around Nam Poui National Protected Area, monitoring livestock-wildlife interactions to gather data on possible sources of infectious disease.

name: National Agriculture and Forestry Research Institute
summary: Institute of the Lao agriculture ministry involved in Pha Khao Lao, a joint initiative with the University of Bern's Centre for Development and Environment, with information centre staff contributing.

name: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP7NR)
summary: GEF-funded project listed by UNDP as ongoing from February 2024 to November 2027, strengthening biodiversity data systems and producing an NBSAP 2026-2030 with 25 targets.

name: National Forest Monitoring System (NFMS) Web-Portal
summary: Web portal that lets non-GIS users view basic information on national REDD+ MRV and is hosted on the NFMS server.

name: Participatory Survey, Assessment and Conservation of Green Peafowl in Dongkhanthung Provincial Protected Area of Champasak, the Southwestern Lao PDR
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project that aimed to survey green peafowl in Dongkhanthung Provincial Protected Area and assess its abundance and distribution, with a grant running September 2011 to September 2012.

name: Pha Khao Lao
summary: Platform built and run jointly by NAFRI and the University of Bern's Centre for Development and Environment, with a database integrating information on plant and animal species.

name: Provincial Deforestation Monitoring System
summary: Satellite-based deforestation monitoring tool, built and run by JICA, in use in 15 of 18 provinces in 2024 and upgraded in 2026 with fire data, detecting 16,395 active fires by mid-March.

name: Rediscovering Saola: State-of-the-Art Methods to Detect Endangered Annamite Species in Lao PDR
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, June 2021 to June 2024, aiming to support a search for remaining saolas by developing rapid field DNA tests and a trained detection dog team.

name: The Project for Enhancing Sustainable Forest Management in Collaboration with REDD+ Programs and REDD+ Funds
summary: Active JICA technical cooperation project in Laos, February 2022 to January 2027, supporting forest monitoring; JICA shows map-making and reported the fourth national forest inventory complete in December 2025.

name: WCS Lao PDR
summary: Conservation organisation in Vientiane that has supported government management of Nam Et-Phou Louey National Park since 2003, including wildlife research and monitoring, and works on wildlife health surveillance and trade.

name: WWF-Laos
summary: Conservation organisation that says it supported the National Tiger Recovery Action Plan and reports a camera trap assessment with Nam Poui Management Authority to monitor livestock-wildlife interactions.

name: Xe Champhone Siamese crocodile conservation and monitoring
summary: Active WCS Laos programme with local communities at the Xe Champhone Ramsar site; IUCN reported in February 2025 that 115 crocodiles had been released and were monitored, including by drone.

name: A Rocha Lebanon
summary: Founded in Lebanon in 1996 and based at Meksé Nature Park, it reports biodiversity research and monitoring; MAVA lists it among funding recipients between 1994 and 2022.

name: Al Shouf Cedar Society
summary: Its reports describe biodiversity monitoring in the Shouf Biosphere Reserve, with CEPF funding and Cartier Philanthropy as a partner.

name: American University of Beirut
summary: University whose researchers, AUB says, are using machine learning to develop a smartphone native plant identification tool, and which hosts a Nature Conservation Center established in 2002.

name: Association for Bird Conservation in Lebanon
summary: Lebanese NGO registered in May 2019 for bird and habitat conservation, whose specialists participated in the 2023–2024 nationwide mammal survey of Lebanon’s nature reserves.

name: AUB Nature Conservation Center
summary: A research centre at the American University of Beirut that describes itself as multidisciplinary; a CEPF report on its 2019-2020 grant ($19,908) says it monitored a rare endemic plant and developed a citizen science method for plant monitoring.

name: BioConnect Programme
summary: EU-funded programme launched in February 2022 and run over 45 months by four Lebanese organisations, combining biodiversity monitoring with agriculture, education and policy work, and reported by SPNL as formally concluded.

name: Community-based Wildfire Risk Management in Lebanon's Vulnerable Landscapes
summary: Active project funded by a US$3.48 million GEF grant approved in October 2024 and run by the World Bank, which includes biodiversity assessments, wildfire plans and early warning equipment, with a Ministry of Environment and UNOPS agreement signed on 13 May 2025.

name: Difaf
summary: Environmental consultancy and technical design bureau, founded in Lebanon in 2014, offering mapping, sampling, analysis, modelling and monitoring; a CEPF-funded river basin project report says its eDNA analysis detected 27 vertebrate taxa.

name: Directorate of Geographic Affairs (Lebanese Army)
summary: Lebanese Army directorate, established in 1962, which says it takes charge of all geographic and geodesic works in Lebanon and provides topographic information to ministries' technical departments.

name: Environment for Life
summary: Organisation whose CEPF-funded Mount Hermon olive project (April 2020 to October 2023) named monitoring protocols for biodiversity, illegally killed birds and threatened lizards, and reported surveys showing the groves host 73 bird species.

name: Eurisko Mobility
summary: Company that TelecomDrive described in January 2020 as working in digital transformation, AI, IoT and smart city technology, and as partnering with the Cedar International Festival's committee to offer a system to seven Lebanese forests.

name: Fire Lab early warning index
summary: Fire risk model developed by the University of Balamand which, Touch says, predicts local fire risk one week ahead and is built into the Fire Patrol App promoted in a 2024 campaign.

name: Friends of Nature
summary: Lebanese national NGO, says it was the country's first environmental NGO, founded in 1972; its CEPF-funded 2023 project developed species distribution maps from field observations and strengthened long-term monitoring of endemic plants.

name: Hima Hammana Raptor Observatory
summary: A raptor migration monitoring site run by the Society for the Protection of Nature in Lebanon, also called the Anahita Bird Watching Site, whose manager Chadi Saad did bird monitoring under the EU-funded Bioconnect project.

name: Institute of the Environment, University of Balamand
summary: University of Balamand institute whose project list includes satellite-based forest cover and fuel mapping in 2010 to 2011, a 2011 to 2012 forest fire early warning system, a 2019 post-fire assessment and 2023 to 2024 fauna monitoring plans.

name: Jouzour Loubnan
summary: A Beirut non-profit funded by CEPF, whose 2022-2024 grant (about $19,699) covered monitoring of three endangered Iris species, and whose members took part in a project building a DNA marker reference library.

name: Lebanese plant species identification tool (AUB and Shouf Biosphere Reserve)
summary: The incubator is developing a plant app with Shouf Biosphere Reserve and $3,810 from APS; IEEE reports 90 training classes with about 400 images each.

name: Lebanese University
summary: OpenAlex lists Lebanese University affiliations for the first three authors of a 2025 forest fire risk assessment paper, including one affiliation with its Faculty of Technology in Saida.

name: Lebanon Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: A butterfly monitoring programme run by the Society for the Protection of Nature in Lebanon, founded in 2018 by Husein Zorkot, using fixed-route transect counts by students and volunteers, with results to be published in an atlas.

name: Lebanon Reforestation Initiative
summary: NatureMetrics describes a reforestation programme established in 2011 with USAID funding and a partnered pilot survey detecting 63 vertebrate taxa; GBIF records habitat monitoring and published occurrence datasets.

name: Ministry of Environment (Lebanon)
summary: Lebanese ministry that says it has worked on problems around protected areas causing biodiversity loss, and whose sites the Convention on Biological Diversity lists as Lebanon's national websites for the Convention.

name: National Council for Scientific Research (Lebanon)
summary: Lebanese research council which, L'Orient Today reported on 30 August 2022, warned of heightened fire danger over three days using fire index maps it had prepared.

name: National Early Warning System Platform (Lebanon)
summary: Platform built by CNRS-L on forest fire data collected since 2016, forecasting fire danger up to 72 hours ahead and issuing a daily bulletin; L'Orient Today in July 2024 reported its data on burned land.

name: Palm Island Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve that, with Tyre Coast Nature Reserve, set up a citizen science initiative in which fishers, divers and others report marine species, which a February 2025 Zenodo paper says produced new tunicate records.

name: Quick Track
summary: A mobile app run by the Society for the Protection of Nature in Lebanon for recording biodiversity sightings and reporting environmental violations, described in February 2025 as in a pilot phase.

name: Saving Lebanese Biodiversity Center Incubator
summary: American University of Beirut incubator whose stated mission is robotic, AI and machine learning solutions for Lebanese biodiversity, with current work on tree health detection, a plant recognition app and a seed-deploying drone.

name: Smart Forest (Lebanon)
summary: Forest fire system that TelecomDrive says uses machine learning to sharpen a fire risk index, with development, deployment and maintenance for seven forests estimated at USD 700,000, sponsored by Eurisko Mobility.

name: Society for the Protection of Nature in Lebanon
summary: Established in 1983, this BirdLife partner reports establishing 39 Himas, conducting bird surveys in early 2025 and proposing Smart Himas combining AI with traditional knowledge.

name: STEPping up Nature Reserves Capacity (STEP4Nature)
summary: Project run by UNDP and funded by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation, credited in a 2026 paper with contributing to field surveys for the 2023-2024 mammal survey across 17 Lebanese nature reserves.

name: Tyre Coast Nature Reserve
summary: Lebanese nature reserve whose monitoring team began a 2023 campaign to track sea turtle nests on sandy beaches, with LBC reporting in June 2023 dozens of loggerhead nests found.

name: University of Balamand
summary: Lebanese university whose Institute of the Environment lists a 2013–2014 project to produce fire management maps for the FireWise web application, funded by USAID and the Lebanon Reforestation Initiative.

name: Université Saint-Joseph de Beyrouth
summary: A Beirut university that was grantee of a CEPF-funded 2018-2021 botanical project ($111,990.72), which gathered population data on 16 target plant species, and that led a project creating a DNA marker reference library, according to Jouzour Loubnan.

name: Conserving the Saint Lucia Racer and Strengthening Regional Capacity for Racer Conservation
summary: Active CEPF-funded project, March 2023 to December 2026, with Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust as grantee for Antigua and Barbuda and Saint Lucia, including biosecurity monitoring and habitat enhancement on four Saint Lucian islands.

name: Department of Sustainable Development, Saint Lucia
summary: Saint Lucian government department whose Permanent Secretary the CBD lists as primary CBD focal point, with officers also listed as clearing-house mechanism and protected areas focal points.

name: Engaging local communities in reversing the Endangered White-breasted Thrasher's decline in St. Lucia
summary: Project on the Endangered White-breasted Thrasher in Saint Lucia that used camera traps across the Mandelé range, recording 19 nests at four field sites from July 2020.

name: Flowing Clean
summary: Active project launched on World Environment Day 2025 to restore the Soufrière River, using a multispectral drone operated by six community members trained as certified pilots, funded at US$150,000.

name: Forest Management Information Systems unit (FMIS), Saint Lucia
summary: Unit run by the Forestry Department that, according to the ministry, holds all data the Division collects and handles data collection, analysis, GIS mapping, digitising and reporting, with a team of trained drone pilots.

name: Forestry Department, Saint Lucia
summary: Official body for managing Saint Lucia's forest reserves and terrestrial wildlife, supported by FMIS, and reported in 2024 to use camera traps, drones and real-time cameras for monitoring and feral pig detection.

name: Rejuvenating coral ecosystems by involving local communities and creating new livelihood opportunities
summary: Open coral reef project, December 2025 to December 2026, run by the Saint Lucia National Conservation Fund and funded by the International Climate Initiative, empowering two communities to protect and monitor corals.

name: Saint Lucia National Conservation Fund
summary: Saint Lucia's national conservation trust fund, incorporated in 2016, which funds the Soufriere Marine Management Association.

name: Saint Lucia National Environmental Information System
summary: Saint Lucia's first national environmental information system, launched in August 2018 with UN Environment on a GEF-funded project, and reported by GEF to involve an agreement among 17 major environmental data providers.

name: Saint Lucia National Trust
summary: Established in 1975, this statutory membership body gathers Maria Islands ecological data, supports turtle and mangrove monitoring, organised drone training and received turtle-tagging training in 2021.

name: Securing the future of two Critically Endangered Saint Lucia endemic reptiles
summary: Closed 2023 to 2024 project under the Fondation Segré Conservation Action Fund, aiming to improve population and genetic knowledge of two Critically Endangered reptiles on Maria Major.

name: Soufriere Marine Management Association
summary: Non-profit established in 1994 to oversee marine resources on Saint Lucia's southwestern coast, acting as Local Fisheries Management Authority over about 11 kilometres, and receiving a February 2025 post-Hurricane Beryl grant.

name: Sustenance of monitoring, maintenance and operation of the Pointe Sables Environmental Protection Area (PSEPA) and the Pigeon Island National Landmark (PINL) impacted by COVID-19
summary: Closed BIOPAMA-funded project run by the Saint Lucia National Trust, May 2021 to April 2022, which aimed to improve monitoring and management capacity and planned remote monitoring devices for the Pointe Sables protected area.

name: Amt für Statistik Liechtenstein
summary: National statistics office in Liechtenstein, based in Vaduz, whose annual landscape, forest, soil and biodiversity statistic (2024 edition published 5 February 2026) includes forest area by type since 1984 and species maps.

name: Amt für Tiefbau und Geoinformation (Liechtenstein)
summary: Liechtenstein government office that publishes the Orthophoto Liechtenstein 2020 dataset, 10 cm true-colour aerial imagery flown May to September 2020, and was named in the 2024 draft Biodiversity Action Plan as responsible for measures.

name: Amt für Umwelt (Liechtenstein)
summary: Former Liechtenstein environment office, closed on 1 August 2026 when its name was replaced in law by two offices, and which held main responsibility for many measures in the 2024 draft action plan.

name: Amt für Wald, Natur und Landwirtschaft (Liechtenstein)
summary: Liechtenstein government office listed in the organisation ordinance from 1 August 2026, whose name replaces "Amt für Umwelt" in a set of laws under a July 2026 ordinance.

name: Arten-Monitoring Liechtenstein
summary: Liechtenstein species monitoring programme based on long-term observation of indicator species, set out in a 2020 government concept under which biodiversity had been observed since 2020, as the 2024 draft action plan reported.

name: Botanisch-Zoologische Gesellschaft Liechtenstein-Sargans-Werdenberg
summary: Founded in 1970, this registered Vaduz association studies regional flora and fauna, has taxonomic working groups and had 200 members in 2017.

name: Brutvogelatlas des Fürstentums Liechtenstein
summary: Breeding bird atlas of Liechtenstein, cited by EBBA2 as Willi (2019), published in Vaduz in 180 pages, whose observations were among the data used for EBBA2.

name: Hilti Foundation
summary: Liechtenstein foundation, based in Schaan, that says it acts for biodiversity in the country and commissioned two studies, in 2021 and 2023, from a RENAT biologist on documenting biodiversity and landscape.

name: Inventar der Naturvorrangflächen (Liechtenstein)
summary: An inventory of nationally and locally important areas and objects worthy of protection in Liechtenstein, as of 2025, offered as WMS map layers including habitats worthy of protection.

name: Landeswaldinventar (Liechtenstein)
summary: Surveys Liechtenstein’s forest structure, condition and development every twelve years; official statistics report 48% had high biotope value in 2022, with the next publication expected in 2036.

name: Neophytenstandorte (Liechtenstein)
summary: Geodata set of known neophyte locations in Liechtenstein, issued 13 November 2013 with an irregular update interval, and its current status is unknown.

name: Arthur C Clarke Institute for Modern Technologies
summary: Institute designated in 1994 as Sri Lanka's national focal point for space technology applications; its Space Applications Division works on remote sensing and GIS, and offers consultancy.

name: Biodiversity and Habitat Mapping of Urban Reefs in Colombo
summary: Surveys five offshore reef sites with photo quadrats, fish censuses and drop cameras to develop a habitat management plan; run by Blue Resources Trust, funded by Lanka Environment Fund.

name: Biodiversity Secretariat, Sri Lanka
summary: Run by the Ministry of Environment and described in a ministry addendum to the national biodiversity framework as the national focal point for the CBD.

name: Blue Carbon Stock Assessment of Seagrasses in the Vidattaltivu Nature Reserve
summary: Closed 18-month project that mapped three seagrass species and aimed to assess carbon sequestration for a planned blue carbon credit; funded by Lanka Environment Fund and Blue Marine Foundation.

name: Blue Resources Trust
summary: Registered non-profit in Sri Lanka that says it has created long-term datasets for elasmobranch fisheries and coral reef monitoring.

name: BRT - TCG Coral Reef Monitoring
summary: Annual reef monitoring around Kayankerni Marine Sanctuary, run by Blue Resources Trust with Tokyo Cement Group funding since 2016, alongside GIS mapping and support for Allen Coral Atlas mapping.

name: Central Environmental Authority (Sri Lanka)
summary: Sri Lankan authority whose staff wrote a 2024 conference paper on mapping Western Province wetlands, digitised in QGIS from Google Earth imagery and checked at 789 random field locations.

name: Ceylon Bird Club
summary: Founded in 1943, it reports non-profit, non-governmental status, annual countrywide waterbird censuses since 1984 with Wetlands International and its predecessor, threatened bird monitoring and country bird list maintenance.

name: Conservation of Coral Reefs Associated with the Erumaitivu-Kakkativu Seascape for Community and Ecosystem Resilience
summary: Project run by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, partnered with Sampath Bank, using baseline surveys of coral reefs as a foundation for conservation and future monitoring.

name: Corridors for Conservation
summary: Project run by Wilderness and Wildlife Conservation Trust to establish forest corridors in the Central Highlands, where two have been established; Oak Foundation gave $45,000 in July 2025.

name: Department of Agricultural Biology, University of Ruhuna
summary: University department that is the lead affiliation of the first author on a paper on acoustic records of free-tailed bats in Sri Lanka, which the Daily Mirror says used microphones in eleven tea plantations.

name: Department of Computer Science, University of Ruhuna
summary: University department that is the lead affiliation of the first author on a paper on identifying kingfisher species using machine learning and deep learning.

name: Department of Computing and Information Systems, Wayamba University of Sri Lanka
summary: University department that is the lead affiliation of the first author on a paper on using deep learning to identify fish species in Sri Lanka, including endemic and endangered ones.

name: Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, University of Peradeniya
summary: Engineering department run by the University of Peradeniya, where a group of members initiated and conducted the Elephant-Train Collision Prevention System; its site lists a Multidisciplinary AI Research Center.

name: Department of Forestry and Environmental Science, University of Sri Jayewardenepura
summary: University department that is the lead affiliation of the first and corresponding author on a paper on camera trap monitoring of Indian pangolin in a lowland rainforest in southwest Sri Lanka.

name: Department of Information Technology, Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology
summary: Department listed as the lead affiliation of the first author of a paper on a leopard monitoring and identification system.

name: Department of Wildlife Conservation, Sri Lanka
summary: A department report tabled in Parliament says it is legally responsible for establishing and managing wildlife protected areas, of which 109 have been declared.

name: Department of Zoology and Environmental Sciences, University of Colombo
summary: University department that is the lead affiliation of the first and corresponding author on a paper on elephants crossing electric fences at Udawalawe, using camera traps on 18 posts and a gate over 605 days from 2016 to 2019.

name: Department of Zoology, University of Sri Jayewardenepura
summary: University department that is the lead affiliation of the first author on a paper using camera trap data on the Sri Lanka Spurfowl.

name: Dunkeld Conservation Station
summary: Reported in 2017 as a WWCT study base, with remote cameras at 45 tea estate locations over 11 months identifying 27 individual leopards and 22 other mammal species.

name: Ecosystem Conservation and Management Project (Sri Lanka)
summary: World Bank-funded project in Sri Lanka, approved on 25 April 2016 with a US$45 million IDA credit; a 2020 restructuring paper reports the SMART tool was used for enforcement in southern protected areas.

name: Elephant-Train Collision Prevention System
summary: Prototype AI sensor system built by Peradeniya's electrical and electronic engineering department; its second-phase in-cabin unit was described in February 2025 as detecting elephants up to 500 metres ahead.

name: Field Ornithology Group of Sri Lanka
summary: Non-governmental grantee of a GEF Small Grants Programme-funded project running from November 2015 to April 2017, whose objectives included citizen science bird monitoring in three urban wetlands.

name: Forest Department, Sri Lanka
summary: Department that aims to conserve forests, uses Global Forest Watch, and according to a 2020 Global Forest Watch blog monitors two-thirds of Sri Lanka's natural forest.

name: IUCN Sri Lanka
summary: Country office in Colombo whose researchers surveyed coral reefs around Kakkativu Island, and the planned base for the Sri Lanka Coral Reef Initiative’s management unit.

name: Kumana Leopards
summary: Citizen science initiative started by wildlife enthusiasts, which had documented 80 individual leopards in Kumana since 2019 (Mongabay, May 2025), mainly from visitor observations, using named individuals.

name: Lanka Environment Fund
summary: Non-governmental organisation established in 2019 that gives grant funding to Sri Lankan conservation work and says it has mobilised over $1.7 million for 30 projects since 2019.

name: Leopocon Sri Lanka
summary: Nonprofit for Sri Lankan leopard conservation that, according to Mongabay in June 2026, carried out the initial data collection for a study recording 164 human-caused leopard deaths from 2008 to 2024.

name: Life To Our Coral Reefs - Conservation of Reefs for all Life and Livelihoods as a Nature-based Solution
summary: Collaborative Biodiversity Sri Lanka initiative run by Blue Resources Trust in Kayankerni for 2025 to 2030, including ecosystem monitoring and plans to establish a resource management research database.

name: LOLC Holdings PLC
summary: Colombo-listed company that runs a leopard research and conservation project with WNPS, which its own page says has set up six research stations using camera traps and surveys.

name: Ministry of Environment, Sri Lanka
summary: Ministry whose Secretary chaired the first combined steering committee on national biodiversity strategic action plans and environmentally sensitive areas in May 2024.

name: Multi-Regional Leopard Research and Conservation Project
summary: Leopard study outside protected areas, which the Daily Mirror says the Wildlife and Nature Protection Society launched in 2022 with LOLC Holdings, using camera traps at six field stations, with intensified studies reported as planned from 2027.

name: National Research Council of Sri Lanka
summary: Council whose stated mission is to promote, fund, facilitate and monitor research; GBIF says it funded the soil bacterial eDNA research behind a Sri Lanka Institute of Nanotechnology dataset.

name: Oceanswell
summary: Marine conservation organisation that says it has maintained photo-identification databases on all key marine mammal species since 2008; its flagship is the Sri Lankan Blue Whale Project.

name: People's Bank
summary: Bank reported by The Sunday Times as giving full financial backing to the Rail-Elephant Accident Prevention System, including its first 13 warning systems.

name: Rail-Elephant Accident Prevention System
summary: Collision prevention project targeting 39 hotspots along about 89 km of track; The Morning reported in September 2026 that installation of a 13-location AI sensor pilot had just begun.

name: Siamese Attention U-Net forest change detection model
summary: AI model reported by Charles Darwin University in May 2025, adapting U-Net to compare past and present images and detect forest loss, with a lead institution named only as "the University of Sri Lanka".

name: SLButterflies
summary: Online database of photographs of 244 of Sri Lanka's 248 butterfly species, upgraded after 2013 so recorders can enter field data, with regularly updated distribution maps and seasonal abundance graphs.

name: Small Cat Advocacy And Research
summary: NGO co-founded by Anya Ratnayaka that studies fishing cats, with a 2025 camera trap project and a reported EUR 17,920 grant from the Van Tienhoven Foundation for camera traps and community surveys.

name: Sri Lanka Coral Reef Initiative
summary: Coral reef programme run by IUCN Sri Lanka and funded by the Global Fund for Coral Reefs, planning community reef monitoring training, with monitoring data held in MERMAID and Blue Resources Trust surveys reported for 2025.

name: Sri Lanka Institute of Nanotechnology
summary: Self-described first public-private research institute in Sri Lanka, publishing a CC0 soil bacterial eDNA dataset with 14,958 records from research GBIF says the National Research Council funded.

name: Sri Lanka island-wide wild elephant survey 2024
summary: Closed island-wide elephant survey held on 17 to 19 August 2024 at 3,130 observation points across 12 wildlife zones, with preliminary findings reported in November 2025 including about 420 calves.

name: Sri Lanka National Forest Monitoring System
summary: Online geo-portal for forest data, described as newly launched in a 2017 report, with satellite land monitoring, a National Forest Inventory and greenhouse gas inventory data as components, built by the Forest Department.

name: Sri Lanka national seagrass habitat map (OCPP, 2026)
summary: Described as Sri Lanka’s first standardised national-scale seagrass map in a 2026 OCPP report, using Google Earth Engine Random Forest classification, with Blue Resources Trust supporting accuracy assessment.

name: Sri Lanka Wildlife Conservation Society
summary: Says its research, conservation and community programmes involve local communities, while its Carnivore Project aims to provide findings and datasets to the Department of Wildlife Conservation.

name: Survey Department of Sri Lanka
summary: Described in Sri Lanka’s 2019 UN-GGIM report as the national mapping organisation with established digital topographic vector data; its website welcomes visitors in Sinhala, Tamil and English.

name: The Carnivore Project (GPS satellite tracking of Sri Lankan leopards and sloth bears)
summary: Run by Sri Lanka Wildlife Conservation Society, partnering with the Department of Wildlife Conservation, and described as Sri Lanka’s first leopard and sloth bear GPS-collar study, launched in 2023.

name: The Pearl Protectors
summary: Volunteer-based marine conservation non-profit established in 2018, whose 2026 report records 168 conserved turtle nests, 89 at Dehiwala and 79 at Mount Lavinia.

name: The Sri Lankan Blue Whale Project
summary: Active project run by Oceanswell, established in 2008 and described as the longest-running blue whale project in the northern Indian Ocean, focused on conserving a non-migratory population from threats such as ship strike.

name: The Sri Lankan Marine Mammal Photo-identification Database
summary: Active database run by Oceanswell, which says it has kept photo-identification databases on all key marine mammal species since 2008, used to assess population size and demographics.

name: The value of eDNA in avoiding shark and ray extinctions in Sri Lanka
summary: Closed project funded by Save Our Seas Foundation and led by Nimna Wickramasingha, which planned to test eDNA sampling for monitoring sharks and rays at landing sites.

name: The Wilderness & Wildlife Conservation Trust
summary: Active trust that in 2024 maintained long-term monitoring at seven sites and began new camera surveys with the Department of Wildlife Conservation, and which the Lanka Environment Fund says set up 18 leopard camera stations in Kotagala.

name: Turtle Conservation Project (Sri Lanka)
summary: Independent NGO that, according to a page citing Kapurusinghe (2006), was established in 1993 and set up Sri Lanka's first in situ turtle nest protection and research programme at Rekawa in 1996.

name: University of Colombo
summary: University whose department is the lead affiliation on an Udawalawe elephant fence-crossing paper and which is the first author’s affiliation on a Mangrove Quality Index paper.

name: University of Peradeniya
summary: Higher education and research institution described in its GBIF record, awaiting endorsement, as strongly focused on biodiversity research, and the partner in WWCT camera surveys begun in 2024 in the Peradeniya-Hantane-Galaha region.

name: University of Ruhuna
summary: University whose departments are lead affiliations on papers about acoustic records of free-tailed bats and kingfisher identification using machine learning and deep learning.

name: University of Sri Jayewardenepura
summary: University listed, alongside the Open University of Sri Lanka, among the affiliations of the first author of the Maduru Oya Indian pangolin camera-trap paper.

name: Wildlife and Nature Protection Society of Sri Lanka
summary: Sri Lankan NGO first formed in 1894 as the Ceylon Game Protection Society, reported as the first NGO there incorporated by Act of Parliament and partner of LOLC Holdings in leopard monitoring.

name: Yala Leopard Diary
summary: Project started in 2013 by Milinda Wattegedara and team to collect data and photographs of leopards in Yala Block I, with records of 102 leopards by July 2020, according to Mongabay.

name: Building Capacity for Biodiversity Data Mobilization and Conservation in Liberia
summary: A 2018 GBIF dataset record for a project, funded by the European Commission and GBIF, that sought to build Liberian capacity to mobilise and publish biodiversity data in Darwin Core, covering all taxa, mainly observational.

name: Building Capacity to Monitor Forest Vegetation and Carbon Change in the Upper Guinea Forest through Permanent Sample Plots
summary: A USAID-funded permanent sample plot project in Liberian forests, planned for September 2022 to October 2024, whose database holds 5,403 occurrence records of 308 species from 20 sites.

name: Community-Based Forestry and Protected Area Management project
summary: A Sweden-funded UNDP and FAO project using SMART for biodiversity monitoring, which UNDP reported in March 2025 had equipped the Forestry Development Authority, with eighty eco-guards patrolling.

name: Digital forest monitoring system (Joint CBFM Project, Liberia)
summary: Active Swedish-funded cloud-based system, reported by UNDP, for real-time forest monitoring in Liberia, with a ranger incident-reporting app and web dashboard, and a August 2025 training of eleven FDA staff to scale it.

name: Environmental Protection Agency of Liberia
summary: Liberian government agency that hosts the CMS focal point and the Nagoya Protocol focal point, ran a 2015 to 2017 mangrove study, and was reported in February 2026 to be finalising Liberia's first Nagoya Protocol report.

name: Forestry Development Authority
summary: Liberian semi-public forestry corporation created by legislation in 1976, which led the 2025 management effectiveness assessment of Gola Forest National Park with technical support from SCNL.

name: GBIF Liberia
summary: Liberia's country node in GBIF, listed in the registry with associate participation status and managed by Benedictus Freeman.

name: GOLAMA Project
summary: A systematic biomonitoring programme in Gola, run by the RSPB and SCNL before it became a national park, whose mammal dataset covers 2010 to 2016 and is published under the Forestry Development Authority.

name: Interactive Forest Atlas of Liberia
summary: Active FDA-run GIS atlas with WRI support combines forest allocations with Global Forest Watch’s near-real-time cover and change data; data are CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise noted.

name: Liberia Ecosystem Extent Maps
summary: A set of ecosystem maps built by Conservation International and NASA from satellite data and field surveys, which a March 2021 article reports Liberia's government used to analyse ecosystem change over time.

name: Liberia Forest Monitoring with Parley Liberia
summary: A closed field experiment with Parley across 120 communities in Bong County, where a June 2020 brief reported preliminary survey and satellite findings of no change in forest activity, with final analysis pending.

name: Liberia Geospatial Capacity Building Workshops for Forest Monitoring
summary: Workshops, built by Spatial Informatics Group with Environment and Climate Change Canada funding, that aim to train participants in satellites, drones and machine learning for forest monitoring, including random forest classification in Google Earth Engine.

name: Liberia National Forest Monitoring System
summary: National forest monitoring system for which, before March 2019, UN-REDD reported ongoing development and technical support for a draft methodology and guidelines, later validated and implemented.

name: Liberian Bird Atlas
summary: Bird atlas effort, supported by a Rufford-funded early-steps project, which a February 2022 report says was better known afterwards, with clubs, birding groups and protected area staff seen as sources of citizen-science data.

name: Liberian National Forest Inventory
summary: Launched in Lofa County in June 2018 with Forest Carbon Partnership Facility funding and FDA implementation, Liberia's first national forest inventory used digitised Open Foris data collection.

name: Manatee Monitoring and Habitat Conservation in Lake Piso Basin, Western Liberia
summary: A closed Rufford-funded project whose final report covers April 2010 to March 2011 and says it gave FACE additional information for its bio-monitoring exercise.

name: Manatee Protection through Community-Led Actions in Lake Piso Multiple Use Reserve, Liberia
summary: A closed project that, according to its February 2014 page, planned to update the Lake Piso manatee database through periodic camera trap bio-monitoring while protecting manatees and habitat through community empowerment.

name: Raising local awareness and outreach work for the Olive Ridley Sea Turtle
summary: A US$2,750 grant awarded in October 2012 by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, planning daily beach monitoring and training of local monitors to record sea turtle tracks and nests in Liberia.

name: REDD+ Implementation Unit (Forestry Development Authority)
summary: Unit within the Forestry Development Authority which, according to UN-REDD's account of progress before March 2019, managed AFOLU activities on forest-cover monitoring and change assessment.

name: Safeguarding the White-Necked Picathartes (Picathartes gymnocephalus) in the Greater Gola Landscape of Liberia
summary: Active Rufford-funded project planning field surveys, GPS mapping, colony monitoring and community monitoring teams for the white-necked picathartes in Gola Forest National Park, with ecoguard training reported in September 2025.

name: SAMFU Foundation
summary: A non-profit Liberian organisation associated with Liberia's first specialised sea turtle study, conducted from April 2000 to April 2001 and followed by a Borgor Point pilot.

name: Society for the Conservation of Nature of Liberia
summary: Self-described as Liberia's oldest conservation organisation, it uses SMART, and the RSPB reports its community ecoguards record wildlife signs and share data by smartphone, while a September 2025 report describes its ecoguard training workshop.

name: Status Survey of the African Dwarf Crocodile in the Guinean Rainforest Biodiversity Hotspot
summary: A survey project in Sapo National Park, Sinoe County, which its February 2025 page says aims to document crocodile distribution, abundance and threats, estimate encounter rate and develop a distribution map.

name: Support for Community-Based Marine Turtle Monitoring and Conservation Education Project along the Liberian Bassa Coastline
