summary: Closed Rufford-funded project in Liberia, used October 2017 to July 2018, in which community monitors carried out beach and bycatch monitoring and received small stipends, according to its final evaluation report.

name: Updated Liberia Land Cover and Forest Map 2015
summary: A 10 m GeoTIFF land cover and forest map derived from high-resolution satellite imagery, intended as a national REDD+ baseline, with country-wide validation by a GeoVille and Metria joint venture.

name: Environmental and Sustainability Education Network of Lesotho
summary: Lesotho NGO with GEF Small Grants Programme support, which the GEF reports surveyed Southern Bald Ibis with local communities, counting up to 29 birds on one cliff.

name: EOSTAT Lesotho
summary: Land cover mapping project run and built by FAO under Lesotho's Integrated Catchment Management programme; FAO said in March 2023 it had trained 61 national staff and set six annual baselines for 2017 to 2022.

name: Lesotho Bird Atlas Bash
summary: Closed bird-recording series run by BirdLife South Africa and the LHDA, reportedly logging 2,601 records of 135 species in 2023, with another bash in February 2025.

name: Lesotho Highlands Development Authority
summary: Statutory body managing the Lesotho portion of the Lesotho Highlands Water Project, with sources reporting bird atlas participation and catchment restoration work since 2019.

name: Lesotho wetlands occurrence and health maps
summary: Wetland maps built by GMV from 20 m imagery for 2017 to 2019, with GMV reporting area losses in 43 per cent of sub-catchments and gains in 16.

name: LHDA Instream Flow Requirements biophysical monitoring
summary: Programme run by the Lesotho Highlands Development Authority that monitored whether instream flow requirements on four rivers were working; the 2015–2016 report covers six components, with geomorphology not assessed that year.

name: Ministry of Environment and Forestry (Lesotho)
summary: Lesotho government ministry whose acting Department of Environment director spoke at the Biodiversity Finance Initiative launch in Maseru on 15 December 2025, where it was reported to remain committed to mainstreaming biodiversity.

name: Monitoring and Early Warning System for Wetland Health in Lesotho
summary: System built by two National University of Lesotho students, reported to use satellites and drones to produce a digital map and dashboard intended to give early warning of damage to high mountain wetlands.

name: MyLINONYANA App
summary: Web-based bird visualisation app developed in Lesotho with R Shiny, showing bird species sightings in Lesotho using species data from GBIF.

name: National University of Lesotho
summary: University that reported two of its students built a wetland health monitoring and early warning system.

name: Next Generation Land Cover Database 2017-2022 (Lesotho)
summary: Land cover dataset for 2017 to 2022, built by EOSTAT Lesotho and listed by FAO among the project's main achievements, alongside a dashboard for land cover change statistics.

name: NUL soil erosion forecasting web app
summary: Web app built by Makhosane Morapeli that combines map and satellite data using the RUSLE model to map safe, at-risk and endangered land by village and year, with field tests under way in August 2025.

name: Polihali Southern Bald Ibis monitoring
summary: Monitoring of the Masakong Southern Bald Ibis colony, run by the LHDA with BirdLife South Africa, whose nesting site the Polihali reservoir will inundate, with satellite tags fitted to some birds, reported in February 2024.

name: A deep learning-based automated system for seabed imagery recognition and quantitative analysis (DEMERSAL)
summary: Closed Kaunas University of Technology project (June 2019 to June 2022, Research Council of Lithuania funding) that aimed to automate seabed image recognition with deep learning, producing an unsupervised training method and an annotated image database.

name: Aukštaitija Integrated Monitoring Station
summary: Lithuanian monitoring station founded in 1993, run by Vytautas Magnus University and the Environmental Protection Agency, which the site record says has measured continuously since and feeds national programmes, ICP Integrated Monitoring, ICP Forests and eLTER.

name: Benthic Habitat Ecology Research Group, Marine Research Institute, Klaipėda University
summary: Klaipėda University Marine Research Institute group, headed by Martynas Bučas, that does long-term benthic monitoring and habitat mapping, including machine learning models of species distribution and satellite and drone habitat detection.

name: BIGIS, distribution of habitats of European importance in Lithuania
summary: Database of the distribution of habitats of European importance in Lithuania, run and built by the Nature Research Centre's Laboratory of Flora and Geobotany.

name: Biodiversity Data Capacity Building in Lithuania
summary: Active project run by four bodies to improve biodiversity data availability, quality and use, with a GBIF publishing meeting and an invitation for 19 October 2026.

name: Biologinės įvairovės informacinė sistema (BĮIP)
summary: Information system whose modules cover protected species sites, wildlife monitoring data, large carnivore reports and game counts, aiming at one platform for collecting, managing, analysing and publishing biodiversity information.

name: BIOMON
summary: Dataset built by the LIFE IP PAF-NATURALIT project with open-source GIS; in 2019 it held conservation objectives, management maps and large carnivore records, and BIOMON2 had no public module.

name: Branto pelėausio, mažojo nakvišos ir šikšniuko mažylio inventorizacija
summary: Closed bat inventory with field work in 2019 to 2022, using ultrasound detectors at survey points and recording 4,503 bat observations, with regular monitoring of all species recommended.

name: Capacity Building in Biodiversity Data in Lithuania
summary: Active project run by Vilnius University Life Sciences Center and others, which held training in Vilnius on 16 to 20 March 2026 and notes Lithuania's own GBIF contribution remains limited.

name: Coetus
summary: Company that says it uses AI algorithms and satellite data in agriculture, forestry and urban infrastructure, and runs an Earth observation project.

name: Development of Earth Observation Algorithms and Experimental Activities and Market Introduction of Services Using Remote Sensing Tools and Artificial Intelligence
summary: Closed project, run by Coetus, that planned remote sensing and AI services for forest clear-cutting, regeneration and inventory, and meadow conservation value, with a budget of 1,272,667 euros.

name: Drūkšiai Biological Station, Nature Research Centre
summary: Core ecological research station of the Nature Research Centre at Lake Drūkšiai, whose fish communities have been monitored annually for over 60 years; it was recently used for FISHPAR, TRANSWAT and INVA.

name: Dzūkija National Park Living Lab wildlife monitoring network
summary: Camera trap network in Lithuania's Dzūkija National Park Living Lab, built by Vytautas Magnus University, tracking how large and medium herbivore mammals use forest gaps and clearcuts.

name: Environmental Projects Management Agency under the Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Lithuania
summary: Agency named on the LIFE IP Naturalit site as action leader for overall project management and administration.

name: Environmental Protection Agency (Lithuania)
summary: State budget institution that publishes a map of surface water body status and risk factors, and reports that a digital map of planned renaturalisation measures has been prepared.

name: Forest 4.0 forest data processing model
summary: According to KTU, a model built by three universities combines blockchain, IoT and AI to analyse tree sensor data for examining forest health and biodiversity.

name: INVA – Invazinių rūšių informacinė sistema
summary: Information system collecting invasive species data for Lithuania, with distribution maps and public submission of records; its footer carries the Ministry of Environment's copyright, but no page read names an operator.

name: Kaunas Tadas Ivanauskas Zoological Museum
summary: Kaunas budget institution that organises and coordinates bird ringing in Lithuania, and runs the Lithuanian Bird Ringing Centre and the Ventės Ragas Ornithological Station.

name: Kaunas University of Technology
summary: University giving its address as K. Donelaičio St. 73, Kaunas.

name: Klaipėda University
summary: University that said in May 2023 its Marine Research Institute researchers had applied satellite data to aquatic environment research for over a decade; it is based at 84 Herkaus Manto Street, Klaipėda.

name: Kongsberg NanoAvionics
summary: Company that Kongsberg says is contributing to Lemu's biodiversity observation satellite; the Lemu Nge hyperspectral camera passed its final test at its facility, and Lemu Nge launched on 16 August 2024.

name: KTU forest sound analysis model (CNN-BiLSTM)
summary: Model built by Kaunas University of Technology that, KTU says, combines a convolutional network with a bidirectional LSTM to identify forest sounds and flag anomalies, and integrates into its Forest 4.0 smart forest IoT.

name: Laboratory of Avian Ecology, Nature Research Centre
summary: Nature Research Centre laboratory, led by Mindaugas Dagys, that studies bird population dynamics and status using field surveys, ringing, satellite and GPS-GSM transmitters, loggers and geolocators, mostly on waterfowl, raptors, white storks and great reed warblers.

name: Laboratory of Flora and Geobotany, Nature Research Centre
summary: Laboratory within the Nature Research Centre that uses classical and remote sensing methods for vegetation, and runs and built the BIGIS habitats database among several biodiversity databases.

name: Laboratory of Mammalian Ecology, Nature Research Centre
summary: Nature Research Centre laboratory founded in 2003, reporting citizen science and wildlife cameras in 2017–2021, GIS analysis of roadkill hotspots, and IENE use of its hotspot data.

name: Lietuvos gamtos fondas
summary: Active since 1991, this Lithuanian charitable foundation protects nature, researches hermit beetle habitats and collaborated with Klaipėda University on planned Curonian Lagoon fish spawning site mapping.

name: Lietuvos jūrų muziejus
summary: State budget museum in Klaipėda with a marine animal rehabilitation centre; Lithuania’s 2024 marine strategy report credits its seal data with supporting regional grey seal indicator development.

name: LIFE Osmo Baltic. The Path of Old Oaks for the Hermit Beetle in Lithuania and Latvia
summary: Lithuanian and Latvian project running in 2024–2030, aiming to monitor hermit beetles and inform Natura 2000 expansion; its 2024 report records 2,929 inventoried trees in Lithuania.

name: LIFE TERNS, improving the conservation status of common and little terns in Lithuania
summary: Closed project run by the Lithuanian Ornithological Society, from July 2018 to December 2022, that planned GPS tagging of 30 breeding common terns and a GIS database of monitoring results.

name: Lithuanian Bird Ringing Centre
summary: Centre founded in 1978 and run by the Kaunas Tadas Ivanauskas Zoological Museum, which coordinates and stores Lithuanian bird ringing data, with about 103,700 birds ringed yearly on average.

name: Lithuanian Breeding Bird Atlas
summary: Atlas programme with data collected from 2014 and planned through 2023, using about 750 squares of 10 by 10 km and a web application for entering observations.

name: Lithuanian Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: Lithuanian butterfly monitoring network that began collecting transect counts in 2009, now gathers all data through the eBMS website and ButterflyCount app, and is coordinated by Eglė Vičiuvienė with ministry and entomological society support.

name: Lithuanian Common Bird Monitoring scheme
summary: Bird monitoring scheme run by the Lithuanian Ornithological Society, listed by PECBMS in 2025 as ongoing since 1994, with 61 fieldworkers, 170 species and point counts.

name: Lithuanian Entomological Society
summary: Independent voluntary scientific-social organisation of Lithuanian entomologists, described on the eBMS page, which holds first-sighting records for many butterfly species and supports the national butterfly monitoring scheme.

name: Lithuanian Ornithological Society
summary: Bird research and protection society that BirdLife International says finished five years of Breeding Bird Atlas fieldwork; its own news reports GSM transmitters fitted to four roller chicks in 2026.

name: Lithuanian Research Centre for Agriculture and Forestry
summary: Research centre whose Institute of Forestry studies forest ecosystem condition and forest protection, with a planned April to end 2026 project of 82,576.64 euros to upgrade a laboratory for forest monitoring research.

name: Lithuanian wintering waterbird counts
summary: Annual counts run by the Lithuanian Ornithological Society since it revived them in winter 2009-2010, with data passed to Wetlands International and 2026 counts planned for 16 to 18 January.

name: Marine Research Institute, Klaipėda University
summary: Institute run by Klaipėda University, which reported in May 2023 over a decade of satellite research, three completed space projects and Qredo ongoing.

name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Lithuania
summary: Ministry whose adviser InforMEA lists as Lithuania's Convention on Biological Diversity focal point; in 2021 it sought a forest stand segmentation technology through a GovTech Lab challenge, with no chosen solution stated.

name: Modernizing and optimizing biomonitoring of Lithuania rivers
summary: Nature Research Centre project aiming to modernise Lithuanian river biomonitoring with type-specific and DNA-based indices under the Water Framework Directive, including an eDNA microorganism index and new benthic invertebrate DNA sequences.

name: Mokslinė studija: buveinių ir agrarinės aplinkosaugos priemonių stebėsena nuotoliniais metodais (LIFE IP NATURALIT, action C7.2)
summary: Closed study within the LIFE IP NATURALIT project, written by Donatas Jonikavičius, on remote sensing for habitat monitoring, including a Sentinel-2 image classified into four classes with Random Forest.

name: National Forest Inventory of Lithuania
summary: Programme running since 1998 that covers the whole country by sampling; a poster says its information system needs modernising, planning integration with AI-driven analysis and remote sensing sources.

name: Nature Research Centre
summary: State research institute created in 2009 by merging three institutes, with 25 laboratories studying ecosystems, habitats and species, including bird populations followed partly with satellite and GPS-GSM transmitters.

name: Near-infrared reflectance thresholding model for macrophyte identification in temperate lakes using Sentinel-2
summary: Satellite-data algorithm, built by Yahor Levachou and funded by Vilnius University, that separates open water, submerged or floating macrophytes and emergent macrophytes, trained with regression trees on clustering-derived labels, for Nemunas Basin lakes.

name: Optimizing the management of Natura 2000 network in Lithuania (LIFE IP PAF-NATURALIT)
summary: Project financed by the EU LIFE Programme and Lithuania, run by the Environmental Projects Management Agency; its C.7.2 remote-sensing report classified a Sentinel-2 image into four classes with Random Forest.

name: Sequench Lithuania
summary: Klaipėda laboratory saying it specialises in eDNA and eRNA analysis of environmental samples, and listing eDNA projects including GuardIAS, with which it partners.

name: State Service for Protected Areas under the Ministry of Environment
summary: Service that BISE said in 2015 coordinated protected-area administrations; its Methodical-Analytical Center, set up in 2018, collects and analyses data on species and habitats of Community interest.

name: Unified Forest Fire Monitoring System (Lithuania)
summary: Proposed Lithuanian forest fire detection system; a March 2024 announcement planned a market consultation ahead of procurement, with at least 151 detectors tentatively planned on existing towers and isolated forests up to 25 ha excluded.

name: Ventės Ragas Ornithological Station
summary: Ornithological station founded in 1929, run by the Kaunas Tadas Ivanauskas Zoological Museum, whose staff ring 60,000 to 100,000 birds a year, with 2.9 million marked since ringing began.

name: Vilkų populiacijos būklės stebėsena Lietuvoje
summary: Lithuanian articles report nationwide wolf monitoring since 2018, including genetic studies of hunted wolves, over a thousand studied by October 2024, and at least 63 families in 2020–2021.

name: Vilnius University
summary: University whose Life Sciences Center researchers implement a biodiversity data capacity project, and whose planned data centre would make science data accessible under FAIR principles and build machine learning and quantum computing models.

name: Vilnius University Life Sciences Center
summary: University centre giving its address as Saulėtekio al. 7, Vilnius.

name: Vytautas Magnus University
summary: University whose Agriculture Academy co-leads LIFE IP Naturalit action C.7 on new population and habitat monitoring methods with the State Service for Protected Areas.

name: White stork census in Lithuania, 2024
summary: Closed 2024 count of Lithuania's breeding white storks, run by the Nature Research Centre and led by Daiva Vaitkuvienė, using 10 by 10 km squares or defined areas.

name: Žemaitija Integrated Monitoring Station
summary: Integrated monitoring station in the strict reserve zone of Žemaitija National Park, in the 147.3 ha Juodupis brook basin, funded by the Environmental Protection Agency of Lithuania and recorded as operational.

name: Administration de la nature et des forêts
summary: Public administration attached to Luxembourg's environment ministry, responsible for protecting nature, forests and biodiversity, with regional services doing field work nationwide, including managing protected areas.

name: Administration du cadastre et de la topographie
summary: Public administration whose main mission is supplying cadastral information to notaries, property professionals and the public, and which also issues topographic and thematic maps at various scales.

name: Atlas of Breeding Birds in Luxembourg (2026–2032)
summary: Luxembourg's latest breeding bird atlas, listed by the European Bird Census Council with a 2026 to 2032 census period, using a 5 by 5 km grid, line transects and territory mapping.

name: Biodiversity Monitoring and Assessment group (LIST)
summary: A group at the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology, led by Nicolas Titeux, describing itself as national coordinator of biodiversity monitoring, using camera traps, acoustic recorders, eDNA and metabarcoding, and developing automated monitoring devices.

name: Biota.lu
summary: An ecological studies and biodiversity consultancy registered as a SàRL in Hostert, founded in December 2022 by Raf Stassen and Louis Lestang, partnering with the Luxembourg Pollinator Monitoring Scheme.

name: CAMPHIBIAN
summary: Active project that builds on NEWTRAP, an earlier FNR-funded underwater camera trap with AI image analysis, and aims to turn it into a freshwater wildlife monitoring tool.

name: Centrale Ornithologique du Luxembourg
summary: Programme run by natur&ëmwelt that collects and analyses all data on Luxembourg's bird fauna, including ringing at three stations and, since 2011, observations entered on ornitho.lu.

name: CITIPOL
summary: A project that builds a structured citizen science framework into the LUPoMS programme, responding to volunteers collecting field observations with standardised protocols, funded by the Fonds pour la protection de l'environnement and led by Sarah Vray.

name: Common Bird Monitoring (Luxembourg)
summary: A common bird monitoring scheme that PECBMS lists as ongoing since 2009 and run by natur&ëmwelt, with 25 fieldworkers covering 120 species.

name: DiMON: Digital Insect Monitoring
summary: Active project funded by the Luxembourg National Research Fund that combines automated multi-angle imaging with data processing to monitor invertebrates without killing them, reportedly improving deep learning species identification.

name: Département de l'aménagement du territoire
summary: Luxembourg government department named on the national open data portal as producer of the LIS-L Land Cover 2018, 2021, 2024 dataset.

name: Fondation Hëllef fir d'Natur
summary: A Luxembourg nature protection foundation, founded in 1982 and recognised as of public utility, which coordinated LIFE Eislek (2012 to 2017), whose planned actions included monitoring its three target species.

name: Fonds pour la protection de l'environnement
summary: Luxembourg fund named, alongside the environment ministry, as a financial supporter of the Luxembourg Pollinator Monitoring Scheme.

name: Forest Pioneer
summary: Closed University of Luxembourg project that aimed to combine remote sensing and citizen science on forest health, and planned to identify individual trees using deep learning with LiDAR and hyperspectral sensors.

name: GBIF Luxembourg
summary: Luxembourg's country GBIF node, run by the National Museum of Natural History, with Luxembourg becoming a voting participant on 15 November 2017 after associate participation.

name: INSPECT
summary: A project exploring eDNA methods for monitoring invasive alien species in freshwater ecosystems, aiming to allow national scale-up, funded by the environment ministry and the Fonds pour la protection de l'environnement.

name: Inventaire forestier national (Luxembourg)
summary: National forest inventory whose third cycle, carried out from January 2023 to July 2024 on 1,845 sampling points, found dead wood had risen from 6 to 27 cubic metres per hectare.

name: LIFE Bats & Birds
summary: A project run by Fondation Hëllef fir d'Natur whose team reported on 14 April 2023 monitoring great grey shrike to identify occupied territories, with 2023 news also listing bat, red-backed shrike and wryneck monitoring.

name: LIFE Eislek
summary: A closed project that ran from 1 September 2012 to 31 August 2017 to restore Ardennes wetlands and endangered species, with a planned monitoring programme and 883,387 euros from the European Commission, half the budget.

name: LIS-L Land Cover 2018, 2021, 2024
summary: Land cover dataset for 2018, 2021 and 2024 with changes between them, updated every three years, whose 2024 map used semi-automatic classification and reached 91.44% overall validation accuracy.

name: LuxDev
summary: Luxembourg's development cooperation agency, working in about fifteen partner countries, which runs the SFERE project in Rwanda and held a conference on Rwanda's Forest Monitoring and Evaluation System.

name: Luxembourg Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: A butterfly monitoring scheme begun in 2010 with repeated standardised counts across the country, run by LIST and funded by the environment ministry, whose long-term abundance data fed a Nature Ecology & Evolution study projecting trends to 2050.

name: Luxembourg Cooperation
summary: According to LuxDev, finances the upcoming technical upgrade of Rwanda's Forest Monitoring and Evaluation System through the SFERE project.

name: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology
summary: Public research centre formed by merger in 2015, whose biodiversity group coordinates national monitoring using cameras and acoustic recorders, and which says it develops AI-powered insect monitoring tools.

name: Luxembourg National Research Fund
summary: Research funder that, according to the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology's project page, funds the DiMON project through the JUMP programme.

name: Luxembourg Pollinator Monitoring Scheme
summary: National scheme run by the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology that integrates wild pollinator and butterfly monitoring, using transects and pan traps with trained citizen scientists and partner organisations.

name: Luxembourg Space Agency
summary: National agency set up by the Ministry of the Economy in 2018 that represents Luxembourg in European and UN space programmes and lists a data centre giving free Copernicus Earth observation access.

name: LUXIAS: Invasive alien species surveillance system in Luxembourg
summary: Active project establishing a multi-taxa surveillance system for invasive alien species in Luxembourg, building on existing networks and using camera traps, hair traps and baited crayfish traps.

name: Mdata
summary: Online application for nature conservation professionals, run by the Luxembourg natural history museum, that aggregates Luxembourg observation data from several citizen science platforms, GBIF and the museum's databases, and uses iNaturalist.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et de la Biodiversité
summary: Luxembourg's environment ministry, responsible for protecting nature and water, which reported in October 2026 it was finalising a first national biodiversity finance plan and funds a pollinator monitoring scheme.

name: MONIPOL
summary: A programme setting up a standardised, long-term nationwide monitoring scheme for wild pollinating insects using coloured pan traps and laboratory identification, run by LIST, led by Lisette Cantu Salazar and funded by two bodies.

name: Musée national d'histoire naturelle Luxembourg
summary: Luxembourg's state natural history museum, which serves as the national GBIF node, with 56 datasets recorded by GBIF, and aggregates observation data to monitor biodiversity locally.

name: NAMPHIMO
summary: Active project proposing to combine acoustic sensors, underwater camera traps, eDNA and field surveys, with real-time entry on Observation.org, aiming for a national amphibian monitoring programme ready to implement.

name: National Biodiversity Monitoring Programme in Luxembourg
summary: Long-term national framework, running since 2010, that tracks biodiversity in Luxembourg through standardised protocols and targeted species and habitat monitoring, funded by the environment ministry.

name: natur&ëmwelt
summary: Luxembourg conservation organisation with more than 9,000 members across member associations, which runs the Centrale Ornithologique and names bird census and protection as a main field of work.

name: Naturpark Öewersauer
summary: A nature park whose biological station has counted pyramid bugle flower heads annually since 2009 and tries to coordinate road works with the roads administration to protect the plant's populations.

name: Naturschutzsyndikat SICONA
summary: A nature conservation syndicate of two municipal associations, SICONA Centre and SICONA Sud-Ouest, whose scientific department surveys flora and fauna and which supports state conservation under an agreement with the environment ministry.

name: NewtCam
summary: A newt monitoring device built by Xavier Mestdagh, prototyped from 2016 at LIST, where AI image processing distinguished newt species at test sites in Luxembourg and southern France, with LIST and NHBS now developing it for market.

name: ornitho.lu
summary: A bird watching and survey portal for Germany and Luxembourg, run by natur&ëmwelt, which collates bird data in verified form for science and conservation, accepting all Luxembourg observations since 2011.

name: space4environment
summary: A private Luxembourg Sàrl founded in 2007 that maps ecosystem types and land cover or land use, analyses animal movements with tracking technologies, and lists the 2015, 2018 and 2021 land cover map updates among its references.

name: Sustainable forestry and efficient renewable energy for improved livelihood (SFERE)
summary: Active project, run by LuxDev and funded by Luxembourg Development Cooperation, leading the institutionalisation of Rwanda's Forest Monitoring and Evaluation System, including upgrades, staff recruitment support, training and handover.

name: University of Luxembourg
summary: Financed Forest Pioneer through its Audacity programme; the project planned to identify individual trees using deep learning on LiDAR and hyperspectral data.

name: Baltic Satellite Service
summary: Company that, according to the Latvian Space Office, launched satellite-based remote forest monitoring; it reports testing over 5,000 square kilometres, detecting bark beetle infestation and beaver dam activity.

name: Bat acoustic background monitoring (Latvia)
summary: Nature Conservation Agency funded programme using stationary ultrasonic detectors in randomly selected 25 by 25 km squares; a 2024 report says it has run five years in 99 squares and 689 stations.

name: Dabas eksperti
summary: Organisation that prepared the 2024 bat acoustic background monitoring report under a contract, and thanks the Nature Conservation Agency for financial and technical support.

name: Dabasdati.lv
summary: Nature observation and citizen science portal built by the Latvian Fund for Nature and the Latvian Ornithological Society, reported in July 2024 to have run since 2008 with nearly 9,000 species reported.

name: Daugavpils University
summary: Regional state university in Daugavpils describing biological diversity as a key research area, with an ecology department covering IT/AI solutions, and a partner in HiQBioDiv.

name: Dynland
summary: Land use and land cover classification approach for remote sensing images, run by the Institute of Electronics and Computer Science, built around a clustering algorithm for multispectral pixels.

name: Forest biodiversity monitoring (Latvia)
summary: Monitoring programme described in a 2024 Silava presentation, which says 483 forest resource monitoring plots were surveyed in 2019 to 2023 to assess it.

name: High-resolution ecogeographical variables for species distribution modelling describing Latvia, 2024
summary: Dataset of high-resolution ecogeographical variables for species distribution modelling in Latvia, built by Andris Avotiņš and presenting results of three University of Latvia projects.

name: High-resolution quantification of biodiversity for nature conservation and management: HiQBioDiv
summary: Project led by the University of Latvia, running 1 October 2024 to 31 December 2026, which by December 2025 reported developing and testing over 500 eco-geographic variables covering Latvia.

name: ICT-based wild animal census approach for sustainable wildlife management
summary: Project run by the Institute for Environmental Solutions, whose 2021 abstract described plans for an aerial wildlife detection workflow and a study of four even-toed ungulate species.

name: Institute for Environmental Solutions
summary: Organisation in Cēsis, Latvia, whose staff authored a 2021 EGU abstract on an ERDF co-financed ICT-based wild animal census project.

name: Institute of Electronics and Computer Science
summary: Riga-based institute that lists its self-learning land cover classification technology Dynland among its solutions, and whose Dynland-2 project aimed at an unsupervised classification prototype.

name: Invasive Species Manager
summary: Reporting platform run by the Nature Conservation Agency, launched in 2021, which received 9,774 reports of wild invasive species in 2025, reviewed by experts and including reports from platforms such as Dabasdati.lv.

name: Laboratory of Ornithology, University of Latvia Institute of Biology
summary: University of Latvia Institute of Biology laboratory that studies mainly at the Lake Engure site and Pape Ornithological Station, and contains the Latvian Ringing Centre.

name: LatMare
summary: Open Latvian marine monitoring dataset from 1995, built and run by the Latvian Institute of Aquatic Ecology, set up within HELCOM's Baltic Data Flows project.

name: Latvian breeding bird counts
summary: Volunteer based counts run by the Latvian Ornithological Society since 2005 and funded by the Nature Conservation Agency, with volunteers submitting counts from 44 routes in 2025.

name: Latvian Council of Science
summary: Administers the state research programme on biodiversity priority actions, which funded one project application on high-resolution quantification of biodiversity, and funds HiQBioDiv.

name: Latvian Environmental Protection Fund
summary: Fund named in an agreement on the lynx status assessment project, according to the Silava project page.

name: Latvian Fund for Nature
summary: Funded by the Latvian Environmental Protection Fund, it offers nature live streams, and 2024 was reportedly its tenth season streaming a white-tailed eagle nest in Durbe.

name: Latvian Geospatial Information Agency
summary: Agency that prepares orthophoto maps for all of Latvia, renewing them on a three-year cycle, with maps up to and including cycle 6 open data.

name: Latvian Institute of Aquatic Ecology
summary: Riga institute responsible for marine monitoring in the Gulf of Riga and Latvian Baltic waters, working on freshwater too, and developing water transparency analysis tools in AquaINFRA.

name: Latvian Ornithological Society
summary: Latvian society whose monitoring and atlas data, according to LV portāls, will feed a forthcoming University of Latvia-led report on bird populations.

name: Latvian Ringing Centre
summary: Part of the Institute of Biology's Laboratory of Ornithology and a EURING member, managing Latvia's ringing material accumulated since 1925, covering about 1.7 million ringed birds.

name: Latvian State Forest Research Institute "Silava"
summary: Forest research institute in Salaspils that carried out the statistical inventory of Latvian forest resources in 2010 to 2011 under state delegation and lists forest biodiversity monitoring projects.

name: LIFE PeatCarbon
summary: Project led by the University of Latvia with an EU contribution of 2,655,444 euros, planning to monitor restored peatland at three Latvian sites using field measurement and remote sensing.

name: LIFE REEF
summary: Closed Baltic Sea project, led by the Nature Conservation Agency, that ran from September 2020 to August 2025 with 4,007,105 euros to map and study protected sandbank and reef habitats.

name: LIFE-IP LatViaNature
summary: Active nature conservation project, led by the Nature Conservation Agency and funded by the ministry, with actions on remote sensing at pilot sites and a central data portal.

name: Lāču monitorings 2023–2025
summary: Closed project run by Silava under agreement with the Nature Conservation Agency, led by Guna Bagrade, covering molecular genetic monitoring, hair traps and camera traps from June 2023 to March 2026.

name: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development
summary: Latvian ministry that says it is responsible for implementing policy on nature protection, regional development and digital transformation, and leads on environmental protection nationally.

name: National Forest Inventory of Latvia
summary: Forest inventory run by Silava, which keeps the data electronically by inventory period, reports yearly results to the Ministry of Agriculture, and lists a project running 2014 to 2026.

name: National LTER Network of Latvia
summary: Network of two terrestrial, two freshwater and one marine site plus the Lake Engure platform, with Latvia accepted as an ILTER member in 2004 and supported by the Council of Sciences of Latvia.

name: Nature Census
summary: Closed project, led by Irisa Mukane and using OZOLS, that ran from November 2016 to June 2023 to map EU-important habitats across all of Latvia and assess their status.

name: Nature Conservation Agency
summary: Agency based in Sigulda that says it manages all protected areas in Latvia, including seven marine areas, and maintains the OZOLS nature data management system.

name: Nature Conservation and IT-AI Solutions Laboratory
summary: Daugavpils University laboratory that says it develops AI tools for population and habitat monitoring, uses satellite imagery for ecosystem mapping, and has launched citizen science mobile applications.

name: Nature Data Management System OZOLS
summary: State information system, run by the Nature Conservation Agency, that stores Latvian biodiversity data on protected areas, species and habitats, used for permitting, planning, status assessments and reporting.

name: Object based context aware self-learning network for land cover classification (Dynland-2)
summary: Completed project, April 2021 to May 2022, run by the Institute of Electronics and Computer Science and funded by the European Space Agency, aiming at an unsupervised land cover classification prototype.

name: Obtaining internationally comparable parameters for the status assessment of the Eurasian lynx population in Latvia
summary: Closed project led by Guna Bagrade, ending 15 April 2024, that aimed to estimate lynx density in central Latvia using trail cameras and hair traps.

name: Pape Ornithological Field Station
summary: Field station run by the University of Latvia Institute of Biology, between Lake Pape and the Baltic Sea, which has monitored and ringed migrating birds and bats since 1967.

name: Real time observations of water quality conditions in urban lakes using smart buoys (LAKES GO DIGITAL)
summary: Project led by the Latvian Institute of Aquatic Ecology, running 1 March 2025 to 28 February 2027 with a 702,584 euro budget, to deploy six smart buoys for urban lake water quality monitoring.

name: State research programme "Development of research identified in the Biodiversity Priority Action Programme"
summary: Ministry-run state research programme whose open call, planning to fund three projects, closed for applications on 19 August 2024, with a second part also listed.

name: Telemetrijas datu ieguve ūpim (Bubo bubo)
summary: Project run by the Latvian Ornithological Society, funded by the Latvian Environmental Protection Fund, in which seven eagle owls had been fitted with GPS transmitters by September 2025 to study locations, threats and survival.

name: University of Latvia
summary: University named on Daugavpils University's project page as lead partner of HiQBioDiv.

name: University of Latvia Institute of Biology
summary: Riga institute within the University of Latvia that contains the Latvian Ringing Centre and a herbarium, and is listed as a partner in SEPPI, a 2024 to 2027 pollinator monitoring project.

name: UrbUmbrella
summary: Interreg project for 2025 to 2027, with Daugavpils City Council and Zarasai District Municipality Administration as partners, centred on an AI mobile app for wetland management and AI-assisted wetland assessment.

name: Alhayat Organisation for the Protection of Wildlife and Marine Organisms
summary: Libyan organisation whose 2021–2022 CEPF-funded project surveyed 25 random points across a 1,377 square kilometre area for the Egyptian tortoise, which the report calls the first structured and complete work on it in Libya.

name: Amwaj Society for Environment Conservation
summary: CEPF-funded organisation that its January 2021 plan says was set up by researchers working since 2005 in the Libyan Sea Turtle Conservation Program, covering beach monitoring, tagging and satellite tracking.

name: BADO Association for Environment
summary: Libyan NGO that received a CEPF small grant for a June 2019 to March 2021 project on awareness of the Farwa Marine Protected Area, and is listed among NGOs collecting stranding data.

name: Department of Botany, Faculty of Sciences, University of Benghazi
summary: University botany department linked to a paper using GIS and NDVI to assess Storm Daniel's effects around El-Gabal El-Akhdar, and a 2025 article mapping the invasive plant Bassia indica in Benghazi from satellite images.

name: Department of Forest and Rangeland, Omar Al-Mukhtar University
summary: University department named in OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a paper evaluating vegetation indices for assessing rangeland vegetation in eastern Libya.

name: Department of Natural Resources, Faculty of Natural Resources and Environmental Sciences, University of Tobruk
summary: University department named in OpenAlex as the first author's affiliation on a paper using GIS and remote sensing to study how topography influences vegetation cover in the Akramah region, eastern Libya.

name: Department of Natural Resources, Omar Al-Mukhtar University
summary: University department that OpenAlex lists as the affiliation on two remote sensing papers by different first authors, one from 2022 on wildfire effects on vegetation moisture and one from 2024 on desertification near Tobruk.

name: Department of Soil and Water, College of Agriculture, University of Tripoli
summary: University department named in OpenAlex as the first author's affiliation on a paper assessing how well the soil-adjusted vegetation index detects vegetation cover change in the Al-Jafara region, Libya.

name: Department of Spatial Information Systems and Remote Sensing, Omar Al-Mukhtar University
summary: University department named as the lead author's affiliation on a 2025 paper assessing vegetation cover in El Kouf reserve, Libya, with remote sensing and GIS for 2015 to 2023.

name: Fostering Stakeholder Participation in Preparing a Management Plan for Farwa Marine Protected Area
summary: Closed project, run by the Libyan Society for Birds and funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund, that ran from 1 September 2019 to 31 December 2021; its final report marks a result as partly achieved, with field biodiversity data collected.

name: Green Fingerprint Association
summary: Benghazi-based NGO listed in a CEPF final report among the organisations collecting stranding data.

name: Libya winter waterbird census (Libya IWC)
summary: Started in 2005 and continued regularly until 2012, with Libyan Society for Birds teams conducting counts from 2013 to 2021; the 2022 count ran 10 to 29 January.

name: Libyan Authority for Scientific Research
summary: Government body affiliated with the lead author of a 2024 vegetation change paper using Google Earth Engine, reportedly discussing a national CubeSat project in August 2026.

name: Libyan Climate Change Research Center
summary: Government research centre in Tripoli, listed as the affiliation of both authors of a 2025 paper assessing wetland dynamics at Sabkhat Tawergha with remote sensing and GIS.

name: Libyan Organization for Conservation of Nature
summary: Misurata-based NGO listed in a CEPF final report among the organisations collecting stranding data, within coordination with partner NGOs along the Libyan coast.

name: Libyan Sea Turtles Programme
summary: Volunteer group that The National reported in April 2023 was patrolling beaches around Misurata at night for turtle tracks and nests, relaunched without funding or official support.

name: Libyan Society for Birds
summary: Based in Tripoli, coordinated five partner NGOs collecting sea turtle stranding data under a CEPF project, and supplied counters for Libya’s 2022 winter waterbird census.

name: Libyan Wildlife Conservation Society
summary: Received CEPF funding to prepare a zoning plan for the Karabolli Key Biodiversity Area, with several biodiversity field surveys listed among the project’s results.

name: Management support and expansion of marine protected areas in the State of Libya
summary: GEF-funded project run by IUCN, partnering with Libya’s Ministry of Environment, includes centralising marine biodiversity data nationally and advancing the Ain El-Ghazala, El Kouf and Farwa Lagoon MPAs.

name: Ministry of Environment (Libya)
summary: Government ministry whose staff are Libya's protected-areas focal points for the CBD, and which took part in the 2026 meeting launching an IUCN cooperation roadmap for 2026 to 2030.

name: Omar Al-Mukhtar University
summary: University that OpenAlex lists as the institution on papers from 2022 to 2026 using remote sensing, GIS and vegetation indices such as NDVI to study vegetation, rangeland and soil in eastern Libya.

name: Sea Turtle Conservation in Partnership with Artisanal Fishermen in the Gulf of Sirte, Libya
summary: CEPF-funded project run by the Libyan Society for Birds from June 2021 to September 2023, coordinating five partner NGOs collecting stranding data, with daily beach surveys in the nesting season.

name: University of Tripoli
summary: University that OpenAlex lists as authors’ affiliation on work covering Libyan loggerhead turtles, winter waterbird counts, citizen science, social media mining and marine fish surveys.

name: Abdelmalek Essaâdi University
summary: A Moroccan institution in OpenAlex, listed with a 2023 paper on forecasting Mediterranean basin vegetation and a 2024 paper on trait-based biomonitoring of rivers in the north-western Rif.

name: Adaptation aux changements climatiques et biodiversité (Maroc)
summary: Run by GIZ from 2013 to 2017, this project included extending climate adaptation and biodiversity monitoring, which GIZ says the observatory planned for 16 regions.

name: Agence Nationale des Eaux et Forêts
summary: A Moroccan agency that in July 2024 was reported to use an AI-based system to identify likely forest fire areas, and in December 2025 held a workshop on updating protected-area planning.

name: Al Hoceima National Park Observatory
summary: An observatory presented by AGIR at a 2019 ODYSSEA review meeting, listing biodiversity monitoring of emblematic species, water and sediment quality monitoring, and mapping of heritage areas among its missions.

name: Algal Bloom Monitoring (Morocco)
summary: According to Capgemini, staff are developing an AI drone to detect harmful algal blooms, preparing satellite forecasting models and planning testing at a northern Moroccan dam.

name: Andalusian buttonquail conservation programme (Morocco)
summary: A conservation programme run by Morocco's national forest agency (ANEF), reported in September 2026 as launched with Spain for the Andalusian buttonquail, combining wild monitoring, captive breeding and preservation of genetic diversity.

name: Association de Gestion Intégrée des Ressources
summary: Reported by Hespress in October 2019 as an ODYSSEA partner, its president said the Al Hoceima observatory was becoming fully operational and collecting data for the platform.

name: Association des Enseignants des Sciences de la Vie et de la Terre
summary: A Moroccan teachers' association with a network of 40 sections, whose Khémisset section received a CEPF grant and produced a 2021–2022 inventory of threatened freshwater biodiversity in the Bouregreg basin.

name: Association Marocaine de Protection des Oiseaux et de la Vie Sauvage
summary: Moroccan bird and wildlife association that, with partners, colour-ringed and fitted GPS transmitters to White-backed Vultures at the Jbel Moussa centre in May to June 2024, reported as three or four birds.

name: Association Marocaine pour l'Ecotourisme et la Protection de la Nature
summary: Moroccan association, CEPF-funded, that produced an aquatic biodiversity database for Khénifra National Park (2020 to 2022) and initiated a wetland observatory for the Atlas Cedar Biosphere Reserve.

name: Association Nature Solutions
summary: Association created in 2017 to conserve Morocco's natural heritage through nature-based solutions; a CEPF grant (2019 to 2021) produced updated plant distribution maps and a monitoring protocol for Talassemtane National Park.

name: Atlas Programme
summary: A wildlife monitoring programme, described by IUCN in 2019, meant to provide basic information on Morocco's threatened fauna, including the first survey of cliff-nesting raptors, run by two named bodies.

name: Barbary Macaque Conservation in the Rif Mountains
summary: Founded in 2012, this association’s CEPF-funded Bouhachem project (2021 to 2023) found 70 macaque groups, installed monitoring cameras after a fire and trained 10 local representatives.

name: Born to be Wild - Morocco
summary: An active project in which local scouts patrol Ifrane National Park to monitor macaques, with IFAW reporting a 31.1% average rise across 13 monitored groups since 2017.

name: Cadi Ayyad University
summary: A Moroccan institution in OpenAlex, listed with a 2025 paper on a deep learning system for automated coral reef monitoring.

name: Centre Royal de Télédétection Spatiale
summary: Based in Rabat, this remote sensing centre supplies satellite imagery and mapping products and requested help applying AI to satellite images in its Space 2030 report.

name: Chouaib Doukkali University
summary: A Moroccan institution in OpenAlex, listed with a 2021 paper on spatial analysis of degraded forest areas in the Idmine forest.

name: Département du Développement Durable
summary: A department of Morocco's energy transition and sustainable development ministry, which a September 2025 listing said was organising a technical workshop under Nagoya ABS Project II with UNDP support.

name: Emirates Center for Wildlife Propagation
summary: A centre set up in October 1995 to preserve North Africa's houbara bustard, which monitors its managed zone through observers and shares Eastern Morocco ecosystem data with local officials.

name: GREPOM/BirdLife Maroc
summary: This Moroccan bird conservation organisation participates in waterbird monitoring and, under a CEPF grant, revised 42 inland wetland site sheets and compiled flora and fauna data.

name: Human–Carnivore Conflict and Threatened Species Management and Conservation in the Central High Atlas Mountains, Morocco
summary: A closed project which, in its 2019 description, planned to study carnivore ecology and local community interactions in the central High Atlas, using camera traps and 400 km of surveys over 56 days.

name: Initiative Bleue Maroc
summary: Under a 2023 partnership agreement, this association committed to monitoring species and habitats; its experts joined the September 2023 Jbel Moussa campaign using Zostera marina quadrats and temperature loggers.

name: Institut Agronomique et Vétérinaire Hassan II
summary: A Moroccan institution in OpenAlex, listed with 2018 and 2022 papers on processing multispectral image time series for crop and forest mapping.

name: Institut National de Recherche Halieutique
summary: An ACCOBAMS project summary names this Moroccan body in connection with plans for a national cetacean stranding monitoring network, including data sharing with MEDACES.

name: Institut Scientifique de Rabat
summary: Run by Mohammed V University, this Rabat institute holds natural history collections and publishes one herbarium dataset through GBIF, which lists no other publisher registered in Morocco.

name: Living Planet Morocco
summary: A Moroccan non-profit reports working with the national forestry agency since early 2023 on Atlas Cedar Biosphere Reserve wildlife monitoring, supporting seven eco-guards geolocating sightings for monthly maps.

name: Ministry of Energy Transition and Sustainable Development
summary: According to the national clearing-house site, this Moroccan ministry and UNDP organised a Rabat workshop in January 2026 to prepare the 7th National Biodiversity Report.

name: Mohamed I University
summary: A Moroccan institution in OpenAlex, listed with a 2025 paper on GIS and remote sensing for tracking vegetation cover in two north-eastern basins.

name: Mohammed V University in Rabat
summary: A Rabat university that OpenAlex lists with papers on fish detection in underwater videos, deep neural network land cover classification, forest stand dynamics and deep learning for plant identification.

name: Monitoring and Protection of Shore and Meadow Birds in Morocco
summary: According to Dutch agriculture ministry news, this six-month citizen science project finished in late 2025, training over 70 volunteers and producing Morocco's first wintering shore and meadow bird atlas.

name: Moroccan Biodiversity and Livelihoods Association
summary: Founded in 2014 to support Amazigh conservation in the High Atlas, this association trained community researchers in transect monitoring and reported field sessions in its 2021 review.

name: Morocco Biodiversity Clearing-House Mechanism
summary: This national biodiversity platform reports GEF/UNEP and Belgian support for its creation and a CBD Secretariat certificate awarded to Morocco at COP15 in December 2022.

name: Muséum d'Histoire Naturelle de Marrakech
summary: A research centre of Cadi Ayyad University that analyses water quality from pollution indicator species, keeps a database of its collections, and has described new species of subterranean crustacean and hydrobiid molluscs.

name: Observatoire des Zones Humides de la Réserve de Biosphère du Cèdre de l'Atlas
summary: CEPF-funded monitoring platform for water resources, biodiversity and ecosystems of the Atlas Cedar Biosphere Reserve, with a scientific council and accredited observers, described in its final report as a first in Morocco.

name: Observatoire National de l'Environnement du Maroc
summary: Moroccan environmental observatory which, according to GIZ, decided to extend the regional monitoring system to Morocco's 16 regions and integrate its data into the Regional Environmental Information Systems (SIRE).

name: Renforcement du réseau de suivi des échouages des cétacés des côtes marocaines
summary: A 24-month project, run by the Institut National de Recherche Halieutique with a total budget of 15,000 euros all from ACCOBAMS, to strengthen cetacean stranding monitoring and lay the basis for Morocco's first tissue bank.

name: Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University
summary: Moroccan university, listed in OpenAlex, with a 2026 paper by Hayat Hachimi, affiliated with it, assessing the impact of the Green Morocco Plan on terrestrial ecosystems.

name: Souss-Massa National Park
summary: A national park whose 2018 breeding report describes bald ibis breeding monitoring with GREPOM, using the same telescope-based method since 1994 within the species' national action plan.

name: Suivi des oiseaux d'eau en Afrique du Nord pour la conservation des zones humides
summary: Closed waterbird monitoring project for wetland conservation, funded by CEPF and built by Tour du Valat with bird societies in Tunisia, Algeria, Morocco and Libya.

name: Système d'Information sur le Patrimoine Naturel
summary: Active digital platform for recording habitats and species, ecological monitoring and decision support, set up during the Protected Areas Master Plan update under the Ghabati Hayati programme, financed by the Agence Française de Développement.

name: Système de gestion de la biodiversité marocaine
summary: Funded by UNEP, this system aims at a unified database of Morocco’s species with GIS spatial data, according to the clearing-house site.

name: Toubkal National Park Directorate
summary: The directorate of a Moroccan national park, featured in a Clearing-House Mechanism story on local eco-guards, which says its three assigned forest technicians were too few to monitor tourist activities.

name: Ungulates in the northern Sahara
summary: A closed project planned 30 camera traps to determine three ungulates' presence, distribution and abundance in the northern Atlantic Sahara, with Francisco Javier Herrera Sánchez as researcher.

name: University of Hassan II Casablanca
summary: Moroccan university, listed in OpenAlex, with affiliated papers on machine learning for mining-induced vegetation change (2024) and a 2026 paper on automatic video annotation of coral taxa with YOLOv11.

name: Université Ibn Zohr
summary: Moroccan university, listed in OpenAlex, with an affiliated 2022 paper by Sarrah Ezaidi on vegetation cover degradation in part of the Arganeraie Biosphere Reserve.

name: Université Ibn-Tofail
summary: Moroccan university, listed in OpenAlex, with affiliated papers on deep learning and remote sensing for Atlas cedar resilience (2026) and vegetation change in Talassemtane National Park (2024).

name: Université Mohammed VI Polytechnique
summary: Moroccan university, listed in OpenAlex, with affiliated remote sensing and machine learning papers on argan tree location (2021), rangeland biomass in the Middle Atlas (2024) and crop and land cover mapping (2026).

name: Université Moulay Ismail de Meknès
summary: OpenAlex lists this Moroccan university in Meknès with affiliated papers on forest fire mapping (2021), rosemary biomass (2021) and Azrou forest land cover (2018).

name: Université Sultan Moulay Slimane
summary: Moroccan university, listed in OpenAlex, with affiliated papers on forest cover dynamics from ASTER and Sentinel-2A data (2018) and a 2025 review of remote sensing for forest degradation monitoring.

name: École Nationale d'Agriculture de Meknès
summary: A Moroccan institution in OpenAlex, listed with 2025 and 2026 papers on European bee and hoverfly databases.

name: École Nationale Forestière d'Ingénieurs
summary: A Moroccan institution in OpenAlex, listed with a 2023 paper on assessing cork oak decline using digital multispectral imagery.

name: Aire Marine Éducative de Monaco
summary: Monaco marine area created in 2018 by the AMPN with Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation and government support, managed yearly by a school class, whose pupils collected biodiversity data in 2024–2025 using environmental DNA, BRUVS and FAST counts.

name: Association Monégasque pour la Protection de la Nature
summary: Monaco's nature protection association, founded in 1975, has managed the country's two marine protected areas since 2018 and uses juvenile fish surveys, a hyperspectral camera and baited underwater video.

name: Centre Scientifique de Monaco
summary: Public establishment in Monaco that monitors penguin populations long term, with over 30,000 penguins tagged since 1998, and analyses climate effects on coral ecosystems.

name: Direction de l'Aménagement Urbain
summary: Monaco government department that monitors compliance with the ordinances protecting plant species under the Tree Code, with state staff recording all trees in public and private areas and mapping the data on a Geographic Information System.

name: Direction de l'Environnement (Monaco)
summary: Monaco's environment directorate, created in 2008, carries out continuous environmental quality monitoring and commissioned in situ monitoring of noble pen shell mortality up to autumn 2018.

name: Département de Biologie Polaire, Centre Scientifique de Monaco
summary: Monaco polar biology department created in 2010 with CNRS-IPHC, which per a 2019 flyer follows penguins since 1998 using electronic monitoring and sensors, and says it also develops AI-based tools for its field databases.

name: Institut océanographique, Fondation Albert Ier, Prince de Monaco
summary: Oceanographic foundation in Monaco involved, from June 2019, in a protocol with the Direction de l’Environnement to capture noble pen shell larvae carried by the Ligurian current.

name: Larvotto marine reserve baited underwater video monitoring
summary: Baited underwater video study in Larvotto marine reserve recorded 332 fish in January 2024 against 123 in July 2023, with planned coverage of habitats 40 to 50 metres deep.

name: Monaco Explorations
summary: Initiative under Prince Albert II’s High Patronage, with 15 planned world missions, ten scientists selecting research and plans described by David Mouillot for an environmental DNA reference database.

name: Monaco noble pen shell research and conservation programme
summary: Research and conservation programme on Monaco's noble pen shell, involving late 2018 prospecting dives and, from June 2019, a larvae capture protocol, with five named partners.

name: Multiannual monitoring of 3D printed artificial reefs in the Larvotto Marine Protected Area
summary: Monitoring project, January 2019 to December 2022, of 3D printed artificial reefs in the Larvotto marine protected area, using a hyperspectral camera and finding colonisation comparable to natural rock.

name: Observations Monaco (OBSenMER sea-user observations)
summary: Citizen science scheme in Monaco asking sea users to report turtle and marine mammal sightings via the OBSenMER platform and app, with over 120 observations recorded in 2019 to 2020, per a 2021 release.

name: Seahorse population study in Monegasque waters
summary: A citizen science study of seahorses in Monegasque waters, partnered with the Prince Albert II Foundation and Oceanographic Institute, observed three Hippocampus guttulatus in summer 2020.

name: Agency for Geodesy, Cartography and Cadastre (Moldova)
summary: Moldovan agency whose stated mission is to develop, implement and monitor public policy and regulation in cartography, geoinformatics and remote sensing, and spatial data infrastructure.

name: Assessment of species status for the fourth edition of the Red Book of the Republic of Moldova
summary: Funded by the National Environmental Fund, this active project assesses plant, fungi and animal species for rare-species listing in the Red Book’s fourth edition, with two seminar programmes.

name: Conservation and sustainable management of wetlands with focus on high-nature value areas in the Prut River basin
summary: Active 2022 to 2027 UNDP-listed project funded by the Global Environment Facility, with a budget of US$913,242, that aims to strengthen protected area capacity to monitor biodiversity and wetlands.

name: Czech-Moldovan cooperation on protected area management and volunteer rangers
summary: Czech-funded cooperation project with UNDP, Arnika and Biotica Moldova which, UNDP said in November 2024, had contributed to better management of three protected areas, each given a drone and a small boat for monitoring.

name: Environmental Agency (Moldova)
summary: Moldovan agency listing nature protection and biodiversity among its fields, whose 2025 action plan sets an objective to develop and implement a monitoring system for biodiversity and natural ecosystems.

name: HydroEcoNex
summary: A closed project, run by the Institute of Zoology (Moldova) from September 2018 to September 2021 under a Black Sea Basin programme, that developed a common methodology and indicators for monitoring hydropower impacts on the Dniester and Prut rivers.

name: Institute of Ecology and Geography, Moldova State University
summary: An active research institute at Moldova State University whose affiliated authors developed cartographic models of degraded land in the Cogâlnic basin for 2004 and 2020 in a 2022 paper.

name: Institute of Forest Research and Management (Moldova)
summary: State enterprise that the government says will carry out the technical work of the National Forest Inventory, and which JICA says received forest monitoring equipment and satellite image training in 2023.

name: Institute of Zoology, Moldova State University
summary: Research institute within Moldova State University, with an accredited profile including monitoring of aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, which launched two editions of the Red Book of the Republic of Moldova, in 2001 and 2015.

name: Integrated natural resources management and land degradation neutrality in Moldova (FAO-GEF)
summary: A project run by FAO and funded by the GEF, which a 2024 paper says used a deep learning model on four Sentinel-2 images to map land cover across 32 localities (88,528 ha) in north-eastern Moldova.

name: LIFE RENATA, Roadmap for the alignment of the Emerald network to Natura 2000 standards in Moldova
summary: Closed project, 1 February 2024 to 31 May 2026, coordinated by Lever Development Consultants S.A., with objectives to update the national Emerald Network database and develop monitoring and reporting tools.

name: LiveEO deforestation monitoring for Moldova
summary: Monthly deforestation monitoring for Moldova, run by LiveEO, which says it has used 3 m optical satellite data since December 2022 and that a pilot found 216 instances between September and December 2022.

name: Mainstreaming biodiversity conservation into Moldova's territorial planning policies and land use practices
summary: Closed 2015 to 2018 project, budgeted at 998,904 US dollars, funded by the GEF and run by Moldova's environment ministry and Moldsilva, which carried out a red list species inventory in two districts and trained 29 officers.

name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Moldova
summary: Opened consultation on the 2026-2030 biodiversity programme, will coordinate the National Forest Inventory, and began drafting a decision establishing the Protected Natural Areas Administration in January 2026.

name: Moldova State University
summary: Its botanical garden institute partners in MONFORGENDIV (2024 to 2026); a January 2026 Red Book seminar announcement names the university and Academy of Sciences as organisers.

name: Moldsilva Agency
summary: Agency trained by JICA in March 2023, mentioning forest monitoring in its 2025 risk register, managing forest databases and maps according to the 2019 CBD report.

name: National Forest Inventory (Moldova)
summary: Proposed programme whose Cycle I the government approved for 2026 to 2030, covering field data collection, verification and publication, at a stated total cost of 2.4 million euros, of which 1.6 million is a Romanian grant.

name: Protected Natural Areas Administration (Moldova)
summary: Proposed state-funded public institution, under a draft decision with the Ministry of Environment as founder, planned to monitor biodiversity, manage geospatial data and run territorial units for several national parks and reserves.

name: Protected Natural Areas Register information system (Moldova)
summary: Proposed in a Ministry of Environment draft government decision, the information system would provide a single centralised database for recording and monitoring protected natural areas.

name: Biodiversity Mainstreaming into Sectoral Policies and Practices and Strengthened Protection of Biodiversity Hot-Spots in Montenegro
summary: Five-year project (2022 to 2027), run by Montenegro's ecology ministry and funded by the Global Environment Facility, whose mid-term review says it procured drones and tree tags for forest health and illegal activity monitoring.

name: Biologer Montenegro
summary: National biodiversity recording platform, built on Biologer free software and built by the invasive plants mapping project, reported in May 2023 to have Android and iOS apps and described as Montenegro's first public biodiversity database.

name: Brown bear GPS collaring in Durmitor National Park (ForestConnect)
summary: A project run by CZIP in Durmitor National Park: a brown bear was fitted with a GPS/GSM collar on 10 June 2025, and the same bear was recaptured and recollared on 18 June 2026.

name: Centar za zaštitu i proučavanje ptica
summary: Montenegrin bird conservation organisation, named as BirdLife Montenegro in a census report, whose reports describe camera trap, common bird and illegal activity monitoring, and which has had CEPF funding.

name: Center of Excellence in Nature-Based Solutions and Technologies for Protected Areas (CENNA)
summary: Active project, led by the University of Montenegro with Antwerp and Aarhus, planning a centre for smart environmental monitoring; it says it will address AI analytics, with pilots at Skadar Lake and Durmitor, from November 2026 to October 2032.

name: CGIS Bioportal of Montenegro
summary: Announced in June 2017, this public protected area data platform was developed by Digital Control DOO with MAVA Foundation funding; its current status is unknown.

name: Department of Biology, Faculty of Science, University of Montenegro
summary: University of Montenegro department in Podgorica, run by the university, listed as the affiliation of the first and corresponding author of a paper on Corsican water mites.

name: Department of Geography, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Montenegro
summary: Nikšić department that is the affiliation of the first author of a 2022 paper assessing vegetation condition before and after a Luštica wildfire using the dNBR index.

name: Environment Programme (EnvPro)
summary: NGO funded by CEPF, with a June 2024 to June 2025 Mt. Orjen project on rare endemic plants and translocation monitoring, and an earlier Lower Bojana River Basin project.

name: Environmental Protection Agency of Montenegro
summary: Podgorica agency whose tasks include monitoring nature protection and biodiversity, setting up Natura 2000 and preparing red lists, and which takes part in FunDive and shares data through GBIF.

name: Establishing a bird ringing program in Ulcinj Salina
summary: Small project of €34,000 under PROZHUM, running January 2024 to December 2026 and run by CZIP, to set up bird ringing at Ulcinj Salina and share data with managers and decision-makers.

name: Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of Montenegro
summary: Podgorica faculty that is the affiliation of the first author of a 2025 paper on a relay-based LPWAN network and artificial intelligence for wildfire detection.

name: Green Home
summary: Podgorica-based NGO that reported Posidonia oceanica monitoring at five sites in the future Katič protected area in 2020, and presented otter monitoring for 2024 to 2025 with PPNEA and WLMNE.

name: Innovative Technology for Forest Protection in Montenegro
summary: Active project introducing digital tree tags in Prokletije National Park to improve forest monitoring, with partners including national parks and the ministry; it created a digital inventory of 20,000 trees.

name: Institute of Marine Biology, University of Montenegro
summary: Kotor research institute founded in 1961, part of the University of Montenegro since 2004, which monitors the marine ecosystem and is the only Montenegrin research institution working solely on the sea.

name: International Waterbird Census in Montenegro
summary: Active census run by the Natural History Museum of Montenegro, with a web application for data collection; its 2022 count involved 19 participants from 5 organisations.

name: Mammals of Montenegro
summary: Dataset built by Wildlife Montenegro, holding more than 1,700 mammal occurrences from Montenegro, drawn from human observations, camera traps and audio recordings.

name: Mapping the Invasive Alien Plant Species and Establishing Biologer Platform for Biodiversity Data in Montenegro
summary: Closed project, led by Bojana Mijović, which in March 2023 aimed to map invasive alien plants and establish Biologer as Montenegro's first online biodiversity database; a final report is dated March 2024.

name: Mediterranean Center for Environmental Monitoring
summary: A Montenegrin NGO and CEPF grantee (grant CEPF-108820) that monitored Posidonia oceanica markers and monk seals in the 2018 to 2021 Katič project, and installed 10 pilot ecological moorings in 2013.

name: Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development and Northern Region Development
summary: Montenegrin ministry whose remit includes nature protection, whose Directorate for Nature Protection head is the CBD focal point, and which in 2021, under an earlier name, announced Platamuni Nature Park as the first marine protected area.

name: Montenegrin Society of Ecologists
summary: Montenegrin NGO in Podgorica, funded by CEPF, with projects on Skadar frogs, oak, bats, Natura 2000 habitats and fish, and a 2025 to 2026 project aiming to improve herpetofauna data.

name: Montenegro Dolphin Research
summary: Rufford Foundation funded project whose 2017 to 2018 annual report called it the first and only annual cetacean monitoring project in Montenegro and described an acoustic monitoring effort; current status unknown.

name: Natural History Museum of Montenegro
summary: Based in Podgorica, with roots in a 1961 government decree, it coordinated the 2022 waterbird count and describes the census as Montenegro’s longest-running biomonitoring programme.

name: Public Enterprise for National Parks of Montenegro
summary: Podgorica public enterprise responsible for national park protection and management, which set 8 trail cameras in Prokletije and Durmitor under ForestConnect and began monitoring large carnivore corridors.

name: Second National Forest Inventory of Montenegro
summary: Proposed inventory, for which FAO published a tender in May 2026 for consulting services to implement the pilot phase, within an FAO project working with three Montenegrin bodies.

name: Sound-based logging detection model (University of Montenegro)
summary: A 2022 TELFOR conference paper from the University of Montenegro that uses deep learning, comparing MLP and CNN approaches to detecting chainsaw sound, built by Budimir Anđelić.

name: Support to local communities in the promotion and protection of future Marine Protected Area – Katič
summary: Closed Green Home project, funded by CEPF, that ran from December 2018 to November 2021 and included collecting data on Posidonia oceanica meadows.

name: University of Montenegro
summary: Podgorica university that coordinates the CENNA project with the University of Antwerp and Aarhus University, intended to strengthen Montenegro's capacity for environmental management.

name: Vegetation Database of Montenegro
summary: National database established in 2019 at the University of Montenegro, which a 2023 paper reports holds 3,293 georeferenced vegetation plots and is part of the European Vegetation Archive with semi-restricted access.

name: Wildlife Montenegro
summary: Civil society organisation based in Kotor, described by GBIF as working on Montenegrin mammals, which publishes the Mammals of Montenegro dataset and did the Montenegro fieldwork for the 2024 to 2025 Skadar Lake otter project.

name: Achieving sustainable forest management through community managed protected areas in Madagascar
summary: Active project aiming to reduce deforestation and forest degradation in Madagascar's national park network by supporting community and regional authorities to manage and monitor resources, funded by Defra with five named partners.

name: Alaotran gentle lemur and Alaotra wetland conservation project (IUCN SOS, 2025 to 2027)
summary: A 2025 to 2027 IUCN Save Our Species project that aims to estimate the whole range's Alaotran gentle lemur population using drone thermal sensors and AI, with the Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust named as implementer.

name: Ankarafantsika National Park: saving Endangered lemurs through community-based forest restoration and fire management
summary: An active 2025 to 2027 project under the SOS Lemurs initiative in Madagascar, run by Planet Madagascar Association, that works to improve fire detection with satellite data and drones and to introduce drone and camera-trap monitoring.

name: Ankarafantsika National Park: Saving Endangered Lemurs Through Community-Based Forest Restoration and Fire Management
summary: An IUCN Save Our Species project for 2025 to 2027, run by Planet Madagascar Association, which is working to improve fire detection with satellite data and drones and to introduce drone and camera-trap monitoring of forest and lemurs.

name: Ankoatsifaka Research Station
summary: A research station set up in 2006 in Kirindy Mitea National Park by Rebecca Lewis of the University of Texas, where over 12,000 trees and vines have been marked and measured.

name: Asity Madagascar
summary: A national conservation NGO described by its site in June 2015 as co-managing protected areas with communities, whose ornithologists Bôndy reported counting waterbirds in April 2026.

name: Association Fanamby
summary: A Malagasy civil society organisation, funded by the MacArthur Foundation, that in 2018 co-managed five protected areas with communities and, per FAPBM, manages Loky Manambato with local patrols and participatory ecological monitoring.

name: Association Mitsinjo
summary: A Madagascar-registered NGO that has managed the forest station at the Analamazoatra Special Reserve since 2003, under a contract running to 2037, and runs community-based monitoring of lemurs, birds and frogs.

name: Association Réseau Système d'Informations Environnementales
summary: Non-profit association created in May 1999 that produces and publishes its members' metadata; its CEPF completion report records 2,131 new metadata records against a target of 1,500.

name: Association TOSIKA
summary: A CEPF-funded grantee whose April 2020 to June 2022 project deployed patrol and infrared-camera drones to monitor pressures on a new protected area and produced documents on professional drone use and image processing.

name: Association Vahatra
summary: Association registered in Madagascar that conducts biological inventories and field research for up-to-date biodiversity information, grew out of a WWF-Madagascar training programme begun in 1991, and is funded by the Hempel Foundation.

name: Base de Métadonnées sur la Biodiversité de Madagascar
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, run by the Réseau Système d'Informations Environnementales from January 2017 to February 2019 on a 56,110,000 ariary grant, which entered 2,131 new metadata records in its online base.

name: Bureau National de Coordination des Changements Climatiques et de la REDD+
summary: A body that co-published a 2019 national forest inventory manual for Madagascar's spiny forest, with DRGPF and MEDD, which plans to use a national 4 km grid developed with its teams.

name: Bureau National des Changements Climatiques et de la REDD+
summary: An environment ministry office running LOFM, which monitored forest-cover changes for 2000 to 2019 and whose technicians used Open Foris Collect Earth for Madagascar's forest reference emission level.

name: Bôndy
summary: Madagascar-based reforestation startup that says its restoration and regenerative agriculture platform uses AI for satellite monitoring and carbon modelling, and says Bloomberg named it among 25 African startups to watch in 2026.

name: Centre National de Recherches sur l'Environnement
summary: Environmental research body that says it is administratively tied to the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, studies land, water, coastal and marine ecosystems, and collects microbial diversity data.

name: Centre ValBio
summary: Research organisation with a US headquarters at Stony Brook University and a campus at Ranomafana, Madagascar, listing the Razana ecological monitoring system and a 2024 acoustic monitoring and deep learning paper on ruffed lemurs.

name: Changement de la couverture de forêts naturelles à Madagascar 2005-2010-2013
summary: Closed report on historical deforestation in western Madagascar ecoregions for 2005, 2010 and 2013, using Landsat images and Random Forest, with a deforestation map for humid, dry and spiny forest and mangroves.

name: Cétamada
summary: A non-profit association with a whale-watching code of conduct, reported in January 2023 to have used camera-equipped CATS tags since 2018 and studied humpback whale mother and calf pairs for seven years with research partners.

name: Département de Zoologie et Biodiversité Animale, Université d'Antananarivo
summary: A university department listed among the first author's affiliations, alongside NeuroPSI, in a study that used a simple drone-based photogrammetric method on humpback whale mother and calf pairs in the Sainte Marie channel.

name: Ecoacoustic machine learning survey of black-and-white ruffed lemurs in the COFAV
summary: Closed survey in which recorders at 30 COFAV sites, December 2021 to June 2022, fed a neural network detecting ruffed lemur calls in 550,000 minutes; the preprint is not peer reviewed.

name: EcoSounds Madagaskar
