summary: A project aiming to develop passive acoustic monitoring of endangered species in the Menabe Antimena Protected Area, asking zoos to help describe vocal repertoires for automatic species identification; its page does not say who runs it.

name: Fitsinjo
summary: Independent fisheries observatory for Madagascar and the Indian Ocean that monitors fishing vessels using satellite data, remote sensing and coastal communities, partnering with Blue Ventures, Global Fishing Watch and Skylight.

name: Foiben-Taosarintanin'i Madagasikara
summary: National geographic and hydrographic institute in Antananarivo, which a 2011 UN-GGIM report says a 2010 decree charged with building a reference geographic and hydrographic data infrastructure; its current status is unknown.

name: Fondation pour les Aires Protégées et la Biodiversité de Madagascar
summary: Private foundation under Malagasy law that finances protected areas from the returns on its invested capital; its 2024 report describes equipment grants focused on fire-fighting, including drones, and surveillance.

name: GBIF Madagascar
summary: Madagascar's voting participant node in GBIF's Africa region, registered in Antananarivo, which the Centre National de Recherches sur l'Environnement says it hosts and which endorses MadBIF as a publisher.

name: German Primate Center Kirindy Field Station
summary: A field station in Kirindy Forest near Morondava studying eight sympatric lemur species, where a researcher reports that a mouse lemur population monitored over many years collapsed.

name: Groupe d'Étude et de Recherche sur les Primates de Madagascar
summary: A Madagascar-registered NGO in Antananarivo, founded in 1994 by two university departments, that studies lemur distribution, has managed the Maromizaha forest since 2008, and collected 2005 to 2018 lemur observations held in a GBIF dataset.

name: Hay Natiora
summary: A digital application run by the Office National pour l'Environnement, collecting geo-referenced data on forests, protected areas, locally managed marine ecosystems and land tenure.

name: Indice d'Intégrité Biotique (FAPBM)
summary: A biotic integrity index in FAPBM's monitoring and evaluation plan, calculated from manager-supplied data on habitat area and target species abundance, which FAPBM's 2024 report says rose from 2.59 in 2021 to 2.94 in 2024.

name: JeryMotro
summary: A wildfire alert programme that aggregates FIRMS satellite data across all 22 regions of Madagascar and uses a machine learning model trained on three years of data to predict next-day fire risk; the site presents it as a 2026 undergraduate thesis.

name: Kew Madagascar Conservation Centre
summary: Kew programme in Madagascar listed by GBIF for research, collection holdings and biodiversity information management, with datasets including a Poaceae checklist after Bosser's 1969 book and georeferenced TAN herbarium grass specimens.

name: Kirindy Mitea National Park Biodiversity Monitoring Initiative
summary: An ongoing monitoring effort launched in April 2023 by Domenic Romanello, in which trained local community members track primate and bird abundance and density in Kirindy Mitea National Park.

name: Laboratoire d'Observation des Forêts de Madagascar
summary: Forest observation laboratory whose 2021 procedure covers data collection for sample-based visual interpretation, mainly from remote sensing, and which uses Collect Earth; its 2019 reference grid guidance is cited under BNCCREDD+.

name: Leveraging AI for Reforestation in Madagascar
summary: Closed project, built by Omdena, to build a machine learning model monitoring reforestation from satellite and drone images; the team developed a model reported to detect tree patches and estimate tree numbers.

name: LMMA Portal Madagascar
summary: Active portal that WIOMSA reported in June 2025 aims to centralise data on locally managed marine areas for monitoring and evaluation, open to all stakeholders, and built by the Mihari Network.

name: Madagascar Biodiversity Center, Parc Botanique et Zoologique de Tsimbazaza
summary: Organisation at the Tsimbazaza park in Antananarivo that says it has a strong record of arthropod surveys, and received BID funding for the African Insect Atlas project centred on remaking its analogue collection.

name: Madagascar Biodiversity Partnership
summary: An NGO based in Antananarivo, accredited with UNCCD, which in a January 2015 profile said it monitored re-established sifaka and ruffed lemur populations in Analamazoatra Special Reserve using radio collars and other technology.

name: Madagascar Lemurs Portal
summary: Portal set up to improve sharing of existing lemur data, with a species database, visualisations and an iNaturalist-based citizen science app, and GBIF datasets of lemur observations from four contributing organisations.

name: Madagascar mangrove change diagnostic (CGI and Planète Urgence)
summary: A closed project run by CGI, partnering with Planète Urgence, mapping mangrove change pro bono; CGI reports 16% average annual deforestation in north-western Madagascar during 2010 to 2022.

name: Madagascar National Mangrove Mapping from 2019 to 2023 for Pêche Côtière Durable Phase II
summary: A closed project, running January 2020 to February 2024, in which Hatfield built machine learning mangrove extent, height and canopy closure products for 2019 to 2023, with a web portal, for Pêche Côtière Durable Phase II.

name: Madagascar National Parks
summary: Body with a mandate to manage a network of 43 protected areas, collecting biodiversity data through ecological monitoring; WCS Madagascar says it adopted SMART, after a WCS pilot, as the national law enforcement monitoring tool.

name: Madagascar Research and Conservation Institute
summary: Self-described NGO on Nosy Komba conducting reptile, amphibian, bird and lemur surveys, marine surveys and coral restoration, with sea turtle nest monitoring and behaviour documentation.

name: Madagascar terrestrial biodiversity re-prioritisation workshop 2026
summary: Closed workshop in late March 2026 where 70 participants, including 50 scientists, completed the first full re-prioritisation of Madagascar's terrestrial biodiversity since 1995, producing a consensus map of about 18 million hectares.

name: Madagascar Wetland Knowledge Base
summary: A planned national geospatial platform for Madagascar's 21 Ramsar sites, announced with JRS support in January 2024, to be designed and populated by a Wildfowl & Wetlands Trust team.

name: Madagascar Whale Shark Project
summary: A project studying and protecting young whale sharks off Nosy Be since 2016, with photo-identification recording 546 sharks by the end of the 2025 season and twenty acoustic receiver stations in use that season.

name: Madagasikara Voakajy
summary: Antananarivo-based organisation with applied research and monitoring work on species such as Grandidier's baobab, which signed a contract in August 2025 to manage seven protected areas covering 31,006 hectares.

name: MAMPITA
summary: A Malagasy grassroots NGO described by IUCN SOS as taking over community-based forest conservation leadership from MBG Madagascar, partnering with Chester Zoo.

name: Manombo ecoacoustics and eDNA biodiversity monitoring
summary: Project, announced in May 2023, planning to combine acoustic and eDNA data to set a biodiversity baseline and monitor 100 species in Manombo, run by Rainforest Connection with NatureMetrics.

name: MIHARI Network
summary: Independent Malagasy civil society network created in 2012, grouping over 300 LMMAs, with an online national database and, WIOMSA reports, a portal launched in May 2025.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement et du Développement Durable (Madagascar)
summary: Madagascar's environment ministry has mapped protected areas and conservation zones, and its rebuilt SPSE planning tool includes national indicators for Global Biodiversity Framework targets.

name: Office National pour l'Environnement (Madagascar)
summary: Madagascar's environmental office, created in 1990, which manages the environmental information system and publishes the Tableau de Bord Environnemental, an indicator-based tool for monitoring the state of the environment.

name: Pioneering approaches for drone use in biodiversity conservation (Madagascar)
summary: Darwin Initiative-funded project whose workshop, reported by Newsmada in September 2024, covered AI for conservation, reforestation assessment and lemur detection from satellite and drone images, with 70 people from 42 organisations.

name: Planet Madagascar Association
summary: An organisation founded in 2015, working mainly around Ankarafantsika National Park to improve satellite and drone fire detection, with a CEPF-funded 2020 to 2022 fire and forest monitoring grant.

name: Protecting seven threatened lemur species in Vangaindrano's final refuge
summary: An active project, run by Chester Zoo and MAMPITA, that aims to set baseline abundance and distribution data for seven lemur species using camera traps and occupancy modelling, alongside restoration, protection and livelihood support.

name: Reef Doctor
summary: Self-described UK-based non-profit working in southwest Madagascar, which has monitored the coral reef system of the Bay of Ranobe since 2004 through a long-term survey programme.

name: Rewilding Madagascar
summary: A research programme led by Sheila Holmes at SLU, funded by the Swedish Research Council, whose study used cameras and acoustic recorders at five eastern rainforest sites and tested LifePlan classification models on bird audio at one.

name: Réseau de la Biodiversité de Madagascar
summary: Established in 2000, this free Madagascar biodiversity data tool, built and run by WCS, says its work supported selecting four million hectares of new terrestrial protected areas.

name: SADABE
summary: An NGO registered with the Madagascar government in June 2009, which monitored diademed sifaka groups at Tsinjoarivo from 2004 to 2011 and, IUCN reports, is building habitat corridors for them under an SOS Lemurs grant.

name: SMART in Madagascar
summary: Adopted nationally in 2016, this patrol tool had USAID-funded training initiated by WCS in 2013, with 200 users, mainly patrollers, trained since 2013 according to WCS.

name: SYNERGI-MNP
summary: A programme run by Madagascar National Parks carrying information between patrol teams, protected-area managers and headquarters, where a control room centralises environmental alerts.

name: The Peregrine Fund Madagascar Program
summary: A programme combining community investment, species monitoring, habitat restoration and protected area management, which reported in September 2025 that it managed four protected areas and, over the preceding year, monitored 26 waterbird species.

name: University of Antananarivo
summary: An education institution in Antananarivo that OpenAlex links to 79 remote sensing works since January 2022, including a 2022 humpback whale drone study, and which partnered with Cétamada on whale research, as Newsmada reported.

name: Wildlife Conservation Society Madagascar Program
summary: Antananarivo-based programme of the Wildlife Conservation Society, listed by GBIF as a data publisher, which researches lemurs, carnivores and marine species and began SMART training in 2013 with USAID funding.

name: Benthic Habitat Mapping of Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
summary: Satellite-based habitat maps of Majuro atoll's shallow waters, showing reefs, seagrass and sand, visually interpreted from Quickbird II imagery collected 2004 to 2006 and built by NOAA.

name: College of the Marshall Islands
summary: Majuro community college that NFWF lists on a reef monitoring grant, was named in 2025 as a partner in coral heat-tolerance work, and received a 2015 US Interior grant for spatial analytics.

name: Community-Based Reef Monitoring (Marshall Islands)
summary: A $24,000 NFWF award under its Coral Reef Conservation programme to the College of the Marshall Islands for community-based reef monitoring in Majuro, with current status unknown.

name: Exploration of Deep-Sea Habitats in the Marshall Islands (NA174)
summary: A closed Ocean Exploration Trust expedition, 27 July to 17 August 2025, funded by NOAA, that mapped 19,130 km2 of the Marshall Islands exclusive economic zone and collected 161 eDNA samples to support marine spatial planning.

name: Marshall Islands Conservation Society
summary: Says it incorporated in 2004, with 2025 reports describing coral heat-tolerance testing, two nurseries, TNC collaboration on Majuro reef refugia and MIMRA partnership on heat-tolerance work.

name: Marshall Islands Marine Resources Authority
summary: Body whose board oversees the Protected Areas Network since 2018, works with communities on resource management plans under Reimaanlok, and reports training in a community marine monitoring toolkit.

name: National Geographic Pristine Seas Marshall Islands expedition (2026)
summary: National Geographic Pristine Seas expedition, reported in March 2026 as starting that week, planning to survey seven atolls with MIMRA and establish ecological baselines on reef responses to bleaching.

name: National Geographic Pristine Seas Marshall Islands expedition to Bikar, Bokak, Bikini and Rongerik
summary: Reported in September 2023 as arriving to survey four atolls, this National Geographic Pristine Seas expedition planned scuba surveys, underwater video, seabird counts and eDNA sampling.

name: Nature-based-Solutions (NbS) for Resilient Societies to Climate Change in Pacific Atoll Nations
summary: Research project on nature-based solutions in a Pacific atoll nation, funded by the Environmental Restoration and Conservation Agency, with NIES researchers surveying Majuro Atoll in July 2026 to identify priority coral conservation areas in the lagoon.

name: Reimaanlok Conservation Area Management Planning Framework
summary: Community-based conservation area planning process for atoll communities, updated in 2025 according to MICS, whose third step gathers socioeconomic, ecological and physical datasets.

name: RMI Environmental Protection Authority
summary: Listed on the CBD Secretariat's Marshall Islands national focal points page, with its General Manager serving as CBD operational focal point.

name: RMI Protected Areas Network
summary: National protected areas system created by the PAN Act 2015, run by MIMRA, with monitoring eligible for funding and a $25,000 award reported in February 2026 for Bokanbotin.

name: Agency for Real Estate Cadastre
summary: Responsible for topographic and orthophoto maps under the consolidated May 2025 law; its project manager featured in 2021 reporting on lidar mapping and a public portal.

name: Association for Ecology and Tourism ECOTOURISM-2016
summary: An Ohrid association named in a CEPF report on Preserving Belchishta Wetland (June 2020 to August 2022), which lists monitoring guidelines, a protocols manual and a volunteer monitoring school.

name: Balkan Foundation for Sustainable Development
summary: Regional non-governmental organisation founded in 2005 with a Skopje office, funded by CEPF for a June 2020 to June 2022 project studying Prespa trout in three rivers to improve long-term monitoring.

name: Center for Environmental Research and Information Eko-svest
summary: Skopje citizen association founded in 2002, funded by CEPF for an October 2021 to June 2022 project building species and habitat monitoring capacity through citizen science, using a Macedonian-translated iNaturalist.

name: Centre for Development of the South-East Planning Region
summary: Regional development centre in Strumica covering 10 municipalities, whose eFIDAR page lists a forest fire early-warning ICT system and fire risk maps, and which hosted a July 2021 Natura 2000 monitoring meeting.

name: Common plans for biodiversity conservation and sustainable targets for the development of a bilateral network of protected areas
summary: Closed project, April 2018 to April 2020, led by the south-east planning region centre, aiming to test Earth observation for monitoring conservation status and to map habitats and species, including Monospitovo Wetland in Strumica.

name: Department of Animal Ecology, Institute of Biology, Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University in Skopje
summary: University department in Skopje studying terrestrial invertebrates, especially saproxylic beetles as forest indicators, which says its work includes applying artificial intelligence to monitoring and which co-holds the Macedonian National Collection of Invertebrates.

name: Department of Hydrobiology, Systematics and Biotechnology of Algae, Institute of Biology, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University in Skopje
summary: University department in Skopje that says it was first in the region to use algae for aquatic biomonitoring, and which researches toxic algal blooms using molecular genetic analyses including 16S rRNA sequencing.

name: Department of Vertebrate Zoology, Biogeography and Valorization of Natural Ecosystems, Institute of Biology, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University in Skopje
summary: University department in Skopje whose research focuses on monitoring lynx and bear, with work on large carnivores, wetland birds and wetland inventories, including a first inventory of CORINE biotopes in Macedonia with Carl Bro International.

name: Developing and Implementing Smart and Sustainable Integrated Wildfire Management System in the Cross-border Area
summary: Closed cross-border wildfire project, January 2022 to December 2024, led by the Protection and Rescue Directorate, which installed early-detection sensors and cameras at four points on Mount Jablanica and bought four drones.

name: Galičica National Park
summary: National park that began capture-mark-recapture monitoring of the Macedonian newt with the Macedonian Ecological Society in May 2020, and had five representatives trained in monitoring endemic plants, according to a CEPF report.

name: Hydrobiological Institute Ohrid
summary: Public scientific institution whose site offers the Hydro Status application for water quality and biodiversity data on lakes Ohrid and Prespa, and posts 2022 to 2025 reports on a PONT-funded Lake Prespa pressures project.

name: Improving Biodiversity Knowledge and Informing Management Practices for Lake Dojran
summary: Small project run by the Macedonian Ecological Society, January 2024 to December 2026, with a 34,000 euro award, collecting waterbird and habitat data to inform the Lake Dojran management plan.

name: Integrated Forest Information System
summary: Digital system, IFIS, which an EU project page says was developed to improve forest resource monitoring and wood tracking, helping address illegal logging.

name: Macedonian Ecological Society
summary: Environmental NGO that runs the ptici.mk bird portal, uses camera traps, monitors amphibians and Lake Prespa waterbirds, and is named by the ministry as a partner in the LIFE DinPin Bear project.

name: Mavrovo National Park
summary: National park whose monitoring department set up video surveillance at 60 locations, with cameras intended to monitor wild animal species and their numbers.

name: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy
summary: Government ministry that runs the national forest monitoring system design project, which FAO reported in May 2019 had designed a national forest monitoring system over two years with the ministry.

name: Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning
summary: Reports participation in LIFE DinPin Bear, started in January 2026, funds Mavrovo and Pelister parks, and may use the National Red List to inform conservation policy.

name: National forest monitoring system design project (North Macedonia)
summary: Closed FAO-run project that ended with a Skopje workshop on 15 May 2019 and used high-resolution satellite imagery to find forests cover 43 percent of the country and other wooded land 16.8 percent.

name: National Red List of North Macedonia
summary: Red List based on IUCN methodology whose first official assessments covered all 32 reptile and 14 amphibian species, with the Balkan lynx assessment drawing on Mavrovo camera-trapping surveys in 2013, 2015 and 2018.

name: Pelister National Park
summary: National park that reported organised Balkan chamois monitoring on pre-planned transects with its employees in November 2024, and planned a camera-trapping survey with the Macedonian Ecological Society from February 2014.

name: Prespa Green & Blue Initiative: Empowering Conservation through Research, Education and Communication
summary: Co-funded by the Prespa-Ohrid Nature Trust, the project included bird monitoring reported by MES in June 2026, with study and ranger data integration into one digital platform planned.

name: Protection and Rescue Directorate
summary: Public body in Skopje formed under the law on protection and rescue, which led the DISSIWMS project that provided equipment for a fire early-warning monitoring connection with Albania's civil protection agency.

name: ptici.mk
summary: Bird records portal run by the Macedonian Ecological Society, with a website and Android collection app, which MIA reported in March 2026 had logged over 34,000 records from 30 active users in under two years.

name: Shar Mountains National Park
summary: National park established in 2021 covering over 627 square kilometres, funded by Global Conservation, which reported in a post on 2023 plans that it had tested three donated camera traps and held joint monitoring talks with Kosovo's Sharri National Park.

name: Strengthening the capacities for effective implementation of the acquis in the field of nature protection in the North Macedonia
summary: Closed project, 2017 to 2019, run by the Finnish Environment Institute, whose results included monitoring protocols for 20 habitats, 20 species and 20 birds, a draft national biodiversity monitoring programme and two pilot site inventories.

name: Centre Régional de Recherche Agronomique de Mopti
summary: Regional agronomic research centre in Mopti, part of the Institut d'Économie Rurale, whose staff authored a 2023 study using 1987, 2007 and 2018 satellite images to analyse land cover change in Gondolidogon and Kedou.

name: Direction Générale des Eaux et Forêts (Mali)
summary: Malian forestry directorate, listed in the 2025 Journal officiel as created by a text, with a forestry engineer named Director General by decree of 26 February 2025.

name: GBIF Mali
summary: Mali's GBIF country node, listed with observer participation status, with no publishing organisation based in Mali listed by GBIF.

name: Institut d'Économie Rurale
summary: Malian public research institute established in 1961 according to a 2004 brief, mandated to preserve biodiversity, which funded Bamako small mammal trapping from 2021 to 2024.

name: Institut Géographique du Mali
summary: National public administrative establishment created by ordinance, with its mission set as amended in 2018, and named among national geospatial actors in Mali's 2025 UN-GGIM presentation.

name: Landscape Restoration Scale Up (RESILAND Mali Additional Financing)
summary: Proposed additional financing for RESILAND Mali, with concept approved by the GEF on 6 June 2025, planning AI-based forest inventory systems, drones and digital monitoring tools under component 1.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de l'Assainissement et du Développement Durable
summary: Malian environment ministry whose head of the section for biosphere reserves and national parks is listed by the CBD among Mali's focal points.

name: Petits mammifères de Bamako
summary: Closed 2021 to 2024 small mammal trapping project in Bamako, run and funded by the IER and IRD, whose peripheral-district dataset covers 7,433 trap nights and 835 captured animals, openly licensed.

name: Système d'Information Forestier (Mali)
summary: INSTAT lists its CG/SIFOR management unit and cites DNEF’s SIFOR database for tables; Alwihda Info reported a September 2024 ministerial visit assessing flood damage at its Bamako headquarters.

name: Biodiversity and Nature Conservation Association
summary: Myanmar non-profit environmental NGO, active since 2002 and recognised in 2004, that reports monthly shorebird surveys in the Gulf of Mottama from October 2016 to March 2017, and partners with BirdLife International and the ministry.

name: Chatthin Wildlife Sanctuary
summary: A wildlife sanctuary whose staff patrolled regularly, with Eld's deer densities in its core zone reported from the 2015, 2016 and 2017 censuses in a Friends of Wildlife report to CEPF.

name: Data Analytics Lab, University of Computer Studies, Yangon
summary: Research lab at the University of Computer Studies, Yangon, listed as an affiliation by the first author of the 2024 paper Estimation of Annual Deforestation Using Random Forest.

name: Development of Community-Based Models for Biodiversity Conservation in Tanintharyi
summary: Closed project, funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund, that aimed to set up and strengthen village conservation groups to survey, monitor and protect threatened species and habitats in Tanintharyi.

name: Forest Department, Myanmar
summary: Government forest body under the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Conservation, reported in 2019 to use Open Foris tools and GLAD forest products, and to have developed the National Forest Monitoring Action Plan.

name: Friends of Wildlife
summary: A local conservation NGO and CEPF grantee, an Asian Species Action Partnership partner since 2020, whose Chatthin Eld's deer project report records two completed annual censuses.

name: Geo-Myanmar
summary: A closed 2015 to 2025 project, funded by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, that developed an open-access spatial data platform combining land use, cover and tenure data with participatory and crowdsourced maps.

name: Gulf of Mottama Project
summary: Run by IUCN, this Myanmar project included January 2023 shorebird surveying with Nature Conservation Society Myanmar, monitoring since 2018 and local bird identification and flock counting training.

name: Htamathi Wildlife Sanctuary
summary: Wildlife sanctuary where, according to a February 2025 report citing Myanmar state media, forest department workers monitor tigers and installed 24 camera traps in 12 locations in 2024.

name: Indawgyi Lake Wildlife Sanctuary
summary: Wildlife sanctuary whose warden, as reported by The Star, said its January 2026 figures came from the Asian Waterbird Census carried out with Fauna and Flora International, Inn Chit Thu and local bird enthusiasts.

name: Meinmahla Kyun Wildlife Sanctuary
summary: Ramsar-listed mangrove sanctuary in Myanmar where staff counted 115 crocodiles in a November 2021 census, which was compared with the November 2020 count and described as a declining population to be monitored.

name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Conservation
summary: Myanmar government ministry under which UN-REDD placed the Forest Department in 2019, and which BANCA lists among the ministries it works with.

name: Moeyungyi Wildlife Sanctuary
summary: Protected area for endangered birds, run by the Myanmar Forest Department, where a May 2022 report described bird surveys and aquatic plant, fish and water quality assessments for habitat restoration projects.

name: Myanmar Biodiversity Fund
summary: Described by the Asian Species Action Partnership's site as Myanmar's first independent conservation trust fund, registered in 2019 as a not-for-profit company limited by guarantee.

name: Myanmar Biodiversity Zone
summary: A website with sections on species, ecosystems, protected areas, marine, a map and data, listed in Myanmar's 2018 CBD submissions among the country's biodiversity web addresses.

name: Myanmar Clearing House Mechanism
summary: Biodiversity information portal, said in a 2018 Myanmar presentation to have launched in January 2016, which noted that species data from Species Encoders was not directly available on it.

name: Myanmar Forest Certification Committee
summary: Originating in a 1998 timber certification committee, this body has no endorsed national certification system; an associated ITTO project proposes QR log tracking and lists a digital tracking manual.

name: Myanmar Forest Type Map 2020
summary: Dataset showing nine forest types across Myanmar for 2020 at about 20 m resolution, made in Google Earth Engine with a random forest algorithm and funded by a NASA programme.

name: Myanmar Mangrove Extent Explorer
summary: Tool mapping mangrove extent in all of Myanmar's mangrove regions for 2016 and 2021 and the change between them, using supervised random forest, with maps to view and raster data to download.

name: Myanmar National Forest Inventory
summary: Forest Department programme supported by FAO, with a design developed in 2017 and 2018, field tests in early 2019, Open Foris training for staff, and Tanintharyi field work scheduled for January 2020.

name: National Forest Inventory of Myanmar
summary: Forest Department programme with FAO and UN-REDD whose new design was developed in 2017 and 2018 and field-tested in early 2019, using Collect Earth and Collect Earth Online in planning.

name: National Unity Government Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Conservation
summary: National Unity Government ministry that, according to Forest Trends, partnered with it in a nine-month monitoring effort from 2024 to 2025 covering over one million hectares of protected forest in five townships.

name: Nature and Wildlife Conservation Division, Forest Department, Myanmar
summary: Division of the Forest Department whose Director was listed in 2018 as national focal point for the Clearing House Mechanism, and which WCS said it supported at Rakhine Yoma Elephant Reserve in 2017.

name: Nature Conservation Society-Myanmar
summary: A membership-based local environmental NGO working closely with the Forest Department, an IUCN National NGO member since March 2024, behind a 2024 ASAP-funded project with community patrols and shorebird monitoring surveys.

name: Rakhine Yoma Elephant Reserve
summary: Reserve where, WCS reported in December 2017, the warden supervised guard-post upgrades and patrol teams reviewed four years of SMART patrol data and drew up new patrol plans.

name: Sagaing and Magway protected forest monitoring pilot
summary: Closed pilot, run by Forest Trends and the NUG ministry, whose system detected 55,340 deforestation alerts over nine months from 2024 to 2025 and investigated 209 hotspots, leading to enforcement actions.

name: Strengthening Sustainability of Protected Area Management in Myanmar
summary: A GEF-funded project closed on 1 April 2021, run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, that aimed to strengthen the national protected area system and developed SMART patrolling, reportedly taken up nationally by 2020.

name: Survey Department, Myanmar
summary: Government mapping body under the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Conservation, which a May 2016 presentation says reproduced nationwide digital maps from 2000 to 2008 on Myanmar Datum 2000.

name: Tanintharyi Nature Reserve
summary: Protected area established and managed since 2005, which a 2014 review says used remote sensing for forest cover monitoring and camera trapping, with a team of 62 including Forest Department staff.

name: University of Computer Studies, Yangon
summary: University in Yangon whose Data Analytics Lab is listed as an affiliation by the first author of the 2024 paper Estimation of Annual Deforestation Using Random Forest.

name: Update Checklist of Higher Plants in Myanmar (2023)
summary: GBIF dataset of Myanmar higher plants, published on 10 January 2023 under CC BY 4.0, digitised from herbarium specimens at four herbaria and literature as baseline floristic data.

name: WahPlaw Wildlife Watch
summary: A local organisation whose staff, with three village conservation groups and Karen Forest Department staff, ran a bird and mammal survey with camera traps under a CEPF grant, and which uses SMART.

name: WCS Myanmar
summary: Myanmar programme of the Wildlife Conservation Society, which says it has worked there since 1993 and in December 2017 trained patrol teams in camera trapping at Rakhine Yoma Elephant Reserve.

name: Administration of the Great Gobi A Strictly Protected Area
summary: Protected area administration based in Bayantooroi village, whose rangers collect monitoring and patrol data through SMART and report to the director within three days of returning from expeditions, according to a 2025 study.

name: Administration of the Great Gobi B Strictly Protected Area
summary: Administration of a strictly protected area, run by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change, using SMART for patrols and launching waterhole camera traps in summer 2025.

name: AtkinsRéalis eDNA fish survey for irrigation schemes in Mongolia
summary: Closed AtkinsRéalis survey that NatureMetrics calls Mongolia's first eDNA study, informing a development bank's irrigation investment; it identified 19 fish taxa, including four species electric fishing had not recorded.

name: Bactrian camel detection model for drone imagery in the Gobi Desert
summary: Automated detection system for Bactrian camels in Gobi Desert drone imagery, which the paper's authors developed and validated using YOLOv8 and 1,479 images.

name: Baigali (Mongolian Biodiversity app)
summary: App for identifying Mongolia's species with expert help; an opinion piece of March 2024 reported over 12,000 observations from more than 2,700 citizens.

name: Belcheer
summary: A mobile application for rangeland photo monitoring, reported on gazar.gov.mn as introduced from August 2025 by order of the head of GALAGC, for use by land administration staff and rangeland specialists.

name: Biodiversity and adaptation to climate change in Mongolia (Phases I–III)
summary: KfW grant of EUR 39 million over phases I to III, per a May 2021 page, supporting protected-area management in Mongolia, including monitoring equipment such as cameras.

name: Botanic Garden and Research Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences
summary: Institute researching Mongolian plant taxonomy and flora, endorsed as a GBIF publisher, with an algae checklist covering literature through 2025 and about 80,000 herbarium sheets in 2020.

name: Checklist of Algae Reported from Mongolia
summary: GBIF checklist of algae reported from Mongolia, compiled from literature covering 1904 to 2025, with 3,010 name usages and coverage of the whole country.

name: Combating Illegal Trade in Animal Products by Rapid On-Site DNA Sequencing in Mongolia
summary: A closed Rufford-supported project whose 28 November 2022 report records sequencing 31 mammal samples and 96 plant barcodes for a planned database to identify illegally traded species.

name: Community-Based Carnivore Monitoring in the Sutai–Myang Ugalzad Ecological Corridor
summary: A community monitoring project in an ecological corridor, run by Wildlife Initiative, which Snow Leopard Conservancy reported in July 2026 involved 30 herder families and a 49-station camera-trap network recording snow leopards nearly 200 times.

name: Conservation of the Gobi snow leopard: A study in Khurkh Mountain Range
summary: Snow leopard monitoring run by WCS Mongolia, restarted with camera traps in February 2025 after beginning in 2017/2018; a sample check found images on four of five cameras.

name: Environmental Information Database of Mongolia
summary: Database whose site reports 23 base databases and 54 sub-databases, including protected areas, and cites EIC Mongolia for 81.9 per cent of the land being affected by desertification and degradation.

name: Evaluation of transboundary snow leopard subpopulations between Mongolia and the Russian Federation
summary: Closed transboundary snow leopard assessment led by Bariushaa Munkhtsog within wider cooperation, with phases in 2020–2021 and 2022–2023 and slides listing camera-trap installation for September 2022.

name: GBIF Mongolia
summary: Mongolia's country node of GBIF with associate participant status, which has endorsed the Institute of Biology of the Mongolian Academy of Sciences as a data publisher.

name: General Agency for Land Administration and Management, Geodesy and Cartography (Mongolia)
summary: Government implementing agency for land administration, geodesy and cartography in Mongolia, which describes its address system as dividing the country into grid squares based on geographic coordinates.

name: GeoAI for Land Degradation, Climate Resilience and Sustainable Development in Mongolia's Rangelands
summary: Active HeiGIT project that, it says, maps rangeland condition around Töv province and Ulaanbaatar using a custom deep learning model, radar and multispectral imagery and AlphaEarth embeddings, with openly available maps.

name: Gobi Gurvansaikhan National Park administration
summary: Park administration whose rangers asked the Snow Leopard Trust in 2021 to extend the survey to the Bayanbor mountains, where 10 of 11 pilot cameras captured snow leopards.

name: Gun Galuut Nature Conservation Center
summary: A bird-focused ringing station and research and information centre in central Mongolia, described in a brochure from the Saraana Nature Conservation Foundation, which built it.

name: Hustai National Park Trust
summary: Trust that manages the administration of Hustai National Park, employing 12 rangers with GPS and reporting 223 bird and 55 mammal species from continuous scientific evaluation of the park.

name: Institute of Geography and Geoecology, Mongolian Academy of Sciences
summary: A Mongolian Academy of Sciences institute in Ulaanbaatar, listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2025 Remote Sensing paper using Landsat data and machine learning to map grassland vegetation change.

name: Irbis Mongolia Center
summary: A Mongolian snow leopard organisation that partnered with Snow Leopard Conservancy on a 2009 survey with 977 scat samples, 274 genetically confirmed as snow leopard, and reports camera-trap surveys from 2008 to 2024.

name: Khomyn Talyn Takhi
summary: Organisation whose 2025 report covers Khomyn Tal National Park work on Przewalski's horses, giving a population of 157 at the end of 2025 and SMART patrols since 2024.

name: Khurkh Bird Ringing Station
summary: Volunteer-based bird ringing station in Khentii province, run by the Wildlife Science and Conservation Center of Mongolia, which says it is the only one regularly operating in the country.

name: Landscape-level mitigation in the Mongolian Gobi Desert
summary: Closed planning process, completed between 2009 and 2017 by the Mongolian government and The Nature Conservancy, which used Marxan; Marxan's case study reports 68,800 square kilometres of new protected areas designated.

name: Long-Term Ecological Study of snow leopards, South Gobi
summary: A snow leopard study in the South Gobi that the Snow Leopard Trust says it has run since 2009 using GPS collars and remote cameras, with SMART used in a 2025 gazelle survey.

name: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (Mongolia)
summary: Government ministry hosting CBD focal points and listing protected-area, forest and animal databases, which Wikipedia says manages special protected areas.

name: Mongolia nationwide snow leopard population survey
summary: Closed snow leopard census run by WWF, reported to have run from May 2018 to October 2020 with 1,475 camera traps, combined with field signs, prey counts and modelling, as part of PAWS.

name: Mongolian Ornithological Society
summary: Wikipedia describes a Ulaanbaatar non-profit founded in 1999 for bird research and conservation, contributing database information, with waterfowl census, black stork tracking and wind farm survey projects.

name: Multipurpose National Forest Inventory of Mongolia
summary: According to FAO, national forest inventory conducted in 2014–2017 under the National Forest Agency and published through its microdata catalogue, with another planned for 2027 using Open Foris Arena.

name: National Agency for Meteorology and Environmental Monitoring (Mongolia)
summary: A Mongolian government agency which, according to the 2018 national rangeland health report, has implemented new monitoring and interpretation procedures at its 1,516 long-term monitoring sites since 2011.

name: National Forensic Agency of Mongolia
summary: Works with Hanns Seidel Foundation since 2022 on animal DNA databases; 58 species entered an international database by September 2023; hosted a tree identification publication launch in November 2025.

name: National Forest Agency (Mongolia)
summary: Agency under the environment ministry, formerly the Forest Research and Development Centre, which FAO says led the national forest inventory and is helping move its database to Arena.

name: National rangeland health monitoring (Mongolia)
summary: A national rangeland monitoring programme which, a 2018 report says, began in 2011 and was continuing at 1,516 sites as of 2016, and is run by NAMEM.

name: National University of Mongolia
summary: Mongolian university describing itself as the country's first, 82 years old; a 2023 paper by an affiliated author applied random forest machine learning to MODIS data on Dornod forest fires, and its herbarium holds about 20,000 sheets.

name: Nomadic Nature Conservation
summary: Mongolian NGO partnered with WCS on the Nomadic Nature Trunk curriculum, first launched in 2007; a national report says it conducts community-based wildlife monitoring and education.

name: Participatory Rangeland Monitoring System (Mongolia)
summary: Rangeland monitoring programme built by UNDP and a Mongolian land agency, which UNDP says combines photo-monitoring, satellite imagery, AI and herder data; the Belcheer app was piloted in two provinces, with nationwide scale-up next.

name: Research Laboratory of Geo-Informatics (GEO-iLAB), National University of Mongolia
summary: Laboratory run by the National University of Mongolia, the contact for a 2025 wildfire detection presentation saying research continues and a wildfire and yellow dust platform is in development.

name: Round River Conservation Studies Mongolia programme
summary: A programme run and built by Round River, launched in 2018 with Ulaan Taiga administration guidance, using camera-trap grids for large mammals and 84 permanent Darhad Valley plots for pika and pasture work begun in 2019.

name: Saraana Nature Conservation Foundation
summary: A non-governmental charity based in Mongolia, established in 2021 according to its brochure, whose research includes waterfowl monitoring, shorebird ringing and bird breeding and migration surveys.

name: Science and Technology Fund
summary: Mongolian science funding body whose portal is titled the National Science and Technology Fund; a biodiversity checklist names a biodiversity database produced with its financial support.

name: SMART monitoring by herder community rangers, southern Mongolia
summary: WCS Mongolia says it introduced SMART to herder community rangers in southern Mongolia, who use it to report observations, GPS locations and patrol distances while documenting wildlife and human activity.

name: SMART patrol monitoring in Mongolia's protected areas
summary: Mongolia's use of SMART patrol monitoring, which its report to the CMS Central Asian Mammals Initiative says over 120 state protected areas were integrating as of 2023, under a national working group and a directive.

name: Snow leopard camera-trap population study, Bumbat and Sutai mountain ranges
summary: Closed snow leopard population study run by The Nature Conservancy, using camera traps in the Bumbat and Sutai ranges from 2016 to 2022, with over 200 cameras set up.

name: Snow Leopard Conservation Foundation
summary: Mongolian conservation organisation that, according to the Mountain Partnership, has researched snow leopards since 2007 and began a South Gobi ecological study in 2008; it partners with Snow Leopard Trust and lists a SMART programme.

name: South Gobi snow leopard GPS collaring and corridor study
summary: Project run by WCS Mongolia, which put GPS collars on two adult male snow leopards to identify South Gobi movement corridors; collar data will allow almost real-time monitoring.

name: Study on goitered gazelles, Great Gobi B Strictly Protected Area
summary: A study in which, the International Takhi Group reported in September 2024, twelve goitered gazelles in three areas of Great Gobi B SPA were fitted with GPS solar collars, with university partners.

name: TNC gazelle and vulture movement study, Mongolia
summary: Active TNC study in Mongolia, working with 10 research organisations and using satellite and drone technology to study gazelle and vulture population movements.

name: Ulaan Taiga Specially Protected Areas Administration
summary: A protected area administration in northern Mongolia whose rangers, Round River says, are supported with camera-trap wildlife monitoring, and which shares 84 permanent Darhad Valley monitoring plots with Round River's research.

name: WCS Mongolia
summary: Wildlife Conservation Society programme that introduced SMART to herder rangers and reports seven herder groups helping protect 3,184 square kilometres across Umnugobi and Dornogobi.

name: Wildlife Initiative
summary: A non-profit established in Mongolia in 2020 for wildlife research and conservation, with camera-trap snow leopard work in western Mongolia, a Pallas's cat project, and a partnership with Snow Leopard Conservancy since 2022.

name: Wildlife monitoring at waterholes, Great Gobi B Strictly Protected Area
summary: Built and run by the area's administration; over 300,000 images downloaded in 2025 are being analysed partly using AI, with 20 more cameras planned for 2026.

name: Wildlife Science and Conservation Center of Mongolia
summary: Ulaanbaatar-based NGO registered in 2004, researching and conserving wildlife and habitats through education and bird migration monitoring, with an agreement to transfer reserve management to its team.

name: Annual winter waterbird counts at Iwik, Banc d'Arguin
summary: Annual winter waterbird counts in the Iwik region of Banc d'Arguin park, run by NIOZ since December 2003, recorded numbers falling from 120,000 to 80,000 between 2003 and 2023.

name: Exploring Essential Habitats of Threatened Sharks and Rays in the Banc D’Arguin, Mauritania
summary: An active project using baited underwater video and mark-recapture studies in the Banc d'Arguin park, aiming to produce the first fisheries-independent baseline data on shark and ray diversity, abundance and habitat use.

name: GBIF Mauritania
summary: Country node of GBIF with voting participation, according to GBIF's registry, which also lists Moulaye Mohamed Baba Ainina as node manager and shows a partnership with GBIF.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement et du Développement Durable (Mauritanie)
summary: Mauritanian environment ministry that, UNDP reports, revised the national biodiversity strategy with GEF support, and held its validation workshop on 10 October 2024 with UNDP and GIZ funding and technical backing.

name: Observatoire du Parc National du Banc d'Arguin
summary: The park's observatory, run by the national park, coordinates and monitors its indicators and produces and stores data, but its 2025 to 2029 management plan notes it has no online database covering all themes.

name: Parc National du Banc d'Arguin
summary: Mauritanian national park whose field staff lead colonial breeding bird monitoring, per a 2025 assessment that also notes bird database limitations; a 2024 paper reports yearly waterbird counts at Iwik, 2003 to 2023.

name: Parc National du Diawling
summary: A Mauritanian national park whose eco-guards received waterbird monitoring training, with a planned ornithological station agreed with Nature Mauritanie and OrnithoSchool, and a 2017 census report giving 122,259 birds counted there.

name: Promouvoir la gestion participative des ressources naturelles (Mauritanie)
summary: During 2022–2024, this Mauritanian project worked on vegetation cover remote sensing and used an environmental information system to compile and share data between partners.

name: Protection of the Mediterranean monk seal colony of the Cap Blanc Peninsula, Mauritania
summary: A closed 2014 to 2016 project, partnered with IUCN Save Our Species and the CBD Habitat Foundation, to support surveillance of a Mauritanian monk seal reserve; IUCN reported 67 births in 2014 and growth from 109 to 250 animals.

name: RESSOURCE+ in Mauritania
summary: An active project, run by the Sustainable Wildlife Management Programme and funded by the French Global Environment Facility, whose agreement was signed on 13 January 2026 and which plans tests of AI-assisted drone and satellite waterbird counting in Senegal River valley wetlands.

name: Ambjent Malta
summary: Government entity tasked with preserving and enhancing Malta's natural capital and biodiversity, which chose 37 valleys for a drone survey and had a biologist label the invasive species in the images.

name: AMBULANT
summary: Project led by MCAST, with AquaBioTech Group researchers, that developed a system identifying Mediterranean benthic habitats using computer vision and machine learning, trained on more than 20,000 images from Maltese waters.

name: Applied Research and Innovation Centre, Malta College of Arts, Science and Technology
summary: Research centre at MCAST in Paola, Malta, listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first and corresponding author of a 2025 PeerJ paper comparing GAM and MaxEnt models for bottlenose dolphin habitat mapping.

name: Biodiversity and Ecology Research Group, Institute of Earth Systems, University of Malta
summary: University of Malta research group within the Institute of Earth Systems, whose researchers spent six months, reported in March 2024, on the continuation of the Wild Future for Orchids project.

name: BirdLife Malta
summary: Malta's oldest environmental NGO by its own account, established in 1962 and a BirdLife International partner, which led a seabird project using GPS loggers and runs LIFE PanPuffinus!.

name: BirdLife Malta Ringing Scheme
summary: BirdLife Malta's bird ringing scheme, which it says is the only ringing carried out in Malta and the only EURING-recognised partner there, and has used GPS and satellite loggers on several species.

name: Comino Bird Observatory
summary: Bird observatory on Comino operated by BirdLife Malta's ringing scheme, which says it has run a standardised ringing project in spring and autumn migration every year since 1991.

name: Conservation Biology Research Group, Department of Biology, University of Malta
summary: Based in the University of Malta's Department of Biology, the group is listed by OpenAlex as all three authors' affiliation on a 2025 paper about marine vertebrate eDNA detection.

name: Detection of Invasive Alien Plant Species from High-Resolution Drone Images
summary: Closed project in which the University of Malta and Ambjent Malta mapped invasive alien plants using open-source deep learning models on labelled drone image mosaics, with Malta Information Technology Agency funding.

name: ECHO-AI (Enhancing Cetacean Habitat Observation through Artificial Intelligence)
summary: Project launched in January 2026 by EcoMarine Malta with the University of Malta, funded through Xjenza Malta, that plans to train machine-learning models on acoustic recordings to identify key sound patterns.

name: EcoMarine Malta
summary: For-profit enterprise set up by Patrizia Patti, whose DelfishPAM project collected over 1,000 hours of underwater acoustic recordings, which ECHO-AI plans to catalogue into labelled datasets for machine-learning models.

name: Environment and Resources Authority
summary: Malta's competent authority under the 2023 national report to EUROBATS, which says it may issue derogations from protection rules and generally requests post-construction monitoring reports from developers.

name: Flight for Insight: Monitoring Yellow-legged Gulls
summary: Project in which BirdLife Malta fitted six rehabilitated Yellow-legged Gulls with GPS transmitters, aiming to understand their ecology, assess rehabilitation and identify threats, funded by Xjenza Malta's National STEM Community Fund.

name: Friends of the Earth Malta
summary: Voluntary organisation, enrolled since 2008, which a June 2026 post says is doing biodiversity monitoring and citizen science on Comino using wildlife cameras and iNaturalist, with Xjenza Malta funding.

name: Green House Malta
summary: A voluntary organisation that initiated the Wild Future for Orchids citizen science project in 2016, according to the University of Malta.

name: Institute of Earth Systems, University of Malta
summary: University of Malta institute in Msida that includes the Biodiversity and Ecology Research Group, and is listed by OpenAlex on a 2023 paper investigating the marine soundscape of Malta.

name: Kaċċaturi San Ubertu
summary: Voluntary organisation reported in April 2024 to have captured 20 turtle doves in Malta since 2021 for satellite tagging, and listed in 2025 with a EUR 19,118.40 grant for satellite tagging of common quail.

name: LIFE Arċipelagu Garnija
summary: Closed BirdLife Malta project, begun in 2015, focused on Yelkouan Shearwater recovery, which by August 2020 had handled almost 1,500 adults and over 500 chicks and analysed thousands of camera trap and thermal images.

name: LIFE BaĦAR for N2K
summary: Research programme on benthic habitats in Maltese waters to support marine Natura 2000 designation, 50% co-financed by EU LIFE+, with Oceana saying it surveyed areas down to 1,039 m.

name: LIFE PanPuffinus!
summary: Closed project run by BirdLife Malta, whose migration atlas gives its duration as 2021 to 2025 and records a Yelkouan shearwater tracked by GPS logger in 2021.

name: LIFE+ Malta Seabird Project
summary: Closed BirdLife Malta-led project, running September 2011 to June 2016, that tracked shearwaters with GPS loggers and geolocators and monitored colonies by mark-recapture and boat transect counts.

name: Malta Bird Migration Atlas
summary: Atlas built by the BirdLife Malta Ringing Scheme combining ringing recoveries, sightings and tracking data on bird movements in the Maltese Islands, still early in development, with live tracking and Flight for Insight gull data.

name: Malta Bird Sightings
summary: Portal built by BirdLife Malta in January 2021 for local birders' records, with more than 19,000 sessions logged by about 80 users by 1 October 2024 and nightly data sent to EuroBirdPortal since September 2024.

name: Malta College of Arts, Science and Technology
summary: Maltese college whose Applied Research and Innovation Centre is listed on a 2025 dolphin habitat paper, and which says it is a partner in the Xjenza Malta-funded PAGES project on monitoring Europe's seas.

name: Mapping And monitoring of Posidonia oceanica using Remote and Sentinel technology
summary: Closed project, September 2021 to June 2023, led by Ambjent Malta and funded by MCST, that aimed to map Posidonia oceanica using remote sensing including Sentinel-2, drones and SCUBA dives.

name: Merilli Malta Project
summary: Research project led by Benjamin Metzger and Marie Claire Gatt studying the movement and breeding ecology of the Blue Rock-thrush using colour-ringing, part-funded by the Malta Environment Foundation.

name: Nature Trust Malta
summary: Maltese environmental NGO that, per Malta's 2023 EUROBATS report, rescues and rehabilitates bats with ERA funding, and in July 2024 was reported to have found a turtle nest and sought monitoring volunteers.

name: Oceanography Malta Research Group, Department of Geosciences, University of Malta
summary: University of Malta research group, per its GBIF publisher record, that studies central Mediterranean marine ecosystems, collects biodiversity data and expects to publish citizen science data on non-native species.

name: PIXAM Ltd
summary: Maltese company in Msida, named by the University of Malta as a partner in the MAARES Posidonia remote sensing project and listed as an exhibitor at London Tech Week.

name: REVIVing marine Ecosystems through habitat restoration measures
summary: Active Interreg Italia-Malta 2021-2027 project, announced by the University of Malta in 2025, that aims to develop monitoring tools and conservation measures to restore marine ecosystems.

name: Sharklab-Malta
summary: A non-profit voluntary organisation founded in 2008 researching sharks, rays and skates, whose 2011–2024 bull ray data yielded 135 individuals across 407 sightings, according to a 2025 paper.

name: Spot the Alien Fish
summary: Campaign launched by the University of Malta in 2016 with partners including ISPRA, aiming at long-term monitoring of selected alien fish species through an informal network across Malta, Tunisia and Sicily.

name: Spot the Jellyfish
summary: Citizen science project described in July 2021 as one of Malta's largest, with over 4,000 verified reports then, and a neural network trained on 1,000 images to recognise five jellyfish.

name: Tracking Mediterranean Gulls and Yellow-legged Gulls
summary: Closed BirdLife Malta project from March 2022 to March 2023 that followed Mediterranean and Yellow-legged Gulls, especially around Salina Nature Reserve, using satellite transmitters, funded by the Conservation of Wild Birds Funding Scheme 2021.

name: University of Malta
summary: Msida-based university that was a partner in the MAARES seagrass mapping project and runs the Oceanography Malta Research Group, with staff setting up species monitoring tools and a molecular genetics laboratory.

name: Wild Future for Orchids
summary: A citizen science project to conserve and ecologically monitor Malta's wild orchids, with large-scale data collection and continued University of Malta research reported in March 2024.

name: Wild Kemmuna
summary: Citizen science project on iNaturalist, launched by Friends of the Earth Malta in 2025, collecting photos of wild flora and fauna across a Natura 2000 site, with 1,380 observations and 309 species reported in April 2026.

name: Xjenza Malta
summary: A Maltese government agency promoting and coordinating research, innovation and science communication, whose MCST Space Research Fund funded MAARES, dated September 2021 to June 2023.

name: A Systematic Survey of Long-Tailed Macaques in Mauritius Using Drone-Mounted Thermal Infrared Cameras
summary: Closed project that established a thermal drone survey protocol for Mauritius's macaques; its 2025 final report gives a baseline of around 60,000 animals from 1,550 hectares surveyed.

name: Checklist of flowering plants of the island of Mauritius, Indian Ocean
summary: A checklist of the native flowering species of Mauritius, built by The Mauritius Herbarium and funded by Biodiversity Information for Development, expected to support scientists, government and the public.

name: Department of Biosciences and Ocean Studies, Faculty of Science, University of Mauritius
summary: University of Mauritius department listed by OpenAlex as the first author's affiliation on a 2023 paper on remote sensing monitoring of mangrove growth rate at planted sites.

name: Department of Software and Information Systems, Faculty of Information, Communication and Digital Technologies, University of Mauritius
summary: University of Mauritius department listed by OpenAlex as the first author's affiliation on a 2023 paper on identifying Crown of Thorns Starfish with a convolutional neural network and attention model.

name: Ebony Forest Ltd
summary: Implemented a CEPF-funded forest restoration and threatened bird project from August 2019 to June 2022, reporting monthly bird surveys and bimonthly predator monitoring in August 2022.

name: Echo parakeet nest monitoring and ringing programme
summary: Mauritian Wildlife Foundation programme checking nest boxes and cavities each breeding season and ringing chicks, yielding a 1994 to 2022 capture-mark-recapture dataset of 2,734 known-aged wild individuals.

name: Eco-Sud
summary: An NGO registered in 2000 to protect the Blue Bay Marine Park, listed in a directory for Pointe d'Esny lagoon monitoring and turtle identification, and funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund.

name: EcoMode Society
summary: An NGO whose 2021 to 2024 Tech4Nature coral programme at Pointe-aux-Feuilles planned camera monitoring and a proof of concept of AI for coral monitoring, with no progress reports submitted.

name: Ecosystem Restoration Alliance Indian Ocean
summary: A Mauritian NGO that says it is the only one working with all Mauritian bat species, reporting an 80% fall in cave bats from its surveys.

name: eDNA monitoring of seagrass restoration in Mauritius
summary: eDNA monitoring accompanying a pilot seagrass transplantation led by local stakeholders and Reef Conservation, with baseline samples from three sites analysed by 12S and COI metabarcoding.

name: Forestry Service (Mauritius)
summary: A 2012 FAO report identified this government body within Mauritius's Ministry of Agro Industry and Food Security and reported a system for managing and monitoring forestry resources.

name: ICT Department, Faculty of Information, Communication and Digital Technologies, University of Mauritius
summary: University of Mauritius ICT department listed by OpenAlex as the first author's affiliation on a 2024 paper on automatic recognition of marine creatures using deep learning.

name: Le Velo Vert
summary: Mauritian NGO working to mainstream organic agriculture, whose biannual surveys of non-crop plants in pilot organic fields set up in 2017 produced 1,003 records in a GBIF dataset.

name: Marine Megafauna Conservation Organisation
summary: A 2022 paper links this Mauritian NGO to Maubydick, which monitors sperm whales in Mauritius and compiled a catalogue of 38 individuals from underwater observations and video.

name: MariScope
summary: Mobile and cloud platform that, its page says, ingests satellite and oceanographic data each morning to detect temperature anomalies, coral bleaching risks and algal bloom indicators, with a 2025 copyright line for Joytech Solutions.

name: Mauritian Wildlife Foundation
summary: A registered charity founded in 1984 and described as the largest Mauritian NGO focused only on endangered species, which in 2021 used AudioMoth recorders and a sound classifier to detect Echo Parakeets.

name: Mauritian Wildlife Foundation AudioMoth acoustic monitoring project
summary: Mauritian Wildlife Foundation project in which 15 AudioMoth recorders were deployed on a grid at the Ferney fenced plot in August 2021, with endemic birds detected using Kaleidoscope Pro.

name: Mauritius Coral Reef Conservation Project
summary: A closed Huawei-funded Tech4Nature project run by EcoMode Society; Huawei reports solar buoys, underwater cameras and 25,000 coral fragments transplanted at Pointe-aux-Feuilles by August 2023.

name: Mauritius Mangrove Atlas
summary: A national mangrove atlas for mainland Mauritius, described as field-validated and combining ground surveys, GPS observations and imagery, with its May 2026 update mapping about 244.5 ha.

name: Mauritius Oceanography Institute
summary: A body established in January 2000 to coordinate oceanographic research in Mauritius, with projects on coral culture and ecological monitoring and satellite oceanography capacity built with the Indian Ocean Commission.

name: Mauritius RECOS pilot project, Bel Ombre watershed (eDNA monitoring)
summary: RECOS-financed Mauritius pilot for 2024 to 2026, led by Reef Conservation with NatureMetrics as partner, using eDNA to strengthen monitoring in the Bel Ombre watershed; NatureMetrics' service is priced at about 20,000 euros.

name: Mauritius Wetlands Monitoring and Assessment
summary: Public domain map dataset assessing land degradation for 2001, 2011 and 2017, within the GMES and Africa programme, crediting RCMRD, the AUC, the EU and ESA.

name: Ministry of Environment, Solid Waste Management and Climate Change
summary: The Mauritian ministry whose stated vision includes protecting environmental assets, and which its 2024-25 report names as the national focal point for the Nairobi Convention.

name: MOL Mauritius International Fund for Natural Environment Recovery and Sustainability
summary: A fund set up by Mitsui O.S.K. Lines within an 800 million yen package announced in September 2020, which supports Mauritian conservation projects and funds EcoMode Society and Reef Conservation.

name: National Parks and Conservation Service
summary: The Mauritian service responsible for managing native terrestrial biodiversity and its ecosystems.

name: Reef Conservation
summary: A Mauritian NGO founded in 2004 that monitors marine ecosystems, with a 2023 to 2024 mangrove report recording drone mapping and aims for an eDNA inventory and a volunteer mangrove app.

name: Shoals Rodrigues
summary: A Mauritian marine conservation NGO supporting reserve selection, whose 2007 report records reef monitoring since 1999 and an address at Pointe Monier, Rodrigues.

name: The Mauritius Herbarium
summary: A herbarium at Reduit that describes itself as the main repository of Mascarene plant specimens.

name: University of Mauritius
summary: A university at Reduit whose researchers study reef buoy data, according to Huawei; OpenAlex lists papers with its authors on starfish, bird songs, marine creatures and mangroves.

name: University of Technology, Mauritius
summary: Mauritian university whose OpenAlex-listed work includes 2024 and 2025 papers on mangrove mapping and modelling and on invasive Vachellia nilotica spread on Rodrigues, using remote sensing and GIS.

name: Using Drones to Protect the Endangered Mauritian Flying Fox
summary: Closed 2022 to 2023 project that planned to use a thermal-camera drone to assess the Mauritian flying fox's distribution and behaviour and improve roost estimates, according to the IUCN SOS page.

name: Big Fish Network
summary: Programme built by the Maldives Whale Shark Research Programme, with 239 contributors in May 2025, including guesthouses, resort guides and dive operators, and 648 encounters logged in 2023.

name: Can Gulper Sharks Recover? Building a National Monitoring Programme for Deep-Sea Sharks in the Maldives
summary: A project led by Sara Scroglieri that aims to gather baseline gulper shark data in the Maldives and build a standardised national monitoring framework, combining local knowledge, genetic sampling and fisheries data.

name: Environmental Regulatory Authority
summary: Agency renamed in August 2025 from the Environmental Protection Agency under Presidential Directive No. 14/2025, now operating directly under the Ministry of Tourism and Environment.

name: FC Frigator
summary: Maldivian NGO from Haa Alif Hoarafushi Island associated with GEF-funded lesser noddy research that UNDP says involved the Maldives’ first satellite tracking of seabirds.

name: Fulhadhoo coral reef monitoring project
summary: Coral reef monitoring project run by Stream Foundation, whose cameras recorded 15,728 individual fish in 2024, according to Ooredoo Maldives as reported by MV+.

name: GEMANA
summary: Art and conservation NGO reported to have conducted reef monitoring and Reef Check training, whose Shaha Hashim helped organise the first all-Maldivian Reef Check survey in 2014.

name: Geomatics Department (Maldives)
summary: Department under the Ministry of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development, according to OneMap.

name: Maldives Manta Conservation Programme
summary: A Maldives registered charity since 2022, formerly the Maldivian Manta Ray Project, that collects manta ray population data and whose 2023 report counts more than 80,000 photo-ID sightings.

name: Maldives Marine Research Institute
summary: Institute with the official mandate to monitor the Maldives' coral reefs, which uses the machine learning tool ReefCloud and, AIMS reports, has increased its data collection rate and scale.

name: Maldives National Seagrass Monitoring Network
summary: Seagrass monitoring network whose protocol launched in January 2020 and was accepted by the Maldives Marine Research Institute as a national standard, according to a 2020 Six Senses Laamu report.

name: Maldives Resilient Reef Ecosystem and Economy for the Future (Maldives RREEF)
summary: UNDP-run project, funded by the Global Fund for Coral Reefs, planned for June 2023 to December 2029, with Addu and Fuvahmulah Atolls as priority coral reef sites.

name: Maldives Space Research Organisation
summary: A non-governmental organisation describing itself as the first dedicated to the Maldives space sector, whose 2023 Goidhoo Atoll pilot used UAV, satellite, survey and citizen science data on seagrass, coral and mangroves.

name: Maldives Whale Shark Research Programme
summary: Maldivian research-based conservation charity established in 2013, which trains guides to photo-identify whale sharks and identified its 800th individual in May 2025.

name: Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology
summary: Ministry whose DMADD project piloted passive acoustic monitoring of underwater ecosystems, after which MV+ reported in May 2025 that the government began using it.

name: Ministry of Tourism and Environment
summary: Ministry reporting over 15 rangers employed across the Maldives in August 2025, under which the Environmental Regulatory Authority has operated directly since that month.

name: Miyaru Programme
summary: A Maldivian NGO and research network for shark research and conservation, according to its research manager, run entirely by volunteers, with field work from eDNA and BRUV to drone surveys and citizen science.

name: National Coral Reef Monitoring Program (Maldives)
summary: Coral reef monitoring programme established in 1998, run by the Maldives Marine Research Institute and one of its two main programmes, according to ICRI.

name: OneMap (Maldives)
summary: Self-described official national portal for geospatial, mapping and land information, run and built by the Geomatics Department, offering reef and lagoon downloads and an API without authentication.

name: Rasfari passive acoustic monitoring pilot
summary: Closed pilot run by the Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology that collected baseline sound data at the damaged Rasfari reef in April 2025 and trained 17 stakeholders.

name: Reef Check Maldives
summary: Local NGO founded in 2017, according to a Rufford grantee report, to take over Reef Check training of Maldivians, and listed by Reef Check as an EcoDiver training facility.

name: Sea Turtle Beach Guardian Programme, L. Gaadhoo
summary: A community programme protecting endangered sea turtles at L. Gaadhoo through beach monitoring, nest protection and engagement, which introduced the Maldives' first sea turtle ranger programme and is presented by UNDP under GEF Small Grants.

name: Tech4Nature project in South Ari Marine Protected Area
summary: A project launched on 5 February 2026, the first Tech4Nature initiative in the Maldives, built by IUCN, the Ministry of Tourism and Environment and Huawei, planning to equip South Ari Marine Protected Area rangers with monitoring and communication technology.

name: The Coral Database (Maldives)
summary: Online national repository for Maldivian coral reef data, relaunched in December 2021, which a World Bank paper said held only citizen science data at the time of writing.

name: African Bat Conservation
summary: Run by Conservation Research Africa, this programme monitors bats and biodiversity in Malawi; a 2025 report says a University of Bath PhD student will develop an AI acoustic classifier.

name: Assessing habitat connectivity and fragmentation for Opsaridium microlepis conservation in Malawi
summary: A closed 2024 project, listed under the Fondation Segré Conservation Action Fund, that planned GIS and remote sensing analysis of habitat connectivity and fragmentation between the Linthipe and Bua rivers.

name: Assessing the Grey Crowned Crane Population in Nyika National Park
summary: Project led by George Malembo M'manga that aims to assess the Grey Crowned Crane population and wetland habitat condition in and around Nyika National Park, with community monitoring outside the reserve.

name: Assessment of the Impact of Sanctuary Areas on Biodiversity, Distribution, Conservation and Productivity of Aquatic Organisms in Lake Malawi and Lake Malombe
summary: A May 2024 project planning comparisons of fish, macroinvertebrate and macrophyte diversity inside and outside sanctuaries in Lake Malawi's South Eastern Arm and Lake Malombe.

name: Bats and Biodiversity Monitoring Programme
summary: A programme which Malawi's sixth national CBD report says ABC (African Bats Conservation) implements, and which the report says created a bats and biodiversity database.

name: Bio-physical and Ecological Monitoring System (BEMS), Malawi
summary: A Malawi system for tracking and reporting sustainable land management and coordinating restoration programmes, for which NIRAS says it developed and operationalised the spatial data infrastructure and analytic capabilities.

name: Biodiversity Monitoring Project, Liwonde National Park
summary: An active Lilongwe Wildlife Trust monitoring programme in Liwonde National Park, supporting African Parks with priority species, especially reintroduced carnivores, and reporting in January 2022 almost 2,000 species reports and studbooks for every large carnivore.

name: Carnivore Research Malawi
summary: Active programme run by Conservation Research Africa, working on carnivore conservation, especially spotted hyaena, in Malawi since 2011, using camera traps and GPS collar data to monitor hyaena clans and dens.

name: CLIMB - Conservation Livelihoods In Malawi's Biospheres
summary: A closed 2022 to 2026 project around the Mulanje, Viphya and Mtangatanga forest reserves, run by three bodies, which trained 390 community members in a citizen science programme monitoring water, soil and forests.

name: Conformal triage for camera-trap classification: Nkhotakota Wildlife Reserve, Malawi
summary: Active Zenodo record of code and derived data for a paper, submitted to Ecological Informatics, applying conformal prediction to a camera-trap classifier in Nkhotakota Wildlife Reserve using LILA BC images.

name: Conservation grounded in science: the Spotted ground thrush in Malawi
summary: A project funded by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund that planned field surveys of the subspecies' distribution, population size and habitat preference on Mount Mulanje, with field work in November and December 2020.

name: Conservation Research Africa
summary: UK charity (number 1170640) whose project is Carnivore Research Malawi, and which a June 2017 Lilongwe Wildlife Trust article named as a partner in biodiversity monitoring at Vwaza Wildlife Reserve.

name: Conserving Malawi's Vultures
summary: A Lilongwe Wildlife Trust project launched in 2019 combining research, monitoring and public engagement; its January 2019 announcement reported 16 critically endangered vultures tagged in Majete and Nyika.

name: Department of Forestry
summary: Government forestry department under Malawi's Ministry of Natural Resources, protecting 88 gazetted forest reserves and producing the first national forest inventory and initial forest reference level with academic partners.

name: Department of Forestry, Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources
summary: A department of Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources, named as an affiliation of the first author of a 2024 paper evaluating machine learning elephant recognition from drone imagery in Kasungu.

name: Department of Museums and Monuments
summary: Government department mandated to collect, preserve and research Malawi's natural and cultural history, which publishes bird specimen and Scarabaeoidea beetle records through GBIF.

name: Department of National Parks and Wildlife
summary: Malawi government department that says it manages nine protected areas, five national parks and four wildlife reserves, and whose research section runs ecological monitoring including animal population surveys and patrol analysis.

name: Department of Surveys
summary: Described by the Ministry of Lands as Malawi's National Land Surveying and Mapping Authority, with a Map Production Unit that makes maps and images and a role coordinating spatial data sharing.

name: Drone-Based Monitoring and Protection of Wildlife in National Parks
summary: Project reported by The Nation in June 2023 as launched, planning drones with high-resolution and thermal cameras in Kasungu National Park, in partnership with Tech265.

name: Enhancing accessibility of biodiversity data in Malawi
summary: A project identified as African Biodiversity Challenge 2018, planning a national biodiversity data platform accessible through government museum and WESM websites, with four Malawian participating institutions.

name: Environmental Affairs Department
summary: Malawi government department that is the focal point for the Convention on Biological Diversity, whose Biodiversity Unit led a September 2024 workshop on National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan targets.

name: Evaluating machine learning-based elephant recognition in complex African landscapes using drone imagery
summary: A completed study using about 3,180 drone images from Kasungu National Park to evaluate three machine learning object detection models, Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet and Mask R-CNN, for elephant recognition.

name: Fisheries Research Station, Monkey Bay
summary: Fisheries research station in Mangochi whose head described biomass survey aims in November 2020, partnering with Restoring Fisheries for Sustainable Livelihoods in Lake Malawi.

name: Fruit Bats Conservation through Monitoring and Community Science in Mangochi District, Malawi
summary: Project that aims to start a community science programme monitoring fruit bat populations in Mangochi District, with roost inspections and surveys, and plans a genetic dietary analysis of guano.

name: GAF Geospatial GmbH
summary: Munich-based company that worked with Malawi's Department of Forestry in 2019 on a cloud-based forest monitoring project supported by the European Space Agency.

name: GBIF Malawi
summary: Country node for Malawi in GBIF, with associate participant status, which the registry lists as endorsing most of ten Malawian publishing organisations.

name: Habitat Ecology, Distribution and Mobilizing Community Conservation Strategies of Threatened "Mwanamphepo" Plants in Mulanje Mountain
summary: A project, described in July 2025, that plans forest inventories in Mulanje Mountain Forest Reserve to assess threatened Mwanamphepo plant populations and contribute to updating the National Plant Red Data List.

name: Kasungu elephant monitoring operation
summary: An active operation, run by DNPW and funded by IFAW, in which 20 elephants received new or replacement tracking collars in October 2026 alongside an aerial assessment.

name: Kasungu National Park drone monitoring
summary: Drone monitoring effort at Kasungu National Park reported in 2023, using DroneDeploy to protect elephants, with AI elephant counting reported as being tested; the report's firm name differs from The Nation's Tech265.

name: Last chance for survival for one of the least studied endemic reptiles of Malawi: Chapman's pygmy chameleon
