summary: A survey project, funded by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, that estimated population size using 400 square metre plots, recorded preferred vegetation and produced a Biodiversity Express Survey report.

name: Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources
summary: Active university in Lilongwe that received two JRS grants totalling $592,000, announced in April 2020, for biodiversity data portals and tools, and is the affiliation of the Nkhotakota classifier code's first creator.

name: Lilongwe Wildlife Trust
summary: Malawian NGO reporting biodiversity monitoring at Vwaza in 2017 and, in 2026, telemetry use, drone research and plans for eDNA in a pangolin survey.

name: Liwonde National Park trail camera monitoring network
summary: A trail camera project NatureSpy says is being launched in Liwonde's northern corridor, intended as a permanent network to document priority species, track individuals and show movement towards Mangochi Forest Reserve.

name: MajeteWatch
summary: Described by PixCams as an AI wildlife detection and survey system across Majete Wildlife Reserve, built and run by PixCams, using live video analysis, MegaDetector and BirdNET.

name: Malawi Clearing House Mechanism
summary: Reported in February 2024 as introduced by the Environmental Affairs Department under the CBD, this biodiversity portal aimed to fill a central platform gap; experts were adding data.

name: Malawi ecological condition maps
summary: An ecological condition map for Malawi, planned as an SBAPP output in May 2025, building on the national land cover map, with planned additions of fishing, water quality and invasive species data.

name: Malawi ecosystem types map
summary: A map of Malawi's ecosystem types built through SBAPP, cross-referenced with the IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology and ingested into the Global Ecosystems Atlas by the GEO team.

name: Malawi Fish Biodiversity Portal
summary: JRS announced in April 2020 that a JRS-funded project led by Emmanuel Kaunda would develop this portal, a mobile data collection app and mobilise thousands of fish records.

name: Malawi National Biodiversity Monitoring System
summary: Active system listed among the Environmental Affairs Department's e-services, tracking progress on the Global Biodiversity Framework, SDGs and NBSAP III with indicators, covering 2026 to 2030.

name: Malawi National Forest Inventory
summary: A Department of Forestry-led series of field forest inventories, with campaigns in 2011, 2012, 2016, 2018 and 2020 to 2023, whose 2018 sampling frame covered 22% of Malawi's land area.

name: Malawi National Forest Monitoring System
summary: Active programme, run by the Department of Forestry, that Malawi's 2024 forest reference level describes as still in development, using Collect Earth for historical deforestation data.

name: Malawi national land cover map (2025 update)
summary: An update of Malawi's national land cover map, whose then-current version dated from 2010, built by SBAPP with government partners using Google Earth Engine and under accuracy assessment in May 2025.

name: Malawi national wildlife crime database (Lilongwe Wildlife Trust)
summary: A national wildlife crime database that Lilongwe Wildlife Trust says it runs alongside a court monitoring programme.

name: Malawi Pollinators Biodiversity Portal
summary: JRS announced in April 2020 that this data portal for Malawian bee pollinators would be implemented and populated with crop-pollinator interaction data from 80 farms.

name: Malawi REDD+ National Forest Reference Level
summary: Malawi's REDD+ forest reference level, which in its interim 2019 form estimated 88,474 hectares deforested in 2006 to 2016 within a sampling frame covering 22% of the country, later expanded to all forests.

name: Malawi University of Science and Technology
summary: Malawi's fourth public university, established by Act of Parliament in 2012, which says it leads biodiversity informatics in Malawi and served as implementing agency for the UNBL-GBF Mapping Project.

name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Climate Change
summary: Malawian ministry that issued the Second National REDD+ Forest Reference Level in August 2024 and, per a September 2024 article, houses the Environmental Affairs Department.

name: Mobilizing endemic and economically useful species data for policy and protection
summary: A GBIF-funded project that plans to digitise specimen collections of pollinator and inland aquatic species and survey data from journals and reports.

name: Monitoring biodiversity of Vwaza Marsh Wildlife Reserve
summary: A Lilongwe Wildlife Trust-run monitoring effort in which citizen scientists supported research in September 2024 and 2025, with the combined report describing 14 camera traps on the main roads and six at animal activity sites.

name: Mount Mulanje Conservation Trust
summary: Conservation trust whose 2024 Save Our Cedar report says it set up permanent monitoring plots across the mountain to track seedling survival and gather soil, climate and vegetation data.

name: Mount Mulanje Restoration Project
summary: An active WeForest Malawi initiative centred on the Mount Mulanje Biosphere Reserve; its 2024 update reports 41 permanent monitoring plots and 231 patrols in two forest blocks.

name: National Commission for Science and Technology
summary: Malawian body that, by its GBIF publisher record, promotes and coordinates science, technology and innovation; the GBIF registry lists an Integrated Publishing Toolkit installation registered under it.

name: National Herbarium and Botanic Gardens of Malawi
summary: Parastatal botanical institution in Zomba, described in its GBIF record as the principal botanical authority; it holds over 90,000 plant specimens, being digitised in BRAHMS, and has 26 GBIF datasets.

name: Nkhotakota Camera Traps
summary: A dataset of annotated camera trap images published on LILA BC, from mammal monitoring in Nkhotakota Wildlife Reserve that uses computer vision models to process data.

name: Nyasa Aerial Data Solutions
summary: Company that, according to Halcyon, uses drones and GIS to map environmental issues in Malawi, including carbon quantification and degraded landscapes, and took part in its accelerator.

name: Nyika Vwaza (UK) Trust
summary: UK registered charity, number 1105105, supporting Nyika and Vwaza financially; its November 2025 call offered research grants of up to 5,000 pounds, including for baseline surveys and monitoring projects.

name: Nyika-Vwaza co-management
summary: Co-management arrangement for Nyika National Park and Vwaza Marsh Wildlife Reserve, reported by Peace Parks as a 20-year agreement dated 2023 or 15 July 2025, with a co-management trust being established.

name: Operational Cloud-Based Forest Monitoring System for Malawi
summary: Closed 2019 project, supported by the European Space Agency and built by GAF, that showed Department of Forestry staff dense Sentinel-2 time series for cloud-based forest monitoring, with in-country capacity building.

name: PixCams, Inc.
summary: Company whose website lists PixLink Starlink live streaming systems and the EZ Streamer-Pi encoder, and which is associated with the MajeteWatch platform at Majete Wildlife Reserve.

name: Post-release tracking of rehabilitated Temminck's pangolins in Malawi
summary: A Lilongwe Wildlife Trust study of rehabilitated Temminck's pangolins in Malawi, which in September 2022 reported satellite tags on 16 pangolins released since the previous year, with VHF tracking also used.

name: Restoring Fisheries for Sustainable Livelihoods in Lake Malawi
summary: USAID-funded Lake Malawi project, described by a November 2020 Nation article as building on the earlier FISH project and supporting a fisheries research unit's biomass survey; current status unknown.

name: Ruo River macroinvertebrate database
summary: A new database of Ruo River aquatic macroinvertebrates classified with SASS version 5, combined with measured flow and physicochemical parameters, which the abstract says informs the need for a locally calibrated biomonitoring index.

name: Tech265
summary: The Nation reported in June 2023 that this local firm would partner the wildlife department on drone monitoring; its founder said drones would carry high-resolution and thermal cameras.

name: UNBL-GBF Mapping Project in Malawi
summary: Closed project, run by the Environmental Affairs Department from the second quarter of 2024 to the fourth quarter of 2025, creating a central national data repository using the UNBL platform's ELSA tool.

name: Upgrade Biodiversity Importance Status of Dedza Forest Reserve Key Biodiversity Area in Malawi
summary: Closed project, funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund and run from June 2016 to February 2018, that aimed to make a baseline tree and orchid inventory and train scouts.

name: Upgrade Biodiversity Importance Status of Zomba Mountains Key Biodiversity Area in Malawi
summary: A closed project, funded by CEPF and granted to the National Herbarium and Botanic Gardens for June 2016 to June 2017, that set out to validate threatened and endemic species in the Zomba Mountains KBA by targeted surveys.

name: Wildlife Action Group
summary: Self-described Malawian conservation NGO protecting Thuma and Dedza-Salima Escarpment Forest Reserves, using ranger sightings, camera trapping and elephant collaring technology from Save the Elephants and Vulcan.

name: Wildlife and Environmental Society of Malawi
summary: BirdLife International's partner in Malawi, described as the oldest conservation NGO there, founded in 1947; it is digitising biodiversity data and has 18 datasets published through GBIF.

name: Agencia Espacial Mexicana
summary: Decentralised Mexican federal public body, listed by CEOS with the year 2015, which said in July 2016 it was strengthening national Earth observation capacity.

name: AI for Manatees
summary: Multi-sector alliance, built by C Minds, that aims to speed up manatee conservation in the Caribbean and Central and South America, and plans AI analysis of underwater vocalisation recordings.

name: Alianza Minga Jaguar
summary: Programme launched at COP16 in 2024 across six countries to share governance and monitoring for jaguar corridors, whose first meeting in 2025 aimed to align protocols and promote AI adoption.

name: Alianza Nacional para la Conservación del Jaguar
summary: Non-profit civil association that runs Mexico's national jaguar census, which it reports showed growth from 4,000 jaguars in 2010 to 5,300 in 2024.

name: Amigos de Calakmul
summary: Organisation which Global Conservation says deployed wildlife camera networks with FundaEco to estimate predator and prey populations and has a community forestry REDD+ project around Calakmul.

name: Amigos de Sian Ka'an
summary: Organisation that lists permanent, systematic study of the health of 600 km of coastal reef as a goal.

name: Biblioteca de Sonidos de las Aves de México
summary: Sound library formally founded in 1994 to document and preserve the vocalisations of Mexican birds.

name: BioChavez Forester
summary: Organisation developing software tools for monitoring wildlife and forests, including BP Channel, an AI engine that identifies fauna by sound and is in pilot testing.

name: BIOCOM
summary: Community biodiversity programme that brings together information from camera traps and monitoring of birds, bats and insects.

name: Bioconciencia
summary: Non-governmental organisation created in 2005 to conserve biological diversity in Mexico, whose jaguar programme researches populations in southern Mexico through community monitoring.

name: Biodiversity Information System of Mexico
summary: Programme listed by GBIF as the voting country node for Mexico, and linked as a partner of GBIF.

name: BioScanner
summary: AI platform built by Tech4Nature México, still under development and in early access, which classifies species and identifies jaguars in camera-trap images, with 333,087 photos and videos analysed by October 2026.

name: Bosque Nuboso AC
summary: Organisation that helps communities obtain camera traps, GPS and binoculars for biodiversity monitoring and carries out early detection of forest pests and diseases.

name: C Minds
summary: Action tank, founded in 2011 according to IUCN's Mexican committee, that says it develops AI policies and ethical frameworks, and leads Tech4Nature México and NaturaTech LAC.

name: Canal-IA
summary: Project built by Tecnológico de Monterrey in which students trained a computer vision camera to identify a monarch butterfly.

name: Causa Natura
summary: Non-profit centre for applied research and data analysis for sustainable development, which Global Fishing Watch says began operations in 2014 and which leads the illegal fishing risk predictor for Mexico.

name: CDFAI
summary: Organisation in Durango, Mexico that develops five-year plans using LiDAR drones, IoT sensors on trees and predictive growth algorithms.

name: Censo Nacional del Jaguar
summary: Closed national jaguar census, led by Gerardo Ceballos and run by the Alianza Nacional para la Conservación del Jaguar, using 920 camera traps over 90 days in 2024 and reported to show 5,326 jaguars.

name: Centinelas del Agua
summary: Organisation that identifies species in cenotes using photomapping, field inspection and photography, and monitors nutrients, heavy metals and other parameters there.

name: Centro de Investigación Científica y de Educación Superior de Ensenada
summary: Research centre whose two groups collaborated on drones and AI models to identify and follow whale sharks, using DeepLabCut and a second model.

name: Centro de Investigación en Ciencias de Información Geoespacial
summary: Research centre with a project to detect mistletoe from the air using multispectral drones and AI.

name: Centro de Investigación en Matemáticas
summary: Research centre whose algorithms, according to the University of Guanajuato, are used to process CONABIO's satellite images, and which partners with CONABIO.

name: Centro del Cambio Global y la Sustentabilidad
summary: Organisation in Villahermosa whose geospatial laboratory processes satellite imagery and field measurements, and which GBIF says manages biodiversity information from long-term ecological monitoring and species records.

name: Centro Ecológico Akumal
summary: Organisation created in 1993 to promote environmental initiatives for Akumal's marine and coastal environment, with reef and juvenile turtle monitoring listed on its site.

name: CICESE whale shark AI monitoring
summary: Project of unknown status, built by the Ensenada research centre CICESE, in which drone images were used to train AI models for automatic detection.

name: Cielito Drone
summary: Organisation of unknown status that sUAS News reported in 2023 flew DJI equipment within the core zone of the Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve.

name: Comisión Estatal de Parques Naturales y de la Fauna
summary: A State of Mexico body whose stated aim, according to a 2026 news report on its recognition by the state government, is conserving protected natural areas and administering parks and spaces for environmental education.

name: Comisión Nacional de Acuacultura y Pesca
summary: Commission with a satellite monitoring centre for fishing vessels, whose vessel monitoring data Oceana Mexico says it got the commission to publish.

name: Comisión Nacional de Áreas Naturales Protegidas
summary: Federal body within SEMARNAT, begun in 2000, that administers 232 protected natural areas, builds the Visor de Fauna, and had 500 camera traps in December 2022.

name: Comisión Nacional del Agua
summary: Water commission that carries out systematic and permanent water quality monitoring.

name: Comisión Nacional Forestal
summary: Forestry commission, based in Zapopan, that developed and runs the Satellite Forest Monitoring System and makes the National Forest Monitoring System available.

name: Comisión Nacional para el Conocimiento y Uso de la Biodiversidad
summary: Inter-ministerial commission created in 1992 that runs the National Biodiversity Information System, receives MODIS, VIIRS and AVHRR imagery, and is the focal point for Mexico's Global Biodiversity Framework process.

name: Comité de Recursos Naturales de la Chinantla Alta, A.C.
summary: A 2023 report says six communities formed the committee in 2004, each voluntarily conserving an average of 80 percent of its land in a connected corridor exceeding 26,000 ha.

name: Comunidad de Capulálpam de Méndez
summary: A community which, according to a 2020 report, keeps 24 percent of its territory (918 ha) for conservation, like a protected natural area, with well-preserved cloud forest.

name: Comunidad de Santa María Zoquitlán
summary: A community which, a July 2026 report says, formalised the safeguarding of almost 26,000 ha as the ADVC La Natividad for 15 years.

name: Comunidad Indígena de Cherán
summary: An Indigenous community which, a 2022 report says, has 16,684 ha of forest land and is organised to look after the forest.

name: Comunidad y Biodiversidad
summary: Founded in 1999, this Mexican civil society organisation trains fishers in underwater monitoring and builds PescaData; Fundación Carlos Slim reports monitoring at 90 Yucatán coastal sites.

name: Conexiones Terramar
summary: Non-profit organisation based in La Paz, Baja California Sur.

name: Consejo Civil Mexicano para la Silvicultura Sostenible
summary: Civil council that makes the SICAMFOR tool available to the public and to community organisations in particular.

name: Conservación de Anfibios A.C.
summary: A civil association which World Land Trust says it would fund to buy an initial 8 ha plot for a cloud forest amphibian sanctuary in Puebla, and for which it funded two local rangers.

name: Conservación de la Biodiversidad en la Sierra Madre Oriental y el Golfo de México
summary: Active project funded by the German government through KfW, at whose 7–9 May 2025 exchange ecosystem monitoring protocols were applied and camera-trap monitoring techniques were described.

name: Conservación Internacional México
summary: Mexican organisation that says it has worked for 30 years protecting places providing water and food, and started the Paisajes Sostenibles Oaxaca-Chiapas project in 2016 with a CONANP regional directorate.

name: Costasalvaje
summary: An organisation whose Tierras Silvestres on the Pacific coast of the Valle de los Cirios were, by its 2016 account, certified by CONANP as 13,346.907 ha of voluntarily conserved areas, with camera traps begun.

name: Cubo de Datos Geoespaciales de México
summary: Programme of unknown status whose platform gives access to, and processes and analyses, large volumes of satellite images.

name: Cuenca Los Ojos
summary: An organisation which, its about page says, has protected and continues to steward over 130,000 acres of wetlands, desert grasslands and woodlands.

name: Deep Bug
summary: Project of unknown status, built by the Instituto Politécnico Nacional, that uses AI to assess water quality by identifying aquatic macroinvertebrates.

name: Detection of manatee vocalisations using the Audio Spectrogram Transformer
summary: A paper proposing an end-to-end approach to detecting manatee vocalisations, built on the Audio Spectrogram Transformer, with a link naming Stefano Schiappacasse as its builder.

name: Dirección Regional Centro y Eje Neovolcánico
summary: A CONANP regional directorate which, according to the agency's July 2025 page, is made up of 42 protected natural areas.

name: Dirección Regional Frontera Sur, Istmo y Pacífico Sur
summary: A CONANP regional directorate which, according to the agency's July 2025 page, is made up of 37 protected natural areas.

name: Dirección Regional Noreste y Sierra Madre Oriental
summary: A CONANP regional directorate which, according to the agency's December 2025 page, is made up of 19 protected natural areas.

name: Dirección Regional Noroeste y Alto Golfo de California
summary: A CONANP regional directorate whose 2022 organisation manual places its seat in Hermosillo, Sonora, and gives it powers over protected natural areas across several states.

name: Dirección Regional Norte y Sierra Madre Occidental
summary: A CONANP regional directorate which, according to the agency's July 2025 page, is made up of 13 protected natural areas.

name: Dirección Regional Occidente y Pacífico Centro
summary: A CONANP regional directorate which, according to the agency's July 2025 page, is made up of 34 protected natural areas.

name: Dirección Regional Península de Baja California y Pacífico Norte
summary: This CONANP regional directorate covers a region that, according to the agency's July 2025 page, is made up of 22 protected natural areas.

name: Dirección Regional Península de Yucatán y Caribe Mexicano
summary: A CONANP regional directorate which, according to the agency's July 2025 page, is made up of 39 protected natural areas.

name: Dirección Regional Planicie Costera y Golfo de México
summary: A CONANP regional directorate which, according to the agency's July 2025 page, is made up of 20 protected natural areas.

name: Ducks Unlimited de México
summary: A Mexican wetland conservation organisation whose work, Ducks Unlimited reported in 2024, had resulted in more than 2.1 million acres of wetlands, including mangroves, being conserved since 1974.

name: Efecto Arena
summary: A coral restoration organisation which, a 2024 report says, has planted almost 10,000 hard coral colonies in the Mexican Pacific and has over 6,000 more growing in underwater nurseries.

name: Ejido Agua de los Pescados
summary: An ejido whose residents, a 2022 report says, have conserved 599 ha of pine and fir forest for almost 70 years.

name: Ejido Cinco de Febrero
summary: An ejido in Champotón, Campeche, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with a 16,000 ha voluntarily conserved area certified in 2024.

name: Ejido Cordón Grande
summary: An ejido which, a 2022 report says, voted to create a voluntarily conserved area, with CONANP to deliver certification for just over 8,573 ha of its forest.

name: Ejido Costa de San Juan
summary: An ejido whose residents, a 2022 report says, restored more than 350 ha of mangrove in the Alvarado lagoon system, Veracruz.

name: Ejido Crucero de San Luis
summary: An ejido in Hopelchén, Campeche, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with a 1,959 ha area certified in 2023.

name: Ejido El Bajío
summary: An ejido in Caborca, Sonora, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with a 2,460 ha area certified in 2023.

name: Ejido General Heriberto Jara
summary: An ejido in Calakmul, Campeche, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with 1,995.55 ha certified in 2022.

name: Ejido Kilómetro 120
summary: An ejido in Calakmul, Campeche, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with 9,113 ha certified in 2017.

name: Ejido La Nueva Vida
summary: An ejido in Calakmul, Campeche, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with 2,388 ha certified in 2022.

name: Ejido Mocontún
summary: An ejido in Tekax, Yucatán, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with 1,500 ha certified in 2025.

name: Ejido Nuevo Bécal
summary: A 2022 report says that 99 percent of the ejido is registered as the largest voluntary conservation area in Mexico.

name: Ejido Panalachi
summary: An ejido in Bocoyna, Chihuahua, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with 4,100 ha certified in 2021.

name: Ejido Pixoyal
summary: An ejido in Champotón, Campeche, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with 10,000 ha certified in 2024.

name: Ejido Puebla de Morelia
summary: An ejido in Calakmul, Campeche, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with 1,696 ha certified in 2017.

name: Ejido San Agustín
summary: An ejido in Tekax, Yucatán, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with 5,633 ha certified in 2024.

name: Ejido San Ignacio de Arareco
summary: An ejido in Bocoyna, Chihuahua, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with 3,918 ha certified in 2021.

name: Ejido Úrsulo Galván
summary: An ejido that, according to a 2022 report, had planted and restored 550 ha of mangroves in its plots and lagoons, mostly red mangrove.

name: El Colegio de la Frontera Sur
summary: Describes itself as a public research centre supporting sustainable development in southern border regions of Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean, and builds the GOTA-Tabasco dashboard.

name: Enabling digital solutions for deforestation-free commodities from smallholders
summary: Project run by Oroverde that supports Mexican small-scale coffee and cocoa producers' cooperatives with capacity building and a digital tool, funded by the International Climate Initiative.

name: EncicloVida
summary: Programme created in 2016, run and built by CONABIO on the national biodiversity information system, gathering specimen records from scientific collections and citizen science platforms.

name: ERISNET
summary: Model that ECOSUR calls the first sargassum detection system based on AI and satellite technology, built by El Colegio de la Frontera Sur; its status is unknown.

name: ESA GDA Forest Management support to Mexico's national forest monitoring
summary: Run by the European Space Agency, this active project supports World Bank work on Mexican national forest monitoring and produced 10 m tree cover density data from Sentinel-2.

name: Estación Científica Las Joyas
summary: Research station established on 31 May 1985 in the Sierra de Manantlán Biosphere Reserve, covering 1,245 hectares, with a June 2024 report listing camera-trap monitoring of wild cats and fire effects.

name: Fomento del Monitoreo de Biodiversidad y Cambio Climático en la Selva Maya
summary: Closed project that received 6 million euros from the German environment ministry and ended with an event on 25 November 2021.

name: Fondo de Agua Metropolitano de Monterrey
summary: A water fund that, with Heineken, has worked 1,779 ha of the Río San Juan basin on forest restoration, native reforestation and erosion works, according to a 2026 Expansión report.

name: Fondo Mexicano para la Conservación de la Naturaleza
summary: Private nonprofit founded in 1994 in Mexico City that channels funds to protect biodiversity; it builds InfOceanos and ran a marine and coastal monitoring project that closed in 2023.

name: Fondo Noroeste y Occidente
summary: Organisation founded to support conservation projects in north-west Mexico, which trained community monitoring brigades to identify jaguars recorded by camera trap, and partners with the Fondo Mexicano.

name: Fundación Carlos Slim
summary: Foundation that said in February 2021 it had created an alliance with WWF in six priority regions of Mexico, and joined CONABIO in supporting the spread of NaturaLista.

name: Fundación Claudia y Roberto Hernández
summary: Organisation that collaborates in the Maya Aquifer Alliance.

name: Fundación Ecológica de Cuixmala
summary: A foundation whose own page says its conservation work covers administration of the biosphere reserve, including monitoring, surveillance and restoration, and which uses motion-activated cameras to track animals.

name: GeoAltia
summary: Organisation that says its headquarters are in Mexico and offers satellite proof of no deforestation after 31 December 2020, plot polygons, and forest carbon baselines and monitoring.

name: Geoportal de CONABIO
summary: Dataset run by CONABIO, listed with 15,845 themes and described in the C Minds toolkit as layers on Mexico's biodiversity.

name: Global Park Defense, Baja California Sur
summary: Active project run by Global Conservation covering over 250,000 hectares on Baja California Sur's east coast, upgrading the Loreto National Park command centre and using EarthRanger and Skylight.

name: Global Park Defense, Islas Marías
summary: Active project in which Global Conservation reported in July 2025 deploying its first Marine Monitor in the archipelago, with support from CONANP, the Navy and Pronatura Noroeste.

name: Gobierno de Michoacán
summary: Organisation that Mongabay Latam reports funded the Guardián Forestal initiative.

name: GOTA-Tabasco
summary: Built by ECOSUR and two researchers, this open dashboard shows daily levels for 14 rivers; its October 2026 page reports flow estimates at two stations and disclaims official alerts.

name: Green Tech Innovation
summary: Company whose GTI Satélites platform uses AI to classify hotspots and wildfires, and which says it was among the top 28 of over 400 teams in the XPRIZE Wildfire semifinals.

name: Grupo de Ecología y Conservación de Islas
summary: Civil association working to restore and protect biodiversity on Mexico's islands, with a data science team developing studies and support applications, and a partner of the Motus Network North-West Mexico.

name: Grupo de Monitoreo Chac Mool
summary: Formed by community leaders of the Dzilam State Reserve, this group co-leads Tech4Nature México.

name: Grupo Ecológico Sierra Gorda
summary: World Land Trust says the group’s reserve network covers 7,487 ha of forest within the Sierra Gorda Biosphere Reserve and that it funds land purchases to expand the network.

name: GTI Satelites
summary: Describes itself as a Mexican startup for predicting, detecting and fighting forest fires with drones and AI.

name: Guardianes de los Manglares Dzinintún
summary: A cooperative in Celestún that, according to a 2025 report, is among those responsible for preserving local mangroves since 2014, with a restoration guide crediting its formation for sustained conservation work.

name: Guardián Forestal
summary: Built by Agriicola and funded by Gobierno de Michoacán, this programme uses satellite monitoring and AI alerts, according to Mongabay Latam.

name: Gulf of California rocky reef monitoring
summary: A rocky reef monitoring project built by Scripps Institution of Oceanography, where Celsius Media reports machine learning models will analyse expedition footage to recognise species and measure population changes once the team has trained the algorithms.

name: IBdata
summary: A web system, built and run by the Unidad de Informática para la Biodiversidad, for viewing records of the Instituto de Biología (UNAM) national collections, giving access to more than 1.7 million specimens, mainly from Mexico.

name: Illegal fishing risk predictor, Mexico
summary: A planned predictor of illegal fishing hot spots, announced in November 2020 and led by Causa Natura, starting with a Loreto Bay pilot using CONANP-identified illegal small-scale fishing events; its current status is unknown.

name: Infraestructura de Datos Espaciales de la Península de Yucatán
summary: A spatial data infrastructure built by Pronatura Península de Yucatán, bringing together data from more than 25 years of its research and work so it can share conservation information with decision makers, NGOs and research institutions.

name: Instituto de Biología, UNAM
summary: UNAM institute founded in 1929, with five staff units including two field stations, which holds Mexico's national biological collections; IBdata gives access to over 1.7 million specimens.

name: Instituto de Ecología, A.C.
summary: A public research centre in Xalapa, Veracruz, linked to CONABIO's ecosystem integrity indicator, the Mexican Tree Assessment (2019 to 2021), and machine learning work in its inteGralidad GAMMA initiative.

name: Instituto Nacional de Astrofísica, Óptica y Electrónica
summary: A Mexican institute that is developing an instrument to map land and sea temperature across Mexican territory.

name: Instituto Nacional de Ecología y Cambio Climático
summary: A Mexican state research body working on ecology and climate change.

name: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía
summary: The Mexican body in charge of national mapping and environmental monitoring, which sets statistical and geographic rules and produces the official vegetation cartography that CONAFOR says it has used to monitor forest loss.

name: Instituto Nacional de Investigaciones Forestales, Agrícolas y Pecuarias
summary: A Mexican research institute that describes training a YOLO model to detect crowns of dead and stressed trees in RGB drone images, saying AI with drones speeds forest health analysis.

name: Instituto para el Manejo y Conservación de la Biodiversidad A.C.
summary: An organisation that Rainforest Trust says had an agreement with three ejidos to start work on a proposed 19,768-acre Técpan mountains conservation area, listed as protected in 2022.

name: Instituto Politécnico Nacional
summary: A Mexican higher education institution whose computing school students developed Deep Bug.

name: Jaguardianes
summary: A community monitoring project in Marqués de Comillas in which, Mongabay Latam reported in September 2025, 25 people from nine ejidos took part and about 100,000 camera-trap records were gathered.

name: Kaxil Kiuic Biocultural Reserve
summary: A reserve that a grants page says holds more than 4,000 acres of dry tropical forest and works on education, research and communities.

name: Laboratorio de Bioacústica y Ecología del Comportamiento
summary: A laboratory at CIIDIR Oaxaca, Instituto Politécnico Nacional, whose main research lines include conservation biology and passive acoustic monitoring.

name: Laboratorio de Ciencia de Datos UNCA
summary: A data science laboratory presenting a deep learning approach to recognise Neobuxbaumia tetetzo in aerial images from the Tehuacán-Cuicatlán Valley, with later extension to other species aimed for.

name: Laboratorio Nacional de Análisis y Síntesis Ecológica
summary: A Morelia-based national laboratory created in 2015 under the CONACyT programme to analyse ecological information on genetic resources, offering metabarcoding libraries and a computing cluster for biological databases.

name: Laboratorio Nacional de Análisis, Monitoreo e Investigación sobre Ficotoxinas asociadas a Florecimientos Algales Nocivos
summary: Brings together laboratories specialising in toxins from harmful algal blooms, with CICESE accredited as its lead institution in the 2023 national laboratory recognition call.

name: Laboratorio Nacional de la Biodiversidad
summary: National laboratory created in 2014 at UNAM's Instituto de Biología, run by it, with a genomic sequencing laboratory and users from more than 35 university bodies, agencies and NGOs.

name: Laboratorio Nacional de Observación de la Tierra
summary: Active since 28 March 2017 at UNAM’s Institute of Geography, this laboratory aims to process and distribute remote sensing data and monitors fires, identifying smoke plumes using AI.

name: Las Chelemeras
summary: A group that, according to a 2025 report, began restoring 110 ha of a Yucatán coastal wetland reserve in 2015 after a road interchange damaged it.

name: MAD-Mex
summary: CONABIO's land cover monitoring system, built with Steffen Gebhardt, which used decision tree classification of satellite data for Mexico's 2015 land-cover map and reached overall accuracies of up to 76% in a 2014 paper.

name: MapBiomas México
summary: A land cover and land use mapping programme that the C Minds toolkit lists for checking changes by year, with free access.

name: MARACC
summary: A programme whose deforestation trends page presents an application developed under UK PACT-Mexico to analyse deforestation and land-use change in Chiapas areas covered by federal agricultural, livestock and forestry programmes.

name: Marine-Coastal Information and Analysis System
summary: A CONABIO system, built and run by it, that brings together satellite and in situ data, models, early-warning systems and citizen science, and includes the SATsum sargassum warning system.

name: Maya Aquifer Alliance
summary: An active programme, partnered with Fundación Claudia y Roberto Hernández, that aims to generate scientific knowledge of the aquifer, including monitoring of water quality.

name: Motus network in north-west Mexico
summary: A Pronatura Noroeste project using Motus tracking, which announced plans in October 2020 for Mexico's first Motus station network and reported 19 stations in 15 priority wetlands by December 2022.

name: Museo de la Ballena y Ciencias del Mar
summary: An organisation named only as the affiliation printed for Valeria Alonso Towns in the vaquita eDNA pilot report.

name: Natura Mexicana
summary: An organisation that says it focuses on saving the Selva Lacandona, monitoring forest cover changes and indicator and endangered species, including mammals through camera traps and community monitors.

name: Naturaleza y Cultura Sierra Madre
summary: An organisation that World Land Trust reports worked to create the Reserva Monte Mojino by buying properties along the Cuchujaqui river to protect dry forest and watershed.

name: Naturalia Comité para la Conservación de Especies Silvestres
summary: A committee that World Land Trust says it was supporting to buy two properties of nearly 4,000 acres to expand Reserva Jaguar del Norte, where Naturalia then owned 3,706 acres.

name: NaturaLista
summary: A CONABIO-built and run platform, partnered with the Carlos Slim Foundation and iNaturalist, that identifies images automatically for curator review and reached 5 million observations in Mexico by 9 March 2023.

name: NaturaTech LAC
summary: A programme launched by IDB Lab, led by C Minds and funded by Climate Collective, whose Studio reports 18 incubated projects and solutions present in six countries.

name: Neovolcanic Axis Conservation Fund
summary: A regional institution in central Mexico, created in 2018 to support the Fondo Monarca, that raises funds for protected areas and in 2023 was reported partnering on drone forestry data collection.

name: Neuraan
summary: An organisation selling AI agents coordinating operations outside the office, with which BioScanner models were worked on, according to the Tech4Nature México team page.

name: Niparajá
summary: An active organisation funded by the David and Lucile Packard Foundation, whose yearly underwater monitoring collects data from 63 sites.

name: Nuevo Centro de Población Ejidal Centauro del Norte
summary: An ejido settlement in Calakmul, Campeche, listed in CONANP's October 2025 register with 9,722.75 ha certified in 2017.

name: Observatorio de la Selva Maya
summary: A network of NGOs, governments and research bodies formed to generate, analyse and share information on deforestation and degradation emissions.

name: Orcas Mexico
summary: An active project, run by Conexiones Terramar, whose stated mission is to monitor orca population, diet, behaviour and health in the Gulf of California.

name: Organismo Público Descentralizado Bosque La Primavera
summary: A public body whose founding law gives it its own legal personality and assets and charges it with administering La Primavera flora and fauna protection area, under management responsibilities CONANP granted to Jalisco.

name: Paisajes Sostenibles Oaxaca-Chiapas
summary: Closed project, announced as finished by CONANP in December 2024, that worked in nine protected areas, updating monitoring protocols and camera-trap use and training community brigades to analyse results.

name: PescaData
summary: A free iOS and Android app for small-scale fishers to record catches and share data, built by Comunidad y Biodiversidad, which reports 2,915 active users and over 1,047 people trained since 2020.

name: Pilot Project to Test Viability of Detecting Vaquita Porpoise Presence through Environmental DNA
summary: A closed pilot project that set out to design a sampling method to test whether eDNA can identify vaquita presence, and whose report says it was detected at 5 of 10 sampled sites.

name: Planet Satellite Image Catalog
summary: A satellite image catalogue covering Chiapas, Central America and the Caribbean, which a conference abstract says UIFS-CIMSUR-UNAM developed, using Planet Labs imagery.

name: Procuraduría Federal de Protección al Ambiente
summary: A Mexican environmental enforcement body that, in June 2016, described a national programme against illegal logging and reported identifying 108 critical forest zones for prioritisation.

name: Profauna A.C.
summary: Runs the Correo Real programme, which Excélsior reported on 6 October 2026 had confirmed monarch butterflies arriving in Coahuila.

name: Programa Correo Real
summary: Programme run by Profauna that, according to Excélsior, detected monarch records through Project Monarch using ultralight solar Bluetooth transmitters.

name: Programa de Monitoreo Biológico en Áreas Naturales Protegidas
summary: A CONANP programme, run without interruption from 2011 to 2015, in which universities, research institutions and civil society groups monitored species of conservation interest in federal protected areas; readers are directed to PROMANP from 2016.

name: Pronatura Noreste
summary: Rainforest Trust says it worked with the organisation on Monarch Corridor (1,372,671 target acres) and threatened-species habitat (3,632 target acres) projects, listed as protected in 2022 and 2024 respectively.

name: Pronatura Noroeste
summary: Established in 1991 within Pronatura, with its main office in Ensenada, it reported technology use in 16 protected areas in December 2022 and uses Motus.

name: Pronatura Península de Yucatán
summary: Regional chapter of Pronatura begun in 1987 that has used camera traps for mammals since 2004, developed a spatial data infrastructure for the peninsula, and partners with Tech4Nature Mexico.

name: Pronatura Sur
summary: A thesis describes bird monitoring by Chiapas farmers; it has a Biodiversity and Landscapes Monitoring Programme and partners with Enabling digital solutions for deforestation-free commodities from smallholders.

name: Red de Observadores Ciudadanos
summary: Citizen environmental observatory in the Bay of La Paz and Gulf of California that reports 207 surveillance patrols in 2025 and partners with Waterkeeper Alliance and EarthRanger.

name: Red Mexicana de Investigación Ecológica a Largo Plazo
summary: Mexican long-term ecological research network created in 2004, which a 2017 review says included 11 sites, and which took part in a June 2025 meeting of monitoring networks at UNAM.

name: Red Nacional de Medición de Calidad del Agua
summary: Programme run by the Comisión Nacional del Agua that measures physico-chemical and microbiological water quality parameters.

name: Red Nacional de Monitoreo de Mariposa Monarca
summary: Initiative of unknown current status, run by CONANP and coordinated with other government institutions, academia and civil society.

name: Reserva de la Biosfera Bahía de los Ángeles, Canales de Ballenas y de Salsipuedes
summary: A biosphere reserve managed with two other protected areas under one directorate, whose page describes sentinel species monitoring and which promotes community sea turtle monitoring.

name: Reserva de la Biosfera El Pinacate y Gran Desierto de Altar
summary: Sonoran biosphere reserve whose monitoring area records species including Sonoran pronghorn, bighorn sheep, bats and desert pupfish, uses camera-trap photo stations, and presents results yearly in a public forum.

name: SATsum-Collect
summary: Run and built by CONABIO with development collaborators including Havana’s CIM, UNAM’s Institute of Marine Sciences and Limnology, and FIU, it records sargassum observations with photos and videos.

name: Secretaría de Ciencia, Humanidades, Tecnología e Innovación
summary: Mexican government body that says national laboratories may receive funding through calls and special projects, and includes a forest ecosystems axis in its 2026 research call.

name: Secretaría de Desarrollo Sustentable de Yucatán
summary: Co-led the Tech4Nature México project from design through field work.

name: Secretaría de Marina
summary: Sea Shepherd reports it conducted 2025 vaquita monitoring projects with SEMARNAT, CONANP and Sea Shepherd; LANOT says it used GOES-13 imagery before December 2017.

name: Secretaría de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales
summary: Federal environment ministry in Mexico City that advertised a 2026 post to lead deep and machine learning work on field sensor data and held the 2025 start-up workshop for the seventh national report to the CBD.

name: Secretaría del Medio Ambiente de la Ciudad de México
summary: A city environment secretariat that, according to a 2024 La Crónica article, administered 15 of Mexico City's 25 decreed protected areas, with CONANP administering the other 10.

name: Secretaría Ejecutiva de la Reserva Ecológica del Pedregal de San Ángel
summary: Executive office of a UNAM ecological reserve; a 2019 Gaceta report said the university protected 237 ha of the reserve, and a 2023 report named Silke Cram Heydrich as executive secretary.

name: Servicios Digitales Para la Pesca Sostenible
summary: Organisation that received the PescaData technology from COBI in 2023.

name: SICAMFOR
summary: Programme run and built by the Consejo Civil Mexicano para la Silvicultura Sostenible, using Collect Earth Online and Google Earth Engine to quantify forest cover and change in the Yucatán Peninsula.

name: Sistema de Alerta Temprana de Incendios
summary: Fire early warning programme built by CONABIO, which lists it among the systems it has developed, with fire detection from AVHRR and MODIS imagery in its monitoring history.

name: Sistema de Gestión de la Información de Biodiversidad
summary: A digital platform built by CONAFOR and the US Forest Service with USAID support, where ejidos and communities must register to store and consult confidential BIOCOMUNI biodiversity monitoring data.

name: Sistema de Información, Monitoreo y Evaluación para la Conservación
summary: A CONANP information system, whose design began in 2002, whose monitoring subsystem publishes technical sheets on emblematic species in protected areas and protocols for monitoring 11 ecosystems that predominate in them.

name: Sistema de Monitoreo de Biodiversidad y Degradación
summary: Digital portal on Mexico's terrestrial ecosystems, built by CONANP, CONABIO and CONAFOR, giving access to biodiversity information and allowing annual statistics on biological resources and ecosystem services.

name: Sistema de Monitoreo Satelital de Embarcaciones Pesqueras
summary: A programme run by the Comisión Nacional de Acuacultura y Pesca that monitors fishing vessels' position, speed, course and route traceability.

name: Sistema de Sitios Permanentes de Calibración y Monitoreo
summary: Monitoring system of unknown current status, named in a vacancy as part of a national bioacoustic defaunation and flora network, and whose design CONABIO says CoSMoS protocols are based on.

name: Sistema Inteligente de Monitoreo del Muérdago
summary: A project, with unknown status, that monitors mistletoe using drones, geospatial analysis and open science.

name: Sistema Nacional de Información sobre Biodiversidad
summary: A dataset on the biological diversity of Mexico, run and built by CONABIO, which began with scientific collections of plants and animals and offers specimen records and taxonomic catalogues as CSV downloads.

name: Sistema Nacional de Monitoreo Forestal
summary: A programme whose components include the national forest and soil inventory, SAMOF and the national monitoring, reporting and verification system.

name: Sistema Satelital de Monitoreo Forestal
summary: A programme built by CONAFOR that produces maps and information on forest cover and its changes, with a 2021 technical note setting out its methods for estimating Mexico's deforestation rate.

name: Tecnológico de Monterrey
summary: An organisation whose students at the Estado de México campus developed Canal-IA.

name: Telenax
summary: Maker of project-specific wildlife telemetry equipment using VHF, GPS, Bluetooth and Iridium satellite links, which says it has specialised in this since 2005 and reports 1,000 or more projects in 80 or more countries.

name: Terra Peninsular
summary: An organisation founded in 2001 to protect the natural heritage of its region, which carries out biological monitoring in protected areas, has an office in Ensenada, and partners with the Motus network in north-west Mexico.

name: Toroto
summary: A Mexican company that Google lists among startups in its AI for Nature accelerator cohort, describing its work on nature-based solutions through carbon, water, biodiversity and communities.

name: UIFS-CIMSUR-UNAM
summary: Organisation named in a source about the Planet Satellite Image Catalog.

name: UniCiencias
summary: A programme run by the Facultad de Ciencias, UNAM, that holds specimen records of the Museo de Zoología Alfonso L. Herrera mammal collection and gives open access to collection databases, with written permission requested for publications.

name: Unidad de Informática para la Biodiversidad
summary: An organisation run by the Instituto de Biología, UNAM, that documents and gives access to specimen information from the institute's biological collections.

name: Universidad Autónoma de Baja California Sur
summary: A university that a 2020 project announcement named among the organisations participating in the planned Motus monitoring network in north-west Mexico.

name: Universidad de la Cañada
summary: University whose data science laboratory presents a deep learning approach to recognise Neobuxbaumia tetetzo in aerial images of the Tehuacán-Cuicatlán Valley, and lists a 2025 paper on classifying columnar cacti.

name: Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México
summary: A university whose Institute of Geography is the headquarters of the National Earth Observation Laboratory.

name: Universidad Politécnica de Yucatán
summary: A university partnering with Tech4Nature Mexico, which developed the first image recognition models with the project and trained students in data engineering and embedded systems.

name: Unión de Comunidades Productoras Forestales Zapoteco-Chinanteca
summary: The union’s technical deputy director said in 2020 that its four Sierra Juárez communities balanced timber production with conservation, set aside 14,000 ha and monitored forests using camera traps.

name: Vaquita acoustic and visual monitoring 2025
summary: A closed project run by SEMARNAT, the Secretaría de Marina, CONANP and Sea Shepherd, which ran from May to September 2025 in the Upper Gulf of California and recorded 254 acoustic encounters using 1,228 detectors across 497 sites.

name: Vaquita Survey
summary: A closed project whose 2024 summary reports 9 sightings and 70 acoustic encounters, with detectors deployed at 34 sampling sites in the Zero Tolerance Area in the May 2024 survey.

name: VERA-MX
summary: An active interactive tool covering 757 hydrological basins, showing current and potential environmental water reserves and basins with an ecological flow deficit, based on a 2024 paper according to its viewer.

name: Visor de fauna en las ANP
summary: Dataset of images and videos from protected natural areas, shared by CONANP, the national protected areas commission, which runs it.

name: Visor de Fauna en las Áreas Naturales Protegidas
summary: Image and video platform for protected areas, including camera-trap images, built by the national protected areas commission, which held material on 337 species at its 2022 launch.

name: Vital Oceans
summary: Project built by C-Minds that lets users identify, visualise and analyse potential marine protected areas through an interactive map.

name: Wild Felids Conservation México
summary: Conservation organisation whose director, Fernando Ruíz Gutiérrez, was on the Guerrero Jaguar team; a 2022 report says camera-trap surveys began in 2013, documenting 14 jaguars in three ejidos, and a 32,000 ha community corridor was created.

name: WWF México
summary: Organisation that says it uses AI for local mangrove carbon models and aims to automate aquatic fauna identification, and which began monarch colony monitoring in 2004 and runs Manglaria.

name: Academy of Sciences Malaysia
summary: Formed a biodiversity technology interest group in 2019, organised an October 2025 Precision Biodiversity pilot workshop and says it aims to be at the forefront of this technology.

name: Active Forest Asset Management
summary: Programme built and run by Planters International, which says it integrates AI, drones, LiDAR, IoT and geospatial technologies and uses AI for predictive analysis.

name: ALJ Global Sdn Bhd
summary: Seremban-based company that calls itself Malaysia's regional partner for Deep Forestry and says cloud AI derives per-tree height, diameter, volume, species and health.

name: Alphaswift
summary: Malaysian drone manufacturing company, described by Leave a Nest as a project partner, and linked as a partner of the LVNS forest project in Malaysia.

name: Artificial Intelligence for River 3S
summary: Project partnering Universiti Kuala Lumpur and the National Water Research Institute Malaysia, combining AI, deep learning and satellite data for river basins, with a second workshop held in June 2026.

name: ASEAN Fire Alert Tool
summary: Tool that compares daily satellite hotspot data from the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre with users' registered land.

name: Asia Pacific Telecommunity mangrove drone project, Sarawak
summary: Drone project in Sarawak funded by an Asia Pacific Telecommunity grant from Japan's government, which in May 2023 Sarawak Forestry Corporation planned to use for forest health assessment in Kuching Wetlands National Park.

name: Biji Alam
summary: Organisation whose co-founder says it channels donations to people and projects, including a RM10,000 grant to Friends of Bukit Kiara that partly funds a biodiversity survey.

name: Biodiversity Conservation in Multiple-Use Forest Landscapes in Sabah
summary: Closed project run by Sabah Forestry Department with Global Environment Facility funding, which UNDP says ended at a December 2019 workshop having spent USD 4.098 million of USD 4.4 million.

name: Biodiversity Monitoring programme, Tangkulap, Deramakot and Kuamut
summary: A biodiversity monitoring programme in which camera trapping and opportunistic sightings have identified 75 species in FMU 17A, in partnership with, and funded by, the Leibniz Institute for Zoo and Wildlife Research.

name: Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre
summary: Centre that The Star reports monitors released sun bears with GPS collars, and which had 43 rescued sun bears in July 2026.

name: Borneo Conservation Trust Sabah
summary: Conservation organisation that in 2019 was expected to rehabilitate land bought for a Lower Kinabatangan forest corridor, with its chairman saying about 325 more hectares were still needed.

name: Borneo Marine Research Institute
summary: UMS institute supporting long-term water quality, biodiversity and reef resilience monitoring, whose researchers monitored seagrass at Kampung Kibagu in March 2023 and collaborate with Deus Diving Club.

name: Camera trap study of oil palm landscapes, Sarawak
summary: Camera trap study in Sarawak oil palm landscapes in which MPOGCF and SALCRA joined UNIMAS researchers on 17 February 2025 to retrieve 27 camera traps recording mainly mammals.

name: Coastal Oasis
summary: A project that integrates environmental sensing, ecological intelligence, geospatial analysis and biodiversity monitoring, with the Sungai Klang corridor as an active implementation site, built by Planters International.

name: Continuous Monitoring of Surveillance
summary: A programme combining satellite image analysis with coordinates verified by hyperspectral airborne sensing to assist field enforcement, built and run by Forest Department Sarawak, and discussed in October 2026 for operational enhancement.

name: Counting in the canopy
summary: A project piloting computer vision and deep learning models to count orangutan nests in drone images for population estimates, led by WWF-Malaysia with WWF-UK as partner.

name: Danau Girang Field Centre
summary: A research centre in the Lower Kinabatangan Wildlife Sanctuary, Sabah, run by the Sabah Wildlife Department and Cardiff University, using camera traps, GPS collars, drones and molecular tools, and reporting over 200 publications.

name: Danum 50-Hectare Plot
summary: A forest plot run by the South East Asia Rainforest Research Partnership, where almost 250,000 trees are mapped, measured and identified every five years.

name: Department of Fisheries Malaysia
summary: A Putrajaya-based department whose services include managing marine parks, turtle centres and sanctuaries, with artificial reef work recorded in the environment ministry's 2025 statement.

name: Department of Survey and Mapping Malaysia
summary: Described in an Ecopia AI case study as Malaysia's national authority for geospatial information, which lists its datasets including topography and aerial and satellite imagery.

name: Department of Wildlife and National Parks Peninsular Malaysia
summary: A Kuala Lumpur-based wildlife department that, in March 2024, the minister said had taken initiatives to explore AI-enabled camera traps, and which Panthera says it works with on Malayan tigers.

name: Development of environmental DNA reference database for coastal resource management of Southeast Asian mangroves
summary: Closed project led by Alison Wee and funded by the Asia-Pacific Network for Global Change Research, which started in 2021 to build eDNA metabarcoding reference libraries for Southeast Asian mangrove species.

name: e-PESISIR
summary: A remote-sensing web GIS application begun in 2012 to help forestry departments plan and monitor coastal conservation, built by the Forestry Department of Peninsular Malaysia and the Malaysian Space Agency.

name: Earth Observation Centre, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia
summary: A centre of excellence under the Institute of Climate Change, run by Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, using remote sensing and GIS to research global change impacts, including a mangrove and forest biodiversity geo-database.

name: Enterprise Forest Information Management System
summary: A Forest Department Sarawak system, launched in December 2020 according to its 2020 annual report, which says it includes GIS-based monitoring in a web application.

name: Enviro Land Services Sdn Bhd
summary: A Kuala Lumpur company providing GIS solutions and geospatial products for land and marine environments, with a proprietary platform called OmniGeo, and listed as a partner of OroraTech.

name: FORESIGHT.AI
summary: A programme built by NEUON AI, listed by it as live and as the flagship of NEUNature, with two phases under deployment for Sarawak Forestry Corporation: an orchid identification app and 360 Forest Sight.

name: Forest Department Sarawak
summary: A state body running COMOS, whose development a minister reported in 2024, which discussed satellite and AI surveillance with Enviro Services, Planet and OroraTech in October 2026.

name: Forest Monitoring Remote Sensing Systems
summary: A programme providing satellite images to identify forest activities nationwide, built by the Malaysian Space Agency with the Forestry Department of Peninsular Malaysia, with a reported archive from 2015 onward as of May 2025.

name: Forest Research Institute Malaysia
summary: A forestry research institution in Kepong, Selangor, established in 1926, whose staff paper in 2021 tested drone hyperspectral imaging with Random Forest and Support Vector Machine classifiers to identify six tree species.

name: Forestry Department of Peninsular Malaysia
summary: A forestry department that uses the FMRS satellite system to detect forest reserve changes, with an official reporting about 250 encroachment cases detected in 2024, and builds e-PESISIR.

name: Friends of Tanjung Surat Island Mangrove
summary: Community society on Pulau Tanjung Surat, registered in Johor, that took part in rehabilitating 3.5 hectares of mangrove with more than 5,000 trees planted.

name: Fuze Ecoteer
summary: Social enterprise, self-described as accredited, with three conservation projects on the Perhentian Islands, whose turtle photo-ID database has identified over 260 turtles.

name: GeoDrone
summary: An initiative run by Sarawak Forestry Corporation which StarProperty says will enhance forest management, including monitoring and enforcement.

name: GeoSAWIT
summary: A programme built by the Malaysian Palm Oil Board whose mapping covers estates and smallholders, supporting satellite-based spatial analysis, and which powers a commodity traceability system offering deforestation-free assurance.

name: Geospatial AI Sdn Bhd
summary: A geospatial analytics company founded in 2021 that reports satellite monitoring of emissions and deforestation and AI mapping; Planters reports it co-organised a July 2026 event.

name: Global Environment Centre
summary: Organisation with a Petaling Jaya address, named in a 2018 UK government release as a partner in the PASSES peatland monitoring project; its site describes a fire alert app.

name: GOMPITO (Kiau Nuluh community conservation association)
summary: The conservation association was set up in Kiau Nuluh, where the community decided in 2001 to conserve 1,204 acres of forest and end hunting there.

name: HUTAN
summary: Grassroots wildlife research and conservation non-profit working in Lower Kinabatangan and across Sabah, with a biodiversity monitoring team that its 2024 annual report says uses camera traps.

name: Hutanwatch
summary: Open data platform, described as built by a network of collaborators, that lets users analyse land use data and monitor forest cover changes in Malaysia.

name: iForSABAH
summary: Forest cover monitoring application built by the Malaysian Space Agency and Sabah Forestry Department; a minister said in 2024 it uses satellite images to detect changes in forest reserves.

name: Image and video dataset of nesting green sea turtles
summary: An image and video dataset of nesting green sea turtles, whose dataset paper OpenAlex lists as published in 2024.

name: Improving Connectivity in the Central Forest Spine
summary: Closed project begun in 2014 with GEF and Malaysian funds; GEF lists a US$10.86 million grant, and UNDP lists stronger capacity to monitor wildlife crime among its results.

name: Institute of Oceanography and Environment, Universiti Malaysia Terengganu
summary: Marine institute run by Universiti Malaysia Terengganu, registered as a GBIF publisher, named the national OBIS node according to the university, with a repository of over 20,000 marine specimens.

name: Institute of Tropical Biodiversity and Sustainable Development, Universiti Malaysia Terengganu
summary: Universiti Malaysia Terengganu institute where, according to a Merdeka Award article, a research officer works on passive acoustic monitoring of gibbons.

name: Integrated Landscape Management of Heart of Borneo Landscapes in Sabah and Sarawak
summary: Project in Sabah and Sarawak, run by the Sabah Forestry Department, for which GEF lists a US$7,368,807 grant approved for implementation in June 2023.

name: Integrated Smart Bioacoustic Project for Wildlife & Forest Conservation
summary: Project run by Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris, developing AI, internet-of-things and bioacoustic tools for real-time forest monitoring; the university received an RM3 million international grant.

name: Intelligent Sensing and Smart Integration: AI for River Water Quality Monitoring
summary: Grant project of RM67,000, launched by an agreement signed on 17 April 2025, aiming at AI-driven real-time monitoring and pollution detection at four river stations, led by Kamarul Hawari Ghazali.

name: Johor human-elephant conflict early warning system
summary: A proposed Johor state warning system using satellite collars on elephants, reported on 1 April 2025, with central government allocations said to have been received for collar installation.

name: Johor National Parks Corporation
summary: Johor state body founded in 1992 under a 1989 enactment to safeguard wildlife, plants and scenery in state national parks, including Endau-Rompin, Pulau Kukup and Tanjung Piai.

name: Johor State Forestry Department
summary: The department partners with TH Plantations and the Global Environment Centre to restore 4,300 hectares in Gunung Arong Forest Reserve and was reportedly allocated over RM3 million.

name: Kampung Dagat community (Tidung)
summary: Tidung village of almost 250 people whose territory, governed by the community for generations, overlaps Tabin Wildlife Reserve and includes a 222-hectare customary forest, per a 2026 case study.

name: Kedah State Forestry Department
summary: The department helped Leader Energy and others launch a five-year mangrove conservation programme in which volunteers planted 1,000 mangrove trees in Merbok Forest Reserve in 2024.

name: KenalKayu
summary: Model that identifies timber species in under a second, built by Universiti Teknologi Malaysia and led by Uswah Khairuddin.

name: Klang Valley City Nature Challenge
summary: Project using iNaturalist, in which Universiti Malaya says the Klang Valley has taken part since 2018; the 2018 round produced 25,287 observations of 1,775 species.

name: KOPEL (Koperasi Pelancongan Mukim Batu Puteh)
summary: Community-led cooperative in Lower Kinabatangan that manages ecolodges and supports forest restoration, with sources dating its founding to 1995 (Pulitzer Center) or 2003 (UN Tourism).

name: Kota Damansara Community Forest Society
summary: Formed in 2011 to protect Kota Damansara Community Forest, the society maintains its trails, while the lack of a joint management committee has hindered joint governance.

name: Kuamut Rainforest Conservation Project
summary: Project protecting and restoring 83,381 ha of Sabah rainforest, with species and ecosystem monitoring in its objective; a March 2024 report says its first Monitoring Report was verified.

name: Kudat Turtle Conservation Society
summary: A Sabah non-government organisation registered in 2011, with turtle habitat monitoring and citizen science in Tun Mustapha Park using procedures supervised by Universiti Malaysia Sabah.

name: Labeled passive acoustic monitoring dataset from Danum Valley Conservation Area
summary: An archive of labelled training, validation and test data from passive acoustic monitoring in Danum Valley, associated with a paper on automated detection and classification of female gibbon calls.

name: Labelled dataset of the loud calls of four vertebrates, Malaysian Borneo
summary: Dataset of loud calls of four vertebrates from Danum Valley Conservation Area, recorded March to July 2018, with about 500 hours of recordings chosen to create a training dataset.

name: Lembaga Urus Air Selangor
summary: Selangor water body that gazetted a Protection Zone along Sungai Selangor, which a FRIM programme head credited, with better river management, for signs of firefly recovery.

name: LVNS Forest Project, Malaysia
summary: Forest project in Malaysia led by Leave a Nest with AlphaSwift as partner, where Leave a Nest says drones will be used for planting and monitoring forest health.

name: Machine learning framework for Southeast Asian echolocating bats
summary: Machine learning framework for Southeast Asian echolocating bats, known from a paper published in 2022 that OpenAlex lists.

name: Majlis Pengurusan Taman Negeri Terengganu
summary: Terengganu state parks body that says it monitors protected areas in real time with drones, 20 camera traps, CCTV, GIS and SMART, and partners with research and conservation groups.

name: Malaysia Biodiversity Centre
summary: National biodiversity centre that runs the MyBIS portal for the environment ministry, whose logo and portal were launched at the third National Biodiversity Council meeting, according to a 2025 ministry statement.

name: Malaysia Biodiversity Information System
summary: A Malaysian biodiversity repository database, run by the Malaysia Biodiversity Centre, that aims to be a one-stop source and the national node of the CBD information exchange network, with information abstracted from books, journals, checklists and specimen databases.

name: Malaysia Flora Project on Pl@ntNet
summary: Active Malaysian plant identification project on Pl@ntNet, built by Lee Sue Han, who says it has grown in species and public contributions and serves as a national reference.

name: Malaysia Forest Fund
summary: Agency of the environment ministry, according to Verra, established on 30 June 2021 to implement the REDD Plus Finance Framework and holding the Forest Conservation Certificate and Forest Carbon Offset standards.

name: Malaysia Invasive Alien Species
summary: A portal powered by MyBIS offering a list of invasive species and the National Action Plan on Invasive Alien Species 2021-2025, carrying two ministries' copyright.

name: Malaysian Conservation Alliance for Tigers
summary: Tiger conservation group whose research, according to WildCats Conservation Alliance, showed a drastic local tiger decline and identified poaching hotspots.

name: Malaysian Nature Society
summary: Active nature society whose Bird Conservation Council publishes the checklist of birds of Peninsular Malaysia, according to the Malaysian Bird Report, which also reports a 2024 peregrine survey by a branch team.

name: Malaysian Palm Oil Board
summary: Agency under the Ministry of Plantation and Commodities that developed GeoSAWIT, with its SIMS control room at Wisma Dura in Bangi.

name: Malaysian Palm Oil Green Conservation Foundation
summary: Active foundation that says it aims to support green conservation initiatives related to the palm oil industry.

name: Malaysian Space Agency
summary: Science ministry agency that built FMRS Plus and MyGeoBiod, says it developed 65 GovRS-Apps systems used by over 115 agencies, and signed a May 2023 remote sensing memorandum with Sabah Forestry Department.

name: Maliangin Island Community Association
summary: Island community association which, in a report reposted in 2016, was reviving pandanus weaving to reduce fishing pressure, on an island that was a pilot site for the proposed Tun Mustapha Park.

name: Management and Ecology of Malaysian Elephants
summary: University of Nottingham Malaysia programme, established in 2011 with PERHILITAN, first sponsored by Yayasan Sime Darby with RM3.36 million from January 2012, now developing an elephant early warning prototype using bioacoustics and cameras.

name: MareCet Research Organization
summary: Pew describes it as Malaysia's first non-profit dedicated to marine mammals, with cetacean research on population assessments and behaviour, and the Langkawi Dolphin Research Project as its flagship.

name: Marine Research Foundation
summary: Sabah-based non-profit research foundation, established in 2003 with an office in Kota Kinabalu, which has deployed time-lapse GPS-linked cameras to assess shark and ray bycatch.

name: Maybank
summary: Bank that pledged RM1.55 million in March 2024 for the first year of a 2024 to 2027 tiger conservation project with WWF-Malaysia, which plans continuous monitoring of tigers and prey.

name: MIMOS and WWF-Malaysia anti-poaching solution
summary: Proposed MIMOS and WWF-Malaysia system described in 2019, combining AI, analytics, internet of things, edge and cloud computing, with video analytics planned to detect boats evading a ranger checkpoint.

name: MIMOS Berhad
summary: Registered company at Technology Park Malaysia that in 2019 reported developing an anti-poaching solution with WWF-Malaysia and using AI-based video analytics for forest monitoring.

name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability
summary: Putrajaya ministry building MyBioDTrack and serving as National Biodiversity Council secretariat, which Sarawak Tribune reports said Malaysia submitted its seventh CBD report on 28 February 2026.

name: Multimedia University
summary: Active university whose authors are listed by OpenAlex on a 2022 paper on visual and audio fusion for wildlife surveillance and a 2024 paper on coral type classification.

name: Mumiang Suluk community (Mumiang Locally Managed Marine Area)
summary: The Suluk community established and governs a locally managed marine area in the Kinabatangan River estuary, where fishers have recorded catches using Open Data Kit.

name: MyBioDTrack
summary: Active reporting system built by the environment ministry, through which federal and state bodies report on the National Policy on Biological Diversity 2022-2030, with data intended to support Malaysia's national report to the CBD.

name: MyGardenBird
summary: A dataset of twelve bird species from Peninsular Malaysia and the wider region, holding 7,200 manually reviewed clips, with CNN baselines reported across three architectures.

name: MyGeoBioD
summary: A national integrated biodiversity management system and database, built by the Malaysian Space Agency, whose page describes development with remote sensing, GIS and GPS and aims at a centralised geospatial database.

name: MYSA Remote Sensing Open Data Catalogue
summary: A catalogue run by the Malaysian Space Agency offering satellite data with spatial resolution greater than 5 metres, subject to availability, non-commercial use and satellite-owner licence terms.

name: MyWood-ID
summary: Smartphone wood identification system built by FRIM and Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman, launched on 2 February 2018 at FRIM, when its free trial identified 20 Malaysian wood types.

name: National Biodiversity Council
summary: Main federal and state government forum on national biodiversity direction, at whose fourth meeting in Putrajaya on 18 June 2026 the seventh National Report was launched.

name: National Tiger Survey
summary: A closed project, run by the wildlife department, WWF-Malaysia and WCS Malaysia, whose first survey began in 2015 and reported fewer than 200 Malayan tigers from 75% of survey plots covered in 2016 to 2018.

name: National Water Research Institute Malaysia
summary: An organisation whose River Basin Research Centre sent twenty staff to a June 2026 workshop with Universiti Kuala Lumpur on deep learning for satellite image segmentation; in March 2026 a minister was reported saying AI was deployed in its work.

name: Natural Resources and Environment Board Sarawak
summary: A Sarawak board whose efforts to expand telemetric water quality monitoring were backed by a deputy minister on 1 October 2025, who said only one such river station was then operating.

name: NEUON Artificial Intelligence
summary: Kuching-based company partnering with Swinburne Sarawak and Sarawak Forestry Corporation, listing FORESIGHT.AI, an orchid tool and HerbaLook under NEUNature.

name: OBIS Malaysia
summary: A programme that Universiti Malaysia Terengganu describes as the node central to collecting oceanographic data for Malaysia.

name: OceanX Malaysia Mission 2024
summary: A closed OceanX project, a 16-day mission off Pahang that OceanX says has concluded, which used ReefCloud.

name: One Ocean Empire
summary: Founded by Monica Chin, the group was named alongside Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s Borneo Marine Research Institute in two year-long Mabul Island marine restoration initiatives announced in 2025.

name: Orang-utan nest AI, Sabah
summary: A project by WWF-Malaysia and Universiti Malaysia Sabah that aims to automate analysis of drone images of orang-utan nests through a deep-learning model for detecting and classifying nests.

name: Pahang State Forestry Department
summary: State forestry department that helped install canal blocks with Enggang (Pekan) Sdn Bhd and worked with GEC on peatland rehabilitation in the Pekan forest area to raise water levels.

name: Pahang State Parks Corporation
summary: Pahang reported Tasik Chini redevelopment planning through the corporation in June 2024, and a 2021 opposition account described its intended takeover of Endau Rompin National Park.

name: Panthera Malaysia
summary: Malaysian office of Panthera, incorporated at the beginning of 2020, with Sabah Forestry Department and Rimba as partners.

name: Pasoh Forest Research Station
summary: FRIM's oldest research station, set up in 1970, with a 50-hectare ecology plot and canopy walkways; data requests need approval from the Pasoh Research Committee.

name: Peatland Assessment in SE Asia by Satellite
summary: A £2.2 million project announced by the UK Space Agency in February 2018 to map peat condition in Malaysia and Indonesia from satellites through Copernicus, with CGI and the Global Environment Centre as partners.

name: Penan Peace Park communities of Upper Baram
summary: Seventeen Penan communities proclaimed the Penan Peace Park, about 1,630 square kilometres in Sarawak, in 2009, and a 2026 Mongabay report says a 2024 timber concession overlaps the Upper Baram park they hoped to co-manage.

name: Penang Hill Corporation
summary: Penang statutory body established in 2009 that manages the Penang Hill Biosphere Reserve, designated under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme in 2021.

name: Penang Inshore Fishermen Welfare Association
summary: Fishermen's association whose president described its work protecting the coastal ecosystem at Nibong Tebal, and which joined a 2022 mangrove planting with the Penang Forestry Department and companies.

name: Perak State Forestry Department
summary: State forestry department that worked with the Department of Fisheries on mangrove conservation in South Trong Forest Reserve, where 6,400 seedlings were reported planted in July 2023, and has completed a 2026-2035 forest management plan.

name: Perak State Parks Corporation
summary: State parks body whose rangers record patrols with SMART Mobile, funded by Yayasan Sime Darby, which says it has invested over RM6 million in Royal Belum since 2017.

name: Perhentian Marine Research Station
summary: Station run by Fuze Ecoteer that monitors coral spawning, is starting long-term coral health tracking with CoralWatch, and builds a biodiversity database from iNaturalist observations.

name: Persatuan Kekal Asli Pulau Tigabu
summary: Community association established in 2018 that leads the Pulau Tigabu marine managed area inside Tun Mustapha Park, with patrols against illegal fishing, a turtle hatchery and fish stock monitoring.

name: Persatuan Pelindung Harimau Malaysia
summary: An organisation that founded the Menraq community patrol teams, funded by Yayasan Sime Darby for a project from November 2021 to October 2024 that included training them to collect data using SMART.

name: Persatuan Pencinta Bakau Tanjung Kepah
summary: Mangrove association that co-organised a replanting activity at Tanjung Kepah, Perak, with Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman, involving students and community members, reported in August 2026.

name: Planters International Berhad
summary: A Malaysian company describing itself as an environmental technology and natural capital firm, saying it is developing the AFAM platform and Coastal Oasis initiative, with Restor and SpaceIn as partners.

name: Precision Biodiversity Digitalisation & IoT Programme
summary: A closed five-year pilot run by the Academy of Sciences Malaysia, funded with RM7 million from 1 January 2022 in Pasoh Forest Reserve, that used AI and IoT to capture data and planned AI species identification from 2023.

name: Project Dupot
summary: Wild cat monitoring and protection project for Sunda clouded leopards and other wild cats in the Deramakot Core Area, run by Panthera Malaysia.

name: Project Harimau Selamanya
summary: Malayan tiger project described in July 2014, with Rimba researchers deploying 200 camera traps in the core area, planned until September 2014; funded by Panthera and Woodland Park Zoo.

name: Project Kenyir
