summary: Project run by Panthera Malaysia that monitors and protects three wild cat species and their prey in the Kenyir-Taman Negara Core Area.

name: Pulau Banding Foundation
summary: The self-described conservation NGO in Belum-Temenggor prepared research centre, dormitory and discovery centre facilities on Pulau Banding to support Universiti Malaysia Kelantan’s research and education.

name: Quantifying Stand Structure Dynamics and Productivity in Natural Forest and Planted Forest Stands Using Airborne 3D Ranging Systems
summary: Project which, in August 2025, planned to use 3D LiDAR to assess forest structure, growth and productivity, with Arbonaut as a partner.

name: Rainforest Guardian Research Project
summary: Project launched in November 2021 over a 30 square kilometre protected area, using solar-powered Guardian devices with Huawei's cloud and AI to detect chainsaws and vehicles; five were deployed in Sarawak by then.

name: Redang and Perhentian island communities marine conservation programme
summary: A closed three-year marine programme run by Reef Check Malaysia and funded by Yayasan Hasanah, which trained 24 local youths in reef monitoring and gathered data on reef health and threats.

name: Reef Check Malaysia
summary: Kuala Lumpur-based member of the worldwide Reef Check network, established in 2007, conducting annual surveys at over 300 locations and publishing an interactive reef health map in September 2025.

name: Rimba
summary: Non-profit research group that ceased operations at the end of 2022, which used camera traps and launched a K9 tracking pilot in 2017, according to Panthera.

name: Rimba Project
summary: Education and outreach programme based at Rimba Ilmu Botanic Garden, according to The Star.

name: Rymba
summary: Cyberjaya-listed organisation that fuses satellite and drone data and analyses it with AI for canopy coverage and tree identification, with reports packaged for IFRS S2, TNFD and carbon credit registries.

name: Sabah aboveground carbon map
summary: Carbon map built by the Carnegie Airborne Observatory, which Mongabay reports used airborne LiDAR and satellite imagery to give a wall-to-wall account of carbon in Sabah.

name: Sabah Biodiversity Centre
summary: Sabah body that builds the Sabah Biodiversity Integrated Information System, lists the Biodiversity Enactment 2000 and Strategy 2024-2034, and published its 2025 annual report on Sabah Biodiversity Day 2026.

name: Sabah Biodiversity Experiment
summary: Project run by the South East Asia Rainforest Research Partnership that studies the effect of tree diversity in forest restoration with indigenous species.

name: Sabah Biodiversity Integrated Information System
summary: Online database and information system on biodiversity and natural resources in Sabah, built by the Sabah Biodiversity Centre, with a citizen science field survey mobile application.

name: Sabah Forestry Department
summary: Sandakan-based state department that builds iForSabah and partners with the Malaysian Space Agency, reporting about 48.6% of Sabah as gazetted forest reserve (2021) and mapping forest cover every two years since 2010, per a ministry statement.

name: Sabah Parks
summary: A Sabah government agency under the Parks Enactment 1984, which Reef Check Malaysia says co-conducted its October 2025 Tun Mustapha Park survey and November 2025 Tunku Abdul Rahman Park surveys.

name: Sabah Wetlands Conservation Society
summary: A 2016 paper identified the society as manager of the 24-hectare Kota Kinabalu Wetlands mangrove, opened in March 2000, and reported that it supported over 92 bird species.

name: Sabah Wildlife Department
summary: Kota Kinabalu-based department running Danau Girang Field Centre, which The Star reported in November 2024 launched a wildlife crime plan titled ten-year, with dates 2024 to 2035.

name: SAFE Acoustics
summary: Acoustic monitoring project at the SAFE site, built by Imperial College London, Universiti Malaysia Sabah, the South East Asia Rainforest Research Partnership and Sarab Sethi, with nearly 15 devices deployed since 2018, reported in 2021.

name: Sahabat Hutan Bakau Kampung Dato' Hormat
summary: Community group listed as a partner in the Kampung Dato' Hormat mangrove rehabilitation project, whose members are expected to help plant and maintain a further 2 hectares in the 2025–2028 phase.

name: Sahabat Hutan Bakau Kuala Gula
summary: The group joined a project that planted 22,500 mangroves across Kuala Gula and Pasir Panjang Laut and held a March 2023 closing event, and supplied Sungai Limau rehabilitation saplings.

name: Sahabat Hutan Bakau Lekir Sitiawan
summary: Village mangrove group set up in October 2014 by Kampung Sungai Tiram residents with Global Environment Centre help, later listed as a partner in the completed 2019 to 2023 Sungai Limau rehabilitation project.

name: Sahabat Hutan Bakau Pasir Panjang Laut
summary: Community mangrove group formed in 2020 at Kampung Pasir Panjang Laut, whose members protect and replant local mangroves, with a nursery and planting site described by Yayasan Sime Darby.

name: Sahabat Kuala Langat Utara
summary: Group of Orang Asli from two villages that The Star reported in 2020 as patrolling for open burning and early forest fire signs, within a Gamuda Parks programme that had reforested 14 hectares of peat.

name: Sarawak Aerial Detection Unit
summary: Built by Sarawak Forest Department, it was mandated against illegal logging in 2014 and would provide aircraft-based hyperspectral geospatial services, The Star reported in November 2020.

name: Sarawak Artificial Intelligence Centre
summary: Organisation that in October 2025 signed a memorandum on integrating biodiversity and traditional knowledge databases with AI, with a counterpart the page calls Sarawak Biodiversity Council.

name: Sarawak Biodiversity Centre
summary: Semengoh, Kuching body set up by the Sarawak government in 1998 under a 1997 ordinance, whose role was first mainly inventory and regulation.

name: Sarawak Forestry Corporation
summary: Its conference page reports piloting AI for mangrove health using drone images with Sunway University and advertised an 11–12 July 2026 workshop including AI identification of camera-trap wildlife.

name: Sarawak Multimedia Authority
summary: Organisation that Huawei names as a partner in the Rainforest Guardian Research Project, and which is named first among the parties to the memorandum signed in Kuching in November 2021.

name: Sastena Technology Sdn Bhd
summary: Company that, according to Xinhua in The Star, formed an AI-driven carbon intelligence partnership with FRIM Incorporated in November 2025.

name: Sea Turtle Research Unit
summary: Research unit run by UMT’s Institute of Oceanography and Environment, associated with a long-term sea turtle tagging and nesting study begun in May 1993.

name: SEA-BIRD30
summary: Dataset of 18,000 clips from 30 bird species, prepared for use in machine learning.

name: SEAFDEC Marine Fishery Resources Development and Management Department
summary: Department whose project list includes a hydroacoustic survey off the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia and research on sea turtles in foraging habitats.

name: Seagrass Mapping and Community-Based Restoration Programme
summary: Active project in which fishermen and scientists survey, monitor and restore seagrass, with UMS researchers mapping beds around Kampung Kebagu and Kampung Penimbawan.

name: Selangor State Forestry Department
summary: State forestry body that manages Selangor State Park, gazetted in 2007, and lists the state's recreational forests and forest parks, including eco-forest parks at Kanching, Templer, Sungai Tekala and Gunung Nuang.

name: SEMAI (Sahabat Eko-pelancongan dan Memulihara Alam Indah), Ulu Geroh
summary: The Semai villagers’ cooperative aimed to protect Rafflesia and butterfly habitat and was expected in 2005 to lead an ecotourism project with government and Malaysian Nature Society assistance.

name: Seratu Aatai
summary: Sabah-based group, as described by The Star, protecting Bornean elephants; it lists a completed elephant bioacoustic monitoring project in the Lower Kinabatangan and is registered in Malaysia.

name: Sistem e-Geospatial Perhutanan
summary: A system run by the Forestry Department of Peninsular Malaysia with a mobile app for accessing its data, to which a 2025 parliamentary statement said AI features and high-frequency satellite images were being added.

name: Socially and Environmentally Sustainable Oil Palm Research
summary: Research project run by the South East Asia Rainforest Research Partnership that quantifies the impacts of palm oil agriculture and informs RSPO criteria.

name: South East Asia Rainforest Research Partnership
summary: Established by the UK's Royal Society in 1985, this body requires programme researchers to deposit datasets from January 2024, saying Zenodo will provide open access.

name: SpaceIn
summary: Organisation that, according to Planters, co-organised a MASIC space solutions session on 13 July 2026 covering earth observation, satellite imagery, AI and Space IoT.

name: Stability of Altered Forest Ecosystems Project
summary: SEARRP-run rainforest experiment studying logging, fragmentation and oil palm, based in Maliau Basin according to Options, The Edge, with 161 datasets in its catalogue when read.

name: Sunway University
summary: University that signed a memorandum with the Sarawak Forestry Corporation on a mangrove project, with a 2024 paper on detecting mangrove species from drone imagery using YOLOv5, and 5 OpenAlex-counted AI ecology works since 2018.

name: Swinburne University of Technology Sarawak Campus
summary: Through a partnership with NEUON AI begun in 2022, this campus worked on a plant species identification system that won top honours at PlantCLEF challenges.

name: The Habitat Foundation
summary: A charitable trust established in Penang that lists a Pulau Pinang address and registration number PPAB – 10/2019.

name: Tricolour langur drone monitoring, Jemoreng and Selai Inah
summary: Wildlife monitoring project using modified drone technology at two forests, built by the Forest Department Sarawak; Sarawak Tribune reports its launch and calls it a world first.

name: Tropical Rainforest Conservation & Research Centre
summary: A non-profit conserving rare and endangered Malaysian trees, whose Elmina nursery has recorded 311 fauna species and whose tree tagging surveys locate potential parent trees.

name: Tropical Resources Mapping Research Group
summary: Research group formed for mapping, monitoring and modelling tropical resources, run by Universiti Teknologi Malaysia.

name: Turtle Conservation Society of Malaysia
summary: Kemaman-based group founded in 2011 as the first Malaysian NGO for freshwater turtles; preliminary eDNA work detected river terrapin eDNA in river samples from a site with turtles nearby.

name: Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia
summary: University with OpenAlex-listed papers from 2022 to 2024 on machine learning for logging impacts from drone images, elephant behaviour from collar data and mangrove biomass, and an Earth Observation Centre.

name: Universiti Kuala Lumpur
summary: University that organised AiR3S workshops with the National Water Research Institute Malaysia in October 2025 and June 2026, and says it brings AI and digital technology expertise.

name: Universiti Malaya
summary: University with 16 OpenAlex-counted works on AI in ecology subfields since 2018, a 2021 cephalopod identification paper, and a sustainability site promoting the City Nature Challenge in Klang Valley.

name: Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah
summary: University that signed an agreement on 17 April 2025 with East Automation & Engineering for AI river water quality monitoring, and is the first author's affiliation on a 2025 YOLOv8n elephant intrusion detector paper.

name: Universiti Malaysia Sabah
summary: University whose computer science PhD student was working on AI to recognise orang-utan nests in drone images in August 2023, with 13 OpenAlex-counted AI or machine learning ecology works since 2018.

name: Universiti Malaysia Sarawak
summary: University with 10 OpenAlex-counted AI ecology works since 2018, including a dataset of nesting green sea turtles, a 2024 green turtle detection paper and a bat call classification paper.

name: Universiti Malaysia Terengganu
summary: Malaysian university whose authors have 29 OpenAlex-listed works on AI in ecology subfields since 2018, including a 2023 review of deep learning for coral reef classification; its Faculty of Science and Marine Environment is a GBIF publisher.

name: Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris
summary: Malaysian university that leads a smart forest conservation project at Gerik in the Central Forest Spine under an international grant of RM3 million, and runs and leads the integrated smart bioacoustic project.

name: Universiti Putra Malaysia
summary: Malaysian university with 45 OpenAlex-listed works on AI in ecology subfields since 2018, the most of any Malaysian institution in that query, including a 2026 paper on mapping Sarawak mangroves with machine learning.

name: Universiti Sains Malaysia
summary: Malaysian university with 26 OpenAlex-listed works on AI in ecology subfields since 2018, including a 2026 paper by two authors comparing AI-integrated and conventional camera traps.

name: Universiti Teknologi Malaysia
summary: Malaysian university whose Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics developed KenalKayu, an automated timber species identification system, and which hosts the TropicalMap research group in its Faculty of Built Environment and Surveying.

name: Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman
summary: Malaysian university whose Centre for Computing and Intelligence Systems, with the FRIM Wood Anatomy Lab, created MyWood-ID.

name: University of Nottingham Malaysia
summary: A university campus that runs the Management and Ecology of Malaysian Elephants project, has authors on the WildTechAlert paper and partners with ConservationDrones.

name: UZMASAT-1 Programme
summary: Satellite programme described in a 2024 Emerging Technology Award listing as using high temporal and spectral resolution imagery for ESG applications, with the satellite deployed in low earth orbit on 15 January 2025.

name: WCS Malaysia
summary: Registered Malaysian entity representing the Wildlife Conservation Society, working mainly in southern Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak since 2007 in Endau-Rompin, supporting patrols and biological monitoring and named among collaborators in the 2016–2018 National Tiger Survey.

name: Wetlands International Malaysia
summary: Malaysian wetlands organisation that says it conducts regular site monitoring programmes and that most of its work is financed project by project by corporations, research institutions, government agencies and foreign grants.

name: Wildlife Society of Selangor
summary: Kuala Lumpur-based society that reported in March 2024 about 40 camera traps at its project site, supplying data for assessing interventions in its Malayan tiger project.

name: WildTechAlert
summary: Deep learning models for real-time detection of elephants from sound, described in a 2024 paper whose first author is Yen Yi Loo.

name: WWF-Malaysia
summary: Conservation trust and tax-exempt non-profit established in 1972 and part of WWF, which relies on camera traps for surveys and, per WWF-UK, is piloting deep learning for orang-utan nest detection in Sabah.

name: Yayasan Hasanah
summary: Funder whose grants can reach RM2.5 million over three years, with 2025 guidelines aiming to enhance ecosystem resilience and biodiversity through conservation and restoration.

name: Yayasan Petronas
summary: Foundation whose site says PETRONAS invested RM83 million in the Imbak Canyon Studies Centre.

name: Yayasan Sabah
summary: Statutory body established in 1966 that manages Danum Valley Conservation Area day to day, and says it manages Maliau Basin, working with research partners on biodiversity surveys and citizen science.

name: Yayasan Sime Darby
summary: Philanthropic arm of three Sime Darby companies that funds nature and wildlife work, including RM1.2 million for two new Menraq patrol teams from November 2021 to October 2024.

name: 2025 National Elephant and Large Mammal Census (Mozambique)
summary: Closed national survey, run by CEAGRE under ANAC's leadership and funded by BIOFUND, whose results presented on 24 July 2026 estimate 22,718 elephants, against 9,114 in the 2018 census.

name: Administração do Parque Nacional do Gilé
summary: Covering 453,200 hectares including a buffer zone, this Mozambican national park is run by ANAC in partnership with FFS-IGF and uses radio and remote monitoring technology.

name: Administração Nacional das Áreas de Conservação
summary: Mozambican state institution created in 2011 to coordinate the National System of Conservation Areas, administering parks, reserves and hunting areas, and described by Peace Parks Foundation as the country's conservation authority.

name: Aerial wildlife census of Maputo, Zinave, Banhine and Limpopo National Parks
summary: Two-yearly aerial census run by four national parks with Peace Parks Foundation and ANAC support, combining fixed-wing and helicopter transect surveys; October 2023 was the first full census in all four.

name: Akashinga Mozambique
summary: Akashinga's Mozambique programme, begun in 2022 in the Coutada 5 area, whose country scientist says its monitoring is identifying shark and ray hotspots as well as safeguarding turtles.

name: Banhine National Park
summary: With Maputo, Zinave and Limpopo parks, ran an aerial wildlife census in October 2023 to determine wildlife populations.

name: Bazaruto Center for Scientific Studies
summary: A registered research centre on Benguerra Island that describes itself as Africa's first permanent ocean observatory, using moorings, sensors and remote sensing, and says all validated data are publicly available.

name: Bazaruto dugong satellite tagging project
summary: Satellite-tagging survey in Bazaruto Archipelago National Park, reported in October 2024 by the Mail & Guardian, in which twelve dugongs, seven male and five female, were fitted with tracking tags.

name: Biodiversity Conservation and Community Development Project in Chimanimani
summary: Closed 2021 to 2024 project, funded by the Fonds Français pour l'Environnement Mondial and Fauna & Flora, covering biodiversity assessments, elephant protection and monitoring, and an ANAC information management mechanism, with three elephants fitted with monitoring devices in September 2023.

name: Biodiversity Network of Mozambique
summary: A dataset of research-grade primary biodiversity data from national universities, research centres and conservation areas, which began as a partnership of the Italian development agency, UEM and MITADER.

name: BIOFUND – Fundação para a Conservação da Biodiversidade
summary: Private, non-profit Mozambican environmental fund created in December 2011 for biodiversity conservation, which signed a five-year, USD 16 million agreement with Sida in 2022 and runs and built a conservation areas platform.

name: Centro de Estudos de Agricultura e Gestão de Recursos Naturais
summary: Mozambican university research centre, run by the agronomy and forestry faculty at Eduardo Mondlane University, which carried out a 2015 habitat mapping study and conducted the September to November 2025 national elephant and large mammal census.

name: Centro Nacional de Cartografia e Teledetecção
summary: Independent centre under the Ministry of Agriculture, according to UN-SPIDER, whose main tasks are providing baseline GIS data, facilitating purchase of satellite data and providing topographic and thematic maps.

name: Centro Terra Viva
summary: Mozambican NGO created in 2002, named by Peace Parks Foundation as its preferred Maputo National Park research partner for reef monitoring, catch monitoring and mangrove assessments.

name: Chimanimani National Park
summary: BIOFUND lists the park as implementing the heritage knowledge, protection and promotion component of the 2021 to 2024 Chimanimani project; in September 2023 three elephants were fitted with monitoring devices and technicians trained in virtual monitoring.

name: COMBO+ Program in Mozambique
summary: Closed programme dated 2021 to 2025 by BIOFUND, led by the Wildlife Conservation Society, with technical tools and data production among its four areas and progress reported on an African elephant biodiversity metric.

name: Conservation and Monitoring of Endangered Sawfishes in Mozambique
summary: 2015 project that aimed to collect biological data from sawfishes in Mozambique and build government and community capacity to monitor them, with sampling planned with local fishers and the national fisheries research institute.

name: Conservation of Endangered Endemic Tree Species and Their Habitats in Serra Mesa, Northern Mozambique
summary: Project in northern Mozambique that plans a botanical survey of Serra Mesa to document plant diversity and map vegetation, with field assessments of habitat condition, forest structure, soil and human pressures.

name: Department of Biological Sciences, Eduardo Mondlane University
summary: Eduardo Mondlane University department, named as the first author's affiliation on a 2023 paper combining drones and machine learning to find dugong foraging hotspots at Inhaca Island.

name: Direcção Nacional de Florestas
summary: Forestry directorate placed under the Ministry of Land and Environment by the 2021 national forest monitoring system document.

name: Direcção Nacional do Ambiente e Mudanças Climáticas
summary: Mozambican environment and climate directorate that held an August 2026 technical meeting to harmonise the NBSAP components, with WCS support, and a third biodiversity offsets unit meeting in October 2025.

name: Divisão de Agricultura, Instituto Superior Politécnico de Gaza
summary: Agriculture division in Chókwè, listed among the first author's affiliations on a 2024 paper about DNA barcoding of Mozambican marine and coastal fish.

name: Drones and machine-learning for monitoring dugong feeding grounds and gillnet fishing
summary: Closed study combining drone imaging and machine learning to find dugong foraging hotspots at Inhaca Island's Saco East and West, reporting F1 accuracies of 80% for feeding trails and 93.3% for seagrass beds.

name: E.O. Wilson Biodiversity Laboratory
summary: Research facility at Gorongosa National Park, run by the Gorongosa Project, created to explore, document and protect the park's biodiversity through surveys across all its ecological zones and habitat types.

name: Eduardo Mondlane University
summary: University named Universidade Eduardo Mondlane online, with a Natural History Museum and herbarium of about 63,000 specimens, whose GBIF collection comes from Mozambique expeditions during 1935–2008.

name: Faculdade de Agronomia e Engenharia Florestal, Universidade Eduardo Mondlane
summary: Faculty reported by BIOFUND in December 2024 as leading Gilé fire research with partners, whose forest engineering department is the lead affiliation on a 2025 mangrove imagery paper.

name: Fundação Likhulu para Conservação Marinha
summary: A Maputo-based marine conservation foundation associated with coral reef monitoring for InOM alongside WCS in an April 2025 report produced under an arrangement with JNCC.

name: Fundo Nacional de Desenvolvimento Sustentável
summary: Public-law body overseen by the agriculture minister that finances environmental, forest, biodiversity and land programmes, runs the FNDS MRV unit, and as of November 2019 had a geoportal publishing forest inventory and emissions data.

name: Gorongosa Map of Life
summary: Project aiming to map interactions among organisms and build a genetic and ecological database for Gorongosa, reporting over 1,000 species new to Mozambique and planning acoustic and environmental DNA sampling.

name: Gorongosa Project
summary: US-based non-profit with a 20-year agreement to co-manage Gorongosa National Park, which monitors wildlife with trail cameras, aerial counts and acoustic recorders, and runs WildCam Gorongosa.

name: GPS collaring of elephants in the Incomati Conservation Area
summary: Project that fitted GPS collars on three male elephants in the Incomati Conservation Area in September 2024, described by BIOFUND as part of a one-year effort to monitor elephant movements in real time.

name: Herbário da Universidade Eduardo Mondlane
summary: Herbarium founded in 1964 holding about 63,000 plant and macroalgae specimens, supporting identification services and species research, with its GBIF collection from expeditions across Mozambique between 1935 and 2008.

name: InOM and WCS BRUVS shark and ray monitoring
summary: Programme run by InOM and WCS Mozambique, which have conducted regular baited underwater video monitoring of sharks and rays along Mozambique's coast since 2018, recording 75 hours of video in December 2025.

name: Instituto de Investigação Agrária de Moçambique
summary: Mozambican agricultural research institute that publishes the National Herbarium of Mozambique's botanical collection as a GBIF dataset, described as the country's largest, with over 70,000 accessions of wild plants.

name: Instituto Oceanográfico de Moçambique
summary: Described by the Bazaruto Center for Scientific Studies as Mozambique's oceanographic institute under MIMAIP and national marine research body, it partnered with WCS on BRUVS monitoring in December 2025.

name: Key Biodiversity Areas and Red Lists Program (Mozambique)
summary: Programme developed by WCS Mozambique with government partners from February 2019, conducting a national KBA assessment by 2020 and Red List assessments for 67 endemic or near-endemic species.

name: Limpopo National Park
summary: With Maputo, Zinave and Banhine parks, ran an aerial wildlife census in October 2023 to determine wildlife populations.

name: Mapping and Monitoring the Quirimbas National Park Seascape
summary: November 2020 report describing WWF Germany’s Sentinel-2 and Google Earth Engine workflow for mapping Quirimbas coral reef habitats using Random Forests and WWF-Mozambique field surveys from 2018 and 2019.

name: Maputo National Park
summary: With Zinave, Banhine and Limpopo parks, ran an aerial wildlife census in October 2023 to determine wildlife populations.

name: MICAIA Foundation
summary: Operating foundation set up in 2009 that implements donor-funded projects, including a CEPF-funded 2013 to 2015 botanical survey of upland Chimanimani and an earlier Darwin-funded project with Kew producing a useful plants database.

name: Ministério da Agricultura, Ambiente e Pescas
summary: Mozambican ministry, led by Roberto Mito Albino, to which development projects submit their plans after meeting environmental requirements, according to BIOFUND, and which supervises FNDS among other institutions.

name: Modelled predictions of coral reef diversity along Mozambique's coast (WCS)
summary: WCS-reported study that tested five AI models to predict marine biodiversity in Mozambique, compared them with a larger Western Indian Ocean model, and is to inform national conservation planning including identifying KBAs.

name: Mozambique Dugong & Seagrass Conservation
summary: Project run by the Marine Megafauna Foundation that maps unprotected seagrass meadows in the Bazaruto Seascape and monitors the dugongs feeding on them.

name: Mozambique Flying Labs
summary: Maputo-based organisation, listed under the name AEROMAP, offering drone mapping and geospatial analytics for natural resources, biodiversity and wildlife monitoring, plus training and workshops on drones, geospatial data and AI.

name: Mozambique Historical Vegetation Map and Red List of Ecosystems Assessment
summary: Ecosystem map and Red List assessment covering 162 ecosystems, launched by the Minister of Land and Environment in June 2024, led by WCS and funded by USAID, AFD and FFEM.

name: National Herbarium of Mozambique
summary: Herbarium founded in 1967 holding over 70,000 plant specimens, which says it supports conservation planning and publishes a GBIF dataset of endemic and near-endemic Red Listed plants.

name: Natural History Museum of Maputo
summary: Eduardo Mondlane University museum created in 1913, with insect, fish and bird collections, a DNA biobank, GBIF datasets, and a reported role in a marine resources survey of about 2,700 km of coast.

name: Net Loss: Mitigating the Impacts of Artisanal Fisheries on Whale Sharks in Mozambique
summary: Closed project on artisanal fisheries and whale sharks that planned microlight aerial surveys of net locations; its final report records gill nets between Závora and Pomene by GPS on two flights in May 2016.

name: Niassa Aviation Program
summary: Aviation programme in Niassa, launched, built and run by WCS Mozambique, covering biennial aerial surveys of wildlife and human activity and work on improving aerial survey methods, including for elephants.

name: Niassa Carnivore Project
summary: Promotes coexistence between carnivores and people in Niassa National Reserve, using cameras in 2 km grids, waterholes and villages, with planned SnapshotSafari citizen science analysis.

name: Novel Techniques to Study the Critically Endangered Marine Wildlife in Mozambique
summary: Rufford-funded project built by Jennifer Keeping using remote cameras, reporting 574 hours of footage, where machine-learning software could not reliably separate reef fish schools from megafauna, so analysis stayed manual.

name: Ocean Revolution Moçambique
summary: In 2024, it conducted eight monitoring sessions on restored mangroves and seagrass and restored 3,420 square metres of seagrass with community fisheries councils.

name: Plataforma das Áreas de Conservação
summary: Database on Mozambique's conservation areas network, developed by BIOFUND with ANAC and funded by Agence Française de Développement, whose first phase covers only some categories of area.

name: PROMOVE Biodiversidade
summary: A closed biodiversity programme managed by BIOFUND under a 13 million euro EU agreement signed in 2018, which paid for radio and remote monitoring technology in Gilé National Park.

name: Real-time elephant monitoring in Mágoè National Park
summary: Human-elephant conflict mitigation programme in Mágoè National Park; BIOFUND reported in December 2025 that 12 collared elephants were monitored in real time through EarthRanger.

name: Sistema de Informação de Biodiversidade de Moçambique
summary: Biodiversity information portal, described by DAI as the country's first, built and run by WCS with USAID and UNEP-WCMC funding, launched in 2022 and holding the national ecosystem map.

name: Sistema Nacional de Monitoria Florestal de Moçambique
summary: Forest monitoring system whose May 2021 version 1 document gives a task force of DINAF, the FNDS MRV unit and ANAC the mandate to build it, naming Collect Earth, JJ-FAST and GLAD.

name: Strengthening the Conservation of Globally Threatened Species in Mozambique through Improving Biodiversity Enforcement and Expanding Community Conservancies around Protected Areas
summary: Project to strengthen conservation of threatened species through the Conservation Areas Act, with GEF funding of USD 15,750,000 recorded in its mid-term review, which notes EarthRanger-equipped law enforcement operation rooms in both protected areas.

name: Unidade MRV do FNDS
summary: Monitoring, reporting and verification unit of FNDS, marking eight years of monitoring Mozambique's forests, with a geoportal, deforestation statistics, a REDD+ register, participatory MRV and permanent sample plots.

name: Vamizi community-based turtle monitoring programme
summary: A community-based turtle monitoring programme on Vamizi and Rongui islands since 2002 that says it has protected over 4,500 green turtle nests and plans to extend to more islands.

name: Vamizi marine research base
summary: Marine research base that Vamizi's site calls the leading one in the region, monitoring corals, reefs, marine mammals and birds, with a research partnership with Lúrio University since 2009.

name: Waterbird colony count at Lake Urema
summary: Active monitoring effort since 2014, with counts in 2014, 2019, 2021, 2023 and 2025; the April 2025 count recorded 1,040 active nests across nine species.

name: WCS Mozambique
summary: Organisation set up in 2012 to co-manage Niassa Special Reserve with the government, listing a Key Biodiversity Areas and Red Lists programme and reported by AWS to use MERMAID AI for faster data handling.

name: WildCam Gorongosa
summary: Programme run by the Gorongosa Project in which online volunteers identify animals in photos from the park's motion-activated trail cameras, with the data returned to park scientists.

name: Wildlife Recovery Amid Human Expansion in Mozambique's Gorongosa National Park
summary: Project described in November 2016 as using a systematic camera trap grid to study large mammal distribution across Gorongosa, with plans to supplement ongoing biennial helicopter surveys.

name: Wood Identification of Protected and Endangered Species in Mozambique
summary: April 2014 project that aimed to produce an atlas of anatomical features of protected and endangered tree species, using cored trees as reference material for timber identification and linked to illegal logging.

name: WWF-Mozambique
summary: Organisation that led snorkel, boat and drone field expeditions in Quirimbas National Park, including a seascape mapping survey in September 2018 and an octopus closure survey in April 2019.

name: Zinave National Park
summary: With Maputo, Banhine and Limpopo parks, ran an aerial wildlife census in October 2023 to determine wildlife populations.

name: Alte Kalköfen Bird Observatory
summary: A bird observatory at a lodge in southern Namibia whose main aim is studying nomadic species; 3,440 birds of 56 species were ringed there between 15 January and 20 April 2023.

name: Artemis Alert
summary: Windhoek-headquartered company describing a real-time human detection and alerting system against poaching, with animal trackers and a repeller, and says it launched a collaboration with Hack the Planet and Sigmotec.

name: Assessment of Water Pollution Levels and its Effect on Bat Species Richness in the Kunene Region (Namibia)
summary: January 2017 plan to build an acoustic bat call library for the Kunene region, recording echolocation calls with SM4 detectors during netting and identifying them with Kaleidoscope software.

name: Atlasing in Namibia
summary: Public-participation citizen science project and biodiversity data repository that collects species records from sightings, photos, road kills, spoor, camera traps and telemetry.

name: Biodiversity Research Centre, Namibia University of Science and Technology
summary: Biodiversity research centre run by NUST, describing itself as a network of NUST scientists, external experts and postgraduate students, and listing long-term woodland vegetation monitoring plots among its outputs.

name: Black-footed Cat Research Project Namibia
summary: Project started in 2012 to collect fine-scale black-footed cat distribution records on Namibian farmland and in protected areas; collared females were monitored by telemetry and camera traps into 2021.

name: Brown Hyena Research Project
summary: Self-described non-profit in Lüderitz whose research on the coastal Namib brown hyena population began in 1995; its projects page lists monitoring of the Elizabeth Bay and Atlas Bay clans.

name: Carnivore Tracker
summary: Mobile app for reporting carnivore sightings in Namibia, built by the Cheetah Conservation Fund and announced in a December 2015 post as collecting species, number of individuals and GPS location.

name: Characterizing Growth Forms and Estimating Biomass in Dry Miombo Woodlands Using Terrestrial Laser Scanning
summary: Study aiming to estimate above-ground biomass of dry Miombo woodlands in Namibia, with plots in two state forests guided by GEDI LiDAR footprints and data collected in March 2023.

name: Cheetah Conservation Fund
summary: Namibian conservation body, founded by Laurie Marker, whose centre is in Otjiwarongo and whose cheetah population study, running since 1990, combines monitoring with genetic analysis, including scat detection dogs.

name: Community Conservation Fund of Namibia
summary: Fund that says it financially supports Namibia's communal conservancies and community forests, and which the German embassy says handed over about NAD 31 million in grants to Kunene conservancies in October 2024.

name: Conservation Ecology of Cetaceans within the Namibian Islands Marine Protected Area
summary: Closed project, run by the Namibian Dolphin Project, that aimed to investigate the abundance and population dynamics of Heaviside's and dusky dolphins in the Namibian Islands Marine Protected Area.

name: Department of Land and Spatial Sciences, Namibia University of Science and Technology
summary: Department that is the lead affiliation of the first author of a 2025 paper comparing four supervised image classification algorithms, including Random Forest, for coastal dune change detection.

name: Department of Natural Resource Sciences, Namibia University of Science and Technology
summary: NUST department whose affiliated first and corresponding author wrote a 2024 paper, listed by OpenAlex, on a rangeland management-oriented approach to mapping dry savanna and woodland mosaics.

name: Desert Lion Conservation
summary: Non-profit working on desert-adapted lions in the northern Namib, whose main focus, according to Addax Data Science, is baseline ecological data and the study of lion behaviour.

name: Directorate of Forestry
summary: Forestry directorate whose mandate, as given by MEFT, is sustainable and participatory management of forest and botanical resources, with forest inventory, monitoring and mapping among its work; it says 48 community forests are declared.

name: Directorate of Scientific Services
summary: Scientific branch of the environment ministry, which runs it, established as a directorate in 2000, conducting wildlife research and monitoring and coordinating national programmes for species including rhinoceros, elephants and lions.

name: Elephant Alert System
summary: Programme run by Elephant Human Relations Aid which, EHRA says, uses GPS tracking to give real-time warnings of approaching elephants, helping farmers anticipate their presence.

name: Elephant-Human Relations Aid
summary: Organisation monitoring desert-adapted elephants through individual identification, camera traps and GPS tracking, with monitoring data feeding a central database tracking population trends, sex ratios and mortality.

name: Environmental Information Service
summary: Public environmental information service for Namibia, funded by the Namibian Chamber of Environment and built and run by JARO Consultancy, with biodiversity atlasing, a bird information system and a free GIS e-library.

name: Etosha Ecological Institute
summary: Institute within Etosha National Park under the Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism (2026 paper), associated with the Greater Etosha Carnivore Programme established in 2020.

name: Event Book System
summary: Programme whose Event Book database holds summary data giving a national overview of natural resource management, with materials supplied annually by a NACSO working group.

name: GAIA-Sat-IoT
summary: Closed project, run from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2024 with Leibniz-IZW as executing body, that developed a multi-sensor IoT wildlife tag including a camera, with fieldwork in Namibia and Uganda.

name: GBIF Namibia
summary: Country node listed as an associate participant in the GBIF Africa region, which endorsed the National Museum of Namibia as a GBIF data publisher.

name: Gobabeb Namib Research Institute
summary: Research and training institute that became autonomous in 1998 under a joint-venture agreement, with a 2019 brochure listing long-term monitoring such as beetle populations since 1968 and Welwitschia leaf growth since 1982.

name: Greater Etosha Carnivore Programme
summary: Carnivore programme established in 2020 by Etosha Ecological Institute, which deployed GPS collars with accelerometers and audio loggers on lions and spotted hyaenas.

name: Human-Wildlife Conflict and Wildlife Crime Project
summary: Project run by the environment ministry with Global Environment Facility funding, which UNDP Namibia says has reached over 60 communities and supports ranger teams using SMART, GPS devices and digital radios.

name: JARO Consultancy
summary: Organisation that, according to the Environmental Information Service site, maintains that service.

name: Kunene lion population survey
summary: Closed survey run by the ministry, Lion Rangers programme and Namibian Lion Trust photographed 54 of 57 adult lions in Kunene, estimating density at 0.11 per 100 km2.

name: Kuzikus Wildlife Reserve
summary: Private conservation area in the Kalahari in Namibia, a former livestock ranch, which WildDrone says reintroduced and conserves threatened species including the south-western black rhino and Cape pangolin.

name: Kyaramacan Association
summary: Association of Bwabwata National Park’s Multiple Use Area residents, established in 2005 and employing 63 staff according to NACSO, that uses the Event Book System.

name: Large Carnivore Survey, Bwabwata National Park
summary: Second large carnivore survey in Bwabwata National Park, in August 2017 after July 2014, a collaboration of Kwando Carnivore Project, Ministry of Environment and Tourism, Panthera and Kyaramacan Association.

name: Lion Rangers programme
summary: Programme founded in 2018 under the north-west Namibia Human-Lion Conflict Management Plan, which reported 12,002 patrols recorded in the 18 months after SMART began in April 2022.

name: Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism
summary: Government ministry in Windhoek whose stated mission is biodiversity conservation through sustainable resource use and tourism; UNDP Namibia says it led the process for the third NBSAP.

name: Ministry of Fisheries and Marine Resources
summary: Ministry whose management of the Namibian Islands' Marine Protected Area the Namibia Nature Foundation says it aims to help strengthen.

name: Naankuse Rapid Response Unit
summary: Created in 2008, the programme fits trapped carnivores with GPS collars, releases and intensively monitors them, and shares collar data with landowners daily.

name: NACSO
summary: Body whose Natural Resources Working Group, a voluntary association of specialists from NGOs and government ministries, mainly uses the Event Book system to monitor conservancy resources.

name: NACSO Natural Resources Working Group
summary: Working group formed by NACSO to carry out annual Event Book audits and maintain national databases; audits transfer Event Book records to a computer database.

name: Namib-Desert-v1
summary: Camera-trap image classifier built by Addax Data Science for 30 species or higher taxa in Skeleton Coast National Park, reporting 95.3% validation accuracy and 93.4% on out-of-sample 2023 images.

name: Namibia Nature Foundation
summary: Windhoek trust whose 2024 report says it facilitated a SMART data model for K9 units and reports SMART rollout to ministry and Save the Rhino Trust ranger teams.

name: Namibia University of Science and Technology
summary: University whose 2 October 2025 article reports the launch of Namibia's first official Ecosystems Map and says Prof Ben Strohbach led a research team.

name: Namibian Chamber of Environment
summary: Umbrella organisation and voluntary association supporting environmental NGOs in Namibia, per the EIS site, which lists easier access to reliable environmental information as an operational objective.

name: Namibian Dolphin Project
summary: Between 2008 and 2010, visual surveys, photo-ID and static acoustic monitoring were used to study Heaviside's and bottlenose dolphins, with Walvis Bay the primary site and Lüderitz the secondary.

name: Namibian Ecosystems Map
summary: Open dataset identifying 218 ecosystem types in Namibia, built by the SBAPP project to guide land-use planning, conservation and development; NUST reports its launch on 2 October 2025.

name: Namibian Foundation for the Conservation of Seabirds
summary: Seabird body whose census data, according to the Namibia Nature Foundation, indicate rising penguin populations on Halifax Island within the Namibian Islands’ Marine Protected Area.

name: Namibian Lion Trust
summary: Operating since January 2020 according to AfriCat UK, the trust has 12 SMART-trained Lion Guards monitoring lions using GPS collar data, trail cameras and community sightings.

name: NamibRand Nature Reserve
summary: Private non-profit nature reserve, registered in 1992, which runs an annual game count whose May 2025 report estimates wildlife numbers and biomass across ten zones.

name: NamibRand Nature Reserve annual game count
summary: Count combining road strip counts and game distribution mapping to determine game density and distribution; data from May 2025 were entered into the reserve's database and analysed.

name: National Botanical Research Institute
summary: Institute within the Directorate of Forestry under the Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism, with a bio-informatics section, a Threatened Plants Programme and the National Herbarium of Namibia.

name: National Commission on Research, Science and Technology
summary: Namibian commission that describes itself as the coordinating agency for space science, developed a National Space Science Policy launched on 5 June 2021, and has a memorandum of understanding with the Environmental Investment Fund.

name: National Forestry Inventory (Namibia)
summary: Forest inventory programme whose 1992 and 2000 inventories fed FAO's FRA 2005 report, with the 1992 data covering only the north-east and no inventory in Okavango or Kunene for security reasons.

name: National Museum of Namibia
summary: Museum whose natural science collections are, per its GBIF record, the official national reference collections for most Namibian fauna, and which publishes amphibian, entomology and scorpion datasets to GBIF.

name: National Remote Sensing Centre (Namibia)
summary: Ministry centre which, according to a September 2021 ministerial statement to Parliament, monitors fire by satellite across the whole country and produces the fire bulletin.

name: North West Game Count (Namibia)
summary: Game count in communal areas to inform conservancies and MEFT of wildlife trends; the 2024 report says five of six main species stabilised, Oryx and Kudu remaining alarmingly low.

name: Ongava Research Centre camera trap database
summary: Camera trap image database run by Ongava Research Centre, which says it has keyworded and stored over 6.5 million wildlife images since 2009, mainly from waterholes, and invites researchers to use them.

name: Plant Information System
summary: Online database, part of a BRAHMS database covering plants in Namibia and a work in progress, with fields including taxonomic status, synonyms, IUCN listing and criteria, and distribution.

name: Poverty-Oriented Support to Community Conservation in Namibia
summary: Project whose equipment, including lion collars and SMART phones for wildlife monitoring, the German embassy says was handed over to Kunene conservancies in October 2024.

name: Pro-Namib grassland multi-sensor monitoring
summary: Joint project since 2023 between a Göttingen department and NUST monitoring Pro-Namib grasslands with several sensors; plans include fusing EnMAP and PRISMA hyperspectral imagery with Sentinel-2 and Landsat.

name: Project on Strengthening Namibia's Forest and Veld Fire Detection, Monitoring, and Response System
summary: Fire project run by the environment ministry with UNDP and Korean funding, involving a geospatial fire database covering 1990–2022 and training 95 community members in 2023.

name: Raptor Conservation via Cape Griffon Vulture Telemetry in Namibia, Africa
summary: Project using satellite telemetry on Cape Griffon Vultures; a Rufford page dated 2 February 2002 described the team as trying to save the remaining birds.

name: Save the Rhino Trust
summary: Trust formed in 1982 to monitor rhinos in Kunene and Erongo, using local trackers on foot patrols, and which calls its black rhino database the longest running.

name: SAVMAP
summary: Initiative described in a 2015 Zenodo record as developing a monitoring tool for sustainable land use and black rhinoceros conservation in Namibian savanna, using drones designed at EPFL.

name: SCIONA
summary: Closed EU-funded project, led by NUST, that aimed to strengthen cross-border ecosystem management and wildlife protection in the Iona-Skeleton Coast TFCA, co-designing conservation monitoring technology over three years from February 2018.

name: Sigmotec
summary: Namibian LoRaWAN system integrator, described by Hack the Planet as supplying connectivity for its detection hardware in Namibia and named by Artemis Alert as its local IoT company.

name: SMART monitoring in the Namibian Islands' Marine Protected Area
summary: Monitoring project in the Namibian Islands' Marine Protected Area, built by the Namibia Nature Foundation and NAMCOB; the foundation's 2025 highlights say it digitised monitoring there.

name: Teltech
summary: Windhoek systems integrator established in 1950, working across avionics, communications, security, alternative energy and information technologies, and listed by Smart Parks as its technical and operational partner in Namibia.

name: The AfriCat Foundation
summary: Namibian conservation body whose Okonjima reserve camera trap network of almost 200 cameras produces about 50,000 images a month, processed with TrapTagger, with GPS data collected through LoRaWAN gateways.

name: University of Namibia
summary: Windhoek university that publishes researchers' biodiversity data on GBIF and received a 2022 JRS Biodiversity Foundation grant of $249,929 over 36 months for national spatial biodiversity data products.

name: Vultures Namibia
summary: Namibian vulture group, set up in 1997 as the local branch of the Vulture Study Group and renamed in 2005, which is unregistered as a charity and has no paid staff, according to the Environmental Information Service.

name: Walvis Bay waterbird counts
summary: Citizen-science waterbird count programme at Walvis Bay, which a March 2026 presentation reports covers 1983 to 2026 and totals 7,282,729 birds, summer and winter combined.

name: Wetland bird counts in Namibia
summary: Programme of regular wetland bird counts in Namibia, known from a 2011 article by H. Kolberg describing results for eight coastal sites including Sandwich Harbour and Walvis Bay.

name: What Factors Limit Mountain Zebra Populations in Namibia and when is Intervention Necessary for Conservation Management?
summary: Mountain zebra project in Namibia; a July 2018 page planned camera trap monitoring at five main sites, identifying individuals by stripe pattern, and passing population estimates to stakeholders.

name: Association Bwara
summary: A New Caledonian association monitoring and protecting loggerhead turtle nests at Bourail, which the Office français de la biodiversité says it added to Province Sud funding for and will support with nesting data work for three years.

name: Direction du Développement Durable des Territoires de la province Sud
summary: Province Sud directorate that the 2025–2034 Grand Lagon Sud management plan names as main lead, in charge of 59 actions (87 per cent), including continued reef and seabird nesting site monitoring.

name: Endemia
summary: Local NGO active since 2001, hosting New Caledonia’s plant Red List Authority, with species-list maps on endemia.nc, which reports halved grants for the year after May 2024.

name: Gouvernement de la Nouvelle-Calédonie
summary: Government of New Caledonia, which created the Parc naturel de la mer de Corail by decree on 23 April 2014.

name: Manta Initiative in New Caledonia
summary: Identifies rays from photos and videos and uses satellite beacons and genetic analysis, with Conservation International and the Aquarium des Lagons as collaborators, according to the Manta Trust.

name: Nereis project
summary: A closed Province Nord project, run from January 2018 to January 2019, that monitored fairy tern colonies (138 monitoring days in 2018) and trained rangers and volunteers to record tern data on a mobile application.

name: Observatoire de l'environnement en Nouvelle-Calédonie
summary: Association under the 1901 law using satellites for fire reports and forest change, reporting 274 fires detected by 31 October 2026 and announcing Kiwa-supported REPLANT'NC for revegetation data.

name: Pala Dalik
summary: Association that took part in New Caledonia's coral reef monitoring network, mainly acquiring data at nearly 45 stations according to a 2018 report, and credited in the 2024 campaign dataset.

name: Parc naturel de la mer de Corail
summary: Marine park created by decree of the Government of New Caledonia on 23 April 2014, whose four-college management committee drafts and proposes its management plan.

name: Province Nord
summary: Its 2024 services report places environmental action within its economic development and environment directorate and records ten nature wardens whose tasks included monitoring natural environments.

name: RLA Flore NC
summary: Local Red List Authority for New Caledonia's flora, run by Endemia, which says it has led the expert group since 2014 to assess extinction risk for all the flora, with 13 data deliveries counted.

name: Réseau d'Observation des Récifs Coralliens de Nouvelle-Calédonie
summary: Covers over 100 observation points monitored annually by trained volunteers supervised by scientists, according to the government portal, which says data will be updated yearly.

name: Suivi Argos des tortues marines de Nouvelle-Calédonie
summary: An Argos satellite tracking project on New Caledonia's sea turtles, built by WWF France, whose report states 86 tags were deployed and 79 complete migrations obtained.

name: Suivi participatif Acropora
summary: Participatory Acropora monitoring programme run by OEIL, which its 2024 activity report lists with the 2023 monitoring, its continuation, a January 2025 news item on Grand Sud reefs and 3 million XPF from the CCCE.

name: Vulcain
summary: Online fire map and dashboard built and run by OEIL, following the current year's fire impacts live, with a Vulcain Pro version for analyses on data back to 2001 and an alert service.

name: Association des Campements Touristiques pour l'Appui à la Gestion du Parc Régional W
summary: An association supporting W Regional Park management, described by Wildlife Angel as the local NGO with which the Brigade Félins was founded.

name: Atlas des cartes d'occupation du sol (Niger)
summary: Land cover atlas of 354 pages dated 2015, built by the CNSEE and cited in Niger's national inventory report, which says it used the atlas statistics to readjust Collect Earth area estimates from satellite images.

name: Aïr and Ténéré National Nature Reserve Protected Area Management Unit
summary: Management unit of the Aïr and Ténéré reserve that IUCN's 2025 brief says had limited monitoring capacity, though all 17 agents were trained in SMART; it uses the SMART tool.

name: Brigade Félins, Parc W Niger
summary: Ten-member wildlife protection unit founded on 1 December 2016 with the local NGO ACTAG, tasked with monitoring felid populations and behaviour in a sensitive zone of W park on the Niger side.

name: Centre National de Surveillance Ecologique et Environnementale
summary: Niger environment ministry body, created by decree in 2007, that carries out long-term ecological monitoring through nine observatories and collects vegetation data across the country each year.

name: Conseil National de l'Environnement pour un Développement Durable
summary: Niger's national environment council, whose executive secretariat is the country's Convention on Biological Diversity focal point and organised an October 2023 workshop for biodiversity data holders on the clearing-house mechanism.

name: Conservation Status and Socio-Ecological Characterization of Dama Gazelle Metapopulation in Niger
summary: Closed Rufford Foundation project in the Aïr and Ténéré reserve, dated 10 September 2021, planning ecological monitoring missions and analysis of photos from 12 camera traps installed from 2017 to 2020.

name: Contribution à la Gestion des Zones Humides
summary: Nigerien NGO created by decree in 2000 and an IUCN member since August 2025, which trained and supervised a network of 40 local informants from 2017.

name: Delegated management of the Termit and Tin-Toumma National Nature Reserve
summary: Management of a national nature reserve created by Niger in 2012 and supported by the EU, run by Noé, which estimated a fall of nearly 20% in vegetation cover in its southern part.

name: Department of Geography, Faculty of Letters and Human Sciences, Abdou Moumouni University
summary: Geography department in the Faculty of Letters and Human Sciences at Abdou Moumouni University, Niamey, whose first author's 2026 Remote Sensing paper maps land cover in an agropastoral area of Niger using Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 imagery with random forest regression.

name: Department of Life and Earth Sciences (SVT), Higher Normal School, Abdou Moumouni University
summary: Life and Earth Sciences department at the Higher Normal School of Abdou Moumouni University, Niamey, whose first author's 2025 paper studies land cover change and ecosystem degradation in Madarounfa and Gabi using Landsat remote sensing.

name: Direction de la Faune, de la Chasse et des Aires Protégées
summary: Directorate of Niger's environment ministry that holds data on wildlife species, protected areas and threatened species, and published a 2015 dry-season mammal census of W National Park on GBIF.

name: Direction Générale des Eaux et Forêts
summary: Niger's water and forests directorate general, which a GBIF record places above the fisheries and aquaculture directorate, and with which Sahara Conservation reports signing a memorandum of understanding in 2025.

name: Dispositif National de Suivi Environnemental
summary: Niger's national environmental monitoring set-up, formed from the ROSELT observatory network created in October 2000, made up of nine observatories covering most of the country's ecological diversity.

name: Drone Africa Service
summary: Civil drone company launched in 2016, reported in April 2021 to do anti-poaching surveillance in W National Park and giraffe monitoring at Kouré, with its drones designed and made in Niger.

name: Gadabedji Biosphere Reserve giraffe monitoring
summary: Giraffe monitoring in the Gadabedji reserve, where a 2020 report to the Rufford Foundation describes ecoguards using CyberTracker on smartphones and travelling about 804 km on surveys in June 2020.

name: GBIF Niger
summary: Niger's Global Biodiversity Information Facility node, listed as a country node with observer status, which has endorsed ten publishing organisations.

name: Hydro-Geo Consulting
summary: Niger-based company specialising in geospatial technologies and climate services, which Digital Earth Africa says will adopt its platforms under an agreement, including for monitoring ecosystems and water resources.

name: Institut Géographique National du Niger
summary: Niger's national mapping institute, re-created by decree in March 2023 as a public administrative body, which sells maps and satellite images and uses optical and radar imagery for deforestation monitoring.

name: Ministère de l'Hydraulique, de l'Assainissement et de l'Environnement
summary: Niamey-based ministry whose 2023 decree covers protected areas, forest infrastructure, water management and desertification, and whose statistical yearbook reports wildlife indicators such as giraffes protected and patrols in protected areas.

name: Niger Convention on Biological Diversity Clearing House Mechanism
summary: Niger's national Convention on Biological Diversity clearing-house mechanism, set up on 12 March 1999, which a 2023 workshop report says should be the central platform for biodiversity data and information.

name: Preservation of the last wild population of addax in the world
summary: Closed 2020 to 2022 Noé project in Termit and Tin-Toumma reserve that IUCN's 2025 brief reports introduced camel-based monitoring, identified addax sub-groups and suffered weather-related drone failures.

name: Programme de suivi et de conservation des vautours (Niger)
summary: Active vulture monitoring programme run by Sahara Conservation, whose fourth quarter 2025 report records eight active Rüppell's vulture nests and eight active Egyptian vulture nests.

name: Project to secure the habitat of large carnivores' prey in the W National Park
summary: Closed 2020 to 2022 project in W National Park, run by COGEZOH, that set up an informant early warning system and a conflict database; IUCN's brief describes it as reducing human-wildlife conflict.

name: Reversing the decline of threatened Saharan wildlife in the Aïr and Ténéré National Nature Reserve
summary: Closed 2021 to 2024 project in the Aïr and Ténéré reserve, run by Sahara Conservation, which trained 17 agents in SMART, deployed 40 camera traps and reported 17 patrols covering over 8,500 km.

name: Sahara Conservation
summary: International non-profit conserving Saharan and Sahelian wildlife, reporting updated biodiversity data from two 2025 Termit massif missions and a memorandum with Niger's water and forests directorate.

name: Sahel Wood Energy project
summary: Niger-led programme started in April 2022, financed by AFD and FFEM grants totalling 8 million euros, which FFEM said would use weekly Sentinel-2 images to identify new deforestation to the nearest hectare.

name: Saving West Africa's last giraffe: increasing conservation, management and range in support of the Niger National Strategy
summary: Closed 2018 to 2020 Giraffe Conservation Foundation project whose training and four giraffe translocations were reported in IUCN's 2025 brief, alongside a reserve population of 15.

name: SPWA-BD: Integrating the Sustainable Management of Faunal Corridors into Niger's Protected Area System
summary: A GEF-funded project closed on 20 April 2021, with UNDP as implementing agency, aimed to expand Niger's Saharan protected areas and establish faunal corridors.

name: Support for the conservation of the last populations of West African giraffe in Harikanassou and Kouré
summary: Closed 2021 to 2023 project run by COGEZOH using photo-identification monitoring, which counted giraffe rising from 194 in 2021 to 335 in 2023, according to IUCN's 2025 brief.

name: Supporting the conservation of West African lions in W National Park
summary: Closed 2019 to 2021 project in Niger, run by ACTAG, that collected daily telemetry on eight lions and built a database on lion distribution, diet, behaviour, threats and conflicts in W National Park.

name: Système d'Information sur les Terres Restaurées
summary: Presented in 2020 as a georeferenced database of restored sites, Niger's restored-land information system had 10 geospatial analysts participate in WRI and environment ministry training.

name: Unité de Gestion de l'Aire Protégée de la Réserve de Biosphère de Gadabedji
summary: Works with Sahara Conservation, whose fourth quarter 2025 report says two unit agents monitor reintroduced giraffe and identification data will be added to GiraffeSpotter.

name: Université Abdou Moumouni
summary: Public university in Niamey, founded in 1971 and renamed in 1992, whose Department of Geography was the first author's affiliation on a 2026 paper mapping land cover in an agropastoral area of Niger from satellite imagery.

name: Université Dan Dicko Dankoulodo de Maradi
summary: Public university in Maradi, Niger, created by ordinance in 2010, which was the first author's affiliation on a 2022 paper on the spatial distribution of the West African giraffe for conservation in Niger.

name: Université Hummay Salamna de Diffa
summary: Created on 19 August 2014 in Diffa, Niger, this university has authors studying Anogeissus leiocarpa distribution through ensemble modelling and bushfires in the Gadabedji Biosphere Reserve.

name: Urgent Addax Aerial Survey in Niger
summary: Closed 2016 project in Niger, run by Sahara Conservation, with the immediate goal of locating the remaining addax and carrying out priority actions to conserve the species in its last stronghold.

name: West African giraffe tracking in Niger
summary: Giraffe Conservation Foundation project, with partners, that fitted 16 West African giraffe in Niger with solar-powered GPS satellite units, as part of its Africa-wide Twiga Tracker programme.

name: A.P. Leventis Ornithological Research Institute
summary: Run by the University of Jos in Laminga, the institute runs the Nigerian Bird Atlas Project; GBIF reports over two decades of biodiversity data collection.

name: Abiola Ajimobi Technical University
summary: Affiliated authors include the first author of a 2025 paper on AI prediction of tropical forest carbon stocks and co-authors of a 2026 coastal wetland vulnerability dataset and code.

name: Adekunle Ajasin University
summary: University listed, with NASRDA, for the first author of a 2026 paper that names deep learning as its method for analysing deforestation.

name: Africa Nature Investors Foundation
summary: Nigerian not-for-profit co-managing Gashaka Gumti and Okomu with the national park service, reporting SMART use, and publishing a GBIF survey across 86 Gashaka Gumti pentads, January 2025–July 2026.

name: African Regional Centre for Space Science and Technology Education - English
summary: Centre at Obafemi Awolowo University in Ile-Ife, whose affiliated authors OpenAlex lists on a 2026 paper on deep learning for analysing deforestation frontiers.

name: African Regional Centre for Space Science and Technology Education in English
summary: Centre inaugurated in Nigeria in 1998, affiliated to the UN Office for Outer Space Affairs and supervised by NASRDA, whose mandate includes remote sensing and GIS; UNOOSA counts 24 postgraduate diplomas awarded in 2025.

name: African Regional Institute for Geospatial Information Science and Technology
summary: Intergovernmental institution hosted in Nigeria within Obafemi Awolowo University in Ile-Ife, training in remote sensing and other geospatial fields, and partnering with Digital Earth Africa.

name: AG Leventis Foundation
summary: Foundation that, according to a June 2019 IITA article, had supported bird monitoring on the IITA campus for the preceding 30 years.

name: Agro-Climatic Resilience in Semi-Arid Landscapes
summary: Six-year World Bank-funded landscape restoration project in northern Nigeria, run by the Federal Ministry of Environment and described as covering 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with a reported NDVI results indicator.

name: Ahmadu Bello University
summary: The university has an affiliated first author of a 2023 machine learning forest mapping paper and publishes a GBIF dataset of plant specimens from its Botany Herbarium.

name: AIML-BioDoc: AI and Machine Learning Imaging Applications for Bioresource Identification and Documentation in Nigeria
summary: A Nigerian project led by the National Biotechnology Research and Development Agency that uses supervised and deep learning, including convolutional neural networks, to identify and document bioresources from images, drawing on NACGRAB's plant genetic resources.

name: Bauchi State Government (Yankari and Lame-Burra Game Reserves)
summary: State government that took back management of the 2,244 km² Yankari Game Reserve from the National Parks Service in 2006, signed a 2014 MoU with WCS to co-manage it, and is supported by WACN at Lame-Burra.

name: Biakwan Light Green Initiative
summary: Forest restoration initiative launched in 2016 after securing international funding, involving selected community youths in managing and restoring degraded forest in affected Afi communities in Cross River State.

name: Biodiversity checklists of the IITA Forest Center
summary: Open access dataset of biodiversity checklists for the IITA Forest Center, offered on the portal as CSV files with a summary and data dictionary.

name: BirdPlus
summary: Project whose development, according to a paper by the Nigerian Bird Atlas Project team, was supported by that project's data managers.

name: Blockchain-Based Platform to Curb Illegal Logging and Enhance Traceability in Nigeria's Forest Product Supply Chains
summary: Proposed project on forest product traceability in Nigeria, listed in the 2026 National Research Fund with a 36-month duration and a recommended 45,045,525 naira, naming Amusa Tajudeen Okekunle as researcher.

name: Capacity Advancement for the Nigeria node of GBIF
summary: Closed project led by Omokafe Alaba Ugbogu and funded by GBIF, the European Union and three Nigerian bodies, which digitised herbarium, insect and park animal records.

name: Centre for Ecological and Community Development
summary: Active organisation that says it is a registered Nigerian civil society organisation, offers ecological data and biodiversity indexes on its site, and says it promotes ICT for land use mapping and carbon finance verification.

name: Centre for Education, Research and Conservation of Primates and Nature
summary: Non-profit founded in Nigeria in 1995; its 2010 grant profile describes a partnership with Iko Esai village to conserve 400 ha of community forest, with logging and primate hunting banned in a further 3,000 ha.

name: Centre for Environment, Human Rights and Development
summary: Active organisation that says it has monitored seedlings from HYPREP's first mangrove restoration phase with other stakeholders, and that it organised training for community oil spill monitors in 2016.

name: Chad Basin National Park
summary: A 2,258 square kilometre national park in Borno and Yobe states, where the parks chief told Mongabay in October 2026 that research, monitoring and surveillance continue while some ecotourism is suspended.

name: Community Forest Management and Livelihood Improvement Project
summary: Project launched in 2023 as a three-year effort across eight buffer communities around Cross River National Park, built by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and the Nature and Biodiversity Conservation Union; current status unknown.

name: Conservation Association of the Mbe Mountains
summary: Association that has managed the Mbe Mountains (about 85 km2, traditionally owned by nine communities) since 2007, set up with WCS help, which also worked with it on a management plan and boundary demarcation.

name: Conservation of biodiversity and sustainable use of a lowland forest mosaic landscape in Ogun, Edo, Delta and Ondo States
summary: Active project in Ogun, Edo, Delta and Ondo States, run by the Federal Ministry of Environment with GEF funding, where GEF lists a project grant of 3,502,968.

name: Cross River gorilla genetic population assessment
summary: Project described by WCS, in partnership with the WCS Nigeria Program and the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology; its current status is unknown.

name: Cross River Gorilla initiative
summary: Active initiative led and run by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation, including a five-year graduate scholarship programme started in 2022 at the University of Calabar, with trail cameras recording gorillas in 2024.

name: Cross River National Park
summary: Active national park where, in a July 2021 interview, the Conservator-General said drones had not been deployed and the park used cyber trackers, camera traps, GPS and rangers.

name: Cross River State Environment and Carbon Emission Board
summary: Board listed by CEPF as grantee of the Obudu Plateau watershed restoration project, which aimed to restore a 10.55 km stretch of watershed by planting trees on both sides of the watercourse.

name: Cross River State Forestry Commission
summary: State body named in Nigeria's sub-national forest reference level submission as playing a crucial role in forest conservation, in a state UN-REDD reports has a forest monitoring system with a GIS laboratory.

name: Digitization of Species of Odonata (Damselflies and Dragonflies) of Southern Nigeria
summary: Project led by Kehinde Kemabonta and funded by GBIF and the University of Lagos, which had digitised 3,105 dragonfly and damselfly individuals at the time of the record, with DNA barcoding.

name: EcoGIS
summary: Active organisation that offers farm-level deforestation alerts and AI scoring of compliance, climate and quality risks, says its pilot is live in Cross River State, and partners with Esri.

name: Ecological Project Office
summary: Active office whose mandates cover reducing ecological problems, managing the fund and releasing funds for projects.

name: Ecology and conservation of the white-bellied pangolin in Cross River
summary: Closed project that in June 2020 planned four months of telemetry on 10 adult white-bellied pangolins in Cross River, led by Charles Agbor Emogor with University of Washington researchers.

name: Edo State Forestry Commission
summary: State commission created by a bill passed in November 2022 and inaugurated on 7 June 2023; Edo State reported 49 forest reserves in October 2023 and developed a ten-year strategy for them.

name: Ekiti State Government (Ise Forest Conservation Area)
summary: State government that, Mongabay reported in April 2020, issued an executive order establishing a conservation area within the Ise Forest Reserve, where about 20 Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzees were believed to survive.

name: Ekuri Initiative
summary: NGO set up by the Ekuri community, which began community forestry in 1992 and owns 33,600 ha of community forest in Cross River State, listed as the Ekuri ICCA.

name: Esai Conservation Organization
summary: The Iko Esai community formed and registered this organisation with Cross River State, and a CEPF-funded project aimed to strengthen the community’s capacity to manage 20,000 ha of forest.

name: Expanding the visibility of the Lagos Herbarium through digitization and mobilization of plant specimen data
summary: Closed project led by Temitope Onuminya that aimed to digitise and publish herbarium data and reported about 15,000 records, with completion noted in a University of Lagos report.

name: Federal Department of Forestry
summary: A department run by the Federal Ministry of Environment that advises on Nigeria's forest resources and undertakes periodic assessment surveys, and supported a January 2026 workshop in Abuja on institutionalising the national forest monitoring system.

name: Federal Ministry of Environment
summary: Active ministry whose forestry department sets biodiversity and wildlife policy and runs periodic forest surveys, and which in February 2026 was reported validating Nigeria's 7th national report to the Convention on Biological Diversity.

name: Federal University Birnin Kebbi
summary: Active university whose authors wrote a 2026 paper on plant species classification, developing a multimodal Swin Transformer using PlantCLEF images.

name: Forest Herbarium Ibadan
summary: Active dataset holding about 101,000 specimens of vascular plants and cryptogams, mainly from Nigeria.

name: Forest Insect Museum Ibadan
summary: Active dataset, run by the Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria, holding about 40,123 forest insect specimens of 1,512 species.

name: Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria
summary: Active institute in Ibadan, supervised by the Federal Ministry of Environment and GBIF's node institution for Nigeria, with a Data Science and Machine Learning Unit and a herbarium of about 101,000 specimens.

name: Gashaka Gumti camera trap survey
summary: Active survey for which ANI planned 100 camera traps across the whole park in its 2022 report, and which Mongabay reports deployed cameras and recorded new chimpanzee groups.

name: Gashaka Gumti National Park
summary: Active park in Adamawa and Taraba states, described in 2022 as Nigeria's largest, run by the National Park Service and ANI, with planned monitoring using ranger patrol data, satellite imagery and camera traps.

name: Gbanraun Community Conservation Association
summary: Community-based organisation through which local communities manage the Gbanraun community conserved area (ICCA), alongside the Kokoloama area, which is managed in the same way.

name: GBIF Nigeria
summary: Active programme that is the GBIF country node for Nigeria, an associate participant, led by Omokafe Alaba Ugbogu, with 17 endorsed publishers.

name: GBIF Node for Nigeria
summary: Active programme named in a 2023 University of Lagos report, which refers to Prof. Omokafe Ugbogu as the GBIF Node for Nigeria.

name: Geotek Water Solutions
summary: Company that describes AI-powered, IoT-driven water monitoring systems, and says it uses sensor networks and AI to monitor water quality and detect contamination.

name: Hydrocarbon Pollution Remediation Project
summary: Active project led by Nenibarini Zabbey that says it has launched marine worm monitoring and a bird survey alongside mangrove monitoring, with eDNA and carbon stock work upcoming.

name: IITA Forest Center
summary: Forest programme run by IITA, set up in 2015 to manage the Ibadan campus forest, which ran quarterly bird surveys with APLORI and has Leventis funding.

name: Implementation of the biodiversity information and data system for coastal ecosystems in Nigeria
summary: Closed, EU-funded project on a biodiversity data system for Nigerian coastal ecosystems, led by Oluwatoyin Ogundipe, which reported about 30,000 records mobilised and 158 participants trained.

name: Informatics and ICT Resource Center, Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria
summary: A centre run by the Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria, with a unit applying AI to forestry and environmental research that can support forest health monitoring and species identification.

name: Integrated Mangrove Association of Nigeria
summary: Association created and registered during a CEPF-funded project, with members in each of the 15 participating communities, which supervised implementation of the participatory forest management plan for the mangrove forests.

name: International Institute of Tropical Agriculture
summary: Research institute headquartered at Ibadan that runs the IITA Forest Center, and reported in June 2019 that its 1000-hectare campus supported about 270 bird species.

name: Kainji Lake National Park
summary: A 5,382 square kilometre national park in Kwara and Niger states, where WACN, under a memorandum with the National Park Service, deploys camera traps and field monitoring systems, and where the parks chief said monitoring continues.

name: Kano Zoological and Wildlife Management Agency
summary: In March 2021 the agency’s managing director announced that Falgore Game Reserve would admit only its management and sought funding for patrol equipment around the reserve.

name: KHAD EarthSense
summary: Company incorporated in Nigeria that describes a validated prototype processing the satellite archive over the Niger Delta, with a classifier trained on reference sites to detect oil contamination.

name: Kokoloama Community Conservation Association
