summary: Community-based organisation through which local communities manage the Kokoloama community conserved area (ICCA), alongside the Gbanraun area, which is managed in the same way.

name: Lead City University
summary: University affiliated with first authors of a 2026 marine conservation paper on underwater vehicle object detection and a 2026 coastal wetland vulnerability data and code release.

name: Lekki Urban Forestry and Animal Shelter Initiative
summary: Founded in 2013 to preserve urban habitats, this NGO has a Nature Park on its 20 ha farm-forest in Lekki, Lagos, fully operational since November 2016.

name: Leventis Foundation Nigeria
summary: Foundation that, according to the University of Jos, set up APLORI in 2002 and remains its principal funder.

name: National Agency for the Great Green Wall
summary: Agency established by Act of Parliament in 2015 that set up a GIS laboratory at its Abuja headquarters for monitoring and evaluation.

name: National Biotechnology Research and Development Agency
summary: Agency that reports a strategic goal of a national genomics and bioinformatics repository to support the Nigeria BioGenome Project, and is linked as a partner of the African BioGenome Project.

name: National Bureau of Statistics
summary: Statistics body that, according to the land accounts report, led a multi-agency technical working group.

name: National Centre for Remote Sensing, Jos
summary: Centre in Jos, approved in 1998 with a satellite ground receiving station at Kerang, mandated to support remote sensing and GIS research, local resource inventories and environmental monitoring data; run by NASRDA.

name: National Forest Monitoring System of Nigeria
summary: Forest monitoring programme that FAO's GFOI page describes as partly developed, with a satellite land monitoring system and a forest inventory, built by the Nigeria REDD+ Programme with UN-REDD support.

name: National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency
summary: Agency established by Act in 2006 under the Federal Ministry of Environment, responsible for monitoring and responding to oil spills, which runs the Nigerian Oil Spill Monitor and says it developed a shoreline sensitivity map.

name: National Park Service of Nigeria
summary: Federal body established by decree in 1991 to protect and manage vegetation and wildlife in seven national parks covering about 20,156 square kilometres, which has published Kainji Lake bird records on GBIF.

name: National Space Research and Development Agency
summary: Space agency established in 1999, based in Abuja, that lists NigeriaSat-1, NigeriaSat-X and NigeriaSat-2, holds satellite data over Nigeria under its Act, and said in November 2025 it had authorisation to launch four new satellites.

name: Niger Delta mangrove oil spill mapping with AI and Earth observation
summary: Project, published in Remote Sensing in 2025 and led by the University of Galway, that mapped oil pipelines and damage from radar data and estimated mangrove mortality for 2016 to 2024.

name: Nigeria Key Biodiversity Areas National Coordination Group
summary: Coordination group whose fifth annual meeting, on 4 April 2025 in Abuja with seventeen stakeholders, was reported to list three newly confirmed global Key Biodiversity Area sites in Nigeria.

name: Nigeria Land Accounts
summary: Dataset the report calls the first land accounts for Nigeria and for Kaduna and Nasarawa states, based on satellite-derived land cover maps for 2015 and 2020, built by the World Bank and led by the statistics bureau.

name: Nigeria Mangrove Restoration Platform
summary: A community-led carbon sequestration project restoring 5,000 hectares of mangrove within a 50,000-hectare project area, which says it combines traditional ecological knowledge with modern monitoring technology and presents land classification maps of progress.

name: Nigeria national traceability and deforestation-free verification framework
summary: Proposed framework established by an agreement signed in 2025, with the National Space Research and Development Agency as a partner.

name: Nigeria national traceability system for EU Deforestation Regulation compliance
summary: Proposed national traceability system for EU Deforestation Regulation compliance, for which the agriculture ministry reported in November 2025 that NASRDA would provide satellite imagery and monitoring.

name: Nigeria REDD+ Programme
summary: Programme that the ministry says developed a National REDD+ Strategy, a Forest Reference Emission Level, a National Forest Monitoring System and a Safeguard Information System, led by Moses Modey Ama, with Cross River State selected for a nested approach.

name: Nigerian Bird Atlas Project
summary: Citizen science programme running since late 2015 that maps Nigerian bird species using the Birdlasser app, with a published dataset covering May 2015 to January 2022 and over 320 observers reported in a team paper.

name: Nigerian Conservation Foundation
summary: Non-governmental conservation body founded in 1980 and registered as a charitable trust in 1982, which takes part in the International Waterbird Census, reports camera trap and bird monitoring, and is linked as a BirdLife partner.

name: Nigerian Institute for Oceanography and Marine Research
summary: Marine research institute in Lagos, now under the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, which partnered with MarCNoWA on a workshop about Earth observation tools for oil spill and ship detection.

name: Nigerian Marine Biodiversity Reference Library
summary: Project that describes itself as an initiative to build a voucher-linked molecular barcode database for Gulf of Guinea species, and says it is contributing to a preliminary reference library from dominant lagoon taxa.

name: Nigerian Montane Forest Project
summary: Project whose page says its conservation and restoration work rests on a herbarium, weather station, vegetation and phenology data and photo points.

name: Nigerian Oil Spill Monitor
summary: Platform for managing and sharing oil spill data, built on paper Joint Investigation Visit records, run by NOSDRA and built by Stakeholder Democracy Network, with a warning that company data can be incomplete.

name: NigeriaSat
summary: Earth observation satellite programme whose NigeriaSat-1 satellite project began in 2001, built by NASRDA and Surrey Satellite Technology Limited.

name: Nnamdi Azikiwe University
summary: University with an author on a 2026 review of explainable machine learning for species delimitation in Senna, whose herbarium records appear in a GBIF dataset published by the Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria.

name: Obafemi Awolowo University
summary: Active Nigerian university, selected in November 2017 for a GMES and Africa grant for the West Africa water and natural resources service, and partner of the African regional space science centre.

name: Office of the Surveyor General of the Federation
summary: National surveying and mapping authority that describes itself as the apex body in its field, with responsibility for the country's geospatial information and a photogrammetry and remote sensing department.

name: Ogun State Ministry of Forestry
summary: State ministry, by its own account created from the Ministry of Agriculture in August 2004, whose listed duties include forest inventory and maintaining its electronic database.

name: Okomu National Park
summary: Active national park run by the National Park Service, described in 2014 as Nigeria's smallest of seven, whose rangers were trained in SMART by SCERA and patrol using it.

name: Ondo State Agroforestry geolocation campaign
summary: Active campaign, built by Ondo State Government with Open Foris, which the Ground site describes as state-led geolocation of cocoa and oil palm in forest reserves.

name: Pandrillus Foundation
summary: The foundation began community patrols around Afi Mountain in 1993 and helped devise a plan before the state created the roughly 100 km² sanctuary in May 2000.

name: Pangolino
summary: Nigerian conservation non-profit, as described by Conservation Allies, working on two pangolin species in Southeast Nigeria, where its field surveys build baseline data.

name: Promoting Integrated Landscape Management and Sustainable Food Systems in the Niger Delta, Nigeria
summary: Active GEF-funded project on integrated landscape management and food systems in the Niger Delta, with FAO reporting May 2026 workshops in Cross River and Ondo States reviewing progress on geo-referencing, GIS laboratories and REDD+ monitoring.

name: ReforestAI
summary: Forest monitoring system using AI, embedded systems and IoT sensors; TechCabal reports its builders' $10,000 Slingshot Challenge grant in 2025, while Hackster reported no forest deployment.

name: RESLARC
summary: Nigerian organisation that says it was founded in January 1995 and specialises in geospatial technologies and Earth observation, with a Bio-Eco company focused on biodiversity monitoring.

name: Saving Seret's butterfly ray
summary: Active project led by Kehinde Adelakun that plans to record bycatch at landing sites, monitor catches and map habitats.

name: Small Mammal Conservation Organization
summary: Organisation that says it supports cave patrols monitoring disturbance and documenting colony status at priority roost sites.

name: Society for Women and Vulnerable Groups Empowerment
summary: Organisation listed by CEPF as grantee of the Ukpom-Okom community mangrove project, which aimed to restore 10 ha of degraded mangrove and protect about 50 ha of intact community mangrove reserve.

name: Stakeholder Democracy Network
summary: Described by The Guardian Nigeria as a UK-based NGO, focused on the Niger Delta, that has led independent monitoring of the Ogoniland clean-up and uses satellite observations in its Gas Flare Tracker.

name: Strengthening Nigeria's 30x30 Progress through Ecological Connectivity, Terrestrial and Marine OECMs, and Protected Area Management Effectiveness
summary: Active project run by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation, funded by the High Ambition Coalition for Nature and People, to map priority terrestrial and marine OECMs and assess protected area management effectiveness.

name: StrikeClimate
summary: Organisation that says it turns satellite data, AI and IoT sensors into early warnings, risk maps and dashboards, and lists deforestation monitoring, carbon credit and ecosystem monitoring work.

name: Sustainability and Conservation Education for Rural Areas
summary: Active organisation based in Kubwa, Abuja, that organised SMART training for rangers at Okomu National Park and gave the park motorcycles for forest patrols.

name: SW/Niger Delta Forest Project
summary: Organisation working in the Apoi Creek forests, home of the Niger Delta red colobus, listing research and monitoring, with plans for 30 new camera traps and training 24 rangers in SMART.

name: Tai Solarin University of Education
summary: University with an author listed by OpenAlex on one paper; the entry gives no other detail.

name: Tertiary Education Trust Fund
summary: Active Abuja-based funder whose National Research Fund awarded close to 4.25 billion naira to 158 projects in 2024 and whose 2025 call includes a terrestrial ecosystems theme.

name: TETFund Centre for Biodiversity Conservation and Ecosystem Management
summary: Centre run by the University of Lagos, named first in the project partnership.

name: The Okomu Oil Palm Company Plc
summary: Oil palm company that says it keeps about 10% of its total area for conservation, monitored through an HCV officer, ecoguards, quarterly reports and field studies.

name: Tropical Research and Conservation Center
summary: Nonprofit launched in June 2001 that facilitates indigenous conservation in Akwa Ibom; it began mangrove regeneration in coastal communities in March 2018, and the work was ongoing in October 2022.

name: University of Calabar
summary: University at Etagbor, Calabar, with 20 datasets on GBIF; three graduate students began studying Cross River gorillas there in 2023 under an initiative, and their trail cameras recorded the animals.

name: University of Ibadan
summary: University with an author listed by OpenAlex on one paper; the entry gives no other detail.

name: University of Ilorin
summary: University named as a collaborator on a study; the entry gives no other detail.

name: University of Jos
summary: University that an institute is part of; the entry gives no other detail.

name: University of Lagos
summary: University with 63 datasets on GBIF, including a CC BY 4.0 checklist of marine fishes and shellfishes of Nigerian coastal waters, and a partner of the Partnership for Observation of the Global Ocean.

name: University of Nigeria Herbarium
summary: Herbarium founded in 1962 at Nsukka, funded by the International Association of Plant Taxonomy, which says digitisation began in 2022 and that over 4,000 collections are digitised.

name: Usmanu Danfodiyo University
summary: University whose authors wrote a 2025 paper on neural network height-diameter models for trees outside forest.

name: WCS Nigeria
summary: Programme run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, supporting SMART-based ranger patrols in Okwangwo Division, Cross River National Park, and monitoring Cross River gorillas mainly through these patrols.

name: WCS Nigeria Program
summary: Programme run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, supporting SMART-based patrols in Okwangwo, monitoring Cross River gorillas mainly through patrols, and releasing Afi Mountain camera trap images in 2021.

name: West African Conservation Network
summary: A Nigeria-based not-for-profit conservation organisation that signed a 31-year memorandum with the Nigeria National Park Service in October 2023 and deploys camera traps and field monitoring at Kainji Lake National Park to set baseline data.

name: Yankari Game Reserve camera trap monitoring
summary: Camera trap project of unknown status, built by the WCS Nigeria Program; in October 2017 WCS reported that its Yankari Game Reserve cameras had recorded a leopard.

name: Assessment of the Actual and Potential Carbon Stock of Tropical Forest Fragments in the Protected Landscape of Miraflor-Moropotente in Northwest Nicaragua
summary: Closed Rufford-funded project led by Oscar Lanuza; its May 2023 final report lists 40 long-term forest monitoring plots and a tree species checklist, with a carbon map in preparation.

name: Bluefields Indian & Caribbean University
summary: University named in a 2021 report to the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund as having carried out a tapir conservation project, whose study used camera traps.

name: Cetacean Conservation Project of Nicaragua
summary: Closed four-year research project (2016 to 2020) at Padre Ramos and San Juan del Sur, funded by the Rufford Foundation, using land and boat surveys and photo-identification to create catalogues.

name: Conserving a Newly-Discovered Population of the Critically Endangered Robber Frog Craugastor ranoides in Nicaragua
summary: An MBZ Fund-supported project on a critically endangered robber frog population, found in one small stream on Lake Nicaragua's southern shore, aiming to establish baseline data on its size, demographics and breeding.

name: Cooperativa de Profesionales Masangni, R.L.
summary: A professional cooperative named as grantee in a Rufford final report, which says it would buy equipment, train community forest enterprise staff in data collection, and support monitoring plots and transects, with objectives marked fully achieved.

name: Developing and implementing conservation measures for the Lungless salamander (Ometepe)
summary: An MBZ Fund-supported project that planned to set up baseline data on the Ometepe lungless salamander's conservation status, build a participatory monitoring system and develop local capacity for amphibian monitoring.

name: Diversity and Ecology of Native Bees in Southwest Nicaragua
summary: A closed Rufford-funded bee survey at Paso del Istmo that reports collecting 1,400 specimens over 204 sampling days across 16 months, and setting up an iNaturalist project for georeferenced bee records.

name: Educating People for a Local Monitoring Program of the Cana Coral Reef Ecosystem at the Corn Island, Nicaragua
summary: Project from 2010 aiming to set up long-term community-involved ecological monitoring for the Corn Islands Marine Reserve; preliminary surveys chose sites and a baseline, and photo monitoring was stopped for the moment.

name: Empoderamiento de las comunidades para la conservación del danto (Tapirus bairdii) en el Parque Ecológico Municipal Humedales de Mahogany
summary: Tapir conservation project run by Bluefields Indian & Caribbean University and funded by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund; a 2020 study used nine Bushnell camera traps to detect tapir presence.

name: Establishing a Monitoring Baseline for Species and Key Biodiversity Areas in Nicaragua
summary: A closed CEPF-funded project, running from late 2006 to August 2007, intended to help identify globally significant biodiversity sites in Nicaragua by collecting data on species conservation.

name: Establishing Ecological Monitoring Systems to Support Sustainable Management of Indigenous Community Forests in Nicaragua's North Atlantic Autonomous Region
summary: Closed Rufford-funded project to set up monitoring in the SIPBAA and Layasiksa community forests; the final report says forest fire monitoring was developed and the community wanted permanent sample plots.

name: Filling Spatial and Ecological Information Gaps in Threatened Forest-sensitive Bat Species and Endangered Ecosystems in Nicaragua
summary: Active Rufford-funded project, running from August 2025 to an expected October 2026 end; bat capture and acoustic surveys covered 77 sites in the 2026 field season, with faecal samples intended for DNA reference material.

name: Fundación Amigos del Río San Juan
summary: Organisation named in CEPF's final completion report for the Indio Maíz management plan project, which refers to a biological monitoring programme set up within that project.

name: Implementing the Indio Maiz Biological Reserve Management Plan
summary: Closed project run by Fundación Amigos del Río San Juan from June 2006 to December 2007; its report says a biological monitoring system was designed and in operation.

name: Instituto Nacional Forestal
summary: A Nicaraguan forest institute that, per MARENA's SNMRV design document, is responsible for updating the National Forest Inventory, and whose 2007 to 2008 inventory results the sixth CBD national report cites.

name: Instituto Nicaragüense de Estudios Territoriales
summary: A Nicaraguan territorial studies institute offering IDE-INETER spatial data infrastructure, whose site reported maintenance of the national geodetic reference frame on 13 May 2025.

name: Ministerio del Ambiente y los Recursos Naturales
summary: Nicaragua's environment ministry administers protected areas under Law 290, according to a MARENA resolution, builds SNMRV and began community monitoring through ENDE-REDD+.

name: Molecular Biology Center, Universidad Centroamericana
summary: A Managua research centre at the Universidad Centroamericana, known here because the first author of an OpenAlex-listed paper on Nicaraguan dry-corridor river macroinvertebrates and DNA barcoding gives it as an affiliation.

name: Programa de Monitoreo y Anidación de Tortugas Marinas (Paso Pacifico)
summary: A sea turtle nesting monitoring programme, begun in 2008 with fourteen rangers, which a May 2016 report says marked 133 turtles with metal or PIT tags on three beaches from 2013 to 2015.

name: Programa ENDE-REDD+
summary: MARENA-run programme that began preparing an inter-institutional platform in 2015; an October 2019 Mombacho workshop trained staff in biodiversity monitoring, using linear transects to identify 27 bird species.

name: Sistema de monitoreo de puntos de calor (MARENA)
summary: A MARENA heat point monitoring system described in a 2019 presentation, which says satellite sensors provide a very reliable approximation of fire occurrence.

name: Sistema Nacional de Información Ambiental (Nicaragua)
summary: MARENA-run national environmental information system which, per the CBD country profile, collects and gives access to indicators, with national biodiversity indicators monitored every two years.

name: Sistema Nacional de Monitoreo, Reporte y Verificación
summary: A Nicaraguan monitoring, reporting and verification system designed with technical teams from MARENA, INETER, INAFOR, MAG and INTA, each responsible for part of it.

name: Universidad Centroamericana
summary: A university whose Molecular Biology Center and Institute of Interdisciplinary Research in Natural Sciences are the listed affiliations of all authors of an OpenAlex-listed DNA barcoding survey of a dry-corridor river.

name: Universidad Nacional Autónoma de Nicaragua, Managua
summary: University whose professor and researcher led a Forest Ecosystems study, described by CREAF, that set up 40 permanent plots in Miraflor-Moropotente and combined fieldwork with satellite imagery and machine learning to estimate carbon.

name: WCS Hawksbill Project, Pearl Cays
summary: A WCS-run hawksbill turtle nest monitoring project in the Pearl Cays, which reported over 20 nests excavated in the 2015 hatching season, with success rates of 46 to 93%, and school visits.

name: WCS Jaguar Conservation Program in Nicaragua
summary: A WCS-run jaguar programme in Nicaragua, whose coordinator Fabricio Díaz Santos is said in a February 2020 release to have led jaguar surveys and set up the country's largest network of protected forest plots.

name: AccellARISE
summary: A five-year upgrade of the ARISE infrastructure, funded by a 3.2-million-euro NWO grant, that lets Naturalis and the Westerdijk Fungal Biodiversity Institute identify small and hidden Dutch species faster.

name: Acorn
summary: Initiative presented among Rabobank's carbon initiatives. It uses remote sensing to give smallholder farmers access to climate finance through the carbon market.

name: Agrarische Natuurvereniging Waddenvogels
summary: Partnership of the farmers' nature associations of Schiermonnikoog, Ameland and Terschelling, with about 150 members, which says it manages over 2,400 hectares, mainly for meadow birds.

name: AI Nature
summary: Naturalis services for automatic species identification, including the Nature Identification API covering about 45,000 European taxa and AI analyses for DIOPSIS insect cameras.

name: Airborne eDNA pilot in the Reevediep
summary: Pilot in which Witteveen+Bos, EcoPulse, TNO and Datura test airborne eDNA for identifying plant and animal species in the Reevediep waterway near Kampen.

name: Altenburg & Wymenga
summary: Dutch firm working with Aviadrone and Vliegend.nl on the Spectra project to improve observation of animals, vegetation and birds in Noordoost-Fryslân.

name: Amsterdam Water Supply Dunes automated camera network
summary: Network of solar-powered wildlife cameras in the Amsterdam Water Supply Dunes that transmits images wirelessly. Its web portal can send images to AI platforms for species identification. Developed by University of Amsterdam researchers with Waternet.

name: AntScout
summary: App and platform that identifies ant species from photos with AI, with a species database, observation maps and predictions of nuptial flights, aimed at ant keepers.

name: Anugerah services
summary: Dutch maker of bat detectors and LED buckets for moth recording that also helps identify bat sounds.

name: Apodemus Field Equipment
summary: Netherlands-based maker of the BatLure and BatCounter for bat field research, which says its BatCounter software has improved much since 2020 and is listed in a bat detector directory as a high-end producer.

name: Aquila Ecologie
summary: Ecological consultancy with experience of using AI models on camera-trap images together with ecological research.

name: AQUON
summary: Laboratory organisation set up as a joint arrangement of Dutch water boards. Its folder says it has run a DNA laboratory for three years and offers eDNA analyses for water quality.

name: ARK Rewilding Nederland
summary: Dutch rewilding organisation whose wildcat projects used hundreds of wildlife cameras and GPS tagging research. A partner in WildlifeNL.

name: Artificial Intelligence Group, Wageningen University & Research
summary: A chair group of AI scientists at Wageningen, led by Ioannis Athanasiadis, doing applied research with experts in the environmental, social and life sciences.

name: ARTIS
summary: Amsterdam zoo that has worked on ARISE since 2021, with a BirdScan radar, insect and wildlife cameras and special nest boxes installed on its grounds.

name: ATKB
summary: Dutch consultancy developing the CrayScan satellite application with HKV Lijn in Water.

name: Atlas Natuurlijk Kapitaal
summary: Digital platform of detailed maps of Dutch natural capital, including the ecosystem type map used in the CBS natural capital accounts.

name: Automated Biodiversity Monitoring
summary: Initiative of Naturalis, TNO, RIVM and Rijkswaterstaat running from 2026 to 2030 to build a Dutch infrastructure of sensors and AI for biodiversity monitoring at national, regional and local level.

name: Automatische Beeldherkenning Klaverbank
summary: Project to count dead man's fingers on the Klaverbank in the North Sea automatically from underwater video. Informatiehuis Marien works on it with Rijkswaterstaat's Datalab and hydrobiological laboratory and Wageningen Marine Research.

name: AvesEcho
summary: An open birdsong recognition algorithm specialised in European birds, developed at Naturalis and running live in Xeno-canto.

name: Basismonitoring Wadden
summary: Shared monitoring of the Wadden area by its managers, with the Datahuis Wadden as virtual access to data, maps and studies.

name: Basisregistratie Topografie
summary: Digital topographic files of the Netherlands at several scales, available as open data from the Kadaster.

name: Batumi Raptor Count
summary: Annual count of migrating raptors at the Batumi bottleneck in Georgia, supported by a registered Dutch charity. It publishes daily and annual results.

name: Beheerautoriteit Waddenzee
summary: Body that coordinates within the Wadden governance structure, in which the ministries of IenW and LVVN and three northern provinces set policy and its objectives.

name: BIJ12
summary: Implementing organisation of the Interprovinciaal Overleg, the association of the 12 Dutch provinces. It supports provincial nature policy and provides validated nature data in the Nationale Databank Flora en Fauna.

name: BIMISEOM
summary: Project that scaled up Marmoris work on biodiversity monitoring using in-situ eDNA and satellite Earth observation, tested in Belgian coastal water where ILVO took thirty eDNA samples.

name: Biodiversity Genomics Europe
summary: BGE+ builds on the 2023 to 2026 biodiversity genomics project and brings together iBOL Europe, ERGA and CETAF through 22 partner institutions in 17 countries.

name: Biodiversity in Focus
summary: A public-private project of at least four years, begun by Witteveen+Bos and Deltares, developing a practical and affordable strategy to measure biodiversity at local level with sound sensors, cameras, eDNA, remote sensing and drones.

name: Blauwtipje.nl
summary: Website and database of Dutch sea slugs, with descriptions, images and thousands of sightings.

name: Bomenstichting
summary: Dutch national foundation for trees, founded in 1970, that keeps the Landelijk Register van Monumentale Bomen, a register of trees of national importance.

name: Bond Friese VogelWachten
summary: Frisian organisation that speaks for meadow birds and the volunteers who monitor and protect them. Validated nests from Nestdrone can be entered directly into its registration systems.

name: Brabant Water
summary: Water company owned by the province of Noord-Brabant and 50 municipalities, which says it manages 1,600 hectares of nature area surrounding its water sources.

name: Brabants Landschap
summary: Organisation that owns and manages more than 19,000 hectares of nature reserves in Noord-Brabant.

name: Butterfly Conservation Europe
summary: Partnership of organisations conserving butterflies and moths across Europe, formed in 2004 and registered in the Netherlands. Its site lists butterfly monitoring and a ButterflyCount App.

name: Carto
summary: Spheer's AI model and web application for satellite imagery, shown distinguishing kinds of reed around the Lauwersmeer. The province of Groningen lists it for nature monitoring.

name: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek
summary: The Dutch statistics office. It produces nature statistics from the Netwerk Ecologische Monitoring, and publishes species population trends and indicators.

name: Chimbo Foundation
summary: Dutch NGO for community conservation of western chimpanzees in the Boé, Guinea-Bissau. It collects camera trap data with the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, and village patrols record chimpanzee numbers.

name: Coastruction
summary: Rotterdam company making 3D-printed reefs; it installed more than 100 structures in Oostvoornse Lake in November 2024 and plans to monitor them for at least three years.

name: Compendium voor de Leefomgeving
summary: Website of about 600 indicators on the environment, nature, landscape and spatial development in the Netherlands, a joint product of CBS, PBL, Wageningen University & Research and RIVM.

name: COSMONiO
summary: Imaging company named as a partner behind the ObsIdentify app and in developing the DIOPSIS insect monitoring system.

name: Crane Migration Radar
summary: A digital twin from Nature FIRST that predicts migratory shifts of cranes and shares observations and updates, integrated into the Sensing Clues platform.

name: CrayScan
summary: Satellite application in development by HKV Lijn in Water and ATKB to map areas at risk from non-native crayfish. It came out of a feasibility study in the Netherlands Space Agency's Innovation Impact Challenge.

name: Datura
summary: Named by Witteveen+Bos as a partner in the airborne eDNA pilot in the Reevediep.

name: De Rijke Noordzee
summary: Dutch North Sea programme with an eDNA project and a project testing underwater vehicles for monitoring seabed animals and biogenic reefs, carried out with Wageningen University & Research, TNO and Seaward.

name: De Vlinderstichting
summary: Dutch species organisation listed by Statistics Netherlands as coordinating the field work of the national butterfly and dragonfly monitoring networks.

name: Delft University of Technology
summary: Its Department of Intelligent Systems is a partner in CAMBioMed, a Biodiversa+ project.

name: Deltares
summary: Dutch research institute that developed Global Water Watch with the World Resources Institute and WWF, using AI on earth observation data to give public information on freshwater resources.

name: Digitalisering Ecologische Monitoring
summary: Rijkswaterstaat project running from 2024 to 2028 to innovate and digitise ecological monitoring of the North Sea, including AI image recognition for birds and marine mammals, for the Ministry of LVVN.

name: DIOPSIS
summary: Insect camera and image recognition system developed by a Dutch consortium. Cameras in the field send photographs to a central server for analysis, with the aim of following trends in insect numbers and biomass.

name: DIVR
summary: Free dive log for logging species and coral condition. Users can send records to OBIS, GBIF and EMODnet.

name: Dopplium
summary: Radar company whose technology has its roots in research at TU Delft and is being tested for detecting bats around wind turbines, in a system called BatGuardian.

name: DORY
summary: Online Marmoris platform for viewing data on past and present conditions in coastal environments, developed to support decisions in conservation, restoration, monitoring and planning.

name: Dunea
summary: Water company owned by the 17 municipalities in its supply area, managing the Solleveld, Meijendel and Berkheide dune areas between Monster and Katwijk, part of Nationaal Park Hollandse Duinen.

name: Dutch Caribbean Nature Alliance
summary: Started a project to monitor land bird populations across Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Saba, St. Eustatius and St. Maarten.

name: Dutch Research Council
summary: Dutch research funder that granted 4 million euros to SoilProS and funds the NIEBA-ARISE project.

name: Ecogoggle
summary: High-tech ecological consultancy that has mapped nature with artificial intelligence since 2018, and the maker of the Floralyze platform.

name: Ecomoni
summary: Spin-off of the University of Twente specialised in sensor technology for nest boxes with an AI application, whose data is integrated with the ARISE platform.

name: EcoPulse
summary: Named by Witteveen+Bos as a partner in the airborne eDNA pilot in the Reevediep.

name: Ecowende
summary: Developer of the Hollandse Kust (west) Wind Farm Site VI, a joint venture with an ecological monitoring programme run with Waardenburg Ecology.

name: Ecowende ecological programme
summary: Monitoring and research programme on birds, bats and marine life at the Hollandse Kust (west) offshore wind farm site, using bird radars and cameras. DHI said its AI species recognition system MUSE would be deployed there.

name: eDentity
summary: Naturalis programme building a Dutch research infrastructure for eDNA analysis of soil, water and air samples, to be delivered by 2028.

name: eDNA-voedselwebanalyse
summary: Project developing a monitoring method based on environmental DNA that gives a broad picture of underwater life from one water sample.

name: EIS Kenniscentrum Insecten
summary: Dutch insect knowledge centre that provides entomological expertise to DIOPSIS and annotates insect photographs used to train its algorithm.

name: Enclio
summary: Company offering AI analysis of bat recordings, with species recognition and feeding buzz detection, and of other ecological data, using its own AI models.

name: EnvirometriX
summary: Science-based start-up at the Agro Business Park in Wageningen, founded to improve the management of natural resources, using statistical and machine learning methods.

name: Faciliteiten Toegepast Onderzoek
summary: Dutch scheme that invests in research facilities at applied research organisations and government knowledge institutes. It provides the 19.4 million euro grant to Automated Biodiversity Monitoring.

name: FalcoSolutions
summary: Organisation that builds websites and API integrations, and is the initiator of FaunaMap.

name: Faunabit
summary: Produces, sells, leases and supports the DIOPSIS insect camera.

name: FaunaMap
summary: Bird recording app and site with photo and sound identification of species, an initiative of FalcoSolutions.

name: Floralyze
summary: Ecogoggle platform that uses AI models to recognise plant species on drone images and aerial photographs and shows them on a map.

name: FLORON
summary: Dutch organisation founded in 1988 that monitors wild plants with volunteers and coordinates research into their distribution.

name: FlySafe
summary: Dashboard giving real-time and predicted data on bird migration to reduce bird strikes, developed with the University of Amsterdam's Institute for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Dynamics. It draws on weather radar data.

name: Fontys Hogeschool
summary: Dutch university of applied sciences whose AI and big data research includes the Flower Power project on drones and AI for measuring biodiversity, and a data platform for WildlifeNL.

name: ForestPulse
summary: Measure Nature tool that combines Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 optical images, GIS context and field evidence to show candidate disturbances for human review.

name: Fred Foundation
summary: A foundation that supports civil society initiatives, including ones that restore and protect nature, and a long-term supporter of Hack the Planet.

name: FREE Nature
summary: Organisation that manages free-living herds of large grazers in more than 30 nature reserves in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany, aiming to restore spontaneous nature.

name: FruitPunch AI
summary: A global AI for Good community that runs projects and challenges such as AI for Wildlife, listed among the start-ups of a TU/e readiness programme.

name: Fully Documented Fisheries
summary: Project on a system that records fishing catches automatically with GPS, sensors, cameras and an onboard computer. Researchers at Wageningen Marine Research are developing the computer vision methods.

name: Geldersch Landschap & Kasteelen
summary: Gelderland landscape organisation, active since 1929, which gives its nature holdings as 11,905 hectares and is a member of LandschappenNL.

name: Gemeente Alkmaar
summary: Dutch municipality that started the Trackvogel bird sound monitoring network in February 2026.

name: Gemeente Rotterdam
summary: Municipality responsible for maintaining nature in five nature areas at Hoek van Holland.

name: Gemeente Utrecht
summary: Municipality describing 190 hectares of forest and woodland in its care, including the Amelisweerd and Rhijnauwen estates, where natural woodland is left without maintenance.

name: Geodelta
summary: Dutch company that took part in an Innovation Impact Challenge feasibility study on modelling, with radar satellite data, how long Wadden Sea sandbanks fall dry and what that means for birds.

name: Global Water Watch
summary: Platform announced by Deltares, the World Resources Institute and WWF to provide public information on freshwater resources, using AI on earth observation data, with financial support from the Google.org Impact Challenge on Climate.

name: Green Earth Group N.V.
summary: Lelystad company that says it oversees restoration projects from development to long-term operation, listing a chimpanzee project in Uganda and greening the dried Aral Sea in Kazakhstan.

name: Groenmonitor
summary: Service that monitors how green the Netherlands is using satellite images.

name: Het Drentse Landschap
summary: Member of LandschappenNL, based in Assen, that manages nature areas and monuments across Drenthe.

name: Het Flevo-landschap
summary: Organisation headquartered in Lelystad that manages, develops and protects more than 5,100 hectares of nature, landscape and heritage in Flevoland.

name: Het Groninger Landschap
summary: Groningen member of LandschappenNL that looks after more than 8,300 hectares of polders, salt marshes, woods and water.

name: Het Limburgs Landschap
summary: Limburg member of LandschappenNL that announced on 28 October 2026 that it had again been recognised as a sound nature manager.

name: Het Nationale Park De Hoge Veluwe
summary: National park that reported in June 2018 that dozens of camera traps had photographed wildlife since 2013, producing over a million photos a year for ecological research and management.

name: Het Utrechts Landschap
summary: Organisation in the Netherlands that manages more than 5,800 hectares of nature, estates, mills, a castle, a brickworks and military heritage.

name: Het Waterschapshuis
summary: Organisation that coordinates and carries out information technology for the 21 Dutch water boards. It worked with STOWA on an AI search assistant and takes part in NL Veranderdetectie and PCP WISE.

name: Het Zeeuwse Landschap
summary: Organisation that says it manages more than 10,000 hectares of nature areas in Zeeland and plans to buy 200 hectares more.

name: HKV Lijn in Water
summary: Dutch consultancy developing the CrayScan satellite application with ATKB.

name: Hogeschool Leiden
summary: Dutch university of applied sciences. Its Leiden Centre for Applied Bioscience works on an AI tool that recognises prey brought to little owl nests, and it shares an Environmental Metagenomics research group with Naturalis.

name: Hollandse Kust Zuid bird collision camera pilot
summary: A year-long pilot initiated by Vattenfall at the Hollandse Kust Zuid offshore wind farm, with Wildlife Imaging Systems and Wageningen University & Research, testing thermal cameras and AI to observe potential bird collisions.

name: Hoogheemraadschap van Delfland
summary: Dutch water board whose innovation in satellite monitoring was nominated for the top 12 of the Waterinnovatieprijs 2026.

name: Hortus botanicus Leiden
summary: Botanical garden, run by Leiden University, that leads a 2024 NWO-listed Biodiversa+ BiodivMon grant on harmonising plant metabarcoding pipelines in Europe.

name: Human-Bear Conflict Radar
summary: A tool developed by Wageningen University & Research with Sensing Clues and other Nature FIRST partners to monitor and predict conflicts with brown bears, first shown live in Romania in October 2024.

name: Identifying eDNA to understand aquatic biodiversity
summary: Project from 2014 to 2016 that produced DNA barcodes and eDNA methods for aquatic macrofauna and water plants, with KWR, Naturalis and other Dutch partners.

name: Informatiehuis Marien
summary: Dutch body working with Rijkswaterstaat and Wageningen Marine Research on mapping the North Sea bed with automatic image recognition.

name: Innovation Impact Challenge Satellietdata ten behoeve van biodiversiteit in Nederland, subthema water
summary: Netherlands Space Agency challenge on satellite data for biodiversity in and around water, where four consortia receive feasibility funding and the most promising go on to build a prototype.

name: Instant Detect
summary: AI camera traps that run species recognition on each camera and send images through a satellite-connected base station. Hack the Planet adopted the technology from ZSL.

name: Institute for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Dynamics
summary: An institute of the University of Amsterdam whose researchers built the automated wildlife camera network in the Amsterdam Water Supply Dunes and which is a partner in TABMON and HiRAD.

name: It Fryske Gea
summary: Friesland member of LandschappenNL, based in Olterterp, that manages more than 60 nature areas totalling 21,000 hectares.

name: IUCN National Committee of the Netherlands
summary: Works with international partners and IUCN members in the Netherlands, and is named by Rainforest Connection as a funder of an acoustic monitoring project in Sumatra and by Witteveen+Bos as a member of the Biodiversity in Focus knowledge team.

name: Kadaster
summary: Holds the Basisregistratie Topografie, the Dutch national topographic register, whose TOP10NL map is renewed from aerial photographs.

name: KBTS
summary: Dutch firm that applies automated image recognition by AI to fish and mammals and developed the Migrator software for underwater footage of fish migration.

name: KWR Water Research Institute
summary: Dutch water research institute that entered a cooperation agreement with Naturalis in 2015 on biodiversity and water, and ran research projects on eDNA for monitoring aquatic biodiversity.

name: Laboratory of Geo-information Science and Remote Sensing, Wageningen University & Research
summary: A Wageningen laboratory led by Kirsten de Beurs and Sytze de Bruin, whose listed projects include mapping near-future illegal forest activities and carbon loss.

name: Landschap Noord-Holland
summary: Organisation that says it protects nature, landscape and heritage in Noord-Holland, both in its nature areas and beyond them.

name: Landschap Overijssel
summary: Organisation that says it protects, manages and strengthens nature, landscape and heritage in Overijssel.

name: Lobster Robotics
summary: Trade name of Lobster Innovations B.V. in The Hague, whose Scout robot makes georeferenced optical seabed maps; it says it has deployed in eight countries.

name: LTER-LIFE
summary: Dutch scientific infrastructure for shared ecological research towards digital twins of ecosystems, starting with the Wadden Sea and the Veluwe. It was founded in August 2023 with a 10-year NWO grant.

name: Luistervink
summary: Website that shows live which birds are singing at selected places in the Netherlands, and how often each species has been heard.

name: Lumax
summary: Maker of the machine learning models used in Sovon's 2024 drone pilot on bird colonies.

name: Maastricht University
summary: University whose Department of Neuropsychology and Psychopharmacology is the affiliation of the first author of a 2024 paper using deep learning to classify mammal vocalisations.

name: Maatschappij van Weldadigheid
summary: Landowner with about 1,300 hectares of land, including forest, heath and nature, whose nature areas almost all have Natura 2000 status and management plans.

name: Mangrove Maniacs
summary: Non-profit on Bonaire working on mangrove conservation and restoration, whose site says the Ecological Restoration of Lac Bay and South Bonaire project was launched in 2015.

name: Marmoris
summary: Dutch Earth observation company and alumnus of the ESA Business Incubation Centre in Noordwijk. It uses satellite data and in-situ data to monitor coastal and marine environments.

name: Measure Nature
summary: Leiden company that builds evidence workflows for ecological monitoring, starting with ForestPulse, combining Earth observation with AI-assisted interpretation.

name: Meridia
summary: Organisation whose Meridia Verify methodology checks geospatial and documentation aspects of sourcing from protected areas and IPLC territories to identify EUDR legality risks, and which uses Space Intelligence.

name: Migrator
summary: KBTS machine learning program that analyses underwater footage from fish migration studies, counting fish and estimating migration direction and length class.

name: Ministerie van Economische Zaken
summary: Dutch ministry that remains responsible for the financing of the Faciliteiten Toegepast Onderzoek scheme, and that awarded its second round.

name: Ministerie van Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur
summary: The Dutch ministry responsible for nature, agriculture and fisheries. Its state secretary sent the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan to parliament.

name: Monitoring en Onderzoek Natuurversterking en Soortenbescherming
summary: Dutch North Sea research and monitoring programme. Its data are managed alongside Wozep and Digital Ecological Monitoring.

name: Multi-frame AI-analyse van thermische dronebeelden voor weidevogelmonitoring
summary: Dutch Research Council funded project studying whether combining successive thermal drone images lets AI detect meadow bird nests better, with the main applicant at NHL Stenden Hogeschool.

name: Nationaal Dashboard Biodiversiteit
summary: Dutch dashboard of goals and indicators on the state of biodiversity, jointly owned by a consortium of IUCN NL, Naturalis, SoortenNL and Sovon, and paid for by private funds.

name: Nationale Databank Flora en Fauna
summary: Dutch national database of validated species observations, managed and operated by BIJ12 for the provinces.

name: Natural Capital Accounts for the Netherlands
summary: National ecosystem accounts produced by Statistics Netherlands and Wageningen University and Research, which have worked together on natural capital accounting since 2015.

name: Nature FIRST
summary: A project of 12 partners, led by Sensing Clues, that built predictive biodiversity monitoring tools for four European protected areas, including digital twins.

name: Nature Identification API
summary: Naturalis's species identification service, whose 2023 multi-source image recognition model includes about 40,000 European taxa and serves six biodiversity portals in Europe.

name: Natuur- en Recreatieschap IJsselmonde
summary: Joint body of five municipalities that owns more than 560 hectares of nature and recreation areas in IJsselmonde.

name: Natuurkalender
summary: Dutch research on nature and climate change, reported by Wageningen University & Research, that uses GrowApp photographs to record the course of the seasons.

name: Natuurmonitoring met AI door de provincies
summary: Work by the provinces of Fryslân, Groningen, Drenthe and Noord-Brabant with Spheer.ai on nature monitoring with AI on aerial images, which grew from the question of whether AI can support the mandatory twelve-yearly Natura 2000 monitoring.

name: Natuurmonumenten
summary: Dutch nature organisation that sometimes uses drones itself to monitor populations of birds or grazers. A partner in WildlifeNL.

name: Natuurversterking Noordzee
summary: Dutch programme for North Sea nature that funds a De Rijke Noordzee project testing underwater monitoring techniques.

name: Nederlandse Bosinventarisatie
summary: Dutch national forest inventory, carried out by Wageningen Environmental Research with partners, commissioned by the Dutch agriculture and nature ministry. It runs on a five-year cycle and the raw data can be downloaded from Stichting Probos.

name: Nestdrone
summary: Software platform that analyses drone images automatically to find meadow bird nests. In 2026 it became an operational system used daily, linked to the registration systems of the Bond Friese VogelWachten.

name: Netherlands Biodiversity Information Facility
summary: The Dutch national node of GBIF, a department of Naturalis Biodiversity Center that helps Dutch organisations publish biodiversity data to GBIF.

name: Netherlands Institute of Ecology
summary: Dutch ecology institute that studies brent geese with ringed and GPS-tagged birds in Waakvogels, and whose researcher Wim van der Putten is project leader of SoilProS, which will apply AI to soil biodiversity data.

name: Netherlands Space Agency
summary: The Dutch space agency, listed as a member of the Committee on Earth Observation Satellites since 2011.

name: Netherlands Space Office
summary: The Dutch government's space agency. A Dutch government agriculture news site reports that it advises the NVWA on what can contribute to the EU Deforestation Regulation.

name: Netwerk Ecologische Monitoring
summary: Collaboration of Dutch species organisations, ministries, provinces and government bodies including Statistics Netherlands, whose monitoring programmes follow species populations. Volunteers supply most of the data.

name: NL Veranderdetectie
summary: Dutch pilot that uses AI on recent aerial photographs to detect changes in watercourses for a digital water map.

name: Objectherkenning.com
summary: Company that builds AI models and software, including those with which the KOWW platform recognises invasive water plants on drone images.

name: Observation International
summary: Dutch non-profit foundation that provides a worldwide platform for storing, validating and sharing nature information, and offers the ObsIdentify app.

name: ObsIdentify
summary: Species identification app from Observation International with Naturalis and Natuurpunt, trained on millions of observations from users of Waarneming.nl, Waarnemingen.be and Observation.org.

name: OpenAtlas
summary: Start-up founded in 2023 and incubated at ESA BIC Noordwijk from January 2025. It uses satellite images and machine learning models to monitor for deforestation in supply chains.

name: OpenCoral AI
summary: Reef Support AI models for coral reef, seagrass and mangrove monitoring, including benthic classification and habitat mapping.

name: Planbureau voor de Leefomgeving
summary: Dutch environmental planning agency. It publishes on nature and biodiversity and is a joint producer of the Compendium voor de Leefomgeving.

name: Provincie Drenthe
summary: Dutch province that works with Spheer.ai on nature monitoring with AI.

name: Provincie Flevoland
summary: Dutch province whose Natuurbeheerplan describes its nature and landscape goals and sets out the boundaries of nature and agricultural nature areas, with part two issued as electronic maps.

name: Provincie Fryslân
summary: Dutch province that works with Spheer.ai on nature monitoring with AI.

name: Provincie Gelderland
summary: Dutch province whose Natuurbeheerplan, with a 2027 map, shows where subsidy for nature and landscape is possible in the Gelders Natuurnetwerk.

name: Provincie Groningen
summary: Dutch province that lists Spheer.ai in the national algorithm register for identifying differences in vegetation in order to monitor nature.

name: Provincie Limburg
summary: Dutch province whose executive adopted the Natuurbeheerplan Limburg 2027 on 25 August 2026, showing nature area boundaries on two maps, the first being the management type map.

name: Provincie Noord-Brabant
summary: Dutch province for which Spheer shows grass encroachment on heathland year by year.

name: Provincie Noord-Holland
summary: Dutch province responsible for managing nature, whose Natuurbeheerplan sets the boundaries of areas where subsidy for managing and developing nature applies.

name: Provincie Overijssel
summary: Dutch province whose Geoportaal offers maps, GIS files and services, and which publishes a subsidy map for nature management drawn from the Natuurbeheerplan 2027 management type map.

name: Provincie Utrecht
summary: Dutch province that has run monitoring of flora and fauna in its rural area since 1975, with results going to the Nationale Databank Flora en Fauna, and partners with Netwerk Ecologische Monitoring.

name: Provincie Zeeland
summary: Dutch province that follows plants and animals through several monitoring programmes, with counts done by site managers, volunteers and others and data published in its data portal.

name: Provincie Zuid-Holland
summary: Dutch province whose algorithm register lists an AI image recognition method applied to satellite images of Natura 2000 sites. The method has been used only for one-off analyses.

name: PWN
summary: Organisation that says it manages over 7,500 hectares of nature between Zandvoort and Bergen, with the province of Noord-Holland as shareholder commissioning it to manage two dune areas.

name: Q42
summary: The company in which Hack the Planet began as a hackathon project, and which backed it with funding, engineering time and a home.

name: Rabobank
summary: Dutch bank that, with EUSPA support, uses Copernicus-derived land cover data to track landscape cohesion and biodiversity value on Dutch dairy farmland. Its Acorn initiative uses remote sensing for smallholder carbon credits.

name: Radboud Universiteit
summary: Dutch university that carries out the ecological analysis of DIOPSIS insect camera data.

name: Radboud University
summary: A development partner in the DIOPSIS insect camera monitoring system.

name: RAVON
summary: Dutch species organisation listed by Statistics Netherlands as coordinating the field work of the national reptile and amphibian monitoring networks.

name: Recreatieschap Voorne-Putten
summary: Joint arrangement of the municipalities of Voorne aan Zee and Nissewaard that owns and manages land and buildings for nature and recreation, with biodiversity central to its leased grassland.

name: Reef Support
summary: Marine conservation technology company based in Amsterdam that builds AI models and tools for monitoring coral reefs, seagrass and mangroves, with open-source models on Hugging Face.

name: Reefwatchers: Safe, Efficient and Scalable Biodiversity Monitoring for Biogenic and Artificial Reefs
summary: Project led by Rudy Helmons that collects reef biodiversity data from eDNA, acoustic, visual and physical measurements, works on robots to cut data costs, and is funded by the Dutch Research Council from 1 September 2026.

name: Reefy
summary: Delft-based company offering BlueBiodex, a dashboard combining satellite imagery, eDNA and water quality data on aquatic ecosystem health, and a modular breakwater designed to work as an artificial reef.

name: Remote sensing gebiedsclassificatie op basis van AI beeldherkenning
summary: Provincial Zuid-Holland algorithm that segments satellite images of Natura 2000 sites into vegetation structure classes. Three sites are used, and the page says it has so far been applied only for one-off analyses.

name: Rijksvastgoedbedrijf
summary: State property body managing about 26,000 hectares of Defence airbases and training grounds, over 17,000 hectares of it protected nature area, plus the 3,640-hectare Staatsdomein at Het Loo.

name: Rijkswaterstaat
summary: Says it manages over 18,000 hectares of verges along the Dutch national road network. It is a partner in Automated Biodiversity Monitoring and tested AI estimation of vegetation height from satellite images.

name: RIVM
summary: Runs the Integrale Milieumonitoring in Natuur network, which has followed the effects of air pollutants in Dutch nature areas since 2020, and is a partner in Automated Biodiversity Monitoring, where it installs field stations in its monitoring networks.

name: Royal Netherlands Institute for Sea Research
summary: The national oceanographic institute of the Netherlands, which runs the WATLAS bird tracking project and is a partner in Waakvogels.

name: Saba Conservation Foundation
summary: Saba's designated conservation agency, which manages protected areas including the Saba National Marine Park.

name: SandTracer
summary: Prototype that follows Dutch dune dynamics with AI on satellite images and LiDAR data, from research commissioned by STOWA and Rijkswaterstaat. A year of field validation is planned.

name: Satellietdataportaal
summary: Portal giving users in the Netherlands free access to high-resolution satellite images of the Netherlands bought centrally by the national government.

name: SBNL Natuurfonds
summary: Nature fund that manages 18 nature areas of its own across the Netherlands.

name: ScannerEdge
summary: A passive radio-frequency detector from Hack the Planet that warns rangers of phones and radios in zones where there should be none.

name: Smart Deterrent
summary: A non-lethal deterrent from Hack the Planet that pairs with AI cameras and fires light and sound only when the right species is detected.

name: Snapshot Hoge Veluwe
summary: Project run by the national park, in partnership with Wageningen University and Research, that in June 2018 invited the public to view and identify animals in camera-trap photos online.

name: SoilProS
summary: Consortium of researchers with 17 companies, NGOs and government bodies, which received 4 million euros from the Dutch Research Council to map the soil life of Dutch farmlands. It plans to apply AI to recognise patterns in soil biodiversity.

name: Sovon Vogelonderzoek Nederland
summary: Provides knowledge on the numbers, distribution and ecology of bird populations in the Netherlands, coordinates national bird monitoring schemes, and has tested AudioMoth recorders for passive acoustic monitoring.

name: Spectra
summary: Project in Noordoost-Fryslân by Altenburg & Wymenga, Aviadrone and Vliegend.nl to improve observation of animals, vegetation and birds with drones, sensors and data analysis.

name: Spheer
summary: Groningen start-up that built an AI model from satellite images of the Dutch land surface, which provinces are trying out for nature monitoring through its web application.

name: St. Eustatius National Parks Foundation
summary: Manages the island's national parks and garden; in June 2023 it described identifying sea turtles by matching photos of their cheek patterns against an international database.

name: Staatsbosbeheer
summary: Public body with a statutory task to manage the nature areas entrusted to it, about 270,000 hectares, within the domain of the Dutch nature ministry.

name: Stichting ANEMOON
summary: Dutch foundation that researches marine life with citizen scientists. It runs the Monitoringproject Onderwater Oever, in which sports divers have recorded changes in underwater life since 1994.

name: Stichting Bargerveen
summary: Dutch foundation that develops ecological knowledge through research, management experiments, monitoring and landscape ecological system analyses.

name: Stichting De Bovenlanden
summary: Foundation that manages nine nature areas, part of which it owns, using volunteers.

name: Stichting De Hooge Weide
summary: Foundation that owns and manages nature areas in the municipalities of Castricum, Heemskerk and Uitgeest.

name: Stichting Marke Vragender Veen
summary: Foundation that owns 40 hectares of the 110-hectare Vragenderveen raised bog and manages a further 10 hectares owned by other private owners.

name: Stichting Probos
summary: Dutch foundation that has taken part in the Nederlandse Bosinventarisaties for nearly 20 years.

name: Stichting Semblis
summary: Foundation that carries out and promotes knowledge of European freshwater and marine macroinvertebrates, researches their distribution, and is a project partner in the Waterdiertjes.nl AI image recognition pilot.

name: Stichting Twickel
summary: Foundation managing the 4,500-hectare Twickel estate near Delden and other estates, over 7,000 hectares of nature and cultural land in total.

name: Stichting VEEN
summary: Private nature organisation that buys farmland next to existing Peel reserves to help restore raised bog, managing it mainly by reducing nutrients, rewetting and allowing rough vegetation to develop.

name: Stichting Waterlandse Weiden
summary: Foundation working to improve and maintain meadow-bird habitat in Waterland, managing a 75-hectare area under a management plan.

name: Stinapa Bonaire
summary: Nature area manager on Bonaire that runs research and monitoring projects, including tracking and monitoring lionfish with volunteers.

name: STOWA
summary: Dutch body that supports research for the water boards, including an eDNA food web method and a report on monitoring dune dynamics with satellite data and AI.

name: Sylphium molecular ecology
summary: Dutch biotechnology company that develops products and services for environmental DNA analysis and runs an eDNA service laboratory.

name: Tanka Foundation
summary: A foundation that, according to Hack the Planet, funds nature-positive work and is a long-term supporter of it. Its own site disallows the fetcher.

name: TAUW Foundation
summary: Foundation established in 2017 to fund water, nature and living environment projects from the sale of TAUW shares, and co-funding the Waterdiertjes.nl AI image recognition pilot with STOWA.

name: The Fieldwork Company
summary: Dutch company that uses drones for surveys from the air.

name: Tilburg University
summary: Its Department of Cognitive Science and AI is a partner in TABMON, a project on acoustic biodiversity monitoring across Europe.

name: TNO
summary: Develops the sensor field stations for Automated Biodiversity Monitoring, the Dutch national sensor and AI monitoring initiative.

name: Trackvogel
summary: Bird monitoring network of the municipality of Alkmaar, started in February 2026, using measuring boxes with smart software that record and recognise bird sounds. Set up with Vogelwerkgroep Alkmaar and Sovon.

name: Triodos Foundation
summary: Dutch foundation that links donors to pioneers working on nature restoration and food systems. It helped pay for the Nationaal Dashboard Biodiversiteit.

name: Twentynext
summary: Company that describes a 2018 feasibility project on image recognition to count animals and tell species apart on wildlife camera images.

name: Universiteit Leiden
summary: Dutch university. Computer scientist Dan Stowell's post at its Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science links computer science with Naturalis on AI and animal sounds.

name: University of Groningen
summary: Dutch university and a partner in the Waakvogels bird monitoring project in the Wadden Sea.

name: University of Twente
summary: University whose affiliated researcher Zijing Wu was first author of a 2023 paper on deep learning for satellite monitoring of large mammal populations.

name: Utrecht University
summary: A member of the WildlifeNL research consortium on human-wildlife coexistence in the Netherlands.

name: UvA-BiTS
summary: Bird tracking system listed as a facility of the Institute for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Dynamics at the University of Amsterdam, with a solar-powered GPS tracker, a ground station network and automated data processing.

name: Vegetatiehoogte uit hoge-resolutie satellietbeelden
summary: Rijkswaterstaat proof of concept, carried out by NEO, on estimating vegetation height with AI from high-resolution satellite images.

name: Vegetatiemonitor
summary: Rijkswaterstaat AI system that detects vegetation types along the floodplains of the major Dutch rivers from satellite images, for comparison with the legally set vegetation standard.

name: VERA
summary: Recording app for the NDFF Verspreidingsatlas, built by FLORON for field observations of plants, fungi, molluscs and others, with observations going straight to the NDFF for FLORON validators to check.

name: Vislift
summary: Maker of a fish lift that can be fitted with a Fishcounter camera module with automatic fish recognition by species.

name: Vitens
summary: Water company whose 2025 annual report reports managing over 3,300 hectares of nature across 104 extraction areas and commissioning management plans for most areas it manages itself.

name: Vogeltrekstation
summary: Dutch centre for bird migration and demography, a cooperation between NIOO-KNAW and the Ringersvereniging, that organises bird ringing and shows ringing and recovery data for Dutch birds.

name: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
summary: University whose affiliated researcher Inger de Jonge was first author of a 2025 preprint reporting over 40% lichen cover on an Antarctic island where remote sensing showed 0.23%.

name: Waakvogels
summary: Five-year study of six migratory bird species in the Wadden Sea by the University of Groningen, NIOZ and the University of Amsterdam, with ringed and GPS-tagged birds. A work package at NIOO-KNAW is funded by the Waddenfonds.

name: Waardenburg Ecology
summary: Dutch ecological consultancy that developed the monitoring programme for the Ecowende offshore wind farm, using data from bird radars, cameras and bird ecologists.

name: Waarneming.nl
summary: Dutch observation platform named by the government as a source sharing records with the Nationale Databank Flora en Fauna.

name: Wageningen Environmental Research
summary: A member of the knowledge team of Biodiversity in Focus, a Dutch project on biodiversity measurement strategy. It is also listed as a GBIF publisher in the queue, which was not read because GBIF refuses the fetcher.

name: Wageningen Marine Research
summary: Part of Wageningen University & Research, it studies marine, coastal and freshwater systems and uses passive acoustic monitoring of harbour porpoises in monitoring programmes for Dutch offshore wind farms.

name: Waterdiertjes.nl
summary: Dutch citizen science project running since 2018 for water quality measurements. A pilot with two water boards uses AI image recognition developed by Naturalis and Waarneming.nl, funded by STOWA and the TAUW Foundation.

name: Waternet
summary: Dutch water company that worked with University of Amsterdam researchers on the automated camera network in the Amsterdam Water Supply Dunes.

name: WATLAS
summary: NIOZ project that fits waders with small tags to follow their movements in the Dutch Wadden Sea in real time. NIOZ says it is expanding the project to the whole Dutch Wadden Sea in 2026 and 2027.

name: Wegrestaurant Waddenzee: komen trekvogels aan hun trekken?
summary: Project in which Geodelta wants to model, using radar satellite data, how long Wadden Sea sandbanks fall dry and what birds find there; the feasibility study found sandbanks and mussel beds sometimes hard to tell apart.

name: Westerdijk Fungal Biodiversity Institute
summary: An institute of biobanks for filamentous fungi, yeasts and bacteria in Utrecht, partner in building ARISE and in the AccellARISE upgrade.

name: WetlandWatch
summary: Project in which Terramira is developing an application for rangers and provincial staff to see early whether a wetland is drying out and whether this relates to bird numbers, tested at Bargerveen and Fochteloërveen.

name: Wildlife Imaging Systems
summary: Developed a system of sixteen thermal cameras with artificial intelligence, tested on an offshore wind turbine at Hollandse Kust Zuid to observe potential bird collisions.

name: WildlifeNL: The Dutch Wildlife Comeback
summary: An eight-year research project, granted in 2022, on human-wildlife coexistence in the Netherlands, which plans new technologies, governance arrangements and communication strategies.

name: Willem Beijerinck Biologisch Station
summary: Dutch foundation that carries out ecological research in the north of the Netherlands, often with ground beetles as indicators, and keeps long-running beetle sampling series.

name: Wind op Zee Ecologisch Programma
summary: Dutch government programme building knowledge on the effects of offshore wind farms on birds, bats, marine mammals and their habitats. Rijkswaterstaat implements it.

name: Witteveen+Bos
summary: Consultancy testing airborne eDNA for biodiversity research in the Reevediep with EcoPulse, TNO and Datura.

name: WWF Netherlands
summary: Hack the Planet names it as a long-term supporter whose support helps place anti-poaching and monitoring technology in the field. Its own site disallows the fetcher, so this rests on Hack the Planet's page.

name: Zodion Zoogdieronderzoek Nederland
summary: Dutch mammal research organisation that collects data on mice and shrews from owl pellets with the help of many volunteers.

name: Zoogdiervereniging
summary: Dutch mammal society. Its newsletter covers mammal monitoring under the Netwerk Ecologische Monitoring, and it has a Monitoring and Data team led by the project leader for the mammal schemes.

name: Zuid-Hollands Landschap
summary: Organisation that maintains more than 4,700 hectares of nature, spread across more than 120 nature areas in Zuid-Holland.

name: AI for Nature
summary: A proposed national centre for data and AI in managing natural resources, to be set up at Campus Ås under an agreement NIBIO and NMBU signed on 30 June 2026.

name: AI-powered fish trap
summary: An active project, built by Simula with Huawei as partner, that began as an image-classification prototype in the Storelva river in 2022 and spread to more rivers in 2023 and 2024.

name: AILARON
summary: A project with NTNU as partner to characterise plankton in place, using a vehicle that images microorganisms, processes images in place and classifies them with machine learning.

name: Aker BP
summary: An organisation that GeoExpro says collaborated on DeepSee, where the paper names the firm Bergverk AS, and one author of the paper worked for it, located at Lysaker.

name: Aker QRILL Company
summary: An organisation that HUB Ocean's blog says shared raw acoustic fishery data.

name: Akvaplan-niva
summary: A Tromsø-based Norwegian not-for-profit research and consulting company owned by NIVA, with more than 130 researchers and advisers, whose reported work includes machine learning on plastic litter images and autonomous vehicle surveys.

name: Akvariet i Bergen
summary: Norway's largest aquarium, which works with the Institute of Marine Research and NORCE, including tests of AI underwater cameras for counting fish, and released six small-spotted catsharks in June 2026.

name: Allskog
summary: A branch of the Norwegian Forest Owners Association, according to a DJI case study, with an affiliated co-author on the SENTREE poster.

name: AMBIOS
summary: An active project led by SINTEF and funded by the Research Council of Norway, aiming to develop an autonomous platform for mapping marine biodiversity, with planned AI-based data acquisition and targeted sampling.

name: Annotated aerial imagery dataset for harbour seals in Svalbard
summary: Dataset of annotated aerial imagery of harbour seals in Svalbard, with the paper's authors listed by Visual Intelligence as Zoé Lemoine, Puneet Sharma, Kit M. Kovacs, Christian Lydersen and Marie-Anne Blanchet.

name: Anárjohka nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board delegated by the Ministry of Climate and Environment to manage the national park, with members from Kautokeino and Karasjok municipalities, the Sami Parliament and the county council.

name: AR5
summary: A dataset run by NIBIO that it calls the most detailed map of Norway's land resources, which municipalities updated routinely and NIBIO periodically updated for missed changes, as reported in November 2020.

name: Arealrepresentativ naturovervåking
summary: An open-data national monitoring dataset of ecological condition indicators in mainland Norway, owned by the Norwegian Environment Agency, set up in 2020 with 1,000 randomly chosen plots.

name: Arealrepresentativ overvåkning av norske verneområder (fjell/myr)
summary: A monitoring programme for mountain and mire protected areas that uses aerial photographs to interpret interventions and vegetation change; the first round ran from 2012 to 2016 and the second is under way.

name: Arealrepresentativ overvåkning av skog i verneområder
summary: A forest monitoring programme in protected areas, started in 2012 and run in five-year rounds, now in its third, coordinated with the National Forest Inventory using the same parameters inside and outside protected areas.

name: Artskart
summary: A web map service of Norwegian species finds, built on GBIF and Darwin Core, holding over 50 million records of 68,222 taxa as of September 2025, with a 2025 Sabima presentation giving 55.1 million.

name: Artsobservasjoner
summary: A Norwegian citizen science species observation portal run by the Norwegian Biodiversity Information Centre, launched in 2008, with about 25,000 registered users in 2025 according to Sabima.

name: Artsorakel
summary: An AI tool run by the Norwegian Biodiversity Information Centre that tries to identify wild species from images, free and without an account, and builds on the Artsobservasjoner image archive.

name: Aspecto AS
summary: An organisation in Leirfjord, Norway, whose GBIF record says it specialises in autonomous underwater vehicle surveys, mapping the seabed at high resolution with image processing.

name: BarentsWatch
summary: An active programme run by the Norwegian Coastal Administration that shares information on Norwegian coastal and marine areas, mostly as open data, with ten ministries and 29 agencies and institutes as partners.

name: Beefutures
summary: Company named Beefutures Holding AS in its terms, offering Onibi Insight, which uses honey bees as sensors of ecosystem health and detects bird species from sound.

name: Bergen Telemetry Network
summary: An active array of acoustic receivers around Bergen's fjords that uses Thelma Biotel equipment, with a contact team at NORCE LFI.

name: Bergwerk
summary: A Norway-based company, according to GeoExpro, developing tools to minimise resource extraction impacts, with three DeepSee paper authors employed there; the paper names the employer Bergverk AS.

name: Berlevåg AI pink salmon trap
summary: An active Huawei-built trap with local, Simula and Troll Systems partners; Huawei reports camera-based machine-learning identification and over 5,723 pink salmon removed in Kongsfjordelva in 2023.

name: Berlevåg Jeger- og fiskerforening
summary: A hunting and fishing association that leases Kongsfjordelva and Storelva, has counted fish by video in Kongsfjord since 2010, and had 15 to 20 volunteers on the two rivers, per Huawei's July 2024 release.

name: Biodiversity monitoring based on bioacoustics and AI
summary: A closed 2020 to 2023 project run by SINTEF on biodiversity monitoring with bioacoustics and AI, focused on ecosystems and the impact of restoration and human activity.

name: Biodrone
summary: A Steinkjer-based drone services provider, per a company-written DJI case study, specialising in forestry, agriculture and nature management, with an AI portal applying deep learning to orthomosaics.

name: Biofokus
summary: Oslo-based foundation that contributes to knowledge-based management of Norwegian nature and says it has recorded half a million species records in national databases.

name: BirdLife Norge
summary: Trondheim-based, with about 13,500 members per Sabima's 2025 presentation, it monitors migration through annual bird-station netting and collaborates with NINA on national breeding bird monitoring.

name: Blueye Robotics
summary: Sells underwater drones for monitoring changes at marine habitats, and says its environmental monitoring can include coral reefs and marine ecosystems.

name: Blåst Spel AS
summary: Company whose GBIF publisher record describes species observations recorded by users of its mobile application, and which the App Store names as provider of ibbi.

name: Brattefjell-Vindeggen verneområdestyre
summary: Board whose site covers management of the Brattefjell-Vindeggen landscape protected area and the management tasks carried out by the board and manager.

name: Breheimen nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board appointed as the management authority for Breheimen National Park and associated protected areas.

name: Bymiljøetaten
summary: Oslo body that manages Gressholmen and Rambergøya, running the islands day to day, and also manages several hay meadows including Dølerud, Bremsrud and sites in Maridalen.

name: Børgefjell nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board appointed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment as management authority for Børgefjell/Byrkije National Park and the Austre Tiplingan/Luvlie Diehpell landscape protected area.

name: Citizen Sea
summary: Programme in which users can photograph, upload and log sightings of marine wildlife or pollution, built by Hub Ocean.

name: CoastVision
summary: Closed project, 2020 to 2025, that aimed to apply deep learning to detect and size coastal fish caught on camera, led by the Institute of Marine Research.

name: CoffeeLand
summary: Project running from 31 December 2025 to 30 December 2029, which includes mapping coffee-forest extent and structure with AI and machine learning.

name: COGMAR
summary: Closed project that developed a deep learning method for detecting acoustic targets, built by the Norwegian Computing Center and the Institute of Marine Research.

name: County Governor of Troms and Finnmark
summary: Body that, according to Huawei, announced a project in September 2023 to develop an automatic pink salmon trap and buys equipment and makes operating agreements with fishing associations and landowner groups.

name: CRIMAC
summary: Institute of Marine Research-led programme (October 2020 to September 2028) aiming to automate interpretation of broadband acoustics, with funding of about 28 million kroner a year for eight years.

name: Deep Vision fish dataset
summary: Curated fish image data and backgrounds, synthetic image tools and annotated real data for testing classifiers, built from Deep Vision images from two surveys by Vaneeda Allken.

name: DeepSee
summary: Model using YOLOv8 to detect benthic lifeforms in North Atlantic deep-sea environments, presented with a dataset of 2,825 annotated images and built by Bergwerk and Aker BP.

name: DIMARC
summary: Two-year project announced in August 2020, run by Akvaplan-niva, to detect, identify and map plastic litter in the Norwegian Arctic with an autonomous robot and machine learning.

name: DNV
summary: Organisation in Høvik, Norway that offers risk assessments, surveys, monitoring and restoration measures, with surveys combining sampling, eDNA analysis and imagery.

name: Dovrefjell nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board that was delegated responsibility as management authority for the protected areas in Dovrefjell in 2010.

name: DTO-Track
