summary: NORCE-led project that aims to develop a digital twin of the North Sea for tracking aquatic animal movements, and will use tracking technologies and international collaboration.

name: Dugnad for havet
summary: A citizen science programme, built and run by the Institute of Marine Research, where people register marine finds such as a new crab or many jellyfish; launched officially on 16 October 2020.

name: Ecotone
summary: Trondheim company in underwater hyperspectral imaging, a spin-off from NTNU, which provided the UHI technology for a MAREANO pilot survey in 2014.

name: eDepthNA
summary: Akvaplan-niva-led project aiming to integrate an automated eDNA sampler into an underwater glider, with a validated system expected by the end of 2026.

name: Environmental Monitoring of Svalbard and Jan Mayen
summary: Environmental monitoring system for Svalbard and Jan Mayen, built and run by the Norwegian Polar Institute, drawing key indicators from thematic land, air and sea programmes and normally assessing the state of the environment each year.

name: EOCEAN
summary: A collaboration of four research institutes and four municipal partners, including Norwegian water, nature and computing bodies; its page mentions machine learning to upscale monitoring data using satellite images.

name: Equinor
summary: Organisation that completed an eDNA pilot with NORCE at Hywind Scotland, sampled in August 2021 and reported in May 2023, which identified twenty-six fish species in the area.

name: Field Geospatial
summary: Self-described geospatial technology company with its head office in Oslo, developing software based on geodata and AI; NIVA says it brings AI-based analyses to Marint naturkart.

name: Finnmarkseiendommen
summary: Body that manages land and natural resources in Finnmark under the Finnmark Act, balancing use, rights, nature considerations and development.

name: FishOtter
summary: Project aiming at an autonomous acoustic telemetry platform for tracking fish, fusing autonomous vehicles, underwater sensing and machine intelligence, with a stated start of June 2026.

name: FOOTPRINTs
summary: Closed, European Union funded TETTRIs third party project that set out to develop machine learning models to identify an animal from a footprint photo.

name: FOR-instance
summary: UAV laser scanning benchmark dataset for segmentation of individual trees, drawn from five data collections.

name: ForestSAT
summary: Organisation in Norway that, according to the Hub, predicts forest fire risk using geospatial data and AI; it says its platform combines AI, satellite Earth observation and forest science.

name: Færder nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board responsible for managing Færder National Park, with members from Færder municipality and Vestfold county council, appointed by the Environment Agency.

name: GBIF Norway
summary: Norwegian participant node in GBIF, established in 2005 and hosted by the University of Oslo's Natural History Museum, funded by the Research Council of Norway.

name: Geological Survey of Norway
summary: One of three bodies in the MAREANO collaboration, in the group responsible for field sampling, that took part in a December 2014 pilot cruise evaluating underwater hyperspectral imagery.

name: Geonorge
summary: National website for map data and other location information in Norway, run and built by the Norwegian Mapping Authority; NIBIO's SR16 page points to it for download.

name: GPS Collars
summary: Norwegian-registered seller of GPS tracking collars and tags for birds, wildlife and agriculture, which send location data to researchers through Argos, Bluetooth, satellite phone, UHF or cellular links.

name: GreenEO
summary: Project led by NILU and Leonor Tarrason that uses satellite data, models and machine learning for land use, pollution and biodiversity tools, with ecosystem health monitors planned.

name: Hallingskarvet nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board whose site covers management of Hallingskarvet National Park and Finse biotope protected area, and the tasks the board and manager carry out.

name: Hold Norge Rent
summary: Organisation that has collected information through citizen science in the digital tool Rydde.

name: HyVa
summary: Collaboration between NTNU, NIVA and OceanObs using HYPSO hyperspectral data, funded by the Norwegian Space Agency, aiming at new satellite data products for Norwegian water bodies.

name: ibbi
summary: App built by Blåst Spel AS whose AI, according to its description, helps users find the right species, and whose users can share findings with GBIF.

name: INFOBIOM
summary: SNS-funded network of Nordic researchers, led by Johannes Breidenbach, with the Norwegian Institute for Nature Research as a partner.

name: Institute of Marine Research
summary: Bergen-based marine research institute with about 1,030 employees, whose researchers used deep learning to count and identify fish in trawl images; it runs the Norwegian Marine Data Centre.

name: Jomfruland nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board that is the management authority for Jomfruland National Park and Stråholmen landscape protected area.

name: Jostedalsbreen nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board that announced in December 2025 it had had a management plan prepared for the cultural landscape of the summer farm areas in Befringsdalen, Sunnfjord municipality.

name: Kart over naturskog
summary: Active dataset giving an overview of where natural forest may be found in Norway, built by four institutions including NIBIO and NINA; the maps are a first version.

name: Kilden
summary: NIBIO's main map solution, run by the institute, holding all its data alongside other central national datasets.

name: Kongsberg Discovery
summary: Organisation that has been developing a digital solution combining hydroacoustic sensors for ecosystem monitoring and seafloor mapping with other ocean measurements.

name: Kongsberg Maritime
summary: An industrial partner of CRIMAC, a project to automate interpretation of broadband acoustic data from research and fishing vessels using AI, drones and inspection technology; five of its staff are listed.

name: Kongsberg Satellite Services
summary: Tromsø-based company describing itself as a provider of ground networks and Earth observation services, with a 2020 NICFI imagery frame contract of up to MNOK 405.

name: Krill fishery acoustics predator mapping
summary: Closed project that applied machine learning to krill fishery acoustic data shared by Aker QRILL Company, running a trained model on more than 30,000 hours of fisheries acoustics.

name: Langsua nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board that manages ten of the eleven protected areas in Langsua under their protection regulations.

name: LAVDAS
summary: Active project, running April 2024 to March 2027 on a 14 million kroner budget, aiming to improve Norway's bog and wetland map base, with AI and satellite images planned.

name: Lofotodden nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board whose bylaws frame its work as management authority, with the Environment Agency setting them as part of the delegation.

name: Lomsdal-Visten nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board appointed by the Environment Agency as management authority for Lomsdal-Visten National Park and associated protected areas.

name: Lopphavet verneområdestyre
summary: Board appointed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment as management authority for the Lopphavet marine protected area.

name: Lyngsalpan verneområdestyre
summary: Board whose site covers management of the Lyngsalpan landscape protected area and the other protected areas it manages.

name: Machine-readable Nature
summary: Programme run by the University of Oslo and led by Dag Endresen, acting as contact point for research data infrastructures at the Natural History Museum in Oslo.

name: MALINOR
summary: Project of unknown status, run by Akvaplan-niva, whose main objective is mapping marine litter; the Fram Centre reported in January 2021 that it used multicopter drones for validation.

name: MAREANO
summary: Programme running since January 2006, run by the Norwegian Environment Agency, mapping seabed depth, sediments, biodiversity, habitats and pollution offshore Norway, and using machine learning to model biotopes.

name: Maridalens Venner
summary: Organisation founded in 1970 to stop the valley's farms being demolished, whose 2023 goals included finishing restoration of priority semi-natural hay meadows and management measures against overgrowth.

name: Marint naturkart
summary: Active 2025 to 2026 project, run by NIVA for the Norwegian Environment Agency, aiming to map marine habitat types along mainland Norway's coast using drones, machine learning and satellites.

name: MASSIMAL
summary: Coastal habitat mapping methods project, run by UiT and NIVA with Research Council of Norway funding, which ran 2020-2024 and is now finished, combining hyperspectral and underwater images to train machine learning algorithms.

name: Midtre Nordland nasjonalparkstyre
summary: A protected-area board that manages 14 protected areas, running from Rago in the north to Saltfjellet-Svartisen in the south.

name: Miljolare.no
summary: Environment monitoring platform for schools and individuals, built and run by the University of Bergen with ministry funding, where participants investigate their local area and the data they collect becomes available to others.

name: Ministry of Climate and Environment
summary: Ministry with main responsibility for government environment and climate policy, which funds MAREANO and SEAPOP and has the Norwegian Environment Agency under it.

name: Ministry of Energy
summary: Ministry that SEAPOP names as a funder.

name: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries
summary: Ministry to which the Institute of Marine Research is subordinate, providing 40% of its funding.

name: Mohn Technology
summary: Small Bergen firm developing underwater technology for research, fisheries and aquaculture, whose AI-processed Fish Research System cameras were reported in August 2024 as four new units in Finnmark for pink salmon, with NOK 2.5 million reported by iLaks in April 2024.

name: Museum Stavanger
summary: A museum that hosts the Norwegian Bird Ringing Centre, which organises all scientific bird ringing in Norway, where about 200,000 to 250,000 wild birds are ringed each year.

name: Møysalen nasjonalparkstyre
summary: A national park board whose members are appointed by the Environment Agency on nomination from the municipalities, Nordland county council and the Sami Parliament.

name: Nansen Environmental and Remote Sensing Center
summary: Research centre on ocean, sea-ice and atmospheric conditions in the North Atlantic and Arctic, applying AI to satellite, buoy and simulation data and contributing marine forecasting services to Copernicus.

name: NARIN
summary: Digital map solution for forest area surveys, built by Biofokus, with all forest survey data and fact sheets for 2004 to 2020 available on Narin-kart.

name: Nasjonalparkstyret for Femundsmarka og Gutulia
summary: Board whose bylaws frame its work as management authority, with the Environment Agency setting them as part of the delegation.

name: Nasjonalparkstyret for Forollhogna
summary: Board whose bylaws frame its work as the management authority for Forollhogna.

name: Nasjonalparkstyret for Fulufjellet
summary: Board appointed by the ministry as management authority for Fulufjellet National Park and Fregn nature reserve.

name: Nasjonalparkstyret for Jotunheimen og Utladalen
summary: Board that is the management authority for Jotunheimen National Park and Utladalen landscape protected area.

name: Nasjonalparkstyret for Reinheimen
summary: A national park board that is the management authority for Reinheimen National Park and its landscape protected areas and nature reserves.

name: Nasjonalparkstyret for Skarvan og Roltdalen og Sylan
summary: A national park board whose bylaws, set by the Environment Agency as part of the delegation, frame its work as management authority.

name: Nasjonalparkstyret for Øvre Dividal nasjonalpark og Dividalen landskapsvernområde
summary: A national park board whose site covers management of Øvre Dividal National Park and Dividalen landscape protected area, and the tasks of the board and manager.

name: National nature account for Norway
summary: Proposed national nature account that Norway is to establish in 2026, run by the Norwegian Environment Agency, following a NINA pilot with 67 indicators across seven main ecosystems.

name: Natural History Museum, University of Oslo
summary: University of Oslo museum holding Norway's largest collection of natural science objects, hosting the Norwegian GBIF node since 2005 and, through its MaNa group, contact point for research data infrastructures.

name: Nature Index for Norway
summary: Closed programme, run by the Norwegian Environment Agency and led by NINA, that measured biodiversity change across seven ecosystem types, with its last update as a standalone framework in 2025 and a forest value of 0.45.

name: Naturkart
summary: Dataset under early development by the Norwegian Environment Agency with five partners, using remote sensing and AI to give a national map of possible nature types, with a first version expected in spring 2027.

name: Naturvernforbundet Hordaland
summary: A nature conservation organisation reported, in an article updated February 2024, to be restoring about 400 decares of heathland at Rapeneset with partners, and which helped clear Sitka spruce at Hatten in 2020.

name: Naustdal-Gjengedal verneområdestyre
summary: A protected-area board whose site provides information on the protected area, the board and its management.

name: NILU
summary: Organisation that coordinates GreenEO, with Stefan Jetschny of NILU named by the FAIRiCUBE site as coordinator of that project.

name: NIVA Aquamonitor
summary: NIVA's web solution for showing monitoring and research data, run by the Norwegian Institute for Water Research.

name: NIVA FerryBox
summary: Programme run by NIVA and part of the national NorSOOP infrastructure, measuring temperature, salinity, oxygen, turbidity and fluorescence every minute along a ship's fixed route.

name: Noora
summary: Norwegian tech company founded in 2023, according to The Hub, developing forest carbon projects in the Nordics and using satellite data and machine learning to monitor them.

name: NORCE
summary: Research institute in Bergen that describes itself as a leading Norwegian Earth observation institute, says it uses AI to monitor nature, climate and infrastructure, and in December 2025 reported its researcher developing an AI reindeer counting model.

name: Nord University
summary: State university based in Bodø that leads the Horizon Europe project MPA Europe (2023 to 2026, per a 2024 advert) and is a partner in BioBoost+, which applies AI to digital imagery.

name: Nordhordland Biosfæreområde IKS
summary: An organisation named in an article updated February 2024 as working with Naturvernforbundet, landowners and farmers to restore heathlands at Rapeneset on Radøy.

name: Norsk hekkefuglovervåking
summary: National monitoring programme for terrestrial breeding bird population changes, run by NINA and BirdLife Norway, using a network of 492 counting routes with raw data on GBIF.

name: Norsonic
summary: A producer of acoustics and vibration measurement systems, described by SINTEF as one of the world's leading, which co-funds the RoAR project with the Research Council of Norway.

name: Norwegian Agriculture Agency
summary: Agency whose 2024 forest survey tested drones and AI, finding fewer than half the plants found manually; in November 2024 it said it would continue testing with SmartForest partners.

name: Norwegian Barcode of Life
summary: National network and research infrastructure for DNA barcoding, whose members build and maintain an open reference database of Norwegian biodiversity and which is the national node in the BIOSCAN programme.

name: Norwegian Biodiversity Information Centre
summary: National biodiversity knowledge bank set up in 2005 in Trondheim, supplying information on Norwegian biodiversity and running Artsobservasjoner; it also publishes identification keys and datasets.

name: Norwegian Bird Ringing Centre
summary: A programme run by Museum Stavanger that organises all scientific bird ringing in Norway; about 10.5 million birds have been ringed since 1914, and its database holds just over 11 million records.

name: Norwegian Coastal Administration
summary: Organisation that leads the work on the BarentsWatch Centre.

name: Norwegian Computing Center
summary: Independent non-profit contract research foundation in Oslo that builds SeaBee, heading its deep learning development, and develops remote sensing methods for environmental and climate monitoring.

name: Norwegian Environment Agency
summary: Agency of 700 employees under the Ministry of Climate and Environment, managing Norwegian nature, running Rovbase, and using remote sensing and AI to develop a national nature map.

name: Norwegian Environment Agency remote sensing pilots
summary: Running since 2016, this Norwegian Environment Agency programme tests sensors with the Norwegian Space Agency through Copernicus; the Environment Agency also holds an annual remote sensing seminar.

name: Norwegian Hydrographic Service
summary: Division of the Norwegian Mapping Authority since 1986, responsible for the deep water database; Fugro reports a 2023 MAREANO survey contract from it.

name: Norwegian Institute for Water Research
summary: Oslo-based water and environment research institute that leads SeaBee, runs NIVA AquaMonitor and leads a 24-organisation European biodiversity and ecosystems consortium under a 2023 to 2026 agreement.

name: Norwegian Institute of Bioeconomy Research
summary: Ås-based institute that reported training tree-recognition models on laser scanning data in May 2025 and signed an agreement with NMBU in June 2026 to set up AI for Nature.

name: Norwegian Mapping Authority
summary: Based in Hønefoss, this authority collates, manages and communicates public geographical information from mountains to ocean floor, and produces national digital map series.

name: Norwegian Marine Data Centre
summary: Programme run by the Institute of Marine Research that holds the largest collection of marine environmental and fisheries data in Norway.

name: Norwegian Meteorological Institute
summary: Listed by Store norske leksikon as an agency under the Ministry of Climate and Environment, it partners with GreenEO.

name: Norwegian Monitoring Programme for Agricultural Landscapes
summary: Programme launched in 1998 to document the status and change of agricultural landscapes systematically.

name: Norwegian National Forest Inventory
summary: Programme started in 1919 that gives an overview of Norway's forest resources, with data in official statistics; in April 2016 NIBIO described 13,000 sample plots visited.

name: Norwegian Nature Inspectorate
summary: Field body of environmental management, run by the Norwegian Environment Agency, headquartered in Trondheim with local offices and supervising protected areas and carnivore management.

name: Norwegian Orca ID Catalogue
summary: Dataset of 1,500+ identified killer whales, recognised from the fin and saddle patch, built and run by the Norwegian Orca Survey.

name: Norwegian Orca Survey
summary: Organisation that set up year-round killer whale monitoring in northern Norway in 2013 and opens its identification catalogue to everyone.

name: Norwegian Polar Institute
summary: Tromsø-based body for Arctic and Antarctic research, mapping and monitoring that runs SEAPOP; authors from it wrote in 2026 of five years developing drone survey methods for marine mammals.

name: Norwegian Retailers' Environment Fund
summary: Fund that Akvaplan-niva called the largest private environmental fund in Norway in August 2020.

name: Norwegian Ships of Opportunity Program
summary: Closed national infrastructure programme for scientific measurements from available ships, built by NIVA, the Institute of Marine Research and Akvaplan-niva, with a 2018 to 2023 project period.

name: Norwegian Space Agency
summary: Acting for the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries and coordinating Norwegian space policy and industry, it funded Vake in 2020, according to its site, and funds HyVa.

name: Norwegian University of Life Sciences
summary: Signed an agreement with NIBIO on 30 June 2026 to set up the AI for Nature centre.

name: NTNU University Museum
summary: University museum whose molecular laboratory data are used in biodiversity research, with a clean room for DNA from historical, archaeological and environmental samples.

name: Nærøyfjorden verneområdestyre
summary: A protected-area board appointed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment to manage six protected areas, all within the Nærøyfjorden part of the Western Norwegian Fjords World Heritage area.

name: Ocean Access
summary: Organisation whose buoy for remote ocean monitoring is described by ESA BIC Norway.

name: Ocean Data Platform
summary: Programme built and run by HUB Ocean, with a catalogue of ocean, climate and biodiversity datasets from public, scientific and industrial sources.

name: Offshore Norge
summary: Organisation named as a funder of SEAPOP that also sits on its steering committee.

name: OptiMiSe
summary: Project combining eDNA, AI-assisted image analysis and traditional taxonomy, led by the Norwegian Research Centre and funded by the Research Council of Norway.

name: Overvåking av fjellrev
summary: A monitoring programme run by NINA with the Norwegian Nature Inspectorate, combining checks of known den sites with scat collection for DNA analysis, and since 2019 a yearly model-based population estimate.

name: Overvåking av humler og dagsommerfugler
summary: A volunteer monitoring programme recording bumblebees and butterflies to species on fixed transects three times each summer, with Sabima and NINA, supplying European butterfly indicator data and covering the whole country as of 2026.

name: PathFinder
summary: Closed project that NIBIO dates 1 September 2022 to 31 August 2026, with Johannes Breidenbach as project manager and a listed publication using a convolutional neural network.

name: Program for terrestrisk naturovervåking (TOV)
summary: A monitoring programme in seven areas of near-untouched nature, aiming to detect how acid rain, pollutants and climate change affect biodiversity in forests and mountains, with data offered on its site.

name: Raet nasjonalparkstyre
summary: A national park board with delegated authority to manage Raet National Park and Søm landscape protected area.

name: Rainforest Foundation Norway
summary: Organisation whose 1993 Xingu pilot combined satellite monitoring with border expeditions by the park's indigenous inhabitants, and which partnered with The Engine Room on a technology primer.

name: Region Nordhordland biosfæreavdeling
summary: A department of Region Nordhordland that, a June 2023 article reported, worked to implement the UNESCO biosphere status the region received in 2019.

name: Reisa nasjonalparkstyre
summary: A national park board that manages Reisa National Park and Ráisduottarháldi landscape protected area, appointed by the Environment Agency on nomination from municipalities, county council and Sami Parliament.

name: Research Council of Norway
summary: Described by the University of Oslo as a national strategic and funding agency, it announces six AI centres starting in 2025, funds AMBIOS and financed MASSIMAL.

name: RoAR (Robust Acoustic Recognition)
summary: A project by Norsonic, SINTEF and NINA, funded by Norsonic and the Research Council of Norway, to improve AI sound recognition, using urban noise and biodiversity datasets, and to create a service for building sound monitoring systems.

name: Rohkunborri nasjonalparkstyre
summary: A national park board appointed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment as management authority for Rohkunborri National Park.

name: Rondane-Dovre nasjonalparkstyre
summary: A national park board appointed by the Environment Agency as management authority for two national parks, four landscape protected areas and eight nature reserves.

name: Rovbase
summary: Management tool holding information on large carnivores across five species, built and run by the Norwegian Environment Agency, including DNA analysis results.

name: Rovdata
summary: Programme set up in October 2010, run by the Norwegian Institute for Nature Research, supplying monitoring data and population figures on lynx, wolverine, brown bear, wolf and golden eagle.

name: Sabima
summary: Umbrella organisation for Norway's biological societies that works with members to raise volunteer nature mapping, and mobilises an annual national day for finding species.

name: satellittdata.no
summary: Sentinel data service run by the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, partnered with the Norwegian Space Agency, giving simpler access to Sentinel data and storing data over Norwegian areas of interest.

name: Scantrol Deep Vision
summary: Organisation selling systems that record and analyse fish species, sizes and locations in real time, and reporting a pilot for commercial fishing with first images collected in 2022.

name: Science and Technology AS
summary: Organisation with which the authors of the SENTREE poster are affiliated.

name: Sea forest monitoring collaboration
summary: Collaboration on developing a sea forest monitoring solution, announced as an agreement on 27 November 2025 by Kongsberg Satellite Services, SeaForester and Kongsberg Discovery.

name: SeaBee
summary: A NIVA-led drone research infrastructure for coastal and aquatic studies in Norway, using deep learning on image data; NIVA gives its project period as 2020 to 2029.

name: SeaForester
summary: An organisation that says its initiative began in Portugal and grew into an international partner network; SeaForester AS has applied for permission for a research and development project in Hammerfest.

name: SEAPOP
summary: A long-term seabird monitoring and mapping programme in Norway, established in 2005, with a study on its site reporting drone images and neural networks reaching an 87.5% detection rate.

name: SEATRACK
summary: An international collaboration of 69 partners from 52 institutions in 14 countries mapping the non-breeding distribution of North Atlantic seabirds, with Phase III (2023-2026) funded by institutions, government, Offshore Norge and energy companies.

name: SegmentAnyTree
summary: A sensor- and platform-agnostic deep learning model for tree crown segmentation in lidar data, built by Maciej Wielgosz.

name: Seiland/Sievju nasjonalparkstyre
summary: A national park board appointed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment as management authority for Seiland/Sievju National Park.

name: SENTREE
summary: A project whose May 2022 poster described its primary goal as automating classification of Norway spruce, Scots pine and birch using semantic segmentation networks with aerial and satellite data.

name: Simula
summary: An organisation whose website describes an AI-driven fish sorting system aimed at protecting Norway's native salmon species from invasive pink salmon.

name: SINTEF
summary: An organisation whose 2020 to 2023 bioacoustics and AI project aimed to develop recording technology and reduce manual labour adapting AI models; SINTEF Industry coordinates AMBIOS.

name: SINTEF Ocean
summary: A multidisciplinary research institute within the SINTEF Group that leads a demonstrator use case in DTO-BioFlow.

name: SmartForest
summary: An eight-year forest research project, 2020 to 2028, with a NOK 234 million budget per NIBIO, working on AI models for segmenting and classifying laser data.

name: Smågnager-overvåking
summary: A monitoring programme launched by the Norwegian Environment Agency in 2023 using camera traps and an AI algorithm to identify rodent species, with five mountain stations set up that year.

name: Spectrofly
summary: An organisation named as an industry partner in SeaBee and credited for a marine habitat drone image.

name: SR16 forest resource map
summary: A nationwide dataset of Norway's forest resources on a 16 by 16 metre grid, combining field plots with remote sensing data, run by the Norwegian Institute of Bioeconomy Research.

name: Stabbursdalen nasjonalparkstyre
summary: A national park board with management authority for Stabbursdalen National Park and Stabbursdalen landscape protected area.

name: Statskog SF
summary: A state enterprise that manages the state's forest and outfield land, owning nearly 60 million decares (about 20 per cent of mainland Norway), of which about 43 per cent is protected.

name: Stølsheimen verneområdestyre
summary: A protected-area board appointed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment as management authority for Stølsheimen landscape protected area.

name: Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund
summary: An organisation established in 2007 that funds projects protecting Svalbard's natural environment.

name: Sølen verneområdestyre
summary: A protected-area board appointed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment to manage Sølen landscape protected area and the Fuggdalen and Steinfjellet nature reserves.

name: The Nansen Legacy
summary: Closed Arctic marine climate and ecosystem research project, running 2018 to 2023 according to GBIF, with about 280 people from ten institutions, 53 published datasets and final reports approved in March 2025.

name: The Sound of Norway
summary: A project by scientists at NINA and the University of Cambridge that monitors ecosystems nationwide with real-time recording devices and uses machine learning to classify bird vocalisations.

name: Tiepoint
summary: A SeaBee industry partner set up in 2022 by Andøya Space as a joint venture with Sundt Air Group; it says it uses in-house AI-augmented solutions with edge computing.

name: Tilsynsutvalet i Vestland for Hardangervidda nasjonalpark
summary: A committee whose guidelines of 2 November 2020 set conditions for granting motor-traffic permits in Hardangervidda National Park for the winter seasons 2021–2024.

name: Troll Systems
summary: A partner with Huawei, Berlevåg Jeger- og fiskerforening and Simula when a pilot automated trap was first set out in Storelva in Berlevåg in 2021.

name: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
summary: Tromsø-based university that hosts Visual Intelligence and a Machine Learning research group, and has been a partner in DIMARC and MASSIMAL.

name: University of Agder
summary: University with campuses in Kristiansand and Grimstad that advertised posts in 2020, 2021 and 2023 on AI for marine bioacoustics, cod vocalisation processing and coastal video.

name: University of Bergen
summary: Bergen university named by the Institute of Marine Research as a CRIMAC research partner, with a 2025 doctoral thesis on machine learning for fisheries acoustic data.

name: University of Oslo
summary: Oslo university whose Natural History Museum hosts GBIF Norway, and which advertised in 2022 for an engineer on the Horizon Europe-funded BioDT project.

name: University of South-Eastern Norway
summary: University whose affiliated researchers, including Simone Santoro, appear in OpenAlex on a 2025 paper and a 2026 review about AI and image processing in camera trap data.

name: Vake
summary: Company that KSAT reported in 2024 had worked since 2018 on machine learning for satellite images of vessel behaviour, and in which KSAT acquired a 70 percent stake.

name: Vannmiljø
summary: The Norwegian Environment Agency’s system into which monitoring data from operational and baseline monitoring are to be imported.

name: Varangerhalvøya nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board appointed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment as management authority, whose site covers the protected areas and the management tasks the board and manager carry out.

name: Vega verneområdestyre
summary: Protected area board that was delegated management authority for the protected areas in Vega municipality on 5 May 2011.

name: Verdsarvrådet for Vestnorsk fjordlandskap
summary: Council whose primary task is to safeguard and promote the World Heritage status of the Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord areas.

name: Verneområdestyret for Geiranger-Herdalen landskapsvernområde
summary: Board with delegated management authority over Geiranger-Herdalen landscape protected area and the Hyskjet and Kallskaret nature reserves.

name: Verneområdestyret for Kvænangsbotn og Navitdalen landskapsvernområder
summary: Board with delegated management authority for the Kvænangsbotn and Navitdalen landscape protected areas.

name: Verneområdestyret for Nordkvaløya-Rebbenesøya
summary: A protected-area board responsible for Nordkvaløya-Rebbenesøya landscape protected area, Ytre Karlsøy marine protected area and five nature reserves.

name: Verneområdestyret for Oksøy-Ryvingen og Flekkefjord landskapsvernområder
summary: A protected-area board appointed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment to manage Oksøy-Ryvingen and Flekkefjord landscape protected areas and a series of nature reserves.

name: Verneområdestyret for Setesdal Vesthei, Ryfylkeheiane og Frafjordheiane
summary: A protected-area board whose site covers management of the Setesdal Vesthei, Ryfylke and Frafjordheiane landscape protected areas, their protection regulations, and the board and secretariat.

name: Verneområdestyret for Skardsfjella og Hyllingsdalen
summary: A protected-area board whose site covers management of Skardsfjella and Hyllingsdalen landscape protected area and the work of the board and national park manager.

name: Verneområdestyret for Trollheimen
summary: Management authority for the Trollheimen and Innerdalen landscape protected areas and the Svartåmoen and Minilldalsmyrene nature reserves.

name: Visual Intelligence
summary: Research Council of Norway-funded Centre for Research-based Innovation on deep learning for visual data, with marine work including fish acoustics with the Institute of Marine Research and oil spills with KSAT.

name: WWF Norway
summary: Had a web map made with Sabima and DNT showing areas set aside for development and the nature that could be affected.

name: Yggdrasil
summary: Proposed centre on AI for monitoring and projecting Norwegian forest ecosystems, which NIBIO said in June 2026 was in the final round of the SFF scheme with MINA at NMBU.

name: Ytre Hvaler nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board with management responsibility for Ytre Hvaler National Park, Rauerfjorden marine protected area and Teineholmen nature reserve.

name: Ålfotbreen verneområdestyre
summary: Board that manages one protected area, the Ålfotbreen landscape protected area.

name: Ånderdalen nasjonalparkstyre
summary: Board appointed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment as the management authority for Ånderdalen National Park.

name: Økosystemovervåking i ferskvann (Økofersk)
summary: A closed freshwater monitoring programme spanning 2009–2025, aiming to provide reference data from unaffected water bodies and covering about 100 lakes, with about 40 sampled annually.

name: Økosystemovervåking i kystvann (Økokyst)
summary: A coastal and fjord ecosystem monitoring programme run by the Norwegian Environment Agency, covering all counties with a coastline and reporting data to Vannmiljø, the EU, ICES, CBMP and OSPAR.

name: Økosystemovervåkning i store innsjøer (Økostor)
summary: A monitoring programme for 27 large Norwegian lakes covering phytoplankton, aquatic plants, invertebrates and fish, with all data entered in Vannmiljø.

name: Øvre Pasvik nasjonalparkstyre
summary: A national park board that manages Øvre Pasvik National Park and Øvre Pasvik landscape protected area.

name: ACAP Jomsom drone forest surveillance, Mustang
summary: Drone patrols described as AI-powered, run by the Annapurna Conservation Area Project, began in Mustang, reported in May 2026, meant to detect trap poaching and cut fire risk.

name: Acoustic Survey and Monitoring to Lay the Foundation for Conservation of the Endemic Csorba’s Mouse Eared Bat (Myotis csorbai) in Nepal
summary: Closed project on the endemic Csorba's mouse-eared bat in Nepal, which planned acoustic monitoring with AudioMoths and a call library, and reported roost and acoustic surveys in a February 2023 final evaluation.

name: Agriculture and Forestry University
summary: A university whose Faculty of Forestry in Hetauda is listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a paper integrating Earth observation and machine learning for forest fire risk assessment in Rasuwa district.

name: Annapurna Conservation Area Project
summary: An active NTNC project launched in 1986, covering 7,629 square kilometres, reported in December 2025 to have begun studying snow leopard numbers with 161 camera traps.

name: Babai River gharial drone survey (Bardia National Park)
summary: A closed survey of gharials along the Babai River using drone images, compared with ground surveys; the drone flew 12 missions over 102 kilometres and took 11,799 photographs.

name: Bardia Conservation Program
summary: NTNC programme launched in 1994 for biodiversity research and sustainable community development, covering ungulate, Gangetic dolphin and vegetation studies, plus training national park staff in wildlife monitoring.

name: Bardia National Park
summary: A national park that reportedly set up 50 camera traps and 64 CCTV cameras by October 2020, and in 2019 began using a smart patrol mobile app to record rhinos after GPS collars stopped working.

name: Bardiya spotted deer individual identification
summary: A project in Bardiya National Park where, Mongabay reported in October 2023, Wageningen University researchers were developing an algorithm to identify and count chital by their spots, training it on fallow deer in a Dutch enclosure.

name: Bats and Caves: Seasonal Monitoring and Conservation in Kaligandaki Canyon, Nepal
summary: Rufford project, page dated 25 June 2019, planned seasonal baseline data from caves for a management guideline, after earlier work documented 13 bat roosting caves and nearly 16 species.

name: Biodiversity Conservation Center (NTNC)
summary: An NTNC unit whose Sauraha chief reportedly described 32 cameras installed at 16 Tikauli corridor locations in August 2017.

name: Bird Conservation Nepal
summary: A Kathmandu-based organisation whose 2020 checklist describes bird monitoring in Madane protected forest since 2018 with support from Dansk Ornitologisk Forening.

name: Central Department of Environmental Science, Tribhuvan University
summary: A Tribhuvan University department in Kirtipur, established in 2001, listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a paper on Himalayan red panda habitat suitability in Dhorpatan Hunting Reserve.

name: Central Department of Zoology, Tribhuvan University
summary: A Tribhuvan University department in Kathmandu, listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a paper on factors influencing mammalian community occupancy in Dhorpatan Hunting Reserve.

name: Centre for Molecular Dynamics Nepal
summary: A centre founded by Dibesh Karmacharya that Dialogue Earth reports profiled aquatic biodiversity in four rivers using eDNA.

name: Chhimeki Chara
summary: Bird-count app that Nepali Times reports Bird Conservation Nepal designed for its annual census; by February 2022 nearly 1,000 volunteers and partners from 64 districts had downloaded it.

name: Chinese pangolin camera-trap occupancy survey, Kavrepalanchok (Rufford 41455-2)
summary: Closed camera-trap survey of Chinese pangolins in Kavrepalanchok community forests, whose final report records 1,222 camera-trap days.

name: Chitwan National Park
summary: A national park reported in December 2025 to have counted 366 gharials, and in March 2026 to use 25 motion-sensor spy cameras and seven drones.

name: Community Conservation of Chitwan National Park’s Freshwater Ecosystems and Gharials
summary: Project run by Himalayan Nature that surveyed gharial population and distribution along the Rapti and Narayani rivers in Chitwan National Park.

name: Conserving biodiversity through community engagement in Gaurishankar Conservation Area, Nepal
summary: A project running from April 2023 to December 2026, led by Madhu Chetri and funded by the UK's Defra, that includes building a biodiversity database and camera trapping training in Gaurishankar Conservation Area.

name: Conserving Small Carnivores in the Tinjure-Milke-Jaljale Landscape of Nepal
summary: Run by the Nature Conservation and Study Centre, this Tinjure-Milke-Jaljale small carnivore project trained 45 community forest members and deployed camera traps at 12 sites by February 2024.

name: Department of Forests and Soil Conservation
summary: A government department whose site places it under the Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment in Kathmandu.

name: Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation
summary: A government department publishing a protected area coverage database and tiger telemetry manual; The Himalayan Times reports it jointly conducted the 2026 tiger and prey survey.

name: Department of Plant Resources
summary: A government department in Thapathali, Kathmandu, registered with GBIF as a data publisher, publishing datasets on the endemic and alien flora of Nepal held at KATH.

name: Drone monitoring of gharial and mugger populations in the East Rapti River, Chitwan National Park
summary: A closed project, led by Gokarna Jung Thapa and funded by WWF UK, that surveyed a 73 km stretch of the East Rapti River by drone in early 2024, with an analyst counting 323 crocodiles.

name: Ecology of Snow Leopard and Strengthening Community Engagement for its Conservation in Manaslu Conservation Area, Nepal
summary: Closed Rufford-funded snow leopard project in Manaslu Conservation Area, which in 2022 planned camera trap monitoring in the Chum Valley, scat diet analysis and a habitat suitability map.

name: Egyptian Vulture GPS tagging and monitoring in Nepal (Rufford booster grant)
summary: Active Rufford booster grant project whose November 2024 report says five Egyptian Vultures were trapped at Pokhara Valley dumping sites for GPS tagging and monitoring.

name: Forest Guardian programme
summary: A programme built and run by Red Panda Network, which Mongabay reports has recruited about 128 guardians, 44 of them monitoring red pandas in the Panchthar–Ilam–Taplejung Corridor.

name: Forest Research and Training Centre
summary: A centre that, a Banko Janakari article says, developed the National Land Cover Monitoring System with ICIMOD, providing annual Nepal land cover for 2000 to 2019.

name: Friends of Nature (FON) Nepal
summary: A youth-led NGO that says it was established in 2005 and registered in Kathmandu; a former intern describes camera trapping during an internship beginning in November 2015.

name: Gaurishankar Conservation Area Project
summary: A project run by the National Trust for Nature Conservation, which the Government of Nepal entrusted in 2010 for 20 years with managing Gaurishankar Conservation Area, and whose page lists camera trapping news.

name: Geovation Nepal Pvt. Ltd.
summary: A Kathmandu-based company that Nepali ICT reports was founded in January 2021 and offers drone services, including wildlife and ecological monitoring, with thermal and multispectral sensors.

name: Himalayan Gharial Project
summary: Gharial conservation project run by Himalayan Nature, using telemetry and video monitoring of nesting sites, which identified the Rapti as Nepal's most critical habitat; the next phase plans direct action.

name: Himalayan Nature
summary: A Nepal-registered charity with a field centre north of Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve, formerly hosting the Asian Waterbird Census and reportedly recording 22 dolphins with partners in 2025.

name: Himalayan Pollinator Patrol
summary: A project run by the Nature Conservation and Study Centre that, the centre says, engages communities in monitoring and protecting pollinators, with citizen scientists observing, documenting and reporting activity.

name: Hog deer density and habitat study, Shuklaphanta National Park (Rufford 39474-1)
summary: Closed Rufford-funded study of hog deer in Shuklaphanta National Park grasslands, whose final evaluation report describes 30 camera traps with the random encounter model and MaxEnt habitat modelling.

name: Implementing evidence-based conservation measures to protect Chinese Pangolin in Khotang, eastern Nepal
summary: Run by NCSC with Mohamed bin Zayed fund support, this active project reportedly confirmed Chinese pangolins in Khotang community forests through six months of camera trapping ending January 2026.

name: Investigating Population Status and Prevalent Threats of Endangered Black-bellied Tern along the Koshi River, Nepal
summary: Study run by Himalayan Nature that aims to set baseline data by mapping the endangered black-bellied tern population along the Koshi River; listing dated 25 April 2025.

name: Kakarbhitta-Laukahi elephant movement monitoring
summary: A proposed project, under an MoU NTNC signed with the Department of Roads' ADB Project Directorate on 30 May 2025, to fit GPS collars to six wild Asian elephants, with the agreement running to January 2027.

name: Kathmandu University
summary: A university whose Aquatic Ecology Centre is listed by OpenAlex as an affiliation of Prayon Joshi, first author of a paper on monitoring chlorophyll-a in Phewa Lake with satellite images and ensemble-based learning.

name: Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve
summary: A wildlife reserve whose reported annual four-day dolphin census data show 17 dolphins in the Saptakoshi River in 2022 and 19 in both 2023 and 2024.

name: Kosi Bird Observatory
summary: Himalayan Nature's field centre, described as Nepal's first bird observatory, where bird ringing and participatory monitoring were run around Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve to establish a national ringing scheme.

name: Kunming Biodiversity Fund project in Kanchenjunga Conservation Area
summary: An eight-month Kunming Biodiversity Fund project, led by UNESCO and reported by The Himalayan Times as concluded, that trained local communities in the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area to use trail cameras and GPS devices.

name: Linking Citizen Science to turn paper results into red panda conservation outputs in Khotang and Bhojpur Districts, eastern Nepal
summary: Grant awarded 16 June 2023 by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund to train community forest user groups as citizen scientists monitoring red pandas by tracking and camera trapping.

name: Ministry of Forests and Environment
summary: A ministry hosting Nepal’s CBD focal point that sought NBSAP Vision Document (2025-2030) comments; The Himalayan Times reports it unveiled the 2026 tiger survey findings.

name: National Forest Inventory Nepal
summary: A closed forest resource assessment (2010 to 2014) run by FRTC with Finnish support, combining remote sensing and ground sampling, with data used in Nepal's forest reference levels and MRV.

name: National Herbarium and Plant Laboratories
summary: A plant institution at Godawari, Lalitpur, run by the Department of Plant Resources, whose home page links the KATH plant database and shows a digitisation set-up.

name: National Land Cover Monitoring System
summary: A programme built by the Forest Research and Training Centre and ICIMOD, with SERVIR as partner, that an FRTC article says gives annual Nepal land cover information for 2000 to 2019 using Landsat and Google Earth Engine.

name: National Rhino Count (Nepal)
summary: A closed census run in March and April 2021 that put Nepal's one-horned rhino population at 752; DNPWC was reported in September 2026 to be considering genetic sampling or camera traps next.

name: National snow leopard population survey, Nepal
summary: A closed survey led by two government departments with NTNC as partner, published in April 2025, estimating Nepal’s snow leopard population at 397, according to NTNC.

name: National Tiger and Prey Base Survey 2026
summary: A closed survey run by two government departments, with NTNC, WWF Nepal and ZSL as partners, that the Himalayan Times reports used about 1,100 camera traps in three lowland landscapes from December 2025 to July 2026.

name: Nature Conservation and Study Centre
summary: An organisation that runs the Himalayan Pollinator Patrol and said in February 2024 that it had started community-led conservation initiatives in central and eastern Nepal training forest user groups in camera-trap monitoring of mammals.

name: Nepal Bat Call Library
summary: A dataset established, according to the final report to the Rufford Foundation, as Nepal's first bat call library, holding reference calls of 15 bat species from the Kathmandu Valley.

name: Nepal fish DNA reference database
summary: Nepal's first fish DNA reference database, per Dialogue Earth, built by Centre for Molecular Dynamics Nepal in four-river eDNA work, helping embed eDNA in the Trishuli Assessment Tool.

name: Nepal Forest Fire Detection and Monitoring System
summary: Satellite-based fire detection system built by ICIMOD, reported by UN-SPIDER in July 2018 to use MODIS data and text alerts within 20 minutes of detection.

name: Nepal mid-winter water bird census
summary: An annual nationwide count, held every year since 1987, which began again in January 2026 across over 80 sites in 18 major wetland complexes.

name: Nepal Open University
summary: A university whose Faculty of Health, Science and Technology is listed by OpenAlex as an affiliation of Prayon Joshi, first author of a paper on monitoring chlorophyll-a in Phewa Lake using satellite images.

name: Nepal White-rumped Vulture telemetry project
summary: Satellite telemetry project on White-rumped Vultures, with six partners including Bird Conservation Nepal, which reported in November 2017 that seventeen tagged birds were providing movement data.

name: Nepalese Ornithological Union
summary: A non-profit membership organisation founded in 2010 which, according to Himalayan Nature, has led and coordinated the Asian Waterbird Census since 2025, including data management and oversight.

name: NTNC wildlife study in the hill districts of far western Nepal (Doti, Dadeldhura, Baitadi and Darchula)
summary: Camera-trap and occupancy study in four far western hill districts, run by the Shuklaphanta Conservation Program and NTNC, which the Kathmandu Post reported documented 22 mammal species.

name: Parsa National Park
summary: A national park that implemented SMART from 2014 and, per a 2019 ZSL Nepal report, received six smartphones with CyberTracker for data collection.

name: Preparation and sharing of camera traps occurrence database in Asia
summary: A project run by SMCRF with the University of Queensland, covering over 500,000 observations of over 300 vertebrate species across over 200 Asian sites, according to GBIF.

name: Red Panda (Ailurus fulgens fulgens Cuvier, 1825) Status, Distribution and Participatory Conservation Initiatives in Bhojpur District of Eastern Nepal
summary: Closed red panda project in Bhojpur district whose 2017 Rufford page planned baseline status and distribution data, GIS maps, and training local people as citizen scientist monitors.

name: Red Panda Network
summary: An organisation that runs and built the Forest Guardian programme, which Mongabay reports launched in 2010 with local community guardians who count red pandas and track their behaviour and habitat use.

name: Science Hub Nepal
summary: A Kathmandu non-profit that describes itself as using geospatial tools and Earth system models for questions including biodiversity, and lists land cover mapping and agriculture monitoring among its work.

name: Shey Phoksundo National Park
summary: National park where the Kathmandu Post reported in June 2021 that two snow leopards were being monitored with satellite collars, with on-site monitoring also planned.

name: Shuklaphanta Conservation Program
summary: NTNC programme in Shuklaphanta National Park, started in 1999 with regular activities since 2002, whose main objective is monitoring and researching natural resources.

name: Shuklaphanta National Park
summary: A national park that, the Kathmandu Post reported in April 2023, has counted its swamp deer for a decade by four-day head counts using staff, technicians and elephants.

name: Slender-billed vulture nest CCTV monitoring, Pokhara
summary: An active project, reported in December 2025 as Nepal's first, using a CCTV camera to monitor a slender-billed vulture nest in real time, with costs covered by the Rufford Foundation and Pokhara Bird Society.

name: Small Mammals Conservation and Research Foundation
summary: A Kathmandu non-profit working on biodiversity research and conservation, focused on small mammals since 2009, that says it is preparing a camera trap occurrence database for Asia with the University of Queensland.

name: Snow leopard satellite collaring study, Nepal
summary: Government plan, per a June 2021 spokesperson, to study 12 snow leopards in three protected areas over five years; four were collared in Kangchenjunga between 2013 and 2017.

name: Status Survey and Conservation of Fishing Cat (Prionailurus Viverrinus) in Parasi District, Nepal
summary: Run by Wild Care Nepal and led by Asmita Pageni, this closed project planned camera trapping and questionnaires; its final report records 150 trap nights of camera-trap data.

name: Strengthening tiger protection and monitoring in Parsa National Park
summary: A closed ZSL project to strengthen tiger protection and monitoring in Parsa National Park, which handed over six smartphones running CyberTracker for SMART data collection.

name: Survey Department
summary: Nepal's national mapping organisation according to its 2017 country report to UN-GGIM, then under the Ministry of Land Reform and Management, working on producing, disseminating and regulating geospatial information.

name: The National Trust for Nature Conservation
summary: An autonomous, not-for-profit body established by Legislative Act in 1982 that runs the Gaurishankar Conservation Area Project and, with funding support, carried out camera-trap work covering 1,695 grids in the Chure Region in 2016 to 2018.

name: Tribhuvan University
summary: A university that OpenAlex lists as having the most Nepal-affiliated works since 2018 in ecology and nature conservation subfields, with 1,024 of 1,599, and whose authors appear on several species and habitat papers.

name: Wild Care Nepal
summary: An organisation that says it is registered under the Government of Nepal and the Social Welfare Council, and lists a fishing cat status survey in Parasi district and a community gharial habitat initiative among its projects.

name: Wing Watchers
summary: App for recording vulture sightings in real time, which a Rufford final report says focuses on nine species and received checklists from 126 places.

name: WWF Nepal
summary: A conservation organisation active in Nepal since the 1960s that supports government management of six focal species, uses drones, and is listed by OpenAlex as an affiliation on a gharial and mugger drone monitoring paper.

name: Nauru Fisheries and Marine Resources Authority
summary: Nauru's statutory fisheries authority, set up by a 1997 Act with a Board of Directors, which a 2018 mid-term review reported was leading marine biodiversity conservation work in the R2R Nauru project.

name: Nauru's Rapid Biodiversity Assessment Project
summary: A closed 2013 Nauru project listed in the CBD country profile among national biodiversity programmes, with a later 2025 national framework reporting that its Biodiversity Rapid Assessment Programme identified 56 native plant species.

name: R2R: Implementing a "Ridge to Reef" Approach to Protecting Biodiversity and Ecosystem Functions in Nauru
summary: Closed project, funded by the Global Environment Facility with a 2,644,358 US dollar grant approved in March 2015 and closed in May 2022, whose mid-term review reports completed marine health and household mapping surveys.

name: 3D Coastal Mapping programme
summary: A programme launched in 2025 to map up to 40 percent of New Zealand's coastline, run by Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand and led by Stuart Caie, with Woolpert Asia-Pacific and NV5 Geospatial among its suppliers.

name: 800 Trust
summary: A Taranaki-based charity that builds the Hark acoustic monitors, which run Google's Perch v2 model on solar-powered devices to identify over 100 bird, bat and pest species, and is in an AI-for-the-planet accelerator cohort.

name: AI training for rat identification
summary: A project built by Zero Invasive Predators and funded by DOC to improve AI algorithms that distinguish between rat species in ZIP cameras.

name: AI-enabled multi-species kill trap
summary: A self-resetting kill trap, built by Critter Solutions, that uses AI species recognition to trigger only on rats, mice, mustelids and possums.

name: Alita
summary: A free desktop AI classifier for trail camera images, built by the Department of Conservation and Weka Research, that classifies about 80 species and shares its training and validation data.

name: Arthur's Pass Wildlife Trust
summary: Community-driven registered charitable trust at Arthur's Pass, funded by Save the Kiwi, whose 2024 brochure says volunteers survey great spotted kiwi in winter and lists remote monitoring equipment among ongoing costs.

name: ASG Technologies
summary: A company whose PredaCAM uses infrared and a cloud-based AI model to detect rats, funded by DOC and Predator Free 2050 Limited, with over 80% accuracy reported in initial field trials.

name: Atlas of bird distribution in New Zealand
summary: A dataset built by the Ornithological Society of New Zealand, covering 1999 to 2004, with more than 2,100 maps of over 200 bird species, reproduced as Webatlas maps on New Zealand Birds Online.

name: Auckland Zoo
summary: A zoo that says it is part of a charitable trust and Tātaki Auckland Unlimited, and whose Conservation Fund supported a drone and environmental DNA project to detect dugong in Malaysia.

name: Automated Island Biosecurity Detection and Response System
summary: A proposed system for one trial island, planned to use AI-enabled cameras, acoustic sensors, smart traps and lure dispensers to watch for invasive species, with AI detection models developed in year two.

name: AviaNZ
summary: Software built and led by Stephen Marsland to analyse recordings and estimate bird abundance, trained by 2019 to detect two native bat types and described as a national collaboration.

name: Bay Bush Action Trust
summary: Uses AI cameras for pests and wildlife, one family-funded; its deputy chair said in July 2024 that it had led Opua forest pest control for over a decade.

name: Biodiversity Monitoring and Reporting System
summary: A DOC-built and DOC-run programme giving consistent biodiversity information across public conservation lands, with Tier 1 sampling since late 2011 at locations 8 km apart, partnering with the Ministry for the Environment.

name: Bushcraft Analytics
summary: An organisation that DOC named alongside the contractor who used machine learning to find golden dodder in satellite images.

name: Callaghan Innovation
summary: A funder that says its R&D Experience Grants and R&D Career Grants supported Wilderlab's development of TICI.

name: Capital Kiwi Project
summary: Wellington kiwi project, led by Paul Ward, whose founder says it uses acoustic monitors with AI helping to analyse results, alongside tracking tunnels, trail cameras and DNA to identify stoats.

name: Cawthron Institute
summary: An organisation describing itself as New Zealand's largest independent science body, based in Nelson, which led the MBIE-funded Transforming Coastal Monitoring programme testing environmental DNA for estuary monitoring.

name: Citizens of the Sea
summary: An independent charitable trust that began as a Cawthron Institute and New Zealand Geographic partnership, and says it is sending 24 citizen scientist crews across the Southwest Pacific to collect eDNA in 2026.

name: Connected Conservation programme
summary: A pilot run by DOC with One New Zealand, with first sensors installed in early April 2026 in three national parks and around 50 smart sensors planned, plus trials of smart traps and trail cameras.

name: Critter Solutions
summary: A company whose AI self-resetting trap targets predators and whose OWL camera recognises species, with long-range thermal detection systems in development.

name: Department of Conservation
summary: New Zealand's government conservation agency, which runs the Tools to Market programme, funds ASG Technologies, partners with Wildlife AI, and in 2026 trialled machine learning on satellite images to find golden dodder.

name: DigiLab
summary: An organisation evaluating possum acoustic monitoring using large datasets of possum calls, and researching bird monitoring by comparing acoustic data against expert five-minute bird counts.

name: DOC AI camera
summary: A low-power thermal camera built by The Cacophony Project and used by DOC, which uses AI to identify predators and some native species and in 2024 detected a rat on Motutapu Island.

name: DOC Marine Data Portal
summary: A DOC-built and DOC-run portal that in December 2021 made public more than 300 marine data layers, including species distribution models, with an interactive map tool to visualise, analyse and download them.

name: Dragonfly and NASA forest mapping of Aotearoa
summary: A three-year, $1 million MBIE Catalyst Fund project with NASA to build a 3D forest map using NISAR radar and a public, open-access forest monitoring tool.

name: Dragonfly Data Science
summary: A Wellington-based organisation, one of whose team members was working with NASA in August 2024 on AI modelling of tree canopies from LiDAR and aerial imagery.

name: Earth Sciences New Zealand
summary: Formed on 1 July 2025 by the merger of NIWA and GNS Science, it lists AI, machine learning and data science among its purposes, and ecosystem stewardship too.

name: East Taranaki Environment Trust
summary: Charitable trust set up to help North Island western brown kiwi, mainly through Purangi Kiwi, which in 2018 was reported to have studied long-tailed bats with acoustic recorders; funded by Save the Kiwi.

name: Econode Limited
summary: New Zealand owned private company whose main product, SmartTrap, is a wireless biosecurity trap monitoring system that it says signals a base station when a trap is sprung.

name: Encounter Solutions
summary: Organisation whose connected leg-hold traps report in real time over the Celium long-range network, and whose LiveCapture feature lets cage traps be disabled remotely.

name: Envico Technologies
summary: Tauranga company offering drone, trap and seed-pod technologies for conservation and restoration, which says it is working with Manaaki Whenua Landcare Research on thermal imaging and machine learning to classify animals.

name: Friends of Flora
summary: Community group that, with the Department of Conservation, translocated 44 roroa to Flora Stream between 2010 and 2016 and tracked each by radio-telemetry until transmitters were removed in May 2018.

name: GBIF New Zealand
summary: New Zealand's node of GBIF, offering biodiversity data access and contribution guidance, reporting a 2024 pilot of councils uploading data, and currently recruiting a node manager.

name: Ground-truthing acoustic monitoring against five minute bird counts
summary: A project run by DigiLab and funded by DOC, aiming to check acoustic bird monitoring data against five-minute bird counts by expert observers.

name: Groundtruth
summary: New Zealand company supporting conservation and land management, developing a free LoRaWAN network service linked to Trap.NZ for traps and monitoring devices under DOC's Predator Free 2050 science programme.

name: HARK
summary: Model that runs Google's Perch v2 on the device, built by 800 Trust, used in a Taranaki zero possum project, and winner of a 2026 NZ Hi-Tech Awards category.

name: iNaturalist NZ – Mātaki Taiao
summary: New Zealand's iNaturalist regional network, run and built by the New Zealand Bio-Recording Network Trust, and the second country's network of its kind, from 2014.

name: Interpine Innovation
summary: Organisation that worked with the Ministry for the Environment on a planted forest inventory system for carbon monitoring, as of 2015.

name: Kaytoo
summary: Free desktop classifier for acoustic recordings, built by DOC and Weka Research, that classifies about 80 species and involves work on machine learning training data.

name: Kea Aerospace
summary: Christchurch aerospace company founded in 2018, which announced in April 2024 a partnership with NASA research centres on high-altitude airborne Earth observation.

name: Kea Conservation Trust
summary: Trust working to protect kea in the wild and in captivity, offering a Kea Surveys app for backcountry users and a database designed to track kea numbers over time.

name: Kea Surveys app
summary: An app, with DOC as partner, that lets people contribute to long-term monitoring of the kea population, alongside a database designed to track kea numbers over time and across locations.

name: Kiwi call count monitoring programme
summary: A formal DOC-run kiwi call monitoring programme, part of Kiwis for kiwi, in which listening takes place for two hours over four nights at each station.

name: Kiwi Coast
summary: Kiwi conservation group whose monitoring plan calls for acoustic Kiwi Listening Blitzes every five years; its first, in 2016, detected kiwi calls at 31 of 48 sites surveyed.

name: Kiwi Track Ltd
summary: Manufacturer of tracking transmitters mainly for wildlife in New Zealand, established by Daryl Olsen in 2003, with a postal address in Havelock North.

name: Kākāpō Recovery
summary: DOC-run programme, funded by Meridian Energy, that says it develops new technology for kākāpō, including smart transmitters on every bird and long-range data loggers sending data by satellite.

name: Large dataset acoustic monitoring
summary: A project run by DigiLab and funded by DOC, evaluating possum acoustic monitoring using large datasets of possum calls against current monitoring and detection methods.

name: Listening Lab
summary: Multidisciplinary research group that says it builds open-source machine learning models for species detection, offers a Sound Map of New Zealand at no cost, and is in Google DeepMind's APAC AI for the Planet cohort.

name: Marine Metre Squared
summary: Citizen science project, established in 2013 and run and built by the New Zealand Marine Studies Centre, recording seashore species data into BioCollect, with 3,098 completed surveys reported on its site.

name: Ministry for Cities, Environment, Regions, and Transport
summary: Government department listed in the Budget 2026 estimates as holding Vote Environment, placed in the Economic Development and Infrastructure Sector, covering housing, transport, environment, local government and regional development.

name: Ministry for Primary Industries
summary: Government ministry that, according to DOC, funds with DOC the development of remote sensing methods for New Zealand's forests, within research on forest carbon stocks.

name: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
summary: Government ministry that Cawthron Institute says funded the Transforming Coastal Monitoring programme, and whose address GBIF lists for one of New Zealand's GBIF delegates.

name: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa
summary: Museum whose collections API gives access to almost 1 million object and specimen records and 300,000 images, usable in other applications with a free registration key.

name: New Zealand Bio-Recording Network Trust
summary: A registered New Zealand charitable trust associated with iNaturalist NZ – Mātaki Taiao.

name: New Zealand Institute for Bioeconomy Science
summary: Organisation formed by amalgamating AgResearch, Plant & Food Research, Scion and Manaaki Whenua – Landcare Research, the last being custodian of national biological collections and databases.

name: New Zealand invasives and species AI models (AddaxAI)
summary: AI models trained on about 2 million camera trap images, embedded in AddaxAI and built by Weka Research.

name: New Zealand Land Use and Carbon Analysis System
summary: Programme to measure and monitor national carbon stocks in New Zealand's forests and soils, which Interpine described in 2015 as using permanent plots on a 4 km grid for planted forests.

name: New Zealand Marine Studies Centre
summary: University of Otago centre associated with Marine Metre Squared, a citizen science project established in 2013.

name: New Zealand National Bird Banding Scheme
summary: A DOC-run programme managed by the National Bird Banding Office, which certifies banders and keeps the national records; over 1.4 million birds of 241 species have been banded since 1947.

name: New Zealand Nature Fund
summary: A charity registered in New Zealand and the USA that raises funds for endangered species and holds donations for the automated island biosecurity project, disbursing them against milestones.

name: New Zealand Organisms Register
summary: Catalogue aiming to be an authoritative, continuously updated list of about 140,000 names applied to New Zealand biota, with TFBIS-supported infrastructure completed in June 2012.

name: New Zealand Threat Classification System
summary: A system for assessing the conservation status of New Zealand taxa nationally, in which expert panels assess each species group over a five-year cycle and publication data are downloadable from the NZTCS database.

name: Next-Generation Airborne Remote Sensing: High Altitude Persistent Coastal Ocean Monitoring
summary: Project announced in April 2024 to examine fitting cameras to Kea Aerospace's high-altitude solar-powered aircraft, funded with an initial $75,000 that could lead to about $1 million.

name: Ocean Acoustics Ltd
summary: Consultancy with a postal address in Auckland offering underwater noise assessment and passive acoustic monitoring, including work on Pacific coral reefs and British Columbia glass sponge reefs.

name: Omataroa-Rangitaiki No 2 Trust
summary: Māori land trust reported in 2017 to fund all its kiwi work, including trapping, call surveys and transmitter fitting at Puhikoko, partnering with Whakatāne Kiwi Trust.

name: Orbica
summary: Christchurch geospatial company whose work for Fire and Emergency New Zealand, reported in 2021, used a convolutional neural network and open satellite data to classify wildfire fuel types.

name: Orca Research Trust
summary: A charity asking for sightings, which says it was founded in 1998 by Dr Ingrid N. Visser and is the only dedicated orca research project in New Zealand waters.

name: Ornithological Society of New Zealand
summary: Bird society that published national atlases, including the 1999–2004 atlas based on surveys by more than 850 people.

name: OWL AI camera
summary: An AI-equipped trail camera with onboard species recognition and remote communication, intended for real-time species detection.

name: PredaCAM
summary: Rat-detecting camera using infrared and a cloud-based AI model with mobile network alerts, built by ASG Technologies, funded by DOC, and reported in 2024 as over 80% accurate in initial field trials.

name: Predator Free 2050
summary: A DOC-led goal to eradicate rats, possums and mustelids from New Zealand, with scientists and engineers testing AI and remote communications, according to DOC.

name: Predator Free 2050 Limited
summary: Crown-owned charitable company established in 2016 that funded the rat AI model behind PredaCAM, and is closed, with its work absorbed into DOC following the 2025/26 budget decision.

name: Predator Free Wellington
summary: Wellington predator control group whose 500 cameras produce about 380,000 images a year as of July 2024, and which DOC says was trialling PredaCAM at Mount Victoria.

name: Project Kiwi Trust
summary: Trust managing kiwi conservation on the Kūaotunu Peninsula since 1996, servicing over 900 traps 12 times a year, monitoring kiwi and coordinating local call surveys, in partnership with Save the Kiwi.

name: Pukenui-Western Hills Forest Trust
summary: Trust that in March 2018 was reported to have released twelve Northland brown kiwi into 1,700 hectares of forest fringing Whangārei, each fitted with a transmitter for health and movement monitoring.

name: Puketi Forest Trust
summary: Trust started in 2003, according to its founding trustee, whose monitoring in August 2017 covered kiwi call counts, five-minute bird counts and predator control, and which partners with the Department of Conservation.

name: Remote sensing of ecosystem drivers
summary: A DOC-run project that uses remote sensing to detect flowering and seeding events, to support operational planning of predator control.

name: Ross Sea Region Research and Monitoring Programme
summary: In January 2023, Antarctica New Zealand described a five-year Ross Sea Marine Protected Area evaluation programme and reported trackers on emperor penguins at Cape Crozier.

name: Save the Kiwi
summary: A charitable trust trading as Save the Kiwi maps kiwi distribution through citizen science and partners with DOC, which reports over $7 million raised and distributed.

name: SCENZ (Seas, Coasts, Estuaries New Zealand)
summary: A dataset focused on 500 m MODIS-Aqua data, extending from the coast past the 12 nautical mile limit, for which a DOC report on coastal suspended sediment recommends improvements.

name: Scion
summary: An organisation brought together with AgResearch and Plant & Food Research into the New Zealand Institute for Bioeconomy Science, according to Manaaki Whenua, and with a 2021 paper applying deep learning to tree species in aerial imagery.

name: Sirtrack
summary: An organisation that DOC says upgrades kākāpō transmitter hardware.

name: Southern Lakes Sanctuary Trust
summary: Registered charitable trust whose monitoring of mohua and long-tailed bats, the council said in August 2026, is changing through acoustic recorders; Makarora recordings held nearly 1,500 hours, with AI tools distinguishing call types.

name: Southern Royal Albatross satellite AI monitoring on Campbell Island
summary: An active project, led by Mitchell Rogers with DOC as partner, aiming as of June 2025 to use deep learning on satellite imagery and nest GPS data to automate albatross counts; it received a 2025 award.

name: Spyfish Aotearoa
summary: A project run by Wildlife.ai with DOC as partner, using citizen science via Zooniverse and machine learning to classify baited underwater video from the Tapuae Marine Reserve.

name: Stewart Island / Rakiura Community & Environment Trust
summary: Charitable trust founded in 2002 that controls pests and monitors native species, including kiwi, across a 210-hectare project area, with call count monitoring as one tokoeka project objective.

name: Synovus Technology
summary: Division of Aranovus Limited that plans to design and bring to market an autonomous, integrated platform for managing invasive animals, aiming to restore living nature.

name: Takahē Recovery Programme
summary: A DOC-run programme in which many adult takahē wear smart transmitters, and a GPS-equipped aircraft, the Sky Ranger, flies a grid over the mountains logging each bird's location and state.

name: Taranaki Kiwi Trust
summary: Registered charity that reported in November 2020 completing a three-year Egmont National Park kiwi survey with the Taranaki Mounga project, with 26 kiwi radio-tagged, and call surveys since 2006.

name: Taranaki Taku Tūranga – Towards Predator-Free Taranaki
summary: An active project that launched Restore Kaitake with the Taranaki Mounga Project in 2018, aiming to eradicate possums from 4,500 hectares, and uses the HARK AI acoustic monitor, according to Predator Free NZ Trust.

name: Taxon-Independent Community Index (TICI)
summary: A model built by Wilderlab and funded by Callaghan Innovation that, according to both, turns eDNA data into measures of freshwater or whole-ecosystem health.

name: Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
summary: An active university whose Centre for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence hosts AI research on albatross monitoring.

name: The Cacophony Project
summary: An open source non-profit building DOC AI cameras and partnering with DOC; its manager reports AI predator identification, and DOC reported camera use on Motutapu in July 2024.

name: Toi Foundation
summary: An active funder whose $30,000 grant helped Wildlife.ai develop and teach the Wild About AI programme.

name: Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
summary: An active organisation that released high-resolution coastal LiDAR point cloud data in 2026, with points classified into likely ground feature types including vegetation groups and seafloor.

name: Tools to Market
summary: An active DOC-run programme that in July 2024 was reported to allocate $1 million a year to predator-free tools and to have funded 15 projects since 2017.

name: Tracking tunnel machine learning
summary: A project built by DOC and Weka Research, and funded by DOC, creating a footprint training library from tracking tunnel cards, a machine learning tool and a mobile data capture app.

name: Trap.NZ
summary: Built and run by Groundtruth, with over 7,115 trapping projects and 46,689 active trappers in 2020, and hosting CamTrapNZ AI image recognition software by May 2023.

name: University of Auckland
summary: University whose acoustic engineer was reported in April 2026 to be developing a kiwi sound-monitoring device, funded in 2020 by a National Science Challenge and stalled at prototype stage.

name: University of Otago
summary: University associated with the New Zealand Marine Studies Centre, which the Marine Metre Squared website names as the citizen science project’s owner and manager.

name: Waimate North Landcare Trust
summary: Landcare trust whose volunteers organise kiwi listening at each site and train new listeners, with consistent data at many sites back to 2004; funded by Save the Kiwi.

name: Weka Research
summary: An active organisation listed by DOC for Alita, a desktop AI classifier for trail camera images, and for New Zealand species and invasives image models, and also lists a bird-call classifier.

name: Whakatāne Kiwi Trust
summary: Charitable trust set up in 2006 and partner in the Whakatāne Kiwi Project, whose volunteers monitor about 40 North Island brown kiwi using radio transmitters showing incubation and overnight foraging.

name: Whangamarino golden dodder satellite model
summary: A trial model built by Fabian Döweler recognises golden dodder in Whangamarino wetland satellite images; DOC was able to request six specific images, including near-infrared wavelengths.

name: Wild About AI
summary: An active programme, built and run by Wildlife AI and funded by Toi Foundation, that by May 2025 had reached more than 200 students across five Taranaki schools.

name: Wildtech
summary: An active organisation that DOC says does most of the programming of the kākāpō transmitters.

name: Zero Invasive Predators
summary: An active organisation set up to develop technologies to remove rats, possums and stoats from large mainland areas, now improving AI algorithms to tell rat species apart in its cameras.
