name: Arabian gazelle re-settlement project, Shaleem and Al Halaniyat Islands (Environment Authority, Oman)
summary: Times of Oman reported in February 2025 that this Environment Authority project released 12 Arabian gazelles after plant and water surveys, using GPS, satellites and camera traps.

name: Arabian Oryx Department (Arabian Oryx Reserve)
summary: Oman's Arabian Oryx Reserve unit reported in January 2024 that it used a tracking collar and habitat monitoring, with about 900 Arabian oryx, 1,140 sand gazelles and 140 Arabian gazelles.

name: Arabian Sea humpback whale tracking chip project (Environment Authority, Oman)
summary: Environment Authority project begun in December 2023, reported in February 2024 as fitting a humpback whale with a satellite tracking chip and acoustic recorder by drone, meant to allow remote measurement and threat mapping.

name: Arabian Sea Whale Network
summary: Active network that partnered with Wild Me on an Arabian Sea whale and dolphin database and invites members to enter, archive and analyse cetacean data in Flukebook.

name: ASWN Flukebook
summary: Active platform, built by the Arabian Sea Whale Network and Wild Me, that matches humpback and sperm whale tail fluke images by computer vision and archives genetic and tagging data.

name: Birds of Oman Database
summary: Bird records database built by the Diwan of Royal Court and two Sultan Qaboos University centres, holding over 16 million observations across 623 species as of 2019, mapped by GIS at over 455,000 sites.

name: Center for Environmental Studies and Research, Sultan Qaboos University
summary: Sultan Qaboos University centre that invested in database management tools and published four books on Oman's birds since 2001, when support became available for database transfer.

name: Conceptual Project for Satellite Monitoring of the Marine Environment in the Sultanate of Oman
summary: Proposed Environment Authority conceptual project for satellite monitoring of Oman's marine environment, listed at 25 per cent in the 2025 annual report.

name: Coral Reef Monitoring
summary: Active project run by the Environment Society of Oman with National Geographic Society funding, using eight monitoring sites and introducing AI analysis tools ReefCloud and MERMAID at an April 2025 workshop.

name: Coral reef surveys (Environment Authority, Oman)
summary: Active programme of periodic coral reef surveys run by the Environment Authority, reported in 2026 as giving data on live coral cover, growth rates and bleaching impact, using 30-metre transects at Daymaniyat.

name: Department of Geography, College of Arts and Social Sciences, Sultan Qaboos University
summary: Sultan Qaboos University geography department, listed by OpenAlex as the affiliation of the first author of a 2024 paper on using UAVs for seasonal vegetation assessment in arid environments.

name: Department of Soils, Water and Agricultural Engineering, Sultan Qaboos University
summary: Sultan Qaboos University department, listed by OpenAlex as the first author's affiliation on a 2025 paper assessing mangrove carbon stock using field measurements and machine learning-based GIS and remote sensing.

name: Dhofar Centre for Wildlife Research
summary: Company in Oman's Dhofar region, self-described as co-founded by Hadi Al Hikmani and Lawrence Ball, that says it collects data on Arabian Peninsula wildlife using camera traps, acoustic monitoring, UAV analysis and habitat modelling.

name: Diwan of Royal Court
summary: Omani royal court body that collaborated with Sultan Qaboos University on the Birds of Oman Database and, UCL reported in May 2024, was part of the team surveying the Dhofar range for Arabian leopards.

name: Electronic Environmental Monitoring Programme (Environment Authority, Oman)
summary: Environment Authority programme reported in October 2022 as launched to document and analyse wildlife and pollution monitoring data, aiming to let specialists enter daily field data electronically and link it automatically to the Authority's databases.

name: Environment Authority
summary: Established in August 2020 by Royal Decree, it implements Oman's nature conservation laws, issues permits and publishes four GBIF datasets; its pages report 20 declared reserves.

name: Environment Centre, Turtle Reserve in Ras Al Hadd
summary: Centre under the Environment Department of South Al Sharqiyah Governorate whose specialists, Times of Oman reported in July 2026, recorded over 12,000 turtle tracks on the reserve's beaches in the first half of the year.

name: Environment Society of Oman
summary: Non-profit founded in 2004 that researches whales and dolphins, aims to survey turtles on Masirah Island, tracks vultures and partners with the Environment Authority.

name: Environmental Atlas of Oman
summary: Active digital platform, by its own description, for collecting and documenting environmental data, with a biodiversity section and nature reserves, aiming to map ecosystems and their services and offering interactive maps.

name: ESO Coral Reef Monitoring Project
summary: Active project run by the Environment Society of Oman, funded by the National Geographic Society, surveying eight sites twice yearly for bleaching and recovery, launched in April 2025 with AI tool training.

name: ESO Frankincense Research and Conservation Programme
summary: Running since 2010, this ESO programme studies Boswellia sacra health and distribution in Dhofar; its 2025 report records a published rapid assessment and ongoing Wadi Dawkah baseline surveys.

name: ESO Raptors Research and Conservation Programme
summary: Active programme run by the Environment Society of Oman that has surveyed Egyptian and Lappet-faced vultures since 2012 and fitted rings and satellite trackers to juvenile Lappet-faced vultures.

name: ESO Turtle Research and Conservation Programme
summary: Active Environment Society of Oman programme, funded by the US Fish and Wildlife Service, monitoring seasonal nesting and reporting a statistically significant 79% decline in loggerhead nesting on Masirah Island.

name: ESO Whale and Dolphin Research and Conservation Programme
summary: Environment Society of Oman programme whose objectives cover genetics, acoustics, spatial ecology and strandings of Arabian Sea humpback whales and other cetaceans, and which says it is seeking sponsorship to continue.

name: Field surveys of coastal marine ecosystems (Environment Authority, Oman)
summary: Active Environment Authority programme of coastal and wetland field surveys that aims to assess coastal condition and add to the national biodiversity database, using offline electronic field forms at the Masirah centre.

name: Five Oceans Environmental Services
summary: Closed consultancy and marine conservation research organisation based in Oman, the UAE and the UK, whose home page says it has become two new companies.

name: Future Seas Global SPC
summary: Active Oman-based organisation named as coordinator of the November to December 2023 humpback whale survey in the Gulf of Masirah, and as a collaborator in the Environment Society of Oman's turtle programme.

name: Investigating Potential Pressures and Impacts of Ecotourism on Green Sea Turtles (Chelonia mydas) Health and Behaviour at Ad Dimaniyat Island Nature Reserve
summary: Active project listed by the Rufford Foundation on 3 June 2025 that will monitor green turtle abundance, feeding and activity using snorkelling observations and autonomous benthic cameras at Ad Dimaniyyat reserve in Oman.

name: Masirah Environment Centre (Environment Authority, Oman)
summary: Environment Authority centre in Oman that runs coastal ecosystem field surveys; in September 2026 its monitoring unit described bird monitoring at Khor Al Har as part of a periodic biodiversity programme.

name: National Biodiversity Survey
summary: Environment Authority survey building a national wild mammal database, which Oman Daily reported in June 2024 had covered 804 squares, installed 683 camera traps and documented 80 species.

name: National Survey and Geospatial Information Authority
summary: Official body for producing, reviewing and approving Oman's map, according to the Ministry of Defence, which says it was renamed in August 2024 from the National Survey Authority.

name: National survey of tree cover (Environment Authority, Oman)
summary: Closed Environment Authority national survey of tree cover, listed at 100 per cent completion in 2025, with drone-derived data processing for early detection and tree species and number detection at strategic sites.

name: Office for Conservation of the Environment, Diwan of Royal Court
summary: Diwan office whose researcher set Dhofar cameras, per a 2012 project page, and which reportedly recorded Nubian ibex and Arabian wolf in Jabal Samhan by September 2022.

name: Oman Whale Shark Project
summary: Active whale shark project run by the Marine Megafauna Foundation, whose June 2025 field season photo-identified 30 sharks and deployed nine satellite tags, the first on whale sharks in Omani waters, and which uses Sharkbook.ai.

name: Project to study the success rate of Al Rimani turtle nests in Masirah
summary: Five-year project begun in 2022 under an Oman and United States memorandum, which Oman Observer reported in September 2023 was in its second year, counting nests and examining eggs on Masirah, with the Environment Authority and NOAA as partners.

name: Remote Sensing and GIS Research Center, Sultan Qaboos University
summary: Sultan Qaboos University centre, with cited findings from a 2013 study indicating over one million migratory coastal birds visit Barr Al Hikman's wetlands yearly.

name: Sea Turtle Satellite Tracking Project
summary: Environment Authority project whose second phase Oman Daily reported as begun in November 2022, with ten trackers fitted by then, five in each phase.

name: Sooty Falcon Survey Project
summary: Sooty falcon survey run by the Office for Conservation of the Environment with Omani and international institutions, with bases on Al Fahal and the Daymaniyat Islands, where the team counted 369 falcons in 2012.

name: Statistics of the green turtles in Ras al-Hadd, 2012-2019
summary: Dataset of monthly green turtle counts at Ras al-Hadd for 2012 to 2019, covering trails, nesting, stranded, dead and tagged turtles, sourced from Department of Planning and Studies annual reports.

name: Sultan Qaboos University
summary: Omani university collaborating with the Diwan of Royal Court on the Birds of Oman Database through two centres, and where the Oman Observer reported in May 2026 a first conservation drone fleet had been set up.

name: Survey of large mammals on the southern slope of Jabal Samhan Nature Reserve
summary: Closed Environment Authority project in Dhofar that, as of September 2022, was surveying large mammals on the southern slope of Jabal Samhan Nature Reserve using camera-trap images and field surveys.

name: Survey of Marine Mammals Species in Musandam Governorate
summary: Closed Environment Authority survey of marine mammals in Musandam Governorate, reported complete at phase 3 of 3 in 2025, using sonar-based marine surveys covering 1,867.9 km in phases five and six.

name: Turtle Research and Conservation
summary: Active Environment Society of Oman programme, funded by the US Fish and Wildlife Service, that aims to run regular Masirah Island beach surveys, with a seasonal field team doing track counts.

name: Using Artificial Intelligence Technology to Survey Wildlife Species in North Al Batinah
summary: Closed Environment Authority project to survey wildlife species in North Al Batinah using artificial intelligence, listed at 100 per cent completion in its 2025 annual report.

name: Wetlands Bird Survey (Environment Authority, Oman)
summary: Closed Environment Authority project that surveyed and monitored waterbirds in coastal lagoons (khawrs) across seven governorates, with fieldwork from May to October 2024.

name: ACOTMAR sea turtle conservation project, Playa La Barqueta
summary: Sea turtle conservation project at Playa La Barqueta, Chiriquí, run by CRECOBIAN and led by Juan Blas, which a June 2025 university page says ran for over ten years, protecting nests and releasing hatchlings.

name: AVUELO (Airborne Validation Unified Experiment: Land to Ocean)
summary: A closed NASA-led campaign with the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute, which flew the AVIRIS-3 spectrometer over land and marine ecosystems in Panama and Costa Rica in February 2025 to capture hyperspectral imagery.

name: Camera-trap monitoring in Cerro Hoya National Park (MiAmbiente)
summary: A MiAmbiente camera-trap effort in Cerro Hoya National Park which, according to Telemetro in September 2026, recorded wild cats and other species over eight months of monitoring.

name: Censos Centroamericanos de Aves Acuáticas (Panamá)
summary: Waterbird count programme held twice a year, in early February and early July, since 2011, and coordinated in Panama by Audubon Panamá, which runs it.

name: Centro de Capacitación, Investigación y Monitoreo de la Biodiversidad
summary: A biodiversity training, research and monitoring centre run by the Universidad de Panamá, reported in December 2024 to have fitted a dozen satellite transmitters to turtles and sharks in Coiba National Park.

name: Centro de Coordinación para el Monitoreo, Preservación y Protección del Ecosistema Marino y Costero
summary: A marine and coastal monitoring centre led by Panama's environment ministry, opened on 11 September 2025 with Bezos Earth Fund funding, and reported by the ministry as the first interinstitutional one in its Pacific corridor region.

name: Centro de Reproducción y Conservación Biodiversidad Animal (CRECOBIAN)
summary: University research centre attached to the Vice-Rectorate for Research and Postgraduate Studies, run by Universidad Autónoma de Chiriquí, with the ACOTMAR sea turtle project, including nesting research, as one of its research lines.

name: Coiba Island M2 Radar
summary: A radar built by Global Conservation and ProtectedSeas, reported in August 2025 to keep detecting illegal fishing in Coiba's protected waters, and said to have caught six illegal boats in its first month.

name: Conservación de felinos y especies de presas a través de alianzas público-privadas y gestión de conflictos entre humanos y jaguares en Panamá
summary: A ministry and UNEP-led, GEF-funded project producing Panama's first camera-trap jaguar census, TVN reports, worth $1.78 million according to the ministry as reported by Mongabay.

name: Cámaras trampa en el Parque Internacional La Amistad, sector Pacífico
summary: Camera trap monitoring in the Pacific sector of La Amistad International Park, where MiAmbiente reported 12 cameras placed from February 2019 and rangers trained by Fundación Yaguará Panamá.

name: Digital Naturalism Laboratories
summary: A jungle prototyping studio in Gamboa, Panama, aiming to help field biologists build tools, running Mothbox, building Panatrap and describing all its projects as open source.

name: Estación Científica Coiba AIP
summary: A public interest association operating inside Coiba National Park since January 2018, built by SENACYT, with marine monitoring begun in 2019 and an oceanographic buoy transmitting data online.

name: Fundación Agua y Tierra
summary: Reported in 2019 as a Mata Oscura turtle conservation group, with MarViva and LatAm Drones training members from September to locate nesting turtles using a thermal drone.

name: Fundación Almanaque Azul
summary: A Panamanian foundation for education and research on natural and cultural diversity, publishing ecological corridor map layers and data under a CC-BY licence.

name: Fundación Ciudad del Saber
summary: A foundation that, according to SENACYT in December 2023, jointly coordinates the Manglares centinelas mangrove monitoring project, which it leads.

name: Fundación Natura
summary: A Panamanian foundation that, with Sociedad Audubon de Panamá, launched the second Conserva Aves grant call in 2025, requiring funded projects to include bird monitoring plans.

name: Fundación Pro-Conservación de los Primates Panameños
summary: Panamanian non-profit that censuses primate populations in reserves and fragmented forests and maintains annual monitoring in each censused area.

name: Fundación Rapaces y Bosques de Panamá
summary: A Panamanian NGO that describes a community raptor monitoring model in Darién's Indigenous territories running for over twenty years, using GPS, camera traps, drones and participatory maps, and reports monitoring 56 nests.

name: Fundación Yaguará Panamá
summary: A foundation using GPS collars and camera traps, surveying roughly 141,000 hectares across Chagres and Darién parks, Mongabay reports, and named by TVN among a GEF project’s leaders.

name: GBIF Panama
summary: Panama's country node of GBIF with associate participation status, led by Darío Luque, and the route through which the environment ministry ran an October 2025 biodiversity data publishing workshop.

name: Global Conservation park protection agreement with Panama
summary: An agreement with Panama's environment ministry covering three UNESCO national parks and Naso Comarca, according to Global Conservation, with planned satellite communications, camera surveillance, marine radar and EarthRanger systems.

name: Green turtle nesting monitoring in Coiba National Park (MiAmbiente)
summary: A green turtle nesting monitoring project run by Panama's environment ministry in Coiba National Park, which tags nesting females, counts nests and collects population data, reported in January 2026 as joint work with partners.

name: Grupo de Investigación en Tecnologías Avanzadas de Telecomunicación y Procesamiento de Señales
summary: A research group of the Universidad Tecnológica de Panamá whose project developed a platform using a drone-borne hyperspectral camera and artificial intelligence to identify and monitor algal blooms on Panama's coasts.

name: Harpía Watch Forest
summary: Automated system for monitoring forest cover in Panama, detecting vegetation change from Sentinel-2 imagery, spectral indices such as NDVI and temporal analysis; Ministry specialists were scheduled to present it on 21 August 2026.

name: Indigenous community biodiversity monitoring for biodiversity credits in Darién (Health in Harmony and Savimbo)
summary: Closed Darién project in which Indigenous communities used bioacoustic monitoring and camera trapping; Health in Harmony reports 12 people trained in 2024 to 2025, recording 199 bird and 73 animal species.

name: Indigenous community forest monitoring with drones in Panama
summary: Project in which, UN-REDD says, Panama's Indigenous groups have worked with the programme since 2016 on forest monitoring with drones, with volunteers from each people learning to fly drones and map tribal lands.

name: Instituto Geográfico Nacional "Tommy Guardia"
summary: Panama's national geographic institute, a unit of the land administration authority ANATI, with a department of photogrammetry and remote sensing and a listed National Geospatial Data Centre.

name: Manglares centinelas del cambio climático: monitoreo, vulnerabilidad y resiliencia de los ecosistemas marino-costeros en las Bahía de Panamá y Bahía de Chame
summary: Mangrove monitoring project for Panama Bay and Chame Bay, presented on 21 December 2023 by SENACYT with Fundación Ciudad del Saber, with nine research lines including fungal communities and sediment quality.

name: Mapa de corredores naturales de Panamá
summary: A CC-BY dataset built by Fundación Almanaque Azul, modelled with Omniscape at 30 m resolution across Panama's land and 10 km border buffers, using the ministry's 2022 land-use map.

name: MarAlliance Panama marine megafauna monitoring
summary: A MarAlliance project reporting fish monitoring and sawfish protection across Panama, completed baseline monitoring at three Caribbean sites and training for over 40 local fishers, students and biologists.

name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá
summary: Panama's environment ministry reports a remote sensing department and a 2025 GBIF Panama workshop, with park protection and marine monitoring partnerships reported by Global Conservation and Global Fishing Watch.

name: Monitoreo de la presencia y abundancia de la tortuga carey en el Parque Nacional Coiba
summary: Closed monitoring of hawksbill turtle presence and abundance in Coiba National Park, carried out within a wider FIDECO-funded project that MiAmbiente executed, which Fundación Natura lists with a B/. 70,000 FIDECO contribution.

name: Monitoreo de mamíferos en San San Pond Sak (Fundación Natura)
summary: A Fundación Natura project monitoring terrestrial mammals in San San Pond Sak Wetland National Park, Bocas del Toro, using camera traps and other technology to gather data on threatened species.

name: Monitoreo Invernal del Playero Occidental (Panama)
summary: A winter monitoring project for the Western Sandpiper, coordinated in Panama since 2011 by Sociedad Audubon de Panamá as part of a Pacific flyway shorebird project, at the Panama Bay refuge and Panamá Viejo mangrove.

name: Mothbox
summary: A low-cost automated moth camera, begun in November 2022 for biodiversity work on Panamanian reforestation projects, released as open hardware and built by Andrew Quitmeyer, with WILDLABS prize funding planned for mass manufacture.

name: Motus stations for migratory bird monitoring in Panama
summary: A project to install Motus automated radio-telemetry stations for migratory birds, which the sanitation programme says made Panama the first Central American country with them, planned for five years, extendable.

name: Movement and Conservation of Large Endangered Ungulates in the Darién: The Tapir and the White-Lipped Peccary
summary: Closed 2017 project aiming to monitor tapir and white-lipped peccary population trends with camera traps and study their spatial ecology with telemetry in Darién, assisted by local Emberá people.

name: Panacetacea
summary: A marine mammal research non-profit founded in 2009, reporting humpback whale surveys in the Gulf of Chiriquí since 2002 and describing the ONDAS underwater acoustic network.

name: Panama Wildlife Conservation
summary: A charity in England and Wales and an NGO in Panama, working mainly in Veraguas and Azuero on field research, species monitoring and education, including jaguar and mammal monitoring in the Azuero Massif.

name: Panatrap
summary: Open-source design files and code, as Dinalab describes them, for turning 360-degree cameras into panoramic camera traps for wildlife study, built by Digital Naturalism Laboratories and Andrew Quitmeyer and funded by Conservation X Labs.

name: Passive acoustic monitoring of mangrove birds in Parita Bay and Panama Bay
summary: Passive acoustic monitoring of mangrove birds in Parita Bay and Panama Bay, which Audubon reported in January 2025 as being implemented, using software with AI algorithms to identify bird vocalisations.

name: Plataforma de Observación de Florecimientos de Algas en Regiones Costeras Utilizando Imágenes Hiperespectrales e Inteligencia Artificial
summary: A closed project, run by GITTS-UTP and led by Fernando Arias with SENACYT funding, that developed a drone hyperspectral and AI platform for identifying algal blooms on Panama's coasts from December 2021 to December 2024.

name: Población y demografía de aves playeras migratorias (Audubon Panamá)
summary: A banding and flagging project run by Sociedad Audubon de Panamá, begun in January 2014 on three migratory shorebird species with three more added in 2015, which banded 370 shorebirds in its first two years.

name: Proyecto MarineGEO del STRI en Bocas del Toro
summary: Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute project in Bocas del Toro that studies the archipelago's main ecosystems, with weekly physicochemical monitoring and monitoring of seagrass meadows and coral reefs.

name: Proyecto Ondas
summary: Project with MiAmbiente and Fundación Panacetacea that, as reported in March 2021, installed four underwater recorders in Panama's Pacific waters to study the acoustic landscape of Isla Iguana and Coiba National Park.

name: Proyecto Yaug Galu
summary: Active long-term sea turtle monitoring programme with the Guna people, run by The Leatherback Project, using satellite transmitters on nesting female leatherbacks and standardised nightly nesting surveys with community members.

name: Rapaces de Océano a Océano
summary: A project run by Sociedad Audubon de Panamá that has monitored 15 migratory raptor species over Cerro Ancón since 2004, a site described as one of five worldwide with migrations of over a million birds.

name: Sea Turtle Conservancy Bocas del Toro project
summary: Sea Turtle Conservancy project, run and built by the organisation, monitoring hawksbill and leatherback nesting in Bocas del Toro and the Comarca Ngäbe-Buglé since 2003, with community members.

name: Sea turtle conservation and monitoring at Playa La Barqueta Agrícola Wildlife Refuge (MiAmbiente)
summary: A sea turtle project run by Panama's environment ministry at Playa La Barqueta Agrícola refuge, where August 2025 night patrols measured nesting females and georeferenced nests for later relocation to the nursery.

name: Secretaría Nacional de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación
summary: An active national science and technology secretariat that presented a mangrove monitoring project for Panama Bay and Chame Bay with Fundación Ciudad del Saber in December 2023.

name: Sistema de Trazabilidad y Control Forestal (STCF)
summary: Timber traceability programme covered by resolution DM-0068-2018, following timber from forests, lakes or plantations to storage, industry and traders, with versions for natural forest harvesting and plantations.

name: Sistema Nacional de Información Ambiental (Panamá)
summary: Panama's national environmental information system, created under Law 41 of 1998 and run by the Ministerio de Ambiente, whose open data page lists a 2021 forest cover and land use map at 1:25,000.

name: Sistema Nacional de Monitoreo de Bosques Multipropósito
summary: An active ministry-built forest monitoring system generating REDD+ activity data, whose launch was announced alongside a 2019 map putting forest and other wooded land at 65.4% of Panama.

name: Sociedad Audubon de Panamá
summary: Active Panamanian bird conservation society and BirdLife International partner that, La Estrella reports, has run migrating raptor counts since 2004, and whose home page also lists shorebird studies and waterbird censuses.

name: The Mamoni River Valley Jaguar Project
summary: Active camera trap project, run by the Kaminando habitat connectivity initiative, monitoring jaguar movement, behaviour and distribution in the Mamoni River Valley and how fragmentation and human activity affect them.

name: Universidad Autónoma de Chiriquí
summary: University in David, Chiriquí province, Panama, whose CRECOBIAN centre, attached to its Vice-Rectorate for Research and Postgraduate Studies, includes the ACOTMAR sea turtle project, with nesting research, as a research line.

name: Universidad de Panamá
summary: Active university whose Veraguas regional campus biology students and CCIMBIO researchers, Panamá América reports, fitted satellite transmitters to turtles and sharks in Coiba.

name: Universidad Tecnológica de Panamá
summary: A university with a Panama City campus whose GITTS research group had a project that developed a platform to identify and monitor algal blooms on Panama's coasts.

name: #TuFotoAyuda
summary: A project of WCS, SERFOR and iNaturalist to improve iNaturalist's automatic species identifier for wildlife trafficking officers, noting the app needs at least 50 photos of a species.

name: ADETOP v2
summary: A Random Forest model using 10-metre Sentinel-2 imagery, built by OSINFOR and the universities of Sheffield and Cambridge, and used by June 2026 to analyse 181 logging legality cases.

name: AI-powered Global Biodiversity Monitoring Network
summary: A proposed AI-based network, to be launched by the Smithsonian Institution in Peru's parks, combining sound, eDNA, satellite and camera data, with a $50k grant from Bezos Earth Fund.

name: AmazonCam Tambopata
summary: A grid of more than 100 cameras recording wildlife in Tambopata, run by Rainforest Expeditions, where online participants identify the animals in its photos.

name: AmazonTEC
summary: A platform run and led by ACCA for Amazon science and technology; its 2026 edition, within the International Conservation Technology Conference, covered drones, LiDAR, AI and thermal monitoring.

name: Amazónicos por la Amazonía (AMPA)
summary: According to World Land Trust, this Peruvian organisation began in 2003, has managed Alto Huayabamba Conservation Concession and coordinates a national conservation network covering over one million hectares.

name: Animl (San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance)
summary: A model to detect and identify animals, which Mongabay reports was created by Kayra Swanson; an SDZWA researcher puts its error margin at 5 to 10%.

name: ARBOR
summary: An AI plugin for QGIS built by OSINFOR and the University of Sheffield to find shihuahuaco trees in drone images, reported at 65% precision in initial tests.

name: Asistente de Biodiversidad
summary: A proposed biodiversity assistant involving a partnership between WildMon and SERNANP, combining eDNA, camera traps, acoustic monitoring and satellite observation.

name: Asociación Agro Bio Forestal El Porvenir Pelejo (ABIOFORP)
summary: Community association that, according to World Land Trust, voluntarily manages the Bajo Huallaga fragile ecosystem in San Martín through the Áreas Inundables del Bajo Huallaga Conservation Concession.

name: Asociación Comunal de Conservación Yurúa (ACC-Yurúa)
summary: Association of nine Indigenous communities that Upper Amazon Conservancy says led efforts to conserve over 45,000 hectares of Peru-Brazil border rainforest, with a concession granted in 2019.

name: Asociación de Conservación Oso Dorado
summary: A women-led association, per Mongabay, which reported in March 2026 that its monitors had set up a yellow-tailed woolly monkey monitoring system in Hierba Buena Allpayacu with Yunkawasi.

name: Asociación de Conservación Pamau Nain
summary: Nature and Culture International says it helped create this association of leaders from nine Awajún communities, who will coordinate activities on a concession protecting about 46,544 hectares of rainforest.

name: Asociación Ecosistemas Andinos (ECOAN)
summary: American Bird Conservancy says it helped this organisation (founded 2000) create nine community-managed conservation areas spanning 21,285 acres in the Cordillera Vilcanota and plant over 1.5 million Polylepis trees.

name: Asociación para el Manejo y Conservación de la Reserva Comunal Yanesha (AMARCY)
summary: Caretas reports Yanesha Communal Reserve administration experience and membership of Consorcio Kowen Antami, chosen in 2023 to administer Yanachaga Chemillén National Park and San Matías San Carlos Protection Forest.

name: Asociación para la Conservación y el Desarrollo Sostenible Sallqa Perú
summary: A Peruvian nonprofit, listed by OpenAlex, whose site describes MashUPerú as Peru's first bat sound library of acoustically characterised species calls.

name: Asociación para la Investigación y Desarrollo Integral
summary: An organisation executing a partial administration contract for Tambopata and part of Bahuaja-Sonene, with an Alianza Forestal initiative promoting community forest management in Ucayali.

name: Autoridad Regional Ambiental de Amazonas
summary: Regional environmental authority of the Amazonas government, which a 2024 regional council agreement says administers the Regional Conservation Area of Seasonally Dry Tropical Forests of the Marañón.

name: Autoridad Regional Ambiental de San Martín
summary: Regional environmental authority that the San Martín government said in June 2026 signed four agreements with civil society and private partners to strengthen protection of two regional conservation areas.

name: Blume
summary: An organisation monitoring marine biomass in real time with sensors, robotics and AI, with ProInnóvate funding.

name: Central Asháninka del Río Ene
summary: An organisation saying it represents 45 Asháninka communities in the Ene basin, with a geospatial viewer covering over 235,000 hectares and the SAT-CARE early warning system.

name: Centro de Conservación, Investigación y Manejo de Áreas Naturales Cordillera Azul (CIMA Cordillera Azul)
summary: Actualidad Ambiental named this organisation as executor in 2018 for Cordillera Azul National Park (1,353,191 hectares, established 2001), and the executor dates its Sernanp contract to 2008–2028.

name: Centro de Innovación Científica Amazónica
summary: Amazon research and innovation institution, set up in 2016 per Wake Forest's Sabin Center, with an AI, drones and spatial analysis laboratory it calls Peru's most advanced drone programme.

name: Centro de Ornitología y Biodiversidad
summary: A Peruvian NGO dedicated to biodiversity conservation and research, as Peru Aves describes it.

name: Comisión Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo Aeroespacial
summary: Peru's governing body for space activities and seat of the Peruvian Space Agency, which controlled PerúSAT-1 in January 2018 and launched GeoAPP in August 2025.

name: Comunidad Campesina La Jalca
summary: Peasant community in Chachapoyas whose land of more than 17,000 hectares Actualidad Ambiental says the Ministry of the Environment declared a private conservation area in perpetuity.

name: Comunidad Campesina Muchik Santa Catalina de Chongoyape
summary: Actualidad Ambiental says community members complained about invaders at Chaparrí, Peru’s first private conservation area since 2001, whose creation the community promoted with a photographer.

name: Comunidad Campesina San Felipe
summary: Peasant community whose initiative led the Ministry of the Environment to recognise, in perpetuity, the 1,957.75-hectare Páramos y Bosques Montanos private conservation area, according to Actualidad Ambiental.

name: Comunidad Campesina Segunda y Cajas
summary: In January 2026, Mongabay quoted a community leader saying the community was reforesting with its rondas campesinas to conserve páramos, where Mongabay reported a private conservation area existed.

name: Comunidad Campesina Suttoc y Pacchac
summary: Peasant community of over 100 families that Actualidad Ambiental reported in June 2022 was to manage the Suttoc y Pacchac private conservation area, with ECOAN helping start legal recognition.

name: Comunidad Nativa Infierno
summary: Native community that reserved almost 2,000 hectares for conservation, recognised in 2016 as the Ebio Kiabamene private conservation area, then the largest in Madre de Dios, according to Actualidad Ambiental.

name: Comunidad Nativa Nueva York
summary: Native community of the Kukama-Kukamiria people whose 3,421-hectare private conservation area was recognised for an initial ten years, according to Actualidad Ambiental, with support building its surveillance and planning capacity.

name: Comunidad Nativa Once de Agosto Río Ucayali
summary: Native community whose 1,100 hectares in Jenaro Herrera, Requena, were recognised in perpetuity as a private conservation area, Loreto's 31st, according to Actualidad Ambiental.

name: Comunidad Nativa San Jorge del Río Marañón
summary: Native community with a private conservation area of 1,060.86 hectares of primary and humid tropical forest, whose guardians joined the Racol and Amazonía Que Late networks in 2020, according to Actualidad Ambiental.

name: Conservación Amazónica - ACCA
summary: Organisation saying it protects over 5 million hectares of the Amazonian Andes using satellites, drones, acoustic monitoring and camera traps, and running the Monitoring of the Andes Amazon Program.

name: Consorcio Kowen Antami
summary: Consortium of ANAP, AMARCY and the NGO DRIS that Caretas reports has executed the administration contract for Yanachaga Chemillén National Park and San Matías San Carlos Protection Forest since 9 November 2023.

name: Consorcio Manglares del Noroeste del Perú
summary: Consortium of fisher and gatherer organisations that, according to FAO, signed a 20-year agreement with Sernanp to co-manage the Los Manglares de Tumbes National Sanctuary.

name: Developing Communal Monitoring Strategies through Community-Based Tourism in the Peruvian Amazon
summary: A closed 2018 project, listed by the Rufford Foundation on 5 June 2018, that planned community rangers to lead camera-trap monitoring of threatened terrestrial mammal populations.

name: Ejecutor del Contrato de Administración de la Reserva Comunal Amarakaeri
summary: An organisation ANECAP says was formed in 2005 to represent native communities, signing its administration contract in 2006, and a co-creator of the Earth Defenders Toolkit.

name: Ejecutor del Contrato de Administración de la Reserva Comunal Asháninka (ECO Asháninka)
summary: Contract executor for the Asháninka Communal Reserve (184,468.38 hectares), whose president told Caretas in December 2023 that it manages the reserve jointly with Sernanp.

name: Ejecutor del Contrato de Administración de la Reserva Comunal El Sira (Ecosira)
summary: Administration contract executor of the El Sira Communal Reserve that, according to Andina in February 2020, was working with Sernanp to improve the organic coffee supply chain in the Gran Pajonal sector.

name: Ejecutor del Contrato de Administración de la Reserva Comunal Machiguenga (ECA Maeni)
summary: Contract executor that Caretas says manages the 218,905.63-hectare Machiguenga Communal Reserve in Cusco in collaboration with Sernanp, representing the local communities.

name: Ejecutor del Contrato de Administración de la Reserva Comunal Purús (Ecopurús)
summary: Actualidad Ambiental reported this Purús Communal Reserve contract executor worked with Sernanp on a mahogany seed project in 2011 and quoted the reserve chief calling it Sernanp's recognised counterpart.

name: FECONAU
summary: Through its CISAP centre, implements satellite monitoring for early deforestation alerts and Indigenous territories, and trains community forest surveillance committees in GPS, drones and mapping.

name: Fundación Conservación Internacional - CI Perú
summary: Organisation awarded the 2012 Alto Mayo Protection Forest administration contract as sole bidder, which Actualidad Ambiental identifies as the basis of co-management with Sernanp.

name: GBIF Peru
summary: Peru's country node in GBIF, registered as a voting participant, with its address at the Ministry of the Environment in Lima.

name: GeoAPP
summary: Platform built and run by CONIDA that gives institutions, researchers and citizens high-resolution satellite imagery, mainly from PerúSAT-1, and which CONIDA says uses AI to detect land-use change.

name: Geobosques
summary: Peru's official platform for monitoring forest cover change, launched in 2016 and run by the national forest conservation programme, showing forest loss and early deforestation alerts.

name: Gerencia Regional de Desarrollo Forestal y de Fauna Silvestre - Loreto
summary: A regional forestry and wildlife management body in Loreto whose site presents an alert tool and names a unit for information management, cadastre and satellite monitoring.

name: Gerencia Regional de Recursos Naturales y Gestión Ambiental del Gobierno Regional del Cusco
summary: Actualidad Ambiental reported in July 2026 that Cusco’s office was organising the III National Congress of Regional Conservation Areas for 6–9 September, with five areas covering over 345,000 hectares.

name: Gerencia Regional de Recursos Naturales y Gestión del Medio Ambiente del Gobierno Regional del Callao
summary: Callao regional government office that, according to the regional government's page, protects and administers the Humedales de Ventanilla Regional Conservation Area through its Oficina de Áreas Protegidas y Medio Ambiente.

name: Gobierno Territorial Autónomo Awajún
summary: Awajún territorial government, which Mongabay reports is built on communities, 19 territorial sectors across four departments and a central government; in October 2025 its then vice-president cited respect for nature.

name: Gobierno Territorial Autónomo de la Nación Chapra
summary: Chapra territorial government, whose then president told Mongabay in October 2025 that it arose from a wish to regain control of territory and that the Chapra surveyed and zoned all of it.

name: Gobierno Territorial Autónomo de la Nación Wampís
summary: Mongabay says 27 communities’ representatives declared this Wampis government on 29 November 2015 to defend their territory from extractive industries and that economic activity there required Wampis consent.

name: Gobierno Territorial Autónomo Kandozi
summary: Kandozi territorial government that Caretas reported in February 2026 was on the TICCA follow-up committee after over 200 leaders from 54 communities agreed to protect 1,030,000 hectares in Loreto.

name: Grupo de Aves del Perú
summary: A non-profit civil institution founded by waterbird researchers, whose Pisco wetlands project ran rapid monitoring and censuses of the coastal wetlands of Pisco and San Andrés, recording 121 bird species.

name: Impacto antrópico sobre la biodiversidad de los ecosistemas amazónicos utilizando monitoreo acústico pasivo
summary: IIAP project led by Giussepe Gagliardi that studies forest sounds to assess human impact on Amazon biodiversity, with more than 800,000 minutes recorded by July 2026.

name: Instituto de Investigaciones de la Amazonía Peruana
summary: Public research body attached to Peru's environment ministry that runs an AI laboratory and, as reported by Caretas, uses AI, drones and sensors to monitor Amazon biodiversity.

name: Instituto de Investigación para el Desarrollo Sustentable de Ceja de Selva
summary: Affiliation of researchers at the Universidad Nacional Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza in Chachapoyas, whose researchers published a 2022 study of two Amazonas lakes using radar data and machine learning.

name: Instituto del Bien Común
summary: Lima-based organisation that maps community lands and monitors deforestation in the Peruvian Amazon, and runs SICNA, its information system on native communities.

name: Instituto del Mar del Perú
summary: Public research institute attached to the Ministry of Production, based in Callao, that lists SOSMAP among its online services and catalogues marine biodiversity.

name: Instituto Geográfico Nacional
summary: Peru's national cartography body, which describes itself as the lead body producing and updating the country's official base maps.

name: Instituto Nacional de Investigación en Glaciares y Ecosistemas de Montaña
summary: Specialised technical body created by Law 30286 and attached to the environment ministry, producing scientific information on glaciers and mountain ecosystems and named among the bodies Project Guacamaya is meant to strengthen.

name: Instituto Nacional de Investigación y Capacitación de Telecomunicaciones de la Universidad Nacional de Ingeniería
summary: Telecommunications research institute of the Universidad Nacional de Ingeniería, listed as executing entity of a 2024 PROCIENCIA grant for an aguajal remote sensing platform.

name: Instituto para la Conservación de Especies Amenazadas
summary: Cusco-based organisation whose GBIF record says its research involves monitoring species populations.

name: Laboratorio de Inteligencia Artificial del IIAP
summary: IIAP-run laboratory that analyses drone, satellite, sensor and acoustic data, including automatic palm counts from drone images published in Nature Communications and species identification from forest recordings.

name: Laboratorio de Inteligencia Artificial, Drones y Análisis Espacial
summary: A CINCIA programme it describes as Peru's most advanced drone programme, using AI-enhanced analysis of multisensor and high-resolution satellite data to detect mining impacts.

name: Linn Aerospace Perú
summary: Private aerospace company that says it designs its own drones for conservation, and that ACCA names as a co-organiser of AmazonTEC 2026.

name: Manejo de Bosques Sin Fronteras de la cuenca del río La Novia (MABOSINFRON)
summary: Civil association that Actualidad Ambiental reported in May 2012 had obtained approval of the first conservation concession in Purús province, covering 6,718.80 hectares for a renewable ten-year term.

name: MapBiomas Alerta Perú
summary: ACCA-led initiative that validates existing deforestation alerts in Peru with satellite images of up to 3.7 metres resolution, having processed over 90,000 alerts since 2021 by March 2026.

name: MapBiomas Perú
summary: Programme run by Instituto del Bien Común that maps Peru's annual land cover and use, 1985 to 2025, at 30 metres from Landsat using machine learning.

name: MashUPerú
summary: A library for viewing acoustically characterised bat calls and their georeferenced variations, presented as Peru's first bat sound library.

name: Ministerio de Desarrollo Agrario y Riego
summary: Ministry that reported in March 2026 that joint work had geolocated 181,731 farm plots nationally under its EUDR strategy, and that works with FAO on the Whisp platform.

name: Ministerio del Ambiente
summary: Environment ministry that leads the environment sector, and in February 2026 approved the 2030 action plan of the national biodiversity strategy, which it says is aligned with the Kunming-Montreal framework.

name: Monitoreando el bosque amazónico usando genómica ambiental
summary: Project that will compare airborne eDNA with metabarcoding against traditional methods and aquatic eDNA to assess diversity, led by María Gisella Orjeda Fernández and funded by PROCIENCIA.

name: National University of Saint Anthony the Abbot in Cuzco
summary: Peruvian university that OpenAlex lists with authored papers on machine learning for national glacier mapping (2023) and deep learning for segmenting water bodies in high-mountain remote sensing images (2024).

name: National University of San Marcos
summary: Peruvian university that OpenAlex lists with papers by its authors on a satellite glacier dataset for deep learning (2025) and classifying vegetation cover with artificial intelligence (2023).

name: Nereuz
summary: Organisation from Arequipa, funded by ProInnóvate, whose platform ProActivo describes as combining AI and underwater robotics to monitor aquatic resources.

name: Organismo de Supervisión de los Recursos Forestales y de Fauna Silvestre
summary: Forest supervision body that runs Osinforlab and presented ADETOP v2 in July 2025, an AI algorithm for detecting selective logging from space, developed with Sheffield and Cambridge universities.

name: Osinforlab
summary: Innovation and digital transformation laboratory of OSINFOR, set up at the start of 2026 according to El Peruano, with initiatives including Edge AI fire detection and ADETOP v2 Web.

name: Pachamama Raymi
summary: Organisation reporting on GlobalGiving in June 2026 that more than 14 million trees have been planted since its restoration began, with a forestry project covering 38 rural communities in Cusco as of January 2026.

name: Parque Nacional del Manu
summary: A national park that in August 2022 was one of three protected areas collecting data on Andean bear occupancy in Peru.

name: Parque Nacional Sierra del Divisor
summary: A national park where rangers installed 72 camera traps for 60 days in May and June 2023, recording jaguar, giant anteater and red brocket deer.

name: Parque Nacional Yanachaga Chemillén
summary: A national park that in August 2022 was one of three protected areas collecting Andean bear occupancy data, using transects to be complemented by 50 camera traps.

name: Peru Aves
summary: Community bird database under the Peruvian NGO CORBIDI that compiles photographs and vocalisation recordings from bird enthusiasts, based on citizen science principles.

name: PerúSAT-1
summary: Earth observation satellite run by CONIDA, which reported in January 2018 70 centimetre images used for planning, agriculture and forestry, and an archive used by over 70 public bodies.

name: Plataforma de teledetección para la gestión sostenible del ecosistema de aguajales
summary: Project, now in the process of closure, aiming to validate a remote sensing platform for aguajal ecosystems, with software for automatic detection expected; led by Antero Castro Nieto.

name: Pontificia Universidad Católica del Perú
summary: Peruvian university that an OpenAlex count of works since 2020 ranks first among Peruvian institutions for works tagged with AI or machine learning and ecology, biodiversity or remote sensing.

name: Portal BioANP
summary: A portal built by SERNANP to share public information on biodiversity in Peru's protected natural areas, including monitoring data from the Environmental Monitoring System.

name: ProDelphinus
summary: Lima-based organisation that says it has monitored small cetaceans' interaction with artisanal fisheries on the Peruvian coast since 2005.

name: Programa de Inversión Forestal del Perú
summary: A four-project Amazon deforestation programme run by Programa Bosques, funded by the Inter-American Development Bank and World Bank, with monitoring investment covering equipment, infrastructure and furniture.

name: Programa Jaguar, Reserva Nacional Tambopata
summary: A jaguar monitoring programme in Madre de Dios, run by SERNANP since 2021 according to Mongabay, whose first camera-trap survey over 830 square kilometres recorded 15 individual jaguars.

name: Programa Nacional de Conservación de Bosques para la Mitigación del Cambio Climático
summary: A Peruvian environment ministry programme, working on forest conservation with communities and governments since 2010, aiming to conserve 54 million hectares of tropical forest and running Geobosques.

name: Programa Nacional de Investigación Científica y Estudios Avanzados
summary: Self-described public fund for science, technology and innovation offering funding calls, funding the aguajal remote sensing platform and having funded a LiDAR internship in Brazil.

name: ProInnóvate
summary: Peruvian programme that ProActivo reported in June 2025 had financed nearly 500 climate initiatives, with marine ecosystem co-financing attributed to it by the production minister.

name: ProNaturaleza
summary: A Peruvian private non-profit foundation created in 1984 advises on participatory environmental monitoring around extractive activities and held a CEPF grant assessing three Carpish Key Biodiversity Area birds.

name: Protecting Peru's Tambopata National Reserve
summary: A past collaboration in Tambopata National Reserve between SPDA, Rainforest Connection and IUCN NL, in which RFCx says it installed 20 Guardians whose alerts helped stop illegal logging.

name: Proyecto Guacamaya Perú
summary: AI project launched in March 2025 by Peru's environment ministry with Microsoft, planned to analyse satellite images, bioacoustic recordings and camera-trap images, with a 2025 work plan expecting databases, algorithms and training.

name: Radar Mining Monitoring
summary: Satellite tool built and run by ACCA using NASA geospatial technology and Sentinel-1 imagery for near-real-time deforestation and mining information, with gold mining alerts in Madre de Dios.

name: Rainforest Expeditions
summary: An ecotourism company managing three lodges in Tambopata, founded in 1989, which builds Wired Amazon and runs AmazonCam Tambopata, and says it has set up over 100 wildlife cameras.

name: Registros de la Fonoteca del IIAP
summary: Metadata catalogue of 193 Amazon fauna sound recordings from IIAP's sound library, recorded at the Allpahuayo Biological Station, with links to the audio.

name: Reserva de Vida Silvestre Los Pantanos de Villa
summary: A wildlife reserve that was among the first protected areas to start testing SMART Connect in October 2019, which the report said would allow near real time data exchange.

name: Reserva Nacional de Lachay
summary: A national reserve that was among the first protected areas to start testing SMART Connect in October 2019, which the report said would allow near real time data exchange.

name: Reserva Nacional Matsés
summary: A national reserve that, according to an October 2017 report, had implemented surveillance tools including SMART since 2015 with WCS support, with GPS data to be cleaned for entry after ranger training.

name: Reserva Nacional Tambopata
summary: A national reserve that in April 2025 had 13 specialised drones to detect illegal mining and logging and monitor biodiversity, plus computing equipment to process the images.

name: Ronda Campesina del caserío de Juningue
summary: Community patrol of the Juningue hamlet which, per Actualidad Ambiental in June 2020, worked for over two years on the 635.46-hectare Gran Mirador de Juningue conservation concession, granted for 40 renewable years.

name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance-Perú
summary: A civil association constituted in 2012 and registered in Cusco that Mongabay reports processes Programa Jaguar photographs with AI and whose field coordinator installs camera traps.

name: Santuario Histórico de Machupicchu
summary: A historic sanctuary that in August 2022 was one of three protected areas collecting data on Andean bear occupancy in Peru.

name: Servicio Nacional de Áreas Naturales Protegidas por el Estado
summary: The environment ministry agency leading Peru's state protected areas system said in June 2025 it had over 80 species monitoring protocols in nationally administered protected areas.

name: Servicio Nacional Forestal y de Fauna Silvestre
summary: Peru's national forest and wildlife authority, attached to the agrarian ministry and working since 2014, which runs the SNIFFS forest and wildlife information system.

name: SIMON
summary: An open-access monitoring centre built by the environment ministry which, as described in June 2024, would use satellite data and Google Earth Engine to report ecosystem state and project future loss.

name: Sistema de Información de la Diversidad Biológica y Ambiental de la Amazonía Peruana
summary: A Peruvian Amazon biodiversity information system whose new version ACTO says IIAP developed with Bioamazon support, with IIAP described as its main node in May–June 2021.

name: Sistema de Información sobre Comunidades Nativas de la Amazonía Peruana
summary: A database run by the Instituto del Bien Común that, according to its January 2012 page, made 65 fields per native community, plus maps, publicly available.

name: Sistema Nacional de Información Forestal y de Fauna Silvestre
summary: A national forest and wildlife information system run by SERFOR, made up of six modules and four components, which gives forest loss and alert information through Geobosques.

name: Smithsonian Peru Biodiversity Program
summary: A programme whose GBIF publisher record says it conducts biodiversity assessments and long-term monitoring and manages data across terrestrial, aquatic and marine habitats, with an address in Lima.

name: Sociedad Peruana de Derecho Ambiental
summary: An environmental law NGO that Rainforest Connection describes as its local partner in Tambopata and says uses acoustic alert data in its legal cases.

name: Subsistence Hunting in Manu National Park, Perceptions, Coexistence, Impacts and Community-led Management
summary: A project listed by the Rufford Foundation on 19 February 2025, which aims to assess effects of traditional hunting on mammals using camera-trap monitoring and carnivore diet analysis.

name: Technology in indigenous forest protection
summary: A project, per its IATI record, training 25 people in drones, GPS and satellite apps, aiming at an early warning system for indigenous communities in Ucayali.

name: Unidades de Monitoreo Georreferencial Satelital del Ministerio Público
summary: Satellite monitoring units of the public prosecutor's office whose fourth unit, Actualidad Ambiental reported in June 2018, opened in Lima to issue early alerts on environmental crimes.

name: Universidad Nacional Agraria La Molina
summary: Peruvian education institution whose researchers, per OpenAlex, have published on Andean land cover mapping, timber identification and soil carbon mapping, and whose academics, ACCA reports, joined a 2023 TensorFlow training.

name: Universidad Nacional de Ingeniería
summary: A university whose researchers are carrying out OSINFOR's Edge AI forest fire detection pilot together with OSINFOR.

name: Universidad Nacional del Altiplano
summary: Peruvian education institution whose authors, per OpenAlex, published a 2025 paper on classifying algarrobo trees from aerial imagery and a 2026 paper on an open-source fire risk forecasting system.

name: Universidad Nacional Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza de Amazonas
summary: Education institution in Chachapoyas, Peru, whose researchers, per OpenAlex, have published on machine learning for forest fire risk, lakes, land cover change, drone tree detection and open ecological data.

name: Validación de un Prototipo de Vigilancia Forestal mediante Edge AI y Participación Comunitaria
summary: Pilot that OSINFOR is implementing in the Paoyhan native community in Loreto, combining edge AI and LoRaWAN to detect smoke columns and alert in real time, under Amazonía+.

name: Wired Amazon
summary: A Rainforest Expeditions initiative using Zooniverse for AmazonCam Tambopata's 200-square-kilometre camera grid, sending specimens for DNA barcoding, and monitoring trees with drones through Aerobotany, launched in 2016.

name: WWF Perú
summary: A conservation organisation that Mongabay reports installed 60 camera traps in Brazil nut concessions, and that says it monitors dolphins in Ucayali and Loreto with recorders and pingers.

name: Yunkawasi
summary: An organisation Mongabay reports led an eight-month thermal drone trial with community monitors, whose director ACCA reports presented a monkey detection drone project at AmazonTEC 2026.

name: Zona Reservada Lomas de Ancón
summary: A reserved zone that was among the first protected areas to start testing SMART Connect in October 2019, which the report said would allow near real time data exchange.

name: Área de Conservación Regional Comunal Tamshiyacu Tahuayo
summary: A 420,081-hectare protected area in Loreto with three ecosystems, which already had a communal monitoring system that a 2018 Rufford project set out to enhance, with threats recorded during patrols.

name: ÑAWPAQ PACHA
summary: A machine learning model built by Flor Melany Yanarico Huanca forecasts next-month active-fire detection probabilities for Puno’s 108 districts and publishes dashboard risk levels.

name: Adelbert Mountains acoustic survey for conservation land-use planning
summary: A September 2015 article reported that acoustic survey data from Nature Conservancy scientists in the Adelbert Mountains would inform conservation land-use planning, collected across land use types in three communities.

name: Azercosmos forest monitoring programme in Papua New Guinea
summary: A closed forest monitoring programme in Papua New Guinea that Azercosmos said in March 2025 it carried out with the Commonwealth of Nations; a planned AI satellite platform has no confirmed launch.

name: Biodiversity Assessment and Awareness Building in the Kunua and Mount Balbi Key Biodiversity Area of Bougainville, Papua New Guinea
summary: A closed CEPF-funded project (June 2018 to December 2021) covering baseline biological surveys, education and community consultations in a Bougainville key biodiversity area; its final report says over 50 community participants were trained in wildlife surveys.

name: Capacity Development Project for Operationalization of PNG Forest Resource Information Management System for Addressing Climate Change
summary: JICA and PNGFA project that ran from August 2014 to August 2019, following a 2011 to 2014 phase that established PNG-FRIMS, to enhance and operationalize it, including forest disturbance classification and drone introduction.

name: Climate Change and Development Authority
summary: PNG Government statutory body based in Hohola, Port Moresby, which runs and built the PNG Forest and Land Use Monitoring Geo-Portal and is responsible for publishing and updating its online information.

name: Community-based Forest and Coastal Conservation and Resource Management in Papua New Guinea
summary: Project run by the Conservation and Environment Protection Authority that closed on 31 December 2019; its terminal evaluation mentions drone surveys and recommends reviewing biodiversity surveys and recent GoogleEarth images.

name: Community-Led Conservation and Sustainable Landscapes in Papua New Guinea's Highlands
summary: A GBFF-funded project run by CEPA and FAO, described by the GEF in June 2026 as new, covering over 2.2 million hectares in three highland provinces and planning community-based monitoring.

name: Conflict Islands Conservation Initiative Turtle Program
summary: An ongoing programme described in Papua New Guinea’s 2024 IOSEA report as designed to monitor and protect nesting turtles and eggs across the Conflict Island Atoll’s 21 islands.

name: Conservation and Environment Protection Authority
summary: Papua New Guinea's conservation authority, which launched workshops with UNDP in June 2026 to review the national biodiversity strategy and validate the 7th National Report, and identified the Lukim Gather app in 2022.

name: Conservation of Flying Foxes in Papua New Guinea
summary: Closed 2005 project led by Silvia Lomascolo, whose main goal was starting a monitoring programme for Dobsonia moluccensis, a heavily hunted highland bat, centred on Herowana village in Eastern Highlands Province.

name: Cool Earth Rainforest Lab, Wabumari, Papua New Guinea
summary: An active Cool Earth Rainforest Lab at Wabumari, Milne Bay Province, which Cool Earth says it opened in 2024 and describes as equipping Indigenous peoples with tools to monitor their territories.

name: Department of Surveying and Land Studies, Papua New Guinea University of Technology
summary: A university department whose GIS section is the affiliation of both authors of a 2019 paper on remote sensing and GIS forest mapping in Bulolo District, Morobe Province.

name: Enhancing Forest Law Enforcement in Papua New Guinea (ITTO PD449/07)
summary: Completed ITTO project (PD449/07) run by the PNG Forest Authority with an ITTO budget of USD 473,040, aiming among other things at timber tracking and a database to detect illegal forestry.

name: Forest monitoring system (CEPA and UNDP, Papua New Guinea)
summary: According to Mammoth Geospatial, the forest monitoring system links satellite alerts, case management and field verification and is now running in PNG's forest monitoring work.

name: Infinity Blue Mangrove Initiative, New Ireland Province
summary: A locally driven monitoring campaign assessing New Ireland's mangrove extent, carbon storage and degradation rates, with a stated funding duration of 30 months from 2023 to 2025 and BCAF support.

name: Lukim Gather
summary: A free, open-source mobile data collection app built by UNDP Papua New Guinea for monitoring ecosystems, used by trained Kokoda Track rangers in 2022 and in beta that August.

name: Managalas Conservation Foundation
summary: Local NGO that Forests News describes as taking part, with clans and Landscape Alliance, in mapping the biodiversity of the Managalas Plateau.

name: Managalas Plateau community biodiversity monitoring
summary: Active community monitoring on the Managalas Plateau, reported in June 2026, where local team leaders and Landscape Alliance scientists use camera traps, acoustic devices and eDNA, with camera traps producing about 1.5 terabytes per grid monthly.

name: Mapping and Monitoring the Torricelli Mountain Range Conservation Area
summary: BIOPAMA-funded project P636, run by TCA and now complete, which bought 112 smartphones, laptops and other computers, trained all 112 staff in CyberTracker and SMART and began building the Mother Nature portal.

name: Morobe Development Foundation Inc.
summary: A community-based organisation in Lae, Morobe Province, which in a November 2020 article described a remote satellite imagery study of leatherback nesting habitats in the Kamiali Wildlife Management Area.

name: Mother Nature online data portal
summary: Online data portal that TCA began building with a volunteer developer in the USA, with household surveys through its CHAD App planned to feed it.

name: New Guinea Binatang Research Center
summary: A non-profit biological research and conservation organisation in Madang that uses paraecologists and parataxonomists, publishes eight GBIF datasets, and lists the Darwin Initiative, Rainforest Trust and National Geographic Society among its supporters.

name: Papua New Guinea Forest Monitoring Portal
summary: University of PNG portal that an archived 2015 EU page described as mapping recent clearing, logging and fire from Landsat, SPOT and MODIS imagery, with a real-time fire watch website already online.

name: Papua New Guinea leatherbacks, Huon Coast community-based leatherback turtle conservation project (2004 to 2014)
summary: A closed community-based leatherback turtle project (2004 to 2014) run by the Marine Research Foundation, covering seven Huon Coast village sites, with monitoring at Kamiali beach dating from 1999.

name: Papua New Guinea Multi-Purpose National Forest Inventory
summary: A national forest inventory begun in 2016, aiming for 1000 permanent sample plots, with a faunal biodiversity component and field data validated in Open Foris Collect before moving to Open Foris Arena.

name: Papua New Guinea National Forest Monitoring System
summary: An operational national forest monitoring and MRV system, led by the PNG Forest Authority, using Collect Earth and TerraPNG, with a 2017 web portal and a planned prototype deforestation alert system.

name: Papua New Guinea Natural Resource Management Hub
summary: UNDP-run, UNDP-built open-source digital public good hosting data-sharing and mapping tools, including a GeoNode-based Biodiversity and Climate Geoportal and the Bougainville Natural Resource Portal.

name: Piku Biodiversity Network
summary: A biodiversity not-for-profit monitoring sawfish and rhino ray bycatch with Kikori fishers, with a Port Moresby postal address and GBIF registration in 2023, without datasets when checked.

name: PNG Forest and Land Use Monitoring Geo-Portal
summary: Major component of PNG's National Forest Monitoring System, built and run by CCDA with FAO technical support, whose data could only be viewed online, with no downloads, as of January 2024.

name: PNG Forest Authority
summary: The authority that, per the PNG REDD+ site, has led Papua New Guinea's National Forest Monitoring System and forest reference level work, and completed land use change assessments with Collect Earth in 2015 and 2019.

name: PNG Forest Resource Information Management System
summary: Spatial forest data system established during the 2011 to 2014 JICA-PNGFA project, which by August 2019 held databases on topography, concessions, roads and protected areas, with inquiries directed to the PNG Forest Authority.

name: Protecting Tree Kangaroo Habitat, YUS Conservation Area, Papua New Guinea
summary: Active project in the YUS Conservation Area aiming to combine community monitoring with drones and satellite imagery, including 1,227 square kilometres of imagery donated by the Airbus Foundation, to inform community-led management.

name: R2R Strengthening the Management Effectiveness of the National System of Protected Areas (Papua New Guinea)
summary: GEF-funded project with UNDP as implementation agency and CEPA as lead partner, reported in a 2019 midterm review to have a USD 10,929,358 grant and to use SMART and camera traps for ranger data.

name: Sea Women of Melanesia Inc.
summary: Not-for-profit association incorporated in Papua New Guinea, with Indigenous women as all its directors, whose Kimbe-based team of around ten conducts reef surveys in Kimbe Bay with Coral Sea Foundation technical support.

name: Shoreline protection analysis and mangrove cover mapping using remote sensing in Papua New Guinea
summary: Closed project that aimed to map current mangrove extent around Barakau Village using drone surveys, satellite imagery and GNSS field data; Ecoresolve says it processed the images, and results showed local mangrove decline.

name: Sustainable Wildlife Management Programme in Papua New Guinea
summary: A wildlife management programme working with four Indigenous communities in the Bismarck Forest Corridor, run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, which reports installing 48 camera traps at Kwiop in June 2021.

name: Tenkile Conservation Alliance
summary: A not-for-profit based at Lumi, Sandaun Province, working to save tree kangaroos in the Torricelli Mountains, which trained 112 staff in Cybertracker and SMART under a BIOPAMA grant and plans app-based ranger monitoring.

name: Thermal drone monitoring of tree kangaroos in the Torricelli Mountain Range
summary: Thermal drone monitoring in the Torricelli Mountain Range, run by the Tenkile Conservation Alliance, which Perth Zoo reported in March 2026 as finding record numbers of two critically endangered tree kangaroo species.

name: Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program
summary: A partnership between Woodland Park Zoo's programme and TKCP-PNG, begun in 1996, which supports rangers' ecological monitoring and mapping in the YUS Conservation Area, Morobe Province.

name: University of Papua New Guinea
summary: University whose Forest Monitoring Portal was described in an archived 2015 EU page as mapping clearing, logging and fire, and whose Centre for Biodiversity and Natural Products is listed by GBIF as a data publisher.

name: WCS Papua New Guinea Program
summary: Programme run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, with more than 60 staff at four offices, that does rapid biodiversity surveys and works with New Ireland and Manus communities and governments on coral reef monitoring.

name: Where They Walk
summary: Project of unknown status, a collaboration between The Walking Shark Project and CICI, in which rangers run monthly walking shark surveys and record the data in the EarthRanger app to gather baseline data.

name: WWF-PNG trial of drones, camera traps and KoboToolbox in Kikori
summary: A closed May 2024 trial, run with WWF-Pacific, of three technologies including drones and camera traps for biodiversity surveys and participatory mapping in the Kikori District, Gulf Province.

name: Aboitiz Foundation
summary: A foundation that signed an MOU with Archeda on forest carbon projects using satellite remote sensing.

name: Aboitiz Foundation and Archeda forest carbon partnership
summary: A proposed partnership in which Aboitiz Foundation and Archeda signed an MOU to explore forest carbon projects in the Philippines under CarbonPH, with planned feasibility studies, satellite-based assessments and monitoring and verification systems.

name: Advancing ecosystem-based approaches for building climate resilience, livelihoods, and food security in the Coral Triangle Philippines
summary: Closed project run by Environmental Defense Fund, awarded US$269,250, that assessed mangroves, coral reefs and seagrass in eight barangays and used drone mapping of mangroves; completed February 2025.

name: ALOS-2 GEEasy Forest Cover Change Detection Application
summary: A web-based forest cover change tool using ALOS-2 ScanSAR data in Google Earth Engine, built by JAXA with PhilSA's assistance for non-coders, with training attended by several Philippine agencies and Conservation International Philippines.

name: Apo Reef Marine Protection
summary: A marine protection effort at Apo Reef in which Global Conservation says it supports enforcement with M2 radar detecting vessels of 7 metres or more to 9.5 nautical miles, plus Skylight and EarthRanger.

name: Application of eDNA Metabarcoding in Faunal Biodiversity Assessment of IndoPacific Mangroves Vulnerable to Climate Change: Philippine Node (e-Asia)
summary: An e-Asia project which, in October 2023, aimed to use eDNA to develop a standardised tool for monitoring fish and invertebrates in mangroves, with expected completion in 2025.

name: Automated Rapid Reef Assessment System
summary: A boat-towable underwater video platform with software that stitches footage into geotagged coral reef records, described as covering up to 33 km of coastline a day without divers.

name: BALYENA.ORG
summary: Non-profit society set up in 2013 researching whales and dolphins in the Philippines, including blue whale monitoring in the Bohol Sea and a long-term humpback whale study in the Babuyan Marine Corridor.

name: BatMapPH: Philippine Bat Species Occurrence Database
summary: A CC0-licensed database of Philippine bat records from published research and field surveys, published on GBIF by the Eco/Con Lab Biodiversity Synthesis+ Centre, led by Krizler Tanalgo, and said to support species distribution models.

name: Biodiversity Management Bureau
summary: A DENR bureau whose Director the CBD lists as the Philippine clearing-house mechanism national focal point, and which runs the Philippine Clearing House Mechanism website.

name: BlueCARES Project
summary: A project under which a drone training programme was launched for seagrass mapping.

name: Bohol Island State University
summary: A university with two 2025 papers listed in OpenAlex, one on a machine learning web application for counting aerial fauna and one comparing models predicting species distribution in fishing data.

name: Caraga State University
summary: A university with OpenAlex-listed papers on machine learning classifiers for mapping falcata plantations in Sentinel-2 images and, in 2022, on estimating plantation stand age with Landsat.

name: Center for Conservation Innovations Ph Inc.
summary: A nature conservation NGO established in 2015, evolving from Fauna and Flora International Philippines, with biodiversity and technology teams, and linked as builder of the Lawin system and user of EarthRanger.

name: Centre for Sustainability-Philippines
summary: An organisation whose mission, per Rainforest Trust's partner page, is protecting the Philippines' last forests through legally established protected areas, and which partners with Rainforest Trust.

name: Checklist of Philippine Birds
summary: Dataset giving range and conservation status of Philippine birds; the 2025 edition lists 761 species, 274 endemic. Built and run by the Wild Bird Club of the Philippines.

name: Citizen's Action for Monitoring Ecosystems
summary: A Haribon programme, described by Haribon as a system for monitoring Key Biodiversity Areas outside the protected areas system, and listed alongside the Ka-Patrol app.

name: Conservation International Philippines Foundation, Inc.
summary: A non-profit affiliate of Conservation International Foundation that signed a remote sensing conservation agreement with PhilSA in October 2023, when its director reported using its own mapping tools.

name: CopPhil Benthic Habitat Classification Map
summary: A dataset of shallow coastal habitat classes, including coral reefs and seagrass beds, at 10-metre resolution, combining Sentinel data with in situ observations from Filipino partners and built by CopPhil.

name: CopPhil Coastal Marine (Benthic) Habitat Monitoring Service
summary: A CopPhil service that will provide free and open satellite data on coastal waters, including benthic habitat maps combining Sentinel data and in situ data from Filipino stakeholders.

name: CopPhil Forest Area and Type
summary: A dataset mapping annual extent of mangrove, open and closed forest across the Philippines at 10-metre resolution, produced with machine learning from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery and built by CopPhil.

name: CopPhil Forest Mapping Service
summary: A CopPhil service whose Forest Area and Type product maps three forest classes yearly at 10 metres using machine learning, alongside a yearly Tree Cover Density product at 50 metres.

name: CopPhil Land Cover Change map
summary: A dataset identifying and classifying land cover change, detected with BFASTmonitor on Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 time series and classified by machine learning, with annual updates built by CopPhil.

name: Coral Reef Management Hub, Mindanao State University at Naawan
summary: Hub run by Mindanao State University at Naawan that offers drone-based georeferenced coastal and habitat maps and assesses mangroves, seagrass beds and coral reefs over space and time.

name: Davao Oriental State University
summary: A university that was the implementing agency for the PCAARRD-funded ridge-to-reef modelling and monitoring project in Pujada and Mayo Bay, listed as ongoing in February 2024.

name: Department of Biology, College of Arts and Sciences, Manila Central University
summary: Biology department in Caloocan, Metro Manila, listed as an affiliation by the first author of a 2026 paper on a camera trap survey of Bubalus mindorensis and Rusa marianna.

name: Department of Electronics Engineering, Batangas State University
summary: Electronics engineering department in Batangas, listed as an affiliation by the first author of a 2025 paper on a machine-vision monitoring system for mangrove habitat.

name: Department of Environment and Natural Resources
summary: A Philippine government department that, per PhilSA's March 2024 release, committed to set up natural capital accounts including mangroves, and which is the agency NAMRIA belongs to.

name: Department of Science and Technology
summary: A Philippine government department that CopPhil names as a partner of ESA in implementing the programme.

name: Donsol whale shark population survey
summary: A WWF-Philippines survey in which the 2021 round ran over 27 days from March to June, recorded 144 whale shark encounters, and identified individuals by their white spot patterns.

name: Eco/Con Lab Biodiversity Synthesis+ Centre
summary: The hub of the Eco/Con Lab at the University of Southern Mindanao, which aims to mobilise and synthesise Philippine biodiversity data and publishes BatMapPH on GBIF under a CC0 licence.

name: Environmental DNA Research and Development Center, Mindanao State University at Naawan
summary: eDNA research centre in Naawan, Misamis Oriental, listed as an affiliation by the first author of a 2026 paper on eDNA metabarcoding of mangrove-associated fish in selected Philippine bioregions.

name: Fish-i
summary: An underwater camera and computer vision system estimating size, density and biomass for up to 780 marine fish species, with Estancia, Iloilo its first formally adopting local government.

name: Forest Foundation Philippines
summary: Local conservation financing platform that channels investment from international partners, by its own description; its board approved 12 grants totalling PHP 28.38 million for January to June 2026.

name: Forest Management Bureau
summary: Government bureau, run by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources, which the Philippines' forest reference level submission names as responsible for developing it and for the 2013 to 2019 Forest Resource Assessment.

name: Foundation for the Philippine Environment
