summary: University named in the IODE consortium, whose biology faculty announced a project using genetic identification and telemetry, and which runs the Wolf and Lynx at a Crossroads project.

name: University of Life Sciences in Lublin
summary: University that reports a field campaign in May 2026.

name: University of Lodz
summary: University whose department Biodiversa+ lists as a partner in the DNAquaIMG project.

name: University of Silesia in Katowice
summary: University whose R&D project pages list the HabitARS project.

name: University of Warmia and Mazury in Olsztyn
summary: University that OpenAlex lists as the first-author affiliation on two 2021 papers, one reviewing tree species classification from airborne LiDAR and one applying game theory-based machine learning to lagoon climate effects.

name: University of Warsaw
summary: University that led IMBIO, hosts the GBIF Poland node established in 2003, runs the Polish Biodiversity Information Network, and partners in FunDive, with several Sentinel-2 and satellite imagery studies.

name: W. Szafer Institute of Botany, Polish Academy of Sciences
summary: Polish Academy of Sciences institute that says it holds major scientific collections and databases on vascular plants and cryptogams, including a herbarium of over 657,253 accessioned vascular plant specimens.

name: WANDER Buoy
summary: Project aiming to build autonomous sensor buoys monitoring surface water quality, with planned machine learning for optical fouling detection.

name: Warsaw University of Life Sciences
summary: University that OpenAlex lists as the first-author affiliation on a 2018 paper on monitoring free water table area on wetlands with satellite and drone orthophotomaps, a Kampinos National Park case study.

name: Warsaw University of Technology
summary: University that, according to WaterSense, leads the consortium carrying out ASIR, alongside IMGW-PIB and the companies MAGLY and NEBUCODE.

name: Warta Mouth National Park
summary: National park whose 2025 purchase notice covers 10 large and 30 small camera traps for a Forest Fund project on raccoon impact on native species under wolf pressure, and which partners with MoPA.

name: Waterly
summary: System described by GreenEvo in which AI analyses trends, detects anomalies and predicts hazards.

name: WaterSense
summary: Company that says it builds measuring systems, software and analytics for inland waters, with a project described on its site that includes AI modules for anomaly detection and forecasting.

name: West Pomeranian Nature Society
summary: Society partnering with WWF Poland on lynx reintroduction, according to a press report, with released lynx wearing GPS/GSM collars whose locations are checked in the field.

name: West Pomeranian University of Technology in Szczecin
summary: University that the MoPA site names as the lead of the MoPA monitoring project for protected areas.

name: Wetland Conservation Centre
summary: Organisation that produced a wetlands map in 2022 in work financed by WWF Poland, and is linked as builder of the Polish wetlands priority map.

name: Wielkopolska National Park
summary: National park whose archive site publishes a summary of remote sensing carried out in the park.

name: Wielkopolska National Park remote sensing inventory
summary: Closed project on remote sensing in Wielkopolska National Park, with a total cost of PLN 2,802,126.

name: Wigry National Park
summary: Its 2021 report records 30 to 57 camera traps across 125 locations, 51,875 videos, and 11 ZMŚP measurement programmes carried out by its research and education unit.

name: Wilk i ryś na rozdrożu
summary: Project run by the University of Gdańsk, funded by the National Science Centre, planning fieldwork and genetic analyses on how roads affect grey wolves and Eurasian lynx.

name: Wolin National Park
summary: National park that says its amphibian monitoring found its actions concern protected and red-listed species, says it has funding for a 2025 active conservation project, and partners with MoPA.

name: Wrocław University of Science and Technology
summary: University whose computer systems and networks researchers were named in a 2025 article on AI for monitoring African penguins, and which was named in the SILVA NYMPHA consortium.

name: WWF Poland
summary: Based in Warsaw, it reports using satellite images and AI to identify oxbow lakes and coordinated a marine mammal and bird protection project ending in October 2023.

name: YourWeb
summary: Organisation whose material describes software and names AI deforestation detection in its title.

name: Zagrożenie pożarowe lasu
summary: A forest fire danger map for Poland whose data are updated several times a day and which uses the Forest Research Institute.

name: ZERO HERACLEUM
summary: Project funded through Interreg NEXT Poland-Ukraine that will use field data for machine learning and AI, aiming at tools for automatic detection on satellite data.

name: Zespół Lubelskich Parków Krajobrazowych
summary: Voivodeship self-government unit without legal personality covering 17 landscape parks and 17 protected landscape areas in Lubelskie, aiming to protect the parks’ natural, landscape, cultural and historical values.

name: Zespół Opolskich Parków Krajobrazowych
summary: Organisation made up of three landscape parks.

name: Zespół Parków Krajobrazowych Chełmińskiego i Nadwiślańskiego
summary: Landscape parks complex descended from a 1993 predecessor along the southern lower Vistula valley from Bydgoszcz to Nowe, and carrying its present name since 21 May 2003.

name: Zespół Parków Krajobrazowych w Przemyślu
summary: Podkarpackie voivodeship unit seated on Kościuszki Street in Przemyśl, whose site lists five landscape parks under its nature protection pages.

name: Zespół Parków Krajobrazowych Województwa Lubuskiego
summary: Landscape parks complex whose remit is nature protection, landscape, historical and cultural values, and education in the landscape parks of Lubuskie voivodeship.

name: Zespół Parków Krajobrazowych Województwa Małopolskiego
summary: In October 2022 it reportedly directed 11 landscape parks exceeding 181,000 ha and managed 10 protected landscape areas nearing 573,000 ha, with director-reported goat grazing covering 4.47 ha.

name: Zespół Parków Krajobrazowych Województwa Wielkopolskiego
summary: Complex that looks after 14 landscape parks in Wielkopolska.

name: Zespół Parków Krajobrazowych Województwa Zachodniopomorskiego
summary: Body managing landscape parks in West Pomerania, including the Lower Oder Valley Landscape Park, whose listed tasks include inventories of habitats and protected species sites, and which partners with MoPA.

name: Zespół Parków Krajobrazowych Województwa Łódzkiego
summary: Complex of seven landscape parks in Łódź voivodeship, ranging from Wzniesień Łódzkich to Międzyrzecze Warty i Widawki.

name: Zespół Parków Krajobrazowych Województwa Śląskiego
summary: Complex of landscape parks with four branch offices that carry out nature and landscape protection directly in the individual parks.

name: Zintegrowany Monitoring Środowiska Przyrodniczego
summary: Polish integrated natural environment monitoring programme that says standardised stationary research runs at 12 base stations in river or lake catchments, with a ZMŚP Centre director as coordinator, and partners with Adam Mickiewicz University.

name: Zoo Wrocław
summary: Zoo that holds one of the largest African penguin colonies in Europe.

name: Łukasiewicz Institute of Microelectronics and Photonics
summary: An institute whose listed page gives its funding under the project and its address.

name: Świętokrzyski Park Narodowy
summary: National park whose own page says 38 per cent of its area is under strict protection, where human activity is prohibited by law.

name: Żubr Fund
summary: Donated PLN 100,000 to the Mammal Research Institute for a supercomputer; the Trapper AI system analyses data from camera traps and detectors recording birds and bats.

name: Amigos de las Tortugas Marinas
summary: Community-based, volunteer-run NGO in Maunabo, southeast Puerto Rico, protecting endangered sea turtles; in July 2023 it reported using an MCAF-funded drone with visible and infrared cameras to monitor beaches and detect nesting turtles.

name: Arrecifes Pro Ciudad, Inc.
summary: Non-profit foundation that began a water quality monitoring programme in 2018 with The Nature Conservancy's sponsorship, and reported in 2021 sampling five points every Wednesday.

name: BCG shiny app (Biological Condition Gradient for Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands coral reefs)
summary: Publicly available web application, cited as EPA and NOAA (2023), that scores coral reef health from 1 to 6 but currently accepts only line-point-intercept and benthic demographic coral data.

name: Caribbean Coastal Ocean Observing System, Inc.
summary: Puerto Rico not-for-profit serving as the Regional Association for a certified coastal observing system covering Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands and Navassa, and in February 2020 was helping translate coral monitoring data to Darwin Core.

name: Caribbean Coral Reef Institute
summary: Part of the University of Puerto Rico Mayagüez Campus, it describes project funding enabling a seawater quality laboratory at Isla Magueyes, fully functional from May 2023.

name: Chelonia
summary: Nonprofit sea turtle research and conservation association founded in 1980, with Mona Island, Culebra and Dorado projects reported in 2017 and overnight Dorado monitoring in 2025.

name: CoralBASICS
summary: Closed citizen science project in Puerto Rico, reported in a 2021 interview as having trained dive instructors to collect field data for image validation and coral reef characterisation.

name: Departamento de Recursos Naturales y Ambientales
summary: Puerto Rico's natural resources department, whose integrated planning unit advises on government policy on natural resources; its 2024 transition report says it completed documents for new nature reserves such as Laguna Joyuda.

name: Department of Marine Sciences, University of Puerto Rico-Mayagüez
summary: University department named in the first author's affiliation on a 2026 paper, listed in OpenAlex, describing "Coral Intel", a YOLOv8 deep learning framework for monitoring Caribbean corals.

name: Development and implementation of a water quality monitoring program in shallow coral reef areas around Puerto Rico
summary: Closed project, run by the Caribbean Coral Reef Institute, that planned quarterly measurement of 16 water quality parameters at 42 reef sites from May 2023 to May 2025, with data intended for the Biological Condition Gradient model.

name: International Institute of Tropical Forestry
summary: Institute in Río Piedras, Puerto Rico, which with partners has mapped Caribbean forest types and land cover since 2002; a USDA Forest Service clearinghouse says FAO used the data in its 2005 and 2010 assessments.

name: Island-wide acoustic monitoring in Puerto Rico
summary: Acoustic monitoring programme that Rainforest Connection says it developed in 2021 across 900 sites in the Puerto Rico archipelago, with a neural network trained to detect 40 species and about 200 sites planned for re-sampling to 2024.

name: Jobos Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve
summary: One of 30 National Estuarine Research Reserve System areas, run by Puerto Rico's environment department, which publishes water quality monitoring data online, updated every 10 minutes.

name: Junta de Planificación de Puerto Rico
summary: Planning board whose 2024 transition status report lists a geographic information systems subprogramme and names a goal of improving the services of its geographic information system and applications.

name: Leatherback Sea Turtle Research in Puerto Rico
summary: New England Aquarium project tagging and tracking nesting leatherback turtles, using thermal drone surveys; in the 2026 season it sighted 26 nesting turtles and tagged 23.

name: Luquillo Long-Term Ecological Research
summary: Established in 1988, this programme monitors phenology, stream chemistry and animals, including a 16-hectare plot; its 2019 brief reported data on LIMS and Environmental Data Initiative.

name: National Coral Reef Monitoring Program: Assessment of coral reef benthic communities in Puerto Rico, 2021 (NCEI Accession 0272313)
summary: NCRMP dataset from 2021 coral reef surveys across Puerto Rico, including Vieques, Culebra, Mona and Desecheo, holding three analysis-ready datasets on benthic cover, invertebrates and ESA-listed corals, and coral demography.

name: Protectores de Cuencas
summary: Local non-profit that NOAA's NCCOS says works with it on monthly nutrient and sedimentation monitoring in Culebra's watershed and nearshore waters, a project begun in May 2023 and described as ongoing.

name: Puerto Rico Coral Reef Monitoring Program
summary: Coral reef monitoring programme established by the DNER in 1999 for reefs 30 metres deep or less, for which a CCRI project planned quarterly monitoring at 42 sites from May 2023 to May 2025.

name: Puerto Rico Gap Analysis Project
summary: Clearinghouse collection of information on Puerto Rico's land cover, vertebrate occurrences and land stewardship, using national Gap Analysis Program methods to judge how well species and communities are represented in conservation lands.

name: Puerto Rico land cover and forest formations map, 2000 (IITF_GISciRS44_puertorico_landcov2000)
summary: Land cover and forest formations map for Puerto Rico, Vieques and Culebra, made from 1991 and 2000 Landsat mosaics by decision tree classification, and the original basis for the USGS 2001 NLCD data.

name: San Juan Bay Estuary Partnership
summary: San Juan non-profit coordinating remote water quality monitoring in the estuary, with buoy sensors recording every 15 minutes (five buoys planned) and feeding predictive models for events such as microalgal blooms.

name: Sociedad Ambiente Marino
summary: Puerto Rican scientific and community non-profit founded in 2001 for marine conservation and restoration, which reported monthly coral monitoring in Vieques in August 2025 and published a 2026 bulletin on marine heat and bleaching risks.

name: Sociedad Ornitológica Puertorriqueña
summary: Non-profit founded in 1995, described by the National Wildlife Federation as dedicated to studying and conserving birds in Puerto Rico, which organised a Caribbean Waterbird Census survey in San Juan Bay estuary under its 2025 census tag.

name: University of Puerto Rico at Mayagüez
summary: University that runs the Caribbean Coral Reef Institute, which administers a coral reef water quality monitoring project whose funding built a public Puerto Rican institution's first seawater quality monitoring laboratory.

name: Yo Amo el Tinglar
summary: Community nonprofit that began about ten years before 2021 to protect and monitor sea turtle nesting beaches in the Arecibo region; in 2025 its project leader reported over ten years of data, with Playa Grande the main leatherback site.

name: An-Najah National University
summary: Named as lead institution of a planned Ornithogalum fuscescens conservation project in Misilyah, January 2026 to June 2027, whose actions include ecological monitoring of species populations and habitat conditions.

name: Applied Research Institute - Jerusalem
summary: Describes itself as a non-profit founded in 1990, with biodiversity and geo-informatics departments, and developed a website mapping West Bank forest tree species using GIS.

name: Bethlehem University
summary: University named by CEPF as grantee of a June 2023 to October 2024 wetland project that planned environmental DNA analysis, and presented by the Palestine Institute for Biodiversity and Sustainability as its parent.

name: Biodiversity and Environmental Research Center
summary: Non-governmental research organisation based in Til, Nablus, which CEPF lists as grantee of a 2020 to 2022 project assessing endemic plants, focusing on Iris lortetii, and mapping where its communities occur.

name: Biodiversity Conservation and Community Development in Al-Makhrour Valley
summary: Biodiversity conservation project in Al-Makhrour Valley, run by the Palestine Institute for Biodiversity and Sustainability and funded by the Darwin Initiative; PIBS lists it from 2018 to 2021, with surveys using echolocation and camera traps.

name: Conserving Ornithogalum fuscescens in Misilyah
summary: Planned conservation project in Misilyah, Jenin Governorate, from January 2026 to June 2027, with a USD 36,904 CEPF small grant, led by An-Najah National University, starting with field surveys, habitat mapping and baseline monitoring.

name: Department of Geography and Geomatics, An-Najah National University
summary: University department in Nablus, Palestine, listed as the affiliation of the first and corresponding author of a paper analysing West Bank vegetation index change with multitemporal satellite remote sensing data.

name: Environment Quality Authority
summary: Palestinian environmental body, set up in 1996 by presidential decree and renamed in 2002, whose mission is protecting the environment and preventing hazards, with a 2017 to 2022 strategy covering biodiversity management.

name: Forest Trees of Palestine
summary: Website built by ARIJ giving identification and West Bank distribution of forest tree species using GIS, with a herbarium and specimen database emphasis; it was reachable on the fetch date and carries a 2009 copyright line.

name: General Directorate of Forests, Rangelands and Wildlife
summary: A 2021 report described this Ministry of Agriculture directorate as managing reserves and protected areas through four divisions, with 40 ministry rangers not always available.

name: Genomic and herbarium data collection, Al-Arqoub region
summary: Completed project, listed by BGCI as finished in 2024 and run by PIBS, funded through the GGI-Gardens Awards Program, through which PIBS contributed 291 genera and 81 families to GGBN.

name: Geomolg Portal
summary: Free public geospatial data portal, run and built by the Ministry of Local Government, which its 2020 report says hosted all fundamental layers in Palestine, including environmental layers and a natural reserve layer.

name: In Situ Protection of Endangered Plant Species in Siris
summary: A USD 40,000 project in Siris Key Biodiversity Area, Jenin, running November 2025–April 2027, run by An-Najah National University, funded by CEPF, planning plant and bird data collection.

name: Ministry of Local Government
summary: Palestinian ministry designated by a December 2016 Council of Ministers decree to lead the national spatial data infrastructure project, and which runs the Geomolg Portal.

name: Nature Palestine Society
summary: CEPF grantee for March 2020–June 2021 threatened-plant assessments including Iris atrofusca surveys, described in its report as a Palestinian NGO established in late 2017, with a Ramallah mailing address.

name: Palestine Institute for Biodiversity and Sustainability
summary: Bethlehem University institute that says it wrote Palestine's national CBD report and was entrusted with leading the 2023 to 2030 biodiversity strategy, and which runs the Al Makhrour Valley project.

name: Palestine Wildlife Society
summary: Established officially in 1999, this not-for-profit wildlife organisation describes satellite tracking, acoustic monitoring and Palestine's first bird ringing station in Jericho.

name: Science-Based Conservation of Wetlands in Two Key Biodiversity Areas in Palestine
summary: CEPF-funded project, June 2023 to October 2024, that planned to evaluate two Key Biodiversity Areas, the Jordan Valley and Northern Dead Sea Region, using environmental DNA analysis; Bethlehem University was grantee.

name: The Environmental Education Center of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in Jordan and the Holy Land
summary: Palestinian National NGO and IUCN member since October 2015, with reported ringing at Talitha Kumi since 2000, two ringing stations and education programmes described in 2015.

name: +ATLANTIC CoLAB
summary: Not-for-profit applying modelling, remote sensing, data science and AI, listing machine learning for bathymetry and computer vision for aquaculture, which developed Atlantic SENSE in-house.

name: A Rocha Portugal
summary: Organisation that began a bird ringing programme in 1987, has ringed more than 80,000 birds, and counts waders every 15 days at high tide on a set transect.

name: AEROS
summary: Closed project approved and started in 2020, led by Edisoft with a consortium described as nine entities, planning a platform with a hyperspectral sensor, software-defined radio and GNSS reflectometry system.

name: AGA - Associação Geoparque Arouca
summary: Association that Arouca municipality reported in October 2020 was managing entity of Arouca Geopark, with measures including heritage monitoring and conservation, and which has members and associated entities.

name: Agência para a Gestão Integrada de Fogos Rurais
summary: Reported as responsible for strategic coordination of integrated rural fire management; it manages the Rural Fire Information System and signed a memorandum with the Earth Fire Alliance on adopting FireSat.

name: Agência Portuguesa do Ambiente
summary: Agency headquartered in Amadora with five river basin administrations in mainland Portugal, overseen by the Minister of Environment and Energy, and runs a national water resources information system.

name: AI Moonshot Challenge
summary: International competition promoting AI on satellite data, run by the Portuguese Space Agency; the 2021 second edition offered a research prize of up to 500 thousand euros.

name: AIMOS
summary: Project developing a modelling system for Azores marine protected areas, focused on Condor Seamount, with high-resolution domains and vehicle-based validation still in development and due for completion in 2026.

name: Altri Florestal
summary: Organisation that leads the transForm agenda.

name: AMAL - Comunidade Intermunicipal do Algarve
summary: Intermunicipal community of Algarve councils that, as Barlavento reported in July 2025, gave technical support to Ria Formosa Natural Park co-management and, as reported, took delegated powers for Castro Marim reserve co-management.

name: AMPIC Cascais-Mafra-Sintra
summary: Project run by Mardive, listed as under way, that plans systematic sampling campaigns on nine intertidal platforms.

name: Aquamuseu do Rio Minho
summary: Based in Vila Nova de Cerveira, it reports fisheries biology and aquatic ecology research, lists RESTAURAMINHO for 2026–2029, and reportedly placed a water-monitoring buoy in 2018.

name: ArcticMicroML
summary: Project aiming to decipher Arctic Ocean microbial responses to climate change with tailored machine learning, planning to analyse publicly available long-term datasets.

name: ARDITI
summary: Private nonprofit, according to MBARI, supporting research and innovation in Madeira; a University of Helsinki release says its MARE-Madeira researchers joined work on sensors and embedded AI.

name: Associação BioDiversity4All
summary: Non-profit association that runs BioDiversity4All.

name: Associação BIOPOLIS
summary: Private, non-profit scientific and technical association, according to GBIF's record for CIBIO, established in 2020 and placed by Biodiversa+ at Vairão, Portugal.

name: Associação da Região de Benfeita para Objetivos Regenerativos
summary: Residents' association from Benfeita parish that, according to Agroportal in December 2020, was set up that July and began reforesting the Pai das Donas community common land.

name: Associação de Agricultores do Campo Branco
summary: Farmers' association named on LPN's history page as a partner on the management board of the Castro Verde Biosphere Reserve.

name: Associação de Municípios da Região de Setúbal
summary: Association of municipalities named in a 2 March 2026 document as managing entity of the Arrábida Biosphere, and reported by RTP to have presented and coordinated its candidacy.

name: Associação de Municípios do Douro Superior
summary: Association of municipalities that Agroportal reported in May 2023 was a member of the Douro Internacional Natural Park co-management commission.

name: Atlantic Cloud
summary: Dataset run by the AIR Centre, which says it is making Atlantic basin geospatial data freely available; its catalogue holds 14 MODIS collections.

name: Atlantic Constellation
summary: Proposed European system of Earth observation satellites; CEiiA says it is developing 8 high-resolution and 3 very high-resolution ones, and a Portugal-Spain memorandum was announced in November 2022.

name: Atlantic SENSE
summary: A project covering marine heatwave forecasts, ocean health indicators and land use and cover change, built by colab-atlantic and being piloted across mainland Portugal in July 2025.

name: Atlantic Whale Deal
summary: A project from December 2023 to November 2026 aiming to reduce ship strikes; partner AIR Centre says its work uses satellite imagery and artificial intelligence to support whale detection.

name: ATLANTICLAND
summary: A company named in a January 2025 APA announcement as carrying out the three-year COSMO 2.0 phase.

name: ATLAS
summary: A project that turns existing submarine telecommunications cables into listening systems using Distributed Acoustic Sensing.

name: Azorean Biodiversity Portal
summary: A collaborative e-infrastructure for Azorean biodiversity data on around 11,500 species, with almost 2 million spatial records on a 500 m grid, and part of PORBIOTA.

name: BE Bioinsight & Ecoa
summary: An organisation listed by Enterprise League in Odivelas, Portugal, with biodiversity monitoring as a tag.

name: Bee2FireDetection
summary: A project reported as based on AI, video surveillance and thermography to calculate the probability of a fire, built by Compta and using IBM.

name: Biodiversity Data Portal of Portugal
summary: A portal built and run by GBIF Portugal, building on the Atlas of Living Australia, giving access to occurrence data for Portuguese territory published through GBIF.

name: BioDiversity4All
summary: A Portuguese citizen science platform launched in 2010 and run by Associação Biodiversity4All, linked to iNaturalist; a 2020 talk summary reported over 276,000 records from 10,400 species.

name: Biolens
summary: A June 2022 report describes a web application built by Luís Lopes and Eduardo Marques for classifying species from photographs using deep neural networks.

name: BIOPOLIS/CIBIO-InBIO
summary: A research organisation at Vairão, run by Associação BIOPOLIS, that ran a 2023 ecology machine learning course and advertised an eDNA workshop for 22 May 2026.

name: BIOTA
summary: An environmental consulting company specialised in biodiversity and water, developing deep learning software to process wildlife images from camera traps and drones.

name: Blue Azores
summary: A partnership of the regional government, the Oceano Azul Foundation and the Waitt Institute, aiming to protect 30% of the Azores sea through marine protected areas.

name: blueOASIS
summary: A start-up founded in October 2021 by Guilherme Beleza Vaz and based in Horta, Faial, which builds HydroTwin and launched the open-source RAINDROP underwater acoustic modelling framework.

name: Carta de Ocupação do Solo Conjuntural
summary: A land cover dataset built by the Direção-Geral do Território, produced yearly at 10 m resolution, updated to 2022, classifying Sentinel-2 images with machine learning and expert rules.

name: Carta de Uso e Ocupação do Solo
summary: A vector land use and cover dataset built by the Direção-Geral do Território, with a minimum mapping unit of 1 hectare, within SMOS.

name: CeaseFire
summary: An application built by Instituto Dom Luiz, whose main purpose is to help forest managers and firefighters with fire prevention and combat.

name: CEiiA
summary: An organisation that says its Space Unit makes products using space imagery and AI, and that it leads the Atlantic Constellation in Portugal with the Air Force and GEOSAT.

name: Censo de Aves Comuns
summary: A long-term monitoring programme of common breeding birds and their habitats, run by the Sociedade Portuguesa para o Estudo das Aves, aiming to show national population trends.

name: Censo Nacional do Lobo Ibérico 2019/2021
summary: A closed 2019/2021 wolf census run by ICNF, with 641 camera trap stations giving 37,241 trap-nights, aiming to establish wolf presence by 10 by 10 km grid square.

name: Censos Borboletas de Portugal
summary: A butterfly monitoring programme run by Tagis, whose scheme page says the monitoring helps show the status of butterfly species.

name: Centre for Ecology, Evolution and Environmental Changes
summary: A research centre whose Machine Learning in Ecology group works on computational ecology and conservation, developing software and databases, and which is supported by FCT through national funds.

name: Centre for Environmental and Marine Studies
summary: Research centre at the University of Aveiro whose anniversary exhibition, according to EurOcean, covers projects including artificial intelligence for deep-sea conservation.

name: Centro de Ciências do Mar do Algarve
summary: An independent non-profit research organisation in the University of Algarve system, with a Biodiversity Data Science group using AI and machine learning, and an E-services marine data platform.

name: Centro Interdisciplinar de Investigação Marinha e Ambiental
summary: University of Porto research institution whose 2025 report says a team led by Catarina Magalhães developed ulrb, a machine learning tool for finding rare microorganisms in microbiome data.

name: CICLOPE
summary: Forest fire monitoring system with automatic AI detection, whose control centres are normally at civil protection sub-regional commands and GNR territorial commands, built by INOV.

name: Circunforce Lda
summary: Company associated with the database behind the Naturdata portal.

name: CoastNet
summary: Closed coastal research infrastructure, built by MARE, designed to collect biological and environmental data autonomously and provide it in near real time, with completion extended to 13 June 2022.

name: Compta
summary: Portuguese company that ESMARTCITY reported in 2019 as having developed the Bee2FireDetection solution.

name: CORUJA
summary: Project run by INOV that aims to develop automatic night-time rural fire detection using AI and advanced neural networks.

name: COSMO
summary: Coastal monitoring programme run by the Portuguese Environment Agency and funded by the Fundo Ambiental, continuing work begun in 2018, with a second phase planned for three years at about 2 million euros.

name: CyBELE
summary: Organisation that provides geospatial intelligence for environmental case management.

name: Câmara Municipal de Alpiarça
summary: Municipal council that Agroportal reported in August 2023 owns land under the Paul da Gouxa reserve, to be managed jointly with Quinta da Atela under a protocol due for signing.

name: Câmara Municipal de Arganil
summary: Municipal council that Agroportal reported in June 2021 was in the Floresta da Serra do Açor project with Jerónimo Martins and common-land owners' associations, restoring land burnt in 2017, with 58,090 trees planted.

name: Câmara Municipal de Cascais
summary: Municipality that Time Out Cascais reports is turning to space technology, artificial intelligence and ocean science to predict where and when invasive seaweed may wash ashore, and which funds eo4ro.

name: Câmara Municipal de Faro
summary: Municipal council whose mayor, Rogério Bacalhau, chaired the Ria Formosa Natural Park co-management commission as municipalities' representative, Barlavento reported in October 2023.

name: Câmara Municipal de Loulé
summary: Municipal council that Loulé municipality reported in October 2020 manages the Rocha da Pena and Fonte Benémola Local Protected Landscapes, created by municipal decision on 18 October 2010.

name: Câmara Municipal de Loures
summary: Municipality that said in August 2024 that SPEA coordinated LIFE LxAquila in a consortium including it, and that one pair of Bonelli's eagles was monitored regularly there.

name: Câmara Municipal de Portalegre
summary: Municipal council that Agroportal reported in July 2020 signed a cooperation protocol with the Fundo Ambiental and ICNF to promote and implement co-management of Serra de São Mamede Natural Park.

name: Câmara Municipal de Torres Vedras
summary: Municipal council that, according to a landscape awards presentation, manages the Serras do Socorro e Archeira Local Protected Landscape through three management bodies.

name: Câmara Municipal do Funchal
summary: Municipal council that Funchal municipality reported in July 2023 had invested about 1.5 million euros over the preceding year in invasive-species control and native planting across 75% of its Ecological Park.

name: DataFish
summary: Organisation named in a PhD posting as the place where the candidate will work on activities including machine learning model development.

name: Departamento de Ciência de Computadores da Faculdade de Ciências da Universidade do Porto
summary: University of Porto computer science department whose staff developed Biolens, which uses deep neural networks for image classification.

name: Digital-ESAS
summary: Project run by Strix International to develop an AI system automating seabird monitoring at offshore wind farms, with offshore operational testing planned for July 2027.

name: Direção-Geral de Recursos Naturais, Segurança e Serviços Marítimos
summary: Organisation whose site has pages on marine protected areas of the national network and on monitoring and measures projects for the Portuguese sea.

name: Direção-Geral do Território
summary: Central state service for spatial planning and geographic databases that runs and built the land use monitoring system, and is cited by Portugal Space as having substantial Earth observation experience.

name: DRFloresta
summary: Project that will develop AI algorithms from satellite, nano-satellite and drone images, with planned models for stock classes, post-fire landscape evolution and pests.

name: ECOBOTICS.SEA
summary: Project led by the Institute of Systems and Robotics, Coimbra, that aims to extend robotics for analysing and monitoring marine species communities.

name: ElectricBlue
summary: Non-profit technology transfer start-up that says it formed as a co-operative in 2018 and makes environmental monitoring and biologging tools, designed and assembled in Portugal and used worldwide.

name: EMBRC.PT
summary: Marine research programme offering access to mid and long-term observation data, analysis software and bioinformatics, including long-term benthos, plankton and fish datasets from the Mondego estuary.

name: EO4RO
summary: Project with GMV Portugal and Plymouth Marine Laboratory, funded by Cascais municipality, which Time Out reported in June 2026 as a 12-month test of predicting invasive seaweed arrivals using AI and satellite data.

name: ESTRELA - Associação para o Desenvolvimento e Gestão do Geopark e Reserva da Biosfera
summary: Association named in the Serra da Estrela UNESCO biosphere candidacy form, hosted by Manteigas municipality, for the development and management of the Geopark and Biosphere Reserve.

name: Estrutura de Missão para a Extensão da Plataforma Continental
summary: Portuguese mission structure supporting the country's UN submission on continental shelf limits, whose ROV Luso had conducted seventeen oceanographic campaigns since 2008 as of October 2024.

name: FAIA BRAVA - Associação de Conservação da Natureza
summary: Nature conservation association, formerly ATN and created in 2000, whose founder bought 30 hectares on the Côa River; the Faia Brava private reserve had grown to about 1,600 hectares by 2024.

name: FireAI
summary: Project co-financed by COMPETE 2020 to create an intelligent forest fire detection system.

name: FIRELOC
summary: A project on identifying, positioning and monitoring forest fires, aiming to let a citizen with a smartphone report a fire by sending its location and a photograph.

name: Fishmetrics
summary: An organisation that an IPMA call says is developing technology, notably through AI, to automate species identification and body measurements; it partners with the Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera.

name: Flora-On
summary: A portal of native or naturalised vascular plants of Portugal, launched 25 February 2012 and run by volunteers for the Sociedade Portuguesa de Botânica, with 781,688 occurrence records and no funding.

name: Floralens
summary: A deep learning model trained on a dataset of Portuguese native flora, presented in a paper, built by António Filgueiras and building on Flora-On.

name: Floresta Limpa
summary: A platform led by NOVA LINCS that uses AI techniques to monitor maintenance of wildfire fuel management zones.

name: Florestgal
summary: Public company that Agroportal reported in October 2022 had bought 225 hectares in Serra de São Mamede Natural Park, mainly for renaturalisation, as a first step in a strategy of buying private protected-area land.

name: foRESTER
summary: Closed project funded by the Foundation for Science and Technology and run by UNINOVA from March 2019 to January 2023, aiming to build a low-cost sensor network supporting firefighting decisions.

name: ForestSphere
summary: A project funded by Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia, running March 2025 to August 2026, that aimed to develop a digital twin combining multimodal, multi-scale sensor data for forest health and wildfire risk.

name: ForestWISE
summary: A private non-profit association for integrated forest and fire management, named in its newsletter as a collaborative laboratory, which partners with rePLANt and transForm.

name: ForModAn
summary: A start-up that the Portuguese Space Agency lists as experienced in modelling and monitoring forest growth from remotely sensed data.

name: Fundação Belmiro de Azevedo
summary: A foundation that, with a second foundation, contributes equally to annual biodiversity prizes totalling up to 500,000 euros, each worth 100,000 to 250,000 euros, for projects in Portugal.

name: Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian
summary: A foundation that launched core funding for environmental NGOs in 2025, awarding it to eight organisations, and plans a new edition of the call.

name: Fundação Gaspar Frutuoso
summary: An organisation that the Copernicus Marine page names, together with OKEANOS, as delivering AIMOS.

name: Fundação Oceano Azul
summary: A Portuguese nonprofit, as MBARI describes it, working for a healthy ocean and supporting marine protected areas; it partners with Blue Azores.

name: Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia
summary: The national public agency supporting research in science, technology and innovation, which committed 500,000 euros to the BiodivMon call and published a brochure presenting 56 selected projects.

name: Fundo Ambiental
summary: A financing instrument that the Portuguese Environment Agency calls the main one for environment and climate policy in Portugal, with calls including nature conservation under a Blue Forest programme.

name: Fundo Azul
summary: A fund whose eligible support includes digitalisation, robotics, sensors and AI applied to the blue economy, and which is also open to tech start-ups of the new sea economy.

name: GelAvista
summary: A citizen science programme, run by the Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera, for monitoring gelatinous organisms in Portuguese waters, with an app that sends sightings with a photograph.

name: GeoAtlant-AI&BI
summary: A project led by Luís Silva that aims to create a geospatial data platform for the Atlantic Islands, with the Azores as pilot, and plans to involve several partners.

name: GEOAÇORES - Associação Geoparque Açores
summary: Non-profit association based in Horta, Faial, created by public deed on 19 May 2010, whose statutes give managing the Azores Geopark as a means of its aims.

name: GEOSAT
summary: A provider of Earth observation satellite imagery and data analytics, built by CEiiA according to the links, which says it offers AI-based feature detection and supports forestry, deforestation and biodiversity work.

name: GMV Portugal
summary: An organisation whose Senior Project Manager on EO4RO, Filipe Brandão, is quoted by Time Out.

name: Governo Regional dos Açores
summary: A regional government that signed a memorandum with the Oceano Azul Foundation and the Waitt Institute on implementing the marine protected area network.

name: Greenmetrics.ai
summary: An organisation whose founders, according to Diário de Notícias, built monitoring sensors for Iberian lynx migrations before moving to urban floods.

name: Grupo Lobo
summary: A non-governmental, independent, non-profit environmental organisation founded on 18 September 1985, which supports and promotes monitoring of the wolf population.

name: HABEaS
summary: A free online geographic information system covering protected areas, threatened species, habitats and ecosystem services in mainland Portugal, built by WWF Portugal and partnered with Instituto Superior de Agronomia.

name: HydroTWIN
summary: A project launched in January 2025 by blueOASIS to detect underwater sounds for marine species monitoring, combining passive acoustic sensors, Internet-of-Things systems and AI, according to Portugal Startup News.

name: Iberion ProTech
summary: A technology company born in Portugal working on wildfire monitoring and prevention, which sells thermal cameras and sensors with AI-based smoke and heat detection.

name: InBIO Barcoding Initiative
summary: A project using next generation sequencing to build a reference collection of DNA barcodes for Iberian taxa, with BIOPOLIS and CIBIO listed by iBOL Europe as host institutes.

name: INDIMAR
summary: A project whose roadmap, presented on 21 October 2025, proposes 15 scheduled actions to 2030, led by CIIMAR with ICNF and the Portuguese bird society as partners.

name: INESC TEC
summary: A BioProtect partner building MarinEye, with work on autonomous eDNA sampling sensors reported by a researcher, within a Horizon Europe project spanning 18 partners in eight countries.

name: INOV
summary: An organisation whose CORUJA project page says it developed CICLOPE, used in Portugal, Greece and Italy, while CORUJA aims to detect rural fires at night using AI.

name: Insight Venture
summary: A venture capital firm that Portugal Startup News describes as focused on disruptive sustainable projects.

name: Institute of Systems and Robotics, University of Coimbra
summary: A University of Coimbra institute that coordinates the ECOBOTICS.SEA project.

name: Instituto da Conservação da Natureza e das Florestas
summary: Portugal's national authority for nature conservation and biodiversity, a public institute that coordinates the ENCNB 2030 strategy and runs and built the national forest inventory, whose revised strategy cites AI monitoring.

name: Instituto das Florestas e Conservação da Natureza
summary: A Funchal-based body whose 2026 plan gives its mission as nature conservation and sustainable management of biogeodiversity, landscape and forest, including protected areas and the Natura 2000 network.

name: Instituto Dom Luiz
summary: An institute that developed the CeaseFire application.

name: Instituto Nacional de Investigação Agrária e Veterinária
summary: The sole beneficiary named on the SCWM project sheet, which gives an eligible cost of 46,203.75 euros.

name: Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera
summary: A public institute responsible for the sea and atmosphere, which runs MarBIS, partners with FishMetrics, and per its GBIF record owns Portugal's most important marine biodiversity data repository.

name: Instituto Superior de Agronomia
summary: An institute hosting the Portuguese GBIF node since September 2015, whose Forest Research Centre a March 2026 article describes as pioneering drones for early pinewood nematode detection.

name: Instituto Superior Técnico
summary: University institute whose affiliated first authors are listed by OpenAlex on a 2021 review of machine learning for grassland biomass and a 2023 paper on wildfire burnt area severity from drone imagery.

name: INVASORAS.PT
summary: A citizen science listing describes it as a platform for sharing information on biological invasions.

name: Inventário Florestal Nacional
summary: Portugal's national forest inventory, run and built by ICNF, whose sixth edition drew on digital aerial photography and 2015 field surveys and reports about 70 indicators in five themes.

name: IPSentinel
summary: A platform providing Copernicus Sentinel satellite images to Portugal, which Portugal Space says is coordinated by DGT and IPMA.

name: IPSTERS
summary: Project listed among 15 approved in the Foundation for Science and Technology's 2018 data science and AI call for public administration, with UNINOVA and the Directorate-General for the Territory; it is funded by the Foundation and builds on ipsentinel.

name: K1 DIGITAL
summary: An organisation of unknown status that the Portuguese Space Agency lists as based on an Earth observation AI platform.

name: Leitek Innovative Solutions
summary: A company founded in 2016 and based at the DNA Cascais business centre, which says it makes extensive use of AI and machine learning, including in Dronesavior and SafeForest.

name: LIFE Aegypius Return
summary: A project aiming to consolidate and expand the black vulture population in Portugal and western Spain, led by the Vulture Conservation Foundation with a named partner organisation.

name: LIFE LxAquila
summary: Project run by SPEA with Loures and other partners, co-financed by the EU's LIFE programme, which Loures said in August 2024 had carried out study and conservation actions, including camera traps at feeding points for prey species.

name: LIFE Pterodromas4Future
summary: A project led by the Instituto das Florestas e Conservação da Natureza, whose project period a volunteer blog reported as October 2021 to September 2026.

name: LIFE WolFlux
summary: A project led by Rewilding Portugal, with an end date of 30 November 2024 in the EU LIFE database, that worked on wolf monitoring south of the Douro.

name: LifeWatch Portugal
summary: A programme managed by PORBIOTA that joined LifeWatch ERIC in 2019 and is dedicated to organising and sharing environmental and biodiversity data.

name: Liga para a Proteção da Natureza
summary: An organisation that has developed the Castro Verde Sustentável programme since 1993 and lists population monitoring among the field activities on its LIFE Eurobustard page.

name: LTER Portugal
summary: Monitors and collects ecological and socio-ecological data as a network objective, with SPECO involved in its origins and PORBIOTA reporting access to four long-term ecological research sites.

name: LTsER Baixo Sabor
summary: Long-term socio-ecological research site that describes microclimate weather stations and water monitoring in the Sabor river and reservoirs, with a fish occurrence dataset for 2012 to 2020 reported by eLTER as available in DEIMS.

name: LTsER Estuaries
summary: Long-term socio-ecological research site covering the Minho, Mondego and Mira estuaries, listing multi-year Mondego community monitoring and Mira water and tagged-animal monitoring through CoastNet, which it uses.

name: Lusoborboletas
summary: A dataset created to help identify Portugal's butterfly species, relying on contributed photographs.

name: M@rBis
summary: A system for collecting, processing and disseminating marine biodiversity information, run by IPMA, with EMEPC saying its campaigns collected information for it.

name: MACOI - Portuguese Seaweeds
summary: A website on seaweeds found along the Portuguese shoreline, cited by MarineInfo as edited by Leonel Pereira, Nuno Dias and Rui Gaspar in 2005.

name: MARDIVE
summary: An association whose aims include marine research and conservation, listing diving monitoring, BRUVS, intertidal survey, environmental DNA and drone coastal mapping among its services and projects.

name: MARE - Marine and Environmental Sciences Centre
summary: A centre studying aquatic ecosystems and aiming to share scientific data; a March 2024 release named MARE-Madeira researchers among developers of sensor and embedded AI solutions.

name: MARE-Madeira
summary: An organisation where students collect data and apply AI to classification, animal behaviour and migratory patterns, and, with the University of Madeira, can design and build sensors.

name: MarinEye
summary: A multitrophic ocean monitoring prototype led by CIIMAR, under development with IPMA involvement in a document that said the project would end in April 2017.

name: MAYOMBIOAPES
summary: A FCT-funded study of primate biodiversity in a tropical forest using autonomous recordings and AI, with recordings to be uploaded for processing through a neural network pipeline.

name: MED - Mediterranean Institute for Agriculture, Environment and Development
summary: An institute that includes the LABscape research team at the University of Évora and holds the soundClass paper in its section of the Évora repository.

name: Ministério do Ambiente e Energia
summary: A ministry whose XXIV Government mission covered environment, water, nature conservation, biodiversity and energy policy, with Maria da Graça Carvalho as minister in the XXV Government.

name: MONTIS - Association for Nature Management and Conservation
summary: Nature management and conservation association that a 2024 crowdfunding page said then managed around 300 hectares, of which 17.3 hectares were owned by it.

name: Município da Golegã
summary: Municipality that, Agroportal reported on the 2021 protocol, now co-manages Paul do Boquilobo Nature Reserve with Torres Novas and a group of entities, after ICNF managed it.

name: Município de Arcos de Valdevez
summary: Municipality whose mayor, Agroportal reported in March 2021, was appointed by order to chair the seven-member Peneda-Gerês National Park co-management commission for four years from 3 March 2021.

name: Município de Aveiro
summary: Municipality that a government news item of 28 August 2020 says signed protocols with the Fundo Ambiental and ICNF for co-management of the Dunas de São Jacinto Nature Reserve.

name: Município de Castelo Branco
summary: Municipality that a government news item of April 2017 said would join the pilot collaborative-management project for Tejo Internacional Natural Park, bringing municipalities into park management with ICNF.

name: Município de Castro Marim
summary: Municipality whose mayor, with Vila Real de Santo António's, asked ICNF in May 2021, Barlavento reports, to adopt the co-management model for the Sapal de Castro Marim e VRSA Nature Reserve.

name: Município de Castro Verde
summary: Municipality that LPN's history page says sits on the management board of the Castro Verde UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, classified on 14 June 2017.

name: Município de Esposende
summary: Municipality that Agroportal reported in September 2020 signed a protocol with the Fundo Ambiental and ICNF for Litoral Norte Natural Park co-management, to be carried out by a commission including it.

name: Município de Idanha-a-Nova
summary: Portuguese municipality that a government news item of 18 April 2017 said would take part in a pilot collaborative-management project for the Tejo Internacional Natural Park, with ICNF.

name: Município de Manteigas
summary: Portuguese municipality whose mayor, according to Agroportal on 2 April 2024, chaired the co-management commission of the Serra da Estrela Natural Park.

name: Município de Mogadouro
summary: Portuguese municipality whose mayor, Agroportal reported on 11 May 2023, led the co-management model for the Douro Internacional Natural Park, which covers more than 86,000 hectares.

name: Município de Torres Novas
summary: Portuguese municipality that, according to Agroportal's report of a 2021 protocol, now co-manages the Paul do Boquilobo Nature Reserve with Golegã and other entities, after ICNF managed it.

name: Município de Vila Real de Santo António
summary: Portuguese municipality whose mayor, with Castro Marim's, asked ICNF in May 2021 to adopt the co-management model for the Sapal de Castro Marim e VRSA Nature Reserve, Barlavento reports.

name: Município de Vila Velha de Ródão
summary: Portuguese municipality that a government news item of 18 April 2017 said would take part in a pilot collaborative-management project for the Tejo Internacional Natural Park, with ICNF.

name: Naturdata
summary: A dataset built and run by Circunforce that stores and offers information on more than 35,000 species occurring in Portugal.

name: NatureOS
summary: An active project that combines geospatial data, AI agents, expert workflows, carbon estimations, project data rooms and MRV tools.

name: Naturtejo EIM
summary: Intermunicipal company with mostly public capital, set up by member municipalities, which Naturtejo's own page says runs the Naturtejo Geopark.

name: NOVA Information Management School
summary: School whose research centre MagIC is named as its research centre, and which is said to have used satellite imagery and machine learning to produce land cover maps for foRESTER.

name: NOVA LINCS
summary: An active organisation whose researchers led the Floresta Limpa project.

name: NOVA University Lisbon
summary: University whose NOVA FCT researchers lead Floresta Limpa, which uses artificial intelligence to monitor wildfire fuel management zones, and whose affiliated first authors appear in OpenAlex on satellite machine learning and land cover papers.

name: Observatório Golfinhos no Tejo
summary: An active project built by WWF Portugal, with MARE as partner, which the Port of Lisbon calls the first land-based cetacean monitoring programme in the Tagus estuary.

name: Observatório Oceânico da Madeira
summary: A closed project built on four thematic pillars, including biodiversity and remote detection and tracking.

name: Ocean Alive
summary: An organisation mapping Sado estuary seagrass since 2019, reporting 35.62 hectares gained across nine consistently monitored meadows over the four years preceding its 2023/2024 mapping report.

name: OceanPulse Network
summary: A proposed coastal monitoring system of smart buoys using LoRa, described by itself as scalable and real-time, with one prototype buoy tested for short durations.

name: OKEANOS
summary: A marine sciences research unit at Horta, on Faial Island, which says it hosts more than 150 members and develops new technologies for research.

name: Palombar
summary: An active organisation that runs Sentinelas, developed with the University of Oviedo's biodiversity institute, and is named with Dear Wolf in the national census report for the North-East lot.

name: Parques de Sintra - Monte da Lua, S.A.
summary: Company whose mission page says it manages the natural and cultural values of the Sintra Cultural Landscape, and which Agroportal in June 2021 called manager of the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park.

name: Polytechnic Institute of Viana do Castelo
summary: Polytechnic that SeverusPT says forms its core development team with BIOPOLIS/CIBIO, and which is said to have coordinated or joined remote sensing, image processing, spatial modelling and WebGIS projects.

name: PORBIOTA
summary: A programme led by Biopolis-CIBIO that stores, organises and shares biodiversity and environmental data, manages LifeWatch Portugal, and is listed in the national research infrastructure roadmap.

name: Portal de Dados de Biodiversidade de Portugal
summary: A dataset run by GBIF Portugal that contains all records published by Portuguese institutions and records on Portugal from foreign institutions.

name: Portugal Ventures
summary: An active organisation that blueOASIS says invested in it.

name: Portuguese Node of GBIF
summary: Hosted by Instituto Superior de Agronomia since September 2015, it runs the Portuguese biodiversity data portal, offers GBIF publishing training and uses the GBIF Integrated Publishing Toolkit.

name: Portuguese Space Agency
summary: A government-created agency implementing the national space strategy, Portugal Space 2030, whose stated aims include expanding Copernicus data use and a national soil occupation monitoring programme.

name: Projeto Guarda-Rios
summary: A project, built by Grupo Ribadouro, using open-source technology for real-time citizen science monitoring of freshwater, with data free and open on its portal.

name: Quercus - Associação Nacional de Conservação da Natureza
summary: Nature conservation association that a 2017 crowdfunding page says owns and manages 430 ha in the Tejo Internacional area, and which was to join a 2017 pilot collaborative-management project there.

name: RAIZ - Instituto de Investigação da Floresta e Papel
summary: A private non-profit research centre funded by The Navigator Company, whose forest technology area explores remote sensing with drones, satellites and LIDAR.

name: RAMO Earth
summary: A Lisbon-based company that describes itself as a nature intelligence company, uses NatureOS, and says its platform has supported more than 400 projects globally with 20 enterprise partners.

name: Rede de Estações de Borboletas Noturnas
summary: A citizen science programme that aims at long-term monitoring of nocturnal butterflies using a standard protocol.

name: REDUCE
summary: A project whose PhD posting says the post focuses on optimising electronic monitoring systems to reduce bycatch, including developing machine learning models.

name: rePLANt
summary: A project that ForestWISE's newsletter says was led by The Navigator Company and is a collaboration between academic institutions and companies.

name: Rewilding Portugal
summary: A Portuguese non-profit working on nature restoration through rewilding, active in the Greater Côa Valley since 2019, with camera trap monitoring of roe deer reported in 2020 and a volunteer fire monitoring programme opened in 2023.

name: RI Forestry Intelligence
summary: A geospatial intelligence company that says it monitors millions of hectares of forest using satellite images and AI algorithms, and partners with Transform Agenda.

name: SAT-RAMPA Açores
summary: Planned for 2026 to 2028, this project led by Ana Martins aims to develop and run integrated regional monitoring infrastructure for the Azores marine protected area network.

name: Sciaena
summary: An NGO that promotes a healthy marine environment and partners with Fish-X.

name: Sentinelas
summary: A project started in 2019, run by Palombar and funded by Fundo Ambiental, to build a network monitoring illegal persecution of wild animals by GPS tagging sentinel bird and mammal species.

name: SeverusPT
summary: A closed three-year project from 2021, led by CIBIO-InBIO and funded by the Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia, that aimed to use satellite and field data to evaluate and predict fire severity.

name: Sistema de monitorização de linces para condutores
summary: A system that ICNF was reported in March 2024 to be developing, to alert drivers almost in real time to nearby Iberian lynx and avoid road deaths in Alentejo and the Algarve.

name: Sistema de Monitorização de Ocupação do Solo
summary: A programme built and run by the Direção-Geral do Território that applies AI to Sentinel-2 images to map land cover across mainland Portugal, with products free to the public through SNIG.

name: Sistema Nacional de Informação de Recursos Hídricos
summary: A dataset run by the Agência Portuguesa do Ambiente that processes, validates and publishes water monitoring data, including from the Azores and Madeira, through a public portal.

name: Sistema Nacional de Informação Geográfica
summary: A national geographic information dataset run by the Direção-Geral do Território, which Copernicus Portugal says is responsible for reference geographic databases including it.

name: Smart Conservation and Wildlife Monitoring
summary: A project that aimed to build digital solutions for monitoring game and wild fauna using AI, georeferencing and real-time data collection, with a planned finish of 31 March 2026.

name: Sociedade Portuguesa de Botânica
summary: A botanical society created in January 2009 that runs the Flora-On portal, which its 2024 report says was first applied to one municipality, Alenquer.

name: Sociedade Portuguesa para o Estudo das Aves
summary: A bird society that runs the Common Bird Census and whose 2025 report says the Arenaria project monitored wintering coastal birds with 72 volunteers.

name: soundClass
summary: An active machine learning tool for biodiversity monitoring, built by Bruno Silva, that trains convolutional neural networks to classify sound events in recordings.

name: STRIX
summary: An organisation that builds Digital ESAS and describes BIRDTRACK as a radar solution to avoid bird deaths at wind farms.

name: Tagis - Centro de Conservação das Borboletas de Portugal
summary: A butterfly conservation NGO since 2005, and a private entity of public benefit since 2010, that runs the Censos Borboletas de Portugal and is said to coordinate butterfly monitoring in Portugal.

name: Tekever
summary: A Portugal-based company that AltaSea describes as supplying drones for maritime surveillance, fisheries inspection and pollution monitoring, using machine learning, AI and satellite systems.

name: terraDrone
summary: A Portuguese company founded in 2014 that collects geospatial information, including on stands of protected species and forest inventories.

name: Tesselo
summary: Company that, according to its own site, has ended after 7 years; Observador reported in 2019 it was founded in 2017 in Lisbon and used AI on Sentinel-2 images for forest mapping.

name: The Navigator Company
summary: Active company on whose properties in Castelo Branco and Santarém a 2020–2021 CE3C and CESAM project aimed to assess biodiversity, and which RAIZ says mainly finances its activities.

name: transForm
summary: Programme of unknown status, led by Altri Florestal with 56 partners and technical and scientific coordination by ForestWISE.

name: UNINOVA
summary: Research institute named by DGT in connection with foRESTER, which ran from March 2019 to January 2023 and has concluded.

name: Universidade dos Açores
summary: Active university in Ponta Delgada that its GBIF record calls the only public university in the Azores, and which hosts the Azores Bioportal.

name: University of Aveiro
summary: Active university listed by B-Cubed as a partner and by Specify as a member at Aveiro, with a GBIF publisher address on the Santiago campus.

name: University of Coimbra
summary: Active university listed by CETAF as a member, whose herbarium holds about 800,000 specimens according to its GBIF record.

name: University of Lisbon
summary: Active university listed as a Portuguese partner in the DiSSCo Transition project (2023–25) and as a CETAF member, and named by the University of East Anglia among those behind Movetech.

name: University of Madeira
summary: Active university whose researchers, a March 2024 EurekAlert release said, had joined the University of Helsinki group to develop sensor and embedded AI solutions using whale-watching data from Madeira.

name: University of Minho
summary: University whose affiliated first authors are listed by OpenAlex on a 2023 machine learning paper mapping large wildfires in north-west Portugal and a 2024 review of biosensors for non-native freshwater species.

name: University of Porto
summary: Active university listed by CETAF as a member, whose natural history and science museum is a GBIF publisher.

name: University of the Algarve
summary: University that is the main host of CCMAR, whose Biodiversity Data Science group says it uses machine learning and AI, and whose affiliated author is listed on a 2020 paper on acoustic target detection.

name: University of Trás-os-Montes and Alto Douro
summary: University whose affiliated first authors are listed by OpenAlex on a 2024 machine learning paper on forest fire risk and a 2023 paper using pre-fire LiDAR to predict fire severity in central Portugal.

name: University of Évora
summary: University hosting MED, of which LABscape says it is part, with OpenAlex listing a 2023 machine learning paper on vegetation fuel in southern Portugal and a 2025 abstract on ICESat-2 fuel variables.

name: WWF Portugal
summary: Active organisation that, according to its map site, has restored more than 300 hectares of habitats and created the Tagus dolphin observatory, and which builds Habeas.

name: A New Tool to Monitor the Resilience of Mangroves to Sea Level Rise
summary: Active project with Rob Chancia as principal investigator, taking surface elevation table measurements at 30 Babeldaob locations and running a web application that turns iPhone LiDAR scans into elevation change estimates.

name: Babeldaob Island wildfires (2012+)
summary: Dataset of wildfire locations and repeat-fire areas on Babeldaob Island, Palau, for 2012 to 2025, mapped from satellite imagery only from 2016; third edition published in 2026 in the Forest Service archive.

name: Behavioural observations and habitat use of dugongs in the Rock Islands Southern Lagoon
summary: Project, funded by the GEF Small Grants Programme and run by the Coral Reef Research Foundation, using drones and underwater time-lapse cameras to study dugong distribution, behaviour and group composition around the Ngederrak Conservation Area.

name: Belau National Museum
summary: Non-profit museum governed by a board of trustees since 1973, which houses the National Bird Monitoring Program and has distributed the annual State of Palau's Birds report, the 12th edition in April 2023.

name: Beyond the Blue: Palau Mapping
summary: Completed NOAA mapping with PICRC in Palau in 2025 collected 752 eDNA samples across three expeditions and preceding transit; data will go to Palau’s government and PICRC.

name: Coral Reef Research Foundation
summary: In Koror, it describes itself as a US 501(c)(3) and chartered Palauan non-profit, monitors environmental change, hosts temperature and specimen archives, and mapped mangroves using 2021 airborne LiDAR.

name: Ebiil Society
summary: Nonprofit partner described by Seacology in 2019 as monitoring Ngerkeklau plants, dugongs and birds; IUCN says it delivered 8,000 sea cucumbers to 49 participants.

name: Helen Reef Resource Management Program
summary: Programme established in 2000 by the Hatohobei people and partners, overseen by the Helen Reef Management Board, which developed monitoring of marine resources and ecological and socio-economic outcomes.

name: Helen Reef turtle monitoring and tagging program
summary: According to OneReef, rangers began turtle monitoring and tagging on Helen Reef 16 years before its article; upwards of one hundred nesting turtles were recorded in 2019.

name: Jellyfish Lake Conditions and Forecast
summary: Active CRRF programme publishing a three-month forecast for Jellyfish Lake from conditions, jellyfish numbers and weather forecasts; PI-CASC said in August 2024 that CRRF had monitored monthly since 1999.

name: Koror State Department of Conservation and Law Enforcement
summary: Koror State department responsible for surveying and monitoring terrestrial and marine ecosystems, which Island Conservation reports led Ulong Island monitoring that produced over 30,000 hours of acoustic recordings and 11 terabytes of seafloor imagery.

name: Lebuu's Voyage
summary: Closed expedition led by Ocean Exploration Trust and funded by NOAA, with PICRC as partner; Leg I ran 29 October to 8 November 2024, gathering seafloor mapping data and exploring deep-sea habitats.

name: Marine Habitat Mapping Project (Coral Reef Research Foundation)
summary: Active CRRF project to delineate all habitats from the shoreline to 100 metres deep; mangroves were among the first completed, derived from a LiDAR ground elevation model and ground truthed with drones and field observation.

name: Melekeok Conservation Network
summary: Conservation network supported through a 2021 MOU signed by Melekeok State's governor with the Coral Reef Research Foundation for staff training and a planned ForestGEO resurvey.

name: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and the Environment (Palau)
summary: Palau ministry whose Bureau of Environment published the Forest Action Plan, which sets its forestry division the goal of developing a National Forest Monitoring Program.

name: Palau Automated Land and Resource Information System
summary: UNDP quotes its Senior GIS Analyst describing a mandate to provide national spatial data services to government agencies; the Forest Action Plan uses its vegetation maps.

name: Palau Conservation Society
summary: Community-based organisation in Koror, established in June 1994 as Palau's first environmental NGO, which publishes the Palau Invasives marine species dataset on GBIF and had nine staff in October 2025.

name: Palau eDNA Project
summary: A project building a long-term ecological monitoring protocol for the Palau National Marine Sanctuary, collecting eDNA at 32 sites since 2021 and, the team says, developing a machine-learning identification model.

name: Palau International Coral Reef Center
summary: Established as a non-profit public corporation wholly owned by Palau’s National Government, it uses ReefCloud and, Island Times reports, has monitored Palau’s reefs since 2001.

name: Palau Marine Mammal Research and Capacity Building Project
summary: Proposed SeaKeepers project, with an expected time frame of October to December 2026, planning ship-based visual and acoustic surveys of cetaceans in the sanctuary and building local monitoring expertise.

name: Palau Marine Turtle Conservation and Monitoring Program
summary: Nation-wide programme begun in September 2004, within the Bureau of Marine Resources, covering nesting beach monitoring, flipper tagging, satellite tracking and foraging surveys, with telemetry data published in OBIS-SEAMAP in 2024.

name: Palau National Bird Monitoring Program
summary: Housed at Belau National Museum according to Island Times, the programme features in the 12th annual bird report (2021); Ngardmau rangers trained using its protocol.

name: Palau National Forest Monitoring Program
summary: A long-term programme to detect trends in forest cover, begun in 2019 by the PAN Office and Bureau of Agriculture, with plot surveys complete at 6 of 8 PAN sites when the plan was written.

name: Palau Protected Areas Network Fund
summary: It describes itself as an independent non-profit financial trustee for the Protected Areas Network, is based in Koror, and funded marine monitoring training for twelve PAN employees in 2019.

name: PICRC long-term coral reef monitoring
summary: A PICRC-run coral reef monitoring programme running since 2001, whose 2024 surveys covered 31 sites using photo quadrats and stereo-video, led by Victor Nestor, in partnership with The Nature Conservancy.

name: Predicting and managing the future of Ongeim'l Tketau (Jellyfish Lake), Palau in a changing climate
summary: Project with unknown status, led by the University of Guam and CRRF and funded by USGS, awarded about $240,000 in August 2024 to restore monthly lake monitoring and create a forecast tool for Koror State managers.

name: Preventing the Spread of Crab-Eating Macaques in the Republic of Palau
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, January to July 2009, with the Palau Conservation Society as grantee, which planned a nationwide census of crab-eating macaques to find their number and locations.

name: Project for Enhancement of Integrated Management of Coastal Ecosystem in Palau for Strengthening their Resilience to Climate Change
summary: Closed three-year project, February 2022 to February 2025, led by PICRC with JICA and the environment ministry, which set up two mangrove monitoring stations and produced a monitoring protocol for state rangers.

name: Protected Areas Network Office (Palau)
summary: The Forest Action Plan describes a coordinated plan with site managers and rangers; PAN Fund describes its collaboration on the Investment Partnership Program for PAN sites.

name: Restoring Sonsorol
summary: Active Island Conservation project, in partnership with SPREP, with baseline surveys of birds, crabs and vegetation and seabird nest surveys reported in September 2026; Island Conservation says the UK FCDO and New Zealand's foreign ministry fund it.

name: Strengthening the Palau National Marine Sanctuary for the Conservation and Management of Global Marine Biodiversity and Sustainable Fisheries
summary: Closed GEF-funded project, run by PICRC and the environment ministry, that UNDP reported in June 2025 had concluded after four years and $1.8 million, including cetacean monitoring that observed 465 cetaceans of 10 species.

name: Turning the Tide for the Bekai: Identifying Refugee from Climate-Induced Sea Level Rise for the Palau Megapode
summary: Closed Rufford Foundation project, dated 21 September 2015, under Robert Davis, that planned radio-tracking, genetic studies and remote cameras to assess Micronesian Megapode population, predation risk and sea level rise effects in Palau.

name: Ulong Island restoration monitoring
summary: Island Conservation reports collecting 528,310 camera-trap images and 14,796 recording hours on Ulong Island over three years, with Conservation Metrics analysing acoustic calls using a neural network.

name: A Range-Wide Survey to Determine the Current Distribution and Population Status of the Chacoan Peccary in the Paraguayan Chaco
summary: Closed Chacoan peccary survey at Fortín Toledo, documented in 2012, intended to produce distribution maps; a January 2013 update reported coverage of most central and northern Chaco.

name: Actualización de las ecorregiones del Paraguay
summary: Project to update Paraguay's ecoregions, in which UNDP reported on 29 June 2026 that MADES had completed a national field verification to support a more precise ecoregional classification.

name: Agencia Espacial del Paraguay
summary: Paraguayan space agency which, per a JICA completion report, provides space systems and satellite data, supplied forest-fire information by satellite as of August 2025, and cooperated on GuaraniSat-1, released from the ISS in 2021.

name: Atenil S.A.
summary: Private-sector organisation in Asunción whose Chaco Vivo REDD+ project runs biodiversity monitoring including camera trapping and field surveys, and which expects to publish camera-trap records with coordinates generalised to protect sensitive species.

name: Averting Protected Area Failure: Mammalian Responses to Human Pressures in the Dry Chaco
summary: Closed research project, dated 19 April 2023 and set in Defensores del Chaco National Park, aiming to fill the gap in estimates of hunting extent and intensity in protected areas, with a final evaluation report of February 2025.

name: Birds under Attack: Impacts of Habitat Loss and Fragmentation in the Chaco
summary: Closed Rufford-funded project proposing acoustic recording in 2019 to assess habitat loss and fragmentation effects on Paraguayan Chaco birds; the report says Covid-19 extended the grant to two years.

name: Centro Chaqueño para la Conservación e Investigación
summary: Non-profit association in the Paraguayan Chaco, formed in 2010 according to ABC Color, which La Nación reported in May 2026 has bred 70 Chacoan peccaries and tracked tapirs with GPS collars and camera traps.

name: Ecological Study of the White-Winged Nightjar (Eleothreptus candicans)
summary: Closed Rufford-funded study, proposed in 2013 at Reserva Natural Laguna Blanca, that planned year-round bird monitoring and used radio-trackers to gather data on the white-winged nightjar.

name: Ecology and Conservation of the Nocturnal Species Eleothreptus anomalus (Yvyja'u tuju) Through Acoustic Monitoring in the Wetlands of Ñeembucú, Paraguay
summary: Closed project, described in June 2024, that planned passive acoustic monitoring with automatic recorders to study density, habitat and vocal behaviour of a nocturnal bird in Ñeembucú wetlands, with a final evaluation dated July 2025.

name: Estación Biológica Tres Gigantes
summary: Biological station run by Guyra Paraguay, where in September 2019 five forest rangers monitored wildlife and obtained about ten visual records from camera traps installed after the fires.

name: Facultad de Ciencias Agrarias, Universidad Nacional de Asunción
summary: University faculty whose permanent biodiversity monitoring plot network collected forest data across Paraguay; La Nación reported in June 2021 that six new plots were installed and data from 27 plots digitised under a REDD+ carbon project with Japan's FFPRI.

name: Fundación Moisés Bertoni
summary: Paraguayan non-profit created in 1988 for conservation and sustainable development, with camera-trap records of jaguars and breeding in Mbaracayú forest reserve reported by La Nación in December 2021.

name: Fundación Para La Tierra
summary: Research station in Pilar, Ñeembucú, founded in 2010, which describes itself as the only year-round scientific research station in Paraguay, runs long-term wetland projects, and is funded by the Rufford Foundation.

name: Guyra Paraguay
summary: Paraguayan non-profit protecting biodiversity, reported in September 2020 to have launched an AI-based Gran Chaco deforestation tracker, and listed among affiliations on a 2023 camera-trap jaguar density paper.

name: Guyra Paraguay automated deforestation monitoring system for the Gran Chaco
summary: AI-based system reported in September 2020 that automatically compared satellite images with public permit information to identify illegal deforestation in the Gran Chaco, with data said to have led to two lawsuits.

name: Instituto Forestal Nacional (Paraguay)
summary: Paraguay's forest institute, INFONA, described as responsible for national forest policy, which adopted more robust mapping algorithms and field methods that strengthened its early warning system for deforestation and land-use change.

name: Inventario Forestal Nacional (Paraguay)
summary: Active national forest inventory, run by the national forest institute, that UN-REDD Paraguay lists as a programme activity; La Nación reported a first cycle in 2014 to 2016 and results presented in April 2026.

name: Jaguars in Paraguay
summary: Camera-trap project on a private Guyra Paraguay reserve, funded by PTES and described as the first comprehensive jaguar study in Paraguay, also covering pumas, ocelots and tapirs; its funding has finished.

name: MapBiomas Fuego Paraguay
summary: Fire-scar mapping dataset built from satellite imagery, whose Collection 1 shows 31.75 percent of Paraguay burned at least once between 1999 and 2024, with data made available to the public.

name: MapBiomas Paraguay
summary: Active land cover mapping programme led by WWF Paraguay and Guyra Paraguay, using Google Earth Engine, whose Collection 2 methods document describes random forest classification and Landsat imagery.

name: Ministerio del Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible (Paraguay)
summary: Paraguay's environment ministry, which in June 2026 was reported to have driven SMART training for Chaco park rangers with WWF-Paraguay and UNDP support, and which leads the 2025 to 2030 biodiversity strategy.

name: Monitoreo del patrimonio Natural Cultural Totobiegosode (PNCAT) con uso de geo-tecnología
