summary: Active project which Mongabay reported in 2022 had begun in 2017, with Ayoreo-managed satellite and drone monitoring covering about 100,000 hectares of Chaidi community territory.

name: Paisajes sonoros de la Reserva Natural Tapyta (monitoreo acústico pasivo de aves y anfibios)
summary: Run by Fundación Moisés Bertoni at Tapyta, the project reported over 200 sites sampled, 20 TB recorded and manual labelling to train a classification algorithm in August 2025.

name: Portal de Bosques y Usos de la Tierra
summary: Portal launched by INFONA with data on native forest, crops, plantations and land-use change, generated and validated from Landsat, Sentinel and Planet imagery, with over 25,000 visits across INFONA's two portals in under a year.

name: Portal de Manejo Integral del Fuego
summary: Free fire portal and forest fire monitoring viewer, officially launched in July 2025 and available on INFONA's website, giving data on heat points, active fires, fire risk, burned areas and weather.

name: Red de Parcelas Permanentes de Monitoreo de la Biodiversidad
summary: Forest monitoring programme run by the agrarian sciences faculty and funded by Missouri Botanical Garden; La Nación reported in June 2021 that 43 plots in three ecoregions held tagged, georeferenced trees, with 19,787 trees analysed from 40 plots measured since 2001.

name: Saving the Hooded Capuchin through Restoration and Conservation of the Upper Paraná Atlantic Forest in Eastern Paraguay
summary: Closed project, dated March 2023 at Alto Vera and led by Rebecca Smith with Rufford as partner, whose final evaluation report says a camera-trap survey of the Nueva Gambach property recorded 20 species.

name: Sistema de Alertas Tempranas por cambios de uso de la tierra ilegal en bosques nativos
summary: Active early warning system for illegal land-use change in native forests, built and run by the national forest institute, launched in November 2023; La Nación reported its reports rose 47% between 2023 and 2024.

name: The Hooded Capuchins Last Chance: Restoring the Atlantic Forest and Inspiring Conservation Heroes
summary: Active project, dated 10 May 2025 and funded by the Rufford Foundation, that plans camera-trap monitoring of its impact at San Rafael; its December 2025 update reports 5,733 camera-trap nights in Nueva Gambach.

name: Un esquema transfronterizo de monitoreo de biodiversidad y agua en áreas protegidas y corredores (especie clave: Lama guanicoe)
summary: Project of unknown status, run by Guyra Paraguay and Fundación Natura Bolivia, which Última Hora reported in May 2019 had installed 22 camera traps, centred on the guanaco, having begun the previous year.

name: WCS Paraguay
summary: With partner Fundación Moisés Bertoni, began camera-trap research on northern Chaco big cats and ranches in May 2012; named executing agency for the ÑANDE CHACO jaguar project.

name: WWF Paraguay
summary: Its GIS laboratory monitored Eastern Region forests from the Zero Deforestation law’s implementation; it reported protected-area forest loss by satellite and supported SMART training in June 2026.

name: Arabian oryx genome draft assembly, Version 1.0
summary: A WCM-Q-built Arabian oryx genome draft, Version 1.0, dated 3 June 2012, reports about one million SNPs between parental alleles; publishing whole-genome analyses requires providers' consent.

name: Carnegie Mellon University in Qatar
summary: A Qatari university campus partnered with Qatar Foundation since 2004, whose professor reportedly used AI and autonomous marine robots in April 2021 for QNRF-funded marine monitoring.

name: Centre for Geographic Information Systems (Qatar)
summary: Qatar's Ministry of Municipality GIS centre, which the ministry says has run the country's GIS work since 1990, set up an aerial survey system and supplies government bodies with geographic databases and imagery through the National GISNet.

name: Department of Wildlife Development
summary: Ministry-run Qatari wildlife department that held a 2022 biodiversity database workshop with UNEP, aimed at a digital approved species list, and was said in 2026 to have led whale shark research since 2010.

name: Dugong population study in Qatari waters, 2023 to 2026
summary: The closed ministry-run study used aerial surveys and drones to identify dugongs by markings, with the ministry reporting 224 animals, including 27 calves, during 2023 to 2026.

name: Environmental Science Center, Qatar University
summary: Monitored turtle nesting in 2021 within a 19-year-old protection project, tracked turtles, and is the first author’s affiliation on a 2026 mangrove satellite imaging paper.

name: Hawksbill Sea Turtle Protection Project
summary: Ministry-run turtle protection project launched in 2003 with QatarEnergy and Qatar University's Environmental Science Center, reported in 2025 to use environmental data, tagging, DNA sampling and satellite tracking, with 2026 beach monitoring patrols.

name: Marine Protection Department
summary: Conducts marine environment assessments, with a new ministry vessel reported in May 2026 to support sample collection and monitoring of red tides and fish die-offs.

name: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (Qatar)
summary: QNA’s 2026 reports describe its geographic database of around 1,500 rawdas, reported use of GIS, aerial imagery and drones to detect violations, and remotely operated marine sampling boat.

name: National project for the protection and restoration of coral reefs (Qatar)
summary: Qatari national coral project run by the environment ministry, which reported surveys of Qatari waters from 2024 to 2026 recording 49 coral species at 22 sites, and includes coral transplantation and reef rehabilitation.

name: Qatar National Biodiversity Database
summary: A biodiversity database project run by Qatar's environment ministry with UNEP, planned to hold species lists and distribution maps, with a June 2025 launch reported by the University of Doha for Science and Technology.

name: Qatar University
summary: Its Environmental Science Center began monitoring sea turtle nesting on Qatar’s coasts and islands for the 2021 season, according to a May 2021 report.

name: Qatar Whale Shark Research
summary: Whale shark research project begun in 2010 by Qatar's environment ministry and David Robinson, using satellite trackers, photographs and DNA samples, with more than 600 individuals recorded after eight seasons.

name: Smart Observer marine monitoring boat (Qatar)
summary: A marine monitoring boat built and run by Qatar's environment ministry, which uses remote operation and sensing to collect data automatically; the ministry reported in August 2026 that its pilot succeeded and expansion was under way.

name: Teams of Aquatic/Aerial Robots for Marine Environment Monitoring (TARMEM)
summary: Project that CMU reported in April 2021 was using AI to coordinate small aerial and marine robots to gather marine data over large areas, with validation and outdoor testing planned next.

name: Weill Cornell Medicine - Qatar
summary: A research-intensive academic medical institution, a joint venture of Qatar Foundation and Cornell University, whose site offers the 2012 Arabian oryx genome draft assembly and SNP data for oryx breeding.

name: Borbonica
summary: Data platform that is the SINP of La Réunion, where a government procedure page says access requests are now made in the application, after the separate form closed on 6 November 2026.

name: Centre d'Étude et de Découverte des Tortues Marines
summary: Association based in Saint-Leu, La Réunion, coordinator for La Réunion of the 2015–2020 south-west Indian Ocean marine turtle action plan, with national council opinions on its hawksbill and Europa green turtle projects.

name: Conservatoire botanique national de Mascarin
summary: Botanical conservatory in Saint-Leu, La Réunion, with association status; a July 2025 opinion covers its accreditation for La Réunion, Mayotte and the Îles Éparses and says it is to join the Lobelia data system.

name: GIE MAREX
summary: Saint-Leu company that won the January 2024 contract to monitor hard-substrate benthos on the outer reef slopes of La Réunion, and is credited with photographs in a December 2024 Office de l'eau newsletter.

name: MesoRun
summary: Closed project, run by Vie Océane, that aimed to inventory fauna of the mesophotic zone around La Réunion, with 50,000 euros for 14 months under the first LIFE4BEST call.

name: Nature Océan Indien
summary: Association in Petite-Île, La Réunion, that launched a photo-identification capture-mark-recapture programme in 2015 for two Manapany green gecko populations in natural habitat.

name: OCEA Consult
summary: La Réunion company named in an August 2023 EU award notice as a contractor, within a group of operators, for lot 1, covering fish and macrocrustacean monitoring in the island's rivers.

name: Office de l'eau Réunion
summary: Public water body for La Réunion that, as contracting authority, tendered and awarded river and reef monitoring contracts in 2021 to 2024, and reports a 2024 reef campaign at 18 stations.

name: Parc national de La Réunion
summary: National park whose scientific council, in a 19 January 2026 opinion citing the 2007 creating decree, said a project collecting native species in its core, BIOSCAN-FR insect monitoring, needs park authorisation.

name: Programme de suivi de la dynamique et écologie en mer des pétrels endémiques de La Réunion par baguage
summary: Programme monitoring the at-sea dynamics and ecology of La Réunion's endemic petrels by ringing, located in the national park's core, which received a favourable scientific council opinion in November 2025.

name: PVBMT Research Unit
summary: Research unit in Saint-Pierre, Réunion, formed from University of Réunion and CIRAD teams, with four datasets on GBIF and a 2025 paper on predicting invasive plant spread.

name: SAGAP
summary: Project run by Reef Pulse, listed among its La Réunion projects, that monitors the outer reef slope of La Réunion over two years.

name: Société d'Études Ornithologiques de La Réunion
summary: Association whose Réunion cuckooshrike demographic monitoring project received national park authorisation for capture-mark-recapture study in 2026, requiring resulting data to enter SINP 974.

name: SONORUN
summary: Project run by Reef Pulse, listed among its La Réunion projects, that establishes an ecoacoustic reference state for the island's coral reefs.

name: TORSOOI
summary: Marine turtle database for the south-west Indian Ocean, built in MySQL from existing databases under a 2008 to 2010 project, and planned as the store for CEDTM's Europa monitoring data.

name: Université de La Réunion
summary: University whose programme monitoring endemic petrels by ringing, through UMR ENTROPIE, received a favourable opinion from the national park's scientific council in November 2025.

name: Vie Océane
summary: Association that, according to IUCN's September 2020 article, carried the MesoRun project with the consultancy BIORECIF, and runs MesoRun, a faunal inventory of La Réunion's mesophotic zone.

name: Administrația Rezervației Biosferei Delta Dunării
summary: Romanian body that led a 2024–2025 project, with the Danube Delta National Institute as partner, to strengthen its capacity to monitor threatened species and habitats, and partners with the Romanian Ornithological Society.

name: Agenția pentru Protecția Mediului Vrancea
summary: Named as the 2020–2025 LIFE ROsalia coordinator in July 2022, the agency's project reported beginning VHF beetle tracking in Putna Vrancea Natural Park that month.

name: AI wildlife alert system for the Romanian Carpathians
summary: Case study, reported in November 2024, of AI models trained on six years of camera-trap data to classify European mammals, used in an alert system at three locations, with Fundația Conservation Carpathia as partner.

name: Alien vertebrates in Romania: distribution, temporal trends, and introduction pathways
summary: Open dataset, described as the first national-scale FAIR-compliant one of its kind, holding 8,154 georeferenced records of 53 alien vertebrate species in Romania, with distribution, native ranges and introduction pathways.

name: Asociația Agent Green
summary: Romanian non-profit environmental protection organisation, founded in February 2009, whose reports list national monitoring of illegal logging and whose home page counts more than 50 Natura 2000 sites as actively monitored.

name: Asociația pentru Conservarea Diversității Biologice
summary: Based in Focșani, the association supports wild bear, wolf, lynx, otter and wildcat populations and announced thermal-camera drone procurement for bear monitoring in April 2026.

name: Asociația Pentru Protecția Păsărilor și a Naturii „Grupul Milvus”
summary: Bird and nature protection association partnering with the Romanian Ornithological Society on common bird monitoring, according to that society.

name: Babeș-Bolyai University
summary: University whose Department of Taxonomy and Ecology in Cluj-Napoca partners with SEPPI, whose Romanian team tested automated and traditional methods at nine sites in the Eastern Hills of Cluj in 2024.

name: Carpathia forest audio monitoring programme
summary: Programme run by Fundația Conservation Carpathia, developed with the British Trust for Ornithology, using 22 recorders in old-growth, managed and restored forests, with AI software identifying insects, birds and mammals, as reported in July 2025.

name: Carpathia ungulate monitoring study, Făgăraș Mountains
summary: Active study run by Fundația Conservation Carpathia in which 127 camera traps photographed red deer, roe deer and wild boar for a year, producing 1,842,283 photos, which were being processed in July 2025.

name: Centrala Ornitologică Română
summary: Run by the Institute of Biology Bucharest, it trains ringers and collects Romanian ringing and recovery data, including foreign-ringed birds recovered locally, according to SOR.

name: Centrul pentru Cercetarea și Conservarea Liliecilor
summary: Non-profit bat research and conservation association founded in 2017, based in Cluj-Napoca, reporting winter 2025 monitoring at 95 underground sites and describing CHIROHUB as its own project.

name: Checklist of introduced taxa in Romania
summary: Dataset run by Ovidius University of Constanța and the University of Bucharest, covering 827 introduced taxa occurring in Romania and published under a CC BY 4.0 licence.

name: CHIROHUB
summary: Online bat database for Romania and Moldova, built by the bat centre, Moldova’s Institute of Zoology and Szilárd-Lehel Bücs, with a planned autumn 2024 launch unconfirmed.

name: Completarea nivelului de cunoaștere a biodiversității prin implementarea sistemului de monitorizare a stării de conservare a speciilor și habitatelor de interes comunitar din România și raportarea în baza articolului 17 al Directivei Habitate
summary: Ministry-run project, with a financing contract signed on 30 June 2025, a 30-month term and a 49,676,619.82 lei eligible budget, to monitor species and habitats of Community interest and prepare the Article 17 report.

name: Consolidarea sistemului național de gestiune și monitorizare a speciilor de păsări din România în baza articolului 12 din Directiva Păsări
summary: With financing signed on 30 May 2025, the 48-month project has a 48,458,569.71 lei budget to strengthen national monitoring and reporting of bird species of Community interest.

name: Consolidarea sistemului național de management al speciilor alogene invazive din România (SMIS 337191)
summary: Running from 1 May 2025 to 30 April 2029, this ministry-run project with the University of Bucharest has a 44,288,378.89 lei eligible budget to strengthen alien species management tools.

name: COOP4SAFE
summary: WWF Romania-led project with Sensing Clues and a Maramureș hunters' association, using cameras and an app to identify brown bears and send alerts, with five cameras installed and a first real alert by May 2026.

name: Date spațiale privind ariile naturale protejate și distribuția speciilor și habitatelor (Portal GIS MMAP)
summary: GIS portal page offering Habitats Directive Article 17 and Birds Directive Article 12 distribution data, plus distributions from approved management plans updated to the end of 2024.

name: Digiversitate 3.0
summary: Closed project led by Theodor Sebastian Topliceanu, whose December 2025 final report describes analysing wildlife camera photos with DeepFaune and AudioMoth recordings with BirdNET, giving 57 bird species across two quarries.

name: EO4NATURE (Romania)
summary: Active PNRR-funded project integrating Earth observation data, including open Copernicus Sentinel data, into ecosystem monitoring, with drone and field validation at two Natura 2000 sites in November and December 2025.

name: Forest Guardians
summary: App launched by Greenpeace România on 1 October 2018, built by Greenpeace România and mready, that let users compare satellite images to flag canopy changes in Romania's virgin forests and report illegal logging.

name: Fundația ADEPT Transilvania
summary: Foundation whose 2025 annual report describes grassland habitat inventories and monitoring in Târnava Mare, and says one project is developing a satellite-based remote sensing system trained using artificial intelligence.

name: Fundația Conservation Carpathia
summary: Romanian conservation foundation whose monitoring includes acoustic recorders, wildlife cameras, DNA analysis and AI image processing, with partners including the British Trust for Ornithology, University of Freiburg and Hack the Planet.

name: GeoEcoMar
summary: National institute for geological, geophysical and geoecological research on marine, coastal and inland waters, with offices in Bucharest and Constanța, whose applications page presents the past EU project DOORS for the Black Sea.

name: Greenpeace România
summary: Environmental organisation that in 2017 launched the Map of Potential Virgin Forests with two universities, saying it was Europe's first developed and tested remote-sensing method for assessing intact old forests.

name: Harta tăierilor de păduri
summary: Public online application for reporting forest cutting in Romania, made within a volunteer afforestation initiative; it received more than 1,400 reports nationally in its first year.

name: Implementarea Planului național de acțiune pentru conservarea populației de urs brun din România
summary: Closed ministry-led brown bear action plan project that bought genetic analysis equipment and 150 cameras for electric fences; in December 2025 the ministry reported about 24,000 samples gave a conservative estimate of 10,657 to 12,787 bears.

name: Institutul de Biologie București
summary: Bucharest biology institute with a Department of Taxonomy, Ecology and Nature Protection and research stations at Posada and Sulina, whose site lists a POS Mediu project on conservation status monitoring.

name: Institutul de Cercetări Biologice Cluj-Napoca
summary: Cluj-Napoca biological research institute, run by INCDSB as a branch with legal personality, whose taxonomy and ecology department studies biodiversity and ecosystems and which hosts an Experimental Food Webs Research Group.

name: Institutul de Speologie „Emil Racoviță”
summary: Speleology institute whose biospeleology department researches biodiversity and ecosystem dynamics in karst areas, holding specimens gathered over more than 60 years of research in Romania and abroad.

name: Institutul Național de Cercetare-Dezvoltare Delta Dunării
summary: Tulcea research institute founded in 1970 for ecology and environmental research supporting Danube Delta management, whose past Nucleus programmes included species monitoring and sturgeon migration work, and which has a geomatics and GIS department.

name: Institutul Național de Cercetare-Dezvoltare Marină „Grigore Antipa”
summary: Constanța marine research institute covering oceanography, marine ecology and Black Sea living resources, running expeditions averaging 60 to 80 operating days a year and listing DINO-PATH, a telemetry plan to map Russian sturgeon migration.

name: Institutul Național de Cercetare-Dezvoltare pentru Științe Biologice
summary: Bucharest national biological research institute with departments including Taxonomy and Ecology in Cluj and Bioinformatics, which also describes DANUBIUS-RI as a Romanian initiative for a pan-European river-sea research infrastructure.

name: Integrated forest monitoring system (Romania)
summary: Forest monitoring system built by the environment ministry with recovery-plan funding of over 272 million lei, which WWF Romania reports combines satellite monitoring, AI video monitoring of timber transport and LiDAR scanning.

name: Keeping brown bears out of mountain villages
summary: Carpathian project run by Hack the Planet with Fundația Conservation Carpathia, which in 2023 deployed 15 AI cameras paired with 15 Smart Deterrents to keep brown bears out of villages, with prototype testing in 2024.

name: LIFE Bison
summary: European Commission-funded project, run by Rewilding Europe and WWF Romania, that reintroduced bison to the Southern Carpathians, with actions from 2016 to 2021, a GPS-collar and camera monitoring protocol and a breeding centre.

name: LIFE Rosalia
summary: Project led by Vrancea Environmental Protection Agency, planned for 2020 to 2025, which in July 2022 reported starting radio-telemetry monitoring of saproxylic insects in Romania to find their dispersal and home range.

name: LIFE with bison
summary: Project with planned monitoring of bison numbers, genetics, health, ranges and habitat using sampling, cameras, GPS collars and satellite imagery, plus a planned national conservation strategy and Romanian Bison Action Plan.

name: Lower Danube wild sturgeon monitoring system
summary: System run by INCDPM Bucharest, reported by Forbes România as finished by 31 August 2026 with recovery-plan funding, combining acoustic telemetry, genomic sequencing and AI analysis of environmental and transmitter data.

name: Managementul adecvat al speciilor invazive din România (SMIS 120008)
summary: Closed invasive species project under Regulation (EU) 1143/2014, run by the environment ministry with the University of Bucharest, with a total budget of 29,507,870.54 lei and sources giving differing dates.

name: Map of Potential Virgin Forests (Romania)
summary: Dataset built by Greenpeace România with Eberswalde University and Al. I. Cuza University of Iași, launched on 15 November 2017, using satellite analysis to identify over 295,000 hectares of potential virgin forest.

name: Ministry of Environment, Waters and Forests (Romania)
summary: Romanian ministry working on the 2030 biodiversity strategy update, offering a biodiversity geoportal and protected area data, and reported in 2026 to have received a recovery-plan-funded digital forest monitoring system.

name: Monitorizarea Păsărilor Comune
summary: Programme developed and launched in 2006 by the Romanian Ornithological Society, run by it and Grupul Milvus, which aims to detect changes in populations of common breeding birds.

name: Monitorizarea înfloririlor algale agravate de poluare eutrofică și încălzirea climei în ecosisteme din Delta Dunării
summary: A closed project, run by the Politehnica University of Timișoara from September 2025 to August 2026, to monitor severe algal blooms in the lower Danube basin using remote stations and Copernicus satellite data.

name: MonStur in the Danube
summary: Three-year Interreg-co-financed project led by Romania’s environment ministry, reportedly planning the Danube basin’s first transboundary sturgeon monitoring system and tests of eDNA sampling and telemetry.

name: National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration (Romania)
summary: Romanian agency which, according to the 2025 INSPIRE country fiche, provides the presidency and secretariat of the INIS Council and monitors implementation and use of the national spatial data infrastructure.

name: National Agency for Protected Natural Areas (Romania)
summary: Romanian agency responsible for managing protected natural areas and conserving habitats, flora and fauna, which a July 2024 draft ordinance proposed merging into a new agency, ANMAP; whether that happened is unstated.

name: National Forest Inventory (Romania)
summary: Continuous forest inventory run by INCDS Marin Drăcea, started in 2006, combining orthophoto assessment with field plots on a grid in five-year cycles, and supplying data for UNFCCC and biodiversity convention reporting.

name: National Institute for Research and Development in Environmental Protection (Romania)
summary: Research institute coordinated by the Ministry of Research and Innovation, reported by Forbes România to have put into operation a real-time network monitoring environmental parameters and tagged wild sturgeon on the Lower Danube.

name: National Institute for Research and Development in Forestry "Marin Drăcea"
summary: Forestry research institute running the National Forest Inventory, which annually surveys about 6,000 permanent and 1,250 temporary sample plots across Romania, a quarter of the total.

name: Observatorul Ornitologic Agigea
summary: Bird observatory described as Romania's first permanently active migration study station, studying Black Sea migration and climatic influences, staffed by seven to ten volunteer ringers helped by over 50 volunteers yearly.

name: Ornitodata
summary: Bird observation app run by Societatea Ornitologică Română, recording casual observations and monitoring programme data, such as common bird monitoring and breeding waterbirds, which are uploaded to the society's database.

name: Ovidius University of Constanța
summary: Public university established in 1961, described by B-Cubed as the largest EU university on the Black Sea, which runs the GBIF Checklist of introduced taxa in Romania.

name: Parcul Putna Vrancea un Parc Sălbatic și Accesibil pentru Viitor
summary: Funded by Fundația OMV Petrom, the March 2025–January 2027 project includes a permanent fauna monitoring network and announced video and audio monitoring equipment procurement in June 2025.

name: Pilot project to monitor forests with drones
summary: Pilot run by Fundația Conservation Carpathia with Zentiva, using AI analysis of drone images of restoration sites to identify vegetation, assess seedling density and monitor regeneration, with LiDAR drones a stated future aim.

name: Planet Wild x Hula Earth primary forest monitoring in Romania
summary: Project between Planet Wild and Hula Earth, listed on Hula Earth's site, covering biodiversity monitoring and real-time chainsaw recognition to protect 300 hectares of primary forest in Romania.

name: PNRR forest digital monitoring project (Romania)
summary: Recovery-plan project run by the environment ministry, reported by Forbes România as finished and worth 272.605 million lei, combining satellite alerts, 350 AI video monitoring points for timber transport and LiDAR scanning.

name: PRIMOFARO
summary: Inventory of Romania's primary and old-growth forests submitted by EuroNatur Foundation in September 2019, identifying over 525,000 hectares and finding almost half of the 2005 inventory's virgin forests degraded or destroyed.

name: Real-time bear monitoring with WWF Romania
summary: Hack the Planet project dated 2026, with WWF Romania and Sensing Clues, using 4G cameras and a two-stage pipeline of MegaDetector and SpeciesNet to recognise brown bears in real time.

name: Rewilding Romania
summary: An environmental foundation within Rewilding Europe, founded in 2017, reporting Retezat monitoring begun in 2024 with about 60 camera traps, and collecting DNA samples.

name: Romanian Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: Collective initiative of the Romanian Lepidopterological Society and Babeș-Bolyai University, run by the university, which began collecting transect count data in 2017 and later added 15-minute counts.

name: Romanian Space Agency
summary: Romanian space agency whose international projects page lists ROKEO, an Earth observation project coordinated by its research centre, and the Balkan GEO Network, in which it is a partner.

name: Sistemul național de supraveghere a speciilor alogene invazive
summary: National surveillance system recording invasive alien species occurrences across Romania, required under Article 14 of Regulation (EU) No 1143/2014, where users add observations with images and location.

name: SkAIGreen
summary: Active project planning AI and deep-learning drone control to find indicator plant species for Romanian grassland agripayment schemes, with Adept Transilvania, a budget of about 150,000 euros, ending August 2027.

name: Societatea Lepidopterologică Română
summary: Romanian association of lepidopterists, listed among the signatories of a 2010 joint declaration of environmental NGOs, which runs the Romanian Butterfly Monitoring Scheme with Babeș-Bolyai University.

name: Societatea Ornitologică Română
summary: Bird society that launched a generic common bird monitoring programme in 2006, carried out with Grupul Milvus, and runs the Ornitodata app for collecting observations.

name: Specializare în monitoring forestier, diversitatea genetică și sistematica plantelor lemnoase și reziliența stejarilor xerofiți la schimbările climatice
summary: Active 2024 to 2026 Romania-Moldova project funded by UEFISCDI and run by INCDS Marin Drăcea, aiming to harmonise forest monitoring, with tree health data validation and genotyping training completed.

name: Stațiunea Biologică Marină „Prof. Dr. Ioan Borcea” Agigea
summary: Marine biological station with marine ecology and ornithology laboratories, returned to Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iași in 1990, whose Agigea Bird Observatory is described as Romania's first permanently active migration station.

name: SUMAL 2.0
summary: Forest timber tracking system which, the ministry said in May 2026, had over 92,000 users and about 20,000 transport permits issued daily, with satellite, camera and LiDAR monitoring systems to be integrated.

name: SUMAL 3.0
summary: Proposed integrated forest information system, set out in a draft government decision put to consultation, which the ministry says will use AI agents for risk analysis and statistical reports.

name: Universitatea Politehnica din Timișoara
summary: University that was contractor and coordinator of the ALGA-MONITOR algal bloom project, with Moldova State University as partner, from 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2026.

name: Universitatea „Alexandru Ioan Cuza” din Iași
summary: University that regained the Agigea marine biological station in 1990 and took custody of the Agigea marine dunes protected area in 2004; its page calls the Agigea Bird Observatory Romania's first permanently active migration station.

name: University of Bucharest
summary: A university that publishes the GBIF dataset "Alien vertebrates in Romania", originated first by Iulia V. Miu of its Center for Environmental Research, and runs the checklist of introduced taxa in Romania.

name: WWF Romania
summary: The Romanian arm of WWF, working there since 2006, which coordinates the COOP4SAFE bear-detection initiative as reported by Interreg NEXT, and in November 2026 announced a plan for AI wildlife monitoring in Râșnov.

name: Alciphron
summary: Database of the insects of Serbia, run by HabiProt, which says it held almost 430,000 records by 2021, calls it Serbia's largest insect database, and publishes arthropod observations from it to GBIF.

name: Atlas gnezdarica Srbije
summary: Serbian breeding bird atlas programme, run by the Bird Protection and Study Society of Serbia, with data collection since 2013 and more than 150,000 records processed by May 2023.

name: Biodiversity in aquatic ecosystems in Serbia, ex situ conservation (BAES ex situ)
summary: Serbian database of endangered aquatic species and ex situ conservation, linked to the Faculty of Science, Kragujevac; a 2017 assessment said public browsing had been cancelled and data were available only on request.

name: Biodiversity Information Center, Faculty of Biology, University of Belgrade
summary: Unit of the University of Belgrade's Faculty of Biology, founded in 2006, which says it has carried out ecological network, Natura 2000 and red list projects for Serbia's nature conservation institute since then.

name: Biologer
summary: Open source platform for collecting and digitising data on Eastern European biodiversity, built by the University of Niš biology department, with volunteer records, a butterfly counting app and local community sites.

name: Biološko društvo "Dr Sava Petrović"
summary: Citizens' association of biology graduates, students and nature lovers in Niš, which builds Biologer, the Serbian species distribution data website, its software developed through the society under the MAVA-funded Dinaric Arc project.

name: BioRaS (Biološka raznovrsnost Srbije)
summary: Serbian biodiversity portal on which, as reported in December 2014, anyone could share photographs as species data; a GIZ assessment said NGOs managed it, Petnica Research Center supported it technically, and it was then one of two public raw-data sources.

name: BioSense Institute
summary: Research institute for information technologies of biosystems, run by the University of Novi Sad, which says it uses remote sensing to monitor forest vegetation and studies pollinator population changes.

name: Bird Protection and Study Society of Serbia
summary: Novi Sad-based society founded in 1989, which says it has researched birds for over 30 years and became a CEPF implementation partner for the Balkans in 2019.

name: BirdLoger
summary: Programme built by the Bird Protection and Study Society of Serbia, hosted according to Biologer's funding page on a data server alongside Biologer Taxa.

name: Boosting Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy in Water Biomonitoring
summary: Closed project, 1 October 2022 to 30 September 2025, led by the Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy and funded by the EU, to build eDNA metabarcoding capacity for water biomonitoring in Serbia.

name: Centar za markiranje životinja
summary: National animal marking centre founded in 1993 within the Natural History Museum in Belgrade, which has marked more than 300,000 birds and about 10,000 bats and partners with EURING.

name: Comprehensive dataset from high resolution UAV land cover mapping of diverse natural environments in Serbia
summary: Dataset paper published in Scientific Data in 2025 on high-resolution UAV land cover mapping of diverse natural environments in Serbia, with a first author at the BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad.

name: Department of Biology and Ecology, Faculty of Sciences and Mathematics, University of Niš
summary: University of Niš department holding a herbarium of about 25,000 plant specimens and partnering in the DNAquaIMG project.

name: Department of Biology and Ecology, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
summary: University of Novi Sad department whose projects include WildPosh on pollinators (2023 to 2027), Safeguard (2021 to 2025) and an environmental DNA soil quality study, alongside biodiversity monitoring and species distribution modelling.

name: Department of Genetic Research, Institute for Biological Research "Siniša Stanković"
summary: Genetic research department listed as the first author’s affiliation on a 2025 paper presenting a soil eDNA droplet digital PCR assay for monitoring terrestrial mammals.

name: Djerdap National Park (public enterprise)
summary: Public enterprise which said in February 2023 that a rehabilitated lynx would receive a GPS collar for year-long tracking, described as Serbia's first such lynx tracking.

name: Establishing a Long-Term Monitoring Study of the Endemic and Highly Endangered Meadow Viper (Vipera ursinii macrops) in Serbia
summary: A closed project listed under Margareta Lakušić aimed to establish long-term meadow viper monitoring in Serbia, train mountaineering societies and propose a monitoring plan for Mokra Gora.

name: EU for Natura 2000 in Serbia
summary: Closed EU-funded project, May 2019 to May 2021, with an EU donation of 1,589,100 euros, aiming to support a first list of potential Natura 2000 sites with an information system, database and GIS.

name: EU for the Green Agenda in Serbia
summary: EU-funded initiative run by UNDP, in partnership with Serbia's environment ministry, which UNDP Serbia says is implemented in cooperation with Sweden and the European Investment Bank.

name: Faculty of Biology, University of Belgrade
summary: Belgrade faculty that describes itself as Serbia's oldest and largest higher education and scientific institution in biology, ecology and environmental protection, and includes a Biodiversity Information Center.

name: Faculty of Sciences and Mathematics, University of Niš
summary: Faculty in Niš with about 250 professors, 50 researchers and around 1,500 students, which runs the Department of Biology and Ecology.

name: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
summary: University faculty named as the first author's affiliation on a 2023 study towards UAV-assisted monitoring of aquatic vegetation in the middle Danube in Serbia.

name: HabiProt
summary: Association founded in 2005 for sustainable development and habitat conservation in Serbia, which runs the Alciphron insect database and lists saproxylic insect monitoring and GBIF data projects.

name: Institute for Biological Research "Siniša Stanković"
summary: Serbian national institute within Belgrade University, monitoring birds including endangered griffon vultures, with its genetic research department listed as a 2025 soil eDNA mammal monitoring paper affiliation.

name: Institute for Nature Conservation of Serbia
summary: Serbia's self-described central expert institution for nature protection, which a 2021 to 2023 draft programme says keeps the register of protected natural assets and the nature protection information system.

name: Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, University of Belgrade
summary: University of Belgrade institute listed by CORDIS as coordinator of BIOLAWEB, a project to strengthen its research capacity in biodiversity assessment and biomonitoring.

name: Institute of Forestry, Belgrade
summary: Belgrade research institute listed by ICP Forests as Serbia's National Focal Centre, whose laboratory analysed samples in the 2023 national forest condition monitoring report.

name: Institute of Lowland Forestry and Environment
summary: Part of the University of Novi Sad, researching forestry and environmental protection technologies, and taking part in ForBioSink, an EUKI forests, climate and biodiversity project with partners from four countries.

name: International Waterbird Census in Serbia
summary: Waterbird count carried out in Serbia since 1982 at varying intensity, run by the Bird Protection and Study Society of Serbia, which has managed it since 2012; over 90 species recorded.

name: Jadovnik Citizens' Association
summary: Citizens' association linked by UNDP Serbia to a watering troughs project under the EU Green Agenda initiative, with cameras on Jadovnik recording bears leaving winter dormancy.

name: LTER Serbia
summary: Serbian long-term ecological research network, an ILTER member since 2008, with five operational sites studying ecosystem responses to environmental change; DEIMS lists four verified sites and Kopaonik National Park as unverified.

name: Ministry of Environmental Protection (Serbia)
summary: Serbian ministry whose site reports support for conserving nationally important protected natural areas and which, per a 2021-2023 draft programme, includes the Environmental Protection Agency as a body within it.

name: Monitoring and Assessment in the Serpentinite Habitat of Brdjani Gorge
summary: A project, with status unknown and listed under Nenad Zlatić, that aims to survey and map plants in a serpentinite habitat, expanding the area from 15 ha to about 50 ha and sharing data with biodiversity networks.

name: Monitoring of Threatened Saproxylic Beetles Species in Serbia with Public Participation
summary: A closed project, listed under Sanja Banjanac, that planned to map six saproxylic beetle species in Serbian protected areas using public data entry including the Alciphron app, then give managers monitoring protocols.

name: Monitoring Program Establishment on Endangered Species Affected by Wildfires in Serbian Protected Natural Areas
summary: A closed project, listed under Milan Ilić, that set out to establish monitoring of three rare butterfly species in Serbian protected areas after wildfires, continuing work begun under a 2019 grant.

name: Nacionalni park Fruška gora (public enterprise)
summary: Public enterprise that reported in June 2025 an EU-supported long-term raptor conservation project covering monitoring, winter eagle feeding, a photography hide and school workshops.

name: National bird ringing programme of Serbia
summary: National bird ringing programme in which 30 licensed ringers marked 28,955 birds in 2025, with a permit exam held at the Natural History Museum on 20 December 2025.

name: NIMOS
summary: Serbian forest monitoring system combining satellite observations, climate data and machine learning for vitality, fires and pests in all public forests, built and run by the Institute of Lowland Forestry and Environment.

name: Nose-Horned Viper in Serbia, Continuation of Monitoring Population Status and Conservation Efforts
summary: A closed project, listed under Tijana Cubric in 2017, that aimed to continue monitoring nose-horned viper populations in Serbia to assess trends, adding parasite load and camera trap behaviour analyses.

name: Orhideje
summary: Database of orchid observations in Serbia, run by HabiProt, which publishes the records to GBIF and says results can be seen on the Orhideje website.

name: Provincial Institute for Nature Conservation (Vojvodina)
summary: Provincial institute that, according to the 2021-2023 draft Nature Protection Programme, keeps Vojvodina's register of protected natural assets and, with a second institute, collects nature data and monitors species, habitats and protected areas.

name: Ptice moje hranilice
summary: Citizen science feeder bird count run by the Bird Protection and Study Society of Serbia since 2019, in which 811 observers reported 21,540 birds in results reported February 2024.

name: Republic Geodetic Authority (Serbia)
summary: Serbian national spatial data institution which, according to a paper by its staff, first built remote sensing capacity for thematic products such as habitat and habitat fragmentation maps under the IGIS project.

name: Second National Forest Inventory of the Republic of Serbia
summary: Two-phase national forest inventory of Serbia, with a first phase based on aerial and satellite imagery, for which FAO adapted Collect Earth software with the inventory team.

name: Serbian Environmental Protection Agency
summary: Body within Serbia's environment ministry which, per the 2021-2023 draft Nature Protection Programme, reports on the environment, maintains indicator databases and had a Clearing House Mechanism portal established.

name: Setting Up the Base for True Bug (Heteroptera) Conservation and Insect Monitoring in Sandy Grasslands of the Pannonian Region
summary: A closed project, listed under Jelena Šeat in 2023, that planned to revisit sandy grassland sites in Serbia and develop a protocol using true bug indicators, with pollinator monitoring in Hungary and Serbia.

name: Singidunum University
summary: Belgrade university whose affiliated authors published 2025 and 2026 papers using convolutional networks to classify bird calls from audio for African, South American and Australian birds.

name: Srpsko herpetološko društvo "Milutin Radovanović"
summary: An active herpetological society founded in 2007, whose work has mostly been population studies of snakes and turtles in Serbia, North Macedonia and Montenegro.

name: Stara planina large carnivore camera-trap pilot (ForestConnect)
summary: Pilot in which WWF Adria installed five camera traps on Stara planina to monitor bears, wolves and lynxes and check whether they inhabit the nature park and how climate change has affected their corridors.

name: Tara National Park (public enterprise)
summary: Public enterprise in Bajina Bašta managing Tara National Park, declared in 1981, offering fauna and flora databases and inviting participants to an October 2026 brown bear count.

name: The secret life of bears (Tara brown bear camera-collar tracking)
summary: Tara brown bear tracking project with Tara National Park and Telekom Srbija, which fitted a camera collar to a male in summer 2021, described as a first in Serbia, and a camera transmitter to a female two years later.

name: Toward Cost-Effective UAV-Assisted Multimetric System for Detection of Freshwater Patches of High Conservation Value within the Danube Floodplain in Serbia
summary: A closed project, listed under Maja Novković, that aimed to develop a UAV-assisted multimetric system for finding high-value freshwater patches in the Danube floodplain, with data planned from 20 water bodies in 2019.

name: Tracking of Movement of a Brown Bear at the Edge of Its Dinaric Distribution in Serbia
summary: Closed project, planned for 14 months until the end of May 2018, which aimed to capture, collar and track a brown bear at the edge of its Serbian range, with camera trap monitoring.

name: Udruženje ljubitelja prirode "Riparija"
summary: Non-governmental nature organisation founded in 1999 in Subotica, with about 150 members, focused on bird ringing and migration monitoring, which ringed 1,373 roller chicks in 2025.

name: University of Belgrade
summary: Serbian university whose Faculty of Biology has a Biodiversity Information Center that has carried out projects on the country's ecological network and red lists since 2006.

name: University of Belgrade – Faculty of Biology
summary: Faculty of the University of Belgrade, based at Studentski trg 16, which lists a Centre for Biodiversity Information among its centres.

name: University of Niš
summary: Serbian university recorded by OpenAlex as an education institution, linked to a 2023 study on UAV-assisted monitoring of aquatic vegetation in the middle Danube, co-authored by someone in its Faculty of Sciences and Mathematics.

name: University of Novi Sad
summary: Serbian university whose Faculty of Sciences includes a Department of Biology and Ecology, where a laboratory models the potential present and future distribution of species.

name: Uprava za šume
summary: An active forestry directorate responsible for state administration and expert work on forest policy and protection, whose site hosts Second National Forest Inventory reports and a 2024 forest condition monitoring report.

name: A.N. Severtsov Institute of Ecology and Evolution of the Russian Academy of Sciences
summary: Moscow institute, established in 1934 per GBIF, that signed an AI memorandum with Sberbank in November 2023 and says it trained neural networks to count saiga on satellite images.

name: Agency for Strategic Initiatives
summary: Organisation that, according to Kommersant, announced with the Lake Baikal Foundation the start of work on the platform.

name: Aira Flot
summary: Organisation for which NIA Ecology reports June 2025 tests of a catamaran water drone carrying sensors for monitoring water.

name: AIRI
summary: Non-profit in Moscow whose researchers, according to the Russian Science Foundation, helped make the forest tool.

name: Altai State Nature Biosphere Reserve (Алтайский государственный природный биосферный заповедник)
summary: A reserve in Gorny Altai that has preserved the area's pristine nature since 1932.

name: Amur Tiger Center
summary: Organisation that initiated the system for identifying Amur tigers from camera-trap frames.

name: Amur tiger recognition system
summary: System that identifies Amur tigers by stripe pattern in camera-trap images; Ecotech-Pro says it distinguishes 90 tigers, while one report says it needed more training time.

name: ANO Nature and People: Digital Solutions
summary: Organisation that describes itself as a team of experts creating technology for nature conservation in Russia, reports developing web and mobile applications and geospatial analysis, and runs the thermal points on protected areas project.

name: Arctic Research Centre
summary: Enterprise that Rosneft describes as part of its corporate research and development complex, and which organised five expeditions in 2024.

name: ARCTIC: Conserving Biodiversity in the Changing Arctic
summary: Proposed GEF project, concept approved, with a grant of 5,840,850 US dollars, aiming at a modern knowledge base and wildlife monitoring programme across the Russian Arctic.

name: Artificial Intelligence Centre of MIPT
summary: MIPT centre whose laboratory of neural systems and deep learning has a staff member named as a developer of an AI system for monitoring sockeye salmon in the South Kamchatka sanctuary.

name: Astrakhan State Nature Biosphere Reserve (Астраханский государственный заповедник)
summary: A biosphere reserve in the lower Volga delta, Astrakhan region, covering 67,920 ha in three separate parts.

name: Atlas of Russia's Intact Forest Landscapes
summary: A closed atlas project dated 1997 to 2002, which aimed to give a reliable picture of the state and distribution of Russia's remaining intact forests.

name: Avialesookhrana
summary: According to a March 2026 report by the 360 television channel, it manages ISDM-Rosleshoz, a remote monitoring system that tracks fires in real time.

name: Baikal plankton image dataset
summary: Labelled image dataset that Yandex Cloud says is freely available; it says biologists provided almost 50,000 images, of which 20,000 were used for training.

name: Baikal plankton neural network
summary: Neural network for telling zooplankton species apart in water-sample images, published on GitHub under Apache 2.0; Yandex Cloud said in 2022 it worked with 70 plankton forms.

name: Baikalsky State Nature Biosphere Reserve
summary: Biosphere reserve run by the Russian natural resources ministry, whose site has a section of camera-trap footage.

name: Bashkiria National Park (ФГБУ «Национальный парк «Башкирия»)
summary: A federal institution associated with the Zapovednyi Rezerv project for staff development in protected areas.

name: Bastak State Nature Reserve
summary: Federal state budgetary reserve whose site has a section on the Chronicle of Nature and environmental monitoring; its 2023 volume says programme work there began in 2000.

name: Bear Islands polar bear census
summary: Polar bear census led by Ilya Chernook; an October 2023 report gives a preliminary AI count of over 150 bears from more than 25,000 drone images, pending further processing.

name: Bear Land Foundation (Фонд «Медвежья Земля»)
summary: A foundation whose site describes a project, supported by the Presidential Grants Fund, to plant 40,000 tree seedlings restoring the Mordovsky reserve after the 2010 and 2021 fires.

name: Beringia National Park (ФГБУ «Национальный парк «Берингия»)
summary: A national park that reported in March 2022 that its regulation already banned aircraft flights over walrus haul-outs and seabird colonies, with a marine protective zone being prepared.

name: Berkut State Budgetary Institution
summary: North Ossetia-Alania Ministry of Natural Resources institution, supported by the Presidential Fund for Nature, that runs a project to introduce photo monitoring and involve residents in monitoring wildlife.

name: Bikin National Park (ФГБУ «Национальный парк «Бикин»)
summary: A national park that aims to protect Indigenous peoples' habitat and traditional way of life, with a Council of Indigenous Peoples created to take part in decisions.

name: Biodiversity Conservation Center
summary: Organisation that says it organised a census of the desman across Russia in 2000 to 2001, and which uses Web-GIS Faunistics.

name: Biodiversity Research project, Tomsk State University
summary: A university project reporting models trained on 31 Russian species for planned AddaxAI integration, with tools helping Severtsov Institute staff and three protected areas.

name: Bird Ringing Centre of Russia
summary: Department of the Severtsov Institute that coordinates bird ringing in Russia, collects migration data, and relies on a ring recovery database of more than 130,000 records.

name: Botanical Garden-Institute of the Far Eastern Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences
summary: Research institute whose scientists, Naked Science reported in February 2021, applied U-Net-like convolutional neural networks to recognise dead forest on high resolution images and then on satellite images of island forests.

name: Burpriroda (БУ «Природопользование и охрана окружающей среды Республики Бурятия»)
summary: A Buryatia institution that, since 2005, has carried out protection, reproduction, regulation of use and counting of wildlife in the republic's regional sanctuaries.

name: Buzuluksky Bor National Park (Национальный парк «Бузулукский бор»)
summary: A national park whose administration address is in the Buzuluk district of Orenburg region.

name: CAMMON
summary: National photo-monitoring programme, described as the first, drawn up in 2022 for reserves, national parks and sanctuaries, with a goal of replacing separate camera-trap projects with one observatory network.

name: CAMMON-CHECHNYA
summary: Camera-trap network built by the Severtsov Institute with Nature and People Fund support, reportedly comprising 20 locations in 2024, with 50 cameras installed under a modified design.

name: Center for Forest Ecology and Productivity RAS
summary: Moscow-based RAS centre whose forest monitoring laboratory, founded in 1992, developed GIS and remote sensing methods; its site also reports a machine learning project on earthworm communities.

name: Central Chernozem State Nature Biosphere Reserve (Центрально-Черноземный заповедник имени профессора В.В. Алехина)
summary: A biosphere reserve that has belonged to the UNESCO international network of biosphere reserves since 1979.

name: Central Forest Nature Reserve
summary: Reserve that initiated the project for the national wildlife photo-monitoring network.

name: Central Siberian Botanical Garden SB RAS
summary: Botanical garden whose GBIF record gives its collection size and address and names its Flora of Siberia dataset; it partners with the Specify Collections Consortium.

name: Centre for Spatial Research Geointellect
summary: A spatial research centre whose director is named as developer of the photo bank platform.

name: Centre for Sustainable Territorial Development, Graduate School of Management, St Petersburg University
summary: St Petersburg University centre named as the maker of SmartLeo, with advisory support from VTB.

name: Chronicle of Nature
summary: Programme under which GBIF describes a compiled dataset.

name: Coastal waste detection neural network
summary: Yandex said in June 2025 the network detected and classified coastal solid waste from aerial imagery with 80%+ accuracy and had been used in South Kamchatka Federal Nature Reserve.

name: Commander Islands National Park
summary: The Nature and People Fund’s 2025 report describes three park scientists’ 115-day Medny Island stay for fox conservation and biodiversity monitoring, with cameras installed in 2024 recording winter foxes.

name: Complete count of snow leopards in Russia, 2022
summary: Closed 2022 snow leopard count across Altai, Tyva and Buryatia, which GSLEP says involved 82 people from 12 organisations using methods approved by the Russian environment ministry.

name: CROC
summary: Organisation that said in a February 2022 post it had organised the WildHack hackathon with Kronotsky reserve the preceding December.

name: Curonian Spit National Park (Национальный парк «Куршская коса»)
summary: A national park in the part of Kaliningrad region bordering Lithuania.

name: Darwin State Nature Biosphere Reserve (Дарвинский государственный заповедник)
summary: A reserve organised on 15 July 1945, with a protective zone in Vologda and Yaroslavl regions, which gained UNESCO international biosphere reserve status on 16 December 2002.

name: Digital Earth
summary: Roscosmos-run satellite image analysis by Terra Tech using neural networks; Rosleshoz said a continuous forest monitoring experiment in Arkhangelsk and Irkutsk regions began in June 2022.

name: Digital Reindeer Trail
summary: Planned web service, to be run by Nature and People Digital Solutions, for mapping movements of satellite-collared Taimyr wild reindeer, with launch planned for February 2026.

name: Digital Zoology – Preparation of an Atlas of the Distribution of Mammals in Asian Russia
summary: Project to give open access to data on mammal distribution in Asian Russia, listed by the Severtsov Institute as a 2026 Presidential Fund for Nature competition winner, with A.A. Lisovsky as applicant.

name: Directorate for Wildlife and Protected Areas of Amur Region (ГБУ Амурской области «Дирекция ООПТ»)
summary: A regional state budgetary institution responsible for protecting and using wildlife and specially protected natural territories in Amur region.

name: Directorate of Biological Resources, Protected Areas and Nature Parks of Sakha (Yakutia) (ГБУ РС(Я) «ДБР»)
summary: Sakha (Yakutia) state directorate that coordinates and controls its branches, the nature parks Sinyaya, Ust-Viluisky, Lena Pillars, Kolyma and Momsky.

name: Directorate of Ergaki Nature Park (КГБУ «Дирекция природного парка «Ергаки»)
summary: A directorate for a krai-level nature park in southern Krasnoyarsk Krai, created in 2005 and covering 393,478.4 ha.

name: Directorate of Forestry and Nature Parks of Kaliningrad Region (ГБУ КО «Дирекция лесхоза и природных парков»)
summary: A Kaliningrad region state institution whose protected areas department conducts ground patrols under a state assignment to detect and prevent breaches of nature conservation law.

name: Directorate of Protected Areas of Irkutsk Region (Дирекция по ООПТ Иркутской области)
summary: A directorate that manages 13 regional state nature sanctuaries and 59 natural monuments in Irkutsk region.

name: Directorate of Protected Areas of Krasnodar Krai (ГКУ КК «Управление особо охраняемыми природными территориями Краснодарского края»)
summary: A Krasnodar Krai state institution whose site lists the regional protected areas in its remit that are scheduled for ground or water patrols in 2026.

name: Directorate of Protected Areas of Krasnoyarsk Krai (КГБУ «Дирекция по ООПТ Красноярского края»)
summary: A krai state budgetary institution serving as the directorate for specially protected natural territories of Krasnoyarsk Krai, whose state inspectors detain hunters breaching sanctuary regimes.

name: Directorate of Protected Areas of Leningrad Region (ЛОГБУ «Дирекция ООПТ ЛО»)
summary: A directorate that ensures the functioning and management of the regional-level protected areas of Leningrad region.

name: Directorate of Protected Areas of Saint Petersburg (ГКУ «Дирекция ООПТ Санкт-Петербурга»)
summary: A state institution whose main task is the preservation and development of protected natural territories of Saint Petersburg.

name: Directorate of Protected Areas of the Republic of Khakassia (ГБУ РХ «Дирекция ООПТ Хакасии»)
summary: A state budgetary institution of Khakassia serving as the directorate for the republic's specially protected natural territories, whose site covers its regional protected areas.

name: Directorate of Regional Protected Areas of Murmansk Region (ГОКУ «Дирекция ООПТ»)
summary: A directorate of regional protected areas in Murmansk region, named on the Khibiny park site as managing protected areas and checking their regime.

name: eDNA-based occurrence dataset on fungi from forest monitoring plots in Northwestern Siberia
summary: Occurrence dataset on fungi from forest monitoring plots in Northwestern Siberia, for which GBIF describes the eDNA sampling and sequencing.

name: Ekomonitoring federal information system
summary: A federal information system whose first stage a deputy minister said entered service on 25 December 2025, and which was reported in February 2026 to join 18 monitoring modules and 366 data sets from 13 federal suppliers.

name: ER-Telecom Holding
summary: An organisation that Vedomosti names alongside the park in a pilot, with no further detail given.

name: Eurasian Centre for the Conservation of Far Eastern Leopards
summary: An organisation named on the SmartLeo page as strategic partner of the project, and linked to it as a partner.

name: Far Eastern Artificial Intelligence Centre
summary: A centre that ComNews reported in September 2022 was expected to take part in developing an AI model for conserving the Amur tiger and other rare Far East animals.

name: Far Eastern Federal University
summary: A university whose Far Eastern AI centre, according to the Amur Tiger Centre, carries out the recognition project, and which is linked as a partner of the Amur tiger recognition system.

name: Far Eastern Leopards
summary: An organisation that provided financial support when creation of the Land of the Leopard camera-trap network began in 2013, and is linked as its funder.

name: Federal Forestry Agency of the Russian Federation
summary: Its head told TASS of gradual drone adoption plans from 2026; Roslesinforg reported the agency's integration of satellite imagery and AI with Roscosmos in March 2024.

name: Federal Service for Supervision of Natural Resources
summary: A federal natural resources supervision service, led by Svetlana Radionova, which says it presented a Geoportal in April 2026 as a single space for geodata including protected areas and water bodies.

name: Federal State Information System of the Forest Complex
summary: A forest information system that Roslesinforg, which runs it, calls a digital twin of the Russian forest.

name: Flora of Russia
summary: A project built by the Moscow University Herbarium on iNaturalist, where staff created 85 regional projects, one per federal subject, joined in the Flora of Russia portal.

name: Flora of Russia on iNaturalist: a trusted backlog
summary: A dataset of unknown status, described by GBIF as a trusted backlog and built on iNaturalist.

name: FORDIV
summary: A database that a centre lists together with its authors, with no further detail given.

name: Forest change monitoring service
summary: A service of unknown status that says it found 8,643 forest change objects in 2018 to 2020, using Planet, Sentinel and Landsat imagery.

name: Forest Etalon
summary: An active programme whose independent quality control body, the entry says, analyses open data and satellite images.

name: Formoza-Service
summary: An organisation that ComNews reported in 2016 developed the system solution for Lesokhranitel in Smolensk Oblast, and which a software marketplace lists as its owner.

name: Foundation for Applied Environmental Development and Research Lake Baikal
summary: Moscow-addressed foundation that funds the Point No. 1 monitoring programme, said it had supported for eight years by 2024, and was named in 2022 among the Baikal neural network's developers.

name: Friends of the Baltic Seal Foundation
summary: A foundation whose announcement about its tracked seal www1.ru reports, with www1.ru saying one of its seals was among the first marine mammals in Russia with an Argos transmitter.

name: Geoscan
summary: An organisation that reported to RIA Novosti applying AI to assess reforestation from drone data, described as a first for Russia, and that CNews reports has an agreement with the Russian Centre of Forest Protection.

name: Geoscan digital forest survey in Sakhalin
summary: A closed project run by Geoscan in which AI determined tree species, height, diameter and plot boundaries across more than 860 hectares.

name: Geospatial modelling of earthworm communities of the North-West Caucasus with machine learning
summary: Russian Science Foundation-funded machine learning models of North-West Caucasus earthworm communities, based on data from more than a thousand points gathered on expeditions in 2014 to 2023.

name: Gray whale satellite telemetry programme
summary: Programme described as a separate project within the Academy of Sciences' standing expedition on Red Book animals, with Argos tagging of gray whales planned off Sakhalin in 2010 and Kamchatka in 2011.

name: Great Scientific Expedition of Norilsk Nickel and the Siberian Branch of RAS
summary: Closed expedition of Norilsk Nickel and the Siberian Branch of RAS; a February 2024 conference report says scientists used Orlan drones and real-time AI analysis.

name: Guardian of the Mountains and Master of the Forests – the Caucasian Leopard and Bison
summary: Project run by the Berkut State Budgetary Institution, with the Severtsov Institute as partner, aiming to introduce photo monitoring methods and engage residents in public monitoring of wildlife.

name: Gydansky National Park
summary: National park for which Vedomosti, citing Roszapovedtsentr, reported a planned network of 75 camera traps on Shokalsky Island to count polar bears and other rare species, after earlier ground, aerial and marking-based counts.

name: High Conservation Value Forests of Russia
summary: Dataset run by the Nature and People Fund, with Forest Etalon and Transparent World as partners, which says it gives current information on boundaries, identification methods and monitoring of high conservation value forests.

name: HSE University
summary: University running a landscape ecology laboratory established in 2022, whose page reports a team applying convolutional neural networks to high-resolution satellite images of three Siberian landscapes.

name: I.I. Sprygin Zhiguli State Nature Biosphere Reserve
summary: Nature reserve whose site reports installing camera traps in mine galleries.

name: Immanuel Kant Baltic Federal University
summary: University whose staff, Fishnews reported in April 2026, did work with colleagues from other institutes on a model that distinguished plastic waste from birds, glints and droplets.

name: Information System L.
summary: Tool for biological data from various sources, which GBIF says replaced the CRIS platform, led by Alexey Melekhin, with financial support listed from two research funds and three institutes.

name: Information-Analytical Center for Specially Protected Natural Areas Support
summary: A federal institution created in summer 2017 under the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment, whose tasks a 2018 article described as biodiversity conservation, protected-area protection and scientific research.

name: Innogeotech
summary: Organisation that says Innopolis University and RVC created it, builds geographic information solutions for forestry, farming and cities, and uses AI and computer vision on satellite and aerial images.

name: Innopolis University
summary: University that worked with the Perm Krai ministry in June 2020 on neural network processing of satellite images of nine forest districts, using machine learning and computer vision.

name: Institute of Geography, Russian Academy of Sciences
summary: Russian Academy of Sciences institute, represented by Arkady Tishkov, whose site lists a department of cartography and remote sensing and whose databases GBIF lists.

name: Institute of Mathematical Problems of Biology RAS
summary: Russian Academy of Sciences institute in Pushchino whose GBIF record lists an online database of finds of a rare lichen, Lobaria pulmonaria, in Russia.

name: Institute of North Industrial Ecology Problems
summary: Institute whose work and address GBIF describes.

name: International Laboratory of Landscape Ecology, HSE University
summary: HSE University laboratory led by Robert Sandlersky, whose page reports a team applying convolutional neural networks to satellite images of three Siberian landscapes.

name: Irbis Interregional Association
summary: Interregional association whose 2024 report says an AI system for recognising animal species in camera images was started at Sailugemsky National Park with its support and Sberbank, and that it supplied camera traps.

name: Irkutsk State University
summary: University whose biologists Snob named among Baikal plankton network developers in September 2022 and reported sampling at one lake point under a monitoring programme dating from 1945.

name: ISDM-Rosleshoz
summary: Programme including a geographic information system that, an October 2016 page says, gave users current fire data from ground, air and satellite sources, used by Avialesookhrana dispatchers.

name: Joint Directorate of Kostomuksha Reserve and Kalevala National Park (Объединенная дирекция «Костомукшский» и «Калевальский»)
summary: A joint directorate for the Kostomuksha reserve and Kalevala national park, two federal protected areas in Karelia.

name: Joint Directorate of the Orenburg and Shaitan-Tau State Nature Reserves (Заповедники Оренбуржья)
summary: Federal institution based in Orenburg that serves as the joint directorate of the Orenburg and Shaitan-Tau state nature reserves.

name: Joint Directorate of the Sayano-Shushensky State Nature Biosphere Reserve and Shushensky Bor National Park
summary: Joint directorate of the Sayano-Shushensky reserve and Shushensky Bor National Park, renamed in July 2022, which received a Russian Geographical Society grant and reported results including an updated camera-trap layout.

name: Katunsky State Nature Biosphere Reserve (Катунский биосферный заповедник)
summary: A biosphere reserve established on 25 July 1991.

name: Kavkazsky Nature Reserve
summary: One of seven protected areas in the national camera-trap photo-monitoring network project, where the Severtsov Institute says it will observe the effect of mass tourism and resort development on mammals.

name: Kenozero National Park (Национальный парк «Кенозерский»)
summary: A federal institution with its office in Arkhangelsk.

name: Kerzhenskiy State Nature Biosphere Reserve
summary: Nature reserve whose site reports a camera trap recording a lynx with two kittens.

name: Khingansky State Nature Reserve
summary: Federal state budgetary reserve in Arkhara, Amur Oblast, whose site reports camera trap records, bat studies since 2011, and a Japanese crane from its reintroduction station seen wintering in China.

name: Khopersky State Nature Reserve (Хопёрский государственный природный заповедник)
summary: A reserve founded in 1935 on over 16 thousand hectares to preserve the Russian desman, studying and conserving the Khoper valley's old oak and alder forest and floodplain lakes.

name: Komarov Botanical Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences
summary: Russian Academy of Sciences botanical institute that runs the Phytocoenarium database and lists herbarium indexes and the Russian Arctic Vegetation Archive among its databases.

name: Krasnoyarsk Stolby National Park (Национальный парк «Красноярские Столбы»)
summary: National park on the right bank of the Yenisei near Krasnoyarsk, organised to protect the natural complexes of the Stolby rock massif.

name: Kronotsky State Nature Reserve
summary: State nature reserve whose 2024 pages describe ongoing neural network training to detect litter from quadcopter images and conservation research involving AI with Greentech.

name: Kuznetsky Alatau State Nature Reserve (Заповедник «Кузнецкий Алатау»)
summary: Nature reserve in the highest part of the western slope of the Kuznetsky Alatau range, spread across three districts of Kemerovo region.

name: Ladoga Skerries National Park (ФГБУ «Национальный парк «Ладожские шхеры»)
summary: A federal institution associated with a national park whose regulation was approved by Ministry of Natural Resources order of 15 February 2023.

name: Land of the Leopard camera-trap network
summary: Camera-trap network run by Land of the Leopard National Park and funded by Far Eastern Leopards ANO, reportedly reaching 209 stations by 2024.

name: Land of the Leopard National Park
summary: National park that runs a camera-trap network, reportedly producing over a million images a year from more than 450 traps in April 2022, and in August 2022 was reported to be aiming to pass image sorting to a neural network.

name: Landscape Fire Prevention Centre
summary: Centre that says it has existed since March 2021, specialises in forest, peat and grass fires, and collects data through remote monitoring and field sociological research.

name: Lapland State Nature Biosphere Reserve (Лапландский государственный природный биосферный заповедник)
summary: A biosphere reserve in central Murmansk region, 7 km from Monchegorsk, where almost all the territory is untouched nature.

name: Lesokhranitel
summary: Forest fire detection programme built by Formoza Service, partnered with Rostelecom, described as AI-based video monitoring with exact coordinates, with 47 cameras reported in Kurgan Oblast in 2026.

name: Lomonosov Moscow State University
summary: University named in the citation of the Moscow Digital Herbarium and recorded on GBIF as publisher of the Flora of Russia backlog, and it runs the national depository bank of live systems.

name: Losiny Ostrov National Park
summary: National park that Vedomosti reported in February 2026 had joined the environment ministry's pilot with ER-Telecom Holding, with both listed as partners.

name: Manul Working Group
summary: Group of specialists on the manul that runs and built the Small Wild Cats of Eurasia database and uses a faunistics Web-GIS, where Sibecocenter's GBIF record says it has sections.

name: Marine Mammals Research and Expedition Centre
summary: Company that says it organises and runs research projects, and lists organising and running counts among its activities.

name: Marine Research Center of Lomonosov Moscow State University
summary: Marine research company serving oil and gas, according to GBIF, reporting university and Russian corporate founders and listing bird, marine mammal, remote sensing and drone work.

name: MaritimeAI
summary: Developer of AI models for ship control, according to Interfax in 2021, which Yandex Cloud named as a participant in making the Lake Baikal plankton monitoring technology.

name: Meshera National Park (ФГБУ «Национальный парк «Мещера»)
summary: Federal institution whose site presents the Meshera national park in Vladimir region and also the Meshchersky national park in Ryazan region.

name: Ministry of Ecology and Nature Management of the Moscow Region
summary: Regional ministry that, according to an October 2026 report, developed an automatic AI monitoring system for protected natural areas together with Sber.

name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment of the Russian Federation
summary: Federal ministry overseeing three named federal protected areas, which reportedly drew up a programme for robotics and automation of natural resource use to 2036.

name: Ministry of Natural Resources, Forestry and Ecology of Perm Krai
summary: Regional ministry that worked with Innopolis University in 2020 to process space images of nine forest districts with a neural network.

name: Ministry pilot on camera-trap animal recognition
summary: Ministry-run pilot with Losiny Ostrov National Park and Er-Telecom Holding; Vedomosti reports its task as improving camera-trap recognition and counting of wild animals on protected areas.

name: Monitoring of the manul in Sailugem National Park and adjacent areas
summary: Closed manul monitoring project led by Anna Barashkova and Ilya Smelansky, in which participants installed 15 camera traps in the park to estimate manul density, with its area changing in 2019.

name: Monitoring of the manul in South-Eastern Altai
summary: Active camera-trap monitoring project run by the Manul Working Group and Sibecocenter, with volunteers mostly maintaining its network since 2019, according to the Manul Working Group.

name: Mordovsky Nature Reserve
summary: One of seven protected areas in the national camera-trap photo-monitoring network project, where the Severtsov Institute says it will monitor the recovery of mammal communities after fires.

name: MOS AVS (ГКУ МО «МОС АВС»)
summary: A Moscow region state institution associated with 76 peatland rewetting complexes covering about 73,000 ha, 48 percent of the region’s recorded peatland area.

name: Moscow Department of Nature Management and Environmental Protection
summary: City environment department whose head says it has analysed environmental DNA in parks with the Severtsov Institute since 2025, covering 12 areas in the first year.

name: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology
summary: Technical institute that Knife reports had specialists build a neural-network program to analyse camera-trap images in reserves.

name: Moscow parks environmental DNA project
summary: Environmental DNA project in Moscow parks and protected green areas, run by the Severtsov Institute and the Moscow nature department since 2025.

name: Moscow Region protected-area AI monitoring
summary: Proposed protected-area monitoring system, which the ministry described in October 2026 as validated and ready for replication, comparing satellite images, radar readings and other sources to find anomalies.

name: Moscow University Herbarium
summary: University herbarium that Science and Life reported in January 2017 held 786,000 digital specimens open to view, and which started the Atlas of the Flora of Russia project.

name: Mospriroda Moscow City Natural Areas Management (ГБУ «Мосприрода»)
summary: Moscow city institution created in February 2014 to maintain and use the regionally protected green territories and the natural and landscaped areas assigned to it.

name: MSU Digital Herbarium
summary: Digital herbarium dating from 15 October 2016 that Alexey Seregin told Naked Science became a consortium in 2019 and held 1.25 million specimens when interviewed.

name: MTS
summary: Company whose press service says experts at its AI centre developed a computer vision system for recognising animals on camera-trap images.

name: MTS camera-trap recognition in Land of the Leopard
summary: Camera-trap recognition software built by MTS, which its press service said in July 2020 had been installed in Land of the Leopard, with reported accuracy of about 94%.

name: National Depository Bank of Live Systems
summary: Programme run by Lomonosov Moscow State University, whose portal GBIF's record says holds data on 700,000 specimens.

name: National wildlife photo-monitoring network
summary: Project in which seven protected areas are creating a single photo-monitoring system with a common method, led by Sergey Ogurtsov and funded by the Presidential Fund for Nature.

name: Nature and People Fund
summary: Fund led by Sergey Rybakov that says its 2026 programme includes information technology for nature conservation and runs the High Conservation Value Forests of Russia project.

name: Nature Defenders Fund
summary: Fund named by IT Russia as a partner in the audio traps project, and by Yandex Cloud as working on the coast cleaning project with two academic partners.

name: Nenets Nature Reserve
summary: Arctic reserve that, according to the Arctic Fund page, will train AI with MIPT scientists to analyse camera-trap data from walrus haul-outs.

name: Neural-network detection of forest disturbance on Kunashir and Sakhalin
