summary: Russian Science Foundation-funded project, led by Kirill Korznikov, that Naked Science reported in February 2021 trained U-Net-like neural networks on satellite images and masks of windthrow and bark beetle damage from Kunashir and Sakhalin.

name: Nikolai Pertsov White Sea Biological Station
summary: GBIF describes it as an educational and research centre, and its site lists a monitoring collection.

name: Nizhegorodskoe Povolzhye (ФГБУ «Нижегородское Поволжье»)
summary: Federal institution whose site presents the Nizhegorodskoe Povolzhye national park, part of which lies within the Nizhegorodskoe Zavolzhye biosphere reserve and the Kamsko-Bakaldinskie wetlands.

name: Nizhnyaya Kama National Park (ФГБУ НП «Нижняя Кама»)
summary: National park in Tatarstan whose site reports educational work on protecting the forest massifs of the park.

name: Novoorlovsky audio traps
summary: Audio trap system that IT Russia says was started in the Novoorlovsky sanctuary to collect audio files for training neural networks, run by the St Petersburg nature use committee.

name: Obshchestvo Sokhraneniya Dikikh Zhivotnykh
summary: Organisation named as supporting camera monitoring in the park's buffer zone.

name: Open Landscape
summary: Programme which an October 2013 announcement said aimed to strengthen public monitoring of environmental hot spots and heritage sites worldwide, using satellite images managed by crowd-mapping volunteers.

name: Orlovskoe Polesye National Park (ФГБУ «Национальный парк «Орловское Полесье»)
summary: National park of 77,745 ha in north-west Orel region, created in 1994 to preserve a southern Russian taiga community.

name: Pasvik Nature Reserve
summary: One of seven protected areas in the national camera-trap photo-monitoring network project, where the Severtsov Institute says it will assess the effect of engineering structures on mammal migration.

name: Pechora-Ilych State Nature Biosphere Reserve (Печоро-Илычский государственный заповедник)
summary: Komi Republic reserve that received international biosphere reserve status in 1985 and was inscribed on the UNESCO list in 1995 together with Yugyd Va national park.

name: Pelican count neural network
summary: Model that a September 2023 report said analysed quadcopter images to count pelicans, with the team then planning to expand it and a chat-bot into a continuous monitoring tool.

name: Peregrine falcon migration study, Lena Pillars National Park
summary: Project funded by the Nature Defenders Fund to study peregrine falcon flight routes, which Mail.ru, citing Rossiyskaya Gazeta, reports has been launched in Lena Pillars National Park.

name: Photo bank of the protected-area system
summary: A dataset of protected-area photos, free to publish with credit and an accepted offer agreement, built by Roszapovedcentr on a camera-trap neural network and tagging animals and birds from 49 orders.

name: Phytocoenarium
summary: Dataset run by the Komarov Botanical Institute, which says anyone may use its descriptions for joint projects and publications.

name: Plantarium
summary: Online atlas of species and illustrated plant identification key that describes itself as non-commercial and open to additions and corrections.

name: Point No. 1
summary: Baikal monitoring project run continuously since 1945 with more than 5 million records, in which Yandex says a system processed over 250,000 images from 811 samples with 87% zooplankton detection accuracy.

name: Polar-Alpine Botanical Garden-Institute
summary: An organisation in Apatity that GBIF says works on plant acclimatisation and studies the flora and plant communities of the North.

name: Polistovsky Nature Reserve
summary: One of seven protected areas in the national camera-trap photo-monitoring network project, where the Severtsov Institute says it will assess how local residents affect mammals in the reserve and its protected zone.

name: Population Status and Potential Threats to Humpback Whales in Northern Chukotka
summary: Closed project whose 11 May 2020 page planned photo-identification of humpback whales in northern Chukotka, compared against a regional catalogue, to underpin later monitoring for Beringia National Park.

name: Presidential Fund for Nature
summary: A funder that gave grant support to the photo-monitoring project, and which RAPSI reported accepted 2027 grant applications until 30 September 2026 for biodiversity study, conservation or monitoring projects.

name: Prielbrusye National Park (Национальный парк «Приэльбрусье»)
summary: National park that, by its own site's statement, is located in Kabardino-Balkaria.

name: Prioksko-Terrasny State Nature Biosphere Reserve (Приокско-Террасный государственный природный биосферный заповедник)
summary: State institution of the same name that protects and studies the territory of the Prioksko-Terrasny biosphere reserve.

name: Protected Areas of Russia information system
summary: Information system on protected areas whose portal, restored by NextGIS, is read-only and no longer updated, holding content as of May 2024 while a new version is developed.

name: Remote monitoring of forest use in Russia
summary: A programme run by Roslesinforg using Roscosmos data, which covered 546 forest districts and 300 million hectares in April 2024.

name: Research Institute of Biology, Irkutsk State University
summary: Institute running Baikal plankton monitoring since 1945, according to Yandex Cloud, with a neural network reported in 2022 as intended to analyse Baikal water samples.

name: RITM Carbon consortium
summary: A consortium that says it is creating a national system for monitoring the carbon budget of land ecosystems, combining ground measurements, remote sensing and mathematical modelling.

name: Roscosmos
summary: An organisation listed by CEOS with Russia and 1992, reported in April 2024 as supplying high-resolution images for forest monitoring and named as owner of the Digital Earth platform.

name: Roslesinforg
summary: The forest accounting institution of Rosleshoz, which runs the federal forest information system and says a Buryatia, Transbaikal and Amur experiment found neural networks 62% faster and 12% more accurate than people.

name: Rosneft
summary: A company partnering with the natural resources ministry whose Tamura expeditions reportedly took over 90,000 images for future neural network processing, according to a 20 May 2025 report.

name: Rosprirodnadzor Geoportal
summary: A geoportal programme that says AI helps analyse large volumes of satellite images and draws specialists' attention to priority sites.

name: Rosreestr
summary: A federal service whose four-year digitisation review and government subordination Kommersant reported, and which Russia’s UN geospatial report says received geospatial information management responsibilities in 2008.

name: Rostelecom
summary: A company that installed the Lesokhranitel system in Kurgan Oblast and says it supports the system in the Trans-Urals under contracts with the Kurgan forest fire centre.

name: RU-BIRDS
summary: A dataset whose operators say its data are used in scientific projects.

name: RU-BIRDS.RU
summary: A dataset of unknown status, for which the facts given contain only a description by GBIF.

name: Rubius
summary: A company of unknown status, which RIA Tomsk reported in October 2018 had passed the system to a customer in Moscow for testing.

name: RUSSIA-CAMMON
summary: A project that says it aims to form the core of a national camera-trap network on Russian protected areas, funded by the Presidential Fund of Nature, with first work planned for 2026.

name: Russian Arctic National Park (Национальный парк «Русская Арктика»)
summary: A national park covering 8.8 million ha on Novaya Zemlya and Franz Josef Land, two polar archipelagos in Arkhangelsk region.

name: Russian Arctic Vegetation Archive
summary: A dataset joining plant species and vegetation structure data on plots, including historical Soviet data, with 2,873 open-access descriptions and a further 1,912 closed-access plots.

name: Russian Bird Conservation Union
summary: A bird conservation body whose 2026 conference featured a Eurasian crane ringing database developed under its project competition.

name: Russian Centre of Forest Protection
summary: Forest protection centre that in September 2026 described testing trained YOLOv26 and U-Net models on satellite data to find forest changes; it partners with VNIILM and Geoscan.

name: Russian Federal Research Institute of Fisheries and Oceanography
summary: A Russian fisheries and oceanography institute whose Khabarovsk branch is the address of a 2024 chum salmon counting paper, and whose marine mammal sector lists neural network work on photo data and a 2020 to 2024 Ladoga ringed seal aerial survey.

name: Russian Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring
summary: A Russian federal service for hydrometeorology and environmental monitoring, which CEOS lists with Russia and the year 1992.

name: Russian Geographical Society
summary: Society saying it has supported geographical projects since 2009 and regularly gives grants to the White Whale beluga project, which uses satellite tagging, hydroacoustics and aerial survey.

name: Russian Raptor Research and Conservation Network
summary: Non-governmental association, according to its site, whose press organ is the journal Raptors Conservation.

name: Russian satellite animal tracking platform
summary: A proposed platform Kommersant reports the Agency for Strategic Initiatives and Lake Baikal Foundation announced work on as CLS planned to stop serving Russian organisations from 1 November 2026.

name: Russian Science Foundation
summary: Funder of two forest projects: machine learning on satellite images for stand characteristics at Skoltech, and forest cover disturbance recognition with convolutional neural networks at Perm State University.

name: Russky Sever National Park (Национальный парк «Русский Север»)
summary: National park of 168,000 ha in Vologda region, created by Government decision No. 182 of 20 March 1992.

name: Saiga detection network
summary: Model for automated detection and counting of saiga with deep convolutional neural networks, named in an institute paper and built by the Severtsov Institute and ES-PAS.

name: Sailyugemsky National Park
summary: Altai Republic national park where, its director says, staff study snow leopards with camera traps; Yandex said in October 2023 that 24 of Altai's 44 snow leopards lived there.

name: Sailyugemsky National Park camera-trap neural network
summary: Built by Yandex Cloud with the park as partner, this camera-trap model reportedly recognised 10 species, trained on 40,000 objects totalling 150 GB, according to Yandex in October 2023.

name: Sakhalin Energy
summary: Company saying the operators of Sakhalin-2 and Sakhalin-1 have funded a gray whale monitoring programme since 1997.

name: Samarskaya Luka National Park (ФГБУ «Национальный парк Самарская Лука»)
summary: Federal institution with its address in Zhigulevsk, Samara region.

name: Sber
summary: Organisation listed behind a camera-trap monitoring AI use case, which signed a memorandum with the Severtsov Institute on AI models for biodiversity and builds the Sber Biodiversity model.

name: Sber Biodiversity model
summary: Model that Ecotech-Pro says sorts camera-trap images by species, including an other animals category; built by Sberbank, with the Severtsov Institute and Sailyugemsky National Park as partners.

name: Sber camera-trap species classifier
summary: Project run by Sber, described as AI for camera-trap monitoring to classify 25 native species and building on MegaDetector; the ITU entry says code repositories are not public.

name: ScanEx Research and Development Center
summary: Company that USGS says has been private since 1989, with an Irkutsk station and geoportals; it says its Atlantic walrus project with WWF ran yearly from 2011.

name: Scientific Centre for Operational Earth Monitoring
summary: A centre that describes itself as operator of Russian space assets, saying it supplies remote sensing data through the Roscosmos geoportal and a federal data fund created in 2018.

name: SeaVision
summary: Global remote monitoring system that the institute's site reports oceanologists devised, calling it new.

name: Seraya Sheika winter waterbird count
summary: All-Russian winter waterbird count, run by the Russian Bird Conservation Union, announced in a 12 January 2026 report for 17 and 18 January with specialists and birdwatchers taking part.

name: Shirshov Institute of Oceanology
summary: Russian oceanology institute; a news report, citing the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology, says specialists there and at the institute developed a neural network for dolphin whistles, and two authors of a sea surface imagery paper list it.

name: Sibecocenter LLC
summary: Novosibirsk limited company that GBIF describes as a community of wildlife study and conservation experts, and which the Manul Working Group says installed three camera traps in 2016.

name: Siberian AI Centre, Tomsk State University
summary: A Tomsk State University centre whose director said in October 2025 that Sber's hub had started the biodiversity project and the centre would now take it on.

name: Siberian Environmental Center
summary: NGO in whose programme the Manul Working Group says its manul database was first created, and which the group credits for a photograph of a manul in the Altai.

name: Siberian Federal University
summary: Krasnoyarsk university whose authors, all affiliated with it, developed a convolutional neural network model to detect forest fires, according to a 2024 International Research Journal article.

name: Sikhote-Alin State Nature Biosphere Reserve named after K. G. Abramov
summary: Federal state budgetary reserve in Terney, Primorsky Krai, whose site reports camera trap monitoring since 2006 and a science department data series starting in 1936.

name: Sitronics Group
summary: Group that said in December 2021 it was developing satellite and drone monitoring tools, and that its Sputnix part's Zorkiy satellite was in orbit for medium-resolution remote sensing.

name: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology
summary: Its scientists reportedly developed a satellite tree identification algorithm; the Russian Science Foundation reports joint work with Irkutsk and AIRI on tree species, height and forest carbon.

name: Small Wild Cats of Eurasia Database
summary: Database built and run by the Manul Working Group, which gives its address.

name: Smart Forest
summary: Run by Perm Krai’s natural resources ministry, this key digitisation programme reportedly monitored 28 forest districts covering 12.4 million hectares in August 2021.

name: SmartLeo
summary: A GSOM SPbU centre built this archive chatbot, piloted on 1970s Kedrovaya Pad records, with a Far Eastern leopard conservation organisation as project partner.

name: Smolenskoe Poozerye National Park (Национальный парк «Смоленское Поозерье»)
summary: National park created on 15 April 1992 in the Demidov and Dukhovshchina districts of Smolensk region to preserve unique natural complexes.

name: Snow Leopard. Conservation Strategy
summary: Closed project run by the Sayano-Shushensky reserve and funded by the Russian Geographical Society, whose grant report covers scientific observations, including an updated camera-trap layout, and patrols of the reserve.

name: South Kamchatka sockeye salmon monitoring
summary: Project built by Timur Ionov, whose task was a machine learning model to detect sockeye salmon at the counting barrier.

name: Sovzond
summary: Company that lists supplying satellite images for the state forest inventory, naming Roslesinforg as the customer.

name: Space Patrol
summary: A programme named by Sensors and Systems as a public space monitoring system.

name: Space Research Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences
summary: Russian Academy of Sciences institute that lists a section on satellite monitoring of land ecosystems, runs Vega-Science and builds Vega-Pro.

name: SR Data
summary: Sirius says the company develops AI and machine learning solutions for satellite image analysis, and that satellite images can warn of illegal logging.

name: St Petersburg Committee for Nature Use, Environmental Protection and Ecological Safety
summary: St Petersburg environmental committee that IT Russia names as a partner in the audio traps project.

name: St Petersburg State University
summary: University that runs a Centre for Sustainable Territorial Development, named on the SmartLeo page as developer of an AI assistant for Far Eastern leopard conservation, which it built with VTB.

name: State Nature Reserve Nurgush
summary: Nature reserve whose site shows camera-trap footage and whose address GBIF gives.

name: StopBorshchevik hogweed detection service
summary: Service built by Yandex Cloud that, the company says, detects Sosnowsky's hogweed on satellite images.

name: Study of rare animal species (Amur tiger, Far Eastern leopard, snow leopard, polar bear, cetaceans)
summary: Closed Russian Geographical Society-funded project, run by the Severtsov Institute and led by V. V. Rozhnov, studying Amur tiger, Far Eastern leopard, snow leopard, polar bear and cetaceans using methods including satellite telemetry and GIS modelling.

name: Taganay National Park (Национальный парк «Таганай»)
summary: National park whose administration, based in Zlatoust, Chelyabinsk region, issues the permits for visiting it.

name: Tamura
summary: Rosneft's Arctic biodiversity conservation programme, which the company says it intends to carry out through research in northern Krasnoyarsk and the Kara Sea from 2024 to 2027.

name: Teberda National Park (Тебердинский национальный парк)
summary: National park whose administration is in Teberda, Karachay-Cherkessia.

name: Terra Tech
summary: Part of Roscosmos's Russian Space Systems holding; a March 2024 report says it and Roslesinforg had experimented since 2022 with neural networks to detect felling in satellite images.

name: Terra Tech and Roslesinforg illegal logging detection
summary: Project that a September 2022 report says Terra Tech and Roslesinforg were carrying out in Arkhangelsk and Irkutsk regions, using Digital Earth.

name: Thermal Points on Protected Areas
summary: A free early warning web service for possible fires on Russian protected areas and within 10 km of them, launched in 2024 and run by Nature and People Digital Solutions; a 2025 report says it entered test operation on all federal protected areas.

name: Tigirek State Nature Reserve and Salair National Park (Федеральные ООПТ Алтайского края)
summary: The Tigirek reserve was established by Government decision of 4 December 1999 on 40,693 ha in Altai Krai and doubled in 2022.

name: Tomsk State University
summary: A university that says its Siberian AI centre is a joint project with Sberbank, runs a biodiversity research project, and says its scientists use AI to estimate carbon cycling at a Tomsk region test site.

name: Transparent World
summary: A Russian NGO founded in 2000 by its account, with a stated mission supporting conservation through GIS and satellite images, named an Open Landscape founder in 2013.

name: TSU plankton recognition network
summary: A neural network built by Tomsk State University; an August 2023 report says it was intended for a photostimulation method and mentions discussions with regional governments about possible observatories.

name: Ugra National Park (Национальный парк «Угра»)
summary: National park covering 98,624.5 ha, managed since 2012 by a federal institution under the Ministry of Natural Resources, with UNESCO biosphere reserve status since 2002.

name: Ussuriysky State Nature Reserve named after V.L. Komarov (Уссурийский заповедник имени В.Л. Комарова)
summary: Nature reserve named after the botanist Vladimir Komarov, who first described the territory after visiting it in 1913.

name: Valdai National Park (Национальный парк «Валдайский»)
summary: National park created in 1990 to preserve the lake and forest complex of the Valdai Hills.

name: VEGA-PRO
summary: A project, built by the Space Research Institute RAS, that describes itself as a professional information service for monitoring renewable biological resources from satellite data.

name: VEGA-Science
summary: A project run by the Space Research Institute RAS and led by Evgeny Lupyan, which says it gives distributed access to long, daily-updated satellite archives on northern Eurasian vegetation cover.

name: Visimsky Nature Reserve
summary: One of seven protected areas in the national camera-trap photo-monitoring network project, where the Severtsov Institute says it will study how windfalls affect mammal populations.

name: VK Cloud
summary: An organisation on whose platform the pelican count network was developed.

name: VNIRO chum salmon drone count
summary: A paper project on automating counts in drone photographs with neural networks, linked to V. V. Sviridov as builder.

name: Volcanoes of Kamchatka Nature Parks (КГБУ «Природный парк «Вулканы Камчатки»)
summary: Organisation that carries out state control of the regional protected areas of Kamchatka: the Bystrinsky and Nalychevo nature parks and the Kol River salmon sanctuary.

name: Volzhsko-Kamsky National Nature Biosphere Reserve
summary: A Russian nature reserve whose site carries an item on camera-trap recordings.

name: Voronezh State Nature Biosphere Reserve (Воронежский государственный природный биосферный заповедник имени В.М. Пескова)
summary: Biosphere reserve on the Voronezh and Lipetsk region border, whose territory covers the northern half of the Usman forest massif.

name: Web-GIS Faunistics
summary: An interactive system for entering and showing observations of animals and plants, with a photo bank, launched in version 1.0 on 2 March 2013 and included in GBIF in December 2016.

name: WildHack
summary: A closed hackathon, run by Kronotsky State Nature Reserve, that ended in December 2021 with 102 teams, about 500 people, and a student neural network for recognising animals and removing empty camera-trap frames.

name: Wrangel Island State Reserve (Государственный заповедник «Остров Врангеля»)
summary: Federal state budgetary institution that is the Wrangel Island reserve, administered from Pevek, Chukotka, and described by its own site as one of Russia's northernmost reserves and a UNESCO World Heritage site.

name: WWF Russia
summary: An organisation that the Moscow Times reported in June 2023 must stop work in Russia at once under the undesirable label, and whose press service described an open forest monitoring system in 2020.

name: Yandex Cloud
summary: Cloud provider that published Baikal monitoring code in December 2022, reports plankton analysis work, and helped build snow leopard analysis tools and a hogweed detection service.

name: Yu. A. Izrael Institute of Global Climate and Ecology
summary: Russian research institute whose main goal, hydrobiological monitoring guidance and address are given by GBIF.

name: Yugra State University
summary: University whose station site lists the Mukhrino field station, an ecosystem geoinformatics laboratory and a 2025 item on assessing tree stands with unmanned aircraft.

name: Yugyd Va National Park (Национальный парк «Югыд ва»)
summary: National park formed in the Komi Republic by Government decision No. 377 of 23 April 1994 to preserve natural objects and complexes of the Northern and Subpolar Urals.

name: Zapovednaya Osetiya-Alania (Joint Directorate of the North Ossetian Reserve and Alania National Park)
summary: Joint directorate whose site presents the federal protected areas of North Ossetia-Alania, over 85,000 ha, comprising the North Ossetian reserve, Alania national park and Tseyskiy sanctuary.

name: Zapovedniki Taimyra (Joint Directorate of Taimyr Reserves)
summary: Joint directorate of Taimyr reserves whose site reports land held by the institution in permanent (indefinite) use and describes work in the Putorana reserve.

name: Zapovednoe Podlemorye
summary: Organisation whose site reports autumn field work with camera traps in the Barguzinsky reserve.

name: Zapovednoe Posolstvo Fund
summary: Fund whose digital products director presented Zelyonaya Knopka at COP17 in October 2026 and which reported 33,000 electronic passes issued through it in 2025.

name: Zapovednoe Priamurye (Joint Directorate of State Nature Reserves and National Parks of Khabarovsk Krai)
summary: Federal institution, based in Khabarovsk, named as the joint directorate of state nature reserves and national parks of Khabarovsk Krai.

name: Zapovednoe Pribaikalye (Joint Directorate of Baikalo-Lensky Reserve and Pribaikalsky National Park)
summary: Joint directorate of the Baikalo-Lensky reserve and Pribaikalsky national park, created in 2014.

name: Albertine Rift Conservation Society
summary: Regional NGO founded in 1995, based in Kigali, awarded $196,075 by JRS for 2011 to 2013 biodiversity portal work, whose database JRS reported held 824 observation records.

name: ARCOS Biodiversity Information Management System
summary: Biodiversity data portal built by the Albertine Rift Conservation Society on GBIF, which JRS reports launched on 25 October 2014 and gives access to Albertine Rift species checklist and occurrence data.

name: Assessing Population Status, Threats and Conservation Strategies for the Hooded Vultures in Busaga Forest, Muhanga District, Rwanda
summary: Proposed Rufford Foundation project, dated 3 June 2026, planning monthly surveys and nest monitoring at Busaga Forest, described as Rwanda's only confirmed hooded vulture breeding site.

name: Assessing Temporal Changes in Species Composition and Vegetation Structure in Rugezi Marsh Using eDNA, sedaDNA and Drone-Based Remote Sensing
summary: Project on species composition and vegetation change in Rugezi Marsh using eDNA, sedaDNA and drones, listed on the Rufford Foundation's Rwanda projects page under Placide Masengesho, dated 22 December 2025.

name: Biodiversity Monitoring in Rwanda (ACCF Rwanda Project, Volcanoes National Park)
summary: Project run by the African Community and Conservation Foundation in which conservation officers use camera traps, set up in agreement with Volcanoes National Park, and record bird species to inform a biodiversity management plan.

name: Biological surveys of the Gishwati Forest
summary: Closed project, February to September 2017, funded by CEPF with a $14,874 grant to the Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund International, to assess trigger species and record baseline data on less-studied species.

name: Building Awareness and Community Support for Bat Conservation in Muhanga and Gisagara Districts
summary: Rufford Foundation-listed project, dated 22 November 2025, that plans to map bat roosts in two districts using GPS and community knowledge, with field surveys to support national biodiversity databases.

name: Centre for Geographic Information Systems and Remote Sensing, University of Rwanda
summary: Active University of Rwanda centre whose researchers, with Rwandan forestry and space agency authors, appear on a 2026 paper on national scale tree counting by remote sensing.

name: Centre of Excellence in Biodiversity and Natural Resource Management
summary: Rwandan government institution hosted at the University of Rwanda, working on research, monitoring and conservation education, and digitising specimen collections through the Rwanda Biodiversity Specimen Portal.

name: Community Education, Monitoring and Conservation of Eidolon helvum in Rubavu and Nyabihu Districts
summary: Proposed Rufford Foundation project in Rubavu district, dated 16 March 2025, planning regular Eidolon helvum monitoring and a trained network of local conservation guardians.

name: Community-Based Ecological Monitoring of Critically Endangered Hooded Vulture in Rwanda
summary: Project listed by the Rufford Foundation, dated 18 March 2021, under Prudence Ndabasanze, who is also named for a later Busaga Forest hooded vulture project dated 28 November 2022.

name: Consolidating the Conservation of Critical Bat Species Through Community Participation and Ecological Monitoring in Northern Rwanda
summary: Proposed Rufford Foundation project in Susa, dated 13 December 2025, planning to scale up bat monitoring through tagging and faecal analysis, after earlier work set up bat guardian cooperatives.

name: Developing a Dragonfly Biotic Index and Applying it to Prioritizing Restoration Sites within the Congo-Nile Crest Watershed in Rwanda
summary: Project of unknown status, listed by the Rufford Foundation in 2017, to develop a dragonfly-based monitoring tool for habitat recovery; a 2019 report said a preliminary scoring system existed.

name: Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund
summary: Organisation running the Karisoke Research Center that reported in December 2023 two decades of biodiversity monitoring using camera traps, acoustic devices and vegetation plots in gorilla habitats.

name: Drivers Human-Wildlife Conflict: Investigating Factors Behind Rising Chimpanzee Incursions into Banda Rutiritiri Villages Western Rwanda
summary: Rufford Foundation-listed study, dated 7 December 2025, planning surveys, interviews, camera traps and GIS mapping of forest patches and pathways chimpanzees may use outside the park, with a March 2026 progress update.

name: Enhancing Community-Based Ecological Monitoring in Volcanoes National Park
summary: African Wildlife Foundation project aiming to complete an eDNA baseline survey across 30 sites in and around Volcanoes National Park, with a first training held in February 2026.

name: Enhancing Pollinator Dynamics and Conservation for Improved Ecosystem Health and Services in Key Agro-Ecological Landscapes in Rwanda
summary: JRS-funded project, with funding from July 2025 to June 2027, that JRS says will begin with seasonal field surveys of pollinator diversity across ten agroecosystems.

name: Establishing a scientific baseline and capacity for effective conservation management of threatened freshwater fauna in Akagera NP, Rwanda
summary: Grant of $10,000 from the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, awarded 25 May 2023 for Rwanda, to survey freshwater taxa in Akagera and set up monitoring by African Parks staff, with partners Senckenberg and African Parks.

name: Exploring new habitats for the better conservation of the endangered Harrison's giant mastiff bat in Rwanda
summary: Project funded by a $7,500 Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund grant, awarded 14 March 2024, that used acoustic monitoring and nets to identify roosts of Otomops harrisoni and other cave bats in Rwanda.

name: Forest Monitoring and Evaluation System
summary: Mobile app and web platform recording forest boundaries and inventory data across Rwanda, built by Arbonaut with Enabel support and released in 2020, with a Luxembourg-funded upgrade planned.

name: Forest of Hope Association
summary: Active association whose 2025 year in review reports monitoring Gishwati's primates, including ongoing monitoring and habituation of chimpanzees, and says this will continue.

name: Freshwater biodiversity of Rwanda, data recorded from theses of students of University of Rwanda (UR)
summary: GBIF dataset, built by the University of Rwanda's CoEB, digitised from graduates' theses as part of the African Biodiversity Challenge, recording freshwater biodiversity in Rwanda.

name: Gorilla Doctors
summary: Organisation that says it monitors nearly 800 human-habituated mountain and Grauer's gorillas daily across five national parks in Rwanda, Uganda and the DRC.

name: Habitat Restoration, Monitoring, and Community Engagement for the Conservation of Bats in Urban Areas of Southern Province of Rwanda
summary: Closed project that, according to its 2024 description, planned continued bat monitoring and refresher training for local bat champions in urban areas of Rwanda's Southern Province, building on an earlier pandemic-era project.

name: ICF/EWT/IPRC-Kitabi Partnership (Rwanda)
summary: According to an International Crane Foundation report, the partnership developed crane monitoring protocols and conducted crane monitoring and baseline wetland assessments at Nyabarongo and Akanyaru, with CEPF support.

name: Identifying Felids Ranging Out Park Boundaries, Assessing their Impacts on Community Properties Around Nyungwe National Park and Proposing Mitigation Measures
summary: Closed project, dated 29 July 2020 by the Rufford Foundation, that planned 27 camera traps at 342 points over one year to assess felids suspected of attacking livestock near Nyungwe.

name: International Gorilla Conservation Programme
summary: Coalition of Conservation International, Fauna & Flora International and WWF, based in Kigali, which in a January 2020 post reported deploying about 29 camera traps in Volcanoes National Park.

name: Interspecies Money
summary: Tehanu-built project piloted on 20 mountain gorillas in Volcanoes National Park, giving them digital wallets linked to AI facial recognition, and offering rural people payment for wildlife-recording tasks.

name: Karisoke Research Center
summary: Programme run by the Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund and led by Felix Ndagijimana, which says over 100 trackers protect about half of Rwanda's mountain gorilla families daily.

name: Mapping Roosting Habitats of Straw-Coloured (Eidolon helvum) Fruit Bats in Kigali City and Rwamagana District and Enhancing their Conservation
summary: Closed project, dated 4 September 2017 by the Rufford Foundation, that planned to map straw-coloured fruit bat roosts in Kigali and Rwamagana and estimate the population.

name: Ministry of Environment (Rwanda)
summary: Government ministry describing itself as coordinating Rwanda's environment and natural resources sector, with responsibilities including developing laws and regulations to protect the environment and conserve natural ecosystems.

name: Nation-wide map of tree-level aboveground carbon stocks in Rwanda
summary: National dataset mapping carbon stock of individual trees in Rwanda, built by the University of Copenhagen and Maurice Mugabowindekwe; a 2022 release reported over 350 million trees mapped, with natural forests holding about 51% of tree carbon.

name: National Land Authority (Rwanda)
summary: Rwandan government agency that manages and regulates land use and mapping, and creates and maintains maps and geospatial databases on land use, infrastructure and natural resources.

name: NaturAfrica – Nyungwe-Kibira Landscape
summary: EU-financed project (31 March 2025–18 March 2028), budgeted at €2,803,738, planning improved park management and biodiversity monitoring, with Rwanda Forestry Authority and National Land Authority partners.

name: Nature Rwanda
summary: Rwandan non-profit based in Musanze that, per GBIF's publisher record, generates and shares biodiversity data, and says it monitors vulture populations across Rwanda.

name: Non-Primate Mammalian Wildlife Abundance and Distribution in Africa's Youngest National Park, Gishwati-Mukura NP in Rwanda
summary: Closed camera-trap project, listed by the Rufford Foundation in January 2017, that aimed to quantify carnivore and ungulate abundance in Gishwati-Mukura National Park for the first time, with 16 camera traps budgeted.

name: Nyandungu Eco-Park biodiversity survey (2025)
summary: Closed 2025 biodiversity survey of Nyandungu Eco-Park, carried out by RCID, reported to show bird species rising from 83 to 158 since a 2023 baseline.

name: Nyungwe Management Company Ltd
summary: Company named in Nyungwe’s 2023 report, which records 80 camera traps purchased, 37 data collectors trained and chimpanzee and colobus behavioural data collected through EarthRanger.

name: Participatory Action Research in the Protection of Carnivores and Livestock for Sustaining Humans-Wildlife Coexistence Around Gishwati-Mukura National Park
summary: Rufford Foundation-listed participatory research project, dated 5 June 2025, that trains communities in camera trap use and plans better carnivore monitoring through collaboration between park management and local residents.

name: Reducing External Pressure and Improving Management of Nyungwe National Park
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, 1 July 2018 to 31 October 2019, whose final report says it established SMART for law enforcement and camera trap and population monitoring in Nyungwe.

name: Reducing Human–Mountain Gorilla Conflict and Risky Interactions through Community Education and Gorilla Scout Networks
summary: Proposed Rufford Foundation project in Kinigi sector, Musanze district, dated 3 December 2025, that plans community scouts to monitor mountain gorilla movements and report early incursions at conflict hotspots.

name: Regional Research Centre for Integrated Development
summary: Rwandan research and consultancy firm, called RCID by The New Times, which says it carried out the 2025 Nyandungu Eco-Park biodiversity survey.

name: Rugezi Marsh Biodiversity Survey
summary: First comprehensive biodiversity survey of Rugezi Marsh, whose preliminary findings, released by the Rwanda Wildlife Conservation Association on 20 September 2024 and reported by The New Times, documented 638 species.

name: Rwanda bat roost mapping and monitoring
summary: Mongabay reported in April 2025 that Paul Webala and Rwanda Development Board researchers were mapping Egyptian fruit bat roosts for protection and disease surveillance.

name: Rwanda Biodiversity Information System
summary: National biodiversity system developed by CoEB with JRS funding, launched on 24 March 2023 according to JRS, with over 30,000 records mobilised according to CoEB.

name: Rwanda Biodiversity Specimen Portal
summary: Symbiota-based portal holding Rwandan specimen data, images, observations and species inventories, in partnership with CoEB and the Rwanda Biodiversity Conservation Institute, with funding from Biocultural Diversity International.

name: Rwanda bird sound recording citizen science
summary: Citizen science project run by CoEB at the University of Rwanda since 2019, which Mongabay reported had logged over 120,000 bird recordings, made with phones and an app it says uses artificial intelligence.

name: Rwanda Development Board
summary: Body listing tourism and conservation among its services, which Huawei says signed an IUCN memorandum committing Rwanda's four protected areas to Green List evaluation.

name: Rwanda Environment Management Authority
summary: Rwandan environmental authority, supervised by the environment ministry, with the legal mandate for national environmental protection and conservation, which says it publishes a State of Environment report every four years.

name: Rwanda Forestry Authority
summary: Rwandan authority that Digital Earth Africa says oversees forest management and restoration, and which uses the Forest Monitoring and Evaluation System; in 2024 twenty field technicians were trained on Digital Earth Africa tools.

name: Rwanda hooded vulture GPS tracking
summary: Project run by Nature Rwanda, reported on 8 February 2026, in which nine GPS trackers were deployed in December 2025 on vultures at Kigali and Musanze abattoirs, with tagged birds tracked in real time.

name: Rwanda National Satellite Data Programme
summary: National satellite data programme launched by the Government of Rwanda and Planet Labs, run by the Rwanda Space Agency, which government bodies are to use to monitor agriculture and forest health, per a 10 August 2026 press release.

name: Rwanda National Spatial Data Infrastructure Hub
summary: National open platform launched in November 2021, built and run by the National Land Authority, that hosts and publishes harmonised fundamental geospatial datasets from different institutions.

name: Rwanda Nature Foundation
summary: Newly approved foundation which, The New Times reported in July 2026, will oversee management of Volcanoes and Gishwati-Mukura national parks.

name: Rwanda Space Agency
summary: Rwandan agency that, Space in Africa reported, signed a 2023 UNOSAT agreement on satellite imagery and geospatial data, including environmental monitoring.

name: Rwanda Waterbird Counts
summary: Citizen science initiative counting waterbirds in Rwandan wetlands; Wetlands International reports that the January 2026 count recorded 2,871 waterbirds of 58 species across 12 wetlands.

name: Rwanda Wildlife Conservation Association
summary: Rwandan conservation organisation, established in 2015 from a grey crowned crane project, which says it has counted over 54,581 straw-coloured fruit bats and piloted GPS tags on them with Max Planck Institute support.

name: Rwanda's Annual National Crane Census
summary: Annual Grey Crowned Crane census run by RWCA, whose 2021 account reports yearly surveys since 2017, counting 487 cranes in 2017 and 881 in 2020.

name: Rwanda's wetlands biodiversity data from different inventories that were conducted between year 2008 and 2017
summary: GBIF dataset compiled from reports of wetland biodiversity inventories carried out by REMA and partners between 2008 and 2017, with the compilation facilitated by CoEB and technical support from ARCOS.

name: Smart Park in Akagera National Park
summary: Project in Akagera National Park that Smart Parks says it is creating with African Parks, quoting an African Parks staff member saying the technology improved vehicle and field staff management.

name: Supporting Community Rangers at Rugezi Marsh Key Biodiversity Area in Rwanda
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund and run July 2018 to September 2019, that planned to train local rangers to monitor grey crowned cranes at Rugezi Marsh using CyberTracker.

name: Tehanu
summary: Africa-based start-up that The New Times reported in November 2024 created the interspecies money system.

name: Understanding and Reducing Roadkills Resulting from Animal-Vehicle Collisions on the Highway Traversing Nyungwe National Park in South-Western Rwanda
summary: Project dated 8 October 2019 by the Rufford Foundation that aims to set up a monitoring programme for animal-vehicle collisions in Nyungwe National Park, with park rangers trained to lead it.

name: University of Rwanda
summary: Rwandan university under which the government established CoEB, and which GBIF's record says is digitising and publishing its natural history specimen collections data and images.

name: Using Ecological Integrity Assessment to Guide Wetlands Management in Rwanda
summary: Closed JRS-funded grant, led by Sam Kanyamibwa from December 2018 to November 2020, which planned to assess wetland ecological integrity and publish 4,600 new species records to GBIF.

name: Volcanoes National Park carnivore camera-trap pilot
summary: Closed pilot, reported by the Fossey Fund in April 2013 and run and built by it, using five loaned camera traps in Volcanoes National Park that photographed five carnivore and four herbivore species.

name: WCS Rwanda Program
summary: Run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, which reported in 2020 that researchers deployed 54 arboreal camera traps with ground cameras in Nyungwe National Park.

name: AI Center of Excellence (AIEWA)
summary: Programme run by the environment, water and agriculture ministry to lead AI solutions in those sectors, using generative AI, machine learning and computer vision, with vegetation cover and protected area initiatives.

name: AI Eco-360 Analytics Platform
summary: Built by SenseTime MEA, this coral reef digital twin integrated over 1,000 devices across 18 categories and could identify 15 species, SenseTime said in December 2025.

name: Arabian Leopard Initiative
summary: Partnership between Panthera and the Royal Commission for AlUla, begun in 2019, to recover the Arabian leopard, which Panthera says included training rangers in camera trapping in the Sharaan reserve.

name: Arriyadh Development Authority
summary: Saudi public body that directed the 2001 Wadi Hanifah restoration plan near Riyadh, acting as the High Commission's executive arm, with native plants grown from locally collected cuttings and seeds installed along the wadi bed.

name: Bajdah Wildlife Reserve Monitoring Pilot
summary: A pilot study in NEOM, Saudi Arabia, described in a paper as a local-scale case study, using 20 monitoring stations with camera traps and acoustic recorders, with AI preprocessing the files.

name: Benthic biodiversity across the NEOM region
summary: KAUST-built project begun in 2023 to assess the environmental quality of 15 NEOM coral reefs and inventory reef biodiversity using visual surveys, DNA barcoding and eDNA metabarcoding.

name: Biodiversity & Ecosystem Management Lab
summary: A KAUST-run lab that monitors reef cryptobenthic communities with long-term ARMS devices and studies non-native marine species in Saudi waters, and that builds a benthic biodiversity project for the NEOM region.

name: Coral Probiotics Village
summary: Underwater research laboratory in the central Red Sea off the Saudi coast, led by Prof. Raquel S. Peixoto, testing coral restoration with nurseries, sensor networks and AI-assisted monitoring.

name: Coral Reef Baseline Assessment
summary: A planned three-year Red Sea-wide coral reef baseline survey in Saudi waters, run and built by the General Organization for Conservation of Coral Reefs and Turtles in the Red Sea.

name: Coral Research and Development Accelerator Platform
summary: Says it was launched by the G20 and is the only international body fully dedicated to funding coral research and development; KAUST describes it as headquartered there.

name: Coral-AI
summary: KAUST-built automated system that delivers beneficial microorganisms to corals, with bleaching detection at the edge, using image processing, AI and extra reef environment sensors to judge coral health.

name: Council of Royal Reserves
summary: Body set up by royal decree to set strategic directions for the royal reserves and resettle wildlife; it approved 2030 goals in August 2023, covering seven reserves that Saudipedia reports as 13.5 percent of the Kingdom's area.

name: Decade Land Expedition for Terrestrial Ecosystem Exploration
summary: Expedition launched by the National Center for Wildlife, according to Fast Company Middle East, to document Saudi land biodiversity and create a national database and interactive maps of species and sites.

name: digiLab
summary: Partner of KAUST’s coral restoration initiative whose technology, KAUST says, will cut monitoring from two months to two weeks, with chatReef to manage a 22-petabyte digital twin.

name: eCoral
summary: KAUST-built digital twin combining AI and machine learning analytics for coral restoration, scenario modelling and decisions, with AI reef health assessments and drone-based coral health surveillance.

name: Environment Fund
summary: A funder that Al Riyadh Daily reported signed a funding agreement with CORDAP in August 2025 for coral reef protection and restoration research, and which CORDAP lists as a partner.

name: FalconViz
summary: Company with offices in Jeddah and at the Science & Technology Research Park in Thuwal, whose Gharsa page describes drone and AI services for reforestation.

name: General Authority for Survey and Geospatial Information
summary: A Saudi authority that says its regulations task it with regulating the surveying, geospatial information and imaging sector, and that it provides open geospatial data for reuse.

name: General Organization for Conservation of Coral Reefs and Turtles in the Red Sea
summary: A Saudi government body in Jeddah protecting Red Sea reefs and turtle nesting sites, issuing research permits and developing a reef baseline survey expected to take three years.

name: Generalised machine learning model for long-term coral reef monitoring in the Red Sea
summary: 2024 paper proposing a generalised machine learning approach to monitor Red Sea coral cover over 2000 to 2018, using a support vector machine trained on Landsat data and validated against Umluj ground truth.

name: Gharsa
summary: A reforestation and land management platform for Saudi Arabia and the GCC, built by FalconViz, that uses AI on drone imagery to track vegetation change and count plants.

name: Imam Abdulaziz bin Mohammed Royal Reserve Development Authority
summary: A Saudi reserve authority founded in 1439H to protect biodiversity in two royal reserves, whose 2024 annual report lists animal sound recognition and an AI wildlife monitoring device in King Khalid Royal Reserve.

name: Imam Faisal bin Turki Royal Reserve
summary: Royal reserve established by royal order in 2023 across three regions and Red Sea waters, spanning 30,152.7 km2 including territorial waters, overseen by the Council of Royal Reserves and aiming to protect biodiversity and endangered species.

name: Imam Saud bin Abdulaziz Royal Reserve
summary: Royal reserve created by a 2018 decree from the Mahazat as-Sayd Protected Area, about 180 km from Taif, overseen by the Council of Royal Reserves, where Arabian oryx and other species have been released since 1990.

name: Imam Turki bin Abdullah Royal Reserve Development Authority
summary: A Saudi reserve authority set up by royal order in 2018, which International Business Magazine reported in June 2023 launched a drone monitoring project using more than 40 drones within a digital system including AI.

name: KAUST and digiLab AI for coral conservation
summary: Announced in July 2025, this KAUST–digiLab coral AI partnership envisaged two years of integration and a 22-petabyte digital twin to be managed by digiLab’s chatReef.

name: KAUST Beacon Development
summary: An environmental consultancy at KAUST, run by the university, which KAUST reported in November 2024 had specialist researchers using AI to process drone survey footage of marine megafauna habitats.

name: KAUST Coral Restoration Initiative
summary: A KAUST-run Red Sea coral restoration programme, in collaboration with NEOM, that uses the eCoral AI platform and aims to restore 100 hectares of reef at Shushah Island.

name: KAUST Hydrology, Agriculture and Land Observation Lab
summary: A KAUST-run lab led by Matthew McCabe whose researchers reported developing satellite methods for mapping mangrove distribution and health in 2024, following fieldwork reported in 2022.

name: KAUST Reefscape Restoration Initiative
summary: A KAUST-run project, part of its Coral Restoration Initiative, to restore about 100 hectares of reef around Shushah Island by 2040, with plans to incorporate data and AI into a working model.

name: King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology
summary: A science and technology body whose Earth & Space Science Institute provides satellite imagery and consulting, with a wildlife research centre listed by the CBD.

name: King Abdulaziz Royal Reserve Development Authority
summary: A Saudi reserve authority which Al Riyadh Daily reported in February 2026 had deployed 103 camera traps, producing the first confirmed golden jackal record in the reserve and central Saudi Arabia.

name: King Abdulaziz University
summary: A Saudi university in Jeddah whose geomatics researchers authored a 2026 paper on monitoring mangrove deforestation with Google Earth Engine and a random forest machine learning algorithm.

name: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
summary: A graduate research university at Thuwal on the Red Sea, established in 2009, that runs the KAUST Coral Restoration Initiative and builds Coral-AI and eCoral for coral monitoring.

name: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals
summary: A Saudi university with research on mapping Gulf mangroves using Sentinel-2 imagery and predicting phytoplankton absorption coefficients using ensemble machine learning models.

name: King Faisal University
summary: A university with co-authors on a 2024 paper listed by OpenAlex introducing a dataset and ensemble deep learning approach for plant classification in Saudi Arabia.

name: King Khalid Royal Reserve
summary: Royal reserve of about 720 km2, approved on 2 October 2019 as a conversion of al-Thumamah Wildlife Park, overseen by the Council of Royal Reserves and including the King Khalid Wildlife Research Center.

name: King Khalid University
summary: A university whose authors, according to OpenAlex, published 2021 papers predicting Asir land cover using a neural network and modelling ecosystem health in Saudi Arabia.

name: King Salman bin Abdulaziz Royal Reserve Development Authority
summary: Saudi reserve authority that Ajel reports received an IUCN technological innovation certificate and, with stc through Huawei's Tech4Nature, introduced AI-based smart camera monitoring of wildlife.

name: King Saud University
summary: Saudi education body listed in OpenAlex, with 2026 papers on vegetation trend prediction using neural networks and ensemble models, and on identifying behavioural states from movement data.

name: Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture
summary: Saudi national entity for the environment, water and agriculture sectors, formed in 2016; Saudi Gazette reported its minister launching AI and remote sensing vegetation monitoring in August 2023.

name: Nabat
summary: An organisation whose NabatOS combines AI, geospatial analytics and field ecology, with a Saudi coastal assessment using AI land cover classification to identify mangrove planting potential.

name: National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification
summary: Saudi centre established by Council of Ministers decision 417 to oversee grazing lands, forests and national parks and combat desertification; it built a vegetation monitoring programme and partners with KAUST.

name: National Center for Wildlife
summary: Saudi wildlife body set up in 2019, replacing the Saudi Wildlife Authority, with a KAUST memorandum of understanding; Makkah Newspaper reports it used GIS, drones and AI to map baboon hotspots.

name: NCVC Citizen Science Program
summary: An active programme, run by the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification, inviting the public to photograph biodiversity at vegetation sites to help find species and monitor plant health.

name: Neo Space Group
summary: Wholly owned PIF space company announced in 2024, describing itself as Saudi Arabia's national space company and launching the country's first earth observation data marketplace, powered by UP42, which it owns.

name: NEOM
summary: Saudi giga project spanning 26,500 square kilometres, carrying out habitat restoration, species reintroduction and marine conservation; Asharq Al-Awsat reported over 1,100 animals of six species reintroduced by June 2025.

name: NEOM and OceanX Red Sea expedition
summary: Six-week Red Sea expedition by NEOM and OceanX with 30 experts, which 3D-mapped about 1,500 square kilometres of seabed over 42 days; findings announced in October 2021 informed marine protected area design.

name: NEOM Flora Program
summary: NEOM programme launched in 2021 to document local vegetation; in December 2024 NEOM said it had documented 345 plant species, including 28 rare and eight not previously recorded in the Kingdom.

name: NEOM Marine Megafauna Drone Surveys
summary: Marine survey project run by KAUST Beacon Development and funded by NEOM; KAUST reported in November 2024 an AI model processing 180,000 first-phase images to detect dugongs, turtles, dolphins, sharks and rays.

name: NeoMaps
summary: Geospatial platform built by Neo Space Group and launched by NSG Geospatial Services, reported to monitor Red Sea shorelines, mangrove forests, vegetation health and water availability in arid regions.

name: Prince Mohammed bin Salman Royal Reserve
summary: Reserve of about 24,500 square kilometres in north-west Saudi Arabia that reported over 100 trail cameras in February 2025, with camera trap data used with Special Forces for Environmental Security against poaching.

name: Red Sea Coral Bleaching Remote Sensing Tool
summary: A satellite-based tool built by KAUST researchers that maps Red Sea coral bleaching severity at ten metre resolution, described as an early warning system and published in 2025.

name: Red Sea coral reef health detection system (YOLOv8 and YOLOv9)
summary: A proposed deep learning system, built by Afnan Aldhahri, using YOLOv8 and YOLOv9 on 10,285 labelled images to assess Red Sea coral health, detect early bleaching and notify authorities.

name: Red Sea Decade Expedition
summary: An expedition run by OceanX with NCW and KAUST researchers, which OceanX says mapped mesophotic and deep-sea reefs, established a biodiversity baseline and contributed seafloor maps.

name: Red Sea Global
summary: A regenerative developer that, in a 2025 conference presentation, aimed for a 30% net conservation benefit and described its Environmental AI platform as nearing full deployment.

name: Red Sea Research Platform
summary: A KAUST-run research platform that says it integrates remote sensing and real-time environmental monitoring with sequencing tools, and lists coral reef monitoring and habitat mapping projects in the Arabian region.

name: ReefNetAI
summary: A platform that describes itself as monitoring coral reefs with AI image recognition and environmental data, offering AI-assisted segmentation of reef imagery, and was in beta at version 0.4.0.

name: Royal Commission for AlUla
summary: A body that says it manages the Sharaan reserve with rangers, partners with IUCN and Panthera, and uses EarthRanger, which Design Middle East reports covers 12,160 square kilometres.

name: RSG Environmental AI Platform
summary: A programme run by Red Sea Global that, per its presentation, applies AI to reef camera and vehicle data, drone imagery and turtle acoustics, and was nearing full deployment in 2025.

name: SARsatX
summary: A KAUST spin-off founded in 2019 that operates small radar and optical satellites, plans a 16-satellite constellation, offers the AI platform EarthLife, and reportedly raised a $2.6 million seed round in 2025.

name: Saudi Space Agency
summary: A space agency that lists satellite system development among its roles and, Sabq reported in May 2026, observed increased vegetation cover at Arafat between 2024 and 2026 using satellite images and AI.

name: SAUDINet
summary: A national ecological observation network built by KAUST and NCVC, intended to collect standardised long-term biodiversity, vegetation, soil and climate data and train NCVC staff in monitoring.

name: Sea Turtle Populations Assessment
summary: A proposed initiative, built by the General Organization for Conservation of Coral Reefs and Turtles in the Red Sea, to assess Saudi Red Sea turtle populations and map critical habitats.

name: Sedrah Accelerator Program
summary: An accelerator SeaCras says the environment ministry runs through EWAx, prioritising water quality, biodiversity and desertification, with SeaCras among 10 start-ups selected for 2026.

name: SenseTime MEA
summary: Introduced the AI Eco-360 Analytics Platform in December 2025, according to SenseTime, which describes it as a coral reef 3D digital twin system.

name: Shamal Technologies
summary: A company that develops AI around its aerial operations, including detection models for environmental monitoring that flag habitat features or species indicators in coastline and vegetation surveys.

name: Smart Orbits
summary: A Saudi company describing itself as offering geospatial services, remote sensing and space AI, using radar and multispectral sensors and in-house machine learning for soil moisture, vegetation and geology.

name: stc
summary: A telecoms company whose collaboration with the King Salman reserve, through Huawei's Tech4Nature initiative, Ajel reports introduced an AI-based smart monitoring system.

name: Terrestrial High Resolution Habitats Map of the Red Sea Project
summary: An active 2025 to 2026 project run by the BioDeserts research group, funded by Red Sea Global, aiming to produce a high-resolution habitat map from fine-detail remote sensing data.

name: Towards AI Accelerated Reef Ecology Practice: Expert-informed Benchmarks and Machine Learning Systems for Coral Reef 2D/3D Visual Understanding
summary: A project of unknown status, funded by NEOM under an OSSARI grant, which the ReefNet paper credits as its funding and which was awarded to Elhoseiny, Jones and Benzoni.

name: Tree Geo Data
summary: A B2B climate tech start-up that announced itself in January 2025 for Saudi afforestation, combines planting with AI monitoring, and says its software identifies tree species with 98% accuracy.

name: Umm Al-Qura University
summary: A university whose College of Computing hosts all five authors of a 2025 paper using deep learning and computer vision to assess coral reef health.

name: UNDP and NCVC Five-Year Strategic Agreement on Land Restoration
summary: A five-year agreement between UNDP in Saudi Arabia and NCVC, announced in May 2025, on land restoration and nature-based solutions, including digital solutions and data in land monitoring.

name: Unified Habitat Classification System in AlUla County
summary: An active 2025 to 2026 Earth observation and remote sensing project run by the BioDeserts research group and funded by the French Agency for AlUla Development.

name: Vegetation Cover Monitoring and Evaluation Programme
summary: Programme built by the vegetation cover centre, launched, Saudi Gazette reported in August 2023, to monitor vegetation with remote sensing and AI; Ajel reports it covers over 99,000 square kilometres.

name: Vision Transformer model for near-infrared estimation in dryland vegetation mapping
summary: Vision Transformer model built to estimate near-infrared bands from Maxar satellite images to improve dryland vegetation identification, validated against SkySat near-infrared imagery with an R2 of 0.92.

name: Yadgreen
summary: A company with a Khobar office providing green and blue carbon plantations using drones, and listing AI-based bird tracking and protection and drone-based planting monitoring.

name: Arnavons Community Marine Conservation Area
summary: Formed in 1995, the Solomon Islands' first community-based marine protected area labelled and relocated nests in 2016; TNC reported hawksbill nests more than doubling in 20 years.

name: Arnavons hawksbill turtle satellite tracking study
summary: Closed satellite tracking study of hawksbill turtles, reported by The Nature Conservancy, in which Fastloc trackers showed Arnavons turtles returning to South Pacific foraging grounds, an average migration of 2,028 kilometres.

name: Babatana Rainforest Conservation Project
summary: A forest conservation project in South Choiseul, led by the Natural Resources Development Foundation, where landowner rangers patrol transects and boundaries to monitor forest loss, under a monitoring plan developed to meet the Plan Vivo Standard.

name: Census and Classification of Plant Resources in the Solomon Islands
summary: A plant survey project ongoing since 2012, which collected over 15,000 specimen sheets of about 700 vascular plant species in 2012 and 2013.

name: East Rennell invasive rat control and monitoring project
summary: A rat control and wildlife monitoring project run by BirdLife International, in which IUCN says rangers from four villages were trained, including about twenty women since mid-2023 monitoring bait consumption.

name: Ecological Solutions, Solomon Islands
summary: Solomon Islands organisation funded by CEPF, whose founding members were named for hire on the East Makira project, and whose CEPF final report describes a baseline multi-taxa biodiversity survey of a corridor.

name: Establishment of a Ranger Program to Monitor Key Flora and Fauna of Hahorarumu-Uru
summary: A closed ranger programme, led by Edgar Pollard, planned in 2017 to have 12 rangers in four teams monitor palms, vines, Vitex trees and frogs, with the work later moving to Ainapo and Hounamae.

name: Integrated Forest Management in the Solomon Islands
summary: A GEF-funded project, run by two government ministries and partnered with FAO, aiming to help the government manage protected and productive forest landscapes; UN-REDD says its earlier monitoring work formed the foundation for FAO's support.

name: Isabel Province leatherback turtle monitoring and satellite tagging
summary: An active turtle monitoring project in Isabel Province, partnered with The Nature Conservancy, which says it and partners have satellite-tagged turtles since 2022, with rangers patrolling Haevo beach at night.

name: Islands Knowledge Institute
summary: A charitable trust incorporated in 2008 and based in Honiara, which Awana Digital reports led CoMapeo trainings for ranger groups in Western Province in 2026 and equipped them with phones, power banks and GPS devices.

name: Kolombangara Island Biodiversity Conservation Association
summary: Described by CEPF in 2015–2016 as focused on terrestrial monitoring, its rangers reportedly attended CoMapeo training and adapted categories into Duke in 2026, according to Awana Digital.

name: Mai-Maasina Green Belt
summary: A project in Malaita Province spanning thirty tribal communities, which trained local rangers to lead biodiversity monitoring and mapping with the MAPEO application, completing four months of data collection from March to July 2024.

name: Ministry of Environment, Climate Change, Disaster Management & Meteorology
summary: A Solomon Islands government ministry based in Honiara, whose GBIF publisher record describes a mission of safeguarding sustainable natural resource use and lists four published datasets.

name: Ministry of Forestry and Research
summary: A Solomon Islands government ministry named by the GEF as an executing agency of the Integrated Forest Management project, whose forest division director is the UN-REDD Programme focal point.

name: Natural Resources Development Foundation
summary: A local NGO established in 2003, funded by CEPF and the Rufford Foundation, whose CEPF-funded project from July 2018 to January 2022 involved ranger monitoring trips and a revised forest inventory methodology.

name: Sobehatunga forest inventory and ranger monitoring, MCC-Solomon Islands Threshold Program
summary: An active forest inventory and ranger monitoring project partnered with the Natural Resources Development Foundation, where MCC reported over 800 hectares prepared and rangers receiving forest inventory training.

name: Solomon Islands Community Conservation Partnership
summary: Locally established NGO in Honiara, funded by CEPF, that managed project funds and supports a network of community-based organisations; a monitoring protocols handbook was developed.

name: Solomon Islands community-led ranger monitoring network
summary: A community-led ranger monitoring network led by the Islands Knowledge Institute, in which CoMapeo field records feed Remoto; in Kira, rangers photographed logging damage after satellite analysis detected it, and this went into a report to the Ministry of Environment.

name: Solomon Islands National University
summary: Established under the SINU Act 2012 in Honiara, its team reportedly presented on forest monitoring assessment in March 2026 with EFI support, according to the Solomon Islands Rangers Association.

name: Tetepare Descendants' Association
summary: An association formed by descendants of Tetepare's former inhabitants to protect the island when commercial logging threatened it.

name: The Project on Capacity Development for Sustainable Forest Resource Management in the Solomon Islands
summary: A closed project from September 2017 to August 2022, run by the Ministry of Forestry and Research and funded by JICA, which classified national land cover maps using SEPAL.

name: UN-REDD support to the Solomon Islands national forest monitoring system
summary: A UN-REDD Programme effort begun in 2017 to establish a national forest monitoring system and reference emission level, including Collect Earth training for a national forest and land use change assessment covering 2000 to 2016.

name: Wai-Hau Conservation Foundation Inc.
summary: Rural community-based conservation organisation incorporated in 2010 and funded by CEPF, with reported ranger and mobile phone app leatherback monitoring and a draft management plan reported in November 2020.

name: WCS Solomon Islands
summary: An active programme run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, with offices in Munda and Honiara, whose 2021 release describes reef monitoring around Marovo Lagoon with Zaira community rangers and 2016 surveys around Kolombangara.

name: WWF-Solomon Islands
summary: A WWF-Pacific country programme set up in 1996 in Honiara, which works with community rangers on reef health monitoring and reports 20 rangers trained as of March 2024.

name: Zaira Resources Management Area
summary: Community-based organisation established in 2012 to protect tribal lands in South Vangunu, whose rangers reported patrols, monitoring and drone photography of logging between January and October 2023.

name: A Ridge to Reef Approach for the Integrated Management of Marine, Coastal and Terrestrial Ecosystems in the Seychelles
summary: Project listed by SPGA with GOS-GEF-UNDP as donor, running 2019 to 2026, aiming to cut biodiversity threats by strengthening marine protected areas and forested key biodiversity area management; run by SPGA, funded by the Global Environment Facility.

name: Aldabra Atoll dugong drone survey
summary: Drone survey run by the Seychelles Islands Foundation, reported in May 2024 as the first lagoon-wide survey around Aldabra to image dugongs, with images showing 19 dugongs by that report.

name: Aldabra long-term monitoring programme
summary: Programme run by the Seychelles Islands Foundation monitoring Aldabra's climate, plants, birds, tortoises, turtles, coconut crabs and marine ecosystems, with turtle monitoring since the 1960s and reef monitoring launched in 2013.

name: Alphonse Underwater Tracking Observatory
summary: Acoustic receiver network around the Alphonse Group, planned in September 2021 to become permanent and monitor more species, with fifteen milkfish tagged by February 2022.

name: Annual giant Aldabra tortoise census on Curieuse Island
summary: Annual Aldabra giant tortoise census on Curieuse Island, run by the Seychelles Parks and Gardens Authority, which reported 16 tortoises measured, sexed and tagged by 25 February 2026, with data held in EarthRanger.

name: Annual Seychelles Paradise Flycatcher census on Curieuse Island
summary: Annual Seychelles Paradise Flycatcher census on Curieuse Island, run by the Seychelles Parks and Gardens Authority, which used recorded calls to attract birds and documented sixteen in July 2024.

name: App for Reserve Management (ARM), Cousin Island Special Reserve
summary: Closed Nature Seychelles project to build a custom data management app for Cousin Island Special Reserve, planned over 18 months from late 2024, with GPS tracking, real-time data input and central storage.

name: Assessing the effectiveness of Curieuse Marine National Park in the protection of sicklefin lemon sharks
summary: Closed GVI Seychelles telemetry project that tagged 19 sicklefin lemon sharks over 18 months, logging 292,107 detections, and concluded the park size was sufficient to protect the neonates studied.

name: Assomption Island biodiversity baseline assessments
summary: Closed set of biodiversity assessments of Assomption Island, run by the Seychelles Islands Foundation, which a drone survey of 21 zones (1,792 hectares, over 39,000 images) mapped invasive plants, chiefly sisal.

name: Bringing Bats off the Brink (Seychelles sheath-tailed bat)
summary: Active Nature Seychelles project monitoring sheath-tailed bat roosts on Mahé to evaluate threats and the cause of decline, following monitoring begun in 2004 that found two previously unknown roosts.

name: Building capacity in Seychelles to advance marine monitoring and ecosystem management to increase climate resilience
summary: Closed project led by the James Michel Blue Economy Research Institute and funded by CEPF, using remote imagery to study marine ecosystems and build Seychelles' capacity for remote imagery assessments.

name: Centralised Multi-relational Bio-holistic Database for Improved Management of Marine Protected Areas
summary: SPGA project running 2023 to 2026, funded by the Seychelles Conservation and Climate Adaptation Trust, to modernise and centralise its conservation and monitoring data through digital field collection and a central database.

name: Checklist and distribution of the species of Seychelles for conservationists
summary: GBIF dataset aiming to share a nationally agreed species index for Seychelles with conservation, invasiveness and distribution data, building on an existing database; the first version covers plants only, with extension planned.

name: Coral restoration alters reef soundscapes but machine learning and manual analyses suggest different recovery rates
summary: Closed PLOS ONE study of a restoring reef's sounds at Cousin Island Special Reserve, compared with healthy and degraded reefs using manual fish-sound counts and machine learning; Nature Seychelles calls it Seychelles' first reef soundscape recordings.

name: D'Arros Research Centre
summary: Research centre run by the Save Our Seas Foundation which, in June 2016, described four long-term monitoring projects on turtles, reef manta rays, coral reefs and climate around D'Arros and St Joseph Atoll.

name: Developing a freshwater biodiversity information system for long-term conservation and management in the Seychelles
summary: Closed project planned for April 2023 to April 2026 to build a freshwater biodiversity database through 15 river surveys including eDNA, with data intended for GBIF and other databases.

name: Developing Tools and Knowledge for Key Biodiversity Area Management and Delineation in Seychelles Using New IUCN International Standards
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, running March 2018 to December 2020, that aimed to develop an online, accessible plant database for Seychelles Key Biodiversity Areas and strengthen a network of contributors and users.

name: Enhancing Marine Conservation through Technology in the Seychelles
summary: Active SPGA-led project, under a 2025 agreement with the CBD Secretariat, expanding AI cameras that detect nesting turtles and send detections to EarthRanger, plus ranger training for species monitoring and invasive species mapping.

name: Gaea Seychelles
summary: Research and citizen science organisation launched in 2018, funded by the JRS Biodiversity Foundation for a planned April 2023 to April 2026 river project collecting freshwater biodiversity data for monitoring and GBIF.

name: Green Islands Foundation
summary: Seychelles-registered NGO that surveyed the marine environment around Denis and North Islands in late 2015, and whose standard monitoring methods a 2019 to 2020 Fregate Island project planned to use.

name: Hifadhi Blu - Developing and Enhancing a Robust Data Management Framework for Effective Marine Park Governance
summary: Active SPGA project, funded by WIOMSA and running 2025 to 2027, building staff skills in research, ecological monitoring, data collection and analysis across its five marine protected areas.

name: Indian Ocean Tortoise Alliance
summary: Seychelles-based non-profit working on Aldabra giant tortoise research, monitoring and translocations, funded by CEPF for a November 2023 to September 2026 project to eradicate black rats from Curieuse Island.

name: Island Biodiversity and Conservation Centre, University of Seychelles
summary: Joint venture of the University of Seychelles and an NGO, launched in 2016, with turtle and seabird monitoring projects and two CEPF-funded projects; SPGA says a 2025 agreement is supported by a $280,000 CEPF grant.

name: Island Conservation Society
summary: Not-for-profit registered in April 2000, monitoring seabirds, turtles and marine ecosystems on Aride and Alphonse, which opened its sixth conservation centre on Astove in May 2023.

name: James Michel Blue Economy Research Institute
summary: University of Seychelles institute formed in 2015, listed by CEPF as grantee for a June 2023 to June 2026 ocean observation and marine monitoring project in five marine protected areas around Mahé.

name: Kingsgate Electronics
summary: Local company that Nature Seychelles names as one of two it joined to build conservation technology; its current status is unknown.

name: Mapping ecosystem types and land cover types in the Seychelles granitic islands, using Earth Engine and Sentinel-2
summary: Dataset on Zenodo under a CC BY 4.0 licence, including a 10 m Sentinel-2 land cover classification of the granitic islands, built by Bruno Senterre and funded partly by the Seychelles Government and GBIF.

name: Marine Biodiversity Baseline assessment around Fregate Island
summary: Closed project run by the James Michel Blue Economy Research Institute, planned for 2019 to 2020, to set up long-term coral reef monitoring at Fregate Island using GIF methods and Coralive.org spatial monitoring technology.

name: Marine Conservation Society Seychelles
summary: Founded in 1997, with whale shark work including identification by spot patterns and satellite tagging, and an annual monitoring season listed as 1 August to 31 October.

name: Marine megafauna distribution and abundance at Aldabra Atoll via UAV survey
summary: Closed study that Seychelles Nation reported in August 2025 as the first dedicated assessment of marine megafauna at Aldabra by drone, covering 49 western lagoon grid squares for turtles, sharks, rays and dugongs.

name: MCSS community-based cetacean monitoring programme
summary: Active community-based monitoring programme, run by the Marine Conservation Society Seychelles with SeyCCAT support, building baseline data on which whales and dolphins occur, with public photo sightings feeding a national dataset.

name: Ministry of Agriculture, Climate Change and Environment (Seychelles)
summary: Seychelles ministry that, with UNDP, engaged three specialists for studies supporting the national biodiversity strategy, and is named an implementing partner of the Global Biodiversity Framework Early Action Support project.

name: National sooty tern census, Seychelles (2021)
summary: Closed June 2021 census of eight islands, run by the environment ministry, which found the sooty tern population had fallen by 60%, using egg counts, colony mapping, vegetation data and remote sensing.

name: Nature Protection Trust of Seychelles
summary: Non-profit registered in Seychelles in 1992, focused on Silhouette Island, which received a Mohamed bin Zayed grant in August 2009 to establish monitoring for four Seychelles frog species.

name: Nature Seychelles
summary: Organisation founded in 1998 as BirdLife Seychelles, managing Cousin Island Special Reserve, which runs and built the Smart Island System with OceanLabs Seychelles and developed the NEST and DREAM devices, backed by Huawei and Tech4Nature.

name: Next-Gen Conservation: Huawei-IUCN Tech4Nature project in Seychelles
summary: Seychelles part of the Huawei and IUCN Tech4Nature initiative, run by Nature Seychelles, using NEST to transmit turtle nest data over LoRa and DREAM diver sensors for reef restoration.

name: Ocean's Resolve
