summary: SeyCCAT-run programme funded by the Global Fund for Coral Reefs, which SeyCCAT says financed the Status and Trend of Seychelles' Coral Reefs 2026 report and supports reef-positive business development.

name: OceanLabs Seychelles
summary: Local tech company, status unknown, that Nature Seychelles says it developed the NEST and DREAM monitoring devices with, and which is linked as a builder of the Smart Island System.

name: OceanX Seychelles 2024 expedition
summary: Closed expedition run by OceanX from 13 January to 11 February 2024, led by 12 Seychellois researchers, which mapped 22,555 square kilometres of the EEZ, made 125 baited video deployments and collected 206 eDNA samples.

name: Plant Conservation Action group
summary: Voluntary membership NGO, described in 2012 as run by an elected committee, which CEPF names as grantee of a 2018 to 2020 project for an online plant database for Seychelles Key Biodiversity Areas.

name: Population estimate of the Critically Endangered Seychelles endemic giant bronze gecko, Ailuronyx trachygaster
summary: Project of unknown status, funded by a 4,980 US dollar grant awarded on 10 March 2024, aiming at a first island-wide census estimate of the giant bronze gecko and training local monitoring staff.

name: Quantitative and Semi-quantitative survey of the vegetation of Seychelles through stand scale plots
summary: GBIF dataset compiling vegetation plot surveys of 73 sites on Mahé and Silhouette, built by Bruno Senterre, to describe Seychelles vegetation and evaluate ecosystems for a Red List of Ecosystems.

name: Sea Turtle Tracking Study in Ste Anne Marine National Park
summary: Closed 2020 to 2022 study run by the Island Biodiversity and Conservation Centre and funded by the European Commission, aiming to improve knowledge of hawksbill turtle origins and movements in the Western Indian Ocean.

name: Seychelles Conservation and Climate Adaptation Trust
summary: Trust fund describing itself as the leading one in Seychelles, investing in marine conservation and climate adaptation, reported in 2021 as coordinating the seagrass mapping project and listed as donor to SPGA's database project.

name: Seychelles Holistic Biodiversity Database (Bio)
summary: National biodiversity database called Bio, which a GBIF record says grew from a 2011 to 2013 herbarium digitisation project and, with smartphone tools since 2013, from 23,000 to 48,000 records.

name: Seychelles Islands Foundation
summary: Public trust established by the Seychelles government in 1979, now managing Aldabra and the Vallée de Mai, with Aldabra monitoring including a marine programme launched in 2013.

name: Seychelles Manta Ray Project
summary: Project partnered by the Island Conservation Society, Save Our Seas Foundation and Manta Trust, which a February 2022 update described as monitoring reef manta spatial ecology and population dynamics in the outer islands.

name: Seychelles Marine Spatial Plan Atlas
summary: Dataset created from 2014 to support marine spatial planning and zoning design, letting stakeholders share and view Seychelles spatial data, with maps visualising the marine ecosystem and human uses.

name: Seychelles Parks and Gardens Authority
summary: Body responsible for Seychelles' marine and terrestrial national parks and gardens, using EarthRanger and, as of August 2026, an expanded network of AI-assisted cameras in Sainte Anne Marine National Park.

name: Seychelles Seabird Group
summary: Programme whose member organisations' monitoring datasets from five nesting sites fed a paper giving the first nationwide assessment of white-tailed tropicbird breeding success, led by April Burt.

name: Seychelles Seagrass Mapping and Carbon Assessment Project
summary: Closed 2020 to 2022 project, led by the University of Oxford and funded by the Pew Charitable Trusts, that planned to map seagrass using satellite imagery and field data and estimate stored carbon.

name: Seychelles Warbler Research Group
summary: Active research programme led by four university researchers with Nature Seychelles, drawing on over 30 years of continuous monitoring and more than 80 published papers on the Seychelles warbler.

name: Smart Island System
summary: Programme run by Nature Seychelles in which two locally co-designed devices were used: NEST, recording turtle nest conditions in 2023-24, and DREAM, which collected seawater data on dives in January 2024.

name: The importance of Seychelles for blue whales and other whales and dolphins
summary: Active project using acoustic methods and boat-based visual surveys to study blue whales and other cetaceans, particularly around D'Arros Island and St Joseph Atoll, funded by the Save Our Seas Foundation and led by Jeremy Kiszka.

name: Tracking Pelagic Sharks around Alphonse
summary: Satellite-tracking project built and run by the Island Conservation Society, aiming to fit 10 tags to five shark species, with seven deployed at the time of the news item.

name: Tracking Red-footed Booby (Sula sula)
summary: Closed GPS tracking study led by the Island Conservation Society and funded by SeyCCAT, in which devices on 54 red-footed boobies were all recovered, giving 110 foraging tracks.

name: University of Seychelles
summary: University that formed the Blue Economy Research Institute in 2015, has offered a BSc in Environmental Sciences since 2012, and provides logistical and administrative support to the Island Biodiversity and Conservation Centre.

name: Use of Satellite Telemetry on Pelagic Seabirds (Juvenile Sooty Terns) to Identify Potential Marine Protected Areas
summary: Closed project led by Rachel Bristol and funded by SeyCCAT, which planned to satellite-tag juvenile sooty terns over two years and shared the resulting maps with the Seychelles Marine Spatial Plan team.

name: Wetlands of Hope
summary: Two-year EU-funded project run by Nature Seychelles, closed at a ceremony on 27 May 2026, with outcomes including assessments at six wetland sites, the WETSAPP app, an updated National Wetlands Policy and a management plan template.

name: WETSAPP (Wetland Evaluation and Tracking Seychelles app)
summary: Active offline wetland monitoring app in English and Creole, rolled out by Nature Seychelles in May 2026 with the environment ministry, built by Jessica Nasica, with tiered dashboards, species mapping and single-click AI reporting.

name: White-tailed tropicbird tracking study, Aride Island
summary: Active study, reported in July 2026, tracking white-tailed tropicbirds from Aride across both monsoon seasons, led by the Island Biodiversity and Conservation Centre with two partners.

name: 2020 national land cover map of the Republic of Sudan
summary: Land cover map of Sudan made at 10 m resolution in Google Earth Engine from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data, which FAO describes as an important step towards REDD+ readiness.

name: Department of Forest and Environment, Faculty of Forest Science and Technology, University of Gezira
summary: University department in Wad Madani listed as an affiliation by the first author of a 2024 Sentinel-2 analysis of land use and cover change in the Kas locality, Darfur.

name: Department of Forest Management Science, Faculty of Forest Sciences and Technology, University of Gezira
summary: Forest sciences department in Wad Medani, listed by the first author of a paper on mapping and monitoring land use change in the gum arabic belt in conflict-disturbed areas.

name: Department of Forest Management, Faculty of Forestry, University of Khartoum
summary: University department in Khartoum North listed as an affiliation by the first author of a paper evaluating two ecological indices for monitoring forest degradation in Sudan's drylands.

name: Department of GIS and Cartography, University of Khartoum
summary: Department in Khartoum listed by the first author of a paper on Google Earth Engine based forest monitoring and decision support at Elrawashdah Forest, Sudan.

name: Dinder National Park large mammal distance sampling survey, 2021
summary: A closed March 2021 distance sampling survey of 56 line transects around Gelego camp in the park's core area, which confirmed large cattle herds illegally inside and reported declining wildlife numbers over five decades.

name: Dinder-Alatash lion survey
summary: Born Free and WildCRU’s survey, led by Hans Bauer, reported Dinder-Alatash lions in 2017 and estimated up to 183 lions and 198 hyenas in Dinder in 2018.

name: Dungonab Bay manta ray research
summary: The Deep reports leading research with Equipe Cousteau and partner Red Sea University, gathering manta ray behaviour, habitat and population data in Dungonab Bay for five years.

name: Forests National Corporation
summary: State-owned Sudanese corporation that, according to Sudan's 2021 MRV system document, develops and implements the REDD+ MRV system and collects information for the national greenhouse gas inventory.

name: Gums for Adaptation and Mitigation in Sudan (GAMS)
summary: An ongoing GCF-funded project with FAO as accredited entity, which kept remote sensing and satellite monitoring of vegetation change going in 2025 while field restoration was suspended because of insecurity.

name: Higher Council for Environment and Natural Resources
summary: Sudanese body that issued the Fifth National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity in 2014, and which PERSGA says it organised a July 2025 Port Sudan workshop with on marine species action plans.

name: Red Sea University
summary: Sudanese university whose team, according to ICRI, carried out a February 2023 mission off Port Sudan on 3D mapping of shallow coral reefs with machine learning developed at EPFL.

name: Remote Sensing and Seismology Authority
summary: Sudanese authority that Sudan's MRV document lists among relevant national institutions, with a role in applying remote sensing to natural resources, and lead affiliation on a 2025 paper on forest tree volume from radar.

name: RESSOURCE Project in Sudan, Khor Abu Habil Inner Delta
summary: A project run by the Sustainable Wildlife Management Programme, which has carried out waterbird censuses and socio-economic appraisals at the delta since 2017, leading to its Ramsar designation on 10 April 2022.

name: Sanganeb and Dungonab Bay coral reef monitoring programme
summary: An active coral reef monitoring programme for two marine national parks, set up with African Parks Foundation support, restarted by Red Sea University staff with PERSGA support, with monitoring in 2022, 2023 and 2024.

name: Strengthened Protected Areas System and Integrated Ecosystem Management in Sudan
summary: Active 2020 to 2027 project run by HCENR and funded by the GEF and UNDP with a US$23,608,913 budget, investing in ecological monitoring in three parks and in the Wildlife Conservation General Administration.

name: Sudan National Forest Inventory
summary: Sudan's national forest inventory, designed with stratified sampling of 705 sampling units, with the first completed in 1998 and a recent one in 2017 to 2018 covering mostly the subnational reference level states.

name: Sudan National Forest Monitoring System
summary: Run by Forests National Corporation, the programme is named in Sudan’s MRV document, which describes inventories, remote sensing activity data and a previous forest inventory completed in 1998.

name: Sudanese Wildlife Society
summary: Sudanese NGO that the March 2018 RESSOURCE newsletter describes as a partner in waterbird identification and monitoring, working with ONCFS on the International Waterbird Census in Sudan.

name: Support for the design of the MRV System in the framework of REDD+ (Sudan)
summary: Closed FAO-listed project, code UTF /SUD/079/SUD, that ended on 30 July 2021 and supported the design of a monitoring, reporting and verification system for REDD+ readiness in Sudan.

name: Unique Corals of Sudan: Development and Application of an Environmental DNA (eDNA) Protocol for Coral Diversity and Community Structure
summary: Fellowship project, November 2025 to June 2026, under Osama S. Saad, aiming to develop an environmental DNA protocol for monitoring Sudan's coral reef, with testing planned in HIFMB laboratories.

name: University of Gezira
summary: Public university founded in 1975 in Wad Madani, Gezira State, whose departments appear in author affiliations for papers on satellite-based forest degradation and conflict-related land use change.

name: University of Khartoum
summary: Public university in Khartoum, described as Sudan's largest and oldest, whose departments are listed on papers on machine learning tree species mapping and Google Earth Engine forest monitoring.

name: University of Sennar
summary: Sudanese university that the March 2018 RESSOURCE newsletter names among the partners that worked with ONCFS to conduct the International Waterbird Census in Sudan.

name: Wildlife Conservation General Administration
summary: Sudanese body named in the March 2018 RESSOURCE newsletter as a partner in the International Waterbird Census, and receiving institutional capacity investment from UNDP's protected areas project.

name: Wildlife Research Center
summary: Sudanese government body in Khartoum North, listed in wildlife papers, reported by Tour du Valat as participating in waterbird surveys, and identified as needing capacity building.

name: AAK
summary: A company headquartered in Malmö that committed to a verified deforestation-free palm oil supply chain by 2025 and uses Satelligence.

name: Abisko Scientific Research Station
summary: Research station run by the Swedish Polar Research Secretariat that collects environmental and climate data, some since 1913, and whose Abisko-Stordalen ICOS station won the Best ICOS Ecosystem Station Award 2026.

name: Agenda for the Landscape
summary: A closed project run by Metria and funded by Vinnova, from November 2018 to August 2019, which set out conditions for continuously updated landscape data and long-term management of NMD.

name: AI cameras for fish migration in Säveån
summary: Active project funded by Sportfiskarna, partnering with the University of Gothenburg, with AI underwater cameras installed at Jonsered in June 2026 to follow Säveån fish migration.

name: AI map of Swedish forests with high conservation value
summary: Active machine learning map covering 22 million one-hectare areas in Sweden with at least 50 percent forest, showing probability of high conservation value, built on 128 open geographic variables and validated with independent data.

name: AI Sweden
summary: Sweden's national centre for applied AI, working not-for-profit from offices in eight cities, which lists the Baltic seabird dataset and partners with Stockholm Resilience Centre.

name: AlertSat
summary: An active programme built by PandionAI, which says it can detect changes anywhere on Earth, with a forestry service covering forests, green spaces and managed landscapes.

name: AMIME
summary: A Formas-funded project that ran from January 2023 to December 2025, aiming to improve monitoring of marine phytoplankton and microzooplankton using AI-assisted automated imaging and eDNA metabarcoding.

name: Arboair
summary: An organisation that in November 2022 surveyed forests by drone and analysed high-resolution images with AI, offering automated digital forest inventory with tree-specific data.

name: Artfakta
summary: An active dataset of species facts, developed and managed by the Swedish Species Information Centre (SLU Artdatabanken), which both builds and runs it.

name: Articulating Complexity
summary: An active programme led by Guillaume Chapron that uses AI to model systems behind species conservation and biodiversity governance, with SEK 5,933,566 from Formas for its Conservation foresight project.

name: Artificiell Intelligens ska kartlägga naturvärden
summary: A Vinnova-funded project run by Ecogain, with unknown status, in which AI is to be trained to recognise places likely to hold nature values.

name: Artportalen
summary: A dataset and website for reporting and searching observations of Swedish plants, animals and fungi, built and run by SLU Artdatabanken, with 95% of data coming from individuals and NGOs.

name: Askö Laboratory
summary: Stockholm University-run laboratory that serves as a base for national environmental monitoring projects, with regular water and seabed measurements since 1968 and a real-time oceanographic buoy deployed seasonally.

name: AukLab
summary: An active project led by Jonas Hentati-Sundberg and funded by WWF Sweden, using deep learning video detection that generated 144 million bird detections over 2019 to 2021, now expanded to acoustic recordings, according to its partners.

name: Automated environmental monitoring with sailing drones
summary: Unmanned sailing drone project, funded by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences and Stockholm Resilience Centre, that aimed to test processing large datasets on board, planned to end 30 June 2024, possibly extended.

name: Bafication AB
summary: An organisation named as the technology developer on Ground-Eye.

name: Baltic Sea Information on the Acoustic Soundscape
summary: A project led by the Swedish Defence Research Agency, with unknown status, described in April 2013 as a first attempt to map human-induced underwater noise in the Baltic Sea.

name: Baltic Seabird Centre
summary: A proposed project, described as a vision for a new research station on Stora Karlsö, where the page says AI plays an increasingly important part in research.

name: Baltic seabird dataset
summary: An active dataset of 2,000 hours of guillemot video from a ledge on Stora Karlsö, with annotated frames, available to AI Sweden partners and used by SLU with AI to automate behaviour documentation.

name: Baltic Seabird Project
summary: An active project led by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, using video surveillance, AI and sensors to study seabirds on Stora Karlsö, with 144 million detections over the 2019 to 2021 breeding seasons.

name: BalticMicrobeDB
summary: An active dataset run by KTH Royal Institute of Technology, which SBDI describes as an interface for metagenomics data of the Baltic Sea.

name: BAYeFISH
summary: Project, led by Rebecca Whitlock, to build a hierarchical Bayesian model for electrofishing data and a Shiny web tool, funded by the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency for March 2025 to February 2028.

name: BearKin: Förbättrade metoder för att övervaka stora rovdjur
summary: Project funded by the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency, among eight starting in 2026 sharing just over SEK 23 million for 2026 to 2028.

name: Beijer Institute of Ecological Economics
summary: An international research institute under the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, which partners with AI Sweden and Stockholm Resilience Centre and announced a June 2019 partnership to explore AI's biosphere sustainability dimensions.

name: Bifångst av skyddade arter i fisket
summary: Project led by Sara Königson, funded by the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency for March 2025 to February 2028, to detect bycatch and quantify and quality-check boat camera footage.

name: BIODENCITY
summary: Project running from 2025 to 2028 using AI, acoustic and visual monitoring, microbiological sampling and citizen science in Gothenburg, Amsterdam, Milan and Tampere, with Formas funding Chalmers participation.

name: Biodiv
summary: AI-based habitat mapping from satellite data, with a platform bringing together surveying, processing, calculation and monitoring of biodiversity in Nordic nature.

name: Biodiversity and Ecosystem services in a Changing Climate
summary: A research programme that says it is a cooperation between Lund University and the University of Gothenburg, with 2 universities, 20 departments and more than 300 researchers.

name: Biodiversity Data Lab
summary: A lab run by Uppsala University and led by Tobias Andermann, whose stated mission integrates environmental DNA, remote sensing and machine learning, with funding listed from SciLifeLab and Wallenberg.

name: Biologisk mångfald mitt i stan: en "timescape garden" in Norrköping
summary: Closed project, run by KTH Royal Institute of Technology and funded by Vinnova from October 2021 to September 2024, that tested an AI-based method for mapping diversity and built a training database.

name: Biophotonic Sensing Group
summary: A group run by Lund University that says a network of sensors is being deployed across Scandinavia.

name: BIOSCANN
summary: A deep-learning segmentation model for forests of high biodiversity value.

name: Biosfärkontoret Kristianstads Vattenrike
summary: Biosphere office that runs the work of the Kristianstads Vattenrike biosphere reserve, formed in 2005 and covering two thirds of Kristianstad municipality, which is its principal (huvudman).

name: Biosfärområde Voxnadalen
summary: Biosphere organisation whose legal principal, Ovanåker municipality, provides staff and support for a coordinating office; Ovanåker, Ljusdal, Bollnäs and the Swedish EPA fund the office's basic operations.

name: Biosfärområde Vänerskärgården med Kinnekulle
summary: The biosphere organisation of the Vänerskärgården med Kinnekulle biosphere reserve, run as a non-profit association, with daily operations handled by the biosphere office in Mariestad town hall.

name: BioSonic
summary: An organisation describing itself as AI bat sound analysis for ecologists, whose own model identifies bird and bat species from sound and was used in some of Sweden's first biodiversity credit projects in 2024.

name: BirdLife Sverige
summary: Its 2025 annual report lists surveys, follow-up and research on threatened species and habitats among its strategies.

name: BLADE
summary: A closed project, led by Eric Capo, that aimed to collect Swedish lake water samples for environmental DNA using a waterproof drone with a water sampler, from May 2025 to April 2026.

name: Bloom 2.0
summary: A project led by Stadskupan, partnering with IVL Svenska Miljöinstitutet, that maps biodiversity from honey and pollen from urban hives.

name: Botkyrka kommun
summary: Municipality named as the manager (förvaltare) of the Stora träsket nature reserve.

name: Brockmann Geomatics Sweden AB
summary: A Swedish company whose 2012–2013 project investigated satellite-based monitoring of Lake Bolmen's water quality to support water treatment.

name: Báste cearru sameby
summary: One of nine Sami villages that, with the county board, the Swedish EPA and two municipalities, make up the association formed to manage the Laponia World Heritage site.

name: Capture
summary: A platform combining manual metadata management with automatic image recognition through AI and machine learning, built by Sweco, SLU, the Swedish Transport Administration and NINA, and funded by Vinnova.

name: Chalmers Applied Artificial Intelligence group
summary: A research group whose AI applications include forestry and marine ecosystems.

name: Chalmers University of Technology
summary: A university whose research played a key role in developing the Biomass mission.

name: Climate AI Nordics
summary: A registered Swedish non-profit association describing itself as Nordic researchers developing AI and machine learning for climate mitigation and adaptation, including rewilding and rewetting decisions.

name: Combine
summary: A company founded in 2002 with a Gothenburg address, reporting control systems, model-based design and data science work and a May 2022 Ocean Data Factory Sweden lead technical partnership.

name: Common guillemots in the Baltic Sea studied with video surveillance and object detection
summary: Dataset on common guillemots in the Baltic Sea, built by Jonas Hentati Sundberg, in which a YOLOv4 model was trained to detect adult birds, chicks and eggs in video.

name: Conifer Vision
summary: An organisation founded in 2019 that is developing a platform using drone imagery and AI.

name: County Administrative Board of Gotland
summary: Regional body that, according to Sweco, manages Gotland's protected areas and conservation of threatened species, and explored with Sweco whether GeoAI can map the county's rich fens.

name: County Administrative Boards of Sweden
summary: Regional bodies responsible for county area protection and managing most state-protected areas.

name: DarkTree
summary: A project from 2025 onward, led by Fredrik Ronquist and funded by the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, that aims to sequence 3,000 insect genomes and uses machine-learning methods to detect and identify specimens.

name: Dating forest fellings with radar imagery and AI
summary: A pilot project run by Spacemetric, financed by the Advanced Digitisation programme, that adds radar imagery to optical satellite data to improve dating of fellings and follow-up of tree regrowth.

name: Deep Wetlands
summary: A closed project, running March 2022 to December 2023, that worked on a machine learning platform to monitor water extent changes in wetlands.

name: DeepAqua
summary: A closed project, running January 2024 to February 2026, that aimed to combine optical and radar remote sensing with deep learning to monitor changes in water bodies.

name: Department of Aquatic Resources, SLU
summary: Department run by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences that led a completed eDNA project tracing invasive pumpkinseed and, in May 2024, tested a stereo video camera in a trawl.

name: Detecting forest clearcuts year-round with radar and AI
summary: Active project in which Qamcom and Spacemetric are developing an AI-driven solution for monitoring forest clear-cuts in partnership with Skogsstyrelsen.

name: Digital Earth Sweden
summary: Sweden's national platform for satellite data, run and built by RISE Research Institutes of Sweden and Rymdstyrelsen, and funded by Rymdstyrelsen.

name: Digitala värden i skog
summary: Forest nature value indications for boreal and alpine regions, made with machine learning and remote sensing by Skogsstyrelsen, which says the layers need other information or field surveys.

name: DigiWild
summary: A project funded with SEK 3,886,000 from the Wildlife Conservation Fund for 2026 to 2028, planning computer-vision models to extract sex, age and distance from wildlife camera images.

name: Drönarstation
summary: An organisation reported to have a self-driving drone system with built-in image analysis.

name: Ecogain
summary: An organisation with Vinnova funding for AI mapping of nature values, with the AI to be trained to recognise places likely to hold them.

name: EcoVibes
summary: An Örnsköldsvik team whose February 2026 test AI recognised three-toed woodpecker sounds, developing bioacoustics according to North Sweden Cleantech, with OX2 reporting a summer 2026 pilot.

name: eDNA solutions
summary: A company founded in 2016 by Alexander Eiler, with a Gothenburg address, that describes using DNA technologies to track species and assess biodiversity.

name: ELEVATE
summary: Project led by Sven Adler, funded by the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency, to improve alpine vegetation monitoring in Sweden by combining deep learning with drone, aerial, LiDAR and satellite data.

name: Enköpings naturskyddsförening
summary: Nature conservation association named as a nature reserve manager in Uppsala County.

name: Erken Laboratory
summary: Uppsala University-run laboratory in Norrtälje that monitors Lake Erken with manual and automatic measurements, including greenhouse gas fluxes since 2014, and is an accredited water and sediment analysis laboratory.

name: Eye of the Fjord
summary: A project led by Marko Wramen using Tiva and partnering with KTH, in which two cameras had streamed from the Gullmar Fjord seabed for just over a year by September 2026.

name: Falsterbo Bird Observatory
summary: Bird observatory that began standardised autumn counts at Nabben in 1973, which have formed part of the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency's national environmental monitoring since 1978.

name: Fisheye AI
summary: A Vinnova-funded project led by Fortum Sverige that aims to develop and integrate FishFlow AI to improve fish migration in regulated rivers.

name: Flox Edge
summary: An AI-based, ground-based sensor system according to Vinnova's project page, built by Flox Intelligence.

name: Flox Intelligence
summary: A Vinnova-funded company that says it began in 2020 as a KTH AI lab spinoff, with WWF Sweden saying it developed technology to detect and deter wolves in real time.

name: Followit AB
summary: A company whose wildlife division, located in Lindesberg, was formerly Televilt, working in GPS and radio telemetry.

name: Forest Monitor
summary: A web service with a web map on the Swedish forest, run by Protect the Forest Sweden.

name: Formas
summary: A self-described government research council for sustainable development, announcing SEK 30 million for Swedish researchers in a Biodiversa+ call and listed among current and past Trase funders.

name: Fortum Sverige AB
summary: The coordinator of the Fisheye AI project.

name: Gaia by Illuminum
summary: Web-based service, run by Illuminum AB, that gathers biodiversity data onto an interactive map and offers AI-driven reporting through a chat with an AI assistant.

name: GBIF Gap Finder
summary: A programme built by GBIF Sweden on GBIF biodiversity data cubes and national species checklists.

name: GBIF Sweden
summary: The self-described Swedish GBIF node, museum-hosted since 2003, supporting biodiversity data publication and sharing and reporting the Insect Biome Atlas as Sweden's third-largest GBIF contribution.

name: Gemenskapsdriven strategi för 3D hyperspektral AI för universell klassificering av biologisk mångfald
summary: A project led by Linköping University and funded by Vinnova, running October 2023 to September 2026 and now closed, which aimed to develop a 3D hyperspectral imaging AI system.

name: GenomeVault
summary: A Sweden-based company with DNA-based biodiversity monitoring, which coordinates a Vinnova-funded project validating eDNA biodiversity monitoring.

name: GeoAI och biologisk mångfald, Gotland rich fen mapping
summary: Completed Sweco project, led by Marianne Melander Åkerholm, that mapped potential rich fens on Gotland from orthophotos by training a deep learning model on classic image classification output.

name: Geological Survey of Sweden
summary: An organisation the University of Gothenburg named in April 2024 as a partner in developing SUBSIM, a tool adapted to help map Baltic Sea bottom environments.

name: GLOBHE
summary: Stockholm-based company that was closing a SEK 20 million seed round in September 2022 and said then that drones sent out through Crowddroning helped monitor deforestation.

name: Gothenburg Global Biodiversity Centre
summary: Centre made up of 20 partner organisations, eight of them departments and centres at the University of Gothenburg, which SBDI says provides its support office services.

name: Gothenburg Natural History Museum
summary: Museum within Västra Götalandsregionen's culture administration that surveys individual insect species, writes conservation guidance, and reports all insect finds to Artportalen.

name: Government Offices of Sweden
summary: Swedish government body that worked during 2025 on the national strategy and action plan for biodiversity, on which the Climate and Environment Minister answered a parliamentary question.

name: Green Cubes
summary: Project that started with a proof of concept in Costa Rican rainforests, reported in May 2024, collecting data from aircraft and on the ground, with AI used on recorded calls; built and run by R-Evolution.

name: Greensway
summary: Organisation that carried out a study with Skogforsk, supported by Skogsägarnas forskningsfond, using a model that combines standardised open species data with environmental variables in an AI model.

name: Grimsö Wildlife Research Station
summary: SLU-run wildlife station, established in 1974, that runs annual surveys of wildlife and habitats, uses wildlife cameras for population estimates, and publishes several datasets in the SITES data portal.

name: Ground-Eye
summary: Project, run by Hushållningssällskapet Skåne with Bafication AB, that tests a digital system for following small ground-dwelling animals on farms during the 2026 field season.

name: Gällivare sameby
summary: One of nine Sami villages that, with the county board, the Swedish EPA and two municipalities, make up the association formed to manage the Laponia World Heritage site.

name: Göteborgs Stad
summary: City whose stadsmiljönämnden is responsible for about 6,000 hectares of forest land and manages all municipally owned forest protected as nature reserves.

name: Havets Hus
summary: Organisation that has released about 200 tagged aquarium-bred sharks into the Gullmar Fjord since 2003, tracks them with acoustic transmitters from 2021, and released tagged cod with SLU in October 2023.

name: Helsingborgs stad
summary: Municipality named as the manager (förvaltare) of the Väla skog nature reserve.

name: High Coast Forestry
summary: Organisation that says it provides consulting services for forestry and power line corridors and uses Deep Forestry.

name: Holmen
summary: Organisation that reported in February 2020 that it was using its spruce bark beetle damage tool for its own land holdings.

name: Holmen spruce bark beetle damage tool
summary: Tool built by Holmen that is based on satellite images and AI and shows actual damage on a map.

name: Huddinge kommun
summary: Municipality designated nature conservation manager of the Gladö Kvarnsjön nature reserve in the municipal council decision of 9 June 2014.

name: Hushållningssällskapet Skåne
summary: Organisation whose source describes Ground-Eye as operating within Agtech Sweden.

name: Hyggligt
summary: Organisation founded in 2023 that can highlight indicators of conservation value from drone LiDAR data.

name: Illuminum AB
summary: Swedish company registered in Uppsala whose green-tech product, Gaia, is a biodiversity studio including AI-driven reporting in which users chat with an AI to produce reports.

name: Insamlingsstiftelsen Framtidens Natur & Kulturarv
summary: Fundraising foundation that gains control of land through use-right agreements of up to 50 years or purchase, aiming to protect, manage and restore nature and cultural heritage there.

name: Insamlingsstiftelsen Naturarvet
summary: Fundraising foundation that raises money to buy old forest to protect red-listed species and biodiversity; its statutes forbid felling, other forestry, farming and sale, so owned forest is permanently protected.

name: Insect Biome Atlas
summary: Dataset led by Fredrik Ronquist and funded by the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, charting insect faunas of Sweden and Madagascar by DNA sequencing, with over 30,000 species detected in Sweden.

name: IVL Swedish Environmental Research Institute
summary: Independent research institute, partner of the Gothenburg Global Biodiversity Centre, that says it works with environmental DNA methods and is responsible for lab analyses, DNA identification and data quality assurance in Bloom 2.0.

name: Jåhkågasska tjiellde sameby
summary: One of nine Sami villages that, with the county board, the Swedish EPA and two municipalities, make up the association formed to manage the Laponia World Heritage site.

name: Karlskrona kommun
summary: Municipality that manages the Knösö, Ekebacken and Västra Skällön nature reserves.

name: Karlsö Jagt- och djurskyddsförening
summary: Association that is both landowner and manager (förvaltare) of the Stora Karlsö nature reserve.

name: Karolinska Institutet
summary: Institution that SBDI says shares responsibility for integrating sequence-based species observations.

name: Kempe Foundations
summary: Foundations named among the funders of the forest research arena.

name: Klimat- och näringslivsdepartementet
summary: Ministry responsible, with the climate and environment minister, for environmental objectives within the government, according to the Sveriges miljömål site.

name: Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation
summary: Foundation that funds WIFORCE at SLU, the Insect Biome Atlas and WASP.

name: Kolmården Foundation
summary: Foundation that co-finances Project Ngulia, in which the zoo acts as tester.

name: Koster Seafloor Observatory
summary: System built by Combine to identify underwater species, partnered with three organisations, whose page reports no data during architecture restructuring and connection to SUBSIM's computing platform.

name: Kosterhavsdelegationen
summary: Delegation including local interest representatives, to which the county board, which manages Kosterhavet National Park, has delegated some areas of responsibility.

name: Kristineberg Centre for Research and Innovation
summary: Centre located in Fiskebäckskil in Bohuslän.

name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
summary: University working on wildfire detection, SBDI sequence integration, an AI system tested at the Eye of the Fjord, DeepAqua (January 2024 to February 2026) and BalticMicrobeDB.

name: Kullenberg Excursion Journals AI digitisation
summary: Digitisation project led by Britt Andermann, from which a dataset of the Kullenberg Excursion Journals, held at Uppsala University's Museum of Evolution, was published through GBIF Sweden.

name: Kungliga Djurgårdens förvaltning
summary: Estate administration that looks after forest, trees, grazing, wetlands and game on Djurgården and Fjäderholmarna, and manages about 80 percent of the land in the national city park.

name: Lantmäteriet
summary: Swedish mapping, cadastral and land registration authority that supplies maps, images and geographic information, including national laser scanning that Skogsstyrelsen says Skogliga grunddata draws on.

name: Laponiatjuottjudus
summary: Association that manages the 9,400 square kilometre Laponia World Heritage site, took over from the Norrbotten county board on 1 January 2013, and has Sami villages, the Swedish EPA and two municipalities on its board.

name: Lerum Energi
summary: Energy company that, according to Sportfiskarna, paid with Partille Energi for AI underwater cameras in the Säveån's Jonsered fish passes, meant to follow fish migration and threatened species.

name: LIFEPLAN
summary: Project led by Tomas Roslin, funded by a European Research Council Synergy Grant, that aims to establish the state of biodiversity across the globe.

name: Linköping University
summary: University whose researchers and students developed machine learning for watching reserve animals, listed as coordinator of a 3D hyperspectral AI project with an October 2023–September 2026 project period.

name: Linköpings kommun
summary: Swedish municipality named as the manager (förvaltare) of the Vallaskogen nature reserve.

name: Linnaeus University
summary: University whose EEMiS centre, SBDI says, is part of the molecular module team and focuses on the Ampliseq amplicon denoising pipeline.

name: Luleå University of Technology
summary: University that AI Sweden names as a coordinator of the Swedish Space Data Lab.

name: Lund University
summary: Hosts the BIOPATH consortium, with researchers working on the Swedish Bird Survey and responsibility for BioCollect, the Living Atlases tool for systematic monitoring data.

name: Lunds kommun
summary: Swedish municipality that in August 2021 managed 1,200 hectares of nature and forest land with the county board, and had 33 nature reserves, six of them municipal.

name: Luokta-Mávas sameby
summary: One of nine Sami villages that, with the county board, Swedish EPA and two municipalities, make up the association formed to manage the Laponia World Heritage site.

name: Länsstyrelsen Blekinge
summary: County administrative board that is usually responsible for managing protected nature such as nature reserves and national parks.

name: Länsstyrelsen Dalarna
summary: County administrative board that is usually the body responsible for managing protected nature in the county.

name: Länsstyrelsen Gävleborg
summary: County administrative board that is the manager (förvaltare) of Färnebofjärden National Park.

name: Länsstyrelsen Halland
summary: County administrative board that manages just over 190 of the county's more than 200 nature reserves; Västkuststiftelsen, municipalities and landowners manage the rest.

name: Länsstyrelsen Jämtland
summary: County administrative board that manages one national park (Sonfjället), about 260 nature reserves and about 240 Natura 2000 areas.

name: Länsstyrelsen Kalmar
summary: County administrative board that manages most of the county's nature reserves, as well as national parks, seal and bird protection areas and natural monuments.

name: Länsstyrelsen Kronoberg
summary: County administrative board that is the manager (förvaltare) of the Hässlebacken nature reserve.

name: Länsstyrelsen Norrbotten
summary: County administrative board that manages four of Norrbotten's eight national parks; Laponiatjuottjudus manages the other four.

name: Länsstyrelsen Skåne
summary: Swedish county administrative board for Skåne that, as a rule, manages over 300 nature reserves and three national parks in the county.

name: Länsstyrelsen Stockholm
summary: Swedish county administrative board for Stockholm whose nature management unit manages nature reserves and other protected nature across the whole county.

name: Länsstyrelsen Södermanland
summary: Swedish county administrative board for Södermanland that manages about 170 of the county's 195 nature reserves and nature conservation areas.

name: Länsstyrelsen Uppsala
summary: Swedish county administrative board for Uppsala that managed 150 of the county's 194 nature reserves as of August 2023.

name: Länsstyrelsen Värmland
summary: Swedish county administrative board for Värmland that was responsible for the care and management of 227 nature reserves in 2025.

name: Länsstyrelsen Västerbotten
summary: Swedish county administrative board for Västerbotten that manages and supervises all nature reserves and Natura 2000 areas in the lower Ume river compensation area, and builds and maintains visitor facilities there.

name: Länsstyrelsen Västernorrland
summary: Swedish county administrative board for Västernorrland that is responsible for managing the county's state-protected natural areas, including Skuleskogen National Park, nature reserves, Natura 2000 areas and bird protection areas.

name: Länsstyrelsen Västmanland
summary: Swedish county administrative board for Västmanland that is usually responsible for managing protected nature such as nature reserves and national parks.

name: Länsstyrelsen Västra Götaland
summary: Swedish county administrative board for Västra Götaland, named as the nature conservation manager (naturvårdsförvaltare) of the Hornborgasjön nature reserve.

name: Länsstyrelsen Örebro
summary: Swedish county administrative board for Örebro that manages most of the county's protected areas, including national parks, nature reserves, Natura 2000 areas and natural monuments.

name: Länsstyrelsen Östergötland
summary: Swedish county administrative board for Östergötland that manages most of the county's roughly 300 nature reserves.

name: Mai Intelligence
summary: Organisation that the directory says uses Sentinel-2 data for forest health.

name: Malmö stad
summary: Swedish municipality named as the manager (förvaltare) of the Bunkeflo strandängar nature reserve.

name: Malmö University
summary: University where Per Jönsson, in Materials Science and Applied Mathematics, is first author of a 2018 paper on estimating vegetation seasonality from Landsat and Sentinel-2 time series.

name: Metria
summary: Produced national land cover mapping for Naturvårdsverket and has a framework agreement covering land cover data and habitat mapping, among agreements estimated at SEK 430 million over seven years.

name: Mid Sweden University
summary: University whose researchers were part of the team that built a new AI-driven mapping method for Swedish forest land, the forest conservation value map.

name: Miljödata MVM
summary: Web service for land, water and environmental data from two SLU data host assignments, covering agricultural land and lakes and watercourses, including national and regional monitoring water chemistry and biological data.

name: Mistra
summary: Described as the government-backed Swedish foundation for strategic environmental research, it allocated SEK 58 million to the first four years of Mistra Digital Forest and is main funder of FinBio.

name: Mistra BIOPATH
summary: A research programme funded by Mistra at $5.5M and led by Susanne Arvidsson, where industrial partner MDOTM announced in April 2022 that it would advise on AI.

name: Mistra Digital Forest
summary: Active programme funded by Mistra, with a total budget of SEK 224 million for 2019 to 2027 and partners including universities, Holmen, Sveaskog and Södra.

name: Mistra Finance to Revive Biodiversity
summary: A Mistra-funded programme aiming to support the financial sector's transition, with a museum-led part intended to produce open source biodiversity data to inform financial decisions.

name: MIX Research Sweden
summary: Active research and consulting company focused on eDNA.

name: National Forest Data Lab
summary: Active programme run by the Swedish Forest Agency and SLU, funded by Vinnova, working with airborne laser scanning, satellite, drone and field inventory data.

name: National Inventories of Landscapes in Sweden
summary: National landscape monitoring programme run by SLU and funded by the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency, whose 2003 to 2020 basic inventory collected vegetation data to estimate landscape status and change.

name: National research arena for forests
summary: Programme launched in January 2026 to bring forest data together for analysis with computing capacity and AI, with a total investment of about SEK 180 million.

name: Nationella marktäckedata
summary: Nationwide land cover dataset built by Naturvårdsverket and Metria from satellite, laser and thematic data, with classes rising from 25 in NMD2018 to 54 in NMD2023.

name: Naturskyddsföreningen Gotland
summary: Gotland branch of a nature conservation society that owns and manages natural areas, including the Stockvike bird tower, while the national association has owned Lilla Karlsö since 1954.

name: Naturskyddsföreningen i Skåne
summary: Skåne branch of a nature conservation federation that manages conservation sites the federation owns or that have been handed over to its care.

name: Naturstiftelsen
summary: Fundraising foundation that buys natural land with donations to protect it, and may restore heavily used land through planting, more dead wood and restored water flows.

name: Nedre Dalälvens Intresseförening
summary: Interest association that has held the coordinator role of the Nedre Dalälven biosphere reserve since UNESCO designated it in 2011.

name: nf-core/ampliseq
summary: Pipeline for post-processing metabarcoding data, as SBDI describes it, built by Linnaeus University.

name: Nordens Ark
summary: Active organisation whose field conservation includes population monitoring, and which attended a workshop before six camera traps were placed in Altyn Emel national park, Kazakhstan, in October 2025.

name: Nordic BiodiversityAI Network
summary: Active programme led by Junwen Guo, which notes that modern computer vision can help identify and track species.

name: Nordic Microalgae
summary: Dataset run and built by SMHI, covering microalgae in the Baltic Sea, North East Atlantic and Nordic freshwaters, with taxonomic information and expert-provided images.

name: Norrsken VC
summary: Active organisation that says it invested in Terra Labs.

name: Ocean Data Factory Sweden
summary: Closed project led by the University of Gothenburg and funded by Vinnova, listed as completed, whose most successful technical area was machine learning analysis of underwater images.

name: Ottenby Bird Observatory
summary: BirdLife Sverige-run observatory whose trapping, standardised since 1972, BirdLife called the world’s longest such series in 2020, when over 30,000 birds were ringed by 12 October.

name: OX2
summary: Company that is testing acoustic monitoring devices at one of its Swedish wind farm sites to understand how red-throated divers use the landscape.

name: OX2 red-throated diver bioacoustics pilot
summary: Active pilot, launched by OX2 in summer 2026 with ecovibes, Calluna and EnviroPlanning, testing automated sound monitoring of red-throated divers using ecovibes' AI bioacoustic technology to support biodiversity management around renewable energy projects.

name: PandionAI
summary: Active organisation that says it was founded in 2019 to use AI for Earth observation and is built in Stockholm, with funding from the Swedish National Space Agency and Vinnova.

name: Partille Energi
summary: Energy organisation that Sportfiskarna says helped pay, with Lerums Energi, for AI underwater cameras in the Säveån, intended to follow fish migration and collect knowledge on threatened fish species.

name: Project Ngulia
summary: Active project funded by the Kolmården Foundation, in partnership with Linköping University, which develops equipment tested at Kolmården.

name: Protect the Forest Sweden
summary: Active organisation named on Forestmonitor.eu.

name: Qamcom
summary: Organisation of unknown status that will develop machine learning algorithms for the forest felling pilot and is developing an AI-driven solution with Spacemetric.

name: Qarlbo Biodiversity
summary: Active organisation described as a Swedish-based leader in biodiversity credit methodologies, in partnership with Treemetrics.

name: Qulinda
summary: Active Swedish technology company in Linköping, per LEAD, with AI cameras and tracking tags; WWF Sweden says its cameras detect and classify large carnivores at 100 to 150 metres.

name: R-evolution
summary: Active business venture within the Swedish technology group Hexagon, launched by Hexagon in 2021.

name: Region Skåne
summary: Regional body that is the principal (huvudman) of just over ten state nature reserves in Skåne, managed through Stiftelsen Skånska Landskap.

name: Region Sörmland
summary: Regional body named as a manager of protected areas in Södermanland county, alongside the municipalities and Sveaskog.

name: Region Örebro län
summary: Regional body that holds the management responsibility (förvaltaransvaret) in some nature reserves in Örebro county.

name: RISE Research Institutes of Sweden
summary: Active organisation named by others as coordinator of the Swedish Space Data Lab and ESA Phi-Lab Sweden, handling Digital Earth Sweden's technical development and AukLab's acoustic setup.

name: Sametinget
summary: Active organisation that has been the focal point coordinating implementation of Sami and other traditional knowledge under the CBD since 2021, with a 2024 task for articles 8j and 10c.

name: SAV Sweden
summary: Active project built by DHI, partnering with Sweden’s county administrative boards, combining Sentinel-2 imagery and machine learning for a national overview of submerged vegetation.

name: SBDI Biologging Portal
summary: Portal that SBDI describes as a way to explore data through a metadata register.

name: SCA
summary: Active organisation that launched a tool with AI functionality for digital forestry planning and is one of 14 participants in the EU project SingleTree.

name: Scandcam 2
summary: Project of unknown status, led by Tim Hofmeester, that aims to develop a common system for camera use in wildlife management.

name: Seabird project on Stora Karlsö
summary: Active project run by Stockholm Resilience Centre, funded by WWF Sweden, with Stockholm University as partner, which WWF Sweden says studies guillemots and three other bird species.

name: Seabird surveillance system
summary: Active project, built by Jonas Hentati-Sundberg, that uses a deep learning algorithm trained on annotated images.

name: SeAnalytics
summary: Active Swedish company, founded in 2013 as a University of Gothenburg spin-off, that says it aims to help manage marine coastal ecosystems with DNA methods and machine learning, and offers reef monitoring.

name: SHARK
summary: Active dataset run by SMHI, which stores national and regional biological, physical and chemical marine monitoring data, available through a web interface and REST API.

name: SHARK Phyto- and Microzooplankton Data Collected by Imaging FlowCytobots
summary: Active dataset of phyto- and microzooplankton collected with image recognition by Imaging FlowCytobots, with monitoring performed by SMHI, which runs it.

name: Sierri sameby
summary: Sami village that is one of nine, with the county board, the Swedish EPA and two municipalities, in the association formed to manage the Laponia World Heritage site.

name: Sirges sameby
summary: Sami village that is one of nine, with the county board, the Swedish EPA and two municipalities, in the association formed to manage the Laponia World Heritage site.

name: SITES Spectral
summary: Active programme led and run by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, with Lund University, monitoring ecosystems with fixed sensors, phenological cameras, drones and satellite data.

name: Skansen
summary: Active organisation that contributed to a project on mapping animals through airborne RNA and coordinates and takes part in Arctic fox fieldwork, partnering with Stockholm University.

name: Skogforsk
summary: Active organisation described as the central research body for Swedish forestry, which carried out a study on AI and open species data with Greensway.

name: Skogliga grunddata
summary: Active nationwide forest and land geodata, built by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, with six map layers estimating volume, basal area, height, diameter and biomass from laser scanning and field measurements.

name: Skärgårdsstiftelsen
summary: Foundation that owns and manages about 12% of the land in the Stockholm archipelago, covering 12,000 hectares of land and 20,000 hectares of water.

name: SLU Aqua Sailor
summary: Active project run by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, an unmanned sailing drone for research and environmental monitoring.

name: SLU Division of Forest Remote Sensing
summary: Division run by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences that researches forest remote sensing, with a focus on national maps.

name: SLU Forest Map
summary: Dataset built by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, building on the Swedish National Forest Inventory, that includes wall-to-wall raster maps of tree species across the country.

name: SLU Swedish Species Information Centre
summary: Centre run by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences that gathers Swedish species information, and from 1 January 2026 forms a joint organisation with the SLU Centre for Biological Diversity.

name: Sogeti Sweden
summary: Organisation that collaborated with Sveaskog on a satellite and AI solution to track spruce bark beetle damage.

name: Spacemetric
summary: Organisation contributing image data management and processing to the forest felling pilot.

name: SPACEwetland
summary: Active project funded by Rymdstyrelsen, with IVL Svenska Miljöinstitutet and the University of Gothenburg as partners, combining satellite time series, field data and machine learning.

name: Sportfiskarna
summary: Organisation that carried out commissioned electrofishing in summer 2020, with results entered into SERS, and co-finances the Säveån camera project with others.

name: Stadskupan
summary: Organisation named as the initiator and project leader of Bloom 2.0.

name: Statens fastighetsverk
summary: Property body that owns most of the land in the Royal National City Park in Stockholm, mainly Haga, Ulriksdal, central Stockholm and Djurgården.

name: Station Linné
summary: Research station on Öland that collaborated on the Swedish inventory of the Insect Biome Atlas and reports analysing insect fauna at a mire in Pajala municipality.

name: Stiftelsen Friherre Carl Cederströms minne
summary: Foundation named as a nature reserve manager in Uppsala County.

name: Stiftelsen för Fritidsområden i Skåne
summary: Foundation formed in 1967 to preserve areas important for outdoor recreation or natural areas needing protection, managed by Stiftelsen Skånska Landskap.

name: Stiftelsen Naturvård vid nedre Umeälven
summary: Foundation responsible for long-term nature management of the compensation measures, using funds set aside by the Swedish Transport Administration, and administered by Länsstyrelsen Västerbotten.

name: Stiftelsen OD Krooks donation i Kristianstads län
summary: Foundation named as the manager (förvaltare) of the Grytåsa nature reserve, acting through Stiftelsen Skånska Landskap.

name: Stiftelsen Skånska Landskap
summary: Foundation managing just over ten state nature reserves in Skåne and the loop trails in 19 recreation areas, owning just over 2,300 of the foundations' combined 10,759 hectares and managing the rest for five others.

name: Stiftelsen Tyrestaskogen
summary: Foundation responsible for managing and developing Tyresta National Park and nature reserve.

name: Stockholm University
summary: University named as a member of the consortium delivering SBDI and as a partner of the Insect Biome Atlas, which also develops and maintains the Swedish ASV portal with Karolinska Institute.

name: Stockholms stad
summary: City that owns and manages all the land in Nackareservatet (829 hectares, 100 hectares of water).

name: Stornorrfors AI fish monitoring
summary: Project built and run by Vattenfall whose system counts and records individual salmon and trout at Stornorrfors.

name: Stornorrfors fish recognition
summary: Project run by Vattenfall which, in February 2023, Vattenfall said used algorithms that recognised size and fungal attacks and distinguished wild from farmed fish.

name: Strategic Environmental Archaeology Database
summary: Dataset built by Umeå University, described by SBDI as an international database for environmental archaeology and Quaternary science data, which makes the data available to the international research community.

name: SUBSIM
summary: Platform built by the University of Gothenburg and others for managing underwater image and video data, funded by Vinnova, Formas and the Swedish Research Council, and reported to identify marine species with machine learning.

name: Sveaskog
summary: Forest owner described as the largest in Sweden.

name: Sveaskog and Sogeti spruce bark beetle tracking
summary: Project with Sveaskog and Sogeti Sweden as partners, which Capgemini's client story describes as using AI to hunt spruce bark beetles from space.

name: Svenska kyrkan
summary: Church with 114 church reserves, which are land where the forest grows freely or is managed only for nature values, with the church responsible for the biodiversity.

name: SweBITS
summary: Active project led by Per Stenberg that uses a 60-year archive of airborne environmental DNA.

name: Sweco
summary: Organisation whose wildlife camera tool uses AI to distinguish animal species in images.

name: Swedish Agency for Marine and Water Management
summary: Agency responsible for conservation and restoration matters for waters, which SMHI says appointed it as national data host for marine data, and whose page says benthic habitat monitoring is being developed.

name: Swedish Association for Hunting and Wildlife Management
summary: Organisation at Öster Malma, Nyköping, administering six reference areas established in 2023 with 36 cameras each, and reporting responsibility for some state wildlife monitoring since 1938.

name: Swedish ASV portal
summary: Dataset giving access to molecular data in SBDI, with a database of Amplicon Sequence Variants and a web interface, built and run by Stockholm University and Karolinska Institute.

name: Swedish Biodiversity Data Infrastructure
summary: National infrastructure for open biodiversity data, including the Swedish GBIF node, delivered by eleven universities and agencies and funded by the Swedish Research Council.

name: Swedish Bird Survey
summary: Volunteer bird counting programme at several hundred sites for over 40 years, run by Lund University, with a November 2021 report citing 700 to 800 volunteers annually and much data available through SBDI.

name: Swedish Butterfly Monitoring Scheme
summary: Volunteer monitoring programme run by Lund University, which in 2021 covered over 600 sites with more than 300 volunteers.

name: Swedish Defence Research Agency
summary: Agency that, according to an April 2013 report, led and coordinated the BIAS project.

name: Swedish Environmental Protection Agency
summary: State agency for climate, environment and nature that forms national parks, manages wildlife nationally, is the CBD SBSTTA focal point, and partners with the Swedish Bird Survey.

name: Swedish Forest Agency
summary: Agency responsible for forest biotope protection whose 2024 report described AI model development and which launched AI maps of possible high forest nature values in February 2026.

name: Swedish Forest Industries Federation
summary: Organisation named in December 2018 as host of Mistra Digital Forest.

name: Swedish Infrastructure for Ecosystem Science
summary: National infrastructure established in 2013, with nine field stations, openly available data, Swedish Research Council funding and operation by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences.

name: Swedish Insect Monitoring Scheme
summary: Project using Malaise traps and DNA metabarcoding until 2027, jointly run by institutions including the Swedish Museum of Natural History, and partnering with SITES.

name: Swedish Maritime Robotics Centre
summary: Cross-disciplinary industrial research centre for autonomous underwater systems, partnering with the University of Gothenburg.

name: Swedish Metabarcoding Network
summary: Network of partners across Sweden that says it aims to improve the technology readiness of metabarcoding for biodiversity monitoring, with its launch reported by GBIF Sweden in March 2026.

name: Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute
summary: Government agency in Norrköping that operates Sweden's National Oceanographic Data Centre, serves as national marine data host, and identifies plankton with AI-supported image recognition.

name: Swedish Museum of Natural History
summary: Stockholm government agency and research institution that hosts SBDI, leads the Swedish GBIF node, curates specimen, survey and eDNA data, and is developing a machine learning pipeline in DarkTree.

name: Swedish National Forest Inventory
summary: Annual sample inventory of Sweden's whole area, describing forest state since 1923, producing official forest statistics, and run by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences.

name: Swedish National Space Agency
summary: Central government agency under the Ministry of Education and Research that funds space research and remote sensing, coordinates Swedish Copernicus participation, and steers Digital Earth Sweden.

name: Swedish Polar Research Secretariat
summary: Government agency that promotes and coordinates Swedish polar research, and carries out continuous environmental monitoring at Abisko with SMHI, ICOS and SITES.

name: Swedish Red List
summary: Dataset compiling the extinction risk of species in Sweden, built by the SLU Swedish Species Information Centre.

name: Swedish Research Council
summary: Funder of research infrastructure that finances SBDI and SITES, administers the GBIF membership fee, and holds the GBIF Head of Delegation post.

name: Swedish Society for Nature Conservation
summary: Organisation named as a partner in a Säveån research collaboration announced in July 2026.

name: Swedish Space Data Lab
summary: National innovation platform for space data and AI-based analysis, started in 2019, using mainly Sentinel-2 data, led by AI Sweden, RISE and Luleå University of Technology, and funded by Vinnova and the space agency.

name: Swedish Transport Administration
summary: Agency that coordinated the Image recognition for wildlife cameras project from May 2020 to November 2021, with its coordinator listed in Borlänge.

name: Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences
summary: University with sites in Alnarp, Uppsala and Umeå, contributing to SBDI and responsible for official forest statistics, whose DigiWild project combines wildlife cameras, citizen science and AI.

name: SWEDNA
summary: Swedish eDNA lab, run by the University of Gothenburg.

name: Säveån AI fish migration research
summary: Uses a system identifying, counting and measuring fish in real time, with collaboration between the University of Gothenburg, a conservation society and two energy companies planned for 2026.

name: Södra
summary: Forest organisation that said in June 2025 it was leading a project to develop planners' tools using remote sensing and AI.

name: Sök med bild
summary: Machine learning image recognition model built by SLU Artdatabanken, building on Artportalen and millions of species photos from northern Europe.

name: Terra Labs
summary: Company founded in 2023 with an AI platform that turns satellite data into a picture of forest estates; Norrsken VC lists it in Sweden, funds it, and it partners with Södra.

name: TiVA
summary: Swedish company with automatic species recognition that distinguishes up to twelve species, and has delivered fish counters to power plants, hydropower associations, county boards and consultants in Sweden.

name: TREESPEC
summary: Funded for 2023 to 2026 by the Swedish National Space Agency and led by Abdulhakim Abdi, it aims to improve tree species mapping using satellite data and machine learning.

name: TrusTrace
summary: Launched a compliance solution aimed at deforestation-free shipments in October 2024, with a risk assessment that uses geospatial analysis of satellite images.

name: Tuorpon sameby
summary: Sami village that is one of nine, with the county board, the Swedish EPA and two municipalities, in the association formed to manage the Laponia World Heritage site.

name: Udtja sameby
summary: Sami village that is one of nine, with the county board, the Swedish EPA and two municipalities, in the association formed to manage the Laponia World Heritage site.

name: Umeå University
summary: University in Umeå working on forest machines that perceive their surroundings, and investigating whether passive acoustic monitoring of ants and earthworms can help assess soil health.

name: University of Gothenburg
summary: University responsible for the SBDI support office, and launching a 2026 research collaboration using AI fish cameras in the Säveån River.

name: University of Gävle
summary: University that led the research on the Ödmården camera project, which began in 2020 and was extended to the end of 2024.

name: Unna tjerusj sameby
summary: Sami village that is one of nine, with the county board, the Swedish EPA and two municipalities, in the association formed to manage the Laponia World Heritage site.

name: Upplandsstiftelsen
summary: Foundation that manages 49 nature areas, including 27 nature reserves and one cultural reserve, and owns all or part of 24 of them.

name: Uppsala kommun
summary: Municipality that is the manager (förvaltare) of the Stadsskogen nature reserve.

name: Uppsala University
summary: University with a Museum of Evolution providing taxonomic expertise to SBDI, a Biodiversity Data Lab research group, and shared responsibility for integrating sequence-based species observations into SBDI.

name: Vatteninformationssystem Sverige
summary: Dataset with information on Sweden's larger lakes, watercourses, groundwater and coastal waters, built by Vattenmyndigheterna and Länsstyrelserna and partnered with Havs- och vattenmyndigheten.

name: Vattenmyndigheterna
summary: Water authorities named alongside county boards in Havs- och vattenmyndigheten’s account of VISS.

name: Viltbild
summary: Wildlife camera image platform with AI species identification, built by hunting organisations and SLU; a February 2025 page planned limited release in 2025 and opening to everyone in 2026.

name: Viltförvaltning
summary: Organisation whose material, according to LEAD, was used to develop an AI model that identifies animal species, and which scans forest areas with thermal cameras on drones.

name: Viltskadecenter
summary: Organisation that reviews and compiles carnivore survey results for the agency.

name: Vinnova
summary: Swedish innovation agency that granted SEK 3,462,381 to Ocean Data Factory Sweden, and funds Deep Forestry, with SEK 500,000 listed for a Deep Forestry AB drone project.

name: Voice of the Ocean
summary: Organisation that says it is based in Sweden and operates a 24/7 Baltic ocean monitoring system using gliders, sail buoys and sensors.

name: Västkuststiftelsen
summary: Foundation managing about 300 nature reserves, over 50,000 hectares in Halland and Västra Götaland, for the county administrative boards, and owning just over 4,000 hectares bought to protect valuable nature.

name: Wallenberg Initiatives in Forest Research
summary: Basic science forest research programme funded by the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, run by SLU and led by Ove Nilsson, with a national research arena announced in January 2026.

name: WeDNA – Water eDNA Monitoring Center
summary: Centre run by the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences that works with aquatic environmental DNA to monitor Swedish freshwaters.

name: Wireless Remote Animal Monitoring
summary: National competence centre and e-infrastructure for biotelemetry sensor data, run by SLU and part of SBDI, holding data on 24 species and nearly 6,000 individuals.

name: WWF Sweden
summary: Organisation that says it started several AI-centred projects in 2024, mainly to reduce conflict between people and large carnivores, and partners with AI Sweden and Qulinda.

name: Ödmården camera trap wildlife monitoring
summary: Closed project led by the University of Gävle, extended to the end of 2024, which assessed AI image recognition using about 30 cameras across 20,000 hectares.

name: Örebro kommun
summary: Swedish municipality named as the manager (förvaltare) of the Reträtten nature reserve.

name: Örebro University
summary: University whose School of Science and Technology researchers co-authored a 2023 paper on predicting larch casebearer damage using YOLO models and conformal prediction, with Ulf Norinder first author.

name: A Blue Carbon Framework for Singapore's national climate change policy (BlueCarbonSG)
summary: A project listed by NParks among awarded Marine Climate Change Science projects, which says it will do national blue carbon accounting, mapping and predictive modelling across mangrove, seagrass and mudflat ecosystems.

name: Acoustic Research Laboratory, Tropical Marine Science Institute
summary: Tropical Marine Science Institute laboratory listed by OpenAlex as lead affiliation on a 2024 paper on a cloud-enabled passive acoustic monitoring array for detecting marine mammals in real time, with NParks' Karenne Tun as last author.

name: Agridence
summary: Singapore-based technology company in digital agri-commodity supply chains, whose EUDR page says it scores plots and country, supply chain and deforestation risk against satellite layers, with rubber traceability now extended to other commodities.

name: AMBER (AI-assisted Monitoring of Biodiversity using Edge-processing and Remote sensors)
summary: Project that in May 2024 planned a network of 40 monitoring systems in biodiversity hot spots including Singapore and Kenya, funded by abrdn Charitable Foundation and using iNaturalist.

name: Asian School of the Environment
summary: Interdisciplinary school within Nanyang Technological University, run by it, researching ecology and biodiversity conservation; in May 2024 NTU reported 10 moth monitoring stations placed around Singapore.

name: Asian School of the Environment, Nanyang Technological University
summary: School run by Nanyang Technological University; NTU reported in May 2024 an AI biodiversity monitoring unit on campus and ten moth monitoring stations around Singapore, and it publishes dung beetle records to GBIF.

name: Biodiversity Impact Partnership
summary: Programme launched on 21 November 2024 at the COP29 Singapore Pavilion by the NUS Centre for Nature-based Climate Solutions and XPRIZE, focused on technology for biodiversity in Southeast Asia.

name: Biodiversity of Singapore
summary: Online reference collection and research database of Singapore species, hosted by the Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum, which says it adds an average of 200 species a month.

name: BIOME
summary: Biodiversity database run by the National Parks Board, where users can explore and submit sightings of flora or fauna.

name: Bird Society of Singapore
summary: Registered society, launched on 27 August 2023 after the Singapore Birds Project, that partnered with eBird in October 2025 and runs the Singapore Bird Database.

name: Blue Catalyst
summary: Twelve-month Singapore programme, run by WWF Singapore and Hatch Blue, for technologies tackling implementation and MRV challenges in blue carbon credits; its 2026 cohort includes Arkadiah Technology and Kumi Analytics.

name: Centre for Remote Imaging, Sensing and Processing
summary: National University of Singapore centre that, according to Sentinel Asia's site, provides wildfire hotspots for Sumatra, Kalimantan and Malaysia, computed at least twice daily from S-NPP satellite passes.

name: Centre for Wildlife Forensics
summary: A wildlife forensics centre whose molecular work, per its Animal and Veterinary Service page, uses DNA targets and genetic markers to identify wildlife and timber species, and which builds and curates reference libraries.

name: Comprehensive Marine Biodiversity Survey
summary: Survey built by the National Parks Board, whose 2024-25 annual report says its second phase launched and will use seabed corers and mobile DNA labs for reef monitoring.

name: Delta Electronics (Singapore)
summary: Company that says it joined NParks' 100k Corals Initiative with financial support, and says it fitted the St John's Island coral culture facility with custom tank monitoring, alarms and surveillance trackers.

name: Department of Biological Sciences, National University of Singapore
summary: University department listed by OpenAlex as an affiliation of the first author of a paper in Environmental DNA on spatiotemporal eDNA monitoring of marine biodiversity in a hyperurbanised coastal environment.

name: Earth Observation Initiative
summary: Programme launched on 26 February 2025 by OSTIn to apply Earth observation to sustainability and humanitarian challenges across the Asia-Pacific, now led by the National Space Agency of Singapore.

name: Earthsurance
summary: Satellite assessment and monitoring platform for projects reducing deforestation and forest degradation emissions, listed in an ST Engineering annex for a 2026 summit and said to use L-band SAR.

name: Ecological Profiling Exercise
summary: An island-wide NParks programme begun in 2021 that uses spatial models to predict wildlife movement, and which identified four new ecological corridors and, in 2022, ecologically significant habitats on Lazarus and Kusu Islands.

name: Every Singaporean a Naturalist
summary: A Nature Society Singapore programme in which students survey a transect near their school at least every two weeks and upload records to iNaturalist, building a long-term biodiversity database.

name: Forest Fire Detection and Monitoring System
summary: System built by NParks combining CCTV cameras, drones and video analytics to pinpoint fires in real time, operationalised at Bukit Panjang and Ang Mo Kio in February 2023.

name: GROVE
summary: Digital platform that a May 2020 APSIA story says Ryan Merrill developed, using smart contracts and satellite verification so donors could track use of their funds.

name: Kusu Island coral reef restoration programme
summary: Coral reef restoration programme run by WWF Singapore and the NUS Tropical Marine Science Institute, maintaining 300m of restored reef, restoring a further 200m, and using trained citizen science volunteers for monitoring.

name: Lab for Advancing Protection of biodiversity with Innovative Solutions
summary: NUS lab where, according to NUS News, bioacoustics and AI are combined to analyse large volumes of forest recordings from autonomous recorders, with researchers exploring refinement of sound-recognition models using local data.

name: Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum
summary: National University of Singapore museum of Southeast Asian specimens that publishes eight datasets to GBIF and joined a Naturalis-coordinated project to digitise its butterfly specimens.

name: Long-Term Socio-Ecological Research Programme
summary: Research programme led by NParks, which its 2025/26 annual report says includes permanent forest plots for ongoing monitoring of ecosystem and species dynamics.

name: Mandai Wildlife Group
summary: Organisation reporting camera trap and transect monitoring at Mandai Wildlife Reserve in February 2022, and saying it funds gibbon surveys and post-release monitoring of black-winged mynas.

name: Marine Stewards
summary: Singapore organisation aiming to engage sea sports enthusiasts as citizen scientists for marine conservation, whose site describes ReefX as training recreational scuba divers to gather reef survey data.

name: Multi-Agent Robotics Vision and Learning Lab, SUTD
summary: SUTD lab led by Malika Meghjani, whose AI-powered robot creates low-resolution 3D coral reef twins within minutes using Maplion, according to The Straits Times.

name: Nanyang Technological University
summary: Singapore university whose news page reports scientists using AI and moths to assess ecosystem health, and which began a partnership with the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute in 2015.

name: National Institute of Education
summary: An autonomous institute within NTU and the national teacher education institute, whose authors appear on OpenAlex-listed papers on mangrove degradation mapping with deep learning and on connectivity for an arboreal gliding mammal.

name: National Parks Board
summary: Singapore government agency leading on greenery, biodiversity and wildlife, which in 2024-25 reported grants for machine-learning acoustic monitoring and environmental DNA tools, and $1.34 million for drones and robotics.

name: National Space Agency of Singapore
summary: Department under the Ministry of Trade & Industry, established on 1 April 2026 and taking over the functions of OSTIn, Singapore's former national space office.

name: Nature Society Singapore
summary: Society whose Bird Group, inaugurated in 1986, conducts bird surveys and raptor and parrot counts, and reviews rare eBird submissions for scientific use.

name: NParks Biodiversity Watches
summary: Volunteer programme run by the National Parks Board, in which participants learn to identify and survey wildlife through watches including Heron, Dragonfly, Garden Bird, Butterfly and Intertidal.

name: NParks Flora & Fauna Web
summary: Information portal run by the National Parks Board on plants grown in the region and animals found in Singapore, with data updated regularly.

name: NParks-Delta Corals Research Programme
