summary: Collaboration between NParks and Delta Electronics set up to start the 100k Corals Initiative, with tanks announced in December 2024 to carry a smart aquaculture system for remote monitoring, and a citizen science training programme planned.

name: Raffles' banded langur citizen science programme
summary: A citizen science programme under the 2016 species action plan, with Mongabay reporting in April 2026 over 100 weekend surveyors and roughly 900 volunteers trained.

name: ReefX
summary: Citizen science programme run by Marine Stewards with NParks, training recreational scuba divers in reef survey data collection, with CNA reporting an aim of about 60 divers trained in the year reported.

name: SGBioAtlas
summary: App built by NParks, launched on 16 April 2015 according to CNA, that lets users record biodiversity sightings and identify species, with sightings feeding NParks' online database BIOME.

name: SIGNIFY (Singapore in Global Natural History Museums Information Facility)
summary: Digital archive run by the Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum, launched 10 August 2022, that aims to digitise and publish zoological specimens collected from Singapore since 1819, published on GBIF under CC BY-NC 4.0.

name: Singapore Bird Database
summary: Bird dataset run by the Bird Society of Singapore, which says its team uses eBird data and makes it accessible through bar charts and the database.

name: Singapore Botanic Gardens
summary: NParks-listed UNESCO World Heritage Site that launched a ten-garden phenology network in August 2024, set up an Environmental Monitoring section in January 2025, and is sequencing native plant genomes with Nanyang Technological University.

name: Singapore Herbarium Digitalisation Project
summary: Project run by the Singapore Botanic Gardens, begun in 2025 to digitise the herbarium's collections and give online access, aiming to finish by 2027, with a new system planned for March 2027.

name: Singapore Land Authority
summary: Singapore's national geospatial agency by its own description, responsible for land survey and the geodetic survey system, and overseeing development and maintenance of the OneMap national map platform.

name: Singapore University of Technology and Design
summary: University partnered with the National Parks Board; The Star reported in November 2025, citing the Straits Times, that it created an underwater robot making low-resolution 3D coral reef digital twins within minutes.

name: Singapore Wildcat Action Group
summary: Group whose survey, from July 2025 to April 2026 using 18 motion-sensor cameras along the coastline for about a year, found five leopard cats in Changi's coastal forests, The Straits Times reports.

name: Southeast Asia Plant Phenology Network
summary: Network built by the Singapore Botanic Gardens, launched in August 2024 at the 8th Global Botanic Gardens Congress, bringing ten botanic gardens together for long-term phenology monitoring.

name: Southern Islands Biodiversity Survey
summary: An NParks survey begun in January 2020 and reported complete on 31 May 2025, producing the first comprehensive Southern Islands biodiversity database with over 30,000 records and 44 native species recorded for the first time.

name: STDP Thematic Grant Call (Biomass dMRV)
summary: Grant call, run by the National Space Agency of Singapore, for satellite-based digital carbon monitoring in Southeast Asian forests and coastal ecosystems, requiring validated AI or machine-learning performance; its letter of intent window closed on 27 February 2026.

name: Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve
summary: Reserve whose bird census collects monthly species data, and whose team used ringing, geolocators, radio and satellite trackers to follow threatened shorebirds, according to a 2022 government profile.

name: TeamSeaGrass
summary: Volunteer seagrass monitoring programme built by NParks and Seagrass-Watch, established in November 2006, whose volunteers have monitored seagrass health and distribution at three sites since 2007, according to NParks.

name: Thryve.Earth
summary: Carbon project developer with a Singapore address that maps land cover with satellite imagery and machine learning to find eligible parcels, listing restoration in Indonesia and agroforestry in India.

name: Tropical Forest Ecological Research programme
summary: Programme run by the Singapore Botanic Gardens, centred on permanent plots, including 160 in the Central Catchment area and two 2-ha plots in Bukit Timah, supporting long-term tree monitoring.

name: Tropical Marine Science Institute
summary: Institute listed by the UN SDG partnerships platform as the partner on a project to develop acoustic monitoring techniques for marine megafauna in Singapore waters.

name: Underwater Acoustic Monitoring of Marine Megafauna within Coastal Waters of Singapore
summary: Closed project that aimed to develop passive acoustic monitoring of dolphins visiting Sisters' Islands Marine Park, planned for March 2019 to April 2022 and extended to January 2023.

name: WWF-Singapore
summary: Conservation organisation whose site says it and NUS-TMSI are expanding a coral reef restoration programme at Kusu Island.

name: Agencija Republike Slovenije za okolje
summary: Slovenian public body that runs NarcIS, the national nature information system, which it built, and was lead organisation of the LIFE NarcIS project.

name: Atlas ptic Slovenije
summary: Dataset from a 2002 to 2017 nationwide survey by Slovenian ornithologists, with over 350,000 bird observations, prevalence maps for each breeding species and density maps for frequent ones, published in May 2019.

name: Biološki inštitut Jovana Hadžija ZRC SAZU
summary: Institute of ZRC SAZU in Ljubljana whose collections include the FloVegSi database, holding more than 1.5 million faunistic, floristic and vegetation records.

name: Biotehniška fakulteta Univerze v Ljubljani
summary: University of Ljubljana faculty that leads the Interreg project SeaInsights and partners in BIG_PICTURE (April 2024 to March 2027, 105,000 euros co-financing), which will develop AI tools for camera-trap data.

name: BugBit
summary: According to EUSPA, this Yolanda-built concept uses Sentinel-2 imagery and AI for broader forest health monitoring, with stakeholder engagement to test it in real conditions.

name: Center za kartografijo favne in flore
summary: Private non-profit institute founded in 1996 that collects Slovenian plant and animal distribution data, holds over 1,600,000 records with outside contributors, and says it is qualified for habitat mapping and monitoring.

name: Department of Knowledge Technologies, Jožef Stefan Institute
summary: Slovenian research department whose affiliation appears on a 2022 Ecological Modelling paper, listed by OpenAlex, presenting BEFANA, a network-analysis tool for assessing biodiversity-ecosystem functioning.

name: Department of Remote Sensing, ZRC SAZU
summary: Department within ZRC SAZU, led by Žiga Kokalj, that develops machine learning and AI methods for remote sensing and maintains the data processing chain of NEMO-HD, the first Slovenian satellite.

name: Developing and testing approaches to monitor subterranean biodiversity in karst
summary: Project from 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2027, valued at 1,203,931 euros, that will develop standard protocols for monitoring subterranean karst biodiversity, including DNA barcoding and environmental DNA field tests.

name: DEWESoft RealTime
summary: Maribor company founded in 2014 as IRNAS and renamed in 2026, which lists engineering work on OpenCollar wildlife trackers for Smart Parks and built the LIFT Forest project.

name: DivjaLabs d.o.o.
summary: According to Start:up Slovenia, this 2022 Biotechnical Faculty spin-out develops wildlife eDNA monitoring and leads Slovenia’s large carnivore monitoring; it partners with SeaInsights.

name: Društvo Dinaricum
summary: Volunteers carried out wolf howling surveys outside special-purpose hunting grounds on 22–25 August 2017, according to an October 2017 interim monitoring report.

name: Društvo za jamsko biologijo
summary: Based at the Tular Cave Laboratory in Kranj, the society reports a Proteus eDNA study published in March 2017 after sampling 56 karst sites.

name: Društvo za opazovanje in proučevanje ptic Slovenije
summary: Bird society whose 2024 annual report covers Natura 2000 bird monitoring, farmland bird index monitoring (SIPKK) and work on the BirdLife Forestry project.

name: Faculty of Agriculture and Life Sciences, University of Maribor
summary: University of Maribor faculty whose affiliation appears on a 2025 Šumarski list paper, listed by OpenAlex, on detecting bark beetle infestations in spruce forests using drones and image analysis.

name: Faculty of Environmental Protection, Velenje
summary: Faculty named by Biodiversa+ and the Biotechnical Faculty as a partner in BIG_PICTURE.

name: Feasibility study and mapping of vegetative landscape structures important for biodiversity and climate change mitigation with remote sensing
summary: Closed project that ran from October 2019 to July 2020, using nationwide airborne laser scanning data to propose a landscape structure mapping method reaching 90 per cent correct classification, and tested Sentinel-2 images.

name: FloVegSi (Fauna, Flora and Vegetation of Slovenia)
summary: Database of more than 1.5 million faunistic, floristic and vegetation records, mostly from Slovenia and nearby areas, created from 1987 onward, with mapping and GIS export.

name: Flycom Technologies
summary: Ljubljana remote sensing data provider that says its 2021 AI work led to the company Flai, and was a LIFT Forest consortium partner (March 2023 to February 2025) handling geospatial data.

name: GBIF Slovenia
summary: Slovenia's voting participant node in GBIF, managed by Marijan Govedič, which has endorsed four publishers including the Slovenian Forestry Institute.

name: Geodetska uprava Republike Slovenije
summary: Slovenian surveying authority that signed a January 2026 public administration agreement with Planet Labs, citing forest monitoring as one use.

name: Gozdarski inštitut Slovenije
summary: Public forest research institute in Ljubljana that lists the AI-based FORSAID monitoring project, leads its citizen science work package, and built the Machine Learning Forest Simulator.

name: Invazivke
summary: Web and mobile application for reporting invasive alien species, set up in 2017 within LIFE ARTEMIS, which received 21,217 observations from 475 observers between June 2017 and 16 March 2023.

name: IZRK Metadata Portal
summary: GeoNetwork-based metadata portal built at the Karst Research Institute's Data Centre in 2021 and 2022, following FAIR principles, with openly accessible metadata and research data open only to the institute.

name: Januarsko štetje vodnih ptic (IWC) v Sloveniji
summary: January waterbird count running in Slovenia since 1988, led by Luka Božič, in which 249 counters took part on 18 and 19 January 2025.

name: Javni zavod Park Škocjanske jame
summary: Park authority that monitors cave water, microclimate, flora, fauna and ozone, and says most of its research now aims at continuous monitoring of the park.

name: Javni zavod Triglavski narodni park
summary: Park authority that, as a partner to the Slovenia Forest Service, collected wolf data by snow tracking and howling surveys in 2023 and planned a 3,500,985 euro programme budget.

name: Karst Research Institute ZRC SAZU
summary: Postojna-based institute within ZRC SAZU whose Data Centre built the IZRK Metadata Portal in 2021 and 2022, which also lists a CC BY 4.0 Postojna Cave dataset.

name: Laboratory for Computer Graphics and Multimedia, Faculty of Computer and Information Science, University of Ljubljana
summary: University of Ljubljana laboratory that builds MULTI-MON tools for multi-modal biodiversity assessment and monitoring of small stagnant freshwater wetlands, in partnership with the National Institute of Biology.

name: LIFE ARTEMIS
summary: Closed Slovenian project from 2016 to 2020 on invasive alien species in forests, funded by the European Commission and the environment ministry, aiming to improve early detection through training professionals and citizen scientists.

name: LIFE BEAVER
summary: Closed EU-funded LIFE project, run from September 2020 to April 2025, whose BEAVERTRACK citizen science app collected 1,260 data entries and recorded 814 users.

name: LIFE Lynx
summary: Project led by the Slovenian Forest Service whose 2021 to 2022 camera trap survey detected 318 lynx events at 71 of 173 locations, identifying at least 30 adult lynx.

name: LIFE NarcIS
summary: Four-year project, closed at the end of 2024 according to DOPPS, led by the Slovenian Environment Agency, in which the NarcIS nature information system was developed.

name: LIFE TRŠCA
summary: LIFE project led by Notranjska Regional Park to improve conservation of intermittent Lake Cerknica, with water level and temperature sensors installed at eight priority areas in August 2024.

name: LIFE-IP NATURA.SI
summary: Ongoing LIFE integrated project, running from September 2018 to December 2026 with a total value of 17,007,204 euros, including an action to prepare a national Natura 2000 monitoring scheme.

name: LIFT Forest - eVTOL AI Analysis of Forest Biomass
summary: Closed project (March 2023 to February 2025) combining LiDAR on eVTOL aircraft with machine learning for forest monitoring, with expected support of about 990,000 euros.

name: LTER Slovenia
summary: Slovenian long-term ecological research network, established in 2003, with eight consortium partners and 16 research sites across caves, lakes, forests and sea, on the national research infrastructure roadmap since 2016.

name: Machine Learning Forest Simulator
summary: Standalone forest development model for studying growth, regeneration, mortality and felling, developed by members of a department at the Slovenian Forestry Institute.

name: MedvedoFON
summary: Web tool for reporting large carnivore sightings where they threaten people's lives or property, built by the Environment Agency and opened to the public the year before October 2026.

name: Ministrstvo za okolje in prostor
summary: Slovenian ministry preparing a nature restoration plan targeting at least 20 per cent of land and sea by 2030, which reported Slovenian attendance at COP 17.

name: Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation
summary: Slovenian ministry listed as Biodiversa+'s partner for Slovenia and named as a funder of the Biotechnical Faculty's part in BIG_PICTURE.

name: Ministry of the Environment and Spatial Planning
summary: Slovenian ministry whose minister attended the informal meeting of EU environment and climate ministers in Ireland in July 2026.

name: Monitoring bobra (national beaver monitoring, Slovenia)
summary: National beaver monitoring in Slovenia, absent as a systematic programme until 2022, which recorded 22,019 signs of beaver presence across 135 watercourse sections and 54 standing waters in three seasons.

name: Monitoring izbranih ciljnih vrst metuljev
summary: Butterfly monitoring programme using standardised transects, commissioned by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Food and carried out by a mapping centre, with Apollo butterfly transects repeated for the thirteenth time in 2025.

name: Monitoring netopirjev (Slovenian national bat monitoring)
summary: National bat monitoring in Slovenia, with a 2024-2026 report naming the Centre for Cartography of Fauna and Flora as contractor and recording 16 inspections of underground roosts in winter 2025/2026.

name: Monitoring populacij izbranih ciljnih vrst ptic na območjih Natura 2000
summary: Monitoring of selected qualifying bird species at Natura 2000 sites; its 2019 report covers 18 species and says the TRIM program was used for the analysis.

name: Monitoring populacij izbranih ciljnih vrst rib
summary: Monitoring of selected target fish and lamprey species, repeated every six years, with a 2021 report prepared under a Ministry of the Environment and Spatial Planning contract and attributed to ZZRS.

name: Monitoring splošno razširjenih vrst ptic za določitev SIPKK
summary: Standard two-band transect bird survey whose index on 145 transects showed a moderate 21 per cent decline in 2008 to 2018, according to the 2018 DOPPS report.

name: Morigenos - slovensko društvo za morske sesalce
summary: Slovenian marine mammal society collecting northern Adriatic bottlenose dolphin data since 2002, which reported in September 2023 that it had photo-identified over 400 individuals in 20 years.

name: Morska biološka postaja Piran
summary: Marine research unit run by the National Institute of Biology, described by the environment ministry as the only Slovenian unit working only on marine ecosystem research, with long-running environmental monitoring.

name: MULTI-MON - development of multimodal biodiversity monitoring for (small) wetlands
summary: Project dated 2023 to 2026 that develops tools to monitor small stagnant freshwater wetlands from underwater sound and environmental DNA, and plans a regional DNA reference database and sound libraries.

name: Nacionalni inštitut za biologijo
summary: Public research institute in Ljubljana that runs the Marine Biology Station Piran, offers continuous monitoring of Slovenian water quality and invites public help to discover toxic cyanobacteria.

name: Naravovarstveni atlas
summary: Graphic viewer of natural values listed by the government as belonging to the Institute of the Republic of Slovenia for Nature Conservation, which updated its data in 2024.

name: NarcIS
summary: Slovenian species information system, built in the LIFE NarcIS project and run by the environment agency, holding almost 21,000 of an estimated 37,000 or more recorded species in October 2026.

name: Notranjski regijski park
summary: Regional park that monitors birds on Lake Cerknica with a drone carrying thermal and zoom cameras under LIFE TRŠCA, reporting about one hundred nests in its latest count in April 2025.

name: Ocena številčnosti rjavega medveda v Sloveniji v letu 2023 (genetic monitoring of brown bear abundance)
summary: Genetic estimate of Slovenia's brown bear numbers from 2,863 samples collected in 2023, reported by the ministry as a minimum autumn population of 737 bears, run by the Slovenia Forest Service.

name: Prirodoslovni muzej Slovenije
summary: Ljubljana public institute running the Slovenian Bird Ringing Centre, keeping ringing data in a program created in 2000 and holding the Slovenian Archive of Animal Sounds.

name: SeaInsights
summary: Project that plans to use environmental DNA to assess marine fauna in the northern Adriatic and to develop individual-level marine mammal identification, with a first sampling device prototype tested in Piran in June 2024.

name: Slovenian Bird Ringing Centre
summary: Programme within the Slovenian Museum of Natural History that rings more than 100,000 birds a year, relies largely on volunteers and is led by Dare Šere.

name: Slovenian National Forest Inventory
summary: Active national programme, set up in its current form in 2020 and built by the Slovenian Forestry Institute, whose data monitor forest state and change nationally, regionally and in international reports.

name: Slovenian Space Office
summary: Body that coordinates space technology issues within Slovenia's EU membership and ESA cooperation, and presents Slovenia's positions on ESA bodies such as the Earth Observation Programme Board.

name: Slovenian Wildlife Sound Archive
summary: Study collection of mostly original animal call and song recordings held by the Slovenian Museum of Natural History, aiming to cover all vocalising species in Slovenia, with no full-time curator.

name: Slovenski podjetniški sklad
summary: Slovenian enterprise fund whose P2 programme, according to EUSPA, gave public funding to the start-up Yolanda, and which Start:up Slovenia names as a main partner.

name: Sporoči vrsto
summary: Species recording campaign revived within the LIFE NarcIS project, according to a 2024 article, and run by ZRSVN.

name: Spremljanje stanja ohranjenosti volka v Sloveniji
summary: Wolf monitoring commissioned by the Ministry of Natural Resources and Spatial Planning collected 811 non-invasive genetic samples in 2024–2025 and estimated population size using capture-mark-recapture.

name: Univerza v Ljubljani
summary: University whose Biotechnical Faculty leads the SeaInsights eDNA project and was among the bodies that carried out the LIFE NarcIS project.

name: Vrhnika Trapping Site
summary: Ornithological station founded in 1987, run by the Slovenian Bird Ringing Centre, with annual ringing from mid-July to October’s end and a barn swallow study begun in 1987.

name: Vzpostavitev in izvajanje monitoringa populacije vidre (Slovenian otter monitoring)
summary: Otter monitoring for 2022/23 and 2023/24, documented in Lutra’s 2024 report for the ministry, which says Lutra had collected 210 dead otter records since 2003.

name: Yolanda d.o.o.
summary: According to EUSPA, a Maribor-based start-up incorporated after the 2022 CASSINI Hackathon, which won 10,000 euros in the myEUspace competition and received P2 public funding.

name: Zavod Republike Slovenije za varstvo narave
summary: Slovenia's public nature conservation body, which manages biodiversity databases, monitors conservation status, and says it has carried out over thirty internationally or European-funded projects in ten years.

name: Zavod za gozdove Slovenije
summary: Slovenian forest body based in Ljubljana that is coordinating beneficiary of the LIFE Lynx project and was one of the bodies that carried out LIFE NarcIS.

name: Zavod za ribištvo Slovenije
summary: Slovenian fisheries institute that prepared the 2021 Natura 2000 report on the Italian barbel for the environment ministry, using its sampling data and citing its BIOS biological database.

name: ZDrauA
summary: Cross-border project, planned for 2025 to 2027 with four partners, to harmonise next-generation biomonitoring of the Drava/Drau River in Austria and Slovenia and build a shared DNA reference database.

name: Znanstvenoraziskovalni center Slovenske akademije znanosti in umetnosti
summary: Slovenian research centre whose Department of Remote Sensing develops machine learning methods, and which carried out a 2019 to 2020 remote sensing project mapping landscape structures important for biodiversity.

name: Živo podzemlje
summary: Through three web forms requesting photographs, the website collects records of cave and other subterranean animals, according to University of Ljubljana speleobiology group authors writing about LIFE NarcIS.

name: BIG – Flower & invertebrate phenology time series
summary: Active project, listed by UNIS under Arctic Biology and run by it, using time-lapse cameras taking one image per minute above plants and invertebrate traps; the page says machine learning methods for the same data have been advanced elsewhere.

name: Bjørndalen Integrated Gradients (BIG)
summary: A research platform set up in 2019 by UNIS's Department of Arctic Biology, built and run by the University Centre in Svalbard, combining research, learning and monitoring across terrestrial, benthic and marine habitats.

name: Drone-based reindeer counting in Svalbard
summary: A 2021 pilot, built by the University Centre in Svalbard and the Norwegian Polar Institute, comparing drone imagery counts with foot and helicopter counts, mapping over 12 square kilometres; machine learning was then only planned.

name: Governor of Svalbard
summary: Svalbard's principal environmental protection authority, according to the Ny-Ålesund Research Station site, whose Environmental Protection Department handles nature supervision, environmental monitoring and management of protected areas, flora and fauna.

name: International Kongsfjorden Year 2024-2025
summary: Closed year-round monitoring programme in Kongsfjorden from August 2024 to 2025, set up within the Kongsfjorden System Flagship, in which scientists from several institutions and countries collected multidisciplinary marine ecosystem data.

name: Inventory of the terrestrial and freshwater fauna of the Svalbard archipelago
summary: Active GBIF checklist of Svalbard terrestrial and freshwater fauna, built from species names in almost 800 publications from 1869 to 2023, assessed by taxon experts and published by the University Centre in Svalbard.

name: Isfjorden Adventfjorden time series (IsA) station
summary: A marine sampling station established in December 2011, sampled year-round as a model system for climate change effects on Arctic ecosystems and listed as the long-term marine time series of the BIG platform.

name: Isfjorden Marine Observatory Svalbard
summary: Plankton time series project in Isfjorden, led by Janne Søreide and partnered with UNIS, which a 2018 item described as aiming for a long-term series; by 2021 some compiled series reached back 20 years.

name: Kings Bay AS
summary: A company owned by the Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment, state-owned since 1933, that provides the infrastructure for research and monitoring at Ny-Ålesund, including the port, airport and logistics.

name: Kongsfjorden Rijpfjorden Observatory Program
summary: Active underwater observatory programme in two Svalbard fjords, established by UiT, UNIS and SAMS, monitoring the marine environment for almost 20 years, with 2002–2024 Kongsfjorden data published in November 2024.

name: Netherlands Arctic Station
summary: Active station in Ny-Ålesund, run by the University of Groningen, that monitors barnacle geese, Arctic terns and foxes, and offers data on marked barnacle geese and marked foxes.

name: Ny-Ålesund Research Station
summary: A high Arctic station for natural science research and environmental monitoring, run by Kings Bay AS, where more than 20 research institutions carry out long-term monitoring and the Norwegian Polar Institute is Norway's host.

name: Paw Prints to DNA – Non-invasive polar bear monitoring using eDNA derived from snow tracks in Svalbard
summary: An active project running from December 2023 to December 2026, run by the Norwegian Institute of Bioeconomy Research and funded by WWF Sweden, testing eDNA from snow footprints for polar bear mark-recapture monitoring.

name: Svalbard Integrated Arctic Earth Observing System
summary: A 2024 evaluation describes a 28-institution, 10-country consortium offering Svalbard Earth system data and remote sensing services, with its legal entity fully owned by UNIS.

name: Svalbard Italian Observatory
summary: Active observatory run by the CNR Institute of Polar Sciences, with four monitoring sites (three in the Kongsfjorden-Krossfjorden system, one in the Fram Strait) collecting physical, biogeochemical and biological water column data.

name: The Optimisation of the Kongsfjorden Rijpfjorden Observatory Program
summary: Active project funded by the Research Council of Norway's Polar Program, running January 2024 to December 2027, aiming to develop reproducible protocols, a data management plan and a long-term plan for the KROP time series.

name: The University Centre in Svalbard
summary: A Longyearbyen institution listed by GBIF as a data publisher, whose Arctic Biology Department does Arctic research and whose scientists tested drone-based reindeer counting with the Norwegian Polar Institute in 2021.

name: VECNA: Knocking on Arctic Door – Svalbard’s NIMS and door knocker fish species in the marine coastal waters
summary: A project begun in 2023 to monitor the arrival of non-indigenous marine species and possible door-knocker species in Arctic waters, especially Kongsfjorden, with a record covering its 2024 survey and sampling methods.

name: Aevis
summary: Slovak organisation whose experts have long monitored large carnivores in Poloniny National Park; an August 2026 article says it made the Cluey app available in Slovak for COOP4SAFE, and in October 2026 it reported a stalled exemption application.

name: AquaBOL.SK
summary: Slovak programme aiming at a full library of standardised DNA barcodes for all aquatic species in the country, published in the public BOLD database, with a third year of MinION sequencing reported in May 2024.

name: Atlas hniezd bociana bieleho
summary: Dataset created in 2000 that gathers white stork arrival and nesting data in Slovakia from regional correspondents, public on bociany.sk since 2003 and holding 5,900 nest records in the 2025 bulletin.

name: Biodiversa+ pilotný projekt monitoringu biodiverzity (ÚKE SAV)
summary: Completed pilot, 2024 to 2025, run by the Institute of Landscape Ecology SAS, covering habitat mapping and automated monitoring of birds, bats and night insects within Biodiversa+ work package 2.

name: BROZ - ochranárske združenie
summary: Non-governmental organisation in Bratislava protecting and restoring Slovak nature; under LIFE Metamorphosis it asks volunteers to record butterflies, initially Colias myrmidone in the Bošácka and Moravsko-Lieskovská valleys.

name: Chránime spoločné endemity (SPEN)
summary: Led by the Technical University in Zvolen, this project runs until 30 September 2027, with key activities including unified monitoring, data sharing, and genetic and health research.

name: Complex Information and Monitoring System (KIMS)
summary: Slovak database of plant, animal and habitat records, run and built by the State Nature Conservancy, in use since 2015, which the LIFE-IP project expects to update and fill with Natura 2000 status data.

name: DAPHNE – Inštitút aplikovanej ekológie
summary: Non-governmental organisation in Bratislava that began collecting the city's biodiversity data through iNaturalist in spring 2025, held a pilot BioBranie event in May 2026 and plans another for 2027.

name: DNA barcoding Slovenska (SK-BOL)
summary: Closed DNA barcoding project for Slovakia, run by the Institute of Zoology SAS, which in 2022 obtained COI-5P barcode sequences for 270 species and entered full BOLD records for 80 insect species.

name: Ekologický experimentálny stacionár Kremnické vrchy
summary: Long-term ecological research site in a beech forest, founded in 1986 and run by the Institute of Forest Ecology SAS, in LTER Slovakia since 2008 and registered in ILTER.

name: Fatranský spolok
summary: Non-profit based in Varín, Slovakia, that studies wild animals, mainly large carnivores, in Malá Fatra using camera traps and summer bear monitoring; its newest own news item dates from October 2016.

name: FOMON
summary: Closed project, December 2019 to June 2023, researching contactless forest monitoring and cognitive intelligence analysis, with planned point cloud and hyperspectral classification procedures.

name: GBIF Slovakia
summary: Slovakia's country node in GBIF, which has voting participation, is based at the Institute of Botany in Bratislava, is led by Karol Marhold, and has ten endorsed publishers.

name: InfoKliešť
summary: Run by the Institute of Zoology SAS, it asks the public for tick photos and locations to help an AI recognise ticks and map them; an app reported for 2027.

name: Institute of Forest Ecology, Slovak Academy of Sciences
summary: Slovak Academy of Sciences institute named as coordinator of RESDiNET, which aimed to strengthen its remote sensing capabilities in forest disturbance ecology during 2023 to 2025.

name: Institute of Geography, Slovak Academy of Sciences
summary: Slovak Academy of Sciences institute that ran the LAPIA project as contractor, with the Slovak University of Technology and the Soil Science and Conservation Research Institute as subcontractors.

name: Koordinácia ochrany, monitoringu a manažmentu západokarpatskej populácie vlka dravého a rysa ostrovida na československom pomedzí
summary: Closed Slovak-Czech project on Western Carpathian wolf and lynx, which planned camera-trap monitoring across 140 squares of 5 by 5 km, population density estimates from recaptures, and a shared database of field signs and individuals.

name: Krúžkovacia centrála SOS/BirdLife Slovensko
summary: Bird ringing centre within SOS/BirdLife Slovakia; in 2023, 59 ringers ringed 72,658 birds of 151 species in Slovakia and 720 recoveries from abroad were registered.

name: LAnd cover change monitoring for identification of Potential Illegal Activities in Slovakia (LAPIA)
summary: Completed project, run by the Institute of Geography and supported by the European Space Agency, designing ways to detect illegal landscape changes from Sentinel imagery and airborne laser scanning, with the Environmental Inspectorate as potential user.

name: LIFE Danube Free Sky
summary: Six-year project with 15 partners from seven countries, led by Raptor Protection of Slovakia; initial 2021 monitoring checked 12,535 pylons along more than 1,380 km of power lines, with camera traps planned for bird mortality.

name: LIFE-IP NATURA 2000 SK
summary: Ministry-led project running 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2030 to implement Slovakia's Natura 2000 Prioritised Action Framework for 2021-2027, with partners and status data expected in KIMS.

name: Living with Carpathian Spirits
summary: Closed lynx project run by the Slovak Wildlife Society, which used 60-day camera-trapping sessions in two reference areas, plus snow tracking and DNA sampling, and captured 843 lynx images.

name: LTER Slovakia
summary: National long-term ecological research network, run by the Institute of Landscape Ecology SAS, whose sites and platforms are managed by four organisations; a founding member of LTER Europe.

name: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development of the Slovak Republic
summary: Slovak ministry that, according to a 2023 National Forest Centre presentation, has the forest monitoring system ČMS Lesy under its remit, and whose site carries the National Forestry Programme for 2025-2030.

name: Ministry of Environment of the Slovak Republic
summary: Slovak ministry in Bratislava hosting the primary CBD focal point and leading the LIFE-IP NATURA 2000 SK project, with a nature and landscape protection section and a biodiversity department.

name: Monitoring a výskum lesných ekosystémov
summary: Project with Swiss Contribution funding of CHF 2,088,000 that proposes combining a digital aerial camera and airborne laser scanner to collect forest health, structure and timber volume data, partly to deter illegal activity.

name: Monitoring biotopov a druhov európskeho významu na Slovensku
summary: Project running 1 April 2024 to 31 December 2029 under Program Slovensko, contracted at 21,136,912.25 euros, planning nationwide habitat and species monitoring on 12,822 permanent sites with national park administrations as partners.

name: Monitoring reprodukčných párov vlka dravého na Slovensku
summary: Wolf breeding pair monitoring in Slovakia, run by the National Forest Centre; a 2025 notice says it has run continuously since 2016 and is one source used to set the annual hunting quota.

name: MORIDEK: Modelovanie vplyvov rastlinných invázií na Dunajské ekosystémy
summary: Closed research project, run by the Institute of Landscape Ecology SAS, that combined ecology, remote sensing and modelling to study invasive plants in Danube wetlands, producing species occurrence databases and an open leaf spectra dataset.

name: National Forest Centre
summary: State-funded forestry organisation in Zvolen under the agriculture ministry, offering forest inventory and typology datasets, ForestPortal and a grey wolf mapping application, and a partner in LIFE-IP NATURA 2000 SK.

name: New Slovakian breeding bird monitoring scheme
summary: Breeding bird monitoring scheme run by SOS/BirdLife Slovakia, listed on the Pan-European Common Bird Monitoring Scheme's Slovakia page alongside an earlier common bird count that ran from 1994 to 2025.

name: Národná inventarizácia a monitoring lesov SR
summary: Statistical inventory of Slovakia's forests built by the National Forest Centre, with field plots on a 4 by 4 km grid (3,069 plots) and field collection for the next cycle expected in 2025 to 2026.

name: Národná zoologická záhrada Bojnice
summary: Zoo established by the Ministry of Environment; a June 2022 article says wildcat research found hybrids with domestic cats, four being 15% of the Strážovské vrchy population recorded.

name: Orthoptera of Slovakia
summary: Gives distribution maps and habitat, occurrence and conservation status information for Slovak Orthoptera; led by Anton Krištín, mapped since 1994, with public help since 2006, per CVTI SR.

name: Plant Science and Biodiversity Centre, Slovak Academy of Sciences
summary: Bratislava research centre of the Slovak Academy of Sciences that includes the Institute of Botany, hosts GBIF Slovakia's address, and lists remote sensing, DNA barcoding and biodiversity informatics databases among its work.

name: Raptor Protection of Slovakia
summary: Bratislava conservation organisation coordinating LIFE STEPPE ON BORDER for 2022 to 2027, whose members supported eagle monitoring described in a 2022 paper, including drone checks from 2019.

name: Realizácia programov starostlivosti o veľké šelmy na Slovensku
summary: Closed large carnivore project run by the State Nature Conservancy, which by 2022 had tracked 28 animals by telemetry and by end 2020 had collected 1,334 bear DNA samples, recording occurrences in KIMS.

name: RESDiNET
summary: Closed Horizon Europe project, January 2023 to December 2025, led by the Institute of Forest Ecology, aiming to identify spruce bark beetle infestations using drones and machine learning.

name: Slovak Academy of Sciences
summary: Slovak research body listed as a BiodivMon partner in Biodiversa+'s report on its 2022-2023 biodiversity monitoring call; its Institute of Zoology is a GBIF Slovakia-endorsed publisher.

name: Slovak Wildlife Society
summary: Civic association in Liptovský Hrádok, founded in 2005, working on brown bears, wolves and lynx; from 2013 to 2015 it implemented a pilot of systematic lynx monitoring.

name: Slovenská agentúra životného prostredia
summary: Specialist organisation of the Ministry of the Environment, set up in 1993, whose experts processed and updated Slovakia's land cover data for the completed and published CORINE Land Cover 2024 mapping.

name: SOS/BirdLife Slovakia
summary: Bird conservation organisation collecting bird data, organising censuses according to Wikipedia, participating in LIFE STEPPE ON BORDER, and party to a camera-trap and DNA monitoring agreement ending in 2021.

name: Spoločnosť pre ochranu netopierov na Slovensku
summary: Civic association in Bardejov for bat protection and research across Slovakia, founded in 1993 to count bats at winter roosts and later extended to summer attic colonies; says it belongs to BatLife Europe.

name: Správa Chránenej krajinnej oblasti Kysuce
summary: Administration of the Kysuce protected landscape area whose 2023 report describes year-round camera trap monitoring of large carnivores and records 26 wolf track trails during February 2023 monitoring.

name: Správa Národného parku Malá Fatra
summary: Park administration named as organiser of winter large carnivore monitoring with volunteers, first held in 2016, in which wolf and lynx scat is taken for genetic and diet analysis.

name: Správa Národného parku Muránska planina
summary: Park administration that monitors bats each winter with volunteers, is one of three partners restoring capercaillie habitat monitored by camera traps, and partners in the national species and habitats monitoring project.

name: Správa Národného parku Nízke Tatry
summary: Administration of the Low Tatras National Park, seated in Banská Bystrica, whose 28 staff took part in the autumn Tatra chamois count on 28 October 2026.

name: Správa Národného parku Poloniny
summary: Park administration that fitted satellite collars to two adult male bison at the end of winter 2026 and plans camera-trap monitoring of large carnivores and wildcat, using 25 camera traps donated by Aevis.

name: Správa Národného parku Slovenský kras
summary: In February 2022, this park administration reported 30 years of hibernating bat monitoring, starting in 1991/1992, with about 100 underground sites included in annual counts by then.

name: Správa Národného parku Slovenský raj
summary: Park administration that monitors animals with camera traps, mainly in areas closed to visitors; one installed in November 2021 recorded wolves and, two days later, a bear family.

name: Správa Národného parku Veľká Fatra
summary: Park administration that runs year-round monitoring of carnivores, raptors, amphibians and rare plants with more than 40 camera traps, and removed a non-transmitting collar from the bear Slava in May 2018.

name: Správa Pieninského národného parku
summary: Park administration that takes part in national species and habitat monitoring, tracks invasive species, Apollo butterfly and white storks, records data on biomonitoring.sk and bociany.sk, and maps bear, wolf and lynx in autumn and winter.

name: Správa slovenských jaskýň
summary: Cave administration, founded in 1970 and a unit of the State Nature Conservancy since 2008, with long-term bat monitoring and fixed biospeleological plots for sampling cave invertebrates.

name: Správa Tatranského národného parku
summary: Led by Michal Babnič, this administration participated in the November 2025 chamois census involving 111 counters and takes part in SPEN’s planned chamois and marmot DNA work.

name: State List of Specially Protected Parts of Nature and Landscape
summary: Official Slovak list of specially protected parts of nature and landscape, operated by the State Nature Conservancy of the Slovak Republic.

name: State Nature Conservancy of the Slovak Republic
summary: National expert body for nature protection in Banská Bystrica that monitors ecosystems, keeps the protected species register, runs the KIMS and the state list, and uses camera traps and GPS collars.

name: Systém rýchleho varovania (invázne druhy)
summary: Reporting system that sends Slovak sightings of invasive alien species of EU concern to the competent authorities quickly, for early eradication, and also accepts suspected Asian hornet sightings.

name: Technical University in Zvolen
summary: University that was Partner 1 in FOMON (December 2019 to June 2023), which included analysing forest ecosystem data on an artificial intelligence platform, and is a partner in the NLC forest monitoring project.

name: Vtáčia hodinka
summary: Winter feeder count run by SOS/BirdLife Slovensko; CVTI SR reports over 2,500 people recorded over 73,000 birds of 87 species in 2024; next count 8 to 10 January 2027.

name: Vážky (Odonata) Slovenska
summary: Dragonfly mapping project run by the Institute of Landscape Ecology SAS, described by CVTI SR as joint with civic association SOM Vážka, using iNaturalist.

name: Výskumná stanica a Múzeum TANAP-u
summary: Tatra National Park research and documentation unit, run by the park administration, which monitors changes after the 2004 windstorm and later disturbances, and the invasive northern bark beetle.

name: Wolf Mountains
summary: Programme covering 814 square kilometres, started in 2016 and run by Frankfurt Zoological Society, which has added camera traps for national parks and, in Slovakia, improved protection for over 2,000 hectares.

name: WWF Slovakia
summary: Conservation organisation, Bratislava-based, party to a cooperation agreement to 31 December 2021 on camera-trap and DNA monitoring of large carnivores and other species in the Prešov and Košice regions.

name: Zimné sčítanie vodného vtáctva na Slovensku
summary: Slovak part of an international programme counting non-breeding waterbirds, organised in its present form since 1991; the 2026 count in Slovenský raj ran from 10 to 25 January.

name: ÚGKK SR
summary: Slovak geodesy body that, with GKÚ Bratislava and VÚGK, checks and accepts contractors' work in the 2022 to 2026 airborne laser scanning cycle, which includes vegetation classes in point clouds.

name: Ústav krajinnej ekológie SAV, v. v. i.
summary: Bratislava research institute that is a partner in Restore4Life, mainly assessing and monitoring wetlands in Slovakia, and whose MORIDEK project measured leaf spectral properties and traits of invasive and native trees.

name: Ústav zoológie SAV, v. v. i.
summary: Bratislava institute whose 2022 annual report says it was carrying out the DNA barcoding of Slovakia project (SK-BOL), obtaining COI-5P barcode sequences for 270 species.

name: Čiastkový monitorovací systém Lesy
summary: One of ten partial monitoring systems created by government resolution as the basis of Slovakia's environmental information system, run by the agriculture ministry, with Level I forest condition monitoring since 1988.

name: Building Capacity to Monitor Forest Vegetation and Carbon Change in the Upper Guinea Forest through Permanent Sample Plots
summary: Closed project funded by USAID through Tetra Tech and run by RAP-SL, which sampled two one-hectare permanent plots in each of two national parks; the dataset description reports 3,059 occurrence records of 235 species.

name: Camera Trap Survey for Wildcats and Other Threatened Mammals around Gola Rainforest National Park
summary: Grant awarded on 27 May 2020 by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund for a camera trap survey of wild cats and other high conservation value species, mapping habitats for protection.

name: Conservation of the Critically Endangered Freshwater Crab (Afrithelphusa gerhildae) at the Outamba-Kilimi National Park, Sierra Leone, Through Monitoring Strategies
summary: Rufford-listed Sierra Leone project, dated January 2025, that aims to collect population, reproduction and water quality data on a Critically Endangered freshwater crab, for an IUCN Red List reassessment.

name: Conservation Society of Sierra Leone
summary: Sierra Leone NGO, which says it was founded in 1986, and whose CEPF report describes two waterbird censuses and a six-group biodiversity survey in Yawri Bay.

name: Conservation Trust Fund
summary: Fund established in 2012 together with the National Protected Area Authority, which mobilises resources for it and is a source of sustainable financing for biodiversity conservation and wildlife management.

name: Department of Geology, Fourah Bay College, University of Sierra Leone
summary: University department in Freetown, affiliated with the first author of a 2026 paper on land use and land cover change across Sierra Leone's districts using a global deep-learning Sentinel-2 product.

name: Department of Wildlife Management and Conservation, School of Natural Resources Management, Njala University
summary: University department listed as first author Jonathan Johnny's affiliation on a 2025 paper, whose study used field surveys, GIS mapping and biodiversity indices and identified 138 wetlands across seven zones in Bo City.

name: Developing a National Key Biodiversity Area (KBA) Assessment Protocol and Evaluating the Status of a Pilot Legacy KBA
summary: Closed pilot project, led by the Conservation Society of Sierra Leone and funded by JRS with US$34,500 (July 2024 to June 2025), to develop a national Key Biodiversity Area assessment protocol.

name: Environment Protection Agency Sierra Leone
summary: Agency that says it safeguards natural resources and biodiversity; a report on its 2025 work says it updated the NBSAP and prepared the 7th National Biodiversity Report.

name: Forestry Division, Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (Sierra Leone)
summary: Government division, run by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change, which with FAO started a two-week training and data collection activity in April 2024, reported as producing land cover data for designing a national forest inventory.

name: GBIF Sierra Leone
summary: GBIF node for Sierra Leone, listed as an associate country participant, whose node record was created in March 2022.

name: Gola Pygmy Hippo Research
summary: Research run by Gola Rainforest Conservation using questionnaires, river surveys, camera traps and transects, finding pygmy hippos mainly along larger rivers and more abundant in community forest than inside the national park.

name: Gola Rainforest Conservation
summary: Company limited by guarantee formed by the Forestry Division, CSSL, the RSPB and the seven Gola chiefdoms, whose regular monitoring includes remote sensing of forest cover, forest carbon, camera traps and species surveys.

name: Gola Rainforest National Park Park Protection Programme
summary: Ranger patrol programme, run by Gola Rainforest Conservation, to control illegal activity in the national park, with patrol data held in SMART and used for planning and long-term impact assessment.

name: Gola REDD+ Project
summary: Project launched in 2013, built by the Forestry Division, the Conservation Society of Sierra Leone and the RSPB, using carbon credit sales to fund conservation over 30 years and a monitoring programme.

name: Institute of Geography and Development Studies, School of Environmental Sciences, Njala University
summary: Njala University institute at Njala Campus, affiliated with the first author of two 2026 Landsat-based papers, on forest cover change and on land use change and degradation in Njaluahun Chiefdom.

name: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (Sierra Leone)
summary: Its Forestry Division and FAO started a two-week training and data collection activity for national forest inventory design, scheduled for 15 to 26 April 2024.

name: National Protected Area Authority
summary: In August 2026, launched a joint patrol at Mamunta Mayossoh Wildlife Sanctuary with the Conservation Trust Fund and the armed forces.

name: Njala University
summary: University whose Institute of Geography and Development Studies is affiliated with the first author of a 2026 Landsat forest cover study, and whose staff joined CSSL-coordinated waterbird census training on Tasso Island.

name: Primates Biomonitoring, and Capacity Building of Local Community Members for Ecotourism and Conservation Gains in Jaibui Island and Adjacent Human Communities
summary: Rufford-listed Sierra Leone project, now closed, that planned SMART-based wildlife biomonitoring on Jaibui Island with six trained community bio-monitors, and has a final evaluation report dated October 2024.

name: Reptile and Amphibian Program Sierra Leone
summary: Freetown non-profit that, reported in April 2026, monitors sea turtles and manatees in bycatch yearly with local fishermen and youths, and is listed by IUCN as implementer of a 2014-2015 turtle project.

name: Sea Turtle Conservation Programme in Sierra Leone
summary: Run by the Conservation Society of Sierra Leone, the programme hired youths for monitoring; a case study reports five nesting species, with green turtles the most common bycatch species.

name: Support to Sustainable Forestry in Sierra Leone
summary: Project launched in 2023, funded by the EU Delegation in Freetown with FAO technical help, which in April 2024 aimed to build an inventory design for the planned national forest inventory.

name: Understanding the Biodiversity Conservation Benefits Under Carbon Finance Projects (Gola)
summary: Rufford Foundation-listed project of May 2022, carried out as PhD research, using bioacoustic recorders to monitor bird calls; soundscape saturation was higher in Gola Rainforest National Park than in the community agroforestry area.

name: WCF chimpanzee biomonitoring in Sierra Leone
summary: Programme run by the Wild Chimpanzee Foundation with the NPAA in the OKKPS transboundary landscape, defined as repeatedly surveying the distribution and frequency of chimpanzees.

name: Centro Naturalistico Sammarinese
summary: San Marino's CNS has sat within the Department of the Territory and Environment since 2012, serves as CITES Scientific Authority, is legally responsible for wildlife monitoring and censuses, and hosts the Wildlife Observatory.

name: National bat atlas of San Marino
summary: A national bat atlas and database project in San Marino, which a June 2010 report said was ongoing and collecting data for all species, led by the Centro Naturalistico Sammarinese.

name: Segreteria di Stato per il Territorio e l'Ambiente (San Marino)
summary: Holds the agriculture brief in San Marino, with a proposal cited in a December 2025 commission decision and its Secretary of State reportedly chairing and coordinating the Wildlife Observatory.

name: Ufficio Gestione Risorse Ambientali e Agricole (San Marino)
summary: San Marino office whose 2023 service charter lists monitoring and management of animal species, a wild fauna and flora protection sector, and the Wildlife Observatory set up under Law 52 of 2007.

name: Ufficio Tecnico del Catasto e Cartografia (San Marino)
summary: San Marino's land registry and mapping office, which according to its service charter keeps territorial cartography up to date, manages base maps through an integrated GIS and carries out periodic aerial photogrammetric surveys.

name: Wolf monitoring in San Marino
summary: Wolf monitoring run by the Centro Naturalistico Sammarinese, which the Wildlife Observatory judged sound in December 2025, reporting no population increase on previous years and agreeing to strengthen monitoring tools.

name: African Aquatic Conservation Fund
summary: Conservation body working on the Atlantic humpback dolphin in Senegal's Saloum Delta, with yearly eDNA sampling and passive acoustic recorders.

name: African wild dog conservation in Niokolo-Koba
summary: An active project in Senegal, run by ZSL with IUCN as partner, using camera trapping, faecal genetics and possibly GPS tracking, according to IUCN, to inform a national action plan for African wild dogs.

name: Agence Nationale de l'Aménagement du Territoire
summary: Senegal's land-use planning agency. It launched the GéoSénégal geoportal and says it is taking up satellite imagery and AI for territorial planning.

name: Agence Nationale de la Statistique et de la Démographie
summary: Senegal's statistics agency, which publishes land cover accounts and trained staff on Earth observation data with Digital Earth Africa in 2025.

name: Agence Sénégalaise d'Études Spatiales
summary: Senegal's national space agency, set up in March 2023. Its satellite plans cover Earth observation, and it is advancing GEOAGRI-SEN, a project on geospatial data and AI.

name: Agence Sénégalaise de la Reforestation et de la Grande Muraille Verte
summary: State agency for reforestation and the Great Green Wall in Senegal. In July 2026 it held a first training day with Landscape Alliance on Regreening App and digital monitoring of restoration.

name: AGIRE
summary: Organisation that, with Greenpeace Africa and a marine protected areas directorate, organised a mangrove replanting on World Oceans Day 2026, aiming for 10,000 propagules over one hectare in Joal-Fadiouth.

name: AIME
summary: French and African research consortium under the ANR's IA-Biodiv challenge that uses AI to improve marine biodiversity indicators. Its members include Université Gaston Berger, Université Cheikh Anta Diop and IRD.

name: Alliance des Acteurs et Métiers des Energies au Sénégal
summary: NGO that launched the Palmarin ecosystem restoration project with the Palmarin town hall, one result being 5,000 plants reforested in the coastal area of Palmarin Ngallou.

name: Appui à l'exploitation des données ouvertes, de la technologie et de la transparence pour une meilleure gestion des pêches
summary: Three-year project funded by Oceans 5 on open data, technology and transparency for fisheries management in the Sub-Regional Fisheries Commission area, with annual workshops held with Global Fishing Watch.

name: Association des Pêcheurs de la Communauté Rurale de Mangagoulack
summary: Fishermen's association founded in 2008, covering eight central Casamance villages, which gained statutory management rights over Kawawana in 2010, reported by Mongabay to span 9,665 hectares.

name: Association Inter Villageoise Ndiael
summary: Association representing the 32 villages around the Ndiael, based in Ross-Béthio, working to restore the basin's ecological potential, protect and restore trees and monitor ecological change.

name: Association Nébéday
summary: Association founded in 2011 that works mainly in the Sine Saloum delta and other regions, running tree-planting campaigns and mangrove restoration.

name: Atlas des oiseaux du Sénégal
summary: Bird atlas for Senegal and a member of the African Bird Atlas Project. Observers submit records online or through the BirdLasser mobile app.

name: Base de Données Géographique Environnementale du Sénégal
summary: National environmental geodatabase launched by the environment ministry through CSE in February 2026, for centralising, accessing and viewing Senegal's environmental data.

name: Base des Aires de Biodiversité du Sénégal
summary: Application for consulting and mapping Senegal's biodiversity areas, with descriptive, geographic and funding data, developed by International Service Associates with Wetlands International Afrique.

name: BESS
summary: Space for Climate Observatory project piloting a sargassum intelligence system in Senegal that combines satellite images, AI and field measurements collected with community partners at Pointe-Sarène.

name: Carbon Lense Senegal
summary: GIZ-implemented project with data354 and Senegal's environment ministry using AI, open satellite imagery and forest inventory data to generate forest carbon maps, building on the High Carbon Stock Approach.

name: CartoSatTypha
summary: Remote sensing project to map and track Typha in the Senegal River valley by its spectral signatures, for the river basin organisation OMVS and funded by the Adour-Garonne water agency.

name: Centre d'excellence pour la biodiversité et les écosystèmes en Afrique de l'Ouest
summary: West African biodiversity and ecosystem centre of excellence for 2024 to 2027, carried by a consortium including the Centre de Suivi Écologique and RAMPAO, supervised by CIFOR-ICRAF. It follows the BIOPAMA observatory OBAPAO.

name: Centre de Coopération Technique et Scientifique pour l'Afrique de l'Ouest
summary: West Africa's technical and scientific cooperation centre for the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, launched in Dakar in July 2026 and held by CSE on behalf of the OBAPAO technical consortium.

name: Centre de Recherches Océanographiques de Dakar-Thiaroye
summary: ISRA's oceanographic research centre in Dakar. It runs fisheries acoustic assessment, and its researcher co-wrote work applying convolutional networks to echogram labelling.

name: Centre de Suivi Écologique
summary: Dakar environmental monitoring centre, created in 1986 and an association of public utility since 1993, under the technical supervision of the environment ministry. It produces environmental data and decision services and co-authors deep learning land cover work.

name: Centre National de Recherches Forestières
summary: Forest research centre of ISRA in Dakar, recruiting in 2024 for work on satellite, drone and lidar data for forestry and agroforestry.

name: Collectif des GIE de femmes pour la protection de la nature et le développement durable
summary: Collective of women's economic interest groups that has led restoration in the 1,009-hectare Popenguine Natural Reserve, created in 1986 and jointly managed by the national parks directorate and a local association.

name: Comité de gestion de l'aire marine communautaire protégée de la Somone
summary: Management committee, set up around 2007, for the Somone community marine protected area, which now covers 4,098 hectares, up from about 700 hectares at its start.

name: Comité de gestion de l'aire marine protégée communautaire de Bamboung
summary: Management committee for the Bamboung community marine protected area of about 7,000 hectares, bringing together delegates of 13 villages, fishers, women processors and administrative authorities.

name: Comité de gestion de l'aire marine protégée de Joal-Fadiouth
summary: Management committee of the Joal-Fadiouth marine protected area, chaired by a local fisherman, which gave itself an executive board in February 2006.

name: Comité de gestion de la réserve naturelle communautaire de Koyli Alpha
summary: Local committee managing the 1,000-hectare Koyli Alpha community nature reserve in the Linguère department, where an oryx reintroduction began in 2019 and about thirty oryx are held.

name: Commission Sous-Régionale des Pêches
summary: Seven-country West African fisheries commission that meets in Dakar. It works with Global Fishing Watch on data sharing and monitoring of fishing against illegal fishing.

name: Communauté rurale de Bandafassi
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis of community nature reserves, which gives its Tiabédji reserve as 26,020 hectares, declared in 2008.

name: Communauté rurale de Dialakoto
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis, which gives its Mansadala reserve as 35,000 hectares (declared 2003) and its Dar Salam reserve as 3,000 hectares (2005).

name: Communauté rurale de Diokoul Ndiawrigne
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis, which gives its Diokoul Ndiawrigne reserve in the Louga region as 2,000 hectares, declared in 2003.

name: Communauté rurale de Gandon
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis, which gives its Gandon reserve in the Saint-Louis region as 2,000 hectares, declared in 2003.

name: Communauté rurale de Houdalahi
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis, which gives its Loumbol Samba Abdoul reserve as 38,170 hectares, declared in 2003.

name: Communauté rurale de Linkering
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis, which gives its Linkering reserve in the Kolda region as 6,103.25 hectares, declared in 2003.

name: Communauté rurale de Médina Gounas
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis, which gives its Médina Gounas reserve in the Kolda region as 14,962.25 hectares, declared in 2004.

name: Communauté rurale de Notto Gouye Diama
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis, which gives its Notto Gouye Diama reserve as 1,180 hectares, declared in 2003.

name: Communauté rurale de Salémata
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis, which gives the Oubadji reserve, under Salémata and Dakatéli, as 82,882 hectares, declared in 2006.

name: Communauté rurale de Tomboronkoto
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis, which gives its Nyémeniké reserve as 64,523.88 hectares, declared in 2003.

name: Communauté rurale de Toubacouta
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis, which gives its Missirah reserve as 800.59 hectares (declared 2004) and its Néma Bah reserve as 846.61 hectares (2003).

name: Communauté rurale de Wouro Sibi
summary: Rural municipality listed in a 2012 Natural Justice analysis, which gives its Malandou reserve as 72,820 hectares (declared 2003) and lists the 128,676-hectare Moungyel reserve under Wouro Sibi and Sinthiou Bam.

name: Conservatoire de la Réserve naturelle communautaire du Boundou
summary: Body created to preserve the ecosystems of the 120,000-hectare Boundou community nature reserve, managed through the local CORENA association, with 32 volunteer community eco-guards listed in a 2012 report.

name: Constellation sénégalaise de satellites d'observation de la Terre
summary: Planned Senegalese constellation of Earth observation nanosatellites, under a January 2024 agreement between ASES and the French operator Prométhée Earth Intelligence, with deployment set for 2028.

name: COPERNICEA in Senegal
summary: Regional ecosystem accounting project coordinated by the Sahara and Sahel Observatory and funded by AFD. CSE closed the Senegal work in February 2026 after setting up an operational natural capital accounting system.

name: DASE participatory fisheries surveillance in Senegal
summary: Environmental Justice Foundation's DASE app, used in Senegal by artisanal fishers to record geolocated evidence of illegal fishing for verification and reporting to authorities.

name: Data Innovation Centre for Artificial Intelligence
summary: AI4D laboratory at Université Cheikh Anta Diop that works on data and AI skills and data sharing across agriculture, health, climate and the environment in Senegal.

name: DeepCascade GGW-Forecast
summary: Deep learning framework that forecasts land use and land cover change in Senegal’s Great Green Wall from Sentinel-2 images and Dynamic World data, described in a 2026 conference paper listing IRD and other authors.

name: Direction de l'Environnement et des Établissements Classés
summary: Environment directorate of Senegal's ministry. It runs the national antenna of the regional coastal observation network, which collects, processes and shares coastal data.

name: Direction de la Protection et de la Surveillance des Pêches
summary: Senegalese fisheries protection directorate, which hosted the first steering committee of the Global Fishing Watch and Trygg Mat Tracking pilot on satellite vessel tracking for port controls.

name: Direction des Aires Marines Communautaires Protégées
summary: The ministry directorate for community marine protected areas in Senegal. It leads the national mangrove strategy monitoring system and works with Senegal Flying Labs on drone mapping.

name: Direction des Eaux et Forêts, Chasses et de la Conservation des Sols
summary: Senegal's forest authority. It works with GIZ and data354 on AI carbon mapping and is the body the national forest monitoring system is being built for.

name: Direction des Parcs Nationaux
summary: Senegal's national parks agency, which is also the Convention on Biological Diversity focal point. It runs camera-trap surveys with Panthera and trained on drones and AI bird counting with Senegal Flying Labs.

name: Djoudj drone and AI bird counting
summary: Proof of concept by Senegal Flying Labs at Djoudj National Bird Park for the January 2021 International Waterbird Count, using drones and AI to count birds in hard-to-reach sites.

name: Djoudj drone waterbird count
summary: Senegal Flying Labs' use of drones with the ATLAS and Picterra platforms to count waterbirds at Djoudj during the January 2021 international waterbird count, working with ministry agents.

name: Données d'occurrence de la flore du Sénégal, Herbier IFAN
summary: Occurrence records of Senegal's flora from specimens in the IFAN herbarium, published on an open GBIF data publishing tool.

name: Dénombrement des oiseaux d'eau du Sénégal de 2016 à 2018
summary: National waterbird counts made by the Direction des Parcs Nationaux each 15 January from 2016 to 2018, published on GBIF.

name: Earth Geomatique
summary: Senegalese company for high-resolution aerial imagery. WeForest used it in 2024 for drone surveys of its mangrove restoration sites.

name: Fédération locale des GIE de Niodior
summary: Local federation of economic interest groups which, since 2005, has rehabilitated mangroves in the Saloum Delta Biosphere Reserve, with a 22-woman committee regulating harvesting of marine and forest resources.

name: GAINDESAT-1A
summary: Senegal's first satellite, a 1U CubeSat for environmental imagery and natural resource monitoring launched in August 2024, the first step of the SenSAT national space programme.

name: GALILEO agroforestry project
summary: Horizon Europe project on agroforestry in sub-Saharan Africa. In Senegal its Living Labs collect tree inventories, satellite positioning and drone images to feed AI models for mapping trees and identifying species.

name: GDZHAO mangrove monitoring application
summary: Operational application built by a CSE-led consortium that produces annual 10-metre mangrove maps from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data, available online to protected-area managers and researchers.

name: Geomatica
summary: Senegalese geospatial company that in 2019 put about a hundred drone images, geographic datasets and maps of Senegal online as open data.

name: GPS 2: Promotion des principes de transparence et renforcement de la surveillance participative au Sénégal
summary: Environmental Justice Foundation project with Senegal's fisheries protection directorate training artisanal fishing committees in participatory surveillance, including use of the DASE application.

name: Green Sédhiou
summary: Association that has replanted a branch of the Casamance river at the entrance to Diendé, and which the Dutch ambassador says replants mangroves every year with women's groups, authorities and residents.

name: Groupement de femmes Sédar Diaga Senghor de Djilor Djidiack
summary: Women's association of 200 members, founded in 2003, whose idea led residents to plant and protect a 20-hectare community forest with GEF Small Grants Programme support.

name: Guiers lake IoT water quality monitoring system
summary: Water quality monitoring system for Lac de Guiers based on IoT and LPWAN, described in a 2023 conference paper by Ball, Badji, Bah and co-authors.

name: Innovative Monitoring System for Ecosystem-Based Adaptation in Senegal
summary: Global EbA Fund project implemented by CSE, started in July 2026 with US$249,970, to build a digital monitoring system for restored mangroves in the Senegal River Delta from remote sensing and field data.

name: Institut des Sciences de l'Environnement
summary: Environmental science institute in the Faculty of Science at Université Cheikh Anta Diop. It publishes the largest set of Senegal's biodiversity datasets on GBIF, including national plant and bird lists and waterbird counts.

name: Institut Fondamental d'Afrique Noire Cheikh Anta Diop
summary: Research institute at Université Cheikh Anta Diop that publishes herbarium occurrence data for Senegal's flora on GBIF and supports biodiversity training with SOS SAHEL.

name: Institut Sénégalais de Recherches Agricoles
summary: Senegal's agricultural research institute. Its forestry centre recruited an AI and remote sensing researcher, and it houses the oceanographic centre CRODT.

name: Instituto Jane Goodall Senegal
summary: Jane Goodall Institute Spain’s Senegal programme, which monitors chimpanzees around the Dindéfélo Community Nature Reserve and ran a camera-trap grid there for the Max Planck Pan African comparative study.

name: International Service Associates
summary: Consultancy created in 2018 and based in Dakar. It developed the BABs biodiversity areas application.

name: Laboratoire de télédétection appliquée, ENSMG
summary: Applied remote sensing laboratory at the Ecole Nationale Supérieure des Mines et de la Géologie, UCAD, whose research covers coastal and marine environments.

name: Livelihoods Senegal mangrove monitoring
summary: Monitoring of the Livelihoods mangrove carbon project with Océanium in Senegal, through satellite plot mapping developed with Agresta and the European Space Agency and three-dimensional drone measurement.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Transition Écologique
summary: Senegal's environment ministry. It oversees the forest, parks and marine protected area directorates and is a partner in the Carbon Lense Senegal AI carbon mapping project.

name: Nature-Communautés-Développement
summary: Senegalese bird conservation association founded in 2010. It builds ornithological databases from its monitoring, and its strategy plans to train local groups to collect and share bird data with tools such as KoboToolbox.

name: Niokolo-Base
summary: Online digital library launched on 27 October 2026 that gives access to the documentation on Niokolo-Koba National Park, built with support from Ucoopia.

name: Niokolo-Koba park-wide camera trap survey
summary: A 2024 survey by Panthera, the Direction des Parcs Nationaux and the Zoological Society of London to estimate the distribution of all mammals in Niokolo-Koba National Park with 584 remote cameras.

name: OBIS Sénégal
summary: Senegal's node of the Ocean Biodiversity Information System, for marine biodiversity data, managed by the director of CRODT.

name: Observatoire Hommes-Milieux International Téssékéré
summary: CNRS human-environment observatory in the Ferlo, northern Senegal, studying the Great Green Wall zone. It publishes bird and large mammal data on GBIF.

name: Observatoire National du Littoral
summary: Senegal's coastal observatory. It publishes a data catalogue and interactive maps, runs participatory monitoring with coastal communities and maps land cover on the maritime public domain from satellite and drone images.

name: Observatoire Régional du Littoral Ouest-Africain
summary: West African coastal observatory carried by the Centre de Suivi Écologique, covering 12 countries and harmonising how coastal risk is monitored, with Digital Earth Africa coastline services.

name: Océanium de Dakar
summary: Senegalese association for mangrove restoration. According to Beauval Nature it uses drones and aerial photographs to estimate tree height and carbon stored in replanted mangroves.

name: Office des Lacs et Cours d'eau
summary: Senegalese public body created by a 2017 decree and draft law from the Office du Lac de Guiers, with missions extended to all inland lakes and watercourses, including water planning and aquatic plant management.

name: Organisation pour la Mise en Valeur du fleuve Sénégal
summary: Intergovernmental organisation for the Senegal River basin, based in Dakar, which works with IRD on hydrological monitoring from satellite data under the SCREEN project.

name: Panthera large carnivore monitoring in Niokolo-Koba
summary: Panthera’s camera-trap and GPS-collar monitoring of lions and other large carnivores in Niokolo-Koba National Park, under an agreement with the Senegalese national parks directorate.

name: Plateforme d'Imagerie Quantitative Aquatique d'Afrique de l'Ouest
summary: Plankton imaging platform at CRODT in Dakar under the Plankt'Eco programme, with a ZooScan, four planktoscopes and an Underwater Vision Profiler, to produce data for fish stock management.

name: Plateforme de gestion des alertes de coupe de bois
summary: Alert management platform for monitoring illegal logging with IoT sensors for forest agents, the subject of a 2024 master's thesis by Maty Seck at Université Assane Seck de Ziguinchor.

name: Projet de gestion des ressources naturelles au Sénégal
summary: World Bank-supported project of Senegal's environment ministry, started in 2022 for six years. It buys drones and mapping equipment and trains ministry agents to use them for forest and park monitoring.

name: Renforcement de la coopération transfrontière dans le delta du fleuve Sénégal
summary: GEF-funded project of the Senegalese and Mauritanian environment ministries for the Senegal delta transboundary biosphere reserve. It trained park managers and ecoguards on GPS, drones and QGIS for habitat monitoring.

name: RESSOURCE+ waterbird remote sensing trials in Senegal
summary: Trials under the FAO-coordinated RESSOURCE+ project that use drones, very high-resolution satellite images and AI models to count waterbirds in Sahelian wetlands, with applications run in Senegal.

name: Rooted Resilience
summary: Wetlands International project in Casamance, within Mangrove Capital Africa, that aims to protect 65,000 hectares of mangrove and trains local managers on the Global Mangrove Watch platform.

name: Réseau Régional d'Aires Marines Protégées en Afrique de l'Ouest
summary: West African marine protected area network, a member of the consortium implementing the CEBio-Eco/AO biodiversity centre of excellence. Its own site refuses crawlers, so this rests on partner pages.

name: Réserve animalière d'Amboura
summary: Wildlife reserve created in 2016 on 1,050 hectares, holding more than 80 scimitar-horned oryx, which restores habitat and reintroduces wildlife rather than feeding animals.

name: Réserve de Bandia
summary: Reserve of 3,500 hectares in the Mbour department, partly owned by Georges Rezk according to Le Soleil, where poaching is the main threat and guard patrols have been stepped up.

name: Réserve naturelle communautaire de Dindéfélo
summary: Community-managed reserve of about 13,300 hectares, created in 2010 according to the environment minister, awarded the 2024 Equator Prize and employing 24 eco-guards against bush fires.

name: Réserve naturelle communautaire de Palmarin
summary: Community nature reserve created on 15 May 2001 at the local population's initiative, covering 10,480 hectares in the Saloum and its bolongs.

name: Sahel eco-acoustic recorder network in Senegal
summary: Network of passive acoustic recorders laid by the POPCO team of IMBE along agricultural and restoration gradients in Senegal, to set baselines for tracking biodiversity from animal sounds.

name: Saloum Delta Atlantic humpback dolphin survey
summary: A closed survey project, run by the African Aquatic Conservation Fund with the University of St Andrews, whose fifth annual boat survey in February 2025 recovered acoustic recorders and aimed to build a dolphin species classifier library.

name: SEDAD seagrass mapping in Senegal
summary: Seagrass mapping in a marine protected area in southern Senegal, by the Canadian-funded SEDAD project through CSE with satellite data from Digital Earth Africa.

name: Senegal Flying Labs
summary: Senegalese drone and AI centre in the Flying Labs network. It has trained parks and marine protected area staff, tested AI bird counting at Djoudj and mapped mangroves at Somone.

name: Senegalese National Information System on Biodiversity
summary: National information system on Senegal's species, set up under GBIF's Biodiversity Information for Development programme between 2016 and 2018.

name: SENSAT
summary: Senegal’s national satellite programme. Its CubeSat GAINDESAT-1A, launched in August 2024, collected environmental data and imagery, and a second satellite, GAINDESAT-1B, is planned.

name: Somone Marine Protected Area mangrove mapping
summary: Drone mapping of mangrove restoration areas in the Somone Marine Protected Area by Senegal Flying Labs with the DAMCP, combined with Sentinel-2 imagery.

name: SOS SAHEL
summary: NGO training community leaders in eastern Senegal and central Chad to record plants on iNaturalist. JRS says its Oubadji-Linkéring project accounts for about 40% of Senegal's plant observations there.

name: Station ornithologique du delta du Sénégal
summary: An active bird ringing programme at Djoudj National Bird Park, reported as operating again in 2024 after over a decade, with a work plan to ring pelicans, first with colour rings and later satellite transmitters.

name: Sustainable Wetlands and Flood Management in West Africa (GDZHIAO)
summary: GMES and Africa consortium project led by the Centre de Suivi Ecologique, which uses Earth observation for wetland and flood monitoring in ten West African countries.

name: Système national de surveillance des forêts du Sénégal
summary: Senegal's national forest and land-use monitoring system, for which DEFCCS sought technical assistance under a World Bank-backed natural resources project. The terms of reference describe it as still to be made operational.

name: UMMISCO Centre Afrique de l'Ouest
summary: West Africa centre of the UMMISCO modelling research unit. It works on AI for monitoring artisanal fishing and marine biodiversity in Senegal, including detection of pirogues in aerial images and a store of underwater sound recordings.
