name: Université Assane Seck de Ziguinchor
summary: University in Ziguinchor. It works with the Carbon Lense Senegal project to produce biomass data for West African tree species that AI carbon maps depend on.

name: Université Cheikh Anta Diop
summary: University in Dakar behind the Senegal Bird Atlas, and the parent of several research units already on the map.

name: Université Gaston Berger
summary: University in Saint-Louis, Senegal. Its researchers publish on shoreline detection from satellite imagery, and it was a partner in the AIME marine biodiversity AI consortium.

name: WeForest Senegal mangrove drone monitoring
summary: Drone survey in 2024 of WeForest's 7,019 hectares of mangrove restoration in the Sine-Saloum and Casamance, with Earth Geomatique flying and Inverto Earth detecting individual canopies by algorithm.

name: WeForest Senegal mangrove restoration
summary: WeForest project restoring 7,019 hectares of mangrove in the Sine-Saloum Delta and Casamance, monitored with drone imagery that Inverto Earth analyses by algorithm to detect canopies and saplings.

name: WENDOU
summary: Dashboard for monitoring temporary surface water bodies in the Ferlo region of Senegal, from the SERVIR programme, using satellite data.

name: YOLOv11 fish detection for Senegalese artisanal landings
summary: Detection and identification model for fish landed by artisanal canoes in Senegal, trained with YOLO v8 and v11 on images from docks, by authors at the Polytechnic Higher School of UCAD.

name: BRCiS III ecosystem baseline assessment
summary: Ecosystem baseline report from the BRCiS III programme, collecting field data with ICRAF's Land Degradation Surveillance Framework, with CIFOR-ICRAF and the BRCiS Consortium collaborating on Activity 2.1; the report cites both 845 sites and eight Somalia sites.

name: Building Capacity for Biodiversity Data Mobilization and Conservation in Somalia
summary: Biodiversity data project built by the Somali Institute for Environmental Peace, which says it officially launched the project in Mogadishu in July 2026.

name: College of Agriculture, Veterinary Medicine, and Environment Sciences, University of Hargeisa
summary: College at the University of Hargeisa, given by OpenAlex as the first author's affiliation on a 2026 paper on remote sensing of vegetation trends in Somaliland.

name: Conserving Terrestrial and Marine Biodiversity and Restoring Ecosystem Services in Globally Relevant and Vulnerable Sites in Somalia
summary: An ongoing US$18.9 million project (April 2026 to March 2032) covering 11 proposed protected areas, led by the environment ministry with UNDP and GEF, with a planned biodiversity data platform including GIS.

name: Establishing the ecological status of rangelands and identifying mitigation options for their restoration and protection
summary: Project aiming to establish the ecological status of five Somaliland rangelands and identify restoration options, including land cover mapping from remotely sensed data and plant surveys, funded by the World Bank.

name: GBIF Somalia
summary: Somalia's country node of GBIF, recorded by GBIF with voting participation status and created in October 2026, and a partner of the Global Biodiversity Information Facility.

name: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (Somalia)
summary: Somali government ministry in Mogadishu that lists wildlife and biodiversity conservation among its services, and which UNDP said in February 2026 would lead a six-year nationwide biodiversity programme.

name: Puntland Information Management Center for Water and Land Resources
summary: Garowe-based centre set up in late 2019 to collect and disseminate Puntland land and water data, handed to Somalia's Government in December 2021 and publishing a roughly 219 km² Jibagalle land cover assessment in May 2026.

name: Saraar Gazelle Preservation Project
summary: Closed project on the Saraar Plains, listed by the Rufford Foundation in 2006, which said monitoring and research of existing wildlife, particularly what it calls 'Thompson’s Gazelle', would be an essential component.

name: Somali Institute for Environmental Peace
summary: Mogadishu-based non-profit registered with Somalia's environment ministry, which GBIF says started a EU-funded biodiversity data mobilisation project, and which says its BID project led Somalia to join GBIF in October 2026.

name: Somali National Bird Checklist
summary: Described by GBIF as the first comprehensive Somali bird checklist prepared for publication there, it covers 210 species from historical and contemporary sources under CC BY 4.0.

name: Somalia Water and Land Information Management
summary: Programme FAO says it set up from 2002 as a platform on Somalia's water and land resources, with its tools and services handed to the Puntland centre as a first step towards national ownership.

name: Somaliland Camera Trap Project
summary: Cheetah Conservation Fund project, reported by CCF in March 2025 as launched to assess cheetah status and distribution with noninvasive techniques, with 154 cameras deployed across the Awdal region.

name: Trans-Boundary Monitoring and Conservation of Endangered Dragon Tree in Somaliland and Djibouti
summary: Project listed by the Rufford Foundation in 2012, which planned a monitoring programme with local NGOs and GIS maps of the species' distribution and suitable habitats from field data and interviews.

name: UN Joint Programme for Sustainable Charcoal Reduction and Alternative Livelihoods
summary: Joint programme of Somalia's federal government and the United Nations; its 2021 report lists remote sensing monitoring of charcoal sites in Jubaland and Mogadishu, and a vegetation index report requested from FAO's SWALIM.

name: University of Hargeisa
summary: Public university in Somaliland whose biodiversity museum, started in 2015, shares its records, according to GBIF's publisher record.

name: 2020 Marine Turtle Conservation (Suriname)
summary: Closed project funded by WWF under a grant agreement with the Ministry for 1 March to 31 July 2020, which planned daily counts of sea turtle nests and strandings at Braamspunt, Galibi and other sites.

name: Amazon Conservation Team community ranger programme (Suriname)
summary: Run by ACT, this programme reportedly helped train over 60 rangers since 2007 and establish seven posts in Suriname, according to ACT in June 2025.

name: Anton de Kom University of Suriname
summary: University listed as a MapBiomas Suriname co-initiator; its research institute is the National Zoological Collection, and NeoWild reported it signed a two-year jaguar monitoring agreement in June 2021.

name: Ateles Project
summary: A spider monkey research programme launched in August 2024 on the unhunted population around Voltzberg in the Central Suriname Nature Reserve, using canopy cameras, acoustic monitoring and thermal drones to assess group composition and size.

name: Blue Carbon Restoration in the Bigi Pan MUMA
summary: An active project on mangrove degradation in the Bigi Pan Multiple Use Management Area, run by Anton de Kom University, which its 2026 abstract says combines data collection, drone and AI biomass estimation and stakeholder engagement.

name: Central Suriname Nature Reserve TEAM camera-trap dataset
summary: Legacy camera-trap dataset from 2008 to 2017 TEAM Network surveys, with 60 traps giving 54,060 trap-days, analysed with Wildlife Insights tools; the page says nothing is recorded after 2017 and monitoring should resume.

name: Centre for Agricultural Research in Suriname (CELOS)
summary: Research centre that, with SBB, presented mangrove monitoring data collection methods at a 2 and 3 October 2025 workshop, covering carbon stock, deforestation rates and carbon emissions.

name: Conservation International Suriname
summary: Organisation that says it works with Indigenous, Maroon and local communities, aims to protect and restore 100,000 hectares of mangroves, and is listed as a partner by Rainforest Connection.

name: Dienst 's Lands Bosbeheer
summary: Surinamese forest and nature agency whose present parts are Nature Management and Forest Research, with forestry mandated to SBB in 2000, and which runs the Nature Conservation Division handling day-to-day reserve management.

name: ENHANCES: ENHANcing Coastal Ecosystem Services
summary: Active coastal protection project working with stakeholders in Suriname and Guyana plans mangrove health mapping using in-situ and remote-sensing methods, with a £749,959 grant dated December 2023–November 2026.

name: Forest governance (Green Growth Suriname)
summary: Programme described as a three-layered forest governance model, combining satellite monitoring, citizen science and a weekly web series, with bi-weekly forest cover change alerts for Suriname's production forest shared publicly.

name: Foundation for Forest Management and Production Control (SBB)
summary: Foundation whose Forest Cover Monitoring Unit, launched in 2013, aims to strengthen the National Forest Monitoring System; UNDP reports it and CELOS ran an October 2025 mangrove monitoring workshop.

name: GBIF Suriname
summary: Country node for Suriname in GBIF, with associate participation status; in August 2025 GBIF recorded transferring NeoWild's endorsement to it from the Participant Node Managers Committee.

name: GHFS Marine Megafauna Database
summary: A dataset run by Green Heritage Fund Suriname which it says holds over 10,000 records and contributes to regional conservation planning, alongside its field, photo-identification, acoustic and habitat datasets.

name: Gonini
summary: Online database of geographic forest information for Suriname, launched by SBB in December 2016, which hosts the mangrove occurrence map and was named in October 2025 as an existing mangrove monitoring platform.

name: Green Growth Forests app
summary: A citizen reporting app, built by Green Growth Suriname Foundation, that has let anyone report tree logging since August 2020, adding citizen data to Suriname's national forest conservation data.

name: Green Growth Suriname Foundation
summary: A Paramaribo-based foundation that says it develops models using near-real-time satellite monitoring, citizen science and policy building blocks.

name: Green Growth Wildlife app
summary: A citizen science app built by Green Growth Suriname Foundation, running since June 2021 on the SPOTTERON platform, available in several local and Indigenous languages and feeding a central biodiversity database.

name: Green Heritage Fund Suriname
summary: Organisation whose Dolphin Program, begun by volunteers, has collected data on Guiana dolphins in the Suriname River estuary since 2005; it also lists long-term turtle and shorebird monitoring.

name: Jaguar ecology study at Kabalebo Nature Resort
summary: Jaguar population study run by NeoWild, agreed with IUCN Netherlands in February 2021 and funded by Stout Groep from 2023; NeoWild reported 60 camera traps in May 2024.

name: Jaguar protection and monitoring project (Suriname)
summary: Two-year jaguar protection and monitoring project, reported in June 2021 as agreed by WWF-Guianas, Anton de Kom University, ACT Suriname and NeoWild, covering forest, savannah and coastal areas.

name: Khose
summary: Organisation listed among MapBiomas Suriname's co-initiators.

name: Mangrove+ Project (Suriname)
summary: Project funded by the European Union and run by UNDP; on 21 April 2026 it handed over a METT report, bird monitoring equipment and training certificates for bird identification, counting and monitoring.

name: MapBiomas Suriname
summary: Scientific collaboration mapping land cover and land use change since 1985, run by the Mulokot Foundation; it reports more than 166,000 hectares of forest lost in 40 years.

name: Ministry of Land Policy and Forest Management (Suriname)
summary: Ministry whose Nature Conservation Division had 17 staff trained in bird identification, counting and monitoring under Mangrove+, and which received bird monitoring equipment, according to UNDP.

name: Ministry of Oil, Gas and Environment (Suriname)
summary: Ministry whose Minister called in December 2025, per UNDP, for measurable, transparent and achievable biodiversity monitoring systems; its site covers biodiversity, climate change and land management.

name: Mulokot Foundation
summary: Listed under coordination by MapBiomas Suriname.

name: National Biodiversity Monitoring Framework and Monitoring System (Suriname)
summary: Proposed framework with tiered monitoring, a Pressure-State-Response model and three-layer data management, presented for validation at a Ministry workshop with UNDP on 9 June 2026.

name: National Environmental Authority (Suriname)
summary: An independent environmental authority established under the Environmental Framework Act, proclaimed on 26 July 2024 following the NIMOS transition, with environmental enforcement tasks and data management aims.

name: National Forest Monitoring System (Suriname)
summary: A national system with near real time and satellite land monitoring, supported by an EU and AFD project, whose October 2025 presentation reported 212 inventory plots, including 17 mangrove plots.

name: National Mangrove Monitoring System (Suriname)
summary: Active system for which SBB and CELOS presented current data collection methods on carbon stock, deforestation rates and carbon emissions at an October 2025 workshop aimed at adding parameters to its protocols.

name: National Zoological Collection of Suriname
summary: Research institute of Anton de Kom University of Suriname, whose main task is an overview of Suriname's fauna, with 24 datasets published on GBIF.

name: Native Tech Engineering
summary: Listed by MapBiomas Suriname as its technology partner.

name: Nature Conservation Division (Suriname)
summary: A division of Suriname's forest service, run by the land policy and forest ministry, which monitors and enforces on sea turtle nesting beaches and had 17 staff trained in bird monitoring in 2026.

name: NeoWild
summary: A Paramaribo-based NGO founded in January 2019 that researches human impacts on biodiversity, especially large cats, and monitors mammals and amphibians at sites including Brownsberg and Kabalebo.

name: Project Suriname
summary: A conservation project run by the Landbanking Group's non-profit arm Earthly Treasure, which says it has installed 30 camera traps and 50 acoustic recorders and aims to extend protection to a further 525,000 hectares.

name: Protecting the Matawai Rainforest and Cultural Heritage in Suriname
summary: A project built by Rainforest Connection that uses acoustic monitoring to protect the Matawai site, with 13 Guardians installed by 2022 and a planned second step of 20 real-time Guardians.

name: Protection, Restoration and Sustainable use of the Mangrove Forests (PRSUMF) project
summary: A UNDP-run, EU-funded mangrove protection and restoration project that facilitated an October 2025 workshop on a national mangrove monitoring system, carried out by SBB and CELOS.

name: Roaring Resilience: Addressing Suriname's Escalating Threats to Wild Cat Survival
summary: A project reporting that it is deploying 80 camera traps across three villages to build a first ecological baseline for wild cats and measure wider mammal diversity.

name: SMART implementation in Suriname
summary: An active programme in which the Ministry of Land Policy and Forest Management took part in SMART follow-up training on 5 to 10 April 2025, after earlier training in 2022 and a March 2024 memorandum of understanding.

name: Stichting Amazon Conservation Team Guianas
summary: Surinamese foundation whose rangers collect monitoring data in southern Suriname and elsewhere, and which signed a memorandum of understanding with the Ministry of Natural Resources, reported on a government page that gives no year.

name: Stichting Duurzaam Natuurbeheer Alusiaka
summary: A Galibi foundation which a March 2023 report said coordinated monitoring there, mapping jaguars and recording sea turtle nesting with SMART, with wardens and community data collectors, in WWF-Guianas supported projects.

name: Stichting Natuurbehoud Suriname
summary: Founded on 17 June 1969 under the Ministry, manages five protected areas, reports strengthening research departments and had a 2001–2006 programme planning monitoring across its protected areas.

name: Strengthening Management of Protected and Productive Landscapes in the Surinamese Amazon (ASL2 Suriname)
summary: Project to strengthen protected area management and land use planning, led by Suriname's land policy ministry, run by UNDP, funded by the Global Environment Facility, 2022 to 2027.

name: Suriname Biodiversity Project
summary: A Naturalis project, with the National Zoological Collection of Suriname, describing Suriname's biodiversity through collections, fieldwork and field guides, and working on audio recognition of several animal groups for scalable monitoring.

name: Suriname Conservation Foundation
summary: A foundation through which a minister said the updated NBSAP submitted in 2024 was financed, according to UNDP, and which ACT credits for its Sipaliwini ranger station.

name: Sustainable Forest Management Suriname project
summary: Closed two-year project that started in 2023, with forest monitoring as one theme area, and which tested drones and camera traps at Ovia Olo during an April 2024 field week.

name: Sustainable Forestry Information System Suriname
summary: Component of the National Forest Monitoring System that was replacing LogPro in June 2020, with timber harvesting operations reported as approved and monitored under it since mid-2019.

name: TotalEnergies EP Suriname B.V.
summary: Company that signed a contribution agreement with NeoWild in February 2024 to extend NeoWild's research in the Kabalebo area, and which funds the Kabalebo jaguar ecology study.

name: Tropenbos Suriname
summary: Self-described knowledge-based NGO for sustainable forest management, based at the CELOS Building in Paramaribo, which tested drone and camera-trap forest monitoring with Ovia Olo residents, SBB and Dutch partners in April 2024.

name: Vervolgen en uitbouwen gemeenschapsmonitoring Bigi Poika en Galibi (Jaguar Survey)
summary: An active Suriname Conservation Foundation project supporting residents of Bigi Poika and Galibi with training, satellite images and field monitoring around the Boven Coesewijne Nature Reserve, expecting trained monitors with biodiversity monitoring experience.

name: W6 Engineering Suriname NV
summary: Paramaribo company offering drone and satellite monitoring of forest cover and land-use change, drone and satellite supported forest inventories, and traceability systems for legal timber supply chains.

name: Wildlife & People Suriname
summary: A Surinamese conservation organisation working with Indigenous people and local communities, currently piloting training of a community team in Alalapadu and the Kwinti region to run camera traps and acoustic recorders.

name: WWF-Guianas
summary: The WWF Guianas office, established in Suriname in 1999, which a 2019 presentation says manages a nesting beach monitoring and enforcement programme with government agencies and which funded the 2026-2035 sea turtle plan.

name: Aerial Survey, Wildlife Collaring, and Basic Field Ranger Training in Boma and Badingilo National Parks
summary: Closed 2022 to 2025 African Parks project in Boma and Badingilo National Parks, which planned to tag 94 more animals and enhance aerial surveillance, after what is described as South Sudan's largest collaring operation.

name: AI-Powered Habitat Mapping in South Sudan's Reserves
summary: Project listed by the Ecosystem Insights Hub, described there as producing South Sudan's first detailed land cover maps of forests, wetlands and deforestation pressures, with Pleiades imagery distributed by Airbus credited.

name: Assessment of Hydrological Ecosystem and Biodiversity of the Sudd Wetland
summary: The closed World Bank-commissioned assessment (June 2025–March 2026) covered Jonglei, Unity, Lakes and Upper Nile, with wetland and riparian mapping and freshwater biodiversity monitoring pilots in scope.

name: Boma, Badingilo and Jonglei landscape aerial wildlife survey (2023 to 2024)
summary: Aerial surveys run by the wildlife ministry and African Parks from April 2023 to January 2024 across Boma, Badingilo and Jonglei, which the minister said show the world's largest antelope migration.

name: Capacity Development in Reducing Illegal Wildlife Trade and Improving Protected Area Management Effectiveness in South Sudan
summary: Active GEF-funded capacity development project on illegal wildlife trade and protected area management in South Sudan, approved in December 2019, with a USD 5,329,452 grant, run by the ministry, IUCN and WCS.

name: Department of Environmental Studies, University of Juba
summary: Department at the University of Juba, with which the first author of a 2023 paper on land use change from oil exploration and production in Melut County was affiliated.

name: Department of GIS, Remote Sensing and Cartography, National Bureau of Statistics
summary: Unit of the National Bureau of Statistics, described in the Space Hubs Africa database as the country's official mapping authority, mandated to collect, analyse and publish geospatial information.

name: Dr. John Garang Memorial University of Science and Technology
summary: University in Bor Town, listed as the first affiliation of the first and corresponding author of a 2023 species distribution modelling study of Kobus megaceros in South Sudan.

name: Environmental Information Management System (South Sudan)
summary: Programme run by the Ministry of Environment and Forestry, described in its GBIF publisher record as a system where environmental data and information were kept for open public access.

name: ESA GDA Forest Management support to the South Sudan Natural Resources and Livelihoods Project
summary: Active European Space Agency activity using Copernicus satellite data to support a World Bank project, mapping tree cover and change from 2018 to 2024 in the Imatong range; both baseline phases are complete.

name: GBIF South Sudan
summary: Active GBIF node for South Sudan, which GBIF lists as an associate country participant, led by Lwanga Tiba Charles and linked to the Global Biodiversity Information Facility.

name: Improving protected area management in Western Equatoria, South Sudan
summary: Active 2023 to 2026 grant-funded programme with Fauna & Flora International as beneficiary, whose first objective includes ranger biomonitoring and ongoing camera trap monitoring of key wildlife species.

name: Land Cover Atlas of the Republic of South Sudan
summary: FAO-built land cover dataset for South Sudan, published in 2023 as an update to the 2011 edition, classified from Sentinel-2 imagery (December 2016 to November 2017) with Random Forest.

name: Ministry of Environment and Forestry
summary: Government ministry in Juba whose GBIF record describes its environmental protection and conservation mandate and an internal system where environmental data were kept for open public access.

name: Ministry of Wildlife Conservation and Tourism
summary: Government ministry whose minister said it carried out 2023 to 2024 aerial surveys with African Parks, which in November 2025 ran a five-day GIS training there.

name: National Biodiversity Database System (South Sudan)
summary: Database system listed in South Sudan's November 2019 sixth national report, funded by GBIF through BID funds from 2017 to 2019 at 40,000 euros, then still under development and intended to support the EIMS.

name: Population status, Distribution and Threats to the Nile lechwe in the Sudd Wetland, South Sudan (2012)
summary: GBIF dataset of 61 Nile lechwe occurrence records from aerial surveys of about 70,456 square kilometres of the Sudd Wetland, between January and March 2010, published by the Ministry of Environment and Forestry.

name: South Sudan DiversityCam
summary: Closed camera trapping project in the south-western forests, with biodiversity monitoring central since 2012 and about 425,000 images, whose Zooniverse page says it is currently out of data.

name: South Sudan elephant collaring and wildlife tracking programme
summary: Programme run by the wildlife ministry and WCS, with USAID funding, that in 2013 fitted elephants with GPS collars and by July 2013 also monitored collars on kob, tiang and giant eland.

name: South Sudan Wildlife Service
summary: Active wildlife body whose researchers Mongabay names among those behind the 2015 Western Equatoria camera trap survey, and which Community Wildlife Ambassadors support through patrols and camera traps.

name: University of Juba
summary: University whose Department of Environmental Studies is the first author's affiliation on a 2023 study of land use and land cover change in Melut County.

name: Vulture tracking research in the Great Nile Migration Landscape
summary: Active vulture research project led by African Parks with the Endangered Wildlife Trust; Radio Yei reported 15 vultures tagged in Badingilo National Park, and 2024 Boma tags reportedly show travel to Kenya, Ethiopia and Chad.

name: WCS aerial and ground wildlife surveys of the Boma-Badingilo Landscape (2019)
summary: Aerial and ground surveys run by WCS in 2019 to assess the conflict's impact on wildlife, habitats and human activity in the Boma-Badingilo Landscape.

name: Western Equatoria forest camera trap survey (2015)
summary: Closed 2015 camera trap survey of over 8,000 square kilometres of Western Equatoria's forests, run over six months, which produced more than 20,000 photographs.

name: Acoustic Monitoring of the Scops-Owl and Other Threatened Species on Príncipe Island
summary: A closed expedition project, with $6,900 raised by the Bird Conservation Fund and African Bird Club, to install passive acoustic monitors on Príncipe, map the scops-owl's distribution and train park staff.

name: Assessing Elasmobranch Diversity and Distribution in a Tropical Marine Hotspot São Tomé and Príncipe (Gulf of Guinea) using eDNA-Based Method
summary: An active project, listed by the Rufford Foundation on 15 July 2025, that plans to use eDNA methods to baseline shark and ray diversity, identify hotspots, compare them with proposed marine protected areas and explore teleost fish primers.

name: Associação Programa Tatô
summary: Sea turtle conservation NGO on São Tomé, formalised in 2018 from a programme created in 1998, employing more than 60 people, mostly from coastal communities, and holding a Monaco foundation project for January 2024 to December 2026.

name: Characterization of the Threatened Flora of São Tomé and Príncipe
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project (April 2019 to November 2021) aimed to assess endangered plants against IUCN criteria and review Key Biodiversity Areas; resources include an endemic plant Red Data Book.

name: Community conservation of marine biodiversity on the island of São Tomé
summary: A São Tomé sea turtle conservation project, listed by the Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation as running January 2024 to December 2026, partnering with Programa Tatô, which employs over 60 people, mostly from coastal communities.

name: Conservation of the threatened Obô giant land Snail Archachatina bicarinata and of the terrestrial malacological fauna of São Tomé Island, Central Africa
summary: A project of unknown status, awarded funding on 1 November 2019 by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, aiming to identify critical areas for the Obô giant land snail and fill distribution gaps for endemic São Tomé snails and slugs.

name: Direção das Florestas e Biodiversidade
summary: A directorate named in a 2019 forest degradation mission and UNDP’s 2023–2024 review, which placed it within the agriculture ministry and assigned charcoal and forest management co-delivery.

name: Enhancing Biodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Land and Natural Resource Management (São Tomé and Príncipe)
summary: GEF-funded biodiversity and land management project in São Tomé and Príncipe, run by the national environment directorate, with reported SMART monitoring work and training for 49 technical staff.

name: Fundação Príncipe
summary: Príncipe-based NGO that began a thrush project with Fauna & Flora International in April 2018; a revised 2021 protocol reported its Obô giant land snail data collection.

name: General Directorate for Environment and Climate Action (São Tomé and Príncipe)
summary: National environment directorate of São Tomé and Príncipe, named in UNDP's 2023 to 2024 midterm review as implementing partner in charge of overall delivery of the biodiversity project.

name: Green and hawksbill sea turtle nesting in the Gulf of Guinea: A 9-year survey
summary: Published by Dryad on 15 March 2024, this dataset records turtle tags, carapace length, nest types and hatchlings, with its associated study combining nine-year nesting surveys and telemetry.

name: Identifying and protect key sites for the Dwarf olive ibis
summary: This closed project aimed to survey three critically endangered birds and build local monitoring capacity; its case study reports identifying and quantifying oil-palm impacts as the main result.

name: Implementing the Action Plan for the Critically Endangered Principe Thrush, São Tomé and Príncipe
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, July 2018 to March 2021, led by Fauna & Flora International and run by Fundação Príncipe, which set up a thrush monitoring protocol and sightings database and counted birds at more than 750 points.

name: Insectivorous bat activity dataset across different land-use types in the islands of São Tomé and Príncipe
summary: A dataset of acoustic bat surveys from August and September 2022, using AudioMoth recorders at 115 sites on São Tomé and 50 on Príncipe, with species, location, land-use and timing for each pass.

name: Ministério do Ambiente, Juventude e Turismo Sustentável
summary: Government ministry named in a July 2026 Instituto Marquês de Valle Flôr release as a close partner on the Transição Verde project for biodiversity protection.

name: Parque Natural do Príncipe
summary: Protected area on Príncipe whose rangers continued thrush and snail monitoring, according to Fauna & Flora International's January 2022 report, and which the 2019 protocol expected to take over survey responsibility.

name: Participatory Management for Community-based Avoided Deforestation in São Tomé Obô Natural Park
summary: This closed CEPF-funded project aimed to strengthen Obô park community management; reports describe a deforestation reference line, STP-CLIMA carbon modelling and forest inventory work on São Tomé and Príncipe.

name: Participatory Management of Malanza and Praia das Conchas Mangroves in São Tomé
summary: A closed CEPF-funded project (April 2019 to March 2022) that aimed to update mangrove management plans and increase scientific knowledge, with a scientific report containing a biodiversity monitoring protocol for São Tomé mangroves.

name: Programa Tatô marine monitoring programme at Cabras and Rolas islets
summary: Run by Programa Tatô at Cabras and Rolas islets, this marine monitoring programme reportedly monitored 84 turtles through 52 free-diving surveys.

name: Reducing the extinction risk of the three critically endangered birds of Sao Tome
summary: Finished on 30 June 2015, this RSPB-led, US Fish and Wildlife Service-funded project aimed to study three critically endangered endemic birds in Obô Natural Park, São Tomé.

name: The Risks of Degradation in Tropical Forest Ecosystems – Modelling Ecological Vulnerability to Support Conservation in São Tomé
summary: A closed, Rufford Foundation-funded project on forest degradation risk in São Tomé, whose February to April 2013 fieldwork verified satellite data, though its final report says the degradation and vulnerability maps were not yet created.

name: Acuerdo para la Conservación de Bosques Tropicales y Arrecifes de Coral (El Salvador)
summary: A 2021 agreement between the governments of El Salvador and the United States, run by FIAES, which a press report says channels 21 million dollars over a decade, with four projects carried out by other organisations.

name: Asociación de Desarrollo Comunal de Mujeres de Barra de Santiago
summary: Community women's association funded by FIAES, reported to have been created in 2000 and to work on recovering the Barra de Santiago ecosystem.

name: Asociación ProCosta
summary: Salvadoran non-governmental organisation focused on sea turtle research and conservation, which a One Earth page says has defended over 3,000 hawksbill nests with coastal residents, and which is funded by the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation.

name: Asociación Territorios Vivos El Salvador
summary: Non-governmental organisation including the Ateles Conservation Program, affiliated with a 2021 Neotropical Primates paper analysing 73 non-invasive faecal samples from spider monkeys in the Jiquilisco Bay region.

name: Black-handed spider monkey conservation at Laguna Olomega, El Salvador
summary: Fund-supported project whose grantee reports Paso Pacifico is beginning monkey conservation, with goals including baseline range, population and dispersal data and mapping land cover around Laguna Olomega.

name: Catálogo de fotoidentificación de Ballenas Jorobadas de El Salvador
summary: Dataset described in a report as El Salvador's first humpback whale photo-identification catalogue, holding data collected up to 2023, built by Proyecto Megaptera El Salvador and funded by FIAES.

name: Censo Centroamericano de Aves Acuáticas en El Salvador
summary: Annual wetland bird count from Barra de Santiago to La Unión bay, run by SalvaNATURA, with about 6,000 birds reported in that bay in 2025.

name: Conservación, Uso Sostenible de la Biodiversidad y Mantenimiento de los Servicios de los Ecosistemas de Humedales Protegidos de Importancia Internacional
summary: Environment ministry project supported by UNDP and funded by GEF, reported in July 2018 to have provided municipalities and an association with equipment for monitoring wetland threats and risks.

name: Conservation of the Margay and Jaguarundi: Reduction of deaths and guarantee of water in San Pedro Nonualco, El Salvador
summary: Mohamed bin Zayed fund-supported project in San Pedro Nonualco whose camera traps, according to the grantee's report, captured images of margays and jaguarundis visiting watering points.

name: Departamento de Electrónica e Informática, Universidad Centroamericana José Simeón Cañas
summary: University department that is the authors' affiliation on a 2025 Revista ILIA article classifying vegetation types in El Salvador satellite data using U-Net neural networks and a random forest algorithm.

name: Determining the impact of habitat fragmentation on the Geoffroy's Spider Monkey's genetic structure
summary: Mohamed bin Zayed fund-supported project whose grantee reports counting monkeys and calculating range and movement patterns, with Asociación Territorios Vivos El Salvador listed in recipient details.

name: Diagnóstico Bioecológico Integral y Estado de Salud del Ecosistema Arrecifal Salvadoreño
summary: An active 14-month assessment of reefs at Los Cóbanos, Costa del Bálsamo and Punta Amapala, led by FIAES and the Red de Observadores Ciudadanos, funded from a 228,000 dollar TFCCA package, planning a reef health index and citizen science tools.

name: Dirección de Investigaciones, Universidad Tecnológica de El Salvador
summary: University research directorate listed as first author's affiliation on a paper using remote sensing and GIS to analyse mangrove cover change in the Jiquilisco Bay Ramsar site.

name: Environmental DNA project at Los Cóbanos (Universidad de El Salvador)
summary: A project launched by the university in March 2026, built by its marine sciences institute, planning to use environmental DNA to identify reef species and compare communities inside and outside the Los Cóbanos protected area.

name: Estaciones permanentes de monitoreo con cámaras trampa del MARN
summary: Ministry camera-trap monitoring programme, reported in July 2026 to have had only three permanent stations since 2022, with an official saying ratifying an agreement would allow funds to expand it.

name: Fondo de Inversión Ambiental de El Salvador
summary: A Santa Tecla-based fund, also named Fondo de la Iniciativa para las Américas, that a press report says manages a conservation portfolio of over 100 million dollars; its rangers were among 27 trained in drones in 2022.

name: Fundación Doménech
summary: Organisation reported to have worked on the Costa del Sol for over 18 years, with more than 1.3 million eggs incubated, and partnering with FIAES.

name: Fundación Naturaleza El Salvador
summary: A foundation that promoted the 2026 satellite tracking of sea turtles with FIAES and the ministry, and which a December 2025 report says will be local counterpart for the national reef health assessment.

name: Instituto de Ciencias del Mar y Limnología (Universidad de El Salvador)
summary: A university institute that, with the School of Biology, drives the Los Cóbanos eDNA project launched in March 2026, which plans to identify marine species and inform conservation in the marine protected area.

name: Instituto Geográfico y del Catastro Nacional
summary: A national body whose officials appear in the 2023 report of El Salvador's Pan American Institute of Geography and History section, which lists topographic map review and planned cadastral mapping at 1:1,000 urban and 1:2,000 rural scales.

name: Inventario Nacional de Bosques de El Salvador
summary: National forest inventory dated to 2017 and 2018, led by Amilcar Antonio López Melara, whose data the forest reference level used to estimate carbon density in forest categories.

name: Ministerio de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales (El Salvador)
summary: El Salvador's Convention on Biological Diversity focal point reportedly expanded camera trap monitoring; 27 ministry and FIAES rangers received drone training in November 2022.

name: Monitoreo acústico de aves en El Salvador (zona piloto Imposible-Barra de Santiago)
summary: Closed Imposible-Barra de Santiago pilot using AudioMoth and Arbimon, with acoustic monitoring at 52 sites in October 2018 and reported model accuracy of 0.75–1.00 for three bird species.

name: National ecological condition index (El Salvador)
summary: An active initiative, led by the ministry with CATIE, developing monitoring tools for the ecological status of forests and coffee agroecosystems; the ministry plans to expand sampling and design an MRV system.

name: Population assessment of the Bolitoglossa synoria amphibian of the Cerro El Pital Natural Area, El Salvador
summary: Mohamed bin Zayed fund-supported project aiming to gather population and habitat information on Bolitoglossa synoria at Cerro El Pital, with Raúl Ernesto López of IBAES named as recipient.

name: Programa Nacional de Conservación de Caimán y Cocodrilo
summary: Environment ministry programme which, elsalvador.com reported, includes constant monitoring of populations and nests, egg incubation nurseries and environmental education, yielding scientific data on life cycles, mating and nesting.

name: Programa Nacional de Conservación de Cetáceos
summary: Environment ministry programme which Infobae reported in March 2026 seeks to reduce impacts on whales, with a photographic monitoring system producing a catalogue to follow the species and analyse migration routes.

name: Programa Nacional de Conservación de Felinos de El Salvador
summary: Programme of research on the distribution of felines and their prey, with a camera-trap station of 37 cameras in San Carlos Cacahuatique protected area, Morazán, whose first-year results were reported by Revista Minerva.

name: Programa Nacional de Conservación de Tortugas Marinas
summary: Environment ministry programme which, elsalvador.com reported in November 2026, has ranger teams monitoring beaches including at night, and includes a black turtle satellite tagging initiative in its research subprogramme.

name: Proyecto Megaptera El Salvador
summary: Initiative reported to have begun in 2020 to study cetaceans in El Salvador and listed as an author affiliation in a 2023 Revista de Biología Tropical article.

name: SalvaNATURA
summary: A non-profit conservation organisation founded in 1989, described by NatureServe, with a bird banding programme in 2010 across three national parks in El Salvador and one reserve in Honduras, and a study of coffee farms as migratory bird habitat.

name: Satellite tagging of the black turtle in El Salvador
summary: El Salvador's first satellite tagging programme for the black turtle, begun in June 2026 and run by the foundation, FIAES and the ministry, with transmitters fitted to four turtles to gather migration, feeding and behaviour data.

name: Sistema de Alerta Temprana contra Incendios Forestales (El Salvador)
summary: A proposed forest fire early warning system, coordinated by the ministry with UNDP support and Seoul Policy Centre funding, whose design prioritises areas with frequent fires, particularly within protected natural areas.

name: Sistema de Información y Monitoreo Ambiental y Cambio Climático
summary: An active ministry-built platform gathering environmental maps, indicators and databases, presented on 12 August and made official in September 2026, which the ministry says uses AI as support and not a replacement for specialists.

name: Universidad de El Salvador
summary: Diario El Mundo reported its March 2026 launch of MAREADN, aiming for a marine biodiversity baseline using non-invasive environmental DNA techniques; it builds UES eDNA Los Cóbanos.

name: Universidad de Sonsonate
summary: A university named in the affiliation of a 2024 paper that analysed forest change in the San Marcelino protected area from Sentinel-2 imagery and vegetation indices over 2018 to 2022.

name: Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping of the Latakia wildfire (EMSR811)
summary: Copernicus EMS rapid mapping request, reported on 7 July 2025, covering wildfire extent and damage assessment for a Latakia wildfire reported on 3 July in the coastal mountains.

name: Department of Ecology and Forestry, Faculty of Agriculture, Tishreen University
summary: University department in Latakia whose members authored a 2023 paper on monitoring burnt forest areas by remote sensing and GIS, and co-authored a 2025 CA-Markov land use change paper for Bayer and al-Bassit.

name: Department of Topographic Engineering, Faculty of Civil Engineering, Tishreen University
summary: Topographic engineering department in Latakia whose staff co-authored a 2022 land cover map assessment and a 2025 study of July 2025 fire severity using Google Earth Engine.

name: ECO-Syria: Exploring Conflict-Environment Interactions for Sustainable Development and Conservation
summary: Active 2023 to 2026 research project run by Lund University and funded by MECW, whose May 2025 mapathon labelled about 1,600 points, supporting a public 10 m Syria land-cover map.

name: Forest and Fire Monitoring Platform (Syria)
summary: Syrian fire danger monitoring programme, run by the General Organization of Remote Sensing, that estimates danger from vegetation, weather, topography, human factors and the Fire Weather Index, and warned of rising danger in July 2026.

name: Forestry Directorate, Ministry of Agriculture (Syria)
summary: Syrian forestry directorate whose director, in a 3 July 2026 report, described fire-line and road work and put the forest guard force at 1,411 for over 527,000 hectares.

name: General Organization of Remote Sensing
summary: Remote sensing authority under the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, whose Forest and Fire Monitoring Platform warned of rising forest fire danger at the start of July 2026.

name: Latakia University
summary: University whose staff published 2025 and 2026 papers on burned forest mapping, vegetation cover and Syrian shelf chlorophyll-a from satellite data, estimating about 8,230.74 hectares of forest burned in the Lattakia region.

name: Ministry of Emergency and Disaster Management
summary: Syrian ministry whose Latakia directorate, per a July 2026 SANA report, deployed 30 forward points for forest fire monitoring and planned a sensor-based early warning system covering about 4,000 hectares.

name: Ministry of Local Administration and Environment (Syria)
summary: Syrian ministry with a Directorate of Biodiversity, Lands and Natural Reserves, whose director is the CBD primary national focal point and whose biodiversity department head is the protected areas focal point.

name: Syrian Society for the Conservation of Wildlife
summary: Damascus-based NGO that says it conserves Syrian biodiversity, and in February 2021 reported wintering bird surveys, migratory soaring bird counts and data updates for accessible Important Bird Areas.

name: Wildfire Early Detection System in Latakia Governorate
summary: Wildfire early detection system for Latakia Governorate, for which UNDP awarded a provision and installation contract on 13 May 2026; its current status is unknown.

name: All Out Africa
summary: Company that, according to Mbuluzi Game Reserve, rents part of the reserve's property and has set up a Savannah Research Center there.

name: All Out Africa Foundation
summary: Reports 2006 charity registration in Eswatini and work across Eswatini, Mozambique and South Africa, running a savanna research centre and seasonal biodiversity surveys with university researchers.

name: Assessing the Impacts of Commercial Agriculture in Swaziland
summary: A closed project dated 5 June 2014 that aimed to compare bat activity in savanna with adjacent commercial sugarcane, using Anabat II detectors on randomly selected sites.

name: Big Game Parks
summary: Private trust describing itself as funded by self-generated income, with delegated Game Act responsibilities including permitting, CITES and law enforcement, and listed parks including Hlane and Mlilwane.

name: Breeding Biology of African White-Backed Vultures in Swaziland
summary: A closed project dated 29 May 2014 at Mlawula Nature Reserve, Eswatini, which aimed to find what affects breeding success in a small white-backed vulture colony, partly by monitoring nest food provision with camera traps.

name: Department of Biological Sciences, University of Eswatini
summary: A university department listed, according to OpenAlex, as the affiliation of authors of 2024 and 2025 papers on African bat and Eswatini snake databases and on shrub encroachment effects on savanna birds.

name: Department of Forestry (Eswatini)
summary: Government forestry department that, the Coalition for Rainforest Nations reported in February 2025, has built in-house data capacity since 2023, leading to a first Forest Reference Level submitted to the UNFCCC in January 2024.

name: Eswatini annual land use maps, 1990-2020
summary: Annual land use maps of 10 categories covering all of Eswatini from 1990 to 2020, classified with random forest from Landsat time series using CCDC change detection, and validated with over 6,000 reference samples.

name: Eswatini Environment Authority
summary: Government environment body that was executing agency for a GEF-funded capacity needs assessment in 2002 to 2003 and planned a biodiversity strategy revision, with completion envisaged by September 2014.

name: Eswatini forest reference level (2024 submission)
summary: National forest reference level submitted to UNFCCC on 8 January 2024, with 2000 to 2020 land-use activity data from remote sensing products and a 7,702-plot grid assessed by national experts in 2023.

name: Eswatini National Trust Commission
summary: Statutory body managing Eswatini's parks and reserves, SNPAS lead partner and restoration project executing agency, with a 2018 review recording SMART patrolling pilots in its parks.

name: Eswatini snake occurrence database
summary: Repository of snake records for Eswatini, each with species, coordinates, locality, date and record type, with a Shiny map app, linked to a 2025 paper in Database.

name: Ministry of Tourism and Environmental Affairs
summary: Government ministry that implements a five-year GEF-funded biodiversity project in the Lubombo landscape, rolled out in May 2026 with UNDP as GEF agency, and launched a conservation measures framework in 2021.

name: Raptor, vulture and stork nesting monitoring (All Out Africa Foundation)
summary: A long-term monitoring project, run by All Out Africa Foundation with the University of Eswatini, on nesting and breeding success of threatened raptors, vultures and marabou storks in three Eswatini protected areas.

name: Savanna Research Center
summary: Research centre run and built by All Out Africa with University of Florida support, using camera trapping on three grids as part of a ten-year plan to assess savannah biodiversity.

name: Savannah biodiversity monitoring project (All Out Africa Foundation)
summary: A project run by All Out Africa Foundation, ongoing since 2013, with seasonal surveys of birds, mammals and vegetation on long-term grids in three Eswatini reserves, also recording climate, fire and management interventions.

name: Strengthening the National Protected Areas System of Swaziland (SNPAS)
summary: Closed GEF-funded project, run by the Eswatini National Trust Commission from 2015 to 2021, which UNDP says raised protected area coverage from 3.9% to 5.5% and developed a GIS-based biodiversity information system.

name: The distribution and conservation of African ginger (Siphonochilus aethiopicus) in Eswatini
summary: A project to map the distribution and diversity of African ginger in Eswatini and identify environmentally threatened critical locations, funded by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, with the grant awarded on 14 November 2024.

name: University of Eswatini
summary: A university named in a 2022 ICAT land mapping report for Eswatini, where its researcher led the land-use greenhouse gas inventory data, and named by All Out Africa Foundation as a savannah monitoring partner.

name: Aerial count of elephants and large wildlife in Loug Chari and Mayo Lemié (2021)
summary: Closed aerial count of elephants in the Loug Chari and Mayo Lemié departments, held 17 to 26 March 2021, which observed 223 elephants and estimated a population of 223 to 384.

name: Aerial support for anti-poaching, monitoring and management of Zakouma National Park and Periphery, Chad
summary: Closed project led by African Parks and funded by the US Fish and Wildlife Service, with 267,362 euros from September 2017 to September 2019 for surveillance flights and aerial surveys around Zakouma.

name: Bustard study and conservation programme, Ouadi Rimé-Ouadi Achim
summary: Programme established by Sahara Conservation in 2024 to study and conserve bustards in the Ouadi Rimé-Ouadi Achim reserve, with a female Denham's bustard fitted with a transmitter in September 2025.

name: Centre National de Recherche pour le Développement (Chad)
summary: Chadian public scientific and technical institution renamed from CNAR (created in 1991) in 2015, whose remote sensing service an OSS REPSAHEL report says made land cover maps.

name: Decision Support in Land Degradation Neutrality (DS4LDN), Chad component
summary: Chad component of a land degradation decision-support project, active, which aims to support participatory degradation and LDN maps combining national data with Earth observation; its applications are listed as forthcoming.

name: Department of Computer Science, Virtual University of Chad
summary: University department in N'Djamena, listed as the first author's affiliation on a chapter on elephant monitoring in Zakouma National Park, which benchmarked Faster R-CNN, Mask R-CNN and YOLO models.

name: Direction de la Conservation de la Faune et des Aires Protégées
summary: Directorate run by Chad's environment ministry, placed by the CBD's national focal point record at BP 447, N'Djaména.

name: Dénombrements internationaux des oiseaux d'eau au Tchad
summary: Closed waterbird counting project in Chad, run by the DFAP, which in February 2024 had AEWA African Initiative support and included an experimental eDNA study using water samples.

name: Kordofan Giraffe Project (Zakouma National Park)
summary: Closed project in Zakouma National Park whose 2018 page planned Chad's first Kordofan giraffe census using photo identification, and GPS units for 10 to 25 giraffe through the wet season.

name: Large carnivore research project, Greater Zakouma Ecosystem
summary: Closed three-year project, 2020 to 2023, funded by the Lion Recovery Fund and led by Chiara Fraticelli, using camera traps to estimate large carnivore abundance, density and seasonal distribution in Zakouma.

name: Long-term ecological monitoring programme, Ouadi Rimé-Ouadi Achim Faunal Reserve
summary: Monitoring programme in the Ouadi Rimé-Ouadi Achim Faunal Reserve that, Sahara Conservation says, included a July 2025 transect wildlife inventory covering more than 5,000 square kilometres.

name: Mapping antelope habitats in the Ouadi Rimé-Ouadi Achim Reserve, Chad
summary: Closed 2024–2025 project, run by Caleb Ngaba Waye Taroum under an IUCN Save Our Species fund, aiming to assess forage availability, quality and selectivity for six mammal species in the reserve.

name: Mayo-Kebbi Est participatory mapping project
summary: Closed participatory mapping project led by Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim; EOS Data Analytics says it contributed a map from 10 m Sentinel-2 imagery, finalised by the end of December 2021.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Pêche et du Développement Durable
summary: Chad's environment ministry, which hosts the primary CBD national focal point and, per Sahara Conservation, had its minister sign a ten-year management agreement for the Ouadi Rimé-Ouadi Achim reserve in July 2025.

name: Noé programme for Manda National Park
summary: Programme under which Chad's government entrusted Manda National Park to Noé for ten years from 10 December 2025, with operations beginning in early 2026 and camera traps installed.

name: Programme d'appui à la gestion concertée des Aires Protégées et Écosystèmes Fragiles du Tchad
summary: European Union funded programme for protected areas and fragile ecosystems in Chad, with up to EUR 33 million over five operational years, 2017 to 2022, which reports twenty camera traps set in Siniaka Minia reserve from May 2021.

name: Préserver le Complexe d'aires protégées de Binder-Léré
summary: Programme in south-west Chad where Noé says it has managed the Binder-Léré protected areas complex since 2021, reporting GPS-collared elephants and giraffe, an aerial inventory and regenerating forest cover.

name: Research and monitoring programme for large mammals and ostriches, Greater Zakouma Ecosystem
summary: In 2021, JRS reported funding African Parks’ research on large mammals and ostriches in Zakouma and two adjoining reserves, using aerial surveys, collars and ground patrols.

name: Réserve Naturelle et Culturelle de l'Ennedi
summary: Chadian reserve, officially created in February 2019 and reported in 2021 as managed by African Parks Network, which uses CyberTracker for ecoguard monitoring data collected on smartphones or tablets.

name: Scimitar-horned Oryx Reintroduction Project
summary: Initiated in 2008 and led by Sahara Conservation with Environment Agency-Abu Dhabi; Sahara Conservation reports over 650 wild oryx by mid 2026, monitored with satellite collars.

name: Sena Oura National Park wildlife surveys
summary: Wildlife survey project in Sena Oura National Park run by WCS, which in April 2023 reported ground surveys including camera trapping and released an image of a female lion.

name: Siniaka Minia camera-trap survey 2021
summary: Closed 2021 camera-trap survey in Siniaka Minia, with twenty cameras deployed for 886 trap-days and twenty-eight wild species observed, described in a report carrying the African Parks Network name.

name: SOS Éléphants Tchad
summary: Chadian NGO, according to the APEF programme's 2021 report, whose teams and those of the wildlife directorate located the elephants on which the March 2021 aerial count was based.

name: Suivi écologique de la Réserve Naturelle et Culturelle de l'Ennedi
summary: Active monitoring programme in the Ennedi reserve, built by the reserve, in which ecoguards were trained in 2023 to use CyberTracker for 11 new ecological monitoring protocols.

name: Tchad, Atlas des cartes de végétation (REPSAHEL)
summary: Atlas of Chad vegetation maps at 1:200,000, made from 2013 satellite images and field observations, with the data and thematic maps added to the REPSAHEL project information system.

name: Towards Elephants Intelligent Monitoring in Zakouma National Park, Chad
summary: Published Springer chapter, with a 2024 CSCE abstract, proposing an AI approach to protecting endangered species in Zakouma National Park and benchmarking Faster R-CNN, Mask R-CNN and YOLO detection models.

name: Université de Moundou
summary: University in Moundou, Chad, whose geography department planned the LaCEG spatial information laboratory, which lists spatial databases for managing forests and national parks among its missions.

name: AGBO-ZEGUE
summary: Togolese non-governmental organisation giving scientific and technical support to conservation, reporting more than 22 years of sea turtle monitoring through nine projects as of 2023, with partners including the University of Lomé and the World Bank.

name: Direction des ressources forestières
summary: Togolese forest directorate created within the environment ministry in 2013, coordinating wildlife and plant inventories, with 27 GBIF datasets; its director is Togo’s primary CBD focal point.

name: GBIF Togo
summary: Togo's country node of GBIF, a voting participant based at the Faculty of Sciences in Lomé, with Raoufou Pierre Radji listed as node manager.

name: Herbier de l'Université de Lomé
summary: University of Lomé herbarium that acts as the national herbarium, refitted in 2008 with a temperature-controlled room and a computerised database storing information on all species sampled.

name: Institut Géographique National du Togo
summary: Togolese national geographic institute, created by a government decree reported by APA on 20 February 2026, replacing the former directorate general of geographic information and cartography, with administrative and financial autonomy.

name: Inventaire des mammifères du Parc National de Fazao-Malfakassa par caméras trap
summary: Closed camera-trap mammal inventory in Fazao-Malfakassa National Park, run by Agbo-Zégué and the University of Lomé, which recorded 1,564 individuals of 25 species from 61,089 photos taken by 100 traps.

name: Inventaire forestier national du Togo
summary: National forest inventory described in the national REDD+ bulletin as the first in Togo's history, reporting forest cover of 24.24 per cent with very marked degradation.

name: Laboratoire d'Hydrologie Appliquée et Environnement
summary: Université de Lomé research laboratory, run by the university and listed as the first author's affiliation on a paper forecasting land use and land cover on the Agoènyivé Plateau using remote sensing and machine learning.

name: Laboratoire d'Écologie et d'Écotoxicologie
summary: Université de Lomé laboratory in the Faculté des Sciences, led by Guillaume Koffivi Ketoh, linked to a 2022 camera-trap mammal study and a 30 August 2022 session sharing Fazao-Malfakassa National Park inventory results.

name: Laboratoire de Botanique et Ecologie Végétale
summary: Université de Lomé research laboratory, run by the university and led by Koffi Akpagana, listed as an affiliation for five authors of a paper mapping above-ground forest biomass in the Atacora mountains with Google Earth Engine.

name: Laboratoire de Recherche Forestière
summary: Université de Lomé laboratory, led by Kouami Kokou and listing biodiversity informatics among its themes, affiliated with a 2023 study mapping Mono Transboundary Biosphere Reserve land cover for 1986, 2000 and 2015 and predicting it to 2070.

name: Laboratoire de Recherche sur la Dynamique des Milieux et des Sociétés
summary: A geography department laboratory affiliated with a 2024 GIS and remote sensing study of anthropogenic threats to degraded forest land in the Savannahs Region from 1984 to 2020.

name: Laboratoire de Recherches Biogéographiques et d'Etudes Environnementales
summary: A geography department laboratory cited as affiliation by all three authors of a 2026 paper using Maxent and WorldClim variables on climate change and Afzelia africana.

name: Marine turtle monitoring programme on the Togolese coast, 2012 to 2013
summary: Closed monitoring of marine turtles along the whole Togolese coast, September 2012 to August 2013, run by Agbo Zegue and funded by the Lomé container terminal, recording 740 occurrences via 10 ecoguards and 5 fishermen.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement
summary: Togolese environment ministry, whose full name includes forest resources, coastal protection and climate change, and which set up the forest resources directorate by a 2013 order.

name: Mont Balam drone mapping and reforestation initiative
summary: Drone mapping and reforestation initiative led by Togo Flying Labs, which per Pix4D's case study mapped 44 hectares and revealed 10 severely degraded hectares to target reforestation.

name: Office national des aires protégées
summary: Togolese protected areas office, created in 2023 according to the government news site, which manages national parks and wildlife reserves; its headquarters in Kpalimé was under construction in October 2026.

name: Protection des tortues marines sur le littoral togolais
summary: Closed sea turtle project run by Agbo-Zégué and funded by the GEF Small Grants Programme, which began on 28 February 2022, aimed to strengthen monitoring protocols, and cost 33,033,966 CFA francs.

name: Pôle de Recherches et d'Expertise sur la Dynamique des espaces et des Sociétés
summary: Université de Kara research group, led by Assogba Guézéré, named by its acronym PREDES in a 2023 Landsat remote sensing study of land use change in the Mont Balam classified forest, 1985 to 2020.

name: Soutien au renforcement des capacités de la brigade de surveillance de la réserve de biosphère transfrontière du Mono
summary: Closed BIOPAMA-funded technical grant of €98,593.66, planned for 15 November 2020 to 14 July 2021, led by the forest directorate to equip the Mono reserve’s surveillance brigade.

name: Strengthening the biodiversity stakeholders network in Togo
summary: Project to strengthen Togo's biodiversity network and encourage use of open-access data on GBIF through awareness and capacity building, described in its dataset record as illustrating how the GBIF node functions.

name: Togo Clearing-House Mechanism of the Convention on Biological Diversity
summary: Togo's clearing-house mechanism portal for the Convention on Biological Diversity, which posts national targets, including one on biodiversity in spatial planning, and carries organisation profiles such as Agbo-Zégué's from August 2023.

name: Togo Flying Labs
summary: Togolese centre that describes itself as using robotics and artificial intelligence for social challenges, including biodiversity conservation and forestry mapping; it joined the Flying Labs network in 2023, sponsored by Senegal Flying Labs.

name: Togo National Herbarium Database
summary: Dataset extracted from the University of Lomé herbarium's RIHA database, holding specimens from across Togo and covering only angiosperms.

name: Université de Kara
summary: Togolese university in Kara that describes its research as done by laboratories, specialised centres and international partnerships, with PREDES among its laboratories and linked to a 2023 Mont Balam remote sensing paper.

name: Université de Lomé
summary: Active university in Lomé that publishes 39 datasets on GBIF, including the Togo National Herbarium Database and red lists, and in November 2026 signed an agreement with LuxDev to host a protected-areas diploma.

name: Uses, Structural Characterization and Ecological Niches of Three Vulnerable Woody Species in the Guinean Forest Formations of Togo
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project that aimed to inventory uses, study stand structure and model current and future ecological niches of three vulnerable forest species in Togo, with a final evaluation report dated July 2025.

name: Accelerating Tiger Recovery along the Thailand-Myanmar Border: Thailand Component
summary: Project run by IUCN with the Department of National Parks as partner, which in February 2022 aimed to map tigers and prey in the southern Western Forest Complex using camera traps and a GIS database.

name: Aerial Recon & Recovery Initiative
summary: A project against ghost gear using aerial drone surveys and machine learning, which says it has located 605 items across Koh Phangan and Koh Tao and reports 356 surveys covering 350 square kilometres.

name: AI and Robotics Ventures
summary: Organisation that PTTEP says carried out an underwater camera and AI species identification project together with it, and which is listed as a partner of PTTEP.

name: AI-assisted community-led monitoring of individually identified Asian elephants in Kuiburi National Park
summary: An active project using camera traps to identify individual crop-foraging elephants in Kuiburi National Park, with planned SMS-integrated AI camera trap early warnings and a planned database of individual elephants.

name: ARRI ghost gear detection model
summary: An AI program built by the Aerial Recon & Recovery Initiative to identify ghost gear in drone images, as reported by Thai Union.

name: Asian Institute of Technology
summary: Institution given as the affiliation of Werachart Muttitanon, first author of a 2005 paper listed in OpenAlex.

name: Biodiversity CHM Thailand
summary: Active Thai site describing itself as the mechanism for disseminating biodiversity information, carrying national biodiversity plans and linked from the ONEP page on the NBSAP.

name: Bird Conservation Society of Thailand
summary: A registered association offering a bird database and partnering with the national parks department on the January waterbird census, per an MNRE page sourced to ONEP.

name: Bring The Elephant Home Foundation
summary: A registered foundation based in Hua Hin that advertises for a camera trap field officer to survey elephants in five protected areas, and lists enhanced camera trap monitoring in its 2024 report.

name: Burapha University
summary: University given as the affiliation of Narong Pleerux, first author of a 2025 paper listed in OpenAlex.

name: Capacity building for systematic wildlife monitoring in the Doi Phu Kha transboundary landscape
summary: Supported by WWF-US and partnering with the DNP, this project distributed 50 camera trap sets across three protected areas and plans AI-assisted image classification training.

name: Carbon Atlas
summary: Platform built by GISTDA that uses remote sensing and AI to provide Thailand's above-ground biomass and carbon stock data for 2022, drawing on more than 1,000 field plots.

name: CarbonAtlas-THA
summary: Space for Climate Observatory project accepted in May 2025, aiming to improve forest carbon monitoring with satellite data, LiDAR, UAVs and AI, in partnership with GISTDA.

name: Chiang Mai University
summary: University given as the affiliation of first authors of two papers listed in OpenAlex, from 2021 and 2023, the later one on deep learning for forest fire detection.

name: Chiang Rai Hotspot
summary: App that Mongabay reported in 2022 used NASA MODIS data to show fire hotspots in near real time, alert firefighters and communities, and was heavily used at the Mirror Foundation.

name: Chulalongkorn University
summary: University given as the affiliation of Chaichoke Vaiphasa, first author of a 2005 paper listed in OpenAlex.

name: Department of Marine and Coastal Resources
summary: Agency of Thailand's environment ministry that lists a marine data centre, online marine map and surveillance system on its site, and is named as a partner by WWF Thailand and WildAid.

name: Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation
summary: Thai environment ministry agency that, according to a February 2019 WCS Thailand report, had adopted SMART patrolling into regular work; it partners with WWF Thailand and WildAid.

name: Division of Biological Science, Faculty of Science, Prince of Songkla University
summary: University division named as the affiliation of the first author of a 2026 paper on single-leech metabarcoding for biodiversity monitoring in Peninsular Thailand.

name: Dual-branch deep learning coral classification model
summary: Deep learning model for classifying coral in underwater images, described in a 2026 paper and built by Pracharat Sa-ngadsup.

name: Elephant Smart Early Warning System
summary: Active early-warning system built by True Corporation, which The Nation reports has been in Kuiburi National Park since 2018, with AI filtering camera data before staff are alerted.

name: Enhancing SMART Patrol through Real-Time Data Integration with Network-Centric Operations
summary: Active project built by the national parks department, piloting SMART Connect with the Team Awareness Kit at Mae Wong National Park to join patrol records, camera traps, UAVs and GIS.

name: Environmental DNA for monitoring dolphins, whales and dugongs in Thailand
summary: A closed project, dated January 2023, that aimed to develop eDNA surveys to detect marine mammals in Thai coastal and freshwater waters, with a final evaluation report dated July 2024.

name: Eyes on the Forest
summary: Active collaborative deforestation monitoring initiative using specially equipped drones, with a 2024 factsheet reporting 40 automatic camera traps set up in Kaeng Krung National Park.

name: Flat-headed cat camera-trap survey, Princess Sirindhorn Wildlife Sanctuary
summary: Camera-trap survey, run by the Department of National Parks and Panthera, that confirmed the flat-headed cat in Thailand for the first time since 1995, with 13 detections in 2024 and 16 in 2025.

name: Freeland
summary: Active organisation saying its law enforcement and technical experts find and stop traffickers, and which WildCats Conservation Alliance says it has supported in Khao Laem National Park since 2016.

name: Geo-Informatics and Space Technology Development Agency
summary: Self-described primary space and geo-informatics organisation of Thailand, established in 2000, which The Nation reported in June 2025 had developed a certified satellite-based carbon sequestration assessment method.

name: GISTDA wildfire monitoring system
summary: A GISTDA-run system covering Thailand and four neighbouring countries, using Sentinel-2 to map burned areas every three to five days and processing hotspot data to locate hotspots and responsible agencies.

name: Hala-Bala Wildlife Research Station
summary: Research station that Panthera says has collaborated with Panthera Thailand on ecological studies, and which authors of a 2026 leech eDNA metabarcoding paper give as their affiliation.

name: Integrated monitoring of wild elephant populations in Kuiburi National Park, 2025
summary: A closed WWF Thailand-run monitoring effort in Kuiburi National Park, combining direct counts, camera traps and drones over 20 to 25 November 2025, with preliminary counts of up to 104 elephants.

name: Joint Graduate School of Energy and Environment
summary: Institution given as the affiliation of Hong Anh Thi Nguyen, first author of a 2021 paper listed in OpenAlex.

name: Kajanurak
summary: An app built by True Digital Group which, True says, uses AI to identify elephants in images from SIM-equipped cameras and passes sightings to conservation units or village representatives.

name: Kasetsart University
summary: University with a Bangkok address that publishes a GBIF dataset on medically important flies in Thailand.

name: Khao Laem National Park tiger protection project
summary: Active project led by Thailand's national parks department, funded by WildCats Conservation Alliance, which reports 121 camera traps deployed in 2024 and EarthRanger approved for launch.

name: Khon Kaen University
summary: University given as the affiliation of Saysongkham Sayavong, first author of a 2020 paper listed in OpenAlex.

name: King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi
summary: University given as the affiliation of first authors of papers listed in OpenAlex from 2014 and 2026, the later one on mapping deciduous dipterocarp forests at 10 m resolution in the Indo-Burma region.

name: Mae Fah Luang Foundation under Royal Patronage
summary: Active foundation that said in January 2026 it was building biodiversity databases using bioacoustics, machine learning and eDNA, and in 2025 surveyed Trang's mangrove biodiversity with the marine department.

name: Mahasarakham University
summary: University with an OpenAlex-listed 2019 paper whose first author, Warong Suksavate, gives an affiliation there; the facts give nothing further.

name: Mahidol University
summary: University whose Kanchanaburi campus is the affiliation of a paper's first author on remote sensing of vegetation recovery in karst forests, and whose researchers, EarthRanger says, use its elephant early warning data.

name: Mapping Seagrass Meadows, Andaman Coast, Thailand
summary: Project listed by the Connected Conservation Foundation as monitoring habitats and dugongs with Pléiades imagery and drones, to identify areas for restoration.

name: Marine GI Portal
summary: Marine and coastal ecosystem assessment and monitoring system that GISTDA says it developed in 2022, with five marine spatial planning tools, including automatic mangrove status reporting and smartphone data collection by the public.

name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment
summary: Thai ministry whose stated vision covers natural resources, environmental protection and biodiversity, and whose proposed National Biodiversity Action Plan 2023-2027 the cabinet approved, according to ONEP.

name: Nakhon Si Thammarat Rajabhat University
summary: University with an OpenAlex-listed 2026 paper whose first author, Kritaphat Songsri-in, gives an affiliation there; the facts give nothing further.

name: Naresuan University
summary: University with an OpenAlex-listed 2023 paper whose first author, Bhattarapong Somwong, gives an affiliation there; the facts give nothing further.

name: National Science and Technology Development Agency
summary: Agency with an OpenAlex-listed 2021 paper whose first author, Nidhi Jha, gives an affiliation there; the facts give nothing further.

name: New Heaven Reef Conservation Program
summary: Reef conservation programme reporting over eight years of monthly Ecological Monitoring Program data by 2014, used for reports to local government groups and stakeholders.

name: Office of Natural Resources and Environmental Policy and Planning
summary: Agency of Thailand's environment ministry that sent the National Biodiversity Action Plan 2023-2027 to the Convention on Biological Diversity Secretariat on 31 October 2024.

name: Payap University
summary: University with an OpenAlex-listed 2025 paper whose first author, Zhang Enhong, gives an affiliation there; the facts give nothing further.

name: Piloting drone surveys to detect and remove ghost gear in key marine megafauna habitat in Andaman coastal sites
summary: A proposed pilot of ARRI's drone and AI method to detect and map ghost gear in four Andaman provinces, in key sea turtle habitat, alongside turtle presence mapping.

name: Predator Restoration and Conservation Project in the Mae Ping-Omkoi Forest
summary: An active project using camera traps to study wildlife distribution and abundance, especially tigers, and building a database and tracking system, with survey data planned to inform SMART patrols.

name: Prince of Songkla University
summary: University with an OpenAlex-listed 2016 paper whose first author, Werapong Koedsin, gives an affiliation there; the facts give nothing further.

name: Princess of Naradhiwas University
summary: University with an OpenAlex-listed 2019 paper whose first author, S. Chuenjai, gives an affiliation there; the facts give nothing further.

name: Protecting Thailand's River Monsters
summary: A project begun in March 2021 and extended to 2028, run by WCS Thailand and the Mohamed bin Zayed fund, which reported 15 camera traps and cumulative otter and crocodile captures by January 2023.

name: PTT Exploration and Production
summary: Lists aquatic animal detection and microplastic monitoring on its Ocean Data Platform and carried out underwater camera and AI species identification with ARV beneath Gulf of Thailand platforms.

name: Raks Thai Foundation
summary: Foundation with a Bangkok office and offices in many provinces, named among the organisations that co-created the Earth Defenders Toolkit, and with a section on environment and climate change work.

name: Ramkhamhaeng University
summary: University with an OpenAlex-listed 2023 paper whose first author, Patiya Pattanasak, gives an affiliation there; the facts give nothing further.

name: Royal Forest Department
summary: Thai forestry department that Matichon reported in September 2022 would receive duties and resources outside conservation forests, and which partners with the Mae Fah Luang Foundation on a community forest carbon project.

name: Saving Forest Giants, Sai Yok National Park
summary: Listed as wild elephant habitat risk mapping in Sai Yok National Park by the Connected Conservation Foundation, which reports providing imagery, software, funding and analysis with Airbus Foundation.

name: Saving the Spotted Greenshank (Thailand)
summary: A Mubadala-funded project partnering with the Bird Conservation Society of Thailand, whose surveys continued until October 2023 and recorded a highest count of 249 birds in January 2023.

name: Seub Nakhasathien Foundation
summary: Foundation working on forest and wildlife conservation, funded by CEPF for a February 2022 to July 2024 project on community surveys of Somphong's rasbora in the Pakpli floodplain.

name: Shinawatra University
summary: University with an OpenAlex-listed 2025 paper whose first author, Lakshman Kumar Jamili, gives an affiliation there; the facts give nothing further.

name: Smart Coastal Mangrove Monitoring
summary: Closed Kasetsart University project that in 2025 used drones, satellites, and salinity and water quality sensors to assess mangrove ecosystem recovery, with an end date of 25 December 2025.

name: Srinakharinwirot University
summary: University with an OpenAlex-listed 2023 paper whose first author, Keereeluk Sirikarin, gives an affiliation there; the facts give nothing further.

name: Strengthening capacities for biodiversity management in Thailand's community forests
summary: Closed project, funded by the Darwin Initiative, that ran from April 2023 to March 2025 and aimed to build community capacity for biodiversity assessment, monitoring and reporting.

name: Strengthening surveillance and monitoring to tackle forest loss and land degradation in Thailand's border areas
summary: Completed project, run by Kasetsart University and funded by Japan's foreign ministry, that proposed a satellite and drone forest monitoring system for local authorities and communities in border areas.
