name: Suan Sunandha Rajabhat University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation given by the first author of a 2020 paper, Walaiporn Phonphan; no other activity is recorded.

name: Suranaree University of Technology
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation given by the first author of a 2025 paper, Sinlapachat Pungpa; no other activity is recorded.

name: Thaichote
summary: Thailand's first earth observation satellite, launched on 1 October 2008, carrying one panchromatic and one multispectral camera, and built by the Geo-Informatics and Space Technology Development Agency.

name: Thaicom
summary: Thansettakij reported December 2023 plans for an AI carbon credit platform with the Mae Fah Luang Foundation; The Nation reports it developed satellite and AI forest-fire hotspot detection.

name: Thailand Biodiversity Information Facility
summary: Programme describing itself as Thailand's central biodiversity data centre, linking species data between agencies, with a 2023 reported plan for TISTR to share its database under a memorandum of understanding with ONEP.

name: Thailand Bioresource Research Center
summary: A centre under BIOTEC and NSTDA that has developed microbial diversity databases and publishes a GBIF occurrence dataset from 2021 Mekong River bacterial metabarcoding.

name: Thailand elephant early warning system on EarthRanger
summary: An active early warning system on EarthRanger using AI, camera traps and community data, in which 64 camera traps on 32 farms at Kuiburi have helped identify 25 individual elephants since November 2025.

name: Thailand FishAI
summary: A Department of Fisheries citizen science app prototype, reported by Thairath as launched on 2 May 2026, which initially identified 50 fish species from photos.

name: Thaksin University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation given by the first author of a 2019 paper, Jamroon Srichaichana; no other activity is recorded.

name: Thammasat University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation given by the first author of a 2020 paper, Kritchayan Intarat; no other activity is recorded.

name: True Corporation
summary: Company that The Nation reported in March 2024 used 5G, 4G and AI to manage human-elephant conflict through the Elephant Smart Early Warning System.

name: Underwater camera and AI software for aquatic animal identification under offshore petroleum platforms in the Gulf of Thailand
summary: Run by PTT Exploration and Production in partnership with AI and Robotics Ventures, the project develops AI to classify animals filmed beneath an Arthit platform, identifying seven species.

name: University of Phayao
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation given by the first author of a 2021 paper, Jiraporn Kulsoontornrat; no other activity is recorded.

name: Walailak University
summary: University listed in OpenAlex as the affiliation given by the first author of a 2023 paper, Naparat Suttidate; no other activity is recorded.

name: WCS Thailand
summary: Run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, lists SMART Patrol and Siamese crocodile surveys; a February 2019 report described its director as a co-initiator of Smart Patrol in Thailand.

name: WWF Thailand
summary: Reports WWF's presence in Thailand since 1995, lists camera traps and UAVs for wildlife monitoring in its 2024 factsheet, and partners with two government departments.

name: Aerogeodesy Dushanbe
summary: State enterprise run by the State Committee for Land Management and Geodesy, which CAREC says is responsible for fieldwork, data processing and mapping in Tajikistan's national forest inventory.

name: Association of Nature Conservation Organizations of Tajikistan
summary: CEPF-funded Tajik conservation association whose Baljuvan project reported stable or increasing urial numbers across three surveys, while its camera-trap monitoring did not reach the planned scale.

name: Atlas of Environmental Change of the Republic of Tajikistan
summary: Environmental atlas of Tajikistan, presented nationally in Dushanbe on 2 September 2025, combining long-term monitoring data with satellite remote sensing on water, land, forests and biodiversity, built by UNEP and offered in print and a geoportal.

name: Biodiversity monitoring and automated field data collection system (Tajikistan)
summary: A UNDP-linked biodiversity data collection system for Tajikistan's National Biodiversity and Biosafety Centre, which NextGIS says it began building in 2020, based on NextGIS Collector and field-tested in 2021.

name: Bukhara deer thermal drone survey, Beshai Palangon State Nature Reserve
summary: A thermal drone survey of Bukhara deer in a Tajik reserve, run by Tajikistan Nature Foundation, with pilot flights in February 2025 and a full count of 12 flights in September 2025, reported by CAMCA.

name: CESP 2022-001, capacity development at the Tajik GBIF node
summary: GBIF-funded project led by Samariddin Barotov to build data publication and node management capacity in Tajikistan, including a September 2022 training workshop attended by teachers from four institutions.

name: Committee for Environmental Protection under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan
summary: Tajik government committee that hosts the national biodiversity centre and protected areas focal point, and is the executing body of the World Bank-financed Tajikistan Resilient Landscape Restoration Project.

name: Conservation and Sustainable Use of Pamir Alay and Tien Shan Ecosystems for Snow Leopard Protection and Sustainable Community Livelihoods
summary: GEF-funded snow leopard project run by the National Biodiversity and Biosafety Centre from 2016 to 2021, which supported installing 70 camera traps in eight project areas in 2020.

name: Forestry Agency of Tajikistan
summary: Tajik agency whose deputy director announced a satellite and field-based national forest inventory on 15 July 2026, and which reportedly returned 43,082.5 hectares to the state forest fund.

name: GBIF Tajikistan
summary: Tajikistan's associate participant node in GBIF, managed by Samariddin Barotov, with five endorsed publishers and a planned host at the Institute of Botany, Plant Physiology and Genetics.

name: Institute of Botany, Plant Physiology and Genetics, National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan
summary: Tajik academy institute with a herbarium fund created in 1941, which publishes its herbarium records through GBIF and said in January 2022 it would host the national GBIF node.

name: M-Sayod
summary: Operator of the hunting concession in Darvoz, according to Panthera's CEPF report, which also records that its rangers were taught camera-trap use and that it enacted a snow leopard monitoring plan.

name: Markhor survey in southern Tajikistan, 2022
summary: Closed 2022 survey run by the Committee for Environmental Protection, in which five teams covered about 2,000 square kilometres across 10 markhor conservancies in 15 days.

name: National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan
summary: Tajik academy whose experts took part in the March 2022 markhor survey and the Baljuvan project, and whose vice-president reportedly said camera-trap research suggested about 500 snow leopards in Tajikistan.

name: National Biodiversity and Biosafety Centre
summary: Centre under the Committee for Environmental Protection that coordinates Tajikistan's obligations under the CBD, hosts its clearing-house mechanism, and is named as partner on two GEF-funded projects.

name: National Forest Inventory of Tajikistan
summary: Active inventory run by Aerogeodesy Dushanbe and Umweltdaten GmbH under a World Bank project, mapping forest from Sentinel-2 and RapidEye data with machine learning and surveying with mobile LiDAR.

name: Pavlovsky Institute of Zoology and Parasitology, National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan
summary: National Academy of Sciences institute in Tajikistan that Tajikistan's report on the Bukhara deer memorandum (July 2023 to June 2024) lists among the organisations carrying out regular monitoring, with camera traps among the main methods.

name: SMART patrol monitoring in Tajikistan's protected areas
summary: OSCE reports SMART training in December 2024 and 20 smartphones supplied in April 2025; a 2021 project update reported SMART's introduction in Tajik National Park.

name: State Committee for Land Management and Geodesy of the Republic of Tajikistan
summary: Tajik state committee listed in the government procurement register as a public customer, with a legal address in the I. Somoni district of Dushanbe.

name: State Institution Specially Protected Natural Areas
summary: State institution under the Committee for Environmental Protection to which Tajikistan's reserves and natural parks are subordinate, and a main partner of the RESILAND project according to CAREC.

name: Strengthening co-management in Yaghnob National Park, Tajikistan
summary: A closed CEPF-funded project run by Plateau Perspectives in the Yaghnob valley, which included camera-trap wildlife surveys and training of rangers and community members to continue long-term monitoring.

name: Striped hyena conservation in Tajikistan (NABU)
summary: Species project for the striped hyena in Tajikistan, started by NABU and a zoological conservation society after two hyenas were recorded on camera traps in spring 2024, which now gather distribution and population data in the south.

name: Supporting private sector and community conservation co-management in Baljuvan Key Biodiversity Area, Tajikistan
summary: CEPF-funded project run by the Association of Nature Conservation Organizations of Tajikistan from December 2020 to October 2022, which delivered a mapped report on urial and ibex monitoring.

name: Tajikistan Nature Foundation
summary: A Tajik national NGO and IUCN member since May 2017, which CAMCA says worked on migratory mammal conservation from 2021 to 2025 and tested thermal drone surveys in Beshai Palangon reserve.

name: Tajikistan Resilient Landscape Restoration Project
summary: World Bank-funded restoration project, 2022 to 2027, run by the Committee for Environmental Protection, using camera traps and drones against poaching and hosting the national forest inventory.

name: Zarafshan Zakaznik
summary: Tajik protected area that received eight camera traps with monitoring training in a project under the GIZ ILUCA programme, according to the Succow Foundation's 2024 report.

name: Atauro Island MPA Reef Health Monitoring
summary: Active annual reef monitoring programme in which partners collect coral and fish data for one report to the Timor-Leste government; the 2025 round ran 26 September to 2 October and showed fish abundance and biomass up on 2017 baseline data.

name: Blue Ventures Timor-Leste Reef Check monitoring programme
summary: Reef monitoring programme run by Blue Ventures, which selected six young Timorese trainees to conduct monitoring, with a survey covering seven locally managed marine areas on Atauro.

name: Building Capacity for Management and Monitoring of Timor-Leste’s Protected Areas
summary: Closed CEPF grant of $291,955, run by Conservation International Timor-Leste from May 2017 to September 2019, which led rapid biological surveys of three protected areas and prepared a management plan for Mt. Maurei.

name: Coastal Resilience Program (Timor-Leste)
summary: Programme funded by the GEF's Least Developed Countries Fund and run by UNDP, which mapped about 4,775 hectares of mangroves in 11 districts and set up monitoring systems, with a mapping lab planned for 2021.

name: Community-based Landscape Management for Enhanced Climate Resilience and Reduction of Deforestation in Critical Watersheds
summary: Green Climate Fund project, under implementation until an estimated August 2029, that promotes community-based natural resource management and, per JICA in 2024, began drone forest monitoring in 2023 and trains government GIS staff.

name: Conservation International Timor-Leste
summary: Conservation NGO, established in 2009 according to itself, which led 2017–2019 CEPF-funded surveys, planned whale tagging and signed a three-year ministry memorandum in July 2026.

name: Defining critical shark and ray habitat in Timor-Leste
summary: Active project funded by the Save Our Seas Foundation that works with local communities to catalogue sharks, rays and chimaeras, and plans a citizen science baseline and mapping of areas that may meet ISRA criteria.

name: Directorate General of Forestry, Coffee and Industrial Plants
summary: One of the agriculture ministry's four general directorates, responsible for forest protection and protected areas, named in REDD+ readiness work and with two GIS staff trained by JICA in drone operation and image analysis.

name: Enabling University Researchers to Help Protect the Coral Triangle (Laga reef baseline survey)
summary: Proposed 2026 grant-funded project to train eight university researchers in ecological surveys, aiming for one integrated baseline ecological dataset for Baucau reefs using methods including Reef Check, manta tow and BRUV.

name: Establish and Scale-up Atauro Island Marine Protected Area, Timor-Leste
summary: Closed marine protected area project on Atauro Island, run by the Coral Triangle Center with a $170,410 CEPF grant (2017 to 2019); its survey found baseline live coral cover of 55% and fish biomass of 336.8 kg per hectare.

name: Every Turtle Counts
summary: Turtle project run by Conservation International Timor-Leste, which began with interviews on the illegal turtle and egg trade in Dili's markets, plans women-led community data collection, and has begun satellite tagging of nesting turtles.

name: Forest reference level of Timor-Leste (2023 submission)
summary: Forest reference level that Timor-Leste submitted on 24 January 2023, using FAO Collect Earth activity data from 4,215 sampling points and carbon stock estimates from 36 field plots.

name: GBIF Timor-Leste
summary: Country node of GBIF with associate participant status, created in GBIF's directory in February 2024, with no publishing organisation based in Timor-Leste listed in the registry.

name: Identification of priority sites for conservation of dugongs and seagrasses in Timor-Leste
summary: Project aiming to identify priority dugong and seagrass conservation sites in Timor-Leste, under which national partners were to be trained in research techniques to fill gaps in distribution, status and ecology knowledge.

name: IkanAdapt - Securing Timor-Leste’s Fisheries for Sustainability and Ecological Resilience (JCU coastal biodiversity assessment)
summary: Planned March 2025 to March 2027 JCU work, led by Naomi Gardiner under the GEF programme IKANAdapt for WorldFish, covering a coastal biodiversity assessment and conservation plans for two to three provinces.

name: Improving Wetland Management for Biodiversity Conservation and Improved Human-Wildlife Coexistence in Timor-Leste
summary: Active wetland project run by Conservation International Timor-Leste, launched in May 2026, covering monitoring and environmental education; the country director said 35 lagoons were registered and seven chosen to start.

name: Interdisciplinary Baseline Ecosystem Assessment Surveys to Inform Ecosystem-Based Management Planning in Timor-Leste
summary: Closed NOAA assessment conducted from 2012 to 2016 in partnership with USAID to support the agriculture and fisheries ministry, using WorldView-2 habitat data, reef monitoring structures and comparable methods.

name: Konservasaun Flora no Fauna
summary: Reports its 2014 founding by UNTL Biology students in Dili, independent non-profit status, research, habitat mapping and monitoring; HOT reports seagrass mapping with local enumerators since July 2026.

name: Marine Rapid Assessment for the Manufahi and Metinaro MPA expansions
summary: Closed rapid marine assessment run by the Coral Triangle Center on 14 to 24 June 2026, to support expanding two MPAs, with one team on reef health and habitats, another on fishing and livelihoods, and over 20 km of manta-tow surveys.

name: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Forestry
summary: Government ministry whose minister co-chaired the July 2024 steering committee of the JICA landscape management project and which signed a July 2026 memorandum with Conservation International Timor-Leste on biodiversity and restoration.

name: Ministry of Tourism and Environment
summary: Government ministry that prepared the Seventh National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity, which says biodiversity monitoring remains limited, and endorsed the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2026-2030.

name: Monitoring for Seagrass (M4S) Project
summary: Active community-led seagrass mapping project in Metinaro, using drone imagery planned with HOT's DroneTM and KoboToolbox forms, and set to produce the area's first baseline seagrass data.

name: OceanX Timor-Leste expedition 2025
summary: OceanX's first Timor-Leste research mission, fourteen days along the northern coast and Atauro Island, which mapped close to 5,000 square kilometres of seabed and recorded sixty blue whale sightings.

name: Projetu Lenuk Lorosa'e
summary: Project on the long-necked turtle, a subspecies the page describes as restricted to Lake Iralalaro in Lautém District, which collected information on its biology, harvest and threats, with a Mohamed bin Zayed fund grant awarded in 2014.

name: Seagrass Ecosystem Services Project, Timor-Leste
summary: Blue Ventures project setting up community-led seagrass monitoring teams, with replication planned at Beto Tasi and Tasi Tolu, and technical reports on mapping, blue carbon and ecosystem services developed with partners.

name: Timor-Leste blue whale research and citizen science monitoring program
summary: Decade-long blue whale research and citizen science programme led by Karen Edyvane, described in RIEL's 2024 annual report as run with universities, fishing communities, government and whale tour operators.

name: Timor-Leste fire study
summary: Study in which, as FAO reported in May 2021, Timor-Leste was working with FAO to use SEPAL and Landsat 30-metre imagery from 1991 to 2020 to measure wildfire damage.

name: Timor-Leste GCF REDD+ Readiness project
summary: Readiness project whose national forest inventory design was tested in 2022, according to Timor-Leste’s 2023 submission, which reported six test plots measured and no inventory since independence.

name: Agzybir Hereket
summary: Grantee listed by CEPF as an NGO, officially an economic society, which received US$20,000 (December 2020 to December 2021) for bird monitoring in the Tallymergen-Kelif-Zeit Key Biodiversity Area, plus a further US$5,000 for equipment.

name: Amudarya State Nature Reserve
summary: Official reports describe its April 2025 reptile census, intended to feed a specialised database and yearly Chronicle of Nature, and participation in January 2022 waterfowl counts.

name: Badhyz State Nature Reserve
summary: A Turkmen state nature reserve that, per an April 2025 official item, reported at yearly hearings on 2024 results, with its leopard population described as satisfactory and females seen with two or three cubs.

name: Balkan Department of Environmental Protection
summary: Environmental protection department whose rangers, Conservation X Labs says, were trained in SMART in 2023 and given smartphones, and which uses SMART.

name: Center for Technologies of the Academy of Sciences of Turkmenistan
summary: Academy of Sciences centre whose GIS Laboratory was creating a multi-level pasture monitoring system in October 2023, using a spectral library of 27 dominant plant species.

name: Connectivity, Capacity, and Cats: Building Resiliency in the Mountain Ecosystems of Koytendag, Turkmenistan
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, April 2021 to May 2023, with a US$150,001 grant, that aimed to improve management of Koytendag State Nature Reserve by introducing SMART biological monitoring.

name: Conservation and Sustainable Management of Land Resources and High Nature Value Ecosystems in the Aral Sea Basin for Multiple Benefits
summary: UNDP-run project funded by the Global Environment Facility, ongoing until March 2028, aiming to strengthen protected area effectiveness over 1,077,554 ha in Turkmenistan's Amudarya landscape.

name: Hazar State Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve whose ornithologists joined the January 2024 Caspian wintering bird count expedition, which was to survey 33 sites under the Ramsar Convention.

name: Improving Capacity and Connectivity Between Reserves in Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project improving Koytendag and Surkhan management, with the Center for Large Landscape Conservation reporting SMART introduction in Koytendag and training for 20 more rangers in Uzbekistan.

name: Kaplankyr State Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve monitoring wildlife at night with camera traps, which a Turkmen embassy item says recorded a caracal and a sand cat; a 2024 assessment calls it Turkmenistan's largest reserve.

name: Kopetdag State Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve in the central Kopetdag Range, established in 1976 and covering 509.8 km2, where a 2024 assessment says camera traps to record manul were still being installed.

name: Koytendag State Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve where, a 2024 assessment says, camera traps routinely recorded lynx; its scientific adviser coordinated biodiversity monitoring in a CEPF project.

name: Ministry of Environmental Protection of Turkmenistan
summary: Turkmen environment ministry in which Conservation X Labs says SMART was implemented, and which worked with UNDP in 2025 on updating the national biodiversity strategy and action plan and its targets.

name: National Institute of Deserts, Flora and Fauna
summary: Research institute under the environment ministry whose studies, a 2017 article says, underpin a national concept for monitoring desertification, using remote methods, GIS and aerospace imagery.

name: Sunt-Hasardag State Nature Reserve
summary: A Turkmen state nature reserve that, per an April 2025 official item, reported a single brown bear sighting at hearings, and per Turkmenportal supplied Red Book plant and bat information for the 2025 Chronicle of Nature.

name: "Stop to non-indigenous species": community-based monitoring of non-indigenous species in the Lake of Bizerte
summary: Closed project, January 2020 to April 2023 and listed as satisfactorily completed, that aimed to set up community-based monitoring of non-indigenous species in the Lake of Bizerte, including an interactive platform.

name: Agence de Protection et d'Aménagement du Littoral
summary: Tunisian public establishment created by law in 1995 under the Ministry of the Environment and Sustainable Development, working on coastal protection and marine protected areas, and offering a geographic information system and open data inventory.

name: Agence Nationale de Protection de l'Environnement
summary: Tunisian agency that monitors climate, water levels and salinity daily at Lake Ichkeul, water quality monthly at 11 stations, and wintering waterbirds monthly from December to March.

name: Association Les Amis des Oiseaux
summary: Tunisian non-profit, described by Kapitalis as working on biodiversity monitoring and protection, which completed the International Waterbird Census count on 31 January 2022 and in late 2025 published a 2019 to 2023 report recording 105 species.

name: Association Tunisienne de la Vie Sauvage
summary: Tunisian association that set up the COBIOM project on co-management for conserving freshwater biodiversity at Oued Maden, with a 2020 to 2022 scientific report, road-death monitoring and odonate monitoring, funded by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund.

name: Association Tunisienne de Taxonomie
summary: Tunisian association (ATUTAX) that, in a CEPF-funded project from 1 December 2022 to 31 December 2023, made a first trial of Pinna nobilis larval collection with 26 collectors in Kerkennah.

name: Camera-trap monitoring in Dghoumes and Sidi Toui National Parks
summary: Run by Marwell Wildlife in partnership with the forestry directorate; Marwell reported in February 2021 a Dghoumes survey since 2018 and 26 Sidi Toui cameras monitoring oryx.

name: Centre d'alerte et de surveillance des incendies de forêt de Ghardimaou
summary: Forest fire alert and surveillance centre at Ghardimaou, reported as inaugurated on 13 October 2026, led by the forest directorate and meant to rely on the FOCUS unified fire control application.

name: Centre National de la Cartographie et de la Télédétection
summary: Tunisian public body created in 1988 under the Ministry of National Defence as the National Remote Sensing Centre, covering mapping, geodesy and remote sensing, and renamed in 2009.

name: Direction Générale des Forêts (Tunisia)
summary: Tunisian forestry directorate that in October 2025 required prior authorisation for visits to national parks and nature reserves, and says it may refuse requests by park capacity and charge entry fees.

name: Dénombrement international des oiseaux d'eau en Tunisie
summary: Annual waterbird count in Tunisian wetlands run by Les Amis des Oiseaux, which TAP reported began its 2026 count on 4 January 2026 as part of a BirdLife International action.

name: Ecology and Conservation of Three Globally Threatened Waterfowl Species Breeding in Tunisian Wetlands: The Ferruginous Duck, Marbled Teal and White-Headed Duck
summary: Closed project on three globally threatened duck species breeding in Tunisian wetlands; a May 2024 update reports 40 wetlands visited twice between April and June 2023, and a final evaluation report is dated February 2026.

name: Fakrouna
summary: System described by La Presse for tracking sea turtles' movements and behaviour with sensors, data processing and AI, reported in December 2024 to be in deployment in several Tunisian coastal regions.

name: Forfire-AI
summary: Three-year Interreg NEXT Italy-Tunisia project, running 15 May 2025 to 15 May 2028, that aims to use AI, satellite imagery, sensors and drones against Mediterranean forest fires, with first Tunisian tests planned at Dar Chichou.

name: Importance of Tunisian IBA's for Waterbirds During the Wintering Period
summary: Closed, Rufford-funded project that aimed to assess wintering waterbird population sizes in the main Tunisian Important Bird Areas and develop predictive habitat suitability models for individual species.

name: Institut National de Recherches en Génie Rural, Eaux et Forêts
summary: Research institute in Tunis created in 1996 by merging INRF and CRGR, whose forest ecology laboratory lists a forest fire history database with an interactive map among its project results.

name: Institut National des Sciences et Technologies de la Mer
summary: Marine science institute in Salammbô whose Observatoire de la Mer, created in 1992, centralises research project data in databases and builds thematic GIS map bases on aquatic environments, according to a 2004 page.

name: Institut Supérieur Agronomique de Chott-Mariem
summary: Agronomy institute named as a partner in the Forfire-AI project.

name: Interaction of Loggerhead Turtle with Gillnet Fishery in Djerba Islands
summary: Closed study estimating loggerhead turtle catch rates and mortality in Gulf of Gabes gillnet fishing, whose final evaluation report of 29 August 2023 records 20 turtles over 60 moorings in 2021 and 2022.

name: Inventaire Forestier et Pastoral National (Tunisie)
summary: National inventory meant to describe forest and pastoral resources in detail, run by the forestry directorate; its 1995 and 2010 rounds produced land cover maps, and FAO lists a support project completed in March 2024.

name: L'engagement citoyen pour la biodiversité
summary: Active project in which, La Presse reported in November 2025, Tunisian forest guards were trained in the SMART data tool, with 30 tablets handed to forest agents after field exercises in Djebel Zaghouan reserve.

name: Les Amis des Oiseaux, Section Cap Bon
summary: Non-profit bird conservation NGO created in 1993 for Cap Bon and its Important Bird Areas, which organises monitoring camps for migratory birds passing through El Haouaria, and is run by Les Amis des Oiseaux.

name: Liste rouge nationale des espèces menacées (Tunisie)
summary: National red list of threatened species, a process the Ministry of the Environment says it launched in 2019 with IUCN Med, built by the ministry, with breeding birds assessed against IUCN categories and criteria.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement (Tunisia)
summary: Tunisian environment ministry that, according to a ministry statement reported by La Presse, presented the national biodiversity strategy and action plan and its implementation at COP17 in October 2026.

name: North African Wild Traces
summary: Registered Tunisian not-for-profit, formerly ATRAkouda and founded in 2014, focused on wildlife monitoring in Bouhedma National Park since 2019, using camera trapping and a participatory observatory involving scientists, students and local communities.

name: Notre Grand Bleu
summary: Organisation whose main activities, according to the Sigrid Rausing Trust, include biodiversity research and monitoring and protected area designation and management, and which CEPF funded from December 2014 to May 2017.

name: Observatoire Tunisien de l'Environnement et du Développement Durable
summary: Permanent system for collecting, analysing and publishing information on Tunisia's environment and sustainable development, hosted by ANPE and, per the Ministry of the Environment, the national focal point for UNESCO's MAB programme.

name: Parc National de Bou Hedma
summary: National park where Marwell says scimitar-horned oryx have been re-established and reports analysing oryx population data collected by park staff in 2022.

name: Parc National de Dghoumes
summary: National park where Marwell reported in February 2021 that guards had previously received camera-trap training and a survey had run since 2018; Marwell reports oryx data analysis in 2022.

name: Parc National de Sidi Toui
summary: Described by Marwell as a 6,300-hectare protected area in south-western Tunisia within oryx range, where it reported in February 2021 that rangers were managing camera traps.

name: PENELOPE
summary: Posidonia seagrass project listed by FFEM as running from 11 March 2026 to an estimated 31 March 2029, with €2,000,000 total funding including €1,000,000 from FFEM.

name: Programme du suivi scientifique du Parc National de l'Ichkeul
summary: Monitoring programme for Ichkeul National Park, run by the national environment agency, that maps aquatic vegetation annually and produces an annual report sent periodically to UNESCO.

name: Prospection and Restoration of Barbary Deer Habitat in the Northeastern Part of Tunisia: A Tool for its Conservation and Monitoring
summary: Closed Rufford Foundation-funded project, reported for September 2015 to December 2016, that surveyed four protected areas in northern Tunisia and contributed to a basic database on Barbary deer potential habitat.

name: Robocare
summary: Company described as specialising in drones and named as one of the five partners of the Forfire-AI project.

name: Symbiose Management
summary: Tunisian deep-tech start-up that, according to Digital Africa, uses satellite images to build digital twins of forests for their management and preservation.

name: Tunisian Dolphin Project
summary: Rufford described this Rufford-funded programme in April 2022 as studying Tunisian bottlenose dolphins since 2015 using photo-identification and mark-recapture, with southern monitoring expansion planned for 2022-2023.

name: Tunisian Ornithological Association
summary: Tunisian bird organisation based in Sidi Thabet, Ariana, whose listed work includes ringing and telemetry, including a Galite archipelago mission that fitted seven Eleonora's Falcons with GPS tags.

name: TunSea
summary: Describes itself as a Tunisian marine citizen science platform, established in September 2020; La Presse reported its June 2026 appeal for turtle nesting records, photos and GPS positions.

name: École Nationale d'Ingénieurs de Sousse
summary: Engineering school that Webdo reported in June 2026 was launching a cross-border project with Sicily on forest fire prevention using AI and advanced detection technologies, and which leads Forfire-AI.

name: Department of Environment, Government of Tonga
summary: Tonga's environment department, established in 2001 according to GBIF, has published 17 datasets there and, as reported by Island Conservation, had staff help with a 2024 project and a May 2024 Late Island monitoring visit.

name: Department of Forestry (Tonga)
summary: Tongan government department that GGGI reports working with in July 2024 to prepare the National Forest Inventory, and which runs that inventory.

name: Forest invasive species mapping in Tonga
summary: Project mapping invasive species in Tonga's forests, which a FOSS4G 2025 talk says trained a Random Forest model on Sentinel-2 data, with Cordia overestimated early in Toloa Forest and detection at edges improved by a third iteration.

name: GBIF Tonga
summary: Tonga's country node in the Global Biodiversity Information Facility, listed in GBIF's directory with voting participation status.

name: Global Reef Expedition: Kingdom of Tonga
summary: A closed 2013 reef assessment in Tonga that made nearly 500 coral and reef fish surveys and collected over 2,200 km2 of satellite imagery for habitat and bathymetric maps; the foundation says reefs may have changed since.

name: Integrated Environmental Management of the Fanga'uta Lagoon Catchment
summary: A closed GEF-financed project, run by the Department of Environment of Tonga, that set up regular monitoring of Fanga'uta Lagoon, a monitoring manual and a participatory system, according to its terminal evaluation.

name: Lands Geospatial Information Services Division, Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources (Tonga)
summary: Division of Tonga's Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources that an action plan names as lead and monitoring body, with a proposal to recognise it officially as the coordination and accountability body.

name: Late Island rat removal and biodiversity monitoring
summary: Rat removal and monitoring project on Late Island, where a May 2024 point-count survey found bird numbers had doubled in nine months after rat removal.

name: Marine Ecosystem Survey Across Vavaʻu sites in Tonga
summary: Dataset of findings from a marine survey at several sites across the Vavaʻu island group, cited with Siosina Katoa and Sisilia Ulakai as authors and the Department of Environment as publisher, 2026.

name: Palm Tree Detection in Tongatapu
summary: Closed project in which, UN-SPIDER reports, FlyPix AI ran a deep-learning model on Airbus Pleiades Neo imagery to produce a palm tree inventory for Tongatapu, shared with Tonga's climate change authorities.

name: Ridge to Reef Marine Monitoring of Fanga'uta Lagoon, Tonga, October 2017
summary: Dataset of 2,304 records from October 2017 marine monitoring of Fanga'uta Lagoon, published by Tonga's Department of Environment as an outcome of a lagoon catchment management project.

name: Strengthening protected area management in the Kingdom of Tonga
summary: A closed 2019 to 2021 project, funded by the Italian Ministry of the Environment, Land and Sea, in which ENEA mapped over 998 km2 of Tongan marine coastal habitat from Copernicus satellite images.

name: Tonga benthic image source on CoralNet
summary: A public CoralNet source of 15,926 baseline benthic images from about 300 Tongan sites, collected in 2017 and 2018, with a classifier last trained on it in May 2021.

name: Tonga Community Development Trust
summary: An organisation that was the CEPF grantee for a 2009 to 2010 species recovery project, which surveyed Niuafo'ou and completed a Polynesian Megapode action plan, and later partnered with Seacology.

name: Tonga coral reef survey after the Hunga Tonga-Hunga Haʻapai eruption (2022)
summary: Closed survey of Tonga's reefs in August 2022, the first after the eruption and tsunami, which GCRMN reports found macroinvertebrate diversity down from 56 species in 2017 to 27.

name: Tonga National Forest Inventory
summary: Active programme run by the Department of Forestry, with GGGI reporting it uses 50 cm satellite imagery and AI, and a 2024 pilot tree census that identified over 2.2 million trees on Tongatapu.

name: Tonga Panama Rubber Tree Data
summary: Baseline dataset of 133 records on Panama rubber distribution, for its eradication, collected by a Department of Environment team led by Viliami Hakaumotu and published in July 2023.

name: Tonga reef fish survey data 2016-2018
summary: Dataset of coral reef ecological surveys at 375 sites in Tongatapu, Ha'apai and Vava'u from 2016 to 2018, licensed CC BY 4.0.

name: Vava'u Environmental Protection Association
summary: Incorporated society in Tonga focused on community conservation programmes, started in May 2009 by local Vava'u leaders according to the Waitt Institute, and acknowledged by GCRMN for providing reef monitoring data.

name: Vava'u marine biosecurity survey and training, November 2025
summary: Marine biosecurity survey and training in Vava'u, run by Earth Sciences NZ in November 2025, the programme's first fieldwork; 102 specimens were taken to New Zealand for analysis.

name: Vava'u Ocean Initiative
summary: Initiative whose partners signed memoranda of understanding in April 2017 to support marine resource assessment and monitoring, including a survey of nearshore coral reefs in Ha'apai and Vava'u.

name: Vava’u Turtle Monitoring Program
summary: Turtle monitoring programme in Vava'u which, in June 2014, planned a third consecutive year of monitoring outer nesting islands with Rufford support, aiming to give nesting data to national and regional bodies.

name: VEPA: Conservation Monitoring and Assessment in Tonga
summary: Project described by the Waitt Foundation as a collaboration to develop local monitoring programmes for Special Management Areas in Vava'u, involving Tonga's Ministry of Fisheries and the Vava'u association.

name: Akdeniz Koruma Derneği
summary: Association founded after a 2008 study found Gökova Bay the poorest Mediterranean area for fish; its 2024 report says AI work advanced sandbar shark monitoring, with real-time hardware planned for 2025.

name: Akdeniz University
summary: University whose research system lists a 2020 paper using deep-learning object detection to count birds of 38 species and map bird distribution and diversity across Türkiye.

name: Akdeniz'e Nefes - Kaş-Kekova Deniz Çayırları Koruma
summary: WWF-Türkiye project, run since 2021, to protect seagrass in the Kaş-Kekova marine protected area through underwater monitoring and a planned buoy system with public bodies.

name: Akustik Anadolu
summary: Acoustic monitoring project active since 2021, aiming to collect long-term ecological data, with citizen science recordings collected at 49 locations in 24 cities across six Turkish regions.

name: Akyatan sea turtle monitoring and protection
summary: WWF-Türkiye's monitoring and protection work at Akyatan since 2006, which it says helped over 250,000 green turtle hatchlings from about 6,000 nests reach the sea.

name: Altınova Belediyesi
summary: A municipality whose name is carried by the Hersek Lagoon Nature Education Centre and Accessible Bird Watching Area, at a lagoon of about 152 hectares with more than 250 bird species.

name: Andromedy
summary: Organisation combining field sensors, biological indicators and AI for ecosystem monitoring and ESG reporting, with smart hives, NDVI satellite analysis and acoustic measurement.

name: ANG Vakfı
summary: A foundation whose protocol with the Highways directorate allocated the land for the Nezahat Gökyiğit Botanic Garden, eight islands at a highway junction in Istanbul.

name: Ankara Üniversitesi
summary: University hosting TurkBOL, the Turkish Barcode of Life node of iBOL Europe, and party to a wildlife research and genetics cooperation protocol with DKMP and TÜBİTAK.

name: Aras Havzası Kuş Halkalama İstasyonu
summary: Bird ringing station run by Kafkas University; a 2015 local report marking its tenth year said ringing since 2006 had observed and ringed about 51 per cent of Türkiye's bird species.

name: Automated Bird Counting with Deep Learning for Regional Bird Distribution Mapping
summary: A 2020 paper on automated bird counting with deep learning for regional distribution mapping, with all authors listed as affiliated with Akdeniz University.

name: Avcılar Kuş Halkalama Çalışmaları
summary: Ringing work at the university's Avcılar campus where, Anadolu Agency reports, migrating birds are caught in mist nets and examined by experienced ringers licensed by DKMP.

name: Bartin University
summary: University whose Department of Forestry is listed on a 2026 paper estimating above-ground biomass in black pine forest using ALOS-1 data and machine learning.

name: Basin-scale eDNA metabarcoding survey of freshwater fishes in Türkiye
summary: Closed survey described as the first nationwide, basin-scale eDNA study of Turkish freshwater fishes, covering 29 sites in seven basins and detecting 52 species, published in 2026.

name: Başarsoft
summary: Company that says the AI-supported Forest Fires Decision Support System it developed for OGM won second prize in the e-environment category at WSIS’20, using 20 of its staff.

name: Bilgi Teknolojileri Kullanarak Marmara Denizi’ne Özgü Kirlilik Takip Sisteminin Altyapısının Oluşturulması Projesi
summary: TÜBİTAK-funded project that in November 2021 planned to use free satellite images at ITU's UHUZAM to detect mucilage and link them with Istanbul University marine measurements.

name: Bilkent Üniversitesi
summary: University collaborating with OGM on a forest fire warning system funded by TÜBİTAK ARDEB, using software from a team headed by Prof. Dr. Enis Çetin.

name: Black Sea Smart Marine Environmental Outcome System
summary: EU-supported project listed as running October 2024 to April 2027, aiming at a standardised Black Sea environmental data system and planning machine-learning forecasts.

name: Boncuk Koyu kum köpek balığı izleme
summary: Sandbar shark monitoring in Boncuk Bay, run by Akdeniz Koruma Derneği, following sharks around the clock through three cameras installed in 2021.

name: Boğaziçi Üniversitesi
summary: University whose Institute of Environmental Sciences hosts the eDNA lagoon project led by Dr. Onur Doğan.

name: Büyük Etoburların Araştırılması Projesi
summary: KuzeyDoğa's large carnivore research project, which a July 2022 report says had 45 camera traps around Sarıkamış, with data collected every six months.

name: CORINE Arazi Örtüsü Türkiye
summary: Land cover dataset for Türkiye, run by the Tarım ve Orman Bakanlığı, mapped from satellite images by computer-assisted visual interpretation for 1990, 2000, 2006, 2012 and 2018.

name: Cukurova University
summary: University with OpenAlex-listed work including a 2015 neural network paper on forest fire probability mapping and a 2022 paper on machine learning for plankton traits from images.

name: Deniz Kaplumbağaları Araştırma, Kurtarma ve Rehabilitasyon Merkezi
summary: Sea turtle research and rescue centre founded in 2009; it fitted the loggerhead Tuba with a satellite transmitter in 2019, with TUI Care Foundation support, and resumed tracking her in 2025.

name: Denizel İstilacı Yabancı Türler (MarIAS)
summary: Closed UNDP project, funded by GEF from 2018 with USD 3.3 million, to monitor and reduce marine invasive alien species along Türkiye's coast; TurIST data system launched in 2024.

name: Denizlerde Bütünleşik Kirlilik İzleme Programı
summary: Sea pollution monitoring programme run by the environment ministry and TÜBİTAK Marmara Research Center, with 425 monitoring points planned across four seas for 2023 to 2025, on a three-year cycle.

name: Didim Belediyesi
summary: A municipality that, according to its mayor, won the tender to operate Tavşanburnu Nature Park, a 147-decare coastal park it announced as open to visitors for the 2022 season.

name: Dokuz Eylül University
summary: University whose staff publication list includes a machine learning paper on EUNIS habitat maps for Europe and FloraVeg.EU, an online database of European vegetation, habitats and flora.

name: Doğa Araştırmaları Derneği
summary: Association listing a completed otter conservation and monitoring project in Muğla's special environmental protection areas and a completed Doğaya Güç Kat project, and reported as taking part in the Turkish Breeding Bird Atlas.

name: Doğa Derneği
summary: Association that says it has worked since 2002 to protect threatened species, with bird counts at 33 fixed Gediz Delta points and soaring-bird monitoring set up in 2018.

name: Doğa Kaşifi
summary: Programme built by TEMA Vakfı that lets users identify and record Istanbul's common tree and shrub species, with citizen observations meant to contribute to a species inventory, according to TEMA's chair.

name: Doğa Koruma Merkezi
summary: Organisation founded in 2004, based in Ankara, that builds Tech4Nature Türkiye, a pilot biodiversity monitoring system for Kazdağı National Park, with Huawei and IUCN as partners.

name: Doğa Koruma ve Milli Parklar 15. Bölge Müdürlüğü
summary: Regional directorate, run by the General Directorate of Nature Conservation and National Parks, which in December 2022 was reported to have recorded animals with 160 camera traps across seven provinces.

name: Doğa Koruma ve Milli Parklar Genel Müdürlüğü
summary: Directorate general that runs the national biodiversity inventory and monitoring project and the Nuhun Gemisi database; in 2022 the ministry said it monitors wildlife with about 3,180 camera traps.

name: DynaTrack
summary: Organisation in Çankaya, Ankara, that began making wildlife monitoring equipment in 2012 and since 2016 has worked only on wildlife tracking and protection equipment, including bird and mammal tracking devices.

name: Düzce Üniversitesi
summary: University listed as a GBIF publisher in Türkiye that publishes the Alien Flora of Turkey dataset, and runs a wild sheep project that qualified for TÜBİTAK 1001 support in August 2023.

name: easyPEST
summary: Project led by Giresun Valiliği to develop AI-powered, citizen-science monitoring of invasive plant pests around the Black Sea Basin, with EUR 520,308.90 budgeted from December 2025 to June 2027.

name: ecording
summary: Istanbul-based organisation developing forest restoration technology, using machine learning on seedling and ecosystem data through Nature Intelligence, analysing aerial imagery with AI and monitoring planting sites for 12–36 months.

name: eDNA lagoon project, Küçükçekmece Lagoon
summary: TÜBİTAK-funded project applying eDNA metabarcoding to biodiversity assessment, planning to sample zooplankton along the salinity gradient in the Marmara-connected part of Küçükçekmece Lagoon.

name: Erciyes University
summary: University whose research information system lists a 2022 paper comparing deep learning and machine learning to classify water areas of five Turkish wetlands from Sentinel-2 images.

name: Eskisehir Technical University
summary: University with OpenAlex-listed deep learning papers, including DiatomNet for diatom classification (2024), shoreline segmentation from Landsat 8 (2020) and beehive monitoring models (2021).

name: Eymir Kuş Halkalama İstasyonu
summary: An April 2025 report said the station had ringed over 15,000 birds of 95 species during eight years of university and DKMP cooperation, with OSME support.

name: Eğirdir ve Kovada Gölü Çevre Koruma Birliği
summary: A union that in May 2026 re-elected Eğirdir Mayor Mustafa Özer as chair, with members citing his work on natural heritage, and elected municipal officials and village heads to its posts.

name: FireAId
summary: An AI forest fire prediction model built by Koç Holding, KoçDigital and Orman Genel Müdürlüğü, reportedly analysing over 400 variables and detecting fire risk with 86% accuracy.

name: Fisheries Artificial Intelligent Lab
summary: A research group, led by Semra Benzer, that says it studies aquatic biodiversity and water quality using AI methods, with listed papers on crayfish classification, fish age classification and fish population forecasting.

name: Flora Anatolica
summary: A volunteer-managed citizen science initiative documenting Türkiye's plant diversity, which publishes a GBIF dataset of plant observations confirmed by at least two independent users.

name: ForestGuard
summary: A Turkey-based start-up, as TechCrunch describes it, with tree-trunk sensors sending data via geostationary satellites; in October 2024 its two sensor models monitored over 2 million square metres of forest.

name: Gazi University
summary: A university whose research information system has a page for the Fisheries Artificial Intelligent Lab research group.

name: Gebze Technical University
summary: A university in Gebze, Kocaeli, which OpenAlex lists with papers on ensemble learning for land cover classification and a 2024 wildfire susceptibility mapping study using XGBoost, Random Forest and AdaBoost.

name: Gezgin Portal
summary: Türkiye's first national satellite imagery portal, according to TÜBİTAK UZAY, which built it; it has served since 2014 and holds GÖKTÜRK-2 imagery and the RASAT archive.

name: Giresun Valiliği
summary: The governorship of Giresun, which leads the easyPEST project bringing together partners from Türkiye, Greece and Georgia.

name: Gözüm Doğada
summary: A species monitoring app for volunteer observers, built and run by WWF-Türkiye, released for Android and iOS, first covering vultures, dolphins, sea turtles and cranes, with a sharks module added later.

name: Hacettepe Üniversitesi
summary: A university whose affiliated authors published a 2023 neural network study of forest fire susceptibility in Türkiye and a 2021 paper using Maxent and citizen science data on Jacobin cuckoo habitat.

name: Harita Genel Müdürlüğü
summary: Türkiye's national mapping agency, per Wikipedia, under the Ministry of National Defence, responsible for official topographic mapping and for geographic information for defence and development, with two aircraft for aerial coverage.

name: Haykip
summary: A company that says it developed Türkiye's first domestic animal tracking device and makes GPS trackers and AI-supported species identification and counting programs, with bird devices of 9 to 60 grams planned.

name: Inonu University
summary: A university whose research information system lists a 2026 paper using a multilayer perceptron neural network and Markov chain simulations to evaluate land dynamics in the Amanos Mountains.

name: Integrated Approach to Management of Forests in Turkey, with Demonstration in High Conservation Value Forests in the Mediterranean Region
summary: A closed GEF-funded forest management project run by OGM and UNDP, which UNDP says ended after seven years and contributed integrated fire management software and Forest Management System software.

name: Isparta University of Applied Sciences
summary: A university whose staff publication list includes 2022 conference papers on camera trap classification and species distribution modelling, and a 2019 abstract on BİÇEB biodiversity analysis software.

name: Istanbul University
summary: University whose research information system lists the BS-SEOS project, which plans AI forecasting for Black Sea environmental data collection and sharing, and which gives a research projects coordination unit at Beyazıt.

name: Istanbul University-Cerrahpaşa
summary: University whose Faculty of Forest staff profile lists a 2022 chapter on classifying Egyptian fruit bat behaviour from calls using deep learning.

name: İstanbul Teknik Üniversitesi
summary: A university whose geomatics authors published a 2021 comparison of random forest and support vector machine land cover classification, with OpenAlex also listing a 2019 paper on watershed impermeability monitoring.

name: İTÜ Uydu Haberleşme ve Uzaktan Algılama Uygulama ve Araştırma Merkezi
summary: An ITU remote sensing centre describing Türkiye’s first satellite ground station, it imaged 2021 forest fire damage; its director estimated about 160,000 hectares burned across Türkiye that year.

name: İzmir Kuş Cenneti Koruma ve Geliştirme Birliği
summary: A union whose 2008 İzmir Bird Sanctuary protocol expired unrenewed, according to a June 2017 report that quoted then mayor Aziz Kocaoğlu putting spending at 26 million liras.

name: Kafkas Üniversitesi
summary: A university named in an AA report among teams collaborating on the Large Mammals Monitoring Project in Sarıkamış.

name: Kapadokya Alan Başkanlığı
summary: A public legal entity with a special budget tasked under Decree 38 of 2019 with protecting Cappadocia’s natural resources, geological features and immovable cultural and natural assets needing protection.

name: Karaca Arboretum Vakfı
summary: A foundation formed in 2004 for a roughly 110-decare arboretum in Yalova, which a 2022 report called Türkiye's first private arboretum, with the founder's granddaughter as board chair.

name: Karadeniz Technical University
summary: University whose research information system lists a 2026 paper comparing YOLOv8 and YOLOv10 for detecting individual trees in temperate forests from UAV RGB images.

name: Karakulak uydu takibi, Muğla
summary: Caracal tracking project in Muğla where, a February 2024 report said, Dr. Yasin İlemin fitted a satellite transmitter to a caracal for the first time in Türkiye.

name: Karataş Belediyesi
summary: A municipality whose mayor reported it operated Kumluk Nature Park under a 7 plus 22 year right from 2019 and described moves to end the contract over unpaid fees.

name: Kastamonu University
summary: University whose academic data system lists a 2018 paper using artificial neural networks and regression with Landsat 8 OLI data to predict Crimean pine stand attributes.

name: Koç Holding
summary: Conglomerate leading FireAId, whose chief executive said in January 2023 it was ready to share the forest fire prediction algorithm and source code free of charge.

name: KoçDigital
summary: Koç Group company that builds FireAId, credited by Koç Holding's chief executive with the work, carried out with the General Directorate of Forestry.

name: Kum Köpek Balığı İzleme Projesi
summary: Run by Akdeniz Koruma Derneği in Boncuk Bay, this shark monitoring project reported analysing over 6,500 hours of 2023 video and planned real-time AI hardware integration for 2025.

name: Kurt uydu takip projesi, Sarıkamış
summary: Wolf tracking part of the Sarıkamış Large Mammals Monitoring Project, using camera traps and GPS; 31 of 46 collared wolves were analysed in a Wildlife Biology paper.

name: kusatlasi.com Türkiye Kuş Gözlem Portalı
summary: Proposed Turkish bird observation portal whose preview advertises photo and sound identification and observation recording, available at launch, and whose home page showed 26,883 observation records.

name: KuzeyDoğa Derneği
summary: Kars-registered association founded in 2008 that runs and builds a large carnivore research project using camera traps and GPS collars, and uses eBird, as reported by Cumhuriyet.

name: Kuçeder
summary: Association describing a bird ringing station at Boğazkent, Serik, operating regularly since spring 2017, which Anadolu Agency named in May 2024 among Türkiye's four active ringing stations.

name: Kış Ortası Su Kuşu Sayımları
summary: Midwinter waterbird counts coordinated by Doğa Derneği during 2005–2012 and, it reported in January 2019, by the KOSKS committee, OMÜ ornithology centre and DKMP since 2013.

name: Marine Mammals Research Association
summary: Association whose 2021 report describes boat surveys and acoustic research on marine mammals, and which WWF-Türkiye says has given technical cooperation on Istanbul dolphin awareness work since 2021.

name: MARMAL Marmara Denizi İçin Yapay Zeka İle Zararlı Alg Patlamalarını Tahmin Etme ve Önleme Yaklaşımı Olarak Derin Öğrenme
summary: National project, listed for 2024 to 2026 and run by METU's Institute of Marine Sciences, on deep learning to predict and prevent harmful algal blooms in the Marmara Sea.

name: Marmara University
summary: University whose research information system lists a 2025 paper on multi-model tree detection in satellite images, naming DETR, Faster RCNN, Swin transformer and YOLO detectors.

name: Mersin Büyükşehir Belediyesi
summary: Municipality that in October 2026 reported holding its second MINKA citizen science event, under cooperation with MedCities and the ANERIS project, where participants uploaded field observations to MINKA.

name: METU Limnology Laboratory
summary: Limnology laboratory at Middle East Technical University in Ankara, listed as a TRANSPONDER partner, whose team presented findings from the ClimSaltLakes, PONDERFUL and TRANSPONDER projects in 2026.

name: Middle East Technical University
summary: University for which OpenAlex lists a 2000 paper presenting case studies on the use of neural networks in eutrophication modelling.

name: MINKA Projesi, Mersin
summary: Project launched by Mersin Metropolitan Municipality under ANERIS, within MedCities and Horizon 2020, at whose event marine and coastal species were recorded through the MINKA mobile app.

name: Muğla Sıtkı Koçman Üniversitesi
summary: University which in February 2024 reported that a faculty member, Dr Yasin İlemin, fitted a GPS collar with satellite transmission to an endangered caracal, the first time in Türkiye.

name: Nezahat Gökyiğit Botanic Garden
summary: Botanic garden in Ataşehir, Istanbul, whose herbarium holds about 20,000 specimens published through GBIF, and which runs a plant list and lists a threatened plant species platform.

name: Nuh'un Gemisi Ulusal Biyolojik Çeşitlilik Veri Tabanı
summary: Web-based national biodiversity database for Türkiye, run by DKMP, holding about 1.8 million records in 2019 and associated by TEMA with the World Bank-supported GEF II project.

name: Nuh'un Gemisi Ulusal Biyolojik Çeşitlilik Veritabanı
summary: National web biodiversity database of coordinate-based species records for Türkiye, run by DKMP and built by the agriculture and forestry ministry, where registered users can enter observations or query areas and species.

name: ODTÜ Deniz Bilimleri Enstitüsü
summary: Marine sciences institute founded in 1975, listed as coordinator of MARMOD Phase III for 2024 to 2025, and runs a deep learning project on harmful algal blooms in the Marmara.

name: ODTÜ Ekosistem Araştırma Merkezi
summary: Research centre run by METU, whose December 2025 page reported 27 years of Mogan and Eymir monitoring, with fortnightly sampling and continuous sonde data streamed over LoRa.

name: Ondokuz Mayıs University
summary: University whose staff publication list includes machine learning studies of forest fire susceptibility, including a 2024 paper on Antalya and others on Manavgat district and the Aegean region.

name: Ondokuz Mayıs Üniversitesi Ornitoloji Araştırma Merkezi
summary: University ornithology centre whose Cernek ringing station, reported in September 2026 as running since spring 2002, has ringed about 150,000 birds of about 180 species.

name: Orman Genel Müdürlüğü
summary: Türkiye’s forestry directorate handles forestry statistics, uses a fire decision support system, conducts GIS and remote sensing work, and reported camera traps across 30 regional directorates in September 2025.

name: Orman Yangınları Erken Uyarı Sistemi
summary: Forest fire early warning system developed by OGM and Bilkent University with TÜBİTAK ARDEB funding, which in 2013 was reported to detect fires within 15 to 25 seconds using 154 cameras.

name: Ormanları İzleme, Koruma ve Entegre Müdahale Projesi
summary: OGM project started in 2017 using AI-supported monitoring, with OGM reporting 3,150 camera traps active across Türkiye’s forests at the end of 2025 and 136 forest crimes detected.

name: Ormanya Kuş Halkalama İstasyonu
summary: Bird ringing station set up in Ormanya Natural Life Park, reported in May 2023 to have ringed over 100 birds of 21 species in its first week, with ringing planned across four seasons.

name: OTTOSİ
summary: High-technology firm collaborating with Oğuzlar municipality on a system combining satellite data, AI and sensors, which an İHA report said would detect forest fires early in Çorum.

name: Pamukkale Üniversitesi
summary: University that, according to Anadolu Agency, is involved with government ministries and local authorities in DEKAMER, founded in 2009, and is listed as its partner.

name: Rize Belediyesi
summary: A municipality whose 12-hectare Isırlık Nature Park project began in 2014, with ministerial designation on 2 April 2015 and a bird observation house it reports as complete.

name: Sakarya University
summary: University whose SARGEM AI laboratory carries out drone aerial imaging and builds datasets, and lists an ongoing TÜBİTAK project on deep learning monitoring of coastal pollution from drone imagery.

name: Samsun Kızılırmak Deltası Koruma ve Geliştirme Birliği
summary: A legal entity of four member municipalities that aims to protect the 56,000-hectare Kızılırmak Delta, and which the Samsun Governor's Office says received its protection and management under a 2015 protocol.

name: Sarıkaya Lynx Project
summary: Closed lynx project built by the Society for the Protection of Natural Resources and Biodiversity, reported completed by UNDP Türkiye in September 2018, whose cameras photographed poachers.

name: Segmentation, Classification, and GIS-Based Monitoring of Coastal Pollution from Drone Imagery Using Deep Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence
summary: Ongoing TÜBİTAK-funded project for October 2025 to April 2028, led by Ulaş Yurtsever, aiming to monitor coastal pollution using drone imagery, deep learning and explainable AI.

name: Society for the Protection of Natural Resources and Biodiversity
summary: Society that initiated the Sarıkaya Lynx Project in 2016 in western Antalya, which a 2018 UNDP Türkiye story says had been completed.

name: Strengthening the Conservation of Biodiversity and Sustainable Management of Forest Landscapes in Turkey’s Kazdağlari Region
summary: A GEF-funded project approved in fiscal year 2022, with a USD 4,657,534 grant, covering 184,297 hectares in Balıkesir and Çanakkale, run by forestry and nature conservation directorates and partnered with FAO.

name: Sualtı Araştırmaları Derneği-Akdeniz Foku Araştırma Grubu
summary: Mediterranean monk seal research group that monitored the İzmir, Muğla and Antalya coasts in 2019 to 2022 using cave camera traps and a sightings database, and partners with DKMP.

name: Süleyman Demirel Üniversitesi
summary: University listed in its research system as affiliated with a 2026 paper using a U-Net based deep learning model to forecast urbanisation on Istanbul's European side.

name: Tabiat Varlıklarını Koruma Genel Müdürlüğü
summary: Turkish nature conservation directorate, run by the environment, urbanisation and climate change ministry, that coordinates the scientific monitoring in Boncuk Bay, Gökova, which Akdeniz Koruma Derneği carries out.

name: Tarsus Slow Food Earth Market Association
summary: Association which, according to Türkiye Mozaik Foundation, monitored fish owl habitats across 15 Mersin valleys, confirmed five owl pairs, and is expanding habitat mapping and advocating for a species action plan.

name: Tarım ve Orman Bakanlığı
summary: Turkish ministry whose minister said in May 2026 that the nationwide biodiversity inventory was complete and still being updated, and in October 2026 that the national biodiversity strategy was being updated.

name: Tatlarin Barajı Gölü'nde Fitoplankton ve Zooplankton Çeşitliliğinin Mevsimsel Değişimi ve Su Kalitesi Parametreleri ile İlişkisi
summary: Proposed 12-month project, led by Musa Kar, that qualified for TÜBİTAK 1002-A support in October 2024 and plans to use environmental DNA sequencing to identify plankton species in a reservoir.

name: Tech4Nature Türkiye
summary: Biodiversity monitoring project built by IUCN, Huawei and Doğa Koruma Merkezi, deployed from April 2026 over 15,000 hectares, with more than 4,500 images and videos and 45 hours of recordings by September 2026.

name: Tech4Nature Türkiye, Kazdağı National Park
summary: Pilot technology-based biodiversity monitoring system for Kazdağı National Park, built by IUCN, Huawei and Doğa Koruma Merkezi, deployed from April 2026, with a press release saying it focuses on wild goats and fallow deer.

name: TEMA Vakfı
summary: Turkish foundation that, according to an AA report, has worked since its founding to protect natural assets, above all soil.

name: Trabzon Üniversitesi
summary: Turkish university listed as a Turkish partner in easyPEST.

name: TurkBOL – Turkish Barcode of Life
summary: Turkish national node of iBOL Europe, hosted by Ankara University, that carries out DNA barcoding and eDNA metabarcoding of terrestrial and aquatic species.

name: TÜBİTAK Bilişim ve Bilgi Güvenliği İleri Teknolojiler Araştırma Merkezi
summary: Information technology research centre run by TÜBİTAK, reported as collaborating with the General Directorate of Combating Desertification and Erosion on UASİS.

name: TÜBİTAK Marmara Araştırma Merkezi
summary: TÜBİTAK research centre that runs the integrated marine pollution monitoring programme, which a July 2023 report said it would coordinate with the environment ministry for 2023 to 2025.

name: TÜBİTAK Uzay Teknolojileri Araştırma Enstitüsü
summary: TÜBİTAK space technologies institute that builds the Gezgin portal and processes İMECE satellite images, with İMECE described as the first domestic observation satellite with sub-metre resolution.

name: Türk Deniz Araştırmaları Vakfı
summary: Turkish marine research foundation that, according to a July 2026 report, has monitored dolphins in the Istanbul Strait and Sea of Marmara for about 30 years, using hydrophones since 2009.

name: Türkiye Bilimsel ve Teknolojik Araştırma Kurumu
summary: Turkish research council founded in 1963 that runs TÜBİTAK Uzay and the Marmara Research Centre, funds wild sheep research and funded a forest fire warning system.

name: Türkiye Bitkileri Listesi
summary: Interactive taxonomy explorer for Türkiye's vascular plants, lichens, mosses, algae and fungi, run by Nezahat Gökyiğit Botanic Garden, with distribution maps and virtual herbarium links.

name: Türkiye Ulusal İstilacı Yabancı Türler Veri ve Bilgi Sistemi
summary: Turkish national invasive alien species database, launched in May 2024, covering 181 species, which is to receive continuous data from fishers and local NGOs.

name: Türkiye Uzay Ajansı
summary: Turkish space agency whose booklet describes the National Space Programme, and which lists LAGARİ, a micro remote sensing satellite under development with planned forest and vegetation mapping uses.

name: Türkiye'deki Bozkırlarda Anadolu Yaban Koyunu ve Ormanlarda Kızılgeyik Popülasyon Yoğunluklarının Rastgele Karşılaşma Modeli ile Tespiti
summary: TÜBİTAK-funded Düzce University project, announced in August 2023, to compare the random encounter model with line transect counts at four sites for wild sheep and red deer.

name: UAVs-FFDB
summary: High-resolution drone image dataset for forest fire detection and monitoring, presented in a 2024 dataset paper.

name: Uludağ Alan Başkanlığı
summary: A directorate that its 2025 activity report says was set up by Law 7432 and Decree 117 to plan, manage and supervise the Uludağ Area, including natural site and other protected areas.

name: Ulusal Arazi Örtüsü Sınıflandırma ve İzleme Sistemi
summary: AI-supported national land cover system built by the environment ministry, classifying Sentinel-2 images into 5 main and 79 sub-classes, with pilot basin accuracy for main classes of 71% to 95%.

name: Ulusal Halkalama Programı
summary: National bird ringing programme, run by DKMP, begun in March 2002 and reported in May 2024 to have followed 178,941 birds of about 190 species at four active stations over nine years.

name: Ulusal Sulak Alan Envanteri Yönetim Bilgi Sistemi
summary: National wetland inventory database which, according to the Doğaya Güç Kat site, records province, district, basin, type, size, registered area and protection status for Türkiye’s wetlands.

name: WWF-Türkiye
summary: Turkish organisation collaborating with DKMP on Akyatan turtle monitoring since 2006, reporting satellite tracking of adult females and about 270,000 hatchlings reaching the sea over 20 years.

name: Yangın Karar Destek Sistemi
summary: GIS and AI-based fire decision support system built by OGM and Başarsoft, operational since 2022, which the ministry said came second in an ITU competition category in 2024.

name: Yeni Bir Metodoloji Kapsamında Türkiye’deki Nesli Tehlike Altındaki Türler İçin Eylem Planlarının Hazırlanması, Uygulanması ve İzlenmesi Projesi
summary: Closed project, listed as completed, that aimed to prepare species action plans and a national species conservation strategy, and produced a database for monitoring the species with action plans.

name: Yıldız Technical University
summary: Active university whose research information system lists a 2024 conference paper on deep learning semantic segmentation of five tree species from Sentinel-2 images, in pilot regions of Türkiye.

name: Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart Üniversitesi
summary: University affiliated with a 2026 paper in the Polish Journal of Environmental Studies on forest fire susceptibility using remote sensing and machine learning.

name: Çanakkale Savaşları Gelibolu Tarihi Alan Başkanlığı
summary: A directorate set up by Law 6546 of June 2014, which ended the Gallipoli Peninsula's national park status; its history page gives the peninsula as 33,500 hectares.

name: Çankırı Karatekin Üniversitesi
summary: University whose forestry researchers are named on a 2020 deep-learning paper on tree height and diameter, and a machine learning tree species mapping study using Sentinel-2 in Bolu Aladağ.

name: Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı
summary: Ministry that partners with TÜBİTAK on an integrated marine pollution monitoring programme, with data for planned 2023–2025 work to be followed at its Ankara reference laboratory.

name: Çölleşme ve Erozyonla Mücadele Genel Müdürlüğü
summary: General directorate that started UASİS, according to a December 2023 ministry statement, because high-resolution land cover data are needed for erosion, desertification, flood and carbon emission work.

name: Asa Wright Nature Centre
summary: Nature centre that says it protects habitat, monitors key taxa to assess the impact of its management, names oilbird monitoring among its research, and says it supports other NGOs with biodiversity interests.

name: Biodiversity Conservation and Agroecological Land Restoration in Productive Landscapes of Trinidad and Tobago (BIOREACH)
summary: Four-year project on biodiversity conservation, landscape restoration and rural livelihoods, funded by the Global Environment Facility and run by the Food and Agriculture Organization and the Environmental Management Authority.

name: bp Trinidad and Tobago
summary: Company arm that bp says funded the MARIN pilot, with parent company bp reported as committing to a five-year work programme and grant funding with the IMA.

name: Buccoo Reef Trust
summary: Non-governmental organisation registered in Trinidad and Tobago, focused on marine research, education and conservation, which surveyed bleaching on Tobago's reefs after 2005 and is reported to have monitored reefs with the Tobago House of Assembly.

name: Caribbean Geospatial Observation Centre
summary: Centre at UWI St Augustine, reported in June 2025 as operational, set up with the Government of Mexico and INEGI, using the Open Data Cube platform for satellite imagery across Latin America and the Caribbean.

name: CCARO
summary: Non-profit company working on whales and dolphins in Trinidad and Tobago and the wider Caribbean, asking the public to report sightings and strandings, with boat-based surveys described for early 2010.

name: Centre for Maritime and Ocean Studies, University of Trinidad and Tobago
summary: Lead affiliation on a 2024 Caroni Swamp mangrove mapping paper and a 2025 Tobago digital twin paper; its authors also co-authored a 2025 Matura Beach thermal drone paper on sea turtles.

name: Conserving Trinidad's Ocelots: Ecological Baselines and Community Engagement
summary: Active project that plans camera-trap surveys of ocelot density, occupancy and activity at two sites, plus training workshops on camera traps and digital workflows for communities, students and volunteers; a February 2026 progress report is listed.

name: Department of Geomatics Engineering and Land Management, The University of the West Indies, St. Augustine
summary: Lead affiliation on a 2026 paper on annual remote sensing monitoring of mangrove forest dynamics in Nigeria, using Sentinel-2 and Global Mangrove Watch.

name: Department of Life Sciences, The University of the West Indies, St. Augustine
summary: Organises the Trinidad and Tobago Bioblitz with the Field Naturalists' Club, runs the UWI Zoology Museum, and is lead affiliation on a 2026 paper on passive acoustic monitoring of anurans.

name: Department of Natural Resources and the Environment, Tobago House of Assembly
summary: Tobago House of Assembly department that, according to the national biodiversity clearing-house, is primarily responsible for environmental and watershed management, forest industries, parks, protected areas and wildlife management.

name: Dolphin paTTerns Project
summary: Study of bottlenose and common dolphins in north-west Trinidad and Tobago waters, combining photo-identification, passive acoustic monitoring and fine-scale behavioural observation, with Syam Nath listed as principal investigator from 2026.

name: Environmental Management Authority
summary: Describes itself as steward of Trinidad and Tobago's natural resources and environment, and executes the BIOREACH project with NAMDEVCO.

name: Environmental Research Institute Charlotteville
summary: Not-for-profit in Charlotteville, Tobago, with monitoring programmes including Reef Check surveys and a turtle sightings database, and says it is the southern Caribbean's only Reef Check training facility.

name: Fondes Amandes Community Reforestation Project
summary: Registered Trinidad and Tobago non-profit that completed a fire observation tower at Fondes Amandes in 2024, with ReWild Watch described as community wildlife monitoring using iNaturalist.

name: Forestry Division (Trinidad and Tobago)
summary: Government sources report forest reserve, prohibited area and game sanctuary management, Ramsar and CITES technical focal point duties, and GEF project assistance with a GPS-GIS workshop for officers.

name: Green Fund
summary: Grant facility for remediation, reforestation, conservation and environmental education, described by Cari-Bois as the National Environmental Fund, first set up under the Finance Act 2000.

name: IMA Coral Reef Monitoring Programme, Tobago
summary: Run by the Institute of Marine Affairs, annual benthic monitoring of ten permanent Tobago reef sites begun at four sites in 2010; its 2010 to 2021 data are on GBIF as 2,026 records.

name: Improving Forest and Protected Area Management in Trinidad and Tobago
summary: Closed GEF-funded project run by FAO, reportedly deploying 20 cameras in Main Ridge Forest Reserve in April 2017 to estimate mammal abundance, with a monitoring programme planned.

name: Institute of Marine Affairs
summary: Publishes 15 datasets through GBIF, and built and runs a long-term Tobago coral reef monitoring programme that used CoralNet, including its deep-learning annotation, from 2019 to 2021.

name: Marine Resilience Initiative (MARIN) Tobago
summary: Pilot run by the Institute of Marine Affairs and funded by bpTT; bp says the pilot phase is complete and the project is set to enter its main phase.

name: Ministry of Planning, Economic Affairs and Development
summary: National focal point for biodiversity, TTT News reports, which is also revising the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan in line with the Global Biodiversity Framework.

name: Nature Seekers
summary: Local sea turtle conservation organisation, according to the Wildlife Society; over 52 thermal drone flights, researchers recorded and identified 394 leatherback turtles and moved rangers to high-activity areas.

name: North East Sea Turtles
summary: Sea turtle conservation group formed in 2004 and registered in 2008, patrolling throughout nesting and hatching seasons, with nesting data collection recorded in the 2016 National Monitoring Programme report.

name: Ocelot Project, Brasso Seco
summary: Closed community-based project launched in 2021 by West Indian Herping with the Environmental Management Authority, using camera traps from 10 April 2021 to 30 April 2022 to investigate wild ocelots in Brasso Seco.

name: Save Our Sea Turtles Tobago
summary: Community-based organisation formed in 2000, which in a 2018 presentation described nesting beach patrols, leatherback tagging begun in 2005 to 2007, ten years of Courland Bay monitoring by 2014 to 2017, and patrols expanded in 2011-12.

name: SpeSeas
summary: Says it advances marine conservation through scientific research, education and advocacy, with its Turtle Spotter initiative inviting the public to contribute to sea turtle monitoring.

name: The Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Network Trinidad and Tobago (BES-NET TT)
summary: Closed Trinidad and Tobago project, run by UNDP from July 2021 to March 2024, that surveyed bees, trained communities to collect field data and researched bat pollination.

name: The University of the West Indies Zoology Museum
summary: A university zoology museum that its GBIF record calls the de facto national zoology collection of Trinidad and Tobago, publishes 45 GBIF datasets, and says it mainly organises the annual Bioblitz it runs.

name: Trinidad and Tobago Bioblitz
summary: Annual species-recording event held since 2012 and run by UWI's Department of Life Sciences; the 14th, in 2025, recorded about 1,498 species using iNaturalist.

name: Trinidad and Tobago Field Naturalists' Club
summary: Partner of UWI's Department of Life Sciences on the Bioblitz for 14 years as of 2025; TTT News reports the two organised the 2026 Bioblitz.

name: Trinidad Piping-guan bioacoustic surveys
summary: BirdsCaribbean’s 2025 newsletter reports BirdsCaribbean-funded bioacoustic surveys led by Mark Hulme at the University of the West Indies, covering the Northern Range in January–June 2025, suggesting possible westward expansion.

name: Turtle Spotter
summary: Public sightings initiative run by SpeSeas, funded by the Specially Protected Areas Regional Activity Centre, collecting photographs, videos and dive logs to show how sea turtles use habitat.

name: Turtle Village Trust
summary: Non-profit formed in 2006 for Trinidad and Tobago turtle conservation; its 2016 report records seventeen organisations contracted for monitoring in 2013 and offshore telemetry monitoring launched in November 2015.

name: Department of Environment (Tuvalu)
