summary: Tuvalu government environment department, listed by the CBD as a national focal point and registered as a GBIF data publisher, which Island Conservation reports implemented the Predator Free Pacific programme there in 2024.

name: Implementing a Ridge to Reef Approach to Protect Biodiversity and Ecosystem Functions in Tuvalu
summary: Closed biodiversity project run by the Department of Environment, funded by the GEF (grant of 3,762,844 US dollars) and UNDP, which aimed to build a centralised GIS database and improve natural resource data.

name: Ministry of Home Affairs, Climate Change and Environment
summary: Tuvalu government ministry whose Permanent Secretary the CBD lists as a primary national focal point for Tuvalu.

name: National Geographic Pristine Seas Tuvalu expedition
summary: Marine survey led by National Geographic Pristine Seas, reported by PMN as Tuvalu's first full marine survey, finished in 2025 and using baited video, eDNA sampling and a submersible.

name: Niulakita Island restoration project
summary: Ongoing restoration project on Niulakita led by the Department of Environment with Island Conservation, whose teams arrived in March 2026 and, as reported in April 2026, were collecting baseline environmental data.

name: Tuvalu Department of Lands and Survey
summary: Tuvalu government mapping body that partners with the Pacific Community; in 2024 its Director said the partnership helped move the office towards a digital twin, and nearly 40 ground control points were set.

name: 5G AI ecological soundscape collector
summary: Soundscape recording device built by the Biodiversity Research Center, Academia Sinica, which TechBang reports was developed with Far EasTone; field validation found AI analysis identified 369 bird and frog species with over 90% accuracy.

name: Academia Sinica
summary: Independent research organisation under its Organization Act that built the Biodiversity Research Center and, in March 2008, established GBIF-ROC to promote inter-ministerial meetings on biodiversity information.

name: Acoustic detections of birds using the SILIC in Yushan National Park, Taiwan
summary: Dataset of bird acoustic detections from six passive monitoring stations in southern Yushan National Park, built on SILIC, holding 802,670 records after summarising detections per sound class per recording.

name: Aerial Survey and Remote Sensing Branch
summary: Branch run by the Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency that acquires nationwide aerial imagery, builds frequently updated geospatial datasets, and interprets imagery to identify forest types and assess landslide, fire and pest damage.

name: Biodiversity Research Center, Academia Sinica
summary: Taiwanese centre that announced a May 2025 ReefCloud workshop on coral reef monitoring; TechBang reports an Academia Sinica team analyses bird and frog calls across Taiwan.

name: Chinese Wild Bird Federation
summary: Incorporated association that launched the Taiwan New Year Bird Count and, according to an agency report, mainly coordinated Taiwan's survey work for the January 2025 Black-faced Spoonbill census.

name: Department of Systems Engineering and Naval Architecture, National Taiwan Ocean University
summary: Department at National Taiwan Ocean University in Keelung, the affiliation of the first and corresponding author of a 2025 paper on forecasting marine soundscapes with deep learning.

name: FANCA long-term wildlife camera monitoring in national forests
summary: Infrared camera monitoring in Taiwan's national forests, run by the Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency, with 387 long-term points reported in May 2024 and a stated plan to greatly increase coverage.

name: Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency
summary: Agency of Taiwan's Ministry of Agriculture that has set up automatic cameras for long-term wildlife monitoring in national forests and runs the FANCA camera monitoring programme.

name: Kuroshio Ocean Education Foundation
summary: Taiwanese marine non-profit, described in its GBIF record as founded in 1998, which has run Risso's dolphin photo-identification research and, per a 2016 report, kept volunteer cetacean sighting records since 1998.

name: National Academy of Marine Research
summary: Institute founded on 24 April 2019 under the Ocean Affairs Council; a January 2024 report said it had collected marine environmental DNA data from more than 100 stations.

name: Ocean Conservation Administration
summary: Kaohsiung-based agency of the Ocean Affairs Council; a 2022 report said its coral monitoring survey programme, commissioned from the Pingtung marine biology museum, monitored 60 points around Taiwan.

name: Ocean Data Bank
summary: Programme of the National Science and Technology Council which, its August 2023 newsletter said, was building a marine microbial gene database from published Taiwanese eDNA barcode sequence data.

name: SILIC (Sound Identification and Labeling Intelligence for Creatures)
summary: Sound identification model using Python and the yolov5 package for object detection on sounds; the March 2025 release covers 390 sound classes of 272 species, built by the Taiwan Biodiversity Research Institute.

name: Systematics and Biodiversity Informatics Center (Academia Sinica)
summary: Academia Sinica centre established in 2004 and commissioned by the Ministry of Science and Technology to operate TaiBIF.

name: TaiBON
summary: Four-year project planned for 2015 to 2018, funded by the Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency, whose November 2016 report lists completing the TaiBON national biodiversity monitoring and reporting platform among its results.

name: Taiwan Biodiversity Information Facility
summary: Chinese Taipei's associate participant node in GBIF, run by the Systematics and Biodiversity Informatics Center, providing biodiversity open data search and download, teaching materials and data tools.

name: Taiwan Biodiversity Research Institute
summary: Government institute renamed from the Taiwan Endemic Species Research Institute in August 2023, which describes itself as contributing to national conservation strategy and builds the SILIC sound identification model.

name: Taiwan Breeding Bird Survey
summary: National monitoring project established in 2009 as citizen science to build a breeding bird population index, with 822,365 records from 638 sampling sites across breeding seasons 2009 to 2022.

name: Taiwan Marine Microbial Barcode and Metagenome Database
summary: Web database of marine microbial metagenome data for Taiwan and surrounding seas, built and run by the Ocean Data Bank, with eDNA, eRNA and RNA sequencing data listed as targets in a May 2026 newsletter.

name: Taiwan New Year Bird Count
summary: Citizen science project monitoring wintering birds in Taiwan and surrounding islands since 2014; its 2022 report, the ninth, records 1,032 participants counting 368,724 birds of 325 species in 172 circles.

name: Taiwan Roadkill Observation Network
summary: Citizen science project begun in August 2011 and run by the Taiwan Biodiversity Research Institute; a 2018 abstract reported 3,450 contributors, 551 species and 63,227 observations over six years.

name: The Taiwan Roadkill Observation Network Data Set
summary: Dataset of 46,416 georeferenced roadkill occurrences from 2011 to December 2017, collected by TaiRON citizen scientists, with each record having at least one photo checked by managers and experts.

name: Wild Bird Society of Taipei
summary: Founded in 1973, this incorporated association's 2025 project targeted barn swallow mapping and a monitoring database; it co-organised Taiwan New Year Bird Count according to a 2017 report.

name: Yushan National Park Headquarters
summary: Park authority partnered with the Taiwan Biodiversity Research Institute's predecessor ESRI on a passive acoustic monitoring system built in 2020.

name: 中華民國荒野保護協會
summary: Incorporated association founded on 25 June 1995, whose 2025 report describes camera-trap monitoring, a planned Black-faced Spoonbill monitoring effort at Cigu, and nine boat-based white dolphin observations by its Yunlin branch.

name: 國立屏東科技大學野生動物保育研究所
summary: Executing unit of a 2025 report on black kite population monitoring in Taiwan, which says 55 birds were satellite-tracked effectively from 2016 to 2025.

name: 2024/2025 National Wildlife Census (Tanzania)
summary: Closed nationwide census, conducted between September 2024 and October 2025, whose report Daily News says the President received from the Ministry through TAWIRI; held every ten years, per the minister.

name: A Forest Monitoring System for Tanzania
summary: 2021 Remote Sensing paper on forest monitoring in Tanzania, recorded in OpenAlex with keywords including Landsat 8, XGBoost and forest loss, with Elikana John as lead author.

name: Abundance, Distribution and Conservation of Gerenuk (Litocranius walleri) Around Lake Natron Ecosystem
summary: A closed, Rufford Foundation-funded project that aimed to estimate gerenuk population size and structure around Lake Natron, and assess twenty years of habitat trend and what determines distribution.

name: AI-assisted Aerial Imagery Analysis
summary: A workflow built by Development Seed and the Tanzania Wildlife Research Institute, which Development Seed says uses an image classifier and three object detection models to count wildlife, livestock and human activity.

name: Ardhi University
summary: A university whose Department of Geospatial Sciences and Technology is the stated affiliation of the first author of a 2018 paper assessing supervised classifiers for land cover mapping from ALOS PALSAR and Landsat data.

name: Assessing Population Ecology Data and Threats of Abbott's Duiker Using Camera-Trap Survey in Uzungwa-Scarp Forest Reserve
summary: A closed project that planned to monitor Abbott's duiker population and distribution by camera trap and map forest cover change from 2010 to 2019 with satellite imagery; camera traps were set September to November 2021.

name: Behavioral, Ecological and Conservation Studies of Chimpanzees and Other Larger Mammals in the Greater Mahale Area
summary: Closed project, running from 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2026, that aimed to continue long-term ecosystem studies around Mahale chimpanzees using camera traps, DNA samples and line-transect surveys.

name: Blue Alliance PECCA
summary: An organisation that the UN MPTF Office says manages the North Pemba Channel Conservation Area, about 27,000 hectares of reef, mangrove and seagrass, where rangers monitor crown-of-thorns starfish and protect turtle nests.

name: College of African Wildlife Management, Mweka
summary: Wildlife management college that was a grantee of the JRS Biodiversity Foundation's 2017 to 2020 pollinator monitoring project in Tanzania, for which JRS reported 1,252 bee specimens of 135 species.

name: College of Forestry, Wildlife and Tourism, Sokoine University of Agriculture
summary: College at Sokoine University of Agriculture in Morogoro, listed as an affiliation on a 2024 paper on classifying land use and cover of large conservation areas using a drone.

name: Conservation of Large Carnivore Biodiversity in the Masai Steppe, Northern Tanzania
summary: A closed project that set out to train village game scouts and rangers in carnivore monitoring and to determine large carnivore distribution to identify priority conservation areas.

name: Conservation of Striped Hyaena through Improved Livestock Enclosures and Education Program in Maasai Steppe, Tanzania
summary: A project, with unknown status, that planned to use camera traps and participatory rural appraisal to assess striped hyaena distribution across the Maasai Steppe in northern Tanzania.

name: Dar es Salaam Institute of Technology
summary: Institution that received a $240,000 JRS Biodiversity Foundation grant for 2019 to 2022 to develop a national biodiversity data portal.

name: Eastern Arc Mountains Conservation Endowment Fund
summary: A fund reporting approval of Tsh 957 million for 56 projects from 167 proposals in 2024/2025, and Tsh 146 million for five biodiversity and climate change research projects.

name: Ecology and Role of Land Use on Abundance, Diversity and Distribution of Small Mammalian Carnivores in Ruaha Ecosystems, Tanzania
summary: A closed project that planned to study small carnivores' activity, habitat use and threats in the Ruaha ecosystem, with cameras fixed to trees 1 km apart for 30 consecutive nights.

name: Establishing Metadata of Biodiversity Data Generated from Ramsar Sites in Tanzania
summary: A project that ran from October 2017 to March 2019 to inventory scattered Ramsar wetland biodiversity data and publish it to GBIF, including 8,463 bird records for Kilombero Valley Floodplains.

name: Estimating the Current Population, Map the Habitats and Raise Community Awareness on the Rungwecebus Kipunji in the Region
summary: A closed project that planned to estimate the kipunji population with camera traps, indices and transects, show 40 years of land cover change, and train conservation staff for long-term monitoring.

name: Gombe Stream Research Center
summary: A Jane Goodall Institute research programme using camera traps, bioacoustics and GIS, citing its 2024 report for over 165,000 observation hours on more than 320 chimpanzees.

name: Grumeti Fund
summary: A non-profit working with Tanzania’s government in the western Serengeti, reporting two aerial surveys, 30 elephants tracked with GPS collars and EarthRanger adoption in 2017.

name: Honeyguide Foundation
summary: An organisation that Sensing Clues says it trained on its Cluey data collection app and Focus 360 situational awareness tools.

name: Human Impact on Elephant Habitat and Movement Patterns in Kitendeni Wildlife Corridor, Tanzania
summary: A closed project that planned to combine camera traps, aerial survey data and remote sensing habitat assessment to map land use and cover against recorded human-elephant conflicts in the Kitendeni corridor.

name: Institute of Marine Sciences, University of Dar es Salaam
summary: A University of Dar es Salaam institute established in 1978 for marine research, training and consultancy, which says it is Tanzania's National Oceanographic Data Centre.

name: International Waterbird Census in Tanzania
summary: Active waterbird count run by TAWIRI for the Ministry of Natural Resources and Tourism, with Nature Tanzania as partner; its January 2023 census aimed to gather numbers at accessible wetlands.

name: Kingupira Wildlife Research Centre
summary: Research centre run by TAWIRI, established in 1969 as the Miombo Research Centre, whose listed functions include monitoring trends in wildlife populations and ecological processes.

name: KopeLion
summary: Not-for-profit with US and Tanzanian registration that employs local warriors, many of them former lion killers, in lion monitoring; it reports an average 12% yearly rise in lion observations since 2017.

name: Large carnivore research and monitoring in Selous-Nyerere and Ruaha-Rungwa
summary: Large carnivore project in Selous-Nyerere and Ruaha-Rungwa: surveys in 2020 to 2022, lion and wild dog collars in 2023 and 2024, and a 2025 plan for conflict data.

name: Maasai Steppe Carnivore Conservation Trust
summary: An Arusha-based trust that says it carries out long-term lion research and monitoring under the Tarangire Lion Project, providing data on mortality, recruitment, feeding and prey preferences.

name: Mazingira Alliance for Community and Conservation
summary: A Tanzanian conservation NGO, renamed from Associazione Mazingira NGO, that runs the Udzungwa Ecological Monitoring Centre and reports 10,487 km of primate census and 44,205 camera trap images for 2025.

name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Tourism
summary: The Tanzanian ministry responsible for managing natural and cultural resources and developing tourism, whose announcement of the national wildlife census results launch appears on TAWIRI's site.

name: Monitoring the Sokoke Scops Owl and Usambara Eagle Owl Population, and Awareness Raising in the East Usambara Mountains
summary: Closed project that aimed to produce baseline population and distribution data on two owls in Amani Nature Reserve, with an August 2024 update reporting the first recorded Usambara eagle owl nesting site.

name: Mwambao Coastal Community Network
summary: A coastal network training community catch monitors and biodiversity teams, conducting snorkel reef surveys using four methods, with 46 staff in four teams in 2023.

name: National Carbon Monitoring Centre
summary: A centre launched at Sokoine University of Agriculture in January 2016, which SUA says will manage the national system for measuring, reporting and verifying forest carbon.

name: National Forest Resources Monitoring and Assessment of Tanzania Mainland
summary: Tanzania's first comprehensive national forest inventory according to FAO, with a second round planned in 2022 to measure change, and used by TAFORI to monitor its permanent sample plots.

name: National Wildlife Research Information System
summary: Research information system whose guidelines cover submitting research applications, requesting datasets, taking part in conferences and uploading field data; biological or data samples can also be requested from it.

name: Nature Tanzania
summary: Membership conservation NGO in Tanzania that uses birds as indicators of ecosystem health, monitors Key Biodiversity Areas, and describes itself as a BirdLife International partner.

name: Nelson Mandela African Institution of Science and Technology
summary: An Arusha institution that is the stated affiliation of the first author of a 2024 paper on deep learning forest-fire prediction at Mount Kilimanjaro using satellite, weather and human activity data.

name: Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority
summary: A Tanzanian government wildlife management body for the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, whose research page lists lion research and cheetah monitoring that identifies individuals from photographs.

name: Ngorongoro Lion Monitoring Program
summary: Programme run by KopeLion that individually identifies and monitors lions in the conservation area, with GPS collars on a few; zoo scientists are helping move its data into PopLink.

name: Panthera Tanzania
summary: Programme of Panthera, which says it set up a Tanzanian country office in 2025, using SMART for patrol tracking and holding a July 2025 agreement with TAWA covering monitoring in two game reserves.

name: Pollinator Monitoring Project in Tanzania
summary: Closed JRS-funded project, 2017 to 2020 with $284,400, to set up standardised bee monitoring starting in Arusha Region; JRS reported 1,252 specimens of 135 species from 37 landscapes.

name: Rada 360
summary: An organisation whose Rada Agriculture and Rada Forest platforms, according to Climate Policy Initiative's CLIC profile, use satellite imagery and AI for agricultural and forest monitoring and deforestation tracking.

name: Rada Forest
summary: A forest intelligence and ecosystem monitoring programme run by Rada 360, described as using high-resolution satellite data and machine learning, with forest mapping and deforestation detection among its services.

name: Research & Innovation for the Serengeti Ecosystem
summary: Applied research and capacity building facility run by the Grumeti Fund, supporting graduate students, researchers and conservationists since 2019, with programmes including camera trap data analysis and environmental DNA.

name: Sea Sense
summary: Non-governmental organisation working with Tanzanian coastal communities to conserve endangered marine wildlife, which has recruited and trained over 60 Conservation Officers in coastal villages.

name: Serengeti Cheetah Project
summary: Programme monitoring the Serengeti cheetah population through staff fieldwork and visitor citizen science, with monthly surveys, photo identification by spot patterns and scat samples for genetic diversity.

name: Serengeti Wildlife Research Centre
summary: Centre at Seronera, run by the Tanzania Wildlife Research Institute, responsible for wildlife research in Serengeti National Park and surrounding protected areas, with projects on elephant GPS tracking.

name: Sokoine University of Agriculture
summary: A public university in Morogoro listing the National Carbon Monitoring Centre, with an affiliated first author of a 2025 paper comparing machine learning models for drone-derived miombo biomass estimates.

name: Southern Highlands Wildlife Research Centre
summary: Research centre run by TAWIRI, established in 2024 in Iringa Region, that implements Kihansi spray toad monitoring, with 700 toads released into the Upper Kihansi wetlands and 100 into Lululutonya in trials.

name: Southern Tanzania Elephant Program
summary: Tanzanian non-profit founded in 2014 working in the Udzungwa and Ruaha-Rungwa landscapes, reporting 70,000 km of foot patrols and 1,425 hours of aerial support in Ruaha-Rungwa.

name: Surveys and Mapping Division, Ministry of Lands, Tanzania
summary: Division of the Ministry of Lands and Human Settlements Development that the UN SALB programme lists as Tanzania's national geospatial information authority.

name: Tackling Deforestation in Tanzania with AI: A Pilot Project Focused on Mangroves
summary: A completed Omdena pilot project whose stated goal was an AI-based system for real-time deforestation monitoring in mangrove ecosystems.

name: Tanzania Biodiversity Information Facility
summary: Consortium of universities, research institutions and NGOs, set up in 2007, hosted by COSTECH, acting as Tanzania's GBIF node with associate status and 23 published datasets.

name: Tanzania Biodiversity Information Management Tool
summary: Online biodiversity tool built by COSTECH with JRS funding, which JRS says held plant information only before about 150,000 animal records were uploaded under a 2014 grant.

name: Tanzania Bird Atlas
summary: Bird atlas data for Tanzania, which Neil Baker wrote in 2019 had been collected with Liz Baker since 1980, used for maps showing record numbers per species.

name: Tanzania Commission for Science and Technology
summary: Parastatal established by Act of Parliament in 1986, according to JRS, which hosts and coordinates TanBIF and received JRS funding for a 2014 grant.

name: Tanzania Fisheries Research Institute
summary: Public institution under the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries, set up in 1980, which says its research vessels support hydroacoustic fish biomass estimates on Lake Victoria and biodiversity monitoring on Lake Tanganyika.

name: Tanzania Flying Labs
summary: A group describing itself as entirely Tanzanian-led in July 2018, reporting five-day drone training for Community Forests Pemba and drone data use for land rights mapping and marine assessments.

name: Tanzania Forest Conservation Group
summary: An NGO established in 1985, reporting research on Eastern Arc and coastal forests, with surveys it joined finding at least 10 new vertebrate and two new plant species.

name: Tanzania Forest Services Agency
summary: Semi-autonomous government executive agency for forest and bee resources, which Daily News reported in March 2026 had stepped up its use of satellites and drones for forest patrols.

name: Tanzania Forestry Research Institute
summary: Research institute established by Act No. 5 of 1980, whose forest resource assessment programme monitors NAFORMA permanent sample plots to estimate forest cover, stocking and yield for management and carbon accounting.

name: Tanzania National Biodiversity Data Portal
summary: National biodiversity data portal built by the Dar es Salaam Institute of Technology on Atlas of Living Australia technologies, with a $240,000 JRS grant for 2019 to 2022.

name: Tanzania National Parks
summary: Conservation and wildlife management authority which Esri's 2021 blog said managed 22 national parks, had a GIS unit established in 2012, and had configured Survey123 forms for ecological monitoring.

name: Tanzania Wildlife Management Authority
summary: Authority set up by ministerial order in 2014 to conserve and sustainably use wildlife resources in protected areas, which provided aircraft and staff for a 2022 aerial census.

name: Tanzania Wildlife Research Institute
summary: Established in 1980 to conduct, coordinate and oversee wildlife research, it publishes aerial survey reports and, Development Seed says, collaborated on AI-assisted counting after aerial surveys.

name: Tanzanian Elephant Foundation
summary: A Tanzania-based association which Play for Nature describes as protecting African savanna elephants and studying their ecology with camera traps, GPS collars and participatory science.

name: Tarangire Lion Project
summary: A programme run by the Maasai Steppe Carnivore Conservation Trust, whose long-term research and monitoring names the African lion as its primary species.

name: The University of Dodoma
summary: University whose affiliated first author, Cesilia Mambile, published a 2026 paper assessing how well deep learning suits forest fire prediction in Tanzania.

name: Udzungwa Ecological Monitoring Centre
summary: Field station run by MACCO and built by MUSE with TANAPA in 2006, supporting ecological monitoring through a laboratory whose inauguration dates are reported inconsistently.

name: United Republic of Tanzania Convention on Biological Diversity Clearing House Mechanism
summary: Tanzania's national Convention on Biological Diversity clearing-house mechanism, publishing national biodiversity targets to 2030 and linking to a biodiversity indicators summary and a red list.

name: University of Dar es Salaam
summary: University whose affiliated first author, Khadija Mahanga, published a 2026 paper combining Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data with machine learning to estimate aboveground forest carbon stock.

name: Vice President's Office (Union and Environment), Tanzania
summary: Government office whose Minister of State presented the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan, covering 2025 to 2030, to a parliamentary committee in August 2026.

name: WASIMA
summary: Formed in 2011 and initially registered as Landscape and Conservation Mentors Organisation, it monitors wildlife with camera traps in community-based wildlife management areas and works with Honeyguide Foundation.

name: WCS Tanzania
summary: A programme run by the Wildlife Conservation Society that uses the SMART tool, supports law enforcement monitoring in Ruaha-Katavi, and says wild dog surveys begun in 2021 continue.

name: Western Wildlife Research Centre
summary: Research centre run by TAWIRI on the Lake Tanganyika shore at Kigoma-Ujiji, established in 1975 as a chimpanzee station and merged into its current form in 2023, with waterbird and chimpanzee monitoring projects.

name: AnuraSearch
summary: Model used by BioMon to detect amphibians in sound recordings, alongside the BirdNET 2.4 network for birds.

name: Automated System "Pozhezhi" (Fires)
summary: Automated fire detection system that LIAC keeps improving, finding temperature anomalies in real time using NASA satellite data and the State Space Agency of Ukraine's national observation system.

name: Azov-Black Sea Ornithological Station
summary: Interdepartmental ornithological station set up in 1985 at two Ukrainian academic institutions, coordinating regional bird monitoring and publishing field observation datasets through GBIF.

name: Azovo-Syvaskyi National Nature Park
summary: The territory of this national nature park, created by presidential decree No. 62 of 25 February 1993, is listed as a Ramsar wetland of international importance.

name: Beremytske Biodiversity Foundation
summary: Foundation that bought and leased private land for the Beremytske rewilding project, moving eight Konik horses there in 2016 with ARK's help; ARK reports 400 hectares and about 20 horses.

name: BioMon
summary: Project developing a semi-automatic, public biodiversity monitoring system for Ukrainian protected areas, using Deepfaune and BirdNET neural networks and funded by the German Federal Environmental Foundation (DBU).

name: Bird monitoring in western and southern Ukraine (PECBMS scheme)
summary: Ukraine's bird monitoring scheme in the PECBMS network, which PECBMS lists as ongoing since 1980 with 20 fieldworkers and 70 species, run by three Ukrainian bird organisations.

name: Black Sea Biosphere Reserve of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine
summary: Nature reserve covering 109,254.8 hectares on the Kherson and Mykolaiv coast, monitoring since 1953 and publishing bird and jerboa burrow datasets, whose website reports staff continue working despite war.

name: Boikivshchyna National Nature Park
summary: National nature park created in 2019 that collected lynx data with 11 camera traps from 2021 to 2025 and, from 2023, winter track counts.

name: Carpathian Biosphere Reserve
summary: Biosphere reserve of 66,417.4 hectares in the Ukrainian Carpathians, descended from a 1968 state reserve, whose 20,980.5 hectares of beech forest were added to the UNESCO World Natural Heritage list in 2007.

name: Carpathian National Nature Park
summary: National nature park whose staff installed 20 camera traps, after building a GIS project and monitoring grid in winter 2021-2022, to map wolf, bear and lynx distribution.

name: Cheremoskyi National Nature Park
summary: National nature park of 7,117.5 hectares that has run SMART monitoring since September 2022 with Frankfurt Zoological Society support and combined several methods for lynx monitoring from 2012 to 2025.

name: Chornobyl Radiation and Ecological Biosphere Reserve
summary: Reserve monitoring wildlife with camera traps and publishing carnivore, ungulate, bird, reptile and amphibian records to GBIF, whose staff wrote a 2024 paper on geospatial monitoring tools.

name: ClearCut
summary: Deforestation monitoring programme that Quantum says it developed with SCGIS, using computer vision on satellite images processed every five days, first implemented in the Kharkiv region according to Quantum's 2020 report.

name: Conservation of Natural Heritage for LIFE in Ukraine
summary: Project co-financed by the EU and the Czech Ministry of the Environment, with a EUR 1,088,512.07 budget, whose February 2026 deliverable sets guidelines for biodiversity monitoring, mapping and data management.

name: COOP4SAFE early-warning system for human-wildlife coexistence
summary: Planned early-warning system built around Cluey, designed to alert intervention units when camera traps detect bears near homes and to use AI to predict where conflicts may occur.

name: Danube Biosphere Reserve
summary: This 50,252.9-hectare biosphere reserve was created by presidential decree on 10 August 1998 from the Danube Wetlands reserve, in the Danube Delta, a Ramsar wetland designated mainly for waterbirds.

name: Deep Green Ukraine
summary: Closed illegal logging project, dated 2020–2021 or August 2020–March 2022, comparing satellite changes with public data, whose co-founder reported training a neural network on radar and optical imagery.

name: Department of Mathematical Modelling and Data Analysis, Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute
summary: University department at Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute planning machine learning applications for satellite forest monitoring within FutureFOR and listing a land cover change digital twin project.

name: Dnister Regional Landscape Park named after Serhiy Didych
summary: The regional landscape park is managed by the directorate of the Ivano-Frankivsk oblast council’s communal enterprise of the same name, which serves as the park’s special administration.

name: Dnistrovskyi Kanyon National Nature Park
summary: National nature park created by presidential decree No. 96 of 3 February 2010, which the Dniester basin water authority's page says includes 11,730.28 hectares.

name: DroneUA
summary: Organisation whose August 2016 blog describes a Zemli.online-based system identifying mass deforestation within 24 hours of receiving satellite or drone data, tested over 3,284 hectares in Kyiv region.

name: EcoSystem unified environmental platform
summary: National automated environmental information and analysis system, launched in test mode in May 2021, integrated with Diia and holding 66 open environmental data registers by October 2021.

name: EcoZagroza
summary: Ministry web resource and mobile app giving information on air, water, soil and other environmental data, which in 2023 published official information on the Kakhovka dam breach's consequences.

name: Falz-Fein Biosphere Reserve "Askania Nova"
summary: Research and conservation reserve managing Ukraine's largest remaining unploughed steppe, whose main territory its GBIF record says has been under Russian occupation since 2023, while steppe research continues.

name: Fixation of damage caused to natural complexes of the Kharkiv region as a result of the war
summary: SCGIS Ukraine reports its closed project ran from December 2022 to December 2023, mapping Kharkiv war damage through Sentinel-2 and Planet images and recording over 61,000 craters.

name: Forest Initiatives and Communities
summary: Organisation founded in February 2020 with forest monitoring experts, publishing satellite monitoring of Carpathian primeval forests and running near real-time forest cover monitoring, including with drones.

name: Frankfurt Zoological Society biodiversity monitoring in Ukraine
summary: Frankfurt Zoological Society programme running biodiversity monitoring with 13 protected areas in Ukraine, using SMART since February 2021, camera traps and acoustic receivers, and supporting Chornobyl Biosphere Reserve.

name: Frankfurt Zoological Society Ukraine
summary: Ukrainian team of Frankfurt Zoological Society, working since 2001, reporting efforts to strengthen 21 protected areas, with SMART on over 350 smartphones, camera traps and acoustic monitoring.

name: Frankfurt Zoological Society Ukraine programme
summary: Programme described as FZS’s largest in Europe, reporting work strengthening 21 Polissia and Carpathian protected areas, using SMART on over 350 smartphones, camera traps and acoustic receivers.

name: FrogNET
summary: Acoustic classifier adapted from BirdNET by transfer learning for 11 Eastern European frog and toad species, published with a dataset of 15,213 segmented audio clips from a Ukrainian study.

name: From war to nature: engaging internally displaced people and local residents in environmental monitoring in Roztochya region
summary: Planned 24-month project involving displaced people and local residents in biodiversity and environmental monitoring, including installing monitoring equipment, funded by Finland’s foreign ministry.

name: FutureFOR
summary: Horizon Europe project to create satellite monitoring tools supporting EU legislation, with an inaugural meeting in Prague and three Ukrainian institutions starting to take part.

name: FZS Ukraine biodiversity monitoring in Carpathian and Polissia protected areas
summary: FZS Ukraine project that reports SMART adoption by specialists in 14 partner protected areas and two parks, with acoustic monitoring across Polissia and camera traps in Chornobylskyi Biosphere Reserve.

name: GBIF Ukraine
summary: Country node for Ukraine with associate participation in GBIF’s Europe region and Oleksii Marushchak as node manager, with GBIF’s registry listing 42 Ukraine-based publishing organisations.

name: Gorgany Nature Reserve
summary: A paper reviews brown bear monitoring in this strict reserve during 2004–2024, with snow-track counts and ten camera traps used since 2022 and records logged in SMART.

name: Halych National Nature Park
summary: National nature park created by presidential decree on 9 August 2004 to conserve, restore and support responsible use of natural complexes and sites in the Precarpathian region and Opillia.

name: Holosiivskyi National Nature Park
summary: National nature park in Kyiv's Holosiivskyi district, created by presidential decree No. 794 of 27 August 2007, with a total area of 10,988.14 hectares, of which 1,888.18 are in permanent use.

name: Hutsulshchyna National Nature Park
summary: National nature park where, according to a 2022 conference paper, SMART is used mainly by protection, research and recreation staff, with biodiversity monitoring as its first stage.

name: I. I. Schmalhausen Institute of Zoology
summary: Ukrainian zoology institute that describes itself as the principal organisation for its field and publishes bird ringing records of 72,365 birds and protected species records to GBIF.

name: Kaniv Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve founded in 1923 covering 2,027 hectares on the right bank and floodplain islands of the Dnipro near Kaniv, and a scientific unit of Taras Shevchenko Kyiv National University.

name: Kinburn Spit Regional Landscape Park
summary: Regional landscape park of 17,890.2 hectares, according to Mykolaiv oblast's ecology department, whose territory has been occupied since almost the start of the full-scale invasion, so protection staff no longer patrol it.

name: Kremenetski Hory National Nature Park
summary: National nature park created by presidential decree of 11 December 2009, covering 6,951.2 hectares, of which 3,968.6 are in its permanent use and the rest is forestry land included without withdrawal.

name: LANDSCAPE FIRES
summary: Regional fire management information system for northern Ukraine, as described in a 2021 paper; its current status is unknown.

name: LIAC state enterprise
summary: State enterprise that maintains and improves the automated Pozhezhi system, which it says is part of a single digital system for monitoring and protecting Ukraine's forests.

name: Luhansk Nature Reserve
summary: Reserve within the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine that relocated after the full-scale invasion, with staff analysing earlier observations elsewhere; in March 2026 its director reported part of it remained occupied.

name: M. G. Kholodny Institute of Botany
summary: Ukrainian botany institute holding a National Herbarium of over 2 million specimens and publishing the Ukrainian Grassland Database to GBIF, with staff co-authoring recent plant studies.

name: Male Polissia National Nature Park
summary: National nature park created on 2 August 2013 to protect natural complexes and historical and cultural sites of eastern Male Polissia in Khmelnytskyi oblast.

name: Marine Research Station "Zmiinyi Island"
summary: Marine research station of Odessa National I. I. Mechnikov University on Zmiinyi Island, established in 2003 and listed on DEIMS-SDR as an unverified LTER Ukraine site observing water chemistry and quality.

name: Medobory Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve created to protect the natural complexes of the Podilski Tovtry, with a protected territory of 9,516.7 hectares.

name: Ministry of Economy and Environment of Ukraine
summary: Ukrainian ministry, renamed by the Cabinet in July 2026, which announced the government's biodiversity strategy to 2035 with 23 strategic goals and mentions remote sensing for environmental monitoring under the Finland UFEM project.

name: Ministry of Environmental Protection and Natural Resources of Ukraine
summary: Former Ukrainian ministry whose site covered biodiversity monitoring and treaties, and which established a working group in 2023 to prepare proposals for reforming biodiversity monitoring.

name: Mobilization of biodiversity data from Ukraine to GBIF
summary: Closed project run by the Habitat Foundation from January 2020 to June 2021 that helped digitise about 400,000 Ukrainian biodiversity records and localise iNaturalist into Ukrainian.

name: Models of reorganization of war-affected forest ecosystems
summary: Active project funded by the National Research Foundation of Ukraine that uses drones, LiDAR and simulation to study war-affected forests remotely because of landmines, and produced a GBIF flora dataset.

name: Monitoring of Common Bird Species of Ukraine
summary: A proposed count of common breeding birds in Ukraine, run by the Ukrainian Nature Conservation Group with GIZ as partner, planned to follow the Pan-European scheme, with a methods seminar held on 15 April 2026.

name: National Ecological Centre of Ukraine
summary: Ukrainian organisation that presented satellite analysis results for monitoring forest cover change in the More4Nature pilot in Hutsulshchyna National Nature Park.

name: National Forest Inventory of Ukraine
summary: Planned five-year inventory on about 22,000 plots, run by Ukrderzhlisproekt, with over 7,000 plots surveyed in 2021 to 2025 and a satellite-based inventory introduced in 2023.

name: National Geoportal of Ukraine
summary: Geospatial data portal whose prototype at nsdi.gov.ua was in trial operation in August 2021, offering search and free access to datasets from several national bodies and 92 local authorities.

name: National Research Foundation of Ukraine
summary: Funding body that selects and funds research and development projects in all research areas competitively, and is named as a source of results behind a 2024 Kyiv Polytechnic monograph.

name: National Technical University of Ukraine "Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute"
summary: A satellite-based land cover monitoring system integrated into this university uses machine learning on Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 composites, analysing 10 Ukrainian regions, Kyiv and Sevastopol, including war-related changes.

name: National University of Life and Environmental Sciences of Ukraine
summary: University whose forest mensuration department hosts a remote sensing forest monitoring laboratory, inaugurated on 22 July 2025, and whose authors have published on forest regeneration and nationwide forest assessment.

name: Nature Conservation GIS of Ukraine
summary: Organisation describing its work as geospatial technology for nature conservation, using satellite data and GIS with environmental groups, and partnering with the Esri Conservation Program and ClearCut.

name: Nobel National Nature Park
summary: National nature park of 25,318.81 hectares in northern Rivne oblast, reported in a 2026 paper to have lynx camera-trap and track records, and named by UNDP as a recipient of camera traps in May 2026.

name: Passive acoustic monitoring of fauna in the Roztochya region of Ukraine
summary: Records birds using autonomous acoustic equipment funded by the Finnish Embassy, identifies them with BirdNET, checks sampled detections with experts and publishes records to GBIF.

name: Podilski Tovtry National Nature Park
summary: National nature park with a territory of 261,316 hectares, of which 4,536 are owned by the park, which describes itself as the largest park in Ukraine.

name: Polissia Nature Reserve
summary: In Zhytomyr oblast’s Olevsk and Ovruch districts, this 20,104-hectare reserve receives monitoring equipment from Frankfurt Zoological Society, which reports trying to help with operating costs since the invasion.

name: Promoting sustainable livestock management and ecosystem conservation in northern Ukraine
summary: UNDP-run, GEF-funded project for 2022 to 2026 that in May 2026 handed 198 camera traps to protected areas to collect data on 17 peatland-linked species.

name: Pryp'iat-Stokhid National Nature Park
summary: National nature park in Volyn oblast covering 39,315.5 hectares and protecting Polissia natural complexes, including the Pryp'iat and Stokhid floodplains, according to Frankfurt Zoological Society.

name: Pushcha Radziwila National Nature Park
summary: A 2026 paper by authors affiliated with this national nature park reports staff recording lynx signs in recent years and six camera traps installed for winter lynx monitoring.

name: Quantum
summary: Company with Ukrainian R&D centres whose director said ClearCut, a deforestation platform using computer vision and AI, was made open source because of illegal logging.

name: Regional Eastern Europe Fire Monitoring Center
summary: Fire monitoring centre in Kyiv that NULES and partners decided in 2012 to establish, and whose October 2024 bulletin reported September 2024 fires and mapped burned land cover.

name: Remote-sensing-based forest inventory of Ukraine
summary: Forest inventory using Sentinel-2 time series for 2017 to 2023 and random forest classification to map forest cover and dominant species, supported by Ukrainian and German partners.

name: Research Institute of Geodesy and Cartography
summary: Institute named in 2021 as administrator of the national geoportal, tasked with creating and maintaining it and its metadata base and integrating incoming geospatial data.

name: Rewilding Ukraine
summary: Conservation NGO registered in Odesa in 2017, which by May 2021 had begun restoring the Tarutino Steppe with partners and is a partner in the Danube Delta rewilding project reporting reconnected lakes and reflooded marshland.

name: Rivne Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve of 42,291 hectares in four blocks that has run annual winter mammal counts since 2013, began camera-trap lynx monitoring with WWF-Ukraine, and was named by UNDP as a camera-trap recipient in May 2026.

name: Roztochya Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve in western Ukraine that publishes bird and amphibian records from acoustic monitoring analysed with deep learning models, and camera trap observations from a project begun in 2020.

name: Scientific Centre for Aerospace Research of the Earth
summary: Kyiv facility listed by OpenAlex whose researchers published papers on war-related fires in 2023, biotope monitoring in a reserve in 2020, and forest disturbance risk in 2021.

name: Shatsk National Nature Park
summary: National nature park created by Council of Ministers decision on 28 December 1983, with a total area of 48,977 hectares, of which 22,882 hectares are in permanent use.

name: Skolivski Beskydy National Nature Park
summary: National park where, a park official told FZS Ukraine, bat monitoring began in 2015 with about 20 species identified, using FZS-supplied batcorders under a SMART protocol.

name: Society for Conservation GIS Ukraine
summary: Society helping Ukrainian institutions, parks and communities use GIS since 2012, with work on damage monitoring, drone surveys, an open protected areas cadastre and, in 2020, preparation for GBIF accession.

name: Space Research Institute (Kyiv)
summary: Kyiv research facility listed by OpenAlex, whose works include a 2015 paper on retrospective land cover for Ukraine and a 2017 paper on deep learning classification of land cover and crops.

name: Space Research Institute of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine and the State Space Agency of Ukraine
summary: Kyiv institution with 642 works on OpenAlex, responsible for machine learning and forest loss detection in the Deep Green Ukraine consortium, and listed as a partner in FUTUREFOR.

name: State Agency for Forest Resources of Ukraine
summary: Government body that monitors forests and organises the national forest inventory; in 2023 a remote sensing inventory was introduced as a temporary alternative to field work.

name: State Agency of Water Resources of Ukraine
summary: Government agency that publishes State Water Cadastre surface water layers on data.gov.ua and, in 2018, presented the Clean Water river pollution map with the Data Journalism Agency.

name: State Cadastre of Territories and Objects of the Nature Reserve Fund of Ukraine
summary: Cadastre of nature reserve fund territories built and run by the environment ministry; it covered 88% of them at its 2021 launch, and public access was restricted in 2024.

name: State Environmental Inspectorate of Ukraine
summary: Government inspectorate that said in November 2020 it would track illegal logging and quarrying with aerospace imagery, starting as a pilot, as reported by Glavcom.

name: State Service of Ukraine for Geodesy, Cartography and Cadastre
summary: Government service that said in August 2021 it was building the national spatial data infrastructure, and in January 2021 named the administrator of the national geoportal.

name: State Space Agency of Ukraine
summary: Central executive body for state space activity policy that, Mind reported in 2021, would track illegal logging and mining by satellite imagery with the environment ministry.

name: Steppe Biodiversity Cadastre
summary: Database of protected steppe species, kept by volunteers, which at the stage described held 13,678 species records and about 5,400 steppe plots drawn from satellite images.

name: Strengthening the forest monitoring capacity of Ukraine for EU Compliance
summary: Czech-funded project to strengthen Ukraine's forest monitoring with remote sensing, which funded a remote sensing forest monitoring laboratory at NULES, opened on 22 July 2025.

name: Support to Nature Protected Areas in Ukraine
summary: Closed 2016 to 2022 project, run by the environment ministry with a KfW-financed grant of up to 14 million euros, to support a protected-area cadastre.

name: Support to Ukraine in the assessment of environmental damages and development of water quality and terrestrial biodiversity monitoring
summary: Ongoing 2024 to 2028 cooperation between the Finnish Environment Institute and Ukraine's environment ministry on water quality, terrestrial biodiversity and remote sensing monitoring, funded by Finland's foreign ministry.

name: Sviati Hory National Nature Park
summary: National nature park created by presidential decree No. 135/97 of 13 February 1997; parts were occupied in 2022, and fighting damaged about 9,000 hectares of forest in one division.

name: Synevyr National Nature Park
summary: National nature park that gained national status on 5 January 1989 with 40,400 hectares, extended by a further 377 hectares through a presidential decree in 2019.

name: Syniohora National Nature Park
summary: National nature park created in 2009 in the Gorgany range, where camera traps have recorded brown bears every winter since 2022 and a 2026 paper reports its monitoring results.

name: Technical support for the development of forest policy and implementation of the national forest inventory
summary: Project with Ukrainian and German experts, supported by Germany's agriculture ministry, that made the 2023 remote-sensing forest inventory possible using field data from more than 4,000 plots in 18 regions.

name: The first environmental DNA-based inventory of soil fungal diversity in Ukraine
summary: First national-scale DNA metabarcoding record of soil fungal communities in Ukraine, built from 225 topsoil samples collected in 2023 and published to GBIF.

name: Tsumanska Pushcha National Nature Park
summary: Staff have monitored lynx since 2017; a 2026 paper used data from two camera traps, and UNDP named the park as a camera-trap recipient in May 2026.

name: Tuzlivski Lymany National Nature Park
summary: National nature park created by presidential decree No. 1 of 1 January 2010 on 27,865 hectares of the Tuzlivski lagoons, according to the environment ministry's page.

name: Ukraine Fire Perimeters 2022
summary: Dataset titled Ukraine Fire Perimeters 2022, published on Zenodo in 2023, with Sergiy Zibtsev of NULES as first listed author.

name: Ukrainian Bat Rehabilitation Center
summary: Self-described largest bat conservation, research and outreach project in Eastern Europe; its site reports 32,248 rescued bats of 14 species and it publishes bat occurrence data to GBIF.

name: Ukrainian Biodiversity Information Network
summary: Volunteer-supported crowdsourcing platform for biodiversity data, with records from field observations, text mining and museums; its site returned a database error when fetched on 3 November 2026.

name: Ukrainian Bird Ringing Centre
summary: Centre set up in May 1992 on the basis of the Institute of Zoology's ornithology laboratory, within a national system that ringed more than 410,000 birds in Ukraine from 1991 to 2014.

name: Ukrainian Grassland Database
summary: Vegetation-plot database created in 2008 holding more than 10,000 grassland relevés made by 66 authors between 1932 and 2019, updated after each field season and part of several European and global archives.

name: Ukrainian National Forestry University
summary: University whose researchers published a 2026 paper on random forest and deep learning for forest cover change and describe a Random Forest platform for Carpathian old-growth forest monitoring.

name: Ukrainian Nature Conservation Group
summary: Non-profit registered in 2018 that has published 361 datasets to GBIF and works on threatened species, habitats and Emerald Network sites.

name: Ukrainian Research Institute of Forestry and Forest Melioration named after G.M. Vysotsky
summary: Research institute subordinate to the State Forest Resources Agency, whose scientists co-authored the National Forest Inventory method, according to a May 2024 article.

name: Ukrainian Scientific Centre of Ecology of the Sea
summary: Environment ministry's main institution for marine environmental research, per its GBIF record, founded in 1992 and accredited as the Black Sea OBIS node in 2016.

name: Ukrainian State Forest Management Planning Association Ukrderzhlisproekt
summary: State forest management planning association designated from 2020 as responsible for the national forest inventory, which it runs through its National Forest Inventory Centre, with state budget funding.

name: Uzhanskyi National Nature Park
summary: A national nature park whose scientists work with WWF-Ukraine on lynx monitoring, using camera traps at 30 locations and confirming seven individual Eurasian lynx, four of them males.

name: V. N. Karazin Kharkiv National University
summary: A university hosting the CWU herbarium, founded in 1825 with about 300,000 specimens, and publishing myxomycete datasets to GBIF with 5,036 georeferenced occurrences of 339 taxa, mostly from literature of 1842 to 2023.

name: Vyzhnytskyi National Nature Park
summary: A 2026 paper assesses lynx monitoring for 1997–2024 using this national nature park’s Chronicle of Nature, SMART data and camera traps, which recorded lynx in 2022–2024.

name: West-Ukrainian Ornithological Society
summary: Founded in 1984, it unites over 100 ornithologists across Ukraine, Poland and Romania, keeps over 23,700 nest and clutch records covering 223 species, and publishes records to GBIF.

name: WWF-Ukraine
summary: A WWF-CEE conservation organisation working in the Carpathians, Polissya and Danube Delta, collaborating with Uzhanskyi National Nature Park on lynx camera-trap monitoring and using Sensing Clues.

name: Yavorivskyi National Nature Park
summary: This national nature park protects 7,108 hectares, including wetlands, lakes, rivers and rare pine-beech-oak forests found in Ukraine only in Roztochchia and Crimea.

name: 2011 Bwindi mountain gorilla census
summary: Closed census, run by the Uganda Wildlife Authority, that confirmed at least 400 mountain gorillas in Bwindi, up from 302 in 2006, using nest sweeps and faecal samples for genetics.

name: 2025 Bwindi Chimpanzee Census
summary: Closed census, carried out in May and June 2025 with the park's gorilla census, that estimated about 426 chimpanzees in Bwindi Impenetrable National Park using line-transect nest counts over 320.9 square kilometres.

name: 2025 Bwindi-Sarambwe mountain gorilla census
summary: Launched on 6 May 2025, this IGCP-led, WWF-funded gorilla census had nest recording and faecal sampling under way that month, with results expected in 2026.

name: A Rocha Uganda
summary: Christian conservation organisation conducting snake and mammal surveys, whose GBIF record lists participation in an eleven-organisation project and eight datasets totalling 17,390 records for digitisation.

name: Aquawood Uganda
summary: Ugandan innovation, listed at prototype stage in Kampala, that the Uganda Innovation Portal says uses satellite images, AI and GIS to monitor deforestation and water pollution, with a prototype community reporting app.

name: Assessing threats and local perceptions of giant pangolins in the Budongo-Mukihani Forest Linkage Zone (Rufford 48829-1)
summary: Rufford-funded study of giant pangolins in Uganda's Budongo-Mukihani linkage zone; a December 2025 grantee update reports six camera traps in three villages, six trained community monitors, and planned checks every two to three weeks.

name: Bird vocalisation dataset of birds in Uganda
summary: Dataset described in a 2024 data paper, with Mark Abraham Magumba listed by OpenAlex as first author, of Ugandan bird vocalisations for automated bioacoustic monitoring and analysis.

name: Budongo Conservation Field Station
summary: A Ugandan-run NGO in Budongo forest, established in 1990 and funded by the Royal Zoological Society of Scotland, which has collected systematic long-term Waibira chimpanzee data since April 2011 and offers a request form for access.

name: Bulindi Chimpanzee and Community Project
summary: Project that reported in February 2024 monitoring six chimpanzee groups, about half of roughly 300 chimpanzees in unprotected habitat in the Budongo-Bugoma corridor, using camera traps on new groups.

name: Chimpanzee Trust
summary: An organisation that trains community monitors to track chimpanzee movements and report illegal logging in forest corridors of Hoima, Kikuube and Masindi districts in the Northern Albertine Rift.

name: Conservation Through Public Health
summary: A Uganda-based non-profit founded in 2003 that, as reported by Population Connection, monitors 27 mountain gorilla groups in the Bwindi and Mgahinga Conservation Area and works with UWA on disease surveillance.

name: Department of Aeronautics and Space Science, Science, Technology and Innovation Secretariat
summary: Unit of Uganda's Science, Technology and Innovation Secretariat whose technical lead attended the first AfDev-Sat workshop in 2025; Uganda is one of six countries in that joint Earth observation mission.

name: Department of Surveys and Mapping, Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development
summary: Entebbe-based department of the Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development responsible for survey and geodetic controls, topographical maps and the National Atlas, and which provides aerial photographs and printed satellite images.

name: Digital Strategy for Protected Area Management
summary: Programme led by Uganda Conservation Foundation with UWA; UCF reports UWA’s countrywide EarthRanger system is fully operational across three landscapes.

name: Embaka
summary: A Kampala-based, self-described community-led conservation organisation that Mongabay reports uses camera traps and AI tools for African golden cat monitoring, with a planned permanent camera-trap system at Bwindi.

name: Enterprise Neurosystem
summary: Describes itself as an open-source AI research community treating species and ecosystems as one system, and says it has been engaged to develop an AI-capable robotic sensor for Lake Victoria.

name: Environmental Surveys, Information, Planning and Policy Systems
summary: Ugandan company, as Space in Africa describes it, applying geoinformation science and Earth observation to environmental surveys, and a partner in East African consortia of the GMES and Africa programme.

name: Freshwater Biodiversity Portal for Uganda
summary: Online portal for Ugandan freshwater biodiversity data, built by NaFIRRI, which JRS reported fully online in May 2022, with fish, invertebrate and algae datasets mobilised through GBIF.

name: From the Lab to the World: Unlocking Uganda's Freshwater Biodiversity Data for Sustainable Development
summary: Project announced in September 2018, funded by JRS Biodiversity Foundation and led by Vianny Natugonza, aiming to make Uganda's freshwater biodiversity data accessible and identify freshwater KBAs.

name: GBIF Uganda
summary: Country node of GBIF with observer participation status, listed alongside seven publishing organisations in Uganda and acting as endorsing node for the National Fisheries Resources Research Institute.

name: Generating information on bee pollinator diversity and distribution in Uganda through the application of ecological and informatics tools
summary: Closed 2019–2022 project, funded by JRS Biodiversity Foundation and run by Makerere University, that aimed to create a public web database of pollinator information; JRS lists the grant at $275,000 and announced a first online bee identification key.

name: Global Park Defense, Murchison Falls National Park
summary: Programme built by UCF and UWA, with Global Conservation support, now deployed across nearly 85% of Murchison Falls National Park, with lion and elephant satellite collars registered on EarthRanger.

name: Gulu University
summary: University with a researcher listed by OpenAlex as first author of a 2024 paper on land-use and land-cover change modelling and a 2025 spatial analysis of land use change in the Mount Elgon region.

name: Improving Local Capacity for Acoustic-Based Wildlife and Law Enforcement Monitoring in Bwindi Impenetrable National Park, Uganda
summary: A closed project listed by the Rufford Foundation under Badru Mugerwa, first dated 14 October 2020, that aimed to run a demonstration acoustic grid, train rangers in passive acoustic monitoring and develop call-detection algorithms.

name: Institute of Tropical Forest Conservation
summary: Established in 1991 as a Mbarara University research institution and field station at Ruhija beside Bwindi, working on conservation and natural resource management in the Albertine Rift.

name: Investing in Forest and Protected Areas for Climate Smart Development Project
summary: A World Bank-funded six-year project, approved by Parliament on 28 April 2021 and planned for 37 districts, under which UWA invited bids for 11 drones and sought a wildfire detection feasibility study.

name: Jane Goodall Institute Uganda
summary: Organisation that the Uganda Wildlife Authority says led the 2025 Bwindi Chimpanzee Census in partnership with UWA and GVTC.

name: Kabale University
summary: University that leads a JRS-funded consortium to protect biodiversity in Uganda's papyrus wetlands and is listed by GBIF as a Ugandan publisher with five datasets.

name: Kampala International University
summary: University with a researcher listed by OpenAlex as first author of a 2023 study of land use and land cover change in Limoto Wetland.

name: Kibale Chimpanzee Project
summary: Long-term field study of wild chimpanzee behaviour, ecology and physiology, started by Richard Wrangham in 1987, which publishes behavioural and physiological datasets in public repositories such as Dryad.

name: Kibale Ecology and Conservation Project
summary: Project based at the Makerere University Biological Field Station that monitors mammal populations and develops eDNA biodiversity tools, building capacity in Uganda with the Uganda Wildlife Authority.

name: Kyambogo University
summary: University whose staff are first authors of OpenAlex-listed remote sensing studies, including a 2020 Sentinel-1 study of lake inundation and one on environmental degradation in the Lake Victoria watershed.

name: Kyambura Chimpanzee Monitoring Project
summary: A project launched by VSPT with UWA as partner, based at Kyambura Gorge Lodge, where the team plans to record GPS coordinates, photograph individual chimpanzees and log community size and composition.

name: Kyambura Lion Monitoring Project
summary: An active project launched in 2023, run by Volcanoes Safaris Partnership Trust, that monitors wildlife and surveys large carnivores annually in Queen Elizabeth National Park, with lodge guests' lion photos feeding the census.

name: Lake Albert and Murchison Falls land cover change monitoring project
summary: Project announced in December 2018 as Ketty Adoch's AI for Earth Innovation Grant work, planned to detect, quantify and monitor land cover change around Lake Albert and Murchison Falls National Park.

name: Makerere University
summary: University that hosted the National Biodiversity Data Bank from 1990, has two departments publishing to GBIF, and received a JRS grant (October 2019 to December 2022) to build a public pollinator database.

name: Makerere University Biological Field Station
summary: Run by Makerere University, this year-round Kibale Forest research station hosts long-term research, with chimpanzee health monitoring and Pl@ntNet training recorded in the university’s 2025 report.

name: Mbarara University of Science and Technology
summary: University with authors on OpenAlex-listed camera trap and eDNA biodiversity papers, and an Institute of Tropical Forest Conservation set up in 1991 as its field station.

name: Ministry of Tourism, Wildlife and Antiquities
summary: Government ministry that issues CITES permits, enforces international conservation conventions and works against illegal wildlife trafficking, and which UWA says supervises it.

name: Ministry of Water and Environment
summary: Kampala ministry responsible for water, environment, wetlands, forestry, climate and sanitation policy according to Wikipedia, whose website lists forest cover trends and wetlands status data.

name: Murchison Falls National Park aerial imaging and AI wildlife survey
summary: Global Conservation reports sponsoring the closed Richard Lamprey-led aerial imaging and artificial intelligence survey estimating Murchison Falls wildlife numbers, counting elephants, hippos, buffalo and other herbivores.

name: My Gorilla Family
summary: Home of a Gorilla initiative project that the Uganda Wildlife Authority announced as a paid subscription app for virtual trekking in Bwindi and Mgahinga, aiming to fund conservation.

name: National Biodiversity Data Bank
summary: Central repository for Uganda's biodiversity data, set up at Makerere University in 1990, which publishes a GBIF observation dataset; its listed web address showed only a default server page on 8 November 2026.

name: National Environment Management Authority
summary: Leads Uganda's National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan, with NBSAP III covering 2025 to 2030, and said in July 2025 it was preparing Uganda's seventh CBD report.

name: National Fisheries Resources Research Institute
summary: Public research institute in Jinja under NARO that publishes 38 GBIF datasets, received a $260,000 JRS grant in 2018, and says its freshwater data portal is not yet completed.

name: National Forestry Authority
summary: Maps national land cover through its GIS unit; UN-REDD reports its establishment in 2004 for 506 reserves and forest degradation assessment from June 2019 using SEPAL.

name: National Wetland Information System (Uganda)
summary: A Ugandan wetland dataset which, according to a December 2016 JICA completion report, holds wetland monitoring survey sites, was released publicly through ArcGIS Online and became fully operational after modification during the project.

name: NaturAfrica Karamoja and Turkana transboundary landscape project
summary: Active project under the EU's NaturAfrica programme, run by Northern Rangelands Trust, for which UCF has sought bids for a transfrontier aerial survey and GPS elephant collars.

name: NatureUganda
summary: Ugandan NGO and BirdLife partner that documents and monitors biodiversity, produced a 2019 waterfowl count report for UWA, and has a JRS grant for 2023 to 2025 to train herpetologists.

name: NEMA satellite ecosystem monitoring system
summary: A proof-of-concept system that Amilen Africa says it built for NEMA, comparing new satellite images with past ones and drawing an alert where change exceeds half a hectare.

name: Ngogo Chimpanzee Project
summary: An active long-term field project studying and conserving the Ngogo chimpanzee community in Kibale National Park, co-directed by Kevin Langergraber, with a local team collecting faecal samples for genetic monitoring and working with Uganda Wildlife Authority officers to collect snares.

name: Nubian Giraffe Conservation in Uganda (Giraffe Conservation Foundation)
summary: Long-term monitoring of Uganda's Nubian giraffe, begun in 2013 and run by the Giraffe Conservation Foundation with Makerere University and UWA, using individual-based photographic surveys and pattern recognition software.

name: Pian Upe Wildlife Reserve conservation technology
summary: Technology at Pian Upe Wildlife Reserve run by Space for Giants and using EarthRanger, which July 2026 job adverts listed alongside LoRaWAN infrastructure, camera traps and GPS devices for a planned recruit to manage.

name: Pian-Upe Wildlife Reserve aerial wildlife and livestock survey, 2025
summary: Aerial wildlife and livestock survey of Pian-Upe Wildlife Reserve in 2025, listed by WildSpace Image Analytics, using the oblique-camera-count method and Jolly II analysis, for Space for Giants with the Uganda Wildlife Authority.

name: Queen Elizabeth National Park LoRaWAN network
summary: Active LoRaWAN network whose gateways carry data from lion collars and sensors across the park, with infrastructure, software and trackers donated by CCF, Cisco and Actility.

name: Queen Elizabeth Protected Area aerial camera wildlife survey, 2018
summary: Closed 2018 aerial survey of Queen Elizabeth National Park that acquired 32,000 oblique-camera-count images, funded by UCF, and whose imagery a 2023 study used to train and evaluate HerdNet.

name: Sebitoli Chimpanzee Project
summary: Founded in 2008 to protect Uganda’s chimpanzees, the project had 20 camera-trap and audio-recorder locations and offline laptop classification, One Forest Vision reported in February 2025.

name: Securing the future of Nubian giraffes in PUWR, Uganda
summary: A closed 2024 to 2025 project run by Space for Giants under IUCN Save Our Species, which planned a mobile giraffe monitoring officer, an identification database and EarthRanger sighting records.

name: Site Selection to Protect Papyrus Endemic Biodiversity in Uganda
summary: Closed JRS-funded project led by Kabale University, which planned to gather bird, reptile and amphibian data in Albertine Rift papyrus wetlands and build models to identify priority sites for protection.

name: State of Wildlife Resources in Uganda Report 2026
summary: A national wildlife assessment built by UWA, consolidating data on many species groups and reporting that elephants in monitored protected areas fell from 6,621 in 2021-2022 to 6,352 in 2023-2025.

name: Uganda Conservation Foundation
summary: Established in 2001, this UK and Ugandan non-profit supports UWA rangers, uses conservation technology including EarthRanger, and reports over 1,000 UWA staff trained in EarthRanger.

name: Uganda Flying Labs
summary: Organisation that captured forest data in Masindi with RGB, LiDAR and multispectral drone cameras, in partnership with the Jane Goodall Institute, with processing by machine learning and AI planned by a partner.

name: Uganda national AI sensor network
summary: Proposed national AI environmental sensor network with Bwindi suggested first, developed with Enterprise Neurosystem and JPL/Caltech, and approved for funding by Uganda’s science minister, according to Enterprise Neurosystem.

name: Uganda National Forest Monitoring System
summary: Active national forest monitoring programme that Uganda began developing with UN-REDD Programme support, and which the National Forestry Authority team was working to strengthen as of February 2020.

name: Uganda Natural Resource Information System
summary: Deforestation monitoring platform built by UNDP and the National Forestry Authority, with a GIS web interface and field validation app, which UNDP planned to scale to natural resources governance.

name: Uganda Wildlife and Timber Forensics Laboratory
summary: Forensics laboratory at the Uganda Wildlife Education Center in Entebbe, built by UWA with Danish and UNODC funding, which in April 2026 planned full timber DNA analysis in the coming months.

name: Uganda Wildlife Authority
summary: Government agency managing Uganda's national parks, reserves and sanctuaries, which its 2026 report says is moving from SMART to EarthRanger and uses camera traps and drones for monitoring.

name: USAID/Uganda Combating Wildlife Crime Activity
summary: Closed five-year activity (2020 to 2025) run by WCS with AWF and RUSI, which supported SMART roll-out in Uganda Wildlife Authority protected areas and handed over an upgraded offenders database in May 2024.

name: Volcanoes Safaris Partnership Trust
summary: A registered charity in Uganda that launched the Kyambura Lion Monitoring Project in 2023 and a Kyambura Chimpanzee Monitoring Project based at its research centre at Kyambura Gorge Lodge.

name: Vulture tracking in Murchison Falls, Kidepo Valley and Queen Elizabeth National Parks
summary: Project in which the Hawk Conservancy Trust reports deploying 11 tracking units on vultures at three Ugandan national parks with UCF and UWA, tracking 13 vultures whose movements may give early warning of poaching.

name: WCS Uganda
summary: Programme run by the Wildlife Conservation Society, currently focused on three Ugandan landscapes, which reported in March 2025 a method for monitoring wildlife where direct sampling is not possible.

name: Wetlands Monitoring with Earth Observation for SDG 6.6.1 in Uganda
summary: A closed project led by RAMCEA and funded by the Global Partnership on Sustainable Development Data, which piloted a digital wetland monitoring system for Uganda's Ministry of Water and Environment, including a 2016 to 2017 Sentinel-based baseline map.

name: A.I.S., Inc.
summary: US fisheries monitoring provider and NFWF grantee expanding AI discard accounting in New England groundfish and piloting AI species identification in shoreside monitoring.

name: A3EM: Animal-borne Adaptive Acoustic Environmental Monitoring
summary: NSF cyber-physical systems award for animal-borne adaptive acoustic monitoring, with Colorado State University among the collaborators.

name: Advanced Remote Sensing Imaging and Analytics Lab
summary: University of Connecticut lab using sub-metre satellite images, AI and high-performance computing, with emphasis on Arctic permafrost, and forest biomass estimation.

name: Agerpoint
summary: It says its platform combines smartphone scans, LiDAR and satellite imagery, applies AI to digital plant twins for tree carbon verification, and offers digital reforestation measurement, reporting and verification.

name: Agile Restoration & Conservation Hubs
summary: Partnership of Scripps Oceanography and San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance on biobanking and conservation technology, including a digital twin of the Safari Park Biodiversity Reserve.

name: Ahtna Intertribal Resource Commission
summary: Alaska intertribal commission that runs salmon weirs and is exploring AI and computer vision for salmon monitoring, beginning at Tanada Creek.

name: AI edge computing for near real-time flux tower analysis
summary: NSF EAGER award at West Virginia University using AI edge computing to analyse flux tower data in near real time.

name: AI Institute for Climate-Land Interactions, Mitigation, Adaptation, Tradeoffs and Economy
summary: National AI institute led by the University of Minnesota Twin Cities that brings agriculture and forestry knowledge into foundational AI. Reported to have been renamed AI-LEAF, though the page giving that refused automated reading.

name: AI Institute for Intelligent Cyberinfrastructure with Computational Learning in the Environment
summary: NSF AI institute for plug-and-play AI as a service, reported by HPCwire. Ohio State's own site refused automated reading.

name: AI Sense
summary: Ellicott City, Maryland company funded by NSF SBIR to develop an AI-powered humane wildlife deterrent.

name: AI-based automation of acoustic detection of marine mammals
summary: NOAA in-house software for training and deploying machine learning models that detect marine mammals in passive acoustic data.

name: AI-enabled modelling of right whale predator-prey interactions
summary: NSF AI and Geosciences award to develop AI methods for marine food webs, studying the North Atlantic right whale and zooplankton, at Rutgers University.

name: AI-ready Ecology and Biodiversity Data Infrastructure for Open Science
summary: NSF collaborative project building open, scalable data infrastructure for AI-enabled ecological and biodiversity research, with Ohio State University, Duke University and NatureServe.

name: Ai.Fish
summary: Company building AI-assisted video review for fisheries electronic monitoring, with object detection, tracking and classification.

name: Alaska Department of Fish and Game
summary: Alaska state agency that has counted Bristol Bay salmon escapement from towers for more than 70 years, the baseline for drone and AI counting work. KNBA reports it is not directly part of that project.

name: Alaska Longline Fishermen's Association
summary: Sitka-based fishing association that won an NFWF grant to bring AI into electronic monitoring video review for Alaska fixed gear fisheries.

name: Alaska Ocean Observing System
summary: One of 11 regional systems of IOOS, running the Ocean Data Explorer portal of more than 3,000 marine data layers.

name: ALERTCalifornia
summary: UC San Diego public safety programme running a network of cameras and sensors across California, using AI with CAL FIRE for early detection of wildfire. Public feeds cover fire danger, snow melt and hazardous weather.

name: ALERTWest
summary: Subsidiary of DigitalPath offering a network of cameras and a situational awareness platform with AI wildfire detection.

name: Aleut Community of St. Paul Island
summary: Alaska tribal community whose Bering Watch and Island Sentinel programme began what became the Indigenous Sentinels Network.

name: Alliance for Monitoring Biodiversity and Ecosystems Remotely
summary: University of Vermont hosted alliance that runs machine learning models, including SpeciesNet, to identify wildlife in camera and acoustic media.

name: Alliance for the Chesapeake Bay
summary: Regional watershed charity that lists the Chesapeake Monitoring Cooperative among its projects.

name: American Forests
summary: US forest nonprofit working with data, science and policy, and behind Tree Equity Score.

name: American Museum of Natural History
summary: New York museum where Mary Blair presented work for NASA on an integrated biodiversity monitoring system for Colombia's protected areas.

name: American Prairie
summary: Montana conservation organisation inviting volunteers to identify wildlife on trail cameras.

name: American Rivers
summary: US river conservation charity that publishes a public database of dam removals.

name: AmeriFlux
summary: Network of sites and scientists measuring ecosystem carbon, water and energy fluxes across the Americas and sharing eddy covariance data.

name: Anacostia Riverkeeper
summary: Washington, DC nonprofit that, in a DataRobot case study, uses AI to predict E. coli levels in the Anacostia River.

name: Analytics Lab
summary: Software programme run by Conservation Science Partners that combines remote sensing datasets with deep learning to answer questions about nature and society in real time, with Google and Microsoft among listed partners.

name: Anecdata
summary: Free online citizen science platform used to collect, manage and share observations.

name: Animal Detection Network (Andenet)
