summary: Initiative for which BBoxEE was developed to annotate bounding boxes and export object detector training data, with museum researcher Peter Ersts developing the open-source tool according to its repository.

name: Anthropocene Institute
summary: Institute with which the marine conservation organisation ProtectedSeas is associated, per the Global Seafood Alliance.

name: AquaRealTime
summary: Maker of self-cleaning sensors, buoys and shore stations that send live water quality data, sold to agencies, watershed managers and utilities, with one Wisconsin customer reporting it helps treat ponds before algae worsens.

name: Arbor Day Foundation
summary: US tree planting nonprofit whose Impact Fund invested in Vibrant Planet and Convective Capital for wildfire resilience technology.

name: Arkansas Forest Resources Center
summary: Research and extension arm for forest-based programmes in Arkansas, headquartered in Monticello. Its geospatial work includes machine learning on forest biomass and a PhD post in geospatial AI and forest health.

name: Arthur V Davis Foundation
summary: US grant maker recorded in tax filings data on Grantable as funding Conservation X Labs.

name: ArtInStack
summary: Photography and media platform that also describes itself to GBIF as a platform for managing biodiversity media and occurrence records, including camera trap data packages.

name: Assessment, Inventory, and Monitoring Strategy
summary: BLM strategy providing standardised field measurements and data on the condition of public lands.

name: Atlantic Cooperative Telemetry Network
summary: Network of researchers using acoustic telemetry to track aquatic animals along the US Atlantic coast.

name: Atlantic White Shark Conservancy
summary: Nonprofit that publishes white shark information for the Northwest Atlantic, has funded Massachusetts Division of Marine Fisheries white shark studies most since 2013, and runs the Sharktivity sightings app.

name: Automated AI camera trap study
summary: 2026 study led by Washington State University and Google testing whether a fully automated AI system could replace humans in processing camera trap images, finding close agreement for most species.

name: Automated species identification from optical survey data in the Gulf of Mexico
summary: NOAA work building an image library of landed catch and automated image processing to identify and count species in the Gulf.

name: Autonomous Marine Systems
summary: Somerville, Massachusetts company that describes itself as a JASCO Applied Sciences division and offers passive acoustic monitoring for endangered species such as North Atlantic right whales.

name: Axiom Data Science
summary: Data management company behind the SECOORA portal and AOOS Ocean Data Explorer, which also lists an AI system for detecting coral spawning at the Florida Aquarium.

name: Azul Bio
summary: Public benefit venture working on coral reef preservation and restoration, offering genomic and microbiome analysis, including eDNA biodiversity assessment, and microbial reef treatments in selected regions.

name: Bad River Band of Lake Superior Tribe of Chippewa Indians
summary: A tribal government that protects wetlands within the watersheds on its Reservation, and lists the 2012 Ramsar designation of the Kakagon and Bad River Sloughs among its recognitions.

name: Battelle
summary: Operator of the National Ecological Observatory Network for the US National Science Foundation.

name: Belvedere Charitable Foundation
summary: US grant maker recorded in tax filings data on Grantable as funding Global Fishing Watch.

name: Benioff Ocean Science Laboratory
summary: UC Santa Barbara laboratory behind Whale Safe.

name: Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences
summary: Maine ocean research institute developing forecasting tools with AI and long-running monitoring, including a Computational Oceanography Lab working on right whale habitat and shellfish toxicity forecasts.

name: BigMAP
summary: Forest Service project using machine learning on Landsat time series, climatic and topographic data to map US forest resources from national inventory data.

name: BIO-AI conference on cyberinfrastructure and AI for ecological research at NEON
summary: NSF-funded conference on cyberinfrastructure and AI for ecological research at NEON and beyond, at the University of Pittsburgh.

name: BioBase
summary: Service that turns sonar recorded on Lowrance or Simrad devices and uploaded to its cloud into GIS-ready maps of aquatic vegetation coverage and biovolume, including for monitoring invasive plants.

name: Biodiversity Information Serving Our Nation
summary: Former US species occurrence website and database that provided the basis for GBIF-US and has since been taken offline.

name: Biodiversity Institute, University of Kansas
summary: University of Kansas research centre for biodiversity, listed as a TDWG member.

name: Biodiversity Knowledge Integration Center
summary: Arizona State University centre that coordinates the Symbiota Support Hub network with iDigBio, which is a GBIF publisher.

name: Biodiversity On Demand (BOND)
summary: NSF-funded collaborative web platform for discovering, comparing and integrating biodiversity databases.

name: Biological and Chemical Oceanography Data Management Office
summary: Publicly accessible repository curating and publishing data from biological, chemical and biogeochemical research.

name: Bird Conservancy of the Rockies
summary: Conservation organisation for birds of the Rocky Mountains and Great Plains and a Bird Migration Explorer partner.

name: Bird Genoscape Project
summary: Project using genomics to connect bird populations across the Western Hemisphere and build maps for 100 species.

name: Bird Migration Explorer
summary: Interactive maps of the full annual cycle of 458 migratory bird species, with Audubon, Bird Conservancy of the Rockies, Cornell and others among the partners.

name: BirdBot
summary: Tacoma, Washington company, BirdBot Technology LLC, whose software collects and shares bird detections from compatible cameras, combining computer vision with community participation to identify birds.

name: BirdCast
summary: Collaboration of the Cornell Lab of Ornithology, UMass Amherst and Oregon State University using weather radar and machine learning to map and forecast bird migration across the US.

name: BirdHabitatBot
summary: Willimantic, Connecticut company funded by NSF SBIR to develop a mobile robot that removes invasive plants.

name: BirdVox
summary: Collaboration between the Cornell Lab of Ornithology and NYU's Music and Audio Research Laboratory, investigating machine listening to detect and classify flying birds, aiming at a real-time acoustic network for migration monitoring.

name: Bishop Museum
summary: Hawaiʻi museum listed as an institutional member of TDWG.

name: Block Lab, Hopkins Marine Station
summary: Stanford lab in Pacific Grove developing FAST, the Fin Alert Shark Tag, which reports by satellite when a tagged shark is caught.

name: Blue Data Technologies
summary: Essex, Montana start-up designing a low-power submersible trail camera to monitor salmon spawning streams.

name: Blue Ocean Gear
summary: Redwood City company building trackable buoys that prevent lost fishing gear and send alerts about whale entanglement.

name: Blue Water Task Force
summary: Surfrider's national network of chapter-run labs measuring bacteria at ocean, bay, estuary and freshwater sites.

name: Bluefin Data
summary: NFWF grantee piloting elogbooks with image capture and AI species identification in the US Caribbean highly migratory fishery.

name: BlueGreen Water Technologies
summary: The company says it gathers cyanobacteria bloom data from field measurements, remote sensing and satellites and predicts blooms using AI, and offers BGi for monitoring lakes and reservoirs.

name: BlueIQ
summary: Boston start-up making networked hydrophones that use AI to identify sounds at sea, with work on right whales for NOAA and on beaked whales.

name: Bluesonde
summary: Maker of real-time water monitoring systems, mostly used so far for shellfish aquaculture, with a growing share in environmental monitoring.

name: Boettiger Group
summary: UC Berkeley research group led by Carl Boettiger on ecological forecasting and decisions under uncertainty, whose RL for Conservation project trains reinforcement learning agents on environments such as forest fires and overfishing.

name: Borror Laboratory of Bioacoustics
summary: Animal sound archive at The Ohio State University, begun in 1948 and digitised with NSF funding.

name: Bristol Bay Regional Seafood Development Association
summary: NFWF grantee piloting drone video with AI processing to improve sockeye salmon counts in the Wood River system, Bristol Bay, Alaska.

name: Bristol Bay salmon drone and AI counting project
summary: Project on the Wood River in Bristol Bay, Alaska, using automated drone flights and a computer model to produce salmon escapement counts, with Norm Van Vactor as a project lead.

name: BuckEye Cam
summary: Product line from Athens, Ohio, with motion-activated cameras that radio images to a base without mobile coverage and AI that detects people, vehicles or animals.

name: Bureau of Indian Affairs
summary: US federal bureau whose news pages report tribal natural resource work, including Bipartisan Infrastructure Law funding used by the Hualapai Tribe for lidar.

name: Bureau of Land Management
summary: US federal land management agency that runs the Assessment, Inventory, and Monitoring strategy for public lands.

name: Bureau of Ocean Energy Management
summary: US federal offshore energy regulator that funds studies on deep learning for aerial surveys of marine wildlife and on machine learning for Cook Inlet beluga photo identification.

name: C4ADS
summary: Nonprofit that serves as a data and technology hub for a global coalition against wildlife trafficking, and runs the Wildlife Defense Platform.

name: CA Nature
summary: California's geospatial hub of mapping tools for statewide biodiversity, access, climate and conservation data, built by the California Natural Resources Agency with Esri for the state's 30x30 goal.

name: CAIG: AI to reveal phytoplankton
summary: NSF AI and Geosciences collaborative award applying AI to phytoplankton, with the University of Delaware and the University of Louisiana.

name: CAIG: wildfire detection through super-resolution
summary: NSF AI and Geosciences award at the University of Wisconsin on wildfire detection, evolution and control.

name: CALeDNA
summary: California environmental DNA programme. UC Santa Cruz researchers received a $2.2 million state grant to scale an eDNA index of stream health.

name: California Biodiversity Network
summary: California network through which the Sentinel Site Network is organised, and publisher of a 2025 biodiversity assessment of 30x30 areas.

name: California Department of Fish and Wildlife
summary: California state wildlife agency whose Environmental Monitoring and Assessment Framework sets the instrumentation of the Sentinel Site Network, which it also funds.

name: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
summary: California state fire and forestry department that partners with ALERTCalifornia on AI early detection of wildfire.

name: California Forest Observatory
summary: Forest monitoring system that maps forest structure and fuel loads at tree level across California, a partnership of Planet, Salo Sciences and Vibrant Planet.

name: California Imaging FlowCytobot Network
summary: Statewide network of 12 Imaging FlowCytobots photographing water particles, with machine learning used to classify species for early warning of harmful algal blooms.

name: California Natural Resources Agency
summary: California state agency that leads the state's 30x30 initiative and built the CA Nature mapping hub.

name: California Sentinel Site Network
summary: Collaboration of academic, governmental and nonprofit bodies running long-term biodiversity and climate monitoring sites across California as a feedback mechanism for California 30x30, using Wildlife Insights and BirdNET to process camera and sound data.

name: Callahan Family Foundation
summary: US grant maker recorded in tax filings data on Grantable as funding Earth Species Project.

name: Cape Cod Commercial Fishermen's Alliance
summary: Fishing community organisation on Cape Cod and NFWF grantee developing AI to identify sea scallop reproductive stages from electronic monitoring images.

name: CarbonPlan
summary: A Californian non-profit offering open climate tools and data, it has an open-source near-real-time satellite fire pipeline and reported in August 2023 on monitoring wildfires in California’s forest offsets.

name: Cary Institute of Ecosystem Studies
summary: New York ecosystem research institute that gives financial and logistical support to the Global Lake Ecological Observatory Network's website.

name: Cascadia Research Collective
summary: Non-profit marine mammal research organisation in Washington State whose long-term photo identification work was the test application for Wildbook and whose site lists papers on Happywhale.

name: Catena Foundation
summary: US grant maker recorded in tax filings data on Grantable as funding Global Fishing Watch.

name: Center for Conservation Innovation
summary: Defenders of Wildlife's team applying data science, satellite imagery and AI to habitat monitoring, including detection of solar arrays, oil and gas pads and parking lots.

name: Center for Environmental Engineering, Sensing, and Integrated Modeling, Michigan Technological University
summary: Michigan Technological University Great Lakes centre combining environmental sensing, hybrid physics-AI approaches and data assimilation.

name: Center for Fisheries Electronic Monitoring at Mote
summary: Mote research centre on electronic monitoring of fisheries, including AI projects with CVision AI funded through the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation.

name: Center for Global Soundscapes
summary: Purdue University centre promoting research, education and engagement on soundscapes and their preservation.

name: Center for Invasive Species and Ecosystem Health
summary: University of Georgia centre behind Bugwood and EDDMapS, providing invasive species tools and information.

name: CeruleanAI
summary: AI system built by AVI for Coral Restoration Foundation that processes reef imagery and tracks restoration progress.

name: Chesapeake Bay Land Use/Land Cover and Change Data
summary: High-resolution land use and land cover data for the Chesapeake watershed, used to track tree canopy and change over time.

name: Chesapeake Conservancy
summary: NGO working on the Chesapeake Bay watershed, whose Conservation Innovation Center uses geospatial data science and AI, including a wetlands mapping model and high-resolution land cover data.

name: Chesapeake Monitoring Cooperative
summary: Regional cooperative, launched in 2015, that gathers volunteer water quality and macroinvertebrate data into the public Chesapeake Data Explorer.

name: Chronolog
summary: Photo monitoring project that builds crowd-sourced timelapses of natural areas from visitors' phone photos.

name: CLASlite
summary: The Global Green Monitoring homepage describes converting satellite imagery into greenness maps, detecting deforestation and other vegetation disturbance, and technology developed over 30 years of research.

name: Clean Water Hub
summary: Open US database of volunteer water quality results, used by Save Our Streams and other monitoring groups.

name: Climate Engine
summary: Google Earth Engine based tools for drought and rangeland vegetation data, a collaboration of the Desert Research Institute and UC Merced, used by federal agencies and the Navajo Nation.

name: Coastal Change Analysis Program Regional Land Cover
summary: Nationally consistent satellite-derived land cover time series for US coasts, published through NOAA's Digital Coast.

name: Coca-Cola Foundation
summary: US grant maker recorded in tax filings data on Grantable as funding Conservation X Labs.

name: Colorado Mesa University
summary: US university whose faculty and students led the team that won the XPRIZE Rainforest competition.

name: Colorado Parks and Wildlife
summary: A division of the Colorado Department of Natural Resources that manages about 350 state wildlife areas for the benefit of wildlife and has a mission including the state parks system.

name: Colorado Pika Project
summary: Joint initiative of Rocky Mountain Wild and Denver Zoo Conservation Alliance, including the Pika Patrol app, asking community scientists to record pika observations to show how pikas cope with climate change.

name: Colossal Biosciences
summary: Genetics and biosciences company aimed at saving species, whose computational biology division includes an AI and machine learning team and which says it is funding elephant genome sequencing, to be made public.

name: Columbia River Basin wetland classification
summary: NOAA Fisheries Habitat Conservation project with a Microsoft AI for Good award, using remote sensing and machine learning to classify wetlands and predict effects on salmon.

name: Community Forestry (CommFor) Data Collection App
summary: FLARE network project, running from 2022, to develop a Community Forestry mobile app for monitoring, with a planned release supporting primary data collection and automated downloads of satellite forest data.

name: Comon Solutions
summary: Pacific Grove, California company funded by NSF SBIR to produce high-resolution vegetation maps with image segmentation for natural resource management.

name: Computational Sustainability Network
summary: US National Science Foundation-sponsored research network of thirteen academic institutions led by Cornell University, applying machine learning to conservation, with PAWS anti-poaching patrol routing among its sample projects.

name: Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes
summary: A tribal government whose Natural Resources Department aims to manage, protect and conserve natural resources within the Flathead Indian Reservation and the aboriginal territory.

name: Conservation Biology Institute
summary: Science-based nonprofit whose flagship platform Data Basin gives access to geospatial conservation data.

name: Conservation Innovation Center
summary: Chesapeake Conservancy's geospatial data science and AI team.

name: Conservation Science Partners
summary: Provider of quantitative research and planning services for conservation projects, publishing interactive tools such as one on Mojave desert tortoise trends and threats.

name: Conservation Technology Lab, San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance
summary: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance lab that uses AI and machine learning on trail camera data and publishes open source tools including AniML and MatchyPatchy.

name: Conservify
summary: Company named in FieldKit's privacy policy, with a Los Angeles address, that runs FieldKit and has held FieldSchool workshops from upstate New York to the Amazon since 2023.

name: Consortium of Pacific Northwest Herbaria
summary: Consortium giving an online portal to specimen records and images from herbaria across Pacific Northwest North America.

name: Convective Capital
summary: Venture fund focused on wildfire resilience and climate adaptation technologies, including wildfire early detection.

name: Coral Restoration Foundation
summary: Florida Keys reef restoration nonprofit that built CeruleanAI with AVI to process reef imagery and track restoration progress.

name: Cornell K. Lisa Yang Center for Conservation Bioacoustics
summary: Cornell centre whose research faculty includes Connor Wood. Audubon magazine says BirdNET is managed at Cornell University. The Cornell site refused the fetcher.

name: CrocAlarm
summary: WildlifeOS product for AI detection of crocodiles and alligators in Florida's waterways, offered to communities, municipalities, resorts and conservation organisations.

name: Crossfire
summary: Team in the XPRIZE wildfire competition, including University of Maryland leaders, whose proposed system would use drones and AI for early wildfire detection, reconnaissance and suppression.

name: crowsetta
summary: Python tool for working with animal sound annotation formats, with built-in support for Audacity, Praat and Raven, and conversion of annotations into formats for training machine learning models.

name: CTMM Initiative
summary: Programme around ctmm, an R package that analyses animal tracking data as continuous-time stochastic processes, with Kriging, simulation and home-range estimation, and a page listing AniMove workshops.

name: CVision AI
summary: Machine learning company that works with the Gulf of Maine Research Institute on electronic monitoring video and is a partner in NOAA-funded and NSF-funded ocean imagery work.

name: Cyanobacteria Assessment Network
summary: Multi-agency project building an early warning system that detects algal blooms in US lakes and estuaries from satellite data.

name: CyVerse
summary: NSF-supported open cyberinfrastructure at the University of Arizona, a partner in ESIIL.

name: Data Basin
summary: Geospatial conservation data platform run by the Conservation Biology Institute.

name: Data Diversity Lab
summary: University of Arizona lab led by Cristian Román-Palacios that applies bioinformatics and machine learning to large biological datasets.

name: Data Without Limits
summary: NSF research infrastructure collaborative award at the University of New Mexico on cyberinfrastructure for environmental data.

name: Deep learning algorithms to automate right whale photo identification
summary: NOAA work on algorithms that match right whales from different viewpoints and body parts.

name: Deep learning for American eel in imaging sonar
summary: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory publication on deep learning to detect and identify migrating American eels in imaging sonar data.

name: DeepFire
summary: AI platform built at Louisiana State University combining prediction, satellite detection and spread forecasting, with LSU reporting 96% confirmation of its XPRIZE final-round New South Wales fire reports.

name: DeepRed
summary: AI camera platform from Volant for early detection of forest fires in remote places.

name: DeerLab
summary: Trail camera app that uses its own AI to tag animals in photos, works across brands, maps seasonal movements and lists wildlife biologists among its intended users.

name: Defenders of Wildlife
summary: US wildlife NGO whose Center for Conservation Innovation uses machine learning and satellite imagery to monitor habitat under the Endangered Species Act.

name: Dendra
summary: Platform to retrieve, store, manage and curate environmental data from sensor networks, and the repository for California Sentinel Site weather data.

name: Dendroyka
summary: Madison, Wisconsin company that builds the Landscape land conservation software, which it says hundreds of conservation organisations use, and whose managing partner spent nearly a decade at Groundswell Conservancy.

name: Desert Research Institute
summary: Research institute that, with UC Merced, runs Climate Engine.

name: Diet Declassified
summary: NSF BIO-AI collaborative award using AI-enabled multidimensional analysis of diet, with the University of Chicago and the University of Florida.

name: Digital Ecology Laboratory, University of Texas at Austin
summary: University of Texas at Austin lab founded by Timothy Keitt that combines AI, environmental sensing and spatial analysis to monitor biodiversity.

name: Digital Reefs
summary: NSF Convergence Accelerator project at Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution for a globally coordinated digital platform on coral reefs.

name: DigitalPath
summary: Company behind the camera platform and AI wildfire detection model used by ALERTCalifornia. It set up the subsidiary ALERTWest for the platform.

name: Discover Life
summary: Website offering identification guides, a global mapper and tools to identify species and build maps, with species pages and maps served at large scale.

name: DISTRIB-II: Habitat Suitability of Eastern United States Trees
summary: Forest Service model of habitat suitability for 125 eastern US tree species under current and projected climates.

name: DoD AKN Portal
summary: US Department of Defense portal for the Avian Knowledge Network, for bird data on military lands.

name: DrawerDissect
summary: Software that turns a single image of an insect drawer into individual specimen images with structured metadata, using computer vision and large language models.

name: Drone Amplified
summary: The Lincoln, Nebraska company offers IGNIS, a prescribed-fire drone system originating in a University of Nebraska–Lincoln lab, and D.A. Flight software used by researchers to survey whales.

name: Ducks Unlimited
summary: Waterfowl conservation NGO whose geospatial team uses remote sensing and machine learning to map wetlands in North America and publishes spatial data.

name: Dunn Family Charitable Foundation
summary: US grant maker recorded in tax filings data on Grantable as funding Conservation X Labs.

name: Dynamic Habitat Indices
summary: Satellite indices for biodiversity science and conservation from Terra, Aqua, Suomi NPP and JPSS data, presented by Volker Radeloff of the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

name: Earth Discovery Institute
summary: A US non-profit restoring native habitats across San Diego County, including 15 acres of cactus scrub at El Monte Ecological Preserve, where it reports detecting bats through acoustic monitoring.

name: Earth Lab
summary: Data synthesis centre at CU Boulder, part of CIRES, that uses big data and AI to help society understand and adapt to environmental change.

name: Earth PBC
summary: Company that says its AI platform combines Planet Labs satellite imagery with community ground-truth reports to monitor forest carbon, and lists deforestation monitoring and illegal fishing prevention among its uses.

name: Earthrise Media
summary: Organisation that runs satellite-based investigations for environmental reporting, co-founded by Edward Boyda, and supported by the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation.

name: EarthSenseAI Center
summary: 501(c)(3) non-profit that aims to make AI usable for scientists and government agencies with little AI training, for ocean health and conservation.

name: Earthshot Labs
summary: Sebastopol, California public benefit company building an ecosystem forecasting platform for reforestation, with NSF SBIR funding, and a phone app using computer vision to measure trees.

name: East West Technical Services
summary: NOAA-approved at-sea and electronic monitoring provider for Northeast groundfish sectors in 2026.

name: Echidna terrestrial lidar
summary: Terrestrial lidar instrument built by CSIRO that records vegetation structure and, combined with airborne and spaceborne lidar, is meant to support large-area maps of vegetation structure and carbon stocks.

name: Echopype
summary: Open software package for interoperable, scalable processing of water column sonar data.

name: Echospace at the University of Washington
summary: University of Washington research group in Seattle that combines physics-based models with data-driven methods on ocean acoustic data, studies echolocating bats and toothed whales, and develops open-source software.

name: ECO-Drone
summary: Educational and outreach programme, run by oceans-unmanned, that develops and communicates best practices for reducing resource disturbance from drones.

name: EcoCast
summary: NOAA operational tool that uses boosted regression trees to model swordfish and bycatch species in the California Current.

name: ecoEXPLORE
summary: Run and built by the North Carolina Arboretum, this K–8 community science programme accepts wildlife observations from anywhere, with staff reviewing them and submitting approved records to iNaturalist.

name: Ecological Forecasting Initiative
summary: Community for ecological forecasting that holds an annual conference and runs the NEON Ecological Forecasting Challenge.

name: Ecosonus
summary: Start-up incubated at Harvard Innovation Labs that designs passive acoustic monitoring systems combining sensors, satellite data and AI, focused on the Amazon and other biodiversity hotspots.

name: ECosystem Analytics and Intelligence Laboratory, University of Wisconsin-Madison
summary: University of Wisconsin-Madison lab formed in January 2026 working on knowledge-guided machine learning for agricultural and natural ecosystems, including wetland methane emissions.

name: Ecosystem Management Decision Support System
summary: Forest Service spatial decision support system for landscape analysis and planning, listed with machine learning in the federal AI inventory.

name: Ecosystem Planning & Restoration
summary: Founded in 2012, the small company restores eastern US and Gulf Coast ecosystems, co-created the Stream Quantification Tool in 2016 and lists machine learning services.

name: EDDMapS
summary: Web-based mapping system for invasive species and pest distribution, launched in 2005 by the University of Georgia's Center for Invasive Species and Ecosystem Health.

name: eDNA Collaborative
summary: Programme based at the University of Washington's School of Marine and Environmental Affairs that aims to make environmental DNA analysis routine worldwide, developing cheaper methods and focusing on underrepresented countries.

name: Elder Research
summary: Recipient of a NOAA small business award for HABSSED, harmful algal bloom surveillance by environmental DNA sequencing.

name: Electric Power Research Institute
summary: Energy research institute that worked with PNNL on machine learning to identify migrating eels in sonar data.

name: Electronic Monitoring and Reporting Grant Program
summary: Joint NOAA and National Fish and Wildlife Foundation grant programme for electronic technologies in US fisheries. Its 2025 slate funded work on AI tools for processing fisheries data.

name: Elephant Detection (ArcGIS pretrained model)
summary: Pretrained ArcGIS deep learning model, first released in May 2022, that detects elephants in 3–13 cm aerial imagery using FasterRCNN and reports an average precision of 0.857.

name: Elkhorn Slough Foundation
summary: A land trust that the Land Trust Alliance directory lists as owning 3,611 acres.

name: eMammal
summary: Smithsonian camera trap database that archives SNAPSHOT USA data.

name: EnviroAtlas
summary: EPA data portal publishing ecosystem and environmental datasets as web services, including hydrology and land cover layers.

name: Environmental AI Cluster, University of Georgia
summary: University of Georgia presidential faculty hiring initiative of seven posts in environmental AI.

name: Environmental Data Initiative
summary: NSF-funded repository for long-term environmental data.

name: Environmental Data Science Innovation & Impact Lab
summary: NSF synthesis centre led by the University of Colorado Boulder with CyVerse at the University of Arizona and the University of Oslo, enabling environmental data scientists to use emerging analytics.

name: Environmental Defense Fund
summary: US environmental NGO with more than 3 million members. Developed SmartPass, using shore cameras and AI to count fishing vessels.

name: Environmental Policy Innovation Center
summary: US policy nonprofit working on environmental technology adoption. It published a report on AI in government and nonprofit environmental work and is funded by the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation.

name: Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center for Data Science & Environment at Berkeley
summary: Launched in 2022, the UC Berkeley college partnership develops AI models for animal calls, has an open-source Jupyter Bioacoustic toolkit and works with California’s wildlife department to expand Soundhub.

name: Everglades Wildlife Watch
summary: Zooniverse project of the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission using trail cameras across south Florida wildlife management areas, with work on integrating AI machine learning.

name: EWHALE Lab
summary: Laboratory working on wildlife ecology and predictive GIS modelling with machine learning and artificial intelligence.

name: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Biodiversity Science and Conservation
summary: NSF award on explainable AI for extinction and species status prediction, at Oklahoma State University.

name: Eyes on Kelp
summary: Three-year kelp monitoring initiative across 14 index sites in the southern Salish Sea, using dive surveys, robotic monitoring and shared data.

name: Fathom Resources
summary: Rhode Island marine service company and NFWF grantee developing AI-assisted electronic monitoring video review for New England groundfish.

name: Fathom Science
summary: NC State University spin-off building AI-powered ocean digital twins, with fisheries and conservation among its uses.

name: FathomVerse
summary: Mobile app that grows a library of labelled ocean imagery to train AI to identify marine life, created by MBARI, Monterey Bay Aquarium and FathomNet collaborators.

name: Field Museum
summary: US natural history museum listed as an institutional member of Biodiversity Information Standards (TDWG).

name: FieldKit
summary: Open firmware and hardware sensor project, run by conservify, that measures water and weather variables and began in 2016 from a network built for National Geographic's Okavango Wilderness Project.

name: Fire Sentry
summary: Planned geostationary infrared satellite system from Orbital Sentry for persistent monitoring of wildfire across the western United States.

name: Fish and Climate Change Database
summary: Interior Department database that uses natural language processing to automate parts of its literature review.

name: Fish Detection AI
summary: Sonar image models from the US Department of Energy, including a Faster R-CNN trained on Alaska Fish and Game sonar images, to identify, track and count fish.

name: Fish movement in restored coastal wetlands using imaging sonar and machine learning
summary: Interior Department work using machine learning on imaging sonar data to see how fish use restored Great Lakes wetlands.

name: Fisheries Electronic Monitoring Library
summary: NOAA central repository for electronic monitoring data on marine life, listed as in planning or development.

name: FishEye

name: Fishtechy
summary: Small business whose AI phone app measures and weighs anglers' catch, with a research agreement with NOAA's Southwest Fisheries Science Center to relay data to managers.

name: FLARE Network
summary: Network with its secretariat at the University of Notre Dame’s Keough School of Global Affairs that runs CommFor to collect community forestry data across countries.

name: Florida Museum of Natural History
summary: University of Florida natural history museum listed as a TDWG member, whose Soltis lab co-authored deep learning work on herbarium specimens.

name: Florida Wildlife Watch
summary: Zooniverse project of the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission in which volunteers classify trail camera photos, with a stated aim of integrating AI.

name: Fluvial Fish Native Distributions for the Conterminous United States
summary: Interior Department species distribution models for 271 river fish species using boosted regression trees.

name: Flywire Cameras
summary: NOAA-approved electronic monitoring provider for Northeast groundfish sectors in 2026.

name: For the Fishes
summary: A non-profit dedicated to protecting coral reef wildlife, with a postal address in Kihei, Hawaii, and an online tool called Tank Watch for identifying captive-bred fish.

name: Forest Change Analysis Lab
summary: Forest disturbance and data science lab that maps forests at individual tree level with drones, photogrammetry and computer vision.

name: Forest Health Detection Monitoring
summary: Forest Service work using machine learning to upscale field and high-resolution data and map stages of forest mortality and defoliation.

name: Forest Inventory and Analysis
summary: USDA Forest Service research and development programme and national forest inventory, which with the Forest Service Geospatial Office maintains the National Tree Canopy Cover dataset.

name: FOSSA (Free and Open Source Software for Acoustics)
summary: Free and open-source tools under development by NOAA researchers, currently comprising the R packages PAMpal and BANTER, for passive acoustic analysis and machine learning classification.

name: Functional biodiversity through seasonal camouflage
summary: NSF Biodiversity on a Changing Planet award studying seasonally colour-moulting species, with North Carolina State University among the collaborators.

name: Funga
summary: Austin public benefit corporation using soil DNA sequencing and machine learning to identify native microbes, reporting forest fungal restoration and expecting Verra’s carbon methodology approval later in 2026.

name: Gaia AI
summary: Somerville, Massachusetts forestry data company combining below-canopy, above-canopy and satellite sensors with machine learning for forest inventories.

name: Gazelle Ecosolutions
summary: Applied science lab combining remote sensing and ecology for carbon and biodiversity credits, which says it is building a grassland biomass dataset and partnered with Modisa in 2022 on Botswana's first nature-based carbon project.

name: GBIF-US
summary: The US node of the Global Biodiversity Information Facility, managed by the USGS Science Analytics and Synthesis Program with NSF funding. BISON provided the foundation for its current form.

name: GeoAI toolset for salt marsh pond collapse
summary: NSF award for a GeoAI toolset that identifies locations and drivers of pond collapse in salt marshes from high-resolution imagery.

name: George Mason University
summary: US university whose biology professor David Luther leads a study at the Biological Dynamics of Forest Fragments Project in the Amazon, which trained AI models to detect bird songs in acoustic recordings.

name: Global Earth Observation & Dynamics of Ecosystems Lab
summary: Northern Arizona University lab using remote sensing and machine learning to study ecological patterns at several scales.

name: Global Inland Fisheries Risk Index
summary: Interior Department index using boosted regression trees to map threats to inland fisheries globally.

name: Global Names Architecture
summary: System of web services and databases that registers, finds, checks and cross-links the scientific names of organisms.

name: Godwit Key Company
summary: San Diego company building a marketplace platform for biodiversity credits supporting species conservation, with NSF SBIR funding.

name: Great Lakes Fishery Commission
summary: Commission whose project catalogue includes a smart panel project to detect attached sea lamprey, led from Michigan State University.

name: Great Lakes Observing System
summary: Great Lakes observing organisation whose strategic plan commits to AI and machine learning for models and predictive tools, and which runs the Smart Great Lakes initiative.

name: Greater Yellowstone Inventory & Monitoring Network
summary: A monitoring network that tracks seven natural resource vital signs of park health, including amphibian and wetland, land cover and land use, and whitebark pine monitoring.

name: Green Crossing AI
summary: Research project at Southern Oregon University developing computer vision methods for wildlife monitoring, originating in a wildlife crossing proposal on Interstate 5.

name: Greenbridge Family Foundation
summary: US grant maker recorded in tax filings data on Grantable as funding Conservation X Labs.

name: GreenInfo Network
summary: Non-profit technology organisation that helps public interest groups with GIS and created the Land Trust GIS primer.

name: GrizCam
summary: Wildlife camera that records 360-degree video with audio, used near Yellowstone wolf den sites and planned for tribal lands in Idaho associated with the Nez Perce Tribe.

name: Grizzly Systems
summary: Montana company that developed GrizCam, a camera recording 360-degree video and audio.

name: Gulf Coast Inventory & Monitoring Network
summary: A monitoring network, run by the NPS Inventory and Monitoring Division, whose staff design monitoring around top vital signs and write data protocols, with field crews monitoring amphibians at Jean Lafitte National Park.

name: Gulf Fisheries Research Foundation
summary: NFWF grantee funded to build a six-vessel monitoring fleet in the Gulf charter headboat fishery. The project will use AI video processing to quantify reef-fish catch and discards.

name: Gulf of Maine Research Institute
summary: Maine research institute that launched a Maximized Retention Electronic Monitoring programme for groundfish vessels and works with CVision AI and Integrated Monitoring on machine learning for deck video.

name: Gulf of Maine Ventures
summary: Innovation arm of the Gulf of Maine Research Institute, supporting early-stage ocean companies.

name: Habitat Patrol
summary: Defenders of Wildlife app letting the public run automated change detection in areas of interest in the United States.

name: Happywhale
summary: Citizen science platform for marine mammal photo identification, with an AI image recognition algorithm for humpback whale flukes.

name: Harbor Branch Oceanographic Institute
summary: Oceanographic institute at Florida Atlantic University whose researchers developed a machine learning framework to detect shell-crushing feeding sounds underwater.

name: Hardshell Labs
summary: Joshua Tree, California company funded by NSF SBIR for internet-connected devices for wildlife research, management and monitoring.

name: Harte Research Institute
summary: Institute at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi that works with partners on early detection of harmful algal blooms using AI models and underwater imaging.

name: Hawaii Department of Land and Natural Resources
summary: A state department with jurisdiction over nearly 1.3 million acres of State lands, beaches and coastal waters, whose forestry and wildlife division manages over a million acres.

name: Hawk Migration Association of North America
summary: Runs HawkCount, its system to collect, archive, visualise and distribute raptor migration counts. Its own sites refused us, so this comes from Raptor Population Index reports.

name: Hawk Mountain Sanctuary
summary: A sanctuary whose scientists and volunteers have recorded the annual migration past North Lookout since 1934, counting raptors and other migrants and mapping natural history sightings in a database.

name: Hopper-Dean Foundation
summary: US grant maker recorded in tax filings data on Grantable as funding Conservation X Labs.

name: Hualapai Tribe
summary: Tribal nation in northwest Arizona with a land base of over a million acres, using lidar in natural resource management.

name: Hubbard Brook LTER
summary: A research programme studying forest and aquatic ecosystems, designated an NSF Long-Term Ecological Research site in 1988, led by Peter Groffman and producing a long continuous database.

name: Human-in-the-loop AI for ground-dwelling arthropods
summary: NSF BIO-AI award for high-throughput automated identification of ground-dwelling arthropods, at the University of Arkansas with collaborators.

name: i of the Elephant
summary: App built by biologists-without-borders that lets anyone report illegal ivory sales, with reports shown on a map and possibly passed to wildlife authorities.

name: iBeaver
summary: Web app published in May 2021, built by the Center for Conservation Innovation, that records observation locations and asks survey-style questions to understand beaver distribution.

name: Ice seal and polar bear aerial survey AI
summary: NOAA Alaska Fisheries Science Center project building AI models, with Microsoft, Xnor and Kitware, to detect ice seals and polar bears in colour and thermal imagery during aerial surveys.

name: Ice seal detection and species classification in multispectral aerial imagery
summary: NOAA detection and classification pipelines for ice seals in aerial imagery.

name: iDigBio
summary: Integrated Digitized Biocollections, the NSF-funded national coordinating body for digitising US biodiversity collections, at the University of Florida, Florida State University and Arizona State University.

name: IDTReeS (Integrating Data science with Trees and Remote Sensing)
summary: Project funded by the National Science Foundation that combines remote sensing, surveys and data science to study forests, and has published tree crown detection work including the DeepForest package.

name: Illinois Natural History Survey
summary: US state natural history survey listed as an institutional member of TDWG.

name: iMapInvasives
summary: Online all-taxa invasive species database and mapping tool, listed by SciStarter.

name: Indigenous Sentinels Network
summary: Tribally owned programme with its roots in the Aleut Community of St. Paul Island's monitoring work, bringing technology-based monitoring to Indigenous communities.

name: INSECT NET
summary: Penn State programme whose activities include AI tools for biodiversity workshops and student entries to the Nittany AI Challenge such as bioWatch, an insect detection app.

name: INSTINCT
summary: AI program from NOAA's Marine Mammal Laboratory that detects and identifies marine mammal calls in underwater recordings from Alaska waters, released as open source.

name: Integrated Monitoring
summary: Company partnering with the Gulf of Maine Research Institute on machine learning for electronic monitoring of fishing vessels.

name: IntelliReefs
summary: With an Austin, Texas address and a reef restoration division dating to 2017, it deployed its first reef prototypes at three sites off Cole Bay, Sint Maarten.

name: InvestEGGator
summary: Decoy egg with a GPS-GSM tracker, built by paso-pacifico, placed in real nests to map smuggling routes in Central America, and a prize winner in 2016 and 2017.

name: Ishmael
summary: Open-access bioacoustic analysis software that the BON in a Box catalogue describes as one of the most widely used, covering recording, localisation, beamforming and call recognition.

name: Izaak Walton League of America
summary: US conservation group behind Save Our Streams, a volunteer stream monitoring programme founded in 1969, and the Clean Water Hub water quality database.

name: Jackson Hole Land Trust
summary: A land trust that the Land Trust Alliance directory lists as owning 490 acres.

name: Jaia Robotics
summary: Its low-cost aquatic drones use open-source software and include JaiaBot-PAM, which records marine mammals with a hydrophone, and a version that collects water samples for genomic analysis.

name: Jin Lab, University of California Davis
summary: Remote sensing and ecosystem change lab that uses machine learning on satellite imagery, including deep learning mapping of woody vegetation in California.

name: Journey North
summary: Crowdsourced programme of the University of Wisconsin-Madison Arboretum tracking migration and seasonal change, with monarch and hummingbird records published as open data packages.

name: Kansas State University
summary: US university where Brian Spiesman leads AI identification of bumble bees.

name: Karuk Tribe
summary: A tribal government whose Department of Natural Resources works to protect and restore the Tribe's ancestral lands, waters and natural and cultural resources.

name: Kauaʻi Endangered Seabird Recovery Project
summary: Project using acoustic recorders on Kauaʻi to model powerline collisions of Newell's Shearwater and Hawaiian Petrels, with data analysed by Conservation Metrics.

name: Kelp Quest
summary: Seattle Aquarium project on Zooniverse in which volunteers classify ROV image patches of the seafloor, alongside a model trained in CoralNet-Toolbox.

name: Kelpwatch
summary: Open-source web map of kelp forest canopy from Baja California northwards, using machine learning on nearly 40 years of Landsat data.

name: Keystone Climate
summary: The company says it uses AI and remote sensing to anticipate watershed-level risks, measures supply-chain water risk, land-use change, pollution and biodiversity impact, and supports nature-related reporting, including TNFD.

name: KiloCam
summary: Affordable ecological monitoring camera, with public code and documentation, designed for a GoPro Hero4 underwater housing and used on reefs, streams, tidal flats and bird nests.

name: Kitware
summary: Software company that develops AI and computer vision systems, including work for NOAA on automated image analysis of marine life.

name: Klamath Bird Observatory
summary: A bird observatory whose Pacific Crest Trail No. 1 monitoring station was due to turn 25 in May 2017, reporting MAPS data contributions in April 2017.

name: Konza Prairie LTER
summary: A long-term ecological research site led by Jesse Nippert, one of six original LTER sites, maintaining more than 128 long-term datasets, some over 40 years old.

name: Konza woody encroachment mapping
summary: Kansas State University research using remote sensing and machine learning to map shrub and tree spread into grassland, with aerial work over the Konza Prairie.

name: Kurma AI
summary: San Francisco start-up using generative AI and computer vision for aquaculture operations and against illegal fishing.

name: Lab-on-a-Fish
summary: Biotelemetry sensor built by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory that combines edge computing with wireless sensing of fish physiology and environment, validated in rainbow trout, white sturgeon and walleye.

name: Land Change Analysis Tool
summary: USDA tool that uses a learning classifier to produce high resolution land cover maps from aerial or satellite imagery and publishes them as an image service.

name: Land Trust Alliance
summary: Membership body for US land trusts that, with the California chapter of The Nature Conservancy, has run a grant programme helping land trusts take up remote monitoring.

name: LANDFIRE
summary: US programme publishing vegetation, fuel and disturbance data products.

name: LandPulse
summary: Tool that turns satellite imagery into stand inventory, forest health detection, wetland mapping and disturbance history for any parcel in the continental US.

name: Landscape Change Monitoring System
summary: USDA Forest Service dataset of annual landscape change, land cover and land use for the United States, built from an ensemble of remote sensing models.

name: Landscape Ecology & Ecosystem Science Lab
summary: Michigan State University lab studying carbon, water and energy fluxes in terrestrial ecosystems through field work, remote sensing, modelling and AI.

name: Landscape Land Conservation Software
summary: Web and mobile app, built and run by dendroyka, covering conservation work from acquisition to stewardship, including annual monitoring and field species observations.

name: Landseed
summary: Delaware public benefit corporation that builds sensors and drones measuring biodiversity, water, soil and air, feeding a live digital twin of each landscape.

name: Landseed AI

name: Learning to See the Forest and the Trees
summary: University of Washington eScience project building open methods to automate forest mapping for non-industrial landowners in Oregon and Washington.

name: Leon Levy Foundation
summary: US foundation named as a funder of BirdCast.

name: Lesmeister Wildlife Ecology Lab
summary: US Forest Service wildlife ecology lab in Corvallis, Oregon, led by Damon Lesmeister and partnered with Oregon State University, that uses passive acoustic monitoring for northern spotted owls.

name: Leviathan
summary: Company building coastal observatories and the LeviathanOS software that joins acoustic, visual and vessel tracks. Its first observatory is at MBARI in Moss Landing, California.

name: Lidar Applications for the Study of Ecosystems with Remote Sensing Laboratory
summary: Texas A&M University laboratory developing algorithms and tools for lidar and multi-sensor data on forest structure and biomass.

name: Lincoln Park Zoo
summary: Chicago zoo whose Urban Wildlife Institute runs camera monitoring stations across the region, with Zooniverse volunteers classifying images in Chicago Wildlife Watch.

name: Listening Observatory for Hawaiian Ecosystems
summary: UH Hilo lab founded by Patrick Hart that analyses forest sound recordings with AI to monitor Hawaiian forest birds.

name: Little Traverse Conservancy
summary: A land trust that the Land Trust Alliance directory lists as owning 22,736 acres.

name: Living Carbon
summary: The company aims to combine precision tree breeding with marginal-land reforestation, is reforesting former mine land in West Virginia and is developing a five-site former cropland project in Ohio.

name: Lockwood Lab
summary: Rutgers research group that uses AI and machine learning models, evidence synthesis and environmental DNA to describe, track and conserve biodiversity.

name: Long Live the Kings
summary: Salmon recovery NGO that uses AI and machine learning to calibrate a 3D ecosystem model of Puget Sound, with a Microsoft AI for Good award.

name: Long Term Ecological Research Network
summary: US network of long-term ecological research sites with a network office that funds synthesis working groups.

name: Louisiana Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority
summary: A state authority that is designing a project to restore 13 miles of the Chandeleur barrier island chain and leads a wider ongoing effort to adapt Louisiana's coast, including the 2023 Coastal Master Plan.

name: Louisiana State University
summary: A university based in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.

name: Machine learning for biodiversity patterns from passive acoustic sampling
summary: NSF award at Furman University using machine learning on passive acoustic data to study biodiversity patterns.

name: Maine Coast Heritage Trust
summary: Founded in 1970 to protect Maine’s coast, this land trust lists 168 public preserves and reports conserving over 200,000 acres and protecting over 300 islands with partners.

name: Makepath
summary: Geospatial and AI software firm that built a conservation easement monitoring platform with ORBO Systems. Its own site refuses the fetcher.

name: MapHubs
summary: Technology company founded in 2017 that provides software and services for monitoring natural resources, and runs palmoil-io.

name: Mapping Application for Penguin Populations and Projected Dynamics
summary: Open-access continent-wide database of Antarctic penguin data, developed by Oceanites with the Lynch Lab at Stony Brook University and supported by NASA.

name: Marauder Robotics
summary: Named partner on Eyes on Kelp, developing and field-testing robotic monitoring technology with The Bay Foundation.

name: Marine Applied Research and Exploration
summary: Richmond, California group documenting deep water ecosystems with deep diving robotic submarines to assist their conservation and management.

name: Marine Mammal Laboratory
summary: NOAA Fisheries laboratory in the Alaska Fisheries Science Center that runs a passive acoustic mooring array in Alaska waters and develops AI for whale calls and aerial seal surveys.

name: Marine Observer
summary: Maritime infrared camera and AI software system from Toyon Research for detecting marine mammals.

name: Marine Robotics and Remote Sensing Lab
summary: Lab at Duke University's Nicholas School of the Environment using satellites, drones and AI on marine species including the North Atlantic right whale, and generating synthetic training images of rare whales.

name: MarineVERSE
summary: NASA-funded Marine Biodiversity and Scaling Project presented by the University of Miami.

name: MarVivo
summary: A limited liability company aiming to protect marine biodiversity hotspots, it lists the Magdalena Bay Blue Carbon Project first and says it preserves 22,000 hectares of mangroves.

name: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
summary: A state department that reports the acreage of land it owns by unit type, such as State Parks and State Forests.

name: Mast Reforestation
summary: Post-fire reforestation and carbon removal company.

name: Maui Himalayan ginger detection
summary: The Nature Conservancy's use of machine learning on Maui to find and track invasive Himalayan ginger, reported by Fortune in 2022.

name: Maui Nui Marine Resource Council
summary: Maui non-profit using AI and drone technology with Australian start-up Flying Fish Technologies to survey reefs off Lāhainā after the 2023 wildfire.

name: Maximized Retention Electronic Monitoring
summary: Electronic monitoring model for New England groundfish vessels with a dockside monitoring component, approved by NOAA Fisheries under Amendment 23 in January 2023, with machine learning under development for deck video.

name: Meridian Institute
summary: Closed nonprofit, named as secretariat of the Lacuna Fund, which pays for labelled datasets for machine learning in low and middle income settings. The fund says it moved its leadership and management to other partners in July 2025.

name: Michigan Department of Natural Resources
summary: State agency reported by Hoodline to be testing about 200 trail cameras for elk surveys, with MegaDetector and Wildlife Insights. The agency's own release refused us by robots.txt.

name: Michigan Nature Association
summary: A land trust that the Land Trust Alliance directory lists as owning 11,555 acres.

name: Michigan Tech Research Institute
summary: Michigan Technological University research institute offering remote sensing web applications, including harmful algal bloom and water quality products for the Great Lakes from 2013.

name: Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District
summary: An independent special district that preserves a greenbelt of more than 70,000 acres of public open space.

name: Midwest Invasive Species Information Network
summary: Regional platform for invasive species records across the Midwest United States, with verification and mapping tools, run by a Michigan State University lab.

name: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources
summary: State agency whose Ecological and Water Resources Division has a funded work plan to train an AI model to detect beaver dams and wetlands for the National Wetlands Inventory.

name: Mohonk Preserve
summary: A nonprofit preserve that protects and manages over 8,200 acres of ridges, forests, fields and streams, and describes itself as New York's largest nonprofit nature preserve.

name: Mojave Desert Inventory & Monitoring Network
summary: A long-term monitoring network tracking vital signs in park resources, focused on water, vegetation and landscape-scale weather and climate, including early detection of invasive plants.

name: Monarch Joint Venture
summary: National nonprofit coordinating three monarch monitoring programmes, including the Monarch Larva Monitoring Project with volunteer data since 1997.

name: Monitor My Watershed
summary: Data portal for sharing do-it-yourself environmental monitoring data, hosting EnviroDIY sensor data and Leaf Pack Network macroinvertebrate data.

name: Monitoring Avian Productivity and Survivorship
summary: A continent-wide network of constant-effort mist-netting stations, run by the Institute for Bird Populations, where more than 1,400 stations have operated for at least one year since 1989.

name: Montana Fish, Wildlife and Parks
summary: A state agency whose Wildlife Management Areas are managed with wildlife and habitat conservation as the priority.

name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
summary: California aquarium that is MBARI's education and conservation partner on FathomVerse.

name: Morphological Barcoding
summary: NSF BIO-AI award for a machine learning approach to the taxonomic impediment, at Tulane University.

name: Mote Marine Laboratory & Aquarium
summary: Sarasota, Florida marine laboratory whose Center for Fisheries Electronic Monitoring uses AI for catch detection in the Gulf of Mexico reef fish fishery.

name: Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority
summary: A public authority that manages more than 75,000 acres of parkland, either owned by it or owned by the Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy.

name: Multi-Resolution Land Characteristics Consortium
summary: Group of US federal agencies that coordinate and generate national land cover information, including the National Land Cover Database.

name: Museum of Southwestern Biology
summary: University of New Mexico museum holding specimen collections that include amphibians, reptiles, arthropods and birds.

name: Mushroom Observer
summary: Website run by Mushroom Observer, Inc. for recording mushroom observations and getting help identifying them, published as an open dataset through GBIF.

name: MyCoPortal
summary: Web portal for fungal biodiversity data from a network of universities, gardens, museums and agencies, built on Symbiota.

name: Mycota Lab
summary: Non-profit DNA laboratory working towards a biodiversity survey of North American macrofungi, at the core of the MycoMap network.

name: NABIT (Nucleic Acid Barcode Identification Tool)
summary: Handheld DNA analysis device built by conservation-x-labs that reports within 10 to 20 minutes, from a small water sample, whether an animal has been present.

name: Nalaquq UAV salmon counts
summary: Local Yup'ik technicians use drones to count salmon on rivers near Quinhagak, Alaska.

name: Nalaquq, LLC
summary: Subsidiary of the Alaska Native-owned Qanirtuuq Incorporated, based in Quinhagak, that trains local Yup'ik technicians to count salmon by drone.

name: NanoDetector
summary: Open-source on-device camera trap model and device that identifies animals to species across 25 classes, working with MegaDetector and sending detections over satellite. Developed with the WHISL project under NSF award 2317537.

name: NASA Catalyst Preserve Project
summary: Collaboration led by NASA JPL with The Nature Conservancy, UC Santa Barbara and Columbia University using hyperspectral imaging and machine learning for biodiversity management at preserves in California.

name: National Center for Biotechnology Information
summary: US public genetic data body that publishes RefSeq targeted loci sets and NCBI Taxonomy through GBIF. Its own site refused us.

name: National Centers for Environmental Information
summary: NOAA's environmental data archive, holding more than 60 petabytes.

name: National Data Platform
summary: US data platform working with the California Sentinel Site Network on a single species occurrence database across sensors.

name: National Fish and Wildlife Foundation
summary: US conservation funder whose grants library lists fisheries technology grants, including a project testing machine learning software for dockside monitoring.

name: National Land Cover Database
summary: Public domain national land cover dataset for the US, published through the MRLC consortium, with a tree canopy cover layer from the USDA Forest Service.

name: National Marine Sanctuary Foundation
summary: Silver Spring, Maryland foundation that funded restoration and monitoring at Coral Restoration Foundation, per Kindora.

name: National Park Service
summary: US federal protected-area agency. Its Natural Sounds and Night Skies Division uses BirdNET to study bird sound in parks and its Inventory and Monitoring Division runs long-term ecological monitoring.

name: National Tree Canopy Cover
summary: US tree canopy dataset built by the USDA Forest Service Geospatial Office and Forest Inventory and Analysis as part of the National Land Cover Database.

name: National Wetlands Inventory
summary: US Fish and Wildlife Service dataset of the extent, approximate location and type of wetlands and deepwater habitats in the US and its territories.

name: Natural Resources Conservancy
summary: Land trust for landowners that worked with ORBO Systems and Makepath on a platform combining satellite imagery and AI to monitor conservation easements.

name: Navajo Nation
summary: Tribal nation listed by Climate Engine among the bodies that use or support its environmental data tools.

name: NCEI Passive Acoustic Data Archive
summary: NOAA archive of underwater passive acoustic recordings that capture fish, marine mammals, ambient and human-made noise.

name: Nearview
summary: US small business with a NOAA SBIR Phase II award for an AI model to detect and map intertidal vegetation.

name: NeMO-Net
summary: NASA Ames citizen science game and neural network in which players classify corals to train a global coral map.

name: NEON Ecological Forecasting Challenge
summary: Open forecasting challenge built on NEON data, documented by the Ecological Forecasting Initiative, also used in classes.

name: Neotoma Paleoecology Database
summary: Community palaeoecology database.

name: New England Aquarium
summary: Boston aquarium that curates the North Atlantic Right Whale Catalog used to identify individual whales.

name: New England Marine Monitoring
summary: Electronic monitoring services company for New England fishermen, providing video review, vessel technical support and programme design.

name: New Venture Fund
summary: US grant maker recorded in tax filings data on Grantable as funding Conservation X Labs.

name: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
summary: New York's state agency that manages wildlife and is a partner in the Snapshot NY trail camera survey.

name: Next Generation Fire System
summary: NOAA system that uses AI to scan GOES satellite imagery, detect wildfires and track their spread and intensity.

name: Nez Perce Tribe
summary: Tribal nation in Idaho where Colossal has committed to a pilot network of GrizCam units on associated tribal lands. The page does not say whether the tribe runs the pilot.

name: Nisqually Indian Tribe
summary: A tribal government whose Department of Natural Resources maintains native lands and waterways important to fish, plants and wildlife.

name: Niwot Ridge LTER
summary: A long-term ecological research site established in 1980 and led by Nancy Emery, studying plant phenology, species composition, small mammal herbivores and climate change effects on Colorado tundra.

name: NOAA Automated Image Analysis Strategic Initiative
summary: NOAA initiative that co-developed the VIAME computer vision toolkit with Kitware. NOAA's own pages could not be read, so this rests on Kitware's account.

name: NOAA Center for Artificial Intelligence
summary: NOAA's internal centre and community of practice for AI and machine learning in mission science, running an annual AI workshop.

name: NOAA Deep Sea Coral Research and Technology Program
summary: Federal research programme on deep-sea corals and sponges, offering a national coral and sponge database for download.

name: NOAA Fisheries
summary: US federal fisheries agency whose feature stories describe the use of AI on video surveys. Entries already linked to this id had no record behind it.

name: NOAA Small Business Innovation Research Program
summary: NOAA grants to small businesses across topic areas including the blue economy, omics, AI and uncrewed systems.

name: Nocturnal Bird Flight Calls of North America
summary: Reference dataset of nocturnal flight calls of North American birds from remote recordings, with initial calls from Nova Scotia stations, and identifications stated to be putative and possibly wrong.

name: Normandeau Associates
summary: Environmental firm offering the ATOM system for remotely tracking wildlife.

name: North American Bat Monitoring Program
summary: Nationwide repository of bat occurrence records. USGS pages describing it could not be read, so its operator is left open here.

name: North Atlantic Right Whale Catalog
summary: Photo catalogue of individual North Atlantic right whales, against which NOAA and others match new photographs.

name: North Carolina Zoo
summary: State zoo named among the organisations on the SMART conservation tools partnership page.

name: Northeastern University
summary: US university whose Roux Institute and Institute for Experiential AI co-run the Blue w(AI)ve ocean AI accelerator, and which houses the Ocean Genome Legacy Center.

name: Northern Arizona University
summary: Flagstaff university that hosts the PhenoCam Network.

name: NPS Inventory and Monitoring Division
summary: Servicewide National Park Service programme running natural resource inventories and long-term ecological monitoring in park sites.

name: NPS Natural Sounds and Night Skies Division
summary: National Park Service division that helps parks with noise and light pollution and uses automated detectors and BirdNET for bird monitoring.

name: NSF AI and Geosciences
summary: NSF funding programme for AI in the geosciences, whose awards include marine ecosystem modelling.

name: NSF BIO-AI
summary: NSF Biological Sciences awards labelled BIO-AI, covering AI for taxonomy, arthropod identification and ecological cyberinfrastructure.

name: NSF Convergence Accelerator
summary: NSF programme funding use-driven projects, including TealWaters on wetlands and Digital Reefs on coral reefs.

name: Nucleic Sensing Systems
summary: Makes autonomous, web-connected biosensors that report environmental DNA and RNA data in real time, described by the organisation as a genetic smoke alarm for species of concern.

name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory DAAC
summary: NASA Earthdata archive centre hosted at Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

name: OBIS-USA
summary: US node of the Ocean Biodiversity Information System. Its marine biological occurrence data are archived by NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information.

name: Ocean Aero
summary: Gulfport, Mississippi company teamed with ThayerMahan and the Allen Institute for AI on detection of illegal fishing, and a Schmidt Marine partner.

name: Ocean Alliance
summary: Whale research nonprofit in Gloucester, Massachusetts, known for the SnotBot drones that collect whale breath samples. Its own site refused us, so these facts come from CBS Boston and an Intel announcement.

name: Ocean Conservation Research
summary: A US not-for-profit that studies the effects of human-generated noise on marine life to inform ocean policy, and offers five days of hydrophone recordings from off Barrow, Alaska.

name: Ocean Currency Network
summary: Uses satellite data for initial national seagrass maps, monitors coasts with open satellite data and assesses how reefs and mangroves protect coastal assets for insurers.

name: Ocean Data Lab
summary: Directed by Shima Abadi, the lab develops ways to process acoustic data from large underwater networks and studies whale call detection and machine learning for ship noise classification.

name: Ocean Discovery League
summary: Deep ocean exploration organisation working to speed deep ocean exploration, including a 2026 workshop in Hawaii.

name: Ocean Exploration Trust
summary: Exploration and education organisation that maps and samples the deep ocean from its vessel, sharing the results.

name: Ocean Genome Legacy Center
summary: Nonprofit marine research facility and genome bank at Northeastern University, affiliated with the Earth BioGenome Project.

name: Ocean Vision AI
summary: US programme led by MBARI, funded by a 5 million dollar NSF award, using AI to speed processing of ocean video and imagery.

name: Oceanites
summary: Washington DC non-profit that monitors Antarctic penguins, combining field counts with drone imagery, satellite data and AI analysis, and maintains the open MAPPPD database.

name: Oceans Unmanned
summary: A US non-profit that facilitates unmanned aircraft use for oil spills, vessel groundings and whale entanglement responses, and runs Eco-Drone, claiming a decade of experience with unmanned marine systems.

name: OCEARCH
summary: A US nonprofit that leads shark research expeditions and shares real-time tracking data, and runs the OCEARCH Global Shark Tracker, which follows sharks, turtles and dolphins.

name: OCEARCH Global Shark Tracker
summary: A free app, run by OCEARCH, that shows real-time shark movements using tracking data described as supporting science.

name: Odonata Central
summary: Citizen science website recording dragonflies and damselflies in the Western Hemisphere, with records checked by expert vetters.

name: Office of National Marine Sanctuaries
summary: A federal office whose sanctuary system covers 18 underwater parks across over 629,000 square miles of ocean and Great Lakes waters, and which says no other federal agency has its comprehensive mandate.

name: One Tree Planted
summary: US 501(c)3 tree-planting charity working with local partners in more than 80 countries, which lists drone and satellite monitoring as one of five oversight pillars and says it is strengthening its monitoring and verification.

name: Open Green Genomes Initiative
summary: Project to generate genome assemblies for 35 species across land plant lineages, proposed by James Leebens-Mack at the University of Georgia to the Joint Genome Institute.

name: OpenET
summary: Consortium delivering satellite-based evapotranspiration data for water management.

name: Orbital Sentry
summary: Start-up building infrared imaging satellites for geosynchronous orbit, starting with wildfire detection and listing natural systems monitoring among its uses. Superorganism took part in its pre-seed round.

name: ORBO Systems
summary: Sells automated satellite monitoring to land managers. Its platform for land trusts combines Planet imagery with AI to spot possible unauthorised activity on conservation easements.

name: ORCA
summary: Corvallis, Oregon start-up working on AI foundation modelling of the oceans to predict environmental shocks to fisheries.

name: OrcaHello
summary: Open AI model that detects endangered Southern Resident killer whale calls in live hydrophone audio from the Orcasound network, with alerts used to pause coastal construction and redirect boats.

name: Orcasound
summary: Open-source network of underwater microphones in the Puget Sound area off Washington state that livestream underwater audio.

name: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife
summary: Oregon state agency and partner in developing SmartPass, with a trial at Newport, Oregon.

name: Pacific Islands Ocean Observing System
summary: Regional ocean observing system for the US Pacific Islands that collects real-time ocean data and builds tools to access it.

name: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory
summary: US national laboratory that worked with the Electric Power Research Institute on machine learning that identifies migrating eels in sonar data near hydropower sites.

name: Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission
summary: Interstate fisheries commission that partners with the Alaska Longline Fishermen's Association on AI-driven monitoring of sablefish and halibut.

name: Paleobiology Database
summary: Non-profit public resource of global occurrence and taxonomic data for organisms of all geological ages, with data services for others to build on.

name: Palmoil.io
summary: Run by MapHubs, it rates deforestation and social risk using plantation-level evidence, and scores more than 2,450 palm oil mills each month against risk indicators.

name: PALYIM
summary: NSF award for a deep learning platform for pollen image analysis at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.

name: PAMpal
summary: An R package for processing passive acoustic data collected with PAMGuard, organising detections into events and exporting them for the BANTER classifier, within NOAA's FOSSA package set.

name: Panoptes
summary: Company using AI on satellite imagery to find illicit activity, which also lists quantifying deforestation and habitat depletion.

name: ParkServe
summary: Downloadable US dataset of park polygons, 10-minute walk service areas and priority areas for over 15,000 cities and towns.

name: Paso Pacífico
summary: A US-registered nonprofit with offices in Nicaragua and El Salvador that built the InvestEGGator, a GPS-GSM tracker resembling a sea turtle egg, to trace poaching routes.

name: Passive acoustic analysis using ML in Cook Inlet
summary: NOAA analysis of passive acoustic data using neural networks to detect beluga whales and classify their signals.

name: Pathos Wildlife
summary: Organisation combining bio-logging, drones, remote sensing, cameras and AI to study wildlife and support conservation.

name: Peninsula Open Space Trust
summary: A land trust that the Land Trust Alliance directory lists as owning 18,726 acres.

name: Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources
summary: A state department charged with maintaining and protecting 125 state parks and managing 2.2 million acres of state forest land.

name: PhenoCam Network
summary: Cooperative phenological observatory that uses networked digital cameras to track vegetation across North America and elsewhere, used to validate models and satellite products.

name: Photometrics AI
summary: Product of EvariLABS LLC whose system uses BirdCast forecast data to dim streetlights during peak bird migration.

name: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Understanding Coastal Hypoxia Formation Mechanisms
summary: Three-year NSF project led by North Carolina State University with Louisiana State University to forecast coastal dead zones.

name: Pika Patrol
summary: A smartphone app run by the Colorado Pika Project that records American pika observations and teaches users identification, so community scientists can help researchers understand pikas' response to climate change.

name: Planscape
summary: Free, open source decision support tool for prioritising landscape treatments for wildfire resilience, built as a collaboration including the US Forest Service, Google.org and the University of California.

name: PNW Bioacoustics Research Lab
summary: US Forest Service Pacific Northwest research lab that leads large-scale passive acoustic monitoring of forest wildlife, with Adventure Scientists volunteers.

name: Point Blue Conservation Science
summary: California conservation science NGO studying birds and other indicators, using long-term data from sites such as Palomarin and the Farallon Islands, and a partner in Whale Safe.

name: Presidio Trust
summary: A trust responsible, with the National Park Service, for the day-to-day management and long-term stewardship of the Presidio.

name: Prince William Sound Science Center
summary: Alaska science centre with a project applying machine vision and convolutional neural networks to sockeye salmon scale age estimation.

name: Project Inambari
summary: A Grand Challenge entry proposing an open mapping platform using public radar satellite imagery to detect mining-affected land in tropical forests, with field testing in Tambopata, Peru.

name: Protected Areas Database of the United States
summary: USGS national inventory of protected areas, including public land and voluntarily provided private protected areas.

name: Protection Assistant for Wildlife Security
summary: A model that predicts and plans against illegal wildlife poaching, with Python code for machine learning risk prediction and patrol planning, and a paper reporting predictions evaluated in field tests.

name: Public Environmental Data Partners
summary: Coalition of academic and nonprofit organisations preserving public access to US federal environmental data. EDGI's own page refused the fetcher, so this is from Harvard's Salata Institute.

name: Puget Sound Restoration Fund
