summary: Regional restoration group that runs Eyes on Kelp, a kelp forest monitoring initiative with new robotic monitoring technology and shared data.

name: Quail Ridge Automated Animal Tracking
summary: A project whose repository holds software for automated animal tracking, including node software for its receivers, at a reserve that UC Nature says has hosted such research.

name: Radmantis
summary: Toledo, Ohio company funded by NSF SBIR to detect and suppress sea lamprey and protect wild salmonid fisheries in the Great Lakes.

name: Rangeland Analysis Platform
summary: Online platform combining satellite imagery with field vegetation measurements from BLM, NPS and NRCS, using cloud computing and machine learning to map US rangeland vegetation.

name: Raster Report
summary: Identifies recurring vegetation stress locations from multispectral satellite observations to support wildfire mitigation planning, and says its spectral analysis is patent-pending.

name: Raven sound analysis software
summary: A family of sound analysis programs built by the Cornell Yang Center, including Raven Pro, whose Learning Detector runs machine learning models such as BirdNET, and the free Raven Lite.

name: REALIZE Lab
summary: A University of Michigan research group led by Elizabeth Bondi-Kelly that develops machine learning and multi-agent systems for social impact, including image retrieval for wildlife re-identification.

name: Reef Fish Conservation and Education Foundation
summary: NFWF grantee using AI-powered electronic monitoring with satellite data links on five vessels in the Gulf commercial reef fish fishery.

name: Reef halos deep learning model
summary: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa tool using deep learning to find and measure coral reef halos in satellite images, from the Elizabeth Madin Lab.

name: ReefGen
summary: San Francisco company funded by NSF SBIR to develop robotic coral reef restoration.

name: Relae
summary: Carbon management company, formerly Carbon Direct, that acquired the forest carbon monitoring firm Pachama in 2025.

name: Renoster
summary: US climate technology company in Google's AI for Nature accelerator, described as bringing transparency and scientific rigour to carbon markets.

name: Resources Legacy Fund
summary: Sacramento grant maker recorded by Kindora as giving $400,000 to the Vibrant Planet Data Commons in 2025.

name: Restore the Earth Foundation
summary: A 501(c)(3) not-for-profit working to restore 1 million acres in the Mississippi River Basin, which led 18,800 acres of restoration at Salvador Wildlife Management Area.

name: Revive & Restore
summary: Conservation biotechnology nonprofit. A Phase II Bezos Earth Fund awardee for using AI to assemble and interpret genomes of endangered species.

name: Rewyld
summary: Conservation technology company licensing University of Florida work to detect and remove invasive Burmese pythons in the Florida Everglades with AI and robotics.

name: Robert and Patricia Switzer Foundation
summary: Belfast, Maine foundation with a fellowship in environmental leadership. Kindora lists biodiversity data mobilisation among its interests.

name: Robotic microscopes and machine learning for lower trophic levels
summary: NOAA deployment of the Imaging FlowCytobot on docks and survey ships to monitor phytoplankton with machine learning.

name: Robots4Whales
summary: Led by Mark Baumgartner at Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, the project dates its mission archive to 2012 and uses autonomous platforms for near-real-time satellite reporting of marine mammal sounds.

name: Roddenberry Foundation
summary: US grant maker recorded in tax filings data on Grantable as funding Conservation X Labs.

name: SAGE GeoAI Lab
summary: University of Florida lab led by Jane Southworth working on Earth observation, GeoAI and time-series remote sensing of landscape change.

name: Sage Grande Testbed
summary: NSF-funded AI cyberinfrastructure of edge computing nodes with cameras, microphones and environmental sensors, used for applications from wildfire to bird calls.

name: Salmon Vision
summary: Deep learning model that identifies and counts salmon in video from fish weirs, developed by Wild Salmon Center with the Pacific Salmon Foundation, Gitanyow Fisheries Authority and Skeena Fisheries Commission.

name: Salo Sciences
summary: Company in the partnership behind the California Forest Observatory.

name: Saltwater, Inc.
summary: NOAA-approved at-sea and electronic monitoring provider for Northeast groundfish sectors in 2026.

name: Sandin Lab
summary: A Scripps Institution of Oceanography lab that photographs coral reefs worldwide and converts millions of underwater images into 3D models to assess reef health, working with UC San Diego partners.

name: Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy
summary: A conservancy established by the California State Legislature in 1980 that has helped to preserve over 75,000 acres of parkland.

name: Satelytics
summary: Geospatial analytics company whose satellite algorithms detect invasive plants on rangeland through Envu's RangeView tool, according to a release carried by Hay and Forage Grower.

name: Sauk-Suiattle Indian Tribe
summary: Tribal nation in Washington state that co-manages Skagit River salmon with the state and is developing drone and AI surveys of spawning grounds with the University of Washington.

name: Save the Redwoods League
summary: Redwood forest conservation organisation that funded Northern Arizona University work training machine learning to detect fog in redwood forest images.

name: SCAN
summary: Portal and aggregator of arthropod records and images from over 225 North American data providers, global in scope.

name: Scenic Hudson
summary: A conservation organisation that says it has conserved more than 54,000 acres in 10 counties and created more than 45 public parks.

name: Science-i
summary: NSF-funded cyberinfrastructure for forest ecosystem research at Purdue University.

name: Scripps Whale Acoustics Laboratory
summary: The La Jolla lab develops acoustic instruments and analysis methods to study marine animal abundance and behaviour, lists the HARP recorder and offers the Triton software package.

name: SDZWA Conservation Technology Lab
summary: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance's lab for conservation technology, including AI training for individual rhino identification.

name: SeaDeep
summary: Tufts University spin-out founded in 2020 that built underwater monitoring technology using AI image enhancement, aimed in part at coral reef protection. Its site says the product company was wound down in 2025.

name: Seattle Aquarium
summary: Public aquarium whose research team surveys kelp forests by remotely operated vehicle and uses open-source AI to read the images.

name: Seattle Urban Carnivore Project
summary: Project on urban carnivores around Seattle, with wildlife cameras and acoustic monitoring and AI to identify species diversity and density.

name: SECOORA AI Gateway
summary: Hub with a decision tree for AI approaches, worked examples on imagery, video and acoustics, and curated community resources for ocean scientists.

name: SECORE International
summary: An Ohio non-profit founded in 2015, it develops and shares coral restoration tools, including a floating coral rearing basin and Seeding Units, and pilots new tools with partners.

name: SEE Shell app
summary: A machine learning app built by SEE Turtles that identifies tortoiseshell products from photos, launched in March 2022 and reported as 90 to 93 percent accurate.

name: SEE Turtles
summary: An independent Portland non-profit since 2016, it works with coastal communities on turtles, supports Too Rare To Wear partners and built an app to identify tortoiseshell products.

name: Sempervirens Fund
summary: A conservation organisation that owns, directly or through conservation easement, more than 12,000 acres of redwood land.

name: Serendipity Wildlife Foundation
summary: A California non-profit which launched the Wildlife Crime Fingerprint Database and trained Sri Lankan wildlife staff in fingerprint recovery, with DNA collection covered in phase two in November 2019.

name: Sevilleta LTER
summary: A long-term ecological research programme at the University of New Mexico that, in October 2021, monitored plant biomass and phenology and small mammal, grasshopper and bee abundance across southwestern US ecosystems.

name: Sharktivity
summary: A project built and run by the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy showing real-time detections of acoustically tagged white sharks, with public sightings verified by the New England Aquarium.

name: Shellcatch
summary: Sells AI electronic monitoring for fishing fleets, combining onboard cameras, GPS and AI event detection. Its base was not stated on the pages read.

name: Sierra Nevada acoustic bird monitoring
summary: Acoustic monitoring network across California's Sierra Nevada, begun to track Spotted Owls, that gave BirdNET its first large-scale test and was combined with satellite imagery in a decision tool for public land agencies.

name: Sierra Nevada Inventory & Monitoring Network
summary: A monitoring network conducting long-term vital signs monitoring of birds, high-elevation forests, lakes, river hydrology and wetlands, including lake water chemistry and amphibian surveys.

name: SILVIS Lab
summary: University of Wisconsin-Madison spatial analysis lab that maps land use change with satellite imagery and analyses the implications for biodiversity, especially birds.

name: Sitka Tribe of Alaska
summary: Alaska Tribe that Wild Salmon Center says is using Salmon Vision technology to sustain fisheries on Redoubt Lake.

name: Sky Senderos
summary: Texas company running thermal drone wildlife surveys for landowners, with over 900 surveys completed.

name: Smart panel for sea lamprey detection
summary: Great Lakes Fishery Commission project led by Xiaobo Tan of Michigan State University on low-cost smart panels to detect sea lamprey attachment.

name: SmartPass
summary: Fishery monitoring approach that uses shore-based cameras and AI to count vessels at coastal bottlenecks, developed by EDF with Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife, CVision AI, Teem Fish Monitoring and Snap IT.

name: SmartWilds
summary: Multimodal wildlife monitoring dataset and living laboratory at The Wilds, Ohio, built by the naturelab group with funding from ICICLE and Imageomics.

name: Snapshot NY
summary: Participatory trail camera survey of New York's mammals, run as a collaboration of Cornell University, the state Department of Environmental Conservation and the New York Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit.

name: SNAPSHOT USA
summary: Nationwide camera trap survey of US mammals involving more than 150 scientists, with data archived in the Smithsonian's eMammal database.

name: Snapshot Wisconsin
summary: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources trail camera programme with thousands of volunteers, classified with Zooniverse and working with NASA and UW-Madison.

name: Solitons
summary: Company with a US patent for an autonomous marine platform combining surface sailing and underwater gliding, intended to collect ocean observations for AI.

name: Sonoma State University
summary: University whose professor leads the NASA-funded Soundscapes to Landscapes bird monitoring project, and whose Center for Interdisciplinary Geospatial Analysis is a partner in it.

name: Sound Forest Lab
summary: Research laboratory at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, led by Zuzana Burivalova, that uses animal sounds to study tropical forest conservation and presents AI-assisted detections of birds and mammals.

name: Soundbendor Lab
summary: Oregon State University research group using AI and deep learning on sound, with bioacoustics among its project areas.

name: Soundscape Baselines Project
summary: Project run by the Sound Forest Lab that recorded 36 forest soundscapes for a full year, with a pilot of 36 baseline sites in six countries.

name: Soundscapes to Landscapes
summary: NASA-funded project in Sonoma County, California, combining volunteer AudioMoth recordings with satellite data to monitor bird diversity; UC Merced collaborators developed a prototype deep learning bird identification framework.

name: South Dakota State University
summary: US university whose Geospatial Sciences Center of Excellence is a collaboration with the USGS Earth Resources Observation and Science Center.

name: South Florida Water Management District
summary: A regional water management body that manages more than 1 million acres of public conservation lands, and says nearly 1.5 million acres within its boundaries are publicly owned.

name: Southeast Coastal Ocean Observing Regional Association
summary: Regional ocean observing association that hosts the SECOORA AI Gateway, a resource hub for applying AI and machine learning to ocean science.

name: Southern California Coastal Ocean Observing System
summary: Regional ocean observing system whose site hosts the California Imaging FlowCytobot Network, which classifies phytoplankton with machine learning.

name: Southern Oregon University
summary: University in Ashland, Oregon, home of the Green Crossing AI project.

name: Species Distribution Modeling on the A.I. frontier
summary: NSF award using deep generative models for species distribution modelling at Florida International University.

name: Species File Group
summary: Group that endows and maintains TaxonWorks, an open-source web workbench for taxonomists.

name: Specky
summary: Spectrogram viewing application for quickly labelling short WAV or MP3 clips by sound and spectrogram, with default labels for species presence and whether the sound is a song or call.

name: Spheros Environmental
summary: Environmental consultancy in the Pacific Northwest and Midwest, formerly Four Peaks, that built the BlueFish AI-assisted fish counting software used on the Columbia River.

name: Spot a Shark USA
summary: Wild Me platform using computer vision for sand tiger sharks.

name: Stock-Smart.com
summary: Grazing planning tool from Washington State University Extension that uses AI on virtual fence geolocation data and satellite forage data to enhance wildlife habitat and control invasive species.

name: Stony Brook University
summary: New York university where Heather Lynch couples AI and population modelling to track Antarctic penguins from satellite imagery.

name: Stratifyx
summary: Company offering AI ecological screening of land to find restoration opportunities.

name: Stroud Water Research Center
summary: Freshwater research nonprofit behind WikiWatershed and the Monitor My Watershed data portal, which hosts EnviroDIY sensor data.

name: Supporting Tribal-Led Salmon Monitoring Using Computer Vision
summary: University of Washington EarthLab project with the Sauk-Suiattle Indian Tribe combining automated drone flights and AI to detect salmon spawning nests on the Skagit River system.

name: Surfrider Foundation
summary: Coastal conservation group whose Blue Water Task Force labs test bacteria at more than 600 sites and publish all results in a public database.

name: Synthetik Applied Technologies
summary: Company listed by NOAA as a SBIR Phase II awardee for DeepSpace-SI, a deep learning offshore monitoring system using satellite imagery.

name: TagLab
summary: Programme run by Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, created to bring science and engineering talent together to innovate animal-borne tag technology across departments including Biology and Applied Ocean Physics and Engineering.

name: Tahoe Fund
summary: Lake Tahoe funder that gave a grant through its Smartest Forest Fund for the user interface of the California Forest Observatory.

name: TALIN Biodiversity Monitoring
summary: University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science project using machine learning, biological surveys and remote sensing to map and predict biodiversity change, led by Matt Fitzpatrick.

name: Tandy Center for Ocean Forecasting
summary: Bigelow Laboratory centre developing ocean forecasts with big data and machine learning.

name: Tator
summary: Web platform for video and image analytics from CVision AI, used for marine imagery.

name: TealWaters
summary: NSF Convergence Accelerator project mapping current and past US wetlands and their value.

name: Tech4Wildlife at Georgia Tech
summary: Georgia Tech programme aiming to support community-driven wildlife technology, connect students with sponsors, and provide frugal conservation technology education, with planned Atlanta Zoo projects on a tracking system and selective feeders.

name: TerrAdapt
summary: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) founded in 2022 after development from 2018, providing remote-sensing monitoring, species range projection and prioritisation tools, including work on jaguar connectivity with the World Wildlife Fund.

name: TerrAdapt:Cascadia
summary: Programme built and run by TerrAdapt that gives land managers in Washington and southern British Columbia a regional view of landscape and climate change, including a Salmon Landscapes portal.

name: TerrainWorks
summary: Mount Shasta, California company leading TealWaters, an NSF Convergence Accelerator project to map current and past wetlands and their value.

name: Tethys Metadata
summary: Free open source database for acoustic recording metadata, built by NOAA and Scripps Institution of Oceanography, designed mainly for marine mammals, with schemata begun in 2011 and PAMGuard export support.

name: Texas A&M Forest Service
summary: Texas state forestry agency listed by Earth Fire Alliance as a FireSat early adopter.

name: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department
summary: Texas state wildlife agency that works with the Harte Research Institute on bloom warning and has presented a neural network model for detecting prairie dog colonies from satellite imagery.

name: ThayerMahan
summary: Company teamed with Ocean Aero and the Allen Institute for AI on detection of illegal fishing, per Schmidt Marine.

name: The Big Wild
summary: Describes itself as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, aiming to collect data with AI, machine learning and GIS, provide wildlife data quickly and collaborate with local and Indigenous communities.

name: The Community Environmental Health Laboratory at MDI Biological Laboratory
summary: Community science laboratory in Bar Harbor, Maine, that developed the Anecdata.org citizen science platform.

name: The Genomic Observatories Metadatabase
summary: Open access repository for geographic and ecological metadata tied to biosamples and genetic data.

name: The Institute for Bird Populations
summary: A bird research organisation whose MAPS stations, over 1,400 since 1989, have operated in North America, and whose MoSI programme has had stations in 15 countries.

name: The Knowledge Network for Biocomplexity
summary: National network for finding, accessing and analysing ecological and environmental data from field stations, laboratories and researchers.

name: The Lepidopterists' Society Season Summary
summary: Annual compilation of butterfly and moth records from Canada, Mexico and the United States.

name: The Marine Mammal Center
summary: Marine mammal organisation that published the launch of Whale Safe off the San Francisco coast.

name: The NAT
summary: New York organisation with a Patrick J. McGovern Foundation grant to create AI tools for monitoring and storytelling. Its own sites refused the fetcher.

name: The Pennsylvania State University
summary: University named as the owner of the INSECT NET site.

name: The Tree of Life Web Project
summary: Collaborative web project giving information on biodiversity and evolutionary history, with its classification published through GBIF.

name: The Wildlands Conservancy
summary: A conservation organisation that manages 25 preserves covering nearly 210,000 acres and restores native habitats on them.

name: Tohono O'odham Nation
summary: Tribal nation in southern Arizona training AI models to identify animals, with help from the National Park Service's Sonoran Desert Network.

name: Toyon Research
summary: Company listed by NOAA as a SBIR Phase II awardee for detecting and classifying marine mammals in infrared video using AI.

name: Tree Equity Score
summary: Public scoring tool for urban tree cover in the US, now covering Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands.

name: TreeMap
summary: Forest Service tree-level model of US forests that matches Forest Inventory and Analysis plots to a 30 metre grid.

name: Treeswift
summary: Philadelphia company using swarms of autonomous lidar drones for forest inventory, funded by NSF SBIR awards.

name: Triton
summary: Tool built and run by C4ADS linking industrial fishing vessels to their controlling entities for counter-IUU fishing partners, using beneficial ownership data and, at its May 2024 launch, free by invitation only.

name: Triton software package
summary: MATLAB-based package from Scripps Institution of Oceanography for evaluating long-duration acoustic recordings, handling continuous and duty-cycle time series and requiring MATLAB's signal processing toolbox.

name: True Elements
summary: Water intelligence company offering AI that aggregates and forecasts water quality data, in partnership with Waterkeeper Alliance.

name: TrueQi
summary: True Elements' core water intelligence system, which connects data and models changing water conditions for a site, portfolio or watershed.

name: Trust for Public Land
summary: US land conservation charity that publishes the ParkServe park database and the Conservation Almanac and LandVote databases.

name: U.S. Animal Telemetry Network
summary: Multi-agency US network for electronic tag tracking of marine animals, hosted under IOOS.

name: U.S. Department of the Interior
summary: US federal department over the National Park Service, Fish and Wildlife Service, Geological Survey, Bureau of Land Management and Bureau of Indian Affairs. It keeps an inventory of AI use cases across its bureaus.

name: U.S. Endowment for Forestry and Communities
summary: US funder for forests and forestry communities, which has committed 5 million dollars to a forest-sector venture capital fund.

name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
summary: US federal environment agency, which publishes an AI strategy and compliance plan and runs the EnviroAtlas ecosystem services data portal and the National Aquatic Resource Surveys.

name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
summary: US federal wildlife agency and a bureau of the Department of the Interior. Its site refuses automated reading, so its AI work and data systems are not recorded here yet.

name: U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System
summary: NOAA-hosted US ocean observing system, which includes the Marine Biodiversity Observation Network and the Animal Telemetry Network.

name: U.S. Marine Biodiversity Observation Network
summary: US partnership integrating biology and ecosystem surveys with remote sensing and environmental DNA methods.

name: Understory
summary: Organisation using drone and satellite imagery to identify vegetation to species level, saying its software informs land management, habitat conservation and climate risk assessment.

name: University of Alabama in Huntsville
summary: US university whose Earth System Science Center hosted a 2018 AI for Earth Innovation Grant on harmful algal blooms.

name: University of California, Los Angeles
summary: University of California campus that co-launched Kelpwatch, a machine learning map of kelp forests.

name: University of California, Santa Barbara
summary: University of California campus that co-launched Kelpwatch and houses the Benioff Ocean Initiative behind Whale Safe.

name: University of California, Santa Cruz
summary: University of California campus whose researchers hold a state grant to scale an eDNA stream health index.

name: University of Connecticut
summary: US university whose Ecological Modeling Institute runs Biodiversity Exposure Forecasts (BEFore) under a NASA programme.

name: University of Georgia
summary: University hiring a cluster of faculty in environmental AI.

name: University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo
summary: University with a lab developing AI to analyse forest bird soundscapes and track bird population trends, according to Hawaiʻi Public Radio.

name: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa
summary: University whose coral ecologists developed deep learning algorithms that measure reef halos in satellite imagery.

name: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
summary: US university in the BirdCast collaboration.

name: University of Massachusetts Amherst
summary: US university in the BirdCast collaboration.

name: University of Miami
summary: US university presenting MarineVERSE and PICOGRAM coral work at the NASA biodiversity meeting.

name: University of Michigan
summary: University that hosts the REALIZE Lab, a machine learning group in its computer science and engineering division working on environmental monitoring and wildlife conservation.

name: University of Montana
summary: University that first developed the Rangeland Analysis Platform and whose researchers are building an AI and drone system to haze wildlife away from people.

name: University of New Mexico
summary: A university where, according to an October 2021 article, a Sevilleta LTER research team collected long-term ecological data on population dynamics, community structure and ecosystem processes.

name: University of Wisconsin-Madison
summary: US university whose ecologists co-led acoustic bird monitoring in the Sierra Nevada using BirdNET.

name: Upham Lab of Mammal Phylogenetic Ecology
summary: Lab led by Nathan Upham studying mammal evolution and ecology, leading the Mammal Diversity Database of about 6,700 species and working towards a knowledge graph of host-pathogen interactions.

name: Urban Wildlife Information Network
summary: Collaborative research group run by Lincoln Park Zoo and led by Seth Magle, which began as a camera trapping collaboration and describes itself as holding the largest urban wildlife dataset.

name: US Department of Energy Water Power Technologies Office
summary: US Department of Energy office that publishes the Fish Detection AI sonar models.

name: US National Plant Germplasm System
summary: USDA Agricultural Research Service system whose GRIN Taxonomy covers all families and genera of vascular plants and over 46,000 species worldwide.

name: USA National Phenology Network
summary: National monitoring and research initiative collecting and delivering phenological data, information and forecasts for natural resource management.

name: USC Center for Artificial Intelligence in Society
summary: The University of Southern California’s AI centre lists wildlife sensor placement with planned camera-trap collaborations, machine learning for satellite imagery, and participation in Operation Pangolin.

name: USDA Agricultural Research Service
summary: USDA research agency that took on the scientific and technical development of the Rangeland Analysis Platform in 2023.

name: USDA Farm Production and Conservation
summary: US Department of Agriculture mission area listed in the federal AI inventory for the Land Change Analysis Tool, which maps high resolution land cover.

name: USDA Forest Service
summary: US federal forest agency that builds the Landscape Change Monitoring System and the Tree Canopy Cover dataset, and runs Forest Inventory and Analysis. Its research site refuses automated reading, so these facts come from partner pages.

name: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service
summary: USDA agency that co-developed the Rangeland Analysis Platform and supplies field vegetation measurements to it.

name: USDA PLANTS Database
summary: Database of standardised information on the vascular plants, mosses, liverworts, hornworts and lichens of the United States and its territories.

name: USDA-ARS Range Management Research Unit, Jornada Experimental Range
summary: US Department of Agriculture research unit that initiated the Land Potential Knowledge System project.

name: USF Water Institute
summary: University of South Florida institute that develops and maintains the Plant Atlas application and WaterAtlas.org.

name: USGS Bird Banding Laboratory
summary: United States Geological Survey laboratory listed as a partner in the Bird Migration Explorer.

name: VentureWell Ocean Enterprise Accelerator
summary: Accelerator for US coastal and ocean start-ups run by VentureWell with support from NOAA.

name: Vermont Center for Ecostudies
summary: Wildlife conservation non-profit that runs the Vermont Atlas of Life and its data explorer, and publishes a national bee dataset through GBIF.

name: Vermont Land Trust
summary: A land trust that says it has protected more than 650,000 acres, over 11% of Vermont, much of it privately owned, without stating the legal basis.

name: Vermont Reptile and Amphibian Atlas
summary: Project dating to 1994 that aims to gather and share data for conserving Vermont's reptiles and amphibians, inviting electronic submission of observations and photos.

name: Vibrant Planet
summary: US public benefit company whose platform models wildfire and land management, deployed statewide by CAL FIRE. Its original nonprofit became the Vibrant Planet Data Commons.

name: Vibrant Planet Data Commons
summary: Nonprofit dedicated to commissioning and hosting open scientific research for education and academic use, linked to Vibrant Planet.

name: Video and Image Analytics for Marine Environments
summary: Open-source AI system that automates the processing of underwater video and images, developed by NOAA with Mississippi State University's Northern Gulf Institute and Kitware.

name: View Into The Blue
summary: Organisation that designs, builds and deploys long-term ocean monitoring systems with live video, audio and sensors, including the Orca underwater camera for real-time computer vision at the edge.

name: VISION Lab, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
summary: Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute lab in Troy, New York, led by Charles Stewart, designing computer vision applications for ecological conservation.

name: Volant Aerial
summary: Scottsdale, Arizona company funded by NSF SBIR for AI-enabled cameras that detect forest fires.

name: Washington State Department of Natural Resources
summary: A state agency managing 5.6 million acres of trust lands under a mandate including preserving forests, water and habitat, with eight aquatic reserves and 59 natural area preserve sites covering over 41,483 acres.

name: Washington State University
summary: US university whose extension service runs Stock-Smart.com, which uses AI to interpret virtual fence data for grazing that reduces wildfire risk and improves wildlife habitat.

name: Western Fire & Forest Resilience Collaborative
summary: Collaborative listed by Earth Fire Alliance as a FireSat early adopter.

name: Whale Safe
summary: Mapping and analysis tool from the Benioff Ocean Science Laboratory showing whale and ship data to prevent fatal ship collisions off the US West Coast.

name: WhaleSpotter
summary: Whale detection system using thermal imaging and AI with expert verification, sending real-time alerts to maritime operators. Its home country is not stated on the page read, so check.

name: WIFIRE Lab
summary: Laboratory at the San Diego Supercomputer Center, UC San Diego, working on wildfire hazard monitoring, mitigation and response.

name: Wilburforce Foundation
summary: Foundation funding conservation leaders across western North America, using conservation science to set priority regions and running a Leaders in Conservation Science programme.

name: Wild Salmon Center
summary: Portland-based NGO protecting salmon rivers across the North Pacific. It developed Salmon Vision, a deep learning model that counts fish at weirs, with First Nations and other partners.

name: Wild Spotter
summary: Project engaging the public to find, map and prevent invasive species in America's wild places, built on EDDMapS, with its website hosted by the University of Georgia.

name: Wild Vision Systems
summary: Maker of AI-powered smart traps for invasive species that reports a 94% bycatch reduction in a Florida tegu lizard comparison study with the University of Florida and USDA-APHIS.

name: Wildbook Image Analysis (WBIA)
summary: Machine learning engine used by Wildbook to detect image features and identify individual animals, bringing large-scale computer vision to wildlife research.

name: Wildfire Interdisciplinary Research Center
summary: San Jose State University research centre listed as an Earth Fire Alliance partner.

name: WildHealthNet
summary: Programme run by the Wildlife Conservation Society supporting national wildlife health surveillance systems, which began piloting in Viet Nam, Laos and Cambodia in 2019.

name: Wildlife Defense Platform
summary: C4ADS platform for frontline partners to search and analyse data on wildlife seizures and court cases.

name: Wildlife Imaging Systems
summary: Hinesburg, Vermont company developing automated processing of images and video for wildlife conservation, with NSF SBIR awards.

name: Wildlife Materials, Inc.
summary: Murphysboro, Illinois company founded in 1970 by a wildlife biologist and his wife, making radio telemetry equipment and supplying VHF transmitters and receivers for over 50 years.

name: Wildlife Soundhub
summary: UC Berkeley project that processes audio from California sentinel sites, using BirdNET to identify species.

name: WildlifeOS
summary: Maker of CrocAlarm, an AI wildlife threat detection product starting with crocodiles and alligators in Florida's waterways.

name: WildML@UNI
summary: Research lab at the University of Northern Iowa exploring machine learning for wildlife conservation.

name: Window to Wildlife
summary: Company established in 2018 to build the Captiva Eagle Cam, which says it is one of the first US firms specialising in wildlife camera installations, focused on birds of prey.

name: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources
summary: State natural resources agency that runs the Snapshot Wisconsin trail camera programme.

name: Wood River drone salmon counts
summary: Bristol Bay project using automated drone flights on the Wood River and an AI model trained on hand-counted footage to improve salmon escapement counts. Alaska Fish and Game is not directly involved at this stage.

name: Woodland Park Zoo
summary: Seattle zoo running the Seattle Urban Carnivore Project, with a Microsoft AI for Good award for AI on wildlife camera and acoustic data.

name: Woodwell Climate Research Center
summary: Massachusetts climate research centre that runs FishEye, an AI video system for counting river herring.

name: World Forest ID
summary: An international non-profit with US and Dutch legal entities, it facilitates a public research consortium and uses AI-enabled spatial models based on plant samples to trace traded forest products.

name: Yellowstone Forever
summary: Non-profit partner in the AI wolf howl work with the Colossal Foundation and the Yellowstone Wolf Project.

name: Yellowstone Wolf Project
summary: Long-running study of Yellowstone wolves, working with the Colossal Foundation and Yellowstone Forever on cameras that record howls and AI that classifies them.

name: Yurok Tribe
summary: A tribe whose constitution mandates it to restore, enhance and manage natural resources in Yurok Ancestral Territory.

name: ZaminSense Inc.
summary: C-corporation start-up that combines satellite, aerial, drone and ground sensor data with machine learning for forest, water and wetland monitoring, including across New York State.

name: Agencia Nacional de Investigación e Innovación
summary: Research and innovation agency whose Fondo María Viñas, with INIA, funded the Usina de códigos de barra de la vida–Uruguay DNA barcoding project.

name: Ambá
summary: NGO working to restore people's emotional bond with nature, which says it has run camera-trap mammal surveys in the Sierras de Rocha since 2015 and in Río Negro since 2023.

name: App Hornero
summary: Free Android app for tracking hornero nest building in the five countries where the bird lives, designed by a behavioural ecology laboratory and referenced by ANEP in 2026.

name: Asociación Civil JULANA
summary: Montevideo civil association of unknown current status that built the participatory wildlife monitoring project at Paso Centurión, which in a 2016 note reported Uruguay's first wild jaguarundi record.

name: Atlas dinámico de cobertura de suelo de Uruguay
summary: Developed and maintained by Dinot, the atlas had a machine learning layer with 27 classes presented in December 2021; a later report described a 2021–2022 layer in preparation.

name: Aves Uruguay
summary: Uruguayan NGO whose bird monitoring and use of the TESSA and ICP methods are reported as largely funded by contributions via BirdLife International.

name: Base de datos ambientales, oceanográficos y meteorológicos generados en proyectos de exploración de hidrocarburos 2007-2017
summary: Dataset of visual and acoustic marine megafauna detections recorded in Uruguay's exclusive economic zone between 2007 and 2017, built by ANCAP, published by the Ministry of Environment under CC BY 4.0.

name: Base de Datos de Especies (SNAP)
summary: Species database first made in 2013 for Uruguay’s protected area system, mapping species with conservation priorities, potential distributions and museum, botanical garden and university collections as sources.

name: Biodiversidata
summary: Collaborative project aiming to improve knowledge of Uruguay's biodiversity through open data, with nine datasets listed in GBIF's registry.

name: BoL-UY
summary: Programme working towards a national reference database of barcode sequences in Uruguay, begun in 2014 and supported since 2020 by the Ministry of Education and Culture's science directorate.

name: Censos de vegetación de campo natural en Uruguay 2001-2009
summary: Dataset of vascular plant observations from sites across Uruguay between 2001 and 2009, gathered in phytosociological surveys and built by Felipe Lezama, with the Facultad de Agronomía as publisher.

name: Centro Universitario Regional del Este
summary: Universidad de la República centre in Maldonado, run by that university, whose research groups produce biodiversity datasets and monitoring data for eastern Uruguay.

name: Conservación y manejo de los recursos marinos vivos de la Península Antártica: los pingüinos como centinelas del Océano Austral
summary: Active project led by Alvaro Soutullo, aiming to inform Antarctic Peninsula marine conservation, with penguin tracking planned to identify areas used and possible overlaps with fishing.

name: Cupybara challenge
summary: Closed 2025 competition, run by Tryolabs, to build AI models classifying wildlife in 15-second videos, using over 2,000 video segments of Uruguayan wildlife.

name: Departamento de Biodiversidad y Genética, Instituto de Investigaciones Biológicas Clemente Estable
summary: Active department of the Instituto de Investigaciones Biológicas Clemente Estable that studies biodiversity genetics with molecular tools, and since 2023 two of its researchers have monitored fauna in the Santa Lucía wetlands with Intendencia de Montevideo park rangers.

name: Department of Engineering, Universidad Católica del Uruguay
summary: Active engineering department in Montevideo, listed as the affiliation of the first author of two IEEE LASCAS papers, from 2022 on UAVs versus satellites for water quality and from 2024 on Sentinel 3 and machine learning for cyanobacteria.

name: Developing a Baseline for Amphibian Monitoring through Acoustic Surveys in Uruguay, South America
summary: Closed project, on a page dated 5 January 2012, that proposed nationwide acoustic surveys of male anuran calls, with density from a chorus index, to fill knowledge gaps and set a baseline for amphibian monitoring.

name: Dirección General Forestal
summary: Uruguayan forestry directorate whose evaluation and information division has carried out National Forest Inventory campaigns since 2009, and whose page lists forest monitoring, mapping, inventories and a forestry geoportal.

name: Dirección Nacional de Biodiversidad y Servicios Ecosistémicos
summary: Directorate run by Uruguay's environment ministry, responsible for protected areas and biodiversity policy on land and at sea, with 12 datasets listed in GBIF.

name: Dirección Nacional de Ordenamiento Territorial
summary: With FAO support, the national land-planning directorate introduced a method for analysing land cover in more detail to compare changes in land use.

name: Distribución, ecología y abundancia de cetáceos en el Océano Austral
summary: Project of unknown status, led by Passadore and Dimitriadis, planning to use vessel sightings and species distribution models to study cetaceans in the Southern Ocean.

name: Diversity and State of Conservation of Medium and Large Mammal Population at the Conservation Area of Quebrada del Yerbal, Rocha, Uruguay
summary: Closed, Rufford Foundation funded project that used camera traps, tracks and traces to register 20 mammal species, with monitoring extended from 400 to 1,500 hectares between November 2015 and December 2016.

name: ECOBIO Uruguay
summary: Montevideo organisation whose GBIF record says its databases include roadkill and camera-trap records and that it has worked on biodiversity nationally for 15 years.

name: ECOBIO Uruguay wildlife roadkill monitoring network
summary: Reportedly strengthened from 2015, this roadkill monitoring network uses an Epicollect5-based app and has recorded thousands of vertebrates, mainly mammals; a 2026 paper compiled 4,388 records from 2016–2024.

name: Ecología espacial y caracterización poblacional del gato montés en los Humedales de Santa Lucía
summary: Project on wild cat ecology in the Santa Lucía wetlands, led by Mariana Cosse, using camera traps and faecal DNA, with monitoring reported since 2023.

name: Effects of agricultural intensification on ecosystem services at basin level in Uruguay (ANII FMV_3_2020_1_162279)
summary: According to its final report, this closed project assessed agricultural intensification’s effects on ecosystem services, analysed 20 years of change across Uruguay and developed a web application.

name: Effects of Human Disturbance on Occupancy and Activity Patterns of Carnivora (Mammalia) Species in the Uruguayan Savannah
summary: Ongoing binational project built and run by Instituto Pró-Carnívoros, planning camera trapping at at least 108 sites to estimate carnivore occupancy and activity, with results for authorities and farmers.

name: Elaboración de un mapa sonoro de la Isla Rey Jorge: hacia la utilización del monitoreo del paisaje acústico como un indicador ambiental en la Antártida
summary: Project that plans to establish a baseline of human-made sound and noise on Fildes Peninsula, King George Island, and explore effects on local biological communities; led by Lucía Ziegler.

name: Facultad de Agronomía, Universidad de la República
summary: Faculty of the Universidad de la República that holds herbarium collections and thematic databases, including 2001 to 2009 grassland vegetation surveys, and leads Flora Uruguaya Online through its plant biology department.

name: Flora Uruguaya Online
summary: National floristics initiative led by the Facultad de Agronomía across five herbarium collections, combining specimen data with NaturalistaUY and iNaturalist records into a catalogue of Uruguay's vascular flora.

name: Herramientas para el monitoreo y control de la invasión de rana toro
summary: Reported in December 2023, the closed project developed two amphibian monitoring apps, deployed 12 AudioMoth recorders during August 2021–March 2023 and consolidated over 12 years of invasion data.

name: Historical database and alert levels of cyanobacteria in the Uruguay River and Río de la Plata (ANII ICC_X_2021_1_171370)
summary: Closed project, code ICC_X_2021_1_171370, proposed by the Facultad de Ciencias of the Universidad de la República and led by Carla Kruk, that built a 1963 to 2021 database of cyanobacteria, cyanotoxins, alert levels and environmental drivers for the Uruguay River and Río de la Plata.

name: Identidad Franca
summary: Active project of five organisations, named in Uruguay's national report to CMS COP15, that aims to study right whale movements along the coast and update the photo-identification catalogue during 2025.

name: Infraestructura de Datos Espaciales de Uruguay
summary: Spatial data infrastructure whose September 2019 announcement described a geoportal publishing the Uruguayan state's official geographic information as open data, including satellite imagery.

name: Instituto de Investigaciones Biológicas Clemente Estable
summary: Research institute whose biodiversity and genetics department was involved in Santa Lucía wetland monitoring from 2023 and led a DNA barcoding project publishing three open datasets.

name: Instituto Nacional de Investigación Agropecuaria
summary: Agricultural research institute that co-funded the Usina de códigos de barra de la vida–Uruguay project, publishes systematic bird observations from 2021 onwards, and had technicians trained in Google Earth Engine in 2019.

name: Intendencia de Montevideo
summary: Municipal government whose environmental quality service produced a 2022 report on bird monitoring in the Santa Lucía wetlands protected area, and whose water monitoring report records 18 bird species photographed.

name: Inventario Forestal Nacional (Uruguay)
summary: National forest inventory run by the Dirección General Forestal, described by the ministry as a fundamental monitoring tool that aims to fill information gaps, with demand on commercial pine shaping its continuation in December 2019.

name: Karumbé
summary: Sea turtle NGO on the Uruguayan coast, founded in 1999, whose centre Mongabay reported in 2022 had supplied information for over 100 scientific studies.

name: Laboratorio de Ecología del Comportamiento Animal, Facultad de Ciencias
summary: Animal behavioural ecology laboratory of the Facultad de Ciencias, Universidad de la República, using birds as study models.

name: MapBiomas Uruguay
summary: Collaborative programme producing annual maps of 10 land cover classes for 1985 to 2024 at 30 m, reporting 2.9 million hectares of natural grassland lost over that period.

name: MBON Pole to Pole rocky shore monitoring in Uruguay
summary: Proposed Uruguayan rocky shore monitoring, announced in October 2024 after a workshop at Santa Teresa National Park, that would photograph intertidal quadrats and analyse them with deep learning, aiming to extend to coastal protected areas.

name: Ministerio de Ambiente (Uruguay)
summary: Uruguay's environment ministry, whose National Biodiversity Strategy sets 23 targets, including a target to build an open-access biodiversity information system by 2030.

name: Monitoreo de biodiversidad del Paisaje Protegido Quebrada de los Cuervos
summary: Closed biodiversity monitoring project at Quebrada de los Cuervos in 2014 to 2015, using electrofishing and camera traps under a DINAMA agreement, described as a SNAP pilot.

name: Monitoreo participativo de fauna en Paso Centurión
summary: Participatory wildlife monitoring in which residents chose camera locations, maintained cameras and helped identify records, producing Uruguay's first record of a wild jaguarundi in August 2015.

name: Monitoring of Mitigation Measures Implemented in Uruguay to Reduce the Impacts of the Roads on the Populations of Medium and Large Mammals
summary: Closed Rufford-listed project in La Paloma, dated December 2020, proposing to evaluate wildlife crossing signs and monitor bridge use by medium and large mammals.

name: Observatorio Ambiental Nacional
summary: National environmental observatory created by Law 19.147 of 2013 to centralise environmental information through state, pressure and response indicators, including biodiversity and protection levels, with a portal of data and a geoportal.

name: Organización para la Conservación de Cetáceos
summary: Non-profit in La Paloma, Rocha, listed as created in 2000, whose research includes photo-identification and acoustics, and which in 2014 planned to reinforce a stranding network using a phone application.

name: Programa de Monitoreo Interinstitucional de las Lagunas Costeras del Uruguay
summary: Ministry-led coastal lagoon programme which, in June 2022, reported seasonal monitoring of Laguna Garzón since November 2017 and records of potentially toxic cyanobacteria, with no observed blooms.

name: Proyecto REDD+ Uruguay
summary: Project through which MGAP and the then environment ministry worked in 2019 on designing a National Forest Monitoring System, and which organised Google Earth Engine training.

name: Proyecto SoilBon en Península Fildes: Monitoreo temporal de la biodiversidad microbiana en suelo antártico
summary: Active project, run by the Soil Biodiversity Observation Network, planning to send Antarctic soil samples from near the Artigas base to Germany for DNA extraction and 16S, 18S and ITS amplicon analysis.

name: Proyecto Toninas
summary: Dolphin research project created in 2002, with a December 2009 report describing photo-identification surveys at La Coronilla-Cerro Verde and Cabo Polonio and catalogue comparison with Patos Lagoon in Brazil.

name: Red de varamientos de fauna marina
summary: Marine fauna stranding network, described in a November 2020 article as coordinated by Coendú, the Facultad de Ciencias and SOCOBIOMA, with cases reportable through the Epicollect5 app.

name: Reserva Natural Salus wildlife monitoring
summary: Camera-trap monitoring at a reserve in Lavalleja that Montevideo Portal reports recorded a lesser anteater for the first time, in a reserve holding more than 1,050 identified species.

name: Seguimiento de floraciones algales en Uruguay (reportes diarios con imágenes satelitales)
summary: Active Ministry of Environment programme, run by the ministry, that produces daily algal bloom reports, mainly on cyanobacteria, from visual interpretation of satellite images covering 20 water bodies, with a searchable downloadable archive.

name: Sistema de Información sobre la Biodiversidad de Uruguay
summary: Uruguay's GBIF node, run by the Ministerio de Ambiente, listed by GBIF as an associate participant and hosting three DNA datasets from the barcoding project.

name: Species Richness and Conservation Status of Medium and Large Mammal Populations in the Protected Area Quebrada de los Cuervos, Uruguay
summary: Closed project, described on a page dated 29 August 2008, that planned to estimate medium and large mammal richness at four sites in a 4,410 ha protected area using camera traps and surveys on foot.

name: Universidad de la República
summary: Uruguay's main higher education and research institution, by its own description, whose researchers took part in bat call identification, DNA barcoding, participatory monitoring and environmental DNA work.

name: Universidad Tecnológica del Uruguay
summary: Uruguayan university whose staff and students, according to Montevideo Portal, are developing an AI system to prevent forest fires.

name: Uruguay bat acoustic identification algorithm
summary: Random forest algorithm identifying bat species from calls, reported by Mongabay in 2018 as Uruguay's first, open source and already used by wind farm company scientists.

name: Usina de códigos de barra de la vida–Uruguay
summary: Project led by Mariana Cosse of IIBCE that published three DNA datasets, including a genetic plant species reference library, and had concluded by 23 December 2025.

name: UTEC AI wildfire prevention and early detection system
summary: Reportedly being developed by UTEC, this AI wildfire prevention system combines sensors, thermal cameras and supercomputing, uses local training data and gives emergency services real-time recommendations.

name: Vida Silvestre Uruguay
summary: Non-profit founded in 1995 whose January 2025 profile reports 37 voluntary private-land refuges and a first franciscana dolphin abundance estimate with Argentine and Brazilian researchers.

name: Área de Manejo de Hábitat y/o Especies Laguna Garzón
summary: Protected area where, according to the Ministry of Environment, periodic monitoring of mammals, waterbirds and invasive alien species has run since 2020, using camera traps, counts and apps such as iNaturalist and eBird, and where at least 12 mammal species were identified.

name: Agency for Increasing Forests and Green Areas and Combating Desertification
summary: Uzbek forestry agency whose central staff includes an AI technology implementation and data management department, a forest cadastre and monitoring department, and an afforestation and reforestation monitoring department.

name: Agency for increasing forests and green areas and combating desertification
summary: Uzbek forestry and desertification agency that reported in February 2026 a phased national inventory of forest fund lands, working with the Cadastre Agency and Aerogeodesy Center on orthophoto plans and digital maps from aerospace monitoring data.

name: Aktau-Tamdy State Reserve
summary: Desert biodiversity reserve in Navoi region, created by presidential resolution in February 2022, run by the National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change; a December 2024 report described a camera trap recording a fox.

name: Aral Sea Wetlands project
summary: GEF-funded project run by the ecology committee with UNDP, producing ECODATA and restoring wetlands, with UNDP reporting stronger conservation across protected areas exceeding four million hectares.

name: Aralkum National Nature Park
summary: Protected area established in March 2022 in Muynak district, Karakalpakstan, where a camera trap recorded a group of saiga antelopes.

name: Barsakelmes State Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve in Karakalpakstan, established in 2022 and covering 280,000 hectares, run by the National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change; camera traps recorded a caracal and its autumn 2025 survey recorded 42 bird and 17 mammal species.

name: Biodiversity Conservation Information Management System
summary: Online geodatabase of flora, fauna, threatened species and biodiversity threats; UNDP reported a server installed and demo launched in February 2020, with staff training, and its current status is unknown.

name: Cadastre Agency of the Republic of Uzbekistan
summary: Uzbek agency covering geodesy, cartography, the state cadastre and real estate registration, with subordinate bodies including a Geoinnovation Center; a November 2025 decree moved it to the National Committee for Sustainable Development of Urbanization and Housing Market.

name: Central Asia Biodiversity Conservation Network
summary: Regional network, with a Tashkent address, for implementing the Global Strategy for Plant Conservation; its GBIF dataset of Central Asian floristic field survey records is published under CC BY 4.0.

name: Chatkal State Biosphere Reserve
summary: Biosphere reserve run by the National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change, whose staff joined 2019 snow leopard camera-trap surveys and whose camera traps recorded Tien Shan brown bear and Siberian ibex in August 2026.

name: Department of Protected Natural Areas
summary: Subordinate organisation of the National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change that co-organised SMART Patrol training in Zarafshan National Park in July 2026.

name: ECODATA
summary: Geoinformation database of Uzbek biodiversity and protected areas, launched on 28 July 2026 as a product of the Aral Sea Wetlands project, with an offline mobile module and public observation submission.

name: GBIF Uzbekistan
summary: Uzbekistan's node in the GBIF directory, where the country is a voting participant, partnering with the Global Biodiversity Information Facility.

name: Gissar Nature Reserve snow leopard camera trap study
summary: Closed camera trap study led by Bakhtiyor Aromov in late 2013 in Gissar Nature Reserve, which took the first photographs of snow leopards in Uzbekistan alongside bear, lynx and ibex.

name: Gissar State Nature Reserve
summary: Reserve established in 1983 in Kashkadarya Region with four divisions, administered by the National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change; 2026 camera traps recorded snow leopards and Siberian ibex.

name: Information Center on Biodiversity of Uzbekistan
summary: Project built by a UNDP-GEF forest management project, whose public Internet portal, presented in February 2020 alongside BCIMS, holds information on legislation, flora and fauna, protected areas, programmes and strategies.

name: Institute of Botany of the Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Uzbekistan
summary: Tashkent research institute that publishes 100 datasets through GBIF and holds the National Herbarium of Uzbekistan (TASH), and ran the first national IUCN Red List training in 2025 with IUCN.

name: Institute of Zoology of the Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Uzbekistan
summary: Reportedly used chips and GPS trackers to monitor birds of prey, and recorded Uzbekistan’s first Turkmen long-eared bat during a September 2026 expedition.

name: Integrated Conservation Management and Restoration of High-Value Landscapes in Uzbekistan
summary: GEF-funded project implemented by UNDP and the National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change, with IUCN as partner, aiming to conserve 881,000 hectares of Key Biodiversity Areas and restore three landscapes.

name: Karakalpak State University named after Berdakh
summary: University whose affiliated authors wrote a 2025 paper on Bukhara deer trends in the Lower Amu Darya Biosphere Reserve from 2021 to 2024, using route surveys, camera traps and remote sensing analysis.

name: Kyzylkum State Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve established in 1971 across Khorezm and Bukhara regions, home to 359 animal species, where a camera trap recorded a Central Asian otter.

name: Lower Amudarya State Biosphere Reserve
summary: Biosphere reserve where a camera trap recorded Bukhara deer and a jungle cat, and the 2024 spring count recorded 1,566 Bukhara deer.

name: Monitoring of the drained bottom of the Aral Sea
summary: Closed project run by SIC ICWC, with UNDP support for two expeditions in 2019 and 2020 on the drained Aral Sea bottom, covering a study area of 1.2 million hectares.

name: National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change of the Republic of Uzbekistan
summary: Uzbek environmental body responsible for state control over forests and protected areas, with tasks including digital technologies and automated monitoring, partnering with UNDP and running Gissar State Reserve.

name: Nurata State Nature Reserve
summary: Nature reserve run by the National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change, where a camera trap recorded Kyzylkum argali and the 2026 spring survey counted 2,130 argali.

name: Republican Center for Aerogeodesy
summary: Subordinate organisation of the Cadastre Agency whose deputy director said it captured digital images of over 7 million hectares of forest territory for forest mapping.

name: Republican Ecological Resource Centre "Ekomaktab"
summary: Non-governmental non-profit organisation implementing yashiltamojnya.uz with Institute of Zoology support in July 2025, when its director led the project for Uzbekistan.

name: Research Institute of Environment and Nature Conservation Technologies
summary: Research institute that, in August 2024, was reported to be fitting GPS trackers to a vulture and a black vulture with the Institute of Zoology, and is the affiliation of a 2024 Ugam-Chatkal vegetation paper's first author.

name: Saigachy Complex Landscape Reserve
summary: Reserve run by the National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change that has introduced SMART patrolling and, in October 2026, installed ten cameras and ten camera traps at new watering points under the Aral Sea Wetlands project.

name: Samarkand State University named after Sharof Rashidov
summary: University named as one of two affiliations of the first author of a 2024 paper on monitoring and mapping rangeland health in Samarkand using remote sensing and GIS.

name: Satellite tagging and tracking of Egyptian Vultures in Uzbekistan
summary: Active project that began in summer 2021 to satellite tag Egyptian Vultures in Central Asia for the first time; the Hawk Conservancy Trust's page says 16 birds have been tagged in Uzbekistan so far.

name: Smart Forestry
summary: Platform incorporating forest mapping orthophotos, according to CAREC, with UzDaily reporting plans for real-time forest monitoring and a Digital Forestry Center using artificial intelligence.

name: Sociable Lapwing Monitoring Programme at Talimarzhan
summary: Closed monitoring programme run by the Uzbekistan Society for the Protection of Birds, funded by CEPF from August 2020 to September 2022, using daily coastal counts and route counts of 33 to 55 km.

name: Southern Ustyurt National Park
summary: National park designated in 2020 where SMART patrolling has been introduced as a standard patrol tool, according to a Succow Foundation project page.

name: Space monitoring of illegal logging in Uzbekistan
summary: Proposed nationwide year-end space monitoring from 2026 would involve Uzbekcosmos under a presidential decree, with on-site investigations within five days of receiving information about illegal felling.

name: Specification of the Status of the Pallas's Cat (Otocolobus manul) in Uzbekistan
summary: Closed project announced in June 2015 to determine the Pallas's cat's status in Uzbekistan using montane camera-trap surveys, prey counts and interviews, listed under Maria Gritsina's name by the Rufford Foundation.

name: State Programme for Monitoring the Natural Environment in Uzbekistan, 2026-2030
summary: State programme for monitoring Uzbekistan's natural environment from 2026 to 2030, approved by resolution No. 275 of 25 May 2026, covering migratory waterbirds, forest cover classification and a planned remote sensing vegetation monitoring tool.

name: Strengthening digital conservation practices in desert protected areas
summary: Closed project, run by GIZ as part of the EcoAral regional project for BMZ, that introduced SMART as a standard patrol tool in two Uzbek protected areas and produced border fence recommendations from camera-trap monitoring.

name: Surkhan State Reserve
summary: Protected reserve in Sherabad, Uzbekistan, established in 1986, which has introduced SMART patrolling, installed camera traps and publishes a CC BY 4.0 dataset of 108 mammal phenology records from 2010 to 2014 on GBIF.

name: Sustainable Natural Resource and Forest Management in Key Mountainous Areas Important for Globally Significant Biodiversity
summary: UNDP-listed project completed, running January 2017 to May 2024, planned to cover Uzbekistan's snow leopard range, which collected distribution data from 2018 and recorded at least three snow leopards in a July 2019 camera-trap survey.

name: Sustainable natural resource use and forest management in key mountainous areas important for globally significant biodiversity
summary: Completed joint UNDP, GEF and State Ecology Committee project whose 2019 camera-trap survey with two protected areas recorded at least three snow leopards.

name: Tashkent Institute of Irrigation and Agricultural Mechanization Engineers National Research University
summary: Tashkent university of irrigation and agricultural mechanization engineering, with which the first author of a paper on Central Asian desertification trends, using MODIS data and Google Earth Engine, is affiliated.

name: Tree Registry (Tashkent)
summary: Tashkent tree database project whose AI training dataset covered 257,000 trees and nearly two million photographs in December 2025, with 227,013 Shaykhantakhur trees recorded by June 2026.

name: Ugam-Chatkal National Natural Park
summary: Protected area whose researchers and inspectors joined a UNDP/GEF monitoring group in July 2019 for a camera-trap survey, using 23 trail cameras in 14 cells, that recorded at least three snow leopards.

name: Uzbekcosmos Agency
summary: Uzbek space agency that, as reported, signed a satellite monitoring memorandum with the Prosecutor General's Office, analyses farmland and water from space data, and presented AI-based satellite solutions in June 2026.

name: Uzbekistan Resilient Landscape Restoration Project (RESILAND)
summary: US$153 million World Bank-funded restoration project, run by the forest agency, whose forest mapping, reported by CAREC in 2026, found forest coverage over 513,000 hectares above earlier records.

name: Uzbekistan Society for the Protection of Birds
summary: NGO established in 2007, funded by the Sigrid Rausing Trust, doing bird research and monitoring; its 2023 waterbird census covered 15 water bodies in 10 regions with 70 participants.

name: Vozrozhdeniya Island saiga research
summary: Proposed project run by the Saiga Conservation Alliance and funded by the People's Trust for Endangered Species, planning satellite imagery and camera traps to estimate saiga numbers, range and island use.

name: Yashil Tamojnya
summary: Platform presented at its launch on 25 July 2025, developed under a project against wildlife crime in Central Asia, letting customs and border officers identify species, check CITES status and check permits.

name: Yukori Tupalang National Nature Park
summary: National nature park created on 4 March 2022 in Sariasiya District, Surkhandarya Region, run by the National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change; a camera trap there recorded a Tien Shan brown bear.

name: Zaamin State Reserve
summary: State reserve where a camera trap recorded a Tien Shan brown bear, and the autumn 2024 count put brown bears in the reserve at 24.

name: Zarafshan National Park
summary: National park whose rangers were reported in July 2026 to be training in SMART patrol data, with smartphones with SMART Mobile to replace paper logs, after receiving eight camera traps in 2024.

name: BioSleuths Challenge
summary: National initiative run by the Sustainable Development Unit with UNDP as partner; on Earth Day 2026 participants documented biodiversity in the Montreal Watershed, with observations to feed national environmental records.

name: Climate and Conservation Risk Mapping Initiative in St Vincent and the Grenadines
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, February 2024 to April 2025, that aimed to prepare GIS maps of climate change effects and conservation challenges for biodiversity in the St Vincent Central Mountain Range.

name: Conservation of the Endangered Whistling Warbler Project
summary: Project launched in April 2022 with the Forestry Department, built by BirdsCaribbean, to monitor the Whistling Warbler and other forest birds; a January 2023 workshop had participants record counts in eBird.

name: Conserving Biodiversity and Reducing Land Degradation Using a Ridge-to-Reef Approach (Saint Vincent and the Grenadines)
summary: GEF-funded project aiming to enhance biodiversity and ecosystem services conservation through an expanded protected area system and sustainable land management; UNDP says it helped make the 2021 parrot census possible.

name: Fisheries Division (Saint Vincent and the Grenadines)
summary: Division of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, Fisheries, Rural Transformation, Industry and Labour that received sea turtle monitoring supplies from SVGCMEMS on 1 October 2025, for Colonaire and Sandy Bay.

name: Forestry Department (Saint Vincent and the Grenadines)
summary: Government department that runs the national parrot census; sixty staff and volunteers carried out the September 2021 count, which UNDP reports it treats as an indicator of forest health.

name: JEMS Progressive Community Organisation
summary: Organisation that runs a climate and conservation risk mapping initiative; Searchlight reported in January 2025 it is developing a new national vulnerability risk map, with a 30-layer GIS map produced so far.

name: Ministry of Tourism, Civil Aviation and Sustainable Development (Saint Vincent and the Grenadines)
summary: Ministry based on Upper Bay Street, Kingstown, that issued the February 2026 release on the 7th National Report to the CBD and whose Sustainable Development Unit met Conservation International and CEPF in March 2025.

name: National Parks, Rivers and Beaches Authority
summary: Describes itself as a statutory government body protecting heritage through protected areas, and reports monitoring at about 42 water quality stations and eleven mainland beaches.

name: National Parrot Census (Saint Vincent)
summary: Programme started in 1986 and run by the Forestry Department; the 2010 census estimated 800 parrots, none followed until 2021 for lack of funds, and the 2021 count used GEF-funded project resources.

name: Protecting the Union Island Gecko and Pink Rhino Iguana
summary: Closed project in which SVGEF says it funded Fauna & Flora, with the Forestry Department, to protect the Union Island gecko and pink rhino iguana in Chatham Forest, identifying threats and prioritising interventions.

name: Rewilding Pigeon Island
summary: Project run by SVGEF on Pigeon Island, focused on habitat restoration and invasive species monitoring to protect seabirds, using camera traps and surveys for a baseline, with a largely Bequia community team.

name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Coastal and Marine Ecosystems Management Strengthening Project
summary: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines project, funded by the GEF with US$3.65 million and implemented by the World Bank from April 2022 to 2027, aiming to strengthen coastal and marine ecosystem management.

name: Science Initiative for Environmental Conservation and Education
summary: Established in St Vincent in 2011, headed by Lystra Culzac, it partnered with EPIC on Grenadines seabird research; SVGPF funded its National Avian Education Programme.

name: St. Vincent and the Grenadines Environment Fund
summary: Non-profit company registered in the country and member of the Conservation Collective; it runs the Pigeon Island project and sea turtle monitoring, and in June 2026 its rangers surveyed conch in proposed Bequia marine protected areas.

name: Sustainable Development Unit (Saint Vincent and the Grenadines)
summary: National focal point for climate change, biodiversity and related areas; it held the 7th National Report validation workshop with UNDP on 16 February 2026 and runs the BioSleuths Challenge.

name: Sustainable Grenadines Inc
summary: Non-governmental organisation, according to BirdsCaribbean, that trained community researchers in 2020 to identify stony coral tissue loss disease; 31 surveys on 6 islands found it absent from the country and Grenada then.

name: SVGEF Sea Turtle Monitoring Project
summary: Project run by SVGEF that began its fourth year in 2025, expanded to 11 beaches including Bequia, and in June 2026 began a monitoring season for nesting hawksbill and green turtles.

name: Tobago Cays Marine Park
summary: Marine park whose six staff were certified in December 2020 for routine biophysical monitoring, on a course funded by the SVG Conservation Fund; the CBD profile says it regularly inventories seagrass, fish and coral.

name: Union Island Environmental Alliance
summary: Community group, per SVGEF, whose ranger team the UIEA says received the International Ranger Award at the IUCN World Conservation Congress; its work includes forest patrols, gecko monitoring and turtle nest protection.

name: Agencia Bolivariana para Actividades Espaciales
summary: Venezuelan space agency listed in the WMO OSCAR database, which gives its Venezuelan Remote Sensing Satellite programme as running 2012 to 2023, with VRSS-1 to 2022 and VRSS-2 to 2023.

name: Aves y Café
summary: Bird monitoring project that Mongabay reported in August 2019 had recorded 224 resident Venezuelan and eight migratory species, begun in 2017 and awaiting results of a second monitoring round; it partners with Provita.

name: Censo Neotropical de Aves Acuáticas de Venezuela
summary: Long-term waterbird monitoring programme in Venezuela, run by the Unión Venezolana de Ornitólogos, carried out since 2006 and covering 32 localities in its 2022 census.

name: Centro para la Investigación de Tiburones de Venezuela
summary: Organisation that states its mission as shark and ray research and education in Venezuela and the Caribbean, with an objective of collecting data and a project monitoring fisheries.

name: Conotos de Caracas
summary: Citizen science project started in 2016 on the status of Crested Oropendolas in Caracas, built by Fernando Machado-Stredel, which received 652 reports from 103 contributors between January 2016 and March 2019.

name: Evaluación poblacional del Chorlito Nevado en la isla de Coche
summary: Snowy Plover population survey on Coche Island, run by AveZona and the ARA MACAO Scientific Foundation, begun formally in 2019 with monthly visits and funded by BirdsCaribbean; led by Josmar Márquez.

name: Fundación Científica ARA MACAO
summary: Venezuelan research non-profit that builds Venezuela's bird banding programme and, according to a paper, monitored or banded land and seabirds at Los Roques from 2012 until publication.

name: Fundación para el Desarrollo de las Ciencias Físicas, Matemáticas y Naturales
summary: Non-profit civil society organisation founded in 1973 by the Academy of Sciences, whose FUDECI team has, per a funder's report, worked since October 2024 to bolster the Rancho Grande harlequin toad population.

name: Global Park Defense en el Parque Nacional Península de Paria
summary: Project in Península de Paria National Park where, since 2021, rangers use SMART on mobile phones to log patrols and offences; Provita reports over 120 offences and about a hundred biodiversity observations.

name: Global status and conservation of Tucacas killifish in the coastal plains of Venezuela
summary: Closed project in Venezuela, funded by a $4,990 renewal grant awarded on 1 January 2024, that mapped aquatic habitats using field surveys and remote sensing and built a photo and video database; its team considers both phases' objectives accomplished.

name: Instituto de Ciencias Ambientales y Ecológicas
summary: Institute named as responsible for two GLORIA-Andes sites in Venezuela, Gavidia (installed from 2014, resampled 2019) and La Culata (installed 2012), and publisher of a 2020 phenology and pollination protocol.

name: Instituto Experimental Jardín Botánico "Dr. Tobías Lasser"
summary: Institute of the Universidad Central de Venezuela, run by it, which Provita names as publisher of the Libro Rojo de la Flora Venezolana, a book Provita says shows 559 threatened plant species.

name: Instituto Geográfico de Venezuela Simón Bolívar
summary: National mapping authority which GeoWeek News describes as reorganised into the IGVSB in the early 2000s, with output shifting from systematic national mapping to sporadic thematic products.

name: Instituto Nacional de Parques
summary: Venezuelan parks institute that Diario de los Andes (December 2024) describes as attached to MINEC and having a civil park ranger corps, with a president stressing protected area commitments.

name: Laboratorio de Sistemas de Información Geográfica y Modelado Ambiental, Universidad Simón Bolívar
summary: University-run digital geography research centre working in remote sensing, cartography and GIS, which Provita names among three MapBiomas Venezuela co-leads.

name: Libro Rojo de la Fauna Venezolana
summary: Red list of Venezuelan fauna built by Provita, which says it has published four editions; its IUCN-standard assessments find 289 threatened animal species.

name: Libro Rojo de la Flora Venezolana
summary: Red list of Venezuelan plants, built by the Instituto Experimental Jardín Botánico, which Provita says shows 559 threatened species, 117 of them Critically Endangered, and which Provita supported in two editions.

name: MapBiomas Venezuela
summary: Collaborative network, built by Provita, Wataniba, LSIGMA-USB and RAISG, producing free annual land cover maps from 1985 using Landsat and machine learning on Google Earth Engine, with new modules released in 2026.

name: Ministerio del Poder Popular para el Ecosocialismo
summary: Environment ministry reported to have convened a 2025 biodiversity strategy workshop and enabled 0800-Ambiente by March 2026, listed by GEF as an Amazonas project’s executing agency.

name: Movimiento Ambientalista No Gubernamental La Educación
summary: NGO known as Mangle, which Mongabay (2026) says Lermith Torres founded in 2006, working with local fishers to monitor flamingos and reported to have recorded Venezuela's 1,425th bird species.

name: Phynatura
summary: Non-profit civil society organisation founded in 2005, whose founder told Mongabay (2023) that its monitoring recorded 42 ha deforested in its conservation area in the previous year, against over 300 ha the year before.

name: Programa de Anillamiento de Aves de Venezuela
summary: Voluntary programme started in 2018 by several Venezuelan research bodies to coordinate scientific bird ringing, with one aim being a public, coordinated database of ringing data.

name: Provita
summary: Venezuelan non-profit founded in 1987 that says it co-leads MapBiomas Venezuela and reported ringing 159 parrot fledglings and counting 3,203 wild parrots in Macanao in 2026.

name: Provita Biodiversity Portal
summary: Portal built by Provita that brings together GBIF records of Venezuelan species and data from its own projects, including terrestrial ecosystems from the 2010 red book, and is updated periodically.

name: Proyecto Orbicella
summary: Coral monitoring project that Mongabay (2020) reports covers 10 areas in Morrocoy and two in the Cuare Wildlife Refuge, with more than half of the sites in poor condition.

name: Proyecto Oso Andino Guaramacal
summary: Andean bear monitoring project led by Marcos Hidalgo, which Mongabay reports recorded 489 bear events among 7,464 camera-trap events in 2021 and identified 29 individuals in a 230 km2 study area.

name: Proyecto Sebraba
summary: Venezuelan NGO researching and protecting jaguar habitat, whose founder told Mongabay (2020) it estimated 3.37 jaguars per 100 km2 south of Lake Maracaibo, with camera trap monitoring planned.

name: Rewilding the Rancho Grande Harlequin Toad (Atelopus cruciger): First release of captive bred toads (Phase I)
summary: Active project in Venezuela, funded by a $10,000 grant awarded on 30 September 2025, whose first phase released captive-bred harlequin toads and documented early survival, growth and signs of reproduction among adults.

name: Sistema Venezolano de Información sobre Diversidad Biológica
summary: Venezuelan biodiversity information system that Mongabay reported in 2017 depended on the Ministerio de Ecosocialismo y Aguas and listed 42 animal and plant species as exotic.

name: SOS Orinoco
summary: Organisation reported by El Diario and Mongabay to detect mining using satellite imagery; El Diario also reported its August 2026 report of a 5.8-hectare illegal mine in Canaima.

name: Strengthening management to combat threats from Aquatic Invasive Alien Species in Venezuela
summary: Active Global Environment Facility-funded project in Venezuela, run by the environment ministry and approved on 5 August 2024, aiming to strengthen institutional and community capacity to prevent, detect, control and eradicate aquatic invasive species.

name: Universidad Central de Venezuela
