summary: University whose Instituto Experimental Jardín Botánico Dr. Tobías Lasser published the Libro Rojo de la Flora Venezolana with support from Provita, according to Provita.

name: Universidad Simón Bolívar
summary: University whose Laboratorio de Sistemas de Información Geográfica y Modelado Ambiental is attached to its Department of Environmental Studies, according to the laboratory’s GBIF record.

name: Wataniba
summary: Civil society organisation promoting sustainable territorial management in the Venezuelan Amazon, which says it monitors mining, deforestation and burning by satellite; Mongabay reported in 2023 that it found 70 illegal mining sites.

name: Wilson's Plover reproductive monitoring project, Margarita Island
summary: Manomet-funded monitoring project on Margarita Island studying how human disturbance affects Wilson's Plover nesting success, which in its fourth year (2025) banded 18 birds and monitored 16 nests.

name: AI/IoT for environmental management of Tram Chim National Park (AI4TramChim)
summary: Project with University of Wollongong and Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology experts, funded by a competitive Aus4Innovation grant, planning AI and machine learning models to classify Tram Chim National Park ecosystem health data and identify animals and plants.

name: AIMVIE: AI Solutions for Mangrove Blue Carbon in Vietnam
summary: Proposes satellite and drone AI mangrove mapping in Vietnam, led by Quan Le with Irish Aid funding and partner country lead Dr Quan-Quoc Vo of Can Tho University.

name: Bach Ma National Park
summary: National park whose director said targeted monitoring in 2025 documented at least 29 wildlife species across 10 sites, and Dan Tri (2026) reports camera traps recorded rare species, three critically endangered.

name: Ban Quản lý Khu bảo tồn loài Sao la (Quảng Nam)
summary: Board of the Quảng Nam saola reserve, established in 2012, that has used camera traps, SMART Mobile data storage and a GreenViet partnership with leech and water samples to assess biodiversity.

name: Ban Quản lý rừng đặc dụng Nam Quảng Trị
summary: Forest management board that, according to VietnamPlus, surveyed 10 transects and placed 34 camera traps, and reported 228 bird species, 139 directly recorded, in a June to September 2026 study in Đakrông Nature Reserve.

name: Ban quản lý rừng đặc dụng Đà Nẵng
summary: Forest management board that, according to Tiền Phong, recorded nine elephants after months of camera trapping with 45 traps at 15 points in the almost 19,000-hectare Đà Nẵng elephant reserve.

name: Bidoup-Nui Ba National Park
summary: National park whose director reported in 2020 a camera-trap survey with the Southern Institute of Ecology and Leibniz-IZW, aiming to monitor endangered species' status and population dynamics.

name: Biodiversity conservation in the Central Annamites through ecosystem protection and land management
summary: Completed project run by KfW Entwicklungsbank and funded by the International Climate Initiative, which surveyed with 140 camera traps at 64 locations in Laos and Vietnam; Vietnam patrols removed 8,341 snares.

name: Biodiversity Survey and Monitoring Centre (Viet Nam)
summary: Centre run by the Nature and Biodiversity Conservation Agency, structured under Decision 958/QĐ-BNNMT, that carries out baseline surveys, monitoring, inventories and statistics, with tasks including information technology and remote sensing.

name: Camera Trap Monitoring and Community Conservation for Establishing a Protected Area in Yen Mo, Ninh Binh, Vietnam
summary: Closed project that planned camera traps to record larger mammals and human influence in the unprotected Yen Mo limestone complex, described as holding the third largest Delacour's langur population, with a final evaluation of December 2025.

name: Cat Ba National Park
summary: National park whose staff member, Le Ngoc Nghi, told Dan Tri (January 2025) that the park monitors and reports on its langurs daily.

name: Cat Tien National Park
summary: National park where a 2026 paper reports Siamese crocodile monitoring at Bau Sau from 2021 to 2024, citing the park's own earlier monitoring reports, including one for 2017.

name: CBES marine mammals encounters through citizen science apps (2022)
summary: 2022 dataset of marine mammal encounters in Viet Nam recorded by fishers, tourists, ship crews and marine protected area staff, with AppSheet forms given to 20 protected areas, delivered under GBIF's BIFA programme.

name: Center for Biodiversity Conservation and Endangered Species
summary: Not-for-profit research organisation in Ho Chi Minh City, established under a VUSTA decision, that publishes GBIF datasets on cetacean strandings and marine mammal encounters in Vietnam.

name: Center for Nature Conservation and Development
summary: Organisation that says its team carried out three saola investigations in the Northern Annamites in 2023 and 2024, with over 691,200 camera trap hours, and collected eDNA samples.

name: Chư Mom Ray National Park
summary: National park of more than 60,600 hectares of forest, which VOH reported in August 2025 had deployed 280 automatic cameras and listed 1,003 fauna species, 112 endangered or rare.

name: Conservation of Odonates (Insecta: Odonata), Including Globally Threatened Species, in the Karst Ecosystems of Ba Be National Park, a Ramsar Site in Vietnam
summary: Active conservation project on Odonata, including globally threatened species, in the karst ecosystems of Ba Be National Park, aiming to produce a replicable bioindicator monitoring tool for long-term use by park staff and conservation groups.

name: Conservation of the Indo-Pacific Humpback Dolphin (Sousa chinensis) in the Cat Ba
summary: Active project planning boat-based photo-identification surveys, behavioural observations and habitat mapping in the Cat Ba Archipelago, to give baseline population data for marine spatial planning and an Important Marine Mammal Area proposal.

name: Conservation of Two Critically Endangered Species: Red-shanked Douc and Grey-shanked Douc in Chu Mom Ray National Park, Vietnam
summary: Funded by the Rufford Foundation, this project involves CCD surveying and monitoring red-shanked and grey-shanked doucs in partnership with Chư Mom Ray National Park.

name: Côn Đảo National Park
summary: National park on the IUCN Green List for 2025 to 2030, where Viet Nam News (2025) says coral reef biodiversity is monitored regularly and volunteers join turtle nesting patrols.

name: Cúc Phương National Park
summary: National park whose biodiversity monitoring, per Tiền Phong, was strengthened with 37 camera-trap points and 4,373 independent wildlife detections over 4,513 survey nights, and which partners with Save Vietnam's Wildlife.

name: Database System for Forest and Coffee Growing Areas (Viet Nam)
summary: Database launched on 17 December 2024 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, IDH and JDE Peet's, integrating land-use, cadastral and production area data, which IDH says will enable deforestation risk assessments.

name: Department of Forestry and Forest Protection (Viet Nam)
summary: Listed under Decree 35/2025/ND-CP as a Ministry of Agriculture and Environment unit, with a runs link to the Department of Survey, Mapping and Geographic Information of Vietnam.

name: Department of Survey, Mapping and Geographic Information of Vietnam
summary: Unit listed in Decree 35/2025/ND-CP as part of the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, and linked as run by the Department of Forestry and Forest Protection.

name: Discovering Forest Musk Deer Populations from the Karst Mountains in Northern Vietnam
summary: Closed conservation-planning project reporting camera-trap detections of an adult forest musk deer in Huu Lien in early 2021 and a male in Kim Hy.

name: Evaluating Roadkill Impact on Reptiles and Amphibians in Ba Vi National Park, Northern Vietnam
summary: Active project evaluating roadkill impact on reptiles and amphibians in Ba Vi National Park, intended to add to the threat database and identify road sections with high collision risk.

name: Exploring Associations of Dung Beetles With Globally Threatened Mammals in the Tropical Karst Forests of Non Nuoc Cao Bang UNESCO Global Geopark, Vietnam
summary: Active project using dung beetles as ecological indicators of mammal populations in karst forests where camera trapping is hard, aiming for a cost-effective monitoring framework.

name: Forest Inventory and Planning Institute
summary: Institute that, according to a June 2024 article, tested the SEPAL change alert tool with FAO experts in Hoa Binh, Thua Thien Hue and Gia Lai provinces.

name: FPT University
summary: University whose affiliated authors are listed by OpenAlex as first authors of papers on bird classification using transfer learning and phytoplankton classification using feature selection.

name: From Grassland to Forest: Safeguarding Wild Cattle in Vietnam’s Central Highlands
summary: Planned project to use camera traps and thermal drones to assess banteng and gaur distribution, habitat use and threats in Ea So Nature Reserve and Krong Nang Protection Forest, with ranger training.

name: Fulbright University Vietnam
summary: University where, per OpenAlex, an author (among other affiliations) is first author of a paper on extracting reproductive condition and habitat information from text with a transformer-based pipeline.

name: GBIF Viet Nam
summary: Country node for Viet Nam in the GBIF registry with observer participation status, which endorses the Center for Biodiversity Conservation and Endangered Species as a publisher.

name: GEF-UNDP project linking wildlife conservation with nature-based tourism in Viet Nam
summary: Viet Nam News reports a US$7.15 million GEF-funded project through UNDP to 2030, led by NBCA, planning tourism models and SMART patrol deployment or expansion in two national parks.

name: GFD
summary: Hanoi-based remote sensing and GIS provider that says it works on forestry, water and environmental monitoring, with an AI module detecting signs of deforestation or degradation.

name: GFD Forest Monitoring System
summary: Integrated GIS platform, built by GFD, for managing forest change data at provincial, district and forest-owner level, using 10 m Sentinel-2 imagery and field data from the FRMS mobile software.

name: Graduate University of Science and Technology
summary: University where, per OpenAlex, an author (among other affiliations) is first author of a paper on semi-supervised collaborative fuzzy clustering for land cover classification.

name: GreenViet
summary: Non-profit science and technology organisation in Da Nang working on ecosystems and endangered species in central Vietnam; Eco-Business reported in September 2020 that it and Fauna & Flora used 130 camera traps in Kon Plong.

name: Habitat Assessment and Community Engagement for Forest Musk Deer Conservation in Huu Lien Nature Reserve, Northern Vietnam
summary: Proposed project at Huu Lien Nature Reserve whose team reports camera-trap monitoring since 2020, with a population assessment suggesting fewer than 10 forest musk deer remain.

name: Hanoi University of Civil Engineering
summary: University where, per OpenAlex, an author is first author of a paper comparing boosting algorithms for land cover mapping using object-based classification.

name: Hanoi University of Industry
summary: University where, per OpenAlex, an author (among other affiliations) is first author of a paper on semi-supervised collaborative fuzzy clustering for land cover classification.

name: Hanoi University of Natural Resources and Environment
summary: University with OpenAlex-listed first-author affiliations for papers on random forest land cover change in Van Yen and machine learning land cover classification on Google Earth Engine in Hung Yen.

name: Hanoi University of Science and Technology
summary: University with an author listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on segmenting fish in their natural habitat, using deep learning, for fish size measurement.

name: Hue University
summary: University with an author listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on automated wetland mapping, using Google Earth Engine and machine learning, for lotus in central Vietnam.

name: Hue University of Agriculture and Forestry
summary: University with an author listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on automated wetland mapping, using Google Earth Engine and machine learning, for lotus in central Vietnam.

name: Hạt Kiểm lâm Hoàng Liên
summary: Forest protection unit with 46 ranger civil servants and seven ranger stations, reported by Báo Lào Cai in October 2026 to use drones in patrol and monitoring to spot encroachment and new fires.

name: Industrial University of Ho Chi Minh City
summary: University with an author listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on turning a land cover map into a land use map, using Landsat data and a random forest classifier.

name: Institute of Ecology and Biological Resources
summary: Vietnamese institute whose GBIF record gives its aims as studying Vietnam's flora and fauna, and which publishes a dataset of 200 endemic or endangered plant species.

name: Institute of Oceanography
summary: Institute based in Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa province, which says it has three monitoring stations and a museum holding about 23,000 marine specimens of 5,000 species.

name: Integrated Seagrass Conservation for Dugongs and Sea Turtles Through Mapping, Genetic Diversity, and Community Engagement at Con Dao National Park, Vietnam
summary: Active project planning the first comprehensive GIS map of Con Dao's seagrass beds from Sentinel-2 imagery and ground surveys, plus a genetic diversity assessment of key seagrass species using molecular markers.

name: Investigating the Population Status, Distribution, and Threats to the Blackshanked Douc (Pygathrix Nigripes) in EA So Nature Reserve, Vietnam
summary: Active project aiming to run the first baseline survey of black-shanked douc in Ea Sô Nature Reserve, planning 12 days of line-transect surveys to confirm groups, estimate group size and record threats.

name: Joint Vietnam-Russia Tropical Science and Technology Research Center
summary: Research centre with an author listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on mapping wetland tree species in Dong Rui Commune using UAV multispectral images and machine learning.

name: Khu Bảo tồn thiên nhiên Pù Hoạt
summary: Nature reserve in the West Nghệ An Biosphere Reserve, managing over 85,000 hectares, which its director told Đại Đoàn Kết has installed six camera-trap positions in two areas to monitor mammals and threats.

name: Management Board of My Son Landscape Protection Zone
summary: Board that, since late November 2025 with the Da Nang City Special-Use Forest Management Board, installed 30 camera traps under a biodiversity monitoring plan, which documented 27 wild animal species.

name: Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (Viet Nam)
summary: Ministry whose duties, set by Decree 35/2025/ND-CP, include organising biodiversity baseline surveys, monitoring and databases and drawing up the national master plan, and which runs four departments and agencies.

name: Monitoring populations of Black-faced Spoonbill and migratory waterbirds wintering in Xuan Thuy National Park
summary: Closed project supported for three years from 2022 by the Hong Kong Bird Watching Society's Asia Conservation Fund, with 21 survey days in 2024/25 and a January 2025 count of 112 black-faced spoonbills.

name: National Biodiversity Database (dadangsinhhoc.mae.vn)
summary: National biodiversity database that the Ministry says NBCA completed over 2024 to 2026 and put into operation, built and run by NBCA, with five of eight designed modules completed and running.

name: National Biodiversity Database System (Viet Nam)
summary: Database built by the national biodiversity database project, intended to store taxonomy and provincial survey data; a February 2015 newsletter announced a first version holding only Xuan Thuy National Park data.

name: National Remote Sensing Department (Viet Nam)
summary: Department listed on the ministry's page, under which Decision 637/QĐ-BNNMT makes the Centre for Monitoring Agriculture, Natural Resources and Environment a public unit.

name: Nature and Biodiversity Conservation Agency (Viet Nam)
summary: Hanoi-based agency of the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment advising the minister on nature and biodiversity conservation, with a Biodiversity Survey and Monitoring Centre and partners including the GBIF Secretariat.

name: Núi Chúa National Park
summary: National park in the Núi Chúa World Biosphere Reserve that, per Viet Nam News, recorded 585 nesting female turtles and 203 successful nests from 2014 to early October 2025.

name: Phong Nha - Kẻ Bàng National Park
summary: National park reporting that its camera-trap monitoring programme recorded 64 wild animal species from 78,496 photographs, including 34 bird and six primate species, with 2 to 38 species per station.

name: Poachers, Patrols and Protection: An Integrative Solution to Owston’s Civet Conservation in Vietnam
summary: Closed project that aimed to link camera-trap data, SMART anti-poaching data and social research on hunting to improve patrol planning in Pu Mat National Park, with camera trapping planned beyond Khe Choang.

name: Posts and Telecommunications Institute of Technology
summary: Institute with an author listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on detecting coastal forest cover change in Vietnam using satellite images and convolutional neural networks.

name: Project for Development of National Biodiversity Database System in Vietnam
summary: Project run by the Biodiversity Conservation Agency of the Vietnam Environment Administration with JICA technical support from November 2011 to March 2015, including pilot coastal wetland surveys at Xuan Thuy National Park.

name: Pu Mat National Park
summary: According to Save Vietnam's Wildlife, this Nghệ An park co-manages an anti-poaching unit established in 2018 and uses SMART and AI Poachercam for patrols and biodiversity monitoring.

name: Safeguarding Giants: An AI-Powered Initiative for Elephants
summary: Closed Save Vietnam's Wildlife project, described on a Rufford page of 10 August 2023, proposing thermal drone surveys, AI cameras alerting smartphones and citizen science to reduce human-elephant conflict.

name: Satellite mangrove health monitoring system (Cà Mau)
summary: Active satellite monitoring system combining Sentinel-2 imagery, Google Earth Engine, PROSAIL and Gaussian Processes Regression, which has produced forest condition maps for Mũi Cà Mau National Park and the Ngọc Hiển shrimp-forest model.

name: Save Vietnam's Wildlife
summary: Conservation organisation with offices in Ninh Binh Province and Hanoi, which set up an anti-poaching unit at Pu Mat National Park in 2018 and later extended it to other parks, using SMART and AI PoacherCams.

name: Saving Saola from the Brink of Extinction
summary: Closed project funded by the European Union and run by WWF-Vietnam in 2022 to 2024, whose 2023 to 2024 surveys used camera traps and eDNA samples to check for saola.

name: Seasonal Population Dynamics of the Threatened Pasman’s Crocodile Newt (Tylototriton Pasmansi) in Northern Vietnam
summary: Active project to monitor Pasman's crocodile newt across seasons for year-round data on abundance and detectability, feeding conservation recommendations for Phu Canh Nature Reserve.

name: SEPAL near real-time forest change alert pilot in Viet Nam
summary: Closed pilot run by the Forest Inventory and Planning Institute, with FAO experts, that tested the SEPAL change alert tool in three provinces, generating and verifying forest disturbance alerts from medium resolution satellite data.

name: Sustainable Forest Management and Biodiversity Conservation Project (VFBC)
summary: Closed USAID-funded project run by WWF-Viet Nam, whose 2023 workshop presented forest monitoring in 21 areas and a camera-trap baseline, and which ran 91 activities at Cúc Phương from 2021 to 2025.

name: Tay Do University
summary: University with OpenAlex-listed first authors of papers on underwater fish detection and segmentation using YOLOv8, RF-DETR and SAM 2.1, and acoustic machine learning for Pantanal species identification.

name: Tay Nguyen University
summary: University with an author listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on predicting land use and land cover change from multi-temporal satellite imagery with a multi-layer perceptron Markov model.

name: Thai Nguyen University
summary: University with an author listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper predicting the distribution of estuary fish larvae and juveniles by salinity, using remote sensing and fuzzy logic.

name: Thu Dau Mot University
summary: University with an author listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on yearly land cover classification in Thanh Hoa province using random forest, time-series NDVI and topography.

name: Thuyloi University
summary: University whose author is listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on optimising machine learning models for forest fire susceptibility mapping in Gia Lai province.

name: Ton Duc Thang University
summary: University whose author is listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on applying soft computing to predict water quality in a wetland.

name: Tra Vinh University
summary: University with authors listed in OpenAlex as first author of two papers: one on urban bat echolocation calls in Vietnam, one on mangrove CO2 sequestration modelling using random forest.

name: U Minh Ha National Park
summary: National park that Tuổi Trẻ News reported in May 2026 operates one rotating thermal and optical camera cluster covering about 2,500 hectares per camera for fire monitoring, with three more proposed.

name: University of Da Nang
summary: University whose authors are listed in OpenAlex as first authors of two papers: a vision transformer and KNN model for forest plant classification, and an acoustic illegal logging detection system using LoRA.

name: University of Science and Technology - The University of Da Nang
summary: University unit whose author is listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on an acoustic illegal logging detection system with automatic warnings over a LoRA network.

name: University of Science, Vietnam National University Hanoi
summary: University that publishes biodiversity datasets, including endemic insects of Vietnam and a 2023 camera-trap survey of terrestrial vertebrates in Xuan Lien Nature Reserve intended to establish a monitoring database.

name: University of Science, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City
summary: Publishes lichen and bryophyte datasets from its PHH Herbarium, which GBIF describes as holding Vietnam’s largest cryptogam collection; an author has a bird sound classification paper.

name: University of Transport Technology
summary: University whose author is listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper evaluating machine learning methods for forest fire modelling and prediction.

name: Utilizing satellite and drone imagery to monitor deforestation, UHIs, green space degradation, and detect super-emitters
summary: Project page at the VinUniversity Smart Green Transformation Center, led by Pham Huy Hieu, aiming to build an AI and computer vision framework using satellite and drone imagery for deforestation, urban heat, green space and methane monitoring.

name: VAST-VNSC 2019 CEOS Chair Initiative
summary: Initiative led by the Vietnam National Space Center in 2019 to support forest and rice crop monitoring in the Mekong Delta using Sentinel, Landsat and ALOS-2 data, as a regional observatory meant to continue.

name: Viet Nam National Forest Monitoring System
summary: National forest monitoring system of four subsystems set up under the 2017 Law on Forestry, updating forest change annually from satellite and field data, with a 2025 GFOI presentation noting no unified operating protocol.

name: Viet Nature Conservation Centre
summary: Autonomous national conservation NGO from BirdLife's Viet Nam programme, involved in a 2013 Spoon-billed Sandpiper census, with IUCN reporting a new BirdLife migratory species monitoring project in 2021.

name: Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology
summary: Academy whose author is listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on multimodal, multisensor earth observation data for estimating mangrove soil organic carbon in Vietnam.

name: Vietnam National Museum of Nature
summary: State organisation, founded in 2004 under the Vietnamese Academy of Science and Technology according to GBIF, that publishes a GBIF dataset of pteridophyte specimens held at the museum.

name: Vietnam National Space Center
summary: Space centre set up in 2011 under the Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology, working on satellite and remote sensing technology, and a CEOS member since 2013.

name: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City
summary: University whose author is listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper integrating object-based image analysis and tidymodels to compare machine learning algorithms for land cover classification.

name: Vietnam National University of Agriculture
summary: University whose author, among other affiliations, is listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper comparing machine learning algorithms for land cover classification in Hung Yen Province using Google Earth Engine.

name: Vietnam National University of Forestry
summary: University whose author is listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper applying machine learning and Landsat 8 to estimate aboveground carbon stock in evergreen broadleaf forest in Binh Phuoc Province.

name: Vietnam National University, Hanoi
summary: University whose author is listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper comparing machine learning methods for estimating mangrove above-ground biomass in the Red River Delta Biosphere Reserve.

name: VinUniversity
summary: University whose author is listed in OpenAlex as first author of a paper on deep learning for forest canopy height completion using Sentinel-2 imagery and sparse GEDI LiDAR observations.

name: Viện Sinh thái học miền Nam
summary: Institute described by VTC News in August 2024 as part of the Institute of Applied Materials Science, whose 36 camera traps in the Lòng Sông - Đá Bạc protection forest recorded 24 bird and mammal species.

name: VNU University of Science
summary: University whose author, Tien Dat Pham, is listed in OpenAlex as first author of a 2020 paper comparing machine learning methods for mangrove above-ground biomass estimation in the Red River Delta.

name: Vu Quang National Park
summary: National park that announced in December 2023, per Dan Tri, that its 85 biodiversity-monitoring camera traps had captured 58 rare and endangered species, nine found only in the Truong Son range.

name: WWF-Viet Nam
summary: Conservation organisation that, according to VietNamNet, led a four-year camera-trap wildlife survey across 21 forests, totalling more than 350,000 camera-trap days, with WWF-US and others under a USAID project.

name: Xuan Thuy National Park
summary: National park of 15,100 ha, recognised as an ASEAN Heritage Park in September 2025, where the ministry's site says 20 years of monitoring show 36 to 93 black-faced spoonbills a year.

name: Blue Prosperity Vanuatu
summary: According to Blue Prosperity's 2023 review, this initiative jointly assessed reefs and marine life across Vanuatu's six provinces and held a workshop on the draft Marine Spatial Plan.

name: C2O Marine Monitoring and Management Toolkit
summary: Six-module toolkit with standard methods for monitoring fish catch, reefs, mangroves, seagrass and other marine life, which Vanuatu's 2019 CBD report says was being implemented in selected North Efate communities.

name: C2O Pacific
summary: Local consulting company that Vanuatu's 2019 CBD report describes as guiding community toolkit implementation in North Efate, and that GCRMN credits with supplying coral reef monitoring data.

name: CCA Ranger Toolkit and Ranger App
summary: Vanuatu's first CCA Ranger Toolkit and Ranger App, built by Live and Learn Vanuatu and IT Scope with CEPF funding, with ranger data feeding directly into DEPC's data management system.

name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation
summary: Department run through the Ministry of Climate Change that, according to JNCC, supports registration and monitoring of Community Conservation Areas, and which uses the DEPC Data Management System.

name: Department of Forests
summary: Regulator of Vanuatu's forestry sector that collects forest resource information, advises on conservation and protected areas, and publishes the National Herbarium's 17,920 specimen records on GBIF.

name: Department of Lands, Surveys and Records
summary: Vanuatu agency under the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources whose work includes national GIS, remote sensing and aerial surveys; a November 2024 presentation reports a plan to split it into three departments.

name: DEPC Data Management System
summary: Biodiversity data system with an interactive map and monitoring repository, built by Engineering Business Services and DEPC on Nocobase, reported live across all DEPC divisions as of January 2026.

name: Engineering Business Services Limited
summary: An in-country developer that worked with OCPP and DEPC during 2023 to 2026, providing user training and testing for a departmental data management system launched in January 2026.

name: Flora of Vanuatu database
summary: Specimen database and interactive checklist of Vanuatu's vascular flora, built on Symbiota to replace a PlantNote database, with over 17,000 herbarium records and 1,000 photos migrated and sensitive data such as rare species locations hidden.

name: Live and Learn Vanuatu
summary: Local non-government organisation registered in 2001, funded by a $99,697 CEPF grant from 2018 to 2019 for a national ranger toolkit, ranger training and biodiversity surveys in five Community Conservation Areas.

name: Ministry of Climate Change Adaptation, Meteorology, Geo-Hazards, Environment, Energy and Disaster Management
summary: Vanuatu ministry through which DEPC manages, protects and conserves the country's natural environment, according to JNCC; DEPC's Port Vila office is in its compound.

name: The Vanuatu Environmental Science Society
summary: Small local NGO in Port Vila, funded by CEPF, publishing bat, seagrass and dugong datasets to GBIF, including 849 recalled dugong sightings with uncertain dates and locations.

name: Using Earth Observation and AI/ML technologies to support climate change adaptation for sustainable coral reef management and shoreline defence
summary: Climate Change AI 2024 innovation grant of $147,510, which plans to combine drone data, satellite imagery and field measurements with Google Earth Engine and ReefCloud to map coral reefs.

name: Vanua'tai Resource Monitors Network
summary: Network of community-based volunteer turtle monitors, reported in 2019 as having 470 active monitors across Vanuatu, which held its 28th annual general meeting in Luganville in September 2023.

name: Vanuatu Bureau of Statistics
summary: National statistics body that leads a project launched in 2024 using satellite imagery processed through Digital Earth Pacific to produce annual land cover and coral reef health maps, with models validated on field data.

name: Vanuatu Data Science Driving Innovation in Climate Change and Natural Disasters
summary: Project led by the Vanuatu Bureau of Statistics, launched in 2024, combining statistical data, satellite imagery and machine learning, with a full launch of its information system planned for 12 December 2025.

name: Vanuatu National Forest Inventory
summary: A 2019 report describes the first inventory in 1989–1992, a policy requirement for inventories every ten years, and planned visits to over 1,000 areas that year.

name: Vanuatu National Forest Monitoring System
summary: Forest monitoring system designed and developed during 2019 to 2021 and still in final design and approval as of February 2022, with a satellite monitoring system, a Forest Information System, a central dashboard, and tracking of cyclone and wind damage.

name: Vanuatu National Herbarium
summary: Created in Port Vila in 1986 and run by the Department of Forests, with 17,920 published specimen records and a requirement to store all plant collections made in Vanuatu.

name: Eradication of the black rat and Pacific rat from the Wallis lagoon islets
summary: Rat eradication on Wallis lagoon islets, part of the 2019 to 2023 PROTEGE programme, using drone-spread bait over 500 flights in 11 days at a total cost of 1,076,595 euros.

name: IMPACS (Initiative pour la Connaissance et la Conservation des Tortues Imbriquées dans le PACifique Sud)
summary: Project running in Wallis and Futuna and French Polynesia, dated 2024 to 2026, setting up a joint scientific programme to harmonise data collection on nesting green and hawksbill turtles.

name: Inventory of freshwater fish and crustaceans of Wallis and Futuna
summary: OFB-funded inventory of freshwater fish and crustaceans by Vies d'Ô douce in August 2023, following a 2004 inventory that recorded 34 species, four endemic, with another planned for late 2023.

name: Service territorial de l'environnement de Wallis-et-Futuna
summary: Created in 1997, this State and territory service defines and implements environmental policy, monitors rats and turtles, and is associated with reef, flying-fox and feral-pig projects.

name: Workshopping a reef restoration toolkit for Wallis et Futuna as a model for Pacific Island nations
summary: Closed James Cook University project, funded by AFRAN and dated October 2024 to May 2026, which planned CoralNet analysis of April 2024 reef photographs and ReefCloud training in Townsville.

name: Building Forward Better by Safeguarding Natural Capital and Ecosystem Services
summary: UNESCO-led Joint SDG Fund and Samoa Government programme planned to support ecosystem services policy, data collection and valuation, with SROS and MNRE implementing; its 2022 report lists scoping work.

name: Conservation International Samoa
summary: Programme run by Conservation International that says its fieldwork since April 2016 included natural capital mapping and biodiversity surveys, and that it works with government on coral reef monitoring.

name: Developing a framework and methodology for measuring carbon sinks from the forestry sector using Earth observation in Samoa
summary: Completed CTCN assistance, implemented by NIGT at Samoa's environment ministry's request, reported Random Forest mapping from satellite imagery and selection of 80 field survey points for verification.

name: Empowering Rural Communities in Key Biodiversity Areas to Protect the Critically Endangered Manumea and Other Endemic Samoan Fauna
summary: Closed BIOPAMA-funded grant of $49,670 (May 2021 to April 2022), led by the Samoa Conservation Society, that planned to train villagers in two Upolu villages to monitor the manumea.

name: Enhancing integrated sustainable management to safeguard Samoa's natural resources
summary: Active GEF-funded project run by the environment ministry, aiming to protect native species and ecosystems from invasive species and unsustainable land use; NIT reports it funded an invasive species database.

name: Forestry Division, Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (Samoa)
summary: Part of Samoa's environment ministry; its 2024 forest reference level submission says six of nine operators on the land use assessment were Forestry Division staff, using Landsat imagery in Google Earth Engine, with MapInfo then in use.

name: Ministry of Lands and Survey (Samoa)
summary: Samoan ministry that a 2024 UN-GGIM country presentation says carries out land administration and was established in July 2024.

name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (Samoa)
summary: Samoan ministry that the CBD country profile says consolidates land, water, forestry, parks and environmental protection; it has two GBIF datasets and partners with AIMS on reef monitoring.

name: National Geographic Pristine Seas Samoa expedition
summary: Expedition run by National Geographic Pristine Seas, described in an August 2026 release as a planned four-week survey of sea life and geology in Samoa's protected marine areas, using eDNA sampling.

name: Nu'utele Island restoration
summary: Active island restoration project led by the environment ministry, with Island Conservation, BirdLife and SPREP as partners, who Island Conservation says are committing to long-term monitoring and possible species reintroductions.

name: SAMFRIS Project
summary: Project within which the CBD country profile places a GIS-based data management system mapping forest extent and protected-area coverage in MNRE Forestry.

name: Samoa Biodiversity Database
summary: Dataset on GBIF, maintained by the environment ministry, that aggregates historic occurrence records from many contributors and has approximately 7,539 occurrences.

name: Samoa Conservation Society
summary: Conservation NGO that a 2025 Mongabay commentary says has sought help applying AI to manumea calls; a 2025 preprint tested a detection pipeline on its 2021 to 2023 recordings.

name: Samoa Marine Spatial Plan
summary: Active programme that Conservation International describes as a legally adopted framework to protect 30% and manage 100% of Samoa's ocean, with Waitt Foundation funding for monitoring and enforcement.

name: Samoa national coral reef assessment 2022
summary: Closed national coral reef assessment, led by the environment ministry in September 2022, which GCRMN reports was one of Samoa's most comprehensive and feeds into marine spatial planning.

name: Samoa National Forest Monitoring System
summary: Programme described in Samoa's 2024 forest reference level submission, which mentions setting up a national web portal and a remote sensing point-sampling method for land use change assessment.

name: Samoa National Invasive Alien Species Database
summary: Active dataset that NIT reports was launched during National Environment Week 2026 and will be a central repository for invasive species data, funded under a GEF project.

name: Scientific Research Organisation of Samoa
summary: A public body set up by the Government of Samoa in 2006; its GBIF publisher record says it does applied research and environmental monitoring, and intends to publish species occurrence data, with endorsement still awaited.

name: Searching for the Lost Tooth-Billed Pigeon
summary: A project run by the Colossal Foundation with the Samoa Conservation Society and BirdLife International, aiming to develop AI algorithms that detect tooth-billed pigeon calls in audio from microphones deployed in Samoa's forests.

name: The Flora of Samoa Data Portal
summary: Online dataset of native and naturalised flowering plants of the Samoan archipelago, covering 810 species, which the portal says combines Whistler's 40 years of work with specimen collections; it partners with Samoa's environment ministry and is still uploading datasets.

name: Biodiversity Conservation in the Malhan Protected Area
summary: Active project run by Sanid Organization for Relief and Development in Malhan District, Al Mahwit Governorate; its February to April 2026 report says a volunteer team was kept to monitor violations against birds.

name: Building Advocacy and Developing a Management Plan for the High Mountains of Ibb Protected Area
summary: Closed CEPF-funded project, US$108,000 for September 2013 to March 2016, to inventory biodiversity in the High Mountains of Ibb Protected Area, including baseline surveys and a land use and land cover map.

name: Environment Protection Authority
summary: Yemen's national focal point to the CBD, named as executing agency with the Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature on GEF project 11408, and cited as a source of marine turtle survey work.

name: Foundation for the Protection of the Arabian Leopard in Yemen
summary: Yemeni organisation registered in November 2009 and funded by the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, which reported monitoring Hawf Forest biodiversity and photographing a female and a male Arabian leopard in 2011.

name: Green Empowerment for Development
summary: Yemeni non-profit based in Taiz that says it uses satellite imagery and IoT sensors for biodiversity tracking, and has a GBIF dataset of Ziziphus spina-christi occurrences recorded between June and August 2026.

name: Ministry of Water and Environment
summary: Yemeni ministry listed by the GEF as executing agency of project 3067 on Socotra's biodiversity policy framework, which closed in 2018, and named as a participant in developing national CBD targets.

name: Protecting the Arabian Leopard in Yemen from Extinction
summary: Active project run by Sanid Organization for Relief and Development; its December 2025 to February 2026 report says 16 local activists were trained in tracking, monitoring and reporting violations against wildlife.

name: Sanid Organization for Relief and Development
summary: Non-profit, non-partisan Yemeni organisation whose GlobalGiving project aims to verify Arabian leopard presence and population, and which reports training 21 volunteers in the third quarter of 2024 to monitor violations.

name: Socotra archipelago bird surveys
summary: Closed programme of systematic bird surveys led by BirdLife International and Yemen's EPA, which OSME's report says made nine surveys between 1999 and 2011 and supplied data for its Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas report.

name: Acoustic and Boat Based Monitoring of Endangered Humpback Dolphins in an Area Under Threat From Coastal Development
summary: Active project dated 13 February 2026 in Mossel Bay, planning to combine long-term passive acoustic monitoring with boat-based photo-identification linked to Happywhale, building on over a decade of data and a custom whistle classifier.

name: Acoustic Tracking Array Platform
summary: Acoustic telemetry platform hosted by the South African Institute for Aquatic Biodiversity, with more than 285 moored receivers over about 2,300 km of southern African coastline, partnering with the Ocean Tracking Network.

name: Advanced Fire Information System
summary: Programme delivering near-real-time locations of active fires over southern and eastern Africa, run and built by the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research, with Eskom as a partner.

name: Africa Rangeland Watch
summary: Project combining satellite imagery with ground-based rangeland monitoring, built by Conservation International; Kartoza describes work on extending its open-source tool to Sub-Saharan Africa.

name: Africam
summary: Organisation that began in 1998 with live cameras, the first installed in the Sabi Sands.

name: African Bioacoustics Community
summary: Programme initiated in March 2018 to support bioacoustic science on the continent.

name: African Centre for DNA Barcoding
summary: Centre established in 2011 within the University of Johannesburg's Department of Botany, led by Kowiyou Yessoufou, which says it uses modern statistics and AI to accelerate extinction risk assessment.

name: African Lion Database
summary: Dataset led by Sam Nicholson; a 2020 EWT article said it had been recording lion data for 18 months.

name: African Wildlife Tracking
summary: Organisation that The Citizen reported in June 2018 manufactured tracking collars locally at half the cost of imported versions.

name: africanDRONE
summary: Self-described African non-profit for civic drone pilots, based in Cape Town, which says it was tasked with helping WRI pilot drone monitoring of reforested land in northern Malawi.

name: AI-Driven Anti-Poaching
summary: In April 2026, Team Epoch described plans to develop a real-time detection model for fixed-wing drone footage during a 10-week sprint with Strategic Protection of Threatened Species.

name: Alpha-Panga
summary: Organisation that says it is building an AI platform that processes camera feeds and alerts rangers, starting in South Africa.

name: Anchor Environmental Consultants
summary: Cape Town consultancy that SLR says it acquired; it states that it worked with NatureMetrics on eDNA sampling across Africa.

name: Application of eDNA Methods for Assessing Elasmobranch Species Diversity and Distribution along the South African Coastline
summary: Project dated 15 February 2023 in South Africa which, according to its Rufford page, aims to provide a baseline for using eDNA to monitor sharks.

name: Applied Conservation Genetics Unit
summary: Unit that uses eDNA to detect organisms and metabarcoding to identify species, built by the Endangered Wildlife Trust and Stellenbosch University.

name: Association for Water and Rural Development
summary: Non-profit based in Hoedspruit, focused on catchments of north-eastern South Africa such as the Olifants River Basin, which leads BIO-SMART and builds INWARDS.

name: Automated shark detection project
summary: Project begun in February 2019 as an 18-month effort to develop a low-cost computer vision shark detection algorithm, with field work started at Fish Hoek beach.

name: Autonomous Drone-Based Fence Monitoring Project
summary: Proposed project whose objectives include AI algorithms to detect fence damage.

name: Berg-Breede invasive alien tree mapping
summary: Mapping of invasive alien trees in the upper Berg and Breede catchments, part of the SEBEI project, classifying Sentinel 2a imagery with a reported 93% accuracy and a first draft map in 2019.

name: BIO-SMART
summary: Active project led by the Association for Water and Rural Development and funded by JRS Biodiversity Foundation, whose Phase 2 aims to expand into Mozambique and Eswatini and mobilise data from over ten institutions.

name: Biodiversity Advisor
summary: Programme built by the South African National Biodiversity Institute, which a 2023 Frontiers paper said was being redeveloped and scheduled to launch in 2023.

name: Biodiversity and Development Institute
summary: Organisation that described itself in a June 2021 post as an independent non-profit company and said it co-managed the Virtual Museum.

name: Biodiversity, connectivity, and ecological forecasting in the Greater Kruger National Park region
summary: Space in Africa reported April 2021 plans for a NASA-funded ecological forecasting project partnering with SANParks, using field surveys, NASA satellite data and aerial photography.

name: BiodiversityGIS
summary: Programme run by the South African National Biodiversity Institute that manages spatial biodiversity planning information and distributes conservation plans and biodiversity datasets for the South African region from Kirstenbosch.

name: Biomonitoring and Bioassessment of Fish Community Structure in a Marine Protected Area with Environmental DNA Metabarcoding (Pilot EDNAM Project)
summary: Pilot project dated 8 April 2022 that proposed applying marine eDNA metabarcoding to monitor and assess fish communities in the Helderberg Marine Protected Area.

name: BIRDIE
summary: Project led by the South African National Biodiversity Institute and Nancy Job, funded by JRS Biodiversity Foundation, that sources citizen science data and analyses it with statistical models; the online platform is live.

name: BirdLasser
summary: App for recording bird sightings, built by Lejint, which BirdLife South Africa calls the most popular mobile app for capturing SABAP2 data.

name: BirdLife South Africa
summary: South African partner of BirdLife International; the Mail & Guardian reports it leads a project tagging, colour-ringing and monitoring shorebirds, and it provides analytical support to citizen science projects.

name: Black Mamba Anti-Poaching Unit
summary: Anti-poaching unit that Samsung describes as an all-female troop using non-violent methods, and which Sensing Clues lists as a partner.

name: Botanical Society of South Africa
summary: A membership-driven South African organisation that SANBI says was formed in 1913, and which has a link to the CREW programme, founded in 2003 in collaboration with SANBI.

name: Buffelsdrift Foundation
summary: South African foundation and trust whose habitat conservation work preserves and restores ecosystems in the Buffelsdrift Reserve, including quartz-soil habitat, with Buffelsdrift Game Lodge as founder, guardian and funder.

name: BushEars
summary: A programme that detects gunshots and chainsaws from solar field nodes, and is both run and built by Mafutai.

name: Cango Wildlife Ranch
summary: A conservation organisation based in Oudtshoorn, by its own description, and led by Douglas Eriksen.

name: Cape Leopard Trust
summary: An environmental NGO founded in 2004 in the Western Cape, using Argus Wild AI with observer confirmation to identify leopards from its 2025 Boland survey.

name: Cape RADD
summary: An organisation with marine research projects in False Bay.

name: CapeNature
summary: A Western Cape government entity managing 31 nature reserve complexes with 112 reserves, which supports conservation through a Scientific Services Unit and at least four biodiversity information systems.

name: Centre for Statistics in Ecology, Environment and Conservation
summary: An organisation that the CWAC site says SANBI collaborates with on the BIRDIE project, which it partners with.

name: Chief Directorate: National Geo-spatial Information
summary: Described by the OpenStreetMap blog in 2013 as South Africa’s government mapping agency, it holds aerial photography dating to 1926 and provides national digital aerial imagery.

name: Chisl
summary: An organisation named by Timbavati Nature Reserve as a collaborator on Project Gaia, which Daily Maverick reported in March 2026 it had recently completed with Veriphy AI as a wildlife census.

name: City of Cape Town
summary: A local authority that a February 2019 announcement names as a funder of the Shark Spotters programme.

name: City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality
summary: Municipal body that Wikipedia's entry for Rietvlei Nature Reserve names as the reserve's administrator.

name: CLS Southern Africa
summary: A South African company founded in 2003 and part of the CLS Group since March 2021, which applies space-based solutions to environmental projects.

name: Computer Automated Land Cover System
summary: A cloud-based automated land cover tool for South Africa, built by the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment.

name: Conservation Catalysts Africa
summary: An organisation offering GIS and remote sensing solutions to nature reserves.

name: Conservation Outcomes
summary: A non-profit supporting land managed for biodiversity conservation outside traditional state protected areas, and a partner of EarthRanger.

name: Conservation South Africa
summary: An organisation that says it aims to engage in the management of Africa's rangelands and oceans.

name: Contemplate Wild
summary: A South African conservation non-profit working across Greater Kruger, whose analysis work includes AI and machine learning models.

name: Coordinated Avifaunal Roadcounts
summary: A project monitoring large terrestrial birds through coordinated road surveys, run by the FitzPatrick Institute of African Ornithology.

name: Coordinated Waterbird Counts
summary: A project in which citizen scientists count waterbirds twice a year in South Africa and Kenya, with 492 surveys submitted from 221 sites in 2025, run by the FitzPatrick Institute.

name: Council for Geoscience
summary: A body whose authors reported in August 2021 that they tested three machine learning techniques, including k-means clustering, in Table Bay.

name: Council for Scientific and Industrial Research
summary: A research council that researched and implemented the Oceans and Coastal Information System in 2016 and partners with Peace Parks Foundation.

name: Custodians of Rare and Endangered Wildflowers
summary: A citizen science programme in which the public survey, monitor and conserve plants, with data feeding IUCN Red List reporting, in partnership with SANBI and the Botanical Society of South Africa.

name: CyanoLakes
summary: An organisation whose app offers subscribers satellite imagery for monitoring cyanobacteria, algal blooms and aquatic weeds.

name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment
summary: South African government department, renamed in April 2021, with a mandate on citizens' environmental rights; in August 2026 its minister published the draft NBSAP 2026-2035 for public comment.

name: Department of Science, Technology and Innovation
summary: South African government department, renamed in 2024 from Science and Innovation, which SAEON names as its primary investor and which funds the SAEON open data platform.

name: Digital Earth South Africa
summary: Earth observation data platform built and run by the South African National Space Agency, with a beta launched in 2022 covering over 30 years of archived imagery, and partnered with SARAO.

name: Dscvry
summary: An active organisation that names Selati Game Reserve as a client.

name: Dyer Island Conservation Trust
summary: Conservation trust that runs regular baited remote underwater video surveys and has used acoustic tagging on white sharks.

name: Eastern Cape Parks and Tourism Agency
summary: Provincial agency whose annual performance plan, tabled in August 2024, names camera traps, drones and satellite tags as monitoring tools.

name: Ecosystem Monitoring for Management Application (EMMA)
summary: Application reporting vegetation condition, fire history and veld age for Cape Floristic Region protected areas, co-developed with SAEON and academics, led by Adam M. Wilson and funded by NASA.

name: EcoWatch
summary: Proposed full monitoring platform, run by Dscvry, whose requirements were defined in Dscvry's Selati proof of concept.

name: Ekosource
summary: An organisation that SANSA said entered a satellite information agreement with it and GeoTerraImage in November 2021; Kartoza says it worked on WaterSphere360 for Ekosource.

name: Elephants Alive
summary: Registered non-profit near Hoedspruit that tracks elephants with satellite collars, reported in 2020 as 60 active collars across South Africa and Mozambique, and uses EarthRanger.

name: Endangered Wildlife Trust
summary: A non-profit established in 1973 that says it monitors threatened species, uses EarthRanger, is a GBIF Associate Participant Node and described itself as a legal drone operator in 2024.

name: Enviro-Champs
summary: Active organisation that CGIAR describes as involving over a thousand people using citizen science on water quality.

name: Eskom
summary: An organisation with which the CSIR says it collaborated, using CSIR remote sensing expertise, to develop a fire detection system.

name: eThekwini Municipality
summary: According to Wikipedia, manages Durban reserves and parks, some within the Durban Metropolitan Open Space System, and jointly manages the 21-hectare Springside Nature Reserve with Hillcrest Conservancy.

name: eTrack – Linking Indigenous Knowledge, Citizen Science and Artificial Intelligence
summary: Closed project dated 9 February 2022 on San heritage land in South Africa, aiming to create an online app linking indigenous knowledge, citizen science and AI, support a tracking school and research cheetah tracks.

name: EWT Biodiversity DataBank
summary: A central store of ecological and spatial information for EWT and its partners, run by the trust, with data requestable through a sharing form.

name: Expanded Freshwater and Terrestrial Environmental Observation Network
summary: Programme run by the South African Environmental Observation Network, reported as jointly launched by the NRF and the science department, aiming to operate instrumented landscape-level research platforms.

name: Eye on Conservation
summary: Active organisation that says it implemented AI-driven surveillance and licence plate recognition.

name: Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife
summary: A KwaZulu-Natal conservation agency established under a 1997 Act, managing 92 protected areas, with reported drone use and a command centre launched in 2018 in Hluhluwe-iMfolozi Park.

name: FBIS-Africa
summary: Proposed project, funded by the JRS Biodiversity Foundation, to develop a freshwater biodiversity information system for Africa, including a platform and a mobile app.

name: FieldLog
summary: Programme built and run by The Field Company that lets rangers and researchers collect field data on cheap phones without internet.

name: FinSpotter
summary: A citizen science shark database that uses photo identification and AI, run by Cape RADD.

name: FitzPatrick Institute of African Ornithology
summary: An institute whose citizen science projects, it says, supply 32 million of 47 million southern African GBIF records; it curates waterbird count data and is reported as a SABAP2 funder.

name: Foundational Biodiversity Information Programme
summary: A long-term programme to generate, manage and disseminate foundational biodiversity information, run by SANBI and the National Research Foundation, funded by the Department of Science, Technology and Innovation, and running since 2013 per SANBI in March 2020.

name: Freshwater Biodiversity Information System
summary: An open-access platform for freshwater biodiversity data in South Africa, built by the Freshwater Research Centre and Kartoza, which JRS reported in August 2020 had mobilised over 300,000 river records.

name: Freshwater Research Centre
summary: A Cape Town non-profit specialising in aquatic research and conservation that conceptualised FBIS in 2017 and is funded by the JRS Biodiversity Foundation.

name: Gauteng Department of Agriculture and Rural Development
summary: Gauteng provincial government department that Wikipedia describes as responsible for agricultural affairs, with nature conservation assigned to the Department of Environment instead.

name: GeneLethu
summary: An organisation established in 2019 to provide DNA barcoding, sequencing and eDNA services.

name: GeoTerraImage
summary: An organisation included in SANSA’s November 2021 agreement with Ekosource to provide satellite-derived information to government entities for water resource management.

name: Global Overberg Renosterveld Watch
summary: Application built by Glenn Moncrieff on Global Forest Watch; the trust says it uses satellite images and machine learning to detect land cover change, with models run every five days in November 2021.

name: Gouritz Cluster Biosphere Reserve
summary: Non-profit company managing the Gouritz Cluster Biosphere Reserve under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme, which UNESCO designated in 2015 as South Africa's largest, at 3,187,893 hectares.

name: Greater Kruger Environmental Protection Foundation
summary: A registered public benefit organisation led by Sharon Haussmann that says it coordinates technologies into real-time intelligence-sharing platforms and deploys technology, air support and monitoring against wildlife crime.

name: GroundTruth
summary: An organisation that CGIAR says trained a machine learning algorithm on 13,000 photos with Digital Innovation.

name: Herding for Health
summary: A programme, in partnership with Conservation International and Peace Parks Foundation, that tracks results with ground-based and satellite data.

name: Hluhluwe-iMfolozi Park black rhino monitoring programme
summary: Active black rhino monitoring programme in Hluhluwe-iMfolozi Park; Save the Rhino says working cameras rose from a third in early 2024 to over 80% by February 2025.

name: Hluhluwe-iMfolozi Smart Park
summary: A smart park where February 2018 reports described Azure AI returning under 1,300 potential human incursion images from over 25,000 received in just over three months.

name: Improving Accuracy and Precision of Aerial Census in the Savanna Biome, Using Remote Sensed Imagery and Machine Learning
summary: Closed project dated 22 March 2023 in South Africa; its March 2024 final report says RGB and thermal data were collected and four candidate algorithms awaited training and comparison once computing issues were resolved.

name: Ingwe Research Program
summary: A research organisation based in the Greater Kruger that uses TrapTagger and the African Carnivore Wildbook.

name: Institute for Communities and Wildlife in Africa
summary: An organisation working on human-wildlife conflict that launched a project in February 2019 with Shark Spotters and PatternLab to develop a computer-aided vision shark detection algorithm.

name: Institute of Natural Resources
summary: An organisation working on biodiversity and ecosystem management that reported in March 2022 a partnership to assess drones for water quality monitoring.

name: Integrated Water Resources Decision Support System
summary: A collection of frameworks, tools and models integrating factors in water resources management, built by the Association for Water and Rural Development, with Kartoza saying it worked on the next desktop app.

name: iSimangaliso Wetland Park Authority
summary: An authority that reported taking part in the UNESCO eDNA sampling campaign in May 2023.

name: Johannesburg City Parks and Zoo
summary: Johannesburg body that began reopening the city's nature reserves in January 2021 with access controls under Covid-19 regulations, and lists the 150-hectare Melville Koppies Nature Reserve on its site.

name: Kariega Foundation
summary: An organisation that says it partnered with Hikvision in 2022 and is rolling out an upgrade using Hikvision AI cameras.

name: Karoo BioGaps
summary: A project that SANBI listed in March 2020 as funded by the Foundational Biodiversity Information Programme to fill biodiversity information gaps for development decisions in the Karoo.

name: Karoo Gateway Conservancy
summary: Conservancy of 18,000 hectares in the Klaarstroom district, formed by a voluntary agreement among landowners to manage their land for biodiversity conservation.

name: Kogelberg Biosphere Not-for-Profit Company
summary: Section 21 not-for-profit company established in 2002 for the Kogelberg Biosphere, which UNESCO registered in 1998 as South Africa's first and which covers over 103,000 hectares.

name: Kruger Conservation
summary: An organisation that names itself Kruger Conservation NPC, with no further activity described in the entry.

name: Kruger to Canyons Non-Profit Company
summary: Non-profit company established in 2011 as the vehicle for coordinating Biosphere activities.

name: Lejint
summary: An organisation named on the app store as the provider of BirdLasser, with nothing else stated.

name: Leopard Data Portal
summary: A Cape Leopard Trust programme recording leopard activity sightings in the three Cape provinces through three platforms, with a secure database that is not publicly available.

name: Limpopo Department of Economic Development, Environment and Tourism
summary: Limpopo provincial department that ran the Mahala Week campaign of 8 to 14 September 2025, giving South African ID holders free entry to 11 reserves while other charges still applied.

name: LiveTwin
summary: A Reama AI project designed to detect canopy change and give early smoke detection, with Reama AI aiming to pilot a Living Digital Twin.

name: Mabula Ground Hornbill Project
summary: An organisation monitoring the national Southern Ground-hornbill population on four-year cycles using recruited citizen scientists, with a postal address in Bela-Bela.

name: Mafutai
summary: An organisation that describes itself as applied AI built and owned in South Africa.

name: Makuleke Communal Property Association
summary: A September 2011 account reports 25,000 hectares restored to the community in 1999, joint park management and entitlement through its association to 14% of Outpost lodge turnover.

name: Manyeleti Communal Property Association
summary: Communal property association that owns the Manyeleti land restored through a claim, with the Mpumalanga Tourism and Parks Agency as management authority and a co-management agreement under discussion in November 2024.

name: MAPSS
summary: Organisation combining conservation science and geospatial technology to help measure change, which says it is active in over 20 countries with 387 million hectares under monitoring.

name: Maputaland wetland remote sensing study
summary: A Water Research Commission funded study led by the CSIR and Heidi van Deventer, which in February 2022 planned to use Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 at 10 × 10 m pixels, with possible use in national wetland monitoring.

name: Marine Mapping Programme
summary: A Council for Geoscience programme aligned with the mandate of the Council for Geoscience and Operation Phakisa.

name: Meerkat
summary: A radar and optical detection system used against poaching, built by the CSIR in partnership with South African National Parks.

name: miniSASS
summary: A tool that anyone can use to monitor river health, built by GroundTruth.

name: Monitoring and protection of biodiversity on Selati Game Reserve
summary: Closed 2021 to 2022 project, run by the Selati Wilderness Foundation and listed under IUCN SOS's African Wildlife Initiative, aiming to protect the reserve's wildlife through monitoring, security, more staff and camera traps.

name: Mossel Bay Municipality
summary: Municipality appointed as landowner to be the management authority of Diosma Nature Reserve under the reserve's management plan.

name: Mpumalanga Tourism and Parks Agency
summary: An agency using species data and GIS in conservation planning and wind farm assessments, Esri reported in spring 2024, whose Scientific Services plans a Centre of Excellence.

name: MRI Whale Unit
summary: A unit led by Els Vermeulen that has deployed satellite tags on adult southern right whales since 2021.

name: Msinsi Holdings
summary: Subsidiary of a state water utility, set up to manage and conserve the Mgeni River System's major water resources, and listed by Wikipedia as managing resource reserves in eThekwini.

name: Munywana Conservancy
summary: Big Five reserve of about 30,000 hectares, dating from 2007 and collectively owned by local communities and private landowners, including 9,085 hectares returned to the Makhasa and Mnqobokazi communities in restitution.

name: Mzansi Amanzi
summary: Monthly water datasets derived from Sentinel-2 calculations of surface water area and dam water volume across South Africa, distributed by SANSA.

name: National Biodiversity Assessment
summary: A SANBI-built collaborative programme bringing together the best available science on South Africa's biodiversity to inform policy, with the 2025 edition being the fourth after 2004, 2011 and 2018.

name: National Biodiversity Assessment 2025
summary: The fourth and most comprehensive assessment of South Africa's biodiversity, launched on 9 December 2025, which a deputy minister said involved over 110 institutions and 490 contributors and introduces global genetic indicators.

name: National Environmental Screening Tool
summary: A tool built by the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, whose report the Endangered Wildlife Trust says has had to accompany all environmental impact assessments by law since 5 July 2019.

name: National Parks Trust
summary: Trust that bought a 134-hectare Roodeberg property in 2014 for incorporation into Table Mountain National Park, using funds from WWF South Africa and the Table Mountain Fund.

name: National Research Foundation
summary: A South African government agency, established under the National Research Foundation Act, that promotes and supports research through funding and, per SANBI, jointly manages the Foundational Biodiversity Information Programme; it funds BioScape.

name: National Wetland Map
summary: A national wetland programme, partnered with the South African National Biodiversity Institute, whose automated wetland condition assessment method is the national case study in the Global Wetland Outlook 2025.

name: North West Parks and Tourism Board
summary: State-owned body reported in 2009 to be responsible for 14 game parks and nature reserves in North West province.

name: North-West University
summary: A university where a 2024 Master of Science dissertation in Computer Science implemented an automated solution using computer vision and deep learning for camera trap images.

name: Nuwejaars River Nature Reserve
summary: Non-profit company managing and rehabilitating ecosystem processes in the Nuwejaars Wetlands Special Management Area, where 26 landowners and the town of Elim work across 47,000 hectares of private land.

name: Oceanographic Research Institute
summary: A research institute based at uShaka Marine World in Durban.

name: Oceans and Coastal Information Management System
summary: A programme conceptualised by the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment and built by the CSIR, which says it applies satellite remote sensing and geospatial information to support governance of South Africa's oceans and coasts.

name: Oceans Research
summary: A research and conservation organisation, by its own description, which is also the VEMCO agent for Africa.

name: Oppenheimer Generations Research and Conservation
summary: An organisation whose team leads philanthropic investment in applied research, conservation systems and institutional partnerships in Africa, and whose Jennifer Ward Oppenheimer Research Grant gives USD 150,000 to one recipient for up to three years.

name: Oppenheimer Memorial Trust
summary: A trust that awards a limited number of grants each year to support scholarship at public higher education institutions in South Africa.

name: ORI Cooperative Fish Tagging Project
summary: A project run by the Oceanographic Research Institute and listed among its long-term monitoring projects.

name: Overberg Renosterveld Trust
summary: Non-profit trust managing the 547-hectare Haarwegskloof Renosterveld Reserve, owned by WWF South Africa, and by early 2026 holding 23 conservation easements protecting over 5,000 hectares of renosterveld.

name: Overstrand Municipality
summary: Municipality designated as the management authority of Fernkloof Nature Reserve in Hermanus.

name: Pharos Data
summary: An organisation that offers thermal drone wildlife and livestock counts and trains models on footage of the client's property.

name: Piloting a Citizen Science Approach for Reef Monitoring to Improve Conservation of Coral Reefs in South Africa
summary: Closed project dated 3 January 2024 that set out to pilot citizen science for long-term coral reef monitoring in South Africa, with planned reef surveys at two pilot locations and a final evaluation report of November 2024.

name: Postcode Meerkat
summary: A project built by South African National Parks, Peace Parks Foundation and the CSIR, funded by People's Postcode Lottery, which in December 2016 comprised radar and electro-optic sensors intended to detect, classify, monitor and track humans moving in the park.

name: Project Gaia
summary: A completed 100,000-hectare AI- and drone-powered census capturing nearly three million images according to Daily Maverick, with Timbavati noting unreliable sex differentiation for species requiring separate counts.

name: Project Rhino
summary: A rhino-focused association launched in 2011 that supports anti-poaching technologies and the ZAP-Wing aerial surveillance unit.

name: Project ZOA
summary: A project that won the Startup Innovation Award for Top AI Sustainability Project during Davos Innovation Week 2026 and is developing the Ecological Intelligence Dataset.

name: Reama AI Technology
summary: An organisation that describes itself as a deep-tech research and deployment lab.

name: Reel Science Coalition
summary: Non-profit organisation that, according to an April 2022 Rufford page, had been planning and implementing shore-based research on surf-zone fish composition and abundance in the Helderberg Marine Protected Area.

name: REFRESH Project
summary: Closed biodiversity inventory project for South Africa's freshwater systems, led by Albert Chakona and Dewidine van der Colff, which SAIAB says ran up to 2024 to provide baseline information.

name: Rhino Custodians
summary: A registered non-profit, partnered with EarthRanger, whose mission is to deploy the AI-enabled RhinoWatch to vetted reserves.

name: Rhino Protection Programme
summary: A programme run by Peace Parks Foundation with Microsoft, Wildlife Protection Solutions and Smart Parks as partners, where Peace Parks says Microsoft's support focuses on developing cloud-based artificial intelligence technologies.

name: RhinoWatch
summary: An AI-enabled foot collar that monitors an individual rhino, built and run by Rhino Custodians and using EarthRanger.

name: RhODIS
summary: A database of rhinoceros DNA profiles modelled after the FBI's CODIS, which a January 2018 research release said included more than 5,800 forensic case samples.

name: Roc Conservation Tech
summary: An organisation that works on bird detection near wind turbines and conservation drones, and partners with Identiflight.

name: Rouxcel Technology
summary: Conservation company that, according to Stop Rhino Poaching, specialises in AI-enabled rhino collars on a private LoRa network, sending alerts of abnormal behaviour to EarthRanger; SP le Roux founded it, per Rhino Custodians.

name: SAEON Arid Lands Node
summary: Active node of the South African Environmental Observation Network; SAEON eNews says its staff and interns monitored vegetation at the Tierberg-LTER site and nearby farms and reserves during drought years.

name: SAEON Egagasini Node
summary: Established in 2007, this SAEON node reports subsequent growth into an ocean observing and modelling network; SAEON eNews reported its fifth benthic photographic monitoring year in 2022.

name: SAEON Elwandle Coastal Node
summary: Active SAEON node that, according to SAEON eNews in 2024, had run monthly pelagic ecological research at the Algoa Bay sentinel site since 2007 and added a FlowCam for phytoplankton imaging.

name: SAEON Fynbos Node
summary: An active SAEON node, it reports SAEON taking over Jonkershoek in 2009; the Overberg Renosterveld Trust reported its Global Overberg Renosterveld Watch launch in November 2021.

name: SAEON Grasslands-Forests-Wetlands Node
summary: An active SAEON node, it reportedly prioritised four mesic grassland catchments for refurbishment in 2011; SAEON eNews reported a second Maputaland Coastal Plain site in 2023.

name: SAEON Ndlovu Node
summary: Active SAEON node that says it focuses on long-term research into environmental change in north-eastern South Africa's savannas, grasslands and rivers, with tree-monitoring data collected annually.

name: SAEON Open Data Platform
summary: Data infrastructure run by SAEON for publishing, discovering, disseminating and preserving Earth observation and environmental data, certified as a Trustworthy Data Repository on 5 September 2023.

name: SAEON uLwazi Node
summary: Active SAEON node that says it curates data and develops open data systems and applications, which are distributed on an Open Data Platform.

name: Saldanha Bay marine mammal early warning system
summary: Pilot project, built by Vodacom South Africa and WWF South Africa, using cameras and hydrophones in the Saldanha Bay Aquaculture Development Zone.

name: SANBI-GBIF
summary: South African biodiversity data mobilisation programme run by SANBI, partnering with GBIF; its page cites over 12 million records mobilised, and a data library entry cites over 32 million occurrences.

name: Sanbona Nature and Wilderness Reserve
summary: Privately owned 58,000-hectare nature reserve in the Little Karoo, proclaimed with CapeNature's Biodiversity Stewardship Programme, which CALEO Foundation announced in 2021 it would donate and transfer to a non-profit company.

name: SANCCOB
summary: A seabird organisation conducting post-release monitoring, with released African penguins fitted with transponders and monitored using remote ground and hand-held readers.

name: Sappi
summary: Company whose 2024 sustainability report describes using Sentinel-2 to track and monitor harvest operations in South Africa.

name: Sea Change Project
summary: Organisation whose flagship project combines underwater tracking, research and storytelling.

name: Sea Search Research & Conservation
summary: Collective of marine mammal scientists and students focused on peer-reviewed research and training; Daily Maverick reports a post-doc there helped develop machine learning to identify humpback dolphin whistles.

name: SeaKeys
summary: Project funded by the Foundational Biodiversity Information Programme, aimed at collating marine biodiversity information and turning it into products for decision making; its current status is unknown.

name: SeaMap
summary: Three-year project planned for 2022 to 2024, funded by the Foundational Biodiversity Information Programme, that aimed to deliver a data-driven marine ecosystem map of South Africa.

name: Selati Wilderness Foundation
summary: Non-profit company established in 2018 whose page describes reserve monitoring technology, including 25 ecological camera traps at Selati Game Reserve by 2022; it is funded by IUCN Save Our Species.

name: Sentala
summary: Organisation combining custom drones, onboard AI and EarthRanger integration, deployed through pilot programmes in South Africa.

name: Shallow Marine and Coastal Research Infrastructure
summary: One of three national research infrastructures managed by SAEON.

name: Shark Spotters
summary: Programme that had recorded over 2,500 shark sightings since 2004 by February 2019, when it announced a research project aimed at an automated shark spotting system.

name: Snapshot Safari South Africa
summary: Camera trap project funded by the Foundational Biodiversity Information Programme, assessing mammal occupancy and monitoring mammals across South Africa; its current status is unknown.

name: South African Bird Ringing Unit
summary: Based at the University of Cape Town, it administers all bird ringing within southern Africa and other African countries, curates all the southern African ringing data, and is listed among the BirdMap projects.

name: South African Carbon Sinks Atlas
summary: Web-based tool on the spatial distribution of carbon stocks and fluxes in South Africa, built by SAEON and the CSIR from the CSIR's 2014 assessment, with GIZ funding.

name: South African Environmental Observation Network
summary: National network of seven nodes and three research infrastructures, with its national office in Pretoria, mandated to detect, understand and predict environmental change in South Africa.

name: South African Institute for Aquatic Biodiversity
summary: National Research Foundation facility in Makhanda that hosts the Acoustic Tracking Array Platform and a genomics platform, and serves as a scientific resource on aquatic ecosystems.

name: South African National Biodiversity Institute
summary: Public entity under the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, established in 2004 to monitor and report on South Africa's biodiversity, which builds the National Biodiversity Assessment.

name: South African National Land Cover
