summary: National land cover dataset whose 2022 edition uses Sentinel-2 imagery with automated classification, which the department builds, runs and uses, including for protected area monitoring.

name: South African National Parks
summary: Body established under the 2003 Protected Areas Act to conserve and manage national parks, reported to be responsible for 21 parks and to collect camera trap and underwater video data.

name: South African National Space Agency
summary: Space agency whose Earth Observation programme collects, processes, archives and shares satellite data for South Africa, with an archive reaching back to 1972.

name: South African National Status Report on Biological Invasions
summary: A national assessment of biological invasions in South Africa, built by the South African National Biodiversity Institute, which B-Cubed describes as the only one in the world focused specifically on the topic.

name: South African Polar Research Infrastructure
summary: Programme run by the South African Environmental Observation Network that aims to maintain and expand long-term observational datasets.

name: South African shorebird satellite tracking project
summary: BirdLife South Africa-led project that, according to BirdLife South Africa, fitted long-distance Palearctic migratory shorebirds with tracking devices in South Africa for the first time.

name: Southern African Bird Atlas Project
summary: Bird atlas project whose second phase started in 2007 and collects about 1 million records a year.

name: Southern African Bird Atlas Project 2
summary: Volunteer bird atlas project begun on 1 July 2007, run by the FitzPatrick Institute, in which 1500 observers surveyed 15 085 pentads in 2025.

name: Southern African Wildlife College
summary: Conservation training college that announced a partnership with Vulcan Inc. to expand local capacity to train, deploy and support EarthRanger, and offers EarthRanger services at local rates.

name: Spatial Biodiversity Assessment, Prioritisation and Planning project
summary: Project run by the South African National Biodiversity Institute, launched in May 2022 as a EUR 6.7 million effort across four countries and then expected to run until May 2027.

name: Stellenbosch University
summary: Active university whose Department of Botany and Zoology, with the Endangered Wildlife Trust, collaborated to establish the Applied Conservation Genetics Unit.

name: Strategic Protection of Threatened Species
summary: Organisation that describes itself as a registered conservation company using UAVs to reduce poaching.

name: Strategic water source areas of South Africa
summary: Mapping dataset of South African water source areas which, according to WWF South Africa, showed that only 10% of the land produces 50% of surface run-off.

name: The Bateleurs
summary: South African non-profit company with over 220 volunteer pilots that offers a free aerial service to conservation organisations.

name: The Field Company
summary: Open-source technology collective based in Cape Town.

name: Threatened Species No-Go Map Tool
summary: Programme built and run by the Endangered Wildlife Trust that uses the data underlying the Environmental Screening Tool to identify areas of significant biodiversity impact.

name: Tihlo Henhla - The Eye Above
summary: Project in which the BushRanger carries thermal and optical cameras and a snare-detecting radar.

name: Tswalu Foundation
summary: Organisation with a Tswalu source describing Snapshot Safari as a long-term project funded by FBIP.

name: Two Oceans Aquarium Foundation
summary: Aquarium foundation whose Turtle Conservation Centre collects data on turtles for research and whose team acoustically tags turtles with ATAP, a partner.

name: uMngeni-uThukela Water
summary: Water utility that tested satellite-based water quality monitoring at four dams during 2024/2025 and partners with Enviro Champs.

name: University of Cape Town
summary: University where, according to UCT News in 2022, an associate professor in electrical engineering planned to use robotics and AI to monitor wildlife health.

name: University of Johannesburg
summary: Active university that runs the African Centre for DNA Barcoding, which was established in 2011 within its Department of Botany and says it uses statistics and AI to speed extinction risk assessment.

name: University of the Western Cape
summary: University in Bellville, Cape Town, whose Institute for Water Studies published a paper classifying satellite images with Random Forest and Support Vector Machine classifiers.

name: Veriphy
summary: Company offering wildlife census surveys and fauna and flora mapping, which says it operates in South Africa, Botswana and the United States and runs Project Gaia.

name: Veriphy Technologies
summary: Run by Chisl and described by Timbavati Nature Reserve as Project Gaia’s originator, with Chisl reporting that it has counted livestock since 2022.

name: Vhembe Biosphere Reserve NPC
summary: Non-profit company registered for the Vhembe Biosphere Reserve, which has a surface area of 30,700 square kilometres in northern Limpopo.

name: Virtual Museum
summary: Citizen science platform for contributing to biodiversity research and mapping, originally developed in 2005 by the University of Cape Town's Animal Demography Unit, now run by two institutes.

name: Vodacom South Africa
summary: Company whose own page says it developed an AI-powered early warning system with WWF South Africa, deployed in Saldanha Bay to alert mussel farmers when marine mammals approach.

name: VulPro
summary: Organisation that monitored six Cape Vulture colonies in 2023 and used a drone during its second surveys that year.

name: Walker Bay Fynbos Conservancy
summary: Conservancy formed by landowners in 1999 to protect fynbos in Walker Bay, which CapeNature says collectively manages 12,179 hectares.

name: Water Research Commission
summary: Funder that, according to the Sentinel story, gave CyanoLakes a research grant in 2015 and, per Engineering News in February 2022, was funding a three-year CSIR-led satellite wetland monitoring project.

name: Waterberg Biosphere Reserve
summary: Registered not-for-profit company that manages the affairs of the biosphere under the UNESCO Man and Biosphere Programme.

name: Wild Me mobile app for AI elephant ID
summary: Offline-capable mobile app that identifies individual elephants from ear notches, scars and tusks, built by two bodies, with a first field test at Kariega Game Reserve reported in October 2026.

name: Wildlands Conservation Trust
summary: Trust that, in May 2013, was announced by the Department of Environmental Affairs as recipient of R33 million over three years for a greening project, and that manages the 12,000-hectare Somkhanda community-owned game reserve.

name: Wildlife ACT
summary: Organisation specialising in daily monitoring of endangered and priority species across key protected areas, using radio, GPS and satellite collars and, by its own account, camera trap surveys.

name: Wildlife ACT Innovations
summary: Wildlife tracking technology company based in KwaZulu-Natal, launched in May 2021, which formalises a partnership between Wildlife ACT Fund Trust and AWE Telemetry Systems to produce telemetry products.

name: Wildlife and Environment Society of South Africa
summary: Registered non-profit organisation, headquartered at uMngeni Valley Nature Reserve, which it runs as its own 900-hectare reserve in Howick, KwaZulu-Natal.

name: Wildlife vital signs robotics and AI project
summary: Project that in May 2022 planned to measure wildlife vital signs remotely using computer vision and sensors, with SANParks officials reported in June 2022 as agreeing to use it once ready.

name: WildSky Foundation
summary: Funder that supports and facilitates drone, remote sensing and data tools, extending to AI-driven monitoring software.

name: Wireless Wildlife
summary: Organisation that designs, develops and distributes wildlife tracking products.

name: WWF South Africa
summary: Organisation that says it researched strategic water source areas with the CSIR in 2013, mapping them, and that partnered with Vodacom South Africa in Saldanha Bay.

name: 2015 Aerial Survey of Elephants in Zambia
summary: Closed national aerial survey of elephants in Zambia in September 2015, covering the Kafue, Luangwa, Sioma Ngwezi and Lower Zambezi Valley ecosystems, with the African Elephant Database citing a 2016 departmental report.

name: 2025 Dry-Season Aerial Survey of Large Mammals and Waterbirds, Kafue Flats
summary: Closed aerial survey of large mammals, including Kafue lechwe, and large waterbirds, including cranes, whose report the Ministry of Tourism launched on 30 October 2026 with the Kafue Flats Wetland Information System.

name: Advancing Community Conservation Management through Integrated Habitat Monitoring in Northern Zambia Game Management Areas
summary: Active project, funded by JRS Biodiversity Foundation, on plant diversity, habitat and land cover in the Tondwa Game Management Areas; 274 herbarium specimens were collected in 2024 and maps and tools were reported almost ready in August 2024.

name: Bats in Zambia Project
summary: A project that a GBIF record says was established in 2014 to collate and collect Zambian bat data, funded by the Rufford Foundation and led by Helen Taylor-Boyd.

name: Biodiversity Impact of Land-use and Farming Practices in the Greater Kafue Ecosystem, Zambia
summary: Active project with $129,388 listed by JRS for 2026 to 2028, planning multi-taxa biodiversity monitoring across land-use types using remote sensing, camera traps, acoustic sensors and patrol data.

name: BirdWatch Zambia
summary: Zambian membership NGO, established in 1969 and the BirdLife International partner there, that says it leads national bird monitoring; it received a $15,000 JRS planning grant in 2016.

name: Conservation South Luangwa
summary: A South Luangwa conservation organisation that partners with DNPW, Panthera and the Zambian Carnivore Programme, and whose aircraft flew over 305 hours in 2019, 177 of them for anti-poaching.

name: Copperbelt University
summary: University in Kitwe, Zambia, whose affiliated authors wrote a 2024 paper, listed in OpenAlex, on seasonal home ranges and habitat selection of elephants in the Kabompo landscape.

name: Department of Geomatics Engineering, Copperbelt University
summary: University department that is the lead affiliation on two 2026 papers on land use and land cover classification in the Upper Kafue River Basin using machine learning.

name: Department of National Parks and Wildlife
summary: The Zambian government department, under the Ministry of Tourism, that administers national parks, created by Act of Parliament in 2015 and partnering with many conservation organisations.

name: Department of Urban and Regional Planning, Copperbelt University
summary: University department that is the lead affiliation on a 2023 paper on drone-based tree species classification and a 2025 paper on drone lidar, both on Zambia's Miombo woodlands.

name: Designing and Implementing a Wetland Information System for the Kafue Flats Wetlands, Zambia
summary: Closed International Crane Foundation project funded by JRS ($249,359, July 2023–July 2026), which the Foundation said in October 2026 trained 13 DNPW officers in SMART.

name: Ecological Monitoring in the Nsumbu-Mweru ecosystem of Zambia
summary: Closed project with a JRS-listed $263,684 for 2022 to 2024 that planned an Ecological Monitoring Unit, using camera traps, transects and eDNA sampling, with data to be shared on GBIF.

name: Flora of Zambia
summary: Website on the flowering plants and ferns of Zambia, one of six e-flora sites based on Flora Zambesiaca, with species pages still being edited in 2026.

name: Forestry Department
summary: A department of the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment, in which FAO says Zambia's national forest monitoring system is anchored.

name: Game Rangers International
summary: A registered Zambian non-governmental organisation and UK charity, working around Zambia's national parks for over 18 years and partnering on the Kafue Connected Conservation Project.

name: Giraffe survey south of the previously accepted southern range boundary, Luangwa (2023)
summary: Closed 2023 giraffe survey, run by the Giraffe Conservation Foundation, reported as the first south of the previously accepted southern range boundary, covering four game reserves and West Petauke GMA.

name: Integrated Land Use Assessment (Zambia)
summary: Zambia's national forest inventory programme, in two phases (ILUA I and II), whose ground survey data underpin the 2021 forest reference emission level; ILUA II increased sampling intensity and measured more ecosystem attributes.

name: Integrated Water Resources Management Centre, University of Zambia
summary: University of Zambia centre in Lusaka, listed as an affiliation by the first author of a 2024 paper modelling land use and land cover change in the Bangweulu wetland with machine learning.

name: Kafue Flats Collaborative Management Partnership
summary: Active 20-year partnership signed in 2022 with the Department of National Parks and Wildlife and WWF Zambia, under which the Ministry of Tourism says a wetland information system, monitoring plan and 2025 survey report were developed.

name: Kafue Flats Wetland Information System
summary: Online Kafue Flats biodiversity platform, launched 30 October 2026, documenting 480 bird species and, the International Crane Foundation said, combining data from GBIF, eBird, iNaturalist and others.

name: Kafue National Park Connected Conservation Project
summary: A USAID-funded anti-poaching project at Lake Itezhi-Tezhi, where WWF Zambia reported in 2020 thermal cameras covering about 20 km and ivory poaching down almost 50% from 2015.

name: Kafue River Transect 2024
summary: Closed 2024 expedition from the Kafue's source to its Zambezi confluence, assessing biodiversity, water quality and flow, which recorded 5,119 animals of 18 species; the Wilderness Project re-sampled Kafue National Park sites in June 2025.

name: Kapasa Makasa University
summary: Zambian university proclaimed in 2016 whose affiliated authors wrote a 2025 remote sensing study of forest degradation in Kafue National Park, and appear on a 2025 biomass paper.

name: Kasanka straw-coloured fruit bat research
summary: Research at Kasanka on straw-coloured fruit bats, involving cameras, tags and a drone in November 2019, with annual camera counts planned by Kasanka Trust.

name: Kasanka Trust
summary: Not-for-profit conservation organisation registered in Zambia in 1987 that manages Kasanka National Park, carried out mammal monitoring in late 2019, and uses the Smart Spatial Monitoring and Reporting Tool.

name: Lion Landscapes Zambia biodiversity monitoring survey (2021)
summary: Camera trap and distance sampling survey run by Lion Landscapes in 2021, with 104 camera traps at 52 stations, aiming to build a biodiversity monitoring system for the Lower Zambezi REDD+ Project area and LCFP.

name: Livingstone Museum
summary: Zambia's oldest and largest museum, which says it holds the largest reference collection on Zambian biodiversity and publishes Zambian bat specimen and monitoring datasets through GBIF.

name: Manyinga District pilot forest inventory
summary: Pilot forest inventory run by Zambia's Forestry Department with FAO, UN-REDD and AIM4Forests support, assessing 44 three-plot clusters in 2024, expected to inform an updated district management plan.

name: Ministry of Green Economy and Environment
summary: A Zambian government ministry responsible for environmental management, proposed by the President in September 2021, and home to the Forestry Department.

name: Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources
summary: Zambian ministry in Lusaka whose Chief Natural Resources Management Officer is named as CBD National Focal Point, with the Clearing-House Mechanism focal point in its Planning and Information Department.

name: Mobilising Bat Occurrence Data in Zambia
summary: A GBIF Biodiversity Information for Development project, funded by the European Union through GBIF, to publish Zambian bat specimen data not already on GBIF, with an aim of a bat atlas.

name: Mulungushi University
summary: University with both authors of a 2025 Zambia ICT Journal paper, listed in OpenAlex, on using AI to reduce monkey-human conflicts.

name: Munyamadzi Game Reserve
summary: Game reserve in Nyimba, Zambia, saying it has monitored large mammals with ground transects since late 2016, added camera traps in 2020 and held an aerial survey in 2023.

name: Musekese Conservation
summary: A Zambian organisation founded in 2018 that monitors wildlife across the Greater Kafue Ecosystem using camera traps, acoustic monitoring, surveys and remote sensing, and is registered with GBIF.

name: National Remote Sensing Centre
summary: A body established in 1999 that says its mandate is providing remote sensing data and geo-information products, using Sentinel and Landsat imagery, and is a WeMAST consortium member.

name: North Luangwa Conservation Programme
summary: Partnership between FZS and DNPW, established in 1986, conserving about 22,000 square kilometres around North Luangwa National Park and monitoring with collars, transects and camera traps.

name: Nsumbu-Tanganyika Conservation Programme
summary: Programme whose Ecological Monitoring Unit, JRS reported in November 2023, had collared seven animals and collected 192 water samples for eDNA.

name: Panthera SMART programme in Kafue National Park
summary: A Panthera-run programme that, as Panthera said in July 2021, had used SMART in Kafue National Park since 2016 to monitor carnivore distribution and movement.

name: Project Lavushimanda (Miombo Belt Regeneration Program)
summary: Active WeForest project under its Miombo Belt Regeneration Program, aiming to reconnect Lavushimanda National Park with the Luangwa Valley and using camera trapping to monitor wildlife, per a May 2025 post.

name: Reducing carbon emissions in Zambia's forest using computer vision
summary: Early-stage forestry project entered in 2021, built by Zamculture, which described using satellite and drone imagery with convolutional neural networks, and reported a prototype but limited funding had prevented scaling up.

name: Rinato Space
summary: A Lusaka-based organisation with satellite land and crop monitoring tools that monitors about 32,000 hectares across 2,700 sites.

name: RX AI
summary: A programme run and built by Rinato Space that combines up to 39 data layers, with 94.5% of assessed restoration sites reported stable or improving, at medium confidence pending field validation.

name: Simalaha Smart Park Project
summary: Project led by Zambia's national parks department with Peace Parks Foundation that, in May 2025, used EarthRanger in an operations room and on scouts' phones, and supported elephant collaring.

name: Sioma Ngwezi large carnivore collaring
summary: Collaring of a wild dog, a lion and a lioness in Sioma Ngwezi National Park by WWF, DNPW and Panthera in September 2020, to study large carnivore ecology.

name: SWM Programme in the Mize Community Conservancy, Zambia
summary: Active programme supporting the establishment and management of the Mize Community Conservancy in Nyawa Chiefdom, Kazungula District, where twelve natural resource monitors were trained in ecological monitoring, data management and SMART.

name: University of Zambia
summary: Active university in Lusaka, listed through its Integrated Water Resources Management Centre as an affiliation by the first author of a 2024 machine learning study of Bangweulu wetland land cover change.

name: Using Drones To Monitor the Health of Endangered Elephants (2024-2025)
summary: Closed 2024-2025 project in Kafue National Park combining satellite collar data, drones and camera traps to evaluate elephant movements and body condition, using photogrammetry on drone and camera trap images.

name: Wattled and Grey Crowned Crane survey in Liuwa Plains, Barotse Floodplains and Busanga Plains
summary: Closed survey of Wattled and Grey Crowned Crane populations in Liuwa Plains, the Barotse Floodplains and Busanga Plains, by the International Crane Foundation with BirdWatch Zambia, as part of planned satellite tagging and long-term monitoring.

name: Wildlife Crime Prevention
summary: A Zambian company limited by guarantee with public benefit status that says it supports DNPW with a pangolin rehabilitation centre and better information gathering against wildlife trafficking.

name: World Vision Zambia
summary: Non-governmental organisation that, with Rinato Space, launched a youth-led forest change monitoring project, with young people in three districts trained by August 2025 to map forest sites using mobile survey tools.

name: WWF Zambia
summary: Conservation organisation that began the Kafue National Park Connected Conservation Project in 2016 after Zambia Wildlife Authority authorisation, and had a GIS analyst and technology projects officer in its wildlife programme in 2020.

name: Youth-Led Forest Change Monitoring Technology Project
summary: Active project launched by World Vision Zambia with Rinato Space to train local youth in data collection and forest surveillance tools, with a Chibombo youth champion saying it equips them to monitor mapped forests.

name: Zambia Jurisdictional Baseline for Verra REDD+ Methodology
summary: Closed 2023 to 2025 project by Arbonaut for Verra REDD+, which says it delivered jurisdictional baseline data, including forest and non-forest maps for 2012, 2017 and 2021, from sample-based assessment of very-high resolution imagery.

name: Zambia National Forest Monitoring System
summary: National forest monitoring programme that FAO describes as well established but partly institutionalised, developed mainly through UN-REDD, with Integrated Land Use Assessments, provincial laboratories and national land cover mapping as core parts.

name: Zambia Survey Department
summary: Government mapping body that in a 2014 country report gave its mandate as providing spatial data and aerial photography and producing national maps, and whose mapping branch had evaluated imagery contractors by then.

name: Zambia Wildlife and Protected Areas Accounts
summary: Accounts the World Bank said in April 2025 Zambia was updating under its Natural Capital Accounting Programme, intended to track wildlife using aerial surveys and ranger reports.

name: Zambian bat echolocation call library
summary: Dataset, built by Helen Taylor-Boyd, that a 2025 paper says is the first publicly available call library of this scale from Zambia, covering 238 individuals of 22 bat species recorded from 2015 to 2023.

name: Zambian Carnivore Programme
summary: Field-based non-profit, headquartered at Chinzombo, Mfuwe, that conserves Zambia's large carnivores through long-term monitoring, and says it intensively monitored 483 lions and 455 wild dogs in 2024.

name: Zambian Carnivore Programme leopard camera trap surveys
summary: Programme run by the Zambian Carnivore Programme, which continued leopard camera trap surveys in the Luangwa Valley and Greater Kafue Ecosystem in 2024, reporting 22,615 camera trap days across three grids.

name: African Wildlife Conservation Fund
summary: Its 2024 report records 70 adult wild dogs and three collared dogs in Savé Valley Conservancy, with Gonarezhou surveys planned for 2027.

name: Animal Population Management Database
summary: Database run by the Malilangwe Trust, recording GPS-referenced wildlife sightings, mortalities, movements, nests and poaching activity, and reportedly being integrated with QGIS to map queried events.

name: BirdLife Zimbabwe
summary: Based in Harare, it describes January and July waterbird counts in Zimbabwe, emphasising long-term monitoring and aiming to submit data to the African Waterbird Census Programme.

name: Dambari Wildlife Trust
summary: Non-profit conservation and research organisation active since 1997, which runs the Matobo Biodiversity Monitoring Project and, according to JRS, holds a $155,667 grant for 2025 to 2027 for Somabhula grassland surveys.

name: Department of Geography Geospatial Sciences and Earth Observation, University of Zimbabwe
summary: Based in Harare, its geospatial group maps and manages natural resources using Earth observation, while OpenAlex records lead affiliations on giraffe habitat and poaching-risk papers.

name: Department of Geoinformatics and Environmental Conservation, Chinhoyi University of Technology
summary: Chinhoyi University of Technology department recorded by OpenAlex as lead affiliation on 2024 and 2025 elephant papers, covering habitat occupancy from vegetation indices and landscape connectivity modelling.

name: Department of Wildlife Ecology and Conservation, Chinhoyi University of Technology
summary: Chinhoyi University of Technology department recorded by OpenAlex as lead affiliation, with ZimParks, on a 2026 paper modelling baobab habitat vulnerability to elephant pressure in the Mid-Zambezi Valley.

name: Environmental Management Agency
summary: Statutory body established under the Environmental Management Act of 2002, which The Herald reported in September 2026 uses fire risk mapping and near real-time satellite monitoring in fire-prone provinces.

name: Forestry Commission of Zimbabwe
summary: Parastatal established in 1954 to manage Zimbabwe's forests, whose research division applies drone mapping, GIS and remote sensing, and which is a GBIF endorsed publisher with no datasets published when read.

name: GBIF Zimbabwe
summary: GBIF country node for Zimbabwe, a voting participant in GBIF, with Luke Jimu listed in GBIF's directory as node manager.

name: Gonarezhou Conservation Trust
summary: Manages Gonarezhou National Park through a ZimParks and Frankfurt Zoological Society partnership, with aerial surveys, lion satellite tracking, vegetation monitoring and ecological databases.

name: Hwange elephant collaring programme
summary: ZimParks-led programme with IFAW, funded by Nationale Postcode Loterij, which fitted six more elephants with GPS satellite collars in September 2026, bringing the total since early 2024 to 30.

name: Lowveld Rhino Trust
summary: Trust that, according to Save the Rhino International in 2024, has monitored Bubye Valley Conservancy rhinos since 2002 by ear notch identification, averaging over 160 identifications a month in 2023.

name: Matetsi Unit 5 camera trap baseline survey
summary: Baseline survey of species distribution and habitat use in Matetsi Unit 5, begun in February 2026 when IFAW, ZimParks and Munchkin deployed 11 camera traps.

name: Matobo Biodiversity Monitoring Project
summary: Launched by Dambari Wildlife Trust in 2012, this schools programme involves transects, quadrats and pitfall traps, with the trust analysing data and maintaining an electronic database.

name: Ministry of Environment, Climate and Wildlife
summary: Zimbabwean ministry that develops and monitors environment and natural resources policy, coordinates environmental agreements, and, per a clearing-house site, was implementing a six-year GEF-funded project with UNDP in 2021.

name: Painted Dog Conservation
summary: Private voluntary organisation at Dete, Zimbabwe, that tracks painted dogs with radio collars, keeps a photo-based digital identity register, and takes samples for DNA analysis and disease screening.

name: Sengwa Wildlife Research Area
summary: Research area where, according to ZimParks' saved list, an ongoing project monitors key species population trends, dispersal and status.

name: Silent Signals, Investigating Cheetah Communication Hubs to Inform Conservation in Northwestern Zimbabwe
summary: Project that aims to identify the cheetah's core home range and communication hubs in Hwange National Park and use camera traps to record who visits them and when.

name: The Malilangwe Trust
summary: Zimbabwean non-profit working within the 50,000 ha Malilangwe Wildlife Reserve, whose scouts have recorded GPS wildlife sightings since 1998 and which runs the Animal Population Management Database.

name: Victoria Falls Wildlife Trust
summary: Its wildlife disease diagnostics and forensics laboratory in Victoria Falls National Park aims to study zoonotic and transboundary animal diseases, and it partners with a vulture nesting study.

name: Wildlife Conservation Action
summary: Founded in 2019 and based in Harare, it promotes human-wildlife coexistence, researches Sebungwe elephants and lions, and aims to improve conflict mitigation and monitoring in Mbire District.

name: Zimbabwe Ecological Conservation, white-backed vulture nesting sites study
summary: Closed project on white-backed vulture nesting sites in Zimbabwe that used Landsat 5, 8 and 9 imagery to assess vegetation health and landscape change from 1994 to 2024.

name: Zimbabwe Flying Labs
summary: Harare drone organisation that mapped 45 hectares of Monavale Wetland in 2021 and, in 2024, trained and certified ZimParks drone pilots in Mana Pools as a consultancy.

name: Zimbabwe National Geospatial and Space Agency
summary: Government-owned agency launched in 2021 that delivered the Zimbabwe Wetlands Master Plan 2021 through satellite mapping and, by its own statement, was working on drone game counts.

name: Zimbabwe national wetlands map and geo-database
summary: Wetlands inventory built by the national geospatial agency, reported by The Herald in 2021 as a national map, 10 provincial and 63 district maps, a geo-database and an interactive GIS web map.

name: Zimbabwe Parks and Wildlife Management Authority
summary: Zimbabwe's wildlife protection and management authority, with 19 terrestrial ecologists, 20 rangers and 16 aquatic ecologists, whose monitoring projects include collared elephants in Hwange, Matetsi and Kazuma Pan.
